declarations.name: Ideal.idealOfDefinition_support_length_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B00, finite-length conditions.** Let `M` be a finite module over a
Noetherian local ring and `I` an ideal. If `M / IM` is nonzero, then the following are
equivalent: `I + Ann(M)` is an ideal of definition; the image of `I` in `R / Ann(M)` is an
ideal of definition; the support of `M / IM` is contained in the closed point; that support
has dimension at most zero; and `M / IM` has finite length.
declarations.statement:
theorem idealOfDefinition_support_length_tfae
    {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (I : Ideal R) (hMI : Nontrivial (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) :
    letI := hMI
    letI : Nontrivial M := (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)).mkQ_surjective.nontrivial
    letI : Nontrivial (R ⧸ Module.annihilator R M) :=
      Ideal.Quotient.nontrivial_iff.mpr
        (mt Module.annihilator_eq_top_iff.mp (not_subsingleton M))
    letI : IsLocalRing (R ⧸ Module.annihilator R M) :=
      IsLocalRing.of_surjective' (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Module.annihilator R M))
        Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective
    List.TFAE [
      IsIdealOfDefinition (I + Module.annihilator R M),
      IsIdealOfDefinition
        (Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Module.annihilator R M)) I),
      Module.support R (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) ⊆ {IsLocalRing.closedPoint R},
      Module.supportDim R (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) ≤ 0,
      Module.length R (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) < ⊤]
declarations.comment: finite_length_conditions

declarations.name: Ideal.generalizedHilbertFunction
declarations.doc: The generalized Hilbert function `χ_{I,M}(n) = length_R(M / I^n M)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def generalizedHilbertFunction
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (M : Type*)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (n : ℕ) : ℕ∞
declarations.comment: generalized_hilbert_function

declarations.name: Ideal.generalizedHilbertFunction_lt_top
declarations.doc: If `M / IM` has finite length, then so does `M / I^n M` for every `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem generalizedHilbertFunction_lt_top
    {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (I : Ideal R)
    (hIM : Module.length R (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) < ⊤)
    (n : ℕ) : Ideal.generalizedHilbertFunction I M n < ⊤
declarations.comment: generalized_hilbert_function

declarations.name: Ideal.generalizedHilbertFunction_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
The length of `M / I^n M` is the sum of the lengths of its successive `I`-adic layers,
including the empty sum when `n = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem generalizedHilbertFunction_eq_sum
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (M : Type*)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (n : ℕ) :
    Ideal.generalizedHilbertFunction I M n =
      ∑ p ∈ Finset.range n,
        Module.length R
          (↥(I ^ p • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) ⧸
            (I ^ (p + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule R M)).submoduleOf
              (I ^ p • (⊤ : Submodule R M)))
declarations.comment: generalized_hilbert_function

declarations.name: Ideal.exists_computesGeneralizedHilbertPoly_degree_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B00, eventual polynomiality.** Let `M` be a finite module over a
Noetherian local ring and let `I` be an ideal with `M / IM` of finite length. For every
`d ≥ dim(Supp(M))` there is a rational polynomial of degree at most `d` which computes
`χ_{I, M}(n) = length(M / I ^ n M)` for all large `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_computesGeneralizedHilbertPoly_degree_le
    {A M : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M] (I : Ideal A)
    (hI : Module.length A (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule A M)) < ⊤)
    {d : ℕ} (hd : Module.supportDim A M ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    ∃ P : ℚ[X], I.ComputesGeneralizedHilbertPoly M P ∧ P.degree ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ)
declarations.comment: eventual_polynomiality

declarations.name: Ideal.exists_degree_lt_generalizedHilbertFunction_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B00, asymptotics of the generalized Hilbert function.** Let `M` be
a finite module over a Noetherian local ring and let `I` be an ideal with `M / IM` of finite
length. For every `d ≥ dim(Supp(M))` there are lower order terms, a rational polynomial of
degree `< d`, such that for all large `n` the length `χ_{I, M}(n) = length(M / I ^ n M)` is
finite and equals `e_I(M, d) * n ^ d / d !` plus those terms.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_degree_lt_generalizedHilbertFunction_eq
    {A M : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M] (I : Ideal A)
    (hI : Module.length A (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule A M)) < ⊤)
    {d : ℕ} (hd : Module.supportDim A M ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    ∃ Q : ℚ[X], Q.degree < (d : WithBot ℕ) ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ p : ℕ,
        I.generalizedHilbertFunction M n = (p : ℕ∞) ∧
          (p : ℚ) = I.generalizedHilbertSamuelMultiplicity M d * (n : ℚ) ^ d
            / (d.factorial : ℚ) + Q.eval (n : ℚ)
declarations.comment: asymptotics

declarations.name: Ideal.generalizedHilbertSamuelMultiplicity
declarations.doc:
The generalized Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity `e_I(M, d)`: `d !` times the coefficient of
degree `d` in the rational polynomial eventually computing `length_R (M / I ^ n M)`.

For a finite module over a Noetherian local ring, when `M / I M` is nonzero of finite length
and `d` is at least the dimension of the support of `M`, this is the generalized multiplicity
of Tag 0B00.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Ideal.generalizedHilbertSamuelMultiplicity {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (d : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.comment: generalized_multiplicity

declarations.name: Ideal.generalizedHilbertFunction_add_annihilator
declarations.doc: Adding the annihilator of `M` to `I` does not change the length of `M / I^n M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem generalizedHilbertFunction_add_annihilator
    {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (I : Ideal R) (n : ℕ) :
    Ideal.generalizedHilbertFunction (I + Module.annihilator R M) M n =
      Ideal.generalizedHilbertFunction I M n
declarations.comment: invariance_under_adding_annihilator

declarations.name: Ideal.generalizedHilbertFunction_add_annihilator_eq_map_quotientAnnihilator
declarations.doc:
The generalized Hilbert function is unchanged by passing from `I + Ann(M)` over `R` to the
image of `I` over `R / Ann(M)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem generalizedHilbertFunction_add_annihilator_eq_map_quotientAnnihilator
    {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (I : Ideal R) (n : ℕ) :
    letI : Module (R ⧸ Module.annihilator R M) M := Module.quotientAnnihilator
    Ideal.generalizedHilbertFunction (I + Module.annihilator R M) M n =
      Ideal.generalizedHilbertFunction
        (Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Module.annihilator R M)) I) M n
declarations.comment: invariance_under_quotient_by_annihilator

declarations.name: Ideal.generalizedHilbertSamuelMultiplicity_add_annihilator_eq_map_quotientAnnihilator
declarations.doc:
Generalized Hilbert–Samuel multiplicities are unchanged by passing to the quotient ring by
the annihilator of the module.
declarations.statement:
theorem generalizedHilbertSamuelMultiplicity_add_annihilator_eq_map_quotientAnnihilator
    {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (I : Ideal R) (d : ℕ) :
    letI : Module (R ⧸ Module.annihilator R M) M := Module.quotientAnnihilator
    Ideal.generalizedHilbertSamuelMultiplicity (I + Module.annihilator R M) M d =
      Ideal.generalizedHilbertSamuelMultiplicity
        (Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Module.annihilator R M)) I) M d
declarations.comment: invariance_under_quotient_by_annihilator

declarations.name: Ideal.add_annihilator_pow_smul_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B00, quotient power equalities.** Adjoining the annihilator of a
module to an ideal does not change the submodule generated by any power of that ideal.
declarations.statement:
lemma add_annihilator_pow_smul_top
    {R M : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
    (I : Ideal R) (n : ℕ) :
    (I + Module.annihilator R M) ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule R M) =
      I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule R M)
declarations.comment: quotient_power_equalities

declarations.name: Ideal.map_quotientAnnihilator_pow_smul_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B00, quotient power equalities.** If `M` is regarded as a module
over `R / Ann(M)`, the image of a power of `I` generates the same submodule as that power of
`I` does over `R`.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_quotientAnnihilator_pow_smul_top
    {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (I : Ideal R) (n : ℕ) :
    letI : Module (R ⧸ Module.annihilator R M) M := Module.quotientAnnihilator
    ((Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Module.annihilator R M)) I) ^ n •
        (⊤ : Submodule (R ⧸ Module.annihilator R M) M)).restrictScalars R =
      I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule R M)
declarations.comment: quotient_power_equalities

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.localIntersectionMultiplicity_stalk_eq_length_stalk_sup_of_isCohenMacaulay
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B02, the multiplicity formula at one component.** Let `Y` be a
locally Noetherian regular scheme and `V`, `W` sheaves of ideals, and let `ξ` be a point lying
on both of them which is a generic point of `V ∩ W` and at which `V` and `W` intersect
properly. If `𝒪_{V, ξ}`
and `𝒪_{W, ξ}` are Cohen-Macaulay, then

`e(X, V · W, Z) = length_{𝒪_{X, ξ}}(𝒪_{V ∩ W, ξ})`,

where `Z` is the component of `V ∩ W` with generic point `ξ` and `V ∩ W` is the
scheme-theoretic intersection, cut out by `V ⊔ W`. Every hypothesis is imposed at `ξ` alone.
declarations.statement:
theorem localIntersectionMultiplicity_stalk_eq_length_stalk_sup_of_isCohenMacaulay
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] (hY : IsRegular Y) (V W : Y.IdealSheafData) (z : Y)
    (hzV : z ∈ V.support) (hzW : z ∈ W.support)
    (hCMV : haveI := isLocalRing_quotient_stalk V z hzV
      IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (Y.presheaf.stalk z ⧸ IdealSheafData.stalk V z))
    (hCMW : haveI := isLocalRing_quotient_stalk W z hzW
      IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (Y.presheaf.stalk z ⧸ IdealSheafData.stalk W z))
    (hproper : ringKrullDim (Y.presheaf.stalk z) ≤
      ringKrullDim (Y.presheaf.stalk z ⧸ IdealSheafData.stalk V z) +
        ringKrullDim (Y.presheaf.stalk z ⧸ IdealSheafData.stalk W z))
    (hcomponent : (IdealSheafData.stalk V z ⊔ IdealSheafData.stalk W z).radical =
      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Y.presheaf.stalk z)) :
    (IdealSheafData.stalk V z).localIntersectionMultiplicity
        (Y.presheaf.stalk z ⧸ IdealSheafData.stalk W z) =
      ((Module.length (Y.presheaf.stalk z)
        (Y.presheaf.stalk z ⧸ IdealSheafData.stalk (V ⊔ W) z)).toNat : ℚ)
declarations.comment: the first clause, at one component: `e(X, V · W, Z) = length_{𝒪_{X, ξ}}(𝒪_{V ∩ W, ξ})` for an irreducible component `Z` of `V ∩ W` with generic point `ξ`, assuming only that `𝒪_{V, ξ}` and `𝒪_{W, ξ}` are Cohen-Macaulay. The nonsingular variety is a locally Noetherian regular scheme `Y`, the closed subvarieties are sheaves of ideals `V` and `W`, and every hypothesis is read at `ξ` alone: `ξ` lies on `V` and on `W`, that `ξ` is a generic point of a component of `V ∩ W` is the radical condition `√(V_ξ ⊔ W_ξ) = 𝔪_ξ`, and proper intersection at `Z` is the dimension inequality `dim 𝒪_{X, ξ} ≤ dim 𝒪_{V, ξ} + dim 𝒪_{W, ξ}` of Tag 0B1I (for a variety, `dim Z ≤ dim V + dim W - dim X`). `e(X, V · W, Z)` is `Ideal.localIntersectionMultiplicity`, the alternating sum of lengths of `Tor` modules by which Section 43.14 defines the coefficient of `Z` in `V · W`, and `𝒪_{V ∩ W, ξ}` is the stalk at `ξ` of the scheme-theoretic intersection, cut out by `V ⊔ W`. The final `In particular` clause is `AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.cohenMacaulayIntersectionFormula`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.cohenMacaulayIntersectionFormula
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B02.** Let `X` be a nonsingular variety and `V`, `W ⊆ X` closed
subvarieties which intersect properly, let `Z` be an irreducible component of `V ∩ W` with
generic point `ξ`, and assume `𝒪_{V, ξ}` and `𝒪_{W, ξ}` are Cohen-Macaulay. Then

`e(X, V · W, Z) = length_{𝒪_{X, ξ}}(𝒪_{V ∩ W, ξ})`,

where `V ∩ W` is the scheme-theoretic intersection; and in particular, if both `V` and `W` are
Cohen-Macaulay, then `V · W = [V ∩ W]_{dim V + dim W - dim X}`.

The nonsingular variety is a regular scheme `Y` of dimension at most `d`, the two closed
subvarieties are sheaves of ideals `V` and `W`, and `ξ` is a point `z` of delta-dimension `k`
lying on both of them, which under `hVW` is exactly the generic point of a component of
`V ∩ W`. The multiplicity `e(X, V · W, Z)` is `Ideal.localIntersectionMultiplicity`, the
alternating sum of lengths of `Tor` modules by which Section 43.14 computes it, and
`𝒪_{V ∩ W, ξ}` is the stalk of the scheme-theoretic intersection, cut out by `V ⊔ W`. The
product `V · W` is the cycle `AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.intersectionProductCycle` of
Tag 0AZR.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohenMacaulayIntersectionFormula
    (C : Stacks.Chow.ChowSituation.{u}) (f : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] (hY : IsRegular Y) (V W : Y.IdealSheafData) (k : ℤ)
    (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim Y ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hVW : Stacks.Chow.schemeDeltaDimension C ((V ⊔ W).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ (k : EInt))
    (hFk : ∀ i : ℕ,
      haveI := isCoherent_torSheaf_of_isRegular Y hY (subschemeStructureSheaf V)
        (subschemeStructureSheaf W) (isCoherent_subschemeStructureSheaf V)
        (isCoherent_subschemeStructureSheaf W) i
      Stacks.Chow.schemeDeltaDimension C
        ((Stacks.Chow.reducedSupport
          (torSheaf Y (subschemeStructureSheaf V) (subschemeStructureSheaf W) i)).subschemeι ≫ f)
        ≤ WithBotTop.coe k)
    (hpt : ∀ z : Y, Stacks.Chow.relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction f z = k →
      ∀ (hzV : z ∈ V.support) (hzW : z ∈ W.support),
        haveI := isLocalRing_quotient_stalk V z hzV
        haveI := isLocalRing_quotient_stalk W z hzW
        IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (Y.presheaf.stalk z ⧸ IdealSheafData.stalk V z) ∧
        IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (Y.presheaf.stalk z ⧸ IdealSheafData.stalk W z) ∧
        ringKrullDim (Y.presheaf.stalk z) ≤
          ringKrullDim (Y.presheaf.stalk z ⧸ IdealSheafData.stalk V z) +
            ringKrullDim (Y.presheaf.stalk z ⧸ IdealSheafData.stalk W z) ∧
        (IdealSheafData.stalk V z ⊔ IdealSheafData.stalk W z).radical =
          IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Y.presheaf.stalk z)) :
    (∀ z : Y, Stacks.Chow.relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction f z = k →
        z ∈ V.support → z ∈ W.support →
          (IdealSheafData.stalk V z).localIntersectionMultiplicity
              (Y.presheaf.stalk z ⧸ IdealSheafData.stalk W z) =
            ((Module.length (Y.presheaf.stalk z)
              (Y.presheaf.stalk z ⧸ IdealSheafData.stalk (V ⊔ W) z)).toNat : ℚ)) ∧
      (Stacks.Chow.cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C f (V ⊔ W).subschemeι k).1 =
        intersectionProductCycle C f hY (subschemeStructureSheaf V) (subschemeStructureSheaf W)
          (isCoherent_subschemeStructureSheaf V) (isCoherent_subschemeStructureSheaf W) k hFk
declarations.comment: the whole lemma: both the multiplicity formula `e(X, V · W, Z) = length_{𝒪_{X, ξ}}(𝒪_{V ∩ W, ξ})` at the generic point of each component of `V ∩ W` and the source's final `In particular` clause, `V · W = [V ∩ W]_{dim V + dim W - dim X}`, as an identity of algebraic cycles. The nonsingular variety is a regular scheme `Y` of dimension at most `d`, the two closed subvarieties are sheaves of ideals `V` and `W`, and `V · W` is the Section 43.14 product of Tag 0AZR, `AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.intersectionProductCycle`, which takes the delta-dimension bounds `hFk` on the supports of the `Tor` sheaves exactly as the definition of that tag does. The source's hypotheses are local at the generic point `ξ` of a component of `V ∩ W`, and that is where they are read: at a point `z` of delta-dimension `k` lying on both subvarieties — which under `hVW` is exactly such a generic point — `𝒪_{V, z}` and `𝒪_{W, z}` are Cohen-Macaulay, proper intersection is the dimension inequality of Tag 0B1I, and that `z` is a generic point of `V ∩ W` is the radical condition. `e(X, V · W, Z)` is `Ideal.localIntersectionMultiplicity`, the alternating sum of lengths of `Tor` modules by which Section 43.14 computes the multiplicity, and `𝒪_{V ∩ W, ξ}` is the stalk at `z` of the scheme-theoretic intersection, cut out by `V ⊔ W`. `WithBot ℕ∞` has no subtraction, so the source's dimension index `dim V + dim W - dim X` is generalised to an arbitrary `k`, the index at which the two cycles are formed and whose relation to `V ∩ W` is the delta-dimension bound `hVW`. Here the hypotheses are imposed at every such generic point at once, as the `In particular` clause needs; the first clause at a single component, with hypotheses at its generic point alone, is `TorFormula.localIntersectionMultiplicity_stalk_eq_length_stalk_sup_of_isCohenMacaulay`.

declarations.name: Ideal.generalizedHilbertSamuelMultiplicity_eq_alternatingSum_tor_length
declarations.doc:
The generalized multiplicity of an ideal generated by a regular sequence equals the
alternating sum of the lengths of the Tor groups of `A / I` and `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem generalizedHilbertSamuelMultiplicity_eq_alternatingSum_tor_length
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A) (M : Type u)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
    (hf : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular A (List.ofFn f))
    (hI : I = Ideal.span (Set.range f))
    (hM : Module.supportDim A (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule A M)) = 0) :
    I.generalizedHilbertSamuelMultiplicity M r =
      ∑ i : Fin (r + 1), (-1 : ℚ) ^ (i : ℕ) *
        ((Module.length A
          (((Tor (ModuleCat.{u} A) (i : ℕ)).obj (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I))).obj
            (ModuleCat.of A M))).toNat : ℚ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.localIntersectionMultiplicity_eq_factorial_mul_leadingCoeff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B04, in local form at the generic point.** Let `A` be a regular local ring, let `I`
be an ideal generated by a regular sequence `f₁, …, f_c`, and let `J` be an ideal with
`dim (A ⧸ (I ⊔ J)) = 0` and `dim A ≤ dim (A ⧸ I) + dim (A ⧸ J)`. Then the function
`t ↦ length_A ((A ⧸ J) ⧸ I ^ t (A ⧸ J))` is computed for `t ≫ 0` by a rational polynomial of
degree `c` with positive leading coefficient, and the Tor-formula intersection multiplicity of
the pair is `c !` times that leading coefficient.

Geometrically, for `A` the local ring of a nonsingular variety `X` at the generic point `ξ` of an
irreducible component `Z` of `V ∩ W`, with `I` and `J` the local ideals of two closed
subvarieties intersecting properly and `I` cut out by a regular sequence of length `c`, this says
that `e(X, V · W, Z)` is `c !` times the leading coefficient of the Hilbert polynomial
`t ↦ length_{𝒪_{X, ξ}} 𝒪_{W, ξ} / (f₁, …, f_c) ^ t`, and that this coefficient is positive.
declarations.statement:
theorem localIntersectionMultiplicity_eq_factorial_mul_leadingCoeff {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [IsRegularLocalRing A] {c : ℕ} (f : Fin c → A) (I J : Ideal A)
    (hf : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular A (List.ofFn f))
    (hI : I = Ideal.span (Set.range f))
    (h0 : ringKrullDim (A ⧸ (I ⊔ J)) = 0)
    (hproper : ringKrullDim A ≤ ringKrullDim (A ⧸ I) + ringKrullDim (A ⧸ J)) :
    ∃ P : ℚ[X], I.ComputesGeneralizedHilbertPoly (A ⧸ J) P ∧
      P.degree = (c : WithBot ℕ) ∧ 0 < P.leadingCoeff ∧
      I.localIntersectionMultiplicity (A ⧸ J) = (c.factorial : ℚ) * P.leadingCoeff
declarations.comment:
the multiplicity formula and the positivity of the leading coefficient, in local
form at the generic point

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.localIntersectionMultiplicity_eq_length_quotient_smul_of_isDomain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B05.** In the situation of Tag 0B04, assume `c = 1`, so that `I = (f₁)` with `f₁` a
nonzerodivisor of `A`, and assume `A ⧸ J` is a domain. Then the Tor-formula intersection
multiplicity of the pair is the single length `length_A ((A ⧸ J) ⧸ f₁ (A ⧸ J))`.

Geometrically, for `A = 𝒪_{X, ξ}` at the generic point `ξ` of an irreducible component `Z` of
`V ∩ W` and `I`, `J` the local ideals of two closed subvarieties intersecting properly, `c = 1`
says that `V` is an effective Cartier divisor and `A ⧸ J = 𝒪_{W, ξ}` is a domain because `W` is
a variety; the conclusion is
`e(X, V · W, Z) = length_{𝒪_{X, ξ}}(𝒪_{W, ξ} / f₁ 𝒪_{W, ξ})`. The hypothesis
`dim (A ⧸ (I ⊔ J)) = 0` forces `f₁ ∉ J`, so `f₁` is a nonzerodivisor on the one-dimensional
domain `A ⧸ J` and `length_A ((A ⧸ J) ⧸ f₁ⁿ (A ⧸ J)) = n · length_A ((A ⧸ J) ⧸ f₁ (A ⧸ J))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localIntersectionMultiplicity_eq_length_quotient_smul_of_isDomain {A : Type u}
    [CommRing A] [IsRegularLocalRing A] (f : Fin 1 → A) (I J : Ideal A) [IsDomain (A ⧸ J)]
    (hf : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular A (List.ofFn f))
    (hI : I = Ideal.span (Set.range f))
    (h0 : ringKrullDim (A ⧸ (I ⊔ J)) = 0)
    (hproper : ringKrullDim A ≤ ringKrullDim (A ⧸ I) + ringKrullDim (A ⧸ J)) :
    I.localIntersectionMultiplicity (A ⧸ J) =
      ((Module.length A ((A ⧸ J) ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule A (A ⧸ J)))).toNat : ℚ)
declarations.comment: the multiplicity formula for an effective Cartier divisor, in local form at the generic point: for `I` generated by a single nonzerodivisor `f₁` of the regular local ring `A` and `A ⧸ J` a domain, the Tor-formula multiplicity of the pair is `length_A ((A ⧸ J) ⧸ f₁ (A ⧸ J))`. The hypotheses are those of Tag 0B04, transported to `A = 𝒪_{X, ξ}` exactly as there, with the extra hypothesis that `A ⧸ J` is a domain, which the source carries in the standing assumption that `W` is a closed subvariety and which the local form of Tag 0B04 does not need; without it the conclusion fails, for instance for `A = k[x, y]` at the origin with `I = (y)` and `J = (x², xy)`.

declarations.name: Ideal.localIntersectionMultiplicity_eq_length_quotient_smul_of_isCohenMacaulayLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B06.** In the situation of Tag 0B04 — `A` a regular local ring, `I` generated by a
regular sequence `f₁, …, f_c`, `J` an ideal with `dim (A ⧸ (I ⊔ J)) = 0` and
`dim A ≤ dim (A ⧸ I) + dim (A ⧸ J)` — assume moreover that `A ⧸ J` is Cohen-Macaulay. Then the
Tor-formula intersection multiplicity of the pair is the single length
`length_A ((A ⧸ J) ⧸ (f₁, …, f_c)(A ⧸ J))`, with no Hilbert polynomial left over.

Geometrically, for `A = 𝒪_{X, ξ}` at the generic point `ξ` of an irreducible component `Z` of
`V ∩ W` and `I`, `J` the local ideals of two closed subvarieties intersecting properly with `V`
cut out at `ξ` by the regular sequence, this says
`e(X, V · W, Z) = length_{𝒪_{X, ξ}}(𝒪_{W, ξ} / f₁𝒪_{W, ξ} + … + f_c𝒪_{W, ξ})` as soon as
`𝒪_{W, ξ}` is Cohen-Macaulay.
declarations.statement:
public theorem localIntersectionMultiplicity_eq_length_quotient_smul_of_isCohenMacaulayLocalRing
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsRegularLocalRing A] {c : ℕ} (f : Fin c → A) (I J : Ideal A)
    [IsLocalRing (A ⧸ J)] (hJ : IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (A ⧸ J))
    (hf : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular A (List.ofFn f))
    (hI : I = Ideal.span (Set.range f))
    (h0 : ringKrullDim (A ⧸ (I ⊔ J)) = 0)
    (hproper : ringKrullDim A ≤ ringKrullDim (A ⧸ I) + ringKrullDim (A ⧸ J)) :
    I.localIntersectionMultiplicity (A ⧸ J) =
      ((Module.length A ((A ⧸ J) ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule A (A ⧸ J)))).toNat : ℚ)
declarations.comment: the multiplicity formula when the local ring of the second subvariety is Cohen-Macaulay, in local form at the generic point: for `I` generated by a regular sequence of length `c` in the regular local ring `A` and `A ⧸ J` Cohen-Macaulay, the Tor-formula multiplicity of the pair is `length_A ((A ⧸ J) ⧸ I (A ⧸ J))`. The source's hypotheses are those of Tag 0B04, transported to `A = 𝒪_{X, ξ}` exactly as there, with proper intersection the dimension inequality of Tag 0B1I and `ξ` being the generic point of a component of `V ∩ W` the vanishing of `dim (A ⧸ (I ⊔ J))`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.tag_0B07
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B07.** Let `X` be a nonsingular variety over an algebraically closed
field, let `a ≠ b` be closed points of `ℙ¹` and let `k` be an integer. Writing `X × a` for the
image of the section of `X ×_S ℙ¹_S ⟶ X` at `a`:

0. that section is constant at `a` — its second projection sends every point of `X` to `a` — so
   `X × a` is the fibre of `X ×_S ℙ¹_S ⟶ ℙ¹_S` over `a`, and likewise at `b`;
1. if `W ⊆ X ×_S ℙ¹_S` is a closed subvariety of delta-dimension `k + 1` meeting `X × a`
   properly, then (a) `[W_a]_k = W · (X × a)` as cycles on `X ×_S ℙ¹_S`, and (b)
   `[W_a]_k = pr_{X,*}(W · X × a)` as cycles on `X`;
2. for every `(k + 1)`-cycle `α` on `X ×_S ℙ¹_S` meeting `X × a` and `X × b` properly,
   `pr_{X,*}(α · X × a - α · X × b)` is rationally equivalent to zero;
3. conversely, every `k`-cycle rationally equivalent to zero is of that form.

The intersection products are the Section 43.14 products of Tag 0AZR, read on cycles by the Tag
0B08 product; rational equivalence is `Stacks.Chow.rationalEquivalences`, the group of Tag 02RW;
and "of that form" is `Stacks.Chow.PointCycle.IsSectionPairFibreIntersectionDifference`, which
spells out the conclusion of (2). Nothing is assumed about the ambient family `X ×_S ℙ¹_S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tag_0B07 (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] (Kf : Type u) [Field Kf] [IsAlgClosed Kf]
    (hC : C.S = AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of Kf))
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsVariety Kf (p ≫ eqToHom hC)] (hX : IsRegular X) (k : ℤ)
    (a b : relativeProjectiveLine C.S) (ha : IsClosed {a}) (hb : IsClosed {b}) (hab : a ≠ b) :
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian (projectiveLineProduct p) :=
      LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian
        (pullback.fst p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S) ≫ p)
    ((∀ x : X, (closedPointSection Kf hC a ha p ≫
            pullback.snd p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S)) x = a) ∧
        ∀ x : X, (closedPointSection Kf hC b hb p ≫
          pullback.snd p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S)) x = b) ∧
      (∀ W : (projectiveLineProduct p).IdealSheafData, IsIntegral W.subscheme →
        (∀ ξ : genericPoints W.subscheme,
          relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction (familyBase p W) ξ.1 = k + 1) →
        ∀ hWD : schemeDeltaDimension C
            ((W ⊔ (closedPointSection Kf hC a ha p).ker).subschemeι ≫
              (pullback.fst p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S) ≫ p)) ≤ (k : EInt),
          (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C
              (pullback.fst p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S) ≫ p)
              (W ⊔ (closedPointSection Kf hC a ha p).ker).subschemeι k).1 =
            intersectionProductCycle C (pullback.fst p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S) ≫ p)
              (isRegular_projectiveLineProduct_of_eq p hC hX)
              (subschemeStructureSheaf W)
              (subschemeStructureSheaf (closedPointSection Kf hC a ha p).ker)
              (isCoherent_subschemeStructureSheaf W)
              (isCoherent_subschemeStructureSheaf (closedPointSection Kf hC a ha p).ker) k
              (schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_torSheaf_le C
                (pullback.fst p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S) ≫ p)
                (isRegular_projectiveLineProduct_of_eq p hC hX) W
                (closedPointSection Kf hC a ha p).ker k hWD) ∧
          properPushforward C (pullback.fst p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S) ≫ p) p
              (pullback.fst p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S)) rfl k
              ⟨intersectionProductCycle C
                  (pullback.fst p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S) ≫ p)
                  (isRegular_projectiveLineProduct_of_eq p hC hX)
                  (subschemeStructureSheaf W)
                  (subschemeStructureSheaf (closedPointSection Kf hC a ha p).ker)
                  (isCoherent_subschemeStructureSheaf W)
                  (isCoherent_subschemeStructureSheaf (closedPointSection Kf hC a ha p).ker) k
                  (schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_torSheaf_le C
                    (pullback.fst p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S) ≫ p)
                    (isRegular_projectiveLineProduct_of_eq p hC hX) W
                    (closedPointSection Kf hC a ha p).ker k hWD),
                intersectionProductCycle_mem_cyclesOfDimension C
                  (pullback.fst p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S) ≫ p)
                  (isRegular_projectiveLineProduct_of_eq p hC hX) W
                  (closedPointSection Kf hC a ha p).ker k hWD⟩ =
            cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p
              (W.comap (closedPointSection Kf hC a ha p)).subschemeι k) ∧
      (∀ α : CycleGroup C (pullback.fst p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S) ≫ p) (k + 1),
          ∀ hT₁ : ∀ x ∈ Function.support α.1, ¬ Set.range (integralComponentAt x).subschemeι ⊆
            Set.range (closedPointSection Kf hC a ha p),
          ∀ hT₂ : ∀ x ∈ Function.support α.1, ¬ Set.range (integralComponentAt x).subschemeι ⊆
            Set.range (closedPointSection Kf hC b hb p),
            properPushforward C (pullback.fst p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S) ≫ p) p
                (pullback.fst p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S)) rfl k
                ⟨torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct C
                    (pullback.fst p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S) ≫ p)
                    (isRegular_projectiveLineProduct_of_eq p hC hX) k α.1
                    (@Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single (projectiveLineProduct p) _ ℤ
                      (Classical.decEq _) _
                      ((closedPointSection Kf hC a ha p) (genericPoint X)) (1 : ℤ)),
                  torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct_section_mem_cyclesOfDimension C p Kf hC
                    (isRegular_projectiveLineProduct_of_eq p hC hX) k
                    (exists_closedPointSection_eq_pointSection_or_eq_infinitySection Kf hC a ha p)
                    α hT₁⟩ -
              properPushforward C (pullback.fst p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S) ≫ p) p
                (pullback.fst p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S)) rfl k
                ⟨torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct C
                    (pullback.fst p (relativeProjectiveLine C.S ↘ C.S) ≫ p)
                    (isRegular_projectiveLineProduct_of_eq p hC hX) k α.1
                    (@Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single (projectiveLineProduct p) _ ℤ
                      (Classical.decEq _) _
                      ((closedPointSection Kf hC b hb p) (genericPoint X)) (1 : ℤ)),
                  torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct_section_mem_cyclesOfDimension C p Kf hC
                    (isRegular_projectiveLineProduct_of_eq p hC hX) k
                    (exists_closedPointSection_eq_pointSection_or_eq_infinitySection Kf hC b hb p)
                    α hT₂⟩ ∈
            rationalEquivalences C p k) ∧
      (∀ β : CycleGroup C p k, β ∈ rationalEquivalences C p k →
        PointCycle.IsSectionPairFibreIntersectionDifference C p
          (isRegular_projectiveLineProduct_of_eq p hC hX) k
          (closedPointSection Kf hC a ha p) (closedPointSection Kf hC b hb p) β)
declarations.comment: the whole tag, at an ARBITRARY pair of distinct closed points `a`, `b` of `P^1` over an algebraically closed field: (1)(a) `[W_a]_k = W · X × a` as cycles on `X × P^1`, (1)(b) `[W_a]_k = pr_{X,*}(W · X × a)` as cycles on `X`, (2) `pr_{X,*}(α · X × a - α · X × b)` is rationally equivalent to zero for every `(k + 1)`-cycle `α` meeting the two fibres properly, and (3) the converse, that every `k`-cycle rationally equivalent to zero is of that form. The hypotheses are the source's own and concern `X`, `a`, `b` and `W` (resp. `α`, `β`) alone: `X` is nonsingular (`hX`) and a variety over an algebraically closed field `Kf`, and `a`, `b` are distinct closed points of the projective line (`ha`, `hb`, `hab`); `k` is an arbitrary integer, the source's `k ≥ 0` being unnecessary. `X × a` is the image of the section of the family at `a`, which is `Stacks.Chow.closedPointSection`, built from Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.pointOfClosedPoint`: over an algebraically closed field the residue field at a closed point of a scheme locally of finite type is the field itself, so a closed point of `P^1` is a rational point. The first clause of the conclusion records that the second projection of each of the two sections is constant at its point, so that `X × a` and `X × b` are the fibres of `X × P^1` over `a` and over `b`. That this section is `Stacks.Chow.pointSection` at a global function on the base, or `Stacks.Chow.infinitySection`, is `Stacks.Chow.exists_closedPointSection_eq_pointSection_or_eq_infinitySection`, proved from the chart dichotomy `Stacks.Chow.compl_range_affineChart` together with the classification of the `S`-points of the affine chart, `Stacks.Chow.eq_affineLineSection_of_comp_eq`. The products are the honest Section 43.14 products of Tag 0AZR and the Tag 0B08 products `AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct` assembled from them; `rationally equivalent to zero` is `Stacks.Chow.rationalEquivalences`, the group of Tag 02RW; `of that form` in (3) is `Stacks.Chow.PointCycle.IsSectionPairFibreIntersectionDifference`, which spells out the conclusion of (2) at the two sections. Proper intersection is the delta-dimension idiom of chapter 42 (`hWD`, for `dim (W ∩ X × a) ≤ k`) in (1) and the form Section 43.8 and Tag 02S4 part (2) use in (2) — no component of `α` is contained in the section. Nothing is assumed about the ambient `X × P^1`: its regularity is `Stacks.Chow.isRegular_projectiveLineProduct_of_eq`, derived from nonsingularity of `X`; the pointwise readings of (1)(a) are `Stacks.Chow.localConditions_ker_pointSection` and its infinity twin; the delta-dimension bounds on the supports of the Tor sheaves are `AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_torSheaf_le`; and the bound on the Krull dimension of the family that makes the alternating Tor sum finite is `Stacks.Chow.exists_topologicalKrullDim_projectiveLineProduct_le`. Tag 0B2U, the 2-transitivity of the automorphism group of `P^1`, is not invoked: each clause is proved at the pair of points themselves.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.cycleIntersectionProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B08: the intersection product of two cycles.** For a rule `prod` assigning a cycle
to a pair of closed subvarieties of `X`, the bilinear extension `α · β = ∑ᵢⱼ nᵢ mⱼ Wᵢ · Vⱼ` of
`prod` to cycles `α = ∑ᵢ nᵢ [Wᵢ]` and `β = ∑ⱼ mⱼ [Vⱼ]`.
declarations.statement:
def cycleIntersectionProduct (prod : X → X → AlgebraicCycle X ℤ)
    (α β : AlgebraicCycle X ℤ) : AlgebraicCycle X ℤ
declarations.comment: the displayed definition `α · β = ∑ᵢⱼ nᵢ mⱼ Wᵢ · Vⱼ` of the intersection product of an `r`-cycle and an `s`-cycle, with no hypotheses, for the product `Wᵢ · Vⱼ` of two closed subvarieties of Section 43.14 supplied as the parameter `prod`. Closed subvarieties are their generic points, so `prod` is a function of two points and the sum is indexed by `X × X`; the pairs that contribute are the pairs of components of `α` and `β`, and `cycleIntersectionProduct_eq_sum` identifies the value with the finite double sum displayed by the source. The instance of this definition in which `prod` is the Tor-formula product of Section 43.14 is `torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.cycleIntersectionProduct_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
**The display of Stacks 0B08.** For cycles `α = ∑ᵢ nᵢ [Wᵢ]` and `β = ∑ⱼ mⱼ [Vⱼ]` with
finitely many components, `α · β = ∑ᵢⱼ nᵢ mⱼ Wᵢ · Vⱼ` as a finite double sum.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleIntersectionProduct_eq_sum (prod : X → X → AlgebraicCycle X ℤ)
    {α β : AlgebraicCycle X ℤ} (hα : (Function.support α).Finite)
    (hβ : (Function.support β).Finite) :
    cycleIntersectionProduct prod α β =
      ∑ x ∈ hα.toFinset, ∑ y ∈ hβ.toFinset, (α x * β y) • prod x y
declarations.comment: the display `α · β = ∑ᵢⱼ nᵢ mⱼ Wᵢ · Vⱼ` as a finite double sum over the components of the two cycles, assuming each has finitely many components — which on a quasi-compact scheme, in particular on a variety, is automatic by `finite_support_of_compactSpace`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.cycleIntersectionProduct_single_single
declarations.doc:
On two prime cycles the intersection product is the product of the two closed subvarieties:
`[W] · [V] = W · V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleIntersectionProduct_single_single [DecidableEq X]
    (prod : X → X → AlgebraicCycle X ℤ) (x y : X) (m n : ℤ) :
    cycleIntersectionProduct prod (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single x m)
      (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single y n) = (m * n) • prod x y
declarations.comment: the one-term case of the display, with NO hypotheses: on the prime cycles `α = m [W]` and `β = n [V]` the product is `m n (W · V)`, so the bilinear extension really does extend the product of two closed subvarieties of Section 43.14. This is the clause of the section that is carried unrestrictedly; the full display needs each cycle to have finitely many components (`cycleIntersectionProduct_eq_sum`).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.cycleIntersectionProduct_single_right
declarations.doc:
**The clause `α · V` of Stacks 0B08.** For `β = [V]` the prime cycle of a closed subvariety,
the intersection product is `α · V = ∑ᵢ nᵢ Wᵢ · V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleIntersectionProduct_single_right [DecidableEq X]
    (prod : X → X → AlgebraicCycle X ℤ) {α : AlgebraicCycle X ℤ}
    (hα : (Function.support α).Finite) (y : X) :
    cycleIntersectionProduct prod α (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single y 1) =
      ∑ x ∈ hα.toFinset, α x • prod x y
declarations.comment: the final clause of the section: for `β = [V]` the prime cycle of a closed subvariety `V`, the product `α · β`, there written `α · V`, is `∑ᵢ nᵢ Wᵢ · V`. Assumes `α` has finitely many components.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.cycleIntersectionProduct_single_left
declarations.doc:
**The clause `W · β` of Stacks 0B08.** For `α = [W]` the prime cycle of a closed subvariety,
the intersection product is `W · β = ∑ⱼ mⱼ W · Vⱼ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleIntersectionProduct_single_left [DecidableEq X]
    (prod : X → X → AlgebraicCycle X ℤ) {β : AlgebraicCycle X ℤ}
    (hβ : (Function.support β).Finite) (x : X) :
    cycleIntersectionProduct prod (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single x 1) β =
      ∑ y ∈ hβ.toFinset, β y • prod x y
declarations.comment: the first-variable form of the final clause of the section: for `α = [W]` the prime cycle of a closed subvariety `W`, the product `α · β` is `∑ⱼ mⱼ W · Vⱼ`. Assumes `β` has finitely many components.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B08 for the Tor formula.** The intersection product `α · β = ∑ᵢⱼ nᵢ mⱼ Wᵢ · Vⱼ` of
two cycles on a regular scheme, with `Wᵢ · Vⱼ` the Tor-formula product of Section 43.14.
declarations.comment: the intersection product α · β, total in the Tor-support bound

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.torFormulaSubvarietyProductTotal_eq_of_intersectProperly
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B08: the value computed here is the product of the source.** For cycles `α` and `β`
on a regular scheme over a field which intersect properly, with `dim X = m` and the dimensions of
the components summing to `m + n`, every summand of `α · β` that contributes is the genuine
alternating sum `∑ᵢ (-1)ⁱ [Torᵢ^{𝒪_X}(𝒪_{Wᵢ}, 𝒪_{Vⱼ})]_n` of Section 43.14, the
`intersectionProductCycle` of Tag 0AZR. So the double sum of `torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct`
is the `α · β` the source displays.
declarations.statement:
theorem torFormulaSubvarietyProductTotal_eq_of_intersectProperly (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ (Stacks.Chow.fieldChowSituation k).S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (hX : IsRegular X) {m n : ℕ} {α β : AlgebraicCycle X ℤ}
    (hαβ : AlgebraicCycle.IntersectProperly α β)
    (hdimX : topologicalKrullDim X = (m : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hdim : ∀ x ∈ Function.support α, ∀ y ∈ Function.support β,
      topologicalKrullDim (closure ({x} : Set X)) +
        topologicalKrullDim (closure ({y} : Set X)) = (m : WithBot ℕ∞) + (n : WithBot ℕ∞))
    {q : X × X}
    (hq : q ∈ Function.support (cycleIntersectionProductSummand
      (torFormulaSubvarietyProductTotal (Stacks.Chow.fieldChowSituation k) sX hX (n : ℤ)) α β)) :
    torFormulaSubvarietyProductTotal (Stacks.Chow.fieldChowSituation k) sX hX (n : ℤ) q.1 q.2 =
      intersectionProductCycle (Stacks.Chow.fieldChowSituation k) sX hX
        (structureSheafAt q.1) (structureSheafAt q.2) (isCoherent_structureSheafAt q.1)
        (isCoherent_structureSheafAt q.2) (n : ℤ)
        (torSupportBound_of_mem_support_of_intersectProperly k sX hX hαβ hdimX hdim _ hq)
declarations.comment: the summand Wᵢ · Vⱼ at a pair of components, by the Tor formula

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_intersectProperly_torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct_eq_and_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B0E.** Let `X ⊆ 𝐏(V)` be a nonsingular closed subvariety of dimension
`n` of the projective space of a vector space of dimension `N + 1` over an algebraically closed
field; let `Z ⊆ X` be a closed subvariety of dimension `d < n`, and let `T_i ⊆ X` be finitely
many closed subvarieties of dimension `d' < n`. Then there is a closed subvariety `C ⊆ 𝐏(V)`
whose prime cycle intersects that of `X` properly, with

`C · X = [Z] + ∑ m_j [Z_j]`

in the Tor-formula intersection product of Section 0B08, where the `Z_j ⊆ X` are irreducible
closed of dimension `d`, distinct from `Z`, with nonzero multiplicities, and where

* `dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) ≤ dim (Z ∩ T_i)` for every `i` with `Z ∩ T_i` nonempty,
* `dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) ≤ dim (Z ∩ T_i)` or `dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) + n ≤ d + d'` for every `i`, and
* `dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) < dim (Z ∩ T_i)` whenever `Z` does not intersect `T_i` properly inside `X`.

For `Z ∩ T_i = ∅` the first inequality would say `Z_j ∩ T_i = ∅`, which fails for two lines of one
ruling on a quadric surface in `𝐏^3`; there the second clause is what holds.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_intersectProperly_torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct_eq_and_le
    (k V : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    [FiniteDimensional k V] [Nontrivial V] [DecidableEq (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)]
    {N n d d' : ℕ} (hV : Module.finrank k V = N + 1)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (iX : X ⟶ projectiveSpaceOfModule k V) [IsClosedImmersion iX]
    [IsVariety k (iX ≫ projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k V)] (hXreg : IsRegular X)
    (hdimX : topologicalKrullDim X = (n : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hd : d < n) (hd' : d' < n)
    (Z : Set X) (hZcl : IsClosed Z) (hZirr : IsIrreducible Z)
    (hZd : topologicalKrullDim ↥Z = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (T : ι → Set X) (hTcl : ∀ i, IsClosed (T i))
    (hTirr : ∀ i, IsIrreducible (T i))
    (hTd : ∀ i, topologicalKrullDim ↥(T i) = (d' : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (XC ZC : IrreducibleCloseds (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))
    (TC : ι → IrreducibleCloseds (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))
    (hXC : (XC : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) = Set.range iX.base)
    (hZC : (ZC : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) = iX.base '' Z)
    (hTC : ∀ i, (TC i : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) = iX.base '' (T i)) :
    ∃ (C : IrreducibleCloseds (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))
      (S : Finset (IrreducibleCloseds (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)))
      (m : IrreducibleCloseds (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V) → ℤ),
      AlgebraicCycle.IntersectProperly
          (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single C.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ))
          (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single XC.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ)) ∧
        TorFormula.torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct (fieldChowSituation k)
            (projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k V) (isRegular_projectiveSpaceOfModule k V) (d : ℤ)
            (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single C.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ))
            (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single XC.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ)) =
          Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single ZC.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ) +
            ∑ W ∈ S, m W • Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single
              W.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ) ∧
        ZC ∉ S ∧ (∀ W ∈ S, m W ≠ 0) ∧
        (∀ W ∈ S, (W : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ⊆
          (XC : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))) ∧
        (∀ W ∈ S, topologicalKrullDim (W : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) =
          (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧
        (∀ W ∈ S, ∀ i,
          ((ZC : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ∩
              (TC i : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))).Nonempty →
            topologicalKrullDim ↥((W : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ∩
                (TC i : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))) ≤
              topologicalKrullDim ↥((ZC : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ∩
                (TC i : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)))) ∧
        (∀ W ∈ S, ∀ i,
          topologicalKrullDim ↥((W : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ∩
                (TC i : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))) ≤
              topologicalKrullDim ↥((ZC : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ∩
                (TC i : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))) ∨
            topologicalKrullDim ↥((W : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ∩
                  (TC i : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))) + (n : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤
              (d : WithBot ℕ∞) + (d' : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧
        (∀ W ∈ S, ∀ i,
          ¬ (topologicalKrullDim ↥((ZC : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ∩
                  (TC i : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))) +
                topologicalKrullDim (XC : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ≤
              topologicalKrullDim (ZC : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) +
                topologicalKrullDim (TC i : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))) →
            topologicalKrullDim ↥((W : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ∩
                (TC i : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))) <
              topologicalKrullDim ↥((ZC : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ∩
                (TC i : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))))
declarations.comment: the whole lemma, with the erratum that the source's inequality `dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) ≤ dim (Z ∩ T_i)` is stated at each `i` with `Z ∩ T_i` nonempty: for `Z ∩ T_i = ∅` it is false, as a nonsingular quadric surface in 𝐏^3 with Z and T_1 two distinct lines of one ruling shows (see the implementation notes of `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Intersection.MovingLemma.KeyLemma`). At every `i` the statement also carries `dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) ≤ dim (Z ∩ T_i) ∨ dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) + n ≤ d + d'`, which is condition (4) of the source's proof and holds in that bottom case too; the strict inequality, when `Z` and `T_i` do not intersect properly in `X`, is as in the source. `X ⊂ 𝐏^N` is read as `⊆`, so `dim X = N` is covered, with `C = Z` and no `Z_j`. Dimensions are `topologicalKrullDim` in `WithBot ℕ∞`, written additively.

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.localizedModuleFunctor_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
Localizing modules at `S` presents the category of modules over `Localization S` as the Serre
quotient by the modules whose elements are annihilated by members of `S`.

In particular, `CategoryTheory.Localization.equivalenceFromModel` applied to this instance is the
canonical equivalence from the Serre quotient to `ModuleCat (Localization S)`, and
`CategoryTheory.Localization.qCompEquivalenceFromModelFunctorIso` identifies its composite with
the quotient functor with `ModuleCat.localizedModuleFunctor S`.
declarations.statement:
public instance localizedModuleFunctor_isLocalization {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (S : Submonoid R) [Small.{v, u} R] :
    (ModuleCat.localizedModuleFunctor.{v} S).IsLocalization
      (localizationTorsionModuleProperty (R := R) S :
        ObjectProperty (ModuleCat.{v} R)).isoModSerre
declarations.comment: the case S = nonzerodivisors: Mod_A modulo torsion is equivalent to Mod_{Q(A)}

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.fgTorsionModuleProperty_isSerreClass
declarations.doc: Finitely generated torsion modules form a Serre subcategory.
declarations.statement:
public instance fgTorsionModuleProperty_isSerreClass (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] :
    (fgTorsionModuleProperty A : ObjectProperty (FGModuleCat.{v} A)).IsSerreClass
declarations.comment: the Serre subcategory

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.fgFractionModuleFunctor_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
Localizing finitely generated modules at the nonzerodivisors presents the category of
finite-dimensional fraction-field vector spaces as their Serre quotient by the torsion
modules.
declarations.statement:
public instance fgFractionModuleFunctor_isLocalization (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [Small.{v, u} A] :
    (fgFractionModuleFunctor A : FGModuleCat.{v} A ⥤
      FGModuleCat.{v} (FractionRing A)).IsLocalization
      (fgTorsionModuleProperty A : ObjectProperty (FGModuleCat.{v} A)).isoModSerre
declarations.comment: the canonical equivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.extendScalarsRat_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
Rationalization presents rational vector spaces as the Serre quotient of abelian groups by
torsion groups.
declarations.statement:
public instance extendScalarsRat_isLocalization :
    (ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap ℤ ℚ) :
      ModuleCat.{v} ℤ ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} ℚ).IsLocalization
      (localizationTorsionModuleProperty (R := ℤ)
        (nonZeroDivisors ℤ) : ObjectProperty (ModuleCat.{v} ℤ)).isoModSerre

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.properPushforward_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02R5.** Proper pushforward of `k`-cycles is functorial: pushing forward along
`f : X ⟶ Y` and then along `g : Y ⟶ Z` is pushing forward along the composite.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_comp (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (sZ : Z ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sZ] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] (g : Y ⟶ Z) [IsProper g]
    (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) (hg : g ≫ sZ = sY) (k : ℤ) :
    properPushforward C sY sZ g hg k ∘ properPushforward C sX sY f hf k =
      properPushforward C sX sZ (f ≫ g) (by rw [Category.assoc, hg, hf]) k
declarations.comment: functoriality of proper pushforward of cycles, in the case of varieties

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flat_comp_and_flatPullback_comp_of_isVariety
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B0P.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be flat morphisms of varieties
over a field `k`. Then `g ∘ f` is flat and

`f^* ∘ g^* = (g ∘ f)^*`   as maps `Z_j(Z) ⟶ Z_{j + dim X - dim Z}(X)`.

`WithBot ℕ∞` has no subtraction, so `r = dim X - dim Y` and `s = dim Y - dim Z` are natural
numbers together with the relations `dim X = dim Y + r` and `dim Y = dim Z + s`, and the degree
`dim X - dim Z` of the composite is `r + s`. Pulling back first along `g` and then along `f`
lands in degree `(j + s) + r`, so the left-hand side is transported along the equality `hcast`
of that degree with `j + (r + s)`, exactly as `Stacks.Chow.flatPullback_comp` does.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_comp_and_flatPullback_comp_of_isVariety (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (sY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (sZ : Z ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsVariety k sX] [IsVariety k sY] [IsVariety k sZ]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [Flat f] (g : Y ⟶ Z) [Flat g] (hfbase : f ≫ sY = sX) (hgbase : g ≫ sZ = sY)
    (r s : ℕ)
    (hr : topologicalKrullDim X = topologicalKrullDim Y + (r : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hs : topologicalKrullDim Y = topologicalKrullDim Z + (s : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (j : ℤ) (hcast : j + (s : ℤ) + (r : ℤ) = j + ((r + s : ℕ) : ℤ))
    (c : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) sZ j) :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType f := locallyOfFiniteType_of_isVariety_comp k sX sY f hfbase
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType g := locallyOfFiniteType_of_isVariety_comp k sY sZ g hgbase
    Flat (f ≫ g) ∧
      (hcast ▸ flatPullback (fieldChowSituation k) sX sY f hfbase r
            (relativeDimension_of_flat_of_isVariety k sX sY f hfbase r hr) (j + (s : ℤ))
            (flatPullback (fieldChowSituation k) sY sZ g hgbase s
              (relativeDimension_of_flat_of_isVariety k sY sZ g hgbase s hs) j c) :
          CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) sX (j + ((r + s : ℕ) : ℤ))) =
        flatPullback (fieldChowSituation k) sX sZ (f ≫ g)
          (by rw [Category.assoc, hgbase, hfbase]) (r + s)
          (relativeDimension_comp_of_flat_of_isVariety k sX sY sZ f g hfbase hgbase r s hr hs)
          j c
declarations.comment: the whole lemma: both that the composite of two flat morphisms of varieties over a field is flat and the identity `f^* ∘ g^* = (g ∘ f)^*` of flat pullbacks of cycles, as maps `Z_j(Z) ⟶ Z_{j + dim X - dim Z}(X)`, under the source's own hypotheses that `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` are flat morphisms of varieties over `k`. Flat pullback is the homomorphism `Stacks.Chow.flatPullback` of Tag 02RB in the base situation `Spec k` with the zero dimension function, where the delta-dimension of an integral closed subscheme is its dimension, so the cycle groups are the source's `Z_j`. `WithBot ℕ∞` has no subtraction, so the relative dimensions `r = dim X - dim Y` and `s = dim Y - dim Z` are natural numbers together with the relations `dim X = dim Y + r` and `dim Y = dim Z + s`, and the source's degree shift `dim X - dim Z` is `r + s`; `hcast` is the equality in `ℤ` of the degree `(j + s) + r` reached by pulling back along `g` and then `f` with the degree `j + (r + s)` of the right-hand side, along which the left-hand side is transported. That the relative dimension of the composite is `r + s` is `AlgebraicGeometry.relativeDimension_comp_of_flat_of_isVariety`, the fibre-dimension formula of Tag 02JS which the section's introduction invokes, and the coefficientwise form of the identity is `Stacks.Chow.flatPullback_comp_apply_of_isVariety`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.isRegularImmersion_diagonal
declarations.doc:
The diagonal `X ⟶ X ×ₖ X` of a nonsingular variety over a perfect field is a regular
immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularImmersion_diagonal [IsVariety k f] (hX : IsRegular X) :
    Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.IsRegularImmersion (pullback.diagonal f)
declarations.comment: the diagonal is a regular immersion

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_conormalSheaf_diagonal
declarations.doc:
The conormal sheaf of the diagonal of a nonsingular variety over a perfect field is finite
locally free of rank the dimension of the variety: the diagonal is a regular immersion of
codimension `dim X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_conormalSheaf_diagonal [IsVariety k f] (hX : IsRegular X)
    (n : ℕ) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
      (Stacks.Conormal.conormalSheaf (pullback.diagonal f)) n
declarations.comment: the codimension of the diagonal is the dimension of the variety

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.codimension_diagonal_eq_topologicalKrullDim
declarations.doc:
The image of the diagonal of a variety has codimension the dimension of the variety inside
the product `X ×ₖ X`: the codimension of the closure of the image of the generic point is
`dim X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem codimension_diagonal_eq_topologicalKrullDim [IsVariety k f] :
    (codimension (IrreducibleCloseds.closureSingleton
      (pullback.diagonal f (genericPoint X))) : WithBot ℕ∞) = topologicalKrullDim X
declarations.comment: the codimension of the image of the diagonal is the dimension of the variety

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.ExteriorProductProjections.exteriorProduct_projections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B0R.** Let `X` and `Y` be nonsingular varieties over an algebraically
closed field `k`, let `α ∈ Z_r(X)` and `β ∈ Z_s(Y)`. Then

1. `pr_Y^*(β) = [X] × β` and `pr_X^*(α) = α × [Y]`,
2. `α × [Y]` and `[X] × β` intersect properly on `X × Y`, and
3. `α × β = (α × [Y]) · ([X] × β) = pr_X^*(α) · pr_Y^*(β)` in `Z_{r+s}(X × Y)`.

A variety is `AlgebraicGeometry.IsVariety` over `Spec k` and nonsingular is
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular`, as in Section 43.3; `dX`, `dY` are the dimensions of `X` and `Y`.
The product `X × Y` is `pullback sX sY` with structure morphism `pullback.fst sX sY ≫ sX`, and
`pr_X = pullback.fst sX sY`, `pr_Y = pullback.snd sX sY`; `pr_X^*` and `pr_Y^*` are the flat
pullbacks of cycles of Tag 02RB along these flat morphisms of relative dimension `dY` and `dX`.
`[X]` and `[Y]` are the fundamental cycles, `×` is the exterior product of Section 43.16, and
`·` is the intersection product of Section 43.17 on the nonsingular variety `X × Y`. The cycle
groups `Z_{dX+s}`, `Z_{s+dX}` (and their analogues) are distinct types carrying the same cycles,
so the identities are equalities of the underlying algebraic cycles.
declarations.statement:
theorem exteriorProduct_projections (hX : IsRegular X) (hY : IsRegular Y) (dX dY : ℕ)
    (hdX : topologicalKrullDim X = (dX : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hdY : topologicalKrullDim Y = (dY : WithBot ℕ∞)) (r s : ℕ)
    (α : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) sX (r : ℤ))
    (β : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) sY (s : ℤ)) :
    -- (1)
    ((flatPullback (fieldChowSituation k) (pullback.fst sX sY ≫ sX) sY (pullback.snd sX sY)
        pullback.condition.symm dX (relativeDimension_pullbackSnd sX sY dX hdX) (s : ℤ) β).1 =
      (exteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) sX sY (dX : ℤ) (s : ℤ)
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme (fieldChowSituation k) sX (𝟙 X) (dX : ℤ)) β).1 ∧
    (flatPullback (fieldChowSituation k) (pullback.fst sX sY ≫ sX) sX (pullback.fst sX sY) rfl dY
        (relativeDimension_pullbackFst sX sY dY hdY) (r : ℤ) α).1 =
      (exteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) sX sY (r : ℤ) (dY : ℤ) α
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme (fieldChowSituation k) sY (𝟙 Y) (dY : ℤ))).1) ∧
    -- (2)
    AlgebraicCycle.IntersectProperly
      (exteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) sX sY (r : ℤ) (dY : ℤ) α
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme (fieldChowSituation k) sY (𝟙 Y) (dY : ℤ))).1
      (exteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) sX sY (dX : ℤ) (s : ℤ)
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme (fieldChowSituation k) sX (𝟙 X) (dX : ℤ)) β).1 ∧
    -- (3)
    ((exteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) sX sY (r : ℤ) (s : ℤ) α β).1 =
      torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct (fieldChowSituation k) (pullback.fst sX sY ≫ sX)
        (isRegular_pullback_of_isRegular sX sY hX hY) ((r : ℤ) + (s : ℤ))
        (exteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) sX sY (r : ℤ) (dY : ℤ) α
          (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme (fieldChowSituation k) sY (𝟙 Y) (dY : ℤ))).1
        (exteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) sX sY (dX : ℤ) (s : ℤ)
          (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme (fieldChowSituation k) sX (𝟙 X) (dX : ℤ)) β).1 ∧
    (exteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) sX sY (r : ℤ) (s : ℤ) α β).1 =
      torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct (fieldChowSituation k) (pullback.fst sX sY ≫ sX)
        (isRegular_pullback_of_isRegular sX sY hX hY) ((r : ℤ) + (s : ℤ))
        (flatPullback (fieldChowSituation k) (pullback.fst sX sY ≫ sX) sX (pullback.fst sX sY)
          rfl dY (relativeDimension_pullbackFst sX sY dY hdY) (r : ℤ) α).1
        (flatPullback (fieldChowSituation k) (pullback.fst sX sY ≫ sX) sY (pullback.snd sX sY)
          pullback.condition.symm dX (relativeDimension_pullbackSnd sX sY dX hdX) (s : ℤ) β).1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exteriorProduct_rationallyEquivalentToZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B0S.** Let `X` and `Y` be schemes locally of finite type over the spectrum of a
field, let `α` be an `r`-cycle on `X` and let `β` be an `s`-cycle on `Y`. If `α` is rationally
equivalent to zero, or `β` is, then the exterior product `α × β` is rationally equivalent to
zero.

Each of the two cases is the corresponding well-definedness clause of Stacks 0FBV. The instances
of Stacks 02S1 along the projections of the products with a point closure that those clauses use
are supplied internally by
`Stacks.Chow.flatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalenceOnPointClosureFibres_holds`, so nothing
is assumed here.
declarations.statement:
theorem exteriorProduct_rationallyEquivalentToZero (C : ChowSituation.{u}) [Subsingleton C.S]
    [IsIntegral C.S] [JacobsonSpace C.S]
    (hδ : ∀ t : C.S, IsClosed ({t} : Set C.S) → C.dimensionFunction t = 0)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (g : Y ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (r s : ℤ)
    (α : CycleGroup C f r) (β : CycleGroup C g s)
    (h : IsRationallyEquivalentToZero C f r α ∨ IsRationallyEquivalentToZero C g s β) :
    IsRationallyEquivalentToZero C (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) (r + s)
      (exteriorProduct C f g r s α β)
declarations.comment: over a field, unconditionally

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.Diagonal.derivedDiagonalIsos
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B0T], part (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a separated morphism of schemes (for
instance a variety over a field) with projections `pr₁, pr₂ : X ×_S X ⟶ X` and diagonal `Δ`.
For `K, M ∈ D(𝒪_X)` there are canonical isomorphisms, natural in `(K, M)`,

* `LΔ^*(Lpr₁^*K ⊗^L Lpr₂^*M) ≅ K ⊗^L M` (the first component, `diagonalRestrictionIso`), and
* `𝒪_Δ ⊗^L (Lpr₁^*K ⊗^L Lpr₂^*M) ≅ Δ_*(K ⊗^L M)` (the second, `diagonalTensorIso`),

where `𝒪_Δ = Δ_*𝒪_X` is placed in degree zero. They are the composites of canonical maps recorded
by `derivedRestrictionIso_hom` and `diagonalTensorIso_hom`: the comparison of [Stacks, Tag 079U]
with the composition isomorphisms of [Stacks, Tag 0D5S], and the projection formula of
[Stacks, Tag 0B55]. The source's hypotheses (`X` a nonsingular variety, `K, M ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`)
are not needed beyond separatedness; `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` being a full subcategory, these are in
particular isomorphisms in `D_QCoh`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedDiagonalIsos :
    (exteriorDerivedTensor (pullback.fst f f).toLRSHom.toShHom (pullback.snd f f).toLRSHom.toShHom ⋙
        derivedPullback (pullback.diagonal f).toLRSHom.toShHom ≅
      Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor X.toRingedSpace.sheaf)) ×
    (exteriorDerivedTensor (pullback.fst f f).toLRSHom.toShHom (pullback.snd f f).toLRSHom.toShHom ⋙
        (derivedTensorProductFunctor (pullback f f).toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing (pullback f f).toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
          (diagonalStructureModule f)) ≅
      Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor X.toRingedSpace.sheaf) ⋙
        diagonalPushforward f)

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.Diagonal.torDiagonalIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B0T], part (1).** Let `k` be a field and `f : X ⟶ Spec k` separated (for
instance a nonsingular variety), with projections `pr₁, pr₂` and diagonal `Δ`. For
`𝒪_X`-modules `F` and `G` with `G` quasi-coherent (for instance coherent) there are canonical
isomorphisms

`Tor_p^{𝒪_{X ×_k X}}(𝒪_Δ, pr₁^*F ⊗ pr₂^*G) ≅ Δ_* Tor_p^{𝒪_X}(F, G)`.

The isomorphism is `H^{-p}` of the composite of the Tor-independence isomorphism
`exteriorDerivedTensorSingleIso` (inverted, in the second factor) and the second isomorphism of
part (2), `diagonalTensorIso`, followed by the commutation of the exact functor `Δ_*` with
cohomology.
declarations.statement:
def torDiagonalIso (p : ℤ) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.tor (pullback f f).toRingedSpace p (diagonalStructureModule f)
        (exteriorTensor f F G) ≅
      (modulePushforward (pullback.diagonal f).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        (Stacks.Cohomology.tor X.toRingedSpace p F G)

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.ReductionToDiagonal.intersectProperly_exteriorProduct_diagonalCycle
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a variety, let `α` be an `r`-cycle and `β` an `s`-cycle on `X`, and assume `α` and
`β` intersect properly. Then the exterior product `α × β` and the diagonal cycle `[Δ]` intersect
properly on `X ×_k X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem intersectProperly_exteriorProduct_diagonalCycle (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsVariety k f] (r s : ℕ)
    (α : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) f (r : ℤ))
    (β : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) f (s : ℤ))
    (hαβ : AlgebraicCycle.IntersectProperly α.1 β.1) :
    AlgebraicCycle.IntersectProperly
      (exteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) f f (r : ℤ) (s : ℤ) α β).1
      (diagonalCycle f)
declarations.comment: part (1): `α × β` and `[Δ]` intersect properly, for any variety over a field: no nonsingularity is used. Parts (2) and (3), `Δ_*(α · β) = [Δ] · α × β` and `pr_{1,*}([Δ] · α × β) = α · β`, are not stated, because the intersection product of two cycles on a nonsingular variety is not defined in this library; their proof also needs the higher `Tor_i` of Stacks 0B0T, which is `Stacks.Intersection.Diagonal.torDiagonalIso`

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.ReductionToDiagonal.reductionToDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B0U: reduction to the diagonal.** Let `X` be a nonsingular variety
over an algebraically closed field `k`. Let `α` be an `r`-cycle and `β` an `s`-cycle on `X`, and
assume `α` and `β` intersect properly. Then

1. the exterior product `α × β` and the cycle `[Δ]` of the diagonal intersect properly on
   `X ×_k X`;
2. `Δ_*(α · β) = [Δ] · α × β` as cycles on `X ×_k X`;
3. if `X` is proper over `k` then `pr_{1,*}([Δ] · α × β) = α · β`, for `pr₁` the first
   projection.

The intersection products are the ones of Section 43.17 computed by the Tor formula of Section
43.14, `AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct` (Tag 0B08), in the
expected dimension `r + s - dim X`. Everything beyond the source's hypotheses is asserted among
the conclusions rather than assumed: the natural number `dX` carrying the dimension of `X`, which
exists by `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_topologicalKrullDim_eq_natCast_of_isVariety` and is unique,
so that the index `r + s - dX` is the source's `r + s - dim X`; the regularity of `X ×_k X`; and
the delta-dimension of each of the two intersection products, which the two pushforwards need of
their argument.
declarations.statement:
theorem reductionToDiagonal (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [IsVariety k f] (hX : IsRegular X) (r s : ℕ)
    (α : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) f (r : ℤ))
    (β : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) f (s : ℤ))
    (hαβ : AlgebraicCycle.IntersectProperly α.1 β.1) :
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian (pullback f f : Scheme.{u}) :=
      LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (pullback.fst f f ≫ f)
    letI : IsClosedImmersion (pullback.diagonal f) := IsSeparated.isClosedImmersion_diagonal
    AlgebraicCycle.IntersectProperly
        (exteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) f f (r : ℤ) (s : ℤ) α β).1 (diagonalCycle f) ∧
      ∃ dX : ℕ, topologicalKrullDim X = (dX : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧
        ∃ hP : IsRegular (pullback f f : Scheme.{u}),
          ∃ hprod : torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct (fieldChowSituation k) f hX
              ((r : ℤ) + (s : ℤ) - (dX : ℤ)) α.1 β.1 ∈
              cyclesOfDimension (fieldChowSituation k) f ((r : ℤ) + (s : ℤ) - (dX : ℤ)),
            (properPushforward (fieldChowSituation k) f (pullback.fst f f ≫ f)
                  (pullback.diagonal f) (diagonal_comp_fst_comp f)
                  ((r : ℤ) + (s : ℤ) - (dX : ℤ)) ⟨_, hprod⟩).1 =
                torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct (fieldChowSituation k) (pullback.fst f f ≫ f)
                  hP ((r : ℤ) + (s : ℤ) - (dX : ℤ)) (diagonalCycle f)
                  (exteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) f f (r : ℤ) (s : ℤ) α β).1 ∧
              ∀ [IsProper f],
                ∃ hdiag : torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct (fieldChowSituation k)
                    (pullback.fst f f ≫ f) hP ((r : ℤ) + (s : ℤ) - (dX : ℤ)) (diagonalCycle f)
                    (exteriorProduct (fieldChowSituation k) f f (r : ℤ) (s : ℤ) α β).1 ∈
                    cyclesOfDimension (fieldChowSituation k) (pullback.fst f f ≫ f)
                      ((r : ℤ) + (s : ℤ) - (dX : ℤ)),
                  (properPushforward (fieldChowSituation k) (pullback.fst f f ≫ f) f
                      (pullback.fst f f) rfl ((r : ℤ) + (s : ℤ) - (dX : ℤ)) ⟨_, hdiag⟩).1 =
                    torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct (fieldChowSituation k) f hX
                      ((r : ℤ) + (s : ℤ) - (dX : ℤ)) α.1 β.1
declarations.comment: all three parts, for a nonsingular variety over an algebraically closed field — the chapter's convention, and what makes a product of two closed subvarieties a closed subvariety (Stacks 05P3), which part (2) needs. (1) `α × β` and `[Δ]` intersect properly; (2) `Δ_*(α · β) = [Δ] · α × β` on `X ×_k X`; (3) `pr_{1,*}([Δ] · α × β) = α · β` when `X` is proper over the field, the source's own hypothesis for that part. Both intersection products are the Section 43.17 product of Stacks 0B08 computed by the Tor formula of Section 43.14, `AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct`, in the source's dimension `r + s - dim X`; proper pushforward is `Stacks.Chow.properPushforward` (Stacks 02R4). The hypotheses are exactly the source's: the natural number `dX` holding `dim X`, the regularity of `X ×_k X` and the delta-dimension of each of the two products are all asserted among the conclusions. The dimensions `r` and `s` are natural numbers, as the dimensions of the subvarieties the cycles are supported on.

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.Diagonal.intersectionMultiplicity_pos_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B0V.** One of the main results of Serre's *Algèbre locale*. Let `X`
be a nonsingular variety over an algebraically closed field `k` — the chapter's convention — let
`V`, `W ⊆ X` be closed subvarieties which intersect properly and let `Z` be an irreducible
component of `V ∩ W`, with generic point `ξ`. Then `e(X, V · W, Z) > 0`.

Here `V` and `W` are presented by closed immersions `ι_V : V ⟶ X`, `ι_W : W ⟶ X`, the
scheme-theoretic intersection `V ∩ W` is the fibre product `V ×_X W`, and `ξ` is the image in
`X` of a point `ζ` of it. The two numerical hypotheses are the source's own, read at `ξ`:
`dim 𝒪_{V ∩ W, ξ} = 0` says that the closure of `ξ` is an irreducible component `Z` of `V ∩ W`,
and `dim 𝒪_{X, ξ} ≤ dim 𝒪_{V, v} + dim 𝒪_{W, w}` says that `V` and `W` intersect properly along
`Z`, which is Tag 0B1I's criterion: by Tag 0A21 the three local dimensions are
`dim X - dim Z`, `dim V - dim Z` and `dim W - dim Z`, so the inequality is exactly
`dim Z ≤ dim V + dim W - dim X`. The multiplicity `e(X, V · W, Z)` is
`Stacks.Intersection.intersectionMultiplicity` (Tag 0AZR), the alternating sum
`∑ᵢ (-1)ⁱ length 𝒪_{X,ξ} Torᵢ^{𝒪_{X,ξ}}(𝒪_{V,ξ}, 𝒪_{W,ξ})`.

The proof is the source's. The reduction to the diagonal (Tag 0B0U) identifies `e(X, V · W, Z)`
with `e(X ×ₖ X, Δ · V ×ₖ W, Δ(Z))`, by
`Stacks.Intersection.Diagonal.localIntersectionMultiplicity_stalk_comap_diagonal_eq`; the
diagonal of a nonsingular variety is a regular immersion (Tag 0B0Q), so the local ideal of `Δ`
at `Δ(ξ)` is generated by a regular sequence of `dim X` elements
(`Stacks.Intersection.Diagonal.exists_isRegular_fin_generating_ker_stalkMap_diagonal`); and for
such a pair the multiplicity is `dim X !` times the positive leading coefficient of a Hilbert
polynomial (Tag 0B04,
`Stacks.Intersection.localIntersectionMultiplicity_pos_of_isRegularSequence`). The two
numerical hypotheses of that last step are supplied for the diagonal pair by clauses 3 and 4
above, and `X ×ₖ X` is regular because `X` is and `k` is perfect.
declarations.statement:
theorem intersectionMultiplicity_pos_of_isRegular {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X V W : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsVariety k f] (hX : IsRegular X)
    (iV : V ⟶ X) (iW : W ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion iV] [IsClosedImmersion iW]
    (ζ : ↑(pullback iV iW))
    (hcomponent : ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk (iV (pullback.fst iV iW ζ)) ⧸
      AlgebraicGeometry.IdealSheafData.stalk (iV.ker ⊔ iW.ker)
        (iV (pullback.fst iV iW ζ))) = 0)
    (hproper : ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk (iV (pullback.fst iV iW ζ))) ≤
      ringKrullDim (V.presheaf.stalk (pullback.fst iV iW ζ)) +
        ringKrullDim (W.presheaf.stalk (pullback.snd iV iW ζ))) :
    0 < Stacks.Intersection.intersectionMultiplicity iV.ker iW.ker
      (iV (pullback.fst iV iW ζ))
declarations.comment: the whole proposition, for a nonsingular variety over an algebraically closed field — the chapter's own convention, Tag 0AZ8. `V` and `W` are closed subschemes of `X`, presented by closed immersions, so the statement proved is more general than the source's, which takes them integral; `V ∩ W` is the fibre product `V ×_X W` and `ξ` is the image in `X` of a point `ζ` of it. That the closure `Z` of `ξ` is an irreducible component of `V ∩ W` is `dim 𝒪_{V ∩ W, ξ} = 0`, and that `V` and `W` intersect properly along `Z` is `dim 𝒪_{X, ξ} ≤ dim 𝒪_{V, v} + dim 𝒪_{W, w}`, the criterion of Tag 0B1I — by Tag 0A21 it is `dim Z ≤ dim V + dim W - dim X`, so it is implied by, and weaker than, the source's global proper intersection. `e(X, V · W, Z)` is `Stacks.Intersection.intersectionMultiplicity` (Tag 0AZR). Everything the proof uses is proved in this development: the reduction to the diagonal of Tag 0B0U, the regular sequence cutting out the diagonal of Tag 0B0Q, and the Hilbert-polynomial formula of Tag 0B04.

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.ReductionToDiagonal.intersectProperly_coherentSheafCycle
declarations.doc:
Let `ℱ` and `𝒢` be coherent `𝒪_X`-modules whose supports have dimension at most `r` and `s`
and meet in dimension at most `r + s - dim X`. Then the cycles `[ℱ]_r` and `[𝒢]_s` intersect
properly.
declarations.statement:
theorem intersectProperly_coherentSheafCycle (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F G : X.Modules)
    [F.IsCoherent] [G.IsCoherent] (r s : ℕ)
    (hF : schemeDeltaDimension (fieldChowSituation k)
      ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ ((r : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hG : schemeDeltaDimension (fieldChowSituation k)
      ((reducedSupport G).subschemeι ≫ f) ≤ ((s : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hFG : topologicalKrullDim (SheafOfModules.supp F ∩ SheafOfModules.supp G : Set X) +
      topologicalKrullDim X ≤ (r : WithBot ℕ∞) + (s : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    AlgebraicCycle.IntersectProperly
      (coherentSheafCycle (fieldChowSituation k) f F (r : ℤ) hF)
      (coherentSheafCycle (fieldChowSituation k) f G (s : ℤ) hG)
declarations.comment: the clause that `[ℱ]_r` and `[𝒢]_s` intersect properly, for any scheme locally of finite type over a field: no nonsingularity and no variety hypothesis is used. The Tor formula `[ℱ]_r · [𝒢]_s = ∑ (-1)^p [Tor_p(ℱ, 𝒢)]_{r+s-dim X}` is not stated, because the intersection product of two cycles on a nonsingular variety is not defined in this library; its proof also needs the higher `Tor_i` of Stacks 0B0T, which is `Stacks.Intersection.Diagonal.torDiagonalIso`

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.ReductionToDiagonal.torFormula_integerDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B0W**, with the expected dimension an integer. Let `X` be a
nonsingular variety over an algebraically closed field — the chapter's convention, Tag 0AZ8 —
of dimension `dX`, and let `ℱ`, `𝒢` be coherent `𝒪_X`-modules with `dim (Supp ℱ) ≤ r`,
`dim (Supp 𝒢) ≤ s` and `dim (Supp ℱ ∩ Supp 𝒢) ≤ r + s - dX`. Then the cycles `[ℱ]_r` and
`[𝒢]_s` intersect properly and

`[ℱ]_r · [𝒢]_s = ∑ₚ (-1)ᵖ [Torₚ^{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢)]_{r + s - dX}`.

Here `r + s - dX` is the integer `(r : ℤ) + s - dX`, and all of its values are covered, the
negative ones included. `WithBot ℕ∞` has no subtraction, so the third bound is written
`dim (Supp ℱ ∩ Supp 𝒢) + dX ≤ r + s`; when `r + s < dX` it says that the supports are
disjoint, and then both sides are `0` (`torFormula_eq_zero_of_add_lt`). The intersection
product of cycles is the one of Tag 0B08 and the right-hand side is the alternating sum of
Tag 0AZR.
declarations.statement:
theorem torFormula_integerDimension (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsVariety k f] (hX : IsRegular X)
    (F G : X.Modules) (hFc : _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F)
    (hGc : _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent G) (r s dX : ℕ)
    (hdX : topologicalKrullDim X = (dX : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hFr : topologicalKrullDim (SheafOfModules.supp F : Set X) ≤ (r : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hGs : topologicalKrullDim (SheafOfModules.supp G : Set X) ≤ (s : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hFG : topologicalKrullDim (SheafOfModules.supp F ∩ SheafOfModules.supp G : Set X) +
      (dX : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ (r : WithBot ℕ∞) + (s : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := isLocallyNoetherian_of_isRegular hX
    letI := hFc
    letI := hGc
    letI := isFiniteType_of_isCoherent F
    letI := isFiniteType_of_isCoherent G
    have hFr' := schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_le_of_topologicalKrullDim_le k f F r hFr
    have hGs' := schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_le_of_topologicalKrullDim_le k f G s hGs
    have hn : ∀ w ∈ SheafOfModules.supp F ∩ SheafOfModules.supp G,
        relativeDimension (fieldChowSituation k).dimensionFunction f w ≤ (r : ℤ) + s - dX :=
      fun _ hw => relativeDimension_le_of_topologicalKrullDim_add_le k f
        ((SheafOfModules.isClosed_supp F).inter (SheafOfModules.isClosed_supp G)) hFG hw
    AlgebraicCycle.IntersectProperly
        (coherentSheafCycle (fieldChowSituation k) f F (r : ℤ) hFr')
        (coherentSheafCycle (fieldChowSituation k) f G (s : ℤ) hGs') ∧
      torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct (fieldChowSituation k) f hX ((r : ℤ) + s - dX)
          (coherentSheafCycle (fieldChowSituation k) f F (r : ℤ) hFr')
          (coherentSheafCycle (fieldChowSituation k) f G (s : ℤ) hGs')
        = intersectionProductCycle (fieldChowSituation k) f hX F G hFc hGc ((r : ℤ) + s - dX)
            (torSheafDeltaDimension_le_of_forall_mem_inter (fieldChowSituation k) f hX F G hFc
              hGc ((r : ℤ) + s - dX) hn)
declarations.comment: the whole lemma, in every case of the integer expected dimension `r + s - dim X`, the case `r + s < dim X` included: the properness of `[ℱ]_r` and `[𝒢]_s` and the Tor formula `[ℱ]_r · [𝒢]_s = ∑ₚ (-1)ᵖ [Torₚ^{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢)]_{r + s - dim X}`, for a nonsingular variety over an algebraically closed field — the chapter's own convention, Tag 0AZ8 — under the source's own three dimension bounds, read as bounds on the topological dimension of the two supports and of their intersection. `WithBot ℕ∞` has no subtraction, so `dim (Supp ℱ ∩ Supp 𝒢) ≤ r + s - dim X` is spelled `dim (Supp ℱ ∩ Supp 𝒢) + dim X ≤ r + s`, as proper intersection is in Tag 0AZQ; both products are taken in the integer dimension `(r : ℤ) + s - dim X`. The left-hand side is the intersection product of Tag 0B08 and the right-hand side the alternating sum of Tag 0AZR.

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.ReductionToDiagonal.torFormula
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B0W.** Let `X` be a nonsingular variety over an algebraically closed
field — the chapter's convention, Tag 0AZ8 — of dimension `dX`, and let `ℱ`, `𝒢` be coherent
`𝒪_X`-modules with `dim (Supp ℱ) ≤ r`, `dim (Supp 𝒢) ≤ s` and
`dim (Supp ℱ ∩ Supp 𝒢) ≤ r + s - dX`. Then the cycles `[ℱ]_r` and `[𝒢]_s` intersect properly and
