declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_isOpen_isFinite_projection_restrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B1P.** Let `V` be a vector space of dimension `n + 1` over an
algebraically closed field and let `X ⊆ 𝐏(V)` be a closed subscheme with `X ≠ 𝐏(V)`. Then there
is a nonempty Zariski open `U ⊆ 𝐏(V)` such that for every closed point `p ∈ U` the projection
`r_p` away from `p` is defined on `X` and the restriction `r_p|_X : X ⟶ 𝐏(W_p)` is a finite
morphism.

The open is the complement of `X`, which is nonempty because a surjective closed immersion into
the reduced scheme `𝐏(V)` would be an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isOpen_isFinite_projection_restrict [IsAlgClosed k] [FiniteDimensional k V]
    [Nontrivial V] {X : Scheme.{u}} (i : X ⟶ projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (hX : ¬ IsIso i) :
    ∃ U : (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V).Opens,
      (U : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)).Nonempty ∧
      ∀ p ∈ U, IsClosed ({p} : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) →
        ∃ j : X ⟶ (projectionDomain k V (pointSubmodule k V p)).toScheme,
          j ≫ (projectionDomain k V (pointSubmodule k V p)).ι = i ∧
            IsFinite (j ≫ projection k V (pointSubmodule k V p))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_isOpen_projection_isClosedImmersion_and_etaleAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B1Q.** Let `V` be a vector space of dimension `n + 1` over an
algebraically closed field, let `X ⊆ 𝐏(V)` be a closed subvariety and let `x` be a nonsingular
point of `X`. Then

1. if `dim X < n - 1`, there is a nonempty Zariski open `U ⊆ 𝐏(V)` such that for every closed
   point `p ∈ U` the projection `r_p` is defined on `X` and `r_p|_X : X → r_p(X)` is an
   isomorphism over an open neighbourhood of `r_p(x)`;
2. if `dim X = n - 1`, there is a nonempty Zariski open `U ⊆ 𝐏(V)` such that for every closed
   point `p ∈ U` the projection `r_p` is defined on `X` and `r_p|_X : X ⟶ 𝐏(W_p)` is étale
   at `x`.

Each part keeps its own dimension condition as the hypothesis of its clause, as the source
states them. That `r_p` is defined on `X` is the morphism `j` lifting the closed immersion `i`
through the domain of definition of the projection away from `p`. In part (1) the isomorphism
onto the image over a neighbourhood `R` of `r_p(x)` is spelled as `r_p|_X` restricted over `R`
being a closed immersion, which is the same thing: a closed immersion over `R` is an
isomorphism of its source onto its scheme-theoretic image, and that image is `r_p(X) ∩ R`.
`WithBot ℕ∞` has no subtraction, so `dim X < n - 1` and `dim X = n - 1` are written
`dim X + 1 < n` and `dim X + 1 = n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isOpen_projection_isClosedImmersion_and_etaleAt (n : ℕ)
    (hV : Module.finrank k V = n + 1)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (i : X ⟶ projectiveSpaceOfModule k V) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [IsVariety k (i ≫ projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k V)]
    (x : X) (hxreg : x ∈ regularLocus X) :
    (topologicalKrullDim X + 1 < (n : WithBot ℕ∞) →
        ∃ U : (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V).Opens,
          (U : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)).Nonempty ∧
          ∀ p ∈ U, IsClosed ({p} : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) →
            ∃ j : X ⟶ (projectionDomain k V (pointSubmodule k V p)).toScheme,
              j ≫ (projectionDomain k V (pointSubmodule k V p)).ι = i ∧
                ∃ R : (projectiveSpaceOfModule k ↥(pointSubmodule k V p)).Opens,
                  (j ≫ projection k V (pointSubmodule k V p)).base x ∈ R ∧
                  IsClosedImmersion ((j ≫ projection k V (pointSubmodule k V p)) ∣_ R)) ∧
      (topologicalKrullDim X + 1 = (n : WithBot ℕ∞) →
        ∃ U : (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V).Opens,
          (U : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)).Nonempty ∧
          ∀ p ∈ U, IsClosed ({p} : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) →
            ∃ j : X ⟶ (projectionDomain k V (pointSubmodule k V p)).toScheme,
              j ≫ (projectionDomain k V (pointSubmodule k V p)).ι = i ∧
                EtaleAt (j ≫ projection k V (pointSubmodule k V p)) x)
declarations.comment: both parts, for a closed subvariety of the projective space of a vector space of dimension n + 1 over an algebraically closed field and a nonsingular point x of it, each part under its own dimension condition exactly as the source states it: (1) for dim X < n - 1 a nonempty Zariski open of centres p for which r_p|_X is an isomorphism over a neighbourhood of r_p(x), spelled as the restriction of r_p|_X over that neighbourhood being a closed immersion, which is the same thing since a closed immersion over an open R is an isomorphism onto its scheme-theoretic image r_p(X) ∩ R; (2) for dim X = n - 1 a nonempty Zariski open of centres p for which r_p|_X : X ⟶ 𝐏(W_p) is étale at x. Both parts also deliver the source's 'r_p is defined on X' as the lift j of the closed immersion i through the domain of definition of the projection away from p. WithBot ℕ∞ has no subtraction, so the two dimension conditions are written dim X + 1 < n and dim X + 1 = n.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_isOpen_inter_projectionCone_eq
declarations.doc:
For closed subsets `Y` and `Z` of `𝐏(V)` whose union is not all of `𝐏(V)`, there is a
nonempty Zariski open `U` such that for every closed point `p ∈ U` the intersection
`Y ∩ r_p^{-1}(r_p(Z))` is `(Y ∩ Z) ∪ E` with `E ⊆ Y` closed, and, in the range
`n ≤ dim Z + 1`, with `dim E ≤ dim Y + dim Z + 1 - n`, where `dim V = n + 1`.

The decomposition and the closedness of `E` are proved for arbitrary closed `Y` and `Z` rather
than only irreducible ones. The dimension bound is proved in the range `n ≤ dim Z + 1`, that is
for `Z` of codimension at most one, where it already follows from `E ⊆ Y`; see the implementation
notes for the incidence-variety argument that gives it in the remaining range, and for the one
object it needs.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isOpen_inter_projectionCone_eq [IsAlgClosed k] [Module.Finite k V]
    {n : ℕ} (hn : Module.finrank k V = n + 1)
    {Y Z : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)} (hY : IsClosed Y) (hZ : IsClosed Z)
    (hYZ : Y ∪ Z ≠ Set.univ)
    (hdimZ : (n : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ topologicalKrullDim ↥Z + 1) :
    ∃ U : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V), IsOpen U ∧ U.Nonempty ∧
      ∀ p ∈ U, IsClosed ({p} : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) →
        ∃ E : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V), IsClosed E ∧ E ⊆ Y ∧
          topologicalKrullDim ↥E + (n : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤
            topologicalKrullDim ↥Y + topologicalKrullDim ↥Z + 1 ∧
          Y ∩ projectionCone k V p Z = (Y ∩ Z) ∪ E
declarations.comment: the decomposition Y ∩ r_p^{-1}(r_p(Z)) = (Y ∩ Z) ∪ E with E ⊆ Y closed, for every closed point p of a nonempty Zariski open subset of 𝐏(V), and the dimension bound dim E ≤ dim Y + dim Z + 1 - n carrying the hypothesis n ≤ dim Z + 1, that is for Z of codimension at most one, in which range the bound follows from E ⊆ Y; also carrying the hypothesis Y ∪ Z ≠ 𝐏(V), which the source leaves implicit and without which the asserted identity fails, the left-hand side missing p while Y ∩ Z contains it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_isOpen_inter_projectionCone_eq_of_isClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B1R.** For closed subsets `Y` and `Z` of `𝐏(V)` whose union is not
all of `𝐏(V)`, there is a nonempty Zariski open `U` such that for every closed point `p ∈ U` the
intersection `Y ∩ r_p^{-1}(r_p(Z))` is `(Y ∩ Z) ∪ E` with `E ⊆ Y` closed and
`dim E ≤ dim Y + dim Z + 1 - n`, where `dim V = n + 1`.

The decomposition, the closedness of `E` and the dimension bound are all proved for arbitrary
closed `Y` and `Z` rather than only irreducible ones; see the implementation notes for the
incidence-variety argument behind the bound.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isOpen_inter_projectionCone_eq_of_isClosed [IsAlgClosed k] [Module.Finite k V]
    {n : ℕ} (hn : Module.finrank k V = n + 1)
    {Y Z : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)} (hY : IsClosed Y) (hZ : IsClosed Z)
    (hYZ : Y ∪ Z ≠ Set.univ) :
    ∃ U : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V), IsOpen U ∧ U.Nonempty ∧
      ∀ p ∈ U, IsClosed ({p} : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) →
        ∃ E : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V), IsClosed E ∧ E ⊆ Y ∧
          topologicalKrullDim ↥E + (n : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤
            topologicalKrullDim ↥Y + topologicalKrullDim ↥Z + 1 ∧
          Y ∩ projectionCone k V p Z = (Y ∩ Z) ∪ E
declarations.comment: the decomposition Y ∩ r_p^{-1}(r_p(Z)) = (Y ∩ Z) ∪ E with E ⊆ Y closed and the dimension bound dim E ≤ dim Y + dim Z + 1 - n, for every closed point p of a nonempty Zariski open subset of 𝐏(V); also carrying the hypothesis Y ∪ Z ≠ 𝐏(V), which the source leaves implicit and without which the asserted identity fails, the left-hand side missing p while Y ∩ Z contains it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_isOpen_inter_projectionConeWithVertex_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B1R.** Let `V` be a vector space of dimension `n + 1` over an algebraically closed
field and let `Y, Z ⊆ 𝐏(V)` be closed subsets. There is a nonempty Zariski open `U ⊆ 𝐏(V)` such
that for every closed point `p ∈ U`

`Y ∩ r_p^{-1}(r_p(Z)) = (Y ∩ Z) ∪ E`

with `E ⊆ Y` closed and `dim E ≤ dim Y + dim Z + 1 - n`, where `r_p^{-1}(r_p(Z))` is the cone
over `Z` with vertex `p`.

No hypothesis beyond the closedness of `Y` and `Z` is needed, and in particular none on `Y ∪ Z`
or on `dim Z`. The source asks for `Y` and `Z` to be closed subvarieties; the statement is proved
here for arbitrary closed subsets, which is more general, a subvariety being an irreducible
reduced closed subscheme.

The open subset produced is `U₀ ∖ Z` for `U₀` the open of the general-fibre bound, when `Z` is
neither empty nor everything; in those two degenerate cases the cone is respectively empty and
everything, and `E = ∅` serves over all of `𝐏(V)`. The subset `E` produced in the main case is
the closure of `(Y ∖ Z) ∩ r_p^{-1}(r_p(Z))`, and its dimension is bounded through the incidence
variety `T = {(y, z, p) : y ∈ Y ∖ Z, z ∈ Z, p on the line joining y and z}` exactly as in
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_isOpen_inter_projectionCone_eq_of_union_ne_univ`,
whose hypothesis `p ∉ Y` is not available here: the vertex `p` may well lie on `Y`, and when it
does it is itself a point of `(Y ∖ Z) ∩ r_p^{-1}(r_p(Z))` whose membership of the image of the
fibre is witnessed by the collinear triple `(p, z₀, p)` for any closed point `z₀` of `Z`.

With the punctured reading of `r_p^{-1}(r_p(Z))` carried by
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.projectionCone` the statement is false, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.not_exists_isOpen_inter_projectionCone_univ_eq`, and
the registrations of this tag on
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_isOpen_inter_projectionCone_eq` carry the
hypotheses that reading forces.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isOpen_inter_projectionConeWithVertex_eq [IsAlgClosed k] [Module.Finite k V]
    {n : ℕ} (hn : Module.finrank k V = n + 1)
    {Y Z : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)} (hY : IsClosed Y) (hZ : IsClosed Z) :
    ∃ U : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V), IsOpen U ∧ U.Nonempty ∧
      ∀ p ∈ U, IsClosed ({p} : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) →
        ∃ E : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V), IsClosed E ∧ E ⊆ Y ∧
          topologicalKrullDim ↥E + (n : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤
            topologicalKrullDim ↥Y + topologicalKrullDim ↥Z + 1 ∧
          Y ∩ projectionConeWithVertex k V p Z = (Y ∩ Z) ∪ E
declarations.comment: the decomposition Y ∩ r_p^{-1}(r_p(Z)) = (Y ∩ Z) ∪ E with E ⊆ Y closed and dim E ≤ dim Y + dim Z + 1 - n, for every closed point p of a nonempty Zariski open subset of 𝐏(V), with no hypothesis beyond the closedness of Y and Z, reading r_p^{-1}(r_p(Z)) as the cone over Z with vertex p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_isOpen_forall_closedPoint_line_subset_endDomain_intersectProperly
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B1S.** Let `X, Y` be closed subvarieties of `𝐏(V)` which intersect
properly, with `X ≠ 𝐏(V)` and `X ∩ Y ≠ ∅`. Then for a general line `ℓ ⊆ 𝐏 = 𝐏((End V)ᵛ)` with
`[id_V] ∈ ℓ` — that is, for the line through `[id_V]` and any closed point of a nonempty Zariski
open subset of `𝐏` — every representative `g` of every closed point `[g]` of `ℓ` satisfies

1. `X ⊆ U(g)`, and
2. `g(X) = r_g(X)` is a closed subvariety `W` of `𝐏(V)` which intersects `Y` properly.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isOpen_forall_closedPoint_line_subset_endDomain_intersectProperly
    (X Y : IrreducibleCloseds (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) (hXY : IntersectProperly X Y)
    (hXne : (X : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ≠ Set.univ)
    (hXYne : ((X : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ∩
      (Y : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))).Nonempty) :
    ∃ U : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k (ParameterModule k V)), IsOpen U ∧ U.Nonempty ∧
      ∀ q ∈ U, IsClosed ({q} : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k (ParameterModule k V))) →
        ∃ L : Submodule k (ParameterModule k V),
          Module.finrank k (ParameterModule k V ⧸ L) = 2 ∧
          identityParameterPoint k V ∈ linearSubspace k (ParameterModule k V) L ∧
          q ∈ linearSubspace k (ParameterModule k V) L ∧
          ∀ p : ClosedPoints k (ParameterModule k V),
            (p : projectiveSpaceOfModule k (ParameterModule k V)) ∈
              linearSubspace k (ParameterModule k V) L →
            ∀ g : V →ₗ[k] V, RepresentsParameterPoint k V p g →
              (X : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ⊆
                  (endDomain k V g : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ∧
                ∃ W : IrreducibleCloseds (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V),
                  (W : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) =
                      endProjectionImage k V g (X : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ∧
                    IntersectProperly W Y
declarations.comment: both clauses (1) X ⊆ U(g) and (2) g(X) intersects Y properly, for every [g] on a general line through [id_V], at the source's hypotheses; 'general' means: there is a nonempty Zariski open subset of 𝐏 = 𝐏((End V)ᵛ) each of whose closed points lies with [id_V] on such a line (as in Tag 0B2T); clause (2) is IntersectProperly (Tag 0AZQ) of the closed subvariety r_g(X) with Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.endProjectionImage_eq_of_represents_identity
declarations.doc:
**Clause (2) of the Moving Lemma: the fibre over `0` is `C`.** Every endomorphism
representing the point `[id_V]` of the parameter space is a unit scalar multiple of the
identity, so the translate it induces is the identity on subsets of `𝐏(V)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem endProjectionImage_eq_of_represents_identity [Nontrivial V]
    {p : ClosedPoints k (ParameterModule k V)}
    (hp : (p : projectiveSpaceOfModule k (ParameterModule k V)) = identityParameterPoint k V)
    {g : V →ₗ[k] V} (hg : RepresentsParameterPoint k V p g)
    (S : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) :
    endProjectionImage k V g S = S
declarations.comment: clause (2), C'_0 = C, in the fibrewise form of this module: the fibre of the family over 0 = [id_V] is r_g(C) for g a representative of [id_V], and that translate is C itself; the family C' and hence the scheme-theoretic reading of the equality are not constructed, see the implementation notes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_movingFamily_of_subvariety_fixed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B1T, over a given projective line with given points `0 ≠ ∞`.** Let `C`
be a closed subvariety of `𝐏^N = 𝐏(V)`, `X` a subvariety of `𝐏^N` (irreducible and locally
closed, not necessarily closed), `T i ⊆ X` finitely many closed subvarieties of `X`, and assume
`C` and `X` intersect properly. Let `𝐏^1 = 𝐏(W)`, `dim_k W = 2`, and let `0 ≠ ∞` be closed points
of it. Then there is a closed subvariety `C'` of `𝐏^1 × 𝐏^N` such that

1. `C' → 𝐏^1` is dominant;
2. `C'_0 = C` scheme theoretically;
3. `C'` and `X × 𝐏^1` intersect properly;
4. `C'_∞` properly intersects each `T i`.

Proper intersection is the dimension criterion of Definition 0AZQ read on the subsets. The
instance `Nontrivial W` is implied by `dim_k W = 2` and is there only because the products and
sections of `𝐏(W)` are stated under it. The family
of `AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_movingFamily_of_subvariety` is transported
along an isomorphism of projective lines carrying its points to the given ones.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_movingFamily_of_subvariety_fixed
    (C : IrreducibleCloseds (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))
    (X : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) (hX : IsLocallyClosed X) (hXirr : IsIrreducible X)
    (hCX : topologicalKrullDim ↥((C : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ∩ X) +
        topologicalKrullDim (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V) ≤
      topologicalKrullDim ↥(C : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) + topologicalKrullDim ↥X)
    {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (T : ι → Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))
    (hTX : ∀ i, T i ⊆ X) (hTc : ∀ i, IsClosed {x : X | x.1 ∈ T i})
    (hTirr : ∀ i, IsIrreducible (T i))
    (W : Type u) [AddCommGroup W] [Module k W] [FiniteDimensional k W] [Nontrivial W]
    (hW : Module.finrank k W = 2) (zero infty : projectiveSpaceOfModule k W)
    (hzero : IsClosed ({zero} : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k W)))
    (hinfty : IsClosed ({infty} : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k W))) (hne : zero ≠ infty) :
    ∃ Cfam : IrreducibleCloseds (lineProduct k V W),
      closure ((lineProductLine k V W).base '' (Cfam : Set (lineProduct k V W))) = Set.univ ∧
      (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
            (⟨Cfam, Cfam.isClosed'⟩ : Closeds (lineProduct k V W))).comap
          (lineProductSection k V W zero hzero) =
        Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
          (⟨C, C.isClosed'⟩ : Closeds (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ∧
      topologicalKrullDim ↥((Cfam : Set (lineProduct k V W)) ∩ lineProductConstant k V W X) +
          topologicalKrullDim (lineProduct k V W) ≤
        topologicalKrullDim ↥(Cfam : Set (lineProduct k V W)) +
          topologicalKrullDim ↥(lineProductConstant k V W X) ∧
      ∀ i, topologicalKrullDim
            ↥(lineProductFibre k V W infty hinfty (Cfam : Set (lineProduct k V W)) ∩ T i) +
          topologicalKrullDim (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V) ≤
        topologicalKrullDim
            ↥(lineProductFibre k V W infty hinfty (Cfam : Set (lineProduct k V W))) +
          topologicalKrullDim ↥(T i)
declarations.comment: the whole lemma, at the source's hypotheses and no others, over the source's fixed 𝐏^1 with its fixed points: C a closed subvariety of 𝐏^N = 𝐏(V) (an irreducible closed subset with its reduced structure), X a subvariety of 𝐏^N (an irreducible locally closed subset, not necessarily closed), T i ⊆ X finitely many closed subvarieties of X (irreducible, closed in X), C and X intersecting properly; for every projective line 𝐏^1 = 𝐏(W), dim_k W = 2, and every pair of distinct closed points 0, ∞ of it, a closed subvariety C' of 𝐏^1 × 𝐏^N with (1) C' → 𝐏^1 dominant, read as density of the image; (2) C'_0 = C scheme theoretically: the ideal sheaf of the reduced closed subscheme on C' pulled back along the section of 𝐏^1 × 𝐏^N → 𝐏^N at 0 is the ideal sheaf of the reduced closed subscheme on C; (3) C' and X × 𝐏^1 intersect properly; (4) C'_∞ intersects each T i properly. Proper intersection is the dimension criterion of Definition 0AZQ read on the subsets

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_isOpen_forall_closedPoint_line_moving_of_codimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B1T.** Let `C, X` be closed subvarieties of
`𝐏(V)` which intersect properly, with `C ≠ 𝐏(V)` and `C ∩ X ≠ ∅`, and let `T i ⊆ X` be a finite
collection of closed subvarieties. Suppose the bad locus of `(C, X)` in the parameter space
`𝐏 = 𝐏((End V)ᵛ)` is contained in a closed subset `B` which has codimension at least two at each
of its points and does not contain `[id_V]`, and that for each `i` the bad locus of `(C, T i)` is
contained in a closed subset `BT i` other than all of `𝐏`. Then for a
general line `ℓ ⊆ 𝐏` through `[id_V]` — that is, for the line through `[id_V]` and any closed
point `∞` of a nonempty Zariski open subset of `𝐏` — the four clauses of the source hold of the
family whose fibre over a point `[g]` of `ℓ` is the translate `r_g(C)`: that family is dominant
over `ℓ`, because `r_g(C)` is nonempty for every representative `g` of every closed point of
`ℓ`; its fibre over `0 = [id_V]` is `C`; it meets the constant family `X × ℓ` properly, because
`r_g(C)` meets `X` properly at every closed point of `ℓ`; and its fibre over `∞` meets each
`T i` properly.

Both families of hypotheses are carried, this module being upstream of either discharge, which
is why Tag 0B1T is registered not here but on the form over `𝐏^1`
`…ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_movingFamily_of_subvariety_fixed` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Intersection.Projections.MovingLemmaFixedPoints`, which
states all four clauses about the family itself at the source's hypotheses alone.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isOpen_forall_closedPoint_line_moving_of_codimension [Nontrivial V]
    (C X : IrreducibleCloseds (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) (hCX : IntersectProperly C X)
    (hCne : (C : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ≠ Set.univ)
    (hCXne : ((C : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ∩
      (X : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))).Nonempty)
    {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (T : ι → IrreducibleCloseds (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))
    (_hTX : ∀ i, (T i : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ⊆
      (X : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)))
    (B : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k (ParameterModule k V))) (hBc : IsClosed B)
    (hB : ∀ p : ClosedPoints k (ParameterModule k V),
      (p : projectiveSpaceOfModule k (ParameterModule k V)) ∈
          badParameterLocus k V (C : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))
            (X : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) →
        (p : projectiveSpaceOfModule k (ParameterModule k V)) ∈ B)
    (hBid : identityParameterPoint k V ∉ B)
    (hcodim : ∀ x ∈ B, (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ codimension (IrreducibleCloseds.closureSingleton x))
    (BT : ι → Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k (ParameterModule k V)))
    (hBT : ∀ i, IsClosed (BT i)) (hBTne : ∀ i, BT i ≠ Set.univ)
    (hBTbad : ∀ (i) (p : ClosedPoints k (ParameterModule k V)),
      (p : projectiveSpaceOfModule k (ParameterModule k V)) ∈
          badParameterLocus k V (C : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))
            (T i : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) →
        (p : projectiveSpaceOfModule k (ParameterModule k V)) ∈ BT i) :
    ∃ U : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k (ParameterModule k V)), IsOpen U ∧ U.Nonempty ∧
      ∀ q ∈ U, IsClosed ({q} : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k (ParameterModule k V))) →
        ∃ L : Submodule k (ParameterModule k V),
          Module.finrank k (ParameterModule k V ⧸ L) = 2 ∧
          identityParameterPoint k V ∈ linearSubspace k (ParameterModule k V) L ∧
          q ∈ linearSubspace k (ParameterModule k V) L ∧
          (∀ p : ClosedPoints k (ParameterModule k V),
            (p : projectiveSpaceOfModule k (ParameterModule k V)) ∈
              linearSubspace k (ParameterModule k V) L →
            ∀ g : V →ₗ[k] V, RepresentsParameterPoint k V p g →
              (endProjectionImage k V g (C : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))).Nonempty ∧
                IsGoodEndomorphism k V (C : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))
                  (X : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) g) ∧
          (∀ p : ClosedPoints k (ParameterModule k V),
            (p : projectiveSpaceOfModule k (ParameterModule k V)) =
              identityParameterPoint k V →
            ∀ g : V →ₗ[k] V, RepresentsParameterPoint k V p g →
              endProjectionImage k V g (C : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) =
                (C : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))) ∧
          ∀ p : ClosedPoints k (ParameterModule k V),
            (p : projectiveSpaceOfModule k (ParameterModule k V)) = q →
            ∀ g : V →ₗ[k] V, RepresentsParameterPoint k V p g → ∀ i,
              IsGoodEndomorphism k V (C : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))
                (T i : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) g
declarations.comment: clauses (1), (3) and (4), read on the fibres, in the form that assumes bounds on the two bad loci: 𝐏^1 is the source's own line ℓ ⊆ 𝐏 = 𝐏((End V)ᵛ) through [id_V] and the fibre C'_[g] is the translate r_g(C), so that (1) 'C' → 𝐏^1 is dominant' is read as 'the fibre over every closed point of ℓ is nonempty', (3) as 'r_g(C) intersects X properly for every representative g of every closed point of ℓ' and (4) as 'r_g(C) intersects each T i properly for every representative g of the ∞ point of ℓ'; clause (2) is endProjectionImage_eq_of_represents_identity of this module; 'general' is read as in Tags 0B2T and 0B1S, namely that there is a nonempty Zariski open subset of 𝐏 each of whose closed points is the ∞ point of such a line; proper intersection is the dimension criterion defining Tag 0AZQ read on the image set r_g(C), as in Tag 0B1S; X is taken closed in this form, Lemma 0B1S being formalized for a pair of closed subvarieties. The two bad-locus bounds are discharged by AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule .exists_isOpen_forall_closedPoint_line_moving_of_intersectProperly of StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Intersection.Projections.MovingFamilyMain, and the tag is registered for all four clauses about the family C' over 𝐏^1 at the source's own hypotheses on C, X (not necessarily closed) and the T i, clause (2) scheme theoretically, on AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_movingFamily_of_subvariety_fixed of StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Intersection.Projections.MovingLemmaFixedPoints; this form keeps its place here, upstream of the incidence-correspondence construction that either discharge needs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_rationallyEquivalent_forall_intersectProperly
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B1U, for a finite family of cycles.** Let `X` be a nonsingular
projective variety over an algebraically closed field, let `α` be an `r`-cycle on `X` and let
`β i` be finitely many cycles on `X`, of dimensions `s i`. Then there is an `r`-cycle `α'` with
`α' ∼_rat α` which intersects every `β i` properly. This is the case of
`exists_rationallyEquivalent_forall_intersectProperly_of_isQuasiProjectiveVariety` for a
projective variety.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_rationallyEquivalent_forall_intersectProperly (k : Type u) [Field k]
    [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProjectiveVariety k sX]
    (hX : IsRegular X) {r : ℤ} (α : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) sX r)
    {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (s : ι → ℤ) (β : ∀ i, CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) sX (s i)) :
    ∃ α' : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) sX r,
      RationallyEquivalent (fieldChowSituation k) sX r α' α ∧
        ∀ i, AlgebraicCycle.IntersectProperly α'.1 (β i).1
declarations.comment: for a finite family of cycles `β i` of arbitrary dimensions `s i` in place of the single `s`-cycle `β`, which is the case of a one-element family; `r` and the `s i` are arbitrary integers. Nonsingular is `IsRegular X`, projective variety is `IsProjectiveVariety`, cycles are the graded cycle groups `Stacks.Chow.CycleGroup` over `Spec k`, rational equivalence is Tag 02RW and proper intersection is Definition 0AZQ. The proof replaces the source's degeneration of the cone `C` in `𝐏^N × 𝐏^1` (Tags 0B1T, 0B1M, 0B07) by the flat pullback along the finite projection `π : X → 𝐏^n` of the proof of Tag 0B0E, which is flat by miracle flatness, together with moving `π(Z)` inside `𝐏^n`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_rationallyEquivalent_intersectProperly
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B1U.** Let `X` be a nonsingular projective variety over an
algebraically closed field, let `α` be an `r`-cycle and `β` an `s`-cycle on `X`. Then there is an
`r`-cycle `α'` with `α' ∼_rat α` which intersects `β` properly.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_rationallyEquivalent_intersectProperly (k : Type u) [Field k]
    [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProjectiveVariety k sX]
    (hX : IsRegular X) {r s : ℤ} (α : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) sX r)
    (β : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) sX s) :
    ∃ α' : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) sX r,
      RationallyEquivalent (fieldChowSituation k) sX r α' α ∧
        AlgebraicCycle.IntersectProperly α'.1 β.1
declarations.comment: as stated: nonsingular is `IsRegular X`, projective variety is `IsProjectiveVariety`, cycles are the graded cycle groups `Stacks.Chow.CycleGroup` over `Spec k`, rational equivalence is Tag 02RW and proper intersection is Definition 0AZQ; `r` and `s` are arbitrary integers

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct_mem_rationalEquivalences
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B1V.** Let `X` be a nonsingular projective variety of dimension `n` over
an algebraically closed field `k`. Let `α` be an `r`-cycle and `β` an `s`-cycle on `X` which
intersect properly, so that `α · β` is defined, and assume `α ∼_rat 0`. Then `α · β ∼_rat 0`.

The product is the intersection product of Tag 0B08, an `(r + s - n)`-cycle.
declarations.statement:
theorem torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct_mem_rationalEquivalences (k : Type u) [Field k]
    [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProjectiveVariety k p]
    (hX : IsRegular X) {n : ℕ} (hn : topologicalKrullDim X = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)) {r s : ℤ}
    (α : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) p r) (β : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) p s)
    (hαβ : AlgebraicCycle.IntersectProperly α.1 β.1)
    (hα : α ∈ rationalEquivalences (fieldChowSituation k) p r) :
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := isLocallyNoetherian_of_isRegular hX
    (⟨torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct (fieldChowSituation k) p hX (r + s - n) α.1 β.1,
        torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct_mem_cyclesOfDimension (fieldChowSituation k) p hX
          (r + s - n) α.1 β.1⟩ :
      CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) p (r + s - n)) ∈
      rationalEquivalences (fieldChowSituation k) p (r + s - n)
declarations.comment: the whole theorem, for a nonsingular projective variety `X` of dimension `n` over an algebraically closed field: for an `r`-cycle `α` and an `s`-cycle `β` meeting properly (Tag 0AZQ) with `α` rationally equivalent to zero, the Tag 0B08 product `α · β` is a rationally trivial `(r + s - n)`-cycle

declarations.name: TopCat.hasLimits_grp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B20**, part (1). The category of topological groups has all small limits.
This is Mathlib's `HasLimitsOfShape J (Grp C)`, obtained from the fact that
`Grp.forget TopCat` creates limits.
declarations.statement: theorem hasLimits_grp : HasLimits (Grp TopCat.{u})
declarations.comment: part (1): existence of limits

declarations.name: TopCat.preservesLimits_grpForget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B20**, part (a). The forgetful functor from topological groups to topological
spaces preserves all small limits; indeed Mathlib shows it creates them.
declarations.statement: theorem preservesLimits_grpForget : PreservesLimits (Grp.forget TopCat.{u})
declarations.comment: part (a): commutes with forgetful to TopCat

declarations.name: TopCat.preservesLimits_forgetGrp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B20**, part (b). The forgetful functor from topological groups to groups
preserves all small limits.
declarations.statement: theorem preservesLimits_forgetGrp : PreservesLimits (forgetGrp.{u})
declarations.comment: part (b): commutes with forgetful to Grp

declarations.name: TopGrp.forgetToGrpCat_preservesColimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B21**, second part. Colimits of topological groups commute with the forgetful functor
to the category of groups: the forgetful functor is a left adjoint, hence preserves colimits.
declarations.statement: instance forgetToGrpCat_preservesColimits : PreservesColimits forgetToGrpCat.{u}
declarations.comment: commutation with the forgetful functor to groups

declarations.name: TopGrp.hasColimits
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0B21**, first part. The category of topological groups has colimits.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance hasColimits : HasColimits TopGrp.{u}
declarations.comment: existence of colimits

declarations.name: StacksTopologicalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B22**.
A ring `R` equipped with a topology is a topological ring if addition
$(x, y) \mapsto x + y$ and multiplication $(x, y) \mapsto x \cdot y$ are continuous as maps
$R \times R \to R$.
declarations.statement: def StacksTopologicalRing (R : Type*) [Ring R] [TopologicalSpace R] : Prop

declarations.name: StacksTopologicalRingHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B22**.
A bundled ring homomorphism `f : R →+* S` between topological rings is a homomorphism of
topological rings if its underlying function is continuous.
declarations.statement:
def StacksTopologicalRingHom
    {R S : Type*} [Ring R] [Ring S] [TopologicalSpace R] [TopologicalSpace S]
    [IsTopologicalRing R] [IsTopologicalRing S]
    (f : R →+* S) : Prop

registrations.name: TopModuleCat
registrations.comment:
(1), topological modules: the objects of this category are exactly the modules
  over a topological ring equipped with a topology making addition and scalar multiplication
  continuous. The `IsTopologicalAddGroup` field is no strengthening of the source: over a ring
  `-x = (-1) • x`, so continuity of negation follows from `ContinuousSMul`.

registrations.name: TopModuleCat.of
registrations.comment:
(1), a topological module built from exactly the source's two conditions: `of`
  takes only `[ContinuousAdd M]` and `[ContinuousSMul R M]`, deriving `ContinuousNeg M` from
  `-x = (-1 : R) • x`.

registrations.name: ContinuousLinearMap
registrations.comment:
(2), homomorphisms of topological modules: an `R`-linear map bundled with a
  proof that its underlying function is continuous.

compatibility with the forgetful functor: a colimit cocone on the underlying

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DottedTangentArrow
declarations.doc:
A dotted arrow in the tangent-space diagram: a morphism from the spectrum of the dual
numbers which restricts to the point `x` and is a morphism over `S`. Carrying the canonical
`κ(x)`-vector space structure below, this is the tangent space `T_{X/S, x}` of `X` over `S` at
`x`, and its elements are the tangent vectors of `X/S` at `x`.
declarations.statement: def DottedTangentArrow {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X)
declarations.comment: the dotted arrows

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.dottedTangentArrowModule
declarations.doc:
The dotted arrows in the tangent-space diagram carry a canonical vector space structure over
the residue field `κ(x)`. Its operations are characterized by the square-zero pushout and by
scaling the infinitesimal generator.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dottedTangentArrowModule {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) :
    TangentSpaceStructure f x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DottedTangentArrow
declarations.doc:
A dotted arrow in the tangent-space diagram: a morphism from the spectrum of the dual
numbers which restricts to the point `x` and is a morphism over `S`. Carrying the canonical
`κ(x)`-vector space structure below, this is the tangent space `T_{X/S, x}` of `X` over `S` at
`x`, and its elements are the tangent vectors of `X/S` at `x`.
declarations.statement: def DottedTangentArrow {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X)
declarations.comment: the tangent space as a set

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.dottedTangentArrowAddCommGroup
declarations.doc:
The canonical additive commutative group structure on dotted tangent arrows, i.e. the
addition of tangent vectors of `X/S` at `x`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance dottedTangentArrowAddCommGroup {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) : AddCommGroup (DottedTangentArrow f x)
declarations.comment: the additive group of tangent vectors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.dottedTangentArrowModuleInstance
declarations.doc:
The canonical `κ(x)`-vector space structure on dotted tangent arrows; with it the dotted
arrows are the tangent space `T_{X/S, x}`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance dottedTangentArrowModuleInstance {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) : Module (X.residueField x) (DottedTangentArrow f x)
declarations.comment: the canonical κ(x)-vector space structure on the tangent space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tangentSpaceEquivCotangentSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2D.** The relative tangent space at a point is canonically the
`𝒪_{X,x}`-linear dual of the stalk of relative differentials, as a vector space over the residue
field: `T_{X/S,x} = Hom_{𝒪_{X,x}}(Ω_{X/S,x}, κ(x))`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tangentSpaceEquivCotangentSpace :
    DottedTangentArrow f x ≃ₗ[X.residueField x] CotangentSpace f x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tangentSpaceEquivCotangentSpace_apply_germ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2D.** The canonical equivalence sends a dual-number arrow to the
functional which, on the germ `d a` of a universal relative differential, returns the
coefficient of `ε` in the pullback of `a` along the arrow. This is what makes it canonical.
declarations.statement:
theorem tangentSpaceEquivCotangentSpace_apply_germ (θ : DottedTangentArrow f x)
    (U : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ U) (hU : ⊤ ≤ θ.val ⁻¹ᵁ U) (a : X.presheaf.obj (op U)) :
    tangentSpaceEquivCotangentSpace f x θ
        (TopCat.Presheaf.germ (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u})
          (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f).val.presheaf U x hx
          ((Scheme.Hom.universalRelativeDerivation f).d a)) =
      pullbackInfinitesimalCoefficient θ U hU a
declarations.comment: characterization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeCotangentSpaceEquivDifferentialFiber
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes and let `x` be a point of `X` whose residue field
extension `κ(f x) → κ(x)` is separable.  The relative cotangent space
`𝔪_x / (𝔪_x² + 𝔪_{f x} 𝒪_{X,x})` of the stalk map of `f` is canonically the residue-field fibre
`κ(x) ⊗_{𝒪_{X,x}} Ω_{X/S,x}` of the stalk of the sheaf of relative differentials.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeCotangentSpaceEquivDifferentialFiber
    (hsep : Algebra.IsSeparable (S.residueField (f.base x)) (X.residueField x)) :
    Deformation.relativeCotangentSpace (f.stalkMap x).hom ≃ₗ[X.residueField x]
      X.residueField x ⊗[X.presheaf.stalk x] relativeDifferentialStalk f x
declarations.comment: cotangent space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeCotangentSpaceEquivDifferentialFiber_apply_germ
declarations.doc:
The identification of the relative cotangent space with the residue-field fibre of the
relative differentials carries the class of the germ at `x` of a local section of `𝒪_X` vanishing
at `x` to the germ of the universal relative differential of that section.  This is what makes it
canonical.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeCotangentSpaceEquivDifferentialFiber_apply_germ
    (hsep : Algebra.IsSeparable (S.residueField (f.base x)) (X.residueField x))
    (U : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ U) (a : X.presheaf.obj (op U))
    (ha : (X.presheaf.germ U x hx).hom a ∈
      maximalIdeal (ToType (X.presheaf.stalk x))) :
    relativeCotangentSpaceEquivDifferentialFiber f x hsep
        (Submodule.Quotient.mk ⟨(X.presheaf.germ U x hx).hom a, ha⟩) =
      (1 : X.residueField x) ⊗ₜ[X.presheaf.stalk x]
        (show relativeDifferentialStalk f x from
          TopCat.Presheaf.germ (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u})
            (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f).val.presheaf U x hx
            ((Scheme.Hom.universalRelativeDerivation f).d a))
declarations.comment: canonical map on differentials

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.dottedTangentArrowEquivDualRelativeCotangentSpace
declarations.doc:
If the residue field extension `κ(f x) → κ(x)` is separable, the relative tangent space at
`x` — the space of dual-number arrows into `X` over `S` extending the residue-field point `x` — is
canonically the `κ(x)`-linear dual of the relative cotangent space
`𝔪_x / (𝔪_x² + 𝔪_{f x} 𝒪_{X,x})`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dottedTangentArrowEquivDualRelativeCotangentSpace
    (hsep : Algebra.IsSeparable (S.residueField (f.base x)) (X.residueField x)) :
    DottedTangentArrow f x ≃ₗ[X.residueField x]
      (Deformation.relativeCotangentSpace (f.stalkMap x).hom →ₗ[X.residueField x]
        X.residueField x)
declarations.comment: tangent space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.dottedTangentArrowEquivDualRelativeCotangentSpace_apply_germ
declarations.doc:
The identification of the relative tangent space with the dual of the relative cotangent space
evaluates a dual-number arrow on the class of the germ of a local section vanishing at `x` by the
coefficient of `ε` in the pullback of that section along the arrow.
declarations.statement:
theorem dottedTangentArrowEquivDualRelativeCotangentSpace_apply_germ
    (hsep : Algebra.IsSeparable (S.residueField (f.base x)) (X.residueField x))
    (θ : DottedTangentArrow f x) (U : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ U) (hU : ⊤ ≤ θ.val ⁻¹ᵁ U)
    (a : X.presheaf.obj (op U))
    (ha : (X.presheaf.germ U x hx).hom a ∈
      maximalIdeal (ToType (X.presheaf.stalk x))) :
    dottedTangentArrowEquivDualRelativeCotangentSpace f x hsep θ
        (Submodule.Quotient.mk ⟨(X.presheaf.germ U x hx).hom a, ha⟩) =
      pullbackInfinitesimalCoefficient θ U hU a
declarations.comment: canonical map on tangent vectors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tangentMap
declarations.doc:
The tangent map of a morphism over `S`, with the scalar fields identified by the canonical
residue-field isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tangentMap (h : f ≫ q = p) (x : X) [IsIso (f.residueFieldMap x)] :
    DottedTangentArrow p x →ₛₗ[(inv (f.residueFieldMap x)).hom]
      DottedTangentArrow q (f x)
declarations.comment: canonical tangent map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tangentMap_apply
declarations.doc:
The tangent map is induced by composition of dual-number arrows: a tangent arrow is sent to its
composite with `f`, pulled back along any ring homomorphism of dual numbers whose two components
are the residue-field identification.
declarations.statement:
theorem tangentMap_apply (h : f ≫ q = p) (x : X) [IsIso (f.residueFieldMap x)]
    (θ : DottedTangentArrow p x)
    (α : DualNumber (X.residueField x) →+* DualNumber (Y.residueField (f x)))
    (hα₀ : ∀ z, TrivSqZeroExt.fst (α z) =
      (inv (f.residueFieldMap x)).hom (TrivSqZeroExt.fst z))
    (hα₁ : ∀ z, TrivSqZeroExt.snd (α z) =
      (inv (f.residueFieldMap x)).hom (TrivSqZeroExt.snd z)) :
    (tangentMap f p q h x θ).val =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom α) ≫ θ.val ≫ f
declarations.comment: characterization by composition of dual-number arrows

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tangentSpaceEquivDualDifferentialFiber_tangentMap
declarations.doc:
**The tangent map is dual to the map on residue-field fibres.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism
of schemes over `S`, let `x` be a point of `X` with `κ(f x) = κ(x)`. Under the identifications
`T_{X/S,x} = Hom_{κ(x)}(κ(x) ⊗ Ω_{X/S,x}, κ(x))` and
`T_{Y/S,f x} = Hom_{κ(f x)}(κ(f x) ⊗ Ω_{Y/S,f x}, κ(f x))` of Tag 0B2D, the tangent map
`d f : T_{X/S,x} → T_{Y/S,f x}` is the dual of the natural map
`κ(f x) ⊗ Ω_{Y/S,f x} → κ(x) ⊗ Ω_{X/S,x}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tangentSpaceEquivDualDifferentialFiber_tangentMap (h : f ≫ q = p) (x : X)
    [IsIso (f.residueFieldMap x)] (θ : DottedTangentArrow p x) :
    tangentSpaceEquivDualDifferentialFiber q (f.base x) (tangentMap f p q h x θ) =
      differentialFiberMapDual f p q h x (tangentSpaceEquivDualDifferentialFiber p x θ)
declarations.comment: dual to the map Ω_{Y/S,y} ⊗ κ(y) → Ω_{X/S,x} ⊗ κ(x) via the identifications of Tag 0B2D

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.injective_tangentMap_iff_unramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2G.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes over `S`, locally of
finite type, and let `x` be a point of `X` whose residue field agrees with that of `f x`. Then
the tangent map `d f : T_{X/S, x} ⟶ T_{Y/S, f x}` is injective if and only if `f` is unramified
at `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_tangentMap_iff_unramifiedAt (h : f ≫ q = p) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [IsIso (f.residueFieldMap x)] :
    Function.Injective (tangentMap f p q h x) ↔ UnramifiedAt f x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.injective_tangentMap_iff_unramifiedAt_of_locallyOfFiniteType_base
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2G** under the hypotheses of the source: for `X` locally of finite
type over `S`, the tangent map of a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` over `S` is injective at a point where
the residue field is unchanged if and only if `f` is unramified there. Local finite type of `f`
itself is Tag 01T8.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_tangentMap_iff_unramifiedAt_of_locallyOfFiniteType_base (h : f ≫ q = p)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [IsIso (f.residueFieldMap x)] :
    Function.Injective (tangentMap f p q h x) ↔ UnramifiedAt f x
declarations.comment: with the source locally of finite type over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_eq_of_target_dim_le_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2I.** If the local ring of the target at `y` is Noetherian of
dimension at most one, and the fibre dimension at every generic point of an irreducible
component of `X` through `x` is `d`, then the fibre dimension at `x` is `d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_eq_of_target_dim_le_one (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (x : X) (hY : IsNoetherianRing (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)))
    (hYdim : ringKrullDim (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)) ≤ 1) (d : ℕ)
    (hgeneric : ∀ η : X, closure {η} ∈ irreducibleComponents X → x ∈ closure {η} →
      topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f η)) (f.asFiber η) = d) :
    topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) = d

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.specialFiber_equidimensional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2J (equidimensionality).** The special fibre of a surjective,
locally finite type morphism from an irreducible scheme to the spectrum of a valuation ring is
equidimensional.
declarations.statement:
lemma specialFiber_equidimensional {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [ValuationRing R]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [IrreducibleSpace X]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Surjective f] :
    TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional
      (f.fiber (⟨IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R, inferInstance⟩ : PrimeSpectrum R))
declarations.comment: equidimensionality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDim_specialFiber_eq_genericFiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2J (dimension).** The special and generic fibres of a surjective,
locally finite type morphism from an irreducible scheme to the spectrum of a valuation ring
have the same dimension.
declarations.statement:
lemma topologicalKrullDim_specialFiber_eq_genericFiber
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [ValuationRing R]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [IrreducibleSpace X]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Surjective f] :
    topologicalKrullDim
        (f.fiber (⟨IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R, inferInstance⟩ : PrimeSpectrum R)) =
      topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber (⟨⊥, inferInstance⟩ : PrimeSpectrum R))
declarations.comment: equality of fibre dimensions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_add_one_le_of_genericPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2K.** The dimension at a point of a fibre is bounded by the
generic fibre dimension plus the dimension of the base local ring minus one, provided every
irreducible component through the point dominates a nonclosed generalization of its image.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_add_one_le_of_genericPoints (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) [IsNoetherianRing (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x))] (d : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents X, x ∈ Z → ∀ η : X, IsGenericPoint η Z →
      (f η ≠ f x ∧
        topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f η)) (f.asFiber η) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))) :
    topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) + 1 ≤
      (d : WithBot ℕ∞) + ringKrullDim (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFiniteType_fiberToSpecResidueField
declarations.doc:
A fibre of a morphism between locally algebraic schemes is locally algebraic over the
residue field of the corresponding point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem locallyOfFiniteType_fiberToSpecResidueField
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType pX]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX) (y : Y) :
    LocallyOfFiniteType (f.fiberToSpecResidueField y)
declarations.comment: locally_algebraic_fibre

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDim_le_fiber_add_imageClosure
declarations.doc:
**Lower bound for the fibre dimension.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of schemes locally of
finite type over a field with `X` irreducible, the local dimension of every fibre of `f` is at
least the dimension of `X` minus the dimension of the reduced closure of the image of `f`. The
bound is stated additively, since `WithBot ℕ∞` has no subtraction.
declarations.statement:
public theorem topologicalKrullDim_le_fiber_add_imageClosure
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType pX] [LocallyOfFiniteType pY] [IrreducibleSpace X]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX) (x : X) :
    topologicalKrullDim X ≤
      topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) +
        topologicalKrullDim
        (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
            (Closeds.closure (Set.range (fun x : X => f x)))).subscheme
declarations.comment: part (2a): dim_x(X_{f(x)}) ≥ d

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_and_dense_setOf_topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_eq
declarations.doc:
**The fibre dimension is generically the expected one.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of schemes
locally of finite type over a field with `X` irreducible, the set of points at which the local
fibre dimension attains the value `d = dim X - dim Z` is a dense open subset of `X`. Here `Z` is
the reduced closure of the image of `f`, and `d` is the difference of the two dimensions taken in
`ℕ`, since `WithBot ℕ∞` has no subtraction.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpen_and_dense_setOf_topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_eq
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType pX] [LocallyOfFiniteType pY] [IrreducibleSpace X]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : d = ((topologicalKrullDim X).unbotD 0).toNat -
      ((topologicalKrullDim
        (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
          (Closeds.closure (Set.range (fun x : X => f x)))).subscheme).unbotD 0).toNat) :
    IsOpen {x : X | topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)} ∧
      Dense {x : X |
        topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)}
declarations.comment: part (2b): {x | dim_x(X_{f(x)}) = d} is dense open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_add_one_le_of_one_le_ringKrullDim_imageClosure
declarations.doc:
**Upper bound for the fibre dimension over a point of higher codimension.** For a morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` of schemes locally of finite type over a field with `X` irreducible, if the local ring
of the reduced closure `Z` of the image of `f` at `f x` has dimension at least one, then

`dim_x(X_{f(x)}) ≤ d + dim 𝒪_{Z, f(x)} - 1`,

where `d = dim X - dim Z`. Since `WithBot ℕ∞` has no subtraction, the bound is stated by adding
one to the left-hand side, as in Tag 0B2K. The point of `Z` over `f x` is given by `z`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_add_one_le_of_one_le_ringKrullDim_imageClosure
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType pX] [LocallyOfFiniteType pY] [IrreducibleSpace X]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : d = ((topologicalKrullDim X).unbotD 0).toNat -
      ((topologicalKrullDim
        (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
          (Closeds.closure (Set.range (fun x : X => f x)))).subscheme).unbotD 0).toNat)
    (x : X)
    (z : (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
      (Closeds.closure (Set.range (fun x : X => f x)))).subscheme)
    (hz : (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
      (Closeds.closure (Set.range (fun x : X => f x)))).subschemeι z = f x)
    (h1 : 1 ≤ ringKrullDim
      ((Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
        (Closeds.closure (Set.range (fun x : X => f x)))).subscheme.presheaf.stalk z)) :
    topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) + 1 ≤
      (d : WithBot ℕ∞) + ringKrullDim
        ((Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
          (Closeds.closure (Set.range (fun x : X => f x)))).subscheme.presheaf.stalk z)
declarations.comment: part (2c): dim_x(X_{f(x)}) ≤ d + dim O_{Z,f(x)} - 1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_eq_of_ringKrullDim_imageClosure_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**The fibre dimension over a point of codimension one.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of schemes
locally of finite type over a field with `X` irreducible, if the local ring of the reduced closure
`Z` of the image of `f` at `f x` has dimension exactly one, then `dim_x(X_{f(x)}) = d`, where
`d = dim X - dim Z`. The point of `Z` over `f x` is given by `z`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_eq_of_ringKrullDim_imageClosure_eq_one
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType pX] [LocallyOfFiniteType pY] [IrreducibleSpace X]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : d = ((topologicalKrullDim X).unbotD 0).toNat -
      ((topologicalKrullDim
        (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
          (Closeds.closure (Set.range (fun x : X => f x)))).subscheme).unbotD 0).toNat)
    (x : X)
    (z : (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
      (Closeds.closure (Set.range (fun x : X => f x)))).subscheme)
    (hz : (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
      (Closeds.closure (Set.range (fun x : X => f x)))).subschemeι z = f x)
    (h1 : ringKrullDim
      ((Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
        (Closeds.closure (Set.range (fun x : X => f x)))).subscheme.presheaf.stalk z) = 1) :
    topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: part (2d): dim O_{Z,f(x)} = 1 implies dim_x(X_{f(x)}) = d

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDimAt_le_fiber_add_topologicalKrullDimAt_target
declarations.doc:
**Local lower bound for the fibre dimension.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of schemes locally of
finite type over a field and any point `x` of `X` with image `y = f x`,

`dim_x(X_y) ≥ dim_x(X) - dim_y(Y)`.

The source is not assumed irreducible: the bound is obtained by applying part (2a) to each
irreducible component of `X` through `x`, carrying the reduced induced structure. As elsewhere,
the statement is additive because `WithBot ℕ∞` has no subtraction.
declarations.statement:
public theorem topologicalKrullDimAt_le_fiber_add_topologicalKrullDimAt_target
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType pX] [LocallyOfFiniteType pY]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX) (x : X) :
    topologicalKrullDimAt X x ≤
      topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) + topologicalKrullDimAt Y (f x)
declarations.comment: part (3): dim_x(X_y) ≥ dim_x(X) - dim_y(Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDimAt_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2M, part (1).** Let `X` and `Y` be locally algebraic schemes over a
field `k`. At a point `z` of the product `X ×_{Spec k} Y`, the local dimension of the product is
the sum of the local dimensions of `X` and of `Y` at the two images of `z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDimAt_pullback (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (z : ↑(pullback f g)) :
    topologicalKrullDimAt ↑(pullback f g) z =
      topologicalKrullDimAt X ((pullback.fst f g) z) +
        topologicalKrullDimAt Y ((pullback.snd f g) z)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDim_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2M, part (2).** Let `X` and `Y` be locally algebraic schemes over a
field `k`. The dimension of the product `X ×_{Spec k} Y` is the sum of the dimensions of `X` and
of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_pullback (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] :
    topologicalKrullDim ↑(pullback f g) = topologicalKrullDim X + topologicalKrullDim Y
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDim_projectiveSpaceOverRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2P (dimension).** Projective `n`-space over a field has Krull
dimension `n` as a topological space.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_projectiveSpaceOverRing (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) :
    topologicalKrullDim (projectiveSpaceOverRing n (CommRingCat.of k)) = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: projective_space_dimension

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveSpaceOver.smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2P (smoothness).** Projective `n`-space over a scheme `S` is smooth
over `S`, being the base change of the integral model, which is smooth over the terminal
scheme.
declarations.statement: public instance smooth (n : ℕ) (S : Scheme.{u}) : Smooth (projectiveSpaceOver n S ↘ S)
declarations.comment: projective_space_smooth

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProjectiveMorphism_projectiveSpaceOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2P (projectivity).** Projective `n`-space over a scheme `S` is
projective over `S`: the identity is a closed immersion of `ℙⁿ_S` into `ℙⁿ_S` over `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isProjectiveMorphism_projectiveSpaceOver (n : ℕ) (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    IsProjectiveMorphism (projectiveSpaceOver n S ↘ S)
declarations.comment: projective_space_projective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveSpaceOverRing.isVariety
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2P (variety).** Projective `n`-space over a field is a variety over
that field: it is integral, and its structure morphism is separated and of finite type because it
is proper, and quasi-compact because projective space is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
public instance isVariety (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) :
    IsVariety k (projectiveSpaceOverRing n (CommRingCat.of k) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
declarations.comment: projective_space_variety

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.add_le_add_topologicalKrullDim_irreducibleComponent_inter
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2Q.** Let `k` be a field and let `Xs` and `Ys` be closed subsets of
affine `n`-space over `k`, that is, of the prime spectrum of `MvPolynomial (Fin n) k`. If `Xs`
and `Ys` are equidimensional of dimensions `r` and `s`, then every irreducible component `Z` of
`Xs ∩ Ys` satisfies `r + s ≤ n + dim Z`, that is, has dimension at least `r + s - n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem add_le_add_topologicalKrullDim_irreducibleComponent_inter (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (n r s : ℕ) (Xs Ys : Set (PrimeSpectrum (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)))
    (hXc : IsClosed Xs) (hYc : IsClosed Ys)
    (hXe : Equidimensional Xs) (hYe : Equidimensional Ys)
    (hXd : topologicalKrullDim Xs = r) (hYd : topologicalKrullDim Ys = s)
    (Z : Set ↥(Xs ∩ Ys)) (hZ : Z ∈ irreducibleComponents ↥(Xs ∩ Ys)) :
    (r : WithBot ℕ∞) + s ≤ n + topologicalKrullDim Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.inter_nonempty_projectiveSpaceOverRing
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and let `X` and `Y` be nonempty closed subsets of `ℙⁿ_k` of dimensions `r`
and `s`. If `n ≤ r + s` then `X` and `Y` meet.
declarations.statement:
theorem inter_nonempty_projectiveSpaceOverRing
    (X Y : Set (AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveSpaceOverRing n (CommRingCat.of k)))
    (hXc : IsClosed X) (hYc : IsClosed Y) (hXne : X.Nonempty) (hYne : Y.Nonempty)
    (hXd : topologicalKrullDim ↥X = (r : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hYd : topologicalKrullDim ↥Y = (s : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hrs : n ≤ r + s) : (X ∩ Y).Nonempty
declarations.comment: nonemptiness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.le_topologicalKrullDim_inter_projectiveSpaceOverRing
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and let `X` and `Y` be nonempty closed subsets of `ℙⁿ_k` of dimensions `r`
and `s`. If `n ≤ r + s` then `X ∩ Y` has dimension at least `r + s - n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem le_topologicalKrullDim_inter_projectiveSpaceOverRing
    (X Y : Set (AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveSpaceOverRing n (CommRingCat.of k)))
    (hXc : IsClosed X) (hYc : IsClosed Y) (hXne : X.Nonempty) (hYne : Y.Nonempty)
    (hXd : topologicalKrullDim ↥X = (r : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hYd : topologicalKrullDim ↥Y = (s : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hrs : n ≤ r + s) : ((r + s - n : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ topologicalKrullDim ↥(X ∩ Y)
declarations.comment: dimension bound

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.TwoPlanes.length_stalk_quotient_sup_eq_three_and_intersectionMultiplicity_eq_two
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0B2S, the two numbers of the example.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme (for
instance a nonsingular variety of dimension `4` over `ℂ`), let `p ∈ X` and let `V`, `W` be closed
subschemes of `X`, given by their ideal sheaves. Assume there is a ring isomorphism
`e : 𝒪_{X, p}^∧ ≅ ℂ[[x, y, z, w]]` carrying the ideal of `V` in `𝒪_{X, p}^∧` to
`(xz, xw, yz, yw)` and the ideal of `W` to `(x - z, y - w)`. Then
`length_{𝒪_{X, p}} 𝒪_{X, p} ⧸ (I_V + I_W) = 3`, while the intersection multiplicity given by the
Tor formula over `𝒪_{X, p}` is `e(X, V · W, p) = 2`.

The proof transfers the computation in `ℂ[[x, y, z, w]]` along `𝒪_{X, p} → 𝒪_{X, p}^∧ ≅
ℂ[[x, y, z, w]]`, which is flat, local, and carries the maximal ideal onto the maximal ideal, so
that it preserves lengths and commutes with Tor.
declarations.statement:
theorem length_stalk_quotient_sup_eq_three_and_intersectionMultiplicity_eq_two
    {X : Scheme.{0}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (V W : X.IdealSheafData) (p : X)
    (e : AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk p)) (X.presheaf.stalk p) ≃+*
      MvPowerSeries (Fin 4) ℂ)
    (hV : ((IdealSheafData.stalk V p).map (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk p)
      (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk p)) (X.presheaf.stalk p)))).map e =
        unionOfPlanes)
    (hW : ((IdealSheafData.stalk W p).map (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk p)
      (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk p)) (X.presheaf.stalk p)))).map e =
        diagonalPlane) :
    Module.length (X.presheaf.stalk p)
        ((X.presheaf.stalk p) ⧸ IdealSheafData.stalk (V ⊔ W) p) = 3 ∧
      Stacks.Intersection.intersectionMultiplicity V W p = 2
declarations.comment: the example as stated: for X, p, V, W with an isomorphism of the completed local ring at p with ℂ[[x, y, z, w]] carrying the ideals of V and W to (xz, xw, yz, yw) and (x - z, y - w), the length of 𝒪_{X,p} / (I_V + I_W) is 3 and the chapter's intersection multiplicity e(X, V · W, p) is 2; stated for any locally Noetherian X, any point and any closed subschemes, which contains the source's nonsingular fourfold, closed point and subvarieties

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.TwoPlanes.exists_isSmoothVariety_closedPoint_subvarieties_completion
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0B2S, "To make an actual example": the situation of the example exists.** There are a
smooth (that is, nonsingular) variety `X` of dimension `4` over `ℂ`, a closed point `p ∈ X`, and
integral closed subschemes (closed subvarieties) `V, W ⊂ X`, with a ring isomorphism
`e : 𝒪_{X, p}^∧ ≅ ℂ[[x, y, z, w]]` carrying the ideal of `V` to `(xz, xw, yz, yw)` and the ideal of
`W` to `(x - z, y - w)`; for them `length_{𝒪_{X, p}} 𝒪_{X, p} ⧸ (I_V + I_W) = 3` and
`e(X, V · W, p) = 2`.

The instance is `X = 𝔸⁴_ℂ`, `p` the origin, `V` the image of `𝔸² → 𝔸⁴`,
`(s, t) ↦ (s² - 1, t, s (s² - 1), s t)`, which identifies `(1, 0)` and `(-1, 0)` and has two
transverse smooth branches at `p`, and `W` the plane `c = d = 0` through `p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSmoothVariety_closedPoint_subvarieties_completion :
    ∃ (X : Scheme.{0}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of ℂ)), IsSmoothVariety ℂ f ∧
      topologicalKrullDim X = 4 ∧
      ∃ (p : X) (V W : X.IdealSheafData), IsClosed ({p} : Set X) ∧
        IsIntegral V.subscheme ∧ IsIntegral W.subscheme ∧
        (∃ e : AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk p)) (X.presheaf.stalk p) ≃+*
            MvPowerSeries (Fin 4) ℂ,
          ((IdealSheafData.stalk V p).map (algebraMap _ (AdicCompletion _ _))).map e =
              unionOfPlanes ∧
            ((IdealSheafData.stalk W p).map (algebraMap _ (AdicCompletion _ _))).map e =
              diagonalPlane) ∧
        Module.length (X.presheaf.stalk p)
            ((X.presheaf.stalk p) ⧸ IdealSheafData.stalk (V ⊔ W) p) = 3 ∧
          Stacks.Intersection.intersectionMultiplicity V W p = 2
declarations.comment: the existence clause "To make an actual example ...": there exist a smooth variety X of dimension 4 over ℂ, a closed point p and integral closed subschemes V, W with an isomorphism of the completed local ring at p with ℂ[[x, y, z, w]] carrying I_V to (xz, xw, yz, yw) and I_W to (x - z, y - w), and for them the length is 3 and e(X, V · W, p) = 2; proved with one explicit instance in A^4 (V the image of (s, t) ↦ (s² - 1, t, s(s² - 1), st), W the plane c = d = 0) in place of the source's general morphism P^2 → P^4

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.TwoPlanes.length_quotient_sup_eq_three_and_localIntersectionMultiplicity_eq_two
declarations.doc:
**The two numbers of the example, computed in `ℂ[[x, y, z, w]]`.** For the union of the two
planes `x = y = 0` and `z = w = 0`, with ideal `(xz, xw, yz, yw)`, and the plane `x = z`, `y = w`,
with ideal `(x - z, y - w)`, the scheme-theoretic intersection has
`length ℂ[[x, y, z, w]] / (xz, xw, yz, yw, x - z, y - w) = 3`, while the multiplicity given by the
Tor formula is `2`. The two differ, so the alternating sum over all the Tor modules cannot be
replaced by its degree-zero term.

This is the computation in the completed local ring. The example itself is stated for a variety:
`length_stalk_quotient_sup_eq_three_and_intersectionMultiplicity_eq_two` transfers both numbers
to `𝒪_{X, p}` and to the chapter's multiplicity `e(X, V · W, p)` along an isomorphism
`𝒪_{X, p}^∧ ≅ ℂ[[x, y, z, w]]`, and the source's closing sentence, that such
`X, p, V, W` exist with `V` and `W` closed subvarieties, is
`exists_isSmoothVariety_closedPoint_subvarieties_completion`, proved
with an explicit integral surface in `𝔸⁴_ℂ` whose two branches at the origin are transverse smooth
planes.
declarations.statement:
theorem length_quotient_sup_eq_three_and_localIntersectionMultiplicity_eq_two :
    Module.length (MvPowerSeries (Fin 4) ℂ)
        (MvPowerSeries (Fin 4) ℂ ⧸ (unionOfPlanes ⊔ diagonalPlane)) = 3 ∧
      diagonalPlane.localIntersectionMultiplicity
        (MvPowerSeries (Fin 4) ℂ ⧸ unionOfPlanes) = 2
declarations.comment: the power series computation of the example: in ℂ[[x, y, z, w]] the length of the quotient by (xz, xw, yz, yw) + (x - z, y - w) is 3 and the Tor-formula multiplicity of the pair is 2; the statement on a variety and the existence clause are registered separately

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.TwoPlanes.length_quotient_sup_eq_three
declarations.doc:
**The naive count of the intersection of the two planes with the plane `x = z`, `y = w`.**
The length of `ℂ[[x, y, z, w]] / (xz, xw, yz, yw, x - z, y - w)` is `3`: the sum of the two
ideals is `(x - z, y - w) + 𝔪 ^ 2`, whose quotient is `ℂ[[x, y]] / (x, y) ^ 2`. This is the
length of `Tor_0` in the Tor formula for the intersection multiplicity, and it differs from the
true multiplicity `2`.
declarations.statement:
theorem length_quotient_sup_eq_three :
    Module.length (MvPowerSeries (Fin 4) ℂ)
      (MvPowerSeries (Fin 4) ℂ ⧸ (unionOfPlanes ⊔ diagonalPlane)) = 3
declarations.comment: the length-3 computation of the example: the naive count for the pair of ideals

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.TwoPlanes.not_isZero_tor_one
declarations.doc:
**The higher Tor modules are necessary in the Tor formula for intersection multiplicities.**
For `V` the union of the two planes `x = y = 0` and `z = w = 0` in `X` a nonsingular fourfold and
`W` the plane `x = z`, `y = w`, the module `Tor_1^A(𝒪_W, 𝒪_V)` at the point of intersection is
nonzero. Hence the alternating sum of the lengths of the Tor modules, which is the intersection
multiplicity `e(X, V · W, p) = 2`, is not the degree-zero term
`length 𝒪_{V ∩ W, p} = 3` on its own.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isZero_tor_one :
    ¬ IsZero (((Tor (ModuleCat (MvPowerSeries (Fin 4) ℂ)) 1).obj
        (ModuleCat.of (MvPowerSeries (Fin 4) ℂ)
          (MvPowerSeries (Fin 4) ℂ ⧸ diagonalPlane))).obj
      (ModuleCat.of (MvPowerSeries (Fin 4) ℂ)
        (MvPowerSeries (Fin 4) ℂ ⧸ unionOfPlanes)))
declarations.comment: higher Tors are necessary: Tor_1 of the two quotients is nonzero, so the alternating sum is not its degree-zero term; the value e = 2 itself is not computed here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_line_disjoint_and_isOpen_sweep
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B2T.** Let `B` be an irreducible closed subset of codimension at least two in the
projective space of a nonzero finite-dimensional vector space over an algebraically closed field
and let `p` be a closed point outside `B`. Then some projective line through `p` is disjoint
from `B`, and the closed points other than `p` lying on such a line are exactly the closed points
of a nonempty open subset of `𝐏(V)`, namely the complement of the cone over the image of `B`
under the projection away from `p`. The union of the avoiding lines itself is not open: in a
projective plane with `B` a point it contains `p` but no neighbourhood of `p`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_line_disjoint_and_isOpen_sweep [IsAlgClosed k] [FiniteDimensional k V]
    [Nontrivial V]
    (B : IrreducibleCloseds (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) (hcodim : (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ codimension B)
    (p : projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)
    (hp : IsClosed ({p} : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)))
    (hpB : p ∉ (B : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))) :
    (∃ W : Submodule k V, Module.finrank k (V ⧸ W) = 2 ∧ p ∈ linearSubspace k V W ∧
        Disjoint (linearSubspace k V W) (B : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))) ∧
      ∃ U : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V), IsOpen U ∧
        (∃ q ∈ U, IsClosed ({q} : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))) ∧
        ∀ q, IsClosed ({q} : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) → q ≠ p →
          (q ∈ U ↔ ∃ W : Submodule k V, Module.finrank k (V ⧸ W) = 2 ∧
            p ∈ linearSubspace k V W ∧ q ∈ linearSubspace k V W ∧
            Disjoint (linearSubspace k V W) (B : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)))
declarations.comment:
the sweeping-out clause is read as the proof reads it: the avoiding lines through
`p` cover the closed points of an open subset, their union itself being non-open at `p`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.projGenLinGroupEquivInvertibleClasses
declarations.doc:
**`PGL(V)` is the invertible open locus of the projectivized endomorphism space.** The
quotient presentation of `PGL(V)` sends a projective linear transformation to the projective
class of any of its linear representatives.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def projGenLinGroupEquivInvertibleClasses [Nontrivial V] :
    ProjGenLinGroup k V ≃ InvertibleEndomorphismClasses k V
declarations.comment: identification with the invertible open locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.projGenLinGroupEquivInvertibleClasses_apply
declarations.doc:
The equivalence with the invertible locus sends a projective linear transformation to the
projective class of any of its linear representatives.
declarations.statement:
public theorem projGenLinGroupEquivInvertibleClasses_apply [Nontrivial V]
    (g : LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup k V) (hg : (g : V →ₗ[k] V) ≠ 0) :
    ((projGenLinGroupEquivInvertibleClasses k V) (g : ProjGenLinGroup k V)).val =
      Projectivization.mk k (g : V →ₗ[k] V) hg
declarations.comment: representative formula for the invertible locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.dualEndClosedPointsEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The closed points of `P((End V)ᵛ)` are the projective classes of endomorphisms.** This is
the parameter space of a linear projective transformation.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def dualEndClosedPointsEquiv [IsAlgClosed k] [Module.Finite k V] :
    ClosedPoints k (Module.Dual k (V →ₗ[k] V)) ≃ Projectivization k (V →ₗ[k] V)
declarations.comment: closed-point identification for the parameter space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.dualEndClosedPointsEquiv_apply
declarations.doc:
The parameter point corresponding to a class of endomorphisms is cut out by the linear forms
annihilating that class. This fixes the identification.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dualEndClosedPointsEquiv_apply [IsAlgClosed k] [Module.Finite k V]
    (p : ClosedPoints k (Module.Dual k (V →ₗ[k] V))) (φ : Module.Dual k (V →ₗ[k] V)) :
    SymmetricAlgebra.ι k (Module.Dual k (V →ₗ[k] V)) φ ∈ p.val.asHomogeneousIdeal ↔
      φ ((dualEndClosedPointsEquiv k V p).rep) = 0
declarations.comment: annihilator formula for the parameter-space identification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.parameterPointToProjGenLinGroup_of_rep
declarations.doc: A parameter point represented by `g` names the class of `g` in `PGL(V)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem parameterPointToProjGenLinGroup_of_rep
    [Nontrivial V] [IsAlgClosed k] [Module.Finite k V]
    (p : InvertibleParameterPoints k V) (g : LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup k V)
    (hg : (g : V →ₗ[k] V) ≠ 0)
    (hpg : (dualEndClosedPointsEquiv k V) p.val = Projectivization.mk k (g : V →ₗ[k] V) hg) :
    parameterPointToProjGenLinGroup k V p = (g : ProjGenLinGroup k V)
declarations.comment: parameter point to projective linear transformation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.parameterPoint_smul_eq_map
declarations.doc:
On a parameter point represented by `g`, the morphism in the moving family is the action of
the inverse element of `PGL(V)`; the inversion accounts for the contravariance of `Proj`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem parameterPoint_smul_eq_map
    [Nontrivial V] [IsAlgClosed k] [Module.Finite k V]
    (p : InvertibleParameterPoints k V) (g : LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup k V)
    (hg : (g : V →ₗ[k] V) ≠ 0)
    (hpg : (dualEndClosedPointsEquiv k V) p.val = Projectivization.mk k (g : V →ₗ[k] V) hg)
    (x : projectiveSpaceOfModule k V) :
    (parameterPointToProjGenLinGroup k V p)⁻¹ • x = map k V g x
declarations.comment: compatibility of the parameter-point action

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.projGenLinGroup_is_two_pretransitive
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2U.** The projective general linear group of a finite-dimensional
vector space over an algebraically closed field acts doubly transitively on the closed points of
its projective space.
declarations.statement:
public lemma projGenLinGroup_is_two_pretransitive [IsAlgClosed k] [Module.Finite k V] :
    MulAction.IsMultiplyPretransitive (ProjGenLinGroup k V) (ClosedPoints k V) 2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.mapDomain_eq_top
declarations.doc:
An invertible linear map has everywhere-defined projective morphism: the domain of
definition of the induced graded ring homomorphism is all of `P(V)`.
declarations.comment: the invertible locus has full projective domain

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.mapDomain_ι_comp_map
declarations.doc:
On the domain of definition of the induced graded ring homomorphism, the morphism carrying
the comparison maps on all twists is the action of `g` on `P(V)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mapDomain_ι_comp_map (g : LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup k V) :
    (mapDomain (fun n => SymPow.symmetricPower n k V) (fun n => SymPow.symmetricPower n k V)
          (SymPow.gradedSymAlgMap (g : V →ₗ[k] V))).ι ≫ map k V g =
      (projMapData (fun n => SymPow.symmetricPower n k V)
        (fun n => SymPow.symmetricPower n k V)
        (SymPow.gradedSymAlgMap (g : V →ₗ[k] V))).hom
declarations.comment: compatibility with the projective transformation family

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.irreducible_det_genericMatrix
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2V.** The determinant of the generic square matrix of positive
size over a field is an irreducible multivariate polynomial.
declarations.statement:
lemma irreducible_det_genericMatrix (k : Type*) [Field k] (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    Irreducible (Matrix.det (fun i j : Fin n ↦ MvPolynomial.X (i, j) :
      Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin n) k)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.endDomain
declarations.doc:
The open `U(g)` on which the projective transformation attached to an endomorphism `g` of
`V` is defined: the domain of definition of the morphism of projective spectra induced by
`Sym g`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev endDomain (g : V →ₗ[k] V) : (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V).Opens
declarations.comment: the open U(ψ) over the point [g] of the parameter space, i.e. U(g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.endProjection
declarations.doc:
The projective transformation `r_g : 𝐏(V) ⊇ U(g) → 𝐏(V)` attached to an endomorphism `g`
of `V`: the morphism of projective spectra induced by `Sym g` on its domain of definition.
declarations.statement:
public def endProjection (g : V →ₗ[k] V) :
    (endDomain k V g).toScheme ⟶ projectiveSpaceOfModule k V
declarations.comment: the morphism r_ψ over the point [g] of the parameter space, i.e. r_g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.notMem_endDomain_iff
declarations.doc:
A point of `𝐏(V)` lies outside `U(g)` exactly when it lies on the
linear subspace cut out by the image of `g`, that is on `𝐏(Coker g) ⊆ 𝐏(V)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem notMem_endDomain_iff (g : V →ₗ[k] V) (q : projectiveSpaceOfModule k V) :
    q ∉ endDomain k V g ↔ q ∈ linearSubspace k V (LinearMap.range g)
declarations.comment: the complement of U(g) is the image of the closed immersion 𝐏(Coker g) → 𝐏(V)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.endProjection_eq_linearFunctionalPoint
declarations.doc:
The morphism `r_g` sends the point cut out by a functional `f` on `V` to the point cut out by
`f ∘ g`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem endProjection_eq_linearFunctionalPoint (g : V →ₗ[k] V)
    (y : (endDomain k V g).toScheme) (f : Module.Dual k V) (hf : f ≠ 0) (hfg : f ∘ₗ g ≠ 0)
    (hy : (y.val : projectiveSpaceOfModule k V) = linearFunctionalPoint k V f hf) :
    endProjection k V g y = linearFunctionalPoint k V (f ∘ₗ g) hfg
