declarations.comment: the value of r_g on a closed point, namely f ↦ f ∘ g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.range_endProjection_subset
declarations.doc:
Every point in the image of `r_g` lies on the linear subspace cut out by the kernel of `g`,
which is the image of `𝐏(Im g) → 𝐏(V)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem range_endProjection_subset (g : V →ₗ[k] V) :
    Set.range (endProjection k V g).base ⊆ linearSubspace k V (LinearMap.ker g)
declarations.comment: the image of r_g is contained in the image of 𝐏(Im g) → 𝐏(V)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_endProjection_eq
declarations.doc:
Over an algebraically closed field
every closed point of the linear subspace cut out by the kernel of `g` — that is, of the image
of `𝐏(Im g) → 𝐏(V)` — is the image under `r_g` of a point of `U(g)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_endProjection_eq [IsAlgClosed k] [Module.Finite k V] (g : V →ₗ[k] V)
    (q : projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)
    (hq : IsClosed ({q} : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)))
    (hmem : q ∈ linearSubspace k V (LinearMap.ker g)) :
    ∃ y : (endDomain k V g).toScheme, endProjection k V g y = q
declarations.comment: the image of r_g is the image of 𝐏(Im g) → 𝐏(V), on closed points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.endDomain_smul
declarations.doc: A unit multiple of `g` has the same domain of definition `U(g)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem endDomain_smul (c : kˣ) (g : V →ₗ[k] V) :
    endDomain k V ((c : k) • g) = endDomain k V g
declarations.comment: U(g) depends only on the point [g] of the parameter space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.endProjection_smul_apply
declarations.doc:
A unit multiple of `g` induces the same morphism `r_g` on the points cut out by linear
functionals.
declarations.statement:
public theorem endProjection_smul_apply (c : kˣ) (g : V →ₗ[k] V)
    (y : (endDomain k V ((c : k) • g)).toScheme) (y' : (endDomain k V g).toScheme)
    (f : Module.Dual k V) (hf : f ≠ 0) (hfg : f ∘ₗ g ≠ 0)
    (hy : (y.val : projectiveSpaceOfModule k V) = linearFunctionalPoint k V f hf)
    (hy' : (y'.val : projectiveSpaceOfModule k V) = linearFunctionalPoint k V f hf) :
    endProjection k V ((c : k) • g) y = endProjection k V g y'
declarations.comment: r_g depends only on the point [g] of the parameter space, on closed points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.universalEndCoeff
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map `V → (End V)ᵛ ⊗ V = Hom(End V, V)`** of the source, sending `v` to the
evaluation `g ↦ g v`.
declarations.statement: public def universalEndCoeff : V →ₗ[k] Module.Dual k (V →ₗ[k] V) ⊗[k] V
declarations.comment: the canonical map V → V ⊗ Eᵛ = Hom(E, V), v ↦ (g ↦ g v)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.universalEnd
declarations.doc:
**The universal endomorphism `ψ` of `V ⊗ 𝒪` over the affine parameter space**: the `A`-linear
extension of the canonical map `V → (End V)ᵛ ⊗ V ⊆ A ⊗ V`. On the fibre over an endomorphism `g`
it is `g`.
declarations.statement:
public def universalEnd :
    endParamRing k V ⊗[k] V →ₗ[endParamRing k V] endParamRing k V ⊗[k] V
declarations.comment: ψ over the affine parameter space Spec Sym(Eᵛ), the cone over 𝐏: the universal endomorphism of V ⊗ 𝒪, in place of the map of sheaves V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏 → V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏(1) over 𝐏

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.universalEndDomain
declarations.doc:
**The open `U(ψ)` of the universal family**: the domain of definition of the morphism of
relative projective spaces induced by `Sym ψ` over the affine parameter space.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev universalEndDomain :
    (projectiveSpaceOfModule (endParamRing k V) (endParamRing k V ⊗[k] V)).Opens
declarations.comment: U(ψ) ⊆ 𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_S) for S = Spec Sym(Eᵛ) the affine parameter space, the cone over 𝐏; the open over 𝐏 itself is AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.universalEndSheafDomain, built there from the source's own ψ : V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏 → V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏(1) and not from this one by descent along 𝔸(E) ∖ {0} → 𝐏, which is constructed nowhere; what is not identified with 𝐏 × 𝐏(V) is its ambient 𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏(1))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.universalEndProjection
declarations.doc:
**The universal family `r_ψ` of projective transformations**, `𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_S) ⊇ U(ψ) → 𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_S)`
over the affine space `S` of endomorphisms of `V`: the morphism of relative projective spaces
induced by `Sym ψ` on its domain of definition.
declarations.comment: r_ψ : U(ψ) → 𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_S) for S = Spec Sym(Eᵛ) the affine parameter space, the cone over 𝐏; the morphism over 𝐏 itself is AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.universalEndSheafProjection, built there from the source's own ψ and not from this one by descent along 𝔸(E) ∖ {0} → 𝐏, which is constructed nowhere; what is not identified with 𝐏 × 𝐏(V) are its total spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.endParamFibre_universalEnd
declarations.doc:
**The fibre of the universal endomorphism over the parameter point of `g` is `g`.** This is
what makes `universalEnd` universal: the family it defines has `r_g` as its fibre over `g`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem endParamFibre_universalEnd (g : V →ₗ[k] V) (x : endParamRing k V ⊗[k] V) :
    endParamFibre k V g (universalEnd k V x) = g (endParamFibre k V g x)
declarations.comment: the fibre of ψ over the parameter point of g is g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.endParamFibreHom_symAlgMap
declarations.doc:
**`Sym g` is the fibre of `Sym ψ` over the parameter point of `g`.** Reducing the universal
graded endomorphism of `Sym_A(V ⊗ A)` along the point of the parameter space attached to an
endomorphism `g` of `V` gives the graded endomorphism `Sym g` of `Sym_k(V)` out of which `U(g)`
and `r_g` are built.
declarations.statement:
public theorem endParamFibreHom_symAlgMap (g : V →ₗ[k] V)
    (x : SymmetricAlgebra (endParamRing k V) (endParamRing k V ⊗[k] V)) :
    endParamFibreHom k V g (SymPow.symAlgMap (universalEnd k V) x) =
      SymPow.symAlgMap g (endParamFibreHom k V g x)
declarations.comment: the fibre of r_ψ over the parameter point of g is r_g, on the homogeneous coordinate rings: Sym ψ reduces to Sym g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.endParamFibreInclusion
declarations.doc:
**The fibre of the universal family over the parameter point of `g`**: the morphism
`𝐏(V) → 𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_S)` induced by the specialization of the homogeneous coordinate ring, defined on
all of `𝐏(V)` by `endParamFibreInclusionDomain_eq_top`.
declarations.comment: the inclusion of the fibre of 𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_S) over the parameter point of g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.mem_universalEndDomain_iff
declarations.doc:
**`U(g)` is the fibre `U(ψ)` over the parameter point of `g`.** A point of `𝐏(V)`, included
as a point of the fibre of the relative projective space over the parameter point of `g`, lies in
the domain of the universal family exactly when it lies in `U(g)`, the domain of `r_g`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mem_universalEndDomain_iff (g : V →ₗ[k] V)
    (y : (endParamFibreInclusionDomain k V g).toScheme) :
    (endParamFibreInclusion k V g).base y ∈ universalEndDomain k V ↔
      (y.val : projectiveSpaceOfModule k V) ∈ endDomain k V g
declarations.comment: U(g) is the fibre U(ψ) over the parameter point of g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.notMem_universalEndDomain_iff
declarations.doc:
**The domain of the universal family.** A point lies outside `U(ψ)` exactly when every
degree-one form in the image of the universal endomorphism vanishes at it: the relative form of
the description of the complement of `U(g)` as the image of `𝐏(Coker g) → 𝐏(V)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem notMem_universalEndDomain_iff
    (q : projectiveSpaceOfModule (endParamRing k V) (endParamRing k V ⊗[k] V)) :
    q ∉ universalEndDomain k V ↔
      ∀ x : endParamRing k V ⊗[k] V,
        SymmetricAlgebra.ι (endParamRing k V) (endParamRing k V ⊗[k] V) (universalEnd k V x) ∈
          q.asHomogeneousIdeal
declarations.comment: the complement of U(ψ) is the relative 𝐏(Coker ψ), as the vanishing of the degree-one forms in the image of ψ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.universalEndProjection_comp_toSpec
declarations.doc:
**The universal family is a family over the parameter space.** The morphism `r_ψ` commutes
with the two structure morphisms of the relative projective space `𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_S)` to
`S = Spec Sym((End V)ᵛ)`, so it is a family of projective transformations parametrized by `S`
and its fibres are morphisms of the fibres.
declarations.statement:
public theorem universalEndProjection_comp_toSpec :
    universalEndProjection k V ≫
        projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec (endParamRing k V) (endParamRing k V ⊗[k] V) =
      (universalEndDomain k V).ι ≫
        projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec (endParamRing k V) (endParamRing k V ⊗[k] V)
declarations.comment: r_ψ is a morphism over the parameter space S = Spec Sym(Eᵛ), the cone over 𝐏

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.endParamFibreInclusion_comp_toSpec
declarations.doc:
**The fibre of the relative projective space over the parameter point of `g` is where `𝐏(V)`
goes.** The inclusion `ι_g : 𝐏(V) → 𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_S)` is a morphism over the point of `S` attached to
`g`, which is what makes it the inclusion of a fibre rather than merely a morphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem endParamFibreInclusion_comp_toSpec (g : V →ₗ[k] V) :
    endParamFibreInclusion k V g ≫
        projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec (endParamRing k V) (endParamRing k V ⊗[k] V) =
      (endParamFibreInclusionDomain k V g).ι ≫ projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k V ≫
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (endParamPoint k V g).toRingHom)
declarations.comment: the fibre inclusion is a morphism over the parameter point of g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.fibreSquareIso_hom_comp_morphismRestrict
declarations.doc:
**`r_g` is the fibre of `r_ψ` over the parameter point of `g`, as a square of scheme
morphisms.** Including the fibre `𝐏(V)` into the relative projective space and then applying the
universal family `r_ψ` is the same as applying `r_g` and then including the fibre: the square

`U(g) --r_g--> 𝐏(V) --ι_g--> 𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_S)`,  `U(g) --ι_g--> U(ψ) --r_ψ--> 𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_S)`

commutes, after the canonical identification `fibreSquareIso` of the two domains.

This is the composition law of Tag 01MZ applied to the two factorizations
`endParamFibreGradedHom_comp_gradedSymAlgMap` of a single graded ring homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fibreSquareIso_hom_comp_morphismRestrict (g : V →ₗ[k] V) :
    (fibreSquareIso k V g).hom ≫
        (endParamFibreInclusion k V g ∣_ universalEndDomain k V) ≫ universalEndProjection k V =
      (endProjection k V g ∣_ endParamFibreInclusionDomain k V g) ≫
        endParamFibreInclusion k V g
declarations.comment: the fibre of r_ψ over the parameter point of g is r_g, as scheme morphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.isPullback_universalFamilySpace
declarations.doc:
**The relative projective space of the family is a product.** The square formed by the
projection `𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_S) ⟶ 𝐏(V)` and the two structure morphisms is cartesian, so
`𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_S) = S ×_{Spec k} 𝐏(V)` with `S = Spec Sym((End V)ᵛ)` the affine space of
endomorphisms. This is `Stacks.ProjectiveSpaceBaseChange.isPullback_projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec`
for the base change of `V` along `k → Sym((End V)ᵛ)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPullback_universalFamilySpace :
    IsPullback (Stacks.ProjectiveSpaceBaseChange.map k (endParamRing k V) V)
      (projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec (endParamRing k V) (endParamRing k V ⊗[k] V))
      (projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k V)
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (endParamRing k V))))
declarations.comment: the total space of the family is the product 𝔸(E) × 𝐏(V), for 𝔸(E) = Spec Sym(Eᵛ) the cone over 𝐏; the source writes the displayed family on 𝐏 × 𝐏(V)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.universalFamilySpaceIso
declarations.doc:
**The total space of the family, as the product `𝔸(E) × 𝐏(V)`.** The identification of
`𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_S)` with the fibre product of `𝐏(V)` and the affine space of endomorphisms over
`Spec k`, carried by `isPullback_universalFamilySpace`.
declarations.statement:
public def universalFamilySpaceIso :
    projectiveSpaceOfModule (endParamRing k V) (endParamRing k V ⊗[k] V) ≅
      Limits.pullback (projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k V)
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (endParamRing k V))))
declarations.comment: the identification 𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_S) = 𝔸(E) × 𝐏(V) over the cone 𝔸(E) = Spec Sym(Eᵛ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.universalEndSheafMap
declarations.doc:
**The map of sheaves `ψ : V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏 ⟶ V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏(1)` over the projective parameter space
`𝐏 = 𝐏(Eᵛ)`**, attached by the universal property of `V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏` to the canonical `k`-linear map
`V → Γ(𝐏, V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏(1))`.
declarations.comment: ψ : V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏 → V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏(1) over the projective parameter space 𝐏 = 𝐏(Eᵛ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.universalEndSheafDomain
declarations.doc:
**The open `U(ψ) ⊆ 𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏(1))`** of the universal family over the projective parameter
space: Tag 07ZG's open for `Sym ψ`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev universalEndSheafDomain :
    (schemeProjectiveBundle
      (twistObj k (dualEndSpace k V) (constantModule k (dualEndSpace k V) V) ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ))
      (isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _)).scheme.Opens
declarations.comment: U(ψ) ⊆ 𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏(1)) over the projective parameter space 𝐏 = 𝐏(Eᵛ); its identification with an open subscheme of the displayed 𝐏 × 𝐏(V) is exists_iso_universalEndFamily_selfMap

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.universalEndSheafProjection
declarations.doc:
**The universal family of projective transformations over the projective parameter space**,
`𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏(1)) ⊇ U(ψ) --r_ψ--> 𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏)`: the partially defined morphism of relative
projective spaces that Tag 07ZG attaches to `Sym ψ`.
declarations.statement:
def universalEndSheafProjection :
    (universalEndSheafDomain k V).toScheme ⟶
      (schemeProjectiveBundle (constantModule k (dualEndSpace k V) V)
        (isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _)).scheme
declarations.comment: r_ψ : U(ψ) → 𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏) over the projective parameter space 𝐏 = 𝐏(Eᵛ); read through the identifications of both total spaces with 𝐏 × 𝐏(V) over 𝐏, it is the displayed self-map, exists_iso_universalEndFamily_selfMap

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.universalEndSheafProjection_comp_toBase
declarations.doc:
**The universal family is a family over the parameter space `𝐏`**: `r_ψ` is a morphism over
`𝐏`, so it is a family of maps of the fibres and not merely a morphism of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem universalEndSheafProjection_comp_toBase :
    universalEndSheafProjection k V ≫
        schemeProjectiveBundleToBase (constantModule k (dualEndSpace k V) V)
          (isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _) =
      (universalEndSheafDomain k V).ι ≫
        schemeProjectiveBundleToBase
          (twistObj k (dualEndSpace k V)
            (constantModule k (dualEndSpace k V) V) ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ))
          (isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _)
declarations.comment: the universal family over 𝐏 = 𝐏(Eᵛ) is a morphism over 𝐏

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_iso_pullback_universalEndTarget
declarations.doc:
**The target of Tag 0B2W's universal family is the product `𝐏 × 𝐏(V)`.** The relative
projective space `𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏)` over the projective parameter space `𝐏 = 𝐏(Eᵛ)` is the fibre
product of `𝐏` with the projective space of `V` over `Spec k`, by an isomorphism over `𝐏`.

This is the first of the two identifications Tag 0B2W's display uses, and it is the base change
of a relative homogeneous spectrum (Tag 01O3) along the structure morphism of `𝐏`, which is not
an affine morphism and over which nothing is assumed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_iso_pullback_universalEndTarget :
    ∃ e : (Stacks.SymGraded.schemeProjectiveBundle
          (constantModule k (dualEndSpace k V) V)
          (Stacks.SymGraded.isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _)).scheme ≅
        pullback (projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k (dualEndSpace k V))
          (Stacks.SymGraded.schemeProjectiveBundle
            (AlgebraicGeometry.tilde (ModuleCat.of (CommRingCat.of k) V))
            (Stacks.SymGraded.isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _)).toBase,
      e.hom ≫ pullback.fst (projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k (dualEndSpace k V))
          (Stacks.SymGraded.schemeProjectiveBundle
            (AlgebraicGeometry.tilde (ModuleCat.of (CommRingCat.of k) V))
            (Stacks.SymGraded.isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _)).toBase =
        (Stacks.SymGraded.schemeProjectiveBundle
          (constantModule k (dualEndSpace k V) V)
          (Stacks.SymGraded.isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _)).toBase
declarations.comment: the identification 𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏) = 𝐏 × 𝐏(V) over the projective parameter space 𝐏 = 𝐏(Eᵛ), the target of r_ψ; the second factor is the projective bundle of Ṽ over Spec k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_isPullback_universalEndTarget
declarations.doc:
**The target of Tag 0B2W's universal family is the product `𝐏 × 𝐏(V)`, as a cartesian
square.** The projection of `𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏)` to `𝐏`, the comparison with the projective space of `V`
over `Spec k` and the two structure morphisms form a cartesian square.

This is the statement `AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.isPullback_universalFamilySpace`
over the projective parameter space `𝐏` instead of over the affine cone `𝔸(E)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isPullback_universalEndTarget :
    ∃ q : (Stacks.SymGraded.schemeProjectiveBundle
          (constantModule k (dualEndSpace k V) V)
          (Stacks.SymGraded.isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _)).scheme ⟶
        (Stacks.SymGraded.schemeProjectiveBundle
          (AlgebraicGeometry.tilde (ModuleCat.of (CommRingCat.of k) V))
          (Stacks.SymGraded.isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _)).scheme,
      IsPullback (Stacks.SymGraded.schemeProjectiveBundle
          (constantModule k (dualEndSpace k V) V)
          (Stacks.SymGraded.isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _)).toBase q
        (projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k (dualEndSpace k V))
        (Stacks.SymGraded.schemeProjectiveBundle
          (AlgebraicGeometry.tilde (ModuleCat.of (CommRingCat.of k) V))
          (Stacks.SymGraded.isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _)).toBase
declarations.comment: the identification 𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏) = 𝐏 × 𝐏(V) as a cartesian square over Spec k, the affine-cone product identification carried over to the projective parameter space 𝐏 = 𝐏(Eᵛ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_iso_pullback_universalEndTarget_comp_toBase
declarations.doc:
**The universal family is a family over `𝐏` read on the product.** Composing
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.universalEndSheafProjection_comp_toBase` with the
identification of the target with `𝐏 × 𝐏(V)`: the first projection of the product, pulled back
along `r_ψ` and the identification, is the projection of `U(ψ)` to `𝐏`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_iso_pullback_universalEndTarget_comp_toBase :
    ∃ e : (Stacks.SymGraded.schemeProjectiveBundle
          (constantModule k (dualEndSpace k V) V)
          (Stacks.SymGraded.isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _)).scheme ≅
        pullback (projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k (dualEndSpace k V))
          (Stacks.SymGraded.schemeProjectiveBundle
            (AlgebraicGeometry.tilde (ModuleCat.of (CommRingCat.of k) V))
            (Stacks.SymGraded.isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _)).toBase,
      (universalEndSheafProjection k V ≫ e.hom) ≫
          pullback.fst (projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k (dualEndSpace k V))
            (Stacks.SymGraded.schemeProjectiveBundle
              (AlgebraicGeometry.tilde (ModuleCat.of (CommRingCat.of k) V))
              (Stacks.SymGraded.isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _)).toBase =
        (universalEndSheafDomain k V).ι ≫
          Stacks.SymGraded.schemeProjectiveBundleToBase
            (twistObj k (dualEndSpace k V)
              (constantModule k (dualEndSpace k V) V) ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ))
            (Stacks.SymGraded.isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _)
declarations.comment: r_ψ followed by the identification of its target with 𝐏 × 𝐏(V) is a morphism over 𝐏, the first projection of the product

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_iso_universalEndFamily_selfMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B2W].** The universal family of projective transformations of a
finite-dimensional vector space `V` over a field `k`, read as the partially defined self-map

`𝐏 × 𝐏(V) ⊇ U(ψ) --r_ψ--> 𝐏 × 𝐏(V)`

of the product of the parameter space `𝐏 = 𝐏(Eᵛ)`, `E = End(V)`, with the projective space of
`V`, as the source displays it.

Both total spaces of the family built in
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.universalEndSheafProjection` — the twisted
`𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏(1))` and the untwisted `𝐏(V ⊗ 𝒪_𝐏)` — are isomorphic to `𝐏 × 𝐏(V)` by isomorphisms
over `𝐏`; under the first of them the domain of definition `U(ψ)` becomes an open subscheme of
`𝐏 × 𝐏(V)`, and `r_ψ`, read through the second, is a morphism from that open subscheme to
`𝐏 × 𝐏(V)` over `𝐏`, hence a family of partially defined self-maps of `𝐏(V)` indexed by `𝐏`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_universalEndFamily_selfMap :
    ∃ (α : (schemeProjectiveBundle (twistObj k (dualEndSpace k V)
          (constantModule k (dualEndSpace k V) V) ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ))
          (isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _)).scheme ≅ universalProductSpace k V)
      (β : (schemeProjectiveBundle (constantModule k (dualEndSpace k V) V)
          (isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _)).scheme ≅ universalProductSpace k V),
      α.hom ≫ universalProductToParam k V =
          schemeProjectiveBundleToBase (twistObj k (dualEndSpace k V)
            (constantModule k (dualEndSpace k V) V) ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ))
            (isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _) ∧
        β.hom ≫ universalProductToParam k V =
          schemeProjectiveBundleToBase (constantModule k (dualEndSpace k V) V)
            (isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent _) ∧
        IsOpenImmersion ((universalEndSheafDomain k V).ι ≫ α.hom) ∧
        (universalEndSheafProjection k V ≫ β.hom) ≫ universalProductToParam k V =
          ((universalEndSheafDomain k V).ι ≫ α.hom) ≫ universalProductToParam k V
declarations.comment: the universal family of projective transformations as the displayed partially defined self-map of 𝐏 × 𝐏(V): both total spaces identified with the product over 𝐏, U(ψ) as an open subscheme of the product, and r_ψ as a morphism of the product over 𝐏

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.ChowRing.chowPullback_eq_flatPullbackChow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B2X, part (4): for flat `f` the pullback is flat pullback.** If `f` is flat of
relative dimension `e`, then `f^* = f^*_{flat} : CH_k(Y) ⟶ CH_{k+e}(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowPullback_eq_flatPullbackChow [Flat f] (e : ℕ)
    (he : topologicalKrullDim X = topologicalKrullDim Y + (e : WithBot ℕ∞)) {k : ℤ}
    (hkm : k + dX = dY + (k + e)) :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType f := locallyOfFiniteType_of_isVariety_comp K sX sY f hf
    chowPullback K sX sY hX hY hdX hdY f hf hkm =
      flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension (fieldChowSituation K) sX sY f hf e
        (relativeDimension_of_flat_of_isVariety K sX sY f hf e he) k
declarations.comment: part (4): for flat `f` of relative dimension `e`, the pullback `f^*` of Tag 0B0H is the flat pullback `CH_k(Y) → CH_{k+e}(X)` of Section 43.9

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.ChowRing.chowMulFun_properChowPushforward_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B2X, part (3): the projection formula** `f_*(a) · b = f_*(a · f^*b)`. With `s` the
graph, `s_*(a · f^*b) = s_*(a) · pr_Y^* b` on `X × Y` by the remark on graphs, and
`f_* = pr_{Y,*} ∘ s_*`, so this is the flat projection formula (Tag 0B10) for `pr_Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowMulFun_properChowPushforward_eq {r k m n : ℤ} (hkm : k + dX = dY + m)
    (hn : r + m = dX + n) (a : chowGroup (fieldChowSituation K) sX r)
    (b : chowGroup (fieldChowSituation K) sY k) :
    letI := isProper_of_comp_eq f hf
    chowMulFun K sY hY n
        (properChowPushforward (fieldChowSituation K) sX sY f hf r
          (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper (fieldChowSituation K)
            sX sY f hf r) a) b =
      properChowPushforward (fieldChowSituation K) sX sY f hf n
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper (fieldChowSituation K)
          sX sY f hf n)
        (chowMulFun K sX hX n a (chowPullback K sX sY hX hY hdX hdY f hf hkm b))
declarations.comment: part (3): the projection formula `f_*(α) · β = f_*(α · f^*β)` on Chow groups, for `α ∈ CH_r(X)` and `β ∈ CH_k(Y)`, `f^*β ∈ CH_m(X)` with `k + dim X = dim Y + m`, and both products in `CH_n` with `r + m = dim X + n`

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.ChowRing.chowPullback_isRingHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2X, part (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of nonsingular
projective varieties over an algebraically closed field (the chapter's convention, Tag 0AZ8).
Then the pullback `f^* : CH^*(Y) ⟶ CH^*(X)` of Section 43.23 (Tag 0B0H) is a ring map: there is
a ring homomorphism between the Chow rings of Section 43.21 (Tag 0B0G) which is `f^*` on every
graded piece `CH^c(Y) ⟶ CH^c(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowPullback_isRingHom :
    ∃ φ : ChowRing K sY hY dY hdY →+* ChowRing K sX hX dX hdX,
      ∀ (c : ℕ) (a : ChowGrade K sY dY hY hdY c),
        φ (DirectSum.of _ c a) =
          DirectSum.of _ c (chowPullback K sX sY hX hY hdX hdY f hf (k := (dY : ℤ) - c)
            (m := (dX : ℤ) - c) (by ring) a)
declarations.comment: part (1): `f^* : CH^*(Y) → CH^*(X)` is a ring map, stated as the existence of a ring homomorphism between the Chow rings `⨁_c CH^c` which is `f^*` on each graded piece `CH^c(Y) = CH_{dim Y - c}(Y) → CH^c(X) = CH_{dim X - c}(X)`; the content is `chowPullback_chowMulFun` (`f^*(a · b) = f^*a · f^*b`) and `chowPullback_fundamentalClass` (`f^*[Y] = [X]`)

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.ChowRing.chowPullback_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B2X, part (2).** For morphisms `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` of
nonsingular projective varieties, `(g ∘ f)^* = f^* ∘ g^*` on Chow groups. On
`W = (X × Y) × Z`, `f^*(g^*c) = pr_{X,*}(q₁₂^*[Γ_f] · q₂₃^*[Γ_g] · q₃^* c)` by base change
(Tag 02RG), the projection formula for `q₁₂` (Tag 0B10) and Tag 0B0Z; the product
`q₁₂^*[Γ_f] · q₂₃^*[Γ_g]` is the transversal intersection `{(x, f(x), g(f(x)))}`, which `q₁₃`
maps isomorphically onto `Γ_{g ∘ f}`, and the projection formula for `q₁₃` gives `(g ∘ f)^* c`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowPullback_comp {k l m : ℤ} (hkl : k + dY = dZ + l) (hlm : l + dX = dY + m)
    (hkm : k + dX = dZ + m) (c : chowGroup (fieldChowSituation K) sZ k) :
    chowPullback K sX sZ hX hZ hdX hdZ (f ≫ g) (by rw [Category.assoc, hg, hf]) hkm c =
      chowPullback K sX sY hX hY hdX hdY f hf hlm
        (chowPullback K sY sZ hY hZ hdY hdZ g hg hkl c)
declarations.comment: part (2): `(g ∘ f)^* = f^* ∘ g^*` for a composable pair of morphisms of nonsingular projective varieties, on Chow groups `CH_k(Z) → CH_l(Y) → CH_m(X)` with `k + dim Y = dim Z + l`, `l + dim X = dim Y + m`

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_sequential_colimit_not_preserved
declarations.doc:
A sequential diagram of abelian topological groups for which the colimit topology as spaces
differs from the colimit topology as groups.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_sequential_colimit_not_preserved :
    ∃ F : ℕ ⥤ TopGrp.{u},
      (∀ n : ℕ, ∀ x y : F.obj n, x * y = y * x) ∧
        ¬ PreservesColimit F TopGrp.forgetToTopCat

declarations.name: IsLocallyClosed.quasiSober
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0B31 (2).** A locally closed subspace of a quasi-sober space is quasi-sober.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocallyClosed.quasiSober [QuasiSober X] {Y : Set X} (hY : IsLocallyClosed Y) :
    QuasiSober Y

declarations.name: IsLocallyClosed.quasiSober_and_t0Space
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B31 (3).** A locally closed subspace of a sober space is sober, sobriety being
`QuasiSober` together with `T0Space`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocallyClosed.quasiSober_and_t0Space [QuasiSober X] [T0Space X] {Y : Set X}
    (hY : IsLocallyClosed Y) : QuasiSober Y ∧ T0Space Y

declarations.name: quasiSober_of_indiscreteTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B32.** An indiscrete topological space with at least two points is
quasi-sober: its only nonempty closed subset is the whole space, and every point is a
generic point for it.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiSober_of_indiscreteTopology (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X]
    [IndiscreteTopology X] [Nontrivial X] : QuasiSober X
declarations.comment: quasi-sober

declarations.name: not_t0Space_of_indiscreteTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B32.** An indiscrete topological space with at least two points is not
Kolmogorov: any two of its points are inseparable.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_t0Space_of_indiscreteTopology (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X]
    [IndiscreteTopology X] [Nontrivial X] : ¬ T0Space X
declarations.comment: not Kolmogorov

registrations.name: Set.iUnion_of_singleton
registrations.comment: the singleton subspaces cover the space

registrations.name: Subsingleton.discreteTopology
registrations.comment: the singleton subspaces are discrete

declarations.name: t0Space_cofiniteTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B33** (Kolmogorov).
An infinite set with the cofinite topology is Kolmogorov: its singletons are finite, hence
closed, so the space is `T1Space` and a fortiori `T0Space`. Infiniteness is not needed here.
declarations.statement: theorem t0Space_cofiniteTopology : T0Space (CofiniteTopology Y)
declarations.comment: Kolmogorov

declarations.name: not_quasiSober_cofiniteTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B33** (not quasi-sober).
An infinite set with the cofinite topology is not quasi-sober: the whole space is irreducible
and closed, but the closure of a singleton is that singleton, so no point is generic for it.
declarations.statement: theorem not_quasiSober_cofiniteTopology [Infinite Y] : ¬ QuasiSober (CofiniteTopology Y)
declarations.comment: not quasi-sober

declarations.name: singleton_cover_cofiniteTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B33** (covering by sober subspaces).
The singletons of an infinite set with the cofinite topology cover it, and each singleton
subspace is discrete and hence sober: it has exactly one point. So a space covered by sober
subspaces need not be quasi-sober.
declarations.statement:
theorem singleton_cover_cofiniteTopology :
    (⋃ y : CofiniteTopology Y, ({y} : Set (CofiniteTopology Y))) = Set.univ ∧
      ∀ y : CofiniteTopology Y, DiscreteTopology ({y} : Set (CofiniteTopology Y)) ∧
        StacksSober ({y} : Set (CofiniteTopology Y))
declarations.comment: covering by discrete, hence sober, subspaces

declarations.name: not_t0Space_sum_cofiniteTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B34.** The disjoint union of an indiscrete space with at least two points and
an infinite set with the cofinite topology is not Kolmogorov.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_t0Space_sum_cofiniteTopology (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X]
    [IndiscreteTopology X] [Nontrivial X] (Y : Type*) [Infinite Y] :
    ¬ T0Space (X ⊕ CofiniteTopology Y)

declarations.name: not_quasiSober_sum_cofiniteTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B34.** The disjoint union of an indiscrete space with at least two points and
an infinite set with the cofinite topology is not quasi-sober.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_quasiSober_sum_cofiniteTopology (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X]
    [IndiscreteTopology X] [Nontrivial X] (Y : Type*) [Infinite Y] :
    ¬ QuasiSober (X ⊕ CofiniteTopology Y)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.SoberSubspace.unique_genericPoint_cofiniteAway
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B35.** The space `Z` with the topology `cofiniteAway Z z` is sober: every
irreducible closed subset has a unique generic point.
declarations.statement:
theorem unique_genericPoint_cofiniteAway (Z : Type*) [Infinite Z] (z : Z) :
    letI : TopologicalSpace Z := cofiniteAway Z z
    ∀ {S : Set Z}, IsIrreducible S → IsClosed S → ∃! x, IsGenericPoint x S

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.SoberSubspace.not_quasiSober_subtype_ne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B35.** The subspace `Z \ {z}` of the sober space `cofiniteAway Z z` is not
quasi-sober: it is irreducible, yet all of its singletons are closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_quasiSober_subtype_ne (Z : Type*) [Infinite Z] (z : Z) :
    letI : TopologicalSpace Z := cofiniteAway Z z
    ¬ QuasiSober ({x : Z // x ≠ z})

declarations.name: surjective_dualEval_of_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0B36.** The canonical evaluation map from a finite module over a Dedekind domain
to its double dual is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_dualEval_of_finite
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDedekindDomain R]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    Function.Surjective (Module.Dual.eval R M)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.rank_and_determinant_of_vect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B37: rank and determinant of finite locally free modules.** Let
`(X, O_X)` be a ringed space and `Vect(X)` the category of finite locally free `O_X`-modules.

1. `Vect(X)`, with the short exact sequences of `O_X`-modules all of whose terms are finite
   locally free, is an exact category ([Stacks, Tag 05SF]). Its admissible epimorphisms are the
   surjections whose kernel is finite locally free (in particular surjections), and its admissible
   monomorphisms are the kernels of those.
2. `Vect(X)` has a set of isomorphism classes of objects, and `K₀(Vect(X))` is generated by the
   classes `[E]` subject to `[E] = [E'] + [E'']` for every short exact sequence
   `0 → E' → E → E'' → 0` of finite locally free modules.
3. If all stalks `O_{X,x}` are nonzero rings, the rank `rank_E(x) = rank_{O_{X,x}} E_x` is a
   locally constant function, additive in short exact sequences, so that `[E] ↦ rank_E` is a
   homomorphism `K₀(Vect(X)) → Map_cont(X, ℤ)`. The loci `X_i` where the rank is `i` are open and
   closed, pairwise disjoint and cover `X`, `E` is finite locally free of rank `i` on `X_i`, and
   `det(E)` is `⋀ⁱ(E|_{X_i})` on `X_i`.
4. The determinant `det(E)` is an invertible module, finite locally free of rank `1`, and
   `[E] ↦ det(E)` is a homomorphism `det : K₀(Vect(X)) → Pic(X)`.

`det(E)` is the determinant of [Stacks, Tag 0FJN] and the additivity of `det` is the isomorphism
`det(E') ⊗ det(E'') ≅ det(E)` of [Stacks, Tag 0B38].
declarations.statement:
theorem rank_and_determinant_of_vect :
    IsExactStructure (conflation (Vect Osharp)) ∧
    (∀ {E F : (Vect Osharp).FullSubcategory} (p : E ⟶ F),
      AdmissibleEpi (conflation (Vect Osharp)) p ↔ Epi p.hom ∧ Vect Osharp (kernel p.hom)) ∧
    (∀ {E F : (Vect Osharp).FullSubcategory} (i : E ⟶ F),
      AdmissibleMono (conflation (Vect Osharp)) i ↔
        ∃ (G : (Vect Osharp).FullSubcategory) (p : F ⟶ G) (w : i.hom ≫ p.hom = 0),
          (Epi p.hom ∧ Vect Osharp (kernel p.hom)) ∧
            Nonempty (IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι i.hom w))) ∧
    ObjectProperty.EssentiallySmall.{u} (Vect Osharp) ∧
    (∀ (S : ShortComplex
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (toRingCat (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) Osharp)))
        (_ : S.ShortExact) (h₁ : Vect Osharp S.X₁) (h₂ : Vect Osharp S.X₂)
        (h₃ : Vect Osharp S.X₃),
      KZero.of (mkObj S.X₂ h₂) = KZero.of (mkObj S.X₁ h₁) + KZero.of (mkObj S.X₃ h₃)) ∧
    (∀ hO : LocallyFreeRank.StalksNontrivial X Osharp,
      (∀ (E : (Vect Osharp).FullSubcategory) (x : X),
        Module.finrank ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk Osharp.obj x)
          ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk E.obj.val.presheaf x) = vectRank hO E x) ∧
      (∀ (S : ShortComplex
          (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (toRingCat (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) Osharp)))
          (_ : S.ShortExact) (h₁ : Vect Osharp S.X₁) (h₂ : Vect Osharp S.X₂)
          (h₃ : Vect Osharp S.X₃),
        vectRank hO (mkObj S.X₂ h₂) = vectRank hO (mkObj S.X₁ h₁) + vectRank hO (mkObj S.X₃ h₃)) ∧
      (∀ (E : (Vect Osharp).FullSubcategory) (x : X),
        rankHom hO (KZero.of E) x = (vectRank hO E x : ℤ)) ∧
      ∀ E : (Vect Osharp).FullSubcategory,
        IsLocallyConstant (⇑(vectRank hO E)) ∧
        (∀ i : ℕ, IsClopen (@rankStratum X Osharp E.obj hO E.property i : Set X)) ∧
        Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint
          fun i : ℕ => (@rankStratum X Osharp E.obj hO E.property i : Set X)) ∧
        (⨆ i : ℕ, @rankStratum X Osharp E.obj hO E.property i) = ⊤ ∧
        (∀ (i : ℕ) (x : X), x ∈ @rankStratum X Osharp E.obj hO E.property i →
          ∃ (V : Opens X) (_ : x ∈ V) (_ : V ≤ @rankStratum X Osharp E.obj hO E.property i)
            (I : Type u), Nonempty (I ≃ Fin i) ∧
              Nonempty (_root_.SheafOfModules.free.{u} I ≅ E.obj.over V)) ∧
        ∀ i : ℕ, Nonempty ((determinant E.obj).over (@rankStratum X Osharp E.obj hO E.property i) ≅
          (_root_.SheafOfModules.algebras
            (Osharp := Osharp.over (@rankStratum X Osharp E.obj hO E.property i))
            ((Opens.grothendieckTopology X).over (@rankStratum X Osharp E.obj hO E.property i))
            (show _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (toRingCat
              ((Opens.grothendieckTopology X).over (@rankStratum X Osharp E.obj hO E.property i))
              (Osharp.over (@rankStratum X Osharp E.obj hO E.property i))) from
              E.obj.over (@rankStratum X Osharp E.obj hO E.property i))).exteriorPower i)) ∧
    (∀ E : (Vect Osharp).FullSubcategory,
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
          (determinant E.obj) 1 ∧
        haveI := E.property
        IsInvertible Osharp.obj isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf (determinant E.obj)) ∧
    ∀ E : (Vect Osharp).FullSubcategory,
      detHom (KZero.of E) = haveI := E.property
        Picard.classOf Osharp.obj isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf (determinant E.obj)
          (isInvertible_determinant E.obj)
declarations.comment: Vect(X) is an exact category with the conflations, admissible epimorphisms and admissible monomorphisms stated; it has a set of isomorphism classes and K_0(Vect(X)) is given by the stated generators and relations; the rank is the stalk rank, locally constant, additive and defines K_0(Vect(X)) → Map_cont(X, Z); the clopen decomposition X = X_0 ⊔ X_1 ⊔ … with E of rank i on X_i and det(E) = ⋀^i(E|_{X_i}) there; det(E) is invertible and locally free of rank 1 and defines det : K_0(Vect(X)) → Pic(X). The admissible epimorphisms are the surjections whose kernel is finite locally free, which on a ringed space is not every surjection of Vect(X)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.detSummandComparison_ι_unit_wedge
declarations.doc:
**The wedge-and-lift formula for the comparison between determinant summands**, in every
pair of degrees, read inside `⋀ⁿ⁺ᵐ E` through the inclusion of the degree-`n+m` summand of
`det(E)`.

This is the wedge-and-lift formula of [Stacks, Tag 0B38] in the general case: a short exact
sequence of finite locally free sheaves with no constant-rank hypothesis. On the summand
`det(E')ₙ ⊗ det(E'')ₘ` of `det(E') ⊗ det(E'')` the canonical map of
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.determinantTensorDeterminantHom` carries the image of
`(s₁∧⋯∧sₙ) ⊗ (g(l₁)∧⋯∧g(lₘ))` to `f(s₁)∧⋯∧f(sₙ)∧l₁∧⋯∧lₘ`, for **arbitrary** local lifts `lⱼ`.
This is the formula the source gives for its canonical map, and
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.eq_determinantTensorDeterminantHom` and
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.eq_detTensorAnnComparison` say it determines the map.
declarations.statement:
theorem detSummandComparison_ι_unit_wedge
    (hS : (ShortComplex.mk f g hfg).Exact) [Mono f] [Epi g]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E']
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E''] (n m : ℕ)
    (V : (Opens ↥X)ᵒᵖ)
    (w : ToType ((A'.exteriorAnnihilator n).toSheafOfModules.val.obj V))
    (s : Fin n → E'.val.obj V)
    (hw : (A'.exteriorAnnihilator n).ι.val.app V w = wedgeSec A' V n s)
    (z : ToType ((A''.exteriorAnnihilator m).toSheafOfModules.val.obj V))
    (l : Fin m → E.val.obj V)
    (hz : (A''.exteriorAnnihilator m).ι.val.app V z =
      wedgeSec A'' V m fun i => g.val.app V (l i)) :
    (detSummandComparison A' A A'' f g hfg hS n m ≫
          (A.exteriorAnnihilator (n + m)).ι).val.app V
        ((PresheafOfModules.tensorSheafUnit (A'.exteriorAnnihilator n).toSheafOfModules
          (A''.exteriorAnnihilator m).toSheafOfModules).app V (w ⊗ₜ z)) =
      wedgeSec A V (n + m) (Fin.append (fun i => f.val.app V (s i)) l)
declarations.comment: the WEDGE-AND-LIFT FORMULA in the GENERAL case, with no constant-rank hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.isIso_determinantTensorDeterminantHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B38: the canonical map `det(E') ⊗ det(E'') ⟶ det(E)` is an isomorphism**, for a
short exact sequence `0 → E' → E → E'' → 0` of sheaves of modules on a ringed space whose outer
terms are finite locally free of **no particular rank**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_determinantTensorDeterminantHom
    (hS : (ShortComplex.mk f g hfg).Exact) [Mono f] [Epi g]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E']
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E''] :
    IsIso (determinantTensorDeterminantHom A' A A'' f g hfg hS)
declarations.comment: the ISOMORPHISM clause in the GENERAL case: the canonical map det(E')⊗det(E'')⟶det(E) of `Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.determinantTensorDeterminantHom` is an isomorphism, for a short exact sequence of finite locally free sheaves with NO constant-rank hypothesis. Here det is the det of 0FJN. The isomorphism itself is `determinantTensorDeterminantIsoOfFiniteLocallyFree`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.eq_determinantTensorDeterminantHom
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map is the only morphism restricting to
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.detTensorAnnComparison` on every degree-`m` summand of
`det(E'')`.** Together with `Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.eq_detTensorAnnComparison` and the
wedge-and-lift formula `Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.detSummandComparison_ι_unit_wedge` this
is the precise sense in which the map of [Stacks, Tag 0B38] is *canonical*.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_determinantTensorDeterminantHom
    (hS : (ShortComplex.mk f g hfg).Exact) [Mono f] [Epi g]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E']
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E'']
    (ψ : ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor Osharp).obj A'.determinant).obj A''.determinant
        ⟶ A.determinant)
    (hψ : ∀ m : ℕ, (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorLocalProperties.tensorSheafRight
            (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥X) Osharp A'.determinant).map
          (Limits.Sigma.ι (fun j : ℕ => (A''.exteriorAnnihilator j).toSheafOfModules) m) ≫ ψ =
        detTensorAnnComparison A' A A'' f g hfg hS m) :
    ψ = determinantTensorDeterminantHom A' A A'' f g hfg hS
declarations.comment: uniqueness of the canonical map det(E')⊗det(E'')⟶det(E) in the GENERAL case — a short exact sequence of finite locally free sheaves of modules with no constant-rank hypothesis. Together with `eq_detTensorAnnComparison` and the wedge-and-lift formula `detSummandComparison_ι_unit_wedge` this says the map is determined by the formula the source gives for it

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.determinantTensorDeterminantIsoOfFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B38, the general case.** For a short exact sequence `0 → E' → E → E'' → 0` of
sheaves of `O_X`-modules on a ringed space with `E'` and `E''` **finite locally free of no
particular rank**, there is a canonical isomorphism

`det(E') ⊗_{O_X} det(E'') ≅ det(E)`

of the determinants of [Stacks, Tag 0FJN] — the annihilator of the degree-one part of the
exterior algebra.

The underlying map is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.determinantTensorDeterminantHom`, which
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.detSummandComparison_ι_unit_wedge` pins to the wedge-and-lift
formula the source gives for it, which the uniqueness statements
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.eq_determinantTensorDeterminantHom` and
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.eq_detTensorAnnComparison` show that formula determines, and
which `Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.isIso_determinantTensorDeterminantHom` shows is an
isomorphism.

No hypothesis on `E` is needed: the freeness of its stalks is derived from the split stalk
sequence, so the statement is a strengthening of the one in the source, which assumes all three
terms finite locally free.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def determinantTensorDeterminantIsoOfFiniteLocallyFree
    (hS : (ShortComplex.mk f g hfg).Exact) [Mono f] [Epi g]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E']
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E''] :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor Osharp).obj A'.determinant).obj A''.determinant ≅
        A.determinant
declarations.comment: the canonical isomorphism det(E')⊗det(E'')≅det(E) in the GENERAL case, with NO constant-rank hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.determinantTensorDeterminantHom
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map `det(E') ⊗ det(E'') ⟶ det(E)` of [Stacks, Tag 0B38], for a short exact
sequence `0 → E' → E → E'' → 0` of sheaves of modules on a ringed space with `E'` and `E''`
finite locally free of NO PARTICULAR RANK.**

The determinant of [Stacks, Tag 0FJN] is the coproduct over the degrees of the degreewise
annihilators of the degree-one part of the exterior algebra, and the tensor product of sheaves of
modules preserves coproducts in each variable, so a map out of `det(E') ⊗ det(E'')` is the same
thing as a family of maps `det(E')ₙ ⊗ det(E'')ₘ ⟶ det(E)`. This is the family obtained from
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.detSummandComparison` followed by the inclusion of the
degree-`n+m` summand of `det(E)`.

That this map is an isomorphism is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.isIso_determinantTensorDeterminantHom`, the isomorphism itself is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.determinantTensorDeterminantIsoOfFiniteLocallyFree`, and the
wedge-and-lift formula pinning it is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.detSummandComparison_ι_unit_wedge` — all three in
`StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.ExteriorAnnihilatorShortExactIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def determinantTensorDeterminantHom [Mono f] [Epi g]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E']
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E''] :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor Osharp).obj A'.determinant).obj A''.determinant ⟶
        A.determinant
declarations.comment: the canonical MAP det(E')⊗det(E'')⟶det(E) in the GENERAL case, with NO constant-rank hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.determinantTensorDeterminantIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B38 in determinant form, at constant rank.** For a short exact sequence
`0 → E' → E → E'' → 0` of sheaves of modules on a ringed space, with `E'`, `E''` and `E` finite
locally free of constant ranks `r'`, `k + 1` and `r' + k + 1`, there is a canonical isomorphism
`det(E') ⊗ det(E'') ≅ det(E)` of the determinants of [Stacks, Tag 0FJN] — the annihilator of the
degree-one part of the exterior algebra.

It is the comparison of top exterior powers of
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.detComparison`, which
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.isIso_detComparison` shows is an isomorphism, conjugated by the
identifications `⋀ʳ F ≅ det(F)` of [Stacks, Tag 0B37]. The map is pinned by
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.determinantTensorDeterminantIso_hom` to that top-exterior-power
comparison, which `Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.detComparison_wedge` in turn pins to the
wedge-and-lift formula of the source.

This is the CONSTANT-RANK form of the tag. The general case, where the ranks are only locally
constant, is carried by
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.determinantTensorDeterminantIsoOfFiniteLocallyFree` in
`StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.ExteriorAnnihilatorShortExactIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def determinantTensorDeterminantIso
    (A' : _root_.SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥X) E')
    (A : _root_.SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥X) E)
    (A'' : _root_.SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥X) E'')
    (f : E' ⟶ E) (g : E ⟶ E'') (hfg : f ≫ g = 0)
    (hS : (ShortComplex.mk f g hfg).Exact) [Mono f] [Epi g] (r' k : ℕ)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E' r']
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E'' (k + 1)]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E (r' + (k + 1))] :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor Osharp).obj A'.determinant).obj A''.determinant ≅
        A.determinant
declarations.comment: the canonical isomorphism det(E')⊗det(E'')≅det(E) in DETERMINANT form, for a short exact sequence of finite locally free sheaves of CONSTANT rank

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.detComparison_wedge
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B38, the wedge-and-lift formula.** The canonical comparison carries the image of
`(s₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ s_{r'}) ⊗ (g(l₁) ∧ ⋯ ∧ g(l_{k+1}))` to
`f(s₁) ∧ ⋯ ∧ f(s_{r'}) ∧ l₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ l_{k+1}`: the wedge of the images of the sections of `E'` with
**arbitrary local lifts** `lⱼ` of the sections of `E''`. This equation is the one the source
gives for its canonical map, and it determines the comparison, since the wedges of local
sections generate the exterior powers locally.

Here `det` is the top exterior power, which
`SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras.determinantIsoExteriorPower` identifies with the
`det` of [Stacks, Tag 0FJN] at constant rank; what is carried here is `E'` of constant rank `r'`
and `E''` of constant rank `r'' = k + 1`. The ISOMORPHISM clause of the tag is carried separately
by `Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.isIso_detComparison`.

This is the CONSTANT-RANK form of the tag. The general case — a short exact sequence of finite
locally free sheaves with no constant-rank hypothesis — is carried by
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.detSummandComparison_ι_unit_wedge` and
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.determinantTensorDeterminantIsoOfFiniteLocallyFree` in
`StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.ExteriorAnnihilatorShortExactIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem detComparison_wedge [Epi g]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E' r']
    (V : (Opens ↥X)ᵒᵖ) (s : Fin r' → E'.val.obj V) (l : Fin (k + 1) → E.val.obj V) :
    (detComparison A' A A'' f g hfg hS r' k).val.app V
        ((PresheafOfModules.tensorSheafUnit (A'.exteriorPower r')
            (A''.exteriorPower (k + 1))).app V
          (wedgeSec A' V r' s ⊗ₜ wedgeSec A'' V (k + 1) fun i => g.val.app V (l i))) =
      wedgeSec A V (r' + (k + 1)) (Fin.append (fun i => f.val.app V (s i)) l)
declarations.comment: the CONSTANT-RANK form of the canonical map det(E')⊗det(E'')⟶det(E) and of its wedge-and-lift formula

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.eq_detComparison
declarations.doc:
**The canonical comparison is the only morphism satisfying its defining equation.** The
morphism `⋀ʳ' E' ⊗ ⋀ᵏ⁺¹(g)` is an epimorphism, so a morphism out of `⋀ʳ' E' ⊗ ⋀ᵏ⁺¹ E''` is
determined by its composite with it.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_detComparison [Epi g]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E' r']
    (ψ : ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{_, _, _, u, u} Osharp).obj (A'.exteriorPower
        r')).obj
        (A''.exteriorPower (k + 1)) ⟶
      A.exteriorPower (r' + (k + 1)))
    (hψ : ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{_, _, _, u, u} Osharp).obj
      (A'.exteriorPower r')).map ((extHom A A'' g).app ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ)) ≫ ψ =
      wedgeHom A' A f r' (k + 1)) :
    ψ = detComparison A' A A'' f g hfg hS r' k
declarations.comment: uniqueness of the map satisfying the wedge-and-lift formula, which is the precise sense of CANONICAL here — again in the constant-rank form, with the same carried hypotheses as `detComparison_wedge`; the isomorphism clause is carried by `Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.isIso_detComparison`, and the general case by `Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.eq_determinantTensorDeterminantHom`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.isIso_detComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B38, the isomorphism clause in the constant-rank form.** For a short exact
sequence `0 → E' → E → E'' → 0` of sheaves of modules on a ringed space with `E'` finite
locally free of constant rank `r'` and `E''` finite locally free of constant rank `k + 1`, the
canonical comparison `⋀^{r'} E' ⊗ ⋀^{k+1} E'' ⟶ ⋀^{r'+k+1} E` is an isomorphism.

The canonical map `det(E') ⊗ det(E'') ⟶ det(E)` shown invertible here is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.detComparison`. Here `det` is the top exterior power, identified
with the `det` of [Stacks, Tag 0FJN] at constant rank by
`SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras.determinantIsoExteriorPower`; what is carried
here is `E'` of constant rank `r'` and `E''` of constant rank `r'' = k + 1`.

This is the CONSTANT-RANK form of the tag. The general case — a short exact sequence of finite
locally free sheaves with no constant-rank hypothesis — is carried by
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.isIso_determinantTensorDeterminantHom` and
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TopWedge.determinantTensorDeterminantIsoOfFiniteLocallyFree` in
`StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.ExteriorAnnihilatorShortExactIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_detComparison
    (A' : _root_.SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥X) E')
    (A : _root_.SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥X) E)
    (A'' : _root_.SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥X) E'')
    (f : E' ⟶ E) (g : E ⟶ E'') (hfg : f ≫ g = 0)
    (hS : (ShortComplex.mk f g hfg).Exact) [Mono f] [Epi g] (r' k : ℕ)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E' r']
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E'' (k + 1)] :
    IsIso (detComparison A' A A'' f g hfg hS r' k)
declarations.comment: the ISOMORPHISM clause, in the constant-rank form

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SpaceModules.extOneEquivFirstCohomologyCanonical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B3A.** For a ringed space `(X, O_X)` and a sheaf of `O_X`-modules `F`, the
canonical bijection `Ext^1_{Mod(O_X)}(O_X, F) → H^1(X, F)`, an isomorphism of abelian groups.
declarations.statement:
def extOneEquivFirstCohomologyCanonical (M : SheafOfModules.{u} R) :
    Abelian.Ext (SheafOfModules.unit R) M 1 ≃+ Hgroup R ⊤ 1 M
declarations.comment: the canonical bijection, as an isomorphism of abelian groups

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SpaceModules.extOneEquivFirstCohomologyCanonical_extClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B3A.** The canonical bijection sends the class of the extension
`0 → F → E → O_X → 0` to the image of `1 ∈ Γ(X, O_X)` under the boundary map
`H^0(X, O_X) → H^1(X, F)` of the long exact cohomology sequence of the extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem extOneEquivFirstCohomologyCanonical_extClass (M E : SheafOfModules.{u} R) (f : M ⟶ E)
    (g : E ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit R) (w : f ≫ g = 0)
    (hS : (ShortComplex.mk f g w).ShortExact) :
    extOneEquivFirstCohomologyCanonical R M hS.extClass =
      (DerivedIndexing.rightDerivedDeltaFunctorOfEnoughInjectives (secF R ⊤)).δ hS 0
        (oneCohomologyClass R)
declarations.comment: image of an extension: the boundary of `1` in the long exact cohomology sequence

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SpaceModules.extOneEquivFirstCohomologyCanonical_unique
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0B3A.** The boundary formula determines the canonical bijection uniquely.
declarations.statement:
theorem extOneEquivFirstCohomologyCanonical_unique (M : SheafOfModules.{u} R)
    (e : Abelian.Ext (SheafOfModules.unit R) M 1 ≃+ Hgroup R ⊤ 1 M)
    (he : ∀ (E : SheafOfModules.{u} R) (f : M ⟶ E)
      (g : E ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit R) (w : f ≫ g = 0)
      (hS : (ShortComplex.mk f g w).ShortExact),
      e hS.extClass =
        (DerivedIndexing.rightDerivedDeltaFunctorOfEnoughInjectives (secF R ⊤)).δ hS 0
          (oneCohomologyClass R)) :
    e = extOneEquivFirstCohomologyCanonical R M
declarations.comment: uniqueness: the boundary formula determines the bijection

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SpaceModules.extOneEquivFirstCohomologyCanonical_naturality
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0B3A.** The canonical bijection is natural in the coefficient module sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem extOneEquivFirstCohomologyCanonical_naturality {M N : SheafOfModules.{u} R}
    (f : M ⟶ N) (e : Abelian.Ext (SheafOfModules.unit R) M 1) :
    extOneEquivFirstCohomologyCanonical R N
        ((Abelian.Ext.mk₀ f).postcomp (SheafOfModules.unit R) (Nat.add_zero 1) e) =
      (Hfunctor R ⊤ 1).map f (extOneEquivFirstCohomologyCanonical R M e)
declarations.comment: naturality in the coefficient module sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.kernelTensorGeneratingSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B3B.** Let `L` be an invertible sheaf of modules on a locally ringed space, let
`s : I → Γ(X, L)` be global sections generating `L`, and let `F` be the kernel of the induced map
`O_X^{⊕I} ⟶ L`. Then `F ⊗ L` is generated by global sections, by the Koszul sections
`e_i ⊗ s_j − e_j ⊗ s_i`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def kernelTensorGeneratingSections (g : L.GeneratingSections) :
    ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u}
        (⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩ : Sheaf (JX X) CommRingCat.{u})).obj ((kernel g.π))).obj
        (L))).GeneratingSections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRegular_iff_forall_isRegularInCodimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B3C.** A locally Noetherian scheme is regular if and only if it is
regular in codimension `k` for every nonnegative integer `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegular_iff_forall_isRegularInCodimension (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] :
    IsRegular X ↔ ∀ k : ℕ, IsRegularInCodimension X k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCohenMacaulay_of_isNormal_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B3D.** A locally Noetherian normal scheme of dimension at most two is
Cohen–Macaulay.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCohenMacaulay_of_isNormal_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_two (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsNormal X] (hX : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 2) :
    IsCohenMacaulay X

declarations.name: Stacks.AmplePullbackCovering.isAmple_modulePullback_of_immersion_or_isEmbedding
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0B3E.** For `L` an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module and `i : X' ⟶ X` a
quasi-compact immersion, an immersion of a quasi-compact scheme, a quasi-compact homeomorphism
onto its image, or a homeomorphism onto its image out of a quasi-compact scheme, the pullback
`i^* L` is ample on `X'`.

The proof is `Stacks.SectionExtension.isAmple_pullbackModule`; see the module documentation for
why the attribute sits here rather than there.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_modulePullback_of_immersion_or_isEmbedding {X X' : Scheme.{u}} (i : X' ⟶ X)
    (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L] (hL : IsAmple X L)
    (hi : (QuasiCompact i ∧ IsImmersion i) ∨ (CompactSpace X' ∧ IsImmersion i) ∨
      (QuasiCompact i ∧ Topology.IsEmbedding i) ∨
      (CompactSpace X' ∧ Topology.IsEmbedding i)) :
    IsAmple X' (Stacks.AmpleLocallyClosed.pullbackModule i L)

declarations.name: Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.isRelativelyVeryAmple_pullback_fst
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0B3F: relative very ampleness is preserved by base change.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be
a morphism of schemes, `L` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module which is very ample relative to `f`, and
`g : S' ⟶ S` a morphism of schemes. Then the pullback of `L` to `S' ×_S X` is very ample relative
to the projection `S' ×_S X ⟶ S'`.

The proof is the source's. Relative very ampleness gives a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `E`, an
immersion `i : X ⟶ 𝐏(E)` over `S` and an isomorphism `L ≅ i^* 𝒪_{𝐏(E)}(1)`. The module `g^* E` is
quasi-coherent (Tag 01BG), its projective bundle is the base change of `𝐏(E)` and the comparison
morphism `b` pulls the twist back to the twist (Tag 01O3,
`Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.projectiveBundleTwistBaseChange`), so the morphism `i'` induced by
`S' ×_S X ⟶ X ⟶ 𝐏(E)` and `S' ×_S X ⟶ S'` is a base change of `i`, hence an immersion
(Tag 01JY), it lies over `S'`, and the pullback of `L` is `i'^* 𝒪_{𝐏(g^* E)}(1)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyVeryAmple_pullback_fst {X S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S)
    (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L] (hL : IsRelativelyVeryAmple f L) :
    IsRelativelyVeryAmple (pullback.fst g f)
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.snd g f)).obj L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsQuasiProjective.of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B3G].** A base change of a quasi-projective morphism is quasi-projective: if
`f' : X' ⟶ S'` fits into a cartesian square over a quasi-projective `f : X ⟶ S`, then `f'` is
quasi-projective.

Finite type is stable under base change, which is the finite-type half of [Stacks, Tag 01T4],
and the pullback along `X' ⟶ X` of a sheaf ample relative to `f` is ample relative to `f'`,
which is [Stacks, Tag 0893] in the form `Stacks.AmpleBridge.relativelyAmpleBaseChange`.

declarations.name: Stacks.HProjective.isQuasiProjective_of_isQuasiAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0B3H.** A quasi-affine morphism of finite type is quasi-projective: the
structure sheaf `𝒪_X` is ample relative to a quasi-affine morphism by [Stacks, Tag 0891].

Finite type is the conjunction of local finite type and quasi-compactness, as in Tag 01T1, and
quasi-compactness is already a consequence of quasi-affineness, so only the local finite type
half is a hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiProjective_of_isQuasiAffineHom {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsQuasiAffineHom f] (hf : LocallyOfFiniteType f) : IsQuasiProjective f

declarations.name: Stacks.FiniteMorphismProjective.isProjective_of_isFinite
declarations.doc:
**A finite morphism is projective.** For a finite `f : X ⟶ S` over an arbitrary base scheme,
`X` is, over `S`, a closed subscheme of the projective bundle `𝐏(f_*𝒪_X)` of a quasi-coherent
module of finite type.

The module is `f_*𝒪_X`, quasi-coherent by Tag 01SA and of finite type by Tag 01PB, and the closed
immersion is `Stacks.FiniteMorphismProjective.embedding`, which is a morphism over the base by
`Stacks.FiniteMorphismProjective.embedding_comp_toBase` and a closed immersion by
`Stacks.FiniteMorphismProjective.isClosedImmersion_embedding`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isProjective_of_isFinite {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsFinite f] :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_generatingSections_of_support_dim_le_zero
declarations.doc:
A coherent sheaf with support of dimension at most zero on a locally Noetherian
scheme is generated by global sections.

This is also clause (1) of Stacks 0AYT, in a form more general than that clause states it: Stacks
0AYT takes `X` proper over a field `k`, which gives `IsLocallyNoetherian X` through
`LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian`, so the condition here is strictly weaker than the
clause's and the clause follows by instantiation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_generatingSections_of_support_dim_le_zero
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hF : topologicalKrullDim (SheafOfModules.supp F) ≤ 0) :
    Nonempty F.GeneratingSections
declarations.comment: global_generation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_hgroup_top_of_support_dim_le_zero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B3J], the vanishing clause.** For `X` a locally Noetherian scheme and `ℱ` a
coherent `𝒪_X`-module whose support has dimension at most zero, `Hⁱ(X, ℱ) = 0` for every
`i > 0`.

The global generation clause of the same tag is
`AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_generatingSections_of_support_dim_le_zero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_hgroup_top_of_support_dim_le_zero
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hF : topologicalKrullDim (SheafOfModules.supp F) ≤ 0)
    (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    IsZero (Hgroup X.ringCatSheaf ⊤ i F)
declarations.comment: vanishing

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.sheafIsCohenMacaulay_and_supp_eq_univ_iff_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B3K.** Let `X` be a regular scheme and `F` a coherent
`𝒪_X`-module. Then `F` is Cohen–Macaulay with support all of `X` if and only if it is finite
locally free of positive rank at every point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem sheafIsCohenMacaulay_and_supp_eq_univ_iff_isFiniteLocallyFree
    (hX : IsRegular X) (F : X.Modules) [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] :
    (SheafIsCohenMacaulay X F ∧ _root_.SheafOfModules.supp F = Set.univ) ↔
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) F ∧
        ∀ x : X, 0 < Scheme.Modules.fiberRank F x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.restriction_injective_of_associatedPoints_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B3L.** Restriction of sections of a quasi-coherent sheaf on a locally
Noetherian scheme to an open subset containing all associated points is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem restriction_injective_of_associatedPoints_subset (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (U : X.Opens)
    (hU : Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints F ⊆ (U : Set X)) :
    Function.Injective (F.presheaf.map (homOfLE (show U ≤ (⊤ : X.Opens) from le_top)).op)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.restriction_injective_of_weaklyAssociatedPoints_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B3M.** Restriction of sections of a quasi-coherent module to an open
containing all its weakly associated points is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem restriction_injective_of_weaklyAssociatedPoints_subset {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] (U : X.Opens)
    (hU : Stacks.Divisors.weaklyAssociatedPoints F ⊆ U) :
    Function.Injective (F.presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top : U ⟶ ⊤).op)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReflexive_iff_isFiniteLocallyFree_of_isRegular_of_dim_le_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B3N.** A coherent module on a regular scheme of dimension at most
two is reflexive precisely when it is finite locally free.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReflexive_iff_isFiniteLocallyFree_of_isRegular_of_dim_le_two (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hX : IsRegular X) (hXdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 2) (F : X.Modules)
    [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] :
    IsReflexive F ↔ SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree (R := X.ringCatSheaf) F

declarations.name: Stacks.CartierConormal.conormalSheafIsoNegativeTwist
declarations.doc:
For an ideal sheaf datum `D` on a scheme `X`, the conormal sheaf of the closed immersion
`D.subschemeι` is the restriction to the subscheme of the ideal sheaf `ℐ_D`, that is, of
`𝒪_X(-D)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalSheafIsoNegativeTwist {X : Scheme.{u}} (D : X.IdealSheafData) :
    Stacks.Conormal.conormalSheaf D.subschemeι ≅
      (modulePullback D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        (Stacks.ClosedImmersion.idealSheaf D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom)
declarations.comment: conormal sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.conormalSheafIsoNegativeTwist_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B3P**, the canonical-ideal-quotient clause: on an affine open `U` of
`X` carrying an affine model `D ∩ U = Spec (Γ(X, U) ⧸ I)` of the closed subscheme `D`, the affine
computation of the conormal sheaf of `D` sends the image of a section `x` of `ℐ_D` over `U` —
pulled back to `D` by the unit of the adjunction and read on the conormal sheaf through
`Stacks.Divisors.conormalSheafIsoNegativeTwist` — to the class of `x` modulo `I²`.

The sheaf `𝒪_X(-D)` of Tag 01WX is the ideal sheaf `ℐ_D` itself, so this is the normalisation of
both of Tag 0B3P's descriptions of the conormal sheaf at once.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalSheafIsoNegativeTwist_apply {X : Scheme.{u}} (D : X.IdealSheafData)
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (I : Ideal Γ(X, U))
    (e : Limits.pullback D.subschemeι U.ι ≅ Spec (.of (Γ(X, U) ⧸ I)))
    (he : Limits.pullback.snd D.subschemeι U.ι ≫ hU.isoSpec.hom =
      e.hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)))
    (x : (Stacks.ClosedImmersion.idealSheaf D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom).val.obj (op U))
    (hx : (kernel.ι (SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit
      (structureSheafHom D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom))).val.app (op U) x ∈ I) :
    (Stacks.Conormal.affineConormalIsoCotangent D.subschemeι U hU I e he).hom.hom
        ((conormalSheafIsoNegativeTwist D).inv.val.app
          (op ((opensMap D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj U))
          (((modulePullbackPushforwardAdjunction D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom).unit.app
            (Stacks.ClosedImmersion.idealSheaf
              D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom)).val.app (op U) x))
      = I.toCotangent ⟨(kernel.ι (SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit
          (structureSheafHom D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom))).val.app (op U) x, hx⟩
declarations.comment: canonical ideal quotient

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.conormalSheafIsoNegativeTwist
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B3P**, the conormal-sheaf clause: the conormal sheaf of a closed
subscheme `D ⊆ X` is the restriction `ℐ_D|_D = 𝒪_X(-D)|_D` of its ideal sheaf.

The conormal sheaf of Tag 01R2 is computed through the `liftCoborder` factorization of the
immersion; for a closed immersion the open through which it factors is the whole target
(`coborderRange_eq_top`) and its open immersion is an isomorphism
(`isIso_coborderRange_ι`), so `Stacks.ClosedImmersion.pullbackIdealSheafIso` identifies the two
pullbacks. The sheaf `𝒪_X(-D)` of Tag 01WX is the ideal sheaf itself, so the right-hand side is
both descriptions at once.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalSheafIsoNegativeTwist {X : Scheme.{u}} (D : X.IdealSheafData) :
    (modulePullback D.subschemeι.liftCoborder.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        (Stacks.ClosedImmersion.idealSheaf
          D.subschemeι.liftCoborder.toLRSHom.toShHom) ≅
      (modulePullback D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        (Stacks.ClosedImmersion.idealSheaf D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom)
declarations.comment: conormal sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.normalSheafIsoInvertibleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B3P**, the normal-sheaf clause: the normal sheaf of an effective
Cartier divisor `D ⊆ X` is the restriction `𝒪_X(D)|_D` of its associated invertible sheaf
`𝒪_X(D) = SheafHom(ℐ_D, 𝒪_X)`.

There is no hypothesis beyond the divisor. The stalk formula of Tag 0098 for `modulePullback`
along the closed immersion of `D`, which used to be carried here as
`Stacks.RingedSpace.PullbackStalkFormula`, is a theorem
(`Stacks.RingedSpace.pullbackStalkFormula`), so Tag 01CD is available outright as
`Stacks.RingedSpace.isIso_comparison`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def normalSheafIsoInvertibleSheaf {X : Scheme.{u}} (D : X.IdealSheafData)
    [IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D] :
    normalSheaf D.subschemeι ≅
      (modulePullback D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.dualSheaf X.sheaf.obj (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property
          (Stacks.ClosedImmersion.idealSheaf D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom))
declarations.comment: normal sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.normalSheafIsoInvertibleSheaf_eval
declarations.doc:
Let `φ` be a section of `𝒪_X(D) = ℐ_D^∨` over `U` and `x` a section of `𝒪_X(-D) = ℐ_D` over
`U`, both carried to `D` by the unit of `f^* ⊣ f_*` for the closed immersion `f` of `D`. The
functional which `Stacks.Divisors.normalSheafIsoInvertibleSheaf` produces from `φ` on the
conormal sheaf takes the image of `x` to the restriction of `φ(x)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem normalSheafIsoInvertibleSheaf_eval {X : Scheme.{u}} (D : X.IdealSheafData)
    [IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D] (U : Opens X)
    (φ : (dualSheaf X.sheaf.obj (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property
      (Stacks.ClosedImmersion.idealSheaf D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom)).val.obj (op U))
    (x : (Stacks.ClosedImmersion.idealSheaf
      D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom).val.obj (op U)) :
    evalSection D.subscheme.sheaf.obj
        ((modulePullback D.subschemeι.liftCoborder.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
          (Stacks.ClosedImmersion.idealSheaf
            D.subschemeι.liftCoborder.toLRSHom.toShHom)).val
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf
          D.subscheme.sheaf.obj
          (structureSheafRing D.subscheme.toRingedSpace).property)).val
        (op ((opensMap D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj U))
        ((normalSheafIsoInvertibleSheaf D).inv.val.app
          (op ((opensMap D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj U))
          (((modulePullbackPushforwardAdjunction
              D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom).unit.app
            (dualSheaf X.sheaf.obj (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property
              (Stacks.ClosedImmersion.idealSheaf
                D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom))).val.app (op U) φ))
        ((conormalSheafIsoNegativeTwist D).inv.val.app
          (op ((opensMap D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj U))
          (((modulePullbackPushforwardAdjunction
              D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom).unit.app
            (Stacks.ClosedImmersion.idealSheaf
              D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom)).val.app (op U) x)) =
      ((structureSheafHom D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom).hom.app (op U)).hom
        (evalSection X.sheaf.obj
          (Stacks.ClosedImmersion.idealSheaf D.subschemeι.toLRSHom.toShHom).val
          (_root_.SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf
            X.sheaf.obj
            (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property)).val (op U) φ x)
declarations.comment: canonical evaluation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_hasPropertySk
declarations.doc:
An effective Cartier divisor of an `(Sₖ)` locally Noetherian scheme is
`(Sₖ₋₁)` for `k ≥ 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_hasPropertySk
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (hI : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hX : HasPropertySk X k) :
    @HasPropertySk I.subscheme
      (LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian I.subschemeι) (k - 1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isNormal_effectiveCartierDivisor_hasPropertySk_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B3S.**  An effective Cartier divisor on a locally Noetherian normal
scheme satisfies Serre's condition `(S₁)`: the scheme satisfies `(S₂)` by Serre's criterion, and
Tag 0B3R drops the index by one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNormal_effectiveCartierDivisor_hasPropertySk_one (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsNormal X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian I.subscheme :=
      LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian I.subschemeι
    HasPropertySk I.subscheme 1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_reflexiveHull_exteriorPower_iso_tensor_cartier
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B3T.**  In a right-exact sequence of coherent modules of generic
rank `r` on an integral regular scheme of dimension at most two, whose quotient is the direct
image of a module of rank `s` finite locally free on an integral effective Cartier divisor
`D`, the determinant line bundles of the first two terms differ by at most `min s r` copies
of `D`.

The cokernel of the stalk map at the generic point of `D` is `κ ^ s` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.linearEquiv_quotient_range_stalkHom_fin`, which is the one hypothesis of
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_pow_le_min_tensorIso_detMap_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor` still
open.  Local Noetherianness, all the proof needs, comes from regularity.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_reflexiveHull_exteriorPower_iso_tensor_cartier (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsIntegral X] (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular X)
    (hXdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 2)
    (D : X.IdealSheafData) (hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D)
    [IsIntegral D.subscheme]
    (G : D.subscheme.Modules) (s : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} G s]
    (S : ShortComplex X.Modules) [S.X₁.IsCoherent] [S.X₂.IsCoherent]
    (hS : S.Exact) [Epi S.g]
    (hquot : S.X₃ ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pushforward D.subschemeι).obj G)
    (r : ℕ) (U : X.Opens) (hU : ∃ x : X, x ∈ U)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} (S.X₁.over U) r]
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} (S.X₂.over U) r] :
    ∃ k : ℕ, k ≤ min s r ∧ Nonempty ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
      ⟨X.sheaf.obj, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (X.sheaf.obj) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
        (X.ringCatSheaf.property)⟩).obj ((Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf' (D ^ k)))).obj
          ((reflexiveHull (exteriorPower S.X₁ (r : ℤ))))) ≅
      reflexiveHull (exteriorPower S.X₂ (r : ℤ)))
declarations.comment: bounded Cartier twist

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isInvertible_reflexiveHull_exteriorPower_of_genericRank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B3T.**  The reflexive hull `(⋀^r F)^∨∨` of the top exterior power
of a coherent module of generic rank `r` on an integral regular scheme of dimension at most
two is a line bundle.

Generic rank `r` is finite local freeness of rank `r` of `F` on the slice site over a nonempty
open `U`.  The hull is coherent and reflexive, hence finite locally free by Tag 0B3N, and on
the irreducible space of an integral scheme its fibre rank is constant; over `U` the exterior
power `⋀^r F` is finite locally free of rank `binom(r, r) = 1` with free stalks, and the hull
preserves the fibre rank there, so that constant is one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_reflexiveHull_exteriorPower_of_genericRank
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular X)
    (hXdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 2)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (r : ℕ) (U : X.Opens) (hU : ∃ x : X, x ∈ U)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} (F.over U) r] :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property
      (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveModules.reflexiveHull
        (Scheme.Modules.exteriorPower F r))
