declarations.comment: invertibility of the determinant line bundles

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProjective_relativeProj_toBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B3U.** Let `S` be a scheme and `𝒜` a quasi-coherent graded
`𝒪_S`-algebra generated by `𝒜_1` over `𝒜_0` with `𝒜_1` of finite type. Then the projection
`Proj_S(𝒜) ⟶ S` is projective.

The source's proof: the canonical graded-algebra map `Sym(𝒜_1) ⟶ 𝒜` induces a closed immersion
`Proj_S(𝒜) ⟶ 𝐏(𝒜_1)` over `S` by Stacks Tag 07ZK (2), and `𝐏(𝒜_1)` is the projective bundle of a
quasi-coherent module of finite type, so that closed immersion is exactly the condition of Stacks
Tag 01W8.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProjective_relativeProj_toBase {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (A : Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjBridge.SheafGradedAlgebra.{u} S)
    (hgen : Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjRepresentsF1.IsGeneratedInDegreeOne A)
    (hfin : (A.piece 1).IsFiniteType) :
    IsProjective (relativeProj A).toBase

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeProj.isClosedImmersion_of_section_projectiveBundleToBase
declarations.doc:
**A section of the projection of a projective bundle is a closed immersion.** Since
`π : 𝐏(F) ⟶ X` is separated (Tag 01O2) and `σ ≫ π = 𝟙 X` is an isomorphism, `σ` is a closed
immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_of_section_projectiveBundleToBase (X : Scheme.{u}) (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] (σ : X ⟶ projectiveBundle X F)
    (hσ : σ ≫ projectiveBundleToBase X F = 𝟙 X) : IsClosedImmersion σ
declarations.comment: closed immersion

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeProj.sectionOfInvertibleQuotient
declarations.doc:
**A surjection `q : E ⟶ ℒ` onto an invertible `𝒪_X`-module determines a section of
`π : 𝐏(E) ⟶ X`.** This is the direction of Tag 0B3V's bijection that produces a section: `q`
determines a unital homomorphism `(𝟙_X)^*Sym(E) ⟶ ⨁_n ℒ^{⊗ n}` of sheaves of graded algebras
whose degree-one component is surjective — a quadruple of Section 01NS of degree one over
`𝟙_X` — and the representability of the functor of quadruples classifies that quadruple by a
morphism `X ⟶ 𝐏(E)` over `X`.
declarations.statement: def sectionOfInvertibleQuotient [Epi q] : X ⟶ projectiveBundle X E
declarations.comment: from an invertible quotient to a section: the construction

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeProj.sectionOfInvertibleQuotient_comp_projectiveBundleToBase
declarations.doc: **The morphism of `sectionOfInvertibleQuotient` is a section of `π : 𝐏(E) ⟶ X`.**
declarations.statement:
theorem sectionOfInvertibleQuotient_comp_projectiveBundleToBase [Epi q] :
    sectionOfInvertibleQuotient X E L q ≫ projectiveBundleToBase X E = 𝟙 X
declarations.comment: from an invertible quotient to a section: it is a section of the projection

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeProj.exists_iso_of_sectionOfInvertibleQuotient_eq
declarations.doc:
**Two surjections onto invertible modules determining the same section of `π` differ by an
isomorphism of their targets.** This is the injectivity of Tag 0B3V's map from invertible
quotients to sections: the two quadruples are strictly equivalent, which gives an isomorphism
`β : ℒ ≅ ℒ'` carrying one twisting to the other, and in degree one that equation — precomposed
with the pullback of the degree-one generator of `Sym(E)` and postcomposed with the
identification `(ℒ')^{⊗ 1} ≅ ℒ'` — is `q ≫ β = q'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_of_sectionOfInvertibleQuotient_eq [Epi q]
    (L' : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureRingSheaf X.toRingedSpace))
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.toRingedSpace.presheaf (isSheafStruct X) L']
    (q' : E ⟶ L') [Epi q']
    (h : sectionOfInvertibleQuotient X E L q = sectionOfInvertibleQuotient X E L' q') :
    ∃ α : L ≅ L', q ≫ α.hom = q'
declarations.comment: from an invertible quotient to a section: the map is injective, i.e. a section determines the invertible quotient it comes from up to isomorphism of the quotient module

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeProj.projectiveBundle_sections_classification
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B3V].** Let `X` be a scheme, `ℰ` a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and
`π : 𝐏(ℰ) ⟶ X` its projective bundle (`projectiveBundle`, `projectiveBundleToBase`), with
tautological quotient `π^*ℰ ⟶ 𝒪(1)` (`tautologicalDatum ℰ`). Then:

1. **the bijection**: `projectiveBundleSectionsEquiv` is a bijection from the sections `σ` of `π`
   onto the invertible quotients `q : ℰ → 𝓛` up to isomorphism, sending `σ` to the class of
   `σ^*` of the tautological quotient — `σ` goes to the class of `q` exactly when there is
   `e : σ^*𝒪(1) ≅ 𝓛` carrying `σ^*` of the tautological quotient to `q`;
2. every section `σ` is a closed immersion;
3. **the canonical isomorphism** `projectiveBundleConormalIso : Ker(q) ⊗ 𝓛^{⊗ -1} ≅ 𝒞_{σ(X)/𝐏(ℰ)}`
   for `σ` matched with `q` through `e`, whose underlying map is the canonical map
   `Stacks.ProjectiveBundleConormal.conormalCanonicalMap` (locally `k ⊗ s^{-1} ↦ k/s`) read
   through the base-change map of conormal sheaves along the presentation comparison
   `bundlePresentationIso` of `𝐏(ℰ)`;
4. **compatibility with base change** along any morphism `g : X' ⟶ X`, for sections lying over
   each other along `projectiveBundleBaseChange`: the bijection sends `σ'` to the base change
   `Stacks.ProjectiveBundleQuotients.baseChangeClass` of the class of `σ`; and the square formed
   by `g^*` of the canonical isomorphism at `σ`, the canonical isomorphism at `σ'`, the base
   change `Stacks.Divisors.conormalSourceBaseChange` of the source and the base-change map
   `Stacks.Conormal.conormalBaseChangeMap` of conormal sheaves commutes.

No hypothesis is placed on `X`, `X'`, `g`, or on `ℰ` beyond quasi-coherence.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectiveBundle_sections_classification :
    (∀ (σ : X ⟶ projectiveBundle X E) (hσ : σ ≫ projectiveBundleToBase X E = 𝟙 X)
        (Q : Stacks.Divisors.InvertibleQuotient X E),
      projectiveBundleSectionsEquiv ⟨σ, hσ⟩ =
          Quotient.mk (Stacks.Divisors.invertibleQuotientSetoid X E) Q ↔
        ∃ e : (Scheme.Modules.pullback σ).obj (tautologicalDatum E).twist ≅ Q.L,
          (tautologicalDatum E).pullbackQuotientMap σ hσ ≫ e.hom = Q.q) ∧
    (∀ (σ : X ⟶ projectiveBundle X E), σ ≫ projectiveBundleToBase X E = 𝟙 X →
      IsClosedImmersion σ) ∧
    (∀ (Q : Stacks.Divisors.InvertibleQuotient X E) (σ : X ⟶ projectiveBundle X E)
        (hσ : σ ≫ projectiveBundleToBase X E = 𝟙 X)
        (e : (Scheme.Modules.pullback σ).obj (tautologicalDatum E).twist ≅ Q.L)
        (hqe : (tautologicalDatum E).pullbackQuotientMap σ hσ ≫ e.hom = Q.q),
      haveI := isClosedImmersion_of_section_projectiveBundleToBase X E σ hσ
      (projectiveBundleConormalIso E Q hσ e hqe).hom =
        conormalCanonicalMap E Q (presentationSection_comp_toBase E σ hσ)
            (presentationClassifyingIso E Q e)
            (sectionQuotientMap_comp_presentationClassifyingIso E Q hσ e hqe) ≫
          (Scheme.Modules.pullbackId X).inv.app _ ≫
            Stacks.Conormal.conormalBaseChangeMap (presentationSection_square E σ)) ∧
    (∀ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (g : X' ⟶ X) (σ : X ⟶ projectiveBundle X E)
        (hσ : σ ≫ projectiveBundleToBase X E = 𝟙 X)
        (σ' : X' ⟶ projectiveBundle X' ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj E))
        (hσ' : σ' ≫ projectiveBundleToBase X' ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj E) = 𝟙 X'),
        σ' ≫ projectiveBundleBaseChange g E _ (Iso.refl _) = g ≫ σ →
      projectiveBundleSectionsEquiv ⟨σ', hσ'⟩ =
        Stacks.ProjectiveBundleQuotients.baseChangeClass g (Iso.refl _)
          (projectiveBundleSectionsEquiv ⟨σ, hσ⟩)) ∧
    (∀ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (g : X' ⟶ X) (E' : X'.Modules) [E'.IsQuasicoherent]
        (hE : E' ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj E)
        (Q : Stacks.Divisors.InvertibleQuotient X E)
        (Q' : Stacks.Divisors.InvertibleQuotient X' E')
        (hL : Q'.L ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj Q.L)
        (hq : Q'.q ≫ hL.hom = hE.hom ≫ (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).map Q.q)
        (σ : X ⟶ projectiveBundle X E) (hσ : σ ≫ projectiveBundleToBase X E = 𝟙 X)
        (e : (Scheme.Modules.pullback σ).obj (tautologicalDatum E).twist ≅ Q.L)
        (hqe : (tautologicalDatum E).pullbackQuotientMap σ hσ ≫ e.hom = Q.q)
        (σ' : X' ⟶ projectiveBundle X' E') (hσ' : σ' ≫ projectiveBundleToBase X' E' = 𝟙 X')
        (e' : (Scheme.Modules.pullback σ').obj (tautologicalDatum E').twist ≅ Q'.L)
        (hqe' : (tautologicalDatum E').pullbackQuotientMap σ' hσ' ≫ e'.hom = Q'.q)
        (comm : σ' ≫ projectiveBundleBaseChange g E E' hE = g ≫ σ),
      haveI := isClosedImmersion_of_section_projectiveBundleToBase X E σ hσ
      haveI := isClosedImmersion_of_section_projectiveBundleToBase X' E' σ' hσ'
      (Stacks.Divisors.conormalSourceBaseChange g E E' hE Q Q' hL hq).hom ≫
          (projectiveBundleConormalIso E' Q' hσ' e' hqe').hom =
        (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).map (projectiveBundleConormalIso E Q hσ e hqe).hom ≫
          Stacks.Conormal.conormalBaseChangeMap comm)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GlueingNearPoint.finitePresentationAwayBaseChange_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B3X.** Let `s` be a closed point of a scheme `S` whose open
complement `U = S ∖ {s}` has quasi-compact inclusion.  Base change along
`Spec 𝒪_{S, s} ⟶ S` is an equivalence from the category of finitely presented morphisms to `S`
which are isomorphisms over `U` onto the category of finitely presented morphisms to
`Spec 𝒪_{S, s}` which are isomorphisms over the punctured spectrum.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentationAwayBaseChange_isEquivalence (S : Scheme.{u}) (s : S)
    (hs : IsClosed ({s} : Set S)) (hqc : QuasiCompact (puncturedOpen hs).ι) :
    (finitePresentationAwayBaseChange S s hs).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_submodule_generatingSections_finrank_le_dimension_add_one
declarations.doc:
An invertible sheaf generated by a linear family of sections is generated by a
subspace of dimension at most one more than the dimension of the scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_submodule_generatingSections_finrank_le_dimension_add_one
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [Infinite k] (X : Scheme.{u})
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (V : Type u) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] :
    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, ⊤) :=
      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    letI : Module k Γ(L, ⊤) :=
      Module.compHom Γ(L, ⊤) (algebraMap k Γ(X, ⊤))
    ∀ (s : V →ₗ[k] Γ(L, ⊤)),
      Epi (L.freeHomEquiv.symm (fun v : V ↦ Stacks.SheafOfModules.sectionsOfTop L (s v))) →
      ∃ W : Submodule k V,
        FiniteDimensional k W ∧
        Module.finrank k W ≤ ((topologicalKrullDim X).unbotD 0).toNat + 1 ∧
        Epi (L.freeHomEquiv.symm (fun w : W ↦ Stacks.SheafOfModules.sectionsOfTop L (s w.1)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.invertibleCurveDegree_nonneg_of_eval_top_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
**The degree of an invertible module with a nonzero global section is nonnegative**, on a
proper integral scheme of dimension at most one over a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem invertibleCurveDegree_nonneg_of_eval_top_ne_zero [IsProper f] [IsIntegral X]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (L : X.Modules)
    [hL : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L] (s : L.sections)
    (hs : s.eval (op ⊤) ≠ 0) :
    0 ≤ @invertibleCurveDegree k _ X f _ hdim L hL
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.invertibleCurveDegree_pos_of_eval_top_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
**A nonzero section with a zero forces positive degree.** On a proper integral scheme of
dimension at most one over a field, a nonzero global section of an invertible module which
vanishes at some point forces the degree of that module to be positive.
declarations.statement:
theorem invertibleCurveDegree_pos_of_eval_top_ne_zero [IsProper f] [IsIntegral X]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (L : X.Modules)
    [hL : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L] (s : L.sections)
    (hs : s.eval (op ⊤) ≠ 0)
    (hzero : ∃ y : X, y ∉ nonvanishingLocus (X := X.toRingedSpace) L s) :
    0 < @invertibleCurveDegree k _ X f _ hdim L hL
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_unitHomEquiv_symm_of_invertibleCurveDegree_nonpos
declarations.doc:
**A nonzero section of a module of nonpositive degree trivializes it.** On a proper integral
scheme of dimension at most one over a field, let `ℒ` be an invertible module with `deg(ℒ) ≤ 0`
and a nonzero global section `s`. Then multiplication by `s` is an isomorphism `𝒪_X ⟶ ℒ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_unitHomEquiv_symm_of_invertibleCurveDegree_nonpos [IsProper f] [IsIntegral X]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (L : X.Modules)
    [hL : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L] (s : L.sections)
    (hs : s.eval (op ⊤) ≠ 0) (hdeg : @invertibleCurveDegree k _ X f _ hdim L hL ≤ 0) :
    IsIso (L.unitHomEquiv.symm s)
declarations.comment: part (4), in the stronger form the source's proof supports and the text does not state: the multiplication map O_X -> L of the given section is itself an isomorphism, not merely L isomorphic to O_X abstractly. The weaker reading is the corollary isTrivial_of_invertibleCurveDegree_nonpos beside it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isTrivial_of_invertibleCurveDegree_nonpos
declarations.doc:
**An invertible module of nonpositive degree with a nonzero global section is trivial**, on
a proper integral scheme of dimension at most one over a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTrivial_of_invertibleCurveDegree_nonpos [IsProper f] [IsIntegral X]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (L : X.Modules)
    [hL : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L] (s : L.sections)
    (hs : s.eval (op ⊤) ≠ 0) (hdeg : @invertibleCurveDegree k _ X f _ hdim L hL ≤ 0) :
    SheafOfModules.IsTrivial X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L
declarations.comment: part (4) as stated -- L is isomorphic to O_X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isTrivial_of_eval_top_ne_zero_of_inverse
declarations.doc:
**An invertible module whose inverse also has a nonzero section is trivial.** If an
invertible module `ℒ` on an integral scheme universally closed over a field and its inverse
`ℒ^{⊗ -1}` both have nonzero global sections, then `ℒ ≅ 𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTrivial_of_eval_top_ne_zero_of_inverse [IsIntegral X] [UniversallyClosed f]
    (L : X.Modules) [hL : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : L.sections) (hs : s.eval (op ⊤) ≠ 0)
    (t : (tensorPowerModule L (-1)).sections) (ht : t.eval (op ⊤) ≠ 0) :
    SheafOfModules.IsTrivial X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.invertibleCurveDegree_le_of_hom_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
**A nonzero morphism of invertible modules does not decrease the degree.** On a proper
curve over a field, a nonzero morphism `𝒩 ⟶ ℒ` of invertible modules forces
`deg(𝒩) ≤ deg(ℒ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem invertibleCurveDegree_le_of_hom_ne_zero [IsCurve k f] [IsProper f]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (N L : X.Modules)
    [hN : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property N]
    [hL : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (φ : N ⟶ L) (hφ : φ ≠ 0) :
    invertibleCurveDegree k f hdim N ≤ invertibleCurveDegree k f hdim L
declarations.comment: part (5), the inequality deg(N) <= deg(L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_of_invertibleCurveDegree_eq_of_hom_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
**A nonzero morphism of invertible modules of equal degree is an isomorphism**, on a proper
curve over a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_of_invertibleCurveDegree_eq_of_hom_ne_zero [IsCurve k f] [IsProper f]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (N L : X.Modules)
    [hN : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property N]
    [hL : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (φ : N ⟶ L) (hφ : φ ≠ 0)
    (heq : invertibleCurveDegree k f hdim N = invertibleCurveDegree k f hdim L) : IsIso φ
declarations.comment: part (5), the equality case: the morphism is an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.invertibleCurveDegree_eq_of_isIso
declarations.doc:
**An isomorphism of invertible modules preserves the degree**, on a proper scheme of
dimension at most one over a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem invertibleCurveDegree_eq_of_isIso [IsProper f] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1)
    (N L : X.Modules)
    [hN : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property N]
    [hL : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (φ : N ⟶ L) [IsIso φ] :
    invertibleCurveDegree k f hdim N = invertibleCurveDegree k f hdim L
declarations.comment: part (5), the converse of the equality case: an isomorphism has equal degrees, so the equality holds exactly when the morphism is an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiProjective_tfae_of_exists_isAmple
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiProjective_tfae_of_exists_isAmple (f : X ⟶ S)
    (hS : ∃ (M : S.Modules) (hM : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule S M),
      letI : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule S M := hM
      Stacks.Ample.IsAmple S M) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsQuasiProjective f,
        IsHQuasiProjective f,
        ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (p : X' ⟶ S) (j : X ⟶ X'),
          IsOpenImmersion j ∧ QuasiCompact j ∧ j ≫ p = f ∧ IsProjective p,
        (LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧ QuasiCompact f) ∧
          ∃ (L : X.Modules) (hL : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L),
            letI : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L := hL
            Stacks.Ample.IsAmple X L,
        (LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧ QuasiCompact f) ∧
          ∃ (L : X.Modules) (hL : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L),
            letI : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L := hL
            Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple f L]
declarations.comment: all five conditions, with no hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiProjectiveSchemesOver.baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B43, clause (1).** For a morphism of bases `g : S' ⟶ S`, base change
along `g` is a functor `QP_S ⥤ QP_{S'}`: the fibre product `X ×_S S'` of a scheme `X`
quasi-projective over `S` is quasi-projective over `S'`.

The object part is [Stacks, Tag 0B3G], `AlgebraicGeometry.IsQuasiProjective.of_isPullback`,
applied to the fibre-product square. That result is unconditional, so the hypothesis of the
source that `S'` carries an ample invertible sheaf is not needed and is not assumed.
declarations.statement:
def QuasiProjectiveSchemesOver.baseChange {S S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) :
    QuasiProjectiveSchemesOver S ⥤ QuasiProjectiveSchemesOver S'
declarations.comment: part (1), base change; the source's hypothesis that `S'` has an ample invertible sheaf is not needed, Tag 0B3G needing no such hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiProjective_comp_of_exists_isAmple
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B43, clause (2).** Let `S` carry an ample invertible sheaf. If
`X ∈ QP_S` and `Y ∈ QP_X`, then `Y ∈ QP_S`: for `f : Y ⟶ X` and `g : X ⟶ S` quasi-projective,
`f ≫ g` is quasi-projective.

The source reads this off condition (4) of [Stacks, Tag 0B42]. It is taken here from
[Stacks, Tag 0C4M], `AlgebraicGeometry.IsQuasiProjective.comp`, which is already proved over a
quasi-compact base; the ample invertible sheaf on `S` supplies that quasi-compactness and nothing
else is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiProjective_comp_of_exists_isAmple {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) (g : X ⟶ S)
    (hS : ∃ (M : S.Modules) (hM : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule S M),
      letI : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule S M := hM
      Stacks.Ample.IsAmple S M)
    (hf : IsQuasiProjective f) (hg : IsQuasiProjective g) : IsQuasiProjective (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: part (2), composition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiProjective_pullback_snd_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B43, clause (3). `QP_S` is closed under fibre products over `S`.** For
`f : X ⟶ S` and `g : Y ⟶ S` quasi-projective and `S` carrying an ample invertible sheaf, the
structure morphism `X ×_S Y ⟶ S` is quasi-projective.

This is the source's proof: the projection `X ×_S Y ⟶ Y` is a base change of `f`, hence
quasi-projective by clause (1), and clause (2) composes it with `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiProjective_pullback_snd_comp {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    (hS : ∃ (M : S.Modules) (hM : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule S M),
      letI : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule S M := hM
      Stacks.Ample.IsAmple S M)
    (hf : IsQuasiProjective f) (hg : IsQuasiProjective g) :
    IsQuasiProjective (pullback.snd f g ≫ g)
declarations.comment: part (3), fibre products

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiProjectiveOver_isClosedUnderBinaryProducts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B43, clause (3), as a closure property of the category `QP_S`.** For
`S` carrying an ample invertible sheaf, the full subcategory of schemes quasi-projective over `S`
is closed under binary products in the category of schemes over `S` — that is, under fibre
products over `S`.

A binary product in `Over S` is a fibre product of the sources over `S`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isLimitOverBinaryFan`, so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiProjective_pullback_snd_comp` transported along the comparison
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiProjectiveOver_isClosedUnderBinaryProducts (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : ∃ (M : S.Modules) (hM : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule S M),
      letI : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule S M := hM
      Stacks.Ample.IsAmple S M) :
    (quasiProjectiveOver S).IsClosedUnderBinaryProducts
declarations.comment: part (3), fibre products, as closure of the category under binary products

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiProjective_of_isQuasiAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B43, clause (6).** If `f : X ⟶ S` is quasi-affine of finite type then
`X ∈ QP_S`.

This is Morphisms [Stacks, Tag 0B3H],
`Stacks.HProjective.isQuasiProjective_of_isQuasiAffineHom`: the structure sheaf `𝒪_X` is ample
relative to a quasi-affine morphism. It needs no hypothesis on the base. Finite type is the
conjunction of local finite type and quasi-compactness as in [Stacks, Tag 01T1], and
quasi-compactness already follows from quasi-affineness, so only the local finite type half
appears.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiProjective_of_isQuasiAffineHom {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsQuasiAffineHom f] (hf : LocallyOfFiniteType f) : IsQuasiProjective f
declarations.comment: part (6), quasi-affine of finite type; no hypothesis on the base is used

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiProjective_of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B43, clause (7).** If `f : X ⟶ S` is quasi-finite and separated then
`X ∈ QP_S`.

This is the source's proof: a quasi-finite separated morphism is quasi-affine by
[Stacks, Tag 02LR], `AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiAffineHom_of_locallyQuasiFinite`, and clause (6)
applies. Quasi-finiteness is local quasi-finiteness together with finite type, as in
[Stacks, Tag 02NG]. No hypothesis on the base is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiProjective_of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_isSeparated {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    IsQuasiProjective f
declarations.comment: part (7), quasi-finite and separated; no hypothesis on the base is used

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiProjective_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B43, clause (8).** If `f : X ⟶ S` is a quasi-compact immersion then
`X ∈ QP_S`.

The source goes through clause (7) and Morphisms [Stacks, Tag 01TN], an immersion being locally
quasi-finite; here that tag is Mathlib's `LocallyQuasiFinite` instance for an immersion, and an
immersion is locally of finite type as well, so clause (7) applies directly. No hypothesis on the
base is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiProjective_of_isImmersion {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsImmersion f]
    [QuasiCompact f] : IsQuasiProjective f
declarations.comment: part (8), quasi-compact immersion; no hypothesis on the base is used

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiProjective_sigmaDesc
declarations.doc:
Let `S` carry an ample invertible sheaf. If `f i : Z i ⟶ S` is quasi-projective for every
member of a finite family, then the structure morphism `∐ Z ⟶ S` of the disjoint union is
quasi-projective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiProjective_sigmaDesc (f : ∀ i, Z i ⟶ S)
    (hS : ∃ (M : S.Modules) (hM : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule S M),
      letI : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule S M := hM
      Stacks.Ample.IsAmple S M)
    (hf : ∀ i, IsQuasiProjective (f i)) : IsQuasiProjective (Sigma.desc f)
declarations.comment: part (4), finite disjoint unions; proved through clause (6) and clause (2) over the base `∐ S` rather than through the ampleness of a glued module on a disjoint union, which the source asserts with details omitted

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiProjectiveOver_prop_of_isColimit_cofan
declarations.doc:
For `S` carrying an ample invertible sheaf, the full subcategory of schemes quasi-projective
over `S` is closed under finite coproducts in the category of schemes over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiProjectiveOver_prop_of_isColimit_cofan (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : ∃ (M : S.Modules) (hM : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule S M),
      letI : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule S M := hM
      Stacks.Ample.IsAmple S M)
    {ι : Type u} [Finite ι] {X : ι → Over S} (hX : ∀ i, quasiProjectiveOver S (X i))
    (c : Cofan X) (hc : IsColimit c) : quasiProjectiveOver S c.pt
declarations.comment: part (4), finite disjoint unions, as closure of the category under finite coproducts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective.isQuasiProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07RL. A projective morphism is quasi-projective.** Properness supplies
the finite-type half, and the `f`-very ample module of
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective.exists_isRelativelyVeryAmple` is `f`-ample by [Stacks, Tag 01VN],
`f` being quasi-compact. No hypothesis on the base is used, which is how the source states the
tag.

It is also **clause (5) of [Stacks, Tag 0B43]**, which the source proves by citing Tag 07RL:
membership of `X` in the category `QP_S` of that tag is
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsQuasiProjective X.hom`, so "if `X ⟶ S` is projective then `X ∈ QP_S`" is
this statement. Tag 0B43's hypothesis that `S` carries an ample invertible sheaf is not needed
for it and is not assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsProjective.isQuasiProjective {f : X ⟶ S} (hf : IsProjective f) :
    IsQuasiProjective f
declarations.comment: part (5), a projective morphism is in `QP_S`; the source's hypothesis that `S` has an ample invertible sheaf is not needed, Tag 07RL needing no such hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_sheafGradedAlgebra_of_isProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0B45, clause (1) implies clause (8).** A projective morphism exhibits its source
as the relative homogeneous spectrum of a quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_S`-algebra generated in degree
one whose degree-one piece is of finite type.

`AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective` *is* a closed immersion `j : X ⟶ 𝐏(ℰ)` over `S` for a
quasi-coherent `ℰ` of finite type, and `𝐏(ℰ)` *is* `Proj_S(Sym(ℰ))` by definition
(`Stacks.SymGraded.schemeProjectiveBundle`), so no presentation of projective space as a relative
Proj is needed: `exists_sheafGradedAlgebra_of_isClosedImmersion` applies to `j` at once. Its three
hypotheses on `Sym(ℰ)` are proved —
`Stacks.SymGraded.isGeneratedInDegreeOneAt_schemeSheafGradedAlgebra`,
`Stacks.SymGraded.quasiCompact_schemeProjectiveBundleToBase`, and, for the degree-one piece,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.symmetricAlgebraGenIso`, which identifies `Sym¹(ℰ)` with `ℰ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_sheafGradedAlgebra_of_isProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S}
    (hf : IsProjective f) :
    ∃ A : SheafGradedAlgebra.{u} S,
      Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjRepresentsF1.IsGeneratedInDegreeOne A ∧
        (A.piece 1).IsFiniteType ∧
        ∃ e : X ≅ (relativeProj A).scheme, e.hom ≫ (relativeProj A).toBase = f
declarations.comment: clause (8), reached from clause (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProjective_tfae_of_exists_isAmple
declarations.statement:
theorem isProjective_tfae_of_exists_isAmple
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (hS : ∃ (M : S.Modules) (hM : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule S M),
      letI : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule S M := hM
      Stacks.Ample.IsAmple S M) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsProjective f,
        IsProjectiveMorphism f,
        IsQuasiProjective f ∧ IsProper f,
        IsHQuasiProjective f ∧ IsProper f,
        IsProper f ∧
          ∃ (L : X.Modules) (hL : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L),
            letI : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L := hL
            Stacks.Ample.IsAmple X L,
        IsProper f ∧
          ∃ (L : X.Modules) (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf
              X.ringCatSheaf.2 L),
            letI : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf
              X.ringCatSheaf.2 L := hL
            Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L,
        IsProper f ∧
          ∃ (L : X.Modules) (hL : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L),
            letI : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L := hL
            Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple f L,
        ∃ A : SheafGradedAlgebra.{u} S,
          Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjRepresentsF1.IsGeneratedInDegreeOne A ∧
            (A.piece 1).IsFiniteType ∧
            ∃ e : X ≅ (relativeProj A).scheme,
              e.hom ≫ (relativeProj A).toBase = f]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSchemesOver.baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B46, clause (1).** For a morphism of bases `g : S' ⟶ S`, base change
along `g` is a functor `P_S ⥤ P_{S'}`: the fibre product `S' ×_S X` of a scheme `X` projective
over `S` is projective over `S'`.

The object part is the first assertion of Tag 02V6,
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective.of_isPullback`, applied to the fibre-product square. Its Tag
01O3 input is `AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveBundleBaseChangeComparison`, a theorem, so nothing is
assumed.
declarations.statement:
def ProjectiveSchemesOver.baseChange
    {S S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) : ProjectiveSchemesOver S ⥤ ProjectiveSchemesOver S'
declarations.comment: base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProjective_comp_of_hasAmpleInvertibleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B46, clause (2).** Let `S` carry an ample invertible sheaf. If
`f : X ⟶ S` is projective and `g : Y ⟶ X` is projective, then `g ≫ f : Y ⟶ S` is projective.

This is the source's proof. Condition (5) of Tag 0B45 at the base `S` makes `f` proper with `X`
carrying an ample invertible sheaf; the same condition at the base `X` makes `g` proper with `Y`
carrying an ample invertible sheaf; a composition of proper morphisms is proper (Tag 01W3); and
condition (5) read backwards at the base `S` returns projectivity of `g ≫ f`. Condition (5) is
part of the unconditional cycle of Tag 0B45, so nothing is assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProjective_comp_of_hasAmpleInvertibleSheaf
    {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ S)
    (hS : HasAmpleInvertibleSheaf S) (hf : IsProjective f) (hg : IsProjective g) :
    IsProjective (g ≫ f)
declarations.comment: composition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProjective_pullback_snd_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B46, clause (3). `P_S` is closed under fibre products over `S`.** For
`f : X ⟶ S` and `g : Y ⟶ S` projective and `S` carrying an ample invertible sheaf, the structure
morphism `X ×_S Y ⟶ S` is projective.

The source's proof: the projection `X ×_S Y ⟶ Y` is a base change of `f`, hence projective by
clause (1), and clause (2) composes it with `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProjective_pullback_snd_comp
    {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    (hS : HasAmpleInvertibleSheaf S) (hf : IsProjective f) (hg : IsProjective g) :
    IsProjective (pullback.snd f g ≫ g)
declarations.comment: fibre products

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProjective_of_isFinite_of_hasAmpleInvertibleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B46, clause (5).** A finite morphism `f : X ⟶ S` over a base carrying
an ample invertible sheaf is projective, so `X` is an object of `P_S`.

The source cites Tag 0B3I, which is about an arbitrary base and whose proof in this repository
is conditional. Over the base of Tag 0B46 none of that is needed: a finite morphism is proper
and quasi-affine, so `𝒪_X` is `f`-ample by Tag 0891 in the form
`Stacks.AmplePullback.isRelativelyAmple_of_isQuasiAffineHom_of_iso_unitModule`, which is
condition (6) of Tag 0B45, and condition (6) ⟹ condition (1) belongs to the unconditional cycle
of that tag.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProjective_of_isFinite_of_hasAmpleInvertibleSheaf {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsFinite f] (hS : HasAmpleInvertibleSheaf.{u} S) : IsProjective f
declarations.comment: finite morphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveOver_isClosedUnderFiniteCoproducts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B46, clause (4). `P_S` is closed under finite disjoint unions**, for
`S` carrying an ample invertible sheaf. This includes the empty disjoint union.

The empty and the binary cases are `AlgebraicGeometry.isProjective_of_isEmpty` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.isProjective_coprod_desc`, and
`CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderFiniteCoproducts.mk'` assembles them into every
finite disjoint union.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectiveOver_isClosedUnderFiniteCoproducts (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : HasAmpleInvertibleSheaf S) :
    (projectiveOver S).IsClosedUnderFiniteCoproducts
declarations.comment: finite disjoint unions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_of_isFinite_over_dense_open
declarations.doc:
A proper flat morphism which is finite over a dense open of the base is finite, provided it is
locally of finite presentation or the open is retrocompact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_of_isFinite_over_dense_open {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsProper f] [Flat f] (U : S.Opens) (hU : Dense (U : Set S))
    [IsFinite (pullback.snd f U.ι)]
    (hfin : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∨ IsRetrocompact (U : Set S)) :
    IsFinite f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_isFiniteLocallyFree_strictTransform_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B49.** Let `S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let
`f : X ⟶ S` be proper and let `U ⊆ S` be a quasi-compact open over which `X` is finite locally
free. Then there is a `U`-admissible blowup of `S` along which the strict transform of `X` is
finite locally free.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_isFiniteLocallyFree_strictTransform_of_isProper
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f]
    (U : S.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set S))
    [Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree (pullback.snd f U.ι)] :
    ∃ I : S.IdealSheafData,
      Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup U (blowUpToBase I) ∧
        Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree (strictTransformToBlowUp f I)
declarations.comment: the conclusion in full, under exactly the source's hypotheses (1) and (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.normalSheafShiftIsoDerivedSheafHomExactSupport
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B4B].** For `X` a scheme and `D ⊆ X` an effective Cartier divisor with
closed immersion `i : D ⟶ X` and normal sheaf `𝒩 = 𝒩_{D/X}`, there is an isomorphism

`𝒩[-1] ≅ R ℰom(𝒪_D, 𝒪_X)` in `D(𝒪_D)`,

where `R ℰom(𝒪_D, -)` is the right adjoint of derived pushforward of [Stacks, Tag 0A76].

This is `Stacks.Divisors.derivedSheafHomExactSupportIsoNormalShift` precomposed with the
normal-sheaf clause of [Stacks, Tag 0B3P] (`Stacks.Divisors.normalSheafIsoInvertibleSheaf`),
which identifies `𝒩_{D/X}` with `i^* 𝒪_X(D)` — the description of `𝒩` the source fixes before
stating the lemma. See the module documentation for the proof.

This isomorphism is constructed independently of the canonical comparison morphism
`Stacks.Divisors.normalSheafShiftToDerivedSheafHomExactSupport`; that the comparison morphism is
itself invertible is `Stacks.Divisors.isIso_normalSheafShiftToDerivedSheafHomExactSupport`.
declarations.statement:
def normalSheafShiftIsoDerivedSheafHomExactSupport :
    (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor D.subscheme.Modules 1).obj (normalSheaf D.subschemeι) ≅
      (closedQuotient D).derivedSheafHomExactSupport.obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj (structureModule X))
declarations.comment: the isomorphism 𝒩[-1] ≅ R ℰom(𝒪_D, 𝒪_X), which is what the tag asserts; it is not identified with the canonical comparison morphism Stacks.Divisors.normalSheafShiftToDerivedSheafHomExactSupport

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isIso_normalSheafShiftToDerivedSheafHomExactSupport
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B4B].** For an effective Cartier divisor `D ⊆ X` the canonical comparison
morphism

`𝒩_{D/X}[-1] ⟶ R ℰom_{𝒪_X}(𝒪_D, 𝒪_X)`

in `D(𝒪_D)` is an isomorphism.

This is `Stacks.Divisors.isIso_normalSheafShiftToDerivedSheafHomExactSupport_of_sectionsCore`
with its hypothesis supplied by
`…ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.sheafHomPushforwardSectionsCore`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_normalSheafShiftToDerivedSheafHomExactSupport :
    IsIso (normalSheafShiftToDerivedSheafHomExactSupport D)

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B4C.** The canonical map

`Li^*K ⊗^L_{𝒪_Z} R ℰom(𝒪_Z, 𝒪_X) ⟶ R ℰom(𝒪_Z, K)`

in `D(𝒪_Z)`: the map corresponding to `derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomMateMap` under the
adjunction `i_* ⊣ R ℰom(𝒪_Z, -)` of [Stacks, Tag 0A76].
declarations.statement:
def derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomMap
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X))) :
    S.derivedPullbackTensorSheafHom.obj K ⟶ S.derivedSheafHomExactSupport.obj K
declarations.comment: the canonical map, defined for every complex

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomMap_mate
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B4C.** The adjunction equation characterizing the canonical map:
pushing it forward and composing with the counit of [Stacks, Tag 0A76] gives the displayed
composite. This is what "adjoint to" means in the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomMap_mate
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X))) :
    (modulePushforward S.i).mapDerivedCategory.map
          (S.derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomMap K) ≫
        S.derivedSheafHomAdjunction.counit.app K =
      S.derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomMateMap K
declarations.comment: the adjunction equation characterizing the canonical map

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomMap_unique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B4C.** The adjunction equation determines the canonical map: no
other morphism of that type satisfies it. Together with
`derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomMap_mate` this is the canonicality the source asserts.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomMap_unique
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X)))
    (τ : S.derivedPullbackTensorSheafHom.obj K ⟶ S.derivedSheafHomExactSupport.obj K)
    (hτ : (modulePushforward S.i).mapDerivedCategory.map τ ≫
        S.derivedSheafHomAdjunction.counit.app K =
      S.derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomMateMap K) :
    τ = S.derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomMap K
declarations.comment: uniqueness of the canonical map subject to the adjunction equation

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomNatTrans
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B4C], the canonical map as a morphism of functors**
`Li^*(-) ⊗^L R ℰom(𝒪_Z, 𝒪_X) ⟶ R ℰom(𝒪_Z, -)` of `D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_Z)`. Its component at `K` is
`derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomMap K` and its naturality is
`derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomMap_natural`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomNatTrans :
    S.derivedPullbackTensorSheafHom ⟶ S.derivedSheafHomExactSupport
declarations.comment: the canonical map, functorial in the complex, as a morphism of functors

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.commShift_derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomNatTrans
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B4C], compatibility with distinguished triangles.** The canonical map
`Li^*K ⊗^L R ℰom(𝒪_Z, 𝒪_X) ⟶ R ℰom(𝒪_Z, K)`, as a morphism of functors of `K`, commutes with the
shift: `Li^*` carries its commutation as a total left derived functor
(`Stacks.Cohomology.KFlatDerivedPullback.derivedPullback_commShift`) and the derived tensor
product the one of its structure (`tensorRightFunctorCommShift`), so that the source carries
`derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomCommShift`, and `R ℰom(𝒪_Z, -)` carries the commutation
`derivedSheafHomExactSupportCommShift` it has as the right adjoint of the exact functor `i_*`.
Both functors are exact for these commutations (`isTriangulated_derivedPullbackTensorSheafHom`,
`isTriangulated_derivedSheafHomExactSupport`), and the map carries every triangle to a morphism of
the image triangles (`derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomTriangleHom`).
declarations.statement:
theorem commShift_derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomNatTrans :
    NatTrans.CommShift S.derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomNatTrans ℤ
declarations.comment: compatible with distinguished triangles: the canonical map, functorial in the complex, commutes with the shift

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomTriangleHom
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B4C], the map of triangles.** For every triangle `T` of `D(𝒪_X)`, the
components of the canonical map at its three vertices form a morphism from the image of `T`
under `K ↦ Li^*K ⊗^L R ℰom(𝒪_Z, 𝒪_X)` to its image under `R ℰom(𝒪_Z, -)`; for a distinguished
`T` both images are distinguished (`isTriangulated_derivedPullbackTensorSheafHom`,
`isTriangulated_derivedSheafHomExactSupport`).
declarations.statement:
def derivedPullbackTensorSheafHomTriangleHom
    (T : Pretriangulated.Triangle
      (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X)))) :
    S.derivedPullbackTensorSheafHom.mapTriangle.obj T ⟶
      S.derivedSheafHomExactSupport.mapTriangle.obj T
declarations.comment: compatible with distinguished triangles: the canonical map is a morphism of the image triangles

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDecentSpace_pullback_of_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B4D, decency.** The base change of a decent algebraic space along an étale
morphism from a representable presheaf is decent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDecentSpace_pullback_of_isEtale
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hdecentX : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    (V : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y) (hg : IsEtale B S hS g) :
    IsDecentSpace B S hS (pullback f g)
declarations.comment: decent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_irreducibleComponents_pullback_of_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B4D, finitely many irreducible components.** An affine étale localization of a
birational morphism of decent algebraic spaces with finitely many irreducible components has
a source with finitely many irreducible components.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_irreducibleComponents_pullback_of_isEtale
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hdecentX : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (hdecentY : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    (hfiniteX : (letI := pointTopology B S hS X
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS X)).Finite))
    (hfiniteY : (letI := pointTopology B S hS Y
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS Y)).Finite))
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsBirational B S hS hX hY hdecentX hdecentY hfiniteX hfiniteY f)
    (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) [IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)]
    (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y) (hg : IsEtale B S hS g) :
    letI := pointTopology B S hS (pullback f g)
    (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS (pullback f g))).Finite
declarations.comment: finitely many irreducible components

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBirational_pullback_snd_of_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B4D, birationality.** An affine étale localization of a birational morphism of
decent algebraic spaces with finitely many irreducible components is birational.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBirational_pullback_snd_of_isEtale
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hdecentX : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (hdecentY : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    (hfiniteX : (letI := pointTopology B S hS X
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS X)).Finite))
    (hfiniteY : (letI := pointTopology B S hS Y
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS Y)).Finite))
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsBirational B S hS hX hY hdecentX hdecentY hfiniteX hfiniteY f)
    (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) [IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)]
    (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y) (hg : IsEtale B S hS g) :
    IsBirational B S hS
      (isAlgebraicSpace_pullback B S hS f g hX (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS V) hY)
      (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS V)
      (isDecentSpace_pullback_of_isEtale B S hS hX hY hdecentX V f g hg)
      (isDecentSpace_of_isEtale B S hS g (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS V) hY hg hdecentY)
      (finite_irreducibleComponents_pullback_of_isEtale B S hS hX hY hdecentX hdecentY
        hfiniteX hfiniteY f hf V g hg)
      (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isEtale_of_isAffine B S hS hY hdecentY hfiniteY V g hg)
      (pullback.snd f g)
declarations.comment: birational

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_of_isIntegralHom_of_isBirational_of_isNormal_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B4E.** An integral birational morphism from a reduced algebraic space to a normal
algebraic space is an isomorphism, provided both are decent with finitely many irreducible
components.

Being an isomorphism is checked on the jointly locally surjective family of affine étale charts
`V i → Y` supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affine_etale_family_isLocallySurjective`. Integrality of `f`
represents the base change `X ×_Y V i` by an affine object `W` of the site, so the chart base
change is a morphism of schemes `W → V i`; it is birational by Stacks 0B4D together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.isBirational_toScheme_map_of_yonedaIso`, its source is reduced and its
target normal with finitely many irreducible components, whence it is an isomorphism by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_of_isReduced_of_isBirational_of_isNormal`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_of_isIntegralHom_of_isBirational_of_isNormal_of_isReduced
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hdecentX : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (hdecentY : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    (hfiniteX : (letI := pointTopology B S hS X
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS X)).Finite))
    (hfiniteY : (letI := pointTopology B S hS Y
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS Y)).Finite))
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hintegral : IsIntegralHom B S hS f)
    (hbirational : IsBirational B S hS hX hY hdecentX hdecentY hfiniteX hfiniteY f)
    (hnormalY : IsNormal B S hS Y)
    (hreducedX : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X
      (fun Z : Scheme.{u} => _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsReduced Z)) :
    IsIso f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModuleIsoPullbackIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The first identification of Stacks 0B4F**, `𝒞_{Z/X} = 𝓘_Z|_Z`: the conormal module of a
closed subspace `Z` of an algebraic space `X` is the restriction to `Z` of the defining ideal
sheaf `𝓘_Z ⊆ 𝒪_X`, where restriction is the inverse image along the inclusion `i : Z ⟶ X`.
`Z` need not be an effective Cartier divisor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalModuleIsoPullbackIdealSheaf (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) :
    conormalModule B S hS X Z ≅
      (modulePullback B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Z)).obj
        (idealSheafOfModules B S hS X Z)
declarations.comment: the conormal sheaf is the restriction of the ideal sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackIdealSheafIsoPullbackNegativeDivisorSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The second identification of Stacks 0B4F**, `𝓘_D|_D = 𝒪_X(D)^{⊗ -1}|_D`: for an effective
Cartier divisor `D ⊆ X`, the restriction to `D` of the defining ideal sheaf `𝓘_D` agrees with the
restriction to `D` of `𝒪_X(-D) = 𝒪_X(D)^{⊗ -1}`.

It is the inverse image along the inclusion `i : D ⟶ X` of the canonical identification
`𝒪_X(-D) ≅ 𝓘_D` of Stacks 0841, part 3 (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.negativeDivisorSheafIso`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackIdealSheafIsoPullbackNegativeDivisorSheaf
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) :
    (modulePullback B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X D)).obj
        (idealSheafOfModules B S hS X D) ≅
      (modulePullback B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X D)).obj
        (negativeDivisorSheaf B S hS X D hD)
declarations.comment: the restriction of the ideal sheaf is the restriction of the inverse of O_X(D)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_hasPropertySk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B4G.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian algebraic space over a scheme `S`
satisfying Serre's condition `(S_k)`, and let `D ⊆ X` be an effective Cartier divisor.  Then
`D` satisfies `(S_{k-1})`.

Both hypothesis and conclusion are Stacks 03E6 taken at the property of schemes "locally
Noetherian and `(S_k)`", which is item (3) of Remark 03E7.  By Stacks 083C the divisor is cut
out on a surjective étale chart `U` of `X` by an effective Cartier ideal sheaf; `U` inherits
`(S_k)` from `X` by Stacks 03E8, and the closed subscheme it cuts out satisfies `(S_{k-1})` by
the scheme case `AlgebraicGeometry.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_hasPropertySk` (Stacks 0B3R).
That closed subscheme is a surjective étale chart of `D`.

The index `k - 1` is truncated subtraction of natural numbers; at `k = 0` the conclusion is
the vacuous condition `(S_0)` and is supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.hasPropertySk_zero`, so no hypothesis `1 ≤ k` is required.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_hasPropertySk
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) (k : ℕ)
    (hX : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} => ∃ h : IsLocallyNoetherian T, @HasPropertySk T h k)) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS D.1.toFunctor
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} => ∃ h : IsLocallyNoetherian T, @HasPropertySk T h (k - 1))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isNormal_effectiveCartierDivisor_hasPropertySk_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B4H.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian normal algebraic space over a scheme `S`
and let `D ⊆ X` be an effective Cartier divisor.  Then `D` satisfies Serre's condition
`(S_1)`.

Normality and local Noetherianity of `X` are each Stacks 03E6 taken at the corresponding
property of schemes, items (7) and (1) of Remark 03E7.  By Stacks 083C the divisor is cut out
on a surjective étale chart `U` of `X` by an effective Cartier ideal sheaf; `U` is locally
Noetherian and normal by Stacks 03E8, and the closed subscheme it cuts out satisfies `(S_1)`
by the scheme case `AlgebraicGeometry.isNormal_effectiveCartierDivisor_hasPropertySk_one`
(Stacks 0B3S), which is where Serre's criterion is used.  That closed subscheme is a
surjective étale chart of `D`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNormal_effectiveCartierDivisor_hasPropertySk_one
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (hXnoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (hXnormal : IsNormal B S hS X.1) (D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS D.1.toFunctor
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} => ∃ h : IsLocallyNoetherian T, @HasPropertySk T h 1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.projectiveBundleSectionsEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The bijection of Stacks 0B4I** between the sections of `π : 𝐏(ℰ) ⟶ X` and the isomorphism
classes of invertible quotients of `ℰ`, characterized in
`projectiveBundle_sections_invertibleQuotients`.
declarations.comment: the bijection between sections of P(E) -> X and invertible quotients of E

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.projectiveBundle_sections_invertibleQuotients
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B4I: sections of `𝐏(ℰ) ⟶ X`, invertible quotients of `ℰ`, and base change.**

Let `X` be an algebraic space and `ℰ` a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module, with projective bundle
`π : 𝐏(ℰ) = Proj_X(Sym(ℰ)) ⟶ X` (Stacks 084C).

1. **The bijection** `projectiveBundleSectionsEquiv` between the sections `σ` of `π` and the
   isomorphism classes of surjections `ℰ ⟶ ℒ` onto invertible `𝒪_X`-modules is the canonical one:
   it sends `σ` to `c` exactly when, at every scheme point `x : T ⟶ X`, the point `x ≫ σ` of
   `𝐏(ℰ)` over `x` corresponds to the pullback of `c` to `T` under the identification of the points
   of `𝐏(ℰ)` over `x` with the invertible quotients of `x^*ℰ`
   (`pointsEquivInvertibleQuotientClass`: Stacks 084B, the comparison of `x^*Sym(ℰ)` with
   `Sym(x^*ℰ)`, and Stacks 0B3V on `T`).
2. Every section of `π` is a closed immersion.
3. **Compatibility with base change**: for `g : X' ⟶ X`, the square formed by
   `projectiveBundleBaseChange : 𝐏(g^*ℰ) ⟶ 𝐏(ℰ)`, the two projections and `g` is cartesian, and
   a section `σ'` of `𝐏(g^*ℰ) ⟶ X'` lying over a section `σ` of `𝐏(ℰ) ⟶ X` corresponds to the
   pullback along `g` of the invertible quotient `σ` corresponds to.

The homogeneous sections of `Sym(ℰ)` (and of `Sym(g^*ℰ)`) are bounded by the cutoff of the site
(`SymmetricAlgebraBounded`), the set-theoretic convention of Situation 0849 under which the
relative Proj is an algebraic space over the chosen site.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectiveBundle_sections_invertibleQuotients :
    (∀ (σ : {σ : X ⟶ relativeProjSymmetricAlgebra X E hE hb //
          σ ≫ projectiveBundleπ X E hE hb = 𝟙 X})
        (c : InvertibleQuotientClass X E),
      projectiveBundleSectionsEquiv X E hE hb σ = c ↔
        ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (x : yoneda.obj T ⟶ X.1),
          pointsEquivInvertibleQuotientClass X E hE hb T x ⟨x ≫ σ.1.hom,
            comp_section_comp (projectiveBundleπ X E hE hb).hom x
              (congrArg InducedCategory.Hom.hom σ.2)⟩ = pointRestrictClass X E T x c) ∧
    (∀ σ : X ⟶ relativeProjSymmetricAlgebra X E hE hb, σ ≫ projectiveBundleπ X E hE hb = 𝟙 X →
      IsClosedImmersion B S hS σ.hom) ∧
    (∀ (X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (g : X' ⟶ X)
        (hb' : SymmetricAlgebraBounded X' ((modulePullback B S hS g).obj E)),
      IsPullback (projectiveBundleBaseChange X E hE hb g hb').hom
          (projectiveBundleπ X' _ (isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_projectiveBundle X E hE g)
            hb').hom
          (projectiveBundleπ X E hE hb).hom g.hom ∧
        ∀ (σ : {σ : X ⟶ relativeProjSymmetricAlgebra X E hE hb //
            σ ≫ projectiveBundleπ X E hE hb = 𝟙 X})
          (σ' : {σ' : X' ⟶ relativeProjSymmetricAlgebra X' ((modulePullback B S hS g).obj E)
              (isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_projectiveBundle X E hE g) hb' //
            σ' ≫ projectiveBundleπ X' _ _ hb' = 𝟙 X'}),
          σ'.1 ≫ projectiveBundleBaseChange X E hE hb g hb' = g ≫ σ.1 →
            projectiveBundleSectionsEquiv X' _ _ hb' σ' =
              invertibleQuotientBaseChangeClass g (Iso.refl _)
                (projectiveBundleSectionsEquiv X E hE hb σ))
declarations.comment: the bijection between sections of P(E) -> X and invertible quotients of E, its characterization at scheme points, sections are closed immersions, and compatibility with base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.projectiveBundle_sectionConormalIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B4I, the conormal isomorphism and its base change.**  For a section `σ` of
`𝐏(ℰ) ⟶ X` corresponding to `q : ℰ ⟶ ℒ` there is a unique `Ker(q) ⊗ ℒ^{⊗ -1} ≅ 𝒞_{σ(X)/𝐏(ℰ)}`
restricting on every étale chart to the chart isomorphism of Stacks 0B3V; along `g : X' ⟶ X` with
`σ'` over `σ`, these isomorphisms for `q` and `g^*q` commute with the base-change maps.

        ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1, (chartModuleRestriction B S hS X U).map φ.hom =
          (sectionConormalChartFamilyOf X E hE Q hb σ hσ

            T).Modules) (iC := Scheme.Modules.instCategory)

          Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T).presheaf
            (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T).ringCatSheaf.2⟩)

            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower (structureCommRings B S hS X)
            (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property Q.L (-1))).hom ≫ ((zariskiReadingTensorObjIso T
            ((modulePullback B S hS (pointHom x)).obj (kernel Q.q)) ((modulePullback B S hS
            (pointHom x)).obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower (structureCommRings B S
            hS X) (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property Q.L (-1)))
            (isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite B S hS (pointHom x)
            (kernel Q.q) (isQuasicoherentOnSite_kernel_q X E hE Q))
            (isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite B S hS (pointHom x)
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower (structureCommRings B S hS X)
            (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property Q.L (-1))
            (isQuasicoherentOnSite_invertibleTensorPower X Q.L (-1)))).hom ≫
            (monoidalTensorSheafTensorIso ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T)
            ((zariskiReadingFunctor T).obj ((modulePullback B S hS (pointHom x)).obj (kernel Q.q)))
            ((zariskiReadingFunctor T).obj ((modulePullback B S hS (pointHom x)).obj
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower (structureCommRings B S hS X)

        (kernelPointReadingHom X E hE Q T x) (inversePointReadingIso X T x Q.L).hom))
            (fun T x hx => isIso_conormalSourcePointReading_of_isEtale X E hE Q T x hx) hQ U).hom) ∧
    (∀ (X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (g : X' ⟶ X)
        (hb' : SymmetricAlgebraBounded X' ((modulePullback B S hS g).obj E))
        (σ : X ⟶ relativeProjSymmetricAlgebra X E hE hb) (hσ : σ ≫ projectiveBundleπ X E hE hb = 𝟙
            X)
        (σ' : X' ⟶ relativeProjSymmetricAlgebra X' ((modulePullback B S hS g).obj E)
          (isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_projectiveBundle X E hE g) hb')
        (hσ' : σ' ≫ projectiveBundleπ X' ((modulePullback B S hS g).obj E)
          (isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_projectiveBundle X E hE g) hb' = 𝟙 X')
        (comm : σ' ≫ (projectiveBundleBaseChange X E hE hb g hb') = g ≫ σ)
        (Q : InvertibleQuotient X E)
        (hQ : projectiveBundleSectionsEquiv X E hE hb ⟨σ, hσ⟩ = Quotient.mk _ Q)
        (φ : sectionConormalSource X E Q ≅ sectionConormalTarget X E hE hb σ hσ),
        (∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1, (chartModuleRestriction B S hS X U).map φ.hom =
            (sectionConormalChartFamilyOf X E hE Q hb σ hσ
            (fun (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (x : yoneda.obj T ⟶ X.1) =>
          (haveI : IsInvertible (structureCommRings B S hS X) (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property
              Q.L := Q.invertible.toAlgebraicGeometry
          (CategoryTheory.Functor.compBifunctorMap (𝒞 := ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj
              T).Modules) (iC := Scheme.Modules.instCategory)
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T).presheaf,
            Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T).presheaf
              (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T).ringCatSheaf.2⟩)
          ((zariskiReadingFunctor T).map (modulePullbackTensorIso B S hS (pointHom x) (kernel Q.q)
              (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower (structureCommRings B S hS X)
              (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property Q.L (-1))).hom ≫ ((zariskiReadingTensorObjIso T
              ((modulePullback B S hS (pointHom x)).obj (kernel Q.q)) ((modulePullback B S hS
              (pointHom x)).obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower (structureCommRings B

              (isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite B S hS (pointHom x)

              (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower (structureCommRings B S hS X)
              (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property Q.L (-1))
              (isQuasicoherentOnSite_invertibleTensorPower X Q.L (-1)))).hom ≫
              (monoidalTensorSheafTensorIso ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T)
              ((zariskiReadingFunctor T).obj ((modulePullback B S hS (pointHom x)).obj (kernel
              Q.q))) ((zariskiReadingFunctor T).obj ((modulePullback B S hS (pointHom x)).obj
              (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower (structureCommRings B S hS X)
              (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property Q.L (-1))))).hom))

            (fun (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (x : yoneda.obj T ⟶ X'.1) =>
          (haveI : IsInvertible (structureCommRings B S hS X') (structureRingSheaf B S hS

          (CategoryTheory.Functor.compBifunctorMap (𝒞 := ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj
              T).Modules) (iC := Scheme.Modules.instCategory)
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T).presheaf,
            Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T).presheaf
              (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T).ringCatSheaf.2⟩)
          ((zariskiReadingFunctor T).map (modulePullbackTensorIso B S hS (pointHom x) (kernel
              (Q.baseChange g (Iso.refl _)).q) (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower
              (structureCommRings B S hS X') (structureRingSheaf B S hS X').property (Q.baseChange g
              (Iso.refl _)).L (-1))).hom ≫ ((zariskiReadingTensorObjIso T ((modulePullback B S hS
              (pointHom x)).obj (kernel (Q.baseChange g (Iso.refl _)).q)) ((modulePullback B S hS
              (pointHom x)).obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower (structureCommRings B
              S hS X') (structureRingSheaf B S hS X').property (Q.baseChange g (Iso.refl _)).L

              (isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_projectiveBundle X E hE g) (Q.baseChange g

              (pointHom x) (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower (structureCommRings B S hS

              (-1))))).hom))
          (kernelPointReadingHom X' ((modulePullback B S hS g).obj E)
              (isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_projectiveBundle X E hE g) (Q.baseChange g
              (Iso.refl _)) T x) (inversePointReadingIso X' T x (Q.baseChange g (Iso.refl
              _)).L).hom)))
            (fun T x hx => isIso_conormalSourcePointReading_of_isEtale X' ((modulePullback B S hS
                g).obj E) (isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_projectiveBundle X E hE g)

                E hE hb g hb' σ hσ σ' hσ' comm Q hQ) V).hom) →
      (@CategoryStruct.comp _ _ ((modulePullback B S hS g).obj
          (haveI : IsInvertible (structureCommRings B S hS X) (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property
              Q.L := Q.invertible.toAlgebraicGeometry; (MonoidalCategory.tensorObj (C := Modules.{u,
              u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (kernel Q.q) (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower
              (structureCommRings B S hS X) (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property Q.L (-1)))))

          (isImmersion_of_isClosedImmersion B S hS

                B S hS g).obj E) (isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_projectiveBundle X E hE g)
                hb').2 X'.2 σ'.hom
          (isImmersion_of_isClosedImmersion B S hS
            (isClosedImmersion_of_section_projectiveBundleπ X' ((modulePullback B S hS g).obj E)
                (isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_projectiveBundle X E hE g) hb' σ' hσ')))
                ((modulePullback B S hS g).map (X :=
                (haveI : IsInvertible (structureCommRings B S hS X) (structureRingSheaf B S hS
                    X).property Q.L := Q.invertible.toAlgebraicGeometry; (MonoidalCategory.tensorObj
                    (C := Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (kernel Q.q)
