declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CohenMacaulayCurveSituation.nonempty_generatingSections_dualizingSheafOverField_tensorSheaf
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B5H].** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0B5D] — a field `k`, a proper scheme `X` of
dimension one over `k` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k` — let `ℒ` be a very ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module
with `deg(ℒ) ≥ 2`. Then `ω_X ⊗ ℒ` is globally generated, where
`ω_X = H^{-1}(f^×(𝒪_{Spec k}))` is the dualizing sheaf of [Stacks, Tag 0BS2].

This is the source's proof: over `k̄` it is
`nonempty_generatingSections_dualizing_tensorSheaf_of_isAlgClosed_of_isCoherent`, and the general
case is the reduction `nonempty_generatingSections_dualizing_tensorSheaf_of_isoAlgebraicClosure`,
whose two inputs are supplied here — the coherence of `ω_X` by
`isCoherent_dualizingSheafOverField`, and the identification of the inverse image of `ω_X` with
`ω_{X_{k̄}}` (part (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0E32] at the dualizing sheaf) by
`pullbackDualizingSheafOverFieldIso`. Nothing is assumed beyond the source's hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_generatingSections_dualizingSheafOverField_tensorSheaf (L : S.X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible S.X.presheaf S.X.ringCatSheaf.2 L]
    (hL : Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple S.f L)
    (hd : 2 ≤ invertibleCurveDegree S.k S.f (le_of_eq S.dimension_one) L) :
    Nonempty ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨S.X.presheaf,
      Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (S.X.presheaf) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
      (S.X.ringCatSheaf.property)⟩).obj
      ((Stacks.Duality.dualizingSheafOverField S.f))).obj (L))).GeneratingSections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CohenMacaulayCurveSituation.nonempty_generatingSections_tensorSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B5H.** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0B5D], let `ω` be the dualizing sheaf
of `X` and let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module with `deg(ℒ) ≥ 2`. Then `ω ⊗ ℒ` is generated by
its global sections.

Global generation is surjectivity of the map from the free module on all global sections of
`ω ⊗ ℒ`, and `epi_globalSectionsHom_of_forall_isClosed` proves it from a section of `ℒ` vanishing
at each closed point: [Stacks, Tag 0B5F] makes the global sections generate the quotient of
`ω ⊗ ℒ` by `ω`, and Nakayama upgrades that to generation at the point.

The section is [Stacks, Tag 0B58] and its global-section count is the degree theory of Section
[Stacks, Tag 0B5B], both of which `hsec` supplies; the source uses very ampleness of `ℒ` only to
invoke them, so that hypothesis is absent here. Duality for `ω` is `hdual`, `hone` and `hH2`, and
its Cohen--Macaulayness is `hnosub`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_generatingSections_tensorSheaf (ω L : S.X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible S.X.presheaf S.X.ringCatSheaf.2 L] (hωq : ω.IsQuasicoherent)
    (hdual : S.FirstCohomologyDuality ω) (hH2 : S.SecondCohomologyVanishing)
    (hone : Module.finrank S.k (cohomologyOverField S.k S.f ω 1) = 1)
    (hFq : ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨S.X.presheaf,
      Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (S.X.presheaf) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
      (S.X.ringCatSheaf.property)⟩).obj (ω)).obj (L))).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hFft : ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨S.X.presheaf,
      Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (S.X.presheaf) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
      (S.X.ringCatSheaf.property)⟩).obj (ω)).obj (L))).IsFiniteType)
    (hnosub : S.NoSubmoduleOfZeroDimensionalSupport
      ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨S.X.presheaf,
        Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (S.X.presheaf) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
        (S.X.ringCatSheaf.property)⟩).obj (ω)).obj (L))))
    (hd : 2 ≤ invertibleCurveDegree S.k S.f (le_of_eq S.dimension_one) L)
    (hsec : ∀ x : S.X, IsClosed ({x} : Set S.X) →
      S.VanishingSectionData ω ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨S.X.presheaf,
        Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (S.X.presheaf) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
        (S.X.ringCatSheaf.property)⟩).obj (ω)).obj (L)))
        (invertibleCurveDegree S.k S.f (le_of_eq S.dimension_one) L) x) :
    Nonempty ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨S.X.presheaf,
      Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (S.X.presheaf) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
      (S.X.ringCatSheaf.property)⟩).obj (ω)).obj (L))).GeneratingSections
declarations.comment: k algebraically closed; hsec carries Tag 0B58's section and the count of global sections of the twisted quotient, duality is hdual/hone/hH2, Nakayama is proved

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjTwistIntegerComparisonStatement.comparison_existsUnique_functorial_degreeZeroId
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a graded ring, `X = Proj S`, let `ℱ` be a sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules and let
`M = ⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} Γ(X, ℱ(n))` be the graded `S`-module of twisted global sections, taken with its
canonical graded-module structure
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjTwistedSections.twistedGlobalSectionsModule`. Then there is a
canonical `𝒪_X`-module map `M̃ ⟶ ℱ`, functorial in `ℱ`, whose induced map `M₀ → Γ(X, ℱ)` is the
identity.

The three conjuncts are, in order:

1. **Existence and canonicity.** There is exactly one morphism `M̃ ⟶ ℱ` whose restriction to the
  standard open `D₊(f)` of each positive-degree homogeneous element is the chart comparison
  `m / f ^ k ↦ m|_{D₊(f)} ⊗ f ^ (-k)`. The morphism it names is
  `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjTwistIntegerComparison.integerComparison`.
2. **Functoriality in `ℱ`.** For every sheaf `𝒢` and every morphism `ψ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢`, the comparison
  morphisms of `ℱ` and of `𝒢` form a commuting square with `ψ` and with the morphism of
  associated sheaves that `ψ` induces on the graded modules of twisted global sections.
3. **The degree-zero map is the identity.** A global section `t` of `ℱ` is a degree-zero element
  of `M` through the identification `ℱ(0) ≅ ℱ` of
  `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjTwistDegreeZeroNormalization.twistZeroCancelIso`; the global
  section of `M̃` attached to it is sent by the comparison morphism back to `t`.
declarations.statement:
theorem comparison_existsUnique_functorial_degreeZeroId
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (projRingSheaf 𝒮)) :
    (∃! φ : twistedGlobalSectionsAssociatedSheaf 𝒮 F (twistedGlobalSectionsModule 𝒮 F) ⟶ F,
        ∀ p : PositiveElem 𝒮,
          φ.val.app (op (positiveBasicOpen 𝒮 p)) =
            localComparison 𝒮 F (twistedGlobalSectionsModule 𝒮 F) p) ∧
      (∀ (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (projRingSheaf 𝒮)) (ψ : F ⟶ G),
          twistedGlobalSectionsAssociatedSheafMap 𝒮 (twistedGlobalSectionsModule 𝒮 F)
                (twistedGlobalSectionsModule 𝒮 G) ψ ≫
              integerComparison 𝒮 G (twistedGlobalSectionsModule 𝒮 G) =
            integerComparison 𝒮 F (twistedGlobalSectionsModule 𝒮 F) ≫ ψ) ∧
      (letI := (twistedGlobalSectionsModule 𝒮 F).moduleInst
       letI := (twistedGlobalSectionsModule 𝒮 F).gradedSMul
       ∀ t : F.val.obj (op (⊤ : Opens (ProjectiveSpectrum.top 𝒮))),
        (integerComparison 𝒮 F (twistedGlobalSectionsModule 𝒮 F)).val.app
            (op (⊤ : Opens (ProjectiveSpectrum.top 𝒮)))
            (degreeZeroToGlobalSections 𝒮 (twistedGlobalSectionsGrading 𝒮 F)
              ⟨DirectSum.of (fun k : ℤ => twistedSectionsComponent 𝒮 F k) 0
                  ((twistZeroCancelIso 𝒮 F (rfl : (0 : ℤ) = 0)).inv.val.app
                    (op (⊤ : Opens (ProjectiveSpectrum.top 𝒮))) t),
                (DirectSum.mem_rangeGrading ℤ (fun k : ℤ => twistedSectionsComponent 𝒮 F k) 0
                  _).mpr ⟨_, rfl⟩⟩) = t)
declarations.comment:
the tag's three assertions in one statement, for the canonical graded-module
structure on `M = ⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} Γ(X, ℱ(n))`: the comparison morphism `M̃ ⟶ ℱ` exists and is the
unique morphism restricting on each positive-degree standard open to `m / f ^ k ↦ m|_{D₊(f)} ⊗
f ^ (-k)`, it commutes with every morphism of sheaves of modules out of `ℱ`, and it returns each
global section of `ℱ` to itself through the identification `ℱ(0) ≅ ℱ`

declarations.name: Stacks.Veronese.tag0B5J
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B5J].** Let `S` be a graded ring and `d ≥ 1`. Set `S' = S⁽ᵈ⁾`,
`X = Proj S` and `X' = Proj S'`. There is a canonical isomorphism `i : X ⟶ X'` of schemes such
that (1) for any graded `S`-module `M`, setting `M' = M⁽ᵈ⁾`, there is a canonical isomorphism
`M̃ ≅ i^*(M'~)`, and (2) there are canonical isomorphisms `𝒪_X(nd) ≅ i^*𝒪_{X'}(n)`; and these
isomorphisms are compatible with the multiplication maps of Tag 01MK and hence with the maps of
Tags 01MO, 03GJ, 01MP, 03GK, 01MQ and 01MR.

The isomorphism `i` is `Stacks.Veronese.veroneseProjIso 𝒮 d hd`, glued from the chart
isomorphisms; the first conjunct says its underlying morphism `veroneseProjHom` is an
isomorphism of schemes, that on homogeneous primes it is contraction along `S' ⊆ S`, and that on
each standard open `D₊(f) = Spec S₍f₎` it is `Spec` of the identification `S'₍f ᵈ₎ ≅ S₍f₎`
followed by the inclusion of `D₊(f ᵈ)` — the source's "`S₍f₎ ≅ S'₍f ᵈ₎`, compatible with the
restriction maps". These charts cover `Proj S`, so they determine `i` as a morphism of schemes,
not only on points. The next conjunct is the consequence `i⁻¹ D₊(f ᵈ) = D₊(f)`, which the
chart descriptions of assertion (1) are written over. The third conjunct is assertion (1) for a
module in any universe `v`: the
isomorphism `Stacks.Veronese.veroneseAssociatedSheafIso 𝒮 𝒨 d hd : M̃ ≅ i^*(M'~)`, with the
chart description that makes it canonical — on `D₊(f)` its inverse is the degree-zero Veronese
localization comparison `M'₍f ᵈ₎ ≅ M₍f₎`. The fourth conjunct is assertion (2), each isomorphism
exhibited as the source derives it: (1) at `M = S(nd)` followed by `(S(nd))⁽ᵈ⁾ ≅ S'(n)`. The
remaining conjuncts are the trailing clause: the commuting square with the multiplication maps
of Tag 01MK, and the six squares with the maps of Tags 01MO, 03GJ, 01MP, 03GK, 01MQ and 01MR
which the source derives from it and whose precise statements it omits. See the module
documentation for each square, for why the source's proof of the first is corrected here
(the comparison along its lower edge is not injective at `S = k[x, y]`, `d = 2`,
`M = N = S(1)`: `Stacks.Veronese.not_injective_veroneseTensorMap`), and for the universes.
declarations.statement:
theorem tag0B5J (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) :
    letI := veroneseGradingGradedRing 𝒮 d hd
    -- `i` is an isomorphism of schemes, and on homogeneous primes it is contraction along
    -- `S⁽ᵈ⁾ ⊆ S`
    IsIso (veroneseProjHom 𝒮 d hd) ∧
      (∀ (x : ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒮) (g : veroneseSubring 𝒮 d),
        g ∈ ((veroneseProjIso 𝒮 d hd).hom.base x).asHomogeneousIdeal ↔
          (g : S) ∈ x.asHomogeneousIdeal) ∧
      -- on each chart `D₊(f) = Spec S₍f₎`, `i` is `Spec` of `S'₍f ᵈ₎ ≅ S₍f₎` followed by the
      -- inclusion of `D₊(f ᵈ)`: these determine `i` as a morphism of schemes
      (∀ (f : S) (e : ℕ) (he : 0 < e) (hf : f ∈ 𝒮 e),
        Proj.awayι 𝒮 f hf he ≫ (veroneseProjIso 𝒮 d hd).hom =
          Spec.map (veroneseAwayEquiv 𝒮 d f hf hd).toCommRingCatIso.hom ≫
            Proj.awayι (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d) (veronesePower 𝒮 d f hf)
              (veronesePower_mem 𝒮 d f hf) he) ∧
      -- the chart identification `i⁻¹ D₊(f ᵈ) = D₊(f)`
      (∀ (f : S) (e : ℕ), 0 < e → ∀ hf : f ∈ 𝒮 e,
        (veroneseProjIso 𝒮 d hd).hom ⁻¹ᵁ
            Proj.basicOpen (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d) (veronesePower 𝒮 d f hf) =
          Proj.basicOpen 𝒮 f) ∧
      -- assertion (1): `veroneseAssociatedSheafIso 𝒮 𝒨 d hd : M̃ ≅ i^*(M'~)`, for a module in
      -- any universe, with the chart description that makes it the canonical isomorphism
      (∀ (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] (𝒨 : ℤ → AddSubgroup M)
          [Decomposition 𝒨] [SetLike.GradedSMul 𝒮 𝒨],
        letI := veroneseModuleGradingDecomposition 𝒮 𝒨 d hd
        ∀ (f : S) (e : ℕ) (he : 0 < e) (hf : f ∈ 𝒮 e)
          (hvf : veronesePower 𝒮 d f hf ∈ veroneseGrading 𝒮 d e)
          (z : GradedModuleDegreeZeroLocalization (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d)
            (veroneseModuleGrading 𝒮 𝒨 d) (veronesePower 𝒮 d f hf)),
          ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.associatedModuleSheafStandardOpenEquiv 𝒮 𝒨 hf he
              ((veroneseAssociatedSheafIso 𝒮 𝒨 d hd).inv.val.app (op (Proj.basicOpen 𝒮 f))
                (veroneseProjIso_basicOpen 𝒮 d hd f he hf ▸
                  ((SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{max u v}
                        (veroneseProjIso 𝒮 d hd).hom.toRingCatSheafHom).unit.app
                      (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.associatedModuleSheaf (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d)
                        (veroneseModuleGrading 𝒮 𝒨 d))).val.app
                    (op (Proj.basicOpen (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d) (veronesePower 𝒮 d f hf)))
                    ((ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.associatedModuleSheafStandardOpenEquiv
                        (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d) (veroneseModuleGrading 𝒮 𝒨 d)
                        hvf he).symm z))) =
            veroneseModuleAwayEquiv 𝒮 d 𝒨 f hf hd z) ∧
      -- assertion (2), as the source derives it from (1) at `M = S(nd)`
      (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ E : ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistingSheaf 𝒮 (n * d) ≅
          (Scheme.Modules.pullback (veroneseProjIso 𝒮 d hd).hom).obj
            (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistingSheaf (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d) n),
        E.hom =
          (associatedModuleSheafVeroneseIso 𝒮 (twistGradingAddSubgroup 𝒮 (n * d)) d hd).hom ≫
            (Scheme.Modules.pullback (veroneseProjIso 𝒮 d hd).hom).map
              (veroneseShiftSheafIso 𝒮 d hd n).hom) ∧
      -- the trailing clause: compatibility of (1) with the multiplication maps
      (∀ (M N : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N]
          (𝒨 : ℤ → AddSubgroup M) [Decomposition 𝒨] [SetLike.GradedSMul 𝒮 𝒨]
          (𝒩 : ℤ → AddSubgroup N) [Decomposition 𝒩] [SetLike.GradedSMul 𝒮 𝒩],
        veroneseTensorSquareLeft 𝒮 𝒨 𝒩 d hd = veroneseTensorSquareRight 𝒮 𝒨 𝒩 d hd) ∧
      -- "and hence with (01MO)": `𝒪(nd) ⊗ 𝒪(md) ⟶ 𝒪((n+m)d)` against `𝒪'(n) ⊗ 𝒪'(m) ⟶ 𝒪'(n+m)`
      (∀ n m : ℤ, veroneseTwistMulLeft 𝒮 d hd n m = veroneseTwistMulRight 𝒮 d hd n m) ∧
      -- "and hence with (03GJ)": `𝒪(nd) ⊗ ℱ(md) ⟶ ℱ((n+m)d)` against
      -- `𝒪'(n) ⊗ ℱ'(m) ⟶ ℱ'(n+m)`, for `ℱ = i^*ℱ'`
      (∀ (F' : SheafOfModules.{u}
            ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology
              (ProjectiveSpectrum.top (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d)))
              (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj
              (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.structureSheaf (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d)))) (n m : ℤ),
        veroneseTwistSheafMulLeft 𝒮 d hd F' n m = veroneseTwistSheafMulRight 𝒮 d hd F' n m) ∧
      -- "and hence with (03GK)": products of global sections of `𝒪(nd)` and `ℱ(md)`
      (∀ (F' : SheafOfModules.{u}
            ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology
              (ProjectiveSpectrum.top (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d)))
              (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj
              (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.structureSheaf (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d)))) (n m : ℤ)
          (s : (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistingSheaf 𝒮 (n * d)).val.obj (op ⊤))
          (t : (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistSheafOfModules 𝒮 (pullbackProjModule 𝒮
            (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d) (veroneseProjIso 𝒮 d hd).hom F') (m * d)).val.obj (op ⊤))
          (s' : (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistingSheaf (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d) n).val.obj (op ⊤))
          (t' : (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistSheafOfModules (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d) F' m).val.obj
            (op ⊤)),
        ((veroneseTwistingSheafIso 𝒮 d hd n).hom.val.app (op ⊤)).hom s =
            Stacks.Tag01VSPullbackTensor.modulesPullbackUnit (veroneseProjIso 𝒮 d hd).hom
              (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistingSheaf (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d) n) ⊤ s' →
        ((veroneseTwistedModuleIso 𝒮 d hd F' m).hom.val.app (op ⊤)).hom t =
            Stacks.Tag01VSPullbackTensor.modulesPullbackUnit (veroneseProjIso 𝒮 d hd).hom
              (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistSheafOfModules (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d) F' m) ⊤ t' →
        ((veroneseTwistedModuleIso 𝒮 d hd F' (n + m)).hom.val.app (op ⊤)).hom
            (((eqToHom (congrArg (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistSheafOfModules 𝒮
                (pullbackProjModule 𝒮 (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d) (veroneseProjIso 𝒮 d hd).hom F'))
                (add_mul n m (d : ℤ)).symm)).val.app (op ⊤)).hom
              (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.multiplyHomogeneousSections' 𝒮
                (pullbackProjModule 𝒮 (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d) (veroneseProjIso 𝒮 d hd).hom F')
                (n * d) (m * d) s t)) =
          Stacks.Tag01VSPullbackTensor.modulesPullbackUnit (veroneseProjIso 𝒮 d hd).hom
            (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistSheafOfModules (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d) F' (n + m)) ⊤
            (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.multiplyHomogeneousSections' (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d) F' n m
              s' t')) ∧
      -- "and hence with (01MP)": `S → ⨁ₙ Γ(X, 𝒪_X(n))` against `S' → ⨁ₙ Γ(X', 𝒪_{X'}(n))`
      (letI := (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.globalSectionsRingMap 𝒮).gradedRing
       letI := (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.globalSectionsRingMap (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d)).gradedRing
       ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : veroneseSubring 𝒮 d),
        (veroneseTwistingSheafIso 𝒮 d hd n).hom.val.app (op ⊤)
            ((eqToHom (congrArg (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistingSheaf 𝒮)
              (Nat.cast_mul n d))).val.app (op ⊤)
              (DirectSum.component ℤ ℕ (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistGlobalSections 𝒮) (n * d)
                ((ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.globalSectionsRingMap 𝒮).hom (a : S)))) =
          Stacks.Tag01VSPullbackTensor.modulesPullbackUnit (veroneseProjIso 𝒮 d hd).hom
            (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistingSheaf (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d) n) ⊤
            (DirectSum.component ℤ ℕ
              (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistGlobalSections (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d)) n
              ((ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.globalSectionsRingMap (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d)).hom a))) ∧
      -- "and hence with (01MQ)": `M̃ ⊗ 𝒪_X(nd) ⟶ M(nd)~` against `M'~ ⊗ 𝒪_{X'}(n) ⟶ M'(n)~`
      (∀ (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] (𝒨 : ℤ → AddSubgroup M)
          [Decomposition 𝒨] [SetLike.GradedSMul 𝒮 𝒨] (n : ℤ),
        veroneseModuleTwistLeft 𝒮 𝒨 d hd n = veroneseModuleTwistRight 𝒮 𝒨 d hd n) ∧
      -- "and hence with (01MR)": `M → ⨁ₙ Γ(X, M(n)~)` against `M' → ⨁ₙ Γ(X', M'(n)~)`
      (∀ (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] (𝒨 : ℤ → AddSubgroup M)
          [Decomposition 𝒨] [SetLike.GradedSMul 𝒮 𝒨],
        letI := veroneseModuleGradingDecomposition 𝒮 𝒨 d hd
        ∀ (n : ℤ) (m : veroneseSubmodule 𝒮 𝒨 d),
        (veroneseShiftedSheafIsoAny 𝒮 𝒨 d hd n).hom.val.app (op ⊤)
            (DirectSum.component ℤ ℤ _ (n * d)
              ((Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjShiftedSections.globalSectionsModuleMap 𝒮 𝒨).hom
                (m : M))) =
          pullbackUnitAny (veroneseProjIso 𝒮 d hd).hom
            (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.associatedModuleSheaf (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d)
              (shiftedGrading (veroneseModuleGrading 𝒮 𝒨 d) n)) ⊤
            (DirectSum.component ℤ ℤ _ n
              ((Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjShiftedSections.globalSectionsModuleMap
                (veroneseGrading 𝒮 d) (veroneseModuleGrading 𝒮 𝒨 d)).hom m)))
declarations.comment: the canonical isomorphism i : Proj S to Proj S^(d) induced by the inclusion S^(d) in S, described on homogeneous primes and on the standard opens D+(f) = Spec S_(f); assertion (1), the canonical isomorphism from the sheaf of a graded S-module M, in any universe, to the pullback of the sheaf of M^(d), described on the standard opens; assertion (2), the isomorphisms O_X(nd) to i^* O_X'(n) obtained from (1) at M = S(nd); and the compatibility of these isomorphisms with the multiplication maps of associated sheaves (through the comparison map from M^(d) tensor N^(d) to (M tensor N)^(d)), with the multiplication of twists, with the maps O(n) tensor F(m) to F(n+m) and M~ tensor O(n) to M(n)~, with the maps from S and from M to twisted global sections, and with the products of twisted global sections

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.sectionLocalizationMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical map from degree-zero localized twisted sections to sections on `X_s`.
It restricts a numerator to `X_s` and divides by the corresponding power of `s`.
The section is invertible there, so this construction is independent of the fraction
representative.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.sectionLocalizationMap_fraction
declarations.doc:
A homogeneous fraction `m/sⁿ` maps to the section `t` exactly when, on
`X_s`, the restricted numerator is the tensor product of `t` with `sⁿ`.
The local invertibility of `sⁿ` makes this condition a characterization.
declarations.statement:
public theorem sectionLocalizationMap_fraction (s : L.sections) (n : ℕ)
    (m : ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨(sectionSiteRing X),
      Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ ((sectionSiteRing X)) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
      ((sectionSiteSheaf X))⟩).obj (F)).obj ((TensorPower.tensorPower (sectionSiteRing X)
      (sectionSiteSheaf X) L
        (n : ℤ))))).val.obj (op (⊤_ (Opens X.toRingedSpace.toPresheafedSpace))))
    (z : sectionAtNonvanishingOpen X L F s)
    (t : F.val.obj (op (nonvanishingOpen L s)))
    (hz : (z : LocalizedModule.Away
      (R := sectionRing (sectionSiteRing X) (sectionSiteSheaf X) L)
      (homogeneousSection X L s)
      (sectionModule (sectionSiteRing X) (sectionSiteSheaf X) L F)) =
        LocalizedModule.mk (S := Submonoid.powers (homogeneousSection X L s))
          (DirectSum.of _ (n : ℤ) m)
          ⟨(homogeneousSection X L s) ^ n, by exact ⟨n, rfl⟩⟩)
    (hdiv :
      ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨(sectionSiteRing X),
        Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ ((sectionSiteRing X)) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
        ((sectionSiteSheaf X))⟩).obj (F)).obj ((TensorPower.tensorPower (sectionSiteRing X)
        (sectionSiteSheaf X) L
          (n : ℤ))))).val.map (terminal.from _).op m =
      tensorSectionAtOpen X L F
        (nonvanishingOpen L s) n t
        ((TensorPower.tensorPower (sectionSiteRing X) (sectionSiteSheaf X) L
          (n : ℤ)).val.map (terminal.from _).op (sectionPower X L s n))) :
    sectionLocalizationMap X L F s z = t
declarations.comment: homogeneous fraction formula

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.sectionLocalizationMap_smul
declarations.doc:
The restriction-and-division map is linear over the induced map from the
degree-zero homogeneous localization of the section ring to functions on `X_s`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem sectionLocalizationMap_smul (s : L.sections) :
    let U := nonvanishingOpen L s
    letI : Module
        ((TensorSheafification.structureSheaf (sectionSiteRing X)
          (sectionSiteSheaf X)).obj.obj (op U))
        (F.val.obj (op U)) := (F.val.obj (op U)).isModule
    ∃ φ : HomogeneousLocalization.Away
        (sectionRingGrading (sectionSiteRing X) (sectionSiteSheaf X) L)
        (homogeneousSection X L s) →+*
          (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf (sectionSiteRing X)
            (sectionSiteSheaf X)).obj.obj (op U),
      ∀ (a : HomogeneousLocalization.Away
          (sectionRingGrading (sectionSiteRing X) (sectionSiteSheaf X) L)
          (homogeneousSection X L s)) (z : sectionAtNonvanishingOpen X L F s),
        sectionLocalizationMap X L F s (a • z) =
          φ a • sectionLocalizationMap X L F s z
declarations.comment: localized-ring linearity

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.homAtNonvanishingOpen
declarations.doc: The degree-zero localization of the actual graded Hom module.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable def homAtNonvanishingOpen (s : L.sections)
declarations.comment: graded Hom localization

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.homLocalizationMap
declarations.doc:
Restrict a degree-zero localized graded morphism to the open where `s`
trivializes `L`, dividing its degree-`n` numerator by `sⁿ`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def homLocalizationMap (s : L.sections) :
    homAtNonvanishingOpen X L F G s →+
      (F.over (nonvanishingOpen L s) ⟶
        G.over (nonvanishingOpen L s))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.homLocalizationMap_fraction
declarations.doc:
A homogeneous morphism `f : F ⟶ G ⊗ Lⁿ`, divided by `sⁿ`, restricts
to the unique morphism on `X_s` whose tensor product with `sⁿ` is the
restriction of `f`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homLocalizationMap_fraction (s : L.sections) (n : ℕ)
    (f : F ⟶ (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
        ⟨(sectionSiteRing X), Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ ((sectionSiteRing X))
        (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) ((sectionSiteSheaf X))⟩).obj (G)).obj
        ((TensorPower.tensorPower (sectionSiteRing X)
        (sectionSiteSheaf X) L (n : ℤ)))))
    (t : (sheafHomSpace X.toRingedSpace F G).val.obj
        (op (nonvanishingOpen L s)))
    (hdiv :
      ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨(sectionSiteRing X),
          Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ ((sectionSiteRing X)) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
          ((sectionSiteSheaf X))⟩).obj ((sheafHomSpace X.toRingedSpace F G))).obj
          ((TensorPower.tensorPower (sectionSiteRing X)
          (sectionSiteSheaf X) L (n : ℤ))))).val.map
            (terminal.from _).op
              (homToTwistedSection X L F G n f) =
      tensorSectionAtOpen X L
        (sheafHomSpace X.toRingedSpace F G)
        (nonvanishingOpen L s) n t
        ((TensorPower.tensorPower (sectionSiteRing X)
          (sectionSiteSheaf X) L (n : ℤ)).val.map
            (terminal.from _).op (sectionPower X L s n))) :
    homLocalizationMap X L F G s (homFractionClass X L F G s n f) = ⟨t⟩
declarations.comment: homogeneous fraction formula

declarations.name: Stacks.ProperRelativeAmpleProjective.isLocallyProjective_of_isProper_of_exists_isRelativelyAmple
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B5N].** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a proper morphism of schemes. If there exists an
`f`-ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module, then `f` is locally projective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyProjective_of_isProper_of_exists_isRelativelyAmple {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f]
    (hL : ∃ (L : X.Modules) (h : IsInvertibleModule X L),
      letI := h; Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L) :
    IsLocallyProjective f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isAmple_of_forall_isZero_h1_quasicoherentIdeal
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B5P].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact scheme and `𝓛` an invertible
`𝒪_X`-module. If every quasi-coherent submodule `𝒥 ⊆ 𝒪_X` admits an `n ≥ 1` with
`H¹(X, 𝒥 ⊗ 𝓛^{⊗ n}) = 0`, then `𝓛` is ample.

The hypothesis is clause (2) of the tag: a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals is a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module with a monomorphism into `𝒪_X`. It is specialised at the ideal sheaf of a closed
immersion, which is such a submodule — quasi-coherent by
`Stacks.Conormal.isQuasicoherent_idealSheaf` and included in `𝒪_X` by `kernel.ι` — and the
criterion `isAmple_of_forall_exists_isZero_h1_idealSheaf` then concludes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAmple_of_forall_isZero_h1_quasicoherentIdeal {X : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X]
    (L : X.Modules)
    [hL : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L]
    (hvan : ∀ (J : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace))
      (ι : J ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)), Mono ι →
      J.IsQuasicoherent → ∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧
        IsZero (((moduleGlobalSections X).rightDerived 1).obj
          ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
              ⟨((X.toRingedSpace)).presheaf, ((X.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩).obj (J)).obj
            ((tensorPower X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
              (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L (n : ℤ))))))) :
    IsAmple X L

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectionFormula.isAmple_of_hasEventuallyVanishingH1
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a quasi-compact scheme and `L` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module. If for every
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `I ⊆ 𝒪_X` there is an `n ≥ 1` with `H¹(X, I ⊗ L^{⊗ n}) = 0`, then
`L` is ample.

Here `CompactSpace X` is "`X` is quasi-compact", `Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L` is "`L` is
an invertible `𝒪_X`-module", and `Stacks.AmpleCohomologicalCriterion.HasEventuallyVanishingH1 X L`
is the vanishing hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_of_hasEventuallyVanishingH1 (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] (L : X.Modules)
    [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L]
    (h : Stacks.AmpleCohomologicalCriterion.HasEventuallyVanishingH1 X L) :
    Stacks.Ample.IsAmple X L

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjCoherentII.moduleFinite_truncation_of_isCoherent
declarations.doc:
Clause (4) of [Stacks, Tag 0B5Q], equivalently part (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0B5R]. For `S` a
Noetherian graded ring, `X = Proj S`, `ℱ` a coherent `𝒪_X`-module and `k ∈ ℤ`, the graded
`S`-module `⨁_{n ≥ k} Γ(X, ℱ(n))` is a finite `S`-module.

No generation hypothesis on `S` is assumed. The proof is the source's Veronese reduction: a
degree `d` is chosen by
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjCoherentII.exists_reductionDegree`, the degrees are split into the
`d` residue classes, each class is compared with the twisted global sections of a coherent sheaf
on `X' = Proj S⁽ᵈ⁾` where [Stacks, Tag 0AG6] (4) applies, and the `d` resulting finite families
are assembled over `S` by
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjTwistedSections.moduleFinite_gradedActionTruncation_of_residues`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem moduleFinite_truncation_of_isCoherent [IsNoetherianRing S]
    (F : (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj 𝒮).Modules) (hF : _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F) (k : ℤ) :
    letI := (twistedGlobalSectionsModule 𝒮 F).moduleInst
    Module.Finite S ((twistedGlobalSectionsModule 𝒮 F).truncation 𝒮 F k)
declarations.comment: clause (4)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.isNoetherian_proj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B5Q.** The projective spectrum of a Noetherian graded ring is a
Noetherian scheme.
declarations.statement:
public instance isNoetherian_proj
    {A : Type u} {σ : Type v} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [SetLike σ A] [AddSubgroupClass σ A] (𝒜 : ℕ → σ) [GradedRing 𝒜] :
    IsNoetherian (Proj 𝒜)
declarations.comment: proj_noetherian

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjNoetherian.proj_isNoetherian_and_coherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B5Q.** Let `A` be a Noetherian graded ring and `X = Proj A`. Then `X`
is a Noetherian scheme, and every coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ` satisfies the four assertions of the
lemma: `ℱ` is a quotient of a finite direct sum of twisting sheaves, each `Hᵖ(X, ℱ)` is a finite
`A₀`-module, the higher cohomology of the high twists vanishes, and each graded tail
`⨁_{n ≥ k} H⁰(X, ℱ(n))` is a finite `A`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem proj_isNoetherian_and_coherent :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj 𝒜) ∧
      ∀ F : SheafOfModules.{u} (projRingSheaf 𝒜), _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F →
        (∃ (r : ℕ) (dj : Fin r → ℤ)
            (b : Bicone fun j : Fin r => twistingSheaf 𝒜 (dj j)) (_ : b.IsBilimit)
            (φ : b.pt ⟶ F), Epi φ) ∧
          (∀ p : ℕ, Module.Finite (𝒜 0)
            ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars
              (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.GradedProperCohomology.specAlgebraRingHom (𝒜 0)
                (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.toSpecZero 𝒜))).obj
              (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.GradedProperCohomology.cohomologyOf
                (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj 𝒜) p F))) ∧
          (∀ p : ℕ, 0 < p → ∃ e₀ : ℤ, ∀ e : ℤ, e₀ ≤ e →
            IsZero (Hgroup (projRingSheaf 𝒜) ⊤ p (twistSheafOfModules 𝒜 F e))) ∧
          (∀ k : ℤ,
            letI := (ProjTwistedSections.twistedGlobalSectionsModule 𝒜 F).moduleInst
            Module.Finite A
              (TwistedGlobalSectionsModule.truncation 𝒜 F
                (ProjTwistedSections.twistedGlobalSectionsModule 𝒜 F) k))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjCoherentII.truncatedTwistedToShifted
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0B5R (3): the canonical map `N → N'`.** The comparison assembled from the global
sections of Tag 01MQ's maps carries the degrees `≥ k` part of `⨁_n H⁰(X, M̃(n))` into the
degrees `≥ k` part of `⨁_n H⁰(X, M(n)~)`, because it is degreewise.
declarations.statement:
def truncatedTwistedToShifted (k : ℤ) :
    twistedSectionsTruncation 𝒮 𝒨 k →+ shiftedSectionsTruncation 𝒮 𝒨 k
declarations.comment: part (3), the canonical map N → N'

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjCoherentII.moduleToTruncatedShiftedSections
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0B5R (4): for `k` small enough there is a canonical map `M → N'`.** The map is Tag
01MR's `M → ⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} H⁰(X, M(n)~)`, and "`k` small enough" is the hypothesis
`hlow : ∀ n < k, ∀ x ∈ 𝒨 n, x = 0` that `M` vanishes below degree `k`, which is what generators
of `M` in degrees `≥ k` give.
declarations.comment: part (4), the canonical map M → N'

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjCoherentII.exists_pos_forall_bijective_twistedToShiftedComponent
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0B5R (6).** For a Noetherian graded ring `A` and a graded `A`-module `M` there is a
positive `d` such that `N_n = H⁰(X, M̃(n)) → H⁰(X, M(n)~) = N'_n` is bijective for every `n`
divisible by `d`. The `d` is the common degree of a finite standard-open cover of `Proj(A)`,
which is the property the source's `d = lcm(deg f_i)` is used for.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pos_forall_bijective_twistedToShiftedComponent [IsNoetherianRing S] :
    ∃ d : ℕ, 0 < d ∧ ∀ n : ℤ, (d : ℤ) ∣ n →
      Function.Bijective (twistedToShiftedComponent 𝒮 𝒨 n)
declarations.comment: part (6), N_n ≅ N'_n for d | n

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjCoherentII.truncatedSections_finite_and_comparison
declarations.statement:
public theorem truncatedSections_finite_and_comparison [IsNoetherianRing S] [Module.Finite S M]
    {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → S) (deg : Fin r → ℕ) (hdeg : ∀ i, 0 < deg i)
    (hf : ∀ i, f i ∈ 𝒮 (deg i))
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin (Stacks.Veronese.gradeZero 𝒮) (Set.range f) = ⊤)
    (k : ℤ) :
    letI := (globalSectionsModuleMap 𝒮 𝒨).moduleInst
    letI := (twistedGlobalSectionsModule 𝒮 (associatedModuleSheaf 𝒮 𝒨)).moduleInst
    Module.Finite S ((globalSectionsModuleMap 𝒮 𝒨).truncation 𝒮 𝒨 k) ∧
      Module.Finite S ((twistedGlobalSectionsModule 𝒮
        (associatedModuleSheaf 𝒮 𝒨)).truncation 𝒮 (associatedModuleSheaf 𝒮 𝒨) k) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ twistedSectionsTruncation 𝒮 𝒨 k,
        twistedToShiftedSections 𝒮 𝒨 x ∈ shiftedSectionsTruncation 𝒮 𝒨 k) ∧
      (∃ k₀ : ℤ, ∀ k' ≤ k₀, ∀ m : M,
        (globalSectionsModuleMap 𝒮 𝒨).hom m ∈ shiftedSectionsTruncation 𝒮 𝒨 k') ∧
      (∃ n₀ : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n₀ ≤ n → Function.Bijective (degreeNToGlobalSections 𝒮 𝒨 n)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, ((Finset.univ.lcm deg : ℕ) : ℤ) ∣ n →
        Function.Bijective (twistedToShiftedComponent 𝒮 𝒨 n))
declarations.comment: all six parts: (1) N' is a finite A-module; (2) N is a finite A-module; (3) the canonical map N → N'; (4) the canonical map M → N' for k small enough, i.e. for every k at most some k₀; (5) M_n → N'_n is an isomorphism in all sufficiently large degrees; (6) N_n → N'_n is an isomorphism for d | n, with d the lcm of the degrees of homogeneous generators of A over A_0; (1), (2), (3), (5) and (6) for every k ∈ ℤ

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperAmpleCohomology.exists_epi_biproduct_tensorPowModule
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be proper with `S` Noetherian, let `ℒ` be an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module
and let `ℱ` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module. Then there are a finite index type `ι`, exponents
`d : ι → ℤ` and a surjection `⨁_{j ∈ ι} ℒ ^⊗ dⱼ ↠ ℱ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_epi_biproduct_tensorPowModule {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian S] [IsProper f] (F L : X.Modules)
    [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F]
    [IsInvertibleModule X L] (hL : IsAmple X L) :
    ∃ (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι) (d : ι → ℤ)
      (b : Bicone fun j : ι => tensorPowModule X L (d j)) (_ : b.IsBilimit)
      (p : b.pt ⟶ F), Epi p
declarations.comment: clause (2), the surjection from a finite direct sum of tensor powers; clauses (1), (3), (4) and (5) are not covered

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperAmpleCohomology.exists_isZero_Hgroup_tensorPowTwist
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, let `f : X ⟶ Spec R` be proper, let `ℒ` be an ample invertible
`𝒪_X`-module and let `ℱ` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module. Then there is a `d₀` with

`H ᵖ(X, ℱ ⊗ ℒ ^⊗ d) = 0` for every `d ≥ d₀` and every `p > 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isZero_Hgroup_tensorPowTwist {X : Scheme.{u}} {R : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) [IsProper f]
    (F L : X.Modules) [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] [IsInvertibleModule X L]
    (hL : IsAmple X L) :
    ∃ d₀ : ℕ, ∀ d p : ℕ, d₀ ≤ d → 0 < p →
      IsZero (Hgroup X.ringCatSheaf ⊤ p
        (Stacks.RelativeVeryAmple.tensorModules X F (tensorPowModule X L (d : ℤ))))
declarations.comment: clause (4), the eventual vanishing of the higher cohomology of the high twists of a coherent module, with one exponent serving every positive degree

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperAmpleCohomology.coherent_proper_ample
declarations.statement:
theorem coherent_proper_ample {X : Scheme.{u}} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) [IsProper f] (F L : X.Modules)
    [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L]
    (hL : Stacks.Ample.IsAmple X L) :
    RingHom.FiniteType
        ((sectionRingZeroHom X L).comp (specAlgebraRingHom R f)) ∧
      (∃ (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι) (d : ι → ℤ)
        (b : Bicone fun j : ι => Stacks.Ample.tensorPowModule X L (d j)) (_ : b.IsBilimit)
        (p : b.pt ⟶ F), Epi p) ∧
      (∀ p : ℕ, Module.Finite R
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (specAlgebraRingHom R f)).obj (cohomologyOf X p F))) ∧
      (∃ d₀ : ℕ, ∀ d p : ℕ, d₀ ≤ d → 0 < p →
        IsZero (Hgroup X.ringCatSheaf ⊤ p
          (Stacks.RelativeVeryAmple.tensorModules X F
            (Stacks.Ample.tensorPowModule X L (d : ℤ))))) ∧
      (∀ k : ℤ, Module.Finite (sectionRing L)
        (twistModule (F ⊗ Stacks.Ample.tensorPowModule X L k) L))
declarations.comment: all five clauses: the section ring is a finitely generated R-algebra, a finite direct sum of tensor powers of L surjects onto F, the cohomology of F is a finite R-module in every degree, the higher cohomology of the high twists of F vanishes, and the graded module of twisted sections in degrees at least k is a finite module over the section ring

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperAmpleCohomology.moduleFinite_cohomology
declarations.doc:
**Clause (3) of [Stacks, Tag 0B5T].** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, let `f : X ⟶ Spec R` be
proper, let `ℒ` be an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module and let `ℱ` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module. Then
`Hᵖ(X, ℱ)` is a finite `R`-module for every `p`.

This is `moduleFinite_cohomology_of_isProper` with the tag's remaining hypotheses bound; the
ample invertible module is not used, and the more general statement is the one to apply. The
tag's clause (3) is recorded here so that it sits on a declaration stating the clause in the
tag's own setting.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleFinite_cohomology {X : Scheme.{u}} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) [IsProper f] (F L : X.Modules)
    [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] [IsInvertibleModule X L] (_hL : IsAmple X L) (p : ℕ) :
    Module.Finite R ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (specAlgebraRingHom R f)).obj
      (cohomologyOf X p F))
declarations.comment: clause (3), the finiteness of the cohomology of a coherent module over the Noetherian base ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.hasEventualTwistCohomologyVanishing_of_isAmple
declarations.doc:
**The implication (1) ⟹ (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0B5U]**, at the tag's own hypotheses: `R`
Noetherian, `f : X ⟶ Spec R` proper, `𝓛` ample.

This is clause (4) of [Stacks, Tag 0B5T],
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperAmpleCohomology.exists_isZero_Hgroup_tensorPowTwist`,
read through the two comparisons of the implementation notes: ampleness is carried across by
`Stacks.PowerFamilyBridge.isAmple_of_modulesIsAmple` and the conclusion by
`isZero_rightDerived_moduleGlobalSections_of_isZero_Hgroup`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasEventualTwistCohomologyVanishing_of_isAmple {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [IsProper f] (hL : IsAmple X L) :
    HasEventualTwistCohomologyVanishing L
declarations.comment: the implication (1) ⟹ (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.hasIdealTwistH1Vanishing_of_eventualTwistVanishing
declarations.doc:
**The implication (2) ⟹ (3) of [Stacks, Tag 0B5U]**, on a locally Noetherian scheme and with
none of the tag's remaining hypotheses.

A quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals is a quasi-coherent submodule of the structure sheaf, which on a
locally Noetherian scheme is coherent ([Stacks, Tag 01Y1], the structure sheaf itself being
coherent); condition (2) then applies to it, and is read at `p = 1` and at an exponent at least
one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasIdealTwistH1Vanishing_of_eventualTwistVanishing [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (h : HasEventualTwistCohomologyVanishing L) : HasIdealTwistH1Vanishing L
declarations.comment: the implication (2) ⟹ (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isAmple_of_hasIdealTwistH1Vanishing
declarations.doc:
**The implication (3) ⟹ (1) of [Stacks, Tag 0B5U]**, on a quasi-compact scheme and with none
of the tag's remaining hypotheses. This is [Stacks, Tag 0B5P].
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAmple_of_hasIdealTwistH1Vanishing [CompactSpace X]
    (h : HasIdealTwistH1Vanishing L) : IsAmple X L
declarations.comment: the implication (3) ⟹ (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isAmple_of_eventualTwistVanishing
declarations.doc:
**The implication (2) ⟹ (1) of [Stacks, Tag 0B5U]**, at the tag's own hypotheses: `R`
Noetherian, `f : X ⟶ Spec R` proper. Both steps are unconditional; properness and the Noetherian
base enter only through `IsLocallyNoetherian X` and `CompactSpace X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAmple_of_eventualTwistVanishing {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [IsProper f] (h : HasEventualTwistCohomologyVanishing L) :
    IsAmple X L
declarations.comment: the implication (2) ⟹ (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.tfae_isAmple_twistCohomologyVanishing
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B5U].** For `R` Noetherian, `f : X ⟶ Spec R` proper and `𝓛` an invertible
`𝒪_X`-module, the three conditions

1. `𝓛` is ample;
2. the higher cohomology of `ℱ ⊗ 𝓛^{⊗ n}` vanishes for every coherent `ℱ` and all large `n`;
3. `H¹(X, ℐ ⊗ 𝓛^{⊗ n}) = 0` for some `n ≥ 1`, for every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `ℐ`

are equivalent. The implication (1) ⟹ (2) is clause (4) of [Stacks, Tag 0B5T]; the other two are
proved with none of the tag's hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tfae_isAmple_twistCohomologyVanishing {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [IsProper f] :
    List.TFAE
      [IsAmple X L, HasEventualTwistCohomologyVanishing L, HasIdealTwistH1Vanishing L]
declarations.comment: the three equivalent conditions

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleFiniteSurjective.isAmple_modulePullback_of_isFinite_surjective
declarations.doc:
**The forward half of [Stacks, Tag 0B5V]**, at the source's hypothesis list: `X` proper over a
Noetherian ring `R`, `f` finite and surjective. The hypotheses other than finiteness are inert;
`Stacks.AmpleFiniteSurjective.isAmple_modulePullback_of_isFinite` is the same statement without
them.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_modulePullback_of_isFinite_surjective (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [IsProper p] [IsFinite f] [Surjective f]
    (hL : IsAmple X L) :
    IsAmple Y ((modulePullback f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj L)
declarations.comment: the implication `L` ample ⟹ `f^* L` ample

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleFiniteSurjective.isAmple_iff_isAmple_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B5V].** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of schemes
proper over `R` — `X` through `p` and `Y` through `f ≫ p`, which is automatic since a finite
morphism is proper and properness composes — and let `L` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module. If `f` is
finite and surjective, then `L` is ample if and only if `f^* L` is ample.

Every binder is the source's: the Noetherian ring, properness over it, finiteness and
surjectivity of `f`, and invertibility of `L`. `⟹` is `isAmple_modulePullback_of_isFinite`, which
needs only finiteness; `⟸` is `isAmple_of_isAmple_modulePullback`, the source's cohomological
argument.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_iff_isAmple_modulePullback (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [IsProper p] [IsFinite f] [Surjective f] :
    IsAmple X L ↔ IsAmple Y ((modulePullback f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAmple_iff_invertibleCurveDegree_pos
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B5X].** Let `k` be a field, `X` a proper curve over `k` and `𝓛` an invertible
`𝒪_X`-module. Then `𝓛` is ample if and only if `deg(𝓛) > 0`.

The forward direction is `AlgebraicGeometry.invertibleCurveDegree_pos_of_isAmple_of_isCurve` of
`./CurveInputs.lean`. The converse composes the source's second paragraph,
`AlgebraicGeometry.hasAffinePowerOfDegreePos_of_isCurve` of `./CurveSection.lean`, with its third,
which enters through `AlgebraicGeometry.isAmple_of_exists_tensorPower_section_of_isCurve` above.

`hdim` is an explicit argument because `AlgebraicGeometry.invertibleCurveDegree` takes the
dimension bound as one; on a curve it is `le_of_eq (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one f)`, and it
is an unused argument of that definition, so any two proofs of it give the same degree.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAmple_iff_invertibleCurveDegree_pos [IsCurve k f] [IsProper f]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L] :
    Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X L ↔ 0 < invertibleCurveDegree k f hdim L
declarations.comment: both directions, for a proper curve over a field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.invertibleCurveDegree_pos_of_isAmple_of_isCurve
declarations.doc:
**The forward direction of [Stacks, Tag 0B5X], at the source's hypotheses.** On a proper
curve over a field an ample invertible module has positive degree.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.invertibleCurveDegree_pos_of_isAmple_of_devissage` with each of its
four inputs supplied by the theorems above.

The converse implication is `AlgebraicGeometry.isAmple_iff_invertibleCurveDegree_pos` of
`CurveAmple.lean`, which states both directions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem invertibleCurveDegree_pos_of_isAmple_of_isCurve [IsCurve k f] [IsProper f]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L]
    (hL : Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X L) :
    0 < invertibleCurveDegree k f hdim L
declarations.comment: the implication: `L` ample ⟹ `deg(L) > 0`, with no hypothesis beyond the tag's own; both directions are registered on `isAmple_iff_invertibleCurveDegree_pos`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAmple_iff_forall_invertibleCurveDegree_reducedComponent_pos
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B5Y], both directions.** Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a scheme proper of
dimension at most one over `k` and let `𝓛` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module. Then `𝓛` is ample if
and only if the degree of the restriction of `𝓛` to every one-dimensional irreducible component
of `X`, taken with its reduced induced closed subscheme structure, is positive.

The components of dimension one are the tag's `C₁, …, C_t`: they are indexed by their generic
points, `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ComponentDegrees.genericPointsOne X`, the reduced induced
subscheme is `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ComponentDegrees.reducedComponent`, and that it is a
proper curve over `k` is proved with no hypothesis.

The implication (1) ⟹ (2) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.invertibleCurveDegree_reducedComponent_pos_of_isAmple` of
`./ComponentPositivity.lean`, which has no hypothesis beyond the tag's own.

For the implication (2) ⟹ (1) the covering family of the source is formed: all the irreducible
components, which are finitely many because a scheme proper over a field is Noetherian. Each has
dimension zero or one. On a zero-dimensional one the restriction of `𝓛` is ample outright, and on
a one-dimensional one positivity of the degree makes it ample by the converse direction of
[Stacks, Tag 0B5X]; ampleness then descends to `X` along the finite surjection from the disjoint
union, by [Stacks, Tag 0B5V] together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.isAmple_sigma_of_forall_isAmple_pullback_sigmaι`.

**No hypothesis beyond the tag's own.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAmple_iff_forall_invertibleCurveDegree_reducedComponent_pos
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L] :
    Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X L ↔
      ∀ ζ : genericPointsOne X,
        0 < @invertibleCurveDegree k _ (reducedComponent X ζ) (reducedComponentι X ζ ≫ f)
          (isProper_reducedComponentι_comp k f ζ)
          (topologicalKrullDim_reducedComponent_le X hdim ζ)
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (reducedComponentι X ζ)).obj L)
          (SheafOfModules.isInvertible_pullback (reducedComponentι X ζ) L)
declarations.comment: both directions, at the tag's own indexing by the one-dimensional irreducible components with their reduced induced closed subscheme structure

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.invertibleCurveDegree_reducedComponent_pos_of_isAmple
declarations.doc:
**The implication (1) ⟹ (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0B5Y].** Let `k` be a field, let `X` be proper of
dimension at most one over `k` and let `𝓛` be an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module. Then the degree
of the restriction of `𝓛` to every one-dimensional irreducible component of `X`, taken with its
reduced induced closed subscheme structure, is positive.

The components of dimension one are indexed by their generic points,
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ComponentDegrees.genericPointsOne X`, and the reduced induced subscheme
is `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ComponentDegrees.reducedComponent`; that it is a proper curve over
`k` — integral, separated, of finite type and of dimension exactly one — is
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ComponentDegrees.isCurve_reducedComponentι_comp` together with
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ComponentDegrees.isProper_reducedComponentι_comp`, both proved with no
hypothesis. So this is the tag's own family `C₁, …, C_t` and its own conclusion.

**No hypothesis beyond the tag's own.** The reverse implication is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isAmple_iff_forall_invertibleCurveDegree_reducedComponent_pos` of
`ComponentCriterion.lean`, which states the full equivalence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem invertibleCurveDegree_reducedComponent_pos_of_isAmple [IsProper f]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L]
    (hL : Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X L) (ξ : genericPointsOne X) :
    0 < @invertibleCurveDegree k _ (reducedComponent X ξ) (reducedComponentι X ξ ≫ f)
      (isProper_reducedComponentι_comp k f ξ)
      (topologicalKrullDim_reducedComponent_le X hdim ξ)
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (reducedComponentι X ξ)).obj L)
      (SheafOfModules.isInvertible_pullback (reducedComponentι X ξ) L)
declarations.comment: the implication (1) ⟹ (2), at the tag's own indexing by the one-dimensional irreducible components with their reduced induced structure, with no hypothesis beyond the tag's own; the full equivalence is registered on `isAmple_iff_forall_invertibleCurveDegree_reducedComponent_pos`

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.RationalEquivalence.rationallyEquivalent_intersectionProduct_fibreCycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B60.** Let `X` be a nonsingular variety over an algebraically closed
field, of dimension `dX`. Let `W ⊆ X × ℙ¹` be a closed subvariety of dimension `s + 1` dominating
`ℙ¹`, let `a`, `b` be closed points of `ℙ¹` and let `W_a`, `W_b` be the fibres of `W` over them,
viewed as closed subschemes of `X`. Let `V ⊆ X` be the closure of a point `v`, of dimension `r`,
meeting `W_a` and `W_b` properly. Then `[V] · [W_a]_s ∼_rat [V] · [W_b]_s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationallyEquivalent_intersectionProduct_fibreCycle [DecidableEq X] (hX : IsRegular X)
    (dX r s : ℕ) (hdX : topologicalKrullDim X = (dX : WithBot ℕ∞))
