declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_intersectProperly_cycleComap_torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Remark 0B61: the moving lemma on an open subset of the nonsingular locus.**
Let `X ⊆ 𝐏(V)` be a closed subvariety of dimension `n` of the projective space of a vector space
of dimension `N + 1` over an algebraically closed field, let `U ⊆ X` be an open subscheme
contained in the nonsingular locus `X^{reg}`, given as an open immersion `j₀ : U ⟶ X` (written
`Y ⟶ X` below), let `Z ⊆ U` be a closed subvariety of dimension `d < n`, and
let `T_i ⊆ U` be finitely many closed subvarieties, `T_i` of dimension `d' i < n`. Then there is
a closed subvariety `C ⊆ 𝐏(V)` whose prime cycle intersects that of `X` properly, with

`(C · X)|_U = [Z] + ∑ m_j [Z_j]`

in the Tor-formula intersection product of Section 0B08, where `C · X` is supported on `C ∩ X`,
the `Z_j ⊆ U` are irreducible closed of dimension `d`, distinct from `Z`, with nonzero
multiplicities, and where, inside `U`,

* `dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) ≤ dim (Z ∩ T_i)` or `dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) + n ≤ d + d' i`, and
* `dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) < dim (Z ∩ T_i)` whenever `Z` does not intersect `T_i` properly in `U`.

The restriction of `C · X` to `U` is its coefficientwise inverse image `Stacks.Chow.cycleComap`
along `U ⟶ X ⟶ 𝐏(V)`. `U = X^{reg}` is the statement of Remark 0B61, `U` a quasi-projective
variety embedded in a closed subvariety `X` of `𝐏(V)` is the form the remark's 0B1U and 0B1V use,
and `j₀ = 𝟙 X` for a nonsingular `X` is Lemma 0B0E; the dimensions `d' i` may vary with `i`, the
source's single `d'` being the constant family.

**The first clause departs from the source's text, because the source's clause is false.** The
source asks for `dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) ≤ dim (Z ∩ T_i)` outright. When `Z ∩ T_i = ∅` this demands
`Z_j ∩ T_i = ∅` for every `j`, and that fails already for the projective Lemma 0B0E, where
`U = X = X^{reg}`. Take `X ⊆ 𝐏^3` a nonsingular quadric surface (`n = 2`) and `Z`, `T_1` two
distinct lines of one ruling (`d = d' = 1`), so that `Z ∩ T_1 = ∅`. A `C` as in the conclusion
must be a surface: if `dim C ≤ 1` then `C ∩ X` is finite and `Z` does not occur in `C · X`, and
if `C = 𝐏^3` then `C · X` has no component of dimension `1`. A surface `C` meets the line `T_1`,
and every component of `C ∩ X` through such a point has dimension exactly `1`, so it occurs in
`C · X` with a positive multiplicity and meets `T_1`; it is neither `Z` nor any admissible
`Z_j`. The argument is written out in full in the implementation notes of this module. The
disjunction is what condition (4) of the source's proof gives, and its first disjunct is the
source's inequality whenever `Z ∩ T_i` is nonempty, by Tag 0AZP; in the empty case the second
disjunct `dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) + n ≤ d + d' i` is what holds. The second clause is as the source has
it, and is vacuous exactly in the empty case. The statement on `X^{reg}` itself, with the source's
inequality whenever `Z ∩ T_i` is nonempty and proper intersection when it is empty, is
`exists_intersectProperly_cycleComap_regularLocus_eq`; the erratum is recorded in `errata.md`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_intersectProperly_cycleComap_torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct_eq
    (k V : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    [FiniteDimensional k V] [Nontrivial V] [DecidableEq (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)]
    {N n d : ℕ} (hV : Module.finrank k V = N + 1)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (iX : X ⟶ projectiveSpaceOfModule k V) [IsClosedImmersion iX]
    [IsVariety k (iX ≫ projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k V)]
    (hdimX : topologicalKrullDim X = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)) (hd : d < n)
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (j₀ : Y ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j₀] (hU : Set.range j₀.base ⊆ regularLocus X)
    [DecidableEq Y]
    (Z : IrreducibleCloseds Y)
    (hZd : topologicalKrullDim (Z : Set Y) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (T : ι → IrreducibleCloseds Y) {d' : ι → ℕ}
    (hd' : ∀ i, d' i < n)
    (hTd : ∀ i, topologicalKrullDim (T i : Set Y) = (d' i : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (XC : IrreducibleCloseds (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))
    (hXC : (XC : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) = Set.range iX.base) :
    ∃ (C : IrreducibleCloseds (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))
      (S : Finset (IrreducibleCloseds Y)) (m : IrreducibleCloseds Y → ℤ),
      AlgebraicCycle.IntersectProperly
          (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single C.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ))
          (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single XC.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ)) ∧
        cycleComap j₀ j₀.isOpenEmbedding.injective
            (cycleComap iX iX.isClosedEmbedding.injective
              (TorFormula.torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct (fieldChowSituation k)
                (projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k V) (isRegular_projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)
                (d : ℤ)
                (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single C.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ))
                (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single XC.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ)))) =
          Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single Z.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ) +
            ∑ W ∈ S, m W • Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single
              W.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ) ∧
        (∀ p : projectiveSpaceOfModule k V,
          TorFormula.torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct (fieldChowSituation k)
              (projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k V) (isRegular_projectiveSpaceOfModule k V) (d : ℤ)
              (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single C.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ))
              (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single XC.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ)) p ≠
              0 →
            p ∈ (C : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ∩
              (XC : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))) ∧
        Z ∉ S ∧ (∀ W ∈ S, m W ≠ 0) ∧
        (∀ W ∈ S, topologicalKrullDim (W : Set Y) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧
        (∀ W ∈ S, ∀ i,
          topologicalKrullDim ↥((W : Set Y) ∩ (T i : Set Y)) ≤
              topologicalKrullDim ↥((Z : Set Y) ∩ (T i : Set Y)) ∨
            topologicalKrullDim ↥((W : Set Y) ∩ (T i : Set Y)) +
                (n : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞) + (d' i : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧
        (∀ W ∈ S, ∀ i, ¬ AlgebraicGeometry.IntersectProperly Z (T i) →
          topologicalKrullDim ↥((W : Set Y) ∩ (T i : Set Y)) <
            topologicalKrullDim ↥((Z : Set Y) ∩ (T i : Set Y)))
declarations.comment: the variant of the moving lemma 0B0E stated there, for an arbitrary open subscheme U ⟶ X of the nonsingular locus of a closed subvariety X ⊆ 𝐏(V) (the source's U = X^reg), with the dimensions of the T_i allowed to vary; (C · X)|_U is the coefficientwise inverse image of the cycle C · X along U ⟶ X ⟶ 𝐏(V); the non-strict dimension clause is the disjunction dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) ≤ dim (Z ∩ T_i) or dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) + n ≤ d + d', as for 0B0E, because the source's inequality fails when Z ∩ T_i is empty

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_rationallyEquivalent_forall_intersectProperly_of_isQuasiProjectiveVariety
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0B61: the moving lemma for a nonsingular quasi-projective variety, for a finite
family of cycles.** Let `X` be a nonsingular quasi-projective variety over an algebraically closed
field, let `α` be an `r`-cycle on `X` and let `β i` be finitely many cycles on `X`, of dimensions
`s i`. Then there is an `r`-cycle `α'` with `α' ∼_rat α` which intersects every `β i` properly.

`X` is an open subscheme of a closed subvariety `X̄ ⊆ 𝐏(k^{N+1})`
(`exists_isOpenImmersion_projectiveSpaceOfModule_of_isQuasiProjectiveVariety`), contained in the
nonsingular locus of `X̄` because `X` is nonsingular, and the moving lemma on such an open subset
is `isMovableOff_of_isOpenImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_rationallyEquivalent_forall_intersectProperly_of_isQuasiProjectiveVariety
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsQuasiProjectiveVariety k sX] (hX : IsRegular X) {r : ℤ}
    (α : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) sX r)
    {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (s : ι → ℤ) (β : ∀ i, CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) sX (s i)) :
    ∃ α' : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) sX r,
      RationallyEquivalent (fieldChowSituation k) sX r α' α ∧
        ∀ i, AlgebraicCycle.IntersectProperly α'.1 (β i).1
declarations.comment: Lemma 0B1U for a nonsingular quasi-projective variety, which the remark asserts with the same proof; for a finite family of cycles `β i` of arbitrary dimensions `s i` in place of a single `s`-cycle, and with `r` and the `s i` arbitrary integers. Nonsingular is `IsRegular X`, quasi-projective variety is `IsQuasiProjectiveVariety`, cycles are the graded cycle groups `Stacks.Chow.CycleGroup` over `Spec k`, rational equivalence is Tag 02RW and proper intersection is Definition 0AZQ. The moving lemma is run on `X` as an open subset of the nonsingular locus of its closure in projective space, which is the version of Tag 0B0E the remark describes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct_mem_rationalEquivalences_of_isQuasiProjectiveVariety
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B61 for Theorem 0B1V.** Let `X` be a nonsingular quasi-projective
variety of dimension `n` over an algebraically closed field `k`. Let `α` be an `r`-cycle and `β`
an `s`-cycle on `X` which intersect properly, and assume `α ∼_rat 0`. Then `α · β ∼_rat 0`.

`X` is an open subscheme of a closed subvariety `X̄ ⊆ 𝐏^N` of the same dimension, inside the
nonsingular locus of `X̄`, and the proof of Tag 0B1V runs on such an open subscheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct_mem_rationalEquivalences_of_isQuasiProjectiveVariety
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsQuasiProjectiveVariety k p] (hX : IsRegular X) {n : ℕ}
    (hn : topologicalKrullDim X = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)) {r s : ℤ}
    (α : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) p r) (β : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) p s)
    (hαβ : AlgebraicCycle.IntersectProperly α.1 β.1)
    (hα : α ∈ rationalEquivalences (fieldChowSituation k) p r) :
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := isLocallyNoetherian_of_isRegular hX
    (⟨torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct (fieldChowSituation k) p hX (r + s - n) α.1 β.1,
        torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct_mem_cyclesOfDimension (fieldChowSituation k) p hX
          (r + s - n) α.1 β.1⟩ :
      CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) p (r + s - n)) ∈
      rationalEquivalences (fieldChowSituation k) p (r + s - n)
declarations.comment: Theorem 0B1V for a nonsingular quasi-projective variety `X` of dimension `n` over an algebraically closed field, which the remark asserts with the same proof: for an `r`-cycle `α` and an `s`-cycle `β` meeting properly (Tag 0AZQ) with `α` rationally equivalent to zero, the Tag 0B08 product `α · β` is a rationally trivial `(r + s - n)`-cycle. Quasi-projective variety is `IsQuasiProjectiveVariety`; the argument is run on `X` as an open subset of the nonsingular locus of its closure in projective space, the version of Tag 0B0E the remark describes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.exists_intersectProperly_cycleComap_regularLocus_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Remark 0B61: the moving lemma on the nonsingular locus.** Let `X ⊆ 𝐏(V)` be
a closed subvariety of dimension `n` of the projective space of a vector space of dimension
`N + 1` over an algebraically closed field, and let `X^{reg} ⊆ X` be the open subset of nonsingular
points (`Xreg`, an open subscheme of `X` whose underlying set is the regular locus; it exists by
`exists_opens_coe_eq_regularLocus`). Let `0 ≤ d, d' < n`, let `Z ⊆ X^{reg}` be a closed subvariety
of dimension `d` and let `T_i ⊆ X^{reg}`, `i ∈ ι`, be finitely many closed subvarieties of
dimension `d'`. Then there is a closed subvariety `C ⊆ 𝐏(V)` whose prime cycle intersects that of
`X` properly, with

`(C · X)|_{X^{reg}} = [Z] + ∑ m_j [Z_j]`

in the Tor-formula intersection product of Section 0B08 (restriction to `X^{reg}` being the
coefficientwise inverse image `Stacks.Chow.cycleComap` along `X^{reg} ⟶ X ⟶ 𝐏(V)`, and `C · X`
being supported on `C ∩ X`), where the `Z_j ⊆ X^{reg}` are irreducible closed of dimension `d`,
distinct from `Z`, with nonzero multiplicities, and, inside `X^{reg}`,

* `dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) ≤ dim (Z ∩ T_i)` whenever `Z ∩ T_i` is nonempty;
* `Z_j` intersects `T_i` properly, `dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) + n ≤ d + d'`, whenever `Z ∩ T_i` is empty;
* `dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) < dim (Z ∩ T_i)` whenever `Z` does not intersect `T_i` properly.

The source states the first clause without the nonemptiness guard. With `dim ∅ = -∞` (Tag 0055)
that would force `Z_j ∩ T_i = ∅` whenever `Z ∩ T_i = ∅`, and this is false: for `X ⊆ 𝐏^3` a
nonsingular quadric surface (so `X^{reg} = X`) and `Z`, `T_1` two distinct lines of one ruling,
every surface `C` meets `T_1` and some component of `C ∩ X` other than `Z` through such a point
occurs in `C · X`; see the implementation notes of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Intersection.MovingLemma.KeyLemma` and `errata.md`. In that empty
case the second clause is what holds. The strict clause is vacuous exactly when `Z ∩ T_i` is
empty.

The proof is `exists_intersectProperly_cycleComap_torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct_eq` on the
open subscheme `X^{reg}`, whose first clause `dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) ≤ dim (Z ∩ T_i) ∨
dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) + n ≤ d + d'` gives the two guarded clauses: the second disjunct gives the first
clause by Tag 0AZP on the nonsingular variety `X^{reg}`, which bounds `d + d' ≤ n + dim (Z ∩ T_i)`
when `Z ∩ T_i` is nonempty, and the first disjunct gives the second clause when `Z ∩ T_i` is
empty, since then `Z_j ∩ T_i` is empty too.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_intersectProperly_cycleComap_regularLocus_eq
    (k V : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    [FiniteDimensional k V] [Nontrivial V] [DecidableEq (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)]
    {N n d d' : ℕ} (hV : Module.finrank k V = N + 1)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (iX : X ⟶ projectiveSpaceOfModule k V) [IsClosedImmersion iX]
    [IsVariety k (iX ≫ projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k V)]
    (hdimX : topologicalKrullDim X = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)) (hd : d < n) (hd' : d' < n)
    (Xreg : X.Opens) (hXreg : (Xreg : Set X) = regularLocus X) [DecidableEq Xreg.toScheme]
    (Z : IrreducibleCloseds Xreg.toScheme)
    (hZd : topologicalKrullDim (Z : Set Xreg.toScheme) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (T : ι → IrreducibleCloseds Xreg.toScheme)
    (hTd : ∀ i, topologicalKrullDim (T i : Set Xreg.toScheme) = (d' : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (XC : IrreducibleCloseds (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))
    (hXC : (XC : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) = Set.range iX.base) :
    ∃ (C : IrreducibleCloseds (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))
      (S : Finset (IrreducibleCloseds Xreg.toScheme)) (m : IrreducibleCloseds Xreg.toScheme → ℤ),
      AlgebraicCycle.IntersectProperly
          (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single C.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ))
          (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single XC.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ)) ∧
        cycleComap Xreg.ι Xreg.ι.isOpenEmbedding.injective
            (cycleComap iX iX.isClosedEmbedding.injective
              (TorFormula.torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct (fieldChowSituation k)
                (projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k V) (isRegular_projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)
                (d : ℤ)
                (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single C.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ))
                (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single XC.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ)))) =
          Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single Z.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ) +
            ∑ W ∈ S, m W • Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single
              W.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ) ∧
        (∀ p : projectiveSpaceOfModule k V,
          TorFormula.torFormulaCycleIntersectionProduct (fieldChowSituation k)
              (projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k V) (isRegular_projectiveSpaceOfModule k V) (d : ℤ)
              (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single C.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ))
              (Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single XC.isIrreducible.genericPoint (1 : ℤ)) p ≠
              0 →
            p ∈ (C : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V)) ∩
              (XC : Set (projectiveSpaceOfModule k V))) ∧
        Z ∉ S ∧ (∀ W ∈ S, m W ≠ 0) ∧
        (∀ W ∈ S, topologicalKrullDim (W : Set Xreg.toScheme) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧
        (∀ W ∈ S, ∀ i, ((Z : Set Xreg.toScheme) ∩ (T i : Set Xreg.toScheme)).Nonempty →
          topologicalKrullDim ↥((W : Set Xreg.toScheme) ∩ (T i : Set Xreg.toScheme)) ≤
            topologicalKrullDim ↥((Z : Set Xreg.toScheme) ∩ (T i : Set Xreg.toScheme))) ∧
        (∀ W ∈ S, ∀ i, (Z : Set Xreg.toScheme) ∩ (T i : Set Xreg.toScheme) = ∅ →
          topologicalKrullDim ↥((W : Set Xreg.toScheme) ∩ (T i : Set Xreg.toScheme)) +
              (n : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞) + (d' : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧
        (∀ W ∈ S, ∀ i, ¬ AlgebraicGeometry.IntersectProperly Z (T i) →
          topologicalKrullDim ↥((W : Set Xreg.toScheme) ∩ (T i : Set Xreg.toScheme)) <
            topologicalKrullDim ↥((Z : Set Xreg.toScheme) ∩ (T i : Set Xreg.toScheme)))
declarations.comment: the version of the moving lemma 0B0E that the remark states, on the open subscheme X^reg of nonsingular points of a closed subvariety X ⊆ 𝐏(V) (an open of X whose underlying set is the regular locus, which exists by exists_opens_coe_eq_regularLocus); (C · X)|_{X^reg} is the coefficientwise inverse image of the cycle C · X along X^reg ⟶ X ⟶ 𝐏(V). The inequality dim (Z_j ∩ T_i) ≤ dim (Z ∩ T_i) is proved whenever Z ∩ T_i is nonempty, and when Z ∩ T_i is empty Z_j is proved to meet T_i properly: the unguarded inequality is false there (dim ∅ = -∞ would force Z_j ∩ T_i = ∅, refuted by two lines of one ruling on a nonsingular quadric surface in 𝐏^3, recorded in errata.md). The strict clause is as the source has it. Together with the quasi-projective Lemma 0B1U and Theorem 0B1V registered under this tag, this is the whole remark

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CohenMacaulayCurveSituation.isZero_firstCohomology_dualizingSheafOverField_tensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B62**, at the dualizing sheaf `ω_X = H^{-1}(f^×(𝒪_{Spec k}))` of
[Stacks, Tag 0BS2]. In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0B5D], if `ℒ` is an invertible `𝒪_X`-module which
is generated by its global sections and is not isomorphic to `𝒪_X`, then `H¹(X, ω_X ⊗ ℒ) = 0`.

By duality (`dualityVanishing_dualizingSheafOverField`) the tag reduces to
`H⁰(X, ℒ^{⊗ -1}) = 0`, which is `subsingleton_globalSections_inverse_of_generatingSections`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_firstCohomology_dualizingSheafOverField_tensor
    (L : S.X.Modules) [IsInvertible S.X.presheaf S.X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (σ : L.GeneratingSections)
    (hne : ¬ IsTrivial S.X.presheaf S.X.ringCatSheaf.property L) :
    IsZero (cohomologyOverField S.k S.f
      ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨S.X.presheaf,
        Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (S.X.presheaf) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
          (S.X.ringCatSheaf.property)⟩).obj
        (Stacks.Duality.dualizingSheafOverField S.f)).obj L)) 1)
declarations.comment: at the dualizing sheaf H^{-1}(f^×(𝒪_{Spec k})) of Tag 0BS2, nothing carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_exceptionalDivisorToCentre_residuePoint
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B63] clause (1), properness.** The exceptional divisor of the blowup of the
spectrum of a Noetherian local ring in its maximal ideal is proper over the residue field.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_exceptionalDivisorToCentre_residuePoint (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] :
    IsProper (exceptionalDivisorToCentre (residuePoint A))
declarations.comment: clause (1): the exceptional curve is proper over the residue field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDim_exceptionalDivisor_residuePoint
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B63] clause (1), the dimension.** The exceptional divisor of the blowup of
the spectrum of a two-dimensional Noetherian local domain in its maximal ideal is a curve.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_exceptionalDivisor_residuePoint (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2) :
    topologicalKrullDim (exceptionalDivisor (residuePoint A).ker) = 1
declarations.comment: clause (1): the exceptional curve has dimension one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_and_topologicalKrullDim_eq_one_and_isCohenMacaulay_exceptionalDivisor
declarations.doc:
In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0B4W], let `X` be the blowup of `Spec(A)` in the maximal ideal and
`E ⊆ X` its exceptional divisor. Then `E` is a proper Cohen–Macaulay curve over the residue field
`κ`: the morphism `E ⟶ Spec(κ)` is proper, `E` has dimension one, and `E` is Cohen–Macaulay.

Cohen–Macaulayness comes from the normality of `X` ([Stacks, Tag 0B4Z]): `E` is an effective
Cartier divisor on a normal scheme, so it satisfies `(S₁)`, which for a scheme of dimension at
most one is Cohen–Macaulayness.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_and_topologicalKrullDim_eq_one_and_isCohenMacaulay_exceptionalDivisor
    (S : RationalSingularitySituation.{u}) :
    IsProper (exceptionalDivisorToCentre (residuePoint S.A)) ∧
      topologicalKrullDim (exceptionalDivisor (residuePoint S.A).ker) = 1 ∧
      IsCohenMacaulay (exceptionalDivisor (residuePoint S.A).ker)
declarations.comment: clause (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCohenMacaulay_exceptionalDivisor_residuePoint_of_situation
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B63] clause (1), Cohen–Macaulayness.** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0B4W] the
exceptional divisor of the blowup of `Spec(A)` in the maximal ideal is Cohen–Macaulay.

The blowup is normal by [Stacks, Tag 0B4Z]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isNormal_blowUp_maximalIdeal_rationalSingularitySituation`), so the
exceptional divisor satisfies Serre's condition `(S₁)`; in dimension at most one that is
Cohen–Macaulayness.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCohenMacaulay_exceptionalDivisor_residuePoint_of_situation
    (S : RationalSingularitySituation.{u}) :
    IsCohenMacaulay (exceptionalDivisor (residuePoint S.A).ker)
declarations.comment: clause (1): in Situation 0B4W the exceptional curve of the blowup in the maximal ideal is Cohen-Macaulay

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BlowUpDualizing.isZero_firstCohomology_curveTwistSheaf
declarations.doc:
**`H¹(E, 𝒪_E(n)) = 0` for every `n ≥ 0`.**

From the restriction sequence `0 ⟶ ℐⁿ⁺¹ ⟶ ℐⁿ ⟶ i_*𝒪_E(n) ⟶ 0` and its long exact cohomology
sequence: `H¹(X, ℐⁿ) = 0` is [Stacks, Tag 0B4Y] and `H²(X, ℐⁿ⁺¹) = 0` is
`isZero_secondCohomology_exceptionalIdealPow`, so the term between them vanishes; and
`H¹(X, i_*𝒪_E(n))` is `H¹(E, 𝒪_E(n))` because cohomology does not change along a closed
immersion ([Stacks, Tag 01EX]).
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_firstCohomology_curveTwistSheaf (n : ℕ) :
    IsZero (((Stacks.Cohomology.AffineBase.moduleGlobalSections
        (exceptionalCurve S.A)).rightDerived 1).obj (curveTwistSheaf S.A (n : ℤ)))
declarations.comment: clause (4): H^1(E, O_E(n)) = 0 for n >= 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BlowUpDualizing.one_le_invertibleCurveDegree_and_isRegularLocalRing_of_eq_one
declarations.doc:
In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0B4W], with `E` the exceptional curve of the blowup of `Spec(A)` in
the maximal ideal and `𝒪_E(1)` the restriction of `𝒪_X(1)`, `deg 𝒪_E(1) ≥ 1`, and equality holds
only if `A` is a regular local ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem one_le_invertibleCurveDegree_and_isRegularLocalRing_of_eq_one :
    1 ≤ invertibleCurveDegree (ResidueField S.A)
        (exceptionalDivisorToCentre (Stacks.Blowup.residuePoint S.A))
        (le_of_eq (topologicalKrullDim_exceptionalDivisor_residuePoint S.A S.dimension_two))
        (curveTwistSheaf S.A 1) ∧
      (invertibleCurveDegree (ResidueField S.A)
          (exceptionalDivisorToCentre (Stacks.Blowup.residuePoint S.A))
          (le_of_eq (topologicalKrullDim_exceptionalDivisor_residuePoint S.A S.dimension_two))
          (curveTwistSheaf S.A 1) = 1 → IsRegularLocalRing S.A)
declarations.comment: clause (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BlowUpDualizing.nonempty_curveTwistSheafSections_iso_gradedPiece
declarations.doc:
**`H⁰(E, 𝒪_E(n)) = 𝔪ⁿ/𝔪ⁿ⁺¹` for every `n ≥ 0`.**

The global sections of the `n`-th twist on the exceptional curve, read as a module over `A`
through the structure morphism `E ⟶ X ⟶ Spec(A)`, are the `n`-th graded piece `𝔪ⁿ/𝔪ⁿ⁺¹` of the
maximal-ideal filtration. The quotient is written by the submodule `𝔪·𝔪ⁿ` of `𝔪ⁿ`, which is
`𝔪ⁿ⁺¹` by `AlgebraicGeometry.BlowUpDualizing.comap_subtype_eq_smul_top` and is the shape
`Ideal.Cotangent` uses.

This is read off the restriction sequence
`0 ⟶ ℐⁿ⁺¹ ⟶ ℐⁿ ⟶ i_*𝒪_E(n) ⟶ 0` and its long exact cohomology sequence: `H¹(X, ℐⁿ⁺¹) = 0` makes
`H⁰(X, ℐⁿ) ⟶ H⁰(X, i_*𝒪_E(n))` surjective, its kernel is the image of `H⁰(X, ℐⁿ⁺¹)`, and the
first map of the sequence is the inclusion of ideal sheaves, so that image is `𝔪ⁿ⁺¹` inside
`H⁰(X, ℐⁿ) = 𝔪ⁿ`. Both of the latter identifications are [Stacks, Tag 0B4Y]: `H¹(X, ℐⁿ⁺¹) = 0`
and `H⁰(X, ℐⁿ) = 𝔪ⁿ`. **No `H²` is used**, and no hypothesis beyond Situation
[Stacks, Tag 0B4W] is placed on `A`.

The cohomology on `E` is compared with the cohomology of the direct image on `X` by
[Stacks, Tag 01EZ] over the whole space
(`Stacks.Cohomology.AffineBase.sectionsRestrictionIsoTop`), and the `A`-module structure is the
restriction of scalars along `A ≅ Γ(X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ Γ(E, 𝒪_E)`, which
`ModuleCat.restrictScalarsComp'App` splits into the two steps.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_curveTwistSheafSections_iso_gradedPiece (n : ℕ) :
    Nonempty ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars
          ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of S.A)).inv ≫
            (exceptionalImmersion S.A ≫ blowUpToBase (centre S.A)).appTop).hom).obj
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.AffineBase.moduleGlobalSections (exceptionalCurve S.A)).obj
          (curveTwistSheaf S.A (n : ℤ))) ≅
      ModuleCat.of S.A ((IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S.A ^ n : Ideal S.A) ⧸
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S.A • ⊤ :
          Submodule S.A (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S.A ^ n : Ideal S.A))))
declarations.comment: clause (5): H^0(E, O_E(n)) = m^n/m^(n+1) for every n >= 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRelativelyVeryAmple_curveTwistSheaf_one
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B63] clause (2).** For a Noetherian local ring `(A, 𝔪, κ)`, with `X` the
blowup of `Spec(A)` in `𝔪` and `E ⊆ X` the exceptional divisor, the first twist `𝒪_E(1)` is very
ample for the structure morphism `E ⟶ Spec(κ)`.

Very ampleness is [Stacks, Tag 01VM],
`Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple`: there are a quasi-coherent `𝒪_{Spec κ}`-module
`F` and an immersion `E ⟶ 𝐏(F)` over `Spec(κ)` pulling `𝒪_{𝐏(F)}(1)` back to `𝒪_E(1)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyVeryAmple_curveTwistSheaf_one (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] :
    Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple
      (exceptionalDivisorToCentre (residuePoint A)) (curveTwistSheaf A 1)
declarations.comment: clause (2): the first twist on the exceptional curve is very ample over the residue field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BlowUpDualizing.nonempty_dualizingSheafOverField_iso_curveTwist
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B64], clause (1).** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0B4W] let `X` be the blowup of
`Spec(A)` in the maximal ideal with exceptional divisor `i : E ⟶ X`, let `ω_A` be a dualizing
module for `A` and let `ω_X` be the dualizing module of `X`, normalized relative to `ω_A` as in
[Stacks, Remark 0B4R]. Then `ω_E = ω_X|_E ⊗ 𝒪_E(-1)`, where `ω_E` is the dualizing sheaf
`Stacks.Duality.dualizingSheafOverField g` of `E` as a proper curve over the residue field `κ`.

This splices `AlgebraicGeometry.BlowUpDualizing.nonempty_exceptionalDualizingModule_iso_curveTwist`
(the adjunction formula, for the module `H¹(a(ω_X))`) with
`AlgebraicGeometry.BlowUpDualizing.nonempty_exceptionalDualizingModule_iso_dualizingSheafOverField`
(that module is the dualizing sheaf of `E` over `κ`).
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_dualizingSheafOverField_iso_curveTwist
    (ωA : ModuleCat.{u} S.A) (hωA : Stacks.Duality.IsDualizingRingModule S.A ωA)
    (ωX : (blowUpScheme S.A).Modules)
    (N : letI : IsLocallyNoetherian (rationalSingularitySituationBlowUp S).X :=
        isLocallyNoetherian_blowUpScheme S.A
      (rationalSingularitySituationBlowUp S).DualizingNormalization ωA ωX) :
    Nonempty (Stacks.Duality.dualizingSheafOverField
        (X := (cohenMacaulayCurveSituationExceptionalDivisor S).X)
        (cohenMacaulayCurveSituationExceptionalDivisor S).f ≅
      curveTwist S.A ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (exceptionalImmersion S.A)).obj ωX) (-1))
declarations.comment: clause (1) in Situation 0B4W: for omega_A a dualizing module for A and omega_X the dualizing module of the blowup X of Spec(A) in the maximal ideal, normalized relative to omega_A as in Remark 0B4R (DualizingNormalization: omega_X dualizing with f^!(omega_A) = omega_X in degree zero), omega_E = omega_X|_E tensor O_E(-1), omega_E the dualizing sheaf dualizingSheafOverField g of the exceptional curve E as a proper curve over kappa. The source's route, Lemmas 0AA4 and 0A9X, is followed: the adjunction formula and the normal sheaf O_E(-1) give H^1(a(omega_X)) = omega_X|_E tensor O_E(-1), and the propagation of the normalization along g ; j = i ; f identifies H^1(a(omega_X)) with dualizingSheafOverField g. The non-regularity of A is not used and not assumed (a generalization). Nothing is carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BlowUpDualizing.epi_normalizedPullbackMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B64], clause (3).** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0B4W] assume `A` is not
regular, let `ω_A` be a dualizing module for `A`, let `X` be the blowup of `Spec(A)` in the
maximal ideal and let `ω_X` be the dualizing module of `X`, normalized relative to `ω_A` as in
[Stacks, Remark 0B4R] (`DualizingNormalization`: `ω_X` is dualizing and `f^!(ω_A) ≅ ω_X` in
degree zero). Then the canonical map `f^*ω_A ⟶ ω_X` of [Stacks, Tag 0BBU]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RationalSingularitySituation.normalizedPullbackMap`) is surjective.

The source's proof: `ω_X|_E ≅ ω_E ⊗ 𝒪_E(1)` (clause (1)) is globally generated by
[Stacks, Tag 0B5H], reduced to `κ̄` through [Stacks, Tag 0E32]
(`CohenMacaulayCurveSituation.pullbackDualizingSheafOverFieldIso`); `H¹(X, ω_X(1)) = 0` lifts its
generators to `Γ(X, ω_X) = ω_A`, and an epimorphism onto `ω_X` is detected on the closed
fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_normalizedPullbackMap
    (hnot : ¬ IsRegularLocalRing S.A)
    (ωA : ModuleCat.{u} S.A) (hωA : Stacks.Duality.IsDualizingRingModule S.A ωA)
    (ωX : (blowUpScheme S.A).Modules)
    (N : letI : IsLocallyNoetherian (rationalSingularitySituationBlowUp S).X :=
        isLocallyNoetherian_blowUpScheme S.A
      (rationalSingularitySituationBlowUp S).DualizingNormalization ωA ωX) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian (rationalSingularitySituationBlowUp S).X :=
      isLocallyNoetherian_blowUpScheme S.A
    Epi ((rationalSingularitySituationBlowUp S).normalizedPullbackMap hωA N.normalizedIso)
declarations.comment: clause (3) in Situation 0B4W with A not regular: for omega_A a dualizing module for A and omega_X the dualizing module of the blowup X of Spec(A) in the maximal ideal, normalized relative to omega_A as in Remark 0B4R (DualizingNormalization: omega_X dualizing with f^!(omega_A) = omega_X in degree zero), the canonical map f^*omega_A -> omega_X of Tag 0BBU (normalizedPullbackMap) is surjective. The source's route: Tag 0B5H at E (via Tag 0E32 to kappa-bar, clause (2) of Tag 0B63 for very ampleness, clause (3) of Tag 0B63 for the degree) gives global generation of omega_X|_E = omega_E(1) (clause (1)); H^1(X, omega_X(1)) = 0 (clause (2), from that generation) lifts it to Gamma(X, omega_X) = omega_A; surjectivity is detected on the closed fibre. Nothing is carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BlowUpDualizing.isZero_firstCohomology_schemeTwist_of_dualizingNormalization
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B64], clause (2).** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0B4W] assume `A` is not
regular, let `ω_A` be a dualizing module for `A`, let `X` be the blowup of `Spec(A)` in the
maximal ideal and let `ω_X` be the dualizing module of `X`, normalized relative to `ω_A` as in
[Stacks, Remark 0B4R] (`DualizingNormalization`). Then `H¹(X, ω_X(n)) = 0` for every `n ≥ 0`.

The source's proof: `ω_X|_E ≅ ω_E ⊗ 𝒪_E(1)` (clause (1)) is generated by its global sections by
[Stacks, Tag 0B5H] (reduced to `κ̄` through [Stacks, Tag 0E32],
`CohenMacaulayCurveSituation.pullbackDualizingSheafOverFieldIso`), so its twists `(ω_X|_E)(n)`,
`n ≥ 0`, have no first cohomology (`isZero_firstCohomology_curveTwist_of_generatingSections`,
from clause (4) of [Stacks, Tag 0B63]); the restriction sequence and the eventual vanishing of
[Stacks, Tag 02O1] then give the vanishing on `X`
(`isZero_firstCohomology_dualizingTwist_of_restrictionVanishing`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_firstCohomology_schemeTwist_of_dualizingNormalization
    (hnot : ¬ IsRegularLocalRing S.A)
    (ωA : ModuleCat.{u} S.A) (hωA : Stacks.Duality.IsDualizingRingModule S.A ωA)
    (ωX : (blowUpScheme S.A).Modules)
    (N : letI : IsLocallyNoetherian (rationalSingularitySituationBlowUp S).X :=
        isLocallyNoetherian_blowUpScheme S.A
      (rationalSingularitySituationBlowUp S).DualizingNormalization ωA ωX)
    (n : ℕ) :
    IsZero (((cohomologyDeltaFunctor (blowUpScheme S.A)).functor 1).obj
      (schemeTwist S.A ωX n))
declarations.comment: clause (2)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitudeCanonical_derivedTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be a map of commutative rings and let `K` and `L` be complexes of `B`-modules. If
`K` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` as a complex of `B`-modules and `L`, after restriction of
scalars, has Tor amplitude in `[c, d]` as a complex of `A`-modules, then `K ⊗_B^L L`, after
restriction of scalars, has Tor amplitude in `[a + c, b + d]` as a complex of `A`-modules.

All three Tor amplitudes are those of Stacks 0652 at the canonical derived tensor product of
Stacks 0BYI, and `K ⊗_B^L L` is that canonical derived tensor product over `B`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasTorAmplitudeCanonical_derivedTensorProduct
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (K L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} B) ℤ) (a b c d : ℤ)
    (hK : HasTorAmplitudeCanonical B (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) a b)
    (hL : HasTorAmplitudeCanonical A
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A B)).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L)) c d) :
    HasTorAmplitudeCanonical A
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A B)).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        (((canonicalDerivedTensorProduct B).tensor.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)).obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L))) (a + c) (b + d)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitude_iff_localized_at_primes_iff_maximals
declarations.doc:
A complex of `B`-modules has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` over `A` if and only if its localisation
at every prime ideal `q` of `B` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` over `A_{q ∩ A}`; equivalently, it is
enough to test this at every maximal ideal of `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_iff_localized_at_primes_iff_maximals
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} B) ℤ) (a b : ℤ) :
    (StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.FaithfullyFlat.HasTorAmplitude
        ((CochainComplex.restrictScalars (algebraMap A B)).obj K) a b ↔
      ∀ (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime], HasTorAmplitudeAt A K q a b) ∧
    ((∀ (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime], HasTorAmplitudeAt A K q a b) ↔
      ∀ (m : Ideal B) (hm : m.IsMaximal),
        letI : m.IsPrime := hm.isPrime
        HasTorAmplitudeAt A K m a b)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedRelativeCupProduct.relativeCupProduct
declarations.doc:
**The relative cup product** `Rf_*K ⊗^L_{𝒪_Y} Rf_*M ⟶ Rf_*(K ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} M)`: the adjoint
transpose of the derived pullback-tensor comparison of Stacks 079U followed by the counit of
`Lf^* ⊣ Rf_*` in both tensor factors.  It is defined for arbitrary `K, M ∈ D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
def relativeCupProduct
    (K M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    ((Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.sheaf).obj
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).obj K)).obj
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).obj M) ⟶
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).obj
        (((Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).obj K).obj M)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedRelativeCupProduct.relativeCupProduct_natural
declarations.doc: The relative cup product is natural in both derived modules on the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeCupProduct_natural
    {K K' M M' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))}
    (k : K ⟶ K') (m : M ⟶ M') :
    (Functor.uncurry.obj
          (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.sheaf)).map
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).map k ×ₘ
          (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).map m) ≫
        relativeCupProduct f K' M' =
      relativeCupProduct f K M ≫
        (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).map
          ((Functor.uncurry.obj
            (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf)).map
              (k ×ₘ m))
declarations.comment: naturality in both complexes

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedRelativeCupProduct.relativeCupProduct_natural_left
declarations.doc: The relative cup product is natural in the first derived module.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeCupProduct_natural_left
    {K K' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))}
    (k : K ⟶ K')
    (M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    ((Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.sheaf).map
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).map k)).app
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).obj M) ≫
        relativeCupProduct f K' M =
      relativeCupProduct f K M ≫
        (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).map
          (((Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).map k).app M)
declarations.comment: naturality in the first complex

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedRelativeCupProduct.relativeCupProduct_natural_right
declarations.doc: The relative cup product is natural in the second derived module.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeCupProduct_natural_right
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    {M M' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))}
    (m : M ⟶ M') :
    ((Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.sheaf).obj
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).obj K)).map
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).map m) ≫
        relativeCupProduct f K M' =
      relativeCupProduct f K M ≫
        (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f).map
          (((Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).obj K).map m)
declarations.comment: naturality in the second complex

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedInternalHomPushforward.pushforwardSheafHomMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B69: the canonical map `Rf_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, K) ⟶ R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, Rf_*K)`** for a
morphism of ringed spaces `f : (X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Y, 𝒪_Y)` and objects `K, L` of `D(𝒪_X)`.

By the tensor–internal-hom bijection of Stacks 08DI it is the same datum as a map
`Rf_*R𝓗om(L, K) ⊗^L_{𝒪_Y} Rf_*L ⟶ Rf_*K`, and that datum is the relative cup product of
Stacks 0B68 followed by the derived pushforward of the evaluation map.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.globalDerivedHom
declarations.doc:
The global derived hom `RHom_X(K, L) = RΓ(X, RSheafHom(K, L))` of a ringed space: the derived
internal Hom of two objects of `D(O_X)`, followed by derived global sections valued in modules over
the ring `Γ(X, O_X)` of global sections of the structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
def globalDerivedHom :
    (DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc))ᵒᵖ ⥤
      DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (GlobalSectionRing (structureSheaf Rc)))
declarations.comment: the global derived hom RHom_X(K, L) = RΓ(X, RSheafHom(K, L)) in D(Γ(X, O_X)) of a ringed space

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.globalDerivedHomDegreeZeroEquiv
declarations.doc:
The degree-zero cohomology of `RHom_X(K, L)`, read on its underlying complex of abelian groups,
is the group of morphisms `K ⟶ L` in the derived category of `O_X`-modules.
declarations.statement:
def globalDerivedHomDegreeZeroEquiv (K L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
        ((RingedSite.underlyingDerivedGroup (ringedSite Rc)).obj
          (((globalDerivedHom Rc).obj (op K)).obj L)) : Type u) ≃+ (K ⟶ L)
declarations.comment: the degree-zero cohomology of RHom_X(K, L) is Hom_{D(O_X)}(K, L)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.globalDerivedHomHomologyZeroEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The degree-zero cohomology of the global derived hom of a ringed space**, with no
hypothesis: `H^0(RHom_X(K, L))`, read on its underlying complex of abelian groups, is the group
of morphisms `K ⟶ L` in `D(O_X)`.
declarations.statement:
def globalDerivedHomHomologyZeroEquiv (K L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
        ((RingedSite.underlyingDerivedGroup (ringedSite Rc)).obj
          (((globalDerivedHom Rc).obj (op K)).obj L)) : Type u) ≃+ (K ⟶ L)
declarations.comment: H^0(RHom_X(K, L)) = Hom_{D(O_X)}(K, L), for an arbitrary ringed space

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.globalDerivedHomHomologyEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The cohomology of the global derived hom of a ringed space in every degree**, with no
hypothesis: for every integer `p`, `H^p(RHom_X(K, L))`, read on its underlying complex of abelian
groups, is the group `Ext^p_{D(O_X)}(K, L) = Hom_{D(O_X)}(K, L[p])`.
declarations.statement:
def globalDerivedHomHomologyEquiv (K L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)) (p : ℤ) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} p).obj
        ((RingedSite.underlyingDerivedGroup (ringedSite Rc)).obj
          (((globalDerivedHom Rc).obj (op K)).obj L)) : Type u) ≃+ (K ⟶ L⟦p⟧)
declarations.comment: H^p(RHom_X(K, L)) = Ext^p_{D(O_X)}(K, L) = Hom_{D(O_X)}(K, L[p]) for every p ∈ ℤ, for an arbitrary ringed space

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.globalDerivedHomPullbackMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B6A, the canonical map `RHom_X(K, L) ⟶ RHom_Y(Lf^*K, Lf^*L)`** in `D(Γ(X, O_X))`
for a morphism of ringed spaces `f : (Y, O_Y) ⟶ (X, O_X)` and objects `K`, `L` of `D(O_X)`; the
target, an object of `D(Γ(Y, O_Y))`, is read in `D(Γ(X, O_X))` by restriction of scalars along
the ring map `ringedSpaceGlobalSectionRingMap f : Γ(X, O_X) ⟶ Γ(Y, O_Y)`.

It is obtained by taking global sections of the map
`Lf^* RSheafHom(K, L) ⟶ RSheafHom(Lf^*K, Lf^*L)` of Stacks 08I3
(`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedInternalHomPullback.derivedPullbackSheafHomMap`), preceded by the
canonical map `RΓ(X, N) ⟶ RΓ(Y, Lf^*N)` at `N = RSheafHom(K, L)`
(`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedSectionsPullback.sectionsPullback`: derived global sections of the unit
of `Lf^* ⊣ Rf_*`, then `RΓ(X, Rf_* -) = RΓ(Y, -)`). Derived global sections are passed between
the ringed site and the open `X` (resp. `Y`) of the space by `derivedGlobalSectionsTopIso`, and the
scalars of `Γ(Y, O_Y)` are restricted to `Γ(X, O_X)` by
`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedSectionsPullback.changeScalarsIso`.
declarations.statement:
def globalDerivedHomPullbackMap
    (K L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf)) :
    ((globalDerivedHom X.sheaf).obj (op K)).obj L ⟶
      (derivedRestrictScalars (ringedSpaceGlobalSectionRingMap f)).obj
        (((globalDerivedHom Y.sheaf).obj
            (op ((derivedPullback f).obj K))).obj ((derivedPullback f).obj L))
declarations.comment: the canonical map RHom_X(K, L) → RHom_Y(Lf^*K, Lf^*L) in D(Γ(X, O_X)) of a morphism of ringed spaces f : Y → X, by global sections of the map of Remark 08I3

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedProjectionFormula.projectionFormulaMap_derivedBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B6B: the derived projection-formula map is compatible with a commutative square of
ringed spaces.**

For a commutative square `g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g` of ringed spaces and arbitrary `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)`,
`K ∈ D(𝒪_Y)`, the diagram `ProjectionFormulaBaseChangeSquare` commutes at the derived
projection-formula map of Stacks 0B53 for `f` and for `f'`, the derived base change map of
Stacks 08HY and the identification `derivedPullbackSquareIso`: the comparison of Stacks 079U for
`g`, followed by base change in the first tensor factor and by the projection-formula map for
`f'`, equals the derived pullback along `g` of the projection-formula map for `f`, followed by
base change and by `Rf'_*` of the comparison of Stacks 079U for `g'` and of the identification
in the second tensor factor.

There is no boundedness, flatness or quasi-coherence hypothesis on `E` and `K`, and no
associator or symmetry of `⊗^L` is used: the diagram has binary tensor products only.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectionFormulaMap_derivedBaseChangeMap
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y))) :
    ProjectionFormulaBaseChangeSquare (derivedPushforward f) (derivedPushforward f')
      (derivedPullback f) (derivedPullback f') (derivedPullback g) (derivedPullback g')
      (Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.sheaf))
      (Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf))
      (Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor Y'.sheaf))
      (Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor X'.sheaf))
      (pullbackTensorComparison g) (pullbackTensorComparison g') E K
      (projectionFormulaMap f E K)
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.derivedBaseChangeMap g' f' f g sq
        ((Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf)).obj
          (E, (derivedPullback f).obj K)))
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.derivedBaseChangeMap g' f' f g sq E)
      ((derivedPullbackSquareIso g' f' f g sq).inv.app K)
      (projectionFormulaMap f' ((derivedPullback g').obj E) ((derivedPullback g).obj K))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedProjectionFormula.projectionFormulaMapRight_derivedBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**The right-handed projection-formula map is compatible with a commutative square of ringed
spaces.**

For a commutative square `g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g` of ringed spaces and arbitrary `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)`,
`K ∈ D(𝒪_Y)`, the diagram `ProjectionFormulaBaseChangeSquare` commutes at the right-handed
projection-formula map `projectionFormulaMapRight` for `f` and for `f'`, the derived base change
map of Stacks 08HY and the identification `derivedPullbackSquareIso`, with the derived tensor
products read with their arguments interchanged.  This is
`projectionFormulaMap_derivedBaseChangeMap` with the pushforward in the right tensor factor.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectionFormulaMapRight_derivedBaseChangeMap
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y))) :
    ProjectionFormulaBaseChangeSquare (derivedPushforward f) (derivedPushforward f')
      (derivedPullback f) (derivedPullback f') (derivedPullback g) (derivedPullback g')
      (CategoryTheory.Prod.swap _ _ ⋙ Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.sheaf))
      (CategoryTheory.Prod.swap _ _ ⋙ Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf))
      (CategoryTheory.Prod.swap _ _ ⋙ Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor Y'.sheaf))
      (CategoryTheory.Prod.swap _ _ ⋙ Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor X'.sheaf))
      (pullbackTensorComparisonSwap g) (pullbackTensorComparisonSwap g') E K
      (projectionFormulaMapRight f K E)
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.derivedBaseChangeMap g' f' f g sq
        ((CategoryTheory.Prod.swap _ _ ⋙
          Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf)).obj
            (E, (derivedPullback f).obj K)))
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.derivedBaseChangeMap g' f' f g sq E)
      ((derivedPullbackSquareIso g' f' f g sq).inv.app K)
      (projectionFormulaMapRight f' ((derivedPullback g).obj K) ((derivedPullback g').obj E))
declarations.comment: the right-handed form: the pushforward in the right tensor factor

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeCupProductOnRingedTopoi.relativeCupProduct
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B6C].**  For a morphism of ringed topoi
`f : (Sh(C), O_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), O_D)` and objects `K`, `L` of `D(O_C)`, the canonical relative cup
product

`Rf_*K ⊗^L_{O_D} Rf_*L ⟶ Rf_*(K ⊗^L_{O_C} L)`,

with no further hypothesis.  It is the map adjoint, for the adjunction `Lf^* ⊣ Rf_*` of
[Stacks, Tag 07A6], to the bifunctorial identification
`Lf^*(Rf_*K ⊗^L Rf_*L) ≅ Lf^*Rf_*K ⊗^L Lf^*Rf_*L` of [Stacks, Tag 07A4] followed by the counit
`Lf^*Rf_* ⟶ id` in each of the two factors.
declarations.statement:
def relativeCupProduct
    (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.O).obj ((derivedPushforward f).obj K)).obj
        ((derivedPushforward f).obj L) ⟶
      (derivedPushforward f).obj (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.O).obj K).obj L)
declarations.comment: the relative cup product

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeCupProductOnRingedTopoi.relativeCupProduct_naturality_left
declarations.doc: **Naturality of the relative cup product of [Stacks, Tag 0B6C] in the first object.**
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeCupProduct_naturality_left
    {K K' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (k : K ⟶ K')
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.O).map ((derivedPushforward f).map k)).app
          ((derivedPushforward f).obj L) ≫
        relativeCupProduct f hmos K' L =
      relativeCupProduct f hmos K L ≫
        (derivedPushforward f).map (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.O).map k).app L)
declarations.comment: naturality in the first object

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeCupProductOnRingedTopoi.relativeCupProduct_naturality_right
declarations.doc: **Naturality of the relative cup product of [Stacks, Tag 0B6C] in the second object.**
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeCupProduct_naturality_right
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    {L L' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (l : L ⟶ L') :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.O).obj ((derivedPushforward f).obj K)).map
          ((derivedPushforward f).map l) ≫
        relativeCupProduct f hmos K L' =
      relativeCupProduct f hmos K L ≫
        (derivedPushforward f).map (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.O).obj K).map l)
declarations.comment: naturality in the second object

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeCupProductOfToposHom.relativeCupProduct
declarations.doc:
For a morphism of ringed topoi
`f : (Sh(C), 𝒪_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), 𝒪_D)` — a morphism of the underlying topoi together with the
structure map, with no functor between the underlying sites — and objects `K`, `L` of `D(𝒪_C)`,
the relative cup product

`Rf_*K ⊗^L_{𝒪_D} Rf_*L ⟶ Rf_*(K ⊗^L_{𝒪_C} L)`.

It is the map adjoint, for the adjunction `Lf^* ⊣ Rf_*` of [Stacks, Tag 07A6], to the
identification `Lf^*(Rf_*K ⊗^L Rf_*L) ≅ Lf^*Rf_*K ⊗^L Lf^*Rf_*L` of [Stacks, Tag 07A4] followed
by the counit `Lf^*Rf_* ⟶ id` in each of the two factors.
declarations.statement:
def relativeCupProduct
    (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.O).obj ((derivedPushforward f).obj K)).obj
        ((derivedPushforward f).obj L) ⟶
      (derivedPushforward f).obj (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.O).obj K).obj L)
declarations.comment: the relative cup product, for a morphism of ringed topoi in the two-field sense of Tag 01D3, part (2) -- a morphism of the underlying topoi together with the structure map, with no continuous functor between the underlying sites and no morphism-of-sites hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.ProjectionFormulaInternalHomOnRingedTopoi.derivedPushforwardSheafHomMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical map of [Stacks, Tag 0B6D] when the morphism of ringed topoi
`f : (Sh(C), O_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), O_D)` comes from a morphism of sites: for objects `L`, `M` of
`D(O_C)`, the map

`Rf_*RHom_{O_C}(L, M) ⟶ RHom_{O_D}(Rf_*L, Rf_*M)`.

It is the morphism which the tensor–internal-Hom bijection of [Stacks, Tag 08J8] on `D(O_D)`
sends to the relative cup product of [Stacks, Tag 0B6C] followed by `Rf_*` of the evaluation
morphism `RHom_{O_C}(L, M) ⊗^L_{O_C} L ⟶ M`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedPushforwardSheafHomMap
    (L M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    (derivedPushforward f).obj
        (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor (RingedTopos.toRingedSite X)).obj (op L)).obj M) ⟶
      ((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor (RingedTopos.toRingedSite Y)).obj
        (op ((derivedPushforward f).obj L))).obj ((derivedPushforward f).obj M)
declarations.comment:
the canonical map, variant: the special case of a morphism of ringed topoi
presented by a morphism of sites; the tag for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi is
Stacks.Cohomology.PushforwardInternalHomOfToposHom.derivedPushforwardSheafHomMap

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.ProjectionFormulaInternalHomOnRingedTopoi.derivedPushforwardSheafHomMap_homEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The defining property of the canonical map of [Stacks, Tag 0B6D]**: its adjunct under the
tensor–internal-Hom bijection of [Stacks, Tag 08J8] on `D(O_D)` is the relative cup product of
[Stacks, Tag 0B6C] followed by `Rf_*` of the evaluation morphism
`RHom_{O_C}(L, M) ⊗^L_{O_C} L ⟶ M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPushforwardSheafHomMap_homEquiv
    (L M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    (derivedTensorHomBijection (RingedTopos.toRingedSite Y)).homEquiv
        ((derivedPushforward f).obj
          (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor
            (RingedTopos.toRingedSite X)).obj (op L)).obj M))
        ((derivedPushforward f).obj L) ((derivedPushforward f).obj M)
        (derivedPushforwardSheafHomMap f hmos L M) =
      relativeCupProduct f hmos
          (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor
            (RingedTopos.toRingedSite X)).obj (op L)).obj M) L ≫
        (derivedPushforward f).map
          ((derivedTensorHomBijection (RingedTopos.toRingedSite X)).evaluation L M)
declarations.comment:
the defining adjunction property, variant: the special case of a morphism of
ringed topoi presented by a morphism of sites; the tag for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi
is Stacks.Cohomology.PushforwardInternalHomOfToposHom.derivedPushforwardSheafHomMap_homEquiv

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PushforwardInternalHomOfToposHom.derivedPushforwardSheafHomMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B6D].**  For a morphism of ringed topoi
`f : (Sh(C), O_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), O_D)` and objects `L`, `M` of `D(O_C)`, the canonical map

`Rf_*RHom_{O_C}(L, M) ⟶ RHom_{O_D}(Rf_*L, Rf_*M)`.

It is the morphism which the tensor–internal-Hom bijection of [Stacks, Tag 08J8] on `D(O_D)`
sends to the relative cup product
`Rf_*RHom(L, M) ⊗^L_{O_D} Rf_*L ⟶ Rf_*(RHom(L, M) ⊗^L_{O_C} L)` of [Stacks, Tag 0B6C] followed
by `Rf_*` of the evaluation morphism `RHom_{O_C}(L, M) ⊗^L_{O_C} L ⟶ M`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedPushforwardSheafHomMap
    (L M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    (derivedPushforward f).obj
        (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor (RingedTopos.toRingedSite X)).obj (op L)).obj M) ⟶
      ((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor (RingedTopos.toRingedSite Y)).obj
        (op ((derivedPushforward f).obj L))).obj ((derivedPushforward f).obj M)
declarations.comment: the canonical map, for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi (no morphism-of-sites hypothesis); its defining property is `derivedPushforwardSheafHomMap_homEquiv`

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PushforwardInternalHomOfToposHom.derivedPushforwardSheafHomMap_homEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The defining property of the canonical map of [Stacks, Tag 0B6D]**: its adjunct under the
tensor–internal-Hom bijection of [Stacks, Tag 08J8] on `D(O_D)` is the relative cup product of
[Stacks, Tag 0B6C] followed by `Rf_*` of the evaluation morphism
`RHom_{O_C}(L, M) ⊗^L_{O_C} L ⟶ M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPushforwardSheafHomMap_homEquiv
    (L M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    (derivedTensorHomBijection (RingedTopos.toRingedSite Y)).homEquiv
        ((derivedPushforward f).obj
          (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor
            (RingedTopos.toRingedSite X)).obj (op L)).obj M))
        ((derivedPushforward f).obj L) ((derivedPushforward f).obj M)
        (derivedPushforwardSheafHomMap f L M) =
      relativeCupProduct f
          (((RingedSite.derivedSheafHomBifunctor
            (RingedTopos.toRingedSite X)).obj (op L)).obj M) L ≫
        (derivedPushforward f).map
          ((derivedTensorHomBijection (RingedTopos.toRingedSite X)).evaluation L M)
declarations.comment: the defining property: the 08J8 adjunct of the canonical map is the relative cup product of 0B6C followed by Rf_* of evaluation, for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.globalDerivedHomModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B6E.** *Applying the construction of the internal hom in the derived category we
get the object* `RHom_O(K, L) = RΓ(C, RHom(K, L))` *in* `D(Γ(C, O))`: the derived internal Hom of
two objects of `D(O)`, followed by derived global sections valued in modules over the ring of
global sections of the structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
def globalDerivedHomModules :
    (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))ᵒᵖ ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ⥤
        DerivedCategory
          (ModuleCat.{u} (GlobalSectionRing (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
declarations.comment: the global derived hom RHom_O(K, L) = RΓ(C, RHom(K, L)) in D(Γ(C, O))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.globalDerivedHomModulesDegreeZeroEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B6E, the cohomology of the global derived hom.** The degree-zero cohomology of
`RHom_O(K, L)` is the group of morphisms `K ⟶ L` in `D(O)`. This is Stacks 08JA, which is the
statement the source cites for the cohomology modules of the global derived hom, transported to
`RHom_O(K, L)` of `D(Γ(C, O))` along
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedGlobalSectionsModulesForget`; the cohomology is read on the
underlying complex of abelian groups, as Stacks 08JA states it.
declarations.statement:
def globalDerivedHomModulesDegreeZeroEquiv
    (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
        ((underlyingDerivedGroup X).obj
          (((globalDerivedHomModules X).obj (op K)).obj L)) : Type u) ≃+ (K ⟶ L)
declarations.comment: the degree-zero cohomology of RHom_O(K, L) is Hom_{D(O)}(K, L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.globalDerivedHomPullbackMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B6E: the global derived hom along a morphism of ringed topoi.** For a morphism of
ringed topoi `f : (Sh(C'), O') ⟶ (Sh(C), O)` in the sense of Stacks 01D3, part (2), and objects
`K`, `L` of `D(O)`, the canonical map

`RHom_O(K, L) ⟶ RHom_{O'}(Lf^* K, Lf^* L)`

in `D(Γ(C, O))`, the target read through restriction of scalars along `Γ(C, O) ⟶ Γ(C', O')`. It is
the global sections of the map `Lf^* RSheafHom(K, L) ⟶ RSheafHom(Lf^* K, Lf^* L)` of Stacks 08JF
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.derivedPullbackSheafHomMap`): `RΓ(C, -)` of the unit
`RSheafHom(K, L) ⟶ Rf_* Lf^* RSheafHom(K, L)`, read as a map into `RΓ(C', Lf^* RSheafHom(K, L))`,
followed by `RΓ(C', -)` of the map of Stacks 08JF.
declarations.statement:
def globalDerivedHomPullbackMap
    (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))) :
    ((RingedSite.globalDerivedHomModules (RingedTopos.toRingedSite Y)).obj (op K)).obj L ⟶
      (globalSectionsRestrict f).obj
        (((RingedSite.globalDerivedHomModules (RingedTopos.toRingedSite X)).obj
          (op ((derivedPullback f).obj K))).obj ((derivedPullback f).obj L))
declarations.comment:
the canonical map RHom_O(K, L) -> RHom_O'(Lf^*K, Lf^*L) in D(Γ(O)) along a
morphism of ringed topoi f, given by global sections of the map of Tag 08JF

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.globalDerivedHomDegreeEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B6E, the cohomology of the global derived hom in every degree.** The degree-`n`
cohomology of `RHom_O(K, L)` is the group of morphisms `K ⟶ L[n]` in `D(O)`, that is the
`Ext`-group `Ext^n_{D(O)}(K, L)`. This is the abelian-group-valued reading
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.globalDerivedHom` of the global derived hom.

The degree is moved into the covariant variable: the homology functors of the derived category
form a shift sequence, derived global sections commute with the translation, and the derived
internal Hom commutes with the translation in its covariant variable by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHomTargetShiftIso`; in degree zero the cohomology is
the morphism group by Stacks 08JA, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHomGlobalSectionsEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
def globalDerivedHomDegreeEquiv
    (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (n : ℤ) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} n).obj
        (((globalDerivedHom X).obj (op K)).obj L) : Type u) ≃+ (K ⟶ L⟦n⟧)
declarations.comment: the degree-n cohomology of RHom_O(K, L) is Hom_{D(O)}(K, L[n])

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.globalDerivedHomModulesDegreeEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B6E, the cohomology of the global derived hom in every degree**, for the
`D(Γ(C, O))`-valued global derived hom `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.globalDerivedHomModules`:
the degree-`n` cohomology of `RHom_O(K, L)`, read on the underlying complex of abelian groups as
Stacks 08JA states it, is the group of morphisms `K ⟶ L[n]` of `D(O)`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.globalDerivedHomDegreeEquiv` transported along
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedGlobalSectionsModulesForget`, and it is the degree-`n` form
of `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.globalDerivedHomModulesDegreeZeroEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
def globalDerivedHomModulesDegreeEquiv
    (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (n : ℤ) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} n).obj
        ((underlyingDerivedGroup X).obj
          (((globalDerivedHomModules X).obj (op K)).obj L)) : Type u) ≃+ (K ⟶ L⟦n⟧)
declarations.comment: the degree-n cohomology of RHom_O(K, L) in D(Γ(C, O)) is Hom_{D(O)}(K, L[n])

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedStructureSheafGlobalSectionsDegreeEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Hypercohomology in every degree is morphisms out of the structure sheaf.** For an object
`Z` of `D(O)` the hypercohomology group `H^n(C, Z)`, the degree-`n` homology of unbounded derived
global sections, is the group `Hom_{D(O)}(O[0], Z[n])`.

This is Tag 08JA at source the structure sheaf in every degree: derived global sections of the
identification `RSheafHom(O[0], Z) ≅ Z` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedStructureSheafHomIso` turn `H^n(C, Z)` into the degree-`n`
cohomology of the global derived hom `RHom_O(O[0], Z)`, which is `Hom(O[0], Z[n])` by Tag 0B6E
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.globalDerivedHomDegreeEquiv`). In degree zero it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedStructureSheafGlobalSectionsEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedStructureSheafGlobalSectionsDegreeEquiv
    (Z : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringSheaf X.O))) (n : ℤ) :
    ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} n).obj
        ((derivedModuleGlobalSections X).obj Z) : Type u) ≃+
      (derivedStructureSheaf X ⟶ Z⟦n⟧)
declarations.comment: the case K = O[0], where RHom_O(O[0], Z) is RGamma(C, Z)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectPushforward.isPerfect_derivedPushforward_of_flat_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B6F].** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme and `f : X ⟶ S` a flat proper morphism
of schemes. Let `E` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`. Then `Rf_*E` is a perfect object of
`D(𝒪_S)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedPushforward_of_flat_of_isProper [IsNoetherian S] [Flat f] [IsProper f] :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (OXMod.{u, u} S.toRingedSpace)
    ∀ E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace),
      RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) E →
        RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := S.toRingedSpace) ((derivedPushforwardOX f).obj E)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PerfectProperDirectImage.isPerfect_derivedPushforward_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B6G].** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme, let `f : X ⟶ S` be a perfect proper
morphism of schemes and let `E` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`. Then `Rf_*E` is a perfect object
of `D(𝒪_S)`.

By [Stacks, Tag 08CQ] perfectness is pseudo-coherence together with locally finite Tor dimension.
Pseudo-coherence is `isPseudoCoherent_derivedPushforward_of_isPerfect`, and the Tor-dimension half
is `hasFiniteTorDimension_derivedPushforward_affineOpen` fed into
`isPerfect_derivedPushforward_of_isPerfect_of_forall_affineOpen`. Nothing is assumed beyond the
source's own hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedPushforward_of_isPerfect {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsNoetherian S] [Perfect f] [IsProper f] (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) E) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := S.toRingedSpace)
      ((derivedPushforwardModules f).obj E)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PerfectProperDirectImage.isPseudoCoherent_derivedPushforward_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B6G], the pseudo-coherence half of the conclusion, with no hypothesis.** Let
`S` be a Noetherian scheme, let `f : X ⟶ S` be a perfect proper morphism of schemes and let `E`
be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`. Then `Rf_*E` is a pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_S)`.

By [Stacks, Tag 08CQ] perfectness is pseudo-coherence together with locally finite Tor
dimension; this is the first of the two. The hypotheses the pseudo-coherence half of
[Stacks, Tag 08EV] makes of `E` are supplied by `isCoherent_homology_and_bounds_of_isPerfect`,
and its support hypothesis by the fact that every closed subset of the source of a proper
morphism is proper over the target. The hypothesis that half carries for [Stacks, Tag 02O5] is
supplied by the proof of [Stacks, Tag 02O5] in this tree,
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProperCoherenceWitness.higherDirectImageIsCoherentOverAffineBase`, so it is
not assumed here.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_derivedPushforward_of_isPerfect [IsNoetherian S]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.Perfect f] [IsProper f] (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) E) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := S.toRingedSpace)
      ((derivedPushforwardModules f).obj E)
declarations.comment: the pseudo-coherence half of the conclusion: Rf_*E is a pseudo-coherent object of D(𝒪_S), proved under the source's own hypotheses and no others

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.sheafyTrace
declarations.doc:
**Equation 48.3.0.1 of [Stacks, Tag 0B6H].** For a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y`, a right
adjoint `a` of `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, and objects `L` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `K` of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, the canonical map `Rf_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, a(K)) ⟶ R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, K)`: the map of
[Stacks, Tag 0B69] at `L` and `a(K)`, followed by `R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, −)` applied to the counit
`Rf_*a(K) ⟶ K` of `Rf_* ⊣ a`.
declarations.statement:
def sheafyTrace (L : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y) :
    (derivedPushforward f).obj
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).obj (op L.obj)).obj
          (a.obj K).obj) ⟶
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom Y.sheaf).obj
          (op ((derivedPushforward f).obj L.obj))).obj K.obj
declarations.comment: variant: the map for a supplied right adjoint `a`, adjunction `Rf_* ⊣ a` and tensor–Hom data; the tag is Stacks.Duality.qcqsSheafyTrace

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.qcqsSheafyTrace
declarations.doc:
**Equation 48.3.0.1 of [Stacks, Tag 0B6H].** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of quasi-compact
and quasi-separated schemes and `a` the right adjoint of `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` of
[Stacks, Tag 0A9E]. For `L` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `K` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, the canonical map
`Rf_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, a(K)) ⟶ R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, K)`: the map
`Rf_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, a(K)) ⟶ R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, Rf_*a(K))` of [Stacks, Tag 0B69], followed by
`R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, -)` applied to the counit `Rf_*a(K) ⟶ K` of the adjunction.
declarations.statement:
def qcqsSheafyTrace (L : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y) :
    (derivedPushforward f).obj
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).obj (op L.obj)).obj
          ((twistedInverseImage f
            (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)).obj K).obj) ⟶
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom Y.sheaf).obj
          (op ((derivedPushforward f).obj L.obj))).obj K.obj

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.bijective_comp_sheafyTrace_structureSheaf_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B6I].** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of
schemes with `Y` quasi-compact, let `a` be a right adjoint of
`Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, and let `L` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `K` one of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`. Then in every degree `n` the sheafy trace map of [Stacks, Tag 0B6H] induces a
bijection

`Hom_{D(𝒪_Y)}(𝒪_Y⟦-n⟧, Rf_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, a K)) ⟶ Hom_{D(𝒪_Y)}(𝒪_Y⟦-n⟧, R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, K))`,

that is, an isomorphism of global derived Homs `R Hom_X(L, a K) ⟶ R Hom_Y(Rf_*L, K)` read degree
by degree through `H^n(Y, E) = Ext^n_Y(𝒪_Y, E) = Hom(𝒪_Y⟦-n⟧, E)`.

No input of [Stacks, Tag 0A9Q] is a hypothesis. The projection formula of [Stacks, Tag 08EU] is
`Stacks.Duality.isIso_pullbackProjectionFormulaMap`; the quasi-coherence of
`Lf^*(𝒪_Y⟦-n⟧) ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} L` comes from
`Stacks.RingedSpace.pullbackShiftedUnitTensorIso`, which identifies that object with `L⟦-n⟧`,
and the stability of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` under shifts; and the quasi-coherence of `Rf_*` of part (1) of
[Stacks, Tag 08D5], which `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` and hence `a` cannot be written
down without, is `Stacks.Duality.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_qcqs`. All three
need only the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of `f` and the quasi-compactness of `Y`,
which the tag states. `a` and `adj` are parameters because they are the tag's data: `a(K)` is
named by the statement of this tag and the trace map is built from the counit of `Rf_* ⊣ a`, so
quantifying over every right adjoint and every adjunction exhibiting it — which is what the
binders do — is stronger than fixing the one the source fixes. Their existence is the separate
[Stacks, Tag 0A9E], proved at this model as
`Stacks.Duality.AnyModel.isLeftAdjoint_quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward_of_qcqs`. The same holds
for `DX` and `DY`: the trace map is built from a tensor–internal-Hom adjunction of
[Stacks, Tag 08J8] on each side, the statement holds for every choice, and one exists, namely
`Stacks.Cohomology.ProjectionFormulaInternalHomOnRingedTopoi.derivedTensorHomAdjunction`.

No coherator is needed in this form: the chain of five bijections of Tag 0A9Q is already a
statement about morphisms out of the quasi-coherent objects, and `𝒪_Y⟦-n⟧` is one of them.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_comp_sheafyTrace_structureSheaf_of_qcqs
    (L : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y) (n : ℤ) :
    Function.Bijective (fun g : (ι _).obj (derivedStructureSheafInDegree Y n) ⟶
        (derivedPushforward f).obj
          (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).obj (op L.obj)).obj
            (a.obj K).obj) =>
      g ≫ sheafyTrace f DX DY (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_qcqs f) adj L K)
declarations.comment: the whole lemma, for every right adjoint a of Rf_* on D_QCoh and every adjunction exhibiting it: a is the tag's own datum, the statement being written with a(K) in it and the map built from the counit, so the parameters a and adj quantify over more than the source's fixed choice rather than assuming anything; likewise DX and DY, every tensor-internal-hom adjunction of Tag 08J8 the trace map is built from, one being derivedTensorHomAdjunction. Nothing is assumed beyond these data: the projection formula of Tag 08EU, the quasi-coherence of Lf^*(O_Y[-n]) ⊗ᴸ L of Tag 08DX part (1) and the quasi-coherence of Rf_* of Tag 08D5 part (1) are all proved from the hypotheses the tag states, f quasi-compact and quasi-separated and Y quasi-compact. The two global derived homs are read degreewise as the morphism groups Hom(O_Y[-n], -) they corepresent by Tags 0B6A and 08DK, the left-hand one on Y after Rf_*, which is the source's own second expression RGamma(Y, Rf_* RHom(L, a(K))) for it

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.map_trace_eq_baseChange_comp_trace_of_torIndependent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B6J] (trace map and base change).** For a cartesian square of
quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes with `f` and `g` Tor independent, the maps
`1 ⋆ Tr_f : Lg^* ∘ Rf_* ∘ a ⟶ Lg^*` and `Tr_{f'} ⋆ 1 : Rf'_* ∘ a' ∘ Lg^* ⟶ Lg^*` agree via the
base change maps `β : Lg^* ∘ Rf_* ⟶ Rf'_* ∘ L(g')^*` and `α : L(g')^* ∘ a ⟶ a' ∘ Lg^*`
(Equation 48.5.0.1): `Lg^*(Tr_{f,K}) = Tr_{f',Lg^*K} ∘ Rf'_*(α_K) ∘ β_{a(K)}` for every `K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_trace_eq_baseChange_comp_trace_of_torIndependent (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hTor : TorIndependent f g) (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y) :
    haveI := isIso_twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange_of_torIndependent sq hTor
    (quasiCoherentDerivedPullback g (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPullback' g)).map
        ((twistedInverseImageAdjunction f
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)).counit.app K) =
      (quasiCoherentDerivedBaseChange g' f' f g
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs g')
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f')
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs g)
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPullback' g)
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPullback' g') sq.w).app
          ((twistedInverseImage f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)).obj K) ≫
        (quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward f'
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f')).map
          ((twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap g' f' f g
            (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs g')
            (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
            (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f')
            (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs g) sq).app K) ≫
          (twistedInverseImageAdjunction f'
            (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f')).counit.app
            ((quasiCoherentDerivedPullback g
              (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPullback' g)).obj K)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.map_unit_comp_baseChange_comp_baseChange_of_torIndependent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B6K] (unit and base change).** For a cartesian square of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes with `f` and `g` Tor independent, the maps
`1 ⋆ η_f : L(g')^* ⟶ L(g')^* ∘ a ∘ Rf_*` and `η_{f'} ⋆ 1 : L(g')^* ⟶ a' ∘ Rf'_* ∘ L(g')^*` agree
via the base change maps `α` (Equation 48.5.0.1) and `β`:
`a'(β_M) ∘ α_{Rf_*M} ∘ L(g')^*(η_{f,M}) = η_{f',L(g')^*M}` for every `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_unit_comp_baseChange_comp_baseChange_of_torIndependent (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hTor : TorIndependent f g) (M : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) :
    haveI := isIso_twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange_of_torIndependent sq hTor
    (quasiCoherentDerivedPullback g' (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPullback' g')).map
        ((twistedInverseImageAdjunction f
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)).unit.app M) ≫
      (twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap g' f' f g
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs g')
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f')
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs g) sq).app
          ((quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward f
            (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)).obj M) ≫
        (twistedInverseImage f' (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f')).map
          ((quasiCoherentDerivedBaseChange g' f' f g
            (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs g')
            (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
            (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f')
            (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs g)
            (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPullback' g)
            (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPullback' g') sq.w).app M) =
      (twistedInverseImageAdjunction f'
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f')).unit.app
        ((quasiCoherentDerivedPullback g'
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPullback' g')).obj M)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.qcqsTrace_specMap_app_derivedTilde
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B6L.** Let `φ : R ⟶ S` be a ring map, `Y = Spec R`, `X = Spec S` and
`f = Spec φ : X ⟶ Y`, and let `a` be the right adjoint of `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`.
For `K` in `D(R)`, identify `a(K~)` with `RHom_R(S, K)~`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedTildeCompTwistedInverseImageIsoDerivedHom`, [Stacks, Tag 0A9F]) and
