declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinCycleMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical Gysin map on cycles `i^* : Z_{k+1}(X) ⟶ Z_k(D)` attached to a section `s` of an
invertible module whose restriction to the zero scheme `D = Z(s)` is trivial: the extension of
the two rules of `Stacks.Chow.gysinCycleMapComponent` over locally finite presentations by
integral closed subschemes. It does not depend on a trivialization of `L|_D`.
declarations.statement:
def gysinCycleMap
    (_htriv : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsTrivial
      (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subscheme.sheaf.obj
      (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subscheme.ringCatSheaf.property
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι).obj L)) :
    CycleGroup C p (k + 1) →+
      CycleGroup C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) k
declarations.comment: the canonical map on cycles

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinCycleMap_of_le
declarations.doc:
An integral closed subscheme contained in the zero scheme has zero image under the canonical
map on cycles.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinCycleMap_of_le (W : X.IdealSheafData) (hW : IsIntegral W.subscheme)
    (hDim : schemeDeltaDimension C (W.subschemeι ≫ p) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (h : Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s ≤ W) :
    gysinCycleMap C p k L s htriv
      (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p W.subschemeι (k + 1)) = 0
declarations.comment: vanishing on integral closed subschemes contained in the zero scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinCycleMap_of_not_le
declarations.doc:
The canonical map on cycles sends an integral closed subscheme `W` not contained in `D` to the
fundamental cycle of the scheme-theoretic intersection `W ∩ D`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinCycleMap_of_not_le (W : X.IdealSheafData) (hW : IsIntegral W.subscheme)
    (hDim : schemeDeltaDimension C (W.subschemeι ≫ p) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (h : ¬ Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s ≤ W) :
    gysinCycleMap C p k L s htriv
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p W.subschemeι (k + 1)) =
      cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p)
        ((W.comap (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι).subschemeι) k
declarations.comment: agreement with Stacks 02T8 off the zero scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isGysinCycleMap_gysinCycleMap
declarations.doc: The canonical map on cycles satisfies the locally finite component formula.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGysinCycleMap_gysinCycleMap :
    IsGysinCycleMap C p k L s (gysinCycleMap C p k L s htriv)
declarations.comment: the locally finite component formula

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.eq_gysinCycleMap_of_isGysinCycleMap
declarations.doc:
Any additive map `Z_{k+1}(X) ⟶ Z_k(D)` satisfying the locally finite component formula is the
canonical map on cycles.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_gysinCycleMap_of_isGysinCycleMap
    (F : CycleGroup C p (k + 1) →+
      CycleGroup C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) k)
    (hF : IsGysinCycleMap C p k L s F) :
    F = gysinCycleMap C p k L s htriv
declarations.comment: canonicity

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.VirtualNormalTriple
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0B70.** A triple `(D, 𝒩, σ)` on a scheme `X`: a locally principal closed subscheme
`i : D ⟶ X`, an invertible `𝒪_D`-module `𝒩` (the virtual normal bundle of `D` in `X`) and a
surjection `σ : 𝒩^{⊗ -1} ⟶ i^*ℐ_D` of `𝒪_D`-modules.
declarations.statement: structure VirtualNormalTriple (X : Scheme.{u})
declarations.comment: the triple (D, N, σ): D locally principal, N an invertible O_D-module, σ a surjection from the inverse of N onto the pullback of the ideal sheaf of D

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.VirtualNormalTriple.normalIsoOfIsEffectiveCartier
declarations.doc:
**The footnote of Remark 0B70.** If `D` is an effective Cartier divisor, then
`𝒩 ≅ 𝒪_X(D)|_D`.
declarations.statement:
def normalIsoOfIsEffectiveCartier :
    T.N ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback T.D.subschemeι).obj (divisorSheaf T.D)
declarations.comment: footnote: if D is an effective Cartier divisor, then N is isomorphic to the restriction of O_X(D) to D

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.virtualNormalGysinOfIdeal_zeroScheme
declarations.doc:
**The construction generalizes Definition 02T8.** For the zero scheme `D = Z(s)` of a section
`s` of an invertible module `ℒ`, and any invertible `𝒪_D`-module `𝒩 ≅ ℒ|_D`, the Gysin map of
`(D, 𝒩)` is the Gysin map of Definition 02T8.
declarations.statement:
theorem virtualNormalGysinOfIdeal_zeroScheme (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : Γ(L, ⊤)) (N : (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subscheme.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
      (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subscheme.sheaf.obj
      (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subscheme.ringCatSheaf.property N]
    (ψ : N ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι).obj L) :
    virtualNormalGysinOfIdeal C p k (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s) N =
      gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C p k L s
declarations.comment: the construction generalizes Definition 02T8: for D = Z(s) and N isomorphic to the restriction of L the two Gysin maps are equal

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.VirtualNormalTriple.gysin
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0B70.** The Gysin homomorphism `i^* : Z_{k+1}(X) ⟶ A_k(D)` of a triple
`(D, 𝒩, σ)`.
declarations.statement: def gysin : CycleGroup C p (k + 1) →+ chowGroup C (T.D.subschemeι ≫ p) k
declarations.comment: the Gysin homomorphism i^* from (k+1)-cycles on X to CH_k(D) of a triple

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.VirtualNormalTriple.gysin_of_not_le
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0B70, rule (1)(a) of Definition 02T8 for a triple.** For an integral closed
subscheme `W ⊆ X` of delta-dimension `k + 1` with `W ⊄ D`, `i^*[W] = [D ∩ W]_k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysin_of_not_le (W : X.IdealSheafData) (hW : IsIntegral W.subscheme)
    (hDim : schemeDeltaDimension C (W.subschemeι ≫ p) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt)) (h : ¬ T.D ≤ W) :
    T.gysin C p k (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p W.subschemeι (k + 1)) =
      QuotientAddGroup.mk
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C (T.D.subschemeι ≫ p)
          ((W.comap T.D.subschemeι).subschemeι) k)
declarations.comment: rule (1)(a) of Definition 02T8 for a triple: W not contained in D

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.VirtualNormalTriple.gysin_of_le
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0B70, rule (1)(b) of Definition 02T8 for a triple.** For an integral closed
subscheme `W ⊆ D` of delta-dimension `k + 1`, `i^*[W] = i'_*(c₁(𝒩|_W) ∩ [W])`, where
`i' : W ⟶ D` is the induced closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysin_of_le (W : X.IdealSheafData) (hW : IsIntegral W.subscheme)
    (hDim : schemeDeltaDimension C (W.subschemeι ≫ p) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt)) (h : T.D ≤ W) :
    T.gysin C p k (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p W.subschemeι (k + 1)) =
      properChowPushforward C (W.subschemeι ≫ p) (T.D.subschemeι ≫ p)
        (Scheme.IdealSheafData.inclusion h) (by simp) k
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isClosedImmersion
          (Scheme.IdealSheafData.inclusion h) C (W.subschemeι ≫ p) (T.D.subschemeι ≫ p)
          (by simp) k)
        (virtualNormalChernClass C p k T.D T.N W hW hDim h)
declarations.comment: rule (1)(b) of Definition 02T8 for a triple: W contained in D, with c_1(N|_W)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.VirtualNormalTriple.gysin_finsum
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0B70, rule (2) of Definition 02T8 for a triple.** For `α = ∑ n_j [W_j]` locally
finite, `i^*α = ∑ n_j i^*[W_j]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysin_finsum {J : Type u} (W : J → X.IdealSheafData)
    (hW : ∀ j, IsIntegral (W j).subscheme)
    (hDim : ∀ j, schemeDeltaDimension C ((W j).subschemeι ≫ p) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hLocal : LocallyFinite (fun j ↦ ((W j).support : Set X))) (n : J → ℤ)
    (α : CycleGroup C p (k + 1))
    (hα : ∀ x : X, α.1 x = ∑ᶠ j : J, n j *
      (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p (W j).subschemeι (k + 1)).1 x) :
    ∃ β : CycleGroup C (T.D.subschemeι ≫ p) k,
      T.gysin C p k α = QuotientAddGroup.mk β ∧
      ∀ x : T.D.subscheme, β.1 x = ∑ᶠ j : J, n j *
        (gysinComponentCycleOfIdeal C p k (virtualNormalChernRule C p k T.D T.N) T.D
          (W j) (hW j) (hDim j)).1 x
declarations.comment: rule (2) of Definition 02T8 for a triple: locally finite sums

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.VirtualNormalTriple.nonempty_normalIso_of_isEffectiveCartier
declarations.doc:
**The footnote of Remark 0B70.** If `D` is an effective Cartier divisor, then
`𝒩 ≅ 𝒪_X(D)|_D`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_normalIso_of_isEffectiveCartier (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor T.D) :
    Nonempty (T.N ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback T.D.subschemeι).obj (divisorSheaf T.D))
declarations.comment: footnote: if D is an effective Cartier divisor, then N is isomorphic to the restriction of O_X(D) to D

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.VirtualNormalTriple.gysin_heq_of_zeroScheme_eq
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0B70: the construction generalizes Definition 02T8.** If `D = Z(s)` for a global
section `s` of an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `ℒ` and `𝒩 ≅ ℒ|_D`, the Gysin map of the triple is the
Gysin map of Definition 02T8 of `(ℒ, s)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysin_heq_of_zeroScheme_eq (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : Γ(L, ⊤)) (hz : Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s = T.D)
    (ψ : T.N ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback T.D.subschemeι).obj L) :
    HEq (T.gysin C p k) (gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C p k L s)
declarations.comment: the construction generalizes Definition 02T8: agreement when D = Z(s) and N is the restriction of L

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.VirtualNormalTriple.gysin_heq_divisorSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0B70 at an effective Cartier divisor.** If `D` is an effective Cartier divisor (so
that `𝒩 ≅ 𝒪_X(D)|_D` by the footnote), the Gysin map of the triple is the Gysin map of
Definition 02T8 of `(𝒪_X(D), 1_D)`, whose zero scheme is `D`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysin_heq_divisorSheaf (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor T.D) :
    HEq (T.gysin C p k)
      (gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C p k (divisorSheaf T.D) (divisorSheafGlobalSection T.D))
declarations.comment: agreement with Definition 02T8 when D is an effective Cartier divisor

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.VirtualNormalTriple.chowPushforwardOfIso_gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_divisorSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0B70 at an effective Cartier divisor**, as an identity of Chow classes: the Gysin
map of Definition 02T8 of `(𝒪_X(D), 1_D)`, transported along `Z(1_D) = D`, is the Gysin map of
the triple.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowPushforwardOfIso_gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_divisorSheaf
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor T.D) (α : CycleGroup C p (k + 1)) :
    chowPushforwardOfIso C
        ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X (divisorSheaf T.D)
          (divisorSheafGlobalSection T.D)).subschemeι ≫ p) (T.D.subschemeι ≫ p)
        (eqToHom (congrArg Scheme.IdealSheafData.subscheme
          (@zeroScheme_canonicalSection X T.D hD)))
        (by rw [← Category.assoc, eqToHom_subscheme_comp_subschemeι _ _
          (@zeroScheme_canonicalSection X T.D hD)]) k
        (@gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C X p _ k (divisorSheaf T.D)
          (@isInvertible_divisorSheaf X T.D hD) (divisorSheafGlobalSection T.D) α) =
      T.gysin C p k α
declarations.comment: agreement with Definition 02T8 when D is an effective Cartier divisor, as an identity of Chow classes

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.virtualNormalTriple_remark
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0B70**, all of its assertions together. Let `X` be locally of finite type over the
base of a Chow situation (Situation 02QL) and let `(D, 𝒩, σ)` be a triple: `D` a locally
principal closed subscheme, `𝒩` an invertible `𝒪_D`-module and `σ : 𝒩^{⊗ -1} ⟶ i^*ℐ_D` a
surjection. Then:
* (footnote) if `D` is an effective Cartier divisor, `𝒩 ≅ 𝒪_X(D)|_D`, and every effective Cartier
  divisor carries such a triple;
* the Gysin homomorphism `i^* : Z_{k+1}(X) ⟶ A_k(D)` of the triple obeys the rules of
  Definition 02T8 with `𝒩` in place of `ℒ|_D`: `i^*[W] = [D ∩ W]_k` for `W ⊄ D`,
  `i^*[W] = i'_*(c₁(𝒩|_W) ∩ [W])` for `W ⊆ D`, and `i^*(∑ n_j [W_j]) = ∑ n_j i^*[W_j]`;
* it generalizes Definition 02T8: for `D = Z(s)` and `𝒩 ≅ ℒ|_D` it is the Gysin map of `(ℒ, s)`,
  and for `D` an effective Cartier divisor it is the Gysin map of `(𝒪_X(D), 1_D)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem virtualNormalTriple_remark (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] :
    (∀ T : VirtualNormalTriple X, IsEffectiveCartierDivisor T.D →
      Nonempty (T.N ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback T.D.subschemeι).obj (divisorSheaf T.D))) ∧
    (∀ D : X.IdealSheafData, IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D →
      ∃ T : VirtualNormalTriple X, T.D = D) ∧
    (∀ (k : ℤ) (T : VirtualNormalTriple X) (W : X.IdealSheafData), IsIntegral W.subscheme →
      schemeDeltaDimension C (W.subschemeι ≫ p) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt) →
      ¬ T.D ≤ W →
      T.gysin C p k (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p W.subschemeι (k + 1)) =
        QuotientAddGroup.mk
          (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C (T.D.subschemeι ≫ p)
            ((W.comap T.D.subschemeι).subschemeι) k)) ∧
    (∀ (k : ℤ) (T : VirtualNormalTriple X) (W : X.IdealSheafData) (hW : IsIntegral W.subscheme)
      (hDim : schemeDeltaDimension C (W.subschemeι ≫ p) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
      (h : T.D ≤ W),
      T.gysin C p k (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p W.subschemeι (k + 1)) =
        properChowPushforward C (W.subschemeι ≫ p) (T.D.subschemeι ≫ p)
          (Scheme.IdealSheafData.inclusion h) (by simp) k
          (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isClosedImmersion
            (Scheme.IdealSheafData.inclusion h) C (W.subschemeι ≫ p) (T.D.subschemeι ≫ p)
            (by simp) k)
          (virtualNormalChernClass C p k T.D T.N W hW hDim h)) ∧
    (∀ (k : ℤ) (T : VirtualNormalTriple X) {J : Type u} (W : J → X.IdealSheafData)
      (hW : ∀ j, IsIntegral (W j).subscheme)
      (hDim : ∀ j, schemeDeltaDimension C ((W j).subschemeι ≫ p) = ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt)),
      LocallyFinite (fun j ↦ ((W j).support : Set X)) → ∀ (n : J → ℤ)
      (α : CycleGroup C p (k + 1)),
      (∀ x : X, α.1 x = ∑ᶠ j : J, n j *
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p (W j).subschemeι (k + 1)).1 x) →
      ∃ β : CycleGroup C (T.D.subschemeι ≫ p) k,
        T.gysin C p k α = QuotientAddGroup.mk β ∧
        ∀ x : T.D.subscheme, β.1 x = ∑ᶠ j : J, n j *
          (gysinComponentCycleOfIdeal C p k (virtualNormalChernRule C p k T.D T.N) T.D
            (W j) (hW j) (hDim j)).1 x) ∧
    (∀ (k : ℤ) (T : VirtualNormalTriple X) (L : X.Modules)
      [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
      (s : Γ(L, ⊤)), Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s = T.D →
      (T.N ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback T.D.subschemeι).obj L) →
      HEq (T.gysin C p k) (gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C p k L s)) ∧
    (∀ (k : ℤ) (T : VirtualNormalTriple X) [IsEffectiveCartierDivisor T.D],
      HEq (T.gysin C p k)
        (gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C p k (divisorSheaf T.D)
          (divisorSheafGlobalSection T.D)))
declarations.comment: the whole remark: the footnote, the Gysin homomorphism of a triple with the rules of Definition 02T8, and its agreement with Definition 02T8

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_flatPullback_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B71 on the fundamental cycle of a closed subscheme meeting the zero scheme
properly.** For a closed subscheme `Z ⊆ X` of delta-dimension at most `k + 1` whose intersection
with `D = Z(s)` is an effective Cartier divisor on `Z`, and whose inverse image `f^{-1}Z` meets
`D' = Z(f^*s)` in the same way,

  `(i')^* f^* [Z]_{k+1} = g^* i^* [Z]_{k+1}`  in  `CH_{k+r}(D')`.

Here `i^*` and `(i')^*` are the Gysin maps `Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible` of
Stacks 02T8 for `(L, s)` and for `(f^*L, f^*s)`, `f^*` is the flat pullback of cycles of
Stacks 02RB, and `g^*` is the flat pullback on Chow groups of Stacks 0FVK along the comparison
morphism `Stacks.Chow.zeroSchemePullbackHom` of Remark 0B6Y, whose flatness and relative dimension
are supplied by the cartesian square and are **not** hypotheses. No first Chern class component
rule is a parameter, and the invertibility of `f^*L` is an instance.

This is the first case of the source's proof, for an arbitrary closed subscheme rather than only
an integral one. Carried: the vanishing of **Stacks 02S1** along `g`, without which the right hand
side does not exist, and the five side conditions of Stacks 02TB (1) and Stacks 02RB at the two
schemes of the square; see the implementation notes of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.Gysin42.FlatPullbackInvertible`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_flatPullback_cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme
    (Z : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hZ : schemeDeltaDimension C (Z.subschemeι ≫ p) ≤ ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hDZ : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor
      ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).comap Z.subschemeι))
    (hZ' : schemeDeltaDimension C ((Z.comap f).subschemeι ≫ (f ≫ p)) ≤
      ((k + (r : ℤ) + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hDZ' : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor
      ((pullbackZeroScheme f L s).comap (Z.comap f).subschemeι))
    (hZD : schemeDeltaDimension C
      ((Z.comap (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι).subschemeι ≫
        ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p)) ≤ (k : EInt))
    (hfac : FlatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C
      ((pullbackZeroScheme f L s).subschemeι ≫ (f ≫ p))
      ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) (zeroSchemePullbackHom f L s)
      (zeroSchemePullbackHom_comp f L s C p (f ≫ p) rfl) r
      (relativeDimension_zeroSchemePullbackHom f L s r hf) k) :
    gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C (f ≫ p) (k + (r : ℤ))
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj L) (pullbackGlobalSections f L s)
        ((show k + 1 + (r : ℤ) = k + (r : ℤ) + 1 by omega) ▸
          flatPullback C (f ≫ p) p f rfl r hf (k + 1)
            (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p Z.subschemeι (k + 1))) =
      flatPullbackChow C ((pullbackZeroScheme f L s).subschemeι ≫ (f ≫ p))
        ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) (zeroSchemePullbackHom f L s)
        (zeroSchemePullbackHom_comp f L s C p (f ≫ p) rfl) r
        (relativeDimension_zeroSchemePullbackHom f L s r hf) k hfac
        (gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C p k L s
          (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme C p Z.subschemeι (k + 1)))
declarations.comment: closed subscheme meeting the zero scheme properly; 02S1 along g carried

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_flatPullback_of_invertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B71 for an arbitrary cycle at the Gysin map of an invertible module, with no
hypothesis.** Gysin pullback through the zero scheme of a section of an invertible module
commutes with flat pullback:

  `(i')^* f^* α = g^* i^* α`  in  `CH_{k+r}(D')`,  for every `α ∈ Z_{k+1}(X)`.

This is `Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_flatPullback` with both of its remaining
hypotheses discharged: the vanishing of Stacks 02S1 along `g` is
`Stacks.Chow.flatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_general`, and the identity on integral
components is replaced by its rational-equivalence form
`Stacks.Chow.gysinRationallyCompatibleWithFlatPullback_invertible`, which is proved here. Both
Gysin maps are `Stacks.Chow.gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible`, no component rule is a parameter, the
invertibility of `f^*L` is an instance, and `g` is the canonical comparison morphism of Remark
0B6Y.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible_flatPullback_of_invertible (α : CycleGroup C p (k + 1)) :
    gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C (f ≫ p) (k + (r : ℤ)) ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj L)
        (AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackGlobalSections f L s)
        ((show k + 1 + (r : ℤ) = k + (r : ℤ) + 1 by omega) ▸
          flatPullback C (f ≫ p) p f rfl r hf (k + 1) α) =
      flatPullbackChow C ((pullbackZeroScheme f L s).subschemeι ≫ (f ≫ p))
        ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) (zeroSchemePullbackHom f L s)
        (zeroSchemePullbackHom_comp f L s C p (f ≫ p) rfl) r
        (relativeDimension_zeroSchemePullbackHom f L s r hf) k
        (flatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_general C
          ((pullbackZeroScheme f L s).subschemeι ≫ (f ≫ p))
          ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) (zeroSchemePullbackHom f L s)
          (zeroSchemePullbackHom_comp f L s C p (f ≫ p) rfl) r
          (relativeDimension_zeroSchemePullbackHom f L s r hf) k)
        (gysinHomomorphismOfInvertible C p k L s α)
declarations.comment: the Gysin map commutes with flat pullback, (i')^* f^* = g^* i^* on A_{k+r}(D'), with no hypothesis: the component identity is replaced by its rational-equivalence form, proved here, and the vanishing of 02S1 along g by the general theorem

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinNaturality_firstChernIdentityCapRule
declarations.doc:
**The Gysin identity on the test schemes.** For the canonical first Chern class cap product, a
test morphism `g : T ⟶ X`, and an invertible module `𝒩` on `T` with a global section `s` and zero
scheme `i : D = Z(s) ⟶ T`,

  `c₁((i ∘ g)^*ℒ) ∩ i^*α = i^*(c₁(g^*ℒ) ∩ α)`.

This is `Stacks.Chow.IdentityCapRule.GysinNaturality` for
`Stacks.Chow.firstChernIdentityCapRule` at the canonical cap product and the canonical Gysin
system.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinNaturality_firstChernIdentityCapRule :
    IdentityCapRule.GysinNaturality C sX 1
      (firstChernIdentityCapRule C sX (canonicalFirstChernCapRule C) L)
      (canonicalGysinSystem C)
declarations.comment: the Gysin identity read for the identity cap rule of the canonical first Chern class cap product on the test schemes of X, i.e. the predicate `IdentityCapRule.GysinNaturality` that the bivariant class of Stacks 0B77 takes as its third naturality hypothesis, with no hypothesis of its own

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.gysinChowOfInvertible_firstChernClassCapChow
declarations.doc:
Let `ℒ` be an invertible module on `X` with a global section `s` and zero scheme
`i : D = Z(s) ⟶ X`, and let `𝒩` be an invertible module on `X`. Then Gysin pullback along `i`
commutes with capping with the first Chern class of `𝒩`:

  `i^*(c₁(𝒩) ∩ α) = c₁(i^*𝒩) ∩ i^*α`  in  `A_k(D)`,  for every `α ∈ A_{k+2}(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinChowOfInvertible_firstChernClassCapChow (α : chowGroup C p (k + 1 + 1)) :
    gysinChowOfInvertible C p k L s (firstChernClassCapChow C (k + 1) p N α) =
      firstChernClassCapChow C k ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι).obj N)
        (gysinChowOfInvertible C p (k + 1) L s α)
declarations.comment: the identity i^* (c_1(N) cap a) = c_1(i^* N) cap i^* a on Chow groups, for every class a, stated for the descended operations of Stacks 02TO and 02TI that the library proves outright (`gysinChowOfInvertible`, `firstChernClassCapChow`); nothing about the Gysin map, the cap product or their descent is left over. The source proves the tag with the proof of Stacks 0B73 through Stacks 02TM on the integral components; here it is deduced from Stacks 0B73 itself for the pair `(L, s)` and the zero section of `N`, using Stacks 02T9 to read `j_* j^*` as the cap product and Stacks 02TA for the pushforward along `Z(0) = X ⟶ X`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinChowOfInvertible_firstChernClassCapChow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B72, with no hypothesis.** For an invertible module `ℒ` with a global section `s`
whose zero scheme is `i : D = Z(s) ⟶ X`, and a second invertible module `𝒩` on `X`, Gysin
pullback along `i` commutes with capping with the first Chern class of `𝒩`:

  `i^*(c₁(𝒩) ∩ α) = c₁(i^*𝒩) ∩ i^*α`  in  `A_k(D)`,  for  `α ∈ A_{k+2}(X)`.

The Gysin map is the one of Stacks 02TO and the cap product the one of Stacks 02TI, both
constructed in this repository with no hypothesis. Nothing is assumed: the cap product with
`c₁(𝒩)` is itself the Gysin map of the zero section of `𝒩`, so the identity is Stacks 0B73 for
the pairs `(ℒ, s)` and `(𝒩, 0)`, read through Stacks 02T9 on `X` and on `D` and Stacks 02TA
across `Z(0) ⟶ X`. See the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinChowOfInvertible_firstChernClassCapChow (α : chowGroup C p (k + 1 + 1)) :
    gysinChowOfInvertible C p k L s (firstChernClassCapChow C (k + 1) p N α) =
      firstChernClassCapChow C k ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p)
        (zeroSchemeRestrictModule L N s) (gysinChowOfInvertible C p (k + 1) L s α)
declarations.comment: the identity i^*(c_1(N) cap alpha) = c_1(i^* N) cap i^* alpha in A_k(D), for the Gysin map of Stacks 02TO and the cap product of Stacks 02TI, with no hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinChowOfInvertible_comm
declarations.doc:
Let `(S, δ)` be the base situation of chapter 42 of the Stacks Project, let
`X` be locally of finite type over `S`, and let `(L, s, i : D → X)` and `(L', s', i' : D' → X)`
be two triples as in Definition 02T8, so that `D = Z(s)` and `D' = Z(s')` are the zero schemes of
the two sections. Write `j : D ∩ D' → D` and `j' : D ∩ D' → D'` for the two presentations of the
scheme-theoretic intersection as a zero scheme — of the restriction of `s'` to `D`, and of the
restriction of `s` to `D'` — and let `e` be an isomorphism between them over `X`. Then the
diagram

```
  CH_k(X)  --i^*-->  CH_{k-1}(D)
     |                  |
  (i')^*               j^*
     v                  v
  CH_{k-1}(D') --(j')^*--> CH_{k-2}(D ∩ D')
```

commutes, each of the four maps being a Gysin map. The input degree is written `(k + 1) + 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinChowOfInvertible_comm
    (e : (zeroSchemeInter L L' s s').subscheme ≅ (zeroSchemeInter L' L s' s).subscheme)
    (he : e.hom ≫ (zeroSchemeInter L' L s' s).subschemeι ≫
        (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L' s').subschemeι =
      (zeroSchemeInter L L' s s').subschemeι ≫ (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι)
    (α : chowGroup C p (k + 1 + 1)) :
    chowPushforwardOfIso C ((zeroSchemeInter L L' s s').subschemeι ≫
          (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p)
        ((zeroSchemeInter L' L s' s).subschemeι ≫
          (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L' s').subschemeι ≫ p)
        e.hom (iso_zeroSchemeInter_comp_structureMorphism C p L L' s s' e he) k
        (gysinChowOfInvertible C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ p) k
          (zeroSchemeRestrictModule L L' s) (restrictSectionToZeroScheme L L' s s')
          (gysinChowOfInvertible C p (k + 1) L s α)) =
      gysinChowOfInvertible C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L' s').subschemeι ≫ p) k
        (zeroSchemeRestrictModule L' L s') (restrictSectionToZeroScheme L' L s' s)
        (gysinChowOfInvertible C p (k + 1) L' s' α)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatPullbackChow_totalSpaceToBase_bijective
declarations.doc:
Let `(S, δ)` be as in Situation 02QL, let `X` be locally of finite type over `S`, let `ℒ` be an
invertible `𝒪_X`-module and let `p : L = \underline{\Spec}(\Sym^*(ℒ)) ⟶ X` be the associated line
bundle. Then

  `p^* : A_k(X) ⟶ A_{k+1}(L)`

is an isomorphism for every `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullbackChow_totalSpaceToBase_bijective (k : ℤ) :
    Function.Bijective
      (flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension C (D.totalSpaceToBase ≫ sX) sX D.totalSpaceToBase
        rfl 1 D.relativeDimension_totalSpaceToBase k)
declarations.comment: p^* : A_k(X) → A_{k+1}(L) is bijective for all k, p : L → X a line bundle

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantComposite_assoc
declarations.doc:
The composition of bivariant classes is associative: for `a ∈ A^p(X ⟶ Y)`, `b ∈ A^q(Y ⟶ Z)`
and `c ∈ A^r(Z ⟶ W)` the two triple composites `(a ∘ b) ∘ c` and `a ∘ (b ∘ c)` agree in
`A^{p+q+r}(X ⟶ W)`, the equality being heterogeneous because the two sides are indexed by
`(p + q) + r` and `p + (q + r)` [Stacks, Tag 0B75].
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantComposite_assoc (hgys : G.IsNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso)
    (hgysc : G.IsNaturalUnderPullbackCompPushforward) :
    bivariantComposite C G sX sZ sW (f ≫ g) h (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hf hg) hh (p + q) r
        (bivariantComposite C G sX sY sZ f g hf hg p q a b hgys hgysc) c hgys hgysc ≍
      bivariantComposite C G sX sY sW f (g ≫ h) hf (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hg hh) p
        (q + r) a (bivariantComposite C G sY sZ sW g h hg hh q r b c hgys hgysc) hgys hgysc
declarations.comment: the composition of bivariant classes is associative: for a ∈ A^p(X ⟶ Y), b ∈ A^q(Y ⟶ Z) and c ∈ A^r(Z ⟶ W) the triple composites (a ∘ b) ∘ c and a ∘ (b ∘ c) agree in A^{p+q+r}(X ⟶ W), the degrees (p + q) + r and p + (q + r) being the same integer written two ways

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantCompositeBilinear_assoc
declarations.doc:
Associativity of the composition, read on the bilinear map
`Stacks.Chow.bivariantCompositeBilinear` that bundles it [Stacks, Tag 0B75].
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantCompositeBilinear_assoc (hgys : G.IsNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso)
    (hgysc : G.IsNaturalUnderPullbackCompPushforward) :
    bivariantCompositeBilinear C G sX sZ sW (f ≫ g) h (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hf hg) hh
          (p + q) r hgys hgysc
        (bivariantCompositeBilinear C G sX sY sZ f g hf hg p q hgys hgysc a b) c ≍
      bivariantCompositeBilinear C G sX sY sW f (g ≫ h) hf
        (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hg hh) p (q + r) hgys hgysc a
        (bivariantCompositeBilinear C G sY sZ sW g h hg hh q r hgys hgysc b c)
declarations.comment: the bilinear composition A^p(X ⟶ Y) × A^q(Y ⟶ Z) ⟶ A^{p+q}(X ⟶ Z) is associative

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantComposite_add_left'
declarations.doc: Additivity of the composition in the first argument: `(a + a') ∘ b = a ∘ b + a' ∘ b`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantComposite_add_left' (a a' : BivariantClass C G sX sY f hf p)
    (b : BivariantClass C G sY sZ g hg q) :
    bivariantComposite C G sX sY sZ f g hf hg p q (a + a') b hgys hgysc =
      bivariantComposite C G sX sY sZ f g hf hg p q a b hgys hgysc +
        bivariantComposite C G sX sY sZ f g hf hg p q a' b hgys hgysc
declarations.comment: the bilinearity of the composition, additivity in the first argument

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantComposite_add_right'
declarations.doc: Additivity of the composition in the second argument: `a ∘ (b + b') = a ∘ b + a ∘ b'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantComposite_add_right' (a : BivariantClass C G sX sY f hf p)
    (b b' : BivariantClass C G sY sZ g hg q) :
    bivariantComposite C G sX sY sZ f g hf hg p q a (b + b') hgys hgysc =
      bivariantComposite C G sX sY sZ f g hf hg p q a b hgys hgysc +
        bivariantComposite C G sX sY sZ f g hf hg p q a b' hgys hgysc
declarations.comment: the bilinearity of the composition, additivity in the second argument

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantComposite_neg_left
declarations.doc: The composition negates in its first argument: `(-a) ∘ b = -(a ∘ b)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantComposite_neg_left (a : BivariantClass C G sX sY f hf p)
    (b : BivariantClass C G sY sZ g hg q) :
    bivariantComposite C G sX sY sZ f g hf hg p q (-a) b hgys hgysc =
      -bivariantComposite C G sX sY sZ f g hf hg p q a b hgys hgysc
declarations.comment: the bilinearity of the composition, negation in the first argument

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantComposite_neg_right
declarations.doc: The composition negates in its second argument: `a ∘ (-b) = -(a ∘ b)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantComposite_neg_right (a : BivariantClass C G sX sY f hf p)
    (b : BivariantClass C G sY sZ g hg q) :
    bivariantComposite C G sX sY sZ f g hf hg p q a (-b) hgys hgysc =
      -bivariantComposite C G sX sY sZ f g hf hg p q a b hgys hgysc
declarations.comment: the bilinearity of the composition, negation in the second argument

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantComposite_zero_left
declarations.doc: The composite of the zero class with any class is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantComposite_zero_left (b : BivariantClass C G sY sZ g hg q) :
    bivariantComposite C G sX sY sZ f g hf hg p q 0 b hgys hgysc = 0
declarations.comment: the bilinearity of the composition, the zero class on the left

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantComposite_zero_right
declarations.doc: The composite of any class with the zero class is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantComposite_zero_right (a : BivariantClass C G sX sY f hf p) :
    bivariantComposite C G sX sY sZ f g hf hg p q a 0 hgys hgysc = 0
declarations.comment: the bilinearity of the composition, the zero class on the right

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantCompositeAddHomLeft
declarations.doc:
Composition with a fixed class `b ∈ A^q(Y ⟶ Z)` on the right, as a homomorphism
`A^p(X ⟶ Y) ⟶ A^{p+q}(X ⟶ Z)` of groups.
declarations.comment: the bilinearity of the composition: the partial map in the first argument as a homomorphism of groups

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantCompositeAddHomRight
declarations.doc:
Composition with a fixed class `a ∈ A^p(X ⟶ Y)` on the left, as a homomorphism
`A^q(Y ⟶ Z) ⟶ A^{p+q}(X ⟶ Z)` of groups.
declarations.comment: the bilinearity of the composition: the partial map in the second argument as a homomorphism of groups

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantComposite
declarations.doc:
The composite `a ∘ b ∈ A^{p+q}(X ⟶ Z)` of bivariant classes `a ∈ A^p(X ⟶ Y)` and
`b ∈ A^q(Y ⟶ Z)`: the bivariant class of degree `p + q` for `f ≫ g` whose cap operation is
`α ↦ a ∩ (b ∩ α)`, that is, `Stacks.Chow.bivariantCompositeCap` read through the transport of Chow
groups along `k - q - p = k - (p + q)` [Stacks, Tag 0B75].
declarations.comment:
the composite bivariant class, assembled from its cap operation and the three
naturality conditions of Stacks 0B76

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantCompositeBilinear
declarations.doc:
The composition `A^p(X ⟶ Y) × A^q(Y ⟶ Z) ⟶ A^{p+q}(X ⟶ Z)` as a bilinear map, that is,
`Stacks.Chow.bivariantComposite` bundled through its additivity in each argument
[Stacks, Tag 0B75].
declarations.statement:
def bivariantCompositeBilinear (hgys : G.IsNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso)
    (hgysc : G.IsNaturalUnderPullbackCompPushforward) :
    BivariantClass C G sX sY f hf p →+
      BivariantClass C G sY sZ g hg q →+
        BivariantClass C G sX sZ (f ≫ g) (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hf hg) (p + q)
declarations.comment: the composition of bivariant classes is bilinear

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantCompositeOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The composite `a ∘ b ∈ A^{p+q}(X ⟶ Z)` of bivariant classes at the Gysin system of the first
Chern class rule of an invertible module.
declarations.statement:
def bivariantCompositeOfInvertible
    (a : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf p)
    (b : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sY sZ g hg q) :
    BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sZ (f ≫ g)
      (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hf hg) (p + q)
declarations.comment: the composite bivariant class at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with both cases of Stacks 02TA discharged

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantCompositeBilinearOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The composition `A^p(X ⟶ Y) × A^q(Y ⟶ Z) ⟶ A^{p+q}(X ⟶ Z)` of bivariant classes as a bilinear
map, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule.
declarations.statement:
def bivariantCompositeBilinearOfInvertible :
    BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf p →+
      BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sY sZ g hg q →+
        BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sZ (f ≫ g)
          (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hf hg) (p + q)
declarations.comment: the composition as a bilinear map, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with both cases of Stacks 02TA discharged

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantCompositeCap_proper_naturality
declarations.doc:
The proper-pushforward condition of Stacks 0B76 for the composite of two bivariant classes:
the cap operation `α ↦ a ∩ (b ∩ α)` commutes with proper pushforward along a morphism of test
schemes. The condition for `b` moves the pushforward past the inner cap and onto the middle base
change `T' ×_Z Y ⟶ T ×_Z Y`, and the outer cap operation's condition moves it past the outer
cap.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantCompositeCap_proper_naturality {T T' : Scheme.{u}} (t : T ⟶ Z)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType t] (h : T' ⟶ T) [IsProper h]
    (h' : pullback (f ≫ g) (h ≫ t) ⟶ pullback (f ≫ g) t)
    (sq : IsPullback (pullback.snd (f ≫ g) (h ≫ t)) h' h (pullback.snd (f ≫ g) t))
    (hfst : h' ≫ pullback.fst (f ≫ g) t = pullback.fst (f ≫ g) (h ≫ t)) (k : ℤ)
    (α : chowGroup C ((h ≫ t) ≫ sZ) k) :
    letI : IsProper h' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback sq (P := @IsProper) inferInstance
    bivariantCompositeCap C G sX sY sZ f g hf hg hpp p q a b t k
        (properChowPushforward C ((h ≫ t) ≫ sZ) (t ≫ sZ) h (by simp [Category.assoc]) k
          (hpp _ _ _ _ _) α) =
      properChowPushforward C (pullback.fst (f ≫ g) (h ≫ t) ≫ sX)
        (pullback.fst (f ≫ g) t ≫ sX) h' (by rw [← Category.assoc, hfst]) (k - q - p)
        (hpp _ _ _ _ _)
        (bivariantCompositeCap C G sX sY sZ f g hf hg hpp p q a b (h ≫ t) k α)
declarations.comment: the proper-pushforward condition of the composite

registrations.name: Stacks.Chow.instAddCommGroupBivariantClass
registrations.comment: the abelian group of bivariant classes

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.BivariantClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B76.** A bivariant class of degree `p` for `f : X ⟶ Y`: a rule assigning to every
morphism `g : T ⟶ Y` locally of finite type and every `k` an additive map
`A_k(T) ⟶ A_{k-p}(T ×_Y X)`, natural for proper pushforward, for flat pullback of fixed relative
dimension, and for the Gysin map of the zero scheme of a section of an invertible module. The
group of all of them is denoted `A^p(X ⟶ Y)`.

Stated against a `Stacks.Chow.GysinSystem`, which supplies the first Chern class rule of Stacks
02SO and the vanishing of Stacks 02TO; see the module docstring.
declarations.comment: the group A^p(X ⟶ Y) of bivariant classes of degree p for f, stated against a GysinSystem supplying the first Chern class rule of Stacks 02SO and the vanishing of Stacks 02TO

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.BivariantClass.ext
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0B76.** Two bivariant classes agree as soon as all their cap operations agree.
declarations.comment: extensionality: a bivariant class is determined by its cap operations

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.BivariantClass.zero_cap
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0B76.** The zero bivariant class caps to zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem BivariantClass.zero_cap {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)

    (0 : BivariantClass C G sX sY f hf p).cap g k α = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.CanonicalBivariantClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B76.** The group `A^p(X ⟶ Y)` of bivariant classes of degree `p` for a morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` of schemes locally of finite type over the base: a rule assigning to every morphism
`g : T ⟶ Y` locally of finite type and every `k` an additive map
`A_k(T) ⟶ A_{k-p}(T ×_Y X)`, natural for proper pushforward, for flat pullback of fixed relative
dimension, and for the Gysin map of the zero scheme of a section of an invertible module.

This is `Stacks.Chow.BivariantClass` read against `Stacks.Chow.canonicalGysinSystem`, with the
abelian group structure of `Stacks.Chow.BivariantClass`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev CanonicalBivariantClass (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) (p : ℤ)
declarations.comment: the group A^p(X ⟶ Y) of bivariant classes of degree p for f, with nothing assumed: the Gysin system is the canonical one, whose first Chern class rule is the rule of an invertible module and whose vanishing is Stacks 02TO, and the descent conditions Stacks 02S1 and 02S2 of the proper and flat axioms are discharged

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.BivariantClass.flat_naturality_of_relativeDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B76 (2), with Stacks 02S1 discharged.** Cap product with a bivariant class commutes
with flat pullback of fixed relative dimension, the relative dimension of the base change being a
hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem BivariantClass.flat_naturality_of_relativeDimension (c : BivariantClass C G sX sY f hf p)
    {T T' : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (h : T' ⟶ T) [LocallyOfFiniteType h]
    [Flat h] (r : ℕ) (hr : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension h r)
    (h' : pullback f (h ≫ g) ⟶ pullback f g)
    (sq : IsPullback (pullback.snd f (h ≫ g)) h' h (pullback.snd f g))
    (hfst : h' ≫ pullback.fst f g = pullback.fst f (h ≫ g)) (k : ℤ) :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType h' :=
      MorphismProperty.of_isPullback sq (P := @LocallyOfFiniteType) inferInstance
    letI : Flat h' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback sq (P := @Flat) inferInstance
    ∀ (hr' : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension h' r) (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ sY) k),
      HEq
        (c.cap (h ≫ g) (k + (r : ℤ))
          (flatPullbackChow C ((h ≫ g) ≫ sY) (g ≫ sY) h (by simp [Category.assoc]) r hr k
            (flatPullbackDescends C _ _ _ _ _ _ _) α))
        (flatPullbackChow C (pullback.fst f (h ≫ g) ≫ sX) (pullback.fst f g ≫ sX) h'
          (by rw [← Category.assoc, hfst]) r hr' (k - p)
          (flatPullbackDescends C _ _ _ _ _ _ _) (c.cap g k α))
declarations.comment: the flat pullback axiom, with the descent condition Stacks 02S1 discharged; the relative dimension of the base change is assumed, Stacks 02NK being absent

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.BivariantClass.gysin_naturality_gysinChowOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B76 (3), for the canonical Gysin system.** Cap product with a bivariant class read
against `Stacks.Chow.canonicalGysinSystem` commutes with the unconditional Gysin map
`Stacks.Chow.gysinChowOfInvertible` of Stacks 02TO, for every pulled-back divisor; the descent
condition Stacks 02S2 for the identification of the base change of the zero scheme with the zero
scheme of the pulled-back section is discharged.
declarations.statement:
theorem BivariantClass.gysin_naturality_gysinChowOfInvertible
    (c : CanonicalBivariantClass C sX sY f hf p) {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (L : T.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible T.sheaf.obj T.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (pullback f g).sheaf.obj
      (pullback f g).ringCatSheaf.property ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.snd f g)).obj L)]
    (s : Γ(L, ⊤)) (k : ℤ) :
    let D := Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme T L s
    let L' := (Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.snd f g)).obj L
    let s' := AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackGlobalSections (pullback.snd f g) L s
    let E := Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme (pullback f g) L' s'
    ∀ (e : pullback f (D.subschemeι ≫ g) ≅ E.subscheme)
      (_he : e.hom ≫ E.subschemeι = bivariantBaseChangeMap f g D.subschemeι)
      (hbase : e.hom ≫ (E.subschemeι ≫ pullback.fst f g ≫ sX) =
        pullback.fst f (D.subschemeι ≫ g) ≫ sX)
      (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ sY) (k + 1)),
      properChowPushforward C (pullback.fst f (D.subschemeι ≫ g) ≫ sX)
          (E.subschemeι ≫ pullback.fst f g ≫ sX) e.hom hbase (k - p)
          (properPushforwardDescends C _ _ _ _ _)
          (c.cap (D.subschemeι ≫ g) k (gysinChowOfInvertible C (g ≫ sY) k L s α)) =
        gysinChowOfInvertible C (pullback.fst f g ≫ sX) (k - p) L' s'
          (Eq.mp (congrArg (chowGroup C (pullback.fst f g ≫ sX))
            (by omega : (k + 1) - p = (k - p) + 1)) (c.cap g (k + 1) α))
declarations.comment: the Gysin axiom for a class at the canonical Gysin system, stated for the unconditional Gysin map of Stacks 02TO and with the descent condition Stacks 02S2 discharged

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.BivariantChowClass
declarations.doc:
A bivariant class `c` of degree `p` for `f : X ⟶ Y`: a rule assigning to
every morphism `g : Y' ⟶ Y` locally of finite type and every `k` a map
`c ∩ - : CH_k(Y') ⟶ CH_{k-p}(X')`, `X' = Y' ×_Y X`, such that

1. for `h : Y'' ⟶ Y'` proper, `c ∩ h_* α'' = h'_* (c ∩ α'')`, `h' : X'' ⟶ X'` its base change;
2. for `h : Y'' ⟶ Y'` flat, locally of finite type, of relative dimension `r`,
   `c ∩ h^* α' = (h')^* (c ∩ α')`;
3. for an invertible module `L` on `Y'` with a global section `s`, zero scheme
   `i : D = Z(s) ⟶ Y'`, and pullback `(L', s', j : E = Z(s') ⟶ X')` to `X'`,
   `c ∩ i^* α' = j^* (c ∩ α')`, the scheme `D ×_Y X` being identified with `E` by Remark 0B6Y.

The group of all of them is `A^p(X ⟶ Y)`.
declarations.comment: a bivariant class of degree p for f, the elements of A^p(X → Y)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.BivariantChowClass.equivBivariantClass
declarations.doc:
A bivariant class of degree `p` for `f` is the same thing as a `Stacks.Chow.BivariantClass`
at the Gysin system `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible` of the first Chern class; the cap
operations correspond identically.
declarations.statement:
def equivBivariantClass :
    BivariantChowClass C sX sY f hf p ≃ BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf p
declarations.comment: bridge: A^p(X → Y) is BivariantClass at the Gysin system of the first Chern class

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.BivariantClass.proper_naturality_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
Capping with a bivariant class commutes with proper pushforward along a
proper morphism `h : T' ⟶ T` of test schemes and its base change `h'`, pushforward being taken
with the descent of Stacks 02S2,
`Stacks.Chow.properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper`.
declarations.statement:
theorem BivariantClass.proper_naturality_of_isProper (c : BivariantClass C G sX sY f hf p)
    {T T' : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (h : T' ⟶ T) [IsProper h]
    (h' : pullback f (h ≫ g) ⟶ pullback f g)
    (sq : IsPullback (pullback.snd f (h ≫ g)) h' h (pullback.snd f g))
    (hfst : h' ≫ pullback.fst f g = pullback.fst f (h ≫ g)) (k : ℤ)
    (α : chowGroup C ((h ≫ g) ≫ sY) k) :
    letI : IsProper h' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback sq (P := @IsProper) inferInstance
    c.cap g k (properChowPushforward C ((h ≫ g) ≫ sY) (g ≫ sY) h
        (by simp [Category.assoc]) k
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper C ((h ≫ g) ≫ sY)
          (g ≫ sY) h (by simp [Category.assoc]) k) α) =
      properChowPushforward C (pullback.fst f (h ≫ g) ≫ sX) (pullback.fst f g ≫ sX) h'
        (by rw [← Category.assoc, hfst]) (k - p)
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper C
          (pullback.fst f (h ≫ g) ≫ sX) (pullback.fst f g ≫ sX) h'
          (by rw [← Category.assoc, hfst]) (k - p)) (c.cap (h ≫ g) k α)
declarations.comment: the proper pushforward axiom, with the descent condition Stacks 02S2 discharged

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isFirstChernClassBivariant_firstChernClassBivariantCanonical
declarations.doc:
The bivariant class `Stacks.Chow.firstChernClassBivariantCanonical` caps by `c₁(g^*ℒ) ∩ -` on
every test scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFirstChernClassBivariant_firstChernClassBivariantCanonical :
    IsFirstChernClassBivariant C sX (canonicalFirstChernCapRule C) L (canonicalGysinSystem C)
      (firstChernClassBivariantCanonical C sX L)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.firstChernClassBivariantClass
declarations.doc:
For an invertible module `ℒ` on `X`, the rule assigning to `f : X' ⟶ X` the operation
`c₁(f^*ℒ) ∩ - : A_k(X') ⟶ A_{k-1}(X')` is a bivariant class of degree `1`: the class
`c₁(ℒ) ∈ A^1(X)` together with the statement that it caps by `c₁(f^*ℒ) ∩ -` on every test
scheme.
declarations.statement:
def firstChernClassBivariantClass :
    {c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sX (𝟙 X) (Category.id_comp sX) 1 //
      ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)
        (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ sX) k),
        c.idRule C sX (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) g k α =
          (invCap C (g ≫ sX) ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj L)).capOnChow C (g ≫ sX) (k - 1)
            (chowGroupCast C (g ≫ sX) (by omega) α)}

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatPullbackBivariantChowClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B78.** For `f : X ⟶ Y` flat of relative dimension `r` between schemes locally of
finite type over `S`, the rule which assigns to `g : Y' ⟶ Y` the flat pullback
`(f')^* : CH_k(Y') ⟶ CH_{k+r}(X ×_Y Y')` along the base change of `f` is a bivariant class of
degree `-r`, the class `f^* ∈ A^{-r}(X ⟶ Y)`.
declarations.statement: def flatPullbackBivariantChowClass : BivariantChowClass C sX sY f hf (-(r : ℤ))
declarations.comment: the flat-pullback rule as an element of A^{-r}(X → Y), the group of Stacks 0B76 whose three conditions use the genuine proper pushforward, flat pullback and Gysin map; its cap operation is flat pullback along the base change of f (flatPullbackBivariantChowClass_cap)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.existsUnique_bivariantChowClass_cap_eq_flatPullbackChow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B78.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be flat of relative dimension `r` between schemes locally of
finite type over `S`. The rule which assigns to `g : Y' ⟶ Y` the flat pullback
`(f')^* : CH_k(Y') ⟶ CH_{k+r}(X')` along the base change `f' : X' = X ×_Y Y' ⟶ Y'` of `f` is a
bivariant class of degree `-r`: there is exactly one `c ∈ A^{-r}(X ⟶ Y)` whose cap operation is
that rule, read in degree `k - (-r) = k + r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_bivariantChowClass_cap_eq_flatPullbackChow :
    ∃! c : BivariantChowClass C sX sY f hf (-(r : ℤ)),
      ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)
        (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ sY) k),
        c.cap g k α =
          chowGroupDegreeEquiv C (pullback.fst f g ≫ sX) (by ring : k + (r : ℤ) = k - -(r : ℤ))
            (flatPullbackChow C (pullback.fst f g ≫ sX) (g ≫ sY) (pullback.snd f g)
              (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sY f hf g) r
              (relativeDimension_pullback_snd f g r hfr) k
              (flatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_general C _ _ _ _ _ _ _) α)
declarations.comment: the flat-pullback rule is a bivariant class of degree -r, with nothing assumed: exactly one element of A^{-r}(X → Y), the group of Stacks 0B76 whose three conditions use the genuine proper pushforward, flat pullback and Gysin map, caps by (f')^*

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_bivariantChowClass_cap_heq_flatPullbackChow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B78**, with the degree transport removed. For `f : X ⟶ Y` flat of relative
dimension `r`, there is a bivariant class `c ∈ A^{-r}(X ⟶ Y)` whose cap operation on `CH_k(Y')`
is the flat pullback `(f')^* : CH_k(Y') ⟶ CH_{k+r}(X')` along the base change of `f`, landing in
degree `k + r` exactly as in the source. The two degrees `k + r` and `k - (-r)` are equal integers
that are not the same term, so the identity is a heterogeneous equality.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_bivariantChowClass_cap_heq_flatPullbackChow :
    ∃ c : BivariantChowClass C sX sY f hf (-(r : ℤ)),
      ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)
        (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ sY) k),
        c.cap g k α ≍
          flatPullbackChow C (pullback.fst f g ≫ sX) (g ≫ sY) (pullback.snd f g)
            (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sY f hf g) r
            (relativeDimension_pullback_snd f g r hfr) k
            (flatPullbackFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_general C _ _ _ _ _ _ _) α
declarations.comment: the flat-pullback rule (f')^* : CH_k(Y') → CH_{k+r}(X') is the cap operation of an element of A^{-r}(X → Y), with nothing assumed, read in degree k + r as the source writes it

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.existsUnique_bivariantClass_isBivariantFlatPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B78** for `Stacks.Chow.BivariantClass` at the Gysin system of the first Chern
class of an invertible module: exactly one bivariant class of degree `-r` for `f` caps by flat
pullback along the base change of `f`, in the sense of `Stacks.Chow.IsBivariantFlatPullback`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_bivariantClass_isBivariantFlatPullback :
    ∃! c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf (-(r : ℤ)),
      IsBivariantFlatPullback C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf r hfr
        (flatPullbackDescends C) c
declarations.comment: exactly one bivariant class of degree -r, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class, satisfies the characterization Stacks.Chow.IsBivariantFlatPullback, with nothing assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatPullbackBivariantClassOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
For `f : X ⟶ Y` flat of relative dimension `r` between schemes locally of finite type over the
base, the rule which assigns to a test scheme `g : T ⟶ Y` the flat pullback
`A_k(T) ⟶ A_{k+r}(X ×_Y T)` along the base change of `f`, as a bivariant class of degree `-r` for
`f` over the Gysin system `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible`.
declarations.statement:
def flatPullbackBivariantClassOfInvertible (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f] (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) (r : ℕ)
    (hfr : AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f r) :
    BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f hf (-(r : ℤ))
declarations.comment: the flat-pullback rule IS a bivariant class of degree -r, with NOTHING ASSUMED: the Stacks 02S1 descent is the theorem Stacks.Chow.flatPullbackDescends, Stacks 02RG on Chow groups is the theorem Stacks.Chow.properPushforwardFlatPullbackBaseChange above, and Stacks 0B71 with the identification of Stacks 0B6Y is the theorem Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_flatPullbackNaturalityAtZeroSchemeComparison

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinBivariantClass
declarations.doc:
Let `(𝓛, s, i : D ⟶ X)` be a triple as in Definition 02T8 on a scheme `X` locally of finite
type over the base. The rule assigning to every `g : X' ⟶ X` locally of finite type the Gysin map
`(i')^* : CH_k(X') ⟶ CH_{k-1}(D')` of the pulled-back section, where `D' = D ×_X X'`, is a
bivariant class of degree `1` for `i`: the class below caps by that Gysin map on every test
scheme.

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.VeryWeakCapRule.cap_eq_zero_of_isCycleGysinNatural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7A, the very weak form of Fulton's Theorem 17.1.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in
Situation 02QL, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type over `S` and let
`p ∈ ℤ`. A rule assigning to every locally of finite type `g : Y' ⟶ Y` and every `k` a map

  `c ∩ - : Z_k(Y') ⟶ A_{k-p}(X')`,   `X' = Y' ×_Y X`,

which satisfies condition (3) of Definition 0B76 whenever the invertible module restricts
trivially to the divisor, factors through rational equivalence: it kills every cycle rationally
equivalent to zero.

A cycle `α` rationally equivalent to zero is the total fibre difference of a locally finite
family of integral closed subschemes of `Y' ×_S 𝐏¹_S` (Stacks 02S4 part (4)); so `α` is the
difference of the two section Gysin images of the cycle `β` that family presents
(`Stacks.Chow.sub_gysinCycleMapAlong_sections_eq_of_familyFibreDifference`), and the two
sections are effective Cartier divisors with trivial normal bundle, so condition (3) applies at
both and gives the same value
(`Stacks.Chow.cap_gysinCycleMapAlong_zeroSection_eq_infinitySection_of_isCycleGysinNatural`).
declarations.statement:
theorem VeryWeakCapRule.cap_eq_zero_of_isCycleGysinNatural (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) (p : ℤ) (c : VeryWeakCapRule C sX sY f hf p)
    (hc : c.IsCycleGysinNatural) {T : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : T ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ) (α : CycleGroup C (g ≫ sY) k)
    (hα : α ∈ rationalEquivalences C (g ≫ sY) k) :
    c.cap g k α = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.VeryWeakCapRule.capChowOfCycleGysin
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7A.** The operation `c ∩ -` of a very weak cap rule satisfying condition (3) read
on cycles, descended to Chow groups: `A_k(Y') ⟶ A_{k-p}(X')`.
declarations.comment: the operation descended to Chow groups

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.comp_firstChernClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7B (2).** Let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module, let `f : X' ⟶ X` be locally of
finite type and let `c ∈ A^p(X' ⟶ X)` be a bivariant class. Then

  `c ∘ c₁(ℒ) = c₁(f^*ℒ) ∘ c`   in   `A^{p+1}(X' ⟶ X)`,

with `c₁(ℒ) ∈ A^1(X)` and `c₁(f^*ℒ) ∈ A^1(X')` the bivariant first Chern classes of Stacks 0B77.
The left side is a class for `f ≫ 𝟙 X` of degree `p + 1`; the right side, a class for `𝟙 X' ≫ f` of
degree `1 + p`, is read as one for `f ≫ 𝟙 X` of degree `p + 1` along the identity of `X'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_firstChernClass {X' : Scheme.{u}} {sX' : X' ⟶ C.S} [LocallyOfFiniteType sX']
    (L : X.Modules) [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (hf : f ≫ sX = sX') {p : ℤ} (c : BivariantChowClass C sX' sX f hf p) :
    haveI := isInvertible_pullback f L
    c.comp (BivariantChowClass.equivBivariantClass.symm (firstChernClass C sX L)) =
      (((BivariantChowClass.equivBivariantClass.symm
          (firstChernClass C sX' ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj L))).comp c).degreeCongr
        (add_comm 1 p)).transport (comp_comp_structureMorphism_eq hf (Category.id_comp sX))
        (Iso.refl X') (by simp)
declarations.comment: (2): c ∘ c_1(L) = c_1(f^*L) ∘ c in A^{p+1}(X' → X) for every f : X' → X locally of finite type and every bivariant class c in A^p(X' → X) of Stacks 0B76

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.firstChernClass_mem_center
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7B (1).** The first Chern class `c₁(ℒ) ∈ A^1(X)` of an invertible `𝒪_X`-module lies
in the center of the Chow cohomology ring `A^*(X)` of Stacks 0B7E. The ring structure is an
`@[instance_reducible] def` and not an `instance`, which is why it is supplied by hand.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClass_mem_center (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L] :
    letI : Ring (chowCohomology C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX) :=
      chowCohomologyRingOfInvertible C sX
    DirectSum.of (fun q : ℤ ↦ chowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX q) 1
        (firstChernClass C sX L) ∈
      Subring.center (chowCohomology C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX)
declarations.comment: (1): c_1(L) in A^1(X) is in the center of the Chow cohomology ring A^*(X) of Stacks 0B7E, for the bivariant first Chern class of Stacks 0B77

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.BivariantClass.heq_bivariantCompositeOfInvertible_firstChernClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7B (2).** Let `g : X' ⟶ X` be locally of finite type, let `c ∈ A^q(X' ⟶ X)` and
let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module. Then

  `c ∘ c₁(ℒ) = c₁(g^*ℒ) ∘ c`   in   `A^{q+1}(X' ⟶ X)`,

the composites being those of Stacks 0B75, classes for the equal morphisms `g ≫ 𝟙 X` and
`𝟙 X' ≫ g` of the equal degrees `q + 1` and `1 + q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem BivariantClass.heq_bivariantCompositeOfInvertible_firstChernClass
    (c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX' sX g hg q) (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L] :
    haveI := GenuineChern.isInvertible_pullback g L
    bivariantCompositeOfInvertible C sX' sX sX g (𝟙 X) hg (Category.id_comp sX) q 1 c
        (GenuineChern.firstChernClass C sX L) ≍
      bivariantCompositeOfInvertible C sX' sX' sX (𝟙 X') g (Category.id_comp sX') hg 1 q
        (GenuineChern.firstChernClass C sX' ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj L)) c
declarations.comment:
(2), for a homogeneous c in A^q(X' -> X) and the composition of Stacks 0B75 at the
Gysin system of the first Chern class of an invertible module; the two composites are classes for
g ≫ 𝟙 X and 𝟙 X' ≫ g of degrees q + 1 and 1 + q, whence the heterogeneous equality

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.BivariantClass.heq_mulId_firstChernClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7B (1).** The first Chern class `c₁(ℒ) ∈ A^1(X)` of an invertible module is in the
center of `A^*(X)`: for every `c ∈ A^q(X)`,

  `c · c₁(ℒ) = c₁(ℒ) · c`,

the two products lying in `A^{q+1}(X)` and `A^{1+q}(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem BivariantClass.heq_mulId_firstChernClass
    (c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sX (𝟙 X) (Category.id_comp sX) q)
    (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L] :
    c.mulId C sX (GenuineChern.firstChernClass C sX L) ≍
      (GenuineChern.firstChernClass C sX L).mulId C sX c

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyGRingOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The Chow cohomology of `X` as a graded ring, for the Gysin system
`Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible`: the degree `p` component is `A^p(X ⟶ X)`, the multiplication
is `Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyGradedMul` (composition of bivariant classes), the unit is
`Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyGradedOne` (the identity class `1 ∈ A^0(X)`), and `ℤ` maps to the
multiples of `1`.
declarations.statement:
def chowCohomologyGRingOfInvertible :
    DirectSum.GRing fun p : ℤ ↦ chowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX p
declarations.comment: the graded Z-algebra structure on A^*(X): composition of bivariant classes as the multiplication, with associativity, the unit 1 in A^0(X) and the two distributive laws, for the Gysin system of the genuine first Chern class rule and with no hypothesis on that system

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyRingOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The Chow cohomology `A^*(X)` as a ring, for the Gysin system
`Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible`.
declarations.statement:
def chowCohomologyRingOfInvertible :
    Ring (chowCohomology C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX)
declarations.comment: the ring structure on the graded group A^*(X), with no hypothesis on the Gysin system

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyAlgebraOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The *Chow cohomology* of `X`: the graded `ℤ`-algebra `A^*(X)` whose degree `p` component is
`A^p(X ⟶ X)`, for the Gysin system `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible`.
declarations.comment: the graded Z-algebra A^*(X), the Chow cohomology of X, with no hypothesis on the Gysin system

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.ChowCohomologyGroup
declarations.doc:
The group `A^p(X) = A^p(X ⟶ X)` of bivariant classes of degree `p` (Stacks 0B76) for the
identity morphism of `X`.
declarations.statement: abbrev ChowCohomologyGroup (p : ℤ) : Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the degree p component A^p(X) = A^p(X → X) of the Chow cohomology: the bivariant classes of degree p of Stacks 0B76 for id_X

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.ChowCohomologyGroup.instGRing
declarations.doc:
The family `p ↦ A^p(X)` is a graded ring: the product `A^p(X) × A^q(X) ⟶ A^{p+q}(X)` is the
composition of bivariant classes of Stacks 0B75, which is associative and bilinear, with unit the
class `1 ∈ A^0(X)`.
declarations.statement: instance instGRing : DirectSum.GRing (ChowCohomologyGroup C sX)
declarations.comment: the graded Z-algebra structure on A^*(X): the product of the degree p and q components is the composition A^p(X → X) × A^q(X → X) → A^{p+q}(X → X) of Stacks 0B75, associative and bilinear, with unit 1 ∈ A^0(X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.ChowCohomology
declarations.doc:
The *Chow cohomology* `A^*(X)` of `X`: the graded `ℤ`-algebra `⊕_{p ∈ ℤ} A^p(X)` whose degree
`p` component is `A^p(X ⟶ X)`, with the multiplication of
`Stacks.Chow.ChowCohomologyGroup.instGRing`, composition of bivariant classes.
declarations.statement: abbrev ChowCohomology : Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the Chow cohomology A^*(X): the graded Z-algebra ⊕_p A^p(X → X), with multiplication the composition of bivariant classes

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7E.** The degree `p` part `A^p(X)` of the Chow cohomology of a scheme `X` locally
of finite type over the base: the group `A^p(X ⟶ X)` of bivariant classes of degree `p` for the
identity morphism of `X`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev chowCohomologyComponent (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (G : GysinSystem C) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (p : ℤ) : Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the degree p part

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7E.** The Chow cohomology `A^*(X)` of a scheme `X` locally of finite type over the
base: the graded group whose degree `p` part is the group `A^p(X ⟶ X)` of bivariant classes of
degree `p` for the identity morphism of `X`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev chowCohomology (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (G : GysinSystem C) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] : Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the graded group

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7F.** The restriction map `res : A^p(Y) ⟶ A^p(Y')` along a morphism `f : Y' ⟶ Y`
of schemes locally of finite type over the base, a homomorphism of groups: the special case
`X = Y`, `f = 𝟙 Y` of the restriction map of Stacks 0F9Z, followed by the transport of a
bivariant class along the canonical isomorphism `Y ×_Y Y' ≅ Y'`. It is often written `f^*`.

The tag asserts more, namely that the induced map `A^*(Y) ⟶ A^*(Y')` of the graded groups is a
map of `ℤ`-algebras. The multiplication is composition of bivariant classes, and the graded ring
it makes of `A^*(Y)` is `Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyGRing` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.Bivariant.ChowCohomologyCompositionRing`, hypothesis-free for
the Gysin system this repository constructs as `Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyGRingOfInvertible`. Only
the additive map is given here; that it respects that multiplication is
`Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyRestriction_chowCohomologyRingMul` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.Bivariant.ChowCohomologyMultiplicative`, which assembles the
`ℤ`-algebra map of the tag as
`Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyTotalRestrictionAlgHomOfInvertible`.
declarations.statement:
def chowCohomologyRestriction (hgys : G.IsNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso) :
    chowCohomologyComponent C G sY p →+ chowCohomologyComponent C G (f ≫ sY) p
declarations.comment: the canonical map

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyRestriction_cap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7F.** The restriction map on Chow cohomology satisfies the cap formula of Stacks
0F9Z: `res(c) ∩ α = c ∩ α` for every `α ∈ CH_k(T)` and every test scheme `g : T ⟶ Y'`, both
sides read in `CH_{k-p}(T)` through the canonical identifications `Y' ×_{Y'} T ≅ T` and
`Y ×_Y T ≅ T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowCohomologyRestriction_cap (hgys : G.IsNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso)
    (c : chowCohomologyComponent C G sY p) {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ Y') [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    (k : ℤ)
    (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ (f ≫ sY)) k) :
    chowPushforwardOfIso C (pullback.fst (𝟙 Y') g ≫ (f ≫ sY)) (g ≫ (f ≫ sY))
        (identityBaseChangeIso g).hom (identityBaseChangeIso_hom_comp_base C (f ≫ sY) g) (k - p)
        ((chowCohomologyRestriction C G sY f p hgys c).cap g k α) =
      chowPushforwardOfIso C (pullback.fst (𝟙 Y) (g ≫ f) ≫ sY) (g ≫ (f ≫ sY))
        (identityBaseChangeIso (g ≫ f)).hom
        (by rw [← Category.assoc]; exact identityBaseChangeIso_hom_comp_base C sY (g ≫ f))
        (k - p) (c.cap (g ≫ f) k (chowGroupCongr C (Category.assoc g f sY).symm k α))
declarations.comment: the cap formula for the canonical map

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyTotalRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7F.** The restriction map `res : A^*(Y) ⟶ A^*(Y')` of the graded Chow cohomology
groups along `f : Y' ⟶ Y`, a homomorphism of graded groups: the degreewise restriction map.

The tag asserts that this is a map of `ℤ`-algebras. The multiplication on `A^*` is composition of
bivariant classes and the graded ring it produces is `Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyGRing` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.Bivariant.ChowCohomologyCompositionRing`. Only additivity is
proved here; that this map respects that multiplication is
`Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyTotalRestriction_mul` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.Bivariant.ChowCohomologyMultiplicative`, and the `ℤ`-algebra
map of the tag is `Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyTotalRestrictionAlgHomOfInvertible` there.
declarations.statement:
def chowCohomologyTotalRestriction (hgys : G.IsNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso) :
    chowCohomology C G sY →+ chowCohomology C G (f ≫ sY)
declarations.comment: the canonical map of graded groups

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyRestrictionOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7F.** The restriction map `res : A^p(Y) ⟶ A^p(Y')` along a morphism `f : Y' ⟶ Y`
of schemes locally of finite type over the base, a homomorphism of groups, at the Gysin system of
the first Chern class rule of an invertible module. It is often written `f^*`.

This is `Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyRestriction` with its case of Stacks 02TA discharged, by
`Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso`. Nothing is assumed: the Gysin
system itself carries no hypothesis either, so the only hypotheses are those of the tag.
declarations.comment: the canonical map, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with nothing assumed beyond the tag's own hypotheses

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyRestrictionOfInvertible_cap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7F.** The restriction map on Chow cohomology satisfies the cap formula of Stacks
0F9Z: `res(c) ∩ α = c ∩ α` for every `α ∈ CH_k(T)` and every test scheme `g : T ⟶ Y'`, both
sides read in `CH_{k-p}(T)` through the canonical identifications `Y' ×_{Y'} T ≅ T` and
`Y ×_Y T ≅ T`. Nothing is assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowCohomologyRestrictionOfInvertible_cap
    (c : chowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sY p) {T : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : T ⟶ Y') [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)
    (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ (f ≫ sY)) k) :
    chowPushforwardOfIso C (pullback.fst (𝟙 Y') g ≫ (f ≫ sY)) (g ≫ (f ≫ sY))
        (identityBaseChangeIso g).hom (identityBaseChangeIso_hom_comp_base C (f ≫ sY) g) (k - p)
        ((chowCohomologyRestrictionOfInvertible C sY f p c).cap g k α) =
      chowPushforwardOfIso C (pullback.fst (𝟙 Y) (g ≫ f) ≫ sY) (g ≫ (f ≫ sY))
        (identityBaseChangeIso (g ≫ f)).hom
        (by rw [← Category.assoc]; exact identityBaseChangeIso_hom_comp_base C sY (g ≫ f))
        (k - p) (c.cap (g ≫ f) k (chowGroupCongr C (Category.assoc g f sY).symm k α))
declarations.comment: the cap formula for the canonical map, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with nothing assumed beyond the tag's own hypotheses

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyTotalRestrictionOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7F.** The restriction map `res : A^*(Y) ⟶ A^*(Y')` of the graded Chow cohomology
groups along `f : Y' ⟶ Y`, a homomorphism of graded groups, at the Gysin system of the first
Chern class rule: the degreewise restriction map. Nothing is assumed.

That this graded map is a map of `ℤ`-algebras is the `AddMonoidHom` structure here and in each
degree, together with `Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyRestrictionOfInvertible_mul` and
`Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyRestrictionOfInvertible_bivariantIdentityClass`.
declarations.comment: the canonical map of graded groups, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with nothing assumed beyond the tag's own hypotheses

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyRestrictionOfInvertible_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7F.** The restriction map `res : A^*(Y) ⟶ A^*(Y')` along `f : Y' ⟶ Y` is
multiplicative: `res(a ⬝ b) = res(a) ⬝ res(b)` for `a ∈ A^p(Y)` and `b ∈ A^q(Y)`, the
multiplication being composition of bivariant classes, Stacks 0B75. Nothing is assumed.

This is `Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyRestriction_mul` with both of its cases of Stacks 02TA
discharged, by `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso` and
`Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderPullbackCompPushforward`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowCohomologyRestrictionOfInvertible_mul
    (a : chowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sY p)
    (b : chowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sY q) :
    chowCohomologyRestrictionOfInvertible C sY f (p + q)
        (chowCohomologyMulOfInvertible C sY p q a b) =
      chowCohomologyMulOfInvertible C (f ≫ sY) p q
        (chowCohomologyRestrictionOfInvertible C sY f p a)
        (chowCohomologyRestrictionOfInvertible C sY f q b)
declarations.comment: the canonical map is multiplicative: res(a ⬝ b) = res(a) ⬝ res(b), the multiplication on Chow cohomology being composition of bivariant classes -- at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with nothing assumed beyond the tag's own hypotheses

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyRestrictionOfInvertible_bivariantIdentityClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7F.** The restriction map `res : A^*(Y) ⟶ A^*(Y')` along `f : Y' ⟶ Y` is unital:
it carries the identity class `1 ∈ A^0(Y)` of Stacks 0FBS to the identity class `1 ∈ A^0(Y')`.
Nothing is assumed.

This is `Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyRestriction_bivariantIdentityClass` with its case of Stacks
02TA discharged by `Stacks.Chow.gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso` and its two
Gysin axioms for the transported identity cap rule discharged by
`Stacks.Chow.IdentityCapRule.transportGysinNaturality` — exactly the proofs
`Stacks.Chow.bivariantIdentityClassOfInvertible` is built from, so the two identity classes in
the statement are the unconditional ones.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowCohomologyRestrictionOfInvertible_bivariantIdentityClass :
    chowCohomologyRestrictionOfInvertible C sY f 0 (bivariantIdentityClassOfInvertible C sY) =
      bivariantIdentityClassOfInvertible C (f ≫ sY)
declarations.comment: the canonical map is unital: it carries the identity class 1 of A^0(Y) to the identity class of A^0(Y') -- at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with nothing assumed beyond the tag's own hypotheses

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyTotalRestrictionRingOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7F.** The restriction map `res : A^*(Y) ⟶ A^*(Y')` along `f : Y' ⟶ Y` as a map of
the ring structures of the graded Chow cohomology: a homomorphism for addition and for the
multiplication of Stacks 0B75, at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule. It is often
written `f^*`.

Its underlying additive map is `Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyTotalRestrictionOfInvertible`, and that
it also carries `1` to `1` is `Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyTotalRestrictionRingOfInvertible_map_one`
just below; since an additive map between abelian groups is `ℤ`-linear, the two together are the
whole of the tag's "map of `ℤ`-algebras". Nothing is assumed.

The proof reduces to the degreewise statement
`Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyRestrictionOfInvertible_mul`: multiplication on a `DirectSum` is
bilinear, so both sides of `res(x ⬝ y) = res(x) ⬝ res(y)` are additive in `x` and in `y` and it
is enough to check them on the summands.
declarations.comment: the canonical map res : A^*(Y) → A^*(Y') on the graded groups is a homomorphism for addition and for the multiplication of Stacks 0B75 -- at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with nothing assumed beyond the tag's own hypotheses

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyTotalRestrictionRingOfInvertible_map_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7F.** The restriction map `res : A^*(Y) ⟶ A^*(Y')` carries the unit `1` of
`A^*(Y)` to the unit of `A^*(Y')`: the unit of the graded ring is the identity class of Stacks
0FBS sitting in degree `0`, and `res` carries it to the identity class of `A^0(Y')` by
`Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyRestrictionOfInvertible_bivariantIdentityClass`. Nothing is
assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowCohomologyTotalRestrictionRingOfInvertible_map_one :
    chowCohomologyTotalRestrictionRingOfInvertible C sY f 1 = 1
declarations.comment: the canonical map res : A^*(Y) → A^*(Y') on the graded groups carries the unit 1 of A^*(Y) to the unit of A^*(Y') -- at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, with nothing assumed beyond the tag's own hypotheses

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyRestriction_chowCohomologyComposite
declarations.doc:
**The restriction map of Stacks 0B7F is multiplicative:** `res(c ∘ c') = res(c) ∘ res(c')` for
the multiplication `Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyComposite` of `A^*`, and so for the restriction
`Aⁱ(X) ⟶ Aⁱ(Z)` of Stacks 0F9Z that the second pairing of Stacks 0FA0 is built from.

This is the clause of Stacks 0B7F asserting that `res : A^*(Y) ⟶ A^*(Y')` is a map of
`ℤ`-algebras, for the multiplication of `A^*` that this repository has. It is also the first of
the two inputs an associativity proof for the multiplication of Stacks 0FA0 needs: the degree `n`
terms `res(res(c) ∘ c') ∘ c''` and `res(c) ∘ (res(c') ∘ c'')` of the two groupings cannot be
compared without it, however associative the composition of Stacks 0B75 is.

Both sides cap, on a test scheme `g : T ⟶ Y'`, by capping with `c'` and then with `c`, both at
test morphisms over `Y` obtained from `g ≫ f`; the two differ by an isomorphism of test schemes,
which the proper-pushforward axiom of Stacks 0B76 for `c` absorbs.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowCohomologyRestriction_chowCohomologyComposite (i j : ℤ)
    (c : chowCohomologyComponent C G sY i) (c' : chowCohomologyComponent C G sY j) :
    chowCohomologyRestriction C G sY f (i + j) hgys
        (chowCohomologyComposite C G sY hgys hgysc i j c c') =
      chowCohomologyComposite C G (f ≫ sY) hgys hgysc i j
        (chowCohomologyRestriction C G sY f i hgys c)
        (chowCohomologyRestriction C G sY f j hgys c')
declarations.comment: the multiplicativity of the canonical map: res(c ∘ c') = res(c) ∘ res(c') for the multiplication of A^* that is composition of bivariant classes, which is the clause that the map of graded groups is a map of algebras

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.chernCapOnCycles_gysin
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7G.** Let `ℰ` be finite locally free of rank `r` on `X` and let
`(ℒ, s, i : D ⟶ X)` be as in Definition 02T8. Let `α ∈ A_{k+1}(X)`, let `a` be a cycle
representing `α` and `b` a cycle representing `i^*α ∈ A_k(D)`. Then for every `0 ≤ j ≤ r`

  `c_j(ℰ|_D) ∩ b = i^*(c_j(ℰ) ∩ a)`  in  `A_{k-j}(D)`,

for the Gysin map of Stacks 02TO and intersection with Chern classes of Stacks 02U5; that is,
`c_j(ℰ|_D) ∩ i^*α = i^*(c_j(ℰ) ∩ α)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chernCapOnCycles_gysin (E : X.Modules) (r : ℕ)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E r] (k : ℤ)
    (j : Fin (r + 1)) (α : chowGroup C sX (k + 1)) (a : CycleGroup C sX (k + 1))
    (ha : QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences C sX (k + 1)) a = α)
    (b : CycleGroup C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ sX) k)
    (hb : QuotientAddGroup.mk'
        (rationalEquivalences C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ sX) k) b =
      gysinChowOfInvertible C sX k L s α) :
    letI := AlgebraicGeometry.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_pullback
      (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι E r
