    chernCapOnCycles C ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ≫ sX)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι).obj E) r k j b =
      gysinChowOfInvertible C sX (k - (j : ℤ)) L s
        (chowGroupCast C sX (show k + 1 - (j : ℤ) = k - (j : ℤ) + 1 by omega)
          (chernCapOnCycles C sX E r (k + 1) j a))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.chernCap_gysin
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7G.** Let `ℰ` be finite locally free of rank `r` on `Y` and let `(ℒ, s, i : D ⟶ Y)`
be a triple as in Definition 02T8. Then for every `0 ≤ j ≤ r` and every `α ∈ A_{k+1}(Y)`

  `c_j(ℰ|_D) ∩ i^*α = i^*(c_j(ℰ) ∩ α)`  in  `A_{k-j}(D)`,

for the Chern class cap products of Stacks 02U6 and the Gysin map of Stacks 02TO.
declarations.statement:
theorem chernCap_gysin (E : Y.Modules) (r : ℕ)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E r] (k : ℤ)
    (j : Fin (r + 1)) (α : chowGroup C sY (k + 1)) :
    letI := AlgebraicGeometry.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_pullback
      (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme Y L s).subschemeι E r
    chernCap C r ((Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme Y L s).subschemeι ≫ sY)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme Y L s).subschemeι).obj E) k j
        (gysinChowOfInvertible C sY k L s α) =
      gysinChowOfInvertible C sY (k - (j : ℤ)) L s
        (chowGroupCast C sY (show k + 1 - (j : ℤ) = k - (j : ℤ) + 1 by omega)
          (chernCap C r sY E (k + 1) j α))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.chernClassBivariantClass
declarations.doc:
For a finite locally free module `ℰ` of rank `r` on `X` and `0 ≤ j ≤ r`, the rule assigning
to `f : X' ⟶ X` the operation `c_j(f^*ℰ) ∩ - : A_k(X') ⟶ A_{k-j}(X')` is a bivariant class of
degree `j`: the class `c_j(ℰ) ∈ A^j(X)` together with its characterization.

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.chernClassBivariantClassOnCycles
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7H.** For a locally free module `ℰ` of rank `r` on `X` and `0 ≤ j ≤ r`, the rule
assigning to `f : X' ⟶ X` the operation `c_j(f^*ℰ) ∩ - : A_k(X') ⟶ A_{k-j}(X')` of Stacks 02U5 is
a bivariant class of degree `j`: a class `c ∈ A^j(X)` with `c ∩ [α] = c_j(f^*ℰ) ∩ α` for every
`f : X' ⟶ X` and every `k`-cycle `α` on `X'`, the cap operation being read on `X'` through the
identification `X ×_X X' ≅ X'`.
declarations.statement:
def chernClassBivariantClassOnCycles :
    {c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sX (𝟙 X) (Category.id_comp sX) (j : ℤ) //
      ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)
        (α : CycleGroup C (g ≫ sX) k),
        letI := AlgebraicGeometry.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_pullback g F r
        chowPushforwardOfIso C (pullback.fst (𝟙 X) g ≫ sX) (g ≫ sX)
            (identityBaseChangeIso g).hom (identityBaseChangeIso_hom_comp_base C sX g)
            (k - (j : ℤ)) (c.cap g k (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences C (g ≫ sX) k) α)) =
          chernCapOnCycles C (g ≫ sX) ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj F) r k j α}

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.topologicalKrullDim_eq_iSup_localKrullDim
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7I.** The Krull dimension of a topological space is the supremum of its
local Krull dimensions over all of its points. When `X` is empty both sides are `⊥ = -∞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_eq_iSup_localKrullDim (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] :
    topologicalKrullDim X = ⨆ x : X, localKrullDim X x

declarations.name: RingFibreProduct.primeSpectrum_isPushout
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7J.** The prime spectrum of `B ×_A A'`, where `A' → A` is surjective,
is the pushout of `Spec(B)` and `Spec(A')` over `Spec(A)` as a topological space.
declarations.statement:
public theorem primeSpectrum_isPushout
    {A A' B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing A'] [CommRing B]
    {toBase : B →+* A} {surjection : A' →+* A} {I : Ideal A'}
    (s : Situation toBase surjection I) :
    IsPushout
      (TopCat.ofHom ⟨PrimeSpectrum.comap toBase, PrimeSpectrum.continuous_comap toBase⟩)
      (TopCat.ofHom ⟨PrimeSpectrum.comap surjection, PrimeSpectrum.continuous_comap surjection⟩)
      (TopCat.ofHom ⟨PrimeSpectrum.comap s.pullbackCone.fst.hom,
        PrimeSpectrum.continuous_comap s.pullbackCone.fst.hom⟩)
      (TopCat.ofHom ⟨PrimeSpectrum.comap s.pullbackCone.snd.hom,
        PrimeSpectrum.continuous_comap s.pullbackCone.snd.hom⟩)

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleSurjectiveThickening.isQuasiAffine_iff_isQuasiAffine
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B7K].** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion of Noetherian schemes inducing a
homeomorphism of underlying topological spaces — that is, a closed immersion surjective on
points. Then `X` is quasi-affine if and only if `Z` is quasi-affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffine_iff_isQuasiAffine [IsClosedImmersion i] [Surjective i] [IsNoetherian X] :
    X.IsQuasiAffine ↔ Z.IsQuasiAffine

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.isQuasiAffine_iff_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 0B7K].** For a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of Noetherian schemes
inducing a homeomorphism of underlying spaces — equivalently, a surjective closed immersion — the
ambient scheme is quasi-affine if and only if the closed subscheme is.

Both implications are unconditional. *Ambient `⟹` closed subscheme* is the elementary one, a
closed immersion being affine (`Stacks.Thickenings.isQuasiAffine_of_isQuasiAffine_ambient`).
*Closed subscheme `⟹` ambient* is
`Stacks.Thickenings.isQuasiAffine_of_isThickening_of_isLocallyNoetherian`: over a Noetherian
scheme a thickening is of finite order, and along a finite-order thickening an affine basic open
lifts, by the square-zero computation of
`Stacks.Thickenings.affineBasicOpenLifts_of_isFirstOrderThickening_of_isQuasiAffine` along the
filtration by the powers of the ideal sheaf. Neither the ampleness criterion
[Stacks Project, Tag 01QE] nor [Stacks Project, Tag 09MS] nor any cohomology group enters, so the
hypothesis `Stacks.AmpleClosedImmersion.SectionsLiftAfterPower` carried by
`Stacks.AmpleSurjectiveThickening.isQuasiAffine_iff_of_sectionsLiftAfterPower` is discharged.

Noetherianness of the closed subscheme is not used, and of the ambient scheme only local
Noetherianness together with quasi-compactness; both are carried because the source assumes
them.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffine_iff_of_isNoetherian {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [Surjective i] [IsNoetherian Z] [IsNoetherian X] :
    X.IsQuasiAffine ↔ Z.IsQuasiAffine

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.isQuasiAffine_of_isQuasiAffine_ambient
declarations.doc:
**The implication *ambient quasi-affine `⟹` closed subscheme quasi-affine* of
[Stacks Project, Tag 0B7L].** If the ambient scheme of a thickening `i : X ⟶ X'` is quasi-affine,
then so is the closed subscheme.

This is the implication the source calls elementary, and it is: a closed immersion is an affine
morphism, and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsQuasiAffine.of_isAffineHom` says the source of an affine
morphism into a quasi-affine scheme is quasi-affine. Surjectivity of `i` is not used; it is
carried because it is half of the source's hypothesis, so that this is literally one implication
of the source statement.

The source's hypothesis that `i` is a closed immersion inducing a homeomorphism of underlying
spaces is `Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening`: for a closed immersion, being a homeomorphism on
points is being surjective, which is
`Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening.isHomeomorph`.

The reverse implication is the one part (9) of [Stacks Project, Tag 09ZV] needs. It is isolated as
`Stacks.Thickenings.QuasiAffineAscendsAlongThickening`, and it is proved for every **finite-order**
thickening in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/MoreMorphisms/ThickeningMorphism/QuasiAffineAscent.lean`
(`Stacks.Thickenings.isQuasiAffine_of_isFiniteOrderThickening`), hence for every thickening of a
locally Noetherian scheme, and for an arbitrary thickening in
`Stacks.Thickenings.isQuasiAffine_of_isThickening` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/MoreMorphisms/ThickeningMorphism/QuasiAffineLimit.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffine_of_isQuasiAffine_ambient {X X' : Scheme.{u}} {i : X ⟶ X'}
    (hi : IsThickening i) (hX' : Scheme.IsQuasiAffine X') : Scheme.IsQuasiAffine X
declarations.comment: the implication: ambient quasi-affine ⟹ closed subscheme quasi-affine

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.isQuasiAffine_iff_of_isThickening
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 0B7L].** For a closed immersion inducing a homeomorphism of underlying
spaces — equivalently, a surjective closed immersion — the ambient scheme is quasi-affine if and
only if the closed subscheme is. No Noetherian hypothesis.

*Ambient `⟹` closed subscheme* is the elementary implication, a closed immersion being affine
(`Stacks.Thickenings.isQuasiAffine_of_isQuasiAffine_ambient`); *closed subscheme `⟹` ambient* is
`Stacks.Thickenings.isQuasiAffine_of_isThickening`. This supersedes the Noetherian
`Stacks.Thickenings.isQuasiAffine_iff_of_isNoetherian`, which is
[Stacks Project, Tag 0B7K].
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffine_iff_of_isThickening {Y Y' : Scheme.{u}} {k : Y ⟶ Y'}
    (hk : IsThickening k) : Scheme.IsQuasiAffine Y' ↔ Scheme.IsQuasiAffine Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasPushout_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B7M].** The pushout of two closed immersions of schemes exists in the
category of schemes.
declarations.statement:
instance hasPushout_of_isClosedImmersion {Z X Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : Z ⟶ Y)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsClosedImmersion j] : HasPushout i j
declarations.comment: the pushout exists

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_pushout_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B7M].** The defining pushout square of two closed immersions of schemes is
also a fibre square.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_pushout_of_isClosedImmersion {Z X Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : Z ⟶ Y)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsClosedImmersion j] :
    IsPullback i j (pushout.inl i j) (pushout.inr i j)
declarations.comment: the diagram is a fibre square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pushout_inl_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B7M].** The canonical map `a : X ⟶ Y ⨿_Z X` out of the first scheme is a
closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
instance pushout_inl_isClosedImmersion {Z X Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : Z ⟶ Y)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsClosedImmersion j] : IsClosedImmersion (pushout.inl i j)
declarations.comment: the morphism a is a closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pushout_inr_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B7M].** The canonical map `b : Y ⟶ Y ⨿_Z X` out of the second scheme is a
closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
instance pushout_inr_isClosedImmersion {Z X Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : Z ⟶ Y)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsClosedImmersion j] : IsClosedImmersion (pushout.inr i j)
declarations.comment: the morphism b is a closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pushout_structureSheafModule_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B7M].** For two closed immersions `i : Z ⟶ X` and `j : Z ⟶ Y`, the
canonical sequence

`0 ⟶ 𝒪_(Y ⨿_Z X) ⟶ a_* 𝒪_X ⊕ b_* 𝒪_Y ⟶ c_* 𝒪_Z ⟶ 0`

of modules over the structure sheaf of the pushout is short exact, where `a` and `b` are the
two canonical maps into the pushout and `c = a ∘ i = b ∘ j`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pushout_structureSheafModule_shortExact {Z X Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : Z ⟶ Y)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsClosedImmersion j] :
    ∃ zero : pushoutStructureSheafModuleToBiprod i j ≫ pushoutBiprodToIntersection i j = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk (pushoutStructureSheafModuleToBiprod i j)
        (pushoutBiprodToIntersection i j) zero).ShortExact
declarations.comment: the short exact sequence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_image_mul_of_open
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B7N.** The image of `T × U` under parametrized
multiplication is open.
declarations.statement:
lemma isOpen_image_mul_of_open {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (G T : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G] (ψ : T ⟶ G)
    (U : G.left.Opens) :
    IsOpen (Set.image (lift (fst T G ≫ ψ) (snd T G) ≫ μ[G]).left.base
      ((snd T G).left.base ⁻¹' (U : Set G.left)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.compactSpace_of_irreducibleSpace_grpObj
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0B7P.** An irreducible group scheme over a field is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
instance compactSpace_of_irreducibleSpace_grpObj
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (G : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G]
    [IrreducibleSpace G.left] : CompactSpace G.left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.irreducibleSpace_of_connectedSpace
declarations.doc: A connected group scheme over a field is irreducible.
declarations.statement:
theorem irreducibleSpace_of_connectedSpace
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (G : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G]
    [ConnectedSpace G.left] : IrreducibleSpace G.left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.identityComponent
declarations.doc:
The canonical closed subgroup scheme whose support is the connected component of
the identity of `G`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def identityComponent (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) : ClosedSubgroupScheme G
declarations.comment: construction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.identityComponent_flat
declarations.doc: The inclusion of the identity component is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem identityComponent_flat (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) :
    Flat (identityComponent k G).ι.hom.hom.left
declarations.comment: part (1): flatness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.identityComponent_range
declarations.doc: The underlying set of the identity subgroup is the connected component of the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem identityComponent_range (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) :
    Set.range (identityComponent k G).ι.hom.hom.left =
      connectedComponent (identityPoint k G)
declarations.comment: part (2): support

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.identityComponent_geometricallyIrreducible
declarations.doc: The identity component is geometrically irreducible over the field.
declarations.statement:
theorem identityComponent_geometricallyIrreducible (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) :
    GeometricallyIrreducible (identityComponent k G).carrier.X.hom
declarations.comment: part (3): geometric irreducibility

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.identityComponent_compactSpace
declarations.doc: The identity component is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem identityComponent_compactSpace (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) :
    CompactSpace (identityComponent k G).carrier.X.left
declarations.comment: part (4): quasi-compactness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.identityComponent_unique
declarations.doc:
Any flat closed subgroup scheme supported on the identity component is uniquely
isomorphic to the identity component over `G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem identityComponent_unique (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k))))
    (H : ClosedSubgroupScheme G)
    [Flat H.ι.hom.hom.left]
    (hH : Set.range H.ι.hom.hom.left =
      connectedComponent (identityPoint k G)) :
    ∃! φ : H.carrier ≅ (identityComponent k G).carrier,
      φ.hom ≫ (identityComponent k G).ι = H.ι
declarations.comment: canonicality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpen_containing_rational_points
declarations.doc:
A finite family of rational points of a group scheme locally of finite type over an
algebraically closed field lies in an affine open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_containing_rational_points (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    (G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) [LocallyOfFiniteType G.X.hom] {σ : Type v} [Finite σ]
    (g : σ → (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ G.X)) :
    ∃ U : G.X.left.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧
      ∀ i, (g i).left.base (⊥ : PrimeSpectrum k) ∈ U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isHomeomorph_pullback_to_product
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and let `A` be a filtered colimit of
`k`-algebras that are finite products of copies of `k`.  For any scheme `X` over `k`, the
canonical map from the underlying space of `Spec A ×_k X` to `|Spec A| × |X|` is a
homeomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isHomeomorph_pullback_to_product
    (k A : Type u) [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (hA : IsFilteredColimitOfFiniteProducts k A)
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (of k)) :
    IsHomeomorph (fun x :
      (pullback (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k A))) f : Scheme.{u}) ↦
        ((pullback.fst (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k A))) f).base x,
          (pullback.snd (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k A))) f).base x))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpen_range_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B7U.** The image in a Jacobson group scheme of the spectrum of a
filtered colimit of finite products of the algebraically closed ground field is contained in an
affine open, provided every closed point of the group scheme is rational over the ground field.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_range_subset
    (k A : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))))
    [JacobsonSpace G.X.left]
    (hclosed : ∀ x : G.X.left, IsClosed ({x} : Set G.X.left) →
      ∃ p : Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) ⟶ G.X,
        p.left.base (⊥ : PrimeSpectrum k) = x)
    (hA : IsFilteredColimitOfFiniteProducts k A)
    (f : Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))) ⟶ G.X) :
    ∃ U : G.X.left.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ Set.range f.left.base ⊆ U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_image_comp_of_isOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B7V.** If the objects of a groupoid scheme form the spectrum
of a field, the image of the composition of a family of arrows with an open set of arrows
is open.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpen_image_comp_of_isOpen
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (hobjects : G.objects.left ≅ Spec (.of k))
    (Z : Over S) (f : Z ⟶ G.arrows) (W : G.arrows.left.Opens) :
    let p := pullback.snd f (pullback.fst G.source G.target)
    IsOpen ((p ≫ G.comp).left.base ''
      {x | (p ≫ pullback.snd G.source G.target).left.base x ∈ W})

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_specializes_pointsMap_eq_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7W.** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a flat morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let
`x' ⤳ x` be a specialization of points of `X` and assume that every étale chart of `X` by an
affine scheme has a finite fibre above `x'`, which is condition (2) of Stacks 03JS for the
pair `(X, x')`. Then every point `y` of `Y` above `x` is the specialization of a point of `Y`
above `x'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_specializes_pointsMap_eq_of_isFlat
    {Y X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (f : Y ⟶ X) (hf : IsFlat B S hS f)
    {x x' : points B S hS X} (hs : x' ⤳ x)
    (hfinite : ∀ V : BigFppfOver B S hS, IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V) →
      ∀ ψ : yoneda.obj V ⟶ X, (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf ψ →
      (pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) ψ ⁻¹' {x'}).Finite)
    (y : points B S hS Y) (hy : pointsMap B S hS Y f y = x) :
    ∃ y' : points B S hS Y, y' ⤳ y ∧ pointsMap B S hS Y f y' = x'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isClosedSubspace_minimal_not_isRepresentable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7Y.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`
which is not a scheme. Then there is a closed subspace `Z` of `X` which is not a scheme but
every closed subspace of `Z` other than `Z` itself — every *proper* closed subspace of `Z` — is
a scheme.

This is the source's proof, by Zorn's lemma applied to the closed subspaces of `X` which are
not schemes, ordered by inclusion: `⊤` is one of them, and the infimum of a chain of them is
one of them because it is the inverse limit of the chain, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_isRepresentable_sInf_of_isChain`. A minimal one is the required
`Z`, and minimality becomes the inner clause by pushing a proper closed subspace of `Z` forward
to a closed subspace of `X` contained in `Z`.

Nothing is assumed beyond the tag's own hypotheses. In particular no condition is imposed on
the size of the chain and none on the site's size cutoff: the chain step is discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.exists_isRepresentable_system_obj_of_isSiteSmall`,
the library's Stacks 07SR, whose smallness hypothesis is met through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSiteSmall.of_mono` because the transition morphisms of the chain are
closed immersions, hence monomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isClosedSubspace_minimal_not_isRepresentable (hT : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hT X)
    (hXnotScheme : ¬ X.IsRepresentable) :
    ∃ Z : Subfunctor X, IsClosedSubspace B S hS Z ∧ ¬ Z.toFunctor.IsRepresentable ∧
      ∀ Z' : Subfunctor Z.toFunctor, IsClosedSubspace B S hS Z' → Z' ≠ ⊤ →
        Z'.toFunctor.IsRepresentable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasEtaleLocalProperty_isReduced_and_irreducibleSpace_of_forall_ne_top_isRepresentable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B7Z.** Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` which is not a scheme, and assume
that every closed subspace `Z` of `X` with `Z ≠ ⊤` — that is, every *proper* closed subspace of
`X` — is a scheme. Then `X` is reduced and `|X|` is irreducible.

A closed subspace with every point of `X` cannot be a scheme, by the closed-immersion form of
Stacks 07VU. Applied to the reduction of `X` this makes the reduction the whole of `X`, which is
therefore reduced. Applied to the scheme-theoretic union of the reduced induced subspaces on two
proper closed subsets covering `|X|`, which is a scheme by Stacks 0CZ1 and Stacks 0EDP, it shows
that no such cover exists; and `|X|` is nonempty since a space without points is a scheme.

The source also assumes `X` quasi-compact and quasi-separated; the proof does not use either
assumption, so they are omitted.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEtaleLocalProperty_isReduced_and_irreducibleSpace_of_forall_ne_top_isRepresentable
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hproper : ∀ Z : Subfunctor X, IsClosedSubspace B S hS Z → Z ≠ ⊤ →
      Z.toFunctor.IsRepresentable)
    (hXnotScheme : ¬ X.IsRepresentable) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y) ∧
      IrreducibleSpace (points B S hS X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentable_of_isRepresentable_baseChange_specStalkSiteObject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B80.** Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` whose structure morphism
`f` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. If for every point of `X`, with image `s` in `S`, the
base change `X ×_S Spec(𝒪_{S, s})` is a scheme, then `X` is a scheme.

This is the same statement as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentable_of_isRepresentable_baseChange_specStalk` with the
object of the site no longer quantified over: `Spec(𝒪_{S, s})` *is* an object of the big fppf
site of `S` whenever `S` is, by `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.contains_spec_stalk_of_contains`, so
the
base change of the tag is formed inside the site with nothing assumed.

Nothing is assumed beyond the tag's own hypotheses: no condition on the size of the system of
affine open neighbourhoods of `s` and none on the site's size cutoff. See the module
documentation for how Stacks 07SR is met.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_of_isRepresentable_baseChange_specStalkSiteObject
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hloc : ∀ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS X,
      ((baseChangeSiteFunctor f).obj (specStalkSiteObject B S hS
        (p.toBase (IsLocalRing.closedPoint p.carrier)))).IsRepresentable) :
    X.IsRepresentable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_maximal_not_isRepresentable_quotientSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B81.** Let `φ : X ⟶ Spec A` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism from
an algebraic space to an affine scheme. If `X` is not a scheme then there is an ideal `I ⊂ A`
such that the base change `X_{A/I}` is not a scheme while `X_{A/I'}` is a scheme for every
ideal `I'` with `I ⊊ I'`.

By Zorn's lemma applied to the set of ideals `I` with `X_{A/I}` not a scheme. It contains
`(0)` because `X_{A/0} ≅ X`, and the supremum of a chain of such ideals is again one of them
because `X_{A/⨆ K}` is the limit of the `X_{A/K i}`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quotientDescentSituation`), so Stacks 07SR makes one member of the
chain a scheme. A maximal element is the required ideal.

Nothing is assumed beyond the tag's own hypotheses, and in particular no bound on the chain and
no condition on the site's size cutoff. Stacks 07SR is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.exists_isRepresentable_system_obj_of_isSiteSmall`, whose
smallness hypothesis is met by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSiteSmall.of_mono`: the transition
morphisms of this system are closed immersions, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedImmersion_quotientSpaceDiagram_map`, because `A/K i ↠ A/K j`
is surjective, hence monomorphisms, and for such a system nothing is asked of the index.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_maximal_not_isRepresentable_quotientSpace
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B (Spec (.of A)) hA φ)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B (Spec (.of A)) hA φ)
    (hnot : ¬ X.IsRepresentable) :
    ∃ I : Ideal A, ¬ (quotientSpace A B hA φ I).IsRepresentable ∧
      ∀ I' : Ideal A, I < I' → (quotientSpace A B hA φ I').IsRepresentable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentable_of_isPurelyInseparable_of_isRepresentable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B83.** Let `k` be a field and let `X` be an algebraic space over `k`. If there
exists a purely inseparable field extension `k'/k` such that the base change `X_{k'}` is a
scheme, then `X` is a scheme.

The projection `X_{k'} ⟶ X` is integral, surjective and universally injective, hence integral
and bijective on the points of Stacks 03BU, so the proof of Stacks 07VV,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentable_of_isIntegralHom_of_bijective_of_isAffineSpace`,
applies once every open subspace `W ⊆ X` with affine preimage `W_{k'}` is known to be affine.
That preimage is a base change of `W` along `Spec k' ⟶ Spec k`, so `W` is affine by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAffineSpace_of_isPullback_specExtensionToBase`, which descends
affineness along the fpqc covering `Spec k' ⟶ Spec k` by Stacks 041Z; this replaces the appeal
to Stacks 07VT in the proof of Stacks 07VV.

The spectrum of `k'` lies in the chosen big fppf site as soon as the spectrum of `k` does, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.contains_spec_of_isAlgebraic`; membership of the site is a
proposition, so the statement is unchanged if another proof of it is substituted.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_of_isPurelyInseparable_of_isRepresentable [IsPurelyInseparable k k']
    (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X)
    (hXk' : (extensionBaseChange k k' B hk
      (contains_spec_of_isAlgebraic B k k' hk) X).IsRepresentable) :
    X.IsRepresentable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_finite_separable_isRepresentable_relocalizeRestrict
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B84] part (2).** Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated algebraic space over `k`. If there is a field extension `K/k` such that the base
change `X_K` is a scheme, then there is a *finite separable* extension `k'/k` such that `X_{k'}`
is a scheme.

The proof is the source's. `K` is the filtered union of its finitely generated `k`-subalgebras
`A`, and [Stacks, Tag 07SR] makes one of the base changes `X_A` a scheme; this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_fgSubalgebra_isRepresentable_relocalizeRestrict`. A residue
field `k₁` of `A` at a maximal ideal is finite over `k` by the Nullstellensatz, `X_{k₁}` is a
scheme, and the separable closure `k'` of `k` in `k₁` is finite separable over `k` with `k₁/k'`
purely inseparable, so `X_{k'}` is a scheme by the finite case of [Stacks, Tag 0B83],
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentable_of_isRepresentable_extensionBaseChange_of_finite`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_separable_isRepresentable_relocalizeRestrict (k K : Type u) [Field k]
    [Field K] [Algebra k K] (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (hK : B.Contains (Spec (.of K))) (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X)
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B (Spec (.of k)) hk B.contains_terminal X)
    (hXK : ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict (specExtensionHom k K B hk hK)).obj
      X).IsRepresentable) :
    ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : Algebra k k') (_ : Module.Finite k k')
      (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable k k') (hk' : B.Contains (Spec (.of k'))),
      ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict (specExtensionHom k k' B hk hk')).obj
        X).IsRepresentable
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentable_relocalizeRestrict_algebraicClosure
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B84] part (1).** Let `k` be a field with algebraic closure `k̄` and let `X`
be a quasi-separated algebraic space over `k`. If there is a field extension `K/k` such that the
base change `X_K` is a scheme, then `X_{k̄}` is a scheme.

The source reduces this to part (2) by covering `X` with quasi-compact open subspaces and omits
the details; they are supplied in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentable_relocalizeRestrict_of_isAlgClosed`. The spectrum of the
algebraic closure lies in the site automatically.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_relocalizeRestrict_algebraicClosure (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K]
    [Algebra k K] (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (hK : B.Contains (Spec (.of K))) (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B (Spec (.of k)) hk B.contains_terminal X)
    (hXK : ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict (specExtensionHom k K B hk hK)).obj
      X).IsRepresentable) :
    ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict (specExtensionHom k (AlgebraicClosure k) B hk
      (contains_spec_of_isAlgebraic B k (AlgebraicClosure k) hk))).obj X).IsRepresentable
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentable_of_isRepresentable_purelyTranscendental_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B85.** Let `k` be a field and `X` a quasi-separated algebraic space over `k`. If
there is a purely transcendental field extension `K/k` such that `X_K` is a scheme, then `X` is a
scheme. Here `X_K` is the restriction of `X` to the big fppf site over `Spec K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_of_isRepresentable_purelyTranscendental_baseChange
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    [PurelyTranscendental k K]
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k))) (hK : B.Contains (Spec (.of K)))
    (F : (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk F)
    (hqs : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsQuasiSeparatedOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk F)
    (hbase : ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict
      (ObjectProperty.homMk
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) :
          B.obj hK ⟶ B.obj hk)).obj F).IsRepresentable) :
    F.IsRepresentable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_extensionBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B86**, the algebraicity of the base change: the base change of an algebraic space
over `k` along a field extension `k'/k` is, viewed over `k`, an algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_extensionBaseChange
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk (extensionBaseChange k k' B hk hk' X)
declarations.comment: the base change is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFreeOnNonemptyPoints_extensionBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B86**, the freeness assertion: the group of `k`-automorphisms of `k'` acts freely
on `X_{k'}`.  For a finite Galois extension this is the first half of the tag; freeness in fact
needs no assumption on the extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFreeOnNonemptyPoints_extensionBaseChange :
    IsFreeOnNonemptyPoints B (Spec (.of k)) hk (k' ≃ₐ[k] k')
      (extensionBaseChange k k' B hk hk' X)
declarations.comment: the Galois group acts freely on the base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_extensionBaseChangeQuotientLift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B86**, the quotient assertion: for a finite Galois extension `k'/k` with Galois
group `G`, an algebraic space `X` over `k` is the quotient `X_{k'}/G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_extensionBaseChangeQuotientLift [FiniteDimensional k k'] [IsGalois k k']
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X) :
    IsIso (extensionBaseChangeQuotientLift k k' B hk hk' X hX.isSheaf)
declarations.comment: X = X_{k'}/G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_schematicLocus_actionQuotient_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B87.** Let a finite group `G` act freely on an object `V` of a big fppf site over
a scheme `S` and let `y` be a point of the quotient `V/G`. Then `y` lies in the schematic locus
of `V/G` if and only if there is an affine object `U` of the site and an open immersion
`i : h_U ⟶ h_V` whose point set contains every point of `h_V` above `y`.

The quotient map is surjective and finite locally free after every representable base change,
so this is Stacks 0BA1 for it, read on the chart `h_V ⟶ V/G` bundled as a morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_schematicLocus_actionQuotient_iff [Finite G]
    (ha : ActsFreelyOnNonemptyPoints (underlyingOver B hS V) G a)
    (y : points B S hS (actionQuotient G B hS V a)) :
    y ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS
        (schematicLocus B S hS (actionQuotient G B hS V a)).toFunctor
        (schematicLocus B S hS (actionQuotient G B hS V a)).ι) ↔
      ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (i : yoneda.obj U ⟶ yoneda.obj V),
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) ∧ IsOpenImmersion B S hS i ∧
        ∀ x : points B S hS (yoneda.obj V),
          pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) (freeActionQuotientMap G B S hS V a ha) x = y →
            x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj U) i)
declarations.comment: for a free action of a finite group on an object of the big fppf site over `S` in place of an action on an arbitrary algebraic space, the quotient being the quotient sheaf of the graph relation of the action as in the library's form of Tag 071S, freeness being read on the points over the test schemes with nonempty underlying space, and the affine open of condition (2) being presented as in the library's form of Tag 0BA1, by an open immersion into the functor of points of the scheme acted on out of an affine object of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_schematicLocus_orbitQuotient_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B87.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S`, let `G` be a
finite group acting freely on `X` and let `Y = X/G` be the quotient of Tag 071S. For a point
`y` of `Y` the following are equivalent:

1. `y` lies in the schematic locus of `Y` — the point set of
   `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schematicLocus`, the largest open subspace of `Y` which is a
   scheme (Tag 03JH); and
2. there is an affine open subspace of `X`, presented as an open immersion `i : h_V ⟶ X` from
   an affine object `V` of the site, whose point set contains the whole fibre of `y`.

The quotient map `X ⟶ X/G` is surjective and finite locally free after every representable
base change, so this is Stacks 0BA1 for it. Freeness is read on the points over the test
objects with nonempty underlying scheme, which is how the library's form of Tag 071S — the form
producing the quotient here — reads it.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_schematicLocus_orbitQuotient_iff
    (hnat : IsNaturalAction B S hS G X) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hfree : IsFreeOnNonemptyPoints B S hS G X)
    (y : points B S hS (orbitQuotientSheaf B S hS G X hnat).obj) :
    y ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS
        (schematicLocus B S hS (orbitQuotientSheaf B S hS G X hnat).obj).toFunctor
        (schematicLocus B S hS (orbitQuotientSheaf B S hS G X hnat).obj).ι) ↔
      ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (i : yoneda.obj V ⟶ X),
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V) ∧ IsOpenImmersion B S hS i ∧
        ∀ x : points B S hS X,
          pointsMap B S hS X (toOrbitQuotient B S hS G X hnat) x = y →
            x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentable_of_isAlgClosure_finite_rationalPoints_isAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B88.** Let `k` be a field with algebraic closure `K = k̄` and let `X` be an
algebraic space over `k`.  Assume

1. `X` is decent and locally of finite type over `k`,
2. `X_{k̄}` is a scheme, and
3. any finite set of `k̄`-rational points of `X_{k̄}` is contained in an affine.

Then `X` is a scheme.

Hypotheses (1) and (3) are present and not weakened: `hdecent` together with `hfinite` is
hypothesis (1), and `haffine` is hypothesis (3).  Hypothesis (2) is not needed by the proof
below and is omitted, so the statement is stronger than the source's.

`X_{k̄}` is the restriction of `X` to the big fppf site over `Spec k̄` along the morphism
`g : Spec k̄ ⟶ Spec k` of the site, a `k̄`-rational point of it is a section over the terminal
object `Spec k̄` of that site, and an affine open is presented by an open immersion out of an
affine object, as in the library's form of Tag 0BA1. The structure morphism of `X` over `Spec k`
is given explicitly as `f`, the base `Spec k` being terminal in its own big fppf site.

Being decent and locally of finite type over a field, `|X|` is a Jacobson space (Tag 0BA6 and
Tag 0BA3), so it is enough to put every closed point of `|X|` in the schematic locus of
Tag 03JH, and then Tag 03KE in the case `(θ)` finishes.  A closed point is represented by a
closed immersion `Spec l ⟶ X` (Tag 0AHB) with `l/k` finite (Tag 03XG and the Hilbert
Nullstellensatz), so `Spec l ×_X X_{k̄}` is a finite scheme over an algebraically closed field
and hypothesis (3) gives an affine open of `X_{k̄}` through which it factors.  The projection
`π : X_{k̄} ⟶ X` is a base change of the affine, flat, surjective morphism
`Spec k̄ ⟶ Spec k`, hence universally closed and quasi-compact, and closedness converts the
fibrewise containment into a quasi-compact open neighbourhood `N` of the point whose base
change to `k̄` is quasi-affine over `Spec k̄`.  Tag 0423 descends quasi-affineness along that
fpqc covering and Tag 03WM makes `N` a scheme, so the point is in the schematic locus.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_of_isAlgClosure_finite_rationalPoints_isAffine
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsAlgClosure k K]
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k))) (hK : B.Contains (Spec (.of K)))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X)
    (hdecent : IsDecentSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X)
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hk))))
    (hfinite : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B (Spec (.of k)) hk f)
    (haffine :
      let Xbase := (OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict
        (ObjectProperty.homMk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) :
          B.obj hK ⟶ B.obj hk)).obj X
      ∀ s : Finset (Xbase.obj (op (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hK))))),
        ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of K)) hK) (i : yoneda.obj U ⟶ Xbase),
          IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B (Spec (.of K)) hK).obj U) ∧
          IsOpenImmersion B (Spec (.of K)) hK i ∧
          ∀ x ∈ s, x ∈ Set.range (i.app (op (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hK)))))) :
    X.IsRepresentable
declarations.comment: hypotheses (1) and (3) of the source; (2) is not needed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativelyRepresentable_of_isFlat_of_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B8A** (David Rydh). A flat monomorphism of algebraic spaces is representable by
schemes.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_of_mono_of_forall_baseChange_mono_fSharp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B8B.** A quasi-compact monomorphism of algebraic spaces over `S` whose structure
homomorphism `𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T,*}𝒪_{X ×_Y T}` is a monomorphism for every `T ⟶ Y` is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_of_mono_of_forall_baseChange_mono_fSharp
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hqc : Space.IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom) [Mono f]
    (hinj : ∀ (T : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (g : T ⟶ Y),
      Mono (Space.smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS
        (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst g.hom f.hom) :
          AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS g f ⟶ T)).fSharp) :
    IsIso f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_of_mono_of_isQuasiCompact_of_isFlat_of_isSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B8C.** A quasi-compact, flat and surjective monomorphism of algebraic spaces
over `S` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_of_mono_of_isQuasiCompact_of_isFlat_of_isSurjective
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) [Mono f]
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom) (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f.hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GroupOverField.isRepresentable_relocalizeRestrict_algebraicClosure_of_isSeparatedOver
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field with algebraic closure `k̄` and let `G` be a separated group algebraic
space over `k`. Then `G_{k̄}` is a scheme.

By `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GroupOverField.exists_isAlgClosed_isRepresentable_relocalizeRestrict`
the base change `G_L` is a scheme for some algebraically closed extension `L/k`; this is the
source's argument with translations of the group and Jacobson charts. A separated algebraic space
over the affine `Spec k` is quasi-separated, so Stacks 0B84 part (1) descends this to `k̄`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_relocalizeRestrict_algebraicClosure_of_isSeparatedOver
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk (yoneda.obj (⊤_ (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)))
      (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B (Spec (.of k)) hk _))
    (hsep : IsSeparatedOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk G.obj.X.left) :
    ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict (specExtensionHom k (AlgebraicClosure k) B hk
      (contains_spec_of_isAlgebraic B k (AlgebraicClosure k) hk))).obj
        G.obj.X.left).IsRepresentable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GroupOverField.isRepresentable_of_isSeparatedOver_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**A separated group algebraic space locally of finite type over a field is a scheme.** Let
`G` be a group algebraic space over `S ≅ Spec k` which is separated over `k` and locally of
finite type over `k`. Then `G` is representable.

Being separated over `k`, the space `G` is locally separated over `k`, hence decent, and a decent
group algebraic space locally of finite type over a field is a scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_of_isSeparatedOver_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType (e : S ≅ Spec (.of k))
    (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace C S hS (yoneda.obj (⊤_ (BigFppfOver C S hS)))
      (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda C S hS _))
    (hsep : IsSeparatedOver C S hS G.obj.X.left)
    (hlft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType C S hS
      ((isTerminal_yoneda_obj_base C S hS).from G.obj.X.left)) :
    G.obj.X.left.IsRepresentable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GroupOverField.isRepresentable_of_isSeparatedOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B8G.** Let `k` be a field and let `G` be a group algebraic space over `k`. If `G`
is separated, then `G` is a scheme.

By Stacks 0B8E the base change `G_{k̄}` is a scheme `X₀`. For a purely transcendental extension
`K = k(x_σ)` of cardinality above the size of `X₀`, Stacks 0B85 reduces the statement to `G_K`.
With `Ω` the algebraic closure of `K`, the base change `G_Ω = X₀ ×_{k̄} Ω` is a Jacobson scheme
whose closed points are `Ω`-rational (Stacks 0479), and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GroupOverField.isRepresentable_of_relocalizeRestrict_algebraicClosure`
concludes that `G_K` is a scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_of_isSeparatedOver {k : Type u} [Field k] (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk (yoneda.obj (⊤_ (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)))
      (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B (Spec (.of k)) hk _))
    (hsep : IsSeparatedOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk G.obj.X.left) :
    G.obj.X.left.IsRepresentable

declarations.name: Module.IsInvertibleModule
declarations.doc:
An `R`-module `M` is invertible when the functor `M ⊗[R] -` is an equivalence of the
category of `R`-modules.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev Module.IsInvertibleModule
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : Prop

declarations.name: Module.IsTrivialInvertibleModule
declarations.doc: An invertible `R`-module is trivial if it is isomorphic to `R` as an `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev Module.IsTrivialInvertibleModule
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : Prop

declarations.name: Module.finite_projective_rankAtStalk_one_tfae_invertible_exists_tensor_inverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B8I.** For an `R`-module `M`, the following are equivalent: `M` is finite
projective of rank one at every prime, `M` is invertible, and `M` admits a tensor inverse.
Moreover, every tensor inverse of `M` is isomorphic to the linear dual of `M`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.finite_projective_rankAtStalk_one_tfae_invertible_exists_tensor_inverse
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    List.TFAE [
      Module.Finite R M ∧ Module.Projective R M ∧
        Module.rankAtStalk M = Function.const (PrimeSpectrum R) 1,
      Module.Invertible R M,
      ∃ (N : Type (max u v)) (_ : AddCommGroup N) (_ : Module R N),
        Nonempty (TensorProduct R M N ≃ₗ[R] R)] ∧
      ∀ (N : Type w) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N],
        Nonempty (TensorProduct R M N ≃ₗ[R] R) →
          Nonempty (N ≃ₗ[R] Module.Dual R M)

declarations.name: Module.isInvertibleModule_iff_invertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0B8I**, the description of invertibility the Stacks Project takes as its
definition in Tag 0B8H: `M ⊗[R] -` is an equivalence of the category of `R`-modules exactly
when `M` is invertible. Without this, `Module.IsInvertibleModule` and `Module.Invertible`
are two unrelated predicates and the equivalence above is about the wrong condition (2).
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.isInvertibleModule_iff_invertible :
    Module.IsInvertibleModule R M ↔ Module.Invertible R M

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_iso_free_over_of_stalk_iso_free
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B8J.** Let `(X, 𝒪_X)` be a ringed space and let `M` be a finitely
presented sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules. If the stalk of `M` at a point `x` is free of rank `r` over
`𝒪_{X, x}`, then the restriction of `M` to some open neighbourhood of `x` is isomorphic to the
free sheaf of modules of rank `r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_free_over_of_stalk_iso_free {X : TopCat.{u}}
    {R : TopCat.Sheaf RingCat.{u} X} (M : SheafOfModules.{u} R)
    (hM : M.IsFinitePresentation) (x : X) (r : ℕ)
    (hx : Nonempty
      (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk M.val.presheaf x) ≃ₗ[ToType (R.presheaf.stalk x)]
        (ULift.{u} (Fin r) →₀ ToType (R.presheaf.stalk x)))) :
    ∃ U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X, x ∈ U ∧
      Nonempty (M.over U ≅ SheafOfModules.free (ULift.{u} (Fin r)))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorInverseIsoDualSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B8N (c).** A sheaf of `𝒪`-modules `N` whose tensor product with `L` is
isomorphic to the structure sheaf is isomorphic to `SheafHom(L, 𝒪)`.

The hypothesis is clause (2) of the tag, so `L` is invertible and the evaluation pairing
`SheafHom(L, 𝒪) ⊗_𝒪 L ⟶ 𝒪` is an isomorphism by `isIso_evaluation`. That exhibits
`SheafHom(L, 𝒪)` as a two-sided tensor inverse of `L`, the braiding supplying the other order,
while the given isomorphism exhibits `N` as one; a two-sided tensor inverse in a monoidal
category is unique up to isomorphism
(`CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.HasInverse.inv_iso`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorInverseIsoDualSheaf
    (N : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪))
    (e : ((Tensor.sheafTensor
      ⟨𝒪, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ 𝒪 (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) h𝒪⟩).obj L).obj N ≅
      SheafOfModules.unit (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪)) :
    N ≅ dualSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪 L
declarations.comment: the tensor inverse is the dual

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isInvertible_iff_exists_tensor_iso_unit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B8K and Tag 0B8N, (1) ⟺ (2).** A sheaf of `O`-modules `L` is invertible
if and only if there is a sheaf of `O`-modules `N` whose tensor product with `L` is isomorphic
to `O`.

For the forward implication the tensor functor of `L` is an equivalence, so `O` has a preimage `N`
under it, and the universal property identifies the image of that preimage with `L ⊗_O N`. For the
converse the isomorphism `L ⊗_O N ≅ O` is turned into a pairing of presheaves of modules by
composing with the sheafification unit, and `isInvertible_of_pairing` applies.

Tag 0B8K states this for a ringed space and Tag 0B8N for an arbitrary ringed site; the statement
here is the one on a ringed site, so it carries both.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_iff_exists_tensor_iso_unit
    (L : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO)) :
    IsInvertible O hO L ↔ ∃ N : SheafOfModules.{w}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO),
      Nonempty (((Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w}
        ⟨O, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ O (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) hO⟩).obj L).obj N ≅
        SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.isInvertible_iff_exists_tensor_iso_unit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B8K.** A sheaf of modules is invertible if and only if it has a
tensor inverse, that is, if and only if some `N` satisfies `L ⊗ N ≅ 𝒪`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_iff_exists_tensor_iso_unit
    (L : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
      :
    IsInvertible O hO L ↔
      ∃ N : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O
        hO),
        Nonempty (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w}
          ⟨O, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ O (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) hO⟩).obj L).obj N ≅
          _root_.SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O
            hO))
declarations.comment: tensor_inverse_characterization

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.LocallyFiniteFree.isLocallyFiniteFreeSummand_of_isInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B8K.** An invertible sheaf of modules is locally a direct
summand of a finite free sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyFiniteFreeSummand_of_isInvertible
    (X : RingedSpace.{u, w}) (L : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (ringSheaf X))
    [HasWeakSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [(Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [∀ U : Opens X,
      HasWeakSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding).carrier)
        AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [∀ U : Opens X,
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology
        (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding).carrier).WEqualsLocallyBijective
        AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf
      (Presheaf.isSheaf_comp_of_isSheaf _ X.presheaf
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u}) X.IsSheaf) L) :
    ∀ x : X, ∃ (U : Opens X) (_ : x ∈ U) (n : ℕ),
      Nonempty (Retract ((modulePullback (X.ofRestrict U.isOpenEmbedding)).obj L)
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.free (ULift.{u} (Fin n))))
declarations.comment: locally_finite_free_summand

declarations.name: Stacks.RingedSpace.modulePullback_isInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B8L.** The pullback of an invertible module along a
morphism of ringed spaces is invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem modulePullback_isInvertible {X Y : RingedSpace.{u, u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y))
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf
      (Presheaf.isSheaf_comp_of_isSheaf _ _ (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) Y.IsSheaf) L] :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf
      (Presheaf.isSheaf_comp_of_isSheaf _ _ (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) X.IsSheaf)
      ((modulePullback f).obj L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isInvertibleModule_pushforward_of_isIso
declarations.doc:
**The direct image of an invertible module along an isomorphism of schemes is invertible.**
The direct image along the inverse of an isomorphism is its inverse image
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pushforwardInvIsoPullback`), and the inverse image of an
invertible module is invertible (`Stacks.Modules.isInvertible_pullback`).
declarations.comment: the direct image of an invertible module along an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.InvertiblePullback.isInvertible_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0B8L.** The pullback of an invertible sheaf of modules along a morphism of
ringed spaces is invertible.

A tensor inverse `N` of `L`, which Tag 0B8K produces from invertibility, is carried by `f^*` to a
tensor inverse of `f^*L`: Tag 01CD turns `f^*(L ⊗ N)` into `f^*L ⊗ f^*N`, and
`RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePullbackObjUnitIso` turns `f^* 𝒪_Y` into `𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_pullback (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureRingSheaf Y))
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.sheaf.obj (structureRingSheaf Y).property L] :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj (structureRingSheaf X).property
      ((pullbackFunctor f).obj L)

declarations.name: Stacks.RingedSpace.isInvertible_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B8L.** The pullback `f^*L` of an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module along a
morphism of ringed spaces `f : X ⟶ Y` is an invertible `𝒪_X`-module.

The proof is the one the Stacks Project gives. Tag 0B8K produces an `𝒪_Y`-module `N` with
`L ⊗_{𝒪_Y} N ≅ 𝒪_Y`; `Stacks.RingedSpace.tensorIsoUnitPullback` pulls that pairing back, which
is where Tag 01CD enters; and Tag 0B8K read in the other direction concludes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_modulePullback (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y))
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.sheaf.obj (structureSheafRing Y).property L] :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj (structureSheafRing X).property
      ((modulePullback f).obj L)

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePullback_isInvertible
declarations.doc:
The pullback of an invertible module is invertible: if tensoring by `L` is an
autoequivalence of `Mod(𝒪_Y)`, then tensoring by `f^* L` is an autoequivalence of `Mod(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem modulePullback_isInvertible {X Y : RingedSpace.{u, u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf Y.presheaf (structureSheafRing
        Y).property))
    [IsInvertible Y.presheaf (structureSheafRing Y).property L] :
    IsInvertible X.presheaf (structureSheafRing X).property
      ((RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePullback f).obj L)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.isInvertible_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B8M.** A finite locally free sheaf of modules of rank one is
invertible.

This is the statement for `Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank`, and it
lives in that predicate's namespace;
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isInvertible_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one` of
`StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.LocallyTrivialInvertible.Basic` is the statement
for `AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank`, the other rank predicate of
[Stacks, Tag 01CS].

The local generators of rank one give a covering family of the final object on which `L` becomes
isomorphic to the structure sheaf; each such trivialization is a rank-one dual basis, and
`isInvertible_of_dualBasisOne` turns a family of those on a covering family into invertibility
by way of the evaluation pairing `L^∨ ⊗ L ⟶ 𝒪` and Tag 0B8K.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one
    (L : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪))
    [Invertible.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank L 1] : IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 L
declarations.comment: locally free of rank one implies invertible

declarations.name: Stacks.RingedSpace.isInvertible_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules on a ringed space that is finite locally free of rank one is
invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf X.sheaf))
    [h : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
      (C := Opens X) (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology X) L 1] :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property L
declarations.comment: locally free of rank one implies invertible

declarations.name: Stacks.RingedSpace.exists_isInvertible_not_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one
declarations.doc:
**Clause 3 of Stacks Tag 0B8M.** On a general ringed space an invertible sheaf of modules
need not be finite locally free of rank one: there is a ringed space `X` and a sheaf of
`𝒪_X`-modules `L` with `L` invertible and `L` not finite locally free of rank one.

The witness is the one-point ringed space whose ring of global sections is `ℤ[√-5]`, carrying
the sheaf of modules attached to the non-principal invertible ideal `(2, 1 + √-5)`. Its single
stalk is `ℤ[√-5]`, which is not a local ring; this is exactly what the local-stalk hypothesis of
`Stacks.RingedSpace.isInvertible_iff_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one` rules out.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isInvertible_not_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one :
    ∃ (X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.{u})
      (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf X.sheaf)),
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property L ∧
        ¬AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
          (C := Opens X) (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology X) L 1
declarations.comment: the converse fails for general ringed spaces

declarations.name: Stacks.InvertibleLocallyFree.isInvertible_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one
declarations.doc:
**Clause 1 of Stacks Tag 0B8M.** A sheaf of modules that is finite locally free of rank one
is invertible, with invertibility read as
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible` — the predicate every consumer in this
repository uses.

This is unconditional. It does **not** use
`Stacks.InvertibleLocallyFree.InvertibleIsLocal` (which is itself proved, as
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.invertibleIsLocal`): clause 1 does not need
descent of the inverse object, because the inverse is the dual sheaf `L^∨ = SheafHom(L, 𝒪)` and
the only local-to-global step is that a locally bijective pairing is inverted by sheafification.
See the module documentation for the forced universe constraint `w = max u v`, inherited from
the internal hom of Tag 03EM.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one
    (L : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪))
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank L 1] :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 L

declarations.name: Stacks.InvertibleRankOneIff.isInvertible_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one
declarations.doc:
**Clause 1 of Stacks Tag 0B8M.** A finite locally free module of rank one on a ringed space
is invertible. There is no hypothesis on the stalks of the structure sheaf, and none on the site.

The content is `Stacks.SheafDescent.isInvertible_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one`; what is done
here is to restate it over `structureSheaf X.sheaf`, which forces the carrier universe of the
ringed space to agree with the universe of its rings and so makes the sheafification instances
available.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one
    (X : RingedSpace.{u})
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf X.sheaf))
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (C := Opens X)
      (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology X) L 1] :
    SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property L
declarations.comment: locally free of rank one implies invertible

declarations.name: Stacks.InvertibleRankOneIff.isInvertible_iff_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one
declarations.doc:
**Clause 2 of Stacks Tag 0B8M.** On a ringed space all of whose stalks `𝒪_{X, x}` are local
rings, a sheaf of modules is invertible exactly when it is finite locally free of rank one.

The forward implication is `Stacks.SheafRankOne.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one_of_isInvertible`
and is where the local-stalk hypothesis is spent; the reverse implication is clause 1, which
holds on every ringed space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_iff_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one
    (X : RingedSpace.{u})
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf X.sheaf))
    [∀ x : X, IsLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)] :
    SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property L ↔
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (C := Opens X)
        (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology X) L 1
declarations.comment: characterization for local stalks

declarations.name: Stacks.RingedSpace.isInvertible_iff_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one
declarations.doc:
On a ringed space all of whose structure-sheaf stalks are local rings, a sheaf of modules is
invertible if and only if it is finite locally free of rank one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_iff_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf X.sheaf))
    [∀ x : X, IsLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)] :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property L ↔
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
        (C := Opens X) (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology X) L 1
declarations.comment: characterization for local stalks

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isInvertible_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one_of_essentiallySmall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B8M**, clause 1, on an essentially small ringed site. A sheaf of
modules which is locally free of rank one is invertible, with the universe of the sections of
the structure sheaf independent of the universes of the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one_of_essentiallySmall
    (X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.{u₁, v₁, w}) [EssentiallySmall.{w} X.C]
    [HasWeakSheafify X.J AddCommGrpCat.{w}] [X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    (L : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank X L 1) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.O.obj
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).property L
declarations.comment: locally free of rank one implies invertible, on an essentially small site

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorInverseIsoDualSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B8N (c).** A sheaf of `𝒪`-modules `N` whose tensor product with `L` is
isomorphic to the structure sheaf is isomorphic to `SheafHom(L, 𝒪)`.

The hypothesis is clause (2) of the tag, so `L` is invertible and the evaluation pairing
`SheafHom(L, 𝒪) ⊗_𝒪 L ⟶ 𝒪` is an isomorphism by `isIso_evaluation`. That exhibits
`SheafHom(L, 𝒪)` as a two-sided tensor inverse of `L`, the braiding supplying the other order,
while the given isomorphism exhibits `N` as one; a two-sided tensor inverse in a monoidal
category is unique up to isomorphism
(`CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.HasInverse.inv_iso`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorInverseIsoDualSheaf
    (N : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪))
    (e : ((Tensor.sheafTensor
      ⟨𝒪, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ 𝒪 (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) h𝒪⟩).obj L).obj N ≅
      SheafOfModules.unit (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪)) :
    N ≅ dualSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪 L

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFlat_of_isInvertible_ringedSite
declarations.doc: An invertible sheaf of modules on a ringed site is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_of_isInvertible_ringedSite
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
    (L : SheafOfModules.{w} (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O.obj hO))
    (hL : IsInvertible O.obj hO L) :
    IsFlat (O := O) L
declarations.comment: (a), the flatness half

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFinitePresentation_of_isInvertible
declarations.doc:
**An invertible sheaf of modules is of finite presentation.**

This is the step of Tag 0B8M's converse that Stacks attributes to Tag 0B8K. By Tag 0B8N (b)
every object of the site has a covering family on whose members `L` is a split subobject of a
finite product of copies of the structure sheaf, hence has a finite presentation there; the union
over all objects of those families covers the terminal object, and finite presentation is
local.

This is also the finite-presentation half of Tag 0B8N (a).
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_of_isInvertible
    (hO : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureRingPresheaf O))
    (L : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO)) (hL :
      IsInvertible O hO L) :
    L.IsFinitePresentation
declarations.comment: (a), the finite-presentation half

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isInvertible_iff_exists_tensor_iso_unit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B8K and Tag 0B8N, (1) ⟺ (2).** A sheaf of `O`-modules `L` is invertible
if and only if there is a sheaf of `O`-modules `N` whose tensor product with `L` is isomorphic
to `O`.

For the forward implication the tensor functor of `L` is an equivalence, so `O` has a preimage `N`
under it, and the universal property identifies the image of that preimage with `L ⊗_O N`. For the
converse the isomorphism `L ⊗_O N ≅ O` is turned into a pairing of presheaves of modules by
composing with the sheafification unit, and `isInvertible_of_pairing` applies.

Tag 0B8K states this for a ringed space and Tag 0B8N for an arbitrary ringed site; the statement
here is the one on a ringed site, so it carries both.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_iff_exists_tensor_iso_unit
    (L : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO)) :
    IsInvertible O hO L ↔ ∃ N : SheafOfModules.{w}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO),
      Nonempty (((Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w}
        ⟨O, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ O (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) hO⟩).obj L).obj N ≅
        SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_cover_isDirectSummand_finiteFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B8N (b).** On a cover of any object, an invertible module embeds as a
direct summand of a finite free module. The two sheafification hypotheses are used only by
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isLocallyInjective_of_universal`; none is needed on the slice sites.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cover_isDirectSummand_finiteFree
    (hO : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureRingPresheaf O))
    (L : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
      [IsInvertible O hO L] (U : C) :
    ∃ (I : Type (max u v)) (V : I → C) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U),
      Sieve.generate (Presieve.ofArrows V f) ∈ J U ∧
        ∀ i : I, ∃ n : ℕ,
          ∃ s : L.over (V i) ⟶
              ∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n ↦
                SheafOfModules.unit ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O
                  hO).over (V i))),
            IsSplitMono s
declarations.comment: (b), invertible_local_summand

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isInvertible_pullbackModules_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B8P.** The pullback of an invertible module along a morphism of
ringed topoi is invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_pullbackModules_obj (f : RingedToposHom X Y)
    (L : SheafOfModules.{w'} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))
    [hL : IsInvertible Y.O.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O).property L] :
    IsInvertible X.O.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).property
      ((f.pullbackModules).obj L)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isInvertible_pullbackModules_obj_ringedToposHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B8P** for a morphism of ringed topoi in the two-field sense of Tag
01D3 part (2): the pullback of an invertible module is invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_pullbackModules_obj_ringedToposHom
    (f : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom X Y)
    (L : SheafOfModules.{w'} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))
    [IsInvertible Y.O.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O).property L] :
    IsInvertible X.O.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).property
      ((f.toRingedToposModulesHom.pullbackModules).obj L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackInvertible
declarations.doc:
**The inverse image of an invertible module along a morphism of algebraic spaces is
invertible.**  This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isInvertible_modulePullback_obj`, read through

`StacksFrontier/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Sheaf/InvertibleCompare.lean`.
declarations.statement: theorem modulePullbackInvertible : ModulePullbackInvertible B S hS
declarations.comment:
the inverse image of an invertible module along a morphism of algebraic spaces is
invertible

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isInvertible_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B8Q**, the unconditional clause. On the ringed topos of a ringed
site, a sheaf of modules which is locally free of rank one is invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one
    (X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.{u, v, max u v w})
    (L : SheafOfModules.{max u v w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank X L 1) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.O.obj
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).property L
declarations.comment: locally free of rank one implies invertible

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isInvertible_iff_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B8Q**, the characterization clause. On a locally ringed site, a
sheaf of modules is invertible exactly when it is locally free of rank one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_iff_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one
    (X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.{u, max u v, max u v})
    (L : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
    (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsLocallyRinged X) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.O.obj
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).property L ↔
      AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank X L 1
declarations.comment: characterization for locally ringed sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_isInvertible_not_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B8Q**, the parenthetical clause. Without local ringedness the
converse fails: there is a ringed site carrying an invertible sheaf of modules which is not
locally free of rank one.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isInvertible_not_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one :
    ∃ (X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.{u, v, w})
      (L : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)),
