    (F : X.Modules) (hfp : F.IsFinitePresentation)
    (hflat : IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom F) :
    IsLocallyConstant (chiFibre f F
      (DerivedFibreBetti.isPseudoCoherent_of_isPerfect _
        (isPerfect_derivedPushforward_singleFunctor_of_isProper f hf hproper F hfp hflat)))
declarations.comment: the local constancy conclusion, with the function in the derived-fibre form s |-> sum (-1)^i dim_k(s) H^i(Rf_*F tensor^L k(s)) that the source's proof passes to. Rf_*F is perfect by Tag 0B91 (2), proved as isPerfect_derivedPushforward_singleFunctor_of_isProper, and the conclusion is Tag 0BDJ at Rf_*F. The identification with s |-> chi(X_s, F_s) and the statement in that form are in ProperFlatFibreEulerCharacteristicUnconditional.lean (isLocallyConstant_fibreEulerCharacteristic). The base-change conclusion is chiFibre_baseChange

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProperFlatFibreEulerCharacteristic.chiFibre_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B9T], the second conclusion.** Formation of the Euler characteristic of the
derived fibres of `Rf_*ℱ` commutes with base change: for a cartesian square

```
X' --g'--> X
|          |
f'         f
v          v
S' --g---> S
```

the function on `S'` attached to `f'` and `(g')^*ℱ` is the function on `S` attached to `f` and
`ℱ`, composed with `g`.

The base-change isomorphism `Lg^*Rf_*ℱ ≅ Rf'_*(g')^*ℱ` is the base-change half of
[Stacks, Tag 0B91] (2), `nonempty_derivedPullback_derivedPushforward_singleFunctor_iso`; with it,
this is the base-change clause of [Stacks, Tag 0BDI] summed over the degrees,
`AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedFibreBetti.chiDerivedFibre_derivedPullback`, together with the
invariance of the derived-fibre Euler characteristic under isomorphism. The function is defined
from a proof of pseudo-coherence of each object, `hpc` and `hpc'`; the equality holds for every
such proof.
declarations.statement:
public theorem chiFibre_baseChange
    {X S X' S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g' : X' ⟶ X)
    (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (hf : FinitePresentation f) (hproper : IsProper f)
    (F : X.Modules) (hfp : F.IsFinitePresentation)
    (hflat : IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom F)
    (hpc : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := S.toRingedSpace) (derivedPushforwardModule f F))
    (hpc' : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := S'.toRingedSpace)
      (derivedPushforwardModule f' ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj F))) :
    chiFibre f' ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj F) hpc' =
      chiFibre f F hpc ∘ g.base
declarations.comment: the base-change conclusion ('formation of this function commutes with base change'), with the function in the derived-fibre form s |-> sum (-1)^i dim_k(s) H^i(Rf_*F tensor^L k(s)), for every cartesian square. The isomorphism Lg^*Rf_*F = Rf'_*(g')^*F is Tag 0B91 (2), proved as nonempty_derivedPullback_derivedPushforward_singleFunctor_iso; the conclusion is then Tag 0BDI summed over the degrees, chiDerivedFibre_derivedPullback, and invariance under isomorphism, chiDerivedFibre_congr. hpc and hpc' are the pseudo-coherence proofs the function is built from, and the equality holds for all of them. The statement for s |-> chi(X_s, F_s) itself is fibreEulerCharacteristic_baseChange in ProperFlatFibreEulerCharacteristicUnconditional.lean. The local constancy conclusion is isLocallyConstant_chiFibre

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProperFlatFibreEulerCharacteristic.isLocallyConstant_fibreEulerCharacteristic
declarations.doc:
For `f : X ⟶ S` proper and of finite presentation and `ℱ` an `𝒪_X`-module of finite
presentation, flat over `S`, the function `s ↦ χ(X_s, ℱ_s)` is locally constant on `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyConstant_fibreEulerCharacteristic {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (hf : FinitePresentation f) [IsProper f] (F : X.Modules) (hF : F.IsFinitePresentation)
    (hflat : IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom F) :
    IsLocallyConstant (fibreEulerCharacteristic f F)
declarations.comment: local constancy of s |-> chi(X_s, F_s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProperFlatFibreEulerCharacteristic.fibreEulerCharacteristic_baseChange
declarations.doc:
Formation of `s ↦ χ(X_s, ℱ_s)` commutes with base change: for a cartesian square with
`g : S' ⟶ S`, the function attached to the base change `f' : X' ⟶ S'` and `(g')^*ℱ` is the
function attached to `f` and `ℱ`, composed with `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fibreEulerCharacteristic_baseChange {X S X' S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S)
    (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g' : X' ⟶ X) (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (hf : FinitePresentation f)
    [IsProper f] (F : X.Modules) (hF : F.IsFinitePresentation)
    (hflat : IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom F) :
    fibreEulerCharacteristic f' ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj F) =
      fibreEulerCharacteristic f F ∘ g.base
declarations.comment: formation of s |-> chi(X_s, F_s) commutes with base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_c_baseChange_of_isCurve_of_section
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a smooth projective curve over `k` with a `k`-rational
point, given as a section `σ` of its structure morphism `f`. Then `𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T,*}𝒪_{X_T}` is an
isomorphism for every `k`-scheme `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_c_baseChange_of_isCurve_of_section {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k f] [IsProjectiveVariety k f] [Smooth f]
    (σ : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X) (hσ : σ ≫ f = 𝟙 _)
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    IsIso (pullback.snd f g).toLRSHom.toHom.c

declarations.name: Stacks.RigidifiedPicard.cohomologyLocus
declarations.doc:
The rigidified classes `ℒ ∈ Pic_{X/S,σ}(T)` with `Rf_{T,*}ℒ` isomorphic to an invertible
`𝒪_T`-module placed in degree `0`, as a subfunctor of `Pic_{X/S,σ}`.
declarations.statement: def cohomologyLocus : Subfunctor (functor f σ hσ ⋙ forget GrpCat)
declarations.comment: F is a subfunctor, for f flat, proper and locally of finite presentation with a section (the source's smooth projective curve over a field with a rational point is a special case)

declarations.name: Stacks.RigidifiedPicard.isOpenSubfunctor_cohomologyLocus
declarations.doc:
The inclusion `F ⊆ Pic_{X/S,σ}` is representable by open immersions, in the elementwise form
of [Stacks, Tag 01JI]: for every `S`-scheme `T` and every `ℒ ∈ Pic_{X/S,σ}(T)` there is an open
`U ⊆ T` such that for every `g : T' ⟶ T` over `S`, the restriction of `ℒ` to `T'` lies in `F(T')`
exactly when `g` maps `T'` into `U`.
declarations.statement: theorem isOpenSubfunctor_cohomologyLocus : IsOpenSubfunctor (cohomologyLocus f σ hσ)
declarations.comment: the inclusion is representable by open immersions, for f flat, proper and locally of finite presentation with a section

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.genus
declarations.doc: The genus of a scheme `X` over a field `k`, namely `dim_k H¹(X, 𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def genus {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) : ℕ
declarations.comment: smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve over a field

declarations.name: Stacks.RigidifiedPicard.exists_representableBy_cohomologyLocus
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B9X].** Let `k` be a field and `X` a smooth projective curve of genus `g` over
`k` with a rational point `σ`. The open subfunctor `F ⊆ Pic_{X/k,σ}` of [Stacks, Tag 0B9V] is
representable by an open subscheme of `Hilb^g_{X/k}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_representableBy_cohomologyLocus (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k f] [Smooth f] (hproj : IsProjectiveMorphism f)
    (σ : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X) (hσ : σ ≫ f = 𝟙 _) :
    haveI : IsProper f := isProper_of_isProjectiveMorphism f hproj
    haveI : GeometricallyIrreducible f := geometricallyIrreducible_of_isCurve_of_section k f σ hσ
    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f := smoothOfRelativeDimension_one_of_isCurve k f
    ∀ (H : Over (Spec (.of k)))
      (_ : Stacks.Hilbert.RepresentsHilbertFunctorOfRank (Over.mk f) H (genus f)),
      ∃ W : H.left.Opens, Nonempty ((cohomologyLocus f σ hσ).toFunctor.RepresentableBy
        (Over.mk (W.ι ≫ H.hom)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_invertible_baseChangeTwist_finrank_eq_one_of_isSepClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B9Y.** Let `k` be a separably closed field, `X` a smooth projective
curve over `k`, `K/k` a field extension and `X' = X_K` the base change, given as any pullback
square with `X ⟶ Spec k ⟵ Spec K`. For every invertible sheaf `L` on `X'` there is an invertible
sheaf `L₀` on `X` with

`dim_K H⁰(X', L ⊗ p^*L₀) = 1` and `dim_K H¹(X', L ⊗ p^*L₀) = 0`.

The proof is the source's: the start of the descending induction is
`AlgebraicGeometry.ampleTwistStart`, its step is `AlgebraicGeometry.pointIdealTwistStep`, and the
induction joining them is `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_hasPrescribedLowCohomology_one`, whose
cohomology is Tag 0B8Z's step lemma. The genus `g` of the source occurs in neither the assertion
nor the proof and is not a parameter. This form, for an arbitrary pullback square, is the one
`Stacks.PicardFunctor.TwistToNormalized` quantifies over.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_invertible_baseChangeTwist_finrank_eq_one_of_isSepClosed
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [IsSepClosed k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    {X X' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (f' : X' ⟶ Spec (.of K)) (p : X' ⟶ X)
    (hp : IsPullback p f' f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))
    [IsCurve k f] [Smooth f] (hproj : IsProjective f)
    (L : X'.Modules) [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X' L] :
    ∃ L₀ : X.Modules, Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L₀ ∧
      Module.finrank K (cohomologyOverField K f' (baseChangeTwist p L L₀) 0) = 1 ∧
      Module.finrank K (cohomologyOverField K f' (baseChangeTwist p L L₀) 1) = 0
declarations.comment: for X_K given as any pullback square of X ⟶ Spec k along Spec K ⟶ Spec k, with L ⊗ L₀|_{X_K} the twist baseChangeTwist p L L₀ = L ⊗ p^*L₀

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finrank_cohomologyOverField_add_schemePullbackClass_eq_one
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a separably closed field, `X` a smooth proper curve over `k`, `K/k` a field
extension and `p : X_K ⟶ X` the projection of the base change. For every Picard class `c` on
`X_K` (the class of an invertible `𝓛`) there is a Picard class `c₀` on `X` (the class of an
invertible `𝓛₀`) such that the class `c + p^*c₀` (that of `𝓛 ⊗ 𝓛₀|_{X_K}`) has

`dim_K H⁰(X_K, c + p^*c₀) = 1` and `H¹(X_K, c + p^*c₀) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finrank_cohomologyOverField_add_schemePullbackClass_eq_one
    [IsSepClosed k] [IsProper f] [IsCurve k f] [Smooth f] (c : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme 𝔛) :
    ∃ c₀ : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X,
      Module.finrank K (cohomologyOverField K 𝔣
        (Stacks.Picard.picardRepresentative (𝔛).toRingedSpace
          (c + Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClass 𝔭 c₀)).obj 0) = 1 ∧
      IsZero (cohomologyOverField K 𝔣
        (Stacks.Picard.picardRepresentative (𝔛).toRingedSpace
          (c + Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClass 𝔭 c₀)).obj 1)
declarations.comment: on Picard classes: the class c of the invertible sheaf L on X_K and the class c₀ of L₀ on X, with c + p^*c₀ the class of L ⊗ L₀|_{X_K}; H¹ = 0 is stated as vanishing, which gives dim_K H¹ = 0. Properness of X is used in place of projectivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_invertible_baseChangeTwist_finrank_cohomologyOverField_eq_one_of_isSepClosed
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a separably closed field, `X` a smooth proper curve over `k`, `K/k` a field
extension and `p : X_K ⟶ X` the projection of the base change. For every invertible
`𝒪_{X_K}`-module `𝓛` there is an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `𝓛₀` with

`dim_K H⁰(X_K, 𝓛 ⊗ p^*𝓛₀) = 1` and `dim_K H¹(X_K, 𝓛 ⊗ p^*𝓛₀) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_invertible_baseChangeTwist_finrank_cohomologyOverField_eq_one_of_isSepClosed
    [IsSepClosed k] [IsProper f] [IsCurve k f] [Smooth f]
    (L : (𝔛).Modules) [hL : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule 𝔛 L] :
    ∃ L₀ : X.Modules, Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L₀ ∧
      Module.finrank K (cohomologyOverField K 𝔣 (baseChangeTwist 𝔭 L L₀) 0) = 1 ∧
      Module.finrank K (cohomologyOverField K 𝔣 (baseChangeTwist 𝔭 L L₀) 1) = 0
declarations.comment: the source's statement on sheaves, with L ⊗ L₀|_{X_K} the twist baseChangeTwist p L L₀ = L ⊗ p^*L₀; properness of X is used in place of projectivity

declarations.name: Stacks.PicardFunctor.isRepresentable_picardFunctor_of_isSepClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0B9Z.** Let `k` be a separably closed field and `X` a smooth projective
curve over `k`. The Picard functor `Pic_{X/k}` is representable.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_picardFunctor_of_isSepClosed [IsSepClosed k]
    [IsCurve k (B.inclusion.map f)] [Smooth (B.inclusion.map f)]
    [IsProjectiveVariety k (B.inclusion.map f)] :
    (picardFunctor B hX hk f).IsRepresentable

declarations.name: Stacks.RigidifiedPicard.isRepresentable_picardFunctor_of_isSepClosed
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B9Z].** Let `k` be a separably closed field and `X` a smooth projective curve
over `k`. The Picard functor `Pic_{X/k}` is representable.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_picardFunctor_of_isSepClosed (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsSepClosed k]
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (hX : B.Contains X) (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (f : B.obj hX ⟶ B.obj hk) [IsCurve k (B.inclusion.map f)] [Smooth (B.inclusion.map f)]
    (hproj : IsProjectiveMorphism (B.inclusion.map f)) :
    (Stacks.PicardFunctor.picardFunctor B hX hk f).IsRepresentable

declarations.name: Stacks.RigidifiedPicard.exists_grp_iso_functor_of_isSepClosed
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0B9Z].** The Picard functor of a smooth projective curve `X` over a separably
closed field `k` is representable: for a rational point `σ`, the rigidified Picard functor
`Pic_{X/k,σ} ≅ Pic_{X/k}` is represented by a group scheme over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_grp_iso_functor_of_isSepClosed (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsSepClosed k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k f] [Smooth f]
    (hproj : IsProjectiveMorphism f) :
    haveI : IsProper f := isProper_of_isProjectiveMorphism f hproj
    ∃ (σ : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X) (hσ : σ ≫ f = 𝟙 _) (P : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))),
      Nonempty (yonedaGrp.obj P ≅ functor f σ hσ)
declarations.comment: as the rigidified functor Pic_{X/k,σ} at a rational point σ, which the source's proof identifies with Pic_{X/k}

declarations.name: Stacks.AbelMap.picardScheme_clause_one
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0BA0, clause (1).**
declarations.statement:
theorem picardScheme_clause_one :
    haveI := geometricallyIrreducible_of_isSepClosed B hX hk f
    haveI := isProjectiveVariety_of_isProjective B hX hk f hproj
    haveI := isRepresentable_picardFunctor_of_isSepClosed B hX hk f
    Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk (picardScheme B hX hk f)
        fun d => (picardDegreeLocus B hX hk f (curveSection B hX hk f)
          (curveSection_comp B hX hk f) d).ι)) ∧
      ∀ d : ℤ, SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus (B.inclusion.map f))
          (picardDegreeComponentHom B hX hk f (curveSection B hX hk f)
            (curveSection_comp B hX hk f) d) ∧
        IsProper (picardDegreeComponentHom B hX hk f (curveSection B hX hk f)
            (curveSection_comp B hX hk f) d) ∧
        IsVariety k (picardDegreeComponentHom B hX hk f (curveSection B hX hk f)
            (curveSection_comp B hX hk f) d) ∧
        topologicalKrullDim (B.inclusion.obj (picardSchemeDegreeComponent B hX hk f
            (curveSection B hX hk f) (curveSection_comp B hX hk f) d).left) =
          (genus (B.inclusion.map f) : WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: Stacks.AbelMap.picardScheme_clause_three
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0BA0, clause (3).**
declarations.statement:
theorem picardScheme_clause_three :
    haveI := geometricallyIrreducible_of_isSepClosed B hX hk f
    haveI := isProjectiveVariety_of_isProjective B hX hk f hproj
    haveI := isRepresentable_picardFunctor_of_isSepClosed B hX hk f
    ∃ H : AlgebraicGeometry.OpenSubgroupScheme (picardGrp B hX hk f),
      IsClosedImmersion H.ι.hom.hom.left ∧
        Set.range H.ι.hom.hom.left.base = (picardDegreeLocus B hX hk f (curveSection B hX hk f)
          (curveSection_comp B hX hk f) 0 : Set (picardScheme B hX hk f))

declarations.name: Stacks.AbelMap.picardScheme_clauses_four_five_six
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BA0, clauses (4), (5) and (6).** For every `d ≥ 0` the degree-`d`
Hilbert scheme `Hilb^d_{X/k}` exists in the site ([Stacks, Tag 0B9I]), and for every scheme `H`
representing it there is a unique morphism `γ_d : H ⟶ Pic^d_{X/k}` classifying the invertible
module `𝒪(D_univ)` of the universal divisor (clause (4)); it is surjective for `d ≥ g` and smooth
for `d ≥ 2g - 1` (clause (5)), and birational for `d = g` (clause (6)).
declarations.statement:
theorem picardScheme_clauses_four_five_six (d : ℕ) :
    haveI := geometricallyIrreducible_of_isSepClosed B hX hk f
    haveI := isProjectiveVariety_of_isProjective B hX hk f hproj
    haveI := isRepresentable_picardFunctor_of_isSepClosed B hX hk f
    (∃ H : BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk,
      Nonempty (Stacks.Hilbert.RepresentsHilbertFunctorOfRank (Over.mk (B.inclusion.map f))
        (Over.mk (B.inclusion.map H.hom)) d)) ∧
    ∀ (H : BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)
      (hH : Stacks.Hilbert.RepresentsHilbertFunctorOfRank (Over.mk (B.inclusion.map f))
        (Over.mk (B.inclusion.map H.hom)) d),
    ∃! γ : H ⟶ picardSchemeDegreeComponent B hX hk f (curveSection B hX hk f)
        (curveSection_comp B hX hk f) d,
      (∀ {T : BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk} (t : T ⟶ H),
        picardHomEquiv B hX hk f (t ≫ γ ≫ picardSchemeDegreeComponentι B hX hk f
            (curveSection B hX hk f) (curveSection_comp B hX hk f) d) =
          (toPicardFunctor B hX hk f).app (op T) (hH.family (testMap B hk t)).picardClass) ∧
      (genus (B.inclusion.map f) ≤ d → Surjective (B.inclusion.map γ.left)) ∧
      (2 * (genus (B.inclusion.map f) : ℤ) - 1 ≤ d →
        AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth (B.inclusion.map γ.left)) ∧
      (d = genus (B.inclusion.map f) → IsBirational (B.inclusion.map γ.left))

declarations.name: Stacks.AbelMap.picardScheme_clause_two_bijOn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BA0, clause (2).** For a smooth projective curve `X` over a separably
closed field `k`, the natural map from the `k`-points of `Pic^d_{X/k}` to `Pic(X)`, sending a
point `q` to the invertible `𝒪_X`-module whose class in `Pic_{X/k}(Spec k)` is classified by `q`
followed by the inclusion `Pic^d_{X/k} ⟶ Pic_{X/k}`, is a bijection onto the invertible modules of
degree `d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem picardScheme_clause_two_bijOn (d : ℤ) :
    haveI := geometricallyIrreducible_of_isSepClosed B hX hk f
    haveI := isProjectiveVariety_of_isProjective B hX hk f hproj
    haveI := isRepresentable_picardFunctor_of_isSepClosed B hX hk f
    Set.BijOn
      (fun q : baseOver B hk ⟶ picardSchemeDegreeComponent B hX hk f (curveSection B hX hk f)
          (curveSection_comp B hX hk f) d =>
        picardPointsEquiv B hX hk f (curveSection B hX hk f) (curveSection_comp B hX hk f)
          (isIso_baseChangeProj_c_of_isCurve B hX hk f (curveSection B hX hk f)
            (curveSection_comp B hX hk f))
          (q ≫ picardSchemeDegreeComponentι B hX hk f (curveSection B hX hk f)
            (curveSection_comp B hX hk f) d))
      Set.univ
      {x : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X |
        @invertibleCurveDegree k _ X (B.inclusion.map f) _
          (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (k := k) (f := B.inclusion.map f)).le (rep x)
          (Stacks.Picard.picardRepresentative X.toRingedSpace x).property = d}

declarations.name: Stacks.RigidifiedPicard.exists_picardScheme
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_picardScheme (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsSepClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k f] [Smooth f] (hproj : IsProjectiveMorphism f) :
    haveI : IsProper f := isProper_of_isProjectiveMorphism f hproj
    haveI : GeometricallyIrreducible f := geometricallyIrreducible_of_isCurve_of_isSepClosed k f
    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f := smoothOfRelativeDimension_one_of_isCurve k f
    ∃ (σ : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X) (hσ : σ ≫ f = 𝟙 _) (P : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k))))
      (e : yonedaGrp.obj P ≅ functor f σ hσ),
      -- (1)
      (∀ d d' : ℤ, d ≠ d' → Disjoint
        (degreeLocus f (topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le_one_of_isCurve k f) σ hσ P e d : Set P.X.left)
        (degreeLocus f (topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le_one_of_isCurve k f) σ hσ P e d')) ∧
      (⨆ d, degreeLocus f (topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le_one_of_isCurve k f) σ hσ P e d = ⊤) ∧
      (∀ d : ℤ,
        IsClopen (degreeLocus f (topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le_one_of_isCurve k f) σ hσ P e d :
          Set P.X.left) ∧
        IsProperVariety k
          ((degreeLocus f (topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le_one_of_isCurve k f) σ hσ P e d).ι ≫
            P.X.hom) ∧
        SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus f)
          ((degreeLocus f (topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le_one_of_isCurve k f) σ hσ P e d).ι ≫
            P.X.hom) ∧
        topologicalKrullDim
          (degreeLocus f (topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le_one_of_isCurve k f) σ hσ P e d) =
            (genus f : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧
      -- (2)
      (∀ d : ℤ, Set.BijOn (pointClassOf f σ hσ P e)
        {r | Set.range r.left ⊆
          (degreeLocus f (topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le_one_of_isCurve k f) σ hσ P e d :
            Set P.X.left)}
        {c | invertibleCurveDegreeHom k f (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (k := k) (f := f)).le
          c = d}) ∧
      -- (3)
      (∃ K : OpenSubgroupScheme P, ∃ i : degreeLocusOver f
          (topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le_one_of_isCurve k f) σ hσ P e 0 ≅ K.carrier.X,
        degreeLocusι f (topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le_one_of_isCurve k f) σ hσ P e 0 =
          i.hom ≫ K.ι.hom.hom) ∧
      ∀ (H : ℕ → Over (Spec (.of k)))
        (hH : ∀ d, Stacks.Hilbert.RepresentsHilbertFunctorOfRank (Over.mk f) (H d) d),
        -- (4)
        (∀ d : ℕ,
          abelMorphismDegree f (topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le_one_of_isCurve k f) σ hσ P e
              (hH d) ≫
            (degreeLocus f (topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le_one_of_isCurve k f) σ hσ P e d).ι =
              (abelMorphismFull f σ hσ (hH d) P e).left ∧
          ∀ {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (m : T ⟶ H d),
            (e.hom.app (op T)).hom (m ≫ abelMorphismFull f σ hσ (hH d) P e) =
              abelElementFull f σ hσ (hH d) m) ∧
        -- (5), surjectivity
        (∀ d : ℕ, genus f ≤ d → Surjective
          (abelMorphismDegree f (topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le_one_of_isCurve k f) σ hσ P e
            (hH d))) ∧
        -- (5), smoothness
        (∀ d : ℕ, 2 * (genus f : ℤ) - 1 ≤ d → Smooth
          (abelMorphismDegree f (topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le_one_of_isCurve k f) σ hσ P e
            (hH d))) ∧
        -- (6)
        IsBirational (abelMorphismDegree f (topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le_one_of_isCurve k f) σ hσ
          P e (hH (genus f)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_range_pointsMap_schematicLocus_iff_exists_isAffine_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BA1.** Let `X ⟶ Y` be a surjective finite locally free morphism of algebraic
spaces over a scheme `S`, and let `y` be a point of `Y`. Then the following are equivalent:

1. `y` lies in the schematic locus of `Y` — the point set of
   `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schematicLocus`, the largest open subspace of `Y` which is a
   scheme (Tag 03JH); and
2. there is an affine open subspace of `X`, presented as an open immersion `i : h_U ⟶ X`
   from an affine object `U` of the site, whose point set contains the whole fibre of `y`.

Finite local freeness of `f` is taken in the representable sense: `f` is representable and
every represented base change of it is a finite locally free morphism of schemes.  That is
condition (1) of Tag 03ZW, which the source's Definition 03ZV — condition (2) of that tag —
is equivalent to.  Surjectivity is likewise taken after representable base change, which is
condition (1) of Tag 02YN.

The two implications are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffine_isOpenImmersion_of_mem_schematicLocus` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_range_pointsMap_schematicLocus_of_exists_isAffine`; see their
docstrings for the two arguments.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_range_pointsMap_schematicLocus_iff_exists_isAffine_isOpenImmersion
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hsurj : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f.hom)
    (hflf : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f.hom)
    (y : points B S hS Y.obj) :
    y ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (schematicLocus B S hS Y.obj).toFunctor
        (schematicLocus B S hS Y.obj).ι) ↔
      ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (i : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj),
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) ∧ IsOpenImmersion B S hS i ∧
        ∀ x : points B S hS X.obj, pointsMap B S hS X.obj f.hom x = y →
          x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj U) i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_jacobson_atlas_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BA3.** An algebraic space locally of finite type over a Jacobson algebraic
space is Jacobson: if the algebraic space `X` over `S` has a surjective étale atlas by a
Jacobson scheme and `f : Y ⟶ X` is locally of finite type, then so does `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_jacobson_atlas_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hJac : ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X),
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) a ∧
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) a ∧
      JacobsonSpace ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)) :
    ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y),
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) b ∧
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) b ∧
      JacobsonSpace ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isClosed_pointsToScheme_of_isFiniteTypePoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BA4.** Let `X` be a Jacobson algebraic space over `S`, written as having a
surjective étale atlas by a Jacobson scheme, and let `g : h_W ⟶ X` be locally of finite type
with `W` an object of the big fppf site of `S`. A finite type point of `X` in the image of `g`
is the image of a point of `h_W` whose underlying point of the scheme `W` is closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isClosed_pointsToScheme_of_isFiniteTypePoint
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hJac : ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X),
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) a ∧
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) a ∧
      JacobsonSpace ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U))
    (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj W ⟶ X)
    (hg : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g)
    (x : points B S hS X) (hx : IsFiniteTypePoint B S hS X x)
    (himage : x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj W) g)) :
    ∃ y : points B S hS (yoneda.obj W),
      IsClosed ({pointsToScheme B S hS W y} :
        Set ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj W)) ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj W) g y = x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypePoint_iff_isClosed_singleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BA5**, pointwise. Let `X` be a decent Jacobson algebraic space over `S`, the
Jacobson condition being written as the existence of a surjective étale atlas by a Jacobson
scheme. A point of `X` is a finite type point exactly when it is a closed point of `|X|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypePoint_iff_isClosed_singleton
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    (hJac : ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X),
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) a ∧
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) a ∧
      JacobsonSpace ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U))
    (x : points B S hS X) :
    IsFiniteTypePoint B S hS X x ↔ IsClosed ({x} : Set (points B S hS X))
declarations.comment: pointwise form

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finiteTypePoints_eq_setOf_isClosed_singleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BA5.** Let `X` be a decent Jacobson algebraic space over `S`, the Jacobson
condition being written as the existence of a surjective étale atlas by a Jacobson scheme.
Then `X_{ft-pts} ⊂ |X|` is the set of closed points.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteTypePoints_eq_setOf_isClosed_singleton
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    (hJac : ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X),
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) a ∧
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) a ∧
      JacobsonSpace ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)) :
    finiteTypePoints B S hS X = {x | IsClosed ({x} : Set (points B S hS X))}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_jacobson_atlas_iff_jacobsonSpace_points
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BA6.** A decent algebraic space `X` over `S` is Jacobson — the Jacobson
condition being written as the existence of a surjective étale atlas by a Jacobson scheme —
if and only if its topological space `|X|` of points is a Jacobson topological space.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_jacobson_atlas_iff_jacobsonSpace_points
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) :
    (∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X),
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) a ∧
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) a ∧
      JacobsonSpace ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)) ↔
    JacobsonSpace (points B S hS X)

declarations.name: Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible.finiteField_remark
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BA7.** Let `k` be a finite field and `K/k` a geometrically irreducible field
extension.
1. `K` is the directed union of geometrically irreducible `k`-subalgebras of finite type.
2. For every geometrically irreducible `k`-algebra `A` of finite type there is `N` such that
   for every finite extension `k'/k` of degree `n ≥ N` there is a `k`-algebra map `A → k'`.
3. If `X` is a quasi-separated algebraic space over `k` and `X_K` is a scheme, then `X` is a
   scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteField_remark (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Finite k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (hK : Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k K) :
    (∃ (ι : Type u) (A : ι → Subalgebra k K), Directed (· ≤ ·) A ∧ (⨆ i, A i) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ i, Algebra.FiniteType k (A i) ∧ Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k (A i)) ∧
    (∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A],
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k A →
      ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [FiniteDimensional k k'],
        N ≤ finrank k k' → Nonempty (A →ₐ[k] k')) ∧
    (∀ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k))) (hK' : B.Contains (Spec (.of K)))
      (F : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u),
      IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk F →
      IsQuasiSeparatedOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk F →
      ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict
        (ObjectProperty.homMk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) :
          B.obj hK' ⟶ B.obj hk)).obj F).IsRepresentable →
      F.IsRepresentable)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.dominantBirational_iff_exists_nonempty_open_iso
declarations.doc:
Two irreducible schemes are birational, in the sense of being isomorphic in the category of
irreducible schemes and dominant rational maps, if and only if they have isomorphic nonempty
open subschemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem dominantBirational_iff_exists_nonempty_open_iso [IrreducibleSpace X]
    [IrreducibleSpace Y] :
    DominantBirational X Y ↔
      ∃ (U : X.Opens) (V : Y.Opens),
        (U : Set X).Nonempty ∧ (V : Set Y).Nonempty ∧ Nonempty (U.toScheme ≅ V.toScheme)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.dominantBirationalOver_iff_exists_nonempty_open_iso
declarations.doc:
Two irreducible schemes over `S` are `S`-birational, in the sense of being isomorphic in the
category of irreducible schemes over `S` and dominant `S`-rational maps, if and only if there are
nonempty opens `U ⊆ X` and `V ⊆ Y` which are isomorphic over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dominantBirationalOver_iff_exists_nonempty_open_iso [X.Over S] [Y.Over S]
    [IrreducibleSpace X] [IrreducibleSpace Y] :
    DominantBirationalOver S X Y ↔
      ∃ (U : X.Opens) (V : Y.Opens),
        (U : Set X).Nonempty ∧ (V : Set Y).Nonempty ∧
          ∃ e : U.toScheme ≅ V.toScheme, e.hom ≫ V.ι ≫ Y ↘ S = U.ι ≫ X ↘ S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_pullback_snd_fromSpecStalk_of_isBirational
declarations.doc:
The base change of a birational morphism to the spectrum of the local ring at a generic
point of an irreducible component of the target is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
lemma isIso_pullback_snd_fromSpecStalk_of_isBirational
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [Finite (irreducibleComponents X)] [Finite (irreducibleComponents Y)]
    (hf : IsBirational f) (y : Y) (hy : y ∈ genericPoints Y) :
    IsIso (pullback.snd f (Y.fromSpecStalk y))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_dense_opens_isIso_resLE_of_isBirational
declarations.doc:
A birational morphism between schemes with finitely many irreducible components is an
isomorphism between dense open subschemes, provided that it is locally of finite type with reduced
target or locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_dense_opens_isIso_resLE_of_isBirational
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [Finite (irreducibleComponents X)] [Finite (irreducibleComponents Y)]
    (hf : IsBirational f)
    (hfin : (LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧ IsReduced Y) ∨ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (V : Y.Opens) (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V),
      Dense (U : Set X) ∧ Dense (V : Set Y) ∧ IsIso (f.resLE V U hUV)
declarations.comment: dense open isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.dominantBirationalOver_of_isBirational
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAC**, the final assertion: a birational morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` over `S` between
irreducible schemes, locally of finite type with `Y` reduced or locally of finite presentation,
makes `X` and `Y` `S`-birational in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 0A20] (2), i.e. isomorphic in the
category of irreducible schemes over `S` and dominant `S`-rational maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem dominantBirationalOver_of_isBirational [X.Over S] [Y.Over S] (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver S]
    [Finite (irreducibleComponents X)] [Finite (irreducibleComponents Y)]
    [IrreducibleSpace X] [IrreducibleSpace Y] (hf : IsBirational f)
    (hfin : (LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧ IsReduced Y) ∨ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) :
    DominantBirationalOver S X Y
declarations.comment: in particular: irreducible X, Y are S-birational in the sense of 0A20

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.dominantBirationalOver_tfae_generic_stalk_iso
declarations.doc:
For irreducible schemes `X` and `Y` locally of finite presentation over `S`, with generic
points `x` and `y`, the following are equivalent: `X` and `Y` are `S`-birational (isomorphic in
the category of irreducible schemes over `S` and dominant `S`-rational maps); there are nonempty
opens of `X` and `Y` which are isomorphic over `S`; `x` and `y` map to the same point `s` of `S`
and the local rings `𝒪_{X, x}` and `𝒪_{Y, y}` are isomorphic as `𝒪_{S, s}`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem dominantBirationalOver_tfae_generic_stalk_iso {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over S] [Y.Over S]
    [IrreducibleSpace X] [IrreducibleSpace Y]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation (X ↘ S)] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation (Y ↘ S)] :
    List.TFAE
      [DominantBirationalOver S X Y,
        ∃ (U : X.Opens) (V : Y.Opens),
          (U : Set X).Nonempty ∧ (V : Set Y).Nonempty ∧
            ∃ e : U.toScheme ≅ V.toScheme, e.hom ≫ V.ι ≫ Y ↘ S = U.ι ≫ X ↘ S,
        ∃ (h : (X ↘ S) (genericPoint X) = (Y ↘ S) (genericPoint Y))
          (e : X.presheaf.stalk (genericPoint X) ≅ Y.presheaf.stalk (genericPoint Y)),
            h ▸ ((X ↘ S).stalkMap (genericPoint X) ≫ e.hom) =
              (Y ↘ S).stalkMap (genericPoint Y)]
declarations.comment:
Conditions (1), (2) and (3) of the lemma, with (1) the `S`-birationality of Tag
0A20.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ringKrullDim_stalk_add_residueFieldTranscendenceDegree_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAE.** The general dimension formula: for a morphism `f : X ⟶ S` locally of finite
type over a locally Noetherian scheme and a point `x` of `X`,
`dim 𝒪_{X,x} + trdeg_{κ(f x)} κ(x) ≤ dim 𝒪_{S,f x} + E`, where `E` is the supremum of
`trdeg_{κ(f ξ)} κ(ξ)` over the generic points `ξ` of the irreducible components of `X`
containing `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_stalk_add_residueFieldTranscendenceDegree_le {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) + (residueFieldTranscendenceDegree f x : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤
      ringKrullDim (S.presheaf.stalk (f x)) +
        (genericResidueFieldTranscendenceDegreeAt f x : WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDim_le_add_iSup_residueFieldTrdeg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAG.** The dimension of the source of a morphism locally of finite type over a
locally Noetherian scheme is at most the dimension of the target plus the supremum of the
residue-field transcendence degrees at the generic points of the irreducible components of the
source.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_le_add_iSup_residueFieldTrdeg
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    topologicalKrullDim X ≤ topologicalKrullDim Y +
      ((⨆ ξ : genericPoints X, residueFieldTranscendenceDegree f ξ.1 : ℕ∞) : WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiFiniteAt_over_genericPoint_tfae
declarations.doc:
For a locally finite type morphism, the fibre over a generic point consists of generic
points if and only if the morphism is quasi-finite at every point of the fibre, equivalently
if it is quasi-finite at every generic point of the fibre.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiFiniteAt_over_genericPoint_tfae {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (η : Y) (hη : η ∈ genericPoints Y) :
    List.TFAE [
      f ⁻¹' {η} ⊆ genericPoints X,
      ∀ x : X, f x = η → quasiFiniteAt f x,
      ∀ ξ : X, ξ ∈ genericPoints X → f ξ = η → quasiFiniteAt f ξ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_dense_open_isFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAI.** A locally finite type morphism carrying precisely the generic points of its
source to the generic points of its target is finite over a dense open of the target, if it is
quasi-compact or separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dense_open_isFinite {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hX : (genericPoints X).Finite) (hY : (genericPoints Y).Finite)
    (hgeneric : f ⁻¹' genericPoints Y = genericPoints X)
    (hqc_or_sep : QuasiCompact f ∨ IsSeparated f) :
    ∃ V : Y.Opens, Dense (V : Set Y) ∧ IsFinite (f ∣_ V)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_dense_open_isIso_morphismRestrict_of_isBirational
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BAJ.** A birational morphism between schemes with finitely many
irreducible components is an isomorphism over a dense open subscheme of its target, provided it
is quasi-compact or separated and provided it is locally of finite type with reduced target or
locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dense_open_isIso_morphismRestrict_of_isBirational
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [Finite (irreducibleComponents X)] [Finite (irreducibleComponents Y)]
    (hf : IsBirational f) (hqc_or_sep : QuasiCompact f ∨ IsSeparated f)
    (hfin : (LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧ IsReduced Y) ∨ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) :
    ∃ V : Y.Opens, Dense (V : Set Y) ∧ IsIso (f ∣_ V)

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeNormalization.integralClosureSpectrum_isRelativeNormalization
declarations.doc:
**Relative normalization.** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a
quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes, let `𝒪' ⊆ f_* 𝒪_Y` be the integral
closure of `𝒪_X` in `f_* 𝒪_Y`, and let `ν : X' = Spec_X(𝒪') ⟶ X` be its relative spectrum, the
normalization of `X` in `Y`. Then:

* `f` factors as `f = ν ∘ f'`, where `f' : Y ⟶ X'` is the canonical morphism
  `Y ⟶ Spec_X(f_* 𝒪_Y)` followed by the morphism of relative spectra induced by the inclusion
  `𝒪' ⊆ f_* 𝒪_Y`;
* `ν` is integral and `f'` is dominant;
* for every factorization `f = π ∘ g` with `π : Z ⟶ X` integral there is a unique
  `h : X' ⟶ Z` with `h ∘ f' = g` and `π ∘ h = ν`;
* consequently `X'` is uniquely isomorphic, under `Y` and over `X`, to the relative
  normalization `f.normalization`.
declarations.statement:
theorem integralClosureSpectrum_isRelativeNormalization :
    toIntegralClosureSpectrum f ≫ (integralClosureSpectrum f).toBase = f ∧
    toRelativeSpec f ≫ relativeSpectrumMapOfAlgebraHom (integralClosureSituation f)
        (pushforwardAlgebra f) (AlgebraSheaf.isQuasicoherent_pushforwardAlgebra f)
        (integralClosureAlgebraι (pushforwardAlgebra f)) = toIntegralClosureSpectrum f ∧
    IsIntegralHom (integralClosureSpectrum f).toBase ∧
    IsDominant (toIntegralClosureSpectrum f) ∧
    (∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (π : Z ⟶ X), IsIntegralHom π → g ≫ π = f →
      ∃! h : (integralClosureSpectrum f).scheme ⟶ Z,
        toIntegralClosureSpectrum f ≫ h = g ∧ h ≫ π = (integralClosureSpectrum f).toBase) ∧
    ∃! e : (integralClosureSpectrum f).scheme ≅ f.normalization,
      toIntegralClosureSpectrum f ≫ e.hom = f.toNormalization ∧
        e.hom ≫ f.fromNormalization = (integralClosureSpectrum f).toBase

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteIrreducibleComponents_isLocal_fppf
declarations.doc:
Having finitely many irreducible components on every quasi-compact open is local in the
fppf topology.
declarations.statement:
instance finiteIrreducibleComponents_isLocal_fppf :
    ObjectProperty.IsLocal
      (fun X : Scheme.{u} =>
        ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite)
      Scheme.fppfPrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasChartLocalRingDimension_iff_allChartsLocalRingDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAM.** The Krull dimension of the local ring measured on an étale scheme chart
of an algebraic space is independent of the chart and of the point above `x`: one chart
realizes the value `d` exactly when every chart does.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasChartLocalRingDimension_iff_allChartsLocalRingDimension
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (x : points B S hS F) (d : ℕ∞) :
    HasChartLocalRingDimension B S hS x d ↔ AllChartsLocalRingDimension B S hS x d
declarations.comment: equivalence of étale-chart conditions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasChartLocalRingDimension_iff_ringKrullDim_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAM, the representable case.** For a represented algebraic space the chart
condition at a point is the Krull dimension of the local ring of the representing scheme at
the corresponding scheme point.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasChartLocalRingDimension_iff_ringKrullDim_stalk (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (u : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) (x : points B S hS (yoneda.obj U))
    (hx : ChartPoint B S hS U (𝟙 (yoneda.obj U)) u x) (d : ℕ∞) :
    HasChartLocalRingDimension B S hS x d ↔
      ringKrullDim (((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U).presheaf.stalk u) =
        (d : WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: representable case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_eq_iSup_localRingDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAN, quantities (1) and (2).** The dimension of an algebraic space is the
supremum of the Krull dimensions of its local rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimension_eq_iSup_localRingDimension (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    dimension B S hS F hF =
      ⨆ x : points B S hS F, (localRingDimension B S hS x : WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: the dimension of the space is the supremum over its local rings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.iSup_dimensionAtPoint_eq_iSup_localRingDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAN, quantities (3) and (2).** The supremum, over the points `x` of an algebraic
space, of its dimension `dim_x(X)` at `x` is the supremum of the Krull dimensions of its local
rings. By Definition 04N6 the left-hand side is the dimension of the algebraic space, so
together with `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_eq_iSup_localRingDimension` this is the
equality of all three quantities of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem iSup_dimensionAtPoint_eq_iSup_localRingDimension (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    (⨆ x : points B S hS F, dimensionAtPoint B S hS F hF x) =
      ⨆ x : points B S hS F, (localRingDimension B S hS x : WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: the supremum over the points of the dimension at the point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.localRingDimension_eq_zero_iff_exists_etale_genericPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAQ, conditions (1) and (2).** A point of an algebraic space has a local ring of
dimension zero exactly when some étale scheme chart has, above it, a generic point of an
irreducible component.
declarations.statement:
theorem localRingDimension_eq_zero_iff_exists_etale_genericPoint
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (x : points B S hS F) :
    localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 ↔
      ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F)
        (u : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U),
        IsEtale B S hS a ∧ ChartPoint B S hS U a u x ∧
          u ∈ genericPoints ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)
declarations.comment: condition (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.localRingDimension_eq_zero_iff_all_etale_genericPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAQ, conditions (1) and (3).** A point of an algebraic space has a local ring of
dimension zero exactly when every point above it in every étale scheme chart is the generic
point of an irreducible component.
declarations.statement:
theorem localRingDimension_eq_zero_iff_all_etale_genericPoints
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (x : points B S hS F) :
    localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 ↔
      ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F)
        (u : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U),
        IsEtale B S hS a → ChartPoint B S hS U a u x →
          u ∈ genericPoints ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)
declarations.comment: condition (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.localRingDimension_eq_zero_iff_genericPoint_of_isRepresentable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAQ, the representable case.** For a representable algebraic space, a point has a
local ring of dimension zero exactly when it is the generic point of an irreducible component
of the space of points.
declarations.statement:
theorem localRingDimension_eq_zero_iff_genericPoint_of_isRepresentable
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hrep : F.IsRepresentable) (x : points B S hS F) :
    localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 ↔ x ∈ genericPoints (points B S hS F)
declarations.comment: representable case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.codimensionZeroPoints_dense
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAR.** The points of codimension zero of an algebraic space are dense in its
space of points.
declarations.statement:
theorem codimensionZeroPoints_dense (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    Dense {x : points B S hS F | localRingDimension B S hS x = 0}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.codimensionZero_mem_schematicLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAS, codimension-zero points.** If an algebraic space over `S` admits a finite,
étale, surjective morphism from an object of the site whose underlying scheme is
quasi-separated, then every point of codimension zero lies in the schematic locus of
Tag 03JH.
declarations.statement:
theorem codimensionZero_mem_schematicLocus (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hcover : ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (q : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F),
      QuasiSeparatedSpace ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) ∧
      IsFinite B S hS q ∧ IsEtale B S hS q ∧ IsSurjective B S hS q)
    (x : points B S hS F) (hx : localRingDimension B S hS x = 0) :
    x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (schematicLocus B S hS F).toFunctor
      (schematicLocus B S hS F).ι)
declarations.comment: codimension-zero points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.denseRange_schematicLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAS, density.** If an algebraic space over `S` admits a finite, étale, surjective
morphism from an object of the site whose underlying scheme is quasi-separated, then the
schematic locus of Tag 03JH is dense in its space of points.
declarations.statement:
theorem denseRange_schematicLocus (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hcover : ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (q : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F),
      QuasiSeparatedSpace ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) ∧
      IsFinite B S hS q ∧ IsEtale B S hS q ∧ IsSurjective B S hS q) :
    DenseRange (pointsMap B S hS (schematicLocus B S hS F).toFunctor
      (schematicLocus B S hS F).ι)
declarations.comment: density

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isNagata_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAU.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite type
and whose target is Nagata has Nagata source.

A surjective étale chart `q : h_V ⟶ Y` witnessing that the target is Nagata lifts, by
Stacks 02X1, to a surjective étale chart `p : h_U ⟶ X` of the source and a morphism
`α : U ⟶ V` of the site making the square commute. Local finite type of the morphism tests
exactly such squares, so the scheme morphism underlying `α` is locally of finite type with
Nagata target, whence `U` is Nagata by Stacks 035A and `p` is the required chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNagata_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hN : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsNagataScheme T)) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsNagataScheme T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isNagata_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_over_nagataScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAV, part (1).** An algebraic space over `S` locally of finite type over a
Nagata scheme is Nagata.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNagata_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_over_nagataScheme (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (hT : IsNagataScheme ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T))
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun Z : Scheme.{u} => IsNagataScheme Z)
declarations.comment: part (1): over a Nagata scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isNagata_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_over_field
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAV, part (2).** An algebraic space over `S` locally of finite type over a field
is Nagata.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNagata_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_over_field (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (T : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (e : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T ≅ Spec (.of k))
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun Z : Scheme.{u} => IsNagataScheme Z)
declarations.comment: part (2): over a field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isNagata_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_over_completeLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAV, part (3).** An algebraic space over `S` locally of finite type over a
Noetherian complete local ring is Nagata. Completeness is
`IsPrecomplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R`, as in Stacks 032W.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNagata_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_over_completeLocalRing (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsPrecomplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R] (T : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (e : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T ≅ Spec (.of R))
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun Z : Scheme.{u} => IsNagataScheme Z)
declarations.comment: part (3): over a Noetherian complete local ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isNagata_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_over_int
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAV, part (4).** An algebraic space over `S` locally of finite type over the
integers is Nagata. "Over the integers" is read as "over the terminal scheme of the ambient
universe", which is the spectrum of `ULift ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNagata_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_over_int (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (hT : IsTerminal ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T))
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun Z : Scheme.{u} => IsNagataScheme Z)
declarations.comment: part (4): over the integers

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isNagata_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_over_dedekindDomain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAV, part (5).** An algebraic space over `S` locally of finite type over a
Dedekind domain of characteristic zero is Nagata.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNagata_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_over_dedekindDomain (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDedekindDomain R] [CharZero R] (T : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (e : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T ≅ Spec (.of R))
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun Z : Scheme.{u} => IsNagataScheme Z)
declarations.comment: part (5): over a Dedekind domain of characteristic zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_zeroDimensionalSpecializations
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAX, finiteness of the family entering the maximum.** Under the hypotheses of the
dimension formula only finitely many codimension-zero points of the source specialize to a
given point.

The source is locally Noetherian by Stacks 04ZK, hence has locally finite irreducible
components by Stacks 0GMB, so every quasi-compact algebraic space étale over it has finitely
many codimension-zero points by Stacks 0BB1. An affine étale chart through the point is such a
space, its image on points is open by Stacks 03BX and therefore contains every point
specializing to the given one, and codimension zero is étale-invariant by Stacks 0A4H.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_zeroDimensionalSpecializations (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hNoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (x : points B S hS X) :
    {ξ : points B S hS X | x ∈ closure {ξ} ∧ localRingDimension B S hS ξ = 0}.Finite
declarations.comment: finiteness of the family entering the maximum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_genericResidueFieldTranscendenceDegreeAt_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAX, attainment of the maximum.** Under the hypotheses of the dimension formula
the supremum defining the correction term is attained, so it is a maximum.

The family is finite by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_zeroDimensionalSpecializations`, and it
is nonempty because the generic point of an irreducible component of an étale chart through the
chosen point maps to a codimension-zero point specializing to it (Stacks 0BAQ).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_genericResidueFieldTranscendenceDegreeAt_eq (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hNoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (x : points B S hS X) :
    ∃ ξ : {ξ : points B S hS X // x ∈ closure {ξ} ∧ localRingDimension B S hS ξ = 0},
      genericResidueFieldTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f x =
        residueFieldTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f ξ.1
declarations.comment: attainment of the maximum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.localRingDimension_add_residueFieldTranscendenceDegree_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAX, the dimension inequality.** For a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`
locally of finite type with locally Noetherian target, the dimension of the local ring at a
point plus the residue-field transcendence degree there is at most the dimension of the local
ring at the image point plus the largest residue-field transcendence degree at a
codimension-zero point specializing to the given one.

Everything is read on one pointed étale chart of Stacks 04NC: the two local dimensions are the
Krull dimensions of the two chart stalks by Stacks 0BAM, the two residue-field degrees are
those of the morphism of charts by Stacks 04NK, and the inequality between them is the
dimension formula for schemes, Stacks 0BAE. The chart's own maximum is bounded by the one in
the statement because each generic point of the chart through the chart point maps to a
codimension-zero point of the source specializing to the given one, by Stacks 0BAQ and
Stacks 0A4H.
declarations.statement:
theorem localRingDimension_add_residueFieldTranscendenceDegree_le (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hNoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (x : points B S hS X) :
    (localRingDimension B S hS x : WithBot ℕ∞) +
        (residueFieldTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f x : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤
      (localRingDimension B S hS (pointsMap B S hS X f x) : WithBot ℕ∞) +
        (genericResidueFieldTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f x : WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: dimension inequality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_le_add_iSup_residueFieldTranscendenceDegree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BAY.** For a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` locally of finite type with
locally Noetherian target, the dimension of the source is at most the dimension of the target
plus the supremum of the residue-field transcendence degrees at the codimension-zero points of
the source.

Both dimensions are suprema of local-ring dimensions by Stacks 0BAN, and at each point the
pointwise inequality is Stacks 0BAX, whose correction term is attained at a codimension-zero
point and so is bounded by the supremum over all of them.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimension_le_add_iSup_residueFieldTranscendenceDegree (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hNoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    dimension B S hS X hX ≤ dimension B S hS Y hY +
      ((⨆ ξ : {ξ : points B S hS X // localRingDimension B S hS ξ = 0},
        residueFieldTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f ξ.1 : ℕ∞) : WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRelativeNormalization.isFinite_of_isNagata_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a quasi-separated morphism of finite type of algebraic spaces over `S` with
`X` Nagata and `Y` reduced. Then the normalization `ν : X' ⟶ X` of `X` in `Y`, any factorization
`Y ⟶ X' ⟶ X` of `f` satisfying `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRelativeNormalization`, is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsRelativeNormalization.isFinite_of_isNagata_of_isReduced
    (hnorm : IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f ν f')
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X')
    (hXnagata : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X fun Z : Scheme.{u} => IsNagataScheme Z)
    (hYred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y fun Z : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Z)
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f) (_hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsFinite B S hS ν
declarations.comment: for f : Y ⟶ X quasi-separated of finite type, X Nagata and Y reduced, every normalization of X in Y in the sense of Stacks 0823 is finite over X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinite_normalizationInQcqsHom_of_isNagata
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BB0.** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` such that `X`
is Nagata, `f` is quasi-separated of finite type, and `Y` is reduced. Then the normalization
`ν : X' ⟶ X` of `X` in `Y` (Stacks 0822) is finite.

Being Nagata and being reduced are the étale-local properties of schemes of Tag 03E6; the
quasi-compactness that the normalization of Stacks 0822 requires of `f` is the second half of
`f` being of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_normalizationInQcqsHom_of_isNagata {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hXnagata : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1 fun Z : Scheme.{u} => IsNagataScheme Z)
    (hYred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y.1 fun Z : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Z)
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f.hom) (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom) :
    IsFinite B S hS (normalizationInQcqsHom B S hS f hft.2 hfqs).hom
declarations.comment: for f : Y ⟶ X quasi-separated of finite type, X Nagata and Y reduced, the normalization of X in Y (Stacks 0822) is finite over X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_surjective_etale_chart_iff_hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents
declarations.doc:
An algebraic space has a surjective étale scheme chart with finitely many irreducible
components over each of its quasi-compact opens if and only if every étale scheme chart has that
property.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_surjective_etale_chart_iff_hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    (∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (f : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F),
        IsSurjective B S hS f ∧ IsEtale B S hS f ∧
          ∀ V : ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U).Opens,
            IsCompact (V : Set ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)) →
              (irreducibleComponents V).Finite) ↔
      HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS F
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_iff_finite_codimensionZeroPoints
declarations.doc:
Every étale scheme chart of `F` has finitely many irreducible components over each of its
quasi-compact opens exactly when every quasi-compact algebraic space étale over `F` has finitely
many points of codimension zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_iff_finite_codimensionZeroPoints
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} :
    HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS F ↔
      ∀ (G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u), IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G →
        IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS G → ∀ g : G ⟶ F, IsEtale B S hS g →
          {x : points B S hS G | localRingDimension B S hS x = 0}.Finite
declarations.comment: conditions (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_iff_finite_irreducibleComponents
declarations.doc:
Every étale scheme chart of `F` has finitely many irreducible components over each of its
quasi-compact opens exactly when the space of points of every quasi-compact algebraic space étale
over `F` has finitely many irreducible components.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_iff_finite_irreducibleComponents
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} :
    HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS F ↔
      ∀ (G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u), IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G →
        IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS G → ∀ g : G ⟶ F, IsEtale B S hS g →
          (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS G)).Finite
declarations.comment: conditions (2) and (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_iff_of_isRepresentable
declarations.doc:
For an algebraic space represented by a scheme of the site,
`HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents` is finiteness of the irreducible components of the
quasi-compact opens of that scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_iff_of_isRepresentable
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} [F.IsRepresentable]
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS F ↔
      ∀ V : ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj F.reprX).Opens,
        IsCompact (V : Set ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj F.reprX)) →
          (irreducibleComponents V).Finite
declarations.comment: representable case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.normalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BB2, the normalization of an algebraic space.** Let `F` be an algebraic space over
`S` satisfying the equivalent conditions of Tag 0BB1. The *normalization* of `F` is the morphism

`ν_F : F^ν ⟶ F`

constructed in Tag 07U4. Concretely it is the morphism of the normalization datum
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.normalizationData`, which is the construction of Tag 07U4,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormSpaceGluing.normalizationDataOfPresentation`, run on a chosen
surjective étale scheme chart `w : h_U ⟶ F` and its kernel pair `R = U ×_F U`: the
normalizations of the charts `R^ν ⇉ U^ν` form an étale equivalence relation,
`F^ν = U^ν / R^ν` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.normalizationPresheaf`) is its quotient, an
algebraic space by Tag 02WW, and `ν_F` is the morphism `F^ν ⟶ F` through which the
normalization `U^ν ⟶ U ⟶ F` of the chart descends. No normalization datum or other structure is
an input: the definition depends on `F` and on the two hypotheses of the tag only.

**Defining properties.** `ν_F` is characterised, up to unique isomorphism over `F`, by its
*chart condition*: along every surjective étale scheme chart `U ⟶ F` its base change is the
normalization `U^ν ⟶ U` of the chart (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.normalization_chart`). Any
morphism with this property — any `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData` for `F` — is
identified with `ν_F` by a unique isomorphism over `F`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_iso_normalization`), so the choice of the chart made by
the construction affects nothing up to unique isomorphism, as in the source. `ν_F` is moreover
the universal morphism to `F` from a normal algebraic space which carries points of codimension
zero to points of codimension zero (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_lift_normalization`).

**The theorems of Tag 07U4 about it.** Part (1): `F^ν` is an algebraic space
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_normalizationPresheaf`), normal
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isNormal_normalizationPresheaf`), and `ν_F` is integral
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIntegralHom_normalization`); at the hypotheses of the tag this is
also `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_normalizationData_isNormal_isIntegralHom`. Parts (2) to (4)
— the comparison with the normalization of a scheme, the unique lift `f^ν` of a morphism
preserving codimension-zero points, and `X^ν ≅ X ×_Y Y^ν` along a smooth morphism — are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.exists_iso_yoneda_normalizationScheme`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.existsUnique_normalizationLift` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.isIso_pullbackLift_of_isSmooth`, which hold for every
normalization datum and so in particular for `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.normalizationData`, whose
morphism this is. Surjectivity and the bijection on codimension-zero points (Tag 0BB4) are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_normalization` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijOn_codimensionZeroPoints_normalization`.

The hypothesis carried is condition (2) of Tag 0BB1,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents`, which the comparisons of that
tag —
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_surjective_etale_chart_iff_hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_iff_finite_codimensionZeroPoints`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_iff_finite_irreducibleComponents`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_iff_of_isRepresentable` —
identify with each of the other conditions, so it is the hypothesis Tag 0BB2 itself carries.
Nothing further is assumed: `F` is not assumed representable and no bound on sizes is
imposed.
declarations.statement:
def normalization (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS F) :
    normalizationPresheaf B S hS hF hfin ⟶ F
declarations.comment: the normalization ν_F : F^ν ⟶ F of an algebraic space satisfying the conditions of Tag 0BB1, defined as the construction of Tag 07U4 (the quotient of the normalized étale presentation); unique up to unique isomorphism over F by existsUnique_iso_normalization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.existsUnique_lift_hom_reduction
declarations.doc:
The normalization morphism of an algebraic space factors uniquely through any closed subspace
whose points are all the points of the space, in particular through the reduction.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_lift_hom_reduction (D : NormalizationData B S hS F)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (R : Subfunctor F) (hR : IsClosedSubspace B S hS R)
    (hfull : Set.range (pointsMap B S hS R.toFunctor R.ι) = Set.univ) :
    ∃! g : D.space ⟶ R.toFunctor, g ≫ R.ι = D.hom
declarations.comment: the factorization through the reduction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.existsUnique_iso_of_hom_reduction
declarations.doc:
The factorization of the normalization morphism through the reduction exhibits the
normalization of an algebraic space as the normalization of its reduction: it is carried to any
normalization morphism of the reduction by a unique isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_of_hom_reduction (D : NormalizationData B S hS F)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (R : Subfunctor F) (hR : IsClosedSubspace B S hS R)
    (hfull : Set.range (pointsMap B S hS R.toFunctor R.ι) = Set.univ)
    (D' : NormalizationData B S hS R.toFunctor) (g : D.space ⟶ R.toFunctor)
    (hg : g ≫ R.ι = D.hom) :
    ∃! e : D.space ≅ D'.space, e.hom ≫ D'.hom = g
declarations.comment: the normalization of the reduction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.onReduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BB3, the normalization of the reduction.** The normalization of an algebraic
space *is* the normalization of its reduction: the factorization of the normalization morphism
through any closed subspace whose points are all the points of the space — in particular
through the reduced one — is itself normalization data for that subspace, on the same
algebraic space.

The morphism is the unique factorization of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.existsUnique_lift_hom_reduction`, and the chart
condition is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.chart_of_hom_reduction`. Nothing is
assumed about the subspace beyond being closed and carrying every point: no normalization of
it is given, it is constructed.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def onReduction (D : NormalizationData B S hS F)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (R : Subfunctor F) (hR : IsClosedSubspace B S hS R)
    (hfull : Set.range (pointsMap B S hS R.toFunctor R.ι) = Set.univ) :
    NormalizationData B S hS R.toFunctor
declarations.comment: the normalization of the reduction: the factorization is normalization data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_comp_ι_reduction_eq_normalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BB3, the factorization.** Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` satisfying the
equivalent conditions of Tag 0BB1. The normalization morphism `ν_X : X^ν ⟶ X` of Tag 0BB2
factors through the reduction `X_red ⟶ X` of Tag 047X, and the factorization is unique.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.existsUnique_lift_hom_reduction` at the
normalization datum Tag 0BB2 constructs and at the reduction.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_comp_ι_reduction_eq_normalization
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS X) :
    ∃! g : normalizationPresheaf B S hS hX hfin ⟶ (reduction B S hS X hX).toFunctor,
      g ≫ (reduction B S hS X hX).ι = normalization B S hS hX hfin
declarations.comment: the normalization morphism ν_X of Tag 0BB2 factors uniquely through the reduction X_red ⟶ X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_iso_normalization_reduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BB3, the factorization is the normalization of the reduction.** Let `X` be an
algebraic space over `S` satisfying the equivalent conditions of Tag 0BB1, so that its reduction
`X_red` satisfies them too
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_reduction`). Then the
factorization `X^ν ⟶ X_red` of the normalization morphism through the reduction is the
normalization `ν_{X_red} : X_red^ν ⟶ X_red` of Tag 0BB2: there is a unique isomorphism
`X^ν ≅ X_red^ν` over `X_red`.

Nothing is assumed about the normalization of `X_red`: it is the one Tag 0BB2 constructs. The
statement is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.existsUnique_iso_of_hom_reduction` at the
two normalization data Tag 0BB2 constructs, for `X` and for `X_red`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_normalization_reduction {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS X) :
    ∃! e : normalizationPresheaf B S hS hX hfin ≅
        normalizationPresheaf B S hS (isAlgebraicSpace_reduction B S hS hX)
          (hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_reduction B S hS hX hfin),
      e.hom ≫ normalization B S hS (isAlgebraicSpace_reduction B S hS hX)
          (hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_reduction B S hS hX hfin) =
        normalizationToReduction B S hS hX hfin
declarations.comment: the factorization X^ν ⟶ X_red is the normalization ν_{X_red} of Tag 0BB2: they are isomorphic over X_red by a unique isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.hasEtaleLocalProperty_isNormal
declarations.doc: The normalization of an algebraic space is normal.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEtaleLocalProperty_isNormal (D : NormalizationData B S hS F)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS D.space (fun X : Scheme.{u} => IsNormal X)
declarations.comment: part (1): the normalization is normal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.isSurjective_hom
declarations.doc: The normalization morphism of an algebraic space is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_hom (D : NormalizationData B S hS F)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) : IsSurjective B S hS D.hom
declarations.comment: part (2): the normalization morphism is surjective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.isIntegralHom_hom
declarations.doc:
The normalization morphism of an algebraic space is an integral morphism of algebraic
spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegralHom_hom (D : NormalizationData B S hS F)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) : IsIntegralHom B S hS D.hom
declarations.comment: part (2): the normalization morphism is integral

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.bijOn_codimensionZeroPoints_hom
declarations.doc:
The normalization morphism induces a bijection between the codimension-zero points of the
normalization and those of the algebraic space.
declarations.comment: part (3): bijection on codimension-zero points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.existsUnique_lift_hom
declarations.doc:
A morphism to `F` from a normal algebraic space which carries points of codimension zero to
points of codimension zero factors uniquely through the normalization of `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_lift_hom (D : NormalizationData B S hS F)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) {Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z)
    (hZnormal : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Z fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsNormal Y) (f : Z ⟶ F)
    (hgeneric : ∀ z : points B S hS Z, localRingDimension B S hS z = 0 →
      localRingDimension B S hS (pointsMap B S hS Z f z) = 0) :
    ∃! g : Z ⟶ D.space, g ≫ D.hom = f
declarations.comment: part (4): the universal property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.isFinite_hom
declarations.doc:
The normalization morphism of a Nagata algebraic space over `S` is a finite morphism of
algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_hom
    (D : NormalizationData B S hS F) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hNagata : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun X : Scheme.{u} => IsNagataScheme X)) :
    IsFinite B S hS D.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_of_isLocallyNoetherian_of_isDecentSpace
declarations.doc: A locally Noetherian decent algebraic space is quasi-separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_of_isLocallyNoetherian_of_isDecentSpace
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hNoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian Y))
    (hdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) :
    IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReasonableSpace_of_finite_irreducibleComponents_of_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BB8.** An algebraic space over a scheme `S` is reasonable as soon as every
quasi-compact scheme étale over it has finitely many irreducible components and every one of
its points of codimension zero is represented by a monomorphism from the spectrum of a
field.
declarations.statement:
