theorem isReasonableSpace_of_finite_irreducibleComponents_of_mono
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hfinite : ∀ U : BigFppfOver B S hS,
      CompactSpace ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) →
      ∀ f : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X,
        (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
          (@_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f →
        (irreducibleComponents ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)).Finite)
    (hgeneric : ∀ x : points B S hS X, localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 →
      ∃ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS X,
        p.class B S hS X = x ∧ Mono (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value)) :
    IsReasonableSpace B S hS X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsDecentWithFinitelyManyComponents.hasMonomorphicCodimensionZeroPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BB9, condition (1) implies the third clause of condition (2).** A decent
algebraic space has a monomorphic field-valued representative at every point, in particular at
every point of codimension `0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsDecentWithFinitelyManyComponents.hasMonomorphicCodimensionZeroPoints
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (h : IsDecentWithFinitelyManyComponents B S hS X) :
    HasMonomorphicCodimensionZeroPoints B S hS X
declarations.comment: condition (1) implies the third clause of condition (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasQuasiCompactGenericDenseOpenScheme.hasFiniteEtaleIrreducibleComponents
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BB9, condition (3) implies the first clause of condition (2).** If an algebraic
space over `S` has a dense open subspace which is a scheme with finitely many irreducible
components whose generic points are represented by quasi-compact morphisms, then every
quasi-compact scheme étale over it has finitely many irreducible components.

Let `a : U ⟶ X` be étale with `U` compact, and let `V ⊂ U` be the preimage of the point set of
the open subspace: it is open, and dense because an étale morphism is open on points. A
generic point of an irreducible component of `U` lying in `V` has codimension `0` on `X` by
condition (2) of Stacks 0BAQ, so its image is the image of a generic point of the open
subspace; there are finitely many of those, and the fibre of `|U| → |X|` above each is finite
because the morphism representing it is quasi-compact. So `V` meets only finitely many generic
points, which bounds the irreducible components of `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem HasQuasiCompactGenericDenseOpenScheme.hasFiniteEtaleIrreducibleComponents
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (h : HasQuasiCompactGenericDenseOpenScheme B S hS X) :
    HasFiniteEtaleIrreducibleComponents B S hS X
declarations.comment: condition (3) implies the first clause of condition (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasQuasiCompactGenericDenseOpenScheme.hasFiniteCodimensionZeroPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BB9, condition (3) implies the second clause of condition (2).** Only finitely
many points have codimension `0`: each of them lies over the dense open subspace, and is the
image of a generic point of one of its finitely many irreducible components.
declarations.statement:
theorem HasQuasiCompactGenericDenseOpenScheme.hasFiniteCodimensionZeroPoints
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (h : HasQuasiCompactGenericDenseOpenScheme B S hS X) :
    HasFiniteCodimensionZeroPoints B S hS X
declarations.comment: condition (3) implies the second clause of condition (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasQuasiCompactGenericDenseOpenScheme.hasMonomorphicCodimensionZeroPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BB9, condition (3) implies the third clause of condition (2).** A point of
codimension `0` lies over the dense open subspace, which is a scheme, so the residue field at
the corresponding point of that scheme presents it by a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem HasQuasiCompactGenericDenseOpenScheme.hasMonomorphicCodimensionZeroPoints
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (h : HasQuasiCompactGenericDenseOpenScheme B S hS X) :
    HasMonomorphicCodimensionZeroPoints B S hS X
declarations.comment: condition (3) implies the third clause of condition (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasQuasiCompactGenericDenseOpenScheme.hasFiniteEtaleComponentsAndCodimensionZeroPoints
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0BB9, condition (3) implies condition (2).** The three clauses together.
declarations.statement:
theorem HasQuasiCompactGenericDenseOpenScheme.hasFiniteEtaleComponentsAndCodimensionZeroPoints
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (h : HasQuasiCompactGenericDenseOpenScheme B S hS X) :
    HasFiniteEtaleComponentsAndCodimensionZeroPoints B S hS X
declarations.comment: condition (3) implies condition (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsDecentWithFinitelyManyComponents.hasQuasiCompactGenericDenseOpenScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BB9, condition (1) implies condition (3).** A decent algebraic space over `S`
whose space of points has finitely many irreducible components has a dense open subspace which
is a scheme, with finitely many irreducible components, each of whose generic points is
represented by a quasi-compact morphism from the spectrum of a field.

The dense open subscheme is Stacks 086U, in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_denseRange_isRepresentable_isOpenSubspace_of_isDecentSpace`.
Its components are finite in number because the inclusion is an open embedding on points and
an open embedding pulls components back onto components
(`AlgebraicGeometry.finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isOpenEmbedding`), which is the
source's "taking closures sends irreducible components of `|X'|` to irreducible components of
`|X|`". The quasi-compactness of the generic-point morphisms is decency itself, with the
monomorphism condition of Stacks 03JV (4) dropped to Stacks 03JV (5).
declarations.statement:
theorem IsDecentWithFinitelyManyComponents.hasQuasiCompactGenericDenseOpenScheme
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (h : IsDecentWithFinitelyManyComponents B S hS X) :
    HasQuasiCompactGenericDenseOpenScheme B S hS X
declarations.comment: condition (1) implies condition (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasFiniteEtaleComponentsAndCodimensionZeroPoints.isReasonableSpace
declarations.doc:
**Condition (2) of Stacks 0BB9 makes the algebraic space reasonable.** This is Stacks 0BB8,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReasonableSpace_of_finite_irreducibleComponents_of_mono`, whose two
hypotheses are the first and third clauses of condition (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem HasFiniteEtaleComponentsAndCodimensionZeroPoints.isReasonableSpace
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (h : HasFiniteEtaleComponentsAndCodimensionZeroPoints B S hS X) :
    IsReasonableSpace B S hS X
declarations.comment: condition (2) implies the conclusion that the space is reasonable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasFiniteEtaleComponentsAndCodimensionZeroPoints.isDecentWithFinitelyManyComponents
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BB9, condition (2) implies condition (1).** Decency comes from Stacks 0BB8: the
first and third clauses of condition (2) make the space reasonable, and a reasonable algebraic
space is decent. Finiteness of the irreducible components of `|X|` comes from the second
clause together with Stacks 0BAR: the points of codimension `0` are dense, there are finitely
many of them, and so the finitely many irreducible closed sets they generate cover a dense
subset of `|X|`, which bounds the components.
declarations.statement:
theorem HasFiniteEtaleComponentsAndCodimensionZeroPoints.isDecentWithFinitelyManyComponents
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (h : HasFiniteEtaleComponentsAndCodimensionZeroPoints B S hS X) :
    IsDecentWithFinitelyManyComponents B S hS X
declarations.comment: condition (2) implies condition (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDecentWithFinitelyManyComponents_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BB9.** For an algebraic space `X` over a scheme `S` the three conditions are
equivalent: `X` is decent with finitely many irreducible components; every quasi-compact scheme
étale over `X` has finitely many irreducible components, there are finitely many points of
codimension `0` and each is represented by a monomorphism from the spectrum of a field; and
there is a dense open subspace which is a scheme with finitely many irreducible components
whose generic points are represented by quasi-compact morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDecentWithFinitelyManyComponents_tfae
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    [IsDecentWithFinitelyManyComponents B S hS X,
      HasFiniteEtaleComponentsAndCodimensionZeroPoints B S hS X,
      HasQuasiCompactGenericDenseOpenScheme B S hS X].TFAE

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsDecentWithFinitelyManyComponents.isReasonableSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BB9, the concluding assertion that the space is reasonable.** An algebraic space
over `S` which is decent and has finitely many irreducible components is reasonable.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsDecentWithFinitelyManyComponents.isReasonableSpace
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (h : IsDecentWithFinitelyManyComponents B S hS X) :
    IsReasonableSpace B S hS X
declarations.comment: the conclusion that the space is reasonable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.image_genericPoints_eq_genericPoints_of_denseRange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BB9, the concluding assertion about generic points.** If the space of points of
an algebraic space over `S` has finitely many irreducible components and `X' ⊂ X` is an open
subspace whose point set is dense, then the generic points of the irreducible components of
`|X'|` map exactly onto the generic points of the irreducible components of `|X|`.

The inclusion is an open embedding on points, and an open embedding matches up the generic
points of its source with those of its target lying in its range; the range is all of them
because a dense open subset of a space with finitely many irreducible components contains every
generic point.
declarations.statement:
theorem image_genericPoints_eq_genericPoints_of_denseRange
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {G : Subfunctor X} (hG : IsOpenSubspace B S hS G)
    (hdense : DenseRange (pointsMap B S hS G.toFunctor G.ι))
    (hfin : (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS X)).Finite) :
    pointsMap B S hS G.toFunctor G.ι '' genericPoints (points B S hS G.toFunctor) =
      genericPoints (points B S hS X)
declarations.comment: the conclusion identifying the generic points of the dense open subscheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasiFiniteAt_over_codimensionZeroPoint_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBB.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` locally of
finite type and let `y` be a point of `Y` whose local ring has dimension zero. The following
are equivalent: every point of `X` above `y` has local ring of dimension zero; `f` is
quasi-finite at every point above `y`; and `f` is quasi-finite at every point above `y` whose
local ring has dimension zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiFiniteAt_over_codimensionZeroPoint_tfae
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (y : points B S hS Y) (hy : localRingDimension B S hS y = 0) :
    List.TFAE [
      ∀ x : points B S hS X, pointsMap B S hS X f x = y →
        localRingDimension B S hS x = 0,
      ∀ x : points B S hS X, pointsMap B S hS X f x = y → IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x,
      ∀ x : points B S hS X, localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 →
        pointsMap B S hS X f x = y → IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isDenseOpenSubspace_isFinite_pullback_snd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBC.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
locally of finite type, and write `X⁰` and `Y⁰` for the sets of points of `|X|` and `|Y|`
whose local rings have dimension zero. Assume that `Y` is decent, that `X⁰` and `Y⁰` are
finite with `f^{-1}(Y⁰) = X⁰`, and that `f` is either quasi-compact or separated. Then there
is an open subspace `V ⊂ Y` whose set of points is dense in `|Y|` and over which `f` becomes
finite.

The hypothesis `f^{-1}(Y⁰) = X⁰` makes the fibre of `f` over a point of codimension zero of
`Y` finite, so over a suitable neighbourhood of such a point `f` is finite: if `f` is
quasi-compact this is condition (3) of Stacks 0ACZ, and if `f` is separated it is condition
(3) of Stacks 0AD0 together with the vanishing of the complementary open, which carries no
point of codimension zero and is therefore empty by Stacks 0BAR. Since `Y⁰` is finite, finitely
many such neighbourhoods are glued, and the result is dense because it contains `Y⁰`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isDenseOpenSubspace_isFinite_pullback_snd
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hlft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hYdecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    (hXzero : Set.Finite {x : points B S hS X |
      localRingDimension B S hS x = 0})
    (hYzero : Set.Finite {y : points B S hS Y |
      localRingDimension B S hS y = 0})
    (hpreimage :
      (pointsMap B S hS X f) ⁻¹'
        {y : points B S hS Y |
          localRingDimension B S hS y = 0} =
        {x : points B S hS X |
          localRingDimension B S hS x = 0})
    (hqc_or_sep : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f ∨
      IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    letI : TopologicalSpace (points B S hS Y) :=
      pointTopology B S hS Y
    ∃ V : Subfunctor Y,
      IsOpenSubspace B S hS V ∧
        Dense (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor V.ι)) ∧
          IsFinite B S hS (pullback.snd f V.ι)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_pullback_snd_fromGenericStalk_of_isBirational
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBD.** A birational morphism of decent algebraic spaces with finitely many
irreducible components becomes an isomorphism after base change to the spectrum of the local
ring of the target at a generic point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_pullback_snd_fromGenericStalk_of_isBirational
    (hdecentY : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hdecentX : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    (hfiniteX : (letI := pointTopology B S hS X
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS X)).Finite))
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsBirational B S hS hX hY hdecentX hdecentY hfiniteX hfiniteY f) :
    IsIso (pullback.snd f (fromGenericStalk B S hS hY
      (hasDenseRepresentableOpenSubspace_of_isDecentSpace B S hS hY hdecentY)
      hfiniteY y hy))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_dense_isOpenSubspace_isIso_of_isBirational
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBE.** A birational morphism of decent algebraic spaces over `S` with finitely
many irreducible components restricts to an isomorphism between dense open subspaces, provided
it is locally of finite type with reduced target or locally of finite presentation.

The source reduces the statement to schemes and quotes Stacks 0BAC there; the reduction is
carried out on representable open charts with dense point sets, see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dense_isOpenSubspace_isIso_of_isBirational
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hdecentX : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (hdecentY : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    (hfiniteX : (letI := pointTopology B S hS X
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS X)).Finite))
    (hfiniteY : (letI := pointTopology B S hS Y
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS Y)).Finite))
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hbir : IsBirational B S hS hX hY hdecentX hdecentY hfiniteX hfiniteY f)
    (hfin : (IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f ∧
        HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y
          (fun Z : Scheme.{u} => _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsReduced Z)) ∨
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    ∃ (U : Subfunctor X) (V : Subfunctor Y) (ψ : U.toFunctor ⟶ V.toFunctor),
      IsOpenSubspace B S hS U ∧ IsOpenSubspace B S hS V ∧
        DenseRange (pointsMap B S hS U.toFunctor U.ι) ∧
        DenseRange (pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor V.ι) ∧
        ψ ≫ V.ι = U.ι ≫ f ∧ IsIso ψ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isDenseOpenSubspace_isIso_pullback_snd_of_isBirational
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBF.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a birational morphism of algebraic spaces over a
scheme `S` which are decent and have finitely many irreducible components. Assume that `f` is
quasi-compact or separated, and that `f` is locally of finite type with `Y` reduced or locally
of finite presentation. Then there is a dense open subspace `V ⊂ Y` such that `f^{-1}(V) ⟶ V`
is an isomorphism.

The source shrinks `Y` to a dense open over which `f` is finite, by Stacks 0BBC, and
separately to a dense open over which `f` restricts to an isomorphism of dense opens, by
Stacks 0BBE; the intersection of the two is the open subspace produced here. See the module
docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isDenseOpenSubspace_isIso_pullback_snd_of_isBirational
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hdecentX : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (hdecentY : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    (hfiniteX : (letI := pointTopology B S hS X
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS X)).Finite))
    (hfiniteY : (letI := pointTopology B S hS Y
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS Y)).Finite))
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hbir : IsBirational B S hS hX hY hdecentX hdecentY hfiniteX hfiniteY f)
    (hqc_or_sep : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f ∨ IsSeparated B S hS f)
    (hfin : (IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f ∧
        HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y
          (fun Z : Scheme.{u} => _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsReduced Z)) ∨
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    ∃ V : Subfunctor Y,
      IsOpenSubspace B S hS V ∧
        Dense (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor V.ι)) ∧
          IsIso (pullback.snd f V.ι)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_lift_normalization_of_isBirational
declarations.doc:
**The commutative square of Stacks 0BBG, for given normalizations.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
birational morphism of decent algebraic spaces over `S` with finitely many irreducible
components, and let `X^ν ⟶ X` and `Y^ν ⟶ Y` be normalizations. Then `X^ν ⟶ X ⟶ Y` factors
through `Y^ν ⟶ Y` by a unique morphism `X^ν ⟶ Y^ν`, so that the square it closes commutes.

The factorization is the universal property of the normalization of `Y`, part (4) of
Stacks 0BB4. Its two hypotheses on the composite `X^ν ⟶ X ⟶ Y` are normality of `X^ν`, part (1)
of Stacks 0BB4, and preservation of codimension-zero points, which holds for `X^ν ⟶ X` by
part (3) of Stacks 0BB4 and for `f` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.localRingDimension_eq_zero_of_isBirational`.

The normalizations are hypotheses here, whereas the source asserts their existence; that
existence is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_normalizationData_of_isDecentSpace`, and the
whole lemma, which quantifies over no normalization data at all, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_normalizationData_isBirational_lift_of_isBirational`. The
statement here is the stronger one for the
square — it holds for *every* choice of the two normalizations, not just the ones the
existence theorem produces — and it is what the rest of the development consumes.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_lift_normalization_of_isBirational (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hfiniteX : (letI := pointTopology B S hS X
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS X)).Finite))
    (hfiniteY : (letI := pointTopology B S hS Y
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS Y)).Finite))
    (hXdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (hYdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    (DX : NormalizationData B S hS X) (DY : NormalizationData B S hS Y) {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hf : IsBirational B S hS hX hY hXdec hYdec hfiniteX hfiniteY f) :
    ∃! g : DX.space ⟶ DY.space, g ≫ DY.hom = DX.hom ≫ f
declarations.comment: the commutative square, as a unique factorization through the target normalization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBirational_lift_normalization_of_isBirational
declarations.doc:
**Birationality of the induced morphism, for given normalizations.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
birational morphism of decent algebraic spaces over `S` with finitely many irreducible
components, and
let `X^ν ⟶ X` and `Y^ν ⟶ Y` be normalizations. Then any morphism `X^ν ⟶ Y^ν` closing the
square over `f` is birational.

The two normalizations are again decent with finitely many irreducible components, and their
normalization morphisms biject generic points, so the induced morphism does too. At a generic
point `z` of `X^ν` the local-ring map is computed on charts: the chart map of `X^ν ⟶ X` is
surjective on local rings at `z` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.surjective_stalkMap_of_genericChart`, and the
chart map of `f` is an isomorphism there by birationality, so the chart map of `X^ν ⟶ Y^ν`
followed by that of `Y^ν ⟶ Y` is surjective, whence the chart map of `X^ν ⟶ Y^ν` is
surjective. It is injective because its source — the local ring of the normal space `Y^ν` at
a point of codimension zero — is a field.

The normalizations are hypotheses here, as at
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_lift_normalization_of_isBirational`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBirational_lift_normalization_of_isBirational (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hXdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    (hYdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    (hfiniteX : (letI := pointTopology B S hS X
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS X)).Finite))
    (hfiniteY : (letI := pointTopology B S hS Y
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS Y)).Finite))
    (DX : NormalizationData B S hS X) (DY : NormalizationData B S hS Y) {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hf : IsBirational B S hS hX hY hXdec hYdec hfiniteX hfiniteY f)
    (g : DX.space ⟶ DY.space) (hg : g ≫ DY.hom = DX.hom ≫ f) :
    IsBirational B S hS DX.isAlgebraicSpace DY.isAlgebraicSpace
      (DX.isDecentSpace hX hXdec) (DY.isDecentSpace hY hYdec)
      (DX.finite_irreducibleComponents hX hXdec hfiniteX)
      (DY.finite_irreducibleComponents hY hYdec hfiniteY) g
declarations.comment: birationality of the induced morphism of normalizations

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isBirational_lift_normalization_of_isBirational
declarations.doc:
**The square and the birationality together, for given normalizations.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y`
be a birational morphism of decent algebraic spaces over `S` with finitely many irreducible
components, and let `X^ν ⟶ X` and `Y^ν ⟶ Y` be normalizations. Then `X^ν ⟶ X ⟶ Y` factors
through `Y^ν ⟶ Y`, and the factoring morphism `X^ν ⟶ Y^ν` is birational.

The factorization is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_lift_normalization_of_isBirational` and its
birationality is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBirational_lift_normalization_of_isBirational`.

The normalizations are hypotheses here; the whole lemma, with their existence, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_normalizationData_isBirational_lift_of_isBirational`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isBirational_lift_normalization_of_isBirational
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hXdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (hYdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    (hfiniteX : (letI := pointTopology B S hS X
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS X)).Finite))
    (hfiniteY : (letI := pointTopology B S hS Y
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS Y)).Finite))
    (DX : NormalizationData B S hS X) (DY : NormalizationData B S hS Y) {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hf : IsBirational B S hS hX hY hXdec hYdec hfiniteX hfiniteY f) :
    ∃ g : DX.space ⟶ DY.space, g ≫ DY.hom = DX.hom ≫ f ∧
      IsBirational B S hS DX.isAlgebraicSpace DY.isAlgebraicSpace
        (DX.isDecentSpace hX hXdec) (DY.isDecentSpace hY hYdec)
        (DX.finite_irreducibleComponents hX hXdec hfiniteX)
        (DY.finite_irreducibleComponents hY hYdec hfiniteY) g
declarations.comment: the commutative square together with the birationality of the induced morphism of normalizations

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_normalizationData_of_isDecentSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBG, the existence of the normalizations.** A decent algebraic space over `S`
whose space of points has finitely many irreducible components has normalization data: an
algebraic space `F^ν` over `S` with a morphism `F^ν ⟶ F` whose base change along every
surjective étale scheme chart of `F` is the normalization of that chart.

This is the first clause of Stacks 0BBG, and the source proves it the same way: the hypotheses
give the equivalent conditions of Stacks 0BB1 by Stacks 0BB9
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_of_isDecentSpace`), and under
those conditions the normalization exists by the existence half of Stacks 07U4,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_normalizationData`. Applied to the source and the target of
a birational morphism it is the assertion that `X^ν ⟶ X` and `Y^ν ⟶ Y` exist.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_normalizationData_of_isDecentSpace
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hFdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS F)
    (hfinite : (letI := pointTopology B S hS F
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS F)).Finite)) :
    Nonempty (NormalizationData B S hS F)
declarations.comment: the existence of the normalizations

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_normalizationData_isBirational_lift_of_isBirational
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBG.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a birational morphism between algebraic spaces over
`S` which are decent and have finitely many irreducible components. Then the normalizations
`X^ν ⟶ X` and `Y^ν ⟶ Y` exist and there is a commutative diagram with rows `X^ν ⟶ Y^ν` and
`X ⟶ Y` and columns the two normalization morphisms, and the morphism `X^ν ⟶ Y^ν` is
birational.

Nothing is assumed about the normalizations: they are produced by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_normalizationData_of_isDecentSpace` from decency and the
finiteness of the irreducible components, which is the source's own route through Stacks 0BB9
and Stacks 0BB1. The square is then
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_lift_normalization_of_isBirational` and the
birationality of the morphism closing it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBirational_lift_normalization_of_isBirational`, both of which hold
for an arbitrary choice of the two normalizations.

The decency of `X^ν` and `Y^ν` and the finiteness of their irreducible components, which the
conclusion's `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBirational` is parameterised by, are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.isDecentSpace` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.finite_irreducibleComponents`; the source records
them in its second paragraph, citing Stacks 0ABT.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_normalizationData_isBirational_lift_of_isBirational
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hXdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (hYdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    (hfiniteX : (letI := pointTopology B S hS X
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS X)).Finite))
    (hfiniteY : (letI := pointTopology B S hS Y
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS Y)).Finite))
    {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hf : IsBirational B S hS hX hY hXdec hYdec hfiniteX hfiniteY f) :
    ∃ (DX : NormalizationData B S hS X) (DY : NormalizationData B S hS Y)
      (g : DX.space ⟶ DY.space), g ≫ DY.hom = DX.hom ≫ f ∧
        IsBirational B S hS DX.isAlgebraicSpace DY.isAlgebraicSpace
          (DX.isDecentSpace hX hXdec) (DY.isDecentSpace hY hYdec)
          (DX.finite_irreducibleComponents hX hXdec hfiniteX)
          (DY.finite_irreducibleComponents hY hYdec hfiniteY) g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_factorization_normalization_of_isIntegralHom_of_isBirational
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBH.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be an integral birational morphism of decent algebraic
spaces over `S` with finitely many irreducible components, and let `X^ν ⟶ X` and `Y^ν ⟶ Y` be
normalizations. Then the normalization morphism of `Y` factors as `Y^ν ⟶ X ⟶ Y`, and the
first leg `Y^ν ⟶ X` is the normalization of `X`: it is the normalization morphism `X^ν ⟶ X`
precomposed with an isomorphism `Y^ν ≅ X^ν` over `X`.

The induced morphism `X^ν ⟶ Y^ν` of Stacks 0BBG is integral by Stacks 081Z, part (2): its
composite with the normalization morphism of `Y` is the composite of the normalization
morphism of `X` with `f`, both integral, and the normalization morphism of `Y` is integral
hence separated. It is birational by Stacks 0BBG, its source is reduced — being normal — and
its target is normal, both normalizations are decent with finitely many irreducible
components, so Stacks 0B4E makes it an isomorphism. Its inverse is the asserted
factorization.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_factorization_normalization_of_isIntegralHom_of_isBirational
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hXdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (hYdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    (hfiniteX : (letI := pointTopology B S hS X
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS X)).Finite))
    (hfiniteY : (letI := pointTopology B S hS Y
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS Y)).Finite))
    (DX : NormalizationData B S hS X) (DY : NormalizationData B S hS Y) {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hfint : IsIntegralHom B S hS f)
    (hf : IsBirational B S hS hX hY hXdec hYdec hfiniteX hfiniteY f) :
    ∃ (h : DY.space ⟶ X) (e : DY.space ≅ DX.space),
      h ≫ f = DY.hom ∧ h = e.hom ≫ DX.hom

declarations.name: IsLocalization.Away.map_affineBlowupAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBI**, surjectivity. Let `R` be a ring, `I ⊆ R` an ideal and `a f : R`. The canonical
`R`-algebra map from a localization `A` of `R` away from `a` to a localization `B` of `R` away from
`f * a` maps the affine blowup algebra `R[I/a] ⊆ A` onto the affine blowup algebra
`R[fI/(fa)] ⊆ B`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsLocalization.Away.map_affineBlowupAlgebra {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) (a f : R) (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [IsLocalization.Away a A]
    (B : Type*) [CommRing B] [Algebra R B] [Algebra A B] [IsScalarTower R A B]
    [IsLocalization.Away (f * a) B] :
    (affineBlowupAlgebra I a A).map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A B) =
      affineBlowupAlgebra (Ideal.span {f} * I) (f * a) B

declarations.name: IsLocalization.Away.map_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBI**, the kernel. Let `A` be an algebra over a commutative semiring `R`, let `f : R`
and let `B` be a localization of `A` away from the image of `f`. Then `y : A` maps to `0` in `B` if
and only if `y` is `f`-power torsion. Restricted to the affine blowup algebra `R[I/a] ⊆ A` this
describes the kernel of the map `R[I/a] → R[fI/(fa)]` of
`IsLocalization.Away.map_affineBlowupAlgebra`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsLocalization.Away.map_eq_zero_iff {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] {A : Type*}
    [CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A] {B : Type*} [CommSemiring B] [Algebra A B]
    (f : R) [IsLocalization.Away (algebraMap R A f) B] (y : A) :
    algebraMap A B y = 0 ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, f ^ n • y = 0

declarations.name: exists_fg_ideal_strictTransform_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0BBJ.** Let `M` be a finite module over a commutative ring `R`.  If the
localization of `M` away from `f` is finite locally free of rank `r`, then there is a finitely
generated ideal `I` with the same vanishing locus as `f` such that, on every affine blowup chart
`R[I/a]` with `a ∈ I`, the strict transform of `M` is finite locally free of rank `r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fg_ideal_strictTransform_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
    {R : Type u} {M : Type v} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (f : R) (r : ℕ)
    (hf : Module.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (Localization.Away f)
      (LocalizedModule.Away f M) r) :
    ∃ I : Ideal R, I.FG ∧
      PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus ({f} : Set R) = PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set R) ∧
      ∀ a : I,
        let _ : Fact ((a : R) ∈ I) := ⟨a.property⟩
        Module.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (Blowup I a) (strictTransform I a M) r

No small family of fpqc coverings of the spectrum of a nonzero ring is cofinal under

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GermOfScheme.isEtaleLocal_stalk_property
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBL, the germ criterion.** A property of local rings which is invariant under
isomorphisms and unchanged on passing to a prime above it along an étale ring map induces an
étale-local property of germs of schemes, by evaluation on the local ring at the marked
point.
declarations.statement:
theorem GermOfScheme.isEtaleLocal_stalk_property (P : (R : Type u) → [CommRing R] → Prop)
    (hP : ∀ {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
      (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime],
      q.comap (algebraMap A B) = p →
        (P (Localization.AtPrime p) ↔ P (Localization.AtPrime q)))
    (hP_iso : ∀ {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S],
      (R ≃+* S) → (P R ↔ P S)) :
    GermOfScheme.IsEtaleLocal (fun g => P (g.scheme.presheaf.stalk g.point))
declarations.comment: germ_criterion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasLocalRingPropertyAtPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBL, the local ring of an algebraic space.** A property `P` of local rings which
is invariant under étale localization holds for the local ring of an algebraic space `F` at a
point `x` when it holds for the stalk of some étale scheme chart at some point above `x`. By
Stacks 04N2 the chart is immaterial, and the invariance hypothesis `_hP` is what makes that
so; it is carried as an argument of the predicate rather than assumed of `P` globally.
declarations.statement:
abbrev HasLocalRingPropertyAtPoint (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (_hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (x : points B S hS F)
    (P : (R : Type u) → [CommRing R] → Prop)
    (_hP : ∀ {A C : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing C] [Algebra A C] [Algebra.Etale A C]
      (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal C) [q.IsPrime],
      q.comap (algebraMap A C) = p →
        (P (Localization.AtPrime p) ↔ P (Localization.AtPrime q))) : Prop
declarations.comment: local_ring_of_an_algebraic_space_has_p

declarations.name: isNoetherianRing_localizationAtPrime_iff_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBL, Noetherian.** For prime ideals `p` and `q` corresponding under an étale map
`A → B`, the local ring of `A` at `p` is Noetherian if and only if the local ring of `B` at `q`
is Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNoetherianRing_localizationAtPrime_iff_of_etale
    (hq : q.comap (algebraMap A B) = p) :
    IsNoetherianRing (Localization.AtPrime p) ↔ IsNoetherianRing (Localization.AtPrime q)
declarations.comment: Noetherian

declarations.name: ringKrullDim_eq_localizationAtPrime_iff_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBL, dimension `d`.** For prime ideals `p` and `q` corresponding under an étale
map `A → B`, the local ring of `A` at `p` has dimension `d` if and only if the local ring of `B`
at `q` has dimension `d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_eq_localizationAtPrime_iff_of_etale (d : WithBot ℕ∞)
    (hq : q.comap (algebraMap A B) = p) :
    ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime p) = d ↔ ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime q) = d
declarations.comment: dimension d

declarations.name: isRegularLocalRing_localizationAtPrime_iff_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBL, regular.** For prime ideals `p` and `q` corresponding under an étale map
`A → B`, the local ring of `A` at `p` is regular if and only if the local ring of `B` at `q` is
regular.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularLocalRing_localizationAtPrime_iff_of_etale
    (hq : q.comap (algebraMap A B) = p) :
    IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p) ↔
      IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime q)
declarations.comment: regular

declarations.name: isDiscreteValuationRing_localizationAtPrime_iff_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBL, discrete valuation ring.** For prime ideals `p` and `q` corresponding under
an étale map `A → B`, the local ring of `A` at `p` is a discrete valuation ring if and only if
the local ring of `B` at `q` is one. This is regularity together with dimension one, through
item (3) of the characterisation of Tag 00PD.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDiscreteValuationRing_localizationAtPrime_iff_of_etale
    (hq : q.comap (algebraMap A B) = p) :
    (∃ _ : IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime p),
        IsDiscreteValuationRing (Localization.AtPrime p)) ↔
      (∃ _ : IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime q),
        IsDiscreteValuationRing (Localization.AtPrime q))
declarations.comment: discrete valuation ring

declarations.name: isNormalDomain_localizationAtPrime_iff_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBL, normal.** For prime ideals `p` and `q` corresponding under an étale map
`A → B`, the local ring of `A` at `p` is a normal domain if and only if the local ring of `B` at
`q` is one. Neither ring is assumed Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNormalDomain_localizationAtPrime_iff_of_etale
    (hq : q.comap (algebraMap A B) = p) :
    IsNormalDomain (Localization.AtPrime p) ↔ IsNormalDomain (Localization.AtPrime q)
declarations.comment: normal

declarations.name: isNoetherianRing_and_ringDepth_eq_localizationAtPrime_iff_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBL, Noetherian and depth `k`.** For prime ideals `p` and `q` corresponding under
an étale map `A → B`, the local ring of `A` at `p` is Noetherian of depth `k` if and only if the
local ring of `B` at `q` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNoetherianRing_and_ringDepth_eq_localizationAtPrime_iff_of_etale (k : ℕ∞)
    (hq : q.comap (algebraMap A B) = p) :
    (IsNoetherianRing (Localization.AtPrime p) ∧ ringDepth (Localization.AtPrime p) = k) ↔
      (IsNoetherianRing (Localization.AtPrime q) ∧ ringDepth (Localization.AtPrime q) = k)
declarations.comment: Noetherian and depth k

declarations.name: isCohenMacaulayLocalRing_localizationAtPrime_iff_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBL, Noetherian and Cohen-Macaulay.** For prime ideals `p` and `q` corresponding
under an étale map `A → B`, the local ring of `A` at `p` is Noetherian and Cohen-Macaulay if and
only if the local ring of `B` at `q` is.
declarations.comment: Noetherian and Cohen-Macaulay

declarations.name: isGorensteinLocalRing_localizationAtPrime_iff_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBL, Noetherian and Gorenstein.** For prime ideals `p` and `q` corresponding
under an étale map `A → B`, the local ring of `A` at `p` is Noetherian and Gorenstein if and
only if the local ring of `B` at `q` is.
declarations.comment: Noetherian and Gorenstein

declarations.name: isReduced_localizationAtPrime_iff_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBL, reducedness.** For prime ideals `p` and `q` corresponding under an étale
map `A → B`, the local ring of `A` at `p` is reduced if and only if the local ring of `B` at
`q` is reduced.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_localizationAtPrime_iff_of_etale {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B] (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal B)
    [q.IsPrime] (hq : q.comap (algebraMap A B) = p) :
    IsReduced (Localization.AtPrime p) ↔ IsReduced (Localization.AtPrime q)
declarations.comment: reduced

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_schemeStratification_quasiCompactPoint_mem_stratum
declarations.doc:
A quasi-compact algebraic space `X` over `S` carries a descending
chain of open subspaces starting at `X` whose reduced strata, the differences of
consecutive members, each receive an isomorphism from the part lying over them of a
separated scheme surjective and étale over the corresponding member; and every point of
`|X|` represented by a quasi-compact morphism from the spectrum of a field lies in one of
those strata.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_schemeStratification_quasiCompactPoint_mem_stratum
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (X : (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hqc : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X) :
    ∃ strat : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SchemeStratification B S hS X,
      ∀ (x : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.points B S hS X)
        (z : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FieldValuedPoint B S hS X),
        z.class B S hS X = x →
        AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsQuasiCompact B S hS
          (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fieldMorphism B S hS X z) →
        ∃ p : ℕ, x ∈ Set.range (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsMap B S hS
          (strat.stratum p).toFunctor ((strat.stratum p).ι ≫ (strat.openPart p).ι))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affine_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBP.** Every point `x` of a decent algebraic space `X` over `S` has an elementary
étale neighborhood whose scheme is affine, whose distinguished point is the only point above
`x`, and whose residue field at that point is the residue field of `X` at `x` through the
induced homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood'
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hDecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (x : points B S hS X) :
    ∃ E : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX x,
      IsAffine E.scheme.left.1 ∧
      (∀ y : points B S hS (yoneda.obj E.scheme),
        pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj E.scheme) E.toSpace y = x →
          y = presheafPoint B S hS E.scheme E.point E.residueField_contained) ∧
      ∃ φ : residueField B S hS X hDecent x →+* E.scheme.left.1.residueField E.point,
        Function.Bijective φ ∧
          ∃ g : residueFieldObject B S hS E.scheme E.point E.residueField_contained ⟶
              (residueFieldRepresentative B S hS X hDecent x).1.siteObject B S hS X,
            B.inclusion.map g.left = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ) ∧
              yoneda.map g ≫ residueFieldMorphism B S hS X hDecent x =
                yoneda.map (residueFieldMap B S hS E.scheme E.point
                  E.residueField_contained) ≫ E.toSpace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_isomorphismLocus_of_localRingDimension_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBQ, part (1).** Let `X` be a Noetherian algebraic space over `S` and let
`f : Y ⟶ X` be a proper birational morphism with `Y` reduced. The maximal open subspace `U` of
`X` over which `f` is an isomorphism contains every point of `|X|` of codimension `0`.

By Stacks 0BBF the morphism is an isomorphism over a *dense* open subspace `V ⊆ X`, which is
contained in `U` by maximality. A dense subset of the Noetherian point space `|X|` meets the
nonempty open part of every irreducible component, so it meets the component of the given
codimension-zero point, which is therefore in `V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_isomorphismLocus_of_localRingDimension_eq_zero
    (x : points B S hS X) (hx : localRingDimension B S hS x = 0) :
    x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS U.toFunctor U.ι)
declarations.comment: part (1): every point of codimension zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_isomorphismLocus_of_finite_fibre_of_normal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBQ, part (3).** With the hypotheses of part (1), the maximal open subspace over
which `f` is an isomorphism contains every point of `|X|` whose fibre in `|Y|` is finite and
whose local ring is normal.

Stacks 0A4W, applied through Stacks 0ACK to convert the finite set-theoretic fibre into a
finite geometric fibre, makes `f` finite over an open neighbourhood of the point, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_isomorphismLocus_of_isFinite_over_neighbourhood` concludes.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_isomorphismLocus_of_finite_fibre_of_normal
    (x : points B S hS X) (hfibre : ((pointsMap B S hS Y f) ⁻¹' {x}).Finite)
    (hNormal : HasNormalLocalRingAtPoint B S hS X hX x) :
    x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS U.toFunctor U.ι)
declarations.comment: part (3): every point with finite fibre and normal local ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_isomorphismLocus_of_localRingDimension_eq_one_of_normal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBQ, part (2).** With the hypotheses of part (1), the maximal open subspace over
which `f` is an isomorphism contains every point of `|X|` of codimension `1` whose local ring
is normal.

Part (1) already puts the image of every codimension-zero point of `|Y|` in `U`, which makes
`f` quasi-finite there, so the third generic condition of Stacks 0AD2 holds and `f` is finite
over an open neighbourhood of the given point; part (3)'s argument then concludes.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_isomorphismLocus_of_localRingDimension_eq_one_of_normal
    (x : points B S hS X) (hx : localRingDimension B S hS x = 1)
    (hNormal : HasNormalLocalRingAtPoint B S hS X hX x) :
    x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS U.toFunctor U.ι)
declarations.comment: part (2): every point of codimension one with normal local ring

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.normalizedBlowUpScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BBS.** The normalized blowup of `X` at a closed point `x`: the
normalization of the blowup of `X` in the reduced closed subscheme supported at `x`.
declarations.comment: normalized blowup scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.normalizedBlowUp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BBS.** The normalized blowup of `X` at a closed point `x`, as a
morphism to `X`: the normalization of the blowup followed by the blowup morphism.
declarations.statement:
abbrev normalizedBlowUp (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite)
    (x : X) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X)) : normalizedBlowUpScheme X hX x hx ⟶ X
declarations.comment: normalized blowup morphism

declarations.name: Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.exists_normalizedBlowUpChain_dominating
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BBT.** Let `X` be a Noetherian Nagata scheme of dimension two and let
`f : Y ⟶ X` be a proper birational morphism. Then there is a scheme `Z` obtained from the
normalization of `X` by finitely many normalized blowups at closed points which dominates `Y`:
its structure morphism `g : Z ⟶ X` factors as `h ≫ f` for a morphism `h : Z ⟶ Y`, so the whole
diagram commutes over `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_normalizedBlowUpChain_dominating
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (hNagata : IsNagataScheme X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 2) (f : Y ⟶ X)
    [IsProper f] (hf : IsBirational f) :
    ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (g : Z ⟶ X) (h : Z ⟶ Y),
      NormalizedBlowUpChain X finite_irreducibleComponents_isCompactOpen_of_isNoetherian Z g ∧
        h ≫ f = g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalSingularitySituation.bijective_normalizedTrace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BBU.** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0B4W], let `ω_A` be a dualizing
module of `A` and let `ω_X` be the dualizing module of `X` normalized relative to `ω_A`
([Stacks, Remark 0B4R]: `ω_X[2] = f^!(ω_A[2])`, here the isomorphism `e : f^!(ω_A) ≅ ω_X` in
degree zero). Then the trace map `H⁰(X, ω_X) ⟶ ω_A` is an isomorphism. The consequent canonical
map `f^*ω_A ⟶ ω_X` is `AlgebraicGeometry.RationalSingularitySituation.normalizedPullbackMap`.

The proof is duality in degree zero against `𝒪_X`: `H¹(X, 𝒪_X) = 0` because `A` defines a rational
singularity, so `Hom(𝒪_X, ω_X) ⟶ Hom_A(Γ(X, 𝒪_X), ω_A)` is bijective, and its source is
`H⁰(X, ω_X)` and its target `ω_A`, as `Γ(X, 𝒪_X) = A` ([Stacks, Tag 0B4Y]).
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_normalizedTrace (_hωA : Stacks.Duality.IsDualizingRingModule S.A ωA)
    (e : (S.relativeDualizingComplex ωA).obj ≅
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor S.X.Modules 0).obj ωX) :
    Function.Bijective (S.normalizedTrace e).hom
declarations.comment: the trace H^0(X, omega_X) -> omega_A of the dualizing module normalized relative to omega_A (Remark 0B4R: f^!(omega_A) = omega_X in degree zero) is an isomorphism; the canonical map f^*omega_A -> omega_X is normalizedPullbackMap

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalSingularitySituation.normalizedPullbackMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BBU, the canonical map.** The map `f^*ω_A ⟶ ω_X` induced by the trace
isomorphism of the normalized dualizing module: the adjunct, under
`M ↦ f^*M̃ ⊣ ℱ ↦ H⁰(X, ℱ)` (`globalSectionsAdjunction`), of the inverse of the trace.
declarations.statement:
def normalizedPullbackMap (hωA : Stacks.Duality.IsDualizingRingModule S.A ωA)
    (e : (S.relativeDualizingComplex ωA).obj ≅
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor S.X.Modules 0).obj ωX) :
    (Scheme.Modules.pullback S.f).obj (tilde ωA) ⟶ ωX
declarations.comment: the canonical map f^*omega_A -> omega_X induced by the trace isomorphism, for the dualizing module normalized relative to omega_A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_singularPointBlowupChain_isDualizingModule_isInvertible
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a local normal Nagata domain of dimension two which defines a rational singularity
and has a dualizing complex. Then there is a finite sequence of blowups in singular closed points
`X = Xₙ ⟶ … ⟶ X₁ ⟶ X₀ = Spec(A)` with every `Xᵢ` normal such that the dualizing module of `X` is
an invertible `𝒪_X`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_singularPointBlowupChain_isDualizingModule_isInvertible
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNormalDomain A]
    (hN : IsNagataRing A) (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2) (hrat : DefinesRationalSingularity A)
    (hdual : letI : IsNoetherianRing A := hN.1
      letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (ModuleCat.{u} A)
      ∃ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A), Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K) :
    ∃ (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)),
      SingularPointBlowupChain IsNormal (Spec (.of A)) X f ∧
        ∃ _ : IsLocallyNoetherian X, ∃ ω : X.Modules, Stacks.Duality.IsDualizingModule ω ∧
          AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 ω

declarations.name: ideal_smul_top_inf
declarations.doc: Stacks Tag 0BBY: for a flat module `M`, `IM ∩ JM = (I ∩ J) M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ideal_smul_top_inf (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (I J : Ideal R)
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Flat R M] :
    (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) ⊓ (J • (⊤ : Submodule R M))
      = (I ⊓ J) • (⊤ : Submodule R M)

declarations.name: Ideal.map_height_le_spanRank_toENat_of_mem_minimalPrimes_sup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BBZ (2), Krull's height theorem in relative form.** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring
and let `I`, `J` be ideals of `R`. If a prime `q` is minimal over `I + J`, then the height of
`q / I` in `R / I` is at most the minimal number of generators of `J`; equivalently, every chain
of primes between `I` and `q` has length at most that number.
declarations.comment: Item (2), for an arbitrary ideal in place of the prime; item (1) is Mathlib's `Ideal.height_le_spanRank_toENat_of_mem_minimalPrimes`.

declarations.name: symbolicPower_map_of_flat
declarations.doc:
For a flat ring map `R → S` and a prime `p ⊆ R` whose extension `q = p S` is prime,
`p^{(n)} S = q^{(n)}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem symbolicPower_map_of_flat {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S)
    (hφ : φ.Flat) (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (hq : (p.map φ).IsPrime) (n : ℕ) :
    (symbolicPower' p n).map φ = symbolicPower' (p.map φ) n

declarations.name: Module.IsStablyIso
declarations.doc:
Two modules are *stably isomorphic* if adding finite free summands to each gives isomorphic
modules.
declarations.statement:
def IsStablyIso (R : Type u) [Ring R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (N : Type*) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] : Prop

declarations.name: Module.isStablyFree_iff_exists_isStablyIso
declarations.doc:
A module is stably free precisely when it is stably isomorphic to a free module. This
identifies Mathlib's `Module.IsStablyFree` with the source definition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStablyFree_iff_exists_isStablyIso (R : Type u) [Ring R]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    IsStablyFree R M ↔ ∃ F : ModuleCat.{max u v} R, Module.Free R F ∧ IsStablyIso R M F

declarations.name: Module.isStablyFree_two_out_of_three
declarations.doc:
In a short exact sequence of finite modules with projective quotient, if any two of the three
terms are stably free, then so is the third.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStablyFree_two_out_of_three {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    {P' : Type v} [AddCommGroup P'] [Module R P'] [Module.Finite R P']
    {P : Type w} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.Finite R P]
    {P'' : Type x} [AddCommGroup P''] [Module R P''] [Module.Finite R P''] [Module.Projective R P'']
    (f : P' →ₗ[R] P) (g : P →ₗ[R] P'')
    (hf : Function.Injective f) (hfg : Function.Exact f g) (hg : Function.Surjective g) :
    ((IsStablyFree R P' ∧ IsStablyFree R P) → IsStablyFree R P'') ∧
      ((IsStablyFree R P' ∧ IsStablyFree R P'') → IsStablyFree R P) ∧
      ((IsStablyFree R P ∧ IsStablyFree R P'') → IsStablyFree R P')

declarations.name: Module.exists_isStablyFree_lift
declarations.doc:
Let `I` be an ideal of `R` such that every element of `1 + I` is a unit, in other words `I` is
contained in the Jacobson radical. Then every finite stably free `R ⧸ I`-module `E` is the
reduction modulo `I` of a finite stably free `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isStablyFree_lift (I : Ideal R) (hI : ∀ x ∈ I, IsUnit (1 + x))
    {E : Type v} [AddCommGroup E] [Module (R ⧸ I) E] [Module.Finite (R ⧸ I) E]
    [IsStablyFree (R ⧸ I) E] :
    ∃ M : ModuleCat.{max u v} R, Module.Finite R M ∧ IsStablyFree R M ∧
      Nonempty ((M ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) ≃ₗ[R ⧸ I] E)

declarations.name: lift_iso_of_quot_iso
declarations.doc:
**(Lifting isomorphisms.)** If `φ : P → P'` is an `R`-module map between finite
projective modules whose induced map `P/IP → P'/IP'` is an isomorphism (bijective),
then `φ` itself is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem lift_iso_of_quot_iso
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    (hI : ∀ x ∈ I, IsUnit (1 + x))
    {P P' : Type*} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.Finite R P] [Module.Projective R P]
    [AddCommGroup P'] [Module R P'] [Module.Finite R P'] [Module.Projective R P']
    (φ : P →ₗ[R] P') (h : Function.Bijective (inducedQuot I φ)) :
    Function.Bijective φ

declarations.name: quot_iso_lift
declarations.doc:
**(Lifting the isomorphism class.)** If `P/IP ≅ P'/IP'` as `R`-modules, then
`P ≅ P'` as `R`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem quot_iso_lift
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    (hI : ∀ x ∈ I, IsUnit (1 + x))
    {P P' : Type*} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.Finite R P] [Module.Projective R P]
    [AddCommGroup P'] [Module R P'] [Module.Finite R P'] [Module.Projective R P']
    (h : Nonempty ((P ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R P))) ≃ₗ[R] (P' ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R P'))))) :
    Nonempty (P ≃ₗ[R] P')

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.perfectComplexes_filteredColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BC7.** Let `R : I ⥤ CommRingCat` be a filtered system of commutative rings whose
colimit is computed on underlying sets, and let `c` be a colimit cocone. Writing `E f` for the
canonical total derived extension of scalars `- ⊗ᴸ_A B` along `f : A →+* B` ([stacks 064H]), the
following two statements hold.

First, every perfect object `K` of the derived category of `c.pt`-modules descends to a finite
stage: there are an index `i` and a perfect object `Kᵢ` over `R.obj i` with
`K ≅ (E (c.ι.app i)).functor.obj Kᵢ`.

Second, morphisms out of a perfect complex commute with the filtered colimit. Fix a stage `i₀` and
objects `K₀`, `L₀` over `R.obj i₀` with `K₀` perfect. Then derived extension of scalars carries a
composition isomorphism `comp` compatible with the scalar-extension tower on complexes, and the
morphisms `(E (c.ι.app i₀)).functor.obj K₀ ⟶ (E (c.ι.app i₀)).functor.obj L₀` over the colimit ring
form the filtered colimit, over the stages `j` above `i₀`, of the morphisms
`(E (R.map j.hom)).functor.obj K₀ ⟶ (E (R.map j.hom)).functor.obj L₀` over those stages, with the
transition maps and the maps to the colimit given by derived extension of scalars conjugated by
`comp`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem perfectComplexes_filteredColimit
    {I : Type uI} [Category.{uI} I] [IsFiltered I]
    (R : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{uR}) [PreservesColimit R (forget CommRingCat.{uR})]
    (c : Cocone R) (hc : IsColimit c) :
    let E := fun {A B : Type uR} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (f : A →+* B) ↦
      totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{uR, uR, uR} f
    let D := fun {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j) ↦ E (R.map f).hom
    let Dlim := fun (i : I) ↦ E (c.ι.app i).hom
    (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{uR} c.pt)), IsPerfect K →
        ∃ (i : I) (Kᵢ : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{uR} (R.obj i))),
          IsPerfect Kᵢ ∧ Nonempty (K ≅ (Dlim i).functor.obj Kᵢ)) ∧
      (∀ (i₀ : I) (K₀ L₀ : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{uR} (R.obj i₀))),
        IsPerfect K₀ →
        ∃ (comp : ∀ {A B C : Type uR} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
            (f : A →+* B) (g : B →+* C),
            (E f).functor ⋙ (E g).functor ≅ (E (g.comp f)).functor),
          (∀ {A B C : Type uR} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
              (f : A →+* B) (g : B →+* C)
              (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{uR} A) ℤ),
            (E g).functor.map ((E f).comparison.app P) ≫
                (E g).comparison.app
                  (((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{uR, uR, uR} f).mapHomologicalComplex
                    (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P) ≫
                (extensionOfScalarsComplexComp.{uR} f g).inv.app P =
              (comp f g).hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ≫
                (E (g.comp f)).comparison.app P) ∧
        ∃ (H : Under i₀ ⥤ Type (uR + 1))
          (eH : ∀ j : Under i₀,
            H.obj j ≃ ((D j.hom).functor.obj K₀ ⟶ (D j.hom).functor.obj L₀))
          (s : Cocone H)
          (eTarget : s.pt ≃ ((Dlim i₀).functor.obj K₀ ⟶ (Dlim i₀).functor.obj L₀))
          (_hs : IsColimit s),
          (∀ {j k : Under i₀} (w : j ⟶ k) (x : H.obj j),
            let h : (R.map w.right).hom.comp (R.map j.hom).hom = (R.map k.hom).hom :=
              by
                ext x
                calc
                  _ = (R.map (j.hom ≫ w.right)).hom x :=
                    (congrArg (fun q : R.obj i₀ ⟶ R.obj k.right ↦ q.hom x)
                      (R.map_comp j.hom w.right)).symm
                  _ = _ := by rw [w.w]
            let stageComp := comp (R.map j.hom).hom (R.map w.right).hom ≪≫
              derivedExtensionScalarsCongr.{uR} E h
            eH k (H.map w x) =
              stageComp.inv.app K₀ ≫
                (D w.right).functor.map (eH j x) ≫
                stageComp.hom.app L₀) ∧
          (∀ (j : Under i₀)
              (g : (D j.hom).functor.obj K₀ ⟶ (D j.hom).functor.obj L₀),
            let h : (c.ι.app j.right).hom.comp (R.map j.hom).hom = (c.ι.app i₀).hom :=
              congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom (c.w j.hom)
            let limitComp := comp (R.map j.hom).hom (c.ι.app j.right).hom ≪≫
              derivedExtensionScalarsCongr.{uR} E h
            eTarget (s.ι.app j ((eH j).symm g)) =
              limitComp.inv.app K₀ ≫ (Dlim j.right).functor.map g ≫
                limitComp.hom.app L₀))

declarations.name: LiftAcyclic.exists_lift_acyclic_complex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BC9**.
A bounded above acyclic complex of `R/I`-modules with terms of the form `P/IP` has a bounded
above acyclic lift over `R` with terms satisfying `P`, whose reduction is isomorphic to the given
complex as a complex of `R/I`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_lift_acyclic_complex
    (P : ModuleCat.{max v u} R → Prop)
    (hPprojective : ∀ M, P M → Module.Projective R M)
    (hPcomplement : ∀ M₁ M₂, P M₁ → P (M₁ ⊞ M₂) → P M₂)
    (hPsurjective : ∀ (M₁ M₂ : ModuleCat.{max v u} R) (f : M₁ ⟶ M₂),
      P M₁ → P M₂ →
      Function.Surjective
        (((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, max v u} (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).map f).hom) →
      Function.Surjective f.hom)
    (E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} (R ⧸ I)) ℤ)
    (hbdd : ∃ b, E.IsStrictlyLE b) (hac : ∀ i, E.ExactAt i)
    (hterms : ∀ i, ∃ M, P M ∧ Nonempty
      (E.X i ≅ (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, max v u} (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).obj M)) :
    ∃ PC : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) ℤ,
      (∀ i, P (PC.X i)) ∧ (∃ b, PC.IsStrictlyLE b) ∧
      (∀ i, PC.ExactAt i) ∧
      Nonempty
        (((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, max v u} (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj PC ≅ E)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.exists_boundedAbove_lift_representing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BCA.** Let `I ⊆ R` and let `P` be a class of projective `R`-modules, closed under
finite direct sums and complementary summands, such that surjectivity modulo `I` lifts to
surjectivity. A bounded above complex `E` of `R / I`-modules whose terms are reductions of
modules in `P`, and which represents `K ⊗ᴸ[R] R / I`, lifts to a bounded above complex with
terms in `P` representing `K`, provided `K` already has some such representative.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_boundedAbove_lift_representing
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    (P : ModuleCat.{max v u} R → Prop)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} R))
    (E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} (R ⧸ I)) ℤ)
    (hPprojective : ∀ M, P M → Module.Projective R M)
    (hPsum : ∀ M₁ M₂, (P M₁ ∧ P (M₁ ⊞ M₂)) ↔ (P M₁ ∧ P M₂))
    (hPsurjective : ∀ (M₁ M₂ : ModuleCat.{max v u} R) (f : M₁ ⟶ M₂),
      P M₁ → P M₂ →
      Function.Surjective
          (((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, max v u} (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).map f).hom) →
        Function.Surjective f.hom)
    (hEbdd : ∃ b, E.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hEterms : ∀ i, ∃ M, P M ∧ Nonempty
      (E.X i ≅
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, max v u} (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).obj M))
    (hErep : Nonempty
      ((DerivedCategory.Q).obj E ≅
        (totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, v} (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).functor.obj K))
    (hKrep : ∃ KC : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) ℤ,
      (∀ i, P (KC.X i)) ∧ (∃ b, KC.IsStrictlyLE b) ∧
        Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.Q).obj KC ≅ K)) :
    ∃ PC : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) ℤ,
      (∀ i, P (PC.X i)) ∧
      (∃ b, PC.IsStrictlyLE b) ∧
      Nonempty
        (((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, max v u} (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj PC ≅ E) ∧
      Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.Q).obj PC ≅ K)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.exists_boundedAbove_isStablyFree_lift_representing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BCB.** Let `I ⊆ R` be an ideal every element of whose coset `1 + I` is a unit. A
bounded above complex `E` of finite stably free `R ⧸ I`-modules representing `K ⊗ᴸ[R] R ⧸ I`, for
a pseudo-coherent object `K` of `D(R)`, lifts to a bounded above complex `P` of finite stably free
`R`-modules representing `K` with `P ⊗[R] R ⧸ I` isomorphic to `E`. Moreover `P` is free in every
degree in which `E` is free.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_boundedAbove_isStablyFree_lift_representing
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} R))
    (E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} (R ⧸ I)) ℤ)
    (hEbdd : ∃ b, E.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hEterms : ∀ i, Module.Finite (R ⧸ I) (E.X i) ∧ Module.IsStablyFree (R ⧸ I) (E.X i))
    (hErep : Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.Q).obj E ≅
      (totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, v} (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).functor.obj K))
    (hK : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K)
    (hI : ∀ x ∈ I, IsUnit (1 + x)) :
    ∃ P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) ℤ,
      (∀ i, Module.Finite R (P.X i) ∧ Module.IsStablyFree R (P.X i)) ∧
      (∃ b, P.IsStrictlyLE b) ∧
      Nonempty
        (((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, max v u} (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P ≅ E) ∧
      Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.Q).obj P ≅ K) ∧
      (∀ i, Module.Free (R ⧸ I) (E.X i) → Module.Free R (P.X i))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.exists_unique_boundedAbove_free_complex_representing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BCC.** Let `K` be a pseudo-coherent object of the derived category of a commutative
local ring `R` with residue field `κ`. Its cohomology after derived extension of scalars to `κ` is
finite dimensional in every degree and vanishes above some degree `b`. Moreover `K` is represented
by a complex vanishing above `b` whose term in degree `i` is free of rank
`dim_κ Hⁱ(K ⊗ᴸ_R κ)`, and any two complexes with these prescribed terms representing `K` are
isomorphic as complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_unique_boundedAbove_free_complex_representing
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} R))
    (hK : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K) :
    let k := IsLocalRing.ResidueField R
    let H := fun i : ℤ =>
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max v u} k) i).obj
        ((totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, v} (IsLocalRing.residue R)).functor.obj K)
    let IsModel := fun P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) ℤ =>
      (∀ i, Nonempty (P.X i ≅
        ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{v} (Fin (Module.finrank k (H i)) → R)))) ∧
      Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.Q).obj P ≅ K)
    (∀ i, Module.Finite k (H i)) ∧
      ∃ b : ℤ, (∀ i, b < i → IsZero (H i)) ∧
        ∃ P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) ℤ,
          P.IsStrictlyLE b ∧ IsModel P ∧
            ∀ F G, IsModel F → IsModel G → Nonempty (F ≅ G)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.exists_away_bounded_free_complex_representing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BCD.** Let `R` be a commutative ring, `p` a prime of `R` and `K` a perfect object of
`D(R)`. The dimensions `dᵢ = dim_{κ(p)} Hⁱ(K ⊗ᴸ_R κ(p))` are finite and only finitely many of them
are nonzero, and there is an `f ∈ R` outside `p` together with a strictly bounded complex over
`R_f` whose term in degree `i` is free of rank exactly `dᵢ` and which represents
`K ⊗ᴸ_R R_f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_away_bounded_free_complex_representing
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} R)) (hK : IsPerfect K) :
    let k := p.ResidueField
    let H := fun i : ℤ =>
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max v u} k) i).obj
        ((totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, v} (algebraMap R k)).functor.obj K)
    (∀ i, Module.Finite k (H i)) ∧
      {i | Module.finrank k (H i) ≠ 0}.Finite ∧
      ∃ f : R, f ∉ p ∧
        ∃ (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} (Localization.Away f)) ℤ) (a b : ℤ),
          P.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ P.IsStrictlyLE b ∧
            (∀ i, Nonempty (P.X i ≅ ModuleCat.of (Localization.Away f)
              (ULift.{v} (Fin (Module.finrank k (H i)) → Localization.Away f)))) ∧
            Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.Q).obj P ≅
              (totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, v}
                (algebraMap R (Localization.Away f))).functor.obj K)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.exists_boundedAbove_finiteProjective_lift_representing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BCE.** Let `(R, I)` be a henselian pair and let `K` be a pseudo-coherent object of
`D(R)`. A bounded above complex `E` of finite projective `R ⧸ I`-modules representing
`K ⊗ᴸ[R] R ⧸ I` lifts to a bounded above complex `P` of finite projective `R`-modules
representing `K` with `P ⊗[R] R ⧸ I` isomorphic to `E`. Moreover `P` is free in every degree in
which `E` is free.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_boundedAbove_finiteProjective_lift_representing
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} R))
    (E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} (R ⧸ I)) ℤ)
    (hEbdd : ∃ b, E.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hEterms : ∀ i,
      Module.Finite (R ⧸ I) (E.X i) ∧ Module.Projective (R ⧸ I) (E.X i))
    (hErep : Nonempty
      ((DerivedCategory.Q).obj E ≅
        (totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, v} (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).functor.obj K))
    (hK : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K)
    (hI : HenselianPair R I) :
    ∃ P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) ℤ,
      (∀ i, Module.Finite R (P.X i) ∧ Module.Projective R (P.X i)) ∧
      (∃ b, P.IsStrictlyLE b) ∧
      Nonempty
        (((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, max v u} (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P ≅ E) ∧
      Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.Q).obj P ≅ K) ∧
      (∀ i, Module.Free (R ⧸ I) (E.X i) → Module.Free R (P.X i))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ProjectiveAmplitude.hom_eq_zero_and_existsUnique_iso_biprod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BCG.** If `L` has projective amplitude in `[a, b]`, then every morphism from `L` to
an object whose cohomology vanishes in all degrees `≥ a` is zero. A distinguished triangle
`K ⟶ M ⟶ L ⟶ K⟦1⟧` has a splitting `M ≅ K ⊞ L` compatible with its maps as soon as the
cohomology of `K` vanishes in all degrees `≥ a + 1`; if it vanishes in all degrees `≥ a`, that
compatible splitting is moreover unique.
declarations.statement:
theorem hom_eq_zero_and_existsUnique_iso_biprod
    {R : Type u} [Ring R] (K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (a b : ℤ)
    (hL : HasProjectiveAmplitude L a b) :
    ((∀ i : ℤ, a ≤ i → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) →
        ∀ f : L ⟶ K, f = 0) ∧
      ((∀ i : ℤ, a + 1 ≤ i →
          IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) →
        ∀ (M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (f : K ⟶ M) (g : M ⟶ L)
          (h : L ⟶ K⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
          Triangle.mk f g h ∈ distTriang _ →
            ∃ e : M ≅ K ⊞ L, f ≫ e.hom = biprod.inl ∧ g = e.hom ≫ biprod.snd) ∧
      ((∀ i : ℤ, a ≤ i → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) →
        ∀ (M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (f : K ⟶ M) (g : M ⟶ L)
          (h : L ⟶ K⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
          Triangle.mk f g h ∈ distTriang _ →
            ∃! e : M ≅ K ⊞ L, f ≫ e.hom = biprod.inl ∧ g = e.hom ≫ biprod.snd)

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineTilde.exists_finite_span_free_away_of_retract_free
declarations.doc:
**The affine case of Stacks 0BCI, in standard opens.** A direct summand `F` of a finite free
`𝒪_{Spec R}`-module is `N^~` for an `R`-module `N` which becomes finite free over `R_g` for each
`g` in a finite family generating the unit ideal; equivalently, `F` is finite free on each member
of a finite covering of `Spec R` by standard opens.

This is `Stacks.AffineTilde.exists_finiteProjective_tilde_of_retract_free` followed by the
equivalence of "finite projective" with "finite locally free" (Stacks 00NX), whose spanning set
is shrunk to a finite one by `Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finite_span_free_away_of_retract_free {ι : Type u} [Finite ι]
    {F : (Spec R).Modules} (h : Retract F (SheafOfModules.free.{u} ι)) :
    ∃ N : ModuleCat.{u} R, Nonempty ((tilde.functor R).obj N ≅ F) ∧
      ∃ s : Finset R, Ideal.span (s : Set R) = ⊤ ∧
        ∀ g ∈ s, Module.Free (Localization.Away g) (LocalizedModule.Away g N) ∧
          Module.Finite (Localization.Away g) (LocalizedModule.Away g N)
declarations.comment: affine case: a direct summand of a finite free module on Spec R

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.isFiniteLocallyFree_of_retract
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BCI.** A direct summand of a finite locally free sheaf of modules on
a ringed space whose stalks are local rings is finite locally free.

The tag attribute for 0BCI belongs on this declaration and on no other: the tag's covering set
is this one statement. It is deliberately not placed here, attribute placement being the lead's.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFree_of_retract
    [∀ x : X, IsLocalRing (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk O.obj x))]
    {F H : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (LocallyFreeRank.toRingSheaf X O)}
    (hF : Nonempty (Retract F H))
    (hH : @IsFiniteLocallyFree (Opens X) inferInstance (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
      (LocallyFreeRank.toRingSheaf X O) (fun _ ↦ inferInstance) (fun _ ↦ inferInstance) H) :
    @IsFiniteLocallyFree (Opens X) inferInstance (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
      (LocallyFreeRank.toRingSheaf X O) (fun _ ↦ inferInstance) (fun _ ↦ inferInstance) F

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFiniteLocallyFree_of_retract
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BCI.** A direct summand of a finite locally free sheaf of modules
on a ringed space whose structure-sheaf stalks are local rings is finite locally free.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFree_of_retract
    {X : TopCat.{u}} {O : TopCat.Sheaf CommRingCat.{u} X}
    [∀ x : X, IsLocalRing (ToType (O.presheaf.stalk x))]
    {F H : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj O)}
    (hF : Nonempty (@Retract (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj O))
      _root_.SheafOfModules.instCategory F H))
    (hH : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree
      (R := (sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj O) H) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree
      (R := (sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj O) F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPerfect_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_tfae [∀ x : X.carrier, IsLocalRing (ToType (X.presheaf.stalk x))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X)]
    [∀ U : Opens X.carrier, HasDerivedCategory.{d'} (OXMod.{u, u} (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding))]
    (K : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X)) :
    List.TFAE [IsPerfect K,
      ∃ F : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, u} X) ℤ, Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F ≅ K) ∧
        ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → Opens X.carrier), (⨆ i, U i) = ⊤ ∧
          ∀ i : I, ∃ P : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, u} (X.restrict (U i).isOpenEmbedding)) ℤ,
            {j : ℤ | ¬ IsZero (P.X j)}.Finite ∧
              (∀ j : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u}
                (R := structureSheafOfRings (X.restrict (U i).isOpenEmbedding)) (P.X j)) ∧
                Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅
                  DerivedCategory.Q.obj (restrictComplex F (U i))),
      ∃ F : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, u} X) ℤ, Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F ≅ K) ∧
        ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → Opens X.carrier), (⨆ i, U i) = ⊤ ∧
          ∀ i : I, ∃ P : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, u} (X.restrict (U i).isOpenEmbedding)) ℤ,
            {j : ℤ | ¬ IsZero (P.X j)}.Finite ∧
              (∀ j : ℤ, ∃ n : ℕ,
                Nonempty (P.X j ≅ finiteFree (X.restrict (U i).isOpenEmbedding) n)) ∧
                Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅
                  DerivedCategory.Q.obj (restrictComplex F (U i)))]
declarations.comment: perfect iff locally represented by finite complexes of finite (locally) free

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProjective_iff_isQuasiProjective_and_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BCL, clause (1).** A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` to a
quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme is projective — in the sense of
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective`, a closed immersion over `S` into the projective bundle of a
quasi-coherent module of finite type — if and only if it is quasi-projective and proper.

Forwards this is Tags 07RL and 01WC, which need no hypothesis on `S`. Backwards, Tag 07RM factors
`f` as an open immersion followed by a projective morphism, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.isProjective_comp_of_isOpenImmersion_of_isProper` concludes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProjective_iff_isQuasiProjective_and_isProper {X S : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace S]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (f : X ⟶ S) :
    IsProjective f ↔ IsQuasiProjective f ∧ IsProper f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProjectiveMorphism_iff_isHQuasiProjective_and_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BCL, clause (2).** A morphism of schemes is H-projective if and only
if it is H-quasi-projective and proper.

Forwards, an H-projective morphism is proper and H-quasi-projective. Backwards, let
`i : X ⟶ ℙⁿ_S` be an immersion over `S` with `i ≫ (ℙⁿ_S ↘ S) = f` proper. The structure
morphism of `ℙⁿ_S` is separated, so `i` is proper, hence a closed map; an immersion with closed
image is a closed immersion.

The base carries no quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness hypothesis; see the implementation
notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProjectiveMorphism_iff_isHQuasiProjective_and_isProper :
    IsProjectiveMorphism f ↔ IsHQuasiProjective f ∧ IsProper f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIntegral_of_flat_of_isIntegral_genericFiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BCM.** If a flat morphism has integral target and integral generic
fibre, then its source is integral.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegral_of_flat_of_isIntegral_genericFiber
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [Flat f] [IsIntegral Y]
    [IsIntegral (f.fiber (genericPoint Y))] : IsIntegral X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ringKrullDim_stalk_le_one_of_isLocallyPrincipal
declarations.doc: A component of a locally principal closed subscheme has codimension at most one.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_stalk_le_one_of_isLocallyPrincipal
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : IsLocallyPrincipal I)
    (ξ : I.subscheme)
    (hξ : ∃ Z : irreducibleComponents I.subscheme, IsGenericPoint ξ (Z : Set I.subscheme)) :
    ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk (I.subschemeι ξ)) ≤ 1
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_one_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc: A component of an effective Cartier divisor has codimension exactly one.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_one_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I)
    (ξ : I.subscheme)
    (hξ : ∃ Z : irreducibleComponents I.subscheme, IsGenericPoint ξ (Z : Set I.subscheme)) :
    ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk (I.subschemeι ξ)) = 1
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finsupp_eq_prod_of_support_cover
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme and `D` an effective Cartier divisor on `X` whose points are
covered by a family `Dᵢ` of integral effective Cartier divisors. Then `D` is a finite nonnegative
combination of the `Dᵢ`: there is a finitely supported `a : ι →₀ ℕ` with
`ℐ_D = Π ℐ_{Dᵢ}^{aᵢ}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finsupp_eq_prod_of_support_cover
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I)
    {ι : Type v} (D : ι → X.IdealSheafData)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsIntegral (D i).subscheme ∧ IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (D i))
