    (hcover : ∀ x ∈ I.supportSet, ∃ i, x ∈ (D i).supportSet) :
    ∃ a : ι →₀ ℕ, I = a.prod fun i n => D i ^ n
declarations.comment: decomposition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_integral_effectiveCartierDivisors_cover_supportSet
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme and `D` an effective Cartier divisor on `X`. If the local rings
of `X` at the points of `D` are unique factorization domains — in particular if `X` is regular —
then there is a family of integral effective Cartier divisors covering the points of `D`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_integral_effectiveCartierDivisors_cover_supportSet
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I)
    (h : (∀ x : X, x ∈ I.supportSet → UniqueFactorizationMonoid (X.presheaf.stalk x)) ∨
      IsRegular X) :
    ∃ S : Set X.IdealSheafData,
      (∀ J ∈ S, IsIntegral J.subscheme ∧ IsEffectiveCartierDivisor J) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ I.supportSet, ∃ J ∈ S, x ∈ J.supportSet)
declarations.comment: existence of the covering divisors

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isAffineOpen_puncturedSpectrum_iff_krullDimLE_one
declarations.doc:
The punctured spectrum of a Noetherian local ring is affine if and only if the ring has Krull
dimension at most one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineOpen_puncturedSpectrum_iff_krullDimLE_one :
    IsAffineOpen (puncturedSpectrum A) ↔ Ring.KrullDimLE 1 A

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.krullDimLE_one_stalk_at_genericPoint_compl_affineOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
Let `U` be an open subscheme of a locally Noetherian scheme `X` whose inclusion is affine.  At
the generic point `ξ` of an irreducible component of `X ∖ U` the local ring has Krull dimension at
most one.

Pulling `U` back along `Spec 𝒪_{X,ξ} → X` gives the punctured spectrum of `𝒪_{X,ξ}`, which is
affine because the inclusion of `U` is; so Tag 0BCR applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem krullDimLE_one_stalk_at_genericPoint_compl_affineOpenImmersion
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (U : X.Opens) [IsAffineHom U.ι]
    {Z : Set ↑((U : Set X)ᶜ)} (hZ : Z ∈ irreducibleComponents ↑((U : Set X)ᶜ))
    {ξ : ↑((U : Set X)ᶜ)} (hξ : IsGenericPoint ξ Z) :
    Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (X.presheaf.stalk (ξ : X))
declarations.comment: dimension bound

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.ringKrullDim_stalk_at_genericPoint_compl_affineOpenImmersion_eq_one
declarations.doc:
With the hypotheses of
`Stacks.Divisors.krullDimLE_one_stalk_at_genericPoint_compl_affineOpenImmersion`, if `U` is dense
or `ξ` lies in the closure of `U`, then the local ring at `ξ` has dimension exactly one.

Some point of `U` specializes to `ξ`, so it is a point of `Spec 𝒪_{X,ξ}` other than the closed
point; hence the dimension is positive.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_stalk_at_genericPoint_compl_affineOpenImmersion_eq_one
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (U : X.Opens) [IsAffineHom U.ι]
    {Z : Set ↑((U : Set X)ᶜ)} (hZ : Z ∈ irreducibleComponents ↑((U : Set X)ᶜ))
    {ξ : ↑((U : Set X)ᶜ)} (hξ : IsGenericPoint ξ Z)
    (hξU : Dense (U : Set X) ∨ (ξ : X) ∈ closure (U : Set X)) :
    ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk (ξ : X)) = 1
declarations.comment: equality in the closure

declarations.name: Stacks.PuncturedSpectrum.krullDimLE_one_stalk_at_genericPoint_compl_affineOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BCV.** The local ring at the generic point of an irreducible
component of the complement of an affine open in a separated locally Noetherian scheme has
Krull dimension at most one.
declarations.statement:
theorem krullDimLE_one_stalk_at_genericPoint_compl_affineOpen
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [Scheme.IsSeparated X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    {Z : Set ↑((U : Set X)ᶜ)} (hZ : Z ∈ irreducibleComponents ↑((U : Set X)ᶜ))
    {ξ : ↑((U : Set X)ᶜ)} (hξ : IsGenericPoint ξ Z) :
    Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (X.presheaf.stalk (ξ : X))
declarations.comment: dimension bound

declarations.name: Stacks.PuncturedSpectrum.ringKrullDim_stalk_at_genericPoint_compl_affineOpen_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BCV.** Under the hypotheses of the dimension bound, the local ring
has dimension one when the affine open is dense or the generic point is in its closure.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_stalk_at_genericPoint_compl_affineOpen_eq_one
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [Scheme.IsSeparated X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    {Z : Set ↑((U : Set X)ᶜ)} (hZ : Z ∈ irreducibleComponents ↑((U : Set X)ᶜ))
    {ξ : ↑((U : Set X)ᶜ)} (hξ : IsGenericPoint ξ Z)
    (hξU : Dense (U : Set X) ∨ (ξ : X) ∈ closure (U : Set X)) :
    ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk (ξ : X)) = 1
declarations.comment: equality in the closure

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_effectiveCartierDivisor_compl_affineOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EGJ.** The complement of a dense affine open in a Noetherian
scheme with affine diagonal is the support of an effective Cartier divisor if its local
rings along the complement are UFDs.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_effectiveCartierDivisor_compl_affineOpen
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal (terminal.from X))]
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hDense : Dense (U : Set X))
    (hUFD : ∀ x : X, x ∉ U → UniqueFactorizationMonoid (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ∃ I : X.IdealSheafData,
      IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I ∧
        (I.support : Set X) = (U : Set X)ᶜ
declarations.comment: the separated case, where the diagonal is affine

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_effectiveCartierDivisor_compl_affineOpen_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BCW.** Let `X` be a Noetherian separated scheme and `U ⊆ X` a dense
affine open whose complement meets only points with factorial local rings.  Then there is an
effective Cartier divisor `D ⊆ X` with `U = X ∖ D`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_effectiveCartierDivisor_compl_affineOpen_of_isSeparated
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsSeparated X]
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hdense : Dense (U : Set X))
    (hUFD : ∀ x : X, x ∉ U → UniqueFactorizationMonoid (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ∃ I : X.IdealSheafData,
      IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I ∧ (U : Set X) = (I.support : Set X)ᶜ

declarations.name: Stacks.Norm.MorphismNorm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Section 0BCX.** A norm of degree `d` for a morphism of schemes: a
multiplicative map of sheaves preserving pointwise vanishing whose value on a function pulled
back from the target is its `d`-th power.
declarations.statement: structure MorphismNorm {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (d : ℕ) extends MorphismNormMap f
declarations.comment: norm of degree d

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.hasNormPullbackPower_normPicardData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BCY**, the pullback--power clause: the homomorphism of Picard groups
induced by a norm of degree `d` carries the class of `f^*𝒩` to the class of `𝒩^{⊗ d}`, for every
invertible `𝒪_Y`-module `𝒩`.

Together with `Stacks.Divisors.exists_normPicardAddMonoidHom`, which is the tag's other clause,
this completes Tag 0BCY.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasNormPullbackPower_normPicardData (g : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite g] (e : ℕ)
    (M : MorphismNorm g e) :
    HasNormPullbackPower g e (normPicardData g e M).picardMap
declarations.comment: the pullback-power formula

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.exists_normPicardAddMonoidHom
declarations.doc: **The norm descends to a homomorphism of Picard groups.**
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_normPicardAddMonoidHom (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite f] {d : ℕ}
    (N : MorphismNorm f d) :
    ∃ F : X.picardGroup →+ Y.picardGroup,
      ∀ (L : X.Modules) (hL : IsInvertible X.presheaf (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property L),
        F (picardClass X.presheaf (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property L hL) =
          picardClass Y.presheaf (structureSheaf Y.sheaf).property
            (normInvertible f N.toMorphismNormMap L)
            (isInvertible_normInvertible f N.toMorphismNormMap L
              (hasTrivializingTargetCover_of_isFinite_of_isInvertible f L hL))
declarations.comment: the homomorphism of abelian groups

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.normMap
declarations.doc:
**The norm of a map of invertible modules.** A norm `N` of degree `d` on functions along a
finite morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` carries a map `φ : L ⟶ L'` of invertible `𝒪_X`-modules to a map of
the norms of `L` and `L'`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def normMap :
    normInvertible f N.toMorphismNormMap L ⟶ normInvertible f N.toMorphismNormMap L'
declarations.comment: the norm map

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.normMap_generator
declarations.doc:
**In local frames the norm map is multiplication by the norm of the coefficient.** If `φ`
carries a frame `s` of `L` over `f ⁻¹ᵁ U` to `a` times a frame `t` of `L'` there, then the norm
of `φ` carries the normed frame of `s` to `N(a)` times the normed frame of `t`. This pins the
norm map down rather than merely asserting that some map with the right vanishing locus
exists.
declarations.statement:
theorem normMap_generator (U : Y.Opens)
    (s : GeneratorSections X.toRingedSpace L (f ⁻¹ᵁ U))
    (t : GeneratorSections X.toRingedSpace L' (f ⁻¹ᵁ U)) (a : Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ U))
    (ha : φ.val.app (op (f ⁻¹ᵁ U)) s.val =
      @SMul.smul ((structureSheaf X.sheaf).obj.obj (op (f ⁻¹ᵁ U)))
        (L'.val.obj (op (f ⁻¹ᵁ U))) _ a t.val) :
    (normMap f N L L' φ).val.app (op U)
        (normGenerator f N.toMorphismNormMap L
          (hasTrivializingTargetCover_of_isInvertible f L) U s).val =
      @SMul.smul ((structureSheaf Y.sheaf).obj.obj (op U))
        ((normInvertible f N.toMorphismNormMap L').val.obj (op U)) _ (N.app U a)
        (normGenerator f N.toMorphismNormMap L'
          (hasTrivializingTargetCover_of_isInvertible f L') U t).val
declarations.comment: local generator formula

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.normMap_zeroAt_iff
declarations.doc:
**The norm map vanishes at `y` exactly when the original map vanishes at some point of the
fibre over `y`**: the vanishing locus of the norm of `φ` is the image of the vanishing locus
of `φ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem normMap_zeroAt_iff (y : Y) :
    zeroAt (normInvertible f N.toMorphismNormMap L) (normInvertible f N.toMorphismNormMap L')
        (normMap f N L L' φ) y ↔
      ∃ x : X, f x = y ∧ zeroAt L L' φ x
declarations.comment: vanishing locus

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.exists_isAmple_of_morphismNorm
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite morphism of schemes admitting a norm of degree `d ≥ 1`. If `X`
has an ample invertible sheaf, then so has `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAmple_of_morphismNorm (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite f] {d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d)
    (N : MorphismNorm f d) (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L]
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X L) :
    ∃ (M : Y.Modules) (hM : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf
        (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace).property M),
      @AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple Y M hM

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.exists_isAmple_of_hasNormOfDegree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BD0.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite morphism of schemes carrying a
norm of positive degree. If `X` has an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module then so does `Y`: the norm
of a sufficiently high tensor power of the given one.

Positivity of the degree is used exactly once, to see that `f` is surjective; the rest is
`Stacks.Divisors.exists_isAmple_of_morphismNormMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAmple_of_hasNormOfDegree (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite f] (L : X.Modules)
    [IsInvertibleModule X L] (hL : Stacks.Ample.IsAmple X L) {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d)
    (hN : HasNormOfDegree f d) :
    ∃ (M : Y.Modules) (hM : IsInvertibleModule Y M), @Stacks.Ample.IsAmple Y M hM

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isQuasiAffine_of_isFinite_of_hasNormOfDegree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BD1.** The target of a finite morphism carrying a norm of positive
degree is quasi-affine as soon as its source is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffine_of_isFinite_of_hasNormOfDegree (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite f]
    [Scheme.IsQuasiAffine X] {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) (hN : HasNormOfDegree f d) :
    Scheme.IsQuasiAffine Y

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isQuasiAffine_of_morphismNorm
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite morphism of schemes admitting a norm of degree `d ≥ 1`. If `X`
is quasi-affine, then so is `Y`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasiAffine_of_morphismNorm (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite f] {d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d)
    (N : MorphismNorm f d) [X.IsQuasiAffine] : Y.IsQuasiAffine

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.finiteLocallyFreeNorm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BD2.** The canonical determinant norm constructed in the proof,
for an arbitrary finite locally free morphism, including varying and zero rank.

Its defining property is `finiteLocallyFreeNorm_app_affine_eq_projectiveNorm`: on an affine
open of the target it is the determinant of multiplication. Taken with the two fields of
`DeterminantNorm` — the determinant formula on affine opens where the algebra is free, and the
power law at constant rank — this pins the norm down.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def finiteLocallyFreeNorm {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree f] : DeterminantNorm f
declarations.comment: the canonical norm

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.finiteLocallyFreeNormOfRank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BD2.** At positive constant rank `d`, the canonical determinant
norm is a norm of degree `d` in the sense of the Norms section.
declarations.comment: the norm of positive constant degree

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.finiteLocallyFreeNorm_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BD2.** Formation of the canonical determinant norm commutes with
arbitrary base change, even when the rank is not constant: around a cartesian square the base
change `f'` of a finite locally free morphism `f` is again finite locally free, and the norm of a
section of the structure sheaf pulled back around the square is the pullback of its norm.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteLocallyFreeNorm_baseChange
    {X Y X' Y' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y')
    (g' : X' ⟶ X) (g : Y' ⟶ Y)
    [Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree f]
    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) :
    ∃ h' : Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree f',
      letI := h'
      ∀ (U : Y.Opens) (s : Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ U)),
        (finiteLocallyFreeNorm f').app (g ⁻¹ᵁ U)
            (g'.appLE (f ⁻¹ᵁ U) (f' ⁻¹ᵁ (g ⁻¹ᵁ U)) (by
              intro x hx
              change f (g' x) ∈ U
              rw [← Scheme.Hom.comp_apply, sq.w, Scheme.Hom.comp_apply]
              exact hx) s) =
          g.app U ((finiteLocallyFreeNorm f).app U s)
declarations.comment: compatibility with arbitrary base change

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.finiteLocallyFreeNormOfRank_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BD2.** At positive constant rank, arbitrary base change preserves the
specified degree and the norm on sections: around a cartesian square the base change `f'` of a
morphism `f` that is finite locally free of rank `d` is again finite locally free of rank `d`,
and the degree-`d` norm of a section of the structure sheaf pulled back around the square is the
pullback of its degree-`d` norm.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteLocallyFreeNormOfRank_baseChange
    {X Y X' Y' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y')
    (g' : X' ⟶ X) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (d : ℕ)
    [Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank f d] (hd : 0 < d)
    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) :
    ∃ h' : Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank f' d,
      letI := h'
      ∀ (U : Y.Opens) (s : Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ U)),
        (finiteLocallyFreeNormOfRank f' d hd).1.app (g ⁻¹ᵁ U)
            (g'.appLE (f ⁻¹ᵁ U) (f' ⁻¹ᵁ (g ⁻¹ᵁ U)) (by
              intro x hx
              change f (g' x) ∈ U
              rw [← Scheme.Hom.comp_apply, sq.w, Scheme.Hom.comp_apply]
              exact hx) s) =
          g.app U ((finiteLocallyFreeNormOfRank f d hd).1.app U s)
declarations.comment: compatibility of the degree-d norm with arbitrary base change

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.exists_norm_of_finite_surjective_of_normal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BD3.** A finite surjective morphism of integral schemes with
normal target carries a norm of the function-field extension degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_norm_of_finite_surjective_of_normal
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite f] [Surjective f]
    [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y] [IsNormal Y] :
    ∃ φ : Y.functionField →+* X.functionField,
      (∀ (U : Y.Opens) [Nonempty U] [Nonempty (f ⁻¹ᵁ U)]
        (s : Γ(Y, U)),
        φ (Y.germToFunctionField U s) =
          X.germToFunctionField (f ⁻¹ᵁ U) (f.app U s)) ∧
      (letI : Algebra Y.functionField X.functionField := φ.toAlgebra
       HasNormOfDegree f (Module.finrank Y.functionField X.functionField))

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.exists_isAmple_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BD4, case (1).** A finite locally free, finite surjective morphism
descends the existence of an ample invertible module. The canonical determinant norm of
[Stacks, Tag 0BD2] is available at *varying* rank, and no constant degree is needed: the degree
is what Tag 0BD0 uses to get surjectivity, and here surjectivity is a hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAmple_of_isFiniteLocallyFree (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite f] [Surjective f]
    [Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree f] (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L]
    (hL : Stacks.Ample.IsAmple X L) :
    ∃ (M : Y.Modules) (hM : IsInvertibleModule Y M), @Stacks.Ample.IsAmple Y M hM
declarations.comment: finite_locally_free_case

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.exists_isAmple_of_isAmple_reduction_char_p
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BD4, case (3).** On a Noetherian scheme of prime characteristic `p`,
an ample invertible module on the reduction descends to an ample invertible module on the scheme:
a Frobenius power supplies a norm of degree a positive power of `p` for the canonical morphism
from the reduction ([Stacks, Tag 0BDZ]).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAmple_of_isAmple_reduction_char_p (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian Y] (p : ℕ)
    (hp : p.Prime) (hchar : (p : Γ(Y, ⊤)) = 0)
    (L : (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (⊤ : Closeds Y)).subscheme.Modules)
    [IsInvertibleModule (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (⊤ : Closeds Y)).subscheme L]
    (hL : Stacks.Ample.IsAmple
      (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (⊤ : Closeds Y)).subscheme L) :
    ∃ (M : Y.Modules) (hM : IsInvertibleModule Y M), @Stacks.Ample.IsAmple Y M hM
declarations.comment: reduction_characteristic_p_case

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.exists_isAmple_of_isIntegral_isNormal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BD4, case (2).** A finite surjective morphism onto an integral normal
scheme descends the existence of an ample invertible module. The source is replaced by an
irreducible component dominating the target, viewed as a reduced closed subscheme; that component
is integral, so [Stacks, Tag 0BD3] supplies a norm of the function-field degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAmple_of_isIntegral_isNormal {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite f]
    [Surjective f] [IsIntegral Y] [IsNormal Y] (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L]
    (hL : Stacks.Ample.IsAmple X L) :
    ∃ (M : Y.Modules) (hM : IsInvertibleModule Y M), @Stacks.Ample.IsAmple Y M hM
declarations.comment: integral_normal_case

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isQuasiAffine_of_isFinite_surjective_of_isNormal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BD5, case (2).** Quasi-affineness descends along a finite surjective
morphism onto an integral normal scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffine_of_isFinite_surjective_of_isNormal {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsFinite f] [Surjective f] [IsIntegral Y] [IsNormal Y] [Scheme.IsQuasiAffine X] :
    Scheme.IsQuasiAffine Y
declarations.comment: integral normal target case

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isQuasiAffine_of_isFiniteLocallyFree_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BD5, case (1).** Quasi-affineness descends along a finite locally
free surjective morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffine_of_isFiniteLocallyFree_surjective {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsFinite f] [Surjective f] [Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree f] [Scheme.IsQuasiAffine X] :
    Scheme.IsQuasiAffine Y
declarations.comment: finite locally free case

declarations.name: Stacks.InvertiblePullback.exists_isInvertible_pullback_iso_of_isTrivial_genericFiber_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BD7.** Let `φ : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes and `ℒ` an invertible
`𝒪_X`-module. Assume `X` is locally Noetherian, `Y` is locally Noetherian, integral and normal,
`φ` is flat with integral fibres, `φ` is quasi-compact or locally of finite type, and `ℒ` is
trivial on the generic fibre of `φ`. Then `ℒ ≅ φ^*𝒩` for an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module `𝒩`.

The family of meromorphic multipliers of the penultimate paragraph of the source's proof is no
longer a hypothesis: it is
`Stacks.InvertiblePullback.exists_span_eq_top_isPullMeromorphicFamily`.

Invertibility of `ℒ` is the hypothesis `hL` alone: the class instance that
`FamilyDescent.lean` carries beside it is the same statement in another spelling and is
obtained from `hL` inside the proof, so no hypothesis here is absent from
[Stacks, Tag 0BD7].
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isInvertible_pullback_iso_of_isTrivial_genericFiber_of_flat
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral Y] [IsNormal Y]
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj
      (Stacks.Sheaves.Differentials.ringSheaf (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology X) X.sheaf).property
        L)
    (hfibre : ∀ y : Y, AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral (f.fiber y))
    (hfinite : QuasiCompact f ∨ LocallyOfFiniteType f)
    (hgeneric : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsTrivial
      (f.fiber (genericPoint Y)).presheaf
      (Presheaf.isSheaf_comp_of_isSheaf _ _ (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
        (f.fiber (genericPoint Y)).IsSheaf)
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι (genericPoint Y))).obj L)) :
    ∃ N : Y.Modules,
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf
          ((Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_comp _ Y.presheaf
            (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).mp Y.IsSheaf) N ∧
        Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj N ≅ L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_comap_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BD8.** An effective Cartier divisor on an open subscheme of a locally
Noetherian scheme extends to an effective Cartier divisor on the whole scheme, provided the local
rings at the points outside the open are unique factorization domains. The extension is the
scheme-theoretic image.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_comap_eq {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (U : X.Opens) (D : U.toScheme.IdealSheafData) (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D)
    (hUFD : ∀ x : X, x ∉ U → UniqueFactorizationMonoid (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ∃ D' : X.IdealSheafData, IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D' ∧ D'.comap U.ι = D

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isInvertible_pullback_iso_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BD9].** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme, let `U ⊆ X` be an open
subscheme, and let `L` be an invertible `𝒪_U`-module. If the local ring `𝒪_{X, x}` is a unique
factorization domain at every point `x` outside `U`, then `L` is the restriction of an invertible
`𝒪_X`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isInvertible_pullback_iso_of_isLocallyNoetherian {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (U : X.Opens) (L : U.toScheme.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible U.toScheme.sheaf.obj
      U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (hUFD : ∀ x : X, x ∉ U → UniqueFactorizationMonoid (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ∃ L' : X.Modules,
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L' ∧
        Nonempty (L ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback U.ι).obj L')
declarations.comment: the locally Noetherian case, i.e. the tag itself

declarations.name: Stacks.PicardUFD.subsingleton_picardGroup_open_spectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BDA, part (1).** The Picard group of any open subscheme of the
spectrum of a unique factorization domain is trivial.

The empty open is handled separately; for a nonempty one, prime avoidance gives two principal
opens `D(f), D(g) ⊆ U` whose union has trivial Picard group and across whose complement in `U`
regular functions extend, so triviality descends to `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_picardGroup_open_spectrum (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [UniqueFactorizationMonoid R] (U : (Spec (.of R)).Opens) :
    Subsingleton (PicardGroup U.toScheme.presheaf U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf.2)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.PicardUFD.subsingleton_picardGroup_open_affineSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BDA, part (2).** The Picard group of any open subscheme of affine
space over a unique factorization domain is trivial. In particular this holds over a field.

Affine space over `R` is the spectrum of `R[ι]`, which is again a unique factorization domain
(Tag 0BC1, Mathlib's instance for `MvPolynomial`), so this is part (1) transported along
`AlgebraicGeometry.AffineSpace.SpecIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_picardGroup_open_affineSpace (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [UniqueFactorizationMonoid R] (ι : Type u) (U : (AffineSpace ι (Spec (.of R))).Opens) :
    Subsingleton (PicardGroup U.toScheme.presheaf U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf.2)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAmple_of_fieldExtension
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and `X` a scheme over `k`. If there exists an ample invertible sheaf on
`X_K` for some field extension `K/k`, then `X` has an ample invertible sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isAmple_of_fieldExtension
    (h : ∃ L : (pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) f).Modules,
        ∃ _ : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
          (pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) f).toRingedSpace.presheaf
          (structureSheafRing
            (pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) f).toRingedSpace).property L,
          Scheme.Modules.IsAmple
            (pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) f) L) :
    ∃ M : X.Modules, ∃ _ : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
        X.toRingedSpace.presheaf (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property M,
      Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X M

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiAffine_of_fieldExtension
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and `X` a scheme over `k`. If `X_K` is quasi-affine for some field
extension `K/k`, then `X` is quasi-affine.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasiAffine_of_fieldExtension
    (h : Scheme.IsQuasiAffine
      (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))) :
    Scheme.IsQuasiAffine X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiAffine_of_isQuasiAffine_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BDD.** Quasi-affineness descends along an extension of the base
field: if the base change of `X` to `K` is quasi-affine, then so is `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffine_of_isQuasiAffine_baseChange
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (h : Scheme.IsQuasiAffine
      (pullback f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k K))))) :
    Scheme.IsQuasiAffine X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiProjective_of_fieldExtension
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and `X` a scheme over `k`. If `X_K` is quasi-projective over `K` for some
field extension `K/k`, then `X` is quasi-projective over `k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasiProjective_of_fieldExtension
    (h : IsQuasiProjective (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))) :
    IsQuasiProjective f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_of_fieldExtension
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 0BDF].** Let `k` be a field and `X` a scheme over `k`. If `X_K` is
proper over `K` for some field extension `K/k`, then `X` is proper over `k`.

The field extension is faithfully flat, so `Spec(K) → Spec(k)` is a surjective flat quasi-compact
morphism and the statement is the descent of properness along one; that descent is
[Stacks Project, Tag 02L1], of which the source says this lemma is a special case.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isProper_of_fieldExtension
    (h : IsProper (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))) :
    IsProper f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProjective_of_fieldExtension
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 0BDG].** Let `k` be a field and `X` a scheme over `k`. If `X_K` is
projective over `K` for some field extension `K/k`, then `X` is projective over `k`.

This is the source proof verbatim: projectivity over a field is quasi-projectivity together with
properness, and each of those descends along an arbitrary field extension by
[Stacks Project, Tag 0BDE] and [Stacks Project, Tag 0BDF]. The identification of projectivity
with the conjunction is clause (1) of [Stacks Project, Tag 0BCL], applied at the two affine bases
`Spec K` and `Spec k`, where it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isProjective_iff_isQuasiProjective_and_isProper_of_isAffine`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isProjective_of_fieldExtension
    (h : IsProjective (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))) :
    IsProjective f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedFibreBetti.isPseudoCoherent_derivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0BDI, base change: the derived pullback of a pseudo-coherent object is
pseudo-coherent.**  This is what makes the derived-fibre Betti function of `Lf^* E` available
from the pseudo-coherence of `E` alone.

A single complex has to work for every `m`, so the representative is chosen once —
`DerivedCategory.Q.objPreimage` — and Tag 09U7 is applied in each degree, its `m`-specific
representative being transported onto that one choice by Tag 08CC part (2).
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherent_derivedPullback
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) E) :
    RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := Y.toRingedSpace)
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E)
declarations.comment: base_change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedFibreBetti.derivedFiberBetti_derivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0BDI, base change: the derived-fibre Betti function commutes with base change.**  For a
morphism of schemes `f : Y ⟶ X` the `i`-th derived-fibre Betti function of `Lf^* E` is the
pullback along `f` of the `i`-th derived-fibre Betti function of `E`.

The pseudo-coherence of `Lf^* E` that the left-hand side needs is supplied by
`isPseudoCoherent_derivedPullback`, so `E`'s own pseudo-coherence is the only hypothesis.  The
function does not use its pseudo-coherence argument, so nothing is lost by fixing it: the
underlying dimension equality is `finrank_residueFibre_eq`, which has no pseudo-coherence
hypothesis at all.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedFiberBetti_derivedPullback
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) E)
    (i : ℤ) :
    derivedFiberBetti Y ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
      f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E)
        (isPseudoCoherent_derivedPullback f E hE) i =
      derivedFiberBetti X E hE i ∘ f.base
declarations.comment: base_change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedFibreBetti.isLocallyConstructible_derivedFiberBetti_preimage
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BDI], part (3): the level sets of the derived-fibre Betti functions are
locally constructible.**  Let `X` be a scheme and let `E` be a pseudo-coherent object of
`D(𝒪_X)`.  For every `i` and every `n` the set of points `x` with
`dim_{κ(x)} H^i(Li_x^* E) = n` is locally constructible in `X`.

By [Stacks, Tag 054C] it is enough to check that the restriction to each affine open `U` is
constructible.  The open immersion `hU.fromSpec : Spec Γ(X, U) ⟶ X` is a homeomorphism onto the
subspace `U`, so that restriction is constructible exactly when its preimage along `fromSpec` is;
and that preimage is a level set of the derived-fibre Betti function of the derived pullback of
`E`, by part (1) of the tag, to which the affine case applies.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocallyConstructible_derivedFiberBetti_preimage (X : Scheme.{u})
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) E) (i : ℤ) (n : ℕ) :
    IsLocallyConstructible (derivedFiberBetti X E hE i ⁻¹' {n})
declarations.comment: part (3): for E a pseudo-coherent object of D(O_X) on a scheme X, the level sets of the functions beta_i are locally constructible in X. beta_i is AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedFibreBetti.derivedFiberBetti, the dimension over the residue field of the degree-i cohomology of the derived fibre read through global sections on Spec kappa(x), the level set at n is the preimage of the singleton n, and pseudo-coherence of E is the only hypothesis. The affine case is proved, not assumed: it is StacksDraft.Perfect.isConstructible_fibreBetti_preimage, which runs the source's argument through the rank loci of a bounded-above finite free model -- over a field the ideal of r-by-r minors of a matrix is the unit ideal exactly when r is at most its rank (StacksDraft.MinorRank.minorIdeal_eq_top_iff_le_rank), so the locus where the rank at p is at least r is the complement of the zero locus of a finitely generated ideal and hence retrocompact, which is what semi-continuity does not give

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedFibreBetti.upperSemicontinuous_derivedFiberBetti
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BDI], part (2): the derived-fibre Betti functions are upper
semi-continuous.**  Let `X` be a scheme and let `E` be a pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_X)`.  For
every `i` the function `x ↦ dim_{κ(x)} H^i(Li_x^* E)` is upper semi-continuous on `X`.

Every point lies in an affine open `U`, and `U` is the image of the open immersion
`hU.fromSpec : Spec Γ(X, U) ⟶ X`; the derived pullback of `E` along it is pseudo-coherent, so the
affine case applies there, and upper semi-continuity is local on the source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem upperSemicontinuous_derivedFiberBetti (X : Scheme.{u})
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) E) (i : ℤ) :
    UpperSemicontinuous (derivedFiberBetti X E hE i)
declarations.comment: part (2): for E a pseudo-coherent object of D(O_X) on a scheme X, the function beta_i sending x to dim_{kappa(x)} H^i(Li_x^* E) is upper semi-continuous. beta_i is AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedFibreBetti.derivedFiberBetti, the dimension over the residue field of the degree-i cohomology of the derived fibre read through global sections on Spec kappa(x), and pseudo-coherence of E is the only hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedFibreBetti.isLocallyConstant_chiDerivedFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BDJ.** The derived-fibre Euler characteristic of a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` on a
scheme is locally constant.

Near any point, Tag 0BCJ represents `E` by a bounded complex of finite free modules on an open
`V`; base change along the open immersion `V ⟶ X` (Tag 0BDI) identifies the Euler characteristic
on `V` with the restriction of the one on `X`, and on `V` it is the constant
`∑ (-1)^i rank(P^i)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocallyConstant_chiDerivedFibre (X : Scheme.{u})
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPerfect.{u, u + 1} (X := X.toRingedSpace) E) :
    IsLocallyConstant (chiDerivedFibre X E (isPseudoCoherent_of_isPerfect E hE))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.nonempty_iso_singleFunctor_restrict_iff_le
declarations.doc:
**The open subscheme of [stacks 0BDK] is characterised by the first description.** An open of
`X` is contained in `singleDegreeRankOpen` exactly when the restriction of `E` to it is isomorphic
to a finite locally free module of rank `r` placed in degree `i`; so `singleDegreeRankOpen` is the
largest open subscheme on which `E` has that shape.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_singleFunctor_restrict_iff_le (V : X.Opens) :
    (∃ M : V.toScheme.Modules,
        AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} M r ∧
          Nonempty ((restrictFunctor V.ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj E ≅
            (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor V.toScheme.Modules i).obj M)) ↔
      V ≤ singleDegreeRankOpen E i r
declarations.comment: the open description

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isZero_homology_singleDegreeRankOpen
declarations.doc: **The cohomology of `E` vanishes outside degree `i` on the open subscheme of [stacks 0BDK].**
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_homology_singleDegreeRankOpen (j : ℤ) (hj : j ≠ i) :
    IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (singleDegreeRankOpen E i r).toScheme.Modules j).obj
      ((restrictFunctor (singleDegreeRankOpen E i r).ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj E))
declarations.comment: the open description

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.nonempty_iso_singleFunctor_restrict_singleDegreeRankOpen
declarations.doc:
**On the open subscheme of [stacks 0BDK] the derived module `E` is its own degree-`i`
cohomology sheaf placed in degree `i`.** This is the first half of description (1) of the tag.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_singleFunctor_restrict_singleDegreeRankOpen :
    Nonempty ((restrictFunctor (singleDegreeRankOpen E i r).ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj E ≅
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (singleDegreeRankOpen E i r).toScheme.Modules i).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (singleDegreeRankOpen E i r).toScheme.Modules i).obj
          ((restrictFunctor (singleDegreeRankOpen E i r).ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj E)))
declarations.comment: the open description

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_homology_singleDegreeRankOpen
declarations.doc:
**On the open subscheme of [stacks 0BDK] the degree-`i` cohomology sheaf of `E` is finite
locally free of rank `r`.** This is the second half of description (1) of the tag.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_homology_singleDegreeRankOpen :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (singleDegreeRankOpen E i r).toScheme.Modules i).obj
        ((restrictFunctor (singleDegreeRankOpen E i r).ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj E)) r
declarations.comment: the open description

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.factorsThrough_singleDegreeRankOpen_iff
declarations.doc:
**The universal property of the open subscheme of [stacks 0BDK], for open immersions.** An open
immersion `f : Y ⟶ X` factors through `singleDegreeRankOpen` exactly when the restriction of `E`
along `f` is isomorphic to a finite locally free module of rank `r` placed in degree `i`.

This is description (2) of the tag for an open immersion, with the exact restriction functor along
`f` in place of the derived pullback; the tag states it for an arbitrary morphism and the derived
pullback.
declarations.statement:
theorem factorsThrough_singleDegreeRankOpen_iff {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    [IsOpenImmersion f] :
    (∃ g : Y ⟶ (singleDegreeRankOpen E i r).toScheme,
        g ≫ (singleDegreeRankOpen E i r).ι = f) ↔
      ∃ M : Y.Modules,
        AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} M r ∧
          Nonempty ((restrictFunctor f).mapDerivedCategory.obj E ≅
            (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor Y.Modules i).obj M)
declarations.comment: the universal property for open immersions, restriction for the derived pullback

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.existsUnique_opens_singleDegreeRank_int
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BDK].** Let `X` be a scheme, let `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)` be perfect and let `i, r` be
integers. There is a unique open subscheme `U ⊆ X` characterised by the following:

1. `E|_U ≅ H^i(E|_U)[-i]` and `H^i(E|_U)` is a locally free `𝒪_U`-module of rank `r`,
2. a morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` factors through `U` if and only if `Lf^* E` is isomorphic to a locally
   free module of rank `r` placed in degree `i`.

"Locally free of rank `r`" for an integer `r` is read, as the source states it, at each point: a
sheaf of modules has it when every point has a neighbourhood on which the sheaf is free of rank
`r`. For `r ≥ 0` that is finite local freeness of rank `r` and the statement is
`existsUnique_opens_singleDegreeRank` with its witness `singleDegreeRankOpen E i r`; for `r < 0`
the condition forces the scheme to be empty, and the open subscheme is `⊥`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_opens_singleDegreeRank_int (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) E)
    (i r : ℤ) :
    ∃! U : X.Opens,
      (Nonempty ((restrictFunctor U.ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj E ≅
            (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor U.toScheme.Modules i).obj
              ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor U.toScheme.Modules i).obj
                ((restrictFunctor U.ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj E))) ∧
          ∀ _ : U.toScheme, ∃ n : ℕ, (n : ℤ) = r ∧
            AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
              ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor U.toScheme.Modules i).obj
                ((restrictFunctor U.ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj E)) n) ∧
        ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : Y ⟶ X),
          (∃ g : Y ⟶ U.toScheme, g ≫ U.ι = f) ↔
            ∃ M : Y.Modules,
              (∀ _ : Y, ∃ n : ℕ, (n : ℤ) = r ∧
                  AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} M n) ∧
                Nonempty ((derivedPullback f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E ≅
                  (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor Y.Modules i).obj M)
declarations.comment: THE WHOLE TAG, at the source's INTEGER rank: the existence of an open subscheme satisfying description (1), both of its clauses, and description (2) in both directions for an ARBITRARY morphism of schemes and the derived pullback Lf^*E, together with the UNIQUENESS that makes the two descriptions a characterisation. The only premise is the source's own, that E be perfect. The rank clause is read at each point, as the source states it; for a non-negative rank the witness is AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.singleDegreeRankOpen and the statement is AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.existsUnique_opens_singleDegreeRank, and for a negative rank the witness is the empty open subscheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.factorsThrough_singleDegreeRankOpen_iff_derivedPullback
declarations.doc:
Let `E` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`, `i` an integer and `r` a natural number. A morphism
of schemes `f : Y ⟶ X` factors through `singleDegreeRankOpen E i r` exactly when `Lf^*E` is
isomorphic to a finite locally free `𝒪_Y`-module of rank `r` placed in degree `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem factorsThrough_singleDegreeRankOpen_iff_derivedPullback
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPerfect.{u, u + 1} (X := X.toRingedSpace) E) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    (∃ g : Y ⟶ (singleDegreeRankOpen E i r).toScheme,
        g ≫ (singleDegreeRankOpen E i r).ι = f) ↔
      ∃ M : Y.Modules,
        AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} M r ∧
          Nonempty ((derivedPullback f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E ≅
            (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor Y.Modules i).obj M)
declarations.comment: part (2): the universal property along an arbitrary morphism, rank r : N

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BottomRankStratum.isBottomRankStratum_fittingRankStratum
declarations.doc:
**The rank `s` Fitting stratum is a bottom rank `s` stratum for a module placed in degree
`a`.** Its structural morphism is a locally closed immersion and it represents the rank `s`
functor of `F` ([stacks 05P8]), which for a module placed in degree `a` is the condition of being
universally of bottom rank `s`.

This is descriptions (1) and (2) of [stacks 0BDL] for an `E` which is a module placed in degree
`a`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isBottomRankStratum_fittingRankStratum (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType]
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] (a : ℤ) (s : ℕ) :
    IsBottomRankStratum ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules a).obj F) a s
      (fittingRankStratum F s).hom
declarations.comment: parts (1) and (2), for E a finite type quasi-coherent module placed in degree a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BottomRankStratum.pullbackHomologySingleCompIso
declarations.doc:
**`H^a(L(g ∘ j)^* E) ≅ g^* H^a(Lj^* E)` for `E` a module placed in degree `a`.** This is
part (3) of [stacks 0BDL]: a morphism factoring as `Y ⟶ Z ⟶ X` has its degree-`a` cohomology of
the derived pullback the ordinary pullback along `g` of the one on `Z`.

Both sides are identified with an ordinary pullback of `F` by `pullbackHomologySingleIso`, and
the two ordinary pullbacks are identified by `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp`, so
the isomorphism is a composite of canonical maps and not merely an abstract isomorphism of
locally free modules of the same rank.
declarations.statement:
public def pullbackHomologySingleCompIso (F : X.Modules) (a : ℤ) {Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (j : Z ⟶ X)
    (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    pullbackHomology ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules a).obj F) a (g ≫ j) ≅
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj
        (pullbackHomology ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules a).obj F) a j)
declarations.comment: part (3), for E a module placed in degree a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BottomRankStratum.factorsThrough_fittingRankStratum_iff
declarations.doc:
**A morphism factors through the rank `s` Fitting stratum exactly when `H^a(Lf^* E)` is
finite locally free of rank `s`.** This is the equivalence of (a) and (b) in part (4) of
[stacks 0BDL] for `E` a module placed in degree `a`.

No bound on the derived-fibre Betti numbers is needed: the quantification over further morphisms
in description (2) costs nothing for a module placed in degree `a`, because the ordinary pullback
of a finite locally free module of rank `s` is again one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem factorsThrough_fittingRankStratum_iff (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType]
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] (a : ℤ) (s : ℕ) {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    (∃ g : Y ⟶ (fittingRankStratum F s).left, g ≫ (fittingRankStratum F s).hom = f) ↔
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
        (pullbackHomology ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules a).obj F) a f) s
declarations.comment: part (4), (a) iff (b), for E a finite type quasi-coherent module in degree a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BottomRankStratum.isBottomRankStratum_finitePresentation_fittingRankStratum
declarations.doc:
**The rank `s` Fitting stratum of a finitely presented module is a bottom rank `s` stratum
whose structural morphism is of finite presentation.** This is descriptions (1) and (2) of
[stacks 0BDL] together with its assertion that `j : Z ⟶ X` is of finite presentation, for `E` a
finitely presented module placed in degree `a`.

The finite presentation is `AlgebraicGeometry.finitePresentation_fittingRankStratum`; the two
halves are stated together because the tag's "moreover" is about the same `j` that descriptions
(1) and (2) characterise.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isBottomRankStratum_finitePresentation_fittingRankStratum (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsFinitePresentation] (a : ℤ) (s : ℕ) :
    IsBottomRankStratum ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules a).obj F) a s
        (@fittingRankStratum X F (SheafOfModules.instIsFiniteTypeOfIsFinitePresentation F)
          (SheafOfModules.instIsQuasicoherentOfIsFinitePresentation F) s).hom ∧
      FinitePresentation
        (@fittingRankStratum X F (SheafOfModules.instIsFiniteTypeOfIsFinitePresentation F)
          (SheafOfModules.instIsQuasicoherentOfIsFinitePresentation F) s).hom
declarations.comment: parts (1), (2) and finite presentation, E a finitely presented module in degree a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BottomRankStratum.isClosedImmersion_fittingRankStratum_of_isGeneratedByNear
declarations.doc:
**When the module is generated by `s` sections near every point, the rank `s` Fitting stratum
is a closed subscheme.** This is the closedness assertion of part (4) of [stacks 0BDL] for `E` a
module placed in degree `a`, with the hypothesis `β_a ≤ s` in the form it takes for such an `E`:
`β_a(x)` is the dimension of the fibre of `F` at `x`, so `β_a(x) ≤ s` says that `F` needs at most
`s` generators near `x`.

Under that hypothesis the `s`-th Fitting ideal is the unit ideal, so the open subscheme cut out
of the Fitting closed subscheme of index `s - 1` by the generator open of index `s` is the whole
of it, and the structural morphism of the stratum is that closed immersion up to an
isomorphism.
declarations.comment: part (4), closedness of j, E a module in degree a, Betti bound as generation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BottomRankStratum.exists_isBottomRankStratum
declarations.doc:
**The bottom rank stratum of a perfect complex.** Let `E` be perfect of Tor amplitude in
`[a, b]` and `r` a natural number. There is a locally closed immersion `j : Z ⟶ X` with
`H^a(Lj^* E)` finite locally free of rank `r`, through which a morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` factors
exactly when `H^a(L(g ∘ f)^* E)` is finite locally free of rank `r` for every `g : Y' ⟶ Y`
(`IsBottomRankStratum`). The morphism `j` is of finite presentation, and
`H^a(L(g ∘ j)^* E) ≅ g^* H^a(Lj^* E)` for every `g : Y ⟶ Z`. If `β_a ≤ r` everywhere, then `j` is
a closed immersion, a morphism `f` factors through `Z` exactly when `H^a(Lf^* E)` is finite
locally free of rank `r`, and, when `r = 1`, exactly when the scalar action
`𝒪_Y ⟶ SheafHom(H^a(Lf^* E), H^a(Lf^* E))` is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isBottomRankStratum (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) E) (a b : ℤ)
    (htor : Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude X.toRingedSpace E a b) (r : ℕ) :
    ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (j : Z ⟶ X), IsBottomRankStratum E a r j ∧ FinitePresentation j ∧
      (∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ Z), Nonempty (pullbackHomology E a (g ≫ j) ≅
        (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj (pullbackHomology E a j))) ∧
      ((∀ x : X, DerivedFibreBetti.derivedFiberBetti X E
          (Scheme.Modules.isPseudoCoherent_of_isPerfect E hE) a x ≤ r) →
        IsClosedImmersion j ∧
        (∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : Y ⟶ X), (∃ g : Y ⟶ Z, g ≫ j = f) ↔
          SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} (pullbackHomology E a f) r) ∧
        (r = 1 → ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : Y ⟶ X), (∃ g : Y ⟶ Z, g ≫ j = f) ↔
          Mono (Stacks.SheafOfModules.scalarAction Y.toRingedSpace (pullbackHomology E a f)
            (Stacks.Cohomology.SheafHomComplex.sheafHom Y.sheaf _ _))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibreBetti.fibreBetti_baseChange_upperSemicontinuous_isLocallyConstructible
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BDN].** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a proper morphism of finite presentation and let
`ℱ` be an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation, flat over `S`. Fix `i ∈ ℤ` and let `β_i` be the
function `s ↦ dim_{κ(s)} H^i(X_s, ℱ_s)` (`AlgebraicGeometry.FibreBetti.fibreBetti`). Then

1. the formation of `β_i` commutes with arbitrary base change: for every cartesian square with
   `g : S' ⟶ S`, `f' : X' ⟶ S'` and `g' : X' ⟶ X`, the function `β_i` of `(f', (g')^*ℱ)` is
   `β_i ∘ g`;
2. `β_i` is upper semi-continuous;
3. every level set `β_i⁻¹{n}` is locally constructible in `S`.

The proof is the source's. By [Stacks, Tag 0B91], `β_i` is the derived-fibre Betti function of
the perfect object `Rf_*ℱ` (`fibreBetti_eq_derivedFiberBetti`), so the three parts are parts (1),
(2) and (3) of [Stacks, Tag 0BDI].
declarations.statement:
public theorem fibreBetti_baseChange_upperSemicontinuous_isLocallyConstructible
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (hf : FinitePresentation f) [IsProper f] (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsFinitePresentation] (hflat : IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom F) (i : ℤ) :
    (∀ {X' S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g' : X' ⟶ X),
        IsPullback g' f' f g →
          fibreBetti f' ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj F) i = fibreBetti f F i ∘ g.base) ∧
      UpperSemicontinuous (fibreBetti f F i) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, IsLocallyConstructible (fibreBetti f F i ⁻¹' {n})

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasDescentLocus_of_flat_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0BDP.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a flat, proper morphism of finite presentation and
`E` a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module. Assume that `𝒪_T ⟶ p_*𝒪_{X_T}` is an isomorphism for
every `g : T ⟶ S`, where `p : X_T = X ×_S T ⟶ T`. Then there is an immersion of finite
presentation `j : Z ⟶ S` such that `g : T ⟶ S` factors through `Z` if and only if there is a
finite locally free `𝒪_T`-module `N` with `p^*N ≅ q^*E`, `q : X_T ⟶ X` the projection.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasDescentLocus_of_flat_of_isProper {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [IsProper f]
    (hfp : FinitePresentation f)
    (hO : ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S),
      IsIso (structureSheafHom (pullback.snd f g).toLRSHom.toShHom))
    (E : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace))
    [hE : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E] :
    HasDescentLocus f E

registrations.name: LocallyFinite
registrations.comment: a locally finite collection of subsets

declarations.name: CochainComplex.Filtered.exists_iso_gradedHomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BDT.** The graded piece `gr^pH^n(K^•) = F^pH^n(K^•)/F^{p + 1}H^n(K^•)` of the
filtration induced on cohomology is
`(Ker(d) ∩ F^pK^n)/(Ker(d) ∩ F^{p + 1}K^n + Im(d) ∩ F^pK^n)`: there is an isomorphism between the
two compatible with the canonical maps to both from the cycles of `K^•` lying in `F^pK^n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_gradedHomology (p n : ℤ) :
    ∃ (a : (K.cyclesInStep p n : C) ⟶
        (kernelSubobject (K.X.d n (n + 1)) ⊓ K.step p n : Subobject (K.X.X n)))
      (b : (K.cyclesInStep p n : C) ⟶
        image (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (K.filtration.ι.app (op p)) n))
      (e : cokernel (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (K.kernel_inf_step_succ_sup_image_inf_step_le p n)) ≅
        K.gradedHomology p n),
      a ≫ (kernelSubobject (K.X.d n (n + 1)) ⊓ K.step p n).arrow =
        (K.cyclesInStep p n).arrow ≫ K.X.iCycles n ∧
      b ≫ image.ι (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (K.filtration.ι.app (op p)) n) =
        (K.cyclesInStep p n).arrow ≫ K.X.homologyπ n ∧
      a ≫ cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (K.kernel_inf_step_succ_sup_image_inf_step_le p n)) ≫
          e.hom =
        b ≫ cokernel.π (image.preComp
          (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (K.filtration.diagram.map
            (homOfLE (Int.le_add_one le_rfl) : (p : ℤ) ⟶ p + 1).op) n)
          (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (K.filtration.ι.app (op p)) n))

declarations.name: IsRegularChainComplex
declarations.doc:
A cohomological spectral sequence `E` (with `d_r` of bidegree `(r, 1 - r)`) is
*regular* if for every `(p, q) : ℤ × ℤ` there exists `b : ℤ` such that the
differential `d_r^{p,q} : E_r^{p,q} → E_r^{p + r, q - r + 1}` is zero for all
`r ≥ b` (with `r₀ ≤ r`).
declarations.statement: def IsRegularChainComplex (E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence C r₀) : Prop
declarations.comment: regular

declarations.name: IsCoregular
declarations.doc:
A cohomological spectral sequence `E` (with `d_r` of bidegree `(r, 1 - r)`)
is *coregular* if for every `(p, q) : ℤ × ℤ` there exists `b : ℤ` such that the
differential `d_r^{p - r, q + r - 1} : E_r^{p-r, q+r-1} → E_r^{p, q}` is zero for
all `r ≥ b` (with `r₀ ≤ r`).
declarations.statement: def IsCoregular (E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence C r₀) : Prop
declarations.comment: coregular

declarations.name: IsBounded
declarations.doc:
A cohomological spectral sequence `E` is *bounded* if for every total degree
`n : ℤ` there are only finitely many pairs `p : ℤ` such that
`E_{r₀}^{p, n - p}` is nonzero.
declarations.statement: def IsBounded (E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence C r₀) : Prop
declarations.comment: bounded

declarations.name: IsBoundedBelow
declarations.doc:
A cohomological spectral sequence `E` is *bounded below* if for every total
degree `n : ℤ` there exists `b : ℤ` such that `E_{r₀}^{p, n - p} = 0` for all
`p ≥ b`.
declarations.statement: def IsBoundedBelow (E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence C r₀) : Prop
declarations.comment: bounded below

declarations.name: IsBoundedAbove
declarations.doc:
A cohomological spectral sequence `E` is *bounded above* if for every total
degree `n : ℤ` there exists `b : ℤ` such that `E_{r₀}^{p, n - p} = 0` for all
`p ≤ b`.
declarations.statement: def IsBoundedAbove (E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence C r₀) : Prop
declarations.comment: bounded above

declarations.name: CohomologicalSpectralSequence.isRegularChainComplex_iff_Z_eventually_constant
declarations.doc:
Part (1): the spectral sequence is regular iff for all `p, q` the cycles `Z_r^{p,q}` are
eventually constant.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularChainComplex_iff_Z_eventually_constant :
    IsRegularChainComplex E ↔ ∀ p q : ℤ, ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ r, b ≤ r → E.Z (p, q) r = E.Z (p, q) b

declarations.name: CohomologicalSpectralSequence.isCoregular_iff_B_eventually_constant
declarations.doc:
Part (2): the spectral sequence is coregular iff for all `p, q` the boundaries `B_r^{p,q}`
are eventually constant.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoregular_iff_B_eventually_constant :
    IsCoregular E ↔ ∀ p q : ℤ, ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ r, b ≤ r → E.B (p, q) r = E.B (p, q) b

declarations.name: CohomologicalSpectralSequence.isBounded_iff_isBoundedBelow_and_isBoundedAbove
declarations.doc:
Part (3): the spectral sequence is bounded iff it is both bounded below and bounded
above.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBounded_iff_isBoundedBelow_and_isBoundedAbove :
    IsBounded E ↔ IsBoundedBelow E ∧ IsBoundedAbove E

declarations.name: CohomologicalSpectralSequence.isRegularChainComplex_of_isBoundedBelow
declarations.doc: Part (4): if the spectral sequence is bounded below, then it is regular.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularChainComplex_of_isBoundedBelow (h : IsBoundedBelow E) :
    IsRegularChainComplex E

declarations.name: CohomologicalSpectralSequence.isCoregular_of_isBoundedAbove
declarations.doc: Part (5): if the spectral sequence is bounded above, then it is coregular.
declarations.statement: theorem isCoregular_of_isBoundedAbove (h : IsBoundedAbove E) : IsCoregular E

declarations.name: CochainComplex.Filtered.finite_homology_and_sum_negOnePow_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BDW.** Let `(K^•, F)` be a filtered complex of `C` whose filtration is finite in
each degree, and let `E` be its spectral sequence, presented by the identification of its pages
with `Z_s^{p, q}/(D_s^{p, q} ∩ Z_s^{p, q})` of [Stacks, Tag 012M]. If some page `E_r` has only
finitely many nonzero terms, then only finitely many `H^n(K^•)` are nonzero, and for every weak
Serre subcategory `P` of `C` containing the terms of `E_r` (for instance the smallest one) the
`H^n(K^•)` lie in `P` and `∑ (-1)^n [H^n(K^•)] = ∑ (-1)^{p + q} [E_r^{p, q}]` in `K₀(P)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_homology_and_sum_negOnePow_eq (hK : K.filtration.IsDegreewiseFinite)
    (E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence C 0)
    (e : ∀ (r p q n : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (_ : n = p + q), (E.page r hr).X (p, q) ≅
      cokernel (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (inf_le_right : boundaries K.X K.step r p n ⊓
        cycles K.X K.step r p n ≤ cycles K.X K.step r p n)))
    (r : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hfin : {pq : ℤ × ℤ | ¬ IsZero ((E.page r hr).X pq)}.Finite)
    (P : ObjectProperty C) [P.IsWeakSerreClass] (hP : ∀ pq : ℤ × ℤ, P ((E.page r hr).X pq)) :
    {n : ℤ | ¬ IsZero (K.X.homology n)}.Finite ∧
    ∃ hH : ∀ n : ℤ, P (K.X.homology n),
      ∑ᶠ n : ℤ, (n.negOnePow : ℤ) • KZero.mk P.FullSubcategory ⟨K.X.homology n, hH n⟩ =
        ∑ᶠ pq : ℤ × ℤ, ((pq.1 + pq.2).negOnePow : ℤ) •
          KZero.mk P.FullSubcategory ⟨(E.page r hr).X pq, hP pq⟩

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineHom_diagonal_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BDX.** For a scheme `X`, the following are
equivalent: its diagonal is affine; intersections of two affine opens are
affine; and it admits an affine open cover all of whose nonempty finite
intersections are affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_diagonal_tfae (X : Scheme.{u}) : List.TFAE [
    IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal (terminal.from X)),
    ∀ (U V : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen U → IsAffineOpen V → IsAffineOpen (U ⊓ V),
    ∃ 𝒰 : Scheme.AffineOpenCover.{u} X,
      ∀ (p : ℕ) (i : Fin (p + 1) → 𝒰.I₀),
        IsAffineOpen (⨅ j, (𝒰.f (i j)).opensRange)]
declarations.comment: equivalent conditions

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsSeparated.isSeparated_terminal_from
registrations.comment: separated case: the structure morphism is separated

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated.isClosedImmersion_diagonal
registrations.comment: separated case: the diagonal is a closed immersion

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion.instIsAffineHom
registrations.comment: separated case: closed immersions are affine

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.QcohDelta.exists_mono_isZero_hfunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BDY, part (1).** On a quasi-compact scheme with affine diagonal every
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ` admits an embedding `ℱ → ℱ'` into a quasi-coherent module with
`Hᵖ(X, ℱ') = 0` for all `p ≥ 1`.

Take `ℱ' = ∏ᵢ (ιᵢ)_*(ℱ|_{Uᵢ})` for a finite affine open cover `X = ⋃ Uᵢ`: each `ιᵢ` is affine
because the diagonal of `X` is, so `ℱ'` is quasi-coherent and its cohomology is the product of
the cohomologies of the `ℱ|_{Uᵢ}` on the affine schemes `Uᵢ`, which vanish in positive
degrees.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mono_isZero_hfunctor (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal (terminal.from X))]
    (F : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory) :
    ∃ (G : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory) (φ : F ⟶ G),
      Mono ((ObjectProperty.ι (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)).map φ) ∧
        ∀ p : ℕ, 0 < p → IsZero ((Hfunctor X.ringCatSheaf ⊤ p).obj G.obj)
declarations.comment: part (1): the embedding with vanishing higher cohomology

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.QcohDelta.cohomologyDeltaFunctor_isUniversal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BDY, part (2).** On a quasi-compact scheme with affine diagonal the cohomology
functors `{Hⁿ(X, -)}_{n ≥ 0}` form a *universal* δ-functor from `QCoh(𝒪_X)` to `Ab`.

Part (1) effaces every positive-degree component, and an effaceable δ-functor is universal.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologyDeltaFunctor_isUniversal [CompactSpace X]
    [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal (terminal.from X))] :
    (cohomologyDeltaFunctor X).IsUniversal
declarations.comment: part (2): universality of the delta-functor

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.exists_normOfDegree_reduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BDZ.** On a Noetherian scheme in prime characteristic `p` a
sufficiently high Frobenius power supplies a norm of degree a positive power of `p` for the
canonical morphism from the reduction.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_normOfDegree_reduction (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hchar : (p : Γ(X, ⊤)) = 0) :
    ∃ e : ℕ, 0 < e ∧
      HasNormOfDegree (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (⊤ : Closeds X)).subschemeι
        (p ^ e)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyFinite_irreducibleComponents_image
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BE1.** The images of the irreducible components of a closed subscheme of a locally
Noetherian scheme form a locally finite family in the ambient scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyFinite_irreducibleComponents_image
    {X Z : Scheme} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] :
    LocallyFinite (fun C : irreducibleComponents Z ↦ i '' (C : Set Z))

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.PrimeDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BE2 (1).** A prime divisor of `X` is an integral closed subscheme of codimension
one, recorded by its ideal sheaf.
declarations.statement: structure PrimeDivisor (X : Scheme.{u})
declarations.comment: part (1): prime divisors

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.WeilDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BE2 (2).** The group `Div(X)` of Weil divisors: integer-valued coefficient
families indexed by the prime divisors of `X` whose nonzero prime divisors form a locally finite
collection of closed subsets of `X`.
declarations.statement: def WeilDivisor (X : Scheme.{u}) : AddSubgroup (PrimeDivisor X → ℤ)
declarations.comment: part (2): Weil divisors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.PrimeDivisor
declarations.doc:
A prime divisor of a scheme is an integral closed subscheme of codimension one, presented by
its ideal sheaf. The codimension is that of the closure in the ambient scheme of the image of the
generic point of the subscheme.
declarations.statement: structure PrimeDivisor (X : Scheme.{u})
declarations.comment: part (1): prime divisors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.WeilDivisor
declarations.doc:
The Weil divisors of a scheme: the integral coefficient families indexed by prime divisors
whose prime divisors with nonzero coefficient have locally finite supports. The additive group
structure is the coefficientwise one.
declarations.statement: def WeilDivisor (X : Scheme.{u}) : AddSubgroup (PrimeDivisor X → ℤ)
declarations.comment: part (2): Weil divisors

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.principalCycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BE3.** The principal divisor `div(f) = ∑_Z ord_Z(f) [Z]` of a rational function on
a locally Noetherian integral scheme, as an algebraic cycle: the integral closed subscheme
`closure {z}` is indexed by its generic point `z`, and carries the coefficient `ord_z(f)`. Local
finiteness of the family of prime divisors involved is Stacks 02RL.
declarations.statement:
def principalCycle (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (f : X.functionField) : AlgebraicCycle X ℤ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.weilDivisorClassGroup
declarations.doc:
The Weil divisor class group `Cl(X)` of a locally Noetherian integral
scheme: the group of Weil divisors modulo the subgroup of principal Weil divisors.
declarations.statement: abbrev weilDivisorClassGroup : Type u

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.weilDivisorClassOfInvertibleSheaf
declarations.doc:
The Weil divisor class of an invertible sheaf on a locally Noetherian integral scheme: the
class in `Cl(X)` of the Weil divisor of a chosen regular meromorphic section of `L`.
declarations.statement: def weilDivisorClassOfInvertibleSheaf : weilDivisorClassGroup X
declarations.comment: part (2): divisor class of an invertible sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.weilDivisorClassOfInvertibleSheaf_eq
declarations.doc:
The Weil divisor of any regular meromorphic section of an invertible sheaf `L` has class
`AlgebraicGeometry.weilDivisorClassOfInvertibleSheaf X L` in `Cl(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem weilDivisorClassOfInvertibleSheaf_eq (s : MeromorphicSection X.sheaf L)
    (hs : IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf L s) :
    weilDivisorClassOfInvertibleSheaf X L =
      ((weilDivisorOfMeromorphicSection X L s hs : WeilDivisor X) :
        weilDivisorClassGroup X)
declarations.comment: part (2): independence of the meromorphic section

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.weilDivisorOfMeromorphicSection
declarations.doc:
The Weil divisor `div_L(s) = ∑_Z ord_{Z, L}(s) [Z]` of a regular meromorphic section of an
invertible module on a locally Noetherian integral scheme.
declarations.statement: def weilDivisorOfMeromorphicSection : WeilDivisor X
declarations.comment: part (1): divisor of a meromorphic section

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.picardToWeilDivisorClassGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BE7: the first Chern class.** On a locally Noetherian integral scheme the Weil
divisor class of an invertible module defines a homomorphism from the Picard group to the Weil
divisor class group. Additivity is the divisor-class additivity of Tag 02SL,
`AlgebraicGeometry.weilDivisorClassOfInvertibleSheaf_tensorObj`, and well-definedness on
isomorphism classes is `AlgebraicGeometry.weilDivisorClassOfInvertibleSheaf_congr`;
`AlgebraicGeometry.weilDivisorClassOfPicardClass_picardClass` is the characterization of this
homomorphism on the class of an invertible module.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.picardToWeilDivisorClassGroup_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BE8.** On a normal locally Noetherian integral scheme the first Chern class
`Pic(X) → Cl(X)` of Tag 0BE7 is injective.

The map is a group homomorphism, so it is enough that a Picard class in its kernel vanishes.
Such a class is the Picard class of an invertible module `L`, whose image is the Weil divisor
class of `L`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_iso_unit_of_weilDivisorClassOfInvertibleSheaf_eq_zero` then makes
`L` isomorphic to `𝒪_X`, which is triviality of the Picard class.
declarations.statement:
theorem picardToWeilDivisorClassGroup_injective [IsNormal X] :
    Function.Injective (picardToWeilDivisorClassGroup X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isNormal_of_forall_uniqueFactorizationMonoid_stalk
declarations.doc:
A scheme whose local rings are unique factorization domains is normal: a unique
factorization domain is integrally closed, which is Tag 0AFV.

**Stacks 0BE9**, the normality half of the implication from condition (1) to condition (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem isNormal_of_forall_uniqueFactorizationMonoid_stalk
    (h : ∀ x : X, UniqueFactorizationMonoid (X.presheaf.stalk x)) : IsNormal X
declarations.comment: (1) → (2): factorial local rings give a normal scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.picardToWeilDivisorClassGroup_bijective
declarations.doc:
On a normal locally Noetherian integral scheme a surjective first Chern class
`Pic(X) → Cl(X)` is bijective, since it is injective by Tag 0BE8.

**Stacks 0BE9**, the final clause under condition (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem picardToWeilDivisorClassGroup_bijective [IsNormal X]
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (picardToWeilDivisorClassGroup X)) :
    Function.Bijective (picardToWeilDivisorClassGroup X)
declarations.comment: final clause under (2): on a normal scheme a surjective c_1 is bijective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.forall_uniqueFactorizationMonoid_stalk_iff_isNormal_and_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BE9.** For a locally Noetherian integral scheme the local rings are unique
factorization domains exactly when the scheme is normal and the first Chern class
`Pic(X) → Cl(X)` of Tag 0BE7 is surjective.

Forwards, normality is `AlgebraicGeometry.isNormal_of_forall_uniqueFactorizationMonoid_stalk` and
surjectivity is `AlgebraicGeometry.picardToWeilDivisorClassGroup_surjective`; backwards this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.uniqueFactorizationMonoid_stalk_of_surjective_picardToWeilDivisorClassGroup`.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_uniqueFactorizationMonoid_stalk_iff_isNormal_and_surjective :
    (∀ x : X, UniqueFactorizationMonoid (X.presheaf.stalk x)) ↔
      (IsNormal X ∧ Function.Surjective (picardToWeilDivisorClassGroup X))
declarations.comment: the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.picardToWeilDivisorClassGroup_bijective_of_forall_uniqueFactorizationMonoid
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BE9, the final clause.** On a locally Noetherian integral scheme whose local rings
are unique factorization domains the first Chern class `Pic(X) → Cl(X)` is an isomorphism:
factoriality makes `X` normal, so Tag 0BE8 gives injectivity, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.picardToWeilDivisorClassGroup_surjective` gives surjectivity.
declarations.statement:
theorem picardToWeilDivisorClassGroup_bijective_of_forall_uniqueFactorizationMonoid
    (h : ∀ x : X, UniqueFactorizationMonoid (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    Function.Bijective (picardToWeilDivisorClassGroup X)
declarations.comment: the isomorphism Pic(X) = Cl(X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.forall_uniqueFactorizationMonoid_stalk_iff_isNormal_and_surjective_and_picardEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BE9.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian integral scheme and consider the first Chern
class `Pic(X) → Cl(X)` of Tag 0BE7. The following are equivalent:

1. the local rings of `X` are unique factorization domains, and
2. `X` is normal and `Pic(X) → Cl(X)` is surjective.

In this case `Pic(X) → Cl(X)` is an isomorphism.

The equivalence is
`AlgebraicGeometry.forall_uniqueFactorizationMonoid_stalk_iff_isNormal_and_surjective`, and the
isomorphism is
`AlgebraicGeometry.picardEquivWeilDivisorClassGroupOfForallUniqueFactorizationMonoid`, whose
underlying map is the first Chern class.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_uniqueFactorizationMonoid_stalk_iff_isNormal_and_surjective_and_picardEquiv :
    ((∀ x : X, UniqueFactorizationMonoid (X.presheaf.stalk x)) ↔
        IsNormal X ∧ Function.Surjective (picardToWeilDivisorClassGroup X)) ∧
      ((∀ x : X, UniqueFactorizationMonoid (X.presheaf.stalk x)) →
        ∃ e : Stacks.SheafOfModules.PicardGroup X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property ≃+
          weilDivisorClassGroup X, ∀ c, e c = picardToWeilDivisorClassGroup X c)
declarations.comment: the full statement: (1) ⟺ (2), and in that case Pic(X) ≅ Cl(X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tangentSpaceEquivFiber
declarations.doc:
The tangent space of `X` over `S` at `x` is canonically identified with the tangent space of
the fibre `X_{f(x)}` at its corresponding point.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def tangentSpaceEquivFiber : TangentSpaceFiberEquiv f x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tangentSpaceProductEquiv
declarations.doc:
The tangent space of a fibre product at a pair of points rational over the same base point
is the direct sum of the tangent spaces of the factors. The equivalence is induced by the
projections.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tangentSpaceProductEquiv {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S) (z : ↑(pullback f g))
    [IsIso (f.residueFieldMap (pullback.fst f g z))]
    [IsIso (g.residueFieldMap (pullback.snd f g z))] :
    TangentSpaceProductEquiv f g z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tangentSpaceProductFiberEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BEB.** Let `X`, `Y` be schemes over `S` and let `z = (x, y)` be a point
of `X ×_S Y` whose projections `x ∈ X`, `y ∈ Y` have residue fields `κ(x) = κ(s) = κ(y)`, where
`s` is their common image in `S` (every such pair `x`, `y` comes from a point `z`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.exists_preimage_pullback`). Then `z` is the only point over
`x` and `y`, and `T_{X ×_S Y/S, (x, y)} = T_{X/S, x} ⊕ T_{Y/S, y}` canonically: from left to
right by the tangent maps of the projections, from right to left by `1 × y : X_s → X_s ×_s Y_s`
and `x × 1 : Y_s → X_s ×_s Y_s` via the identification of tangent spaces with tangent spaces of
fibres (Stacks, Tag 0BEA).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tangentSpaceProductFiberEquiv {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S) (z : ↑(pullback f g))
    [IsIso (f.residueFieldMap (pullback.fst f g z))]
    [IsIso (g.residueFieldMap (pullback.snd f g z))] :
    TangentSpaceProductFiberEquiv f g z
declarations.comment: T_{X ×_S Y/S,(x,y)} = T_{X/S,x} ⊕ T_{Y/S,y} at the unique point (x,y): left to right by the projections, right to left by 1 × y and x × 1 on the fibres via 0BEA

declarations.name: Stacks.CechKunneth.kunnethIsoOfAffineDiagonal_eq
declarations.doc:
**The Künneth isomorphism is canonical**: it is the isomorphism
`Stacks.CechKunneth.kunnethIsoOfCovers` of *any* pair of finite affine coverings of `X` and `Y`,
which on Čech classes is the Alexander–Whitney product of the pulled-back cocycles
(`Stacks.CechKunneth.kunnethIsoOfCovers_symm_lof_tmul`).
declarations.statement:
theorem kunnethIsoOfAffineDiagonal_eq [CompactSpace X] [CompactSpace Y] (n : ℕ) :
    kunnethIsoOfAffineDiagonal k f g F G n = kunnethIsoOfCovers f g CX CY F G n
declarations.comment: the isomorphism is canonical: independent of the chosen finite affine covers, and on Cech classes given by the cup product of the pulled-back cocycles

declarations.name: Stacks.CechKunneth.kunnethIsoOfAffineDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**The Künneth formula** [Stacks, Tag 0BED]. For a field `k`, quasi-compact schemes `X` and `Y`
over `k` with affine diagonal, a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ` and a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_Y`-module `𝒢`,
`Hⁿ(X ×_k Y, pr₁^*ℱ ⊗_{𝒪_{X ×_k Y}} pr₂^*𝒢) ≅ ⨁_{p + q = n} Hᵖ(X, ℱ) ⊗_k H^q(Y, 𝒢)`.

The isomorphism is the one of the source: computed on finite affine coverings `𝒰` of `X` and `𝒱`
of `Y` (chosen by `Stacks.CechKunneth.finiteAffineCover`), it carries the class of the
Alexander–Whitney product of the pullbacks of two Čech cocycles — the Čech form of
`pr₁^*α ∪ pr₂^*β`, [Stacks, Tag 0BEE] — to `α ⊗ β`; see
`Stacks.CechKunneth.kunnethIsoOfCovers_symm_lof_tmul`. The cohomology groups are Mathlib's right
derived functors of global sections, regarded as `k`-modules through the structure morphisms
(`Stacks.CechKunneth.cohomologyK`).
declarations.comment: for X and Y quasi-compact with affine diagonal over a field k and F, G quasi-coherent: H^n(X x_k Y, pr_1^*F (x) pr_2^*G) is the direct sum over p + q = n of H^p(X, F) (x)_k H^q(Y, G), the isomorphism being the Cech-level cup product of pulled-back cocycles

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_kunnethIso_of_isAffineHom_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**The Künneth formula.** For quasi-coherent modules `F` on `X` and `G` on `Y`, with `X` and
`Y` quasi-compact schemes over a field `k` whose diagonals are affine, the cohomology of the
external tensor product `pr₁^*F ⊗ pr₂^*G` on `X ×_{Spec k} Y` is isomorphic to the direct sum of
the tensor products `Hᵖ(X, F) ⊗_k Hᑫ(Y, G)` over the pairs with `p + q = n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_kunnethIso_of_isAffineHom_diagonal
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [CompactSpace X] [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal (terminal.from X))]
    [CompactSpace Y] [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal (terminal.from Y))]
    (F : X.Modules) (G : Y.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent] (n : ℕ) :
    Nonempty
      (cohomologyOverField k (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) (externalTensorSheaf f g F G) n ≅
        ModuleCat.of k
          (⨁ pq : {pq : ℕ × ℕ // pq.1 + pq.2 = n},
            TensorProduct k (cohomologyOverField k f F pq.1.1)
              (cohomologyOverField k g G pq.1.2)))
declarations.comment: for X and Y quasi-compact with affine diagonal over a field k and F, G quasi-coherent: H^n(X x_k Y, pr_1^*F (x) pr_2^*G) is isomorphic to the direct sum over p + q = n of H^p(X, F) (x)_k H^q(Y, G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.KunnethQcqs.isIso_kunnethMap
declarations.doc:
