declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.isEquivalence_restrictionFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHB.** The functor `F` of Stacks 0BHA, base change of the modifications of `X`
away from the chosen closed points to the chosen elementary étale neighborhoods, is an
equivalence of categories.

The data `D : ClosedPointNeighborhoods B S hS n` is exactly the setting of Stacks 0BH9: a decent
algebraic space `X` over `S`, pairwise distinct closed points `x₁, …, xₙ ∈ |X|`, and for each `i`
an affine elementary étale neighborhood `(Uᵢ, uᵢ) → (X, xᵢ)` with `uᵢ` the only point above `xᵢ`
and no point above `xⱼ` for `j ≠ i`. It carries no excision or base-change hypothesis. The source
of `F` is the category of algebraic spaces over `X` that are isomorphisms over
`X ∖ {x₁, …, xₙ}`, its target the product of the categories of algebraic spaces over `Uᵢ` that
are isomorphisms over `Uᵢ ∖ {uᵢ}`. Full faithfulness is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.full_restrictionFunctor` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.faithful_restrictionFunctor`; essential
surjectivity is proved above from the case `n = 1` of Stacks 0BGY,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isModification_pullback_iso`, as in the source.
declarations.statement: theorem isEquivalence_restrictionFunctor : D.restrictionFunctor.IsEquivalence

declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHC, integrality.** A modification of `X` away from `{x₁, …, xₙ}` is integral
exactly when each of its restrictions under the functor `F` of Stacks 0BHA is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegralHom_iff_forall_restrictionComponent :
    IsIntegralHom B S hS M.obj.hom ↔
      ∀ i, IsIntegralHom B S hS ((D.restrictionComponent i).obj M).obj.hom
declarations.comment: integrality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.isFinite_iff_forall_restrictionComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHC, finiteness.** A modification of `X` away from `{x₁, …, xₙ}` is finite
exactly when each of its restrictions under the functor `F` of Stacks 0BHA is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_iff_forall_restrictionComponent :
    IsFinite B S hS M.obj.hom ↔
      ∀ i, IsFinite B S hS ((D.restrictionComponent i).obj M).obj.hom
declarations.comment: finiteness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.fibreAtPointIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHD.** If `f : Y ⟶ X` corresponds to `gᵢ : Yᵢ ⟶ Uᵢ` under the functor `F` of
Stacks 0BHA, then `Y_{xᵢ} ≅ (Yᵢ)_{uᵢ}` as algebraic spaces: both are the fibre product of `f`
with the monomorphism `Spec κ(uᵢ) ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
def fibreAtPointIso (M : D.modificationsAwayFromPoints) (i : Fin n) :
    fibreAtPoint M i ≅ fibreAtNeighborhoodPoint M i
declarations.comment: the fibres agree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBlowupAtClosedPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHE.** A morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces **is the blowing up of `X` at
the closed point `z`** when there is a blowing up of `X` in the reduced closed subspace
supported on `{z}` to which `f` is isomorphic over `X`.

Being the blowing up in a closed subspace is the universal property of Stacks 085U, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBlowupAlong`; it already determines the morphism up to isomorphism
over `X`, so asking for the isomorphism here changes nothing and makes
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBlowupAtClosedPoint.comp_iso` available.  The centre is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.closedPointSubspace`, which is the `i(Spec(k))` of the source by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_closedPointSubspace`.
declarations.statement:
def IsBlowupAtClosedPoint {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (z : points B S hS X.obj)
    (hz : IsClosed ({z} : Set (points B S hS X.obj))) (f : Y ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.BlowupFactorization
declarations.doc:
**A factorization of `f : Y ⟶ X` as a sequence of blowings up at closed points lying over
the set of points `T ⊆ |X|`**: a tower

`Zₘ ⟶ Zₘ₋₁ ⟶ … ⟶ Z₁ ⟶ Z₀ = X`

of blowings up at closed points, all of whose centres lie over `T`, together with an
identification of `Y` with its top `Zₘ` under which `f` is the composite `Zₘ ⟶ X`.

This is the condition on both sides of **Stacks 0BHF**, taken there with `T = {x₁, …, xₙ}` for
the morphism to `X` and with `T = {uᵢ}` for the morphism to the `i`th étale neighborhood.
declarations.statement:
structure BlowupFactorization (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (T : Set (points B S hS X.obj)) (f : Y ⟶ X)
declarations.comment:
the condition asserted on both sides of the equivalence: a factorization of the
given morphism as a finite sequence of blowings up at closed points lying over the given set of
points. The equivalence itself is
AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.nonempty_globalBlowupFactorization_iff.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.GlobalBlowupFactorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHF**, the condition on the morphism to `X`: `f : Y ⟶ X` factors as

`Y = Zₘ ⟶ Zₘ₋₁ ⟶ … ⟶ Z₁ ⟶ Z₀ = X`

where each `Z_{j+1} ⟶ Z_j` is the blowing up of `Z_j` at a closed point `z_j` lying over
`{x₁, …, xₙ}`.
declarations.statement: abbrev GlobalBlowupFactorization {Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : Y ⟶ D.space)
declarations.comment:
the condition on the morphism to X: it factors as a finite sequence of blowings
up at closed points lying over x₁, …, xₙ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.LocalBlowupFactorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHF**, the condition on the morphism to the `i`th étale neighborhood:
`gᵢ : Yᵢ ⟶ Uᵢ` factors as

`Yᵢ = Z_{i, mᵢ} ⟶ … ⟶ Z_{i, 1} ⟶ Z_{i, 0} = Uᵢ`

where each `Z_{i, j+1} ⟶ Z_{i, j}` is the blowing up of `Z_{i, j}` at a closed point lying over
`uᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev LocalBlowupFactorization (i : Fin n) {Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (g : Y ⟶ D.neighborhoodSpace i)
declarations.comment:
the condition on the morphism to the i-th étale neighborhood: it factors as a
finite sequence of blowings up at closed points lying over uᵢ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.nonempty_localBlowupFactorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHF, the "only if" direction.**  Let `X, xᵢ, Uᵢ ⟶ X, uᵢ` be as in Stacks 0BH9 and
let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces with base change `gᵢ : Yᵢ ⟶ Uᵢ` along
`Uᵢ ⟶ X`.  If `f` factors as a finite sequence of blowings up at closed points lying over
`{x₁, …, xₙ}`, then `gᵢ` factors as a finite sequence of blowings up at closed points lying
over `uᵢ`.

The sequence over `Uᵢ` is the base change of the given one, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.exists_blowupTower_of_isPullback`.  No
hypothesis on `f` beyond the cartesian square is used; in particular `f` need not be an
isomorphism over `X ∖ {x₁, …, xₙ}`, so the statement is stronger than the source's, which fixes
`f` in `C_{X, {x₁, …, xₙ}}`.
declarations.comment:
the only-if direction: a factorization of f as a sequence of blowings up at
closed points lying over x₁, …, xₙ gives, for each i, a factorization of its base change gᵢ as a
sequence of blowings up at closed points lying over uᵢ. The if direction is
AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.nonempty_globalBlowupFactorization_of_isPullback
and the equivalence itself is
AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.nonempty_globalBlowupFactorization_iff.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.nonempty_localBlowupFactorization_restrictionComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHF, the "only if" direction, for the functor `F` of Stacks 0BHA.**  Let
`X, xᵢ, Uᵢ ⟶ X, uᵢ` be as in Stacks 0BH9 and let `f : Y ⟶ X` be an object of
`C_{X, {x₁, …, xₙ}}` corresponding to `gᵢ : Yᵢ ⟶ Uᵢ` under `F`.  If `f` factors as a finite
sequence of blowings up at closed points lying over `{x₁, …, xₙ}`, then for every `i` the
morphism `gᵢ` factors as a finite sequence of blowings up at closed points lying over `uᵢ`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.nonempty_localBlowupFactorization` at
the cartesian square of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.isPullback_restrictionComponent_obj`, which is
what "corresponds under `F`" means.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_localBlowupFactorization_restrictionComponent
    (M : D.modificationsAwayFromPoints) (i : Fin n)
    (F : D.GlobalBlowupFactorization (ObjectProperty.homMk M.obj.hom :
      (⟨M.obj.left, M.property.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ D.space)) :
    Nonempty (D.LocalBlowupFactorization i (ObjectProperty.homMk
      ((D.restrictionComponent i).obj M).obj.hom :
      (⟨((D.restrictionComponent i).obj M).obj.left,
          ((D.restrictionComponent i).obj M).property.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
        D.neighborhoodSpace i))
declarations.comment:
the only-if direction at the functor F: a factorization of f as a sequence of
blowings up at closed points lying over x₁, …, xₙ gives, for each i, a factorization of
gᵢ = F(f)ᵢ as a sequence of blowings up at closed points lying over uᵢ. The if direction at F
is nonempty_globalBlowupFactorization_restrictionComponent and the equivalence itself is
AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.nonempty_globalBlowupFactorization_iff.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.nonempty_globalBlowupFactorization_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHF.**  Let `X, xᵢ, Uᵢ ⟶ X, uᵢ` be as in Stacks 0BH9 and let `f : Y ⟶ X` be an
object of the category `C_{X, {x₁, …, xₙ}}` of Stacks 0BHA.  Then `f` factors as a finite
sequence of blowings up at closed points lying over `{x₁, …, xₙ}` if and only if, for every
`i`, the morphism `gᵢ = F(f)ᵢ` factors as a finite sequence of blowings up at closed points
lying over `uᵢ`.

The "only if" direction is `nonempty_localBlowupFactorization_restrictionComponent` and the
"if" direction is `nonempty_globalBlowupFactorization_restrictionComponent`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_globalBlowupFactorization_iff (M : D.modificationsAwayFromPoints) :
    Nonempty (D.GlobalBlowupFactorization (ObjectProperty.homMk M.obj.hom :
        (⟨M.obj.left, M.property.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ D.space)) ↔
      ∀ i, Nonempty (D.LocalBlowupFactorization i (ObjectProperty.homMk
        ((D.restrictionComponent i).obj M).obj.hom :
        (⟨((D.restrictionComponent i).obj M).obj.left,
            ((D.restrictionComponent i).obj M).property.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
          D.neighborhoodSpace i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_blowupFactorization_isPullbackDefined_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a Noetherian algebraic space over `S` and let `T ⊆ |X|` be a
finite set of closed points `x` such that `X` is regular at `x` and the local ring of `X` at `x`
has dimension `2`. Let `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_X` be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, given by the closed
subspace `Z ⊆ X` it cuts out, such that `𝒪_X/ℐ` is supported on `T`, that is, `|Z| ⊆ T`. **Then
there is a sequence**

`X_m ⟶ X_{m-1} ⟶ … ⟶ X_1 ⟶ X_0 = X`

**where `X_{j+1} ⟶ X_j` is the blowing up of `X_j` at a closed point `x_j` lying above a point
of `T`, such that `ℐ𝒪_{X_m}` is an invertible ideal sheaf** — that is, such that the inverse
image of `Z` along the composite `X_m ⟶ X` is an effective Cartier divisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_blowupFactorization_isPullbackDefined_of_isNoetherian
    (hterm : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (hX : IsNoetherian B S hS hterm X.1)
    (T : Set (points B S hS X.1)) (hTfinite : T.Finite)
    (hTclosed : ∀ x ∈ T, IsClosed ({x} : Set (points B S hS X.1)))
    (hTregular : ∀ x ∈ T, IsRegularAt B S hS X.1 x)
    (hTdim : ∀ x ∈ T, localRingDimension B S hS x = 2)
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hZsupport : subspacePointSet B S hS X.1 Z.1 ⊆ T) :
    ∃ (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : Y ⟶ X),
      Nonempty (BlowupFactorization B S hS T f) ∧ IsPullbackDefined B S hS f Z
declarations.comment:
the lemma in full, with the source's hypotheses and conclusion and nothing
carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_blowupFactorization_factors_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Dominating a modification by blowing up closed points.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a
Noetherian algebraic space over `S` and let `T ⊆ |X|` be a finite set of closed points `x` such
that `X` is regular at `x` and the local ring of `X` at `x` has dimension `2`. Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be
a proper morphism of algebraic spaces which is an isomorphism over `U = X ∖ T`. **Then there
exist a sequence**

`X_n ⟶ X_{n-1} ⟶ … ⟶ X_1 ⟶ X_0 = X`

**where `X_{i+1} ⟶ X_i` is the blowing up of `X_i` at a closed point `x_i` lying above a point
of `T`, and a factorization `X_n ⟶ Y ⟶ X` of the composition.**
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_blowupFactorization_factors_of_isProper
    (hterm : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (hX : IsNoetherian B S hS hterm X.1)
    (T : Set (points B S hS X.1)) (hTfinite : T.Finite)
    (hTclosed : ∀ x ∈ T, IsClosed ({x} : Set (points B S hS X.1)))
    (hTregular : ∀ x ∈ T, IsRegularAt B S hS X.1 x)
    (hTdim : ∀ x ∈ T, localRingDimension B S hS x = 2)
    (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : Y ⟶ X) (hf : IsProper B S hS f.hom)
    (hfU : IsIso (pullback.snd f.hom (openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X.1 Tᶜ).ι)) :
    ∃ (X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (b : X' ⟶ X),
      Nonempty (BlowupFactorization B S hS T b) ∧ ∃ h : X' ⟶ Y, h ≫ f = b

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsNormalizedBlowupAtClosedPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHJ.** A morphism `f : X'' ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces **is the normalized blowing up
of `X` at the closed point `z`** when it is the composition of the normalization of a blowing up
of `X` at `z` with that blowing up: there are an algebraic space `X'`, a blowing up `b : X' ⟶ X`
of `X` at `z`, normalization data on `X'`, and an identification of `X''` with the normalization
carrying `f` to the normalization morphism followed by `b`.

The blowing up at `z` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBlowupAtClosedPoint`, and the normalization
is the datum `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData`.  The decency hypothesis and the
finiteness condition of Stacks 0BB1 are those of the source.
declarations.statement:
def IsNormalizedBlowupAtClosedPoint {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (_hX : IsDecentSpace B S hS X.obj)
    (_hXfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS X.obj)
    (z : points B S hS X.obj) (hz : IsClosed ({z} : Set (points B S hS X.obj)))
    (f : Y ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizedBlowupAtClosedPoint.isNormal_and_isNagata_and_isProper_of_isNagata
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHK.**  If `X` is Nagata, then the normalized blowing up of `X` at a closed point
`z` is a normal Nagata algebraic space proper over `X`.

Spelled out: for every normalized blowing up `X'' ⟶ X' ⟶ X` of `X` at `z` (Stacks 0BHJ), `X''`
is an algebraic space over `S`, it is normal, it is Nagata, and the composite `X'' ⟶ X` is
proper.  The only hypothesis is that `X` is Nagata.

The proof is the source's.  The blowing up `X' ⟶ X` is proper,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizedBlowupAtClosedPoint.isProper_proj` (Stacks 085Z, `X` being
locally Noetherian); hence `X'` is Nagata (Stacks 0BAU), the normalization `X'' ⟶ X'` is finite
(Stacks 0BB5), hence proper (Stacks 04NZ), and the composite is proper (Stacks 04XY); `X''` is
normal by Stacks 0BB4 and Nagata by Stacks 0BAU again.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNormal_and_isNagata_and_isProper_of_isNagata
    (hNagata : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.obj (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsNagataScheme T)) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS N.space.obj ∧
      HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS N.space.obj
        (fun T : Scheme.{u} => _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsNormal T) ∧
      HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS N.space.obj (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsNagataScheme T) ∧
      IsProper B S hS N.hom.hom
declarations.comment: the lemma in full, with NOTHING carried: for a Nagata X, every normalized blowing up of X at a closed point is an algebraic space, normal, Nagata, and proper over X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizedBlowupFactorization
declarations.doc:
**A factorization of `f : Y ⟶ X` as a sequence of normalized blowings up at closed points
lying over the set of points `T ⊆ |X|`**: a tower

`Zₘ ⟶ Zₘ₋₁ ⟶ … ⟶ Z₁ ⟶ Z₀ = X`

of normalized blowings up at closed points, all of whose centres lie over `T`, together with an
identification of `Y` with its top `Zₘ` under which `f` is the composite `Zₘ ⟶ X`.

This is the condition on both sides of Stacks 0BHL, taken there with `T = {x₁, …, xₙ}` for the
morphism to `X` and with `T = {uᵢ}` for the morphism to the `i`th étale neighborhood.
declarations.statement:
structure NormalizedBlowupFactorization (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (T : Set (points B S hS X.obj))
    (f : Y ⟶ X)
declarations.comment:
the condition asserted on both sides of the equivalence: a factorization of the
given morphism as a finite sequence of normalized blowings up at closed points lying over the
given set of points. The equivalence itself is not proved: its proof is the argument of
Tag 0BHF, which this library does carry, together with a comparison of a normalization with an
étale base change of it, which it does not.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.GlobalNormalizedBlowupFactorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHL**, the condition on the morphism to `X`: `f : Y ⟶ X` factors as

`Y = Zₘ ⟶ Zₘ₋₁ ⟶ … ⟶ Z₁ ⟶ Z₀ = X`

where each `Z_{j+1} ⟶ Z_j` is the normalized blowing up of `Z_j` at a closed point `z_j` lying
over `{x₁, …, xₙ}`.
declarations.statement: abbrev GlobalNormalizedBlowupFactorization {Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : Y ⟶ D.space)
declarations.comment: the left-hand side of the equivalence: the factorization of the morphism to X by normalized blowings up at closed points lying over {x₁, …, xₙ}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.LocalNormalizedBlowupFactorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHL**, the condition on the morphism to the `i`th étale neighborhood:
`gᵢ : Yᵢ ⟶ Uᵢ` factors as

`Yᵢ = Z_{i, mᵢ} ⟶ … ⟶ Z_{i, 1} ⟶ Z_{i, 0} = Uᵢ`

where each `Z_{i, j+1} ⟶ Z_{i, j}` is the normalized blowing up of `Z_{i, j}` at a closed point
lying over `uᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev LocalNormalizedBlowupFactorization (i : Fin n) {Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (g : Y ⟶ D.neighborhoodSpace i)
declarations.comment: the right-hand side of the equivalence: the factorization of the morphism to the i-th elementary étale neighborhood by normalized blowings up at closed points lying over uᵢ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods.nonempty_globalNormalizedBlowupFactorization_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHL, for normal `X`.** Let `X, xᵢ, Uᵢ ⟶ X, uᵢ` be as in Stacks 0BHA and let
`f : Y ⟶ X` correspond to `gᵢ : Yᵢ ⟶ Uᵢ` under the functor `F` of Stacks 0BHA. Assume that `X`
satisfies the equivalent conditions of Stacks 0BB1 and that `X` is normal. Then `f` factors as
`Y = Zₘ ⟶ … ⟶ Z₁ ⟶ Z₀ = X` with each `Z_{j+1} ⟶ Z_j` the normalized blowing up of `Z_j` at a
closed point over `{x₁, …, xₙ}` if and only if each `gᵢ` factors as
`Yᵢ = Z_{i, mᵢ} ⟶ … ⟶ Z_{i, 0} = Uᵢ` with each step the normalized blowing up at a closed point
over `uᵢ`.

The normality of `X` is not in the source, but the statement is false without it; see the module
documentation for a counterexample to each direction.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_globalNormalizedBlowupFactorization_iff
    (hXfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS D.space.obj)
    (hXn : Space.IsNormal B S hS D.space.obj) (M : D.modificationsAwayFromPoints)
    (N : ∀ i, D.modificationsAt i) (e : D.restrictionFunctor.obj M ≅ N) :
    Nonempty (D.GlobalNormalizedBlowupFactorization (ObjectProperty.homMk M.obj.hom :
        (⟨M.obj.left, M.property.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ D.space)) ↔
      ∀ i, Nonempty (D.LocalNormalizedBlowupFactorization i (ObjectProperty.homMk (N i).obj.hom :
        (⟨(N i).obj.left, (N i).property.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
          D.neighborhoodSpace i))
declarations.comment: corrected (erratum): with X normal; false as written without it, the normalized blowup normalizes the whole space (counterexamples to both directions in the module documentation); otherwise the full statement, under the source's hypotheses

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.NormalizedBlowupsNotEtaleLocal.not_stacks0BHL
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHL is false as published.** The source asserts, for every scheme `S`, every
decent algebraic space `X` over `S` satisfying the equivalent conditions of Stacks 0BB1, every
choice of pairwise distinct closed points `x₁, …, xₙ` and elementary étale neighbourhoods
`(Uᵢ, uᵢ) ⟶ (X, xᵢ)` as in Stacks 0BHA, and every `f : Y ⟶ X` corresponding to `gᵢ : Yᵢ ⟶ Uᵢ`
under the functor `F` of Stacks 0BHA, that `f` is a sequence of normalized blowings up at closed
points over `{x₁, …, xₙ}` if and only if each `gᵢ` is one at closed points over `uᵢ`. This is
the negation of that assertion, with exactly its hypotheses; `exists_counterexample` is a
counterexample to the "if" direction.

The statement holds once `X` is normal: this is `nonempty_globalNormalizedBlowupFactorization_iff`
in the namespace `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedPointNeighborhoods`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_stacks0BHL :
    ¬ ∀ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) (n : ℕ)
      (D : ClosedPointNeighborhoods B S hS n)
      (_ : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS D.space.obj)
      (M : D.modificationsAwayFromPoints) (N : ∀ i, D.modificationsAt i)
      (_ : D.restrictionFunctor.obj M ≅ N),
      Nonempty (D.GlobalNormalizedBlowupFactorization (ObjectProperty.homMk M.obj.hom :
          (⟨M.obj.left, M.property.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ D.space)) ↔
        ∀ i, Nonempty (D.LocalNormalizedBlowupFactorization i
          (ObjectProperty.homMk (N i).obj.hom :
            (⟨(N i).obj.left, (N i).property.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
              D.neighborhoodSpace i))
declarations.comment: refutation of the published statement: false without X normal; at X = Spec(Z/36Z), two closed points with non-reduced local rings, g₁ the normalized blowing up of U₁ at u₁ and g₂ = id are sequences of normalized blowings up, but the f corresponding to them is not, a nonempty sequence having a normal source and the empty one being an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_normalizedBlowUpChain_dominating
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHM.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a Noetherian Nagata algebraic space over
`S` with `dim(X) = 2`, and let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a proper birational morphism. Then there is a
commutative diagram

```
X_n ⟶ X_{n-1} ⟶ … ⟶ X_1 ⟶ X_0
 |                            |
 v                            v
 Y  ------------------------> X
```

where `X_0 ⟶ X` is the normalization and `X_{i+1} ⟶ X_i` is the normalized blowing up of `X_i`
at a closed point: a sequence `NormalizedBlowUpChain B S hS X A g` with top `A = X_n` and
composite `g : X_n ⟶ X`, and `h : X_n ⟶ Y` with `h ≫ f = g`.

Being Noetherian is Stacks 03EA (quasi-compact, quasi-separated, locally Noetherian), Nagata is
the étale-local property of Stacks 03E6, `dim(X)` is Stacks 04N6, properness is Stacks 04XU, and
birationality is Stacks 0ACV, which is defined for decent spaces with finitely many irreducible
components; those witnesses are carried existentially, being consequences of the Noetherian
hypothesis and of properness rather than extra assumptions.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_normalizedBlowUpChain_dominating {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (hXN : IsNoetherian B S hS B.contains_terminal X.obj)
    (hXnag : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.obj (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsNagataScheme T))
    (hXdim : dimension B S hS X.obj X.property = 2) (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hf : IsProper B S hS f.hom)
    (hbir : ∃ (hDY : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y.obj) (hDX : IsDecentSpace B S hS X.obj)
      (hCY : (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS Y.obj)).Finite)
      (hCX : (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS X.obj)).Finite),
      IsBirational B S hS Y.property X.property hDY hDX hCY hCX f.hom) :
    ∃ (A : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (g : A ⟶ X) (h : A ⟶ Y),
      NormalizedBlowUpChain B S hS X A g ∧ h ≫ f = g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_adicCompletion_ringEquiv_henselianLocalRing_completionSpace
declarations.doc:
Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a local ring with finitely generated maximal ideal, let `X` be a decent
algebraic space over `Spec A` and let `Y = X ×_{Spec A} Spec A^` be its base change to the
`𝔪`-adic completion of `A`. For a point `q` of `Y` whose image `p` in `X` lies over the closed
point of `Spec A`, the canonical local homomorphism `𝒪^h_{X,p} ⟶ 𝒪^h_{Y,q}` — the one compatible
with the local rings of a pair of corresponding elementary étale neighborhoods — induces an
isomorphism on `𝔪`-adic completions.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_adicCompletion_ringEquiv_henselianLocalRing_completionSpace
    (hfg : (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).FG)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (hXdec : IsDecentSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (q : points B (Spec (.of A)) hA (completionSpace A B hA hAc f))
    (p : points B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (hp : pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA (completionSpace A B hA hAc f)
      (completionProjection A B hA hAc f) q = p)
    (hclosed : pointsToScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hA)))
        (pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA X f p) =
      (⟨IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A, inferInstance⟩ : PrimeSpectrum A)) :
    letI hY := isAlgebraicSpace_completionSpace A B hA hAc f hX
    letI hYdec := isDecentSpace_completionSpace A B hA hAc f hX hXdec
    letI := isLocalRing_henselianLocalRing B (Spec (.of A)) hA hX hXdec p
    letI := isLocalRing_henselianLocalRing B (Spec (.of A)) hA hY hYdec q
    ∃ φ : (henselianLocalRing B (Spec (.of A)) hA X hX p hXdec : Type (u + 1)) →+*
        (henselianLocalRing B (Spec (.of A)) hA (completionSpace A B hA hAc f) hY q hYdec :
          Type (u + 1)),
      IsLocalHom φ ∧
      (∃ (E : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B (Spec (.of A)) hA X hX p)
          (N : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B (Spec (.of A)) hA
            (completionSpace A B hA hAc f) hY q)
          (j : N.scheme ⟶ E.scheme) (hj : j.left.1 N.point = E.point),
        yoneda.map j ≫ E.toSpace = N.toSpace ≫ completionProjection A B hA hAc f ∧
          φ.comp (stalkToHenselianLocalRing B (Spec (.of A)) hA X hX p hXdec E) =
            (stalkToHenselianLocalRing B (Spec (.of A)) hA (completionSpace A B hA hAc f) hY q
                hYdec N).comp
              ((E.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalkCongr (Inseparable.of_eq hj.symm)).hom ≫
                j.left.1.stalkMap N.point).hom) ∧
      ∃ e : AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal
            (henselianLocalRing B (Spec (.of A)) hA X hX p hXdec : Type (u + 1)))
            (henselianLocalRing B (Spec (.of A)) hA X hX p hXdec : Type (u + 1)) ≃+*
          AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal
            (henselianLocalRing B (Spec (.of A)) hA (completionSpace A B hA hAc f) hY q hYdec :
              Type (u + 1)))
            (henselianLocalRing B (Spec (.of A)) hA (completionSpace A B hA hAc f) hY q hYdec :
              Type (u + 1)),
        e.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap _ _) = (algebraMap _ _).comp φ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRegularLocalRing_henselianLocalRing_of_completion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHQ, part (1).** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring, let `X` be a decent
algebraic space locally of finite type over `Spec A` and let `Y = X ×_{Spec A} Spec A^` be its
base change to the `𝔪`-adic completion. If the henselian local ring of `Y` at a point `y` is
regular, then so is the henselian local ring of `X` at the image of `y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularLocalRing_henselianLocalRing_of_completion
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (hXdec : IsDecentSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B (Spec (.of A)) hA f)
    (y : points B (Spec (.of A)) hA (completionSpace A B hA hAc f))
    (hy : IsRegularLocalRing
      (henselianLocalRing B (Spec (.of A)) hA (completionSpace A B hA hAc f)
        (isAlgebraicSpace_completionSpace A B hA hAc f hX) y
        (isDecentSpace_completionSpace A B hA hAc f hX hXdec) : Type (u + 1))) :
    IsRegularLocalRing
      (henselianLocalRing B (Spec (.of A)) hA X hX
        (pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA (completionSpace A B hA hAc f)
          (completionProjection A B hA hAc f) y) hXdec : Type (u + 1))
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRegularLocalRing_henselianLocalRing_completion_iff
declarations.doc:
Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring, let `X` be a decent algebraic space locally of finite
type over `Spec A` and let `Y = X ×_{Spec A} Spec A^` be its base change to the `𝔪`-adic
completion. At a point `y` of `Y` lying over the closed point of `Spec A^`, the henselian local
ring of `Y` at `y` is regular if and only if the henselian local ring of `X` at the image of `y`
is regular.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularLocalRing_henselianLocalRing_completion_iff
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (hXdec : IsDecentSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B (Spec (.of A)) hA f)
    (y : points B (Spec (.of A)) hA (completionSpace A B hA hAc f))
    (hy : pointsToScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA (completionBase A B hA hAc)
        (pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA (completionSpace A B hA hAc f)
          (pullback.snd f (completionBaseMap A B hA hAc)) y) =
      (⟨IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A),
        inferInstance⟩ :
        PrimeSpectrum (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A))) :
    IsRegularLocalRing
        (henselianLocalRing B (Spec (.of A)) hA (completionSpace A B hA hAc f)
          (isAlgebraicSpace_completionSpace A B hA hAc f hX) y
          (isDecentSpace_completionSpace A B hA hAc f hX hXdec) : Type (u + 1)) ↔
      IsRegularLocalRing
        (henselianLocalRing B (Spec (.of A)) hA X hX
          (pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA (completionSpace A B hA hAc f)
            (completionProjection A B hA hAc f) y) hXdec : Type (u + 1))
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasEtaleLocalProperty_isRegular_completionSpace_iff_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHQ, part (3).** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring and let `X` be a decent
algebraic space proper over `Spec A`. Then `X` is regular if and only if its base change
`Y = X ×_{Spec A} Spec A^` to the `𝔪`-adic completion of `A` is regular.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEtaleLocalProperty_isRegular_completionSpace_iff_of_isProper
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (hXdec : IsDecentSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (hproper : IsProper B (Spec (.of A)) hA f) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B (Spec (.of A)) hA X (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsRegular T) ↔
      HasEtaleLocalProperty B (Spec (.of A)) hA (completionSpace A B hA hAc f)
        (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsRegular T)
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinite_normalization_of_isAnalyticallyUnramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHR.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be an analytically unramified Noetherian local ring and let
`F` be an algebraic space over `S` whose structure morphism goes to an object of the site with
underlying scheme `Spec A`. If `F` is locally of finite type over `A` and its structure
morphism is étale at every point of codimension zero, then **the** normalization morphism
`F^ν ⟶ F` of `F` is a finite morphism of algebraic spaces.

The normalization is the constructed one, neither assumed nor existentially quantified: `F` is
locally of finite type over a Noetherian ring, so its étale scheme charts are locally
Noetherian and satisfy the finiteness condition of Tag 0BB1, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.normalizationData` is then the normalization of `F`, unique up to a
unique isomorphism over `F` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.existsUnique_iso_hom`. Finiteness of its
normalization morphism is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.isFinite_hom_of_isAnalyticallyUnramified`, which is
Stacks 0BG8 on a surjective étale chart followed by the étale-local characterisation of
finiteness, condition (3) of Stacks 03ZQ.

The base is a representable presheaf with an isomorphism of its underlying scheme onto
`Spec A`, which is the source's hypothesis with no identification of schemes imposed and with
the base scheme `S` of the site left arbitrary.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_normalization_of_isAnalyticallyUnramified {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] (hA : IsAnalyticallyUnramified A)
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    {Z : BigFppfOver B S hS} (f : F ⟶ yoneda.obj Z)
    (a : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [IsIso a]
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (het : ∀ x : points B S hS F, localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 → IsEtaleAt B S hS f x) :
    IsFinite B S hS (normalizationData B S hS hF
      (hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f a hft)).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinite_normalization_and_exists_isDenseOpenSubspace_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHT.** Let `Y` be a Noetherian integral algebraic space over `S`, and suppose there
is an alteration `f : X ⟶ Y` with `X` regular. Then the normalization `Y^ν ⟶ Y` of `Y` is a
finite morphism of algebraic spaces, and `Y` has a dense open subspace which is regular.

Integrality of `Y` is part of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAlteration`. Noetherianity is
Stacks 03EA, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsNoetherian`; its local Noetherianity makes the étale
scheme charts of `Y` satisfy the finiteness condition of Stacks 0BB1, so that
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.normalizationData` is the normalization of `Y`, unique up to a unique
isomorphism over `Y` by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.existsUnique_iso_hom`.

The first assertion is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinite_normalization_of_regular_alteration`
and the second is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isDenseOpenSubspace_hasEtaleLocalProperty_isRegular`. The source
proves finiteness by étale localization to the spectrum of a Noetherian domain followed by
Stacks 08AR; that reduction is not valid for algebraic spaces, whose étale charts need not be
irreducible, and the proof used here goes instead through Chow's lemma (Stacks 089J) over an
affine chart, as the module docstring of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.NormalizationFiniteRegularAlteration` explains.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_normalization_and_exists_isDenseOpenSubspace_isRegular
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (hYnoeth : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsAlteration B S hS f)
    (hXreg : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsRegular T)) :
    IsFinite B S hS (normalizationData B S hS hf.1
        (hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_of_isLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y hf.1
          hYnoeth.2.2)).hom ∧
      ∃ V : Subfunctor Y, IsDenseOpenSubspace B S hS hf.1 V ∧
        HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS V.toFunctor (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsRegular T)
declarations.comment: both assertions: finiteness of the normalization and the existence of a regular dense open. The source's Step 1, etale localization to a Noetherian domain, does not apply to algebraic spaces (etale charts of an integral space need not be irreducible); finiteness is proved instead through Chow's lemma for spaces over an affine chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isRegularRing_localizationAway_of_regular_spaceAlteration
declarations.doc:
**A Noetherian local domain admitting an alteration by a regular algebraic space is regular
after inverting one nonzero element.** The dense regular open of [Stacks, Tag 0BHT] at the
representable target `Spec A` contains a nonempty basic open `D(a)` of `Spec A`, and
`Γ(D(a)) = A_a`.
declarations.statement: public alias exists_isRegularRing_localizationAway_of_regular_spaceAlteration
declarations.comment: clause (1), regular after inverting one element

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.module_finite_integralClosure_of_regular_spaceAlteration
declarations.doc:
**The integral closure of a Noetherian local domain admitting an alteration by a regular
algebraic space is a finite module over it.** The normalization of `Spec A` is finite by
[Stacks, Tag 0BHT], and it is the spectrum of the integral closure of `A` in `Frac(A)`
([Stacks, Tag 035P]).
declarations.statement: public alias module_finite_integralClosure_of_regular_spaceAlteration
declarations.comment: clause (2), finite integral closure

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isNormalRing_adicCompletion_integralClosure_of_regular_spaceAlteration
declarations.doc:
**The completion of the integral closure is normal.** With `C = Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` and `B` the
integral closure of `A` in `Frac(A)`, the inclusion `B ⊆ C` is a map of finite `A`-algebras and
`B` is a normal domain, so [Stacks, Tag 0BGH] reduces normality of `Bˆ` to normality of
`Cˆ = Aˆ ⊗_A C`, which is the global functions of the regular base change `X ×_{Spec A} Spec Aˆ`
([Stacks, Tag 073K], [Stacks, Tag 0BHQ]). Normality here is `IsNormalRing`, which for a finite
algebra over a Noetherian local ring is normality of the completions at the maximal ideals.
declarations.statement: public alias isNormalRing_adicCompletion_integralClosure_of_regular_spaceAlteration
declarations.comment: clause (3), normal completion of the integral closure

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRegularRing_genericFormalFibre_of_regular_spaceAlteration
declarations.doc:
**The generic formal fibre of a Noetherian local domain admitting an alteration by a regular
algebraic space is regular.** For an affine étale chart `V` of `X` through the generic point the
ring `Aˆ ⊗_A Γ(V, 𝒪_V)` is regular by [Stacks, Tag 0BHQ], and the generic formal fibre is
recovered by inverting `A ∖ {0}` and descending along the faithfully flat `Frac(A)`-algebra
`Frac(A) ⊗_A Γ(V, 𝒪_V)` by [Stacks, Tag 07NG].
declarations.statement: public alias isRegularRing_genericFormalFibre_of_regular_spaceAlteration
declarations.comment: clause (4), regular generic formal fibre

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isRegularRing_localizationAway_of_isAlteration_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**A Noetherian local domain admitting an alteration by a regular algebraic space is regular
after inverting one nonzero element.** The dense regular open of [Stacks, Tag 0BHT], read at the
representable target `Spec A` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.denseRegularOpenOfRegularAlteration`, contains a nonempty basic open
`D(a)` of `Spec A`, and `Γ(D(a)) = A_a`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isRegularRing_localizationAway_of_isAlteration_of_isRegular
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A)))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (g : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hA))))
    (hg : IsAlteration B (Spec (.of A)) hA g)
    (hreg : HasEtaleLocalProperty B (Spec (.of A)) hA X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsRegular T)) :
    ∃ a : A, a ≠ 0 ∧ IsRegularRing (Localization.Away a)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.module_finite_integralClosure_of_isAlteration_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**The integral closure of a Noetherian local domain admitting an alteration by a regular
algebraic space is a finite module over it.** This is clause (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0BHU]: `A` is
N-1 (`IsN1`).

The alteration makes `Spec A` an integral algebraic space carrying a regular alteration, so
[Stacks, Tag 0BHT] applies to it; `Spec A` is its own affine surjective étale scheme chart, the
identity being surjective and étale, and along that chart
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.isFinite_normalization_chart_of_regular_alteration`
gives that the normalization morphism of the *scheme* `Spec A` is finite. By [Stacks, Tag 035P]
that morphism is the spectrum map of `A ⟶ integralClosure A (Frac A)`, so the integral closure is
a finite `A`-module; that reading is
`AlgebraicGeometry.module_finite_integralClosure_of_isFinite_normalization`, which takes the
presenting ring of the scheme — here `A` itself — rather than its ring of global sections.

The source argues instead that `C = Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` is a finite `A`-module by [Stacks, Tag 08AR] and
integrally closed, and that the integral closure embeds into `C`; the route above replaces that
by Chow's lemma for algebraic spaces over the chart and the degree-zero case of
[Stacks, Tag 02O6] for *schemes*, which is how [Stacks, Tag 0BHT] is proved here.
declarations.statement:
public theorem module_finite_integralClosure_of_isAlteration_of_isRegular
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A)))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (g : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hA))))
    (hg : IsAlteration B (Spec (.of A)) hA g)
    (hreg : HasEtaleLocalProperty B (Spec (.of A)) hA X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsRegular T)) :
    Module.Finite A ↥(integralClosure A (FractionRing A))
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isNormalRing_adicCompletion_integralClosure_of_isAlteration_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**The completion of the integral closure of a Noetherian local domain admitting an
alteration by a regular algebraic space is normal.** This is part (3) of [Stacks, Tag 0BHU]. Let
`B` be the integral closure of `A` in `Frac(A)` and `C = Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`. Then `C` is a finite
`A`-module and a normal domain containing `A` ([Stacks, Tag 0BH3]), so `B ⊆ C`, and `Cˆ = Aˆ ⊗_A C`
is normal by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.globalFunctions_of_isAlteration_of_isRegular`;
[Stacks, Tag 0BGH] gives normality of `Bˆ`. Normality is `IsNormalRing`: every localization at a
prime is a normal domain, which for the finite algebra `Bˆ` over the complete local `Aˆ` is
normality of the completions of `B` at its maximal ideals.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNormalRing_adicCompletion_integralClosure_of_isAlteration_of_isRegular
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A)))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (g : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hA))))
    (hg : IsAlteration B (Spec (.of A)) hA g)
    (hreg : HasEtaleLocalProperty B (Spec (.of A)) hA X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsRegular T)) :
    IsNormalRing
      (AdicCompletion
        ((IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).map
          (algebraMap A ↥(integralClosure A (FractionRing A))))
        ↥(integralClosure A (FractionRing A)))
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRegularRing_genericFormalFibre_of_isAlteration_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**The generic formal fibre of a Noetherian local domain admitting an alteration by a regular
algebraic space is regular.** For an affine étale chart `V` of `X` through the generic point the
ring `Aˆ ⊗_A Γ(V, 𝒪_V)` is regular, and the generic formal fibre is recovered by inverting
`A ∖ {0}` and descending along the faithfully flat `Frac(A)`-algebra `Frac(A) ⊗_A Γ(V, 𝒪_V)`
by [Stacks, Tag 07NG]. Regularity of the completed base change of the chart is part (3) of
[Stacks, Tag 0BHQ], applied through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_injective_isRegularRing_adicCompletion_tensorProduct`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegularRing_genericFormalFibre_of_isAlteration_of_isRegular
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A)))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (g : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hA))))
    (hg : IsAlteration B (Spec (.of A)) hA g)
    (hreg : HasEtaleLocalProperty B (Spec (.of A)) hA X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsRegular T)) :
    IsRegularRing ((AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A) ⊗[A] (FractionRing A))
declarations.comment: part (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsResolutionOfSingularities
declarations.doc:
A *resolution of singularities* of a Noetherian integral algebraic space `Y` over `S` is a
modification `f : X ⟶ Y` whose source `X` is regular.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsResolutionOfSingularities {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (_hYnoeth : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ Y) (hYint : IsIntegralSpace B S hS Y)
    (_hdecentX : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    (_hdecentY : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasResolutionByNormalizedBlowUps
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHX.** A two-dimensional Noetherian integral algebraic space `Y` over `S` *has a
resolution of singularities by normalized blowups* when the normalization of `Y` can be
followed by finitely many normalizations of blowing ups at closed points, all of them proper
over `Y`, so as to reach a regular algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
abbrev HasResolutionByNormalizedBlowUps (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (_hYdim : dimension B S hS Y.obj Y.property = 2)
    (_hYnoeth : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ Y.obj)
    (_hYint : IsIntegralSpace B S hS Y.obj) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.tfae_resolution_of_dimension_eq_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BHY.** For a two-dimensional integral Noetherian algebraic space `Y` over `S`, the
following are equivalent: (1) there is an alteration `X ⟶ Y` with `X` regular; (2) `Y` has a
resolution of singularities; (3) `Y` has a resolution of singularities by normalized blowups;
(4) the normalization `Y^ν ⟶ Y` is finite, `Y^ν` has finitely many singular points, and the
completion of the henselian local ring of `Y^ν` at each of them is normal.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_resolution_of_dimension_eq_two (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (hYdim : dimension B S hS Y.obj Y.property = 2)
    (hYnoeth : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ Y.obj) (hYint : IsIntegralSpace B S hS Y.obj) :
    List.TFAE
      [∃ (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (f : X ⟶ Y.obj), IsAlteration B S hS f ∧
          HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsRegular T),
        ∃ (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
          (hdecentX : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (f : X ⟶ Y.obj),
          IsResolutionOfSingularities B S hS hZ hX Y.property hYnoeth hYint hdecentX
            (hYint.isDecentSpace B S hS Y.obj) f,
        HasResolutionByNormalizedBlowUps B S hS hZ Y hYdim hYnoeth hYint,
        ∀ D : NormalizationData B S hS Y.obj,
          D.IsSurfaceResolutionCriterion Y.property (hYint.isDecentSpace B S hS Y.obj)]

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.existsUnique_isArtinianRing_or_isRegularLocalRing_or_two_le_depth_or_exists_finite
declarations.doc:
**Kollár's four cases.** For a Noetherian local ring `(R, 𝔪)` exactly one of the following
holds: (0) `R` is Artinian; (1) `R` is regular of dimension `1`; (2) `depth_𝔪(R) ≥ 2`; (3) there
is a finite ring map `R → R'` to a nonzero ring, not an isomorphism, whose kernel and cokernel
are annihilated by a power of `𝔪` and for which `𝔪` is not an associated prime of `R'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem
    IsLocalRing.existsUnique_isArtinianRing_or_isRegularLocalRing_or_two_le_depth_or_exists_finite
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] :
    ∃! i : Fin 4,
      ![IsArtinianRing R,
        IsRegularLocalRing R ∧ ringKrullDim R = 1,
        2 ≤ Module.depth R (maximalIdeal R) R,
        ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : Algebra R R'), Nontrivial R' ∧
          Module.Finite R R' ∧ ¬ Function.Bijective (algebraMap R R') ∧
          maximalIdeal R ∉ associatedPrimes R R' ∧
          ∃ n : ℕ, maximalIdeal R ^ n * RingHom.ker (algebraMap R R') = ⊥ ∧
            maximalIdeal R ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule R R') ≤
              LinearMap.range (Algebra.linearMap R R')] i
declarations.comment:
The four alternatives are indexed by `Fin 4` in the order of the tag, so that
`∃!` states both that they cover and that they are pairwise exclusive. See the module docstring
for the spelling of each one, in particular for case (4).

declarations.name: PowerSeries.instIsIntegrallyClosed
declarations.doc:
The formal power series ring `R⟦X⟧` over a Noetherian normal domain `R` is a normal domain:
it is integrally closed in its fraction field. Together with `PowerSeries.instIsNoetherianRing`
and `PowerSeries.instIsDomain` this says that `R⟦X⟧` is a Noetherian normal domain.
declarations.statement:
public instance instIsIntegrallyClosed {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [IsIntegrallyClosed R] : IsIntegrallyClosed R⟦X⟧

declarations.name: isNagataRing_tfae_isAnalyticallyUnramified
declarations.statement:
theorem isNagataRing_tfae_isAnalyticallyUnramified {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    [IsNagataRing R,
      ∀ (S : Type (max u v)) [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] [Algebra R S] [Module.Finite R S]
        (m' : Ideal S) [m'.IsMaximal], IsAnalyticallyUnramified (Localization.AtPrime m'),
      ∀ (S : Type (max u w)) [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] [IsLocalRing S] [Algebra R S]
        [Module.Finite R S] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)], IsAnalyticallyUnramified S].TFAE

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.resolveCurve_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BI4.** For a one-dimensional integral Noetherian scheme `Y` the
following are equivalent: there is an alteration `X → Y` with `X` regular; there is a resolution
of singularities of `Y`; there is a finite sequence of blowups in closed points
`Y_n → … → Y_1 → Y` with `Y_n` regular; and the normalization `Y^ν → Y` is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem resolveCurve_tfae (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral Y] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (hYdim : topologicalKrullDim Y = 1) :
    List.TFAE [
      ∃ (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Y), IsAlteration f ∧ IsRegular X,
      ∃ (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Y), IsResolution f,
      ∃ (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Y), PointBlowupChain Y Set.univ X f ∧ IsRegular X,
      IsFinite (Scheme.normalization Y
        finite_irreducibleComponents_isCompactOpen_of_isNoetherian)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_pointBlowupChain_chainTransform_isRegular
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme and let `Y ⊆ X` be an integral closed subscheme of dimension
one admitting an alteration by a regular scheme — one of the equivalent conditions of
[Stacks, Tag 0BI4]. Then there is a finite chain of blowups of `X` at closed points along which
the strict transform of `Y` becomes a regular curve.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_pointBlowupChain_chainTransform_isRegular {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsNoetherian X] (Y : X.IdealSheafData) [IsIntegral Y.subscheme]
    (hYdim : topologicalKrullDim Y.subscheme = 1)
    (hY : ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (g : Z ⟶ Y.subscheme), IsAlteration g ∧ IsRegular Z) :
    ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (f : W ⟶ X) (J : W.IdealSheafData),
      PointBlowupChain X Set.univ W f ∧ ChainTransform Y f J ∧ IsIntegral J.subscheme ∧
        topologicalKrullDim J.subscheme = 1 ∧ IsRegular J.subscheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IntersectionMultiplicityContext.intersectionMultiplicity_natCast_eq_length
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BI6.** The intersection multiplicity at `p` is the length of the
local ring of the scheme-theoretic intersection as an `𝒪_{X,p}`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem intersectionMultiplicity_natCast_eq_length
    (S : IntersectionMultiplicityContext) :
    (S.intersectionMultiplicity : ℕ∞) =
      Module.length (S.X.presheaf.stalk S.p) S.intersectionLocalRing

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransformToCurve_isIso
declarations.doc: Part (1): a curve regular at the centre is unchanged by strict transform.
declarations.statement:
public theorem strictTransformToCurve_isIso
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (Y : X.IdealSheafData)
    [IsIntegral Y.subscheme] (hYdim : topologicalKrullDim Y.subscheme = 1)
    (p : X) (hp : IsClosed ({p} : Set X))
    (yPoint : Y.subscheme) (hyPoint : Y.subschemeι yPoint = p)
    (hregular : IsRegularLocalRing (Y.subscheme.presheaf.stalk yPoint)) :
    IsIso (transformToCurve Y p hp)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform_exceptional_unique
declarations.doc: Part (2): the strict transform has exactly one point on the exceptional fibre.
declarations.statement:
public theorem strictTransform_exceptional_unique
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (Y : X.IdealSheafData)
    [IsIntegral Y.subscheme] (hYdim : topologicalKrullDim Y.subscheme = 1)
    (p : X) (hp : IsClosed ({p} : Set X))
    (yPoint : Y.subscheme) (hyPoint : Y.subschemeι yPoint = p)
    (hregular : IsRegularLocalRing (Y.subscheme.presheaf.stalk yPoint)) :
    ∃! q : (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUp (centerIdeal p hp)),
      q ∈ (transformIdeal Y p hp).support ∧
      q ∈ (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal (centerIdeal p hp)).support
declarations.comment: part (2), unique point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform_exceptional_multiplicity_one
declarations.doc: Part (2): the exceptional intersection has multiplicity one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem
    strictTransform_exceptional_multiplicity_one
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (Y : X.IdealSheafData)
    [IsIntegral Y.subscheme] (hYdim : topologicalKrullDim Y.subscheme = 1)
    (p : X) (hp : IsClosed ({p} : Set X))
    (yPoint : Y.subscheme) (hyPoint : Y.subschemeι yPoint = p)
    (hregular : IsRegularLocalRing (Y.subscheme.presheaf.stalk yPoint))
    (q : (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUp (centerIdeal p hp)))
    (hq : q ∈ ((transformIdeal Y p hp) ⊔
      AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal (centerIdeal p hp)).support) :
    intersectionLength (transformIdeal Y p hp)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal (centerIdeal p hp)) q hq = 1
declarations.comment: part (2), multiplicity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform_intersectionMultiplicity_lt
declarations.doc: Part (3): an intersection surviving the blowup has smaller multiplicity.
declarations.statement:
public theorem
    strictTransform_intersectionMultiplicity_lt
    (S : AlgebraicGeometry.IntersectionMultiplicityContext.{u})
    (yPoint : S.y.subscheme) (hyPoint : S.y.subschemeι yPoint = S.p)
    (hregular : IsRegularLocalRing (S.y.subscheme.presheaf.stalk yPoint))
    (q : (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUp (centerIdeal S.p S.p_isClosed)))
    (hqExceptional : q ∈
      (AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal (centerIdeal S.p S.p_isClosed)).support)
    (hq : q ∈ ((transformIdeal S.y S.p S.p_isClosed) ⊔
      (transformIdeal S.z S.p S.p_isClosed)).support) :
    intersectionLength (transformIdeal S.y S.p S.p_isClosed)
      (transformIdeal S.z S.p S.p_isClosed) q hq <
      S.intersectionMultiplicity
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_pointBlowupChain_familyTransform_isRegular_pairwise_disjoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BI8.** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme and let
`Y : Fin n → X.IdealSheafData` be pairwise distinct integral closed subschemes of dimension one,
each admitting a finite chain of blowups in closed points with regular source — one of the
equivalent conditions of [Stacks, Tag 0BI4]. Then there is a finite chain of blowups of `X` at
closed points along which the strict transforms of the `Y i` become pairwise disjoint regular
curves.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_pointBlowupChain_familyTransform_isRegular_pairwise_disjoint
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] {n : ℕ} (Y : Fin n → X.IdealSheafData)
    (hYne : Function.Injective Y) (hYint : ∀ i, IsIntegral (Y i).subscheme)
    (hYdim : ∀ i, topologicalKrullDim (Y i).subscheme = 1)
    (hYres : ∀ i, ∃ (V : Scheme.{u}) (g : V ⟶ (Y i).subscheme),
      PointBlowupChain (Y i).subscheme Set.univ V g ∧ IsRegular V) :
    ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (f : W ⟶ X) (J : Fin n → W.IdealSheafData),
      PointBlowupChain X Set.univ W f ∧ FamilyTransform Y f J ∧
        (∀ i, IsIntegral (J i).subscheme ∧ topologicalKrullDim (J i).subscheme = 1 ∧
          IsRegular (J i).subscheme) ∧
        Pairwise fun i j : Fin n => Disjoint (J i).support (J j).support

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.IsStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor
declarations.doc:
An effective Cartier divisor locally cut out by a product of a nonempty initial segment of a
regular system of parameters.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (D : X.IdealSheafData) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor_iff
declarations.doc:
A locally Noetherian effective Cartier divisor has strict normal crossings
if and only if it is reduced and all finite nonempty intersections of its
irreducible components are regular of the expected codimension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor_iff {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (D : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D) :
    IsStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor D ↔
      (IsReduced D.subscheme ∧
        (∀ C : irreducibleComponents D.subscheme,
          IsEffectiveCartierDivisor
            (componentIdeal D C)) ∧
        (∀ J : Finset (irreducibleComponents D.subscheme), J.Nonempty →
          AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular (componentIntersection D J).subscheme ∧
            ∀ C : irreducibleComponents (componentIntersection D J).subscheme,
              codimension (IrreducibleCloseds.closureSingleton
                ((componentIntersection D J).subschemeι C.2.1.genericPoint)) =
                  (J.card : ℕ∞)))

declarations.name: Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.exists_pointBlowupChain_comap_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BIB.** Let `X` be a regular scheme of dimension (at most) two which is
quasi-compact, and let `Z ⊆ X` be a closed subscheme containing no irreducible component of `X` of
positive dimension: every point in the interior of `Z` is an isolated closed point of `X`. Then
there is a finite sequence `Xₙ → … → X₁ → X` of blowups at closed points, each lying over a point
of `Z`, such that the inverse image `Zₙ` of `Z` in `Xₙ` is an effective Cartier divisor.

On a locally Noetherian scheme the condition says exactly that every irreducible component of `X`
contained in `Z` is a single point; it holds in particular when `Z` contains no irreducible
component of `X` at all (`IsNowhereDense`). The isolated points of `X` inside `Z` are blown up
first, which removes them (`isOpenImmersion_blowUpToBase_of_isClopen`); what is left of `Z` then
contains no irreducible component, and
`exists_pointBlowupChain_comap_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_isNowhereDense` applies.

Both deviations from the literal source are forced. Without quasi-compactness the statement is
false: `Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.not_forall_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_comap_of_isNowhereDense`
(countably many copies of `𝔸²_ℚ`, `Z` one closed point in each). "Proper closed subscheme" cannot
be read literally as `Z ≠ X`, even for Noetherian `X`:
`Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.not_forall_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_comap_of_ne_bot`
(`X = 𝔸²_ℚ ⊔ 𝔸²_ℚ`, `Z` one copy, a component of dimension two). On an irreducible `X` the literal
reading implies the one used here (`isNowhereDense_support_of_ne_bot`). Both counterexamples are in
the sibling module `CartierInverseImageCounterexamples` (same directory).
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_pointBlowupChain_comap_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_isRegular
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 2) (Z : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hZ : ∀ x ∈ interior (Z.support : Set X), IsClopen ({x} : Set X)) :
    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : Y ⟶ X), PointBlowupChain X (Z.support : Set X) Y f ∧
      Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (Z.comap f)
declarations.comment: a closed subscheme containing no positive-dimensional irreducible component of a regular quasi-compact scheme of dimension at most two becomes an effective Cartier divisor after finitely many blowups at closed points lying over it

declarations.name: Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.exists_pointBlowupChain_comap_support_eq_isStrictNormalCrossings
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BIC.** Let `X` be a regular Noetherian scheme of dimension two and let
`Z ⊆ X` be a closed subscheme containing no irreducible component of `X` — the source's "proper
closed subscheme" — each of whose one-dimensional irreducible components satisfies the equivalent
conditions of [Stacks, Tag 0BI4], in the point-blowup form of clause (3) there. Then there is a
sequence `Xₙ → … → X₁ → X` of blowups at closed points such that the inverse image `Zₙ` of `Z` in
`Xₙ` is an effective Cartier divisor whose support is the support of a strict normal crossings
divisor.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_pointBlowupChain_comap_support_eq_isStrictNormalCrossings
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 2) (Z : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hZ : IsNowhereDense (Z.support : Set X))
    (hres : ∀ C : irreducibleComponents Z.subscheme,
      topologicalKrullDim (componentIdeal Z C).subscheme = 1 →
      ∃ (P : Scheme.{u}) (g : P ⟶ (componentIdeal Z C).subscheme),
        PointBlowupChain (componentIdeal Z C).subscheme Set.univ P g ∧
          AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular P) :
    ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (f : W ⟶ X), PointBlowupChain X Set.univ W f ∧
      IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (Z.comap f) ∧
      ∃ (hW : IsLocallyNoetherian W) (D : W.IdealSheafData),
        @IsStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor W hW D ∧
          ((Z.comap f).support : Set W) = (D.support : Set W)

declarations.name: Algebra.trace'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BIF** (trace).
The trace of an `R`-algebra `S`, defined as the linear-map trace of left multiplication
`mul R S : S →ₗ[R] End R S`. This works for any `R`-algebra (no commutativity or finite-freeness
assumption on `S`); it agrees with `Algebra.trace R S` whenever the latter is defined.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def trace' (R S : Type*) [CommSemiring R] [Semiring S] [Algebra R S] : S →ₗ[R] R
declarations.comment: trace

declarations.name: charPoly_mul_eq_minpoly_pow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BIG**.
For a finite free extension `R ⊆ S` and `x ∈ S` such that `R[x]` is free over `R` and `S` is
free over `R[x]`, the characteristic polynomial of `Algebra.lmul R S x` equals
`(minpoly R x) ^ [S : R[x]]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem charPoly_mul_eq_minpoly_pow (R : Type*) {S : Type*}
    [CommRing R] [Ring S] [Algebra R S] [Free R S] [Module.Finite R S]
    (x : S) [Free R R[x]] [Free R[x] S] :
    (mul R S x).charpoly = minpoly R x ^ Module.finrank R[x] S

declarations.name: norm_eq_neg_one_pow_finrank_mul_constantCoeff_minpoly_pow_finrank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BIH**.
For a finite extension `R ⊆ S` and `x ∈ S` such that `R[x]` is free over `R` and `S` is
free over `R[x]` (so that `S` is free over `R`), `norm R x` equals `(-1) ^ [S : R]` times the
constant coefficient of `minpoly R x` raised to the `[S : R[x]]`-th power.
declarations.statement:
theorem norm_eq_neg_one_pow_finrank_mul_constantCoeff_minpoly_pow_finrank (R : Type*) {S : Type*}
    [CommRing R] [Ring S] [Algebra R S] [Module.Finite R S]
    (x : S) [Free R R[x]] [Free R[x] S] :
    norm R x = (-1) ^ finrank R S * (minpoly R x).constantCoeff ^ finrank R[x] S

declarations.name: trace_restrictScalars
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BII** (trace).
In a tower `R ⊆ S ⊆ A` of free extensions, the `R`-trace of an `S`-linear endomorphism
`f : A →ₗ[S] A` factors through the `S`-trace: it equals `trace' R S` applied to `f.trace S A`.
This expresses the transitivity of trace at the level of endomorphisms. No finiteness is
assumed: if `S` is not finite over `R` or `A` is not finite over `S`, both sides are `0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem trace_restrictScalars (R : Type*) {S A : Type*}
    [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S] [Semiring A]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra S A] [Algebra R A] [IsScalarTower R S A]
    [Module.Free R S] [Module.Free S A]
    (f : A →ₗ[S] A) : (f.restrictScalars R).trace R A = trace' R S (f.trace S A)
declarations.comment: trace

declarations.name: charpoly_restrictScalars_of_tower
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BII** (generalization).
In a tower `R ⊆ S ⊆ A` of free extensions, with `A` finite over `S` and over `R`, the
characteristic polynomial of the `R`-linear endomorphism `f.restrictScalars R` is the polynomial
norm of the characteristic polynomial of the `S`-linear endomorphism `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem charpoly_restrictScalars_of_tower (R : Type*) {S A : Type*}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [AddCommGroup A]
    [Algebra R S] [Module S A] [Module R A] [IsScalarTower R S A]
    [Module.Free R S] [Module.Free S A] [Module.Finite S A]
    [Module.Free R A] [Module.Finite R A]
    (f : A →ₗ[S] A) : (f.restrictScalars R).charpoly = f.charpoly.norm R S
declarations.comment: generalization

declarations.name: charpoly_mul_of_tower
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BIJ** (generalization).
Specialization of `charpoly_restrictScalars_of_tower` to left-multiplication: in a tower
`R ⊆ S ⊆ A`, the characteristic polynomial of `mul R A x` equals the polynomial norm over `R[X]`
of the characteristic polynomial of `mul S A x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem charpoly_mul_of_tower (R S : Type*) {A : Type*}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Ring A]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra S A] [Algebra R A] [IsScalarTower R S A]
    [Module.Free R S] [Module.Free S A] [Module.Finite S A]
    [Module.Free R A] [Module.Finite R A]
    (x : A) : (mul R A x).charpoly = (mul S A x).charpoly.norm R S
declarations.comment: generalization

declarations.name: trace_trace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BIJ** (trace).
Transitivity of trace in a tower of free extensions:
`trace' R S ∘ trace' S A = trace' R A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem trace_trace (R S : Type*) {A : Type*}
    [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S] [Semiring A]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra S A] [Algebra R A] [IsScalarTower R S A]
    [Module.Free R S] [Module.Free S A]
    (x : A) : trace' R S (trace' S A x) = trace' R A x
declarations.comment: trace

registrations.name: Algebra.norm_norm
registrations.comment: norm

declarations.name: Algebra.discr'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BIM**.
The discriminant of an `R`-algebra `S` as an element of `QuotSq R`: when `S` is finite free over
`R`, return the class of `discr R b` for any chosen basis `b` (the class is independent of the
basis); otherwise return `0`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def discr' (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] : QuotSq R

declarations.name: Algebra.mk_discr_eq_discr'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BIM**.
For any `R`-basis `b` of `S`, the class of the basis-discriminant `discr R b` in `QuotSq R`
agrees with `discr' R S`, witnessing that the latter is well-defined independently of the
chosen basis.
declarations.statement:
theorem mk_discr_eq_discr' {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (b : Basis ι R S) :
    .mk R (discr R b) = discr' R S

declarations.name: Algebra.IsQuadraticExtension.of_field_char_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BIN** (characteristic two case).
A quadratic field extension `L/K` of a field of characteristic two is either purely inseparable
of the form `K[√a]` for a non-square `a` (with `discr' K L = 0`), or separable of the form
`K[X]/(X^2 + X - a)` for some `a ∈ K` not of the form `x(x+1)` (with `discr' K L = 1`).
declarations.statement:
theorem of_field_char_two (K L : Type*) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    [CharP K 2] [IsQuadraticExtension K L] :
    (discr' K L = 0 ∧ IsPurelyInseparable K L ∧
      ∃ a : K, ¬IsSquare a ∧ Nonempty (L ≃ₐ[K] QuadraticAlgebra K a 0)) ∨
    (discr' K L = 1 ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable K L ∧
      ∃ a : K, (∀ x : K, x * (x + 1) ≠ a) ∧ Nonempty (L ≃ₐ[K] QuadraticAlgebra K a 1))
declarations.comment: characteristic two case

declarations.name: Algebra.IsQuadraticExtension.of_field_two_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BIN** (characteristic not two case).
A quadratic field extension `L/K` over a field with `2 ≠ 0` is automatically separable,
its discriminant class is neither `0` nor `1`, and `L` is `K`-isomorphic to `K[√a]` for some
non-square `a ∈ K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem of_field_two_ne_zero (K L : Type*) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    [NeZero (2 : K)] [IsQuadraticExtension K L] :
    discr' K L ≠ 0 ∧ discr' K L ≠ 1 ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable K L ∧
      ∃ a : K, ¬IsSquare a ∧ Nonempty (L ≃ₐ[K] QuadraticAlgebra K a 0)
declarations.comment: characteristic not two case

declarations.name: Algebra.IsQuadraticExtension.classification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BIN**. Let `L/K` be an extension of fields of degree `2`. Then exactly one of the
following happens:
1. the discriminant is `0`, the characteristic of `K` is `2`, and `L/K` is purely inseparable,
   obtained by taking a square root of a non-square `a ∈ K`;
2. the discriminant is `1`, the characteristic of `K` is `2`, and `L/K` is separable (of the form
   `K[X]/(X^2 + X - a)` with `a` not of the form `x(x+1)`);
3. the discriminant is the class of a non-square `a ∈ K`, the characteristic of `K` is not `2`,
   and `L ≅ K[√a]` is obtained by taking a square root of the discriminant.
declarations.statement:
theorem classification (K L : Type*) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    [IsQuadraticExtension K L] :
    let P₁ := discr' K L = 0 ∧ ringChar K = 2 ∧ IsPurelyInseparable K L ∧
      ∃ a : K, ¬IsSquare a ∧ Nonempty (L ≃ₐ[K] QuadraticAlgebra K a 0)
    let P₂ := discr' K L = 1 ∧ ringChar K = 2 ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable K L ∧
      ∃ a : K, (∀ x : K, x * (x + 1) ≠ a) ∧ Nonempty (L ≃ₐ[K] QuadraticAlgebra K a 1)
    let P₃ := ringChar K ≠ 2 ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable K L ∧
      ∃ a : K, QuotSq.mk K a = discr' K L ∧ ¬IsSquare a ∧
        Nonempty (L ≃ₐ[K] QuadraticAlgebra K a 0)
    (P₁ ∨ P₂ ∨ P₃) ∧ ¬(P₁ ∧ P₂) ∧ ¬(P₁ ∧ P₃) ∧ ¬(P₂ ∧ P₃)
declarations.comment:
complete classification: the three cases hold in every characteristic and
exclude one another, case (3) with `L ≅ K[√a]` for `a` representing the discriminant

declarations.name: affineBlowup_baseChange_iso
declarations.doc:
The map `Φ` of `affineBlowup_baseChange` induces an isomorphism of `S`-algebras
`(S ⊗[R] R[I/a]) / (S ⊗[R] R[I/a])[b^∞] ≅ S[J/b]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem affineBlowup_baseChange_iso :
    Nonempty <|
      (TensorProduct R S (affineBlowup0BIP I a ha) ⧸
        torsionIdeal (TensorProduct R S (affineBlowup0BIP I a ha))
          (algebraMap S _ (algebraMap R S a)))
      ≃ₐ[S]
      (affineBlowup0BIP (I.map (algebraMap R S)) (algebraMap R S a)
        (Ideal.mem_map_of_mem _ ha))

declarations.name: Koszul.exists_affineBlowup_algEquiv_mvPolynomial_quotient_of_isH1Regular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BIQ.** The affine blowup algebra associated to an `H₁`-regular
sequence is the polynomial algebra on the ratios of the remaining terms by the first term,
modulo the evident linear relations.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_affineBlowup_algEquiv_mvPolynomial_quotient_of_isH1Regular
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {n : ℕ} (f : Fin (n + 1) → R)
    (hf : Koszul.IsH1Regular f) :
    Nonempty
      (affineBlowupAlgebraAway (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) (f 0) ≃ₐ[R]
        MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸
          Ideal.span
            (Set.range fun i : Fin n ↦
              MvPolynomial.C (f 0) * MvPolynomial.X i - MvPolynomial.C (f i.succ)))

declarations.name: propertyRing_iff_quotientCompletion_fibers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BIS.** A Noetherian ring has property `P` on all the formal fibres of its
localizations at prime ideals if and only if the corresponding completed localizations of
its prime quotients have property `P` after extension to the residue field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem propertyRing_iff_quotientCompletion_fibers
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (P : RingMapProperty.{u, u}) :
    IsPRing P R ↔
    (∀ (p q : PrimeSpectrum R) (_hqp : q.asIdeal ≤ p.asIdeal),
      let Q := R ⧸ q.asIdeal
      let S := Localization
        (Submonoid.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk q.asIdeal) p.asIdeal.primeCompl)
      P (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := Q)
        (A := AdicCompletion
          ((p.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk q.asIdeal)).map (algebraMap Q S)) S)
        (B := q.asIdeal.ResidueField)).toRingHom)

declarations.name: quasiFinite_preserves_formalFiberProperty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BIT.** Let `R → S` be a finite-type map of Noetherian rings and let
`q' ⊆ p'` be primes of `S`. If the map is quasi-finite at `p'`, then a property of
field-to-Noetherian-ring maps satisfying base change along finitely generated field extensions
and detection on localizations passes from the relevant formal fiber over `R` to that over `S`.
Consequently it passes between the formal fibers of the two local rings, and a quasi-finite
`R`-algebra over a `P`-ring is a `P`-ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiFinite_preserves_formalFiberProperty
    (P : RingMapProperty.{max u v w, max u v w x})
    (hbaseChange : ∀ (k K : Type (max u v w)) (A : Type (max u v w x))
      [Field k] [Field K] [CommRing A]
      [Algebra k K] [Algebra k A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [Algebra.EssFiniteType k K]
      [IsNoetherianRing (A ⊗[k] K)],
      P (algebraMap k A) →
        P (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := k) (A := A) (B := K)).toRingHom)
    (hlocal : ∀ (k : Type (max u v w)) (A : Type (max u v w x))
      [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
      [IsNoetherianRing A],
      (∀ q : PrimeSpectrum A,
        P (algebraMap k (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))) ↔ P (algebraMap k A))
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    (q' p' : Ideal S) [q'.IsPrime] [p'.IsPrime] (_hq'p' : q' ≤ p')
    [Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R p'] :
    (P.Holds.{u, u, max v w, x} (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R)
        (A := AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.under R p')))
          (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.under R p')))
        (B := (Ideal.under R q').ResidueField)).toRingHom →
      P.Holds.{v, v, max u w, x} (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := S)
        (A := AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p'))
          (Localization.AtPrime p')) (B := q'.ResidueField)).toRingHom) ∧
    (FormalFibersHaveAt.{u, max v w, x} P
        (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.under R p')) →
      FormalFibersHaveAt.{v, max u w, x} P (Localization.AtPrime p')) ∧
    (Algebra.QuasiFinite R S → IsPRingAt.{u, max v w, x} P R →
      IsPRingAt.{v, max u w, x} P S)

declarations.name: isPRing_iff_formalFibersHave_localization_maximal
declarations.doc:
For a property of ring maps satisfying ascent through regular maps and
faithfully flat descent, a Noetherian ring is a `P`-ring exactly when the formal fibres of its
localizations at maximal ideals have `P`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPRing_iff_formalFibersHave_localization_maximal
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (P : RingMapProperty.{max u v, max u v w})
    (hC : ∀ (A B C : Type (max u v))
      [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
      [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
      [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsNoetherianRing C]
      [Module.Flat A B] [Module.Flat B C],
      (∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A,
        P.Holds (algebraMap p.asIdeal.ResidueField (p.asIdeal.Fiber B))) →
      (∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B,
        Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular q.asIdeal.ResidueField (q.asIdeal.Fiber C)) →
      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A,
        P.Holds (algebraMap p.asIdeal.ResidueField (p.asIdeal.Fiber C)))
    (hD : ∀ (A B C : Type (max u v))
      [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
      [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
      [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsNoetherianRing C]
      [Module.Flat A B] [Module.FaithfullyFlat B C],
      (∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A,
        P.Holds (algebraMap p.asIdeal.ResidueField (p.asIdeal.Fiber C))) →
      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A,
        P.Holds (algebraMap p.asIdeal.ResidueField (p.asIdeal.Fiber B))) :
    IsPRingAt.{u, v, w} P R ↔
      ∀ (m : Ideal R) [m.IsMaximal],
        FormalFibersHaveAt.{u, v, w} P
          (Localization.AtPrime m)

declarations.name: isPRing_of_essFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BIV.** If a property of maps from fields to Noetherian rings satisfies
properties (A)--(D), then an essentially finite-type algebra over a `P`-ring is a `P`-ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPRing_of_essFiniteType
    (P : RingMapProperty.{max u v, max u v})
    (hA : ∀ (k K A : Type (max u v)) [Field k] [Field K] [CommRing A]
      [Algebra k K] [Algebra k A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [Algebra.EssFiniteType k K]
      [IsNoetherianRing (A ⊗[k] K)],
      P (algebraMap k A) →
        P (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := k) (A := A) (B := K)).toRingHom)
    (_hB : ∀ (k A : Type (max u v)) [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
      [IsNoetherianRing A],
      (∀ q : PrimeSpectrum A, P (algebraMap k (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))) ↔
        P (algebraMap k A))
    (hC : ∀ (A B C : Type (max u v))
      [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
      [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
      [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsNoetherianRing C]
      [Module.Flat A B] [Module.Flat B C],
      (∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A,
        P.Holds (algebraMap p.asIdeal.ResidueField (p.asIdeal.Fiber B))) →
      (∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B,
        Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular q.asIdeal.ResidueField (q.asIdeal.Fiber C)) →
      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A,
        P.Holds (algebraMap p.asIdeal.ResidueField (p.asIdeal.Fiber C)))
    (hD : ∀ (A B C : Type (max u v))
      [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
      [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
      [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsNoetherianRing C]
      [Module.Flat A B] [Module.FaithfullyFlat B C],
      (∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A,
        P.Holds (algebraMap p.asIdeal.ResidueField (p.asIdeal.Fiber C))) →
      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A,
        P.Holds (algebraMap p.asIdeal.ResidueField (p.asIdeal.Fiber B)))
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType R S]
    (hR : IsPRingAt.{u, v, v} P R) :
    IsPRingAt.{v, u, u} P S

declarations.name: geometricReducedness_satisfies_formalFibre_properties
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BIW.** Geometric reducedness satisfies properties (A)--(E) for formal fibres:
base change by a finitely generated field extension, detection on local rings, ascent along a
regular map, faithfully flat descent, and separable algebraic extension of the base field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricReducedness_satisfies_formalFibre_properties :
    (∀ (k : Type u) (k' : Type v) (R : Type w) [Field k] [Field k'] [CommRing R]
      [Algebra k k'] [Algebra k R] [Algebra.EssFiniteType k k'] [IsNoetherianRing R],
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced k R →
