declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.FilteredComplex.spectralSequence_of_filteredKInjectiveResolution
declarations.doc:
The spectral sequence of a filtered complex of module sheaves, computed by a supplied filtered
K-injective resolution: its pages are presented by the cycle and boundary subobjects of the
filtered complex of global sections, its first page is the hypercohomology of the graded pieces,
and under the boundedness hypotheses it converges to the hypercohomology of the complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem spectralSequence_of_filteredKInjectiveResolution
    (hRΓ : RΓ.IsRightDerivedFunctor α
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (j : K ⟶ J)
    (hj : QuasiIso j.hom)
    (hjStep : ∀ p : ℤ, QuasiIso (j.natTrans.app (op p)))
    (hjGraded : ∀ p : ℤ, QuasiIso ((FilteredObject.gr p).map j))
    (hStepInjective : ∀ p n : ℤ, Injective ((J.filtration.obj (op p)).X n))
    (hKInjective : J.X.IsKInjective)
    (hStepKInjective : ∀ p : ℤ, (J.filtration.obj (op p)).IsKInjective)
    (hGradedKInjective : ∀ p : ℤ, ((FilteredObject.gr p).obj J).IsKInjective) :
    let E := CochainComplex.Filtered.spectralSequenceFunctor.obj
      (globalSectionsFilteredComplex X J)
    ∃ (F : ∀ (_p n : ℤ), Subobject ((globalSectionsFilteredComplex X J).X.X n))
        (Z D : ∀ (_r _p n : ℤ),
          Subobject ((globalSectionsFilteredComplex X J).X.X n)),
        (∀ p n : ℤ, F p n = Subobject.mk
          (((globalSectionsFilteredComplex X J).filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n)) ∧
        (∀ r p n : ℤ, Z r p n = F p n ⊓
          (Subobject.pullback ((globalSectionsFilteredComplex X J).X.d n (n + 1))).obj
            (F (p + r) (n + 1))) ∧
        (∀ r p n : ℤ, D r p n = Z (r - 1) (p + 1) n ⊔
          (Subobject.«exists» ((globalSectionsFilteredComplex X J).X.d (n - 1) n)).obj
            (Z (r - 1) (p - r + 1) (n - 1))) ∧
        (∃ e : ∀ (r p q n : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (_ : n = p + q),
            (E.page r hr).X (p, q) ≅ cokernel
              (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (inf_le_right : D r p n ⊓ Z r p n ≤ Z r p n)),
          ∀ (r p q n : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hn : n = p + q),
            ∃ δ : (Z r p n : ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing X).obj.obj (op ⊤))) ⟶
                (Z r (p + r) (n + 1) : ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing X).obj.obj (op ⊤))),
              δ ≫ (Z r (p + r) (n + 1)).arrow =
                  (Z r p n).arrow ≫ (globalSectionsFilteredComplex X J).X.d n (n + 1) ∧
              cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE _ _
                  (inf_le_right : D r p n ⊓ Z r p n ≤ Z r p n)) ≫
                    (e r p q n hr hn).inv ≫
                    (E.page r hr).d (p, q) (p + r, q - r + 1) =
                δ ≫ cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE _ _
                    (inf_le_right : D r (p + r) (n + 1) ⊓ Z r (p + r) (n + 1) ≤
                      Z r (p + r) (n + 1))) ≫
                  (e r (p + r) (q - r + 1) (n + 1) hr (by omega)).inv) ∧
        (∀ p q : ℤ, Nonempty
          ((E.page 1 (by omega)).X (p, q) ≅
            hypercohomology X RΓ ((FilteredObject.gr p).obj K) (p + q))) ∧
        ((∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p₀ : ℤ, ∀ p : ℤ, p₀ ≤ p →
            IsZero (hypercohomology X RΓ (K.filtration.obj (op p)) n)) →
          (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p₁ : ℤ, ∀ p : ℤ, p ≤ p₁ →
            IsIso (hypercohomologyMap X RΓ (K.filtration.ι.app (op p)) n)) →
          (∀ n : ℤ, {p : ℤ | ¬ IsZero ((E.page 1 (by omega)).X (p, n - p))}.Finite) ∧
            ∃ (F : ∀ n : ℤ, ℤ → Subobject (hypercohomology X RΓ K.X n))
              (hF : ∀ n : ℤ, Antitone (F n)),
              (∀ n p : ℤ, F n p = imageSubobject
                (hypercohomologyMap X RΓ (K.filtration.ι.app (op p)) n)) ∧
              (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ F n a = ⊤ ∧ F n b = ⊥) ∧
              (∀ p q : ℤ, E.HasPageInfinityAt (p, q)) ∧
              ∀ p q : ℤ, Nonempty
                (E.pageInfinity (p, q) ≅
                  cokernel (Subobject.ofLE (F (p + q) (p + 1)) (F (p + q) p)
                    (hF (p + q) (by omega)))))
declarations.comment: computation by a supplied filtered K-injective resolution

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.FilteredComplex.exists_spectralSequence_of_filteredComplex
declarations.doc:
A filtered complex of modules on a ringed space has a cohomological spectral sequence whose
first page is the hypercohomology of its graded pieces. If the hypercohomology of the filtration
steps eventually vanishes on the right and maps isomorphically to that of the whole complex on the
left, the spectral sequence is bounded and converges to the hypercohomology of the complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_spectralSequence_of_filteredComplex :
    ∃ (RΓ : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing X).obj.obj (op ⊤))))
      (α : homotopySections (structureSheafRing X) (⊤ : Opens X.carrier) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RΓ),
      RΓ.IsRightDerivedFunctor α
          (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧
      ∃ (J : CochainComplex.Filtered (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) (j : K ⟶ J),
      QuasiIso j.hom ∧
      (∀ p : ℤ, QuasiIso (j.natTrans.app (op p))) ∧
      (∀ p : ℤ, QuasiIso ((FilteredObject.gr p).map j)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, Injective (J.X.X n)) ∧
      (∀ p n : ℤ, Injective ((J.filtration.obj (op p)).X n)) ∧
      (∀ p n : ℤ, Injective (((FilteredObject.gr p).obj J).X n)) ∧
      ∃ (E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence
          (ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing X).obj.obj (op ⊤))) 0)
        (F : ∀ (_p n : ℤ), Subobject ((globalSectionsFilteredComplex X J).X.X n))
        (Z D : ∀ (_r _p n : ℤ),
          Subobject ((globalSectionsFilteredComplex X J).X.X n)),
        (∀ p n : ℤ, F p n = Subobject.mk
          (((globalSectionsFilteredComplex X J).filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n)) ∧
        (∀ r p n : ℤ, Z r p n = F p n ⊓
          (Subobject.pullback ((globalSectionsFilteredComplex X J).X.d n (n + 1))).obj
            (F (p + r) (n + 1))) ∧
        (∀ r p n : ℤ, D r p n = Z (r - 1) (p + 1) n ⊔
          (Subobject.«exists» ((globalSectionsFilteredComplex X J).X.d (n - 1) n)).obj
            (Z (r - 1) (p - r + 1) (n - 1))) ∧
        (∃ e : ∀ (r p q n : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (_ : n = p + q),
            (E.page r hr).X (p, q) ≅ cokernel
              (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (inf_le_right : D r p n ⊓ Z r p n ≤ Z r p n)),
          ∀ (r p q n : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hn : n = p + q),
            ∃ δ : (Z r p n : ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing X).obj.obj (op ⊤))) ⟶
                (Z r (p + r) (n + 1) : ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing X).obj.obj (op ⊤))),
              δ ≫ (Z r (p + r) (n + 1)).arrow =
                  (Z r p n).arrow ≫ (globalSectionsFilteredComplex X J).X.d n (n + 1) ∧
              cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE _ _
                  (inf_le_right : D r p n ⊓ Z r p n ≤ Z r p n)) ≫
                    (e r p q n hr hn).inv ≫
                    (E.page r hr).d (p, q) (p + r, q - r + 1) =
                δ ≫ cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE _ _
                    (inf_le_right : D r (p + r) (n + 1) ⊓ Z r (p + r) (n + 1) ≤
                      Z r (p + r) (n + 1))) ≫
                  (e r (p + r) (q - r + 1) (n + 1) hr (by omega)).inv) ∧
        (∀ p q : ℤ, Nonempty
          ((E.page 1 (by omega)).X (p, q) ≅
            hypercohomology X RΓ ((FilteredObject.gr p).obj K) (p + q))) ∧
        ((∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p₀ : ℤ, ∀ p : ℤ, p₀ ≤ p →
            IsZero (hypercohomology X RΓ (K.filtration.obj (op p)) n)) →
          (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p₁ : ℤ, ∀ p : ℤ, p ≤ p₁ →
            IsIso (hypercohomologyMap X RΓ (K.filtration.ι.app (op p)) n)) →
          (∀ n : ℤ, {p : ℤ | ¬ IsZero ((E.page 1 (by omega)).X (p, n - p))}.Finite) ∧
            ∃ (F : ∀ n : ℤ, ℤ → Subobject (hypercohomology X RΓ K.X n))
              (hF : ∀ n : ℤ, Antitone (F n)),
              (∀ n p : ℤ, F n p = imageSubobject
                (hypercohomologyMap X RΓ (K.filtration.ι.app (op p)) n)) ∧
              (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ F n a = ⊤ ∧ F n b = ⊥) ∧
              (∀ p q : ℤ, E.HasPageInfinityAt (p, q)) ∧
              ∀ p q : ℤ, Nonempty
                (E.pageInfinity (p, q) ≅
                  cokernel (Subobject.ofLE (F (p + q) (p + 1)) (F (p + q) p)
                    (hF (p + q) (by omega)))))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.FilteredComplex.exists_spectralSequence_of_boundedBelowFilteredComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BKL.** Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space and let `K^•` be a filtered complex of
`O_X`-modules which is bounded below and whose filtration is finite in each degree. Then the
spectral sequence of [Stacks, Tag 0BKK] can be built without a filtered K-injective resolution:
a filtered quasi-isomorphism `i : K^• ⟶ I^•` as in [Stacks, Tag 05TW], with `I^•` bounded below,
the filtration on each `I^n` finite and each `gr^pI^n` injective, gives the filtered complex
`Γ(X, I^•)` with `F^pΓ(X, I^•) = Γ(X, F^pI^•)`, whose spectral sequence has first page
`E_1^{p, q} = H^{p + q}(X, gr^pK^•)` and is bounded and converges to `H^*(X, K^•)` with a finite
induced filtration.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_spectralSequence_of_boundedBelowFilteredComplex (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (RΓ : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing X).obj.obj (op ⊤))))
    (α : homotopySections (structureSheafRing X) (⊤ : Opens X.carrier) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RΓ)
    (hRΓ : RΓ.IsRightDerivedFunctor α
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (K : CochainComplex.Filtered (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) (a : ℤ)
    (hK : K.X.IsStrictlyGE a) (hKfin : K.filtration.IsDegreewiseFinite) :
    ∃ (I : CochainComplex.Filtered (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) (i : K ⟶ I),
      I.X.IsStrictlyGE a ∧
      I.filtration.IsDegreewiseFinite ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, (CochainComplex.evalFil I n).IsFilteredInjective) ∧
      (∀ p : ℤ, QuasiIso ((FilteredObject.gr p).map i)) ∧
      (∀ p : ℤ, QuasiIso (i.natTrans.app (op p))) ∧
      QuasiIso i.hom ∧
      (∀ p : ℤᵒᵖ, (globalSectionsFilteredComplex X I).filtration.obj p =
        (globalSectionsComplexFunctor X).obj (I.filtration.obj p)) ∧
      (∀ p q : ℤ, Nonempty
        (((globalSectionsSpectralSequence X I).page 1 (by omega)).X (p, q) ≅
          hypercohomology X RΓ ((FilteredObject.gr p).obj K) (p + q))) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, {p : ℤ | ¬ IsZero
        (((globalSectionsSpectralSequence X I).page 1 (by omega)).X (p, n - p))}.Finite) ∧
      ∃ (F : ∀ n : ℤ, ℤ → Subobject (hypercohomology X RΓ K.X n))
        (hF : ∀ n : ℤ, Antitone (F n)),
        (∀ n p : ℤ, F n p = imageSubobject
          (hypercohomologyMap X RΓ (K.filtration.ι.app (op p)) n)) ∧
        (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ b c : ℤ, b ≤ c ∧ F n b = ⊤ ∧ F n c = ⊥) ∧
        (∀ p q : ℤ, (globalSectionsSpectralSequence X I).HasPageInfinityAt (p, q)) ∧
        ∀ p q : ℤ, Nonempty
          ((globalSectionsSpectralSequence X I).pageInfinity (p, q) ≅
            cokernel (Subobject.ofLE (F (p + q) (p + 1)) (F (p + q) p)
              (hF (p + q) (by omega))))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.FilteredComplex.exists_canonicalTruncationSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BKM.** For every complex of modules on a ringed space, the canonical truncation
filtration gives a spectral sequence with
`E_1^{p, q} = H^{p + q}(X, H^{-p}(K^•)[p]) = H^{2p + q}(X, H^{-p}(K^•))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_canonicalTruncationSpectralSequence (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ℤ) :
    Nonempty (CanonicalTruncationSpectralSequence X K)
declarations.comment: truncation_e1_page

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.FilteredComplex.exists_boundedBelowTruncationSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BKM, through Remark 0BKL.** For a bounded-below complex the canonical truncation
spectral sequence can also be built from a bounded-below filtered replacement whose filtration is
finite in every degree and whose graded terms are injective; the first-page formula is the
same.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_boundedBelowTruncationSpectralSequence (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ℤ)
    (hK : ∃ a : ℤ, K.IsStrictlyGE a) :
    ∃ (S : CanonicalTruncationSpectralSequence X K) (a : ℤ),
      S.injectiveReplacement.X.IsStrictlyGE a ∧
      S.injectiveReplacement.filtration.IsDegreewiseFinite ∧
      ∀ p q : ℤ, Nonempty
        (((globalSectionsSpectralSequence X S.injectiveReplacement).page 1
            (by omega)).X (p, q) ≅
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing X).obj.obj (op ⊤))) (2 * p + q)).obj
              (S.RΓ.obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
                (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) 0).obj
                  ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
                    (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) (-p)).obj
                      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)))))
declarations.comment: truncation_e1_page

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.FilteredComplex.hypercohomologySpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BKM.** The hypercohomology spectral sequence of an object of the derived category
of module sheaves on a ringed space: take a representative, filter it by its canonical
truncations, apply derived global sections, and renumber the resulting spectral sequence.
declarations.comment: hypercohomology_e2_page

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.FilteredComplex.hypercohomologySpectralSequence_e₂
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BKM.** The second page of the hypercohomology spectral sequence is the
hypercohomology of the cohomology objects of `K`: `E_2^{i, j} = H^i(X, H^j(K))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hypercohomologySpectralSequence_e₂ (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) (i j : ℤ) :
    Nonempty (((hypercohomologySpectralSequence X K).spectralSequence.page 2).X (i, j) ≅
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing X).obj.obj (op ⊤))) i).obj
        ((hypercohomologySpectralSequence X K).truncation.RΓ.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) 0).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
              (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) j).obj K))))
declarations.comment: hypercohomology_e2_page

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.FilteredComplex.exists_boundedBelowHypercohomologySpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BKM, the closing clause.**  If `K^•` is bounded below, the renumbered spectral
sequence -- the one whose second page is `H^i(X, H^j(K^•))` -- is **bounded**, and it **converges
to `H^{i + j}(X, K^•)`**: some finite decreasing filtration of `H^n(X, K^•)` has the terms
`E_∞^{i, n - i}` of its infinity page as graded pieces.

The spectral sequence is the one of
`exists_boundedBelowTruncationSpectralSequence`, i.e. the one built through Remark
[Stacks, Tag 0BKL] from a bounded-below filtered replacement; boundedness and convergence of that
sequence *before* the renumbering are `boundedReplacement_convergence`, which needs no hypothesis
beyond degreewise finiteness of the replacement's filtration, and they are carried across the
bidegree change `(i, j) ↦ (-j, i + 2j)` by
`CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.truncationRenumber_finite_not_isZero_page_two` and
`CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.AbutsTo.truncationRenumberRestrictPages`.  The abutment is read
on `K^•` itself rather than on the underlying complex of the filtration by
`CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.AbutsTo.of_iso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_boundedBelowHypercohomologySpectralSequence (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ℤ)
    (hK : ∃ a : ℤ, K.IsStrictlyGE a) :
    ∃ S : HypercohomologySpectralSequence X (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K),
      IsBounded S.spectralSequence ∧
        SpectralSequence.AbutsTo S.spectralSequence
          (fun n => hypercohomology X S.truncation.RΓ K n)
declarations.comment: bounded below: the renumbered sequence is bounded and converges to H^{i+j}(X, K)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.isDerivedLimit_map_derivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
Derived pushforward along a morphism of ringed spaces commutes with derived limits: it carries
an object exhibited as the derived limit of a countable inverse system to the derived limit of the
pushed-forward system.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_map_derivedPushforward
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩]
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (hL : IsDerivedLimit K L) :
    ∃ h : HasProduct (fun n : ℕ ↦ Rf.obj (K.obj ⟨n⟩)),
      @IsDerivedLimit (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y))) _ _ _ _ _ _
        (K ⋙ Rf) h (Rf.obj L)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimits.sheafificationCohomologyPresheafSystemIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BKQ, first assertion.** For an inverse system `(Kₙ)` in `D(O)` and a degree `m`,
the cohomology sheaf `𝓗ᵐ_n = Hᵐ(Kₙ)` is the sheafification of the cohomology presheaf
`underline 𝓗ᵐ_n : U ↦ Hᵐ(U, Kₙ)`, naturally in `n`: sheafifying the system of cohomology
presheaves of the `Kₙ` gives the system of their cohomology sheaves, compatibly with the
transition maps of the system.

This is Tag 0BKJ applied to each `Kₙ`, read as an isomorphism of systems; the same statement for
a derived limit `L` of the system -- that `𝓗ᵐ = Hᵐ(R lim Kₙ)` is the sheafification of
`underline 𝓗ᵐ : U ↦ Hᵐ(U, R lim Kₙ)` -- is Tag 0BKJ at the single object `L`, i.e. the component
`(sheafificationCohomologyPresheafIso O m).app L`. Both appear in
`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimits.cohomologyDerivedLimitDiagram`, which puts them into the
remark's square.
declarations.statement:
def sheafificationCohomologyPresheafSystemIso {X : TopCat.{u}}
    (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} O)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wP} (PresheafOfModules.{u} O.obj)]
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (m : ℤ) :
    (K ⋙ derivedSectionsPresheaf O ⋙
          DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (PresheafOfModules.{u} O.obj) m) ⋙
        PresheafOfModules.sheafification (𝟙 O.obj) ≅
      K ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} O) m
declarations.comment: the cohomology sheaf H^m(K_n) of each member of the inverse system is the sheafification of the cohomology presheaf U ↦ H^m(U, K_n), naturally in n

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimits.cohomologyDerivedLimitDiagram
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BKQ, first assertion and diagram.** Let `O` be a sheaf of rings on a space, let
`(Kₙ)` be an inverse system in `D(O)` and let `L` be a derived limit of it, given by its
structural map `p` and the defining distinguished triangle. Fix a degree `m`, and let `e` be the
Tag 0BKJ identification of the sheafification `S` of the cohomology presheaf `underline 𝓗ᵐ` with
the cohomology sheaf `𝓗ᵐ`; in particular `e.hom.app (K.obj ⟨n⟩)` says that `𝓗ᵐ_n` is the
sheafification of `underline 𝓗ᵐ_n`, and `e.hom.app L` says the same for `L`.

Then there are comparison maps `a` into the limit of the cohomology presheaves, `b` into the
limit of the cohomology sheaves and `c` out of the sheafification of the former, each determined
by its composites with the limit projections -- `a` and `b` by the maps induced by `p ≫ πₙ`, and
`c` by the sheafified projections followed by `e` -- and the square

`S a ≫ c = e L ≫ b`

commutes. The map `c` is not asserted to be invertible: the source warns that `lim 𝓗ᵐ_n` need
not be the sheafification of `lim underline 𝓗ᵐ_n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologyDerivedLimitDiagram {X : TopCat.{u}}
    (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} O)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wP} (PresheafOfModules.{u} O.obj)]
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O))
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O))
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩]
    (p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩)
    (hp : ∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
            K.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
        distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)))
    (m : ℤ) :
    let P := derivedSectionsPresheaf O ⋙
      DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (PresheafOfModules.{u} O.obj) m
    let H := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} O) m
    let S := PresheafOfModules.sheafification (𝟙 O.obj)
    let e := sheafificationCohomologyPresheafIso O m
    ∃ (a : P.obj L ⟶ limit (K ⋙ P))
      (b : H.obj L ⟶ limit (K ⋙ H))
      (c : S.obj (limit (K ⋙ P)) ⟶ limit (K ⋙ H)),
      (∀ n : ℕ,
        a ≫ limit.π (K ⋙ P) ⟨n⟩ =
          P.map (p ≫ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ,
        b ≫ limit.π (K ⋙ H) ⟨n⟩ =
          H.map (p ≫ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ,
        c ≫ limit.π (K ⋙ H) ⟨n⟩ =
          S.map (limit.π (K ⋙ P) ⟨n⟩) ≫ e.hom.app (K.obj ⟨n⟩)) ∧
      (S.map a ≫ c = e.hom.app L ≫ b)
declarations.comment: the cohomology sheaves of the system and of the derived limit are the sheafifications of the cohomology presheaves U ↦ H^m(U, K_n) and U ↦ H^m(U, R lim K_n), and the comparison square of the remark's diagram commutes

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimits.exists_shortExact_limOne_cohomology_derivedLimit_family
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BKQ.** For a family of derived-sections functors indexed by the opens of a
ringed space, the cohomology of a derived inverse limit lies in the Milnor short exact
sequence over each open.

The last map is pinned down by its composites with the limit projections; they are the maps
on cohomology induced by the structural maps `L ⟶ Kₙ`.

This is the last assertion of the remark. Its first assertion, that the cohomology sheaves of
the system and of the derived limit are the sheafifications of the cohomology presheaves, and
the square of its diagram, are
`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimits.sheafificationCohomologyPresheafSystemIso` and
`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimits.cohomologyDerivedLimitDiagram`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_shortExact_limOne_cohomology_derivedLimit_family
    (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ => K.obj ⟨n⟩]
    (p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ => K.obj ⟨n⟩)
    (hL : ∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ => K.obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ =>
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => K.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => K.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
            K.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
        distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))))
    (RGamma : ∀ _U : Opens X.carrier,
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ⥤
        DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (comparison : ∀ U : Opens X.carrier,
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (structureSheafRing X) ⋙
          (sheafSections (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
            (op U)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RGamma U)
    (hRGamma : ∀ U : Opens X.carrier,
      (RGamma U).IsRightDerivedFunctor (comparison U)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (U : Opens X.carrier) (m : ℤ) :
    let Fprev := K ⋙ RGamma U ⋙
      DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (m - 1)
    let Fcur := K ⋙ RGamma U ⋙
      DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} m
    let dprev := Pi.lift fun n : ℕ =>
      Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => Fprev.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => Fprev.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
          Fprev.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op
    ∃ (i : cokernel dprev ⟶
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} m).obj ((RGamma U).obj L))
      (q : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} m).obj ((RGamma U).obj L) ⟶
        limit Fcur)
      (zero : i ≫ q = 0),
      ((ShortComplex.mk i q zero).ShortExact ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, q ≫ limit.π Fcur ⟨n⟩ =
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} m).map
            ((RGamma U).map (p ≫ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => K.obj ⟨n⟩) n)))
declarations.comment: the short exact sequences of Equation 0BKR over each open U: 0 → R¹ lim H^(m-1)(U, K_n) → H^m(U, R lim K_n) → lim H^m(U, K_n) → 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SpaceInverseLimits.isDerivedLimit_single_limit_of_isBasis
declarations.doc:
If the terms of a countable inverse system of modules are acyclic on a basis and `R¹ lim`
of their sections vanishes there, then the ordinary limit, placed in degree zero, is a derived
inverse limit of the system.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDerivedLimit_single_limit_of_isBasis (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (F : Functor ℕᵒᵖ (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (B : Set (Opens X.carrier)) (hB : Opens.IsBasis B)
    (hcoh : ∀ U ∈ B, ∀ n p : ℕ, 0 < p →
      IsZero (Hgroup (structureSheafRing X) U p (F.obj ⟨n⟩)))
    (hlimOne : ∀ U ∈ B, Epi (inverseLimitDifference (sectionsSystem X F U))) :
    ∃ h : HasProduct (fun n : ℕ =>
        (F ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) 0).obj ⟨n⟩),
      @IsDerivedLimit (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) _ _ _ _ _ _
        (F ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) 0) h
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) 0).obj
          (limit F))
declarations.comment: derived limit

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SpaceInverseLimits.isZero_cohomology_limit_of_isBasis
declarations.doc:
Under the same hypotheses, the ordinary inverse limit has vanishing positive-degree
cohomology on every member of the basis.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_cohomology_limit_of_isBasis (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (F : Functor ℕᵒᵖ (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (B : Set (Opens X.carrier)) (hB : Opens.IsBasis B)
    (hcoh : ∀ U ∈ B, ∀ n p : ℕ, 0 < p →
      IsZero (Hgroup (structureSheafRing X) U p (F.obj ⟨n⟩)))
    (hlimOne : ∀ U ∈ B, Epi (inverseLimitDifference (sectionsSystem X F U)))
    (U : Opens X.carrier) (hU : U ∈ B) (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero (Hgroup (structureSheafRing X) U p (limit F))
declarations.comment: higher cohomology

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.homologyIso_derivedSections_of_isAffineOpen
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BKT] over an affine open of a scheme.** For an object `L` of `D(𝒪_X)` with
quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves and an affine open `U`, the hypercohomology `H^p(U, L)` is the
module of sections over `U` of the cohomology sheaf `H^p(L)`.

The cohomology sheaves are acyclic over the affine opens by Serre vanishing
(`Stacks.Algebraization.isZero_rightDerived_evaluation_homology_of_isQuasicoherent`), and the
affine opens are a basis, so
`Stacks.Cohomology.AcyclicOpen.hypercohomologyIso` applies.
declarations.statement:
public def homologyIso_derivedSections_of_isAffineOpen (X : Scheme.{u})
    (L : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hqc : ∀ q : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules q).obj L).IsQuasicoherent)
    (U : X.affineOpens) (p : ℤ) :
    (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1)) p).obj
        ((derivedSections (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace) U.1).obj L) ≅
      ModuleCat.of Γ(X, U.1) Γ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules p).obj L, U.1)
declarations.comment: over an affine open of a scheme, for an object of `D(𝒪_X)` whose cohomology sheaves are all quasi-coherent: the acyclicity hypothesis of the tag is Serre vanishing on the affine opens, which quasi-coherence supplies, and the affine opens are a basis of the topology

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.AcyclicOpen.isIso_hypercohomologyEdge_app_of_isBasis
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project Tag 0BKT.** If every cohomology sheaf of `K` has vanishing higher cohomology
over the members of a basis of opens, then over each member of that basis the hypercohomology
edge morphism `H^q(U, K) ⟶ Γ(U, H^q(K))` is invertible, in every degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_hypercohomologyEdge_app_of_isBasis
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (B : Set (Opens X.carrier)) (hB : Opens.IsBasis B)
    (hK : ∀ V ∈ B, ∀ p : ℕ, 0 < p → ∀ q : ℤ,
      IsZero (((SheafOfModules.evaluation (structureSheafRing X) (op V)).rightDerived p).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) q).obj K)))
    (U : Opens X.carrier) (hU : U ∈ B) (q : ℤ) :
    IsIso ((hypercohomologyEdge (structureSheafRing X) U q).app K)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimits.cohomology_isLimit_of_isDerivedLimit_of_isBasis
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BKU.** Let `(K_n)` be an inverse system of objects of `D(𝒪_X)` and let
`L` be a derived limit of it, exhibited by the structural map `p` and its distinguished triangle.
If on a basis `B` of the topology the cohomology sheaves of the `K_n` are acyclic and the inverse
systems of their sections have vanishing `R¹ lim`, then for every `q` the degree-`q` cohomology
sheaf of `L` is the inverse limit of the degree-`q` cohomology sheaves of the `K_n`, through the
maps induced by `p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomology_isLimit_of_isDerivedLimit_of_isBasis
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    [hprod : HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩]
    (p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩)
    (hL : ∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
            K.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
        distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))))
    (B : Set (Opens X.carrier)) (hB : Opens.IsBasis B)
    (hacyclic : ∀ U ∈ B, ∀ q : ℤ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ r : ℕ, 0 < r →
      IsZero (((SheafOfModules.evaluation (structureSheafRing X) (op U)).rightDerived r).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) q).obj
          (K.obj ⟨n⟩))))
    (hlimOne : ∀ U ∈ B, ∀ q : ℤ,
      IsZero (Rlim.firstDerivedLimit
        (K ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) q ⋙
          SheafOfModules.evaluation (structureSheafRing X) (op U) ⋙
            forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing X).obj.obj (op U))) AddCommGrpCat.{u})))
    (q : ℤ) :
    ∃ τ : (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) q).obj L) ⟶
        K ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) q,
      (∀ n : ℕ, τ.app ⟨n⟩ =
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) q).map
          (p ≫ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n)) ∧
      Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk _ τ))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteCohomologyPresheaf.sheafificationCohomologyPresheafIso
declarations.doc:
Sheafifying the presheaf `U ↦ H^q(U, K)` gives the `q`-th cohomology sheaf of `K`,
naturally in the derived object `K`.
declarations.comment: associated sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteCohomologyPresheaf.sheafificationCohomologyPresheafIso_comp
declarations.doc:
Characterization of the associated-sheaf isomorphism: on a complex, it agrees with the
canonical exact-sheafification comparison after the unit of the total right derived
presheaf-sections functor.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafificationCohomologyPresheafIso_comp (q : ℤ)
    (I : HomotopyCategory (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
      (.up ℤ)) :
    (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (PresheafOfModules.{w}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj) q ⋙
        PresheafOfModules.sheafification (𝟙 (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj)).map
        (((homotopySectionsPresheaf X).totalRightDerivedUnit DerivedCategory.Qh
          (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{w}
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) (.up ℤ))).app I) ≫
      (sheafificationCohomologyPresheafIso X q).hom.app (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj I) =
        (homotopySheafificationHomologyIso X q).hom.app I ≫
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactorsh
            (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) q).inv.app I
declarations.comment: canonical comparison

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteCohomologyPresheaf.cohomologyPresheafEvaluationIso
declarations.doc:
Evaluation of the hypercohomology presheaf at `U` is the established cohomology functor
`H^q(U, -)`.
declarations.statement:
public def cohomologyPresheafEvaluationIso (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u}) (U : X.C) (q : ℤ) :
    derivedSectionsPresheaf X ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (PresheafOfModules.{u}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj) q ⋙
        PresheafOfModules.evaluation (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj
          (Opposite.op U) ⋙
        forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj.obj
          (Opposite.op U))) AddCommGrpCat.{u} ≅
      derivedSectionsOverObject X U ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} q
declarations.comment: values on objects

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteCohomologyPresheaf.cohomologyPresheafEvaluationIso_naturality
declarations.doc: The evaluation identifications commute with the restriction maps.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cohomologyPresheafEvaluationIso_naturality (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u})
    {U V : X.C} (g : U ⟶ V)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
      (q : ℤ) :
    (cohomologyPresheaf X K q).presheaf.map g.op ≫
        (cohomologyPresheafEvaluationIso X U q).hom.app K =
      (cohomologyPresheafEvaluationIso X V q).hom.app K ≫
        (hypercohomologyRestriction X g q).app K
declarations.comment: restriction maps

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteCohomologyPresheaf.cohomologyPresheafSliceIso
declarations.doc:
The same evaluation, expressed using cohomology on the localized site `C/U`; its second
factor is the comparison of Tag 0D6F.
declarations.statement:
public def cohomologyPresheafSliceIso (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u}) (U : X.C) (q : ℤ) :
    derivedSectionsPresheaf X ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (PresheafOfModules.{u}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj) q ⋙
        PresheafOfModules.evaluation (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj
          (Opposite.op U) ⋙
        forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj.obj
          (Opposite.op U))) AddCommGrpCat.{u} ≅
      derivedRestriction X U ⋙ derivedSectionsOnSlice X U ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} q
declarations.comment: cohomology on the slice site

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimitDiagram.cohomologyDerivedLimitDiagram_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BKW.** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site, let `(Kₙ)` be an inverse system
in `D(O)` and let `K` be a derived limit of it, presented by the structural map `p : K ⟶ ∏ Kₙ` of
its distinguished product triangle.  Fix a degree `m`, write `P` for the cohomology presheaf
functor `M ↦ (U ↦ Hᵐ(U, M))`, `H` for the cohomology sheaf functor, `S` for sheafification and
`e` for the Tag 0BKV identification `S ∘ P ≅ H`.  Then:

* there are comparison maps `a : P K ⟶ lim P Kₙ`, `b : H K ⟶ lim H Kₙ` and
  `c : S (lim P Kₙ) ⟶ lim H Kₙ`, each determined by its composites with the limit projections,
  and the square `S a ≫ c = e ≫ b` commutes; and
* for every object `U` of `C` there is a short exact sequence

  `0 ⟶ R¹lim Hᵐ⁻¹(U, Kₙ) ⟶ Hᵐ(U, K) ⟶ lim Hᵐ(U, Kₙ) ⟶ 0`,

  whose surjection is determined by its composites with the limit projections and whose `R¹lim`
  is the cokernel of the difference map `(xₙ) ↦ (xₙ - fₙ₊₁(xₙ₊₁))`.

The third comparison map is *not* asserted to be invertible: sheafification does not in general
commute with this inverse limit, which is the caveat of the remark.

Nothing is assumed: sheafification, local bijectivity, Grothendieck abelianness, the right
derived functor presenting cohomology and the countable product presenting the derived limit are
all theorems at this module universe, and are supplied here.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologyDerivedLimitDiagram_unconditional
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory
      (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (L : DerivedCategory
      (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩)
    (hp : ∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
            K.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
        distTriang (DerivedCategory
          (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))))
    (m : ℤ) :
    let P := DerivedLimitSections.derivedSectionsPresheafMax.{u, v, r, w} X ⋙
      DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (PresheafOfModules.{max u v r w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj) m
    let H := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) m
    let S := sheafificationMax.{u, v, r, w} X
    let e := sheafificationCohomologyPresheafIsoMax.{u, v, r, w} X m
    (∃ (a : P.obj L ⟶ limit (K ⋙ P))
      (b : H.obj L ⟶ limit (K ⋙ H))
      (c : S.obj (limit (K ⋙ P)) ⟶ limit (K ⋙ H)),
      (∀ n : ℕ,
        a ≫ limit.π (K ⋙ P) ⟨n⟩ =
          P.map (p ≫ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ,
        b ≫ limit.π (K ⋙ H) ⟨n⟩ =
          H.map (p ≫ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ,
        c ≫ limit.π (K ⋙ H) ⟨n⟩ =
          S.map (limit.π (K ⋙ P) ⟨n⟩) ≫ e.hom.app (K.obj ⟨n⟩)) ∧
      (S.map a ≫ c = e.hom.app L ≫ b)) ∧
    ∀ U : X.C,
      let RG := derivedSectionsMax.{u, v, r, w} X U
      let Mprev := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (ModuleCat.{max u v r w} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj.obj (.op U)))
          (m - 1)
      let Mcur := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (ModuleCat.{max u v r w} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj.obj (.op U))) m
      let E := K ⋙ RG
      let Fprev := E ⋙ Mprev
      let Fcur := E ⋙ Mcur
      let dprev : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ Fprev.obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ Fprev.obj ⟨n⟩) :=
        Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ Fprev.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
            Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ Fprev.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
              Fprev.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op
      ∃ (i : cokernel dprev ⟶ Mcur.obj (RG.obj L))
        (q : Mcur.obj (RG.obj L) ⟶ limit Fcur)
        (zero : i ≫ q = 0),
        (ShortComplex.mk i q zero).ShortExact ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, q ≫ limit.π Fcur ⟨n⟩ =
          Mcur.map (RG.map (p ≫ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n))
declarations.comment: the commuting square and the short exact sequences over the objects of the site

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteInverseLimits.isDerivedLimit_single_limit_of_acyclic_cover
declarations.doc:
If the terms of a countable inverse system of modules on a ringed site are acyclic on a class
of objects covering every object, and the first derived inverse limit of their sections vanishes
there, then the ordinary inverse limit, placed in degree zero, is a derived inverse limit of the
system.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_single_limit_of_acyclic_cover
    (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ SheafOfModules.{z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
    (B : ObjectProperty X.C) (hB : X.J.HasEnoughObjects B)
    (hcoh : ∀ U, B U →
      letI : (SheafOfModules.evaluation.{z}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) (op U)).Additive :=
        Stacks.SheafOfModules.evaluationAdditive.{z}
          (R := (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) (op U);
      ∀ n p : ℕ, 0 < p →
      IsZero (((sectionsFunctor.{u, v, w, z} X U).rightDerived p).obj (F.obj ⟨n⟩)))
    (hlimOne : ∀ U, B U →
      IsZero (Rlim.firstDerivedLimit (sectionsSystem.{u, v, w, z} X F U))) :
    ∃ h : HasProduct (fun n : ℕ =>
        (F ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) 0).obj ⟨n⟩),
      @IsDerivedLimit
        (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
        _ _ _ _ _ _
        (F ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) 0) h
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) 0).obj
          (limit F))
declarations.comment: ordinary limit is a derived limit

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteInverseLimits.isZero_cohomology_limit_of_acyclic_cover
declarations.doc:
Under the same hypotheses, the ordinary inverse limit has vanishing positive-degree
cohomology on every member of the covering class.
declarations.comment: acyclicity of the ordinary limit

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_hypercohomologyEdge_app_of_isAffineOpen
declarations.doc:
**The hypercohomology edge morphism over an affine open of a scheme is invertible**, at an
object of `D(𝒪_X)` whose cohomology sheaves are all quasi-coherent, in every degree and with no
boundedness hypothesis.

This is [Stacks, Tag 0BKZ] at the basis of affine opens of `X`: the basis has enough objects,
and the cohomology sheaves are acyclic over every member of it by Serre vanishing.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_hypercohomologyEdge_app_of_isAffineOpen
    (hE : ∀ q : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules q).obj E).IsQuasicoherent)
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : U ∈ X.affineOpens) (q : ℤ) :
    IsIso ((Stacks.Cohomology.HypercohomologyEdge.hypercohomologyEdge
      X.ringCatSheaf U q).app E)
declarations.comment: at the affine opens of a scheme, for an object with quasi-coherent cohomology

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.HypercohomologyEdge.isIso_hypercohomologyEdge_app_of_acyclic_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project Tag 0BKZ.** If the cohomology sheaves of an object of the unbounded derived
category of `O`-modules have no higher cohomology over the members of a class of objects covering
the site, then over each member its degree-`q` hypercohomology is the module of sections of its
degree-`q` cohomology sheaf: the hypercohomology edge morphism is invertible there, in every
degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_hypercohomologyEdge_app_of_acyclic_cover (U : C)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{wModule} O))
    (B : ObjectProperty C) (hB : J.HasEnoughObjects B)
    (hvan : ∀ V : C, B V → ∀ p : ℕ, 0 < p → ∀ m : ℤ,
      IsZero (((SheafOfModules.evaluation O (.op V)).rightDerived p).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{wModule} O) m).obj K)))
    (hU : B U) (q : ℤ) :
    IsIso ((hypercohomologyEdge O U q).app K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeHom
declarations.doc:
The relative morphism functor `Mor_S(Z, X)` of two schemes `Z` and `X` over `S`: it sends a
scheme `T` over `S` to the set of morphisms `T ×_S Z ⟶ X` over `S`, and a morphism `T' ⟶ T` over
`S` to the operation of base change along it.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def relativeHom (Z X : Over S) : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u

declarations.name: Stacks.Morphisms.relativeHom_representableBy_affineHom
declarations.doc:
If `Z ⟶ S` is finite locally free and `X ⟶ S` is affine, then the relative morphism functor
`Mor_S(Z, X)` is represented by a scheme affine over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeHom_representableBy_affineHom {S Z X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Z ⟶ S) (g : X ⟶ S)
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree f] [IsAffineHom g] :
    ∃ W : Over S, IsAffineHom W.hom ∧
      Nonempty
        (((prod.functor.obj (Over.mk f)).op ⋙ yoneda.obj (Over.mk g)).RepresentableBy W)

declarations.name: Stacks.Morphisms.homFromFiniteLocallyFree_isRepresentable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BL4.** If `Z` is finite locally free over `S` and every finite set of
points in a fibre of `X` lies in an affine open of `X`, then the functor of `S`-morphisms from
`Z` to `X` is representable.
declarations.statement:
theorem homFromFiniteLocallyFree_isRepresentable
    {S Z X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Z ⟶ S) (g : X ⟶ S)
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree f]
    (hX : ∀ (s : S) (t : Set X), t.Finite →
      (∀ x ∈ t, g.base x = s) →
      ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ t ⊆ U) :
    ((prod.functor.obj (Over.mk f)).op ⋙ yoneda.obj (Over.mk g)).IsRepresentable

declarations.name: Stacks.Morphisms.relativeHom_isRepresentable_of_locallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BL5.** If `Z` is finite locally free over `S` and `X` is separated
and quasi-finite over `S`, then the functor of `S`-morphisms from `Z` to `X` is representable.

The hypothesis of Stacks Tag 0BL4 is supplied by Stacks Tag 07S0: a finite set of points of `X`
in one fibre over `s : S` lies above an affine open `U ∋ s`, so it is a finite set of points of
`g ⁻¹ᵁ U`, which is separated and quasi-finite over the affine scheme `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeHom_isRepresentable_of_locallyQuasiFinite
    {S Z X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Z ⟶ S) (g : X ⟶ S)
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree f] [IsSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [LocallyQuasiFinite g] :
    ((prod.functor.obj (Over.mk f)).op ⋙ yoneda.obj (Over.mk g)).IsRepresentable

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.exists_finiteEtale_internalHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BL7.** The internal hom between two finite étale schemes over `X` is
represented by a finite étale scheme over `X`, compatibly with every base change: the
representing object is exhibited by an isomorphism of functors on the whole of `(Over X)ᵒᵖ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finiteEtale_internalHom (X : Scheme.{u}) (U V : Over X)
    [IsFinite U.hom] [Etale U.hom] [IsFinite V.hom] [Etale V.hom] :
    ∃ W : Over X, IsFinite W.hom ∧ Etale W.hom ∧
      Nonempty
        (yoneda.obj W ≅
          (Limits.prod.functor.obj U).op ⋙ yoneda.obj V)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.finite_localCohomologyModule_one_iff_forall_ringKrullDim_ne_one
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BL9].** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, `I` an ideal, `Z = V(I)` and `M` a
finite `A`-module. Then `H¹_Z(M)` is a finite `A`-module if and only if for every prime `𝔭`
associated to `M` with `I ⊄ 𝔭`, and every prime `𝔮 ⊇ 𝔭 + I`, the completion of `(A/𝔭)_𝔮` has no
associated prime `𝔯` with `dim((A/𝔭)^∧_𝔮 / 𝔯) = 1`.

Kollár's criterion, [Stacks, Tag 0BK3], enters at the open immersion `U = Spec A \ Z ⟶ Spec A`
and the coherent module `M̃|_U`, as `isCoherent_pushforward_iff_forall_two_le_ringKrullDim`. The
rest of the proof is the composite of
`finite_localCohomologyModule_one_iff_isCoherent_pushforward`, which turns finiteness of
`H¹_Z(M)` into coherence of the direct image, and the translation of the geometric condition:
`isAssociatedPoint_tilde_iff` together with `isAssociatedPoint_restrict_iff` identifies the
associated points of `M̃|_U` with the associated primes of `M` outside `Z`,
`forall_adicCompletion_pointClosure_iff` and `forall_quotientPrime_iff` rewrite the condition at
the reduced closure of such a point as a condition on the completions of `(A/𝔭)_𝔮`, and
`one_le_ringKrullDim_quotient_adicCompletion_localization` trades `2 ≤ dim` for `dim ≠ 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_localCohomologyModule_one_iff_forall_ringKrullDim_ne_one (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) [Module.Finite A M] :
    Module.Finite A (localCohomologyModule A I I.fg_of_isNoetherianRing M 1) ↔
      ∀ (p q : PrimeSpectrum A), IsAssociatedPrimeStacks A M p.asIdeal → ¬ I ≤ p.asIdeal →
        ∀ hpq : p.asIdeal ≤ q.asIdeal, I ≤ q.asIdeal →
        let J := q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk p.asIdeal)
        letI : J.IsPrime := Ideal.isPrime_map_quotientMk_of_isPrime hpq
        let B := Localization.AtPrime J
        let R := AdicCompletion (J.map (algebraMap (A ⧸ p.asIdeal) B)) B
        ∀ r : Ideal R, IsAssociatedPrimeStacks R R r → ringKrullDim (R ⧸ r) ≠ 1

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.InverseSystems.isMittagLefflerCategorical_of_finite_cohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BLC.** Let `A` be a ring, `f ∈ A`, `X` a topological space and `… → ℱ₂ → ℱ₁` an
inverse system of sheaves of `A`-modules satisfying condition (1) of Stacks 0H39. If
`H^{p+1}(X, ℱ₁)` has finite length over `A`, or `A` is Noetherian and `H^{p+1}(X, ℱ₁)` is a
finite `A`-module, then the inverse system `n ↦ H^p(X, ℱ_n)` satisfies the Mittag-Leffler
condition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMittagLefflerCategorical_of_finite_cohomology
    {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (R : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})
    [∀ U, IsMulCommutative (R.obj.obj U)]
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [Algebra A (R.obj.obj (op (⊤ : Opens X)))] (f : A)
    (obj : ℕ → SheafOfModules.{u} R)
    (map : ∀ n, obj (n + 1) ⟶ obj n) (p : ℕ) :
    let E := SheafOfModules.evaluation R (op (⊤ : Opens X))
    let G := E.rightDerived (p + 1)
    letI : Module A (G.obj (obj 0)) :=
      Module.compHom (G.obj (obj 0)) (algebraMap A (R.obj.obj (op (⊤ : Opens X))))
    ((IsFiniteLength A (G.obj (obj 0))) ∨
      (IsNoetherianRing A ∧ Module.Finite A (G.obj (obj 0)))) →
    Stacks.Cohomology.InverseSystems.TorsionFreeDivisible.Condition1
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.terminalSectionToEnd R (⊤ : Opens X) isTerminalTop
        (algebraMap A (R.obj.obj (op (⊤ : Opens X))) f)) obj map →
    IsMittagLefflerCategorical
      (Functor.ofOpSequence map ⋙ E.rightDerived p)

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.PrincipalQuotientTowerCompletion.nonempty_iso_derivedSections_limit_quotientTower_derivedCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Formal sections for a principal ideal: the displayed equality of [Stacks, Tag 0BLD].** Let
`A` be a ring, `f ∈ A`, let `X` be a scheme over `A` through `ρ : A ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` and let `ℱ` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module whose `f`-power torsion stabilizes. Let `completion` be a left
adjoint to the inclusion of the objects of `D(A)` that are derived complete for the ideal `(f)`,
so that `(-)^∧ = completion ⋙ P.ι` is derived `f`-adic completion as in [Stacks, Tag 0BKG].
Then

`RΓ(X, lim ℱ/f^(n+1)ℱ) ≅ RΓ(X, ℱ)^∧`,

the object `RΓ(X, lim ℱ/f^(n+1)ℱ)` is itself derived complete for `(f)`, and for every `p` its
`p`-th cohomology module is that of `RΓ(X, ℱ)^∧` — the identification
`Hᵖ(X, lim ℱ/fⁿℱ) = Hᵖ(RΓ(X, ℱ)^∧)` on which the diagram of the source rests.

The levelwise comparison of the two `f`-power Koszul towers, which the source of
[Stacks, Tag 0H3C] asserts with details omitted, is
`nonempty_iso_koszulTower_comp_derivedSections`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_derivedSections_limit_quotientTower_derivedCompletion
    (hℱ : (ℱ : X.Modules).IsQuasicoherent) (hstab : Stabilizes (mulF X ρ f ℱ))
    [HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))]
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ (Csys (mulF X ρ f ℱ)).obj ⟨n⟩]
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ (Ksys (mulF X ρ f ℱ)).obj ⟨n⟩]
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦
      (Ksys (mulF X ρ f ℱ) ⋙ derivedSectionsOver X.toRingedSpace ρ).obj ⟨n⟩] :
    let P : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :=
      fun L ↦ IsDerivedComplete (Ideal.span {f}) L
    ∀ (completion : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ P.FullSubcategory)
      (_ : completion ⊣ P.ι),
      let completed := completion ⋙ P.ι
      let Fhat : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) :=
        (derivedSectionsOver X.toRingedSpace ρ).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
              (limit (quotientTower X ρ f ℱ)))
      Nonempty (Fhat ≅ completed.obj (derivedSectionsModule X ρ ℱ)) ∧
        IsDerivedComplete (Ideal.span {f}) Fhat ∧
        ∀ p : ℤ, Nonempty
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) p).obj Fhat ≅
            (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) p).obj
              (completed.obj (derivedSectionsModule X ρ ℱ)))
declarations.comment: the displayed equality `RΓ(X, lim ℱ/fⁿℱ) = RΓ(X, ℱ)^∧`, with derived f-adic completion presented as in Stacks 0BKG by an arbitrary left adjoint to the inclusion of the derived-complete objects; also derived completeness of `RΓ(X, lim ℱ/fⁿℱ)` and the identification `Hᵖ(X, lim ℱ/fⁿℱ) = Hᵖ(RΓ(X, ℱ)^∧)`. Unconditional. The levelwise identification `RΓ(X, ℱ ⊗_{𝒪_X} (𝒪_X --fⁿ--> 𝒪_X)) ≅ RΓ(X, ℱ) ⊗^L_A (A --fⁿ--> A)` of inverse systems, which the source's proof of Stacks 0H3C asserts with details left out, is proved here as `nonempty_iso_koszulTower_comp_derivedSections`, out of `Stacks.Cohomology.KoszulTowerSections.nonempty_iso_koszulTower_derivedSections`. The middle column of the diagram is carried by `PrincipalQuotientTower.exists_shortExact_homology_derivedSections_limit_quotientTower`; the remaining rows and columns of the diagram are not covered

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.PrincipalQuotientTowerDiagram.exists_formalFunctionsDiagram
declarations.doc:
**The commutative diagram of [Stacks, Tag 0BLD].** Let `A` be a ring, `f ∈ A`, let `X` be a
scheme over `A` through `ρ : A ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` and let `ℱ` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module whose
`f`-power torsion stabilizes. Let `completion` be a left adjoint to the inclusion of the objects
of `D(A)` that are derived complete for `(f)`, so that `(-)^∧ = completion ⋙ P.ι` is derived
`f`-adic completion as in [Stacks, Tag 0BKG]. Then for every `p` there is a commutative diagram

```
                     0                              0
                     ↑                              ↑
0 ⟶  Hᵖ(X, ℱ)^   ⟶  lim Hᵖ(X, ℱ/fⁿℱ)  ⟶  T_f(Hᵖ⁺¹(X, ℱ))  ⟶  0
                     ↑                              ↑              ‖
0 ⟶ H⁰(Hᵖ(X, ℱ)^∧) ⟶ Hᵖ(X, lim ℱ/fⁿℱ) ⟶  T_f(Hᵖ⁺¹(X, ℱ))  ⟶  0
                     ↑                              ↑
      R¹lim Hᵖ(X, ℱ)[fⁿ]  ≅  R¹lim Hᵖ⁻¹(X, ℱ/fⁿℱ)
                     ↑                              ↑
                     0                              0
```

with exact rows and columns, where `Hᵖ(X, ℱ)^ = lim Hᵖ(X, ℱ)/fⁿHᵖ(X, ℱ)` is the ordinary `f`-adic
completion and `T_f(-)` is the `f`-adic Tate module. The right-hand column is the identity: the
two projections to `T_f(Hᵖ⁺¹(X, ℱ))` agree after the middle vertical map.

This is the diagram of [Stacks, Tag 0H32] for `K = RΓ(X, ℱ)`, carried to the honest quotients
`ℱ/fⁿℱ` along the displayed equality `RΓ(X, lim ℱ/fⁿℱ) ≅ RΓ(X, ℱ)^∧` and the two comparisons of
limits provided by the middle-column theorem.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_formalFunctionsDiagram
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ (Csys (mulF X ρ f ℱ)).obj ⟨n⟩]
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ (quotientSections X ρ f ℱ).obj ⟨n⟩]
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ (Ksys (mulF X ρ f ℱ)).obj ⟨n⟩]
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦
      (Ksys (mulF X ρ f ℱ) ⋙ derivedSectionsOver X.toRingedSpace ρ).obj ⟨n⟩]
    (p : ℤ) :
    let Hq : ℤ → ModuleCat.{u} A := fun q ↦
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) q).obj (derivedSectionsModule X ρ ℱ)
    let P : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :=
      fun L ↦ IsDerivedComplete (Ideal.span {f}) L
    ∀ (completion : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ P.FullSubcategory)
      (_ : completion ⊣ P.ι),
      let completed := completion ⋙ P.ι
      let ordinaryCompletion := limit (CompletionSequences.powerQuotientSystem A (Hq p) f)
      let tate := CompletionSequences.adicTateModule A (Hq (p + 1)) f
      let h0Completion := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
        (completed.obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj (Hq p)))
      let torsionR1 := CompletionSequences.firstDerivedLimit A
        (PrincipalTorsionTower.powerTorsionSystem A (Hq p) f)
      let limitQuotientCohomology := limit (quotientCohomology X ρ f ℱ p)
      let previousQuotientR1 := CompletionSequences.firstDerivedLimit A
        (quotientCohomology X ρ f ℱ (p - 1))
      let sectionsCohomology := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) p).obj
        (limitQuotientSections X ρ f ℱ)
      ∃ (topIn : ordinaryCompletion ⟶ limitQuotientCohomology)
        (topOut : limitQuotientCohomology ⟶ tate)
        (htop : topIn ≫ topOut = 0)
        (middleIn : h0Completion ⟶ sectionsCohomology)
        (middleOut : sectionsCohomology ⟶ tate)
        (hmiddle : middleIn ≫ middleOut = 0)
        (leftIn : torsionR1 ⟶ h0Completion) (leftOut : h0Completion ⟶ ordinaryCompletion)
        (hleft : leftIn ≫ leftOut = 0)
        (columnIn : previousQuotientR1 ⟶ sectionsCohomology)
        (columnOut : sectionsCohomology ⟶ limitQuotientCohomology)
        (hcolumn : columnIn ≫ columnOut = 0)
        (bottom : torsionR1 ≅ previousQuotientR1),
        (ShortComplex.mk topIn topOut htop).ShortExact ∧
          (ShortComplex.mk middleIn middleOut hmiddle).ShortExact ∧
          (ShortComplex.mk leftIn leftOut hleft).ShortExact ∧
          (ShortComplex.mk columnIn columnOut hcolumn).ShortExact ∧
          middleIn ≫ columnOut = leftOut ≫ topIn ∧
          middleOut = columnOut ≫ topOut ∧
          bottom.hom ≫ columnIn = leftIn ≫ middleIn
declarations.comment: the commutative diagram with exact rows and columns, in full: the top row `0 ⟶ Hᵖ(X, ℱ)^ ⟶ lim Hᵖ(X, ℱ/fⁿℱ) ⟶ T_f(Hᵖ⁺¹(X, ℱ)) ⟶ 0`, the middle row `0 ⟶ H⁰(Hᵖ(X, ℱ)^∧) ⟶ Hᵖ(X, lim ℱ/fⁿℱ) ⟶ T_f(Hᵖ⁺¹(X, ℱ)) ⟶ 0`, the left column `0 ⟶ R¹lim Hᵖ(X, ℱ)[fⁿ] ⟶ H⁰(Hᵖ(X, ℱ)^∧) ⟶ Hᵖ(X, ℱ)^ ⟶ 0`, the middle column `0 ⟶ R¹lim Hᵖ⁻¹(X, ℱ/fⁿℱ) ⟶ Hᵖ(X, lim ℱ/fⁿℱ) ⟶ lim Hᵖ(X, ℱ/fⁿℱ) ⟶ 0`, the bottom isomorphism `R¹lim Hᵖ(X, ℱ)[fⁿ] ≅ R¹lim Hᵖ⁻¹(X, ℱ/fⁿℱ)`, the identity right column, and the commutativity of the three squares

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.PrincipalQuotientTowerDiagram.exists_shortExact_topRow

**The top row of the diagram of [Stacks, Tag 0BLD].** With `A`, `f`, `X` and `ℱ` as in the

`0 ⟶ Hᵖ(X, ℱ)^ ⟶ lim Hᵖ(X, ℱ/fⁿℱ) ⟶ T_f(Hᵖ⁺¹(X, ℱ)) ⟶ 0`,

theorem exists_shortExact_topRow

    let Hq : ℤ → ModuleCat.{u} A := fun q ↦
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) q).obj (derivedSectionsModule X ρ ℱ)
    ∃ (topIn : limit (CompletionSequences.powerQuotientSystem A (Hq p) f) ⟶
        limit (quotientCohomology X ρ f ℱ p))
      (topOut : limit (quotientCohomology X ρ f ℱ p) ⟶

theorem nonempty_iso_firstDerivedLimit_torsion
