declarations.name: RightLocalizationAsFraction.fInvS
declarations.doc:
Given a morphism `f : X' ⟶ Y` and a morphism `s : X' ⟶ X` with `s ∈ W` (where
`W` is a right multiplicative system, i.e. has a right calculus of fractions),
the morphism `f s⁻¹ : X ⟶ Y` in the localized category `S⁻¹C = W.Localization`.

Concretely, this is the image under `W.Q` of the pair `(f, s)`, which represents
the equivalence class of `(f, s)` under `RightFractionRel`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fInvS [W.HasRightCalculusOfFractions]
    {X Y X' : C} (f : X' ⟶ Y) (s : X' ⟶ X) (hs : W s) :
    W.Q.obj X ⟶ W.Q.obj Y

declarations.name: integralClosure_isReflexive
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0BM4.** If `A` is a Noetherian normal domain, `K` is its fraction field, and `L`
is a finite extension of `K`, then a module-finite integral closure of `A` in `L` is reflexive as
an `A`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem integralClosure_isReflexive
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsIntegrallyClosed A]
    (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (L : Type w) [Field L] [Algebra A L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    [FiniteDimensional K L] (hB : Module.Finite A (integralClosure A L)) :
    Module.IsReflexive A (integralClosure A L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_pow_smul_derivedGlobalSections_eq_zero_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
Let `I` be a finitely generated ideal of `A`, let `J ≤ I` and let `U` be the complement of
`V(I)` in `Spec A`.  If a power of `J` annihilates the degree `p` cohomology of the structure
sheaf of `U`, then for every finite locally free sheaf `F` on `U` some power of `J` annihilates
the degree `p` cohomology of `F`.

Cohomology is the right derived functor of global sections, and the `A`-action is the one
induced by the canonical map `A ⟶ Γ(U, 𝒪_U)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pow_smul_derivedGlobalSections_eq_zero_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I J : Ideal A) (hJI : J ≤ I) (hI : I.FG)
    (U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens)
    (hU : (U : Set (Spec (.of A))) = (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A))ᶜ) (p : ℕ)
    (hn : ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ a ∈ J ^ n,
      ∀ x : (ModuleCat.restrictScalars
          ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv ≫ U.ι.appTop).hom).obj
        (((SheafOfModules.evaluation (U : Scheme).ringCatSheaf
            (op (⊤ : (U : Scheme).Opens))).rightDerived p).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit (U : Scheme).ringCatSheaf)), a • x = 0)
    (F : SheafOfModules (U : Scheme).ringCatSheaf)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} F] :
    ∃ m : ℕ, ∀ a ∈ J ^ m,
      ∀ x : (ModuleCat.restrictScalars
          ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv ≫ U.ι.appTop).hom).obj
        (((SheafOfModules.evaluation (U : Scheme).ringCatSheaf
            (op (⊤ : (U : Scheme).Opens))).rightDerived p).obj F), a • x = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocalLefschetzSituation.fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleRestriction_of_annihilated_of_henselian
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BM6].** In the local Lefschetz situation assume that `H¹_𝔪(A)` and `H²_𝔪(A)`
are annihilated by a power of `f` and that `A` is henselian, or more generally that the pair
`(A, (f))` is henselian. Then `FÉt_U ⟶ FÉt_{U₀}` is fully faithful.

The proof is the source's. Replacing `A` by its `𝔪`-adic completion reduces the statement to the
case of an `f`-adically complete `A`, which is Stacks 0BLI in the form
`fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleRestriction_of_isAdicCompleteCase`; the henselian hypothesis `hS` is
what that reduction consumes, and the annihilation hypothesis passes to the completion by
Stacks 0ALZ, which is `annihilated_completion`. In the complete case completion along `(f)𝒪_U`
is fully faithful on the finite locally free sheaves by Stacks 0EKS,
`Stacks.Algebraization.completionFullyFaithfulOnFiniteLocallyFree_of_isAdicComplete_of_`
`annihilated`, and
`fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleRestriction_of_completionFullyFaithfulOnFiniteLocallyFree` concludes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleRestriction_of_annihilated_of_henselian
    (S : LocalLefschetzSituation.{u})
    (hS : HenselianLocalRing S.A ∨ HenselianPair S.A S.principalIdeal)
    (h1 : ∃ n, ∀ x : localCohomologyModule S.A (maximalIdeal S.A)
      (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing (maximalIdeal S.A)) (ModuleCat.of S.A S.A) 1,
      S.f ^ n • x = 0)
    (h2 : ∃ n, ∀ x : localCohomologyModule S.A (maximalIdeal S.A)
      (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing (maximalIdeal S.A)) (ModuleCat.of S.A S.A) 2,
      S.f ^ n • x = 0) :
    Nonempty (finiteEtaleBaseChange S.U₀ToU).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: for an arbitrary Noetherian local ring `A`, with `H¹_𝔪(A)` and `H²_𝔪(A)` killed by a power of `f` and with `A` henselian or `(A, (f))` a henselian pair

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_iso_spec_sections_punctured_spectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BM8.** A scheme finite over the spectrum of a Noetherian local ring,
whose local rings at closed points all have depth at least two, is canonically the spectrum of
its sections over the inverse image of the punctured spectrum.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_iso_spec_sections_punctured_spectrum
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (π : Y ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [IsFinite π]
    (hdepth : ∀ y : Y, IsClosed ({y} : Set Y) →
      2 ≤ Module.depth (Y.presheaf.stalk y)
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Y.presheaf.stalk y)) (Y.presheaf.stalk y)) :
    let U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens :=
      ⟨({IsLocalRing.closedPoint A} : Set (PrimeSpectrum A))ᶜ,
        IsLocalRing.isClosed_singleton_closedPoint A |>.isOpen_compl⟩
    let V : Y.Opens := π ⁻¹ᵁ U
    ∃ e : Y ≅ Spec Γ(Y, V),
      e.hom ≫ Spec.map (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top).op) = Y.toSpecΓ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NormalPurity.globalSections_isEquivalence_normalFiniteEtaleAwayAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BM9.** On a Noetherian normal local ring of dimension at least two,
global sections give an equivalence from the opposite of the category of finite étale covers of
the punctured spectrum to finite normal torsion-free algebras which are étale there.
declarations.statement:
public theorem globalSections_isEquivalence_normalFiniteEtaleAwayAlgebra
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (hnormal : IsNormalRing A) (hdim : (2 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim A) :
    ∃ F : Functor
        (FiniteEtaleOver (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme)ᵒᵖ
        (NormalFiniteEtaleAwayAlgebra A),
      F.IsEquivalence ∧ Nonempty
        (F ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι _ ≅ globalSections A)
declarations.comment: the equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NormalPurity.exists_finiteEtale_extension_iff_globalSections_finiteEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BM9.** A finite étale cover of the punctured spectrum extends to a
finite étale cover of the whole spectrum exactly when its ring of global sections is finite
étale over the base ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finiteEtale_extension_iff_globalSections_finiteEtale
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (hnormal : IsNormalRing A) (hdim : (2 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim A)
    (V : Scheme.{u}) (π : V ⟶ (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme)
    [IsFinite π] [Etale π] :
    (∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : Y ⟶ Spec (.of A)) (g : V ⟶ Y),
      IsFinite f ∧ Etale f ∧ IsPullback π g (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum A).ι f) ↔
      letI : Algebra A Γ(V, ⊤) :=
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv ≫
          (π ≫ (Stacks.Divisors.puncturedSpectrum A).ι).appTop).hom.toAlgebra
      Module.Finite A Γ(V, ⊤) ∧ Algebra.Etale A Γ(V, ⊤)
declarations.comment: the extension criterion

declarations.name: Stacks.PurityDimensionTwo.quotient_maximalIdeal_counterexample_clauseTwo
declarations.doc:
**Clause (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0BMA] as literally stated is false: the residue field is a
counterexample.** Let `A` be a regular local ring of dimension at least two and `B = A ⧸ 𝔪`.
Then `B` is a finite `A`-algebra and a normal ring, the preimage of the punctured spectrum `U`
under `Spec B ⟶ Spec A` is empty (so `Spec B ×_X U = ∅`), and `Spec B ⟶ Spec A` is étale over
`U` (it is finite everywhere); but `A → B` is not étale. These are the hypotheses of clause (2)
in the spelling of `Stacks.PurityDimensionTwo.etale_of_isNormalRing_of_two_le_ringKrullDim`
without its added hypothesis `Module.IsTorsionFree A B`, which `A ⧸ 𝔪` violates.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotient_maximalIdeal_counterexample_clauseTwo [IsRegularLocalRing A]
    (hdim : (2 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim A) :
    Module.Finite A (A ⧸ maximalIdeal A) ∧ IsNormalRing (A ⧸ maximalIdeal A) ∧
      IsEmpty ↥(Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A (A ⧸ maximalIdeal A))) ⁻¹ᵁ
        Stacks.puncturedSpectrum A) ∧
      Etale (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A (A ⧸ maximalIdeal A))) ∣_
        Stacks.puncturedSpectrum A) ∧
      ¬ Algebra.Etale A (A ⧸ maximalIdeal A)
declarations.comment: clause (2) as literally stated is false: for every regular local ring `A` with `2 ≤ ringKrullDim A`, `B = A ⧸ 𝔪` is a finite `A`-algebra and a normal ring (`IsNormalRing`), the preimage of the punctured spectrum under `Spec B ⟶ Spec A` is empty, so the induced morphism over the punctured spectrum is finite étale, but `A → B` is not étale (`A ⧸ 𝔪` is not even torsion-free over `A`). This is why the clause-(2) declaration `Stacks.PurityDimensionTwo.etale_of_isNormalRing_of_two_le_ringKrullDim` carries the extra hypothesis `Module.IsTorsionFree A B`.

declarations.name: Stacks.PurityDimensionTwo.hasPurity_of_ringKrullDim_eq_two
declarations.doc:
**Purity of the branch locus, [Stacks, Tag 0BMA] clause (1), in dimension two.** Let `A` be
a regular local ring of Krull dimension `2`. Then every finite étale cover of the punctured
spectrum of `A` is the restriction of a finite étale cover of `Spec A`.

This is the source's argument. A regular local ring is a normal ring, so [Stacks, Tag 0BM9]
applies to it: the global sections `B = Γ(V, 𝒪_V)` of a finite étale `V ⟶ U` are a finite normal
`A`-algebra, torsion-free over `A`, whose spectrum is étale over `U`, and `V` extends over
`Spec A` exactly when `B` is finite étale over `A`. The latter is clause (2) of the tag in
dimension two, `etale_of_isNormalRing_of_ringKrullDim_eq_two`, whose hypotheses — normality of
`B`, finiteness and torsion-freeness over `A`, and étaleness over the punctured spectrum — are
precisely what [Stacks, Tag 0BM9] supplies.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasPurity_of_ringKrullDim_eq_two (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsRegularLocalRing A] (hdimA : ringKrullDim A = 2) :
    HasPurity A
declarations.comment: clause (1) of the tag, and in the case `d = 2`: `A` regular local with `ringKrullDim A = 2`, and the conclusion is `AlgebraicGeometry.HasPurity A`, i.e. essential surjectivity of `FÉt_{Spec A} ⟶ FÉt_U`, which is the source's definition of purity for `(A, 𝔪)`. This is the base case of the source's induction on `d`; the inductive step is tag 0BLM.

declarations.name: Stacks.PurityDimensionTwo.etale_of_isNormalRing_of_two_le_ringKrullDim
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BMA] clause (2) for every `d ≥ 2`.** Let `A` be a regular local ring of
dimension at least two and let `B` be a finite `A`-algebra which is a normal ring and
torsion-free over `A`, such that `Spec B ⟶ Spec A` is étale over the punctured spectrum. Then
`A → B` is étale.

This is the source's derivation of clause (2) from clause (1) through [Stacks, Tag 0BM9]: `A` is
normal, so `B` is an object of the category `NormalFiniteEtaleAwayAlgebra A` equivalent to
`(FÉt_U)ᵒᵖ`, hence `B ≅ Γ(V, 𝒪_V)` for some finite étale `V ⟶ U`; purity extends `V` over
`Spec A`, and the extension criterion of [Stacks, Tag 0BM9] then says that `Γ(V, 𝒪_V)` is finite
étale over `A`.

The hypothesis `Module.IsTorsionFree A B` is not in the source, and is necessary: it is exactly
the point at which the source's statement of clause (2) is wrong, and the counterexample is
recorded in the module docstring of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/FundamentalGroup/PurityBranchLocus/RegularDimensionTwo.lean`. In
brief: `B = A ⧸ 𝔪` is finite over `A`, is a field and hence a normal ring, and has empty
punctured spectrum, so it is étale over `U` vacuously; but `A` is a domain with `𝔪 ≠ 0`, so
`A ⧸ 𝔪` is not even flat over `A`; this is proved as
`Stacks.PurityDimensionTwo.quotient_maximalIdeal_counterexample_clauseTwo`. Nor does it help to
ask only that `algebraMap A B` be injective, or that `Spec B ⟶ Spec A` be surjective:
`B = A × (A ⧸ 𝔪)` is a finite normal `A`-algebra satisfying both, is the identity over `U`, and
is not flat over `A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etale_of_isNormalRing_of_two_le_ringKrullDim
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsRegularLocalRing A]
    [Module.Finite A B] [Module.IsTorsionFree A B] (hB : IsNormalRing B)
    (hdim : (2 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim A)
    (hetale : Etale (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)) ∣_
      Stacks.puncturedSpectrum A)) :
    Algebra.Etale A B
declarations.comment: clause (2) of the tag, at every `d ≥ 2`: `A` regular local with `2 ≤ ringKrullDim A`, `B` a finite `A`-algebra which is a normal ring in the sense of `IsNormalRing` (item (1) of tag 030C) and is torsion-free over `A`, and `Spec B ⟶ Spec A` étale over the punctured spectrum; the conclusion is `Algebra.Etale A B`. The source's derivation from clause (1) through tag 0BM9 is the proof, and clause (1) at every `d ≥ 2` is `AlgebraicGeometry.purityAtRegularLocalRings`. Torsion-freeness over `A` is an extra hypothesis, not present in the source and necessary for the statement to be true: the residue field `A ⧸ 𝔪` is a finite normal `A`-algebra whose spectrum misses the punctured spectrum, hence is étale there, and is not flat over `A`. Weakening it to injectivity of `algebraMap A B`, or to surjectivity of `Spec B ⟶ Spec A`, leaves the statement false as well: `B = A × (A ⧸ 𝔪)` is a finite normal `A`-algebra with both properties which is the identity over the punctured spectrum and is not flat over `A`. That clause (2) as literally stated is false is proved in `Stacks.PurityDimensionTwo.quotient_maximalIdeal_counterexample_clauseTwo` (`PurityBranchLocus.PurityClauseTwoCounterexample`); see also the module docstring of `PurityBranchLocus.RegularDimensionTwo`.

declarations.name: Stacks.PurityDimensionTwo.etale_of_isNormalRing_of_ringKrullDim_eq_two
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a regular local ring of Krull dimension `2`, and let `B` be a finite `A`-algebra
which is a normal ring and torsion-free over `A`, such that the induced morphism on punctured
spectra is étale. Then `A → B` is étale.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etale_of_isNormalRing_of_ringKrullDim_eq_two
    [IsRegularLocalRing A] [Module.Finite A B] [Module.IsTorsionFree A B]
    (hB : IsNormalRing B) (hdimA : ringKrullDim A = 2)
    (hetale : Etale (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)) ∣_
      Stacks.puncturedSpectrum A)) :
    Algebra.Etale A B
declarations.comment: clause (2) of the tag, and only in the case `d = 2`: `A` regular local with `ringKrullDim A = 2`, `B` a finite `A`-algebra which is a normal ring in the sense of `IsNormalRing` (item (1) of tag 030C) and is torsion-free over `A`, and `Spec B ⟶ Spec A` étale over the punctured spectrum; the conclusion is `Algebra.Etale A B`. This is the base case of the source's induction on `d`; the inductive step is tag 0BLM, and clause (2) for every `d ≥ 2` is `etale_of_isNormalRing_of_two_le_ringKrullDim` in `PurityBranchLocus.PurityRegularLocal`. Clause (1) at `d = 2` — essential surjectivity of `FÉt_X ⟶ FÉt_U`, i.e. purity for `A` — follows from this result through tag 0BM9 and is `Stacks.PurityDimensionTwo.hasPurity_of_ringKrullDim_eq_two`. Torsion-freeness over `A` is an extra hypothesis, not present in the source and necessary for the statement to be true: the residue field `A ⧸ 𝔪` is a finite normal `A`-algebra whose spectrum misses the punctured spectrum, hence is étale there, and is not étale over `A`. See the module docstring.

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.purityAtRegularLocalRings
registrations.comment:
clause (1) of the tag, at every `d ≥ 2`: for every regular local ring `A` with
  `2 ≤ ringKrullDim A`, `AlgebraicGeometry.HasPurity A`, i.e. essential surjectivity of
  `FÉt_{Spec A} ⟶ FÉt_U` for `U` the punctured spectrum, which is the source's definition of purity
  for `(A, 𝔪)`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleAt_of_quasiFiniteAt_of_unramifiedAt_codimensionOne
declarations.doc:
**Purity of the branch locus, [Stacks, Tag 0BMB], in any dimension.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
morphism of locally Noetherian schemes and let `x : X` be a point whose local ring is normal,
with regular local ring at `f x`, at which `f` is quasi-finite, and such that the two local rings
have the same dimension, which is at least one. If `f` is unramified at every point specializing
to `x` whose local ring has dimension one, then `f` is étale at `x`.

The hypotheses are exactly the tag's own.

The proof is the source's induction on `d = dim 𝒪_{X,x}`. For `d ≤ 2` the conclusion is
`AlgebraicGeometry.etaleAt_of_quasiFiniteAt_of_unramifiedAt_codimensionOne_of_dim_le_two`. For
`d ≥ 3` the induction hypothesis gives étaleness at every proper generization of `x` — their local
rings are normal, the local rings below them regular, `f` is quasi-finite there because the
quasi-finite locus is open, and the two dimensions agree there by
`AlgebraicGeometry.ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_of_specializes_of_quasiFiniteAt` — and that is what makes
`𝒪_{X,x}` Cohen–Macaulay, whence the conclusion. The Cohen–Macaulay step is where
[Stacks, Tag 0BMA] clause (2) enters, through
`Stacks.PurityBranchLocus.purityFiniteNormal`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etaleAt_of_quasiFiniteAt_of_unramifiedAt_codimensionOne
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] (x : X)
    (hX : IsNormalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hY : IsRegularLocalRing (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)))
    (hqf : quasiFiniteAt f x)
    (hdim : ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = ringKrullDim (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)))
    (hone : 1 ≤ ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hunr : ∀ x' : X, x' ⤳ x → ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x') = 1 → UnramifiedAt f x') :
    EtaleAt f x
declarations.comment: the whole tag, in every dimension: hypotheses (1) `𝒪_{X,x}` normal, (2) `𝒪_{Y,f x}` regular, (3) `f` quasi-finite at `x`, (4) `dim 𝒪_{X,x} = dim 𝒪_{Y,f x}` and `1 ≤ dim 𝒪_{X,x}`, and (5) `f` unramified at every point specializing to `x` whose local ring has dimension one; the conclusion is `EtaleAt f x`. The proof is the source's induction on `dim 𝒪_{X,x}`, with the case `dim 𝒪_{X,x} ≤ 2` as its base case and tag 0BMA clause (2) in every dimension, `Stacks.PurityDimensionTwo.etale_of_isNormalRing_of_two_le_ringKrullDim`, supplying Cohen–Macaulayness of `𝒪_{X,x}` above it.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleAt_of_quasiFiniteAt_of_unramifiedAt_codimensionOne_of_dim_le_two
declarations.doc:
**Purity of the branch locus, [Stacks, Tag 0BMB], in dimension at most two.** Let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of locally Noetherian schemes and let `x : X` be a point whose local
ring is normal, with regular local ring at `f x`, at which `f` is quasi-finite, and such that the
two local rings have the same dimension, which is at least one and at most two. If `f` is
unramified at every point specializing to `x` whose local ring has dimension one, then `f` is
étale at `x`.

This is the tag with its hypothesis `1 ≤ dim 𝒪_{X,x}` supplemented by `dim 𝒪_{X,x} ≤ 2`. See the
module docstring for what the case `dim 𝒪_{X,x} ≥ 3` comes down to.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etaleAt_of_quasiFiniteAt_of_unramifiedAt_codimensionOne_of_dim_le_two
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] (x : X)
    (hX : IsNormalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hY : IsRegularLocalRing (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)))
    (hqf : quasiFiniteAt f x)
    (hdim : ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = ringKrullDim (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)))
    (hone : 1 ≤ ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hle : ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) ≤ 2)
    (hunr : ∀ x' : X, x' ⤳ x → ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x') = 1 → UnramifiedAt f x') :
    EtaleAt f x
declarations.comment: the case `1 ≤ dim 𝒪_{X,x} = dim 𝒪_{Y,f x} ≤ 2`. Hypotheses (1), (2), (3) and (5) are the tag's own; hypothesis (4) is the tag's `dim 𝒪_{X,x} = dim 𝒪_{Y,f x} ≥ 1` together with the case restriction `dim 𝒪_{X,x} ≤ 2`. Flatness of `𝒪_{Y,f x} → 𝒪_{X,x}` is miracle flatness (tag 00R4), a normal Noetherian local ring of dimension at most two being Cohen–Macaulay by Serre's criterion (tag 031S) and the fibre ring being zero-dimensional by quasi-finiteness; étaleness at `x` then follows from tag 0BJH. For `dim 𝒪_{X,x} ≥ 3` the same reduction leaves exactly the flatness of `𝒪_{Y,f x} → 𝒪_{X,x}`, which is tag 0BMA clause (2) at a general dimension. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleAt_of_quasiFiniteAt_of_unramifiedAt_codimensionOne_of_dim_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**Purity of the branch locus, [Stacks, Tag 0BMB], in dimension one.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
morphism of locally Noetherian schemes and let `x : X` be a point whose local ring is normal,
with regular local ring at `f x`, at which `f` is quasi-finite, and such that the two local
rings have the same dimension, equal to one. If `f` is unramified at every point specializing
to `x` whose local ring has dimension one, then `f` is étale at `x`.

This is the tag with its hypothesis `1 ≤ dim 𝒪_{X,x}` restricted to `dim 𝒪_{X,x} = 1`, the base
case of the source's induction on the dimension. The whole range `1 ≤ dim 𝒪_{X,x} ≤ 2` is
`etaleAt_of_quasiFiniteAt_of_unramifiedAt_codimensionOne_of_dim_le_two` in
`PurityBranchLocus.DimensionAtMostTwo`, which subsumes this statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleAt_of_quasiFiniteAt_of_unramifiedAt_codimensionOne_of_dim_eq_one
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] (x : X)
    (hX : IsNormalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hY : IsRegularLocalRing (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)))
    (hqf : quasiFiniteAt f x)
    (hdim : ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = ringKrullDim (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)))
    (hone : ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = 1)
    (hunr : ∀ x' : X, x' ⤳ x → ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x') = 1 → UnramifiedAt f x') :
    EtaleAt f x
declarations.comment:
the case `dim 𝒪_{X,x} = dim 𝒪_{Y,f x} = 1`, which is the base case of the
source's induction on the dimension; hypotheses (1), (2), (3) and (5) are the tag's own and
hypothesis (4) is the tag's with `1 ≤ d` restricted to `d = 1`. The range `1 ≤ d ≤ 2` is
`etaleAt_of_quasiFiniteAt_of_unramifiedAt_codimensionOne_of_dim_le_two` in
`PurityBranchLocus.DimensionAtMostTwo`.

declarations.name: mapTopology_nhds_hasBasis
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BMC**.
For every `f : E → E`, the family `{ U_S S f | S : Finset E }` of sets of maps agreeing with `f` on
a finite subset `S` is a basis of neighbourhoods of `f` in the product (equivalently, when `E` is
discrete, the compact-open) topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem mapTopology_nhds_hasBasis (f : E → E) :
    (nhds f).HasBasis (fun _ : Finset E => True) (fun S => U_S S f)

declarations.name: continuous_action
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BMC**.
The action map `Map(E, E) × E → E`, `(f, e) ↦ f e`, is continuous when `E` carries the discrete
topology and `Map(E, E) = (E → E)` carries the product (= compact-open) topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem continuous_action :
    Continuous (fun p : (E → E) × E => p.1 p.2)

declarations.name: continuous_iff_uncurry_continuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BMC**.
A map `g : X → (E → E)` is continuous if and only if the uncurried map `X × E → E`,
`(x, e) ↦ g x e`, is continuous.
declarations.statement:
theorem continuous_iff_uncurry_continuous
    {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] (g : X → (E → E)) :
    Continuous g ↔ Continuous (fun p : X × E => g p.1 p.2)

declarations.name: continuous_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BMC**.
Composition `Map(E, E) × Map(E, E) → Map(E, E)`, `(f, g) ↦ f ∘ g`, is continuous.
declarations.statement:
theorem continuous_comp :
    Continuous (fun p : (E → E) × (E → E) => p.1 ∘ p.2)

declarations.name: continuous_perm_inv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BMC**.
Inversion `σ ↦ σ⁻¹` on `Aut(E) = Equiv.Perm E` is continuous.
declarations.statement:
theorem continuous_perm_inv :
    Continuous (fun σ : Equiv.Perm E => σ⁻¹)

declarations.name: isTopologicalGroup_aut
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BMC**.
`Aut(E) = Equiv.Perm E`, with the subspace topology induced from `Map(E, E)`, is a topological
group.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTopologicalGroup_aut :
    IsTopologicalGroup (Equiv.Perm E)

declarations.name: AlgEquiv.exists_algEquiv_algebraMap_eq_of_normal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BME (1).** Let `L / M / K` be a tower of fields with `M / K` normal. Then every
automorphism `τ` of `L / K` induces an automorphism `τ|_M` of `M / K`, that is, an automorphism
of `M / K` through which `τ` acts on the image of `M` in `L`. No algebraicity of `L / K` is
needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem AlgEquiv.exists_algEquiv_algebraMap_eq_of_normal [Normal K M] (τ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
    ∃ τM : M ≃ₐ[K] M, ∀ m : M, algebraMap M L (τM m) = τ (algebraMap M L m)
declarations.comment:
(1): an automorphism of `L / K` restricts to an automorphism of `M` when `M / K`
is normal

declarations.name: AlgHom.exists_algEquiv_extending_of_normal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BME (2).** Let `L / M / K` be a tower of fields with `L / K` normal. Then every
`K`-algebra map `σ : M → L` extends to an automorphism of `L / K`, that is, an automorphism
`τ` of `L / K` with `τ ∘ (M → L) = σ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem AlgHom.exists_algEquiv_extending_of_normal [Normal K L] (σ : M →ₐ[K] L) :
    ∃ τ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, ∀ m : M, τ (algebraMap M L m) = σ m
declarations.comment:
(2): a `K`-algebra map `M → L` extends to an automorphism of `L` when `L / K`
is normal

declarations.name: NormalClosure
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev NormalClosure (F E : Type*) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E] : Type _
declarations.comment: absolute

declarations.name: normalClosure.algebraOfTower
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance normalClosure.algebraOfTower (K M N L : Type*)
    [Field K] [Field M] [Field N] [Field L]
    [Algebra K N] [Algebra K L] [Algebra M N] [Algebra M L] [Algebra N L]
    [IsScalarTower K N L] [IsScalarTower M N L] :
    Algebra M (normalClosure K N L)
declarations.comment: 2, containment

declarations.name: finiteDimensional_normalClosure_of_tower
declarations.doc:
If we have `L/N/M/K` where `M/K` is normal and `N/M` is finite dimensional then
the normal closure of `N/K` in `L/K` is finite dimensional over `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_normalClosure_of_tower (K M N L : Type*)
    [Field K] [Field M] [Field N] [Field L]
    [Algebra K M] [Algebra K N] [Algebra K L] [Algebra M N] [Algebra M L] [Algebra N L]
    [IsScalarTower K M N] [IsScalarTower K M L] [IsScalarTower K N L] [IsScalarTower M N L]
    [FiniteDimensional M N] [Normal K M] : FiniteDimensional M (normalClosure K N L)
declarations.comment: 2, finite

declarations.name: AlgEquiv.ker_restrictNormalHom_eq_image_restrictScalarsHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BMH** (exactness at the middle term).
For a tower `F ⊂ K ⊂ L` with `K/F` normal, the kernel of the restriction map
`Gal(L/F) →* Gal(K/F)` equals the image of the scalar-restriction map
`Gal(L/K) →* Gal(L/F)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem AlgEquiv.ker_restrictNormalHom_eq_image_restrictScalarsHom
    (F K L : Type*) [Field F] [Field K] [Field L]
    [Algebra F K] [Algebra K L] [Algebra F L] [IsScalarTower F K L] [Normal F K] :
    (AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom K).ker =
      (AlgEquiv.restrictScalarsHom F (S := K) (A := L)).range
declarations.comment: exact at the middle

declarations.name: AlgEquiv.exists_restrictScalars_eq_of_restrictNormal_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BMH** (exactness at the middle term, lift kernel to image).
For a tower `F ⊂ K ⊂ L` with `K/F` normal, any `σ ∈ Gal(L/F)` whose restriction to `K`
is the identity is the restriction of scalars of some `τ ∈ Gal(L/K)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem AlgEquiv.exists_restrictScalars_eq_of_restrictNormal_eq_one
    {F K L : Type*} [Field F] [Field K] [Field L]
    [Algebra F K] [Algebra K L] [Algebra F L] [IsScalarTower F K L]
    [Normal F K] {σ : Gal(L/F)} (hσ : σ.restrictNormal K = 1) :
    ∃ τ : Gal(L/K), τ.restrictScalars F = σ
declarations.comment: exact at the middle -- lift kernel to image

declarations.name: AlgEquiv.restrictNormal_restrictScalars
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BMH** (composition is trivial).
For a tower `F ⊂ K ⊂ L` with `K/F` normal, restricting an element of `Gal(L/K)` to
`K` via the scalar-restriction `Gal(L/K) → Gal(L/F)` followed by `restrictNormal K`
yields the identity.

    [Algebra F K] [Algebra K L] [Algebra F L] [IsScalarTower F K L]
    [Normal F K] (σ : Gal(L/K)) :
    (σ.restrictScalars F).restrictNormal K = 1
declarations.comment: composition is 0

declarations.name: isOpen_krullTopology_apply_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BMJ** (action is continuous).
For `x : L` and `y : L` algebraic over `K`, the set of `σ ∈ Gal(L/K)` sending `x` to `y` is
open in the Krull topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_krullTopology_apply_eq (K : Type*) {L : Type*} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    (x : L) {y : L} (hy : IsAlgebraic K y) : IsOpen {σ : Gal(L/K) | σ x = y}
declarations.comment: continuous

declarations.name: isOpen_krullTopology_apply_eq'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BMJ** (action is continuous, algebraic extension).
For an algebraic extension `L/K` and any `x y : L`, the set of `σ ∈ Gal(L/K)` sending `x`
to `y` is open in the Krull topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_krullTopology_apply_eq' (K : Type*) {L : Type*} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic K L] (x y : L) : IsOpen {σ : Gal(L/K) | σ x = y}
declarations.comment: continuous

declarations.name: continuous_krullTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BMJ** (universal property of the Krull topology).
A map `f : X → Gal(L/K)` from a topological space `X` is continuous whenever the induced
action `X × L → L` is continuous, expressed here as: for every `x : L` and `y : L`,
the set `{i ∈ X | f i x = y}` is open.
declarations.statement:
theorem continuous_krullTopology {K L X : Type*} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    [TopologicalSpace X] {f : X → Gal(L/K)} (hf : ∀ x y, IsOpen {i | f i x = y}) : Continuous f
declarations.comment: universal property

declarations.name: krullTopology.isTopologicalGroup_and_compactSpace_and_t2Space_and_totallyDisconnectedSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BMJ** (2). For a Galois extension `L/K`, the Krull topology makes `Gal(L/K)` a
profinite topological group: a topological group which is compact, Hausdorff and totally
disconnected.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTopologicalGroup_and_compactSpace_and_t2Space_and_totallyDisconnectedSpace
    [IsGalois K L] :
    IsTopologicalGroup Gal(L/K) ∧ CompactSpace Gal(L/K) ∧ T2Space Gal(L/K) ∧
      TotallyDisconnectedSpace Gal(L/K)
declarations.comment: (2): Gal(L/K) is a profinite topological group

declarations.name: krullTopology.isGreatest_and_continuous_and_profinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BMJ**. Let `L/K` be a Galois extension and give `L` the discrete topology.
The Krull topology is the coarsest topology on `Gal(L/K)` for which the action
`Gal(L/K) × L → L` is continuous, and with it
(1) a map `f : X → Gal(L/K)` from a topological space `X` is continuous whenever the induced
action `X × L → L` is continuous, and
(2) `Gal(L/K)` is a profinite topological group.
declarations.comment:
coarsest topology making the action continuous; (1) universal property;
(2) profinite topological group

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isColimit_cofork_of_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BMN.** A coequalizer of schemes can be checked after an fpqc
covering provided it is also a coequalizer on every pairwise overlap.
declarations.statement:
theorem isColimit_cofork_of_fpqc {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (a b : X ⟶ Y) (c : Y ⟶ Z)
    (h : a ≫ c = b ≫ c) {I : Type v} (Z' : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, Z' i ⟶ Z)
    (hfpqc : Presieve.ofArrows Z' f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage Z)
    (hlocal : ∀ i, Nonempty (IsColimit (baseChangeCofork a b c h (f i))))
    (hoverlap : ∀ i j, Nonempty (IsColimit
      (baseChangeCofork a b c h (pullback.fst (f i) (f j) ≫ f i)))) :
    Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofork.ofπ c h))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isColimit_of_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BMP.** The colimit property for a cocone of schemes can be checked
on an fpqc covering of its vertex and on all pairwise overlaps.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isColimit_of_fpqc {J : Type v} [Category.{w} J]
    {F : J ⥤ Scheme.{u}} (c : Cocone F) {I : Type*}
    (W' : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, W' i ⟶ c.pt)
    (hfpqc : Presieve.ofArrows W' f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage c.pt)
    (hlocal : ∀ i, Nonempty (IsColimit (baseChangeCocone c (f i))))
    (hoverlap : ∀ i j, Nonempty (IsColimit
      (baseChangeCocone c (pullback.fst (f i) (f j) ≫ f i)))) :
    Nonempty (IsColimit c)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.isClosedEmbedding_componentEmbedding
declarations.doc:
The componentwise map identifies the automorphism group of a set-valued functor with a
closed subgroup of the product of the automorphism groups of its values.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.isProfiniteGrp_functorAutomorphismTopology
declarations.doc:
If every value of a set-valued functor is finite, its automorphism group with the topology
induced by componentwise evaluation is a profinite group.
declarations.comment: profinite group

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.exists_forget_fiberFunctor_contActionFintypeCat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BMS**, the forgetful functor. For a topological group `G` there is a functor from
the category of continuous actions of `G` on finite sets to finite sets which is a fibre functor,
preserves finite limits and finite colimits, and which becomes the forgetful functor to sets after
composing with the inclusion of finite sets into sets.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_forget_fiberFunctor_contActionFintypeCat
    (G : Type v) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] :
    ∃ F : ContAction FintypeCat.{u} G ⥤ FintypeCat.{u},
      PreGaloisCategory.FiberFunctor F ∧
      PreservesFiniteLimits F ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits F ∧
      Nonempty (F ⋙ FintypeCat.incl ≅ forget (ContAction FintypeCat.{u} G))
declarations.comment: the forgetful functor from finite `G`-sets

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.equiv_finiteContinuousGSet
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BMS**, the subcategory. The full subcategory of the category `G-Sets` of
[Stacks, Tag 04JJ] on the finite objects is the category of continuous actions of `G` on finite
sets.
declarations.statement:
theorem equiv_finiteContinuousGSet (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] :
    Nonempty (AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteContinuousGSet.{u, u} G ≌ ContAction FintypeCat.{u} G)
declarations.comment: the full subcategory of `G`-Sets on the finite objects

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.continuous_actionOnForget
declarations.doc: The canonical action homomorphism is continuous for the componentwise topology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem continuous_actionOnForget (G : Type u) [Group G]
    [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] :
    let _ : TopologicalSpace (Aut (forget (ContAction FintypeCat.{u} G))) :=
      functorAutomorphismTopology _
    Continuous (actionOnForget G)
declarations.comment: continuity of the canonical homomorphism

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.canonicalHom_apply
declarations.doc: On every finite continuous action, the canonical homomorphism acts by the given action.
declarations.statement:
public theorem canonicalHom_apply (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] (g : G) (X : ContAction FintypeCat.{u} G)
    (x : X.obj.V.obj) :
    let _ : TopologicalSpace (Aut (forget (ContAction FintypeCat.{u} G))) :=
      functorAutomorphismTopology _
    ConcreteCategory.hom (((canonicalHom G) g).asIso.hom.app X) x =
      ConcreteCategory.hom (X.obj.ρ g).asHom x
declarations.comment: component action of the canonical homomorphism

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.profiniteCompletionEquiv_forgetAut
declarations.doc:
The automorphism group of the forgetful functor on finite continuous `G`-sets, with its
componentwise topology, is canonically the profinite completion of `G`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem profiniteCompletionEquiv_forgetAut
    (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] :
    let _ : TopologicalSpace (Aut (forget (ContAction FintypeCat.{u} G))) :=
      functorAutomorphismTopology _
    let _ : IsTopologicalGroup (Aut (forget (ContAction FintypeCat.{u} G))) :=
      functorAutomorphismIsTopologicalGroup _
    IsProfiniteCompletion.{u, u + 1, w} (canonicalHom G)
declarations.comment: profinite completion universal property

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.nonempty_iso_forget_of_preservesFiniteLimits_and_colimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BMV.** An exact set-valued functor on finite continuous actions of a
topological group, with finite values, is naturally isomorphic to the underlying-set functor.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_iso_forget_of_preservesFiniteLimits_and_colimits
    {G : Type v} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]
    (F : ContAction FintypeCat.{u} G ⥤ Type u)
    [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteColimits F]
    [∀ X, Finite (F.obj X)] :
    Nonempty (F ≅ forget (ContAction FintypeCat.{u} G))
