declarations.name: CategoryTheory.IsGaloisCategory
declarations.doc:
The Galois category axioms for a category `C` equipped with a fixed functor from `C` to
sets.
declarations.statement: public class IsGaloisCategory {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (F : C ⥤ Type w) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.isInitial_iff_isEmpty_fiber
declarations.doc: An object of a Galois category is initial if and only if its fibre is empty.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isInitial_iff_isEmpty_fiber {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
    (F : C ⥤ Type w) [IsGaloisCategory F] (A : C) :
    Nonempty (IsInitial A) ↔ IsEmpty (F.obj A)
declarations.comment: initial_iff_empty

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.isTerminal_iff_unique_fiber
declarations.doc: An object of a Galois category is terminal if and only if its fibre is a singleton.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isTerminal_iff_unique_fiber {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
    (F : C ⥤ Type w) [IsGaloisCategory F] (Z : C) :
    Nonempty (IsTerminal Z) ↔ Nonempty (Unique (F.obj Z))
declarations.comment: terminal_iff_singleton

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.IsGaloisCategory.mono_iff_injective
declarations.doc: A morphism in a Galois category is mono if and only if its map on fibres is injective.
declarations.comment: mono_iff_injective

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.epi_iff_surjective_on_fiber
declarations.doc:
A morphism in a Galois category is an epimorphism if and only if its map on fibres is
surjective.
declarations.statement:
public lemma epi_iff_surjective_on_fiber {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
    (F : C ⥤ Type w) [IsGaloisCategory F] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    Epi f ↔ Function.Surjective (F.map f)
declarations.comment: epi_iff_surjective

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.fiberFunctor_faithful
declarations.doc: The fibre functor of a Galois category is faithful.
declarations.statement:
public instance fiberFunctor_faithful {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
    (F : C ⥤ Type w) [IsGaloisCategory F] : F.Faithful
declarations.comment: faithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.hom_ext_of_isConnected
declarations.doc: Two morphisms from a connected object agree if their maps on fibres agree at one point.
declarations.statement:
public lemma hom_ext_of_isConnected {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
    (F : C ⥤ Type w) [IsGaloisCategory F] {X Y : C}
    [PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected X] (a b : X ⟶ Y) (x : F.obj X)
    (h : F.map a x = F.map b x) : a = b
declarations.comment: one_element

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.epi_of_connected
declarations.doc: Every morphism between connected objects in a Galois category is an epimorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem epi_of_connected {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
    (F : C ⥤ Type w) [IsGaloisCategory F] {X Y : C}
    [PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected X] [PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) : Epi f
declarations.comment: connected_epi

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.exists_component_maps
declarations.doc:
A map from a coproduct of connected objects to a finite coproduct factors componentwise
through a map of indexing types.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_component_maps {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
    (F : C ⥤ Type w) [IsGaloisCategory F]
    {I : Type x} {J : Type y} [Finite J]
    (A : I → C) (B : J → C) (X Y : C)
    (a : (i : I) → A i ⟶ X) (b : (j : J) → B j ⟶ Y)
    (_ha : IsColimit (Cofan.mk X a)) (hb : IsColimit (Cofan.mk Y b))
    (hA : ∀ i, PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected (A i)) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    ∃ (α : I → J) (g : (i : I) → A i ⟶ B (α i)),
      ∀ i, g i ≫ b (α i) = a i ≫ f
declarations.comment: component_maps

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.exists_aut_app_eq_of_isConnected
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BN3.** The automorphism group of the fibre functor of a Galois
category acts transitively on the fibre of a connected object.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_aut_app_eq_of_isConnected (F : C ⥤ Type w) [hG : IsGaloisCategory F] (X : C)
    [PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected X] (x y : F.obj X) :
    ∃ σ : Aut F, σ.asIso.hom.app X x = y

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.nonempty_fiberIso_of_exact
declarations.doc: An exact functor between Galois categories admits an isomorphism of fibre functors.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_fiberIso_of_exact
    (F : C ⥤ FintypeCat.{w}) (F' : C' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w})
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F)]
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F')]
    (H : C ⥤ C') (hH : exactFunctor C C' H) :
    Nonempty (H ⋙ F' ≅ F)
declarations.comment: existence of the fibre-functor isomorphism

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.nonempty_galoisFunctorData_of_fiberIso
declarations.doc:
For every chosen isomorphism of fibre functors, transport of structure gives a continuous
homomorphism and a 2-isomorphism between the two routes around the finite-action square.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_galoisFunctorData_of_fiberIso
    (F : C ⥤ FintypeCat.{w}) (F' : C' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w})
    (H : C ⥤ C') (t : H ⋙ F' ≅ F) :
    Nonempty (GaloisFunctorData F F' H t)
declarations.comment: continuous homomorphism and 2-commutative square

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.galoisFunctorData_hom_innerConjugate
declarations.doc:
The homomorphisms obtained from two choices of fibre-functor isomorphism differ by an inner
automorphism of the target automorphism group.
declarations.statement:
public theorem galoisFunctorData_hom_innerConjugate
    {F : C ⥤ FintypeCat.{w}} {F' : C' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w}} {H : C ⥤ C'}
    {t₁ t₂ : H ⋙ F' ≅ F} (d₁ : GaloisFunctorData F F' H t₁)
    (d₂ : GaloisFunctorData F F' H t₂) :
    IsInnerConjugate d₁.hom.toMonoidHom d₂.hom.toMonoidHom
declarations.comment: independence up to inner conjugacy

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.nonempty_exactFunctorInducingData
declarations.doc:
Every continuous homomorphism between the automorphism groups of two Galois fibre functors is
induced by an exact functor and an isomorphism of fibre functors.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_exactFunctorInducingData
    (F : C ⥤ FintypeCat.{w}) (F' : C' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w})
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F)]
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F')]
    (h : Aut F' →ₜ* Aut F) :
    Nonempty (ExactFunctorInducingData F F' h)
declarations.comment: converse construction

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.surjective_inducedHom_tfae
declarations.doc:
The five characterizations of surjectivity of the homomorphism induced by an exact functor
between Galois categories.
declarations.statement:
public theorem surjective_inducedHom_tfae
    (F : C ⥤ FintypeCat.{w}) (F' : C' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w})
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F)]
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F')]
    (H : C ⥤ C') (_hH : exactFunctor C C' H) (t : H ⋙ F' ≅ F)
    (d : GaloisFunctorData F F' H t)
    (star : C) (star' : C') (hstar : IsTerminal star) (hstar' : IsTerminal star')
    (hHstar : IsTerminal (H.obj star)) :
    List.TFAE
      [ Function.Surjective d.hom,
        Nonempty H.FullyFaithful,
        ∀ X : C, PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected X →
          PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected (H.obj X),
        ∀ X : C, PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected X →
          Nonempty (star' ⟶ H.obj X) → Nonempty (star ⟶ X),
        ∀ X : C, Function.Bijective (mapFromTerminal H hstar' hHstar X) ]

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.surjective_inducedHom_tfae_of_fiberIso
declarations.doc:
The five characterizations of surjectivity of the homomorphism induced by an exact functor
between Galois categories.

This is the form of the statement in which nothing beyond the exact functor `H`, the two Galois
categories and their chosen final objects is assumed: the continuous homomorphism of the
functoriality diagram is the one produced from the fibre-functor isomorphism `t`, and the
image of the chosen final object is seen to be final using exactness of `H`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem surjective_inducedHom_tfae_of_fiberIso
    (F : C ⥤ FintypeCat.{w}) (F' : C' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w})
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F)]
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F')]
    (H : C ⥤ C') (hH : exactFunctor C C' H) (t : H ⋙ F' ≅ F)
    (star : C) (star' : C') (hstar : IsTerminal star) (hstar' : IsTerminal star') :
    List.TFAE
      [ Function.Surjective (galoisFunctorDataOfFiberIso F F' H t).hom,
        Nonempty H.FullyFaithful,
        ∀ X : C, PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected X →
          PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected (H.obj X),
        ∀ X : C, PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected X →
          Nonempty (star' ⟶ H.obj X) → Nonempty (star ⟶ X),
        ∀ X : C, Function.Bijective
          (mapFromTerminal H hstar' (isTerminalObjOfExactFunctor H hH hstar) X) ]

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.injective_inducedHom_iff_exists_epi_mono
declarations.doc:
The induced homomorphism is injective precisely when every connected target object admits
an epimorphic cover that is a subobject of the image of a source object.
declarations.statement:
public theorem injective_inducedHom_iff_exists_epi_mono
    (F : C ⥤ FintypeCat.{w}) (F' : C' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w})
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F)]
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F')]
    (H : C ⥤ C') (t : H ⋙ F' ≅ F)
    (d : GaloisFunctorData F F' H t) :
    Function.Injective d.hom ↔
      ∀ X'' : C', PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected X'' →
        ∃ (X' : C) (Y'' : C') (p : Y'' ⟶ X'') (i : Y'' ⟶ H.obj X'),
          Epi p ∧ Mono i

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.injective_inducedHom_iff_exists_epi_mono_of_fiberIso
declarations.doc:
The induced homomorphism is injective precisely when every connected target object admits
an epimorphic cover that is a subobject of the image of a source object.

This is the form of the statement in which no part of the functoriality data is assumed: the
continuous homomorphism of the diagram is the one produced from the fibre-functor isomorphism
`t`, whose continuity and whose 2-isomorphism of the functoriality square are constructed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem injective_inducedHom_iff_exists_epi_mono_of_fiberIso
    (F : C ⥤ FintypeCat.{w}) (F' : C' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w})
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F)]
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F')]
    (H : C ⥤ C') (t : H ⋙ F' ≅ F) :
    Function.Injective (galoisFunctorDataOfFiberIso F F' H t).hom ↔
      ∀ X'' : C', PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected X'' →
        ∃ (X' : C) (Y'' : C') (p : Y'' ⟶ X'') (i : Y'' ⟶ H.obj X'),
          Epi p ∧ Mono i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtaleOverSpecEquivOfIsSepClosed
declarations.doc:
For a separably closed field `K`, the category `FÉt_{Spec K}` of schemes finite étale over
`Spec K` is equivalent to the category of finite sets. It is the composite of the relative
spectrum equivalence `FÉt_{Spec K} ≌ (finite étale K-algebras)ᵒᵖ` with Mathlib's
`CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale.equivOfIsSepClosed`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def finiteEtaleOverSpecEquivOfIsSepClosed (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsSepClosed K] :
    FiniteEtaleOver (Spec (.of K)) ≌ FintypeCat.{u}
declarations.comment:
Stated for `k` separably closed, the general case of the example; an algebraically
closed field is separably closed. The scheme-level category `FÉt_{Spec k}` is
`FiniteEtaleOver (Spec k)`.

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.preservesFiniteColimits_finiteEtaleBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BN9, the fourth assertion: base change of finite étale covers preserves finite
colimits.**

Finite colimits of `FÉt_S` are generated by its finite coproducts, which base change preserves by
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.preservesFiniteCoproducts_finiteEtaleBaseChange`, and its coequalizers,
which it preserves by
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.preservesColimitsOfShape_walkingParallelPair_finiteEtaleBaseChange`.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesFiniteColimits_finiteEtaleBaseChange {S X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (finiteEtaleBaseChange f)
declarations.comment: base change preserves finite colimits

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.hasFiniteColimitsWithLocalCoequalizers
declarations.doc:
The category of finite étale covers of a scheme has finite colimits, and the underlying cofork
of schemes of a coequalizer of two morphisms of finite étale covers is a coequalizer over an fpqc
covering of its target and over each pairwise overlap of that covering.
declarations.statement:
instance hasFiniteColimitsWithLocalCoequalizers (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    HasFiniteColimitsWithLocalCoequalizers X
declarations.comment: finite colimits

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.hasFiniteLimits_finiteEtaleOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BN9.** The category of finite étale schemes over a scheme has
finite limits.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance hasFiniteLimits_finiteEtaleOver (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    HasFiniteLimits (FiniteEtaleOver X)
declarations.comment: finite limits

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.preservesFiniteLimits_finiteEtaleBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BN9.** Base change of finite étale schemes preserves finite
limits.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance preservesFiniteLimits_finiteEtaleBaseChange
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (finiteEtaleBaseChange f)
declarations.comment: base change preserves finite limits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.preservesFiniteColimits_finiteEtaleOverForgetOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BNA.** The forgetful functor from finite étale covers to schemes over
the base preserves finite colimits.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesFiniteColimits_finiteEtaleOverForgetOver (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (finiteEtaleOverForgetOver X)
declarations.comment: part (1), over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.preservesFiniteColimits_finiteEtaleOverForget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BNA.** The forgetful functor from finite étale covers to schemes
preserves finite colimits.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesFiniteColimits_finiteEtaleOverForget (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (finiteEtaleOverForget X)
declarations.comment: part (1), underlying schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.preservesFiniteLimits_finiteEtaleOverForgetOver
declarations.doc:
The forgetful functor from finite étale covers to schemes over the base preserves finite
limits.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesFiniteLimits_finiteEtaleOverForgetOver (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (finiteEtaleOverForgetOver X)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.preservesFiniteConnectedLimits_finiteEtaleOverForget
declarations.doc:
The forgetful functor from finite étale covers to schemes preserves limits of every finite
connected shape, in particular equalizers and fibre products.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesFiniteConnectedLimits_finiteEtaleOverForget
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (J : Type v) [SmallCategory J] [FinCategory J] [IsConnected J] :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape J (finiteEtaleOverForget X)
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.isGaloisCategory_finiteEtaleFiberFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BNB.** For a connected scheme `X` and a geometric point `x` of `X`,
the category `FÉt_X` of finite étale covers of `X` together with the geometric fibre functor
`F_x` is a Galois category.

The six axioms are: finite limits and finite colimits of `FÉt_X`
(`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.hasFiniteLimits_finiteEtaleOver` and
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.hasFiniteColimits_finiteEtaleOver`); every cover is a finite coproduct
of connected ones (`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteCoproduct_isConnected_finiteEtaleOver`);
finiteness of every geometric fibre (`AlgebraicGeometry.finite_finiteEtaleFiber`); that `F_x`
reflects isomorphisms (`AlgebraicGeometry.reflectsIsomorphisms_finiteEtaleFiberFunctor`); and
exactness of `F_x`, whose limit half is
`AlgebraicGeometry.preservesFiniteLimits_finiteEtaleFiberFunctor` and whose colimit half is
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.preservesFiniteColimits_finiteEtaleFiberFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
instance isGaloisCategory_finiteEtaleFiberFunctor {X : Scheme.{u}} [ConnectedSpace X]
    (x : GeometricPoint X) : IsGaloisCategory (finiteEtaleFiberFunctor x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtaleFiberFunctor_isGaloisCategory
declarations.doc:
The fibre functor at a geometric point makes finite étale covers of a connected scheme into
a Galois category.
declarations.statement:
instance finiteEtaleFiberFunctor_isGaloisCategory (X : Scheme.{u}) [ConnectedSpace X]
    (x : GeometricPoint X) :
    CategoryTheory.IsGaloisCategory (finiteEtaleFiberFunctor x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleFundamentalGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BNC.** The étale fundamental group of a connected scheme at a
geometric point is the automorphism group of its finite-étale fibre functor, endowed with the
topology induced by its actions on all fibres.
declarations.statement:
public def EtaleFundamentalGroup (X : Scheme.{u}) [ConnectedSpace X]
    (x : GeometricPoint X) : Type (u + 1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteEtaleEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tags 0BND (1) and 03VF (3).** Finite étale covers of a connected scheme `X`
are equivalent to finite sets with a continuous action of `π₁(X, x)`, by an equivalence whose
underlying finite sets are the geometric fibres at `x` and whose action is evaluation of natural
automorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteEtaleEquivalence (X : Scheme.{u}) [ConnectedSpace X]
    (x : GeometricPoint X) :
    ∃ E : FiniteEtaleOver X ≌ ContAction FintypeCat.{u} (EtaleFundamentalGroup X x),
      ∃ α : E.functor ⋙
          forget₂ (ContAction FintypeCat.{u} (EtaleFundamentalGroup X x))
            FintypeCat.{u} ⋙ FintypeCat.incl ≅ finiteEtaleFiberFunctor x,
        ∀ (Y : FiniteEtaleOver X) (σ : EtaleFundamentalGroup X x)
          (y : (E.functor.obj Y).obj.V.obj),
          (α.hom.app Y) (ConcreteCategory.hom ((E.functor.obj Y).obj.ρ σ).asHom y) =
            (σ.asIso.app Y).hom ((α.hom.app Y) y)
declarations.comment: (1) the equivalence of FÉt_X with the finite continuous π₁(X, x)-sets; (2) and (3) not covered here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_finiteEtaleFiberFunctorIso_of_connectedSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BND (2), existence of the isomorphism of fibre functors.** Given a
second geometric point `x'` of a connected scheme `X`, there is an isomorphism
`t : F_x ≅ F_{x'}` between the two geometric fibre functors on `FÉt_X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_finiteEtaleFiberFunctorIso_of_connectedSpace (X : Scheme.{u}) [ConnectedSpace X]
    (x x' : GeometricPoint X) :
    Nonempty (finiteEtaleFiberFunctor x ≅ finiteEtaleFiberFunctor x')
declarations.comment: (2) existence of an isomorphism t : F_x ≅ F_x' of the geometric fibre functors at two base points; the comparison of fundamental groups it induces, that comparison's independence up to inner conjugation and its compatibility with (1) are separate, and (1) and (3) are not covered here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_etaleFundamentalGroupContinuousMulEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BND (2), existence.** The étale fundamental groups of a connected
scheme at two geometric points are isomorphic as topological groups: the two geometric fibre
functors are isomorphic, and conjugation by such an isomorphism is a homeomorphic group
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_etaleFundamentalGroupContinuousMulEquiv (X : Scheme.{u}) [ConnectedSpace X]
    (x x' : GeometricPoint X) :
    Nonempty (EtaleFundamentalGroup X x ≃ₜ* EtaleFundamentalGroup X x')
declarations.comment: (2) existence of the comparison of two base points, as topological groups; its independence up to inner conjugation and its compatibility with (1) are separate, and (1) and (3) are not covered here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isInnerConjugate_etaleFundamentalGroupContinuousMulEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BND (2), independence of the choice.** Two isomorphisms of the geometric
fibre functors at two geometric points induce isomorphisms of étale fundamental groups that differ
by an inner automorphism of the target.
declarations.comment: (2) independence of the base-point comparison up to inner conjugation; its existence and its compatibility with (1) are separate, and (1) and (3) are not covered here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroupContinuousMulEquiv_action
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BND (2), compatibility with the equivalences.** The change-of-base-point
isomorphism of topological groups intertwines the actions on the geometric fibres underlying the
two equivalences of Tag 0BND (1) at the two base points.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleFundamentalGroupContinuousMulEquiv_action {X : Scheme.{u}} [ConnectedSpace X]
    {x x' : GeometricPoint X} (t : finiteEtaleFiberFunctor x ≅ finiteEtaleFiberFunctor x')
    (Y : FiniteEtaleOver X) (σ : EtaleFundamentalGroup X x)
    (y : ((finiteEtaleEquivalenceOfIsGaloisCategory X x).functor.obj Y).obj.V.obj) :
    t.hom.app Y
        ((finiteEtaleEquivalenceOfIsGaloisCategoryFiberIso X x).hom.app Y
          (ConcreteCategory.hom
            (((finiteEtaleEquivalenceOfIsGaloisCategory X x).functor.obj Y).obj.ρ σ).asHom y)) =
      (finiteEtaleEquivalenceOfIsGaloisCategoryFiberIso X x').hom.app Y
        (ConcreteCategory.hom
          (((finiteEtaleEquivalenceOfIsGaloisCategory X x').functor.obj Y).obj.ρ
            (etaleFundamentalGroupContinuousMulEquiv t σ)).asHom
          ((finiteEtaleEquivalenceOfIsGaloisCategoryFiberIso X x').inv.app Y
            (t.hom.app Y
              ((finiteEtaleEquivalenceOfIsGaloisCategoryFiberIso X x).hom.app Y y))))
declarations.comment: (2) compatibility of the base-point comparison with the actions of (1); its existence and its independence up to inner conjugation are separate, and (1) and (3) are not covered here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteEtaleEquivalence_mapIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BND (3), the commuting square.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of connected
schemes, base change `FÉt_Y ⥤ FÉt_X` agrees under the equivalences of Tag 0BND (1) with restriction
of the action along `AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroupMap`, and the comparison isomorphism is
the canonical projection of geometric fibres.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteEtaleEquivalence_mapIso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [ConnectedSpace X]
    [ConnectedSpace Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : GeometricPoint X) :
    ∃ η : (finiteEtaleEquivalenceOfIsGaloisCategory Y (x.map f)).functor ⋙
          ContAction.res FintypeCat (etaleFundamentalGroupMap f x) ≅
        finiteEtaleBaseChange f ⋙
          (finiteEtaleEquivalenceOfIsGaloisCategory X x).functor,
      ∀ (V : FiniteEtaleOver Y)
        (a : (((finiteEtaleEquivalenceOfIsGaloisCategory X x).functor.obj
          ((finiteEtaleBaseChange f).obj V)).obj.V.obj)),
        (finiteEtaleEquivalenceOfIsGaloisCategoryFiberIso Y (x.map f)).hom.app V
            ((η.inv.app V).hom.hom a) =
          finiteEtaleFiberProjection f x V
            ((finiteEtaleEquivalenceOfIsGaloisCategoryFiberIso X x).hom.app
              ((finiteEtaleBaseChange f).obj V) a)
declarations.comment: (3) the square comparing base change with restriction along the induced homomorphism; the homomorphism and the equation determining it are separate, and (1) and (2) are not covered here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroupMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BND (3).** The continuous homomorphism of étale fundamental groups
induced by a morphism of connected schemes and a geometric point of its source.
declarations.statement:
def etaleFundamentalGroupMap {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [ConnectedSpace X] [ConnectedSpace Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : GeometricPoint X) :
    EtaleFundamentalGroup X x →ₜ* EtaleFundamentalGroup Y (x.map f)
declarations.comment: (3) the induced continuous homomorphism; the equation determining it and the commuting square are separate, and (1) and (2) are not covered here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroupMap_finiteEtaleFiberProjection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BND (3).** The induced homomorphism commutes with the canonical
projection from the geometric fibre of a base-changed finite étale cover to the original
geometric fibre. Since the projections are bijective, this equation determines
`AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroupMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleFundamentalGroupMap_finiteEtaleFiberProjection {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [ConnectedSpace X] [ConnectedSpace Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : GeometricPoint X)
    (V : FiniteEtaleOver Y) (σ : EtaleFundamentalGroup X x)
    (p : finiteEtaleFiber x ((finiteEtaleBaseChange f).obj V)) :
    finiteEtaleFiberProjection f x V ((σ.asIso.app _).hom p) =
      ((etaleFundamentalGroupMap f x σ).asIso.app V).hom
        (finiteEtaleFiberProjection f x V p)
declarations.comment: (3) the equation determining the induced continuous homomorphism; the homomorphism itself and the commuting square are separate, and (1) and (2) are not covered here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtaleEquivalenceGaloisSets
declarations.doc:
Finite étale covers of a field are finite continuous sets for its absolute
Galois group.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def finiteEtaleEquivalenceGaloisSets
    (K L Ω : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Field Ω]
    [Algebra K L] [IsSepClosure K L] [Algebra L Ω]
    [Algebra K Ω] [IsScalarTower K L Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic K Ω] :
    FiniteEtaleOver (Spec (.of K)) ≌
      ContAction FintypeCat.{u} Gal(L/K)
declarations.comment: part (1): equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtaleFiberIso
declarations.doc:
The underlying finite Galois set of a cover is naturally its geometric
fibre over the algebraic closure.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def finiteEtaleFiberIso
    (K L Ω : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Field Ω]
    [Algebra K L] [IsSepClosure K L] [Algebra L Ω]
    [Algebra K Ω] [IsScalarTower K L Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic K Ω] :
    (finiteEtaleEquivalenceGaloisSets K L Ω).functor ⋙
        forget₂ (ContAction FintypeCat.{u} Gal(L/K)) FintypeCat.{u} ⋙
      forget FintypeCat.{u} ≅
      finiteEtaleFiberFunctor
        (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint K Ω)
declarations.comment: part (1): natural fibre comparison

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.separableFiberEquiv
declarations.doc:
The Galois set attached to a finite étale cover is the set of its points
over the separable closure.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def separableFiberEquiv
    (K L Ω : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Field Ω]
    [Algebra K L] [IsSepClosure K L] [Algebra L Ω]
    [Algebra K Ω] [IsScalarTower K L Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic K Ω]
  (Y : FiniteEtaleOver (Spec (.of K))) :
    ((finiteEtaleEquivalenceGaloisSets K L Ω).functor.obj Y).obj.V ≃
      { f : Spec (.of L) ⟶ Y.left //
        f ≫ Y.hom = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)) }
declarations.comment: part (1): separable-closure fibre

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtaleFiberIso_apply
declarations.doc:
The natural fibre comparison is extension of a separable-closure point
to the algebraic closure.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finiteEtaleFiberIso_apply
    (K L Ω : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Field Ω]
    [Algebra K L] [IsSepClosure K L] [Algebra L Ω]
    [Algebra K Ω] [IsScalarTower K L Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic K Ω]
    (Y : FiniteEtaleOver (Spec (.of K)))
    (y : ((finiteEtaleEquivalenceGaloisSets K L Ω).functor.obj Y).obj.V) :
    (((finiteEtaleFiberIso K L Ω).hom.app Y) y).1 =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L Ω)) ≫
        (separableFiberEquiv K L Ω Y y).1
declarations.comment: part (1): fibre comparison formula

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.separableFiberEquiv_map
declarations.doc: The separable-closure description is natural in a finite étale cover.
declarations.statement:
public theorem separableFiberEquiv_map
    (K L Ω : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Field Ω]
    [Algebra K L] [IsSepClosure K L] [Algebra L Ω]
    [Algebra K Ω] [IsScalarTower K L Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic K Ω]
    {Y Z : FiniteEtaleOver (Spec (.of K))} (f : Y ⟶ Z)
    (y : ((finiteEtaleEquivalenceGaloisSets K L Ω).functor.obj Y).obj.V) :
    (separableFiberEquiv K L Ω Z
      (ConcreteCategory.hom
        ((finiteEtaleEquivalenceGaloisSets K L Ω).functor.map f) y)).1 =
      (separableFiberEquiv K L Ω Y y).1 ≫ f.left
declarations.comment: part (1): naturality over the separable closure

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.separableFiberEquiv_smul
declarations.doc:
The Galois action on a separable-closure point is precomposition with
the corresponding field automorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem separableFiberEquiv_smul
    (K L Ω : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Field Ω]
    [Algebra K L] [IsSepClosure K L] [Algebra L Ω]
    [Algebra K Ω] [IsScalarTower K L Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic K Ω]
    (Y : FiniteEtaleOver (Spec (.of K)))
    (σ : Gal(L/K))
    (y : ((finiteEtaleEquivalenceGaloisSets K L Ω).functor.obj Y).obj.V) :
    (separableFiberEquiv K L Ω Y
      (ConcreteCategory.hom
        (((finiteEtaleEquivalenceGaloisSets K L Ω).functor.obj Y).obj.ρ σ).asHom y)).1 =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom σ.toAlgHom.toRingHom) ≫
        (separableFiberEquiv K L Ω Y y).1
declarations.comment: part (1): Galois action

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.galoisEquivEtaleFundamentalGroup
declarations.doc:
The canonical isomorphism from the absolute Galois group to the étale
fundamental group: its action on a fibre is precomposition on the corresponding
separable-closure point.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def galoisEquivEtaleFundamentalGroup
    (K L Ω : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Field Ω]
    [Algebra K L] [IsSepClosure K L] [Algebra L Ω]
    [Algebra K Ω] [IsScalarTower K L Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic K Ω] :
    Gal(L/K) ≃ₜ*
      EtaleFundamentalGroup (Spec (.of K))
        (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint K Ω)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.galoisEquivEtaleFundamentalGroup_apply
declarations.doc:
The canonical group isomorphism acts on geometric fibres through the
absolute Galois action on separable-closure points.
declarations.statement:
public theorem galoisEquivEtaleFundamentalGroup_apply
    (K L Ω : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Field Ω]
    [Algebra K L] [IsSepClosure K L] [Algebra L Ω]
    [Algebra K Ω] [IsScalarTower K L Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic K Ω]
    (Y : FiniteEtaleOver (Spec (.of K)))
    (σ : Gal(L/K))
    (p : finiteEtaleFiber
      (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint K Ω) Y)
    (f : Spec (.of L) ⟶ Y.left)
    (hf : p.1 = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L Ω)) ≫ f) :
    ((((galoisEquivEtaleFundamentalGroup K L Ω) σ).asIso.app Y).hom p).1 =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L Ω)) ≫
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom σ.toAlgHom.toRingHom) ≫ f
declarations.comment: part (2): action formula

declarations.name: tor_commutes_filtered_colimits
declarations.doc:
**Tor commutes with filtered colimits.** Applying `Tor_n^R(-, N)` to the direct-limit
colimit cocone of a directed system `(G i)` of `R`-modules yields again a colimit cocone, i.e. the
canonical map `colim_i Tor_n^R(G i, N) → Tor_n^R(colim_i G i, N)` is an isomorphism.

The ring `R : Type u`, the index type `ι : Type v`, the modules `G : ι → Type w` and the second
argument `N : ModuleCat.{x} R` live in four independent universes, and the conclusion is stated
about their canonical `ULift`s into `max u v w x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tor_commutes_filtered_colimits
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {ι : Type v} [DecidableEq ι] [Preorder ι] [IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty ι]
    (G : ι → Type w) [∀ i, AddCommGroup (G i)] [∀ i, Module R (G i)]
    (f : (i j : ι) → i ≤ j → G i →ₗ[R] G j)
    [DirectedSystem G (fun i j h => f i j h)]
    (N : ModuleCat.{x} R) (n : ℕ) :
    Nonempty (CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit
      (((CategoryTheory.Tor (ModuleCat.{max u v w x} (ULift.{max v w x, u} R)) n).flip.obj
            (ModuleCat.of (ULift.{max v w x, u} R) (ULift.{max u v w, x} N))).mapCocone
        (ModuleCat.directLimitCocone
          (fun i : ULift.{max u w x, v} ι => ULift.{max u v x, w} (G i.down))
          (torULiftTransition.{u, v, w, x} G f))))

declarations.name: AdicCompletion.map_shortExact_and_isAdicComplete_of_pow_smul_top_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BNG.** Let `R` be a ring, let `I ⊆ R` be an ideal and let `0 → M → N → Q → 0` be a
short exact sequence of `R`-modules such that `Q` is annihilated by the power `I ^ c` of `I`. Then
`I`-adic completion produces a short exact sequence `0 → M^∧ → N^∧ → Q^∧ → 0`, and `Q` is
`I`-adically complete, so that this third term is `Q` itself as in the source's
`0 → M^∧ → N^∧ → Q → 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem map_shortExact_and_isAdicComplete_of_pow_smul_top_eq_bot
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    {N : Type*} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] {Q : Type*} [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q]
    {f : M →ₗ[R] N} {g : N →ₗ[R] Q} (hf : Function.Injective f)
    (hfg : Function.Exact f g) (hg : Function.Surjective g)
    {c : ℕ} (hQ : I ^ c • (⊤ : Submodule R Q) = ⊥) :
    Function.Injective (map I f) ∧ Function.Exact (map I f) (map I g) ∧
      Function.Surjective (map I g) ∧ IsAdicComplete I Q
declarations.comment: The third term is written `Q^∧`, and the conjunct `IsAdicComplete I Q` identifies it with the source's `Q`. No Noetherian or finiteness hypothesis, unlike `map_injective` and `map_exact`.

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.quotient_pow_equiv_adicCompletion
declarations.doc:
The canonical map `R / f^n R → R^∧ / f^n R^∧` is an isomorphism,
where `R^∧` is the `(f)`-adic completion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quotient_pow_equiv_adicCompletion {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (f : R) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ e : (R ⧸ (Ideal.span {f}) ^ n) ≃+*
        (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R ⧸
          (Ideal.span {(algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R)) f}) ^ n),
      ∀ r : R,
        e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ r) =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk _ ((algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R)) r)

declarations.name: tensorProduct_mk_bijective_of_ideal_power_torsion
declarations.doc:
The canonical map from an ideal-power torsion module to its scalar extension is an
isomorphism when the scalar extension is unchanged modulo every positive power of the ideal. In
particular this holds for the adic completion of a finitely generated ideal; this is a slight
generalization of Beauville--Laszlo, Lemme 1.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tensorProduct_mk_bijective_of_ideal_power_torsion
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (hM : ∀ m : M, ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ r ∈ I ^ n, r • m = 0) :
    (∀ (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S],
      (∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
        Function.Bijective
          (Ideal.quotientMap (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (I ^ n))
            (algebraMap R S) Ideal.le_comap_map)) →
      Function.Bijective (fun m : M => TensorProduct.mk R M S m (1 : S))) ∧
    (I.FG →
      Function.Bijective
        (fun m : M => TensorProduct.mk R M (AdicCompletion I R) m 1))

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.tensorProduct_prod_away_nontrivial_of_quotientMap_bijective
declarations.doc:
If `R → S` induces isomorphisms modulo every positive power of `(f)`, then tensoring
with `S ⊕ R_f` detects nonzero modules. In particular, tensoring with `R^∧ ⊕ R_f`, where
`R^∧` is the `(f)`-adic completion, detects nonzero modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tensorProduct_prod_away_nontrivial_of_quotientMap_bijective
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (f : R) :
    (∀ (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S],
      (∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
        Function.Bijective
          (Ideal.quotientMap
            (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) ((Ideal.span {f}) ^ n))
            (algebraMap R S) Ideal.le_comap_map)) →
      ∀ (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Nontrivial M],
        Nontrivial (TensorProduct R M (S × Localization.Away f))) ∧
    (∀ (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Nontrivial M],
      Nontrivial
        (TensorProduct R M
          (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R × Localization.Away f)))

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.primeSpectrum_cover_of_quotientMap_bijective
declarations.doc:
If `R → S` is an isomorphism modulo `f`, then `Spec(S)` and `Spec(R_f)`
jointly cover `Spec(R)`. The same cover holds with the `(f)`-adic completion in
place of `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem primeSpectrum_cover_of_quotientMap_bijective {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (f : R) :
    (∀ {S : Type*} [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S),
      Function.Bijective
          (Ideal.quotientMap (Ideal.map φ (Ideal.span {f})) φ Ideal.le_comap_map) →
        Function.Surjective
          (Sum.elim (PrimeSpectrum.comap φ)
            (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R (Localization.Away f))))) ∧
      Function.Surjective
        (Sum.elim
          (PrimeSpectrum.comap
            (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R)))
          (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R (Localization.Away f))))

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.finite_iff_tensorProduct_prod_away_of_quotientMap_bijective
declarations.doc:
Finite generation of a module is detected after extension of scalars to the product of
an algebra inducing isomorphisms modulo every positive power of `(f)` and the localization
away from `f`. In particular, it is detected by the product of the `(f)`-adic completion and
that localization.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finite_iff_tensorProduct_prod_away_of_quotientMap_bijective
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (f : R) :
    (∀ (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S],
      (∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
        Function.Bijective
          (Ideal.quotientMap
            (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) ((Ideal.span {f}) ^ n))
            (algebraMap R S) Ideal.le_comap_map)) →
      ∀ (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M],
        Module.Finite R M ↔
          Module.Finite (S × Localization.Away f)
            (TensorProduct R (S × Localization.Away f) M)) ∧
    (∀ (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M],
      Module.Finite
          (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R × Localization.Away f)
          (TensorProduct R
            (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R × Localization.Away f) M) →
        Module.Finite R M)

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.exists_nonflat_adicCompletion_prod_localizationAway
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BNP.** Adic completion and localization do not in general form a flat cover: there
is a commutative ring `R` and an element `f` such that the product of the completion of `R` at
`(f)` and `R_f` is not flat over `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_nonflat_adicCompletion_prod_localizationAway :
    ∃ (R : Type) (_ : CommRing R) (f : R),
      ¬ Module.Flat R
        (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span ({f} : Set R)) R × Localization.Away f)

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.adicCompletionBeauvilleLaszloSequence
declarations.doc:
The canonical sequence `0 → R → R̂ ⊕ Rₑ → R̂ₑ → 0`, where `R̂` is the
completion of `R` along the principal ideal generated by `f`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable abbrev adicCompletionBeauvilleLaszloSequence
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (f : R) : ShortComplex AddCommGrpCat.{u}

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.beauvilleLaszloSequence_exactness_iff_powerTorsionMap
declarations.doc:
If `R → S` is an isomorphism modulo every positive power of `f`, the
Beauville--Laszlo sequence is always exact on the right; its left and middle
exactness are equivalent to injectivity and surjectivity on `f`-power torsion.
Consequently it is short exact precisely when that map is bijective. The same
criterion specializes to the `(f)`-adic completion of `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem beauvilleLaszloSequence_exactness_iff_powerTorsionMap
    (f : R) (φ : R →+* S)
    (hφ : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → Function.Bijective (quotientPowMap f n φ)) :
    Epi (beauvilleLaszloSequence f φ).g ∧
      (Mono (beauvilleLaszloSequence f φ).f ↔
        Function.Injective (powerTorsionMap f φ)) ∧
      ((beauvilleLaszloSequence f φ).Exact ↔
        Function.Surjective (powerTorsionMap f φ)) ∧
      ((beauvilleLaszloSequence f φ).ShortExact ↔
        Function.Bijective (powerTorsionMap f φ)) ∧
      ((beauvilleLaszloSequence f
          (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R))).ShortExact ↔
        Function.Bijective (powerTorsionMap f
          (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R))))

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.adicCompletion_isRegular_and_isGlueingPair
declarations.doc:
A nonzerodivisor `f` remains a nonzerodivisor in the `(f)`-adic completion, and the
canonical Beauville--Laszlo sequence is short exact; equivalently, `(R, f)` is a glueing pair.
declarations.statement:
public theorem adicCompletion_isRegular_and_isGlueingPair {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (f : R) (hf :
  IsRegular f) :
    IsRegular (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R) f) ∧
      (beauvilleLaszloSequence f
        (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R))).ShortExact

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.adicCompletion_isGlueingPair_of_flat
declarations.doc:
If the `(f)`-adic completion of `R` is flat over `R`, then tensoring the exact sequence
given by multiplication by `f ^ n` remains exact for every positive `n`, the canonical map on
`f ^ n`-torsion is an isomorphism, and `(R, f)` is a glueing pair. These conclusions hold in
particular when `R` is Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
public theorem adicCompletion_isGlueingPair_of_flat {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (f : R) :
    let P : Prop :=
      (∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
        let T := Submodule.torsionBy R R (f ^ n)
        let a : T ⊗[R] AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R →ₗ[R]
            AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R :=
          (TensorProduct.lid R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R)).toLinearMap.comp
            (TensorProduct.map T.subtype
              (LinearMap.id (R := R) (M := AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R)))
        let b : AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R →ₗ[R]
            AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R :=
          (LinearMap.lsmul R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R)) (f ^ n)
        Function.Injective a ∧ Function.Exact a b ∧
          Function.Injective
            (fun x : T => algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R) x.1) ∧
          Set.range (fun x : T => algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R) x.1) =
            (Submodule.torsionBy (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R)
              (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R)
              ((algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R) f) ^ n) :
                Set (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R))) ∧
      Function.Injective (fun r : R =>
        (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R) r,
          algebraMap R (Localization.Away f) r)) ∧
      Function.Exact
        (fun r : R => (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R) r,
          algebraMap R (Localization.Away f) r))
        (fun x : AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R × Localization.Away f =>
          algebraMap (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R)
              (Localization.Away
                (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R) f)) x.1 -
            Localization.awayMap
              (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R)) f x.2) ∧
      Function.Surjective
        (fun x : AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R × Localization.Away f =>
          algebraMap (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R)
              (Localization.Away
                (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R) f)) x.1 -
            Localization.awayMap
              (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R)) f x.2)
    (Module.Flat R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R) → P) ∧
      (∀ [IsNoetherianRing R], P)

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.adicCompletion_torsionMap_not_bijective_examples
declarations.doc:
Two quotients of `k[f, T₁, T₂, …]` for which the canonical map on `f`-power torsion
to the adic completion is respectively noninjective and nonsurjective. In the first example
`T₁` is a nonzero kernel element whose image is divisible by every power of `f`. In the second,
the compatible residues of `T₁ + f T₂ + f² T₃ + ⋯` define an `f`-torsion element outside
the image. The two completion maps are not flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem adicCompletion_torsionMap_not_bijective_examples (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    let P := MvPolynomial (Option ℕ) k
    let F : P := MvPolynomial.X none
    let T : ℕ → P := fun n ↦ MvPolynomial.X (some n)
    let I₁ : Ideal P := Ideal.span ({F * T 0} ∪ Set.range (fun n ↦ F * T (n + 1) - T n))
    let R₁ := P ⧸ I₁
    let f₁ : R₁ := Ideal.Quotient.mk I₁ F
    let t₁ : ℕ → R₁ := fun n ↦ Ideal.Quotient.mk I₁ (T n)
    let J₁ : Ideal R₁ := Ideal.span {f₁}
    let c₁ := AdicCompletion.of J₁ R₁
    let I₂ : Ideal P := Ideal.span (Set.range (fun n ↦ F ^ (n + 1) * T n))
    let R₂ := P ⧸ I₂
    let f₂ : R₂ := Ideal.Quotient.mk I₂ F
    let t₂ : ℕ → R₂ := fun n ↦ Ideal.Quotient.mk I₂ (T n)
    let J₂ : Ideal R₂ := Ideal.span {f₂}
    let c₂ := AdicCompletion.of J₂ R₂
    t₁ 0 ≠ 0 ∧ t₁ 0 ∈ Ideal.primaryComponent R₁ J₁ ∧ c₁ (t₁ 0) = 0 ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, f₁ ^ n • c₁ (t₁ n) = c₁ (t₁ 0)) ∧
    (¬ Function.Injective (Ideal.primaryComponent.map J₁ c₁)) ∧
    (¬ Module.Flat R₁ (AdicCompletion J₁ R₁)) ∧
    (¬ Function.Surjective (Ideal.primaryComponent.map J₂ c₂)) ∧
    (∃ x : Ideal.primaryComponent (AdicCompletion J₂ R₂) J₂,
      (∀ n : ℕ, AdicCompletion.evalₐ J₂ n x.1 =
        Ideal.Quotient.mk (J₂ ^ n) (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, f₂ ^ i * t₂ i)) ∧
      f₂ • x.1 = 0 ∧
      x ∉ Set.range (Ideal.primaryComponent.map J₂ c₂)) ∧
    (¬ Module.Flat R₂ (AdicCompletion J₂ R₂))

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.isGlueable_iff_adicCompletion_beauvilleLaszloModuleSequence_shortExact
declarations.doc:
An `R`-module is glueable at `f` exactly when
`0 → M → (M ⊗[R] R̂) ⊕ (M ⊗[R] R_f) → M ⊗[R] R̂_f → 0`
is short exact, where `R̂` is the `(f)`-adic completion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGlueable_iff_adicCompletion_beauvilleLaszloModuleSequence_shortExact {R : Type u}
  [CommRing R] (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (f : R) :
    IsGlueable M f ↔
      (beauvilleLaszloModuleSequence
        (S := AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R) M f).ShortExact

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.beauvilleLaszloModuleSequence_exactness_iff_powerTorsionMap
declarations.doc:
If `R → S` is an isomorphism modulo every positive power of `f`, the module
Beauville--Laszlo sequence is surjective on the right; its left and middle exactness
are equivalent to injectivity and surjectivity of the canonical map on `f`-power torsion.
Thus the module is glueable exactly when this map is bijective. If the ring sequence is
short exact, surjectivity on power torsion is automatic, so injectivity alone characterizes
glueability. The latter criterion also applies to the `(f)`-adic completion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem beauvilleLaszloModuleSequence_exactness_iff_powerTorsionMap :
    (∀ (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
      (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (f : R),
      (∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → Function.Bijective
        (quotientPowMap f n (algebraMap R S))) →
      Epi (beauvilleLaszloModuleSequence (S := S) M f).g ∧
        (Mono (beauvilleLaszloModuleSequence (S := S) M f).f ↔
          Function.Injective (tensorProductPowerTorsionMap (S := S) M f)) ∧
        ((beauvilleLaszloModuleSequence (S := S) M f).Exact ↔
          Function.Surjective (tensorProductPowerTorsionMap (S := S) M f)) ∧
        ((beauvilleLaszloModuleSequence (S := S) M f).ShortExact ↔
          Function.Bijective (tensorProductPowerTorsionMap (S := S) M f)) ∧
        ((beauvilleLaszloSequence f (algebraMap R S)).ShortExact →
          ((beauvilleLaszloModuleSequence (S := S) M f).ShortExact ↔
            Function.Injective (tensorProductPowerTorsionMap (S := S) M f)))) ∧
    (∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (f : R),
      (beauvilleLaszloSequence f
          (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R))).ShortExact →
        ((beauvilleLaszloModuleSequence
            (S := AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R) M f).ShortExact ↔
          Function.Injective
            (tensorProductPowerTorsionMap
              (S := AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R) M f)))

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.glueable_criteria
declarations.doc:
Criteria ensuring that a module is glueable for a Beauville--Laszlo glueing pair.

For completion at `f`, glueability is equivalent to injectivity on `f`-power torsion.
Injectivity of `M[f] → M̂` is equivalent to
`M[f] ∩ ⋂ n ≥ 1, f ^ n M = 0` and implies glueability. For a general glueing pair
`R → S`, vanishing of `Tor₁(M, S_f)` is sufficient and is equivalent to
`Tor₁(M, S)` being `f`-power torsion. Consequently flat modules are glueable; if
`S` is flat over `R`, every module is glueable. The latter applies to completion over
a Noetherian ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem glueable_criteria :
    (∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
      (f : R),
      (beauvilleLaszloSequence f
        (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R))).ShortExact →
        ((IsGlueable M f ↔
            Function.Injective
              (tensorProductPowerTorsionMap
                (S := AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R) M f)) ∧
          (Function.Injective
              (fun x : Submodule.torsionBy R M f ↦
                AdicCompletion.of (Ideal.span {f}) M x.1) ↔
            Submodule.torsionBy R M f ⊓
                (⨅ n : ℕ, (Ideal.span {f}) ^ (n + 1) • ⊤) = ⊥) ∧
          (Function.Injective
              (fun x : Submodule.torsionBy R M f ↦
                AdicCompletion.of (Ideal.span {f}) M x.1) →
            IsGlueable M f))) ∧
    (∀ (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
      (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (f : R),
      (beauvilleLaszloSequence f (algebraMap R S)).ShortExact →
        ((IsZero
            (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{max u v w} (ULift.{max v w} R)) 1).obj
              (ModuleCat.of (ULift.{max v w} R) (ULift.{max u v} M))).obj
                (ModuleCat.of (ULift.{max v w} R)
                  (ULift.{max u w} (Localization.Away (algebraMap R S f))))) →
            IsGlueableFor (S := S) M f) ∧
          (IsZero
              (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{max u v w} (ULift.{max v w} R)) 1).obj
                (ModuleCat.of (ULift.{max v w} R) (ULift.{max u v} M))).obj
                  (ModuleCat.of (ULift.{max v w} R)
                    (ULift.{max u w} (Localization.Away (algebraMap R S f))))) ↔
            modulePowerTorsion
                (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{max u v w} (ULift.{max v w} R)) 1).obj
                  (ModuleCat.of (ULift.{max v w} R) (ULift.{max u v} M))).obj
                    (ModuleCat.of (ULift.{max v w} R) (ULift.{max u w} S)))
                (ULift.up f) = ⊤) ∧
          (Module.Flat R M → IsGlueableFor (S := S) M f) ∧
          (Module.Flat R S → IsGlueableFor (S := S) M f))) ∧
    (∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
      (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (f : R),
      IsGlueable M f)

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.exists_non_glueable_module_over_smooth_germ_ring
declarations.doc:
The ring `R` of germs at zero of smooth functions on `ℝ`, with coordinate germ `f`, has
completion `ℝ[[X]]`. The flat germs `φ(x) = exp (-1 / x²)` and `ψ(x) = φ(x) / x` vanish
in the completion, while the class of `ψ` in `M = R / φR` is nonzero `f`-torsion. It therefore
lies in the kernel of the completion base-change map, so `M` is not glueable.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_non_glueable_module_over_smooth_germ_ring :
    let S := smoothSheafCommRing (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℝ)
      (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℝ) ℝ ℝ
    let R := S.presheaf.stalk (0 : ℝ)
    ∃ (f₀ φ₀ ψ₀ : S.presheaf.obj (op ⊤)),
      (∀ x : ℝ, f₀ ⟨x, Set.mem_univ x⟩ = x) ∧
      (∀ x : ℝ, φ₀ ⟨x, Set.mem_univ x⟩ =
        if x = 0 then 0 else Real.exp (-1 / x ^ 2)) ∧
      (∀ x : ℝ, ψ₀ ⟨x, Set.mem_univ x⟩ =
        if x = 0 then 0 else Real.exp (-1 / x ^ 2) / x) ∧
      let f : R := S.presheaf.germ ⊤ 0 (Set.mem_univ 0) f₀
      let φ : R := S.presheaf.germ ⊤ 0 (Set.mem_univ 0) φ₀
      let ψ : R := S.presheaf.germ ⊤ 0 (Set.mem_univ 0) ψ₀
      IsRegular f ∧ IsRegular φ ∧ f * ψ = φ ∧
      ∃ e : AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R ≃+* PowerSeries ℝ,
        e (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R) f) = PowerSeries.X ∧
        algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R) φ = 0 ∧
        algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R) ψ = 0 ∧
        (let M := R ⧸ Ideal.span {φ}
         let m : M := Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {φ}) ψ
         let C := AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R
         m ≠ 0 ∧ f • m = 0 ∧
          TensorProduct.mk R M C m 1 = 0 ∧
          (∃ q : TensorProduct R M C ≃ₗ[R] C,
            ∀ (r : R) (c : C),
              q (TensorProduct.mk R M C (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {φ}) r) c) =
                algebraMap R C r * c) ∧
          ¬ Function.Injective
            (fun x : {x : M // ∃ n : ℕ, f ^ n • x = 0} ↦
              TensorProduct.mk R M C x.1 1))

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.isZero_Tor_one_ideal_pow_of_beauvilleLaszlo_shortExact
declarations.doc:
If `(R → R', f)` is a gluing pair, then
`Tor₁ʿ(R', f ^ n R) = 0` for every positive `n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_Tor_one_ideal_pow_of_beauvilleLaszlo_shortExact
    {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (f : R) (φ : R →+* S)
    (hφ : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
      Function.Bijective (quotientPowMap f n φ))
    (hglue : (beauvilleLaszloSequence f φ).ShortExact) :
    ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
      Limits.IsZero (((Tor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).obj
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).obj (ModuleCat.of S S))).obj
        (ModuleCat.of R ↑((Ideal.span {f}) ^ n)))

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.isZero_Tor_one_quotient_powerTorsion_of_beauvilleLaszlo_shortExact
declarations.doc:
If `(R → R', f)` is a glueing pair, then
`Tor₁ᴿ(R', R / R[f^∞]) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_Tor_one_quotient_powerTorsion_of_beauvilleLaszlo_shortExact
    {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (f : R) (φ : R →+* S)
    (hφ : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → Function.Bijective (quotientPowMap f n φ))
    (hglue : (beauvilleLaszloSequence f φ).ShortExact) :
    Limits.IsZero (((Tor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).obj
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).obj (ModuleCat.of S S))).obj
      (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ powerTorsion f)))

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.isZero_Tor_one_coker_localizationMap_of_beauvilleLaszlo_shortExact
declarations.doc:
If `(R → R', f)` is a Beauville--Laszlo glueing pair, then for every `R`-module `M`,
`Tor₁ᴿ(R', coker(M → M_f)) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_Tor_one_coker_localizationMap_of_beauvilleLaszlo_shortExact
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {M : Type w}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (f : R) (φ : R →+* S)
    (hφ : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → Function.Bijective (quotientPowMap f n φ))
    (hglue : (beauvilleLaszloSequence f φ).ShortExact) :
    Limits.IsZero (((Tor (ModuleCat.{max u v w}
      (ULift.{max u v w} R)) 1).obj
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (φ.ulift.{max u v w, max u v w})).obj
        (ModuleCat.of (ULift.{max u v w} S) (ULift.{max u v w} S)))).obj
      (ModuleCat.of (ULift.{max u v w} R)
        (ULift.{max u v w}
          (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f) M ⧸
            LinearMap.range (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers f) M)))))

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.canonicalOnGlueableModules_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Beauville--Laszlo glueing.** For a glueing pair `(R → S, f)`, the canonical functor
from glueable `R`-modules to module glueing data is an equivalence of categories. Compatible
sections of every glueing datum are glueable, and the canonical map from any module to the
sections of its canonical datum induces isomorphisms after extension of scalars to `S` and
localization away from `f`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem canonicalOnGlueableModules_isEquivalence
    (hquot : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
      Function.Bijective (quotientPowMap f n (algebraMap R S)))
    (hglue : (beauvilleLaszloSequence f (algebraMap R S)).ShortExact) :
    let C := moduleGlueingConstruction.{u, v, w} S (fun _ : Fin 1 ↦ f)
    letI := C.category
    (canonicalOnGlueableModules f C).IsEquivalence ∧
      (∀ X : ModuleGlueingDatum.{u, v, w} S (fun _ : Fin 1 ↦ f) C.comparison,
        glueableModules (S := S) f (C.sections.obj X)) ∧
      (∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R,
        Function.Bijective
            (TensorProduct.map (LinearMap.id (R := R) (M := S))
              (C.canonicalSectionsUnit.app M).hom) ∧
          Function.Bijective
            (LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers f)
              (C.canonicalSectionsUnit.app M).hom))

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.gluingDatum_difference_shortExact_of_quotientMap_surjective
declarations.doc:
The kernel of the difference map attached to a gluing datum fits into the short exact
sequence `0 → ker(d) → M' × M₁ → M'ₑ → 0`.

Here the difference map sends `(x, y)` to `x / 1 - α⁻¹(1 ⊗ y)`. It is surjective as
soon as `R → S` is surjective modulo every positive power of `f`; in particular the result
applies to a Beauville--Laszlo gluing pair.
declarations.statement:
public theorem gluingDatum_difference_shortExact_of_quotientMap_surjective
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (f : R)
    (hmod : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
      Function.Surjective
        (Ideal.quotientMap
          (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) ((Ideal.span {f}) ^ n))
          (algebraMap R S) Ideal.le_comap_map))
    (M' : Type w) [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M'] [Module S M']
    [IsScalarTower R S M']
    (M₁ : Type x) [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module R M₁]
    [Module (Localization.Away f) M₁] [IsScalarTower R (Localization.Away f) M₁]
    (α : LocalizedModule.Away (algebraMap R S f) M' ≃ₗ[S]
      TensorProduct R S M₁) :
    let localizationMap : M' →ₗ[R] LocalizedModule.Away (algebraMap R S f) M' :=
      (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers (algebraMap R S f)) M').restrictScalars R
    let tensorMap : M₁ →ₗ[R] TensorProduct R S M₁ := TensorProduct.mk R S M₁ 1
    let d : (M' × M₁) →ₗ[R] LocalizedModule.Away (algebraMap R S f) M' :=
      localizationMap.comp (LinearMap.fst R M' M₁) -
        ((α.symm.toLinearMap.restrictScalars R).comp tensorMap).comp
          (LinearMap.snd R M' M₁)
    Function.Injective (LinearMap.ker d).subtype ∧
      Function.Exact (LinearMap.ker d).subtype d ∧
        Function.Surjective d

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.exists_exact_quotient_powerTorsion
declarations.doc:
Suppose `A → L` is localization away from `f`, the difference map
`A × B → L`, `(a, b) ↦ g a - h b`, is surjective, and multiplication by `f` is
injective on `B`. If `M` is the kernel of the difference map, projection to `B` induces
the canonical short exact sequence
`0 → M / M[f^∞] → B → L / range(g) → 0`.

The displayed compatibility uniquely specifies the induced left-hand map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_exact_quotient_powerTorsion
    (f : R) (g : A →ₗ[R] L) [IsLocalizedModule.Away f g] (h : B →ₗ[R] L)
    (hd : Function.Surjective
      (g.comp (LinearMap.fst R A B) - h.comp (LinearMap.snd R A B)))
    (hf : Function.Injective (fun b : B ↦ f • b)) :
    let d := g.comp (LinearMap.fst R A B) - h.comp (LinearMap.snd R A B)
    let M := LinearMap.ker d
    let T := Submodule.torsion' R M (Submonoid.powers f)
    let q := (Submodule.mkQ (LinearMap.range g)).comp h
    ∃ i : (M ⧸ T) →ₗ[R] B,
      (∀ m : M, i (Submodule.mkQ T m) = m.1.2) ∧
        Function.Injective i ∧ LinearMap.range i = LinearMap.ker q ∧
          Function.Surjective q

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.gluingDatum_baseChange_localizationQuotient_shortExact
declarations.doc:
Let `(R → S, f)` be a Beauville--Laszlo glueing pair and let `(M', M₁, α)` be a
glueing datum. If `M` is the kernel of
`M' × M₁ → (M')_f`, `(x, y) ↦ x / 1 - α⁻¹(y ⊗ 1)`, projection to `M₁`
induces a map `i : M / M[f^∞] → M₁`. After extending `i` to `S` and using
`α`, it is the left map of the canonical short exact sequence
`0 → (M / M[f^∞]) ⊗_R S → (M')_f → (M')_f / M' → 0`.

The first displayed condition characterizes the induced map `i`; thus the assertion
also records the canonical construction, rather than only the existence of some exact
sequence with isomorphic terms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem gluingDatum_baseChange_localizationQuotient_shortExact
    (R : Type uR) [CommRing R] (S : Type uS) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (f : R)
    (hmod : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
      Function.Bijective
        (Ideal.quotientMap
          (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) ((Ideal.span {f}) ^ n))
          (algebraMap R S) Ideal.le_comap_map))
    (hglue : (beauvilleLaszloSequence f (algebraMap R S)).ShortExact)
    (M' : Type uM) [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M'] [Module S M']
    [IsScalarTower R S M']
    (M₁ : Type uM₁) [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module R M₁]
    [Module (Localization.Away f) M₁] [IsScalarTower R (Localization.Away f) M₁]
    (α : LocalizedModule.Away (algebraMap R S f) M' ≃ₗ[S]
      TensorProduct R S M₁) :
    let localizationMap : M' →ₗ[R] LocalizedModule.Away (algebraMap R S f) M' :=
      (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap
        (Submonoid.powers (algebraMap R S f)) M').restrictScalars R
    let tensorMap : M₁ →ₗ[R] TensorProduct R S M₁ :=
      TensorProduct.mk R S M₁ 1
    let d : (M' × M₁) →ₗ[R] LocalizedModule.Away (algebraMap R S f) M' :=
      localizationMap.comp (LinearMap.fst R M' M₁) -
        ((α.symm.toLinearMap.restrictScalars R).comp tensorMap).comp
          (LinearMap.snd R M' M₁)
    let M := LinearMap.ker d
    let T := Submodule.torsion' R M (Submonoid.powers f)
    let q : LocalizedModule.Away (algebraMap R S f) M' →ₗ[R]
        AwayCokernel R S f M' :=
      ((LinearMap.range
        (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap
          (Submonoid.powers (algebraMap R S f)) M')).mkQ).restrictScalars R
    ∃ i : (M ⧸ T) →ₗ[R] M₁,
      (∀ m : M, i (Submodule.mkQ T m) = m.1.2) ∧
        let iS :=
          (TensorProduct.map (LinearMap.id (R := R) (M := S)) i).comp
            (TensorProduct.comm R (M ⧸ T) S).toLinearMap
        let a := (α.symm.toLinearMap.restrictScalars R).comp iS
        Function.Injective a ∧ Function.Exact a q ∧ Function.Surjective q

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.finite_projective_iff_baseChange_and_localization
declarations.doc:
Let `(R → S, f)` be a Beauville--Laszlo glueing pair. An `R`-module `M` is finite
projective if and only if its scalar extension to `S` is finite projective over `S` and its
localization away from `f` is finite projective over `R_f`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finite_projective_iff_baseChange_and_localization
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (f : R)
    (hquot : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
      Function.Bijective (quotientPowMap f n (algebraMap R S)))
    (hglue : (beauvilleLaszloSequence f (algebraMap R S)).ShortExact)
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    (Module.Finite R M ∧ Module.Projective R M) ↔
      ((Module.Finite S (S ⊗[R] M) ∧ Module.Projective S (S ⊗[R] M)) ∧
        (Module.Finite (Localization.Away f) (LocalizedModule.Away f M) ∧
          Module.Projective (Localization.Away f) (LocalizedModule.Away f M)))

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.flat_iff_flat_baseChange_and_localization
declarations.doc:
Let `(R → S, f)` be a Beauville--Laszlo glueing pair. An `R`-module `M` is flat
if and only if its scalar extension to `S` is flat over `S` and its localization away
from `f` is flat over `R_f`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_iff_flat_baseChange_and_localization
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (f : R)
    (hquot : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
      Function.Bijective (quotientPowMap f n (algebraMap R S)))
    (hglue : (beauvilleLaszloSequence f (algebraMap R S)).ShortExact)
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    Module.Flat R M ↔
      Module.Flat S (S ⊗[R] M) ∧
        Module.Flat (Localization.Away f) (LocalizedModule.Away f M)

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.beauvilleLaszlo_completion_comparison
declarations.doc:
For a nonzerodivisor `f : R`, passage to the `(f)`-adic completion gives a
Beauville--Laszlo glueing pair. Every module on which `f` is a nonzerodivisor is
glueable, the canonical functor identifies all glueable modules with glueing data, and
finite projectivity can be checked after completion and localization for an arbitrary
module, with no torsion-freeness or glueability assumption on that module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem beauvilleLaszlo_completion_comparison
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (f : R) (hf : IsSMulRegular R f) :
    let Rhat := AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {f}) R
    (beauvilleLaszloSequence f (algebraMap R Rhat)).ShortExact ∧
      (∀ (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M], IsSMulRegular M f →
        (beauvilleLaszloModuleSequence (S := Rhat) M f).ShortExact) ∧
      (let C := FormalGlueing.moduleGlueingConstruction.{u, u, w} Rhat (fun _ : Fin 1 ↦ f);
        let _ := C.category;
        (canonicalOnGlueableModules f C).IsEquivalence) ∧
      (∀ (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M],
        (Module.Finite R M ∧ Module.Projective R M) ↔
          ((Module.Finite Rhat (Rhat ⊗[R] M) ∧ Module.Projective Rhat (Rhat ⊗[R] M)) ∧
            (Module.Finite (Localization.Away f) (LocalizedModule.Away f M) ∧
              Module.Projective (Localization.Away f) (LocalizedModule.Away f M))))

declarations.name: BeauvilleLaszlo.canonicalToSections_surjective
declarations.doc:
Let `(R → S, f)` be a Beauville--Laszlo glueing pair and let `M` be any
`R`-module. The canonical map from `M` to the compatible sections of its canonical
glueing datum is surjective. Its target is glueable, and the map becomes an isomorphism
after extension of scalars to `S` and after localization away from `f`.

The equations on the generic and local coordinates characterize the canonical map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem canonicalToSections_surjective
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (f : R)
    (hquot : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
      Function.Bijective (quotientPowMap f n (algebraMap R S)))
    (hglue : (beauvilleLaszloSequence f (algebraMap R S)).ShortExact)
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    let C := FormalGlueing.moduleGlueingConstruction.{u, v, w} S (fun _ : Fin 1 ↦ f)
    letI := C.category
    let X := C.canonical.obj (ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{max u v w} M))
    let Mbar := C.sections.obj X
    ∃ g : M →ₗ[R] Mbar,
      (∀ m : M,
        let x := C.sectionsObj X (g m)
        C.canonicalGeneric (ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{max u v w} M)) x.1.1 =
          1 ⊗ₜ[R] ULift.up m ∧
          C.canonicalLocal (ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{max u v w} M)) 0 (x.1.2 0) =
            LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers f) (ULift M) (ULift.up m)) ∧
      glueableModules (S := S) f Mbar ∧
      Function.Bijective
        (TensorProduct.map (LinearMap.id (R := R) (M := S)) g) ∧
      Function.Bijective (LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers f) g) ∧
      Function.Surjective g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GlueingNearPoint.restrictionFunctorAtPoint_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BPA.** Let `s` be a closed point of a scheme `S` whose open
complement `U = S \ {s}` has quasi-compact inclusion.  Restricting a scheme of finite
presentation over `S` to `U` and to `Spec 𝒪_{S, s}`, together with the canonical comparison of
the two induced restrictions to `V = Spec 𝒪_{S, s} ∩ U`, is an equivalence onto the category of
such glueing data.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocalLefschetzSituation.hasPurity_quotientRing_of_isAdicComplete
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BPC.**  Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring and let `f ∈ 𝔪`.
Assume

1. `A` is `f`-adically complete,
2. `f` is a nonzerodivisor,
3. `H¹_𝔪(A/fA)` and `H²_𝔪(A/fA)` are finite `A`-modules,
4. purity holds for `(A_f)_𝔭` for every maximal ideal `𝔭 ⊂ A_f`, and
5. purity holds for `A`.

Then purity holds for `A / fA`.

The source proves this by the proof of Stacks 0DXZ with Stacks 0EKA in place of Stacks 0EK9, and
that is what happens here.  A finite étale cover of `U₀` is, by Stacks 0EKA, the restriction of a
finite étale cover of `U`; hypothesis (5) extends the latter over `X`; and the restriction of that
extension to `X₀ = Spec (A / fA)` is the extension of the original cover.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPurity_quotientRing_of_isAdicComplete
    (hcomplete : IsAdicComplete S.principalIdeal S.A) (hnzd : S.f ∈ nonZeroDivisors S.A)
    (hH1 : Module.Finite S.A (localCohomologyModule S.A (maximalIdeal S.A)
      (maximalIdeal S.A).fg_of_isNoetherianRing (ModuleCat.of S.A S.quotientRing) 1))
    (hH2 : Module.Finite S.A (localCohomologyModule S.A (maximalIdeal S.A)
      (maximalIdeal S.A).fg_of_isNoetherianRing (ModuleCat.of S.A S.quotientRing) 2))
    (haway : ∀ (p : Ideal (Localization.Away S.f)) [p.IsMaximal],
      HasPurity (Localization.AtPrime p))
    (hpurity : HasPurity S.A) :
    HasPurity S.quotientRing
declarations.comment: purity for A/fA under the tag's five hypotheses; nothing beyond them is assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasPurity_of_isCompleteIntersectionRing
declarations.doc:
**Purity for a complete intersection of dimension at least three, [Stacks, Tag 0BPD].** Let
`(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring which is a complete intersection of dimension at least
three. Then purity holds for `A`: every finite étale cover of the punctured spectrum of `A` is,
up to isomorphism, the restriction of a finite étale cover of `Spec A`.

Purity descends from the completion of `A`, which by hypothesis is the quotient of a regular
local ring by an ideal generated by a regular sequence.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPurity_of_isCompleteIntersectionRing
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (hA : LocalCompleteIntersection.IsCompleteIntersectionRing A)
    (hdim : 3 ≤ ringKrullDim A) :
    HasPurity A
declarations.comment: purity for a complete intersection local ring of dimension at least three; the complete intersection hypothesis is `LocalCompleteIntersection.IsCompleteIntersectionRing` (Tag 09Q3 (1)) and purity is `AlgebraicGeometry.HasPurity`

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.isThickening_comp
declarations.doc: A composite of thickenings is a thickening.
declarations.statement:
theorem isThickening_comp {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y ⟶ Z}
    (hf : IsThickening f) (hg : IsThickening g) : IsThickening (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.isThickening_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BPF.** Being a thickening is fpqc local on the target: a morphism
whose base changes along the members of an fpqc covering of the target are all thickenings is
itself a thickening.
declarations.statement:
instance isThickening_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget (@IsThickening : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage
declarations.comment: thickenings

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.isFirstOrderThickening_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BPF.** Being a first-order thickening is fpqc local on the target: a
morphism whose base changes along the members of an fpqc covering of the target are all
first-order thickenings is itself a first-order thickening.
declarations.statement:
instance isFirstOrderThickening_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFirstOrderThickeningHom_of_isFpqcCovering
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ X'` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `{gᵢ : X'ᵢ ⟶ X'}` be an
fpqc covering of `X'` by algebraic spaces. If every base change `fᵢ : Xᵢ ⟶ X'ᵢ` of `f` is a

declarations.statement:
theorem isFirstOrderThickeningHom_of_isFpqcCovering {I : Type v}

    {Xi X'i : I → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (g : ∀ i, X'i i ⟶ X')

    (hsq : ∀ i, IsPullback (p i).hom (fi i).hom f.hom (g i).hom)
    (hg : IsFpqcCovering B S hS fun i ↦ (g i).hom)
    (h : ∀ i, IsFirstOrderThickeningHom B S hS (fi i)) :
    IsFirstOrderThickeningHom B S hS f
declarations.comment: first-order clause, for an arbitrary fpqc covering

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isThickeningHom_and_isFirstOrderThickeningHom_of_isFpqcCovering
declarations.doc:
Being a thickening is fpqc local, and similarly for first order thickenings. Let
`f : X ⟶ X'` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `{gᵢ : X'ᵢ ⟶ X'}` be an fpqc
covering of `X'` by algebraic spaces, with `fᵢ : Xᵢ ⟶ X'ᵢ` the base change of `f` along `gᵢ`.
Then: if every `fᵢ` is a thickening so is `f`, and if every `fᵢ` is a first-order thickening so
is `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isThickeningHom_and_isFirstOrderThickeningHom_of_isFpqcCovering {I : Type v}
    {X X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ X')
    {Xi X'i : I → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (g : ∀ i, X'i i ⟶ X')
    (fi : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X'i i) (p : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X)
    (hsq : ∀ i, IsPullback (p i).hom (fi i).hom f.hom (g i).hom)
    (hg : IsFpqcCovering B S hS fun i ↦ (g i).hom) :
    ((∀ i, IsThickeningHom B S hS (fi i)) → IsThickeningHom B S hS f) ∧
      ((∀ i, IsFirstOrderThickeningHom B S hS (fi i)) →
        IsFirstOrderThickeningHom B S hS f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isThickeningHom_iff_forall_of_isFpqcCovering
declarations.doc:
A morphism `f : X ⟶ X'` of
algebraic spaces over `S` is a thickening if and only if its base change along every member of

declarations.statement:
theorem isThickeningHom_iff_forall_of_isFpqcCovering {I : Type v}

    (hsq : ∀ i, IsPullback (p i).hom (fi i).hom f.hom (g i).hom)
    (hg : IsFpqcCovering B S hS fun i ↦ (g i).hom) :
    IsThickeningHom B S hS f ↔ ∀ i, IsThickeningHom B S hS (fi i)
declarations.comment: thickenings, as an equivalence along an fpqc covering

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFirstOrderThickeningHom_iff_forall_of_isFpqcCovering
declarations.doc:
A morphism `f : X ⟶ X'` of

declarations.statement:
theorem isFirstOrderThickeningHom_iff_forall_of_isFpqcCovering {I : Type v}

    (fi : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X'i i) (p : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X)
    (hsq : ∀ i, IsPullback (p i).hom (fi i).hom f.hom (g i).hom)
    (hg : IsFpqcCovering B S hS fun i ↦ (g i).hom) :

declarations.comment: first-order clause, as an equivalence along an fpqc covering

declarations.name: Stacks.Spaces.UniversalThickening.isClosedSubspace_and_isFirstOrderThickening_of_surjectiveEtaleChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPI, the first-order clause, along a surjective étale chart.** Let `Y` be a
subfunctor of an algebraic space `Q` over `S` which is a sheaf for the big fppf topology, and
let `q : V ⟶ Q` be a surjective étale chart of `Q` by an object of the site. If the base change
of the inclusion of `Y` along `q` is a closed immersion whose range is a first-order thickening
of `V`, then `Y` is a closed subspace of `Q` and a first-order thickening of it.

The source states the clause for an arbitrary fpqc covering of the target; this is the case of
a one-member covering by a surjective étale scheme chart, which is the case the construction
below consumes, together with the sheaf condition on `Y` that the fpqc statement does not ask
for. Algebraicity of `Y` and closedness of its inclusion are Stacks 03I2 at the closed
immersions, whose effective-descent input is discharged outright by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveEtale_isClosedImmersion`;
surjectivity on points follows from surjectivity of `q` and of the base change; and the order
clause is `Stacks.Spaces.UniversalThickening.definingIdealAt_pow_eq_bot_of_surjectiveEtaleChart`,
which descends the vanishing of the square of the defining ideal from the charts of `V` to the
charts of `Q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedSubspace_and_isFirstOrderThickening_of_surjectiveEtaleChart
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {Q : AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (Y : Subfunctor Q.1)
    (hYsheaf : Presheaf.IsSheaf (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) Y.toFunctor)
    {V : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS} (q : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Q.1)
    (hqsurj : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf q)
    (hqetale : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf q)
    (hclosed : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsClosedImmersion B S hS
      (Limits.pullback.snd Y.ι q))
    (hfirst : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS
      (AlgebraicGeometry.schemeSpace V)
      (Subfunctor.range (Limits.pullback.snd Y.ι q))) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsClosedSubspace B S hS Y ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS Q Y
declarations.comment: first-order clause, along a surjective etale chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.formallyUnramifiedCharts_iff_of_cartesianMorphismOfThickenings
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPJ, part (4).** In a cartesian morphism of thickenings of algebraic spaces whose
two component maps are locally of finite type, the module of relative differentials of `f`
vanishes exactly when the module of relative differentials of `f'` does.

The vanishing of `Ω_{X/Y}` is expressed by the condition that the morphism of schemes in every
commuting square of étale charts of `f` is formally unramified, which on an affine chart is the

declarations.statement:
