    HoldsOnEveryEtaleChart B S hS
        (@_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.FormallyUnramified.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) T.f ↔
      HoldsOnEveryEtaleChart B S hS
        (@_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.FormallyUnramified.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) T.f'
declarations.comment: vanishing_differentials

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyQuasiFiniteProperty_iff_of_cartesianSquareOfThickeningHoms
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPJ, part (1), at the point test of Section 04XB.** Let
`(f, f') : (X ⊂ X') → (Y ⊂ Y')` be a morphism of thickenings of algebraic spaces over `S` with
`f` and `f'` locally of finite type and `X = Y ×_{Y'} X'`. Then `f` is locally quasi-finite if
and only if `f'` is locally quasi-finite.

The square is given by morphisms of the category of algebraic spaces over `S` and the three
properties by morphism properties of that category.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasiFiniteProperty_iff_of_cartesianSquareOfThickeningHoms
    {X X' Y Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {i : X ⟶ X'} {j : Y ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    (hi : IsThickeningHom B S hS i) (hj : IsThickeningHom B S hS j) (hsq : IsPullback f i j f')
    (hft : locallyOfFiniteTypeProperty B S hS f)
    (hft' : locallyOfFiniteTypeProperty B S hS f') :
    locallyQuasiFiniteProperty B S hS f ↔ locallyQuasiFiniteProperty B S hS f'
declarations.comment: part (1): locally quasi-finite, at the Section 04XB point test

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.formallyUnramifiedCharts_iff_of_cartesianSquareOfThickeningHoms
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPJ, part (4), at the point test of Section 04XB.** Let
`(f, f') : (X ⊂ X') → (Y ⊂ Y')` be a morphism of thickenings of algebraic spaces over `S` with
`f` and `f'` locally of finite type and `X = Y ×_{Y'} X'`. Then `Ω_{X/Y} = 0` if and only if
`Ω_{X'/Y'} = 0`, the vanishing of the relative differentials being expressed, as in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.formallyUnramifiedCharts_iff_of_cartesianMorphismOfThickenings`, by
formal unramifiedness of the morphism of schemes in every commuting square of étale charts.

The square is given by morphisms of the category of algebraic spaces over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem formallyUnramifiedCharts_iff_of_cartesianSquareOfThickeningHoms
    {X X' Y Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {i : X ⟶ X'} {j : Y ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    (hi : IsThickeningHom B S hS i) (hj : IsThickeningHom B S hS j) (hsq : IsPullback f i j f')
    (hft : locallyOfFiniteTypeProperty B S hS f)
    (hft' : locallyOfFiniteTypeProperty B S hS f') :
    HoldsOnEveryEtaleChart B S hS
        (@_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.FormallyUnramified.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) f.hom ↔
      HoldsOnEveryEtaleChart B S hS
        (@_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.FormallyUnramified.{u} :
          MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) f'.hom
declarations.comment: part (4): vanishing relative differentials, at the Section 04XB point test

If `f` is a monomorphism, the first projection of `X' ×_{Y'} X'` is a monomorphism by
`mono_pullback_fst_of_mono` and a split epimorphism retracted by the diagonal, hence an

declarations.statement:
theorem immersionProperty_iff_of_cartesianSquareOfThickeningHoms
    (hi : IsThickeningHom B S hS i) (hj : IsThickeningHom B S hS j) (hsq : IsPullback f i j f')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mono_iff_of_cartesianSquareOfThickeningHoms
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPJ, part (6), at the point test of Section 04XB.** Let
`(f, f') : (X ⊂ X') → (Y ⊂ Y')` be a morphism of thickenings of algebraic spaces over `S` with
`f` and `f'` locally of finite type and `X = Y ×_{Y'} X'`. Then `f` is a monomorphism if and
only if `f'` is a monomorphism.

The direction from `f'` to `f` is base change. In the other direction, `f'` is a monomorphism as
soon as the first projection of `X' ×_{Y'} X'` is an isomorphism, and that projection is
obtained as follows. Pull the thickening `i : X ⟶ X'` back along the first projection; the
resulting square

```
X ×_{X'} (X' ×_{Y'} X') --→ X
|                           |
↓                           ↓
X' ×_{Y'} X' ------fst-----→ X'
```

is again a cartesian morphism of thickenings with both horizontal maps locally of finite type,
and its upper map is an *isomorphism*: a section of the upper left corner is a pair `(a, b)` of
sections of `X'` with `f'(a) = f'(b)` and `a` a section of `X`, the cartesian square of the
given morphism of thickenings exhibits `b` as a second factorisation of that pair through `X`
with the same image under `f`, and monomorphy of `f` identifies the two. An isomorphism is a
closed immersion, so part (3) above makes `fst` a closed immersion, hence a monomorphism; it is
also split by the diagonal of `f'`, and a monomorphism which is a split epimorphism is an
isomorphism.

This is the argument of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CartesianFiniteOrderMorphismOfThickenings.mono_iff` for part (9) of
**Stacks 09ZZ**, with part (3) above in place of part (1) of that tag; the source's own proof of
this case instead compares the conormal sheaf of the diagonal of `f` with that of `f'`, which
needs the algebraic-space form of **Stacks 08S2** and so is not available here.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_iff_of_cartesianSquareOfThickeningHoms
    (hi : IsThickeningHom B S hS i) (_hj : IsThickeningHom B S hS j) (hsq : IsPullback f i j f')
    (_hft : locallyOfFiniteTypeProperty B S hS f)
    (hft' : locallyOfFiniteTypeProperty B S hS f') :
    Mono f ↔ Mono f'
declarations.comment: part (6): monomorphism, at the Section 04XB point test

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramified_iff_of_cartesianMorphismOfThickenings
declarations.doc:
Being unramified is invariant under a cartesian morphism of thickenings of algebraic spaces
whose two component maps are locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_iff_of_cartesianMorphismOfThickenings
    (T : CartesianLocallyFiniteTypeMorphismOfThickenings B S hS) :
    IsUnramified B S hS T.f ↔ IsUnramified B S hS T.f'
declarations.comment: unramified

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.unramifiedMorphismProperty_iff_of_cartesianSquareOfThickeningHoms
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPJ, part (5), at the point test of Section 04XB.** Let
`(f, f') : (X ⊂ X') → (Y ⊂ Y')` be a morphism of thickenings of algebraic spaces over `S` with
`f` and `f'` locally of finite type and `X = Y ×_{Y'} X'`. Then `f` is unramified if and only if
`f'` is unramified.

The two thickenings are given as morphisms `i : X ⟶ X'` and `j : Y ⟶ Y'` of the category of
algebraic spaces over `S` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsThickeningHom`) and the three properties
as morphism properties of that category, which is the shape the point test of **Stacks 03YK**
reads a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces in; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasRelativeProperty`. The equivalence itself is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramified_iff_of_cartesianMorphismOfThickenings`, the same statement
with the two smaller spaces presented as subfunctors of the two ambient ones.
declarations.statement:
theorem unramifiedMorphismProperty_iff_of_cartesianSquareOfThickeningHoms
    {X X' Y Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {i : X ⟶ X'} {j : Y ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    (hi : IsThickeningHom B S hS i) (hj : IsThickeningHom B S hS j) (hsq : IsPullback f i j f')
    (hft : locallyOfFiniteTypeProperty B S hS f)
    (hft' : locallyOfFiniteTypeProperty B S hS f') :
    unramifiedMorphismProperty B S hS f ↔ unramifiedMorphismProperty B S hS f'
declarations.comment: part (5): unramified, at the Section 04XB point test

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedImmersion_iff_of_cartesianMorphismOfThickenings
registrations.comment: part (3): f is a closed immersion iff f' is

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isImmersion_iff_of_cartesianMorphismOfThickenings
registrations.comment: part (7): f is an immersion iff f' is

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsThickening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPP**, part (1). A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` *is a thickening* when it
is a closed immersion, in the sense of Stacks 04YL part (2), and is surjective on the underlying
sets of points.

The source's part (1) also asserts that the induced map of underlying topological spaces is a
homeomorphism; that clause needs the point topology of Stacks 04XL, which has no library site, so
it is not stated here.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsThickening {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (i : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1): thickening

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ThickeningMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPP**, part (2). A *morphism of thickenings* from the thickening `i` to the
thickening `j` of algebraic stacks over `S`: a 1-morphism of the ambient stacks, a 1-morphism of
the closed substacks, and a 2-isomorphism saying that the former restricts to the latter.
declarations.statement:
structure ThickeningMorphism {𝒳 𝒳' 𝒴 𝒴' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (i : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳') (j : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒴') (_hi : IsThickening i) (_hj : IsThickening j)
declarations.comment: part (2): morphisms of thickenings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ThickeningOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPP**, part (3). A thickening of algebraic stacks over `S` together with a
1-morphism from its ambient stack to a fixed algebraic stack `𝒵`.
declarations.statement: structure ThickeningOver (𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
declarations.comment: part (3): thickenings over a stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ThickeningMorphismOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPP**, part (3). A morphism of thickenings of algebraic stacks over a fixed
algebraic stack `𝒵`: a morphism of the underlying thickenings whose ambient component lies over
the base up to 2-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
structure ThickeningMorphismOver {𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (𝒳 𝒴 : ThickeningOver.{u, w} 𝒵)
declarations.comment: part (3): morphisms over a stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsFirstOrderThickening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPQ.** A closed immersion `i : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳'` of algebraic stacks over `S` exhibits `𝒳'`
as a *first-order thickening* of `𝒳` when, for every scheme-valued point `U ⟶ 𝒳'` and every
algebraic space `F` representing the base change of `i` along it, the image of the structural
morphism of `F` is a first-order thickening of the representable algebraic space of `U` in the
sense of Stacks 05ZK, part (2) — that is, the ideal cutting it out is square-zero on every object
of the small étale site.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsFirstOrderThickening (i : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳') : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFirstOrderThickening_fst_of_isTwoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
If `𝒴 ⊂ 𝒴'` is a first-order thickening of algebraic
stacks over `S` and `𝒳 = 𝒴 ×_{𝒴'} 𝒳'` for a 1-morphism `g : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒴'`, then `𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳'` — the
projection `P.fst` — is a first-order thickening.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFirstOrderThickening_fst_of_isTwoFibreProduct
    {𝒴 𝒴' 𝒳' : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {j : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒴'} {g : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒴'}
    (hj : IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS j)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g j) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P) :
    IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS P.fst
declarations.comment: first order thickening base-changes to a first order thickening

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isThickening_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPR.** Let `i : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒴'` be a thickening of algebraic stacks over `S`, let
`f : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒴'` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks, and let `P` be a 2-fibre product of that
cospan in the 2-category of algebraic stacks. Then the second projection
`P.snd : 𝒴 ×_{𝒴'} 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳'` is a thickening.

A thickening is a closed immersion which is surjective on points, and each of its three
constituents base-changes: representability by algebraic spaces by Stacks 0302, the
closed-immersion property of Stacks 04XB by Stacks 045C, and surjectivity on points by
Stacks 04ZU.
declarations.statement:
theorem isThickening_baseChange (i : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒴') (f : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒴')
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq i f) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hi : IsThickening i) :
    IsThickening P.snd
declarations.comment: base-changed thickening

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.baseChangeThickeningMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPR.** A 2-fibre product square of a thickening `i : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒴'` of algebraic stacks
along a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒴'` *is* a morphism of thickenings from the base-changed thickening
`P.snd` to `i`: its ambient 1-morphism is `f`, its restricted 1-morphism is the first projection
`P.fst`, and the 2-isomorphism filling the square is exactly the assertion that `f` restricts to
`P.fst`.
declarations.statement:
def baseChangeThickeningMorphism (i : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒴') (f : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒴')
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq i f) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hi : IsThickening i) :
    ThickeningMorphism P.snd i (isThickening_baseChange B S hS i f P hP hi) hi
declarations.comment: morphism of thickenings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isThickening_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPS.** A composite of thickenings of algebraic stacks over `S` is a thickening:
the composite is a closed immersion by Stacks 0502, and it is surjective on points because each
factor is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isThickening_comp
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : IsThickening f) (hg : IsThickening g) :
    IsThickening (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: the composite of two thickenings is a thickening

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isThickening_stackReductionInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPT, assertion (1).** An algebraic stack over `S` is a thickening of its reduction:
the inclusion of the reduction is a closed immersion and is surjective on points, which are the
two clauses of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsThickening` (**Stacks 0BPP**, part (1)).

Surjectivity on points is the clause of Definition 050C that the set of points of the reduction is
all of `|𝒳|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isThickening_stackReductionInclusion (R : StackReduction B S hS 𝒳) :
    IsThickening R.inclusion
declarations.comment: assertion (1): an algebraic stack is a thickening of its reduction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isClosedSubstack_stackReductionEssImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPT, assertion (1), substack form.** The reduction of an algebraic stack `𝒳` over
`S` is realised as a closed substack of `𝒳` carrying every point of `𝒳`, which is what it means
for `𝒳` to be a thickening of it in the substack language of **Stacks 04YM**, part (2).

The substack is the essential image of the inclusion of the reduction, a closed substack by
**Stacks 0506**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedSubstack_stackReductionEssImage (R : StackReduction B S hS 𝒳) :
    ∃ hP : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS
        (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor R.inclusion.hom).essImage),
      AlgebraicStacks.IsClosedImmersion B S hS
          (fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒳
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor R.inclusion.hom).essImage hP) ∧
        IsSurjective B S hS
          (fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒳
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor R.inclusion.hom).essImage hP)
declarations.comment: assertion (1), substack form: the reduction is a closed substack with every point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.stackReductionOfThickening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPT, assertion (2).** Let `𝒳 ⊆ 𝒳'` be a thickening of algebraic stacks over `S`.
Then the reduction of `𝒳` is a reduction of `𝒳'`, included through `𝒳`: this is the source's
`𝒳'_red = 𝒳_red ⊆ 𝒳`.

The inclusion is the composite of the inclusion of the reduction of `𝒳` with the given thickening,
which is again a thickening by **Stacks 0BPS**, and the source stack is untouched, so it is still
reduced.
declarations.statement:
def stackReductionOfThickening
    [(Space.closedImmersionProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, u} B S hS)]
    (R : StackReduction B S hS 𝒳) (i : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳') (hi : IsThickening i) :
    StackReduction B S hS 𝒳'
declarations.comment: assertion (2): a thickening has the same reduction as its ambient stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isReducedStack_iff_essImage_stackReduction_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPT, assertion (3).** Let `R` present the reduction of an algebraic stack `𝒳` over
`S`. Then the closed substack of `𝒳` cut out by that reduction is all of `𝒳` exactly when `𝒳` is a
reduced algebraic stack.

Read through assertion (2) this is the source's assertion (3): for a thickening `𝒳 ⊆ 𝒳'` the
reduction of `𝒳'` is the reduction of `𝒳`, so `𝒳 = 𝒳'_red` says precisely that the reduction of
`𝒳` is all of `𝒳`.

One direction is **Stacks 050A** at the closed substack cut out by the essential image of the
inclusion of the reduction, which carries every point of `𝒳`. For the other, a reduction whose
substack is all of `𝒳` has fully faithful and essentially surjective inclusion, so reducedness
transports from the reduction to `𝒳`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReducedStack_iff_essImage_stackReduction_eq_top (R : StackReduction B S hS 𝒳) :
    (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor R.inclusion.hom).essImage = ⊤ ↔
      IsReducedStack B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: assertion (3): the reduction is the whole stack exactly when the stack is reduced

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isThickening_stackReduction_inclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPT, assertion (1).** An algebraic stack `𝒳'` over `S` is a thickening of its
reduction `𝒳'_red` (**Stacks 050C**): the inclusion of the reduction is a closed immersion which
is surjective on points, the two clauses of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsThickening`
(**Stacks 0BPP**).
declarations.statement:
theorem isThickening_stackReduction_inclusion (𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    IsThickening (stackReduction 𝒳').inclusion
declarations.comment: assertion (1): an algebraic stack is a thickening of its reduction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.essImage_stackReduction_eq_of_isThickening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPT, assertion (2).** Let `i : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳'` be a thickening of algebraic stacks over
`S`. Then `𝒳'_red = 𝒳_red ⊆ 𝒳`: the reduction of `𝒳'` is the substack of `𝒳'` cut out by the
reduction of `𝒳` included through `i`, and it lies in the substack cut out by `𝒳`.

The composite of the inclusion of `𝒳_red` with `i` is again a thickening by **Stacks 0BPS** and
has reduced source, so its essential image is a reduction of `𝒳'` in the sense of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsReduction`; so is that of the inclusion of `𝒳'_red`, and the two agree
by uniqueness of the reduction (**Stacks 0509**).
declarations.statement:
theorem essImage_stackReduction_eq_of_isThickening {𝒳 𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (i : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳') (hi : IsThickening i) :
    (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (stackReduction 𝒳').inclusion.hom).essImage =
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor ((stackReduction 𝒳).inclusion ≫ i).hom).essImage ∧
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (stackReduction 𝒳').inclusion.hom).essImage ≤
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor i.hom).essImage
declarations.comment: assertion (2): a thickening has the same reduction as its ambient stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.essImage_stackReduction_eq_essImage_iff_isReducedStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPT, assertion (3).** Let `i : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳'` be a thickening of algebraic stacks over
`S`. Then `𝒳 = 𝒳'_red` — the reduction of `𝒳'` and `𝒳` cut out the same substack of `𝒳'` —
exactly when `𝒳` is a reduced algebraic stack.

By assertion (2) the reduction of `𝒳'` is the substack cut out by the reduction of `𝒳` through
`i`; since `i` is fully faithful (**Stacks 0506**), that is the substack cut out by `i` exactly
when the reduction of `𝒳` is all of `𝒳`, which is reducedness of `𝒳` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isReducedStack_iff_essImage_stackReduction_eq_top`.
declarations.statement:
theorem essImage_stackReduction_eq_essImage_iff_isReducedStack
    {𝒳 𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (i : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳') (hi : IsThickening i) :
    (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (stackReduction 𝒳').inclusion.hom).essImage =
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor i.hom).essImage ↔
      IsReducedStack B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment:
assertion (3): a thickening is the reduction of its ambient stack exactly when it
is reduced

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isThickening_diagonalComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPU, the first assertion.** In a morphism of thickenings
`(f, f') : (𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳') → (𝒴 ⊂ 𝒴')` of algebraic stacks over `S`, the comparison 1-morphism
`𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳' ×_{𝒴'} 𝒳'` is a thickening.

Since `𝒳 → 𝒴'` factors through the closed substack `𝒴`, the enlargement of the target
identifies `𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳` with `𝒳 ×_{𝒴'} 𝒳` (**Stacks 04ZZ** (1) ⟹ (2) makes `j` fully faithful);
the latter maps to `𝒳' ×_{𝒴'} 𝒳'` by two base changes of the thickening `i`, one factor at a
time, each a thickening by **Stacks 0BPR**, so their composite is one by **Stacks 0BPS**.

This carries the part key *first assertion* of Stacks 0BPU for *this* comparison 1-morphism. The
other assertion of that tag, that the diagonal square is cartesian, is not proved for it — see
the implementation notes, which name the obstruction. Both assertions are proved for the rebuilt
comparison with an explicit body: the first by `isThickening_selfProductDiagonalMap` below, which
carries the same part key, and the cartesian one by
`isTwoFibreProduct_selfProductDiagonalSquare`. The 2-isomorphism between the two comparisons is
still open, which is why the first assertion is registered twice rather than once.

The fppf-target-locality instance is Stacks 0420. The library proves it at the fpqc precoverage,
`isClosedImmersion_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc`, and restricts it to the fppf precoverage asked for
here in `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedImmersion_isLocalAtTarget_fppf`, which is an instance;
the hypothesis below is therefore discharged automatically.
declarations.statement:
theorem isThickening_diagonalComparison
    [(Space.closedImmersionProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, u} B S hS)] :
    IsThickening (diagonalComparison B S hS m)
declarations.comment: first assertion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isThickening_selfProductDiagonalMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPU, the first assertion, for the comparison with an explicit body.** For a morphism
of thickenings `(f, f') : (𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳') → (𝒴 ⊂ 𝒴')` of algebraic stacks over `S`, the canonical
comparison 1-morphism `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.selfProductDiagonalMap : 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳' ×_{𝒴'} 𝒳'`
is a thickening.

The source's factorisation of the comparison into two base changes of `i`, one factor at a time,
is carried here *strictly*: the comparison is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.selfProductFstLift`
followed by the base change of `i` along the first projection of `𝒳' ×_{𝒴'} 𝒳'`, on the nose
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.selfProductFstLift_comp_snd`, which holds by `rfl`). The second factor
is a thickening by **Stacks 0BPR**
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isThickening_ambientFstRestriction_snd`); the first is one because
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_selfProductSndSquare` exhibits it too as a base change
of `i`, so **Stacks 0BPR** applies again; and their composite is a thickening by **Stacks 0BPS**,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isThickening_comp`.

This carries the part key *first assertion* of Stacks 0BPU, and together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_selfProductDiagonalSquare` — which carries the part key
*cartesian diagonal square* — it puts **both** assertions of the tag on this one comparison
1-morphism. The part key *first assertion* is also carried by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isThickening_diagonalComparison`, the same assertion for the other
canonical comparison `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.diagonalComparison`; that registration is kept, the
two comparisons being 2-isomorphic but not yet identified in the library.

The fppf-target-locality instance is Stacks 0420 and is discharged automatically, exactly as in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isThickening_diagonalComparison`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isThickening_selfProductDiagonalMap
    [(Space.closedImmersionProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, u} B S hS)] :
    IsThickening (selfProductDiagonalMap B S hS m)
declarations.comment: first assertion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_selfProductDiagonalSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPU, the second assertion: the diagonal square of a morphism of thickenings of
algebraic stacks is cartesian.** For a morphism of thickenings
`(f, f') : (𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳') → (𝒴 ⊂ 𝒴')` of algebraic stacks over `S`, the square

```text
  𝒳  --Δ-->  𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳
  |              |
  v              v
  𝒳' --Δ'--> 𝒳' ×_{𝒴'} 𝒳'
```

is a 2-fibre product in the 2-category of algebraic stacks over `(Sch/S)_fppf`, the right-hand
leg being the canonical comparison
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.selfProductDiagonalMap` — canonical strictly, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.selfProductDiagonalMap_comp_fst` and `…_comp_snd`.

The source proves this by applying **Stacks 0CBB** to `𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒴'`, using that the thickening
`i : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳'` is a monomorphism. Here it is the over-the-base form of 0CBB with a growing target,
`CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.isEquivalence_selfProductDiagonalComparison`, whose three
hypotheses are met because a closed immersion of algebraic stacks is fully faithful
(**Stacks 04ZZ** (1) ⟹ (2),
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.full_and_faithful_homFunctor_of_isClosedImmersion`),
applied to `i` for fullness and faithfulness and to `j` for the faithfulness the growing target
costs. The passage from an equivalence of underlying categories to the universal property is
`CategoryTheory.Bicategory.isTwoFibreProduct_of_isEquivalence_to` against the canonical 2-fibre
product square of the cospan, and the passage from the 2-category of categories fibred in
groupoids down to the full sub-2-category of algebraic stacks is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isTwoFibreProduct_of_toCatFiberedInGroupoids`.

This carries the part key *cartesian diagonal square* of Stacks 0BPU; the other assertion, that
the comparison is a thickening, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isThickening_selfProductDiagonalMap`, for **this same** comparison
1-morphism, so the two assertions of the tag are both statements about
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.selfProductDiagonalMap`. The first assertion is registered a second time
on `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isThickening_diagonalComparison`, which asserts it of the other
canonical comparison `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.diagonalComparison`; the implementation note above
says why the cartesian assertion cannot be carried by that one.

**What identifying the two comparisons still lacks.** The two 1-morphisms are 2-isomorphic, being
two canonical comparisons into a 2-fibre product, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isThickening_congr_twoIso` would then make either of the two
first-assertion registrations redundant. The 2-isomorphism is *not* available from
`CategoryTheory.Bicategory.twoFibreProduct_twoIso_of_legs`, however: that result needs the two
comparison 2-cells to be compatible with the filler of `𝒳' ×_{𝒴'} 𝒳'`, and that compatibility
mentions the filler whiskered by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.diagonalComparison`, which is the very
thing the `Quotient.out` in `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.selfProductComparison` makes uncomputable.
It would instead have to come from
`CategoryTheory.Bicategory.twoFibreProduct_twoIso_of_preHom`, i.e. by exhibiting
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.diagonalComparison` as the 1-morphism of a pre-morphism of
2-commutative squares assembled by `CategoryTheory.Bicategory.TwoCommSq.PreHom.comp` from its
four stages — the enlargement of the target, the comparison of the two models of the cospan
`(f ≫ j, f ≫ j)`, and the two base changes of `i` — which is a chase through two cospan
reindexings that the library does not currently assemble.
declarations.statement:
def isTwoFibreProduct_selfProductDiagonalSquare :
    Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct (selfProductDiagonalSquare B S hS m)
declarations.comment: cartesian diagonal square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.thickeningMorphism_relativeDiagonal_inner_iff_outer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPV.** Let `(f, f') : (𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳') → (𝒴 ⊂ 𝒴')` be a morphism of thickenings of
algebraic stacks over `S`, `f = m.inner` and `f' = m.outer`, and let `Δ : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳` and
`Δ' : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳' ×_{𝒴'} 𝒳'` be the relative diagonals. Then `Δ` has each of the following
properties if and only if `Δ'` has it:
(a) representable by schemes, (b) affine, (c) surjective, (d) quasi-compact,
(e) universally closed, (f) integral, (g) quasi-separated, (h) separated,
(i) universally injective, (j) universally open, (k) locally quasi-finite, (l) finite,
(m) unramified, (n) monomorphism, (o) immersion, (p) closed immersion, (q) proper.

The conjuncts are, in order, the seventeen properties of the source; (b) and (d)–(q) are the
conditions of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB, at the corresponding properties of morphisms of
algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem thickeningMorphism_relativeDiagonal_inner_iff_outer (m : ThickeningMorphism i j hi hj) :
    -- (a) representable by schemes
    (Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism 𝒳.val.val.p
        (AlgebraicStacks.twoFibreProduct B S hS m.inner m.inner).val.val.p
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor
          (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.inner).hom) ↔
      Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism 𝒳'.val.val.p
        (AlgebraicStacks.twoFibreProduct B S hS m.outer m.outer).val.val.p
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor
          (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.outer).hom)) ∧
    -- (b) affine
    (Stack.IsAffineHom B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.inner).hom ↔
      Stack.IsAffineHom B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.outer).hom) ∧
    -- (c) surjective
    (IsSurjective B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.inner) ↔
      IsSurjective B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.outer)) ∧
    -- (d) quasi-compact
    (Stack.IsQuasiCompact B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.inner).hom ↔
      Stack.IsQuasiCompact B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.outer).hom) ∧
    -- (e) universally closed
    (Stack.UniversallyClosed B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.inner).hom ↔
      Stack.UniversallyClosed B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.outer).hom) ∧
    -- (f) integral
    (HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS (Space.integralMorphismProperty B S hS)
        (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.inner).hom
        (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeDiagonal_algebraicStacks B S hS m.inner) ↔
      HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS (Space.integralMorphismProperty B S hS)
        (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.outer).hom
        (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeDiagonal_algebraicStacks B S hS m.outer)) ∧
    -- (g) quasi-separated
    (Stack.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.inner).hom ↔
      Stack.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.outer).hom) ∧
    -- (h) separated
    (Stack.IsSeparated B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.inner).hom ↔
      Stack.IsSeparated B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.outer).hom) ∧
    -- (i) universally injective
    (UniversallyInjective B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.inner) ↔
      UniversallyInjective B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.outer)) ∧
    -- (j) universally open
    (HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS (Space.universallyOpenMorphismProperty B S hS)
        (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.inner).hom
        (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeDiagonal_algebraicStacks B S hS m.inner) ↔
      HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS (Space.universallyOpenMorphismProperty B S hS)
        (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.outer).hom
        (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeDiagonal_algebraicStacks B S hS m.outer)) ∧
    -- (k) locally quasi-finite
    (Stack.IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.inner).hom ↔
      Stack.IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS
        (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.outer).hom) ∧
    -- (l) finite
    (HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS (Space.finiteMorphismProperty B S hS)
        (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.inner).hom
        (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeDiagonal_algebraicStacks B S hS m.inner) ↔
      HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS (Space.finiteMorphismProperty B S hS)
        (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.outer).hom
        (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeDiagonal_algebraicStacks B S hS m.outer)) ∧
    -- (m) unramified
    (haveI : (Space.unramifiedMorphismProperty B S hS).IsStableUnderBaseChange :=
      Space.isUnramified_isStableUnderBaseChange B S hS
    haveI : (Space.unramifiedMorphismProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
        (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, u} B S hS) :=
      (Space.isUnramified_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc.{u, u} B S hS).of_le
        (Space.fppfPrecoverage_le_fpqcPrecoverage.{u, u} B S hS)
    HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS (Space.unramifiedMorphismProperty B S hS)
        (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.inner).hom
        (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeDiagonal_algebraicStacks B S hS m.inner) ↔
      HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS (Space.unramifiedMorphismProperty B S hS)
        (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.outer).hom
        (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeDiagonal_algebraicStacks B S hS m.outer)) ∧
    -- (n) monomorphism
    (HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS
        (MorphismProperty.monomorphisms (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
        (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.inner).hom
        (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeDiagonal_algebraicStacks B S hS m.inner) ↔
      HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS
        (MorphismProperty.monomorphisms (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
        (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.outer).hom
        (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeDiagonal_algebraicStacks B S hS m.outer)) ∧
    -- (o) immersion
    (Stack.IsImmersion B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.inner).hom ↔
      Stack.IsImmersion B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.outer).hom) ∧
    -- (p) closed immersion
    (Stack.IsClosedImmersion B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.inner).hom ↔
      Stack.IsClosedImmersion B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.outer).hom) ∧
    -- (q) proper
    (Stack.IsProper B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.inner).hom ↔
      Stack.IsProper B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS m.outer).hom)

**Stacks 0BPW, clause (5).** If `𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳'` is a thickening of algebraic stacks over `S` then
`𝒳` is separated if and only if `𝒳'` is — the absolute axiom, part (7) of **Stacks 050D**.

Both sides are separatedness over `Spec(ℤ)` of the stacks viewed by **Stacks 04X6**, and the
thickening viewed over `Spec(ℤ)` is a thickening
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isThickening_changeBaseHomAlgebraicStacks`), so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparatedOver_iff_isThickening` at the base `Spec(ℤ)`.

declarations.comment: clause (5): separated, the absolute axiom of Stacks 050D part (7)

`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiSeparatedOver_iff_isThickening`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_of_isThickening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPW, clause (1), from the ambient stack to the closed substack.** If `𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳'` is a
thickening of algebraic stacks over `S` and `𝒳'` is an algebraic space, then so is `𝒳`.

The thickening `i` is a closed immersion, hence representable by algebraic spaces, and `𝒳` is the
apex of the degenerate 2-fibre product `𝒳' ×_{𝒳'} 𝒳` of
`CategoryTheory.Bicategory.TwoCommSq.idCospan`; so **Stacks 04ZP**, the implication (1) ⟹ (2)
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_of_isTwoFibreProduct`), applies. Only
the closed-immersion half of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsThickening` is used.

theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_of_isThickening (i : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳') (hi : IsThickening i)
    (h : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS 𝒳'.val) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS 𝒳.val
declarations.comment: clause (1): algebraic space -- only part of the clause, namely the implication from the ambient stack to the closed substack; the whole equivalence is AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_iff_isThickening

The thickening is read as a morphism of thickenings over the base
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.structureThickeningMorphism`) and

`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDMOver_iff_isThickening` in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Stacks.ThickeningQuasiDMDeligneMumford`, which is item (9) of
**Stacks 0CJ9** at the same viewing and carries the part key.

theorem isDMOver_of_isThickening (i : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳') (hi : IsThickening i)
    (h : IsDMOver B S hS 𝒳') : IsDMOver B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: clause (3): DM over the base -- only part of the clause, namely the implication from the ambient stack to the closed substack; the whole equivalence is AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDMOver_iff_isThickening

theorem isQuasiSeparatedOver_iff_isThickening (i : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳') (hi : IsThickening i) :

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.exists_pow_smul_localCohomology_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPX.** If a power of `J` annihilates the `i`-th local cohomology of `A` supported
on `V(I)`, then a power of `J` annihilates the corresponding local cohomology of every finitely
presented `A`-module which is finite locally free after localization at every element of `I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pow_smul_localCohomology_eq_bot (J I : Ideal A) (hJI : J ≤ I) (hI : I.FG) (i : ℕ)
    (hA : ∃ n : ℕ,
      J ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A
        (localCohomologyWithSupportIn.{u, 0} A (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A))
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
            (ModuleCat.of A A)) (i : ℤ))) = ⊥) :
    ∀ (M : ModuleCat.{u} A), Module.FinitePresentation A M →
      (∀ f ∈ I, Module.IsFiniteLocallyFree (Localization.Away f) (LocalizedModule.Away f M)) →
      ∃ m : ℕ,
        J ^ m • (⊤ : Submodule A
          (localCohomologyWithSupportIn.{u, 0} A (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A))
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj M) (i : ℤ))) = ⊥

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.localCohomologyWithSupportIn_finite_of_finiteLocallyFree_away
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BPY.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal, `Z = V(I)` and `n ≥ 0`. If
the local cohomology `H^i_Z(A)` of the ring is finite for `0 ≤ i ≤ n`, then `H^i_Z(M)` is finite
for `0 ≤ i ≤ n`, for every finite `A`-module `M` such that `M_f` is a finite locally free
`A_f`-module for every `f ∈ I`.

Finiteness for `A` through degree `n` produces a power `I ^ e` annihilating `H^i_Z(A)` for
`i ≤ n`; that power-torsion property transfers to `M`, degree by degree, and the exponents are
collected into a single one; the annihilator criterion then returns finiteness for `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localCohomologyWithSupportIn_finite_of_finiteLocallyFree_away
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (n : ℕ)
    (hA : ∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ n → Module.Finite A
      (localCohomologyWithSupportIn.{u, 0} A
        (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A))
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of A A)) (i : ℤ)))
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) [Module.Finite A (M : Type u)]
    (hM : ∀ f ∈ I, Module.IsFiniteLocallyFree (Localization.Away f)
      (LocalizedModule.Away f (M : Type u))) :
    ∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ n → Module.Finite A
      (localCohomologyWithSupportIn.{u, 0} A
        (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A))
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj M) (i : ℤ))

declarations.name: IsUnibranch
declarations.doc:
A local ring is unibranch if its reduction is a domain and the integral closure of its
reduction in its field of fractions is local.
declarations.statement: def IsUnibranch (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] : Prop

declarations.name: IsGeometricallyUnibranch
declarations.doc:
A local ring is geometrically unibranch if it is unibranch and the residue field of the
normalization of its reduction is purely inseparable over its residue field.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def IsGeometricallyUnibranch
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] : Prop

declarations.name: isUnibranch_iff_henselization_has_unique_minimalPrime
declarations.doc: A local ring is unibranch if and only if a henselization of it has a unique minimal prime.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnibranch_iff_henselization_has_unique_minimalPrime
    (A Ah : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [CommRing Ah] [IsLocalRing Ah]
    [Algebra A Ah]
    [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) Ah] :
    IsUnibranch A ↔ ∃! p : Ideal Ah, p ∈ minimalPrimes Ah

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsUnibranchAt
declarations.doc: A scheme is unibranch at a point if its local ring there is unibranch.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsUnibranchAt
    (X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}) (x : X) : Prop
declarations.comment: unibranch at a point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsGeometricallyUnibranchAt
declarations.doc:
A scheme is geometrically unibranch at a point if its local ring there is geometrically
unibranch.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsGeometricallyUnibranchAt
    (X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}) (x : X) : Prop
declarations.comment: geometrically unibranch at a point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsUnibranch
declarations.doc: A scheme is unibranch if it is unibranch at every point.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsUnibranch
    (X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}) : Prop
declarations.comment: unibranch schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsGeometricallyUnibranch
declarations.doc: A scheme is geometrically unibranch if it is geometrically unibranch at every point.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsGeometricallyUnibranch
    (X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}) : Prop
declarations.comment: geometrically unibranch schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGeometricallyUnibranch_of_isNormal
declarations.doc: A normal scheme is geometrically unibranch.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGeometricallyUnibranch_of_isNormal {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsNormal X] : IsGeometricallyUnibranch X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGeometricallyUnibranch_iff_isConnected_puncturedSpectrum
declarations.doc:
A locally Noetherian scheme is geometrically unibranch exactly when, at every point which is
not the generic point of an irreducible component, the punctured spectrum of a strict
henselization of the local ring is connected.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyUnibranch_iff_isConnected_puncturedSpectrum
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] :
    IsGeometricallyUnibranch X ↔
      ∀ x : X, x ∉ genericPoints X →
        ∀ (κsep : Type u) [Field κsep] [Algebra (ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x)) κsep]
          [IsSepClosure (ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x)) κsep]
          (Ash : Type u) [CommRing Ash] [IsLocalRing Ash]
          [Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) Ash]
          [IsHenselization (X.presheaf.stalk x) κsep Ash],
          IsConnected ({closedPoint Ash}ᶜ : Set (PrimeSpectrum Ash))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GlueingNearPoint.glueingEquivalenceNearPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BQ5.** Finite-presentation schemes on open neighbourhoods of a
retrocompact open together with a point are equivalent, as a germ, to compatible
finite-presentation schemes on the open and on the local scheme at the point. The natural
identifications with base change intertwine the gluing comparison with the canonical
iterated-pullback comparison on the overlap.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def glueingEquivalenceNearPoint
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (U : S.Opens) (s : S)
    (hU : IsRetrocompact (U : Set S)) :
    { e : FinitePresentationGerm S U s ≌ glueingDataNearPoint S U s //
      ∃ a : (((FinitePresentationNeighborhoodModel.restrictionMorphisms
        (S := S) (U := U) (s := s)).Q ⋙ e.functor ⋙ openComponent S U s) ≅
        (neighborhoodModelToAmbient S U s ⋙ Over.pullback U.ι)),
      ∃ b : (((FinitePresentationNeighborhoodModel.restrictionMorphisms
        (S := S) (U := U) (s := s)).Q ⋙ e.functor ⋙ localComponent S U s) ≅
        (neighborhoodModelToAmbient S U s ⋙ Over.pullback (S.fromSpecStalk s))),
      overlapComparisonCompatible S U s e a b }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroupContinuousMulEquivOfIsEquivalence
declarations.doc:
If base change along `f : X ⟶ Y` is an equivalence on finite étale covers, then `f` identifies
the étale fundamental group of `X` at a geometric point `x` with the étale fundamental group of `Y`
at the image geometric point, as topological groups.
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isHomeomorph_connectedComponentsMap_of_finiteEtaleBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BQA, part (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes such that the base change functor `FÉt_Y ⥤ FÉt_X` is an equivalence of
categories. Then the induced map `π₀(X) → π₀(Y)` on spaces of connected components is a
homeomorphism.

The equivalence identifies the clopen subsets of `Y` with those of `X` by taking preimages, and
in a spectral space that lattice determines the connected components; both spaces of connected
components are profinite, so a continuous bijection between them is a homeomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isHomeomorph_connectedComponentsMap_of_finiteEtaleBaseChange {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [CompactSpace Y]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] (hf : (finiteEtaleBaseChange f).IsEquivalence) :
    IsHomeomorph f.continuous.connectedComponentsMap
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.connectedSpace_iff_of_finiteEtaleBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BQA, part (2), the "or equivalently".** Under the hypotheses of
Tag 0BQA the source is connected if and only if the target is: part (1) puts the two spaces of
connected components in bijection, and a space is connected exactly when its space of connected
components is a single point.
declarations.statement:
theorem connectedSpace_iff_of_finiteEtaleBaseChange {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y]
    (hf : (finiteEtaleBaseChange f).IsEquivalence) : ConnectedSpace X ↔ ConnectedSpace Y
declarations.comment: part (2), the source is connected iff the target is

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fundamentalGroupContinuousMulEquivOfFiniteEtaleBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BQA, part (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of connected schemes
such that the base change functor `FÉt_Y ⥤ FÉt_X` is an equivalence of categories, and let `x` be
a geometric point of `X`. Then the induced continuous homomorphism
`AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroupMap` is an isomorphism of topological groups
`π₁(X, x) ≅ π₁(Y, f ∘ x)`.

The two connectedness hypotheses are equivalent to one another whenever `X` and `Y` are
quasi-compact and quasi-separated, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.connectedSpace_iff_of_finiteEtaleBaseChange`. Combined with
`AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroupMap_finiteEtaleFiberProjection`, the recorded
identification of the underlying map says that the isomorphism intertwines the actions of the two
fundamental groups on the geometric fibre of every finite étale cover of `Y`.
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtaleBaseChange_isEquivalence_of_isThickening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BQB.** Let `X ⊆ X'` be a thickening of schemes. The functor
`FÉt_{X'} ⟶ FÉt_X`, `U' ↦ U' ×_{X'} X`, is an equivalence of categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteEtaleBaseChange_isEquivalence_of_isThickening {X X' : Scheme.{u}} (i : X ⟶ X')
    (hi : IsThickening i) : (finiteEtaleBaseChange i).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.faithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_isDominant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BQE.** Pullback of finite étale schemes along a
dominant morphism of schemes is faithful.
declarations.statement:
public lemma faithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_isDominant
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsDominant f] :
    (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback
      ((@IsFinite ⊓ @Etale) : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ⊤ f).Faithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_dense_of_noetherianSpace
declarations.doc:
Let `U` be a dense open of a scheme `X` with Noetherian underlying space, and suppose that for
every point `x` of `X` outside `U` the punctured spectrum of every strict henselization of
`𝒪_{X, x}` is connected.  Then base change of finite étale covers along `U ⟶ X` is fully
faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_dense_of_noetherianSpace
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens) [NoetherianSpace X] (hU : Dense (U : Set X))
    (hconn : ∀ x : X, x ∉ U →
      IsConnectedPuncturedStrictHenselization (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    Nonempty (finiteEtaleBaseChange U.ι).FullyFaithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_finite_irreducibleComponents
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BQG.** Let `U` be a dense open subscheme of a scheme `X` such that
every quasi-compact open of `X` has only finitely many irreducible components, and such that for
every point `x` of `X` outside `U` the punctured spectrum of every strict henselization of
`𝒪_{X, x}` is connected.  Then base change of finite étale covers along `U ⟶ X` is fully
faithful.

Faithfulness holds because a dense open inclusion is dominant (Stacks 0BQE).  For fullness, a
morphism between the restrictions to `U` of two covers `Y` and `Z` is a section over `U` of the
finite étale internal Hom scheme `Hom_X(Y, Z)`; that section extends to a section over `X`, which
is read back as a morphism of covers over `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_finite_irreducibleComponents
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens)
    (hfinite : ∀ V : X.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite)
    (hU : Dense (U : Set X))
    (hconn : ∀ x : X, x ∉ U →
      IsConnectedPuncturedStrictHenselization (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    Nonempty (finiteEtaleBaseChange U.ι).FullyFaithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.galoisToFundamentalGroup
declarations.doc:
The canonical continuous homomorphism from the absolute Galois group of the function field of
an irreducible scheme to its étale fundamental group, based at a geometric generic point.
declarations.statement:
def galoisToFundamentalGroup
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IrreducibleSpace X]
    (L Ω : Type u) [Field L] [Field Ω]
    [Algebra (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) L]
    [IsSepClosure (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) L]
    [Algebra L Ω] [Algebra (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ω]
    [IsScalarTower (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) L Ω]
    [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ω] :
    Gal(L / X.residueField (genericPoint X)) →ₜ*
      EtaleFundamentalGroup X
        ((algebraicClosureGeometricPoint
          (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ω).map
          (X.fromSpecResidueField (genericPoint X)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_opensι_of_isGeometricallyUnibranch
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an irreducible, geometrically unibranch
scheme, let `U ⊆ X` be a nonempty open subscheme and let `ū` be a geometric point of `U`. The
canonical homomorphism

```
π₁(U, ū) ⟶ π₁(X, ū)
```

of étale fundamental groups is surjective. Equivalently, every connected finite étale cover of `X`
stays connected over `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_opensι_of_isGeometricallyUnibranch
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IrreducibleSpace X] (hX : IsGeometricallyUnibranch X)
    (U : X.Opens) [Nonempty U] (x : GeometricPoint U.toScheme) :
    Function.Surjective (etaleFundamentalGroupMap U.ι x)
declarations.comment: the claim for a nonempty open subscheme, that π₁(U, ū) → π₁(X, ū) is surjective; the claim for the generic point is `surjective_galoisToFundamentalGroup_of_isGeometricallyUnibranch`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_galoisToFundamentalGroup_of_isGeometricallyUnibranch
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an irreducible, geometrically unibranch
scheme with function field `K = κ(η)` at its generic point `η`, let `L` be a separable closure of
`K` and let `Ω` be an algebraically closed algebraic extension of `K` containing `L`. The
canonical continuous homomorphism

```
Gal(L / K) = π₁(η, η̄) ⟶ π₁(X, η̄)
```

is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_galoisToFundamentalGroup_of_isGeometricallyUnibranch
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IrreducibleSpace X] (hX : IsGeometricallyUnibranch X)
    (L Ω : Type u) [Field L] [Field Ω]
    [Algebra (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) L]
    [IsSepClosure (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) L]
    [Algebra L Ω] [Algebra (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ω]
    [IsScalarTower (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) L Ω]
    [IsAlgClosed Ω] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ω] :
    Function.Surjective (galoisToFundamentalGroup X L Ω)
declarations.comment: the claim for the generic point, that the map π₁(η, η̄) → π₁(X, η̄) of Tag 0BQH is surjective; the claim for a nonempty open subscheme is `surjective_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_opensι_of_isGeometricallyUnibranch`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.unramified_normalization_iff_etale
declarations.doc:
The morphism from the relative normalization of a normal integral scheme in a dominant
morphism of integral schemes is unramified exactly when it is étale: the normalization is
irreducible and dominates the normal, hence geometrically unibranch, target.
declarations.statement:
theorem unramified_normalization_iff_etale
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsIntegral Y] [IsIntegral X] [IsNormal X]
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [IsDominant f] :
    Unramified f.fromNormalization ↔ Etale f.fromNormalization
declarations.comment: unramified iff étale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_normalization_iff_finite_etale
declarations.doc:
The morphism from a relative normalization is étale exactly when it is finite étale: it is
always integral, and an étale morphism is locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_normalization_iff_finite_etale
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] :
    Etale f.fromNormalization ↔ (IsFinite f.fromNormalization ∧ Etale f.fromNormalization)
declarations.comment: étale iff finite étale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isNormal_of_etale
declarations.doc:
The source of an étale morphism with normal target is normal, an étale morphism being
smooth.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNormal_of_etale {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [Etale f] [IsNormal Y] :
    IsNormal X
declarations.comment: normality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIntegral_of_finite_etale_connected
declarations.doc: A connected finite étale cover of a normal integral scheme is integral.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegral_of_finite_etale_connected {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    [IsIntegral X] [IsNormal X] [IsFinite f] [Etale f]
    [ConnectedSpace Y] : IsIntegral Y
declarations.comment: integrality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalizationDesc_isIso_of_finite_etale_connected
declarations.doc:
A connected finite étale cover of a normal integral scheme is canonically the
normalization of the base in the function field of the cover.
declarations.statement:
theorem normalizationDesc_isIso_of_finite_etale_connected
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    [IsIntegral X] [IsNormal X] [IsFinite f] [Etale f]
    [ConnectedSpace Y] :
    let : IsIntegral Y := isIntegral_of_finite_etale_connected f
    IsIso ((Y.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint Y) ≫ f).normalizationDesc
      (Y.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint Y)) f rfl)
declarations.comment: normalization in the function field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuotientMap_absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BQM.** Let `X` be a normal integral scheme with function field
`K = κ(η)` and let `η̄` be an algebraic geometric point over the generic point, with
algebraically closed residue field `Ω = κ(η̄)`. Let `M ⊆ Ω` be the union of the finite
subextensions of `K` in which `X` is unramified, that is `AlgebraicGeometry.maximalEtaleExtension`.
Then `M` has that defining property and is the largest subextension with it, `M/K` is Galois —
in particular `M` is separable over `K`, so it lies in a separable closure `K^sep` of `K` inside
`Ω` — and the canonical homomorphism `Gal(Ω/K) → π₁(X, η̄)` is identified with the quotient map
`Gal(Ω/K) → Gal(M/K)`: there is an isomorphism of topological groups
`π₁(X, η̄) ≃ Gal(M/K)` carrying the canonical homomorphism to restriction of automorphisms
to `M`.

No Noetherian hypothesis is needed; this is the difference between the present tag and Stacks
Tag 03VG, which the library also proves without the Noetherian hypothesis, for an algebraic
geometric point over the generic point as that tag requires
(`AlgebraicGeometry.fundamentalGroupIsoGalMaximalEtaleExtension`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuotientMap_absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup
    [IsIntegral X] [IsNormal X]
    (hs : GeometricPoint.IsAlgebraic sbar)
    (hgeneric : sbar.hom default = genericPoint X) :
    letI : Normal (X.residueField (sbar.hom default)) (maximalEtaleExtension X sbar) :=
      normal_maximalEtaleExtension X sbar hs
    (∀ L : IntermediateField (X.residueField (sbar.hom default)) sbar.residueField,
        FiniteDimensional (X.residueField (sbar.hom default)) L →
          L ≤ maximalEtaleExtension X sbar → FiniteEtaleNormalization X sbar L) ∧
      (∀ N : IntermediateField (X.residueField (sbar.hom default)) sbar.residueField,
        (∀ L : IntermediateField (X.residueField (sbar.hom default)) sbar.residueField,
            L ≤ N → FiniteDimensional (X.residueField (sbar.hom default)) L →
              FiniteEtaleNormalization X sbar L) →
          N ≤ maximalEtaleExtension X sbar) ∧
      Normal (X.residueField (sbar.hom default)) (maximalEtaleExtension X sbar) ∧
      Algebra.IsSeparable (X.residueField (sbar.hom default)) (maximalEtaleExtension X sbar) ∧
      ∃ e : AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleFundamentalGroup X sbar ≃ₜ*
          Gal(maximalEtaleExtension X sbar / X.residueField (sbar.hom default)),
        ∀ σ : Gal(sbar.residueField / X.residueField (sbar.hom default)),
          e (absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup X sbar σ) =
            AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom (maximalEtaleExtension X sbar) σ
declarations.comment: π₁(X, η̄) = Gal(M/K), with the canonical generic-point homomorphism identified with the quotient map onto Gal(M/K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_galoisToFundamentalGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BQM, surjectivity.** For a normal integral scheme `X` with function field
`K = κ(η)` at its generic point `η`, a separable closure `L` of `K` and an algebraically closed
algebraic extension `Ω` of `K` containing `L`, the canonical continuous homomorphism

```
Gal(L / K) → π₁(X, η̄)
```

is surjective. Equivalently, every connected finite étale cover of `X` stays connected over the
function field.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_galoisToFundamentalGroup
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [IsNormal X]
    (L Ω : Type u) [Field L] [Field Ω]
    [Algebra (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) L]
    [IsSepClosure (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) L]
    [Algebra L Ω] [Algebra (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ω]
    [IsScalarTower (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) L Ω]
    [IsAlgClosed Ω] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ω] :
    Function.Surjective (galoisToFundamentalGroup X L Ω)
declarations.comment: surjectivity of the generic-point map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtaleBaseChange_normalizationOfIrreducible_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BQN at the normalization of a geometrically unibranch scheme.** Let
`X` be an irreducible, geometrically unibranch scheme. Base change along the normalization
`ν : X^ν → X` is an equivalence `FÉt_X ⥤ FÉt_{X^ν}`, `V ↦ V ×_X X^ν`.

The normalization of an irreducible geometrically unibranch scheme is a universal homeomorphism
by Stacks Tag 0GIQ, and base change along a universal homeomorphism is an equivalence of
categories of finite étale covers by
`AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtaleBaseChange_isEquivalence_of_universalHomeomorphism`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteEtaleBaseChange_normalizationOfIrreducible_isEquivalence (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IrreducibleSpace X] (hX : IsGeometricallyUnibranch X) :
    (finiteEtaleBaseChange (Scheme.normalizationOfIrreducible X)).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: fullness and essential surjectivity of the base change functor `FÉt_X ⥤ FÉt_Xᵛ`, alongside faithfulness, i.e. the whole equivalence, specialised to the normalization of an irreducible geometrically unibranch scheme. No part of Tag 0BQN is reproved here. All three halves are already available for an arbitrary universal homeomorphism, unconditionally, as `AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtaleBaseChange_isEquivalence_of_universalHomeomorphism`, which also carries this tag, and whose faithfulness half is additionally isolated as `AlgebraicGeometry.faithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_universalHomeomorphism`. What this declaration adds is only that the normalization morphism of an irreducible geometrically unibranch scheme is such a universal homeomorphism, which is Tag 0GIQ, so that the equivalence becomes available at the morphism along which the source reduces Tag 0GIY

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.faithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_universalHomeomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BQN, faithfulness of the base change functor.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
universal homeomorphism. Base change along `f` is faithful on finite étale covers: two morphisms
`V₁ ⟶ V₂` of finite étale covers of `Y` whose base changes `V₁ ×_Y X ⟶ V₂ ×_Y X` agree are
equal.

A universal homeomorphism is surjective, which is all that faithfulness uses.
declarations.statement:
theorem faithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_universalHomeomorphism (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [UniversalHomeomorphism f] : (finiteEtaleBaseChange f).Faithful
declarations.comment: faithfulness of the base change functor `FÉt_Y ⥤ FÉt_X`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtaleBaseChange_isEquivalence_of_universalHomeomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Topological invariance of finite étale covers.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a universal
homeomorphism of schemes. Then base change `FÉt_Y ⥤ FÉt_X`, `V ↦ V ×_Y X`, is an equivalence of
categories.

Base change along `f` is an equivalence of small étale sites (Stacks 04DZ), and an étale
`V ⟶ Y` is finite exactly when `V ×_Y X ⟶ X` is, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_of_isFinite_pullback_snd_of_universalHomeomorphism`; so the
equivalence restricts to the finite étale covers.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteEtaleBaseChange_isEquivalence_of_universalHomeomorphism (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [UniversalHomeomorphism f] : (finiteEtaleBaseChange f).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the equivalence `FÉt_Y ⥤ FÉt_X`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fundamentalGroupContinuousMulEquivOfUniversalHomeomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Topological invariance of the étale fundamental group.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a universal
homeomorphism of connected schemes and `x` a geometric point of `X`. Then the induced continuous
homomorphism `AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroupMap f x : π₁(X, x) → π₁(Y, f ∘ x)` is an
isomorphism of topological groups.
declarations.comment: the isomorphism of fundamental groups

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafExt
declarations.doc:
**The Ext sheaves.** For objects `K`, `L` of `D(O_X)` and an integer `n`, the Ext sheaf
`SheafExt^n(K, L)` is the degree-`n` cohomology sheaf of the derived internal Hom
`RSheafHom(K, L)`, an `O_X`-module.
declarations.statement:
abbrev derivedSheafExt (K L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)) (n : ℤ) :
    StructureSheafModules Rc
declarations.comment: the definition of the Ext sheaves: SheafExt^n(K, L) is the n-th cohomology sheaf of RSheafHom(K, L), for K and L objects of D(O_X) and n an integer

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafExtFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The Ext sheaves as a bifunctor.** `SheafExt^n(-, -)` is a functor of both variables,
contravariant in the first: it is the derived internal Hom followed by the degree-`n` cohomology
sheaf.
declarations.comment: the Ext sheaves are functorial in both variables, contravariantly in the first

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafExtIsoSheafifyPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**The Ext sheaf is a sheafification.** `SheafExt^n(K, L)` is the sheaf of `O_X`-modules
associated to the presheaf of degree-`n` hypercohomology of `RSheafHom(K, L)`, whose value over
an open `U` is `Ext^n_{D(O_U)}(K|_U, L|_U)` by [Stacks, Tag 08DK].

This is [Stacks, Tag 0BKJ] — a cohomology sheaf is the sheafification of the cohomology presheaf
— read at `RSheafHom(K, L)`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedSheafExtIsoSheafifyPresheaf (K L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc))
    (n : ℤ) :
    (PresheafOfModules.sheafification (𝟙 (structureSheaf Rc).obj)).obj
        (derivedSheafExtPresheaf Rc K L n) ≅ derivedSheafExt Rc K L n
declarations.comment: the Ext sheaf is the sheafification of the presheaf of degree-n hypercohomology of RSheafHom(K, L) on the opens of X; the identification of that presheaf's values with the Ext groups Ext^n(K|_U, L|_U) is Tag 08DK and is cited, not composed in here

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.hypercohomologySpectralSequence_e₂_derivedSheafExt
declarations.doc:
**The second page of the local-to-global spectral sequence of Ext.** The hypercohomology
spectral sequence of [Stacks, Tag 0BKM] applied to `RSheafHom(K, L)` has second page

`E_2^{p, q} = H^p(X, SheafExt^q(K, L))`,

the hypercohomology of the Ext sheaves. Its abutment is `H^{p + q}(X, RSheafHom(K, L))`, which is
`Ext^{p + q}_{D(O_X)}(K, L)` by [Stacks, Tag 08DK].
declarations.statement:
theorem hypercohomologySpectralSequence_e₂_derivedSheafExt
    (K L : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y))) (p q : ℤ) :
    Nonempty ((((hypercohomologySpectralSequence Y
          (((derivedSheafHom Y.sheaf).obj (op K)).obj L)).spectralSequence.page 2).X (p, q)) ≅
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing Y).obj.obj (op ⊤))) p).obj
        ((hypercohomologySpectralSequence Y
            (((derivedSheafHom Y.sheaf).obj (op K)).obj L)).truncation.RΓ.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y)) 0).obj
            (derivedSheafExt Y.sheaf K L q))))
declarations.comment: the second page of the local-to-global spectral sequence of Ext: the Tag 0BKM hypercohomology spectral sequence of RSheafHom(K, L) has E_2^{p, q} = H^p(X, SheafExt^q(K, L)); convergence to Ext^{p+q}(K, L) is not claimed here -- the Tag 0BKM convergence clause needs a bounded below complex representing RSheafHom(K, L) and is stated of an existentially produced spectral sequence rather than of the canonical one carrying this second page, and the Ext reading of the abutment is Tag 08DK

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleNonvanishing.exists_nonzero_hypercohomology_tensorPower
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BQR].** Let `X` be a scheme, `L` an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module and `K` a
**nonzero** object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`. Then there are an exponent `n` and a degree `p` with

`H^p(X, K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} L^{⊗ n}[0]) ≠ 0`.

The tensor product is the derived tensor product of [Stacks, Tag 06YH] with the `n`-th tensor
power of `L` placed in degree zero, and the cohomology is the derived hypercohomology, the
degree-`p` homology of unbounded derived global sections. The object the conclusion is about is
`K` itself, read in the standard model of the derived category; see the implementation notes on
the two models.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_nonzero_hypercohomology_tensorPower (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : X.Modules)
    [IsInvertibleModule X L] (hL : IsAmple X L)
    (K : (@DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB X.Modules _ _
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.hasDerivedCategory X)
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory)
    (hK : ¬ IsZero K) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (p : ℤ),
      ¬ IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} p).obj
        ((derivedModuleGlobalSections
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite X.toRingedSpace.sheaf)).obj
          (((Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.derTensor X.toRingedSpace).tensor.obj
              ((Stacks.Injectives.grothendieckModelEquiv X.Modules).inverse.obj K.1)).obj
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
              ((HomologicalComplex.single (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.Modules X.sheaf)
                (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj (tensorPowModule X L (n : ℤ)))))))
declarations.comment: the general derived statement: K is an arbitrary nonzero object of D_QCoh(O_X), the tensor product is the derived one of Tag 06YH with a tensor power of L in degree zero, and the cohomology is the derived hypercohomology of Tag 08JA in degree p. The hypothesis is stated at the locally small model of D(O_X), the only model Tag 08DB is available at, and the conclusion at the standard model, the only model Tag 08JA is available at; the object in the conclusion is K itself, Stacks.Injectives.grothendieckModelEquiv being the identity on objects. The degree-zero module case, which this does not subsume because it carries an explicit witness, is the separate carrier Stacks.AmpleNonvanishingChart.exists_twistedSection_restrict_eq_tensorSection

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleNonvanishingChart.exists_twistedSection_restrict_eq_tensorSection
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BQR] for a quasi-coherent module.** For `L` an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module
and `F` a nonzero quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module there are an exponent `p`, a global section `σ` of
`L ^⊗ p` with affine nonvanishing open `U = X_σ`, a **nonzero** section `t` of `F` over `U`, and a
**nonzero** global section `τ` of `F ⊗ L ^⊗ p` with `τ|_U = t ⊗ σ|_U`.

These are the five steps of the source argument run on a module instead of on a complex: the
point with nonzero stalk, the affine chart of ampleness, the nonzero section on it, the
surjectivity half of [Stacks, Tag 01PW], and — for `τ ≠ 0` — the whiskered clause 2 of
[Stacks, Tag 01CY] in the form
`Stacks.SectionProduct.eq_zero_of_tensorSection_eq_zero`: over an open inside `X_σ` the product
with `σ` kills no section of `F`, so `τ|_U = t ⊗ σ|_U` with `t ≠ 0` forces `τ ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_twistedSection_restrict_eq_tensorSection {X : Scheme.{u}} (L : X.Modules)
    [IsInvertibleModule X L] (hL : IsAmple X L) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hF : ¬ IsZero F) :
    ∃ (p : ℕ) (σ : Γ(tensorPowModule X L (p : ℤ), ⊤)) (U : X.Opens)
      (τ : Γ(F ⊗ tensorPowModule X L (p : ℤ), ⊤)) (t : Γ(F, U)),
      U = Stacks.AmpleTheory.powNonvanishingOpen X L p σ ∧ IsAffineOpen U ∧ t ≠ 0 ∧ τ ≠ 0 ∧
        resTop U τ = tensorSection F (tensorPowModule X L (p : ℤ)) t (resTop U σ)
declarations.comment: run at a quasi-coherent module rather than at an object of D_QCoh(O_X) in a degree: Gamma(X, F tensor L^p) is nonzero, witnessed by an explicit tau. The derived-category form is a separate assertion; see the module docstring

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjKoszulComplex.acyclic_koszulComplex_and_locallyFree_koszulTerm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BQS.** Let `A` be a ring and `X = P^n_A = Proj A[X₀, …, Xₙ]`. For every integer `a`
there is an exact complex of vector bundles

`0 ⟶ 𝒪_X(a) ⟶ … ⟶ 𝒪_X(a+j)^{⊕ binom(n+1, j)} ⟶ … ⟶ 𝒪_X(a+n+1) ⟶ 0`

on `X`, namely the Koszul complex `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjKoszulComplex.koszulComplex` of
the coordinates `X₀, …, Xₙ`, graded so that the generators of the `j`-th exterior power sit in
degree `j` and twisted by `a`. Its `j`-th term is the direct sum of copies of `𝒪_X(a+j)` indexed
by the `j`-element subsets of the coordinates, of which there are `binom(n+1, j)`, and each term
is free on that index set over every standard open of a degree-one element, those opens covering
`X`; the complex is acyclic, so it is exact in every degree, and it is concentrated in degrees
`0, …, n+1` because outside that range the index set is empty.
declarations.statement:
theorem acyclic_koszulComplex_and_locallyFree_koszulTerm (j : ℕ) :
    (koszulComplex A n a).Acyclic ∧
      (koszulComplex A n a).X (j : ℤ) =
        (⨁ fun _ : koszulIndex (n + 1) (j : ℤ) =>
          twistingSheaf (polyGrading A n) (a + (j : ℤ))) ∧
      Fintype.card (koszulIndex (n + 1) (j : ℤ)) = (n + 1).choose j ∧
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → Opens (ProjectiveSpectrum.top (polyGrading A n))),
        (Opens.grothendieckTopology (ProjectiveSpectrum.top (polyGrading A n))).CoversTop U ∧
          ∀ f : I, Nonempty (SheafOfModules.free.{u} (ULift.{u} (koszulIndex (n + 1) (j : ℤ))) ≅
            (koszulTerm A n a (j : ℤ)).over (U f))

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.DerivedPushforward.conditions_of_multiplicativeClosure
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BQT]: the three conditions hold when `f` is affine, when `f` is an open
immersion, and when `f` is a composition of such.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite composite of
affine morphisms and open immersions between quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, and let
`E` be a weak generator of `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`. Then

1. every object `K` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` with `Rf_*K` zero is itself zero;
2. `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` reflects isomorphisms;
3. `Lf^*E` is a weak generator of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.

Condition (3) is
`isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_quasiCoherentDerivedPullback_of_openFactorization`, applied to the
trivial factorization `f = f ≫ 𝟙 Y`; (1) and (2) follow from it by
`tfae_isZero_quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward`, the equivalence of the three conditions.
declarations.statement:
theorem conditions_of_multiplicativeClosure {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hf : ((@IsAffineHom) ⊔ (@IsOpenImmersion) :
      MorphismProperty (Scheme.{u})).multiplicativeClosure f)
    (E : Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y)
    (hE : (ObjectProperty.singleton E).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator) :
    (∀ K : Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X,
        IsZero ((qcqsRestrictedDerivedPushforward f).obj K) → IsZero K) ∧
      (qcqsRestrictedDerivedPushforward f).ReflectsIsomorphisms ∧
      (ObjectProperty.singleton
        ((Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' f).obj E)
        ).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator
declarations.comment: the clause that the three conditions hold when f is affine, when f is an open immersion, and when f is a composition of such

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.DerivedPushforward.isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_restrictedTwistSum
declarations.doc:
For `i : W ⟶ P^n_A` an immersion with `W` quasi-compact, the object
`𝒪_W ⊕ 𝒪_W(-1) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ 𝒪_W(-n)`, placed in degree zero, generates `D_QCoh(𝒪_W)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_restrictedTwistSum [IsImmersion i] [CompactSpace W] :
    (ObjectProperty.singleton (restrictedTwistSum i)).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator
declarations.comment: the second consequence drawn from the remark: for X a quasi-compact locally closed subscheme of P^n_A, the object O_X ⊕ O_X(-1) ⊕ … ⊕ O_X(-n) is a generator for D_QCoh(O_X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.DerivedPushforward.tfae_isZero_quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BQT].** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of
schemes with `Y` quasi-compact, and let `E` be a weak generator of `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` — the object
[Stacks, Tag 09IS] provides, and the one hypothesis the source's remark carries. Then the
following are equivalent:

1. every object `K` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` with `Rf_*K` zero is itself zero;
2. `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` reflects isomorphisms;
3. `Lf^*E` is a weak generator of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.

(1) ⇒ (2): complete a morphism `α` whose image is invertible to a distinguished triangle; `Rf_*`
is exact, so it carries that triangle to a distinguished triangle whose first morphism is
`Rf_*α`, whence its third vertex `Rf_*(cone α)` is zero, whence `cone α` is zero by (1), whence
`α` is invertible. (2) ⇒ (1): if `Rf_*K` is zero then the zero endomorphism of `Rf_*K` is its
identity, so the zero endomorphism of `K` is invertible by (2) and `𝟙 K = 0`.

(1) ⇔ (3): `K` is right orthogonal to the shifts of `Lf^*E` exactly when `Rf_*K` is right
orthogonal to the shifts of `E`, by
`rightOrthogonal_shiftClosure_singleton_quasiCoherentDerivedPullback_iff`, and the latter says
exactly that `Rf_*K` is zero because `E` generates.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_isZero_quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward
    (E : Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y)
    (hE : (ObjectProperty.singleton E).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator) :
    [∀ K : Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X,
        IsZero ((qcqsRestrictedDerivedPushforward f).obj K) → IsZero K,
      (qcqsRestrictedDerivedPushforward f).ReflectsIsomorphisms,
      (ObjectProperty.singleton
        ((Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' f).obj E)
        ).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator].TFAE

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.DerivedPushforward.isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_quasiCoherentDerivedPullback_specMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BQT] for a morphism of affine schemes: `L(Spec φ)^*` carries a generator to a
generator.** Let `φ : R ⟶ S` be a map of commutative rings and let `E` be a weak generator of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})`. Then `L(Spec φ)^*E` is a weak generator of `D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec S})`.

This is the implication (2) ⇒ (3) of `tfae_isZero_quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward`, whose
condition (2) holds for `Spec φ` by [Stacks, Tag 08I8]; it is the source's clause that the three
conditions of the remark hold when `f` is affine, in the case of a morphism of affine
schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_quasiCoherentDerivedPullback_specMap
    (E : Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedCategory (Spec R))
    (hE : (ObjectProperty.singleton E).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator) :
    (ObjectProperty.singleton
        ((Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' (Spec.map φ)).obj E)
      ).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator
declarations.comment: the conditions hold for an affine morphism: the case of a morphism Spec φ of affine schemes, where Lf^* carries a generator to a generator

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.DerivedPushforward.isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_derivedStructureSheaf_of_isQuasiAffine
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BQT]: if `X` is a quasi-affine scheme then `𝒪_X` generates
