`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.** This is the first consequence the source draws from its remark.

A quasi-affine scheme is quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and its canonical morphism
`j : X ⟶ Spec Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` is an open immersion; the target is affine, hence quasi-compact and
quasi-separated. The remark's clause for an open immersion therefore applies to `j`, and `𝒪` is
a generator on the affine target by
`isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_derivedStructureSheaf_spec`, so `Lj^*𝒪` is a generator — and
`Lj^*𝒪` is `𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_derivedStructureSheaf_of_isQuasiAffine (X : Scheme.{u})
    [X.IsQuasiAffine] :
    (ObjectProperty.singleton (derivedStructureSheaf X)).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator
declarations.comment: the first consequence drawn from the remark: if X is a quasi-affine scheme then the structure sheaf O_X is a generator for D_QCoh(O_X)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Beilinson.beilinson_equivalence_matrixAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BQU] (Beilinson).** Let `A` be a ring, `X = P^n_A = Proj A[X₀, …, Xₙ]`,
`P = 𝒪_X ⊕ 𝒪_X(-1) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ 𝒪_X(-n)` as in Tag 0CS8, and `R = Hom_{𝒪_X}(P, P)` as in Tag 0CS9,
viewed as the differential graded algebra `Hom_{Comp^dg(𝒪_X)}(P, P)` with zero differential.
Then `- ⊗_R^𝐋 P : D(R) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is an equivalence of categories, is exact, sends `R` to
`P`, and is `A`-linear (for `A ⊂ center(R)` acting on `D(R)` and `A → Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` acting on
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`); and the ring of `R` is the upper triangular algebra of matrices over
`A[X₀, …, Xₙ]` with `(i, j)` entry homogeneous of degree `j - i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem beilinson_equivalence_matrixAlgebra :
    ((tensorWithGenerator A n).IsEquivalence ∧ (tensorWithGenerator A n).IsTriangulated ∧
      Nonempty ((tensorWithGenerator A n).obj (regular A n) ≅ twistSumQCoh A n) ∧
      letI := derivedCategoryRLinear A n
      letI := quasiCoherentDerivedCategoryLinear A n
      (tensorWithGenerator A n).Linear A) ∧
      Nonempty ((endAlgebra A n).A ≃+* endomorphismMatrices A n)
declarations.comment: Beilinson's equivalence - ⊗_R^L P : D(R) → D_QCoh(O_X) on X = P^n_A, with P = O_X ⊕ O_X(-1) ⊕ ... ⊕ O_X(-n) of Tag 0CS8 and R = Hom_{O_X}(P, P) of Tag 0CS9 read as the differential graded algebra Hom^dg(P, P) with zero differential: an equivalence, exact, A-linear, sending R to P, with the ring of R identified with the upper triangular matrix algebra of Tag 0CS9 by endAlgebraRingEquivMatrices

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.normalSheafToSheafExtOne
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map `c` of [Stacks, Tag 0BQW].** The normal sheaf
`𝒩 = 𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(ℐ/ℐ², 𝒪_X)` maps canonically to `𝓔xt¹_{𝒪_Y}(𝒪_X, 𝒪_X)`: precompose with
`ℐ ↠ ℐ/ℐ²` to land in `𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(ℐ, 𝒪_X)`, identify that with the degree-zero cohomology of
`𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(ℐ, J)` for the injective resolution `J` of `𝒪_X` that the derived functor uses, and
take the degree-one connecting map of `sheafHomComplexSequence`. On a local section of `𝒩` this
is the class of the pushout of the second-order thickening sequence of [Stacks, Tag 0BQX] along
it, which is how the source constructs `c`.
declarations.comment: the canonical map `c` itself; `isIso_normalSheafToSheafExtOne` is the assertion that it is an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isIso_normalSheafToSheafExtOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BQW.** Let `Y` be a ringed space, let `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_Y` be a sheaf of
ideals, put `𝒪_X = 𝒪_Y/ℐ` and let `𝒩 = 𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(ℐ/ℐ², 𝒪_X)` be the normal sheaf. The
canonical map `c : 𝒩 ⟶ 𝓔xt¹_{𝒪_Y}(𝒪_X, 𝒪_X)` of `normalSheafToSheafExtOne` is an
isomorphism.

All four inputs of the source's proof are proved here:
`isIso_internalHomMapLeft_cokernelπ_idealSquareInclusion` (every `𝒪_Y`-linear map
`ℐ ⟶ 𝒪_X` factors uniquely through `ℐ/ℐ²`), `internalHomMapLeft_ι_app_quotient_eq_zero`
(the degree-zero map vanishes, because `ℐ` annihilates `𝒪_X`),
`sheafHomComplexSequence_shortExact` ([Stacks, Tag 01DR] for sheaves of modules) and
`Stacks.RingedSpace.isZero_sheafExt_unit_succ` (`𝓔xt¹_{𝒪_Y}(𝒪_Y, 𝒪_X) = 0`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_normalSheafToSheafExtOne :
    IsIso (normalSheafToSheafExtOne Y I)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.secondOrderThickening_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BQX.** For an ideal sheaf `I` on a ringed space, the canonical
sequence
`0 ⟶ I / I² ⟶ 𝒪_Y / I² ⟶ 𝒪_Y / I ⟶ 0`
is short exact. The displayed equations say that its arrows are induced by the inclusion
`I ⟶ 𝒪_Y` and the identity of `𝒪_Y`, respectively.
declarations.statement:
public theorem secondOrderThickening_shortExact (Y : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (I : (SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing Y)).Submodule) :
    let I2 := idealSquare Y I
    ∃ (j : I2.toSheafOfModules ⟶ I.toSheafOfModules)
      (_hj : j ≫ I.ι = I2.ι)
      (f : cokernel j ⟶ cokernel I2.ι)
      (g : cokernel I2.ι ⟶ cokernel I.ι)
      (hzero : f ≫ g = 0),
      (cokernel.π j ≫ f = I.ι ≫ cokernel.π I2.ι) ∧
        (cokernel.π I2.ι ≫ g = cokernel.π I.ι) ∧
          (ShortComplex.mk f g hzero).ShortExact

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isIso_desc_app_isKoszulRegularIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
Let `Y` be a ringed space, `𝓘 ⊆ O_Y` a Koszul-regular sheaf of ideals and `O_X = O_Y/𝓘`.
Let `A` be, with its degree-one generator `ι`, the exterior algebra over `O_X` of
`Ext¹_{O_Y}(O_X, O_X)`.  Then the homomorphism of sheaves of graded algebras that the identity of
`Ext¹_{O_Y}(O_X, O_X)` induces out of `A` — the comparison

`⋀ⁿ(Ext¹_{O_Y}(O_X, O_X)) ⟶ Extⁿ_{O_Y}(O_X, O_X)`

that composition makes — is an isomorphism in every degree `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_desc_app_isKoszulRegularIdealSheaf (hJ : IsKoszulRegularIdealSheaf Y J)
    (A : _root_.SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.{u, u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} (quotientRingSheaf.{u, u, u} J)))
    (ι : (koszulRegularSelfExtAlgebra J hJ).piece 1 ⟶ A.piece 1)
    (hA : _root_.SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.IsExteriorAlgebra A ι) (n : ℤ) :
    IsIso ((hA.desc (koszulRegularSelfExtAlgebra J hJ)
      (𝟙 ((koszulRegularSelfExtAlgebra J hJ).piece 1))
      (squareZero_id_koszulRegularSelfExtAlgebra J hJ)).app n)

declarations.name: Stacks.RegularSequence.KoszulChainData.isZero_derivedSheafExt_unit_of_notMem_Icc
declarations.doc:
**The Ext sheaves of a Koszul-regular quotient into the structure sheaf vanish outside the
degrees `0, …, r`.** For an ideal sheaf `ℐ ⊂ O_Y` generated by a Koszul-regular sequence of `r`
global sections, with quotient `O_X = O_Y/ℐ`,

`𝓔xt^n_{O_Y}(O_X, O_Y) = 0` for `n < 0` and for `n > r`.

This is part of the vanishing half of [Stacks, Tag 0BQZ], whose conclusion
`R𝓗om_{O_Y}(O_X, O_Y) = ⋀^r 𝒩 [-r]` says that these Ext sheaves vanish in every degree other
than `r` and that the `r`-th one is the top exterior power of the normal sheaf. The degrees
`0, …, r - 1` and the degree `r` itself are not treated: they are where the differential of the
Hom complex, which is not zero, has to be computed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_derivedSheafExt_unit_of_notMem_Icc (K : KoszulChainData.{u, u, u} A φ)
    [QuasiIso K.augmentation] {n : ℤ} (hn : n < 0 ∨ (r : ℤ) < n) :
    IsZero (derivedSheafExt Rc
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        ((single (StructureSheafModules Rc) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj
          (quotient Rc (φ := φ))))
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (unitSingleComplex Rc)) n)
declarations.comment: ONLY the degrees outside `0, …, r` of the vanishing half of the tag: the Ext sheaves `Ext^i_{O_Y}(O_Y/I, O_Y)` are zero for `i < 0` and for `i > r`. Carried: the ideal sheaf is presented GLOBALLY by a Koszul-regular sequence of `r` sections -- a Koszul chain datum for `φ : (O_Y)^r ⟶ O_Y` whose augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism -- where the tag assumes only the local condition that `I` be Koszul-regular, so the opening reduction of its proof is not performed and the tag's locally varying `r` is here constant. NOT covered: the degrees `0, …, r - 1`, the identification of `Ext^r` with the top exterior power of the normal sheaf, and the derived-category isomorphism `RHom(O_X, O_Y) = (top exterior power of N)[-r]`

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.nonempty_derivedSheafHom_iso_rankExterior
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BQZ.** Let `Y` be a ringed space, `𝓘 ⊆ O_Y` a sheaf of ideals,
`O_X = O_Y/𝓘` and `𝒩 = 𝓗om_{O_Y}(𝓘/𝓘², O_X)`. If `𝓘` is Koszul-regular, then

`R𝓗om_{O_Y}(O_X, O_Y) ≅ ⋀^r 𝒩 [-r]`

in `D(O_Y)`, where `r : Y → ℕ` sends `y` to the minimal number of generators of `𝓘` needed in a
neighbourhood of `y` (`localGeneratorCount`). The right-hand side is the complex with zero
differential whose degree-`n` term is the `n`-th exterior power of `𝒩` over `O_X` (the exterior
algebra `SheafOfModules.algebras` of `normalSheafQuotient`) on the locus where `r = n`, extended
by zero (`rankExteriorTerm`): `r` is locally constant on the support of `O_X`, and every term of
the formula vanishes off it. See the module docstring for the codomain of `r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_derivedSheafHom_iso_rankExterior (hJ : IsKoszulRegularIdealSheaf Y J) :
    Nonempty (((derivedSheafHom Y.sheaf).obj (op (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        ((single (StructureSheafModules Y.sheaf) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj (cokernel J.ι))))).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((single (StructureSheafModules Y.sheaf) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj
          (_root_.SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheaf Y.sheaf)))) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj (CochainComplex.zeroDifferentialComplex (rankExteriorTerm (J := J)
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.algebras (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y.carrier)
          (normalSheafQuotient J)).exterior)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.KoszulRegular.nonempty_normalExteriorComplex_iso_rightAdjoint_structureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BR0.** Let `Y` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let
`i : X ⟶ Y` be a Koszul-regular closed immersion, and let `a` be the right adjoint of
`Ri_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` of [Stacks, Tag 0A9E]. Then there is an isomorphism

`⋀^r 𝒩 [-r] ≅ a(𝒪_Y)`,

where `𝒩 = 𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(𝒞_{X/Y}, 𝒪_X)` is the normal sheaf of `i` (`Stacks.Divisors.normalSheaf`)
and `r` is its rank, a locally constant function on `X` (`normalRank`). Since `r` is only locally
constant, `⋀^r 𝒩 [-r]` is the complex with zero differential whose degree-`n` term is `⋀ⁿ𝒩` on
the open and closed locus where `r = n`, extended by zero (`normalExteriorComplex`): on that locus
it is `⋀ⁿ𝒩[-n]`.

The right adjoint `a` is quantified over together with its adjunction, which determines it up to
unique isomorphism; the derived categories are the locally small models
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.hasDerivedCategory`, at which [Stacks, Tag 0A9E] produces `a`.
The isomorphism is one of objects of `D(𝒪_X)`; `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` being a full subcategory, it is an
isomorphism there.

The proof is the source's. By [Stacks, Tags 0A9X and 0A77], `a(𝒪_Y)` is `R ℰom(𝒪_X, 𝒪_Y)` and its
pushforward is `R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(i_*𝒪_X, 𝒪_Y)`, which [Stacks, Tag 0BQZ] computes: its cohomology
sheaves are `⋀ⁿ𝒩` on the locus where `r = n`, extended by zero
(`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.extIsoRankExteriorTerm`). As `i_*` is exact and fully
faithful on modules ([Stacks, Tag 08KS]), the cohomology sheaves of `a(𝒪_Y)` are the terms of
`⋀^r 𝒩 [-r]`; they are concentrated in one degree on each member of the disjoint open cover of
`X` by the rank loci, so `a(𝒪_Y)` is isomorphic to the complex of its cohomology sheaves with zero
differential (`Stacks.SheafOfModules.nonempty_iso_zeroDifferentialComplex_homology_of_cover`).
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_normalExteriorComplex_iso_rightAdjoint_structureSheaf
    [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] (hi : IsKoszulRegularImmersion i)
    (a : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y ⥤ quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)
    (adj : DerivedPushforward.qcqsRestrictedDerivedPushforward i ⊣ a) :
    Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.Q (C := X.Modules)).obj (normalExteriorComplex i hi) ≅
      (a.obj (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf Y)).obj)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chapter05.Tag_0BR1.tfae_profinite_group
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BR1**.
For a topological group `G`, the following are equivalent: `G` is profinite as a topological space;
`G` is a limit of a diagram of finite discrete topological groups; `G` is a cofiltered limit of
finite discrete topological groups.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_profinite_group (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] :
    List.TFAE
      [ IsProfiniteTop G,
        IsLimitOfFiniteDiscreteGroups G,
        IsCofilteredLimitOfFiniteDiscreteGroups G ]

registrations.name: ProfiniteGrp
registrations.comment: a profinite group

registrations.name: ProfiniteGrp.of
registrations.comment:
the profinite group attached to a compact, Hausdorff, totally disconnected
  topological group

declarations.name: normal_iff_splits_minpoly_of_adjoin_eq_top
declarations.statement:
theorem normal_iff_splits_minpoly_of_adjoin_eq_top
    {F E : Type*} [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
    {s : Set E} (hs : adjoin F s = ⊤) :
    Normal F E ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, IsAlgebraic F x ∧ ((minpoly F x).map (algebraMap F E)).Splits

declarations.name: Algebra.IsPushout.surjective_and_ker_eq_map_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a surjective ring map and let `S'` be the base change of `S` along an arbitrary
ring map `R → R'`, i.e. `R'`, `S'` complete `R`, `S` to a pushout square of `R`-algebras. Then
`R' → S'` is surjective and its kernel is the ideal of `R'` generated by the image of the kernel of
`R → S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem surjective_and_ker_eq_map_of_surjective
    {R S R' S' : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing R'] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra R R'] [Algebra R S'] [Algebra S S'] [Algebra R' S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
    [IsScalarTower R R' S'] [IsPushout R S R' S']
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R S)) :
    Function.Surjective (algebraMap R' S') ∧
      RingHom.ker (algebraMap R' S') = (RingHom.ker (algebraMap R S)).map (algebraMap R R')
declarations.comment: (3), the kernel of the base change: for a surjective ring map, the base change is surjective with kernel generated by the image of the original kernel.

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.isHomeomorph_comap_of_surjective_of_ker_le_nilradical
declarations.doc:
A surjective ring map `φ : R → S` whose kernel is locally nilpotent induces a homeomorphism
`Spec(S) → Spec(R)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeSpectrum.isHomeomorph_comap_of_surjective_of_ker_le_nilradical
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) (hsurj : Function.Surjective φ)
    (hker : RingHom.ker φ ≤ nilradical R) : IsHomeomorph (PrimeSpectrum.comap φ)
declarations.comment: (1): the homeomorphism of spectra.

declarations.name: RingHom.residueFieldMap_bijective_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
A surjective ring map `φ : R → S` induces isomorphisms on residue fields: for every prime `q`
of `S`, the map `κ(φ⁻¹ q) → κ(q)` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem RingHom.residueFieldMap_bijective_of_surjective
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) (hsurj : Function.Surjective φ)
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] :
    Function.Bijective (Ideal.ResidueField.map (q.comap φ) q φ rfl)
declarations.comment: (2): the isomorphisms on residue fields. Local nilpotence of the kernel is not needed for this; it ensures, through (1), that every prime of `R` is of the form `φ⁻¹ q`.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsPushout.surjective_and_ker_le_nilradical_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a surjective ring map with locally nilpotent kernel and let `S'` be its base
change along an arbitrary ring map `R → R'` (a pushout square of `R`-algebras). Then `R' → S'` is
surjective with locally nilpotent kernel.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.IsPushout.surjective_and_ker_le_nilradical_of_surjective
    {R S R' S' : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing R'] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra R R'] [Algebra R S'] [Algebra S S'] [Algebra R' S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
    [IsScalarTower R R' S'] [Algebra.IsPushout R S R' S']
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R S))
    (hker : RingHom.ker (algebraMap R S) ≤ nilradical R) :
    Function.Surjective (algebraMap R' S') ∧ RingHom.ker (algebraMap R' S') ≤ nilradical R'
declarations.comment: (3): the base change is surjective with locally nilpotent kernel, for an arbitrary pushout square.

declarations.name: RingHom.isHomeomorph_comap_and_residueFieldMap_bijective_and_baseChange_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
Let `φ : R → S` be a surjective ring map with locally nilpotent kernel. Then `φ` induces a
homeomorphism `Spec(S) → Spec(R)` and isomorphisms `κ(φ⁻¹ q) → κ(q)` on residue fields, and for
any ring map `R → R'` the ring map `R' → R' ⊗[R] S` is surjective with locally nilpotent
kernel.
declarations.statement:
theorem RingHom.isHomeomorph_comap_and_residueFieldMap_bijective_and_baseChange_of_surjective
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R S))
    (hker : RingHom.ker (algebraMap R S) ≤ nilradical R) :
    IsHomeomorph (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S)) ∧
      (∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime],
        Function.Bijective
          (Ideal.ResidueField.map (q.comap (algebraMap R S)) q (algebraMap R S) rfl)) ∧
      ∀ (R' : Type*) [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R'],
        Function.Surjective (algebraMap R' (R' ⊗[R] S)) ∧
          RingHom.ker (algebraMap R' (R' ⊗[R] S)) ≤ nilradical R'

declarations.name: forall_exists_pow_mem_iff_isPurelyInseparable_or_isAlgebraic_bot
declarations.doc:
Let `k'/k` be a field extension. Then every element of `k'` has a positive power lying in `k`
if and only if either `k'/k` is purely inseparable — which in characteristic zero means `k' = k` —
or `k'` has positive characteristic and is algebraic over its prime field `𝐅_p`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem forall_exists_pow_mem_iff_isPurelyInseparable_or_isAlgebraic_bot
    {k k' : Type*} [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] :
    (∀ x : k', ∃ n > 0, x ^ n ∈ (algebraMap k k').range) ↔
      IsPurelyInseparable k k' ∨
        (ringChar k' ≠ 0 ∧ Algebra.IsAlgebraic (⊥ : Subfield k') k')

declarations.name: Ideal.ResidueField.exists_pow_mem_range_map
declarations.doc:
Let `f : R →+* S` be a ring map such that every element of `S` has a positive power in the
image of `f`, let `q` be a prime of `S` and let `p = f⁻¹(q)`. Then every element of the residue
field `κ(q)` has a positive power in the image of the canonical embedding `κ(p) → κ(q)`; that is,
the induced residue field extensions satisfy the equivalent conditions of
`forall_exists_pow_mem_iff_isPurelyInseparable_or_isAlgebraic_bot`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Ideal.ResidueField.exists_pow_mem_range_map {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    {f : R →+* S} (H : ∀ x : S, ∃ n > 0, x ^ n ∈ f.range) (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal S)
    [q.IsPrime] (hpq : p = q.comap f) (x : q.ResidueField) :
    ∃ n > 0, x ^ n ∈ (Ideal.ResidueField.map p q f hpq).range
declarations.comment: The residue field extensions.

declarations.name: satisfiesGeneratingCondition_iff_structuralCondition
declarations.doc:
Let `K / k` be a field extension and `p` a prime. Then `K` is generated as a field extension
of `k` by the elements `x` admitting an `n > 0` with `x ^ p ^ n ∈ k` and `p ^ n • x ∈ k` — the
generating condition of the source — if and only if either `k = K`, or the characteristic is `p`
and `K / k` is purely inseparable, which is the source's structural condition.

The two directions are the two halves of the perfect closure: in characteristic `p` the generators
lie in the perfect closure of `k`, which is therefore all of `K`; away from `p` the multiple
`p ^ n • x` of a generator is `x` times a unit of `k`, so the generators lie in `k` already.
declarations.statement:
public theorem satisfiesGeneratingCondition_iff_structuralCondition
    {K : Type*} [Field K] (k : Subfield K) (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    Subfield.closure ((k : Set K) ∪ {x : K | ∃ n > 0, x ^ p ^ n ∈ k ∧ (p ^ n : ℕ) • x ∈ k}) = ⊤ ↔
      k = ⊤ ∨ (ringChar K = p ∧ IsPurelyInseparable k K)

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.isHomeomorph_comap_and_isPurelyInseparable_and_baseChange_of_adjoin_pow_eq_top
declarations.doc:
Let `p` be a prime number and let `φ : R → S` be a ring map whose kernel is locally nilpotent
and such that `S` is generated as an `R`-algebra by elements `x` for which there is an `n > 0` with
`x ^ p ^ n` and `p ^ n • x` in the image of `φ`. Then `Spec(S) → Spec(R)` is a homeomorphism, every
induced residue field extension `κ(𝔭) → κ(𝔮)` is either surjective or of characteristic `p` and
purely inseparable — the equivalent conditions of
`satisfiesGeneratingCondition_iff_structuralCondition` — and both hypotheses hold again for every
base change `R' → S'` of `R → S` along an arbitrary ring map `R → R'`, i.e. for every pushout
square of `R`-algebras completing `R`, `S` by `R'`, `S'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isHomeomorph_comap_and_isPurelyInseparable_and_baseChange_of_adjoin_pow_eq_top
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime)
    (hker : RingHom.ker (algebraMap R S) ≤ nilradical R)
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin R {x : S | ∃ n > 0, x ^ p ^ n ∈ (algebraMap R S).range ∧
      p ^ n • x ∈ (algebraMap R S).range} = ⊤) :
    IsHomeomorph (comap (algebraMap R S)) ∧
      (∀ (𝔭 : Ideal R) [𝔭.IsPrime] (𝔮 : Ideal S) [𝔮.IsPrime]
        (h : 𝔭 = 𝔮.comap (algebraMap R S)),
        Function.Surjective (Ideal.ResidueField.map 𝔭 𝔮 (algebraMap R S) h) ∨
          ringChar 𝔮.ResidueField = p ∧
            (Ideal.ResidueField.map 𝔭 𝔮 (algebraMap R S) h).IsPurelyInseparable) ∧
      ∀ (R' : Type u') (S' : Type v') [CommRing R'] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra S S']
        [Algebra R' S'] [Algebra R S'] [IsScalarTower R R' S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
        [Algebra.IsPushout R S R' S'],
        RingHom.ker (algebraMap R' S') ≤ nilradical R' ∧
          Algebra.adjoin R' {x : S' | ∃ n > 0, x ^ p ^ n ∈ (algebraMap R' S').range ∧
            p ^ n • x ∈ (algebraMap R' S').range} = ⊤

declarations.name: Algebra.IsPushout.injective_comap_and_residueFieldMap_isPurelyInseparable
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a ring map which induces an injective map of spectra and purely inseparable
residue field extensions, and let `S'` be the base change of `S` along an arbitrary ring map
`R → R'`, i.e. `R'`, `S'` complete `R`, `S` to a pushout square of `R`-algebras. Then `R' → S'`
also induces an injective map of spectra and purely inseparable residue field extensions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.IsPushout.injective_comap_and_residueFieldMap_isPurelyInseparable
    {R S R' S' : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing R'] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra R R'] [Algebra R S'] [Algebra S S'] [Algebra R' S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
    [IsScalarTower R R' S'] [IsPushout R S R' S']
    (hinj : Function.Injective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S)))
    (hins : ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
      (hpq : p = q.comap (algebraMap R S)),
      (Ideal.ResidueField.map p q (algebraMap R S) hpq).IsPurelyInseparable) :
    Function.Injective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R' S')) ∧
      ∀ (p' : Ideal R') [p'.IsPrime] (q' : Ideal S') [q'.IsPrime]
        (hpq : p' = q'.comap (algebraMap R' S')),
        (Ideal.ResidueField.map p' q' (algebraMap R' S') hpq).IsPurelyInseparable

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.isClosedEmbedding_comap_of_isIntegral
declarations.doc:
An integral ring map `f : R → S` whose induced map of spectra is injective induces a
homeomorphism from `Spec(S)` onto a closed subset of `Spec(R)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isClosedEmbedding_comap_of_isIntegral {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S) (hf : f.IsIntegral) (hinj : Function.Injective (comap f)) :
    Topology.IsClosedEmbedding (comap f)

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.isClosedEmbedding_comap_and_baseChange_of_injective_comap_of_isPurelyInseparable
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be an integral ring map which induces an injective map of spectra and purely
inseparable residue field extensions. Then `Spec(S) → Spec(R)` is a homeomorphism onto a closed
subset of `Spec(R)`, and for every base change `R' → S'` of `R → S` along an arbitrary ring map
`R → R'`, i.e. for every pushout square of `R`-algebras completing `R`, `S` by `R'`, `S'`, the
map `R' → S'` is again integral and again induces an injective map of spectra and purely
inseparable residue field extensions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isClosedEmbedding_comap_and_baseChange_of_injective_comap_of_isPurelyInseparable
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.IsIntegral R S]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (comap (algebraMap R S)))
    (hins : ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
      (hpq : p = q.comap (algebraMap R S)),
      (Ideal.ResidueField.map p q (algebraMap R S) hpq).IsPurelyInseparable) :
    Topology.IsClosedEmbedding (comap (algebraMap R S)) ∧
      ∀ (R' : Type u') (S' : Type v') [CommRing R'] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra S S']
        [Algebra R' S'] [Algebra R S'] [IsScalarTower R R' S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
        [Algebra.IsPushout R S R' S'],
        Algebra.IsIntegral R' S' ∧ Function.Injective (comap (algebraMap R' S')) ∧
          ∀ (p' : Ideal R') [p'.IsPrime] (q' : Ideal S') [q'.IsPrime]
            (hpq : p' = q'.comap (algebraMap R' S')),
            (Ideal.ResidueField.map p' q' (algebraMap R' S') hpq).IsPurelyInseparable

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.isHomeomorph_comap_and_baseChange_of_bijective_comap_of_isPurelyInseparable
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be an integral ring map which induces a bijective map of spectra and purely
inseparable residue field extensions. Then `Spec(S) → Spec(R)` is a homeomorphism, and for every
base change `R' → S'` of `R → S` along an arbitrary ring map `R → R'`, i.e. for every pushout
square of `R`-algebras completing `R`, `S` by `R'`, `S'`, the map `R' → S'` is again integral and
again induces a bijective map of spectra and purely inseparable residue field extensions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isHomeomorph_comap_and_baseChange_of_bijective_comap_of_isPurelyInseparable
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.IsIntegral R S]
    (hbij : Function.Bijective (comap (algebraMap R S)))
    (hins : ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
      (hpq : p = q.comap (algebraMap R S)),
      (Ideal.ResidueField.map p q (algebraMap R S) hpq).IsPurelyInseparable) :
    IsHomeomorph (comap (algebraMap R S)) ∧
      ∀ (R' : Type u') (S' : Type v') [CommRing R'] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra S S']
        [Algebra R' S'] [Algebra R S'] [IsScalarTower R R' S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
        [Algebra.IsPushout R S R' S'],
        Algebra.IsIntegral R' S' ∧ Function.Bijective (comap (algebraMap R' S')) ∧
          ∀ (p' : Ideal R') [p'.IsPrime] (q' : Ideal S') [q'.IsPrime]
            (hpq : p' = q'.comap (algebraMap R' S')),
            (Ideal.ResidueField.map p' q' (algebraMap R' S') hpq).IsPurelyInseparable

declarations.name: MulSemiringAction.exists_monic_map_eq_X_sub_C_pow_card
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BRF.** Let `φ : A → B` be a surjective `G`-equivariant ring homomorphism for a
finite group `G`.  Every `b ∈ B^G` is matched by a monic polynomial `P` over `A^G` whose image
under the restriction `A^G → B^G` of `φ` is `(X - C b) ^ |G|`.

The witness is the orbit polynomial `∏_{g ∈ G} (X - C (g • a))` of any lift `a` of `b`: its
coefficients are `G`-invariant, and each factor maps to `X - C b`, since
`φ (g • a) = g • b = b`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_monic_map_eq_X_sub_C_pow_card
    {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G]
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [MulSemiringAction G A] [MulSemiringAction G B]
    (φ : A →+*[G] B) (hφ : Function.Surjective φ)
    (b : FixedPoints.subring B G) :
    ∃ P : Polynomial (FixedPoints.subring A G), P.Monic ∧
      Polynomial.map
          ((φ : A →+* B).restrict (FixedPoints.subring A G) (FixedPoints.subring B G)
            (by
              intro a ha g
              change g • φ a = φ a
              rw [← map_smul φ, ha g])) P =
        (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C b) ^ Nat.card G

declarations.name: FixedPoints.exists_monic_polynomial_and_pow_eq_of_invariant_tensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BRG.** Invariants in `A ⊗[R^G] R` lift to monic degree-`|G|` polynomial
relations over `A`; moreover, an element in the kernel of the canonical map from `A` to those
invariants satisfies `(X - C a) ^ |G| = X ^ |G|`.

Present `A` as a quotient of `MvPolynomial A R^G`.  Base change along `R^G → R` presents
`A ⊗[R^G] R` as the corresponding quotient of `MvPolynomial A R`, whose invariant subring is
`MvPolynomial A R^G` (`fixedPolynomialEquiv`), and the kernel of the base-changed presentation
is the extension `JR` of the kernel `J` of the original one
(`baseChangePresentation_ker_eq_JRideal`).  Both assertions are therefore the corresponding
assertions of Stacks 0H35 for `J`, transported along the presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_monic_polynomial_and_pow_eq_of_invariant_tensorProduct
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    (G : Type v) [Group G] [Finite G] [MulSemiringAction G R]
    (A : Type w) [CommRing A] [Algebra (FixedPoints.subring R G) A]
    [MulSemiringAction G (A ⊗[(FixedPoints.subring R G)] R)]
    (smul_tmul : ∀ (g : G) (a : A) (r : R),
      g • (a ⊗ₜ[(FixedPoints.subring R G)] r) = a ⊗ₜ[(FixedPoints.subring R G)] (g • r)) :
    let ι : A →+* FixedPoints.subring (A ⊗[(FixedPoints.subring R G)] R) G :=
      RingHom.codRestrict
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom (R := FixedPoints.subring R G))
        (FixedPoints.subring (A ⊗[(FixedPoints.subring R G)] R) G)
        (fun a g => by
          simpa [Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom_apply] using smul_tmul g a 1)
    (∀ b : FixedPoints.subring (A ⊗[(FixedPoints.subring R G)] R) G,
      ∃ P : Polynomial A, P.Monic ∧
        Polynomial.map ι P = (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C b) ^ Nat.card G) ∧
    ∀ a : A, a ∈ RingHom.ker ι →
      (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) ^ Nat.card G =
        (Polynomial.X : Polynomial A) ^ Nat.card G

declarations.name: FixedPoints.canonicalMap_to_invariants_bijective_of_flat_and_isIntegral_isHomeomorph
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BRH.** The canonical map from a flat algebra over an invariant ring to the
invariants after extension of scalars is bijective.  In general, the map is integral, is a
homeomorphism on prime spectra, and induces purely inseparable residue field extensions.

The unconditional half follows from Stacks 0BRG: the monic witnesses generate the target over
`A`, and the kernel is nil, so
`PrimeSpectrum.isHomeomorph_comap_and_isPurelyInseparable_and_baseChange_of_adjoin_eq_top`
applies.  In the flat case `A ⊗[R^G] R → ∏_{g ∈ G} (A ⊗[R^G] R)` has `A` as the equalizer of
the two maps `r ↦ (g • r)` and `r ↦ r`, because taking equalizers commutes with a flat base
change.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalMap_to_invariants_bijective_of_flat_and_isIntegral_isHomeomorph
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    (G : Type v) [Group G] [Finite G] [MulSemiringAction G R]
    (A : Type w) [CommRing A] [Algebra (FixedPoints.subring R G) A]
    [MulSemiringAction G (A ⊗[(FixedPoints.subring R G)] R)]
    (smul_tmul : ∀ (g : G) (a : A) (r : R),
      g • (a ⊗ₜ[(FixedPoints.subring R G)] r) =
        a ⊗ₜ[(FixedPoints.subring R G)] (g • r)) :
    let ι : A →+* FixedPoints.subring (A ⊗[(FixedPoints.subring R G)] R) G :=
      RingHom.codRestrict
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom (R := FixedPoints.subring R G))
        (FixedPoints.subring (A ⊗[(FixedPoints.subring R G)] R) G)
        (fun a g => by
          simpa [Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom_apply] using smul_tmul g a 1)
    (Module.Flat (FixedPoints.subring R G) A → Function.Bijective ι) ∧
      ι.IsIntegral ∧
      IsHomeomorph (PrimeSpectrum.comap ι) ∧
      ∀ (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime]
        (q : Ideal (FixedPoints.subring (A ⊗[(FixedPoints.subring R G)] R) G)) [q.IsPrime]
        (hpq : p = q.comap ι),
        (Ideal.ResidueField.map p q ι hpq).IsPurelyInseparable

registrations.name: Ideal.IsFractionRing.normal
registrations.comment: normality, hence algebraicity, of the residue field extension

registrations.name: IsFractionRing.stabilizerHom_surjective
registrations.comment: surjectivity of the decomposition group onto the relative automorphisms

declarations.name: IsIntegralClosure.exists_smul_of_under_eq_and_residue_normal_stabilizerHom_surjective
declarations.doc:
In a possibly infinite Galois extension, the primes of an integral closure above a fixed
prime form one Galois orbit.  The induced residue-field extension is normal, and its
decomposition group surjects onto the relative automorphism group.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_smul_of_under_eq_and_residue_normal_stabilizerHom_surjective
    (A : Type uA) (K : Type uK) (L : Type uL) (B : Type uB)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Field K] [Field L]
    [Algebra A K] [Algebra B L] [IsFractionRing A K] [IsFractionRing B L]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra K L] [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    [IsScalarTower A B L] [IsIntegrallyClosed A] [IsIntegralClosure B A L]
    [IsGalois K L] :
    letI := IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K L B
    letI : SMulCommClass Gal(L/K) A B :=
      ⟨fun σ a b ↦ by
        simp only [Algebra.smul_def, smul_mul']
        congr 1
        exact (galRestrict A K L B σ).commutes a⟩
    (∀ (Q Q' : Ideal B) [Q.IsPrime] [Q'.IsPrime],
      Q.under A = Q'.under A → ∃ σ : Gal(L/K), Q' = σ • Q) ∧
    ∀ (P : Ideal A) (Q : Ideal B) [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver P],
      ∀ (k l : Type*) [Field k] [Field l] [Algebra k l]
        [Algebra (A ⧸ P) k] [IsFractionRing (A ⧸ P) k]
        [Algebra (B ⧸ Q) l] [IsFractionRing (B ⧸ Q) l]
        [Algebra (A ⧸ P) l] [IsScalarTower (A ⧸ P) (B ⧸ Q) l]
        [IsScalarTower (A ⧸ P) k l],
        Normal k l ∧
          Function.Surjective (IsFractionRing.stabilizerHom Gal(L/K) P Q k l)

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.ramificationIdx_and_inertiaDeg_tower
declarations.doc:
Ramification indices and residue degrees multiply in a tower of extensions
of discrete valuation rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem ramificationIdx_and_inertiaDeg_tower
    (A B C : Type*)
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsDiscreteValuationRing B]
    [CommRing C] [IsDomain C] [IsDiscreteValuationRing C]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
    [FaithfulSMul A B] [FaithfulSMul B C]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap B C)] :
    (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal C).ramificationIdx A =
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B).ramificationIdx A *
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal C).ramificationIdx B ∧
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal C).inertiaDeg A =
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B).inertiaDeg A *
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal C).inertiaDeg B

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.formallySmooth_localizations_of_ramificationIndex_dvd
declarations.doc:
**Abhyankar's lemma.** A tamely ramified extension of discrete valuation rings becomes
formally smooth at every local factor after a finite fraction-field extension whose local
ramification index is divisible by the original one.
declarations.statement:
theorem formallySmooth_localizations_of_ramificationIndex_dvd
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) (K : Type w) (L : Type x) (K₁ : Type y)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Field K] [Field L] [Field K₁]
    [IsDomain A] [IsDomain B] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing B]
    [Algebra A B] [IsExtension A B]
    [Algebra A K] [Algebra A L] [Algebra B L] [Algebra K L] [Algebra K K₁]
    [Algebra A K₁]
    [IsScalarTower A B L] [IsScalarTower A K L] [IsScalarTower A K K₁]
    [IsFractionRing A K] [IsFractionRing B L] [Module.Finite K K₁]
    (htame : ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) = 0 ∨
      Nat.Coprime (ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A))
          (ramificationIndex A B) ∧
        Algebra.IsSeparableExtension (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
          (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B)) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (E : Fin n → Type (max u v w x y))
      (_ : ∀ i, Field (E i))
      (_ : ∀ i, Algebra K (E i))
      (_ : ∀ i, Algebra L (E i))
      (_ : ∀ i, Algebra K₁ (E i))
      (_ : ∀ i, Algebra B (E i))
      (_ : ∀ i, IsScalarTower K L (E i))
      (_ : ∀ i, IsScalarTower K K₁ (E i))
      (_ : ∀ i, Module.Finite L (E i))
      (decomp : ((L ⊗[K] K₁) ⧸ nilradical (L ⊗[K] K₁)) ≃ₐ[K] ∀ i, E i),
      0 < n ∧
      (∀ i (z : L),
        decomp (Ideal.Quotient.mk _
          ((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft : L →ₐ[K] L ⊗[K] K₁) z)) i =
          algebraMap L (E i) z) ∧
      (∀ i (z : K₁),
        decomp (Ideal.Quotient.mk _
          ((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : K₁ →ₐ[K] L ⊗[K] K₁) z)) i =
          algebraMap K₁ (E i) z) ∧
      (∀ i (z : B), algebraMap B (E i) z =
        algebraMap L (E i) (algebraMap B L z)) ∧
      ∀ i, let A₁ := integralClosure A K₁
        let B₁ := integralClosure B (E i)
        ∃ f : A₁ →+* B₁,
          (∀ z : A₁, ((f z : B₁) : E i) =
            algebraMap K₁ (E i) ((z : A₁) : K₁)) ∧
          (∀ z : A, f (algebraMap A A₁ z) =
            algebraMap B B₁ (algebraMap A B z)) ∧
          ∀ p : Ideal A₁, p.IsMaximal →
            ramificationIndex A B ∣ p.ramificationIdx A →
            ∀ q : Ideal B₁, q.IsMaximal → q.comap f = p →
              ∃ (_ : q.IsPrime) (_ : p.IsPrime),
                (∃ _ : IsDomain (Localization p.primeCompl),
                  IsDiscreteValuationRing (Localization p.primeCompl)) ∧
                (∃ _ : IsDomain (Localization q.primeCompl),
                  IsDiscreteValuationRing (Localization q.primeCompl)) ∧
                ∃ φ : Localization p.primeCompl →+* Localization q.primeCompl,
                  Function.Injective φ ∧ IsLocalHom φ ∧
                    (∀ z : A₁, φ (algebraMap A₁ _ z) =
                      algebraMap B₁ _ (f z)) ∧
                    RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic φ
                      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization q.primeCompl))

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.exists_isSeparableSolution_of_exists_isSolution
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be an extension of discrete valuation rings with separable fraction-field
extension `L/K`. If `B` is Nagata and there is a solution for `A → B`, then there is a
separable solution for `A → B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSeparableSolution_of_exists_isSolution
    (A : Type uA) (B : Type uB) (K : Type uK) (L : Type uL)
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsDiscreteValuationRing B]
    [Field K] [Field L]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A K] [Algebra A L] [Algebra B L] [Algebra K L]
    [IsScalarTower A B L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    [IsExtension A B]
    [IsFractionRing A K] [IsFractionRing B L]
    (hsep : Algebra.IsSeparableExtension K L)
    (hB : IsNagataRing B)
    (hsolution :
      ∃ (K₂ : Type uE) (_ : Field K₂) (_ : Algebra K K₂) (_ : Algebra A K₂)
      (_ : IsScalarTower A K K₂) (_ : Module.Finite K K₂),
      ∃ D₂ : IntegralClosureBaseChange.{uA, uB, uK, uL, uE,
          max uL uE, uE, max uL uE} A B K L K₂,
        D₂.IsSolution.{uA, uB, uK, uL, uE,
          max uL uE, uE, max uL uE, max uL uE}) :
    ∃ (K₁ : Type uE) (_ : Field K₁) (_ : Algebra K K₁) (_ : Algebra A K₁)
      (_ : IsScalarTower A K K₁) (_ : Module.Finite K K₁),
      ∃ D₁ : IntegralClosureBaseChange.{uA, uB, uK, uL, uE,
          max uL uE, uE, max uL uE} A B K L K₁,
        D₁.IsSeparableSolution.{uA, uB, uK, uL, uE,
          max uL uE, uE, max uL uE, max uL uE}

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.exists_isSeparableSolution_of_essFiniteType
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be an extension of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields `K ⊂ L` such that
`B` is essentially of finite type over `A`, `A` or `B` is a Nagata ring, and `L / K` is separable.
Then there exists a separable solution for `A → B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSeparableSolution_of_essFiniteType
    (A : Type uA) (B : Type uB) (K : Type uK) (L : Type uL)
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsDiscreteValuationRing B]
    [Field K] [Field L]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A K] [Algebra A L] [Algebra B L] [Algebra K L]
    [IsScalarTower A B L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    [IsExtension A B]
    [IsFractionRing A K] [IsFractionRing B L]
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType A B]
    (hNagata : IsNagataRing A ∨ IsNagataRing B)
    (hsep : Algebra.IsSeparableExtension K L) :
    ∃ (K₁ : Type uK) (_ : Field K₁) (_ : Algebra K K₁) (_ : Algebra A K₁)
      (_ : IsScalarTower A K K₁) (_ : Module.Finite K K₁),
      ∃ D₁ : IntegralClosureBaseChange.{uA, uB, uK, uL, uK,
          max uL uK, uK, max uL uK} A B K L K₁,
        D₁.IsSeparableSolution.{uA, uB, uK, uL, uK,
          max uL uK, uK, max uL uK, max uL uK}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteExtension_smoothAt_genericPoints_fiber_normalization_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BRQ (variant of the reduced fibre theorem over curves), corrected:
the source omits quasi-compactness, and the statement is false without it.**  Let `f : X ⟶ S` be
flat and of finite type with `X` quasi-compact.  Assume `S` is Nagata, integral with function
field `K`, and regular of dimension `1`.  Then there is a finite extension `L / K` such that, with
`T` the normalization of `S` in `Spec L` (`(S.genericExtensionHom L).normalization`, Tag 035H) and
`ν : Y ⟶ X ×_S T` the normalization, the morphism `g = ν ≫ pr₂ : Y ⟶ T` is smooth at every
generic point of every fibre.

The finiteness witness `hW` is the one the normalization of a scheme takes as an argument; it is a
theorem here (`X ×_S T` is locally Noetherian), not a hypothesis.

**Correction.**  The source states the lemma for arbitrary `S`, and its proof begins "choose a
finite affine open covering of `S`".  Without quasi-compactness the statement is false: this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.not_forall_exists_finiteExtension_smoothAt_genericPoints_fiber_normalization`,
the negation of the statement exactly as the source writes it, in the vocabulary of this theorem.
There `S` is the affine line over a field `k` with infinitely many origins (countably many copies
of `Spec k[t]` glued along `Spec k[t, t⁻¹]`), integral, regular of dimension one and Nagata but not
quasi-compact, and `X` is glued from countably many copies of the plane `Spec k[x, y]` along the
torus `Spec k[x, t, (xt)⁻¹]`, the `n`-th copy lying over the `n`-th copy of the line by
`t = x ^ (n + 1) y`; `f` is flat, affine and of finite type.  Over the `n`-th origin the fibre
contains the line `x = 0` with multiplicity `n + 1`, and smoothness of `g` at the generic points
of the fibres over the points of `T` above it forces `n + 1 ≤ [L : K]`; no `L` serves every `n`.
Quasi-compactness of `S` repairs the statement, and it is enough that `X` be quasi-compact, since
then only the finitely many affine opens of `S` covering the image of `X` matter; with `S`
quasi-compact this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteExtension_smoothAt_genericPoints_normalization_of_compactSpace`.

The proof is the source's: cover the image of `X` by finitely many affine opens `Spec A_i` with
`A_i` a Nagata Dedekind domain with fraction field `K`, apply Tag 09IL
(`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteExtension_smoothAt_genericPoints_fiber_normalization_pullback`)
over each, and take `L` dominating the resulting extensions; this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteExtension_smoothAt_normalization_of_forall_affine`
with the trivial property.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteExtension_smoothAt_genericPoints_fiber_normalization_of_isRegular
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [CompactSpace X] [IsIntegral S] (hN : IsNagataScheme S) (hR : IsRegular S)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim S = 1) :
    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra S.functionField L)
      (_ : FiniteDimensional S.functionField L),
      ∃ hW : ∀ V : (pullback f (S.genericExtensionHom L).fromNormalization : Scheme.{u}).Opens,
        IsCompact (V : Set (pullback f (S.genericExtensionHom L).fromNormalization :
          Scheme.{u})) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite,
      ∀ b : (S.genericExtensionHom L).normalization,
      ∀ y : (Scheme.normalization _ hW ≫
        pullback.snd f (S.genericExtensionHom L).fromNormalization).fiber b,
      y ∈ genericPoints ↥((Scheme.normalization _ hW ≫
        pullback.snd f (S.genericExtensionHom L).fromNormalization).fiber b) →
      InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt (Scheme.normalization _ hW ≫
          pullback.snd f (S.genericExtensionHom L).fromNormalization)
        ((Scheme.normalization _ hW ≫
          pullback.snd f (S.genericExtensionHom L).fromNormalization).fiberι b y)
declarations.comment: corrected statement: the source omits quasi-compactness and is false without it (`not_forall_exists_finiteExtension_smoothAt_genericPoints_fiber_normalization`); stated here with `X` quasi-compact, which is implied by `S` quasi-compact (see the `_of_compactSpace` corollary)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteSeparableExtension_smoothAt_genericPoints_fiber_normalization_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BRR (the reduced fibre theorem with a separable extension).**  Let `A`
be a Dedekind domain with fraction field `K` and let `f : X ⟶ Spec A` be flat, quasi-compact and
locally of finite type.  Assume `A` is a Nagata ring and that for every generic point `η` of an
irreducible component of `X` the residue field `κ(η)` is a separable extension of `K`.  Then there
is a finite separable extension `L / K` such that, with `B` the integral closure of `A` in `L`,
the normalization `Y` of `X ×_{Spec A} Spec B` is smooth over `Spec B` at every generic point of
every one of the fibres of `Y ⟶ Spec B`.

The separability hypothesis is stated over the residue field of `Spec A` at `f η`, through the
residue field map of `f`: since `f` is flat, `f η` is the generic point of `Spec A`, whose residue
field is the fraction field `K`, so this is the separability of `κ(η) / K` of the source, for the
notion of separability of Tag 030O which does not require `κ(η) / K` to be algebraic.

The fraction field is allowed its own universe: the statement is the one in the scheme's universe
transported along the `A`-algebra isomorphism `K ≃ₐ[A] FractionRing A`, as for Tag 09IL.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteSeparableExtension_smoothAt_genericPoints_fiber_normalization_pullback
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsDedekindDomain A] (K : Type v) [Field K]
    [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] (hA : IsNagataRing A) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (hsep : ∀ x : X, x ∈ genericPoints X →
      letI : Algebra ((Spec (.of A)).residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x) :=
        (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
      Algebra.IsSeparableExtension ((Spec (.of A)).residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x)) :
    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra K L) (_ : FiniteDimensional K L)
      (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L) (_ : Algebra A L) (_ : IsScalarTower A K L),
      ∃ hW : ∀ U : (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap A ↥(integralClosure A L)))) : Scheme.{u}).Opens,
        IsCompact (U : Set (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap A ↥(integralClosure A L)))) : Scheme.{u})) →
        (irreducibleComponents U).Finite,
      ∀ b : Spec (.of ↥(integralClosure A L)),
      ∀ y : (Scheme.normalization _ hW ≫ pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
        (algebraMap A ↥(integralClosure A L))))).fiber b,
      y ∈ genericPoints ↥((Scheme.normalization _ hW ≫ pullback.snd f (Spec.map
        (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A ↥(integralClosure A L))))).fiber b) →
      InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt (Scheme.normalization _ hW ≫ pullback.snd f
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A ↥(integralClosure A L)))))
        ((Scheme.normalization _ hW ≫ pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap A ↥(integralClosure A L))))).fiberι b y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteSeparableExtension_smoothAt_genericPoints_fiber_normalization_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BRS (variant with separable extensions over curves), corrected: the
source omits quasi-compactness, and the statement is false without it.**  Let `f : X ⟶ S` be
flat and of finite type with `X` quasi-compact.  Assume `S` is Nagata, integral with function
field `K`, and regular of dimension `1`, and that the field extension `κ(η) / K` is separable for
every generic point `η` of an irreducible component of `X`.  Then there is a finite separable
extension `L / K` such that, with `T` the normalization of `S` in `Spec L`
(`(S.genericExtensionHom L).normalization`) and `ν : Y ⟶ X ×_S T` the normalization, the
morphism `g = ν ≫ pr₂ : Y ⟶ T` is smooth at every generic point of every fibre.

The separability hypothesis is that of `κ(η)` over `κ(f η)`; flatness puts `f η` at the generic
point of `S`, whose residue field is `K`.  The finiteness witness `hW` is the argument the
normalization of a scheme takes; it is a theorem (`X ×_S T` is locally Noetherian), not a
hypothesis.

**Correction.**  The source's proof is that of Tag 0BRQ, which begins with a finite affine open
covering of `S`; without quasi-compactness the statement is false: this is
`not_forall_exists_finiteSeparableExtension_smoothAt_genericPoints_fiber_normalization`, the
negation of the statement exactly as the source writes it, in the vocabulary of this theorem.
The counterexample is that of Tag 0BRQ
(`AlgebraicGeometry.not_forall_exists_finiteExtension_smoothAt_genericPoints_fiber_normalization`)
over `ℚ`, where the separability hypothesis holds because every extension of a field of
characteristic zero is separable, and the conclusion of Tag 0BRS contains that of Tag 0BRQ.
Quasi-compactness of `X` repairs the statement (only the finitely many affine opens covering the
image of `X` matter), and it is implied by that of `S`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteSeparableExtension_smoothAt_genericPoints_normalization_of_\
compactSpace`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteSeparableExtension_smoothAt_genericPoints_fiber_normalization_of_isRegular
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [CompactSpace X] [IsIntegral S] (hN : IsNagataScheme S) (hR : IsRegular S)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim S = 1)
    (hsep : ∀ x : X, x ∈ genericPoints X →
      letI : Algebra (S.residueField (f.base x)) (X.residueField x) :=
        (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
      Algebra.IsSeparableExtension (S.residueField (f.base x)) (X.residueField x)) :
    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra S.functionField L)
      (_ : FiniteDimensional S.functionField L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable S.functionField L),
      ∃ hW : ∀ V : (pullback f (S.genericExtensionHom L).fromNormalization : Scheme.{u}).Opens,
        IsCompact (V : Set (pullback f (S.genericExtensionHom L).fromNormalization :
          Scheme.{u})) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite,
      ∀ b : (S.genericExtensionHom L).normalization,
      ∀ y : (Scheme.normalization _ hW ≫
        pullback.snd f (S.genericExtensionHom L).fromNormalization).fiber b,
      y ∈ genericPoints ↥((Scheme.normalization _ hW ≫
        pullback.snd f (S.genericExtensionHom L).fromNormalization).fiber b) →
      InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt (Scheme.normalization _ hW ≫
          pullback.snd f (S.genericExtensionHom L).fromNormalization)
        ((Scheme.normalization _ hW ≫
          pullback.snd f (S.genericExtensionHom L).fromNormalization).fiberι b y)
declarations.comment: corrected statement: the source omits quasi-compactness and is false without it (`not_forall_exists_finiteSeparableExtension_smoothAt_genericPoints_fiber_normalization`); stated here with `X` quasi-compact, which is implied by `S` quasi-compact (see the `_of_compactSpace` corollary)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.singleFunctorExteriorPowerIsoRelativeDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BRT].** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme and `f : X ⟶ S` a smooth proper
morphism of relative dimension `d`, and let `a` be the right adjoint of
`Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_S)` ([Stacks, Tag 0A9E]). Then there is an isomorphism
`∧^d Ω_{X/S}[d] ≅ a(𝒪_S)` in `D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
def singleFunctorExteriorPowerIsoRelativeDualizingComplex {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian S]
    (f : X ⟶ S) (d : ℕ) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] [IsProper f] :
    haveI : CompactSpace X := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace f
    haveI : QuasiSeparatedSpace X := quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated f
    (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules (-d)).obj
        (Scheme.Modules.exteriorPower (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f) d) ≅
      (relativeDualizingComplex f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf S)).obj

registrations.name: Stacks.Duality.relativeDualizingComplexRigidityIso
registrations.comment: the rigidity isomorphism ω_{X/Y}^• ≅ c(L pr₁^* ω_{X/Y}^• ⊗ᴸ L pr₂^* ω_{X/Y}^•) of Equation 0E2R

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree
declarations.doc:
The degree of a finite locally free sheaf of constant rank on a proper scheme of
dimension at most one over a field.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def curveDegree (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
    (_hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (E : X.Modules) (rank : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E rank] : ℤ
declarations.comment: the degree formula

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree_eq_chowDegree_firstChernCapOnCycles_fundamental
declarations.doc:
**Equation [Stacks, Tag 0BRY]**, in the orientation of the source:
`deg(ℰ) = deg(c₁(ℰ) ∩ [X]_1)` for `ℰ` finite locally free of constant rank on a proper scheme of
dimension at most one over a field, with `c₁(ℰ) ∩ -` the operation of Stacks 02U5 at the Chern
classes of Stacks 02U0 and `deg` the degree of Stacks 0AZ1.

Two conventions are fixed here. In rank zero Stacks 02U5 defines no `c₁`; the total Chern class
of a module of rank zero is `1`, so `c₁ = 0`, and `GenuineChern.firstChernCapOnCycles` is zero
there by definition. The operation of Stacks 02U5 extends `[W] ↦ i_*(c₁(i^*ℰ) ∩ [W])` over
cycles through representatives of the classes of Stacks 02U0 (`GenuineChern.chowRep`); the choice
does not matter here, since `[X]_1` is a finite sum of fundamental cycles of one-dimensional
components and on each the class is the one of Stacks 02U0
(`GenuineChern.chernCapOnCycles_integral_cycle`).
declarations.statement:
theorem curveDegree_eq_chowDegree_firstChernCapOnCycles_fundamental
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (E : X.Modules) (r : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E r] :
    curveDegree k p hdim E r =
      chowDegree (fieldChowSituation k) (fieldChowSituation_dimensionFunction_eq_zero k) p
        (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k)
        (chowGroupCast (fieldChowSituation k) p (show (1 : ℤ) - 1 = 0 by simp)
          (GenuineChern.firstChernCapOnCycles (fieldChowSituation k) p E r 1
            (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme (fieldChowSituation k) p (𝟙 X) 1)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eulerCharacteristic_eq_chowDegree_firstChernCapOnCycles_add
declarations.doc:
**Riemann-Roch**: on a proper scheme `X` of dimension at most one over a field `k`, a finite
locally free `𝒪_X`-module `ℰ` of constant rank `r` satisfies

`χ(X, ℰ) = deg(c₁(ℰ) ∩ [X]_1) + rank(ℰ) · χ(X, 𝒪_X)`.

Here `c₁(ℰ) ∩ -` is intersection with the first Chern class of [Stacks, Tag 02U5],
`Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.firstChernCapOnCycles`: on an integral closed subscheme `i : W ⟶ X` it is
`i_*(c₁(i^*ℰ) ∩ [W])` with the class of [Stacks, Tag 02U0] read off the projective space bundle
formula, extended coefficientwise; in rank zero it is zero. It is applied to the fundamental
one-cycle `[X]_1` ([Stacks, Tag 02QU]), and `deg` is the degree of zero cycles of
[Stacks, Tag 0AZ1]. `X` is not assumed integral, reduced, or of dimension exactly one, and every
rank is covered, rank zero included. The Euler characteristics ([Stacks, Tag 0BEJ]) are taken at
the coherence of `ℰ` and of `𝒪_X` that properness over `k` provides.
declarations.statement:
theorem eulerCharacteristic_eq_chowDegree_firstChernCapOnCycles_add
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (E : X.Modules) (r : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E r] :
    letI :=
      Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CurveEulerBridge.isCoherent_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank k p E r
    letI := Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CurveEulerBridge.isCoherent_unit k p
    eulerCharacteristic k p E =
      chowDegree (fieldChowSituation k) (fieldChowSituation_dimensionFunction_eq_zero k) p
          (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k)
          (chowGroupCast (fieldChowSituation k) p (show (1 : ℤ) - 1 = 0 by simp)
            (GenuineChern.firstChernCapOnCycles (fieldChowSituation k) p E r 1
              (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme (fieldChowSituation k) p (𝟙 X) 1))) +
        (r : ℤ) * eulerCharacteristic k p (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eq_invertibleCurveDegree_of_isSelfIntersectionNumber
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BS1] and [Stacks, Tag 0BS0]**: on a proper scheme of dimension at most one
over a field, the numerical intersection number of an invertible module with the whole space is
the degree of that module,

`(𝓛 · X) = deg(𝓛)`.

The polynomial of [Stacks, Tag 0BEM] has total degree at most one, so it is determined by its
values at `0` and `1`, where the twists of `𝒪_X` are `𝒪_X` and `𝓛`; its linear coefficient is
therefore `χ(X, 𝓛) - χ(X, 𝒪_X)`, which is the degree of [Stacks, Tag 0AYR].
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_invertibleCurveDegree_of_isSelfIntersectionNumber
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L] {c : ℚ}
    (hc : IsSelfIntersectionNumber k f 1 L c) :
    c = (invertibleCurveDegree k f hdim L : ℚ)
declarations.comment: the numerical intersection number is the degree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eq_invertibleCurveDegree_of_isSelfIntersectionNumber
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BS1] and [Stacks, Tag 0BS0]**: on a proper scheme of dimension at most one
over a field, the numerical intersection number of an invertible module with the whole space is
the degree of that module,

`(𝓛 · X) = deg(𝓛)`.

The polynomial of [Stacks, Tag 0BEM] has total degree at most one, so it is determined by its
values at `0` and `1`, where the twists of `𝒪_X` are `𝒪_X` and `𝓛`; its linear coefficient is
therefore `χ(X, 𝓛) - χ(X, 𝒪_X)`, which is the degree of [Stacks, Tag 0AYR].
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_invertibleCurveDegree_of_isSelfIntersectionNumber
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L] {c : ℚ}
    (hc : IsSelfIntersectionNumber k f 1 L c) :
    c = (invertibleCurveDegree k f hdim L : ℚ)
declarations.comment: the intersection number and the degree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSelfIntersectionNumber_one_iff_of_topologicalKrullDim_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**The number of factors that [Stacks, Tag 0BEW] prescribes on a scheme of dimension one is
one.** This is the left equality `deg_𝓛(X) = (𝓛 · X)` of [Stacks, Tag 0BS1]: the degree of `X`
with respect to `𝓛` is the self-intersection number with `dim X` factors.

Ampleness of `𝓛`, which [Stacks, Tag 0BEW] assumes, is not needed: it makes the notation
`deg_𝓛(X)` defined and the integer positive, the latter being [Stacks, Tag 0B5X].
declarations.statement:
theorem isSelfIntersectionNumber_one_iff_of_topologicalKrullDim_eq_one
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L] (c : ℚ) :
    IsSelfIntersectionNumber k f ((topologicalKrullDim X).unbotD 0).toNat L c ↔
      IsSelfIntersectionNumber k f 1 L c
declarations.comment: the degree of X with respect to an invertible module

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isDualizingComplex_dualizingComplexOverField
declarations.doc:
**`ω_X^• = f^×(𝒪_{Spec k})` is a dualizing complex** on a proper scheme over a field
([Stacks, Tag 0FVV]).
declarations.statement:
theorem isDualizingComplex_dualizingComplexOverField :
    letI := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    IsDualizingComplex (dualizingComplexOverField f).obj
declarations.comment: the existence assertion: ω_X^• = f^× O_{Spec k} is a dualizing complex

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isZero_homology_dualizingComplexOverField_of_ne
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BS2], clause (1).** On a proper scheme of dimension at most one over a field,
`H^i(ω_X^•)` is nonzero only for `i = -1, 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_homology_dualizingComplexOverField_of_ne (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1)
    {i : ℤ} (hi : i ≠ -1) (hi0 : i ≠ 0) :
    IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj
      (dualizingComplexOverField f).obj)
declarations.comment: clause (1), at the constructed ω_X^• = f^× O_{Spec k}

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualizingSheafOverField_clauseTwo
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BS2], clause (2).** On a proper scheme of dimension at most one over a field,
`ω_X = H^{-1}(ω_X^•)` is a coherent Cohen--Macaulay module whose support is the union of the
irreducible components of dimension `1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingSheafOverField_clauseTwo (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent (dualizingSheafOverField f) ∧
      SheafIsCohenMacaulay X (dualizingSheafOverField f) ∧
      _root_.SheafOfModules.supp (dualizingSheafOverField f) =
        ⋃₀ {C ∈ irreducibleComponents X | topologicalKrullDim C = 1}
declarations.comment: clause (2), at the constructed ω_X = H^{-1}(f^× O_{Spec k})

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.nontrivial_stalk_homology_zero_dualizingComplexOverField_iff
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BS2], clause (3).** On a proper scheme of dimension at most one over a
field, for `x ∈ X` closed the module `H^0(ω_{X,x}^•)` is nonzero if and only if either
`dim 𝒪_{X,x} = 0`, or `dim 𝒪_{X,x} = 1` and `𝒪_{X,x}` is not Cohen--Macaulay.
declarations.statement:
theorem nontrivial_stalk_homology_zero_dualizingComplexOverField_iff
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) {x : X} (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X)) :
    letI := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    Nontrivial (moduleStalkAtPoint ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules 0).obj
        (dualizingComplexOverField f).obj) x) ↔
      ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = 0 ∨
        ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = 1 ∧
          ¬ IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)
declarations.comment: clause (3), at the constructed ω_X^• = f^× O_{Spec k}

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualizingComplexOverField_properties
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingComplexOverField_properties (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) :
    letI := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    -- `ω_X^•` is a dualizing complex
    IsDualizingComplex (dualizingComplexOverField f).obj ∧
    -- (1)
    (∀ i : ℤ, ¬ IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj
      (dualizingComplexOverField f).obj) → i = -1 ∨ i = 0) ∧
    -- (2)
    (_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent (dualizingSheafOverField f) ∧
      SheafIsCohenMacaulay X (dualizingSheafOverField f) ∧
      _root_.SheafOfModules.supp (dualizingSheafOverField f) =
        ⋃₀ {C ∈ irreducibleComponents X | topologicalKrullDim C = 1}) ∧
    -- (3)
    (∀ x : X, IsClosed ({x} : Set X) →
      (Nontrivial (moduleStalkAtPoint ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules 0).obj
          (dualizingComplexOverField f).obj) x) ↔
        ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = 0 ∨
          ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = 1 ∧
            ¬ IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x))) ∧
    -- (4): isomorphisms on `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`
    (∀ (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (i : ℤ),
      Function.Bijective (dualityLinearMap f K.obj i)) ∧
    -- (4): functoriality
    (∀ (K L : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (i : ℤ) (g : K ⟶ L)
      (α : DerivedCategory.Ext L (dualizingComplexOverField f).obj i)
      (x : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-i)).obj
        ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj K)),
      dualityLinearMap f K i (g ≫ α) x =
        dualityLinearMap f L i α
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-i)).map
            ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).map g) x)) ∧
    -- (4): compatibility with shifts
    (∀ (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (i n : ℤ)
      (α : DerivedCategory.Ext K (dualizingComplexOverField f).obj i)
      (x : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-(i + n))).obj
        ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj (K⟦n⟧))),
      dualityLinearMap f (K⟦n⟧) (i + n) (ShiftedHom.comp (𝟙 (K⟦n⟧)) α rfl) x =
        dualityLinearMap f K i α
          ((((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f ⋙
            DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) 0).shiftIso n (-(i + n)) (-i)
              (by omega)).hom.app K) x)) ∧
    -- (4): compatibility with distinguished triangles
    (∀ (T : Pretriangulated.Triangle (DerivedCategory X.Modules)) (i : ℤ)
      (α : DerivedCategory.Ext T.obj₁ (dualizingComplexOverField f).obj i)
      (x : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (-(i + 1))).obj
        ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj T.obj₃)),
      dualityLinearMap f T.obj₃ (i + 1)
          (ShiftedHom.comp (T.mor₃ : DerivedCategory.Ext T.obj₃ T.obj₁ 1) α rfl) x =
        dualityLinearMap f T.obj₁ i α
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f ⋙
            DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) 0).homologySequenceδ T (-(i + 1)) (-i)
              (by omega) x)) ∧
    -- (5)
    (∃ e : ∀ F : X.Modules, F.IsQuasicoherent →
        ((F ⟶ dualizingSheafOverField f) ≃ₗ[k] (cohomologyOverField k f F 1 →ₗ[k] k)),
      ∀ (F G : X.Modules) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) (hG : G.IsQuasicoherent) (u : F ⟶ G)
        (φ : G ⟶ dualizingSheafOverField f),
        e F hF (u ≫ φ) = (e G hG φ).comp (cohomologyOverFieldMap k f u 1).hom) ∧
    -- (6)
    (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f →
      Nonempty (dualizingSheafOverField f ≅ Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f))

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.clauseFiveAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Clause (5) of [Stacks, Tag 0BS2] at the dualizing sheaf of a proper curve**: for a
quasi-coherent `ℱ` on a proper `X` of dimension at most one over `k`,

  `Hom_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, ω_X) = Hom_k(H¹(X, ℱ), k)`.

This is `Stacks.Duality.dualityAddEquiv` at `m = 1`, followed by the comparison
`H¹(X, ℱ) = H¹(X, ℱ[0])` of `Stacks.Duality.cohomologyOverFieldIsoDerivedCohomologyOverField`.
declarations.comment: clause (5)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.clauseFiveAddEquiv_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Clause (5) of [Stacks, Tag 0BS2] is natural in the module**: precomposing a map to `ω_X`
with `u` corresponds to precomposing the functional with `H¹(X, u)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem clauseFiveAddEquiv_naturality (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ (1 : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (F G : X.Modules) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) (hG : G.IsQuasicoherent) (u : F ⟶ G)
    (φ : G ⟶ dualizingSheafOverField f) :
    clauseFiveAddEquiv f hdim F hF (u ≫ φ) =
      (clauseFiveAddEquiv f hdim G hG φ).comp (cohomologyOverFieldMap k f u 1).hom
declarations.comment: clause (5): naturality

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.homDualizingSheafAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BS2], clause (5).** For a proper `f : X ⟶ Spec k` with `X` of dimension at
most one and a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ` there is an isomorphism

  `Hom_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, ω_X) = Hom_k(H^1(X, ℱ), k)`,

where `ω_X = H^{-1}(ω_X^•)` is the dualizing sheaf. It is natural in `ℱ` by
`Stacks.Duality.homDualizingSheafAddEquiv_naturality`.
declarations.comment: clause (5)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.homDualizingSheafAddEquiv_naturality
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BS2], clause (5), is natural in `ℱ`**: the isomorphism
`Hom_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, ω_X) = Hom_k(H^1(X, ℱ), k)` turns precomposition with `g : 𝒢 ⟶ ℱ` into
precomposition with `H^1(X, g)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homDualizingSheafAddEquiv_naturality (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ (1 : WithBot ℕ∞))
    {G F : X.Modules} (hG : G.IsQuasicoherent) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) (g : G ⟶ F)
    (α : F ⟶ dualizingSheafOverField f) :
    homDualizingSheafAddEquiv f hdim G hG (g ≫ α) =
      cohomologyOverFieldMap k f g 1 ≫ homDualizingSheafAddEquiv f hdim F hF α
declarations.comment: clause (5): naturality

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_natural_linearEquiv_hom_dualizingSheafOverField
declarations.doc:
**Clause (5) of [Stacks, Tag 0BS2]** for the constructed dualizing sheaf
`ω_X = H^{-1}(f^×(𝒪_{Spec k}))`: for `X` proper of dimension at most one over `k` there are
isomorphisms of `k`-vector spaces `Hom(ℱ, ω_X) = Hom_k(H¹(X, ℱ), k)` for `ℱ` quasi-coherent,
functorial in `ℱ`. The `k`-structure on `Hom(ℱ, ω_X)` is the one `X.Modules` carries over `k`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.linearOver f`. The isomorphisms are
`Stacks.Duality.clauseFiveLinearEquiv`, and their functoriality is
`Stacks.Duality.clauseFiveAddEquiv_naturality`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_natural_linearEquiv_hom_dualizingSheafOverField [IsProper f]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ (1 : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    letI := Scheme.linearOver f
    ∃ e : ∀ F : X.Modules, F.IsQuasicoherent →
        ((F ⟶ dualizingSheafOverField f) ≃ₗ[k] (cohomologyOverField k f F 1 →ₗ[k] k)),
      ∀ (F G : X.Modules) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) (hG : G.IsQuasicoherent) (u : F ⟶ G)
        (φ : G ⟶ dualizingSheafOverField f),
        e F hF (u ≫ φ) = (e G hG φ).comp (cohomologyOverFieldMap k f u 1).hom
declarations.comment: clause (5): functorial isomorphisms of k-vector spaces Hom(F, ω_X) = Hom_k(H^1(X, F), k) for F quasi-coherent, at the constructed ω_X = H^{-1}(f^× O_{Spec k})

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.nonempty_dualizingSheafOverField_iso_relativeDifferentials
declarations.doc:
**Clause (6) of [Stacks, Tag 0BS2]**: if `f : X ⟶ Spec k` is proper and smooth of relative
dimension one, the dualizing sheaf `ω_X = H^{-1}(f^×(𝒪_{Spec k}))` is isomorphic to the sheaf of
relative differentials `Ω_{X/k}`.

The proof is that of [Stacks, Tag 0BRT] at `d = 1`; see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_dualizingSheafOverField_iso_relativeDifferentials [IsProper f]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] :
    Nonempty (dualizingSheafOverField f ≅ Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f)
declarations.comment: clause (6): ω_X ≅ Ω_{X/k} when X → Spec k is smooth of relative dimension 1, at the constructed ω_X = H^{-1}(f^× O_{Spec k})

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.extDualityAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BS2], clause (4).** For a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism
`f : X ⟶ Spec k` to the spectrum of a field and for every object `K` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` there is an
identification

  `Ext^i_X(K, ω_X^•) = Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, K), k)`,

where `ω_X^• = f^×(𝒪_{Spec k})` is the dualizing complex. It is an isomorphism of abelian groups,
and it is natural in `K` by `Stacks.Duality.extDualityAddEquiv_naturality`.

The source states this for `X` proper over `k` of dimension at most one; neither hypothesis is
used, the identification being, as the source says, a matter of the construction of `ω_X^•`.
`Stacks.Duality.extDualityAddEquivOfIsProper` is the statement at the source's own hypotheses.
declarations.comment: clause (4)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.extDualityAddEquiv_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Clause (4) of [Stacks, Tag 0BS2] is natural in `K`.** The identification
`Ext^i_X(K, ω_X^•) = Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, K), k)` turns precomposition with `g : K ⟶ L` into
postcomposition with `H^{-i}(X, g)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem extDualityAddEquiv_naturality (K L : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (i : ℤ)
    (g : K.obj ⟶ L.obj)
    (α : DerivedCategory.Ext L.obj (dualizingComplexOverField f).obj i) :
    extDualityAddEquiv f K i (g ≫ α) =
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) (-i)).map
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).map g) ≫ extDualityAddEquiv f L i α
declarations.comment: clause (4): naturality

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.extDualityAddEquiv_shift
declarations.doc:
**Clause (4) of [Stacks, Tag 0BS2]: the identifications are compatible with the shift.**
The degree-`i` identification at `K` is the degree-zero identification at `K⟦-i⟧`, transported
along the canonical isomorphisms on the two sides: the shift adjunction
`Ext^i_X(K, ω_X^•) = Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(K⟦-i⟧, ω_X^•)` on the left, and the shift comparison
`H^{-i}(X, K) = H^0(X, K⟦-i⟧)` of `Stacks.Duality.derivedCohomologyShiftNatIso` on the right.
declarations.statement:
theorem extDualityAddEquiv_shift (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (i : ℤ)
    (α : DerivedCategory.Ext K.obj (dualizingComplexOverField f).obj i) :
    extDualityAddEquiv f K i α =
      (derivedCohomologyShiftIso f K.obj (-i)).inv ≫
        dualityAddEquivZero f (shiftQuasiCoherent K (-i)) (dualityStepShift f K i α)
declarations.comment: clause (4): compatibility with the shift

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.extDualityAddEquivOfIsProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BS2], clause (4), for a proper morphism** — the situation of the source.
A proper morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so this is
`Stacks.Duality.extDualityAddEquiv`; the source's bound on the dimension of `X` plays no part in
this clause.
declarations.statement:
def extDualityAddEquivOfIsProper {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [IsProper f] (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)
    (i : ℤ) :
    DerivedCategory.Ext K.obj (dualizingComplexOverField f).obj i ≃+
      (derivedCohomologyOverField f K.obj (-i) ⟶ ModuleCat.of k k)
declarations.comment: clause (4) for a proper morphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.extDualityLinearEquiv
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BS2], clause (4), as an isomorphism of `k`-vector spaces.** For a
quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism `f : X ⟶ Spec k` and every object `K` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`,

  `Ext^i_X(K, ω_X^•) ≃ₗ[k] Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, K), k)`,

where `ω_X^• = f^×(𝒪_{Spec k})` is the dualizing complex. This is
`Stacks.Duality.extDualityAddEquiv` together with
`Stacks.Duality.extDualityAddEquiv_smul`; the `k`-structure on the left is the one `X.Modules`
carries over the base, and the `k`-linearity is what makes the identification count dimensions
over `k`.
declarations.comment: clause (4) as an isomorphism of k-vector spaces for the k-linear structure over the base, which is what makes it count dimensions over k

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isDualizingModuleOf_dualizingSheafOverField
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BS3], clause (1).** Let `X` be a proper scheme over a field `k` which is
Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension one. Then `ω_X = H^{-1}(ω_X^•)` is a dualizing
module on `X` in the sense of [Stacks, Section 0AWH]: `ω_X^• = f^×(𝒪_{Spec k})` is a dualizing
complex, `-1` is the least degree in which it has nonzero cohomology, and `ω_X` is that
cohomology sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDualizingModuleOf_dualizingSheafOverField
    (hcm : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X) (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) :
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    IsDualizingModuleOf (dualizingSheafOverField f) (dualizingComplexOverField f).obj (-1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualizingSheafOverField_isCoherent_isCohenMacaulay_supp_eq_univ
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BS3], clause (2).** Let `X` be a proper scheme over a field `k` which is
Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension one. Then `ω_X = H^{-1}(ω_X^•)` is a coherent
Cohen–Macaulay `𝒪_X`-module ([Stacks, Tag 0343]) whose support is `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingSheafOverField_isCoherent_isCohenMacaulay_supp_eq_univ
    (hcm : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X) (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent (dualizingSheafOverField f) ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafIsCohenMacaulay X (dualizingSheafOverField f) ∧
      _root_.SheafOfModules.supp (dualizingSheafOverField f) = Set.univ

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_extDualityShiftOne
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BS3], clause (3).** Let `X` be a proper scheme over a field `k` which is
Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension one, and `ω_X = H^{-1}(ω_X^•)`. There are
isomorphisms

  `Ext^i_X(K, ω_X[1]) = Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, K), k)`

for `K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `i ∈ ℤ`, functorial in `K` and compatible with shifts: they come from
isomorphisms `Hom(K, ω_X[1]) = Hom_k(H^0(X, K), k)`, functorial in `K`, by reading
`Ext^i_X(K, ω_X[1])` as `Hom(K⟦-i⟧, ω_X[1])` (the shift adjunction) and `H^{-i}(X, K)` as
`H^0(X, K⟦-i⟧)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_extDualityShiftOne
    (hcm : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X) (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) :
    ∃ (e : ∀ (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (i : ℤ),
        DerivedCategory.Ext K.obj (dualizingSheafShiftOne f) i ≃+
          (derivedCohomologyOverField f K.obj (-i) ⟶ ModuleCat.of k k))
      (e₀ : ∀ K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X,
        (K.obj ⟶ dualizingSheafShiftOne f) ≃+
          (derivedCohomologyOverField f K.obj 0 ⟶ ModuleCat.of k k)),
      (∀ (K L : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (i : ℤ) (g : K.obj ⟶ L.obj)
          (α : DerivedCategory.Ext L.obj (dualizingSheafShiftOne f) i),
        e K i (g ≫ α) =
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) (-i)).map
            ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).map g) ≫ e L i α) ∧
      (∀ (K L : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (g : K.obj ⟶ L.obj)
          (β : L.obj ⟶ dualizingSheafShiftOne f),
        e₀ K (g ≫ β) =
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) 0).map
            ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).map g) ≫ e₀ L β) ∧
      (∀ (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (i : ℤ)
          (α : DerivedCategory.Ext K.obj (dualizingSheafShiftOne f) i),
        e K i α = (derivedCohomologyShiftIso f K.obj (-i)).inv ≫
          e₀ (shiftQuasiCoherent K (-i))
            (((shiftEquiv' (DerivedCategory X.Modules) (-i) i (by omega)).toAdjunction.homEquiv
              K.obj (dualizingSheafShiftOne f)).symm α))

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_extSuccDuality
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BS3], clause (4).** Let `X` be a proper scheme over a field `k` which is
Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension one, and `ω_X = H^{-1}(ω_X^•)`. There are
isomorphisms

  `Ext^{1 + i}_X(ℱ, ω_X) = Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, ℱ), k)`

for quasi-coherent `ℱ` on `X` and `i ∈ ℤ`, functorial in `ℱ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_extSuccDuality
    (hcm : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X) (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) :
    ∃ e : ∀ (F : X.Modules) (_ : F.IsQuasicoherent) (i : ℤ),
        DerivedCategory.Ext ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F)
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj (dualizingSheafOverField f))
