            (1 + i) ≃+
          (derivedCohomologyOverField f ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F) (-i) ⟶
            ModuleCat.of k k),
      ∀ (F G : X.Modules) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) (hG : G.IsQuasicoherent) (i : ℤ) (u : F ⟶ G)
        (α : DerivedCategory.Ext ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj G)
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj (dualizingSheafOverField f)) (1 + i)),
        e F hF i ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).map u ≫ α) =
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) (-i)).map
              ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).map
                ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).map u)) ≫
            e G hG i α

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_cohomologyOverField_one_eq_zero_tensorPowerModuleNegOneTensorDualizing
declarations.doc:
**`dim_k H¹(X, ℒ) = dim_k H⁰(X, ℒ^{⊗ -1} ⊗ ω_X)`** for an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `ℒ` on a
proper scheme `X` of dimension at most one over a field `k`, with
`ω_X = H^{-1}(f^×(𝒪_{Spec k}))` the dualizing sheaf of [Stacks, Tag 0BS2].

This is the last of the four formulas displayed in [Stacks, Tag 0BS4]. The proof is the duality
of dimensions at a vector bundle,
`AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_cohomologyOverField_zero_dualTensorDualizingSheafOverField_eq_one`,
at `ℒ` itself — an invertible module being finite locally free of rank one — with the dual `ℒ^∨`
rewritten as the inverse `ℒ^{⊗ -1}` by the last clause of [Stacks, Tag 0B8K]. Neither the
Cohen--Macaulay nor the equidimensionality condition under which the Remark states it is
used.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finrank_cohomologyOverField_one_eq_zero_tensorPowerModuleNegOneTensorDualizing
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ (1 : WithBot ℕ∞)) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L] :
    Module.finrank k (cohomologyOverField k f L 1) =
      Module.finrank k (cohomologyOverField k f
        ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨X.presheaf,
            CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ X.presheaf
              (CategoryTheory.forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) X.ringCatSheaf.property⟩).obj
            (tensorPowerModule L (-1))).obj (Stacks.Duality.dualizingSheafOverField f))) 0)
declarations.comment: the fourth display, dim_k H^1(X, L) = dim_k H^0(X, L^(tensor -1) tensor omega_X), at an invertible L and the dualizing sheaf of Tag 0BS2, for every proper X of dimension at most one over k; the Remark's Cohen-Macaulay and equidimensionality conditions are not needed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_cohomologyOverField_zero_eq_one_tensorPowerModuleNegOneTensorDualizing
declarations.doc:
**`dim_k H⁰(X, ℒ) = dim_k H¹(X, ℒ^{⊗ -1} ⊗ ω_X)`** for an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `ℒ` on a
proper scheme `X` over a field `k` which is Cohen--Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension one,
with `ω_X` the dualizing sheaf of [Stacks, Tag 0BS2].

This is the third display of [Stacks, Tag 0BS4], and the source's proof: the second display at
`ℰ = ℒ` and `i = 0`, `Hom_k(H⁰(X, ℒ), k) ≃ₗ[k] H¹(X, ℒ^∨ ⊗ ω_X)`, which is
`Stacks.Duality.LocallyFreeTwist.dualityTensorDualizingSheafLinearEquiv`, together with the
equality of the dimensions of a vector space and of its dual, and the identification of the dual
`ℒ^∨` with the inverse `ℒ^{⊗ -1}` ([Stacks, Tag 0B8K]).
declarations.statement:
public theorem finrank_cohomologyOverField_zero_eq_one_tensorPowerModuleNegOneTensorDualizing
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
    (hcm : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X) (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L] :
    Module.finrank k (cohomologyOverField k f L 0) =
      Module.finrank k (cohomologyOverField k f
        ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨X.presheaf,
            CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ X.presheaf
              (CategoryTheory.forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) X.ringCatSheaf.property⟩).obj
            (tensorPowerModule L (-1))).obj (Stacks.Duality.dualizingSheafOverField f))) 1)
declarations.comment: the third display, dim_k H^0(X, L) = dim_k H^1(X, L^(tensor -1) tensor omega_X), for X proper over k, Cohen-Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension one, at the dualizing sheaf of Tag 0BS2

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.LocallyFreeTwist.dualityDerivedTensorLinearEquiv
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BS4], first display**: for a finite locally free `E` with dual `E^∨`,

  `Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, E), k) ≃ₗ[k] H^i(X, E^∨ ⊗^L ω_X^•)`,

with `ω_X^•` the dualizing complex of [Stacks, Tag 0BS2] and `⊗^L` the derived tensor product of
[Stacks, Tag 06YU]. The source assumes `X` proper of dimension at most one over `k`; only the
quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of `f`, under which clause (4) of Tag 0BS2 holds, are
used.
declarations.statement:
def dualityDerivedTensorLinearEquiv (i : ℤ) :
    Module.Dual k (derivedCohomologyOverField f ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj E)
        (-i)) ≃ₗ[k]
      derivedCohomologyOverField f (((Stacks.Duality.derivedTensor X).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj (dual E))).obj
          (dualizingComplexOverField f).obj) i
declarations.comment: the first display, Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, E), k) = H^i(X, E^dual tensor^L omega^bullet), as an isomorphism of k-vector spaces, for E finite locally free; for every quasi-compact quasi-separated X over k, of which a proper X of dimension at most one is a case

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.LocallyFreeTwist.dualityTensorDualizingSheafLinearEquiv
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BS4], second display**: if `X` is proper over `k`, Cohen--Macaulay and
equidimensional of dimension one, then for a finite locally free `E` with dual `E^∨`,

  `Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, E), k) ≃ₗ[k] H^{1+i}(X, E^∨ ⊗_{𝒪_X} ω_X)`,

with `ω_X` the dualizing sheaf of [Stacks, Tag 0BS2]. This is the first display with
`ω_X^• = ω_X[1]` of [Stacks, Tag 0BS3] substituted.
declarations.statement:
def dualityTensorDualizingSheafLinearEquiv [IsProper f]
    (hcm : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X) (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) (i : ℤ) :
    Module.Dual k (derivedCohomologyOverField f ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj E)
        (-i)) ≃ₗ[k]
      derivedCohomologyOverField f ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u} (R X)).obj (dual E)).obj
          (dualizingSheafOverField f))) (1 + i)
declarations.comment: the second display, Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, E), k) = H^{1+i}(X, E^dual tensor omega_X), as an isomorphism of k-vector spaces, for X proper over k, Cohen-Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension one, and E finite locally free

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.LocallyFreeTwist.dualityTensorDualizingSheafLinearEquiv_naturality
declarations.doc:
**The second display of [Stacks, Tag 0BS4] is natural in `E`**: for `g : E₁ ⟶ E₂` between
finite locally free modules, precomposition with `H^{-i}(X, g)` corresponds to
`H^{1+i}(X, g^∨ ⊗ ω_X)`, `g^∨` being the dual of `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualityTensorDualizingSheafLinearEquiv_naturality [IsProper f]
    (hcm : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X) (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) (i : ℤ)
    (φ : Module.Dual k (derivedCohomologyOverField f
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj E₂) (-i))) :
    dualityTensorDualizingSheafLinearEquiv E₁ f hcm hequi hdim i
        (φ ∘ₗ ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) (-i)).map
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).map
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).map g))).hom) =
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) (1 + i)).map
        ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).map ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).map
          (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u} (R X)).map
            (dualMap g)).app (dualizingSheafOverField f))))).hom
        (dualityTensorDualizingSheafLinearEquiv E₂ f hcm hequi hdim i φ)
declarations.comment: the second display: the canonical isomorphism is natural in the finite locally free E, for the dual map E_2^dual -> E_1^dual of E_1 -> E_2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eulerCharacteristic_unit_eq_neg_eulerCharacteristic_dualizingSheafOverField
declarations.doc:
**The second formula of [Stacks, Tag 0BS5]: `χ(X, 𝒪_X) = -χ(X, ω_X)`** for a proper scheme
`X` over a field `k` which is Cohen--Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension one, with
`ω_X = H^{-1}(f^×(𝒪_{Spec k}))` the dualizing sheaf of [Stacks, Tag 0BS2].

As in the source, it is the first formula
`eulerCharacteristic_unit_eq_eulerCharacteristicDerived_dualizingComplexOverField` read through
`ω_X^• = ω_X[1]` of [Stacks, Tag 0BS3]
(`Stacks.Duality.dualizingSheafShiftOneIsoOfIsCohenMacaulay`), in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.finsum_alternating_finrank_unit_eq_neg_dualizingSheafOverField_of_iso`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem eulerCharacteristic_unit_eq_neg_eulerCharacteristic_dualizingSheafOverField
    (hcm : IsCohenMacaulay X) (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    letI : (Stacks.Ample.unitModule X).IsCoherent :=
      Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherenceCriteria.structureSheaf_isCoherent X
    letI : (Stacks.Duality.dualizingSheafOverField f).IsCoherent :=
      Stacks.Duality.isCoherent_homology_of_isDualizingComplex
        (Stacks.Duality.isDualizingComplex_dualizingComplexOverField_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_one
          f hdim.le) (-1)
    eulerCharacteristic k f (Stacks.Ample.unitModule X) =
      -eulerCharacteristic k f (Stacks.Duality.dualizingSheafOverField f)
declarations.comment: second formula, chi(X, O_X) = - chi(X, omega_X), for X proper over a field, Cohen-Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension one, omega_X = H^(-1)(f^x(O_Spec k)) of Tag 0BS2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eulerCharacteristic_unit_eq_eulerCharacteristicDerived_dualizingComplexOverField
declarations.doc:
**The first formula of [Stacks, Tag 0BS5]: `χ(X, 𝒪_X) = χ(X, ω_X^•)`** for a proper scheme `X`
of dimension at most one over a field `k`, with `ω_X^• = f^×(𝒪_{Spec k})` the dualizing complex of
[Stacks, Tag 0BS2] and `χ(X, ω_X^•)` the alternating sum
`∑_{i ∈ ℤ} (-1)^i dim_k H^i(X, ω_X^•)` that the source defines it to be.

Both sides collapse to `dim_k H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) - dim_k H¹(X, 𝒪_X)`: on the right by the duality
`dim_k H^i(X, ω_X^•) = dim_k H^{-i}(X, 𝒪_X)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.eulerCharacteristicDerived_dualizingComplexOverField_eq_sub`), on the left
because `X` is at most one-dimensional ([Stacks, Tag 02UZ]).
declarations.statement:
public theorem eulerCharacteristic_unit_eq_eulerCharacteristicDerived_dualizingComplexOverField
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ (1 : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    letI : (Stacks.Ample.unitModule X).IsCoherent :=
      Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherenceCriteria.structureSheaf_isCoherent X
    eulerCharacteristic k f (Stacks.Ample.unitModule X) =
      eulerCharacteristicDerived f (Stacks.Duality.dualizingComplexOverField f).obj
declarations.comment: first formula, chi(X, O_X) = chi(X, omega^bullet), for X proper of dimension at most one over a field, omega^bullet = f^x(O_Spec k) of Tag 0BS2, and chi(X, omega^bullet) the alternating sum of the dimensions of its hypercohomology, as the source defines it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree_dualizingSheafOverField_eq_neg_two_mul_of_isGorenstein
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BS6], clause (2).** Let `X` be a proper scheme over a field `k` which is
Gorenstein and equidimensional of dimension one, and `ω_X = H^{-1}(f^×(𝒪_{Spec k}))` the
dualizing sheaf of [Stacks, Tag 0BS2], which is invertible by clause (1). Then

  `deg(ω_X) = -2 χ(X, 𝒪_X)`,

with `deg` the degree of [Stacks, Tag 0AYR] (`AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree`, at rank one).
The proof is the source's: `deg(ω_X) = χ(X, ω_X) - χ(X, 𝒪_X)` and
`χ(X, 𝒪_X) = -χ(X, ω_X)` by [Stacks, Tag 0BS5].
declarations.statement:
public theorem curveDegree_dualizingSheafOverField_eq_neg_two_mul_of_isGorenstein
    (hG : IsGorenstein X) (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    letI : (Stacks.Ample.unitModule X).IsCoherent :=
      Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherenceCriteria.structureSheaf_isCoherent X
    letI := (Stacks.Duality.isInvertible_dualizingSheafOverField_of_isGorenstein f hG hequi
      hdim).2
    curveDegree k f hdim.le (Stacks.Duality.dualizingSheafOverField f) 1 =
      -2 * eulerCharacteristic k f (Stacks.Ample.unitModule X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eulerCharacteristic_eq_and_finrank_cohomology_eq_of_isGorenstein
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BS6], clause (3).** Let `X` be a proper scheme over a field `k` which is
Gorenstein and equidimensional of dimension one, `ω_X = H^{-1}(f^×(𝒪_{Spec k}))` the dualizing
sheaf of [Stacks, Tag 0BS2] (invertible by clause (1)), and `ℰ` a finite locally free
`𝒪_X`-module of constant rank `r`. Then

  `χ(X, ℰ) = deg(ℰ) - ½ rank(ℰ) deg(ω_X)`

with `deg` the degree of [Stacks, Tag 0AYR], and

  `dim_k H^i(X, ℰ) = dim_k H^{1-i}(X, ℰ^∨ ⊗_{𝒪_X} ω_X)` for all `i ∈ ℤ`,

with `H^i(X, -)` the hypercohomology of a module placed in degree zero, which is sheaf cohomology
for `i ≥ 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem eulerCharacteristic_eq_and_finrank_cohomology_eq_of_isGorenstein
    (hG : IsGorenstein X) (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) (E : X.Modules) (r : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E r] :
    letI : E.IsCoherent :=
      Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CurveEulerBridge.isCoherent_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank k f E r
    letI := (Stacks.Duality.isInvertible_dualizingSheafOverField_of_isGorenstein f hG hequi
      hdim).2
    (eulerCharacteristic k f E : ℚ) =
        (curveDegree k f hdim.le E r : ℚ) -
          1 / 2 * (r : ℚ) *
            (curveDegree k f hdim.le (Stacks.Duality.dualizingSheafOverField f) 1 : ℚ) ∧
      ∀ i : ℤ, Module.finrank k (Stacks.Duality.derivedCohomologyOverField f
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj E) i) =
        Module.finrank k (Stacks.Duality.derivedCohomologyOverField f
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj
            (dualTensorDualizingSheafOverField f E)) (1 - i))

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isInvertible_dualizingSheafOverField_of_isGorenstein
declarations.doc:
**The dualizing sheaf of a proper Gorenstein curve is invertible.** Let `X` be a proper scheme
over a field `k` which is Gorenstein and equidimensional of dimension one, and let
`ω_X = H^{-1}(f^×(𝒪_{Spec k}))` be the dualizing sheaf of [Stacks, Tag 0BS2]. Then `ω_X` is an
invertible `𝒪_X`-module, and it is finite locally free of rank one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_dualizingSheafOverField_of_isGorenstein
    (hG : AlgebraicGeometry.IsGorenstein X) (hequi : TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2
        (dualizingSheafOverField f) ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
        (dualizingSheafOverField f) 1

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.inducedHom_comp_eq_one_iff_forall_isFiniteCoproductOfTerminal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BS8.** Let `H : C ⥤ C'` and `H' : C' ⥤ C''` be functors between
Galois categories with fibre functors `F`, `F'`, `F''`, and let `t : H ⋙ F' ≅ F` and
`t' : H' ⋙ F'' ≅ F'` be isomorphisms of fibre functors, with induced homomorphisms
`h : Aut F' →* Aut F` and `h' : Aut F'' →* Aut F'`. Then `h ∘ h'` is trivial if and only if every
object in the image of `H ⋙ H'` is a finite coproduct of terminal objects.
declarations.statement:
public theorem inducedHom_comp_eq_one_iff_forall_isFiniteCoproductOfTerminal
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {C' : Type u'} [Category.{v'} C']
    {C'' : Type u''} [Category.{v''} C'']
    (F : C ⥤ FintypeCat.{w}) (F' : C' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w}) (F'' : C'' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w})
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F)]
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F')]
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F'')]
    (H : C ⥤ C') (H' : C' ⥤ C'') (t : H ⋙ F' ≅ F) (t' : H' ⋙ F'' ≅ F') :
    (inducedHom F F' H t).comp (inducedHom F' F'' H' t') = 1 ↔
      ∀ X : C, IsFiniteCoproductOfTerminal ((H ⋙ H').obj X)
declarations.comment:
for every choice of fibre-functor isomorphisms; continuity of the induced
homomorphisms and the 2-commutative squares are constructed, not assumed

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.comp_hom_eq_one_iff_forall_isFiniteCoproductOfTerminal
declarations.doc:
The composite homomorphism associated to two successive functors of Galois categories is
trivial exactly when every object in the image of the composite functor is a finite coproduct of
terminal objects.
declarations.statement:
public theorem comp_hom_eq_one_iff_forall_isFiniteCoproductOfTerminal
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {C' : Type u'} [Category.{v'} C']
    {C'' : Type u''} [Category.{v''} C'']
    (F : C ⥤ FintypeCat.{w}) (F' : C' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w})
    (F'' : C'' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w})
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F)]
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F')]
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F'')]
    (H : C ⥤ C') (H' : C' ⥤ C'')
    (t : H ⋙ F' ≅ F) (t' : H' ⋙ F'' ≅ F')
    (d : GaloisFunctorData F F' H t)
    (d' : GaloisFunctorData F' F'' H' t') :
    d.hom.toMonoidHom.comp d'.hom.toMonoidHom = 1 ↔
      ∀ X : C, IsFiniteCoproductOfTerminal ((H ⋙ H').obj X)

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.galoisExact_iff_categorical_conditions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BS9.** For composable exact functors between Galois categories, exactness of the
induced sequence of automorphism groups is equivalent both to the essential-image criterion and to
its epimorphic-cover variant.
declarations.statement:
theorem galoisExact_iff_categorical_conditions
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    {C' : Type u'} [Category.{v'} C']
    {C'' : Type u''} [Category.{v''} C'']
    (F : C ⥤ FintypeCat.{w}) (F' : C' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w})
    (F'' : C'' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w})
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F)]
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F')]
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F'')]
    (H : C ⥤ C') (H' : C' ⥤ C'')
    (_hH : exactFunctor C C' H) (_hH' : exactFunctor C' C'' H')
    (t : H ⋙ F' ≅ F) (t' : H' ⋙ F'' ≅ F')
    (d : GaloisFunctorData F F' H t)
    (d' : GaloisFunctorData F' F'' H' t') :
    List.TFAE
      [ IsExactSequence d'.hom d.hom,
        Nonempty H.FullyFaithful ∧
          ∀ X' : C',
            (H.essImage X' ↔ IsFiniteCoproductOfTerminal (H'.obj X')),
        Nonempty H.FullyFaithful ∧
          (∀ X : C, IsFiniteCoproductOfTerminal ((H ⋙ H').obj X)) ∧
          (∀ X' : C', IsFiniteCoproductOfTerminal (H'.obj X') →
            ∃ (X : C) (f : H.obj X ⟶ X'), Epi f) ]

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.galoisExact_iff_categorical_conditions_of_fiberIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BS9.** For composable exact functors between Galois categories, exactness of the
induced sequence of automorphism groups is equivalent both to the essential-image criterion and to
its epimorphic-cover variant.

This is the form of the statement in which no part of the functoriality data is assumed: the two
continuous homomorphisms are the ones produced from the fibre-functor isomorphisms `t` and `t'`,
whose continuity and whose 2-isomorphisms of the two functoriality squares are constructed by
`CategoryTheory.galoisFunctorDataOfFiberIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem galoisExact_iff_categorical_conditions_of_fiberIso
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    {C' : Type u'} [Category.{v'} C']
    {C'' : Type u''} [Category.{v''} C'']
    (F : C ⥤ FintypeCat.{w}) (F' : C' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w})
    (F'' : C'' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w})
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F)]
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F')]
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F'')]
    (H : C ⥤ C') (H' : C' ⥤ C'')
    (hH : exactFunctor C C' H) (hH' : exactFunctor C' C'' H')
    (t : H ⋙ F' ≅ F) (t' : H' ⋙ F'' ≅ F') :
    List.TFAE
      [ IsExactSequence (galoisFunctorDataOfFiberIso F' F'' H' t').hom
          (galoisFunctorDataOfFiberIso F F' H t).hom,
        Nonempty H.FullyFaithful ∧
          ∀ X' : C',
            (H.essImage X' ↔ IsFiniteCoproductOfTerminal (H'.obj X')),
        Nonempty H.FullyFaithful ∧
          (∀ X : C, IsFiniteCoproductOfTerminal ((H ⋙ H').obj X)) ∧
          (∀ X' : C', IsFiniteCoproductOfTerminal (H'.obj X') →
            ∃ (X : C) (f : H.obj X ⟶ X'), Epi f) ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_quasiCompact_of_isClosed_compl
declarations.doc:
Let `j : U ⟶ X` be a dense open immersion of schemes which is quasi-compact, and assume that
every point of `X ∖ U` is closed and that the punctured spectrum of every strict henselization of
its local ring is connected. Then restriction of finite étale covers along `j` is fully
faithful.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_quasiCompact_of_isClosed_compl
    {U X : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] [IsDominant j]
    [QuasiCompact j]
    (hclosed : ∀ x : X, x ∉ Set.range j.base → IsClosed ({x} : Set X))
    (hconnected : ∀ x : X, x ∉ Set.range j.base →
      IsConnectedPuncturedStrictHenselization (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    Nonempty (finiteEtaleBaseChange j).FullyFaithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isExactSequence_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_puncturedSpectrum_of_quasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BSB.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a local ring whose punctured spectrum
`U = Spec A ∖ {𝔪}` is retrocompact, let `Aˢʰ` be a strict henselization of `A` whose punctured
spectrum `Uˢʰ` is connected, and let `ū` be a geometric point of `Uˢʰ`. Then

```
π₁(Uˢʰ, ū) → π₁(U, ū) → π₁(X, ū) → 1
```

is exact: `π₁(U) → π₁(X)` is surjective, the composite is trivial, and the kernel of
`π₁(U) → π₁(X)` is the smallest closed normal subgroup containing the image of `π₁(Uˢʰ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isExactSequence_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_puncturedSpectrum_of_quasiCompact
    (hAsh : Stacks.StrictHenselization.IsStrictHenselization A κsep Ash)
    (hconnected : _root_.IsConnected ({closedPoint Ash}ᶜ : Set (PrimeSpectrum Ash)))
    [QuasiCompact (puncturedSpectrum A).ι]
    (w : GeometricPoint
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A Ash)) ⁻¹ᵁ puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme) :
    letI : ConnectedSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) := connectedSpace_spec_of_isLocalRing A
    letI : ConnectedSpace (puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme :=
      connectedSpace_puncturedSpectrum_of_isStrictHenselization A κsep Ash hAsh hconnected
    letI : ConnectedSpace
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A Ash)) ⁻¹ᵁ puncturedSpectrum A) :=
      connectedSpace_preimage_puncturedSpectrum_of_isStrictHenselization A κsep Ash hAsh
        hconnected
    IsExactSequence
      (etaleFundamentalGroupMap
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A Ash)) ∣_ puncturedSpectrum A) w)
      (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (puncturedSpectrum A).ι
        (w.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A Ash)) ∣_ puncturedSpectrum A)))
declarations.comment: the full exact sequence, with the descent half discharged

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.connectedSpace_puncturedSpectrum_of_isStrictHenselization
declarations.doc:
**Connectedness of `U` in Stacks Project, Tag 0BSB.** The punctured spectrum of `A` is
connected as soon as the punctured spectrum of a strict henselization `Aˢʰ` is: the latter is the
preimage of the former under the faithfully flat `Spec Aˢʰ ⟶ Spec A`, so the restriction
`Uˢʰ ⟶ U` is surjective and connectedness transfers along it. This is implicit in the statement
of the tag, since `π₁(U, ū)` appears in it.
declarations.statement:
theorem connectedSpace_puncturedSpectrum_of_isStrictHenselization
    (hAsh : Stacks.StrictHenselization.IsStrictHenselization A κsep Ash)
    (hconnected : _root_.IsConnected ({closedPoint Ash}ᶜ : Set (PrimeSpectrum Ash))) :
    ConnectedSpace (puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme
declarations.comment: connectedness of `U`, implicit since `π₁(U, ū)` appears in the statement

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroupMap_comp_eq_one_puncturedSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Triviality of the composite in Stacks Project, Tag 0BSB.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a local ring,
`X = Spec A`, `U = X ∖ {𝔪}` the punctured spectrum, `Aˢʰ` a strict henselization of `A` and
`Uˢʰ` its punctured spectrum, presented as the preimage of `U`. If `Uˢʰ` is connected then the
composite

```
π₁(Uˢʰ, ū) ⟶ π₁(U, ū) ⟶ π₁(X, ū)
```

is the trivial homomorphism. This is the complex condition of the exact sequence asserted by the
tag; it is Stacks 0BS8 applied to the composite base-change functor, which lands in finite
coproducts of copies of `Uˢʰ` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isFiniteCoproductOfTerminal_finiteEtaleBaseChange_puncturedSpectrum`.

The quasi-compactness of `U` assumed by the tag is not needed for this assertion; it enters only
the descent half of the source's proof, which is the remaining obligation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.isExactSequence_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_puncturedSpectrum`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleFundamentalGroupMap_comp_eq_one_puncturedSpectrum
    (hAsh : Stacks.StrictHenselization.IsStrictHenselization A κsep Ash)
    (hconnected : _root_.IsConnected ({closedPoint Ash}ᶜ : Set (PrimeSpectrum Ash)))
    (w : GeometricPoint
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A Ash)) ⁻¹ᵁ puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme) :
    letI : ConnectedSpace (Spec (.of A)) := connectedSpace_spec_of_isLocalRing A
    letI : ConnectedSpace (puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme :=
      connectedSpace_puncturedSpectrum_of_isStrictHenselization A κsep Ash hAsh hconnected
    letI : ConnectedSpace
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A Ash)) ⁻¹ᵁ puncturedSpectrum A) :=
      connectedSpace_preimage_puncturedSpectrum_of_isStrictHenselization A κsep Ash hAsh
        hconnected
    (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (puncturedSpectrum A).ι
          (w.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A Ash)) ∣_
            puncturedSpectrum A))).toMonoidHom.comp
        (etaleFundamentalGroupMap
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A Ash)) ∣_ puncturedSpectrum A)
          w).toMonoidHom = 1
declarations.comment: triviality of the composite `π₁(Uˢʰ) → π₁(U) → π₁(X)` only

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_puncturedSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Surjectivity in Stacks Project, Tag 0BSB.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a local ring, `X = Spec A`,
`U = X ∖ {𝔪}` the punctured spectrum, and `Aˢʰ` a strict henselization of `A` whose punctured
spectrum is connected. Then for every geometric point `ū` of `U` the induced homomorphism

```
π₁(U, ū) ⟶ π₁(X, ū)
```

is surjective. This is the criterion of Stacks 0BN6, whose second condition is full faithfulness
of `FÉt_X ⥤ FÉt_U`, which is Stacks 0BLQ
(`AlgebraicGeometry.fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_to_puncturedSpectrum`); the transport
between the abstract automorphism groups of that criterion and the étale fundamental groups is
`AlgebraicGeometry.autMulEquivEtaleFundamentalGroup_galoisFunctorData_hom`.

The quasi-compactness of `U` assumed by the tag is not needed for this assertion; it enters only
the descent half of the source's proof, which is the remaining obligation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.isExactSequence_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_puncturedSpectrum`.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_puncturedSpectrum
    (hAsh : Stacks.StrictHenselization.IsStrictHenselization A κsep Ash)
    (hconnected : _root_.IsConnected ({closedPoint Ash}ᶜ : Set (PrimeSpectrum Ash)))
    (u : GeometricPoint (puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme) :
    letI : ConnectedSpace (Spec (.of A)) := connectedSpace_spec_of_isLocalRing A
    letI : ConnectedSpace (puncturedSpectrum A).toScheme :=
      connectedSpace_puncturedSpectrum_of_isStrictHenselization A κsep Ash hAsh hconnected
    Function.Surjective (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (puncturedSpectrum A).ι u)
declarations.comment: surjectivity of `π₁(U) → π₁(X)`, the `→ 1` of the sequence, only

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_of_finite_isClosed_compl
declarations.doc:
**Surjectivity of `π₁(U) → π₁(X)` for the complement of finitely many closed points.** Let
`X` be a connected scheme, let
`x₁, …, xₙ ∈ X` be finitely many closed points, and let `U = X ∖ {x₁, …, xₙ}`, presented as an
open immersion `j : U ⟶ X` whose image has finite complement consisting of closed points.
Assume that

1. `U` is connected and retrocompact in `X` — `[ConnectedSpace U]` and `[QuasiCompact j]`;
2. for each `i` the punctured spectrum of the strict henselization of `𝒪_{X,xᵢ}` is connected —
   `hconnected`.

Then for every geometric point `ū` of `U` the induced continuous homomorphism

```
π₁(U, ū) ⟶ π₁(X, ū)
```

is surjective; equivalently, every connected finite étale cover of `X` stays connected over `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_of_finite_isClosed_compl
    {U X : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ X) [ConnectedSpace U] [ConnectedSpace X] [IsOpenImmersion j]
    [QuasiCompact j]
    (hfinite : ((Set.range j.base)ᶜ : Set X).Finite)
    (hclosed : ∀ x : X, x ∉ Set.range j.base → IsClosed ({x} : Set X))
    (hconnected : ∀ x : X, x ∉ Set.range j.base →
      IsConnectedPuncturedStrictHenselization (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (u : GeometricPoint U) :
    Function.Surjective (etaleFundamentalGroupMap j u)
declarations.comment: the surjectivity clause `π₁(U) → π₁(X)` for `U` the complement of finitely many closed points, under hypotheses (1) and (2); the kernel description is not proved here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ker_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_eq_closedNormalClosure_biUnion_range
declarations.doc:
**The kernel of `π₁(U) ⟶ π₁(X)`.** Let `X` be a connected scheme, let
`x₀, …, xₙ₋₁ ∈ X` be pairwise distinct closed points and let `U = X ∖ {x₀, …, xₙ₋₁}`, assumed
connected and retrocompact in `X`. Let `Aᵢˢʰ` be a strict henselization of the local ring at `xᵢ`
and let `Uᵢˢʰ` be the preimage of the complement of `xᵢ` in `Spec Aᵢˢʰ`, that is, the punctured
spectrum of `Aᵢˢʰ`; assume every punctured spectrum of every strict henselization of that local
ring is connected. Let `ū` be a geometric point of `U`, let `ūᵢ` be a geometric point of `Uᵢˢʰ`
and let `s i` compare the geometric fibre functors of `U` at the image of `ūᵢ` and at `ū`. Then

```
ker (π₁(U, ū) ⟶ π₁(X, ū))
```

is the smallest closed normal subgroup of `π₁(U, ū)` containing the images of the maps
`π₁(Uᵢˢʰ, ūᵢ) ⟶ π₁(U, ū)`, each read through `s i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ker_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_eq_closedNormalClosure_biUnion_range
    [ConnectedSpace X] [ConnectedSpace (chainOpen x hclosed 0).toScheme]
    [QuasiCompact (chainOpen x hclosed 0).ι]
    (hconn : ∀ (j : ℕ) (y : (chainOpen x hclosed (j + 1)).toScheme),
      y ∉ Set.range (chainStep x hclosed j).base →
        IsConnectedPuncturedStrictHenselization
          ↥((chainOpen x hclosed (j + 1)).toScheme.presheaf.stalk y))
    (κsep : Fin n → Type u) [∀ i, Field (κsep i)]
    [∀ i, Algebra (maximalIdeal ↥(chainStalk x hclosed hinj i)).ResidueField (κsep i)]
    [∀ i, IsSepClosure (maximalIdeal ↥(chainStalk x hclosed hinj i)).ResidueField (κsep i)]
    (Ash : Fin n → Type u) [∀ i, CommRing (Ash i)] [∀ i, IsLocalRing (Ash i)]
    [∀ i, Algebra ↥(chainStalk x hclosed hinj i) (Ash i)]
    (hAsh : ∀ i, Stacks.StrictHenselization.IsStrictHenselization
      ↥(chainStalk x hclosed hinj i) (κsep i) (Ash i))
    (u : GeometricPoint (chainOpen x hclosed 0).toScheme)
    (w : ∀ i, GeometricPoint (chainLocalPunctured x hclosed hinj i (Ash i)).toScheme)
    (s : ∀ i, finiteEtaleFiberFunctor ((w i).map (chainLocalLift x hclosed hinj i (Ash i))) ≅
      finiteEtaleFiberFunctor u) :
    letI : ∀ i : Fin n, ConnectedSpace (chainLocalPunctured x hclosed hinj i (Ash i)) :=
      fun i ↦ connectedSpace_preimage_puncturedOpen_of_isStrictHenselization
        (isClosed_chainRemovedPoint x hclosed hinj i) (κsep i) (Ash i) (hAsh i)
        (hconn (i : ℕ) (chainRemovedPoint x hclosed hinj i)
          (notMem_range_chainStep x hclosed hinj i) (κsep i) (Ash i) (hAsh i))
    MonoidHom.ker (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (chainOpen x hclosed 0).ι u).toMonoidHom =
      (Subgroup.normalClosure (⋃ i : Fin n, Set.range
        ((etaleFundamentalGroupChange (s i)).comp
          (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (chainLocalLift x hclosed hinj i (Ash i))
            (w i))))).topologicalClosure
declarations.comment: the kernel clause, in union-of-images form, with the factorisation `Uᵢˢʰ ⟶ U` proved; the removed points are assumed pairwise distinct, and hypothesis (2) is stated at the stalks of the stages of the chain, where it is used

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_and_ker_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_of_finite_isClosed_compl
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a connected scheme, let
`x₀, …, xₙ₋₁ ∈ X` be pairwise distinct closed points and let `U = X ∖ {x₀, …, xₙ₋₁}`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.chainOpen x hclosed 0`. Assume

1. `U` is connected and retrocompact in `X` — `[ConnectedSpace (chainOpen x hclosed 0).toScheme]`
   and `[QuasiCompact (chainOpen x hclosed 0).ι]`;
2. for each `i` the punctured spectrum `Uᵢˢʰ` of the strict henselization of the local ring at
   `xᵢ` is connected — `hconn`.

Then for every geometric point `ū` of `U` the map `π₁(U, ū) ⟶ π₁(X, ū)` is surjective, and its
kernel is the smallest closed normal subgroup of `π₁(U, ū)` containing the images of the maps
`π₁(Uᵢˢʰ, ūᵢ) ⟶ π₁(U, ū)` for `i = 0, …, n - 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_and_ker_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_of_finite_isClosed_compl
    [ConnectedSpace X] [ConnectedSpace (chainOpen x hclosed 0).toScheme]
    [QuasiCompact (chainOpen x hclosed 0).ι]
    (hconn : ∀ (j : ℕ) (y : (chainOpen x hclosed (j + 1)).toScheme),
      y ∉ Set.range (chainStep x hclosed j).base →
        IsConnectedPuncturedStrictHenselization
          ↥((chainOpen x hclosed (j + 1)).toScheme.presheaf.stalk y))
    (κsep : Fin n → Type u) [∀ i, Field (κsep i)]
    [∀ i, Algebra (maximalIdeal ↥(chainStalk x hclosed hinj i)).ResidueField (κsep i)]
    [∀ i, IsSepClosure (maximalIdeal ↥(chainStalk x hclosed hinj i)).ResidueField (κsep i)]
    (Ash : Fin n → Type u) [∀ i, CommRing (Ash i)] [∀ i, IsLocalRing (Ash i)]
    [∀ i, Algebra ↥(chainStalk x hclosed hinj i) (Ash i)]
    (hAsh : ∀ i, Stacks.StrictHenselization.IsStrictHenselization
      ↥(chainStalk x hclosed hinj i) (κsep i) (Ash i))
    (u : GeometricPoint (chainOpen x hclosed 0).toScheme)
    (w : ∀ i, GeometricPoint (chainLocalPunctured x hclosed hinj i (Ash i)).toScheme)
    (s : ∀ i, finiteEtaleFiberFunctor ((w i).map (chainLocalLift x hclosed hinj i (Ash i))) ≅
      finiteEtaleFiberFunctor u) :
    letI : ∀ i : Fin n, ConnectedSpace (chainLocalPunctured x hclosed hinj i (Ash i)) :=
      fun i ↦ connectedSpace_preimage_puncturedOpen_of_isStrictHenselization
        (isClosed_chainRemovedPoint x hclosed hinj i) (κsep i) (Ash i) (hAsh i)
        (hconn (i : ℕ) (chainRemovedPoint x hclosed hinj i)
          (notMem_range_chainStep x hclosed hinj i) (κsep i) (Ash i) (hAsh i))
    Function.Surjective (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (chainOpen x hclosed 0).ι u) ∧
      MonoidHom.ker (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (chainOpen x hclosed 0).ι u).toMonoidHom =
        (Subgroup.normalClosure (⋃ i : Fin n, Set.range
          ((etaleFundamentalGroupChange (s i)).comp
            (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (chainLocalLift x hclosed hinj i (Ash i))
              (w i))))).topologicalClosure
declarations.comment: both clauses, surjectivity and the kernel, under one set of hypotheses; the removed points are assumed pairwise distinct, and hypothesis (2) is stated at the stalks of the stages of the chain, where it is used

declarations.name: filteredColimitEtale_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BSH.** Let `A` and `R'` be commutative `R`-algebras, equivalently ring
maps `R → A` and `R → R'`. If `A` is a filtered colimit of étale `R`-algebras, then
`R' ⊗[R] A`, regarded as an `R'`-algebra via the canonical map `R' → R' ⊗[R] A`, is a
filtered colimit of étale `R'`-algebras. Here `TensorProduct R R' A` is `R' ⊗[R] A`
with its canonical `R'`-algebra structure.
declarations.statement:
theorem filteredColimitEtale_baseChange
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    {R' : Type u} [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R']
    (hA : IsFilteredColimitOfEtale R A) :
    IsFilteredColimitOfEtale R' (TensorProduct R R' A)

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.ind_etale_of_isPushout
declarations.doc:
**An ind-étale algebra stays ind-étale after cobase change.** Let `R → S` and `R → R'` be ring
maps and let `S'` be a pushout of `S` and `R'` over `R`, that is, `S' = S ⊗[R] R'`. If `R'` is a
filtered colimit of étale `R`-algebras, then `S'` is a filtered colimit of étale `S`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem ind_etale_of_isPushout (R S R' S' : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [CommRing R'] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R S] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra R S'] [Algebra S S']
    [Algebra R' S'] [IsScalarTower R S S'] [IsScalarTower R R' S']
    [Algebra.IsPushout R S R' S']
    (h : (CommAlgCat.etale.{u} R).ind.{u} (CommAlgCat.of R R')) :
    (CommAlgCat.etale.{u} S).ind.{u} (CommAlgCat.of S S')
declarations.comment:
"`Λ` is a filtered colimit of étale `R`-algebras" is
`(CommAlgCat.etale R).ind.{u} (CommAlgCat.of R Λ)`, as in Lemma `04GN`, and the source's `S ⊗_R R'`
is an abstract `Algebra.IsPushout R S R' S'` rather than a model of the tensor product. Tagged
jointly with `filteredColimitEtale_baseChange`, which is this lemma for the predicate
`IsFilteredColimitOfEtale` and the model `TensorProduct R R' A`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: StacksDraft.indEtale_comp
declarations.doc:
**Lemma 0BSI across universes.** If `B` is ind-étale over `A` and `C` is ind-étale over `B`,
then `C` is ind-étale over `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem indEtale_comp {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {C : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
    (hB : IndEtale A B) (hC : IndEtale B C) : IndEtale A C
declarations.comment:
"`A → B` is a filtered colimit of étale ring maps" is `StacksDraft.IndEtale A B`
(Lemma `097I`), with `A`, `B` and `C` in independent universes, and the source's `A → B → C` is an
`IsScalarTower A B C`. The single-universe form is `CommAlgCat.ind_etale_comp`.

declarations.name: isFilteredColimitOfEtaleUnder_of_isColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BSJ.** Let `R` be a commutative ring, let `J` be a small filtered category and let
`G : J ⥤ Under (CommRingCat.of R)` be a diagram of `R`-algebras with colimit cocone `cA` and
apex isomorphic to `A`. If every `G.obj j` is a filtered colimit of étale `R`-algebras, then so
is `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFilteredColimitOfEtaleUnder_of_isColimit (R : Type) [CommRing R]
    (A : Under (CommRingCat.of R))
    (J : Type) [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J]
    (G : J ⥤ Under (CommRingCat.of R))
    (cA : Limits.Cocone G) (hcA : Limits.IsColimit cA) (hA : cA.pt ≅ A)
    (hEach : ∀ j, IsFilteredColimitOfEtaleUnder R (G.obj j)) :
    IsFilteredColimitOfEtaleUnder R A

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.exists_strictHenselization_iUnion_finiteEtale
declarations.doc:
**The strict henselization as a union of finite étale extensions of the henselization**
(Stacks 0BSL). Let `R → Rh` be a henselization of the local ring `R` and let `κsep` be a separable
algebraic closure of the residue field `κ` of `R`, identified with that of `Rh` by `e`. For every
finite subextension `κ ⊆ κ' ⊆ κsep` there is a finite étale local extension `Rh ⊆ Rh(κ')` with
residue field extension `κ ⊆ κ'`, unique up to unique isomorphism; for `κ' ⊆ κ''` there is exactly
one map `Rh(κ') → Rh(κ'')` compatible with `κ' ⊆ κ''`; and the union `Rsh` of the resulting
directed system is strictly henselian, and is a strict henselization of `Rh` and of `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.exists_strictHenselization_iUnion_finiteEtale
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (Rh : Type u) [CommRing Rh] [IsLocalRing Rh]
    [Algebra R Rh] [IsHenselization R (ResidueField R) Rh] (κsep : Type u) [Field κsep]
    [Algebra (ResidueField R) κsep] [IsSepClosure (ResidueField R) κsep] :
    ∃ e : ResidueField R ≃+* ResidueField Rh,
      (∀ x : R, e (residue R x) = residue Rh (algebraMap R Rh x)) ∧
      letI : Algebra (ResidueField Rh) κsep :=
        ((algebraMap (ResidueField R) κsep).comp e.symm.toRingHom).toAlgebra
      IsSepClosure (ResidueField Rh) κsep ∧
      ∃ (Rsh : Type u) (_ : CommRing Rsh) (_ : IsLocalRing Rsh) (_ : Algebra R Rsh)
        (_ : Algebra Rh Rsh) (_ : IsScalarTower R Rh Rsh)
        (A : ∀ L, FiniteEtaleLocalResidueLift.{u, u, u} R Rh κsep e L)
        (map : ∀ {L L'}, L ≤ L' → A L →ₐ[Rh] A L') (ι : ∀ L, A L →ₐ[Rh] Rsh),
        (∀ L L' (h : L ≤ L') (f : A L →ₐ[Rh] A L'), f = map h ↔
          ∀ a, residue _ (f a) = residueMap (A L) (A L') (IntermediateField.inclusion h)
            (residue _ a)) ∧
        (∀ L, map (le_refl L) = AlgHom.id Rh (A L)) ∧
        (∀ L₁ L₂ L₃ (h₁₂ : L₁ ≤ L₂) (h₂₃ : L₂ ≤ L₃),
          (map h₂₃).comp (map h₁₂) = map (h₁₂.trans h₂₃)) ∧
        (∀ L (B : FiniteEtaleLocalResidueLift.{u, u, t} R Rh κsep e L),
          ∃! f : A L ≃ₐ[Rh] B,
            ∀ a, residue B (f a) = residueMap (A L) B (RingHom.id L) (residue _ a)) ∧
        (∀ L L' (h : L ≤ L') a, ι L' (map h a) = ι L a) ∧
        (∀ L, Function.Injective (ι L)) ∧ (∀ x, ∃ L a, ι L a = x) ∧
        HenselianLocalRing Rsh ∧ IsSepClosed (ResidueField Rsh) ∧
        IsHenselization Rh κsep Rsh ∧ IsHenselization R κsep Rsh
declarations.comment:
The rings `R^h(κ')` are local `Rh`-algebras `A κ'` with injective embeddings `ι`
into `Rsh` exhausting it, which is the union of the source. The transition maps are pinned as the
unique maps compatible with the inclusions of residue fields, and each `A κ'` is unique up to a
unique isomorphism inducing the identity of `κ'`. That `Rsh` is the strict henselization is
`IsHenselization` over `Rh` and over `R` with residue field `κsep`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isExactSequence_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_fractionField_of_isHenselization
declarations.doc:
**The local exact sequence for a normal local ring.** Let
`A` be a normal local domain with fraction field `K`, let `A^sh` be a strict henselization of `A`
and `K^sh` its fraction field, and let `x` be a geometric point of `Spec K^sh`. Then

```
π₁(Spec K^sh, x) → π₁(Spec K, x) → π₁(Spec A, x) → 1
```

is exact.

The criterion of Stacks 0BS9 reduces this to two statements. Base change to the generic point is
fully faithful because a connected finite étale cover of `Spec A` with a section over `K` has a
section over `A`. A cover of `Spec K` comes from `Spec A` exactly when it becomes a finite
coproduct of copies of the base over `Spec K^sh`: one direction is that a cover pulled back from
`Spec A` is already split over the strictly henselian `Spec A^sh`, and the other is that the
integral closure of `A` in such a cover is finite étale over `A` — which it is because it is so
after the faithfully flat base change to `A^sh` — and has the cover as its generic fibre.

The four spectra are spectra of local rings, hence connected, so the Galois-category property
of Stacks Tag 0BNB applies at each of their geometric points.
declarations.statement:
theorem isExactSequence_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_fractionField_of_isHenselization
    [IsIntegrallyClosed A] [IsSepClosure (ResidueField A) κsep] [IsHenselization A κsep Ash]
    (x : GeometricPoint (Spec (.of Ksh))) :
    IsExactSequence
      (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K Ksh))) x)
      (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A K)))
        (x.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K Ksh)))))

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.isAlgClosed_residueField_of_normal
declarations.doc:
The residue field at a nonzero prime ideal of a normal domain whose fraction field is
separably closed is algebraically closed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAlgClosed_residueField_of_normal
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] [IsSepClosed K]
    (hA : IsIntegrallyClosed A) (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (hp : p ≠ ⊥) :
    IsAlgClosed p.ResidueField

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_etale_completeOrthogonalIdempotents_integral_isPurelyInseparable
declarations.doc:
**Splitting an integral algebra after an étale extension.**
If an integral `R`-algebra `S` has finitely many primes over `p`, and the maximal separable
subextension of every corresponding residue-field extension is finite, then after an étale base
change the algebra splits into integral factors having one prime over the chosen prime and purely
inseparable residue-field extensions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_etale_completeOrthogonalIdempotents_integral_isPurelyInseparable
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.IsIntegral R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (hfinite : Set.Finite {q : Ideal S | q.IsPrime ∧ q.LiesOver p})
    (hseparable : ∀ (q : Ideal S) (hq : q.IsPrime) (hqover : q.LiesOver p),
      letI := hq
      letI := hqover
      letI := Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver p q
      Module.Finite p.ResidueField
        (separableClosure p.ResidueField q.ResidueField)) :
    ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : Algebra R R') (_ : Algebra.Etale R R')
      (p' : Ideal R') (_ : p'.IsPrime) (_ : p'.LiesOver p) (n : ℕ)
      (e : Fin n → R' ⊗[R] S) (_ : CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents e)
      (r : (i : Fin n) → Ideal (Localization.Away (e i)))
      (_ : ∀ i, (r i).IsPrime) (_ : ∀ i, (r i).LiesOver p'),
      (∀ i : Fin n, Algebra.IsIntegral R' (Localization.Away (e i))) ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin n) (q : Ideal (Localization.Away (e i))),
        q.IsPrime → q.LiesOver p' → q = r i) ∧
      ∀ i : Fin n,
        letI := Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver p' (r i)
        IsPurelyInseparable p'.ResidueField (r i).ResidueField

declarations.name: MulSemiringAction.inertia_eq_inertia_baseChange
declarations.doc:
The inertia group of an ideal is unchanged after arbitrary base change from the invariant
subring, for any ideal of the base change lying above it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem inertia_eq_inertia_baseChange
    (q : Ideal R)
    (q' : Ideal (TensorProduct (FixedPoints.subring R G) A R))
    (hq' : q = q'.comap Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight) :
    let := baseChangeMulSemiringAction (G := G) (R := R) (A := A)
    q.inertia G = q'.inertia G

declarations.name: MulSemiringAction.exists_etale_away_fixedPoints_inertia
declarations.doc:
For a finite group acting on a ring, the inclusion of the invariant ring into the ring of
invariants of the inertia subgroup at a prime `q` is étale at the prime below `q`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_etale_away_fixedPoints_inertia (q : Ideal R) [q.IsPrime] :
    let I := q.inertia G
    let RG := FixedPoints.subring R G
    let RI := FixedPoints.subring R I
    letI : Algebra RG RI := (Subring.inclusion (by
      intro x hx g
      exact hx g)).toAlgebra
    ∃ g : RI, g ∉ q.comap RI.subtype ∧ Algebra.Etale RG (Localization.Away g)

declarations.name: IsIntegralClosure.isFilteredColimitOfEtale_localization_fixedPoints_inertia
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BSU.** Let `A` be a normal domain with fraction field `K`, let `L / K` be a
possibly infinite Galois extension with group `G = Gal(L/K)`, and let `B` be the integral
closure of `A` in `L`. For a prime `q` of `B` with inertia subgroup
`I = {σ ∈ G | σ q = q and σ ≡ id modulo q}`, the localization of `B ^ I` at the prime below `q`
is a filtered colimit of étale `A`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFilteredColimitOfEtale_localization_fixedPoints_inertia
    (q : Ideal (integralClosure A L)) (hq : q.IsPrime) :
    let C := FixedPoints.subalgebra A (integralClosure A L)
      (q.inertia Gal(L/K))
    let p := q.comap C.val
    IsFilteredColimitOfEtaleHom (A := Localization.AtPrime p)
      ((algebraMap C (Localization.AtPrime p)).comp (algebraMap A C))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroupMap_inertiaSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BSV.** The square formed by the generic and local spectra of a ring
extension commutes on fundamental groups. In the inertia diagram the extension is `A → Ah`, with
fraction fields `K → Kh`. The heterogeneous equality accounts for the two propositionally equal
induced geometric points of `Spec A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleFundamentalGroupMap_inertiaSquare
    (A Ah K Kh : Type u)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing Ah] [Algebra A Ah]
    [Field K] [Algebra A K]
    [Field Kh] [Algebra Ah Kh] [Algebra K Kh] [Algebra A Kh]
    [IsScalarTower A Ah Kh] [IsScalarTower A K Kh]
    [ConnectedSpace (Spec (.of Ah))] [ConnectedSpace (Spec (.of A))]
    [ConnectedSpace (Spec (.of Kh))] [ConnectedSpace (Spec (.of K))]
    (x : GeometricPoint (Spec (.of Kh)))
    (σ : EtaleFundamentalGroup (Spec (.of Kh)) x) :
    HEq
      (etaleFundamentalGroupMap
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A K)))
        (x.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K Kh))))
        (etaleFundamentalGroupMap
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K Kh))) x σ))
      (etaleFundamentalGroupMap
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A Ah)))
        (x.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Ah Kh))))
        (etaleFundamentalGroupMap
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Ah Kh))) x σ))
declarations.comment: right-hand square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroupMap_fractionField_strictHenselization_to_henselization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BSV.** The diagonal of the inertia diagram is the trivial map: it
factors through the fundamental group of the strictly henselian spectrum of `Ash`, which is
trivial.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleFundamentalGroupMap_fractionField_strictHenselization_to_henselization
    (A Ah Ash Ksh κsep : Type u)
    [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsIntegrallyClosed A]
    [CommRing Ah] [IsLocalRing Ah] [Algebra A Ah]
    [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) Ah]
    [CommRing Ash] [IsLocalRing Ash] [Algebra A Ash] [Algebra Ah Ash]
    [IsScalarTower A Ah Ash]
    [Field κsep] [Algebra (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) κsep]
    [IsSepClosure (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) κsep]
    [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization A κsep Ash]
    [Field Ksh] [Algebra Ash Ksh] [Algebra A Ksh] [IsFractionRing Ash Ksh]
    [Algebra Ah Ksh]
    [IsScalarTower Ah Ash Ksh] [IsScalarTower A Ash Ksh]
    [ConnectedSpace (Spec (.of Ksh))] [ConnectedSpace (Spec (.of Ah))]
    (x : GeometricPoint (Spec (.of Ksh))) :
    etaleFundamentalGroupMap (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Ah Ksh))) x = 1
declarations.comment: trivial diagonal

declarations.name: Stacks.RamificationTheory.surjective_and_ker_absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BSW.** The right vertical arrow `π₁(U) → π₁(X)` of the diagram is
surjective, and its kernel is the subgroup fixing the maximal subextension `M` unramified with
respect to `X` — that is, `Gal(K^sep/M)`.

Both come from Stacks Tag 0BQM, where the arrow is identified with restriction to `M`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.fundamentalGroupIsoGalMaximalEtaleExtension_apply`) and `M/K` is shown to be
Galois (`AlgebraicGeometry.normal_maximalEtaleExtension`): restriction onto a normal
subextension is surjective with kernel its fixing subgroup.

This is the lower right corner `π₁(X) = Gal(M/K)` of the translated diagram, with the right
vertical arrow read as restriction to `M`; the rest of the lemma — every other object and arrow,
the square, and both kernels — is `Stacks.RamificationTheory.inertiaDiagram_translation`, which
also shows that for `X = Spec A` its right vertical arrow agrees with the one here
(`exists_absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup_eq_etaleFundamentalGroupMap`).
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_and_ker_absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup
    [IsIntegral X] [IsNormal X]
    (hs : GeometricPoint.IsAlgebraic sbar)
    (hgeneric : sbar.hom default = genericPoint X) :
    let _ : Normal (X.residueField (sbar.hom default)) (maximalEtaleExtension X sbar) :=
      normal_maximalEtaleExtension X sbar hs
    Function.Surjective (absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup X sbar) ∧
      (absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup X sbar).toMonoidHom.ker =
        (maximalEtaleExtension X sbar).fixingSubgroup
declarations.comment: the lower right corner π₁(X) = Gal(M/K) of the translated diagram, M the maximal subextension unramified with respect to X: the right vertical arrow, from the absolute Galois group of the function field, is surjective with kernel Gal(K^sep/M), for a general integral normal X. The other objects and arrows of the diagram, the square and the kernels are Stacks.RamificationTheory.inertiaDiagram_translation, which also proves that its right vertical arrow, for X = Spec A, is this one

declarations.name: Stacks.RamificationTheory.inertiaDiagram_translation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BSW.** Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)` be a normal local domain with fraction field
`K`, let `K^sep = L` be a separable closure of `K` inside an algebraically closed algebraic
extension `Ω`, let `A^sep` be the integral closure of `A` in `K^sep` and `𝔪^sep = q` a maximal
ideal of `A^sep` over `𝔪`, with decomposition group `D` and inertia group `I` in
`G = Gal(K^sep/K)`. Let `A^h` be a henselization of `A` with fraction field `K^h`, embedded in
`K^sep` through the canonical local map `A^h → (A^sep)_{𝔪^sep}` (`hcompat`), let `κ(𝔪^sh)` be a
separable algebraic closure of `κ` inside `κ(𝔪^sep)`, and write `U = Spec K`, `U^h = Spec K^h`,
`X = Spec A`, `X^h = Spec A^h`. Then, via the isomorphism `π₁(U) = Gal(K^sep/K)` of Stacks Tag
0BNE, the diagram

```
π₁(U^sh) → π₁(U^h) → π₁(U)
             ↓         ↓
          π₁(X^h) →  π₁(X)
```

translates into

```
I → D → Gal(K^sep/K)
    ↓        ↓
 Gal(κ(𝔪^sh)/κ) → π₁(X)
```

in the following sense, objects and arrows alike:

* the top arrow `π₁(U^h) → π₁(U)` is injective with image `D` (so `π₁(U^h) = D`, the arrow
  being the inclusion), and the image of `π₁(U^sh)` in `π₁(U)` is `I`, for
  `U^sh = Spec (K^sep)^I` the spectrum of the fraction field of the strict henselization
  `A^sh = ((A^sep)_{𝔪^sep})^I`;
* the left vertical arrow `D → Gal(κ(𝔪^sh)/κ)` (`decompositionResidueHom`) is surjective with
  kernel `I`, so the diagonal `I → Gal(κ(𝔪^sh)/κ)` is trivial;
* there is an isomorphism `e : Gal(κ(𝔪^sh)/κ) ≅ π₁(X^h)` carrying the left vertical arrow to the
  arrow `π₁(U^h) → π₁(X^h)`: for `γ ∈ π₁(U^h)` corresponding to `τ ∈ D`, `e(τ̄) = γ|_{X^h}`;
  this is the identification `π₁(X^h) = Gal(κ(𝔪^sh)/κ)` of the lower left corner, and `e` is
  determined by this property since the left arrow is surjective;
* under `e` the bottom arrow `π₁(X^h) → π₁(X)` becomes the bottom arrow `Gal(κ(𝔪^sh)/κ) → π₁(X)`
  of the translated diagram, i.e. the square commutes: for `τ ∈ D`, the image of `e(τ̄)` in
  `π₁(X)` is the image of `τ` under the right vertical arrow (a heterogeneous equality, the two
  geometric points of `X` being equal only propositionally);
* the right vertical arrow `Gal(K^sep/K) = π₁(U) → π₁(X)` is surjective, and its kernel is the
  smallest closed normal subgroup of `Gal(K^sep/K)` containing `I`.
* the right vertical arrow is the arrow `absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup` of Stacks Tag 0BQM:
  every `σ ∈ Gal(K^sep/K)` lifts to an automorphism `τ` of `Ω` over the residue field of `X` at
  the generic point, and both arrows send them to the same element of `π₁(X)`.

The lower right corner `π₁(X)` is `Gal(M/K)` for `M` the maximal subextension of `K^sep/K`
unramified with respect to `A` by Stacks Tag 0BQM, which in this library is
`AlgebraicGeometry.fundamentalGroupIsoGalMaximalEtaleExtension`, carrying
`absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup` to restriction to `M`
(`Stacks.RamificationTheory.surjective_and_ker_absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup`); the last
clause on the right vertical arrow identifies it with that arrow, so under Tag 0BQM the right
vertical arrow is restriction `Gal(K^sep/K) → Gal(M/K)`.

The hypotheses are the source's: `A` a normal local domain, `K^sep` a separable closure of `K`,
`𝔪^sep` a maximal ideal over `𝔪`, `A^h` a henselization, `κ(𝔪^sh)` a separable closure of `κ`;
`K^sep` being separably closed, which the canonical map `A^h → (A^sep)_{𝔪^sep}` needs, is derived
from it being a separable closure.
declarations.statement:
theorem inertiaDiagram_translation [q.IsMaximal]
    (hcompat : letI : IsSepClosed L := IsSepClosure.sep_closed K
      ∀ x : Ah, algebraMap Kh L (algebraMap Ah Kh x) =
        IsIntegralClosure.henselizationToField A K L q Ah x)
    (κ : Type uk) [Field κ] [Algebra (A ⧸ maximalIdeal A) κ]
      [IsFractionRing (A ⧸ maximalIdeal A) κ]
    (κmsep : Type ul) [Field κmsep] [Algebra (integralClosure A L ⧸ q) κmsep]
      [IsFractionRing (integralClosure A L ⧸ q) κmsep]
      [Algebra (A ⧸ maximalIdeal A) κmsep]
      [IsScalarTower (A ⧸ maximalIdeal A) (integralClosure A L ⧸ q) κmsep]
      [Algebra κ κmsep] [IsScalarTower (A ⧸ maximalIdeal A) κ κmsep]
    (κmsh : Type us) [Field κmsh] [Algebra κ κmsh] [IsSepClosure κ κmsh]
      [Algebra κmsh κmsep] [IsScalarTower κ κmsh κmsep] :
    letI : ConnectedSpace (Spec (.of A)) := connectedSpace_spec_of_isLocalRing A
    letI : ConnectedSpace (Spec (.of Ah)) := connectedSpace_spec_of_isLocalRing Ah
    letI := IsIntegralClosure.isFractionRing_integralClosure A K L
    letI := IsIntegralClosure.galAction A K L
    letI := IsIntegralClosure.galSMulCommClass A K L
    ∃ hx : (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint Kh Ω).map
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K Kh))) = algebraicClosureGeometricPoint K Ω,
      -- the top row: `π₁(U^h) = D`, the top arrow being the inclusion
      (galoisEquivEtaleFundamentalGroup K L Ω) ⁻¹'
          Set.range (fun γ : EtaleFundamentalGroup (Spec (.of Kh))
              (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint Kh Ω) =>
            hx ▸ etaleFundamentalGroupMap (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K Kh)))
              (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint Kh Ω) γ) =
        (MulAction.stabilizer Gal(L/K) q : Set Gal(L/K)) ∧
      Function.Injective (fun γ : EtaleFundamentalGroup (Spec (.of Kh))
          (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint Kh Ω) =>
        hx ▸ etaleFundamentalGroupMap (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K Kh)))
          (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint Kh Ω) γ) ∧
      -- the top row: the image of `π₁(U^sh)` is `I`
      (∃ hx' : (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint
            (IsIntegralClosure.inertiaFixedField A K L q : Type u) Ω).map
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K
              (IsIntegralClosure.inertiaFixedField A K L q : Type u)))) =
          algebraicClosureGeometricPoint K Ω,
        (galoisEquivEtaleFundamentalGroup K L Ω) ⁻¹'
            Set.range (fun τ : EtaleFundamentalGroup
                (Spec (.of (IsIntegralClosure.inertiaFixedField A K L q : Type u)))
                (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint
                  (IsIntegralClosure.inertiaFixedField A K L q : Type u) Ω) =>
              hx' ▸ etaleFundamentalGroupMap (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K
                  (IsIntegralClosure.inertiaFixedField A K L q : Type u))))
                (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint
                  (IsIntegralClosure.inertiaFixedField A K L q : Type u) Ω) τ) =
          (q.inertia Gal(L/K) : Set Gal(L/K))) ∧
      -- the left vertical arrow `D → Gal(κ(𝔪^sh)/κ)`: surjective with kernel `I`
      Function.Surjective (decompositionResidueHom A K L (integralClosure A L) q κ κmsep κmsh) ∧
      (decompositionResidueHom A K L (integralClosure A L) q κ κmsep κmsh).ker =
        q.inertia (MulAction.stabilizer Gal(L/K) q) ∧
      -- the right vertical arrow: surjective, kernel the closed normal subgroup generated by `I`
      Function.Surjective (fun σ : Gal(L/K) =>
        etaleFundamentalGroupMap (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A K)))
          (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint K Ω) (galoisEquivEtaleFundamentalGroup K L Ω σ)) ∧
      Subgroup.comap (galoisEquivEtaleFundamentalGroup K L Ω).toMonoidHom
          (MonoidHom.ker (etaleFundamentalGroupMap
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A K)))
            (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint K Ω)).toMonoidHom) =
        (Subgroup.normalClosure
          ((q.inertia Gal(L/K) : Subgroup Gal(L/K)) : Set Gal(L/K))).topologicalClosure ∧
      -- the right vertical arrow is the arrow `absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup` of Tag 0BQM,
      -- whose target is `Gal(M/K)` through `fundamentalGroupIsoGalMaximalEtaleExtension`
      (∀ σ : Gal(L/K), ∃ τ : Gal(((algebraicClosureGeometricPoint K Ω).map
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A K)))).residueField /
          (Spec (.of A)).residueField (((algebraicClosureGeometricPoint K Ω).map
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A K)))).hom default)),
        (∀ y : L, τ (algebraMap L Ω y) = algebraMap L Ω (σ y)) ∧
        absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup (Spec (.of A))
            ((algebraicClosureGeometricPoint K Ω).map
              (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A K)))) τ =
          etaleFundamentalGroupMap (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A K)))
            (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint K Ω) (galoisEquivEtaleFundamentalGroup K L Ω σ)) ∧
      -- `π₁(X^h) = Gal(κ(𝔪^sh)/κ)`, carrying the left arrows to each other, and the square
      ∃ e : Gal(κmsh/κ) ≃* EtaleFundamentalGroup (Spec (.of Ah))
          ((algebraicClosureGeometricPoint Kh Ω).map
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Ah Kh)))),
        ∀ (γ : EtaleFundamentalGroup (Spec (.of Kh)) (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint Kh Ω))
          (τ : MulAction.stabilizer Gal(L/K) q),
          galoisEquivEtaleFundamentalGroup K L Ω τ =
              hx ▸ etaleFundamentalGroupMap (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K Kh)))
                (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint Kh Ω) γ →
            e (decompositionResidueHom A K L (integralClosure A L) q κ κmsep κmsh τ) =
                etaleFundamentalGroupMap (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Ah Kh)))
                  (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint Kh Ω) γ ∧
              HEq (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A Ah)))
                  ((algebraicClosureGeometricPoint Kh Ω).map
                    (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Ah Kh))))
                  (e (decompositionResidueHom A K L (integralClosure A L) q κ κmsep κmsh τ)))
                (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A K)))
                  (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint K Ω)
                  (galoisEquivEtaleFundamentalGroup K L Ω τ))
declarations.comment: the whole translated diagram: π₁(U^h) = D with the top arrow the inclusion, the image I of π₁(U^sh), the left vertical arrow D → Gal(κ(𝔪^sh)/κ) surjective with kernel I and identified with π₁(U^h) → π₁(X^h) through an isomorphism Gal(κ(𝔪^sh)/κ) ≅ π₁(X^h), the bottom arrow and the commutative square, and the right vertical arrow surjective with kernel the smallest closed normal subgroup containing I and equal to absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup, the arrow which Tag 0BQM identifies with restriction Gal(K^sep/K) → Gal(M/K)

declarations.name: IsIntegralClosure.image_stabilizer_and_inertia_restrictNormalHom
declarations.doc:
In a tower of possibly infinite Galois extensions, restriction maps the decomposition group
and the inertia group at a prime of the larger integral closure onto the corresponding groups at
its contraction to the smaller integral closure.
declarations.statement:
theorem image_stabilizer_and_inertia_restrictNormalHom
    (A : Type uA) (K : Type uK) (L : Type uL) (M : Type uM)
    (B : Type uB) (C : Type uC)
    [CommRing A] [Field K] [Field L] [Field M] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra A K] [Algebra K L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra K M]
    [Algebra A L] [Algebra A M] [IsScalarTower A K L] [IsScalarTower K L M]
    [IsScalarTower A K M] [IsScalarTower A L M]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra B L] [IsScalarTower A B L]
    [Algebra A C] [Algebra C M] [IsScalarTower A C M]
    [Algebra B C] [Algebra B M] [IsScalarTower A B C]
    [IsScalarTower B L M] [IsScalarTower B C M]
    [IsFractionRing A K] [IsFractionRing B L] [IsFractionRing C M]
    [IsIntegrallyClosed A] [IsIntegralClosure B A L] [IsIntegralClosure C A M]
    [IsGalois K L] [IsGalois K M]
    (r : Ideal C) [r.IsPrime] :
    letI := IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K M C
    letI : SMulCommClass Gal(M/K) A C :=
      ⟨fun σ a c ↦ by
        simp only [Algebra.smul_def, smul_mul']
        congr 1
        exact (galRestrict A K M C σ).commutes a⟩
    letI := IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K L B
    letI : SMulCommClass Gal(L/K) A B :=
      ⟨fun σ a b ↦ by
        simp only [Algebra.smul_def, smul_mul']
        congr 1
        exact (galRestrict A K L B σ).commutes a⟩
    let q := r.under B
    let res : Gal(M/K) →* Gal(L/K) := AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom L
    res '' (MulAction.stabilizer Gal(M/K) r : Set Gal(M/K)) =
        (MulAction.stabilizer Gal(L/K) q : Set Gal(L/K)) ∧
      res '' (r.inertia Gal(M/K) : Set Gal(M/K)) =
        (q.inertia Gal(L/K) : Set Gal(L/K))

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModule
declarations.doc:
The relative dualizing module `Hom_A(B', A) ⊗_{B'} B` of a finite-open factorization
`A → B' → B`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.exists_finite_subalgebra_dominating
declarations.doc:
Two finite algebra factorizations, the first of which induces an open immersion on spectra,
are dominated by a finite subalgebra inducing an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_finite_subalgebra_dominating
    {A : Type u} {B B₁ : Type v} {B₂ : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing B₁] [CommRing B₂]
    [Algebra A B]
    [Algebra A B₁] [Module.Finite A B₁] [Algebra A B₂] [Module.Finite A B₂]
    (f₁ : B₁ →ₐ[A] B) (f₂ : B₂ →ₐ[A] B)
    [IsOpenImmersion (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom f₁.toRingHom))] :
    ∃ C : Subalgebra A B,
      Module.Finite A C ∧
        IsOpenImmersion (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom C.val.toRingHom)) ∧
          (∃ g₁ : B₁ →ₐ[A] C, C.val.comp g₁ = f₁) ∧
            ∃ g₂ : B₂ →ₐ[A] C, C.val.comp g₂ = f₂

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModuleEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BT1.** The dualizing modules obtained from any two
finite-open factorizations are canonically equivalent as modules over the target.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dualizingModuleEquiv
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, x} A B) :
    dualizingModule F ≃ₗ[B] dualizingModule G
declarations.comment: canonical comparison

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModuleEquiv_tmul
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison carries a tensor arising from a functional on a common finite-open
refinement inside the target to the tensor induced by the same functional in the other
factorization.  Injectivity of the map to the target expresses the subalgebra condition in
Tag 0BT0 used by the source proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingModuleEquiv_tmul
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, x} A B)
    (H : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, y} A B)
    (hH : Function.Injective (algebraMap H.middle B))
    (rF : F.middle →ₐ[A] H.middle)
    (rG : G.middle →ₐ[A] H.middle)
    (hF : ∀ c : F.middle,
      algebraMap H.middle B (rF c) = algebraMap F.middle B c)
    (hG : ∀ c : G.middle,
      algebraMap H.middle B (rG c) = algebraMap G.middle B c)
    (φ : Module.Dual A H.middle) (b : B) :
    dualizingModuleEquiv F G
        (dualizingModule.tmul F (φ.comp rF.toLinearMap) b) =
      dualizingModule.tmul G (φ.comp rG.toLinearMap) b
declarations.comment: characterization on a common refinement

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModuleEquiv_refl
declarations.doc: The canonical comparison of a factorization with itself is the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingModuleEquiv_refl
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B) :
    dualizingModuleEquiv F F = LinearEquiv.refl B (dualizingModule F)
declarations.comment: identity comparison

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModuleEquiv_trans
declarations.doc: Canonical comparisons compose independently of an intermediate factorization.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingModuleEquiv_trans
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, x} A B)
    (H : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, y} A B) :
    (dualizingModuleEquiv F G).trans (dualizingModuleEquiv G H) =
      dualizingModuleEquiv F H
declarations.comment: composition of comparisons

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModule_equiv_of_isLocalization_away
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BT2, part (1).** If `A → B` factors through the localization of
`A` away from `f`, then computing the relative dualizing module over that localization does not
change it.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def dualizingModule_equiv_of_isLocalization_away
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {Af : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing Af]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A Af] [Algebra Af B] [IsScalarTower A Af B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    (f : A) [IsLocalization.Away f Af]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, x} A B)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{w, v, y} Af B) :
    dualizingModule F ≃ₗ[B] dualizingModule G
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModule_equiv_of_isLocalization_away_tmul
declarations.doc:
The base-localization identification carries a functional to its scalar extension along a
compatible finite-open factorization.  The displayed equation characterizes this operation on
generators and avoids treating the equivalence as an arbitrary module isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dualizingModule_equiv_of_isLocalization_away_tmul
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {Af : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing Af]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A Af] [Algebra Af B] [IsScalarTower A Af B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    (f : A) [IsLocalization.Away f Af]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, x} A B)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{w, v, y} Af B)
    [Algebra A G.middle] [IsScalarTower A Af G.middle]
    (r : F.middle →ₐ[A] G.middle)
    (hrloc : letI := r.toRingHom.toAlgebra
      IsLocalization.Away (algebraMap A F.middle f) G.middle)
    (hr : ∀ c : F.middle,
      G.algebraTarget.algebraMap (r c) = F.algebraTarget.algebraMap c)
    (φ : Module.Dual A F.middle) (ψ : Module.Dual Af G.middle)
    (hψ : ∀ c : F.middle, ψ (r c) = algebraMap A Af (φ c)) (b : B) :
    dualizingModule_equiv_of_isLocalization_away f F G
        (dualizingModule.tmul F φ b) = dualizingModule.tmul G ψ b
declarations.comment: part (1), characterization

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModule_equiv_of_isLocalization_away_natural
declarations.doc: Changing either finite-open factorization does not change the base-localization map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dualizingModule_equiv_of_isLocalization_away_natural
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {Af : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing Af]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A Af] [Algebra Af B] [IsScalarTower A Af B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsNoetherianRing Af]
    [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    (f : A) [IsLocalization.Away f Af]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, x} A B)
    (F' : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, z} A B)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{w, v, y} Af B)
    (G' : FiniteOpenFactorization.{w, v, t} Af B) (m : dualizingModule F) :
    dualizingModuleEquiv G G'
        (dualizingModule_equiv_of_isLocalization_away f F G m) =
      dualizingModule_equiv_of_isLocalization_away f F' G'
        (dualizingModuleEquiv F F' m)
declarations.comment: part (1), naturality

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv_of_baseLocalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BT2, part (3).** After localizing the base away from `f` and the
target away from its image, the relative dualizing module is the corresponding localization of
the original relative dualizing module.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv_of_baseLocalization
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {Af : Type w} {Bf : Type x} {M : Type y}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing Af] [CommRing Bf]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A Af] [Algebra B Bf] [Algebra A Bf] [Algebra Af Bf]
    [IsScalarTower A B Bf] [IsScalarTower A Af Bf]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    (f : A) [IsLocalization.Away f Af]
    [IsLocalization.Away (algebraMap A B f) Bf]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, z} A B)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{w, x, q} Af Bf)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [Module Bf M] [IsScalarTower B Bf M]
    (localizationMap : dualizingModule F →ₗ[B] M)
    (hM : IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (algebraMap A B f)) localizationMap) :
    M ≃ₗ[Bf] dualizingModule G
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv_of_baseLocalization_eq_comp
declarations.doc:
Simultaneous localization is the composite of localization in the target and replacement
of the base by its localization.  This fixes the canonical identification, rather than merely
asserting the existence of a linear equivalence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv_of_baseLocalization_eq_comp
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {Af : Type w} {Bf : Type x} {M : Type y}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing Af] [CommRing Bf]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A Af] [Algebra B Bf] [Algebra A Bf] [Algebra Af Bf]
    [IsScalarTower A B Bf] [IsScalarTower A Af Bf]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsNoetherianRing Bf]
    [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A Bf]
    (f : A) [IsLocalization.Away f Af]
    [IsLocalization.Away (algebraMap A B f) Bf]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, z} A B)
    (H : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, x, t} A Bf)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{w, x, q} Af Bf)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [Module Bf M] [IsScalarTower B Bf M]
    (localizationMap : dualizingModule F →ₗ[B] M)
    (hM : IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (algebraMap A B f)) localizationMap) :
    localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv_of_baseLocalization
        f F G localizationMap hM =
      (localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv
        (algebraMap A B f) F H localizationMap hM).trans
        (dualizingModule_equiv_of_isLocalization_away f H G)
declarations.comment: part (3), compatibility with parts (1) and (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BT2, part (2).** Localizing the relative dualizing module away from
an element of the target gives the relative dualizing module of the localized target.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {Bg : Type w} {M : Type x}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing Bg]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra B Bg] [Algebra A Bg] [IsScalarTower A B Bg]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    (g : B) [IsLocalization.Away g Bg]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, y} A B)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, z} A Bg)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [Module Bg M] [IsScalarTower B Bg M]
    (localizationMap : dualizingModule F →ₗ[B] M)
    (hM : IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers g) localizationMap) :
    M ≃ₗ[Bg] dualizingModule G
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv_tmul
declarations.doc:
On compatible finite-open factorizations, the target-localization map sends a pure tensor
to the tensor obtained by localizing its coefficient in the target.
declarations.statement:
public theorem localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv_tmul
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {Bg : Type w} {M : Type x}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing Bg]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra B Bg] [Algebra A Bg] [IsScalarTower A B Bg]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    (g : B) [IsLocalization.Away g Bg]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, y} A B)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, z} A Bg)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [Module Bg M] [IsScalarTower B Bg M]
    (localizationMap : dualizingModule F →ₗ[B] M)
    (hM : IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers g) localizationMap)
    (r : G.middle ≃ₐ[A] F.middle)
    (hr : ∀ c : G.middle,
      algebraMap B Bg (F.algebraTarget.algebraMap (r c)) =
        G.algebraTarget.algebraMap c)
    (φ : Module.Dual A F.middle) (b : B) :
    localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv g F G localizationMap hM
        (localizationMap (dualizingModule.tmul F φ b)) =
      dualizingModule.tmul G (φ.comp r.toLinearMap) (algebraMap B Bg b)
declarations.comment: part (2), characterization

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv_natural
declarations.doc:
The target-localization identification is natural in the finite-open factorization of the
localized algebra.
declarations.statement:
public theorem localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv_natural
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {Bg : Type w} {M : Type x}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing Bg]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra B Bg] [Algebra A Bg] [IsScalarTower A B Bg]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    (g : B) [IsLocalization.Away g Bg]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, y} A B)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, z} A Bg)
    (G' : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, t} A Bg)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [Module Bg M] [IsScalarTower B Bg M]
    (localizationMap : dualizingModule F →ₗ[B] M)
    (hM : IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers g) localizationMap) (m : M) :
    dualizingModuleEquiv G G'
        (localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv g F G localizationMap hM m) =
      localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv g F G' localizationMap hM m
declarations.comment: part (2), naturality

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv_natural_in_source
declarations.doc:
