Localization commutes with the canonical comparison of two factorizations of the original
algebra, as well as with the comparison of factorizations after localization.  A map between
abstract localized modules is specified by its action on their localization maps.
declarations.statement:
public theorem localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv_natural_in_source
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {Bg : Type w} {M : Type x} {M' : Type y}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing Bg]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra B Bg] [Algebra A Bg] [IsScalarTower A B Bg]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    (g : B) [IsLocalization.Away g Bg]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, z} A B)
    (F' : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, t} A B)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, q} A Bg)
    (G' : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, s} A Bg)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [Module Bg M] [IsScalarTower B Bg M]
    [AddCommGroup M'] [Module B M'] [Module Bg M'] [IsScalarTower B Bg M']
    (localizationMap : dualizingModule F →ₗ[B] M)
    (hM : IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers g) localizationMap)
    (localizationMap' : dualizingModule F' →ₗ[B] M')
    (hM' : IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers g) localizationMap')
    (comparison : M →ₗ[Bg] M')
    (hcomparison : ∀ m : dualizingModule F,
      comparison (localizationMap m) =
        localizationMap' (dualizingModuleEquiv F F' m))
    (m : M) :
    dualizingModuleEquiv G G'
        (localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv g F G localizationMap hM m) =
      localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv g F' G' localizationMap' hM'
        (comparison m)
declarations.comment: part (2), naturality in both factorizations

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModule_isBaseChange_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BT3.** Flat base change identifies the scalar extension of
the relative dualizing module with the relative dualizing module after base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingModule_isBaseChange_of_flat
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B)
    (A₁ : Type x) [CommRing A₁] [Algebra A A₁] [Module.Flat A A₁] :
    letI : Algebra B (A₁ ⊗[A] B) := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    letI : Module B
        (dualizingModule (FiniteOpenFactorization.baseChange F A₁)) :=
      Module.compHom _ (algebraMap B (A₁ ⊗[A] B))
    letI : IsScalarTower B (A₁ ⊗[A] B)
        (dualizingModule (FiniteOpenFactorization.baseChange F A₁)) :=
      IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul (fun _ _ => rfl)
    IsBaseChange (A₁ ⊗[A] B) (dualizingModule.baseChange F A₁)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModule.comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BT4.** The canonical composition map for relative
dualizing modules of two composable quasi-finite algebra maps.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def comp
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {C : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsNoetherianRing C]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, x} A B)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{v, w, y} B C)
    (H : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, z} A C) :
    letI : Module B (dualizingModule G) :=
      Module.compHom _ (algebraMap B C)
    letI : SMulCommClass B C (dualizingModule G) :=
      ⟨fun b c m => by
        change (algebraMap B C b) • c • m = c • (algebraMap B C b) • m
        rw [smul_comm]⟩
    letI : Module C
        (dualizingModule G ⊗[B] dualizingModule F) :=
      TensorProduct.leftModule
    letI : Module C
        (dualizingModule F ⊗[B] dualizingModule G) :=
      (TensorProduct.comm B (dualizingModule F)
        (dualizingModule G)).toAddEquiv.module C
    (dualizingModule F ⊗[B] dualizingModule G) →ₗ[C]
      dualizingModule H

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModule.comp_of_compatible
declarations.doc:
For compatible finite-open factorizations, a functional on the middle
algebra that descends to the finite intermediate algebra composes with the
first functional. This applies to nonfinite quasi-finite maps as well.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_of_compatible
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {C : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsNoetherianRing C]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, x} A B)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{v, w, y} B C)
    (H : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, z} A C)
    [Algebra F.middle H.middle] [IsScalarTower A F.middle H.middle]
    (j : H.middle →+* G.middle)
    (hjF : ∀ s : F.middle,
      j (algebraMap F.middle H.middle s) =
        algebraMap B G.middle (algebraMap F.middle B s))
    (hjC : ∀ t : H.middle,
      algebraMap G.middle C (j t) = algebraMap H.middle C t)
    (hjspan : Submodule.span B (Set.range j) = ⊤)
    (f : Module.Dual A F.middle) (g : Module.Dual B G.middle)
    (g' : Module.Dual F.middle H.middle)
    (hg : ∀ t : H.middle, g (j t) = algebraMap F.middle B (g' t))
    (d : F.middle) (c : C) :
    letI : Module B (dualizingModule G) :=
      Module.compHom _ (algebraMap B C)
    letI : SMulCommClass B C (dualizingModule G) :=
      ⟨fun b c m => by
        change (algebraMap B C b) • c • m = c • (algebraMap B C b) • m
        rw [smul_comm]⟩
    letI : Module C
        (dualizingModule G ⊗[B] dualizingModule F) :=
      TensorProduct.leftModule
    letI : Module C
        (dualizingModule F ⊗[B] dualizingModule G) :=
      (TensorProduct.comm B (dualizingModule F)
        (dualizingModule G)).toAddEquiv.module C
    ∃ h : Module.Dual A H.middle,
      (comp F G H ((dualizingModule.tmul F f
          (algebraMap F.middle B d)) ⊗ₜ[B]
        (dualizingModule.tmul G g c)) =
          dualizingModule.tmul H h c) ∧
      (∀ t : H.middle,
        h t = f (d * g' t))
declarations.comment: composition of Hom maps for compatible factorizations

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModule.comp_naturality
declarations.doc:
The composition map commutes with the canonical comparison isomorphisms
when any of the three finite-open factorizations is changed.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_naturality
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {C : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsNoetherianRing C]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, x} A B)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{v, w, y} B C)
    (H : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, z} A C)
    (F' : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, x'} A B)
    (G' : FiniteOpenFactorization.{v, w, y'} B C)
    (H' : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, z'} A C)
    (ω : dualizingModule F)
    (η : dualizingModule G) :
    letI : Module B (dualizingModule G) :=
      Module.compHom _ (algebraMap B C)
    letI : SMulCommClass B C (dualizingModule G) :=
      ⟨fun b c m => by
        change (algebraMap B C b) • c • m = c • (algebraMap B C b) • m
        rw [smul_comm]⟩
    letI : Module C
        (dualizingModule G ⊗[B] dualizingModule F) :=
      TensorProduct.leftModule
    letI : Module C
        (dualizingModule F ⊗[B] dualizingModule G) :=
      (TensorProduct.comm B (dualizingModule F)
        (dualizingModule G)).toAddEquiv.module C
    letI : Module B (dualizingModule G') :=
      Module.compHom _ (algebraMap B C)
    letI : SMulCommClass B C (dualizingModule G') :=
      ⟨fun b c m => by
        change (algebraMap B C b) • c • m = c • (algebraMap B C b) • m
        rw [smul_comm]⟩
    letI : Module C
        (dualizingModule G' ⊗[B] dualizingModule F') :=
      TensorProduct.leftModule
    letI : Module C
        (dualizingModule F' ⊗[B] dualizingModule G') :=
      (TensorProduct.comm B (dualizingModule F')
        (dualizingModule G')).toAddEquiv.module C
    comp F' G' H'
        ((dualizingModuleEquiv F F' ω) ⊗ₜ[B]
          (dualizingModuleEquiv G G' η)) =
      dualizingModuleEquiv H H' (comp F G H (ω ⊗ₜ[B] η))
declarations.comment: independence of factorization

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModuleProdEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BT5.** The dualizing module of a product of quasi-finite
Noetherian algebras is canonically the product of their dualizing modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dualizingModuleProdEquiv
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {C : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A C]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsNoetherianRing C]
    [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A C]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, max v w, x} A (B × C))
    (FB : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, y} A B)
    (FC : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, z} A C) :
    letI : Module (B × C) (dualizingModule FB) :=
      Module.compHom _ (RingHom.fst B C)
    letI : Module (B × C) (dualizingModule FC) :=
      Module.compHom _ (RingHom.snd B C)
    dualizingModule F ≃ₗ[B × C] (dualizingModule FB × dualizingModule FC)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModuleProdEquiv_tmul
declarations.doc:
For a product factorization, the product equivalence sends a pure tensor to the pair
obtained by restricting its functional to the two factors and projecting its coefficient.
The compatibility condition identifies the map from the middle algebra to the product target
with the componentwise maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingModuleProdEquiv_tmul
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {C : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A C]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsNoetherianRing C]
    [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A C]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, max v w, x} A (B × C))
    (FB : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, y} A B)
    (FC : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, z} A C)
    (e : (FB.middle × FC.middle) ≃ₐ[A] F.middle)
    (hcompat : ∀ p : FB.middle × FC.middle,
      (algebraMap F.middle (B × C)) (e p) =
        ((algebraMap FB.middle B) p.1, (algebraMap FC.middle C) p.2))
    (f : Module.Dual A F.middle) (b : B) (c : C) :
    (dualizingModuleProdEquiv F FB FC) (dualizingModule.tmul F f (b, c)) =
      (dualizingModule.tmul FB
        (f.comp (e.toLinearMap.comp (LinearMap.inl A FB.middle FC.middle))) b,
       dualizingModule.tmul FC
        (f.comp (e.toLinearMap.comp (LinearMap.inr A FB.middle FC.middle))) c)
declarations.comment: pure-tensor formula for a product factorization

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModuleProdEquiv_naturality
declarations.doc:
Changing the finite-open factorizations of the product and its two factors commutes
with the canonical product equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingModuleProdEquiv_naturality
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {C : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A C]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsNoetherianRing C]
    [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A C]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, max v w, x} A (B × C))
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, max v w, x'} A (B × C))
    (FB : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, y} A B)
    (GB : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, y'} A B)
    (FC : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, z} A C)
    (GC : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, z'} A C)
    (ω : dualizingModule F) :
    (dualizingModuleProdEquiv G GB GC) (dualizingModuleEquiv F G ω) =
      (dualizingModuleEquiv FB GB
        ((dualizingModuleProdEquiv F FB FC ω).1),
       dualizingModuleEquiv FC GC
        ((dualizingModuleProdEquiv F FB FC ω).2))
declarations.comment: independence of factorization

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.finiteFactorRestriction
declarations.doc:
The canonical restriction of a relative dualizing element to a finite direct factor
after base change, together with the pure-tensor formula that characterizes it. The formula
is the first component of the product map of Tag 0BT5, written through the finite-projective
trace of the factor over the intermediate algebra.
declarations.statement:
def finiteFactorRestriction
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B)
    (A₁ : Type x) [CommRing A₁] [Algebra A A₁]
    (C : Type y) (D : Type z) [CommRing C] [CommRing D]
    [Algebra A₁ C] [Algebra A₁ D]
    (e : (A₁ ⊗[A] B) ≃ₐ[A₁] (C × D))
    [Algebra (FiniteOpenFactorization.baseChange F A₁).middle C]
    (hcompat : ∀ a : (FiniteOpenFactorization.baseChange F A₁).middle,
      algebraMap _ C a =
        (e (algebraMap _ (A₁ ⊗[A] B) a)).1)
    (hfinite : Module.Finite A₁ C)
    (hprojective : Module.Projective A₁ C)
    (hmfinite : Module.Finite
      (FiniteOpenFactorization.baseChange F A₁).middle C)
    (hmprojective : Module.Projective
      (FiniteOpenFactorization.baseChange F A₁).middle C) :
    let F₁ := FiniteOpenFactorization.baseChange F A₁
    letI : Module A₁ (dualizingModule F₁) :=
      Module.compHom _ (algebraMap A₁ (A₁ ⊗[A] B))
    { h : dualizingModule F₁ →ₗ[A₁] Module.Dual A₁ C //
      letI : Module.Finite F₁.middle C := hmfinite
      letI : Module.Projective F₁.middle C := hmprojective
      ∀ (f : Module.Dual A₁ F₁.middle) (b : A₁ ⊗[A] B) (c : C),
        h (dualizingModule.tmul F₁ f b) c =
          f ((finiteProjectiveTrace F₁.middle C)
            (Algebra.lmul F₁.middle C ((e b).1 * c))) }
declarations.comment: the restriction of a dualizing element to a finite direct factor

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.IsTraceElement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BT6.** A trace element is an element of the relative dualizing
module whose image in every finite direct factor, after an arbitrary Noetherian base change,
is the finite-projective trace of that factor.
declarations.statement:
def IsTraceElement
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [Module.Flat A B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B)
    (τ : dualizingModule F) : Prop
declarations.comment: trace_element_property

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isTraceElement_congr
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BT6.** The trace-element condition does not depend on the
finite-open factorization chosen to represent the relative dualizing module. The three test
universes are independent of each other and of the universes of the two factorizations.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTraceElement_congr
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Module.Flat A B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, x} A B)
    (τ : dualizingModule F) :
    IsTraceElement.{u, v, w, s, t, r} F τ ↔
      IsTraceElement.{u, v, x, s, t, r} G (dualizingModuleEquiv F G τ)
declarations.comment: trace_element_property; independence of factorization

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isTraceElement_unique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BT7.** A flat quasi-finite algebra of Noetherian rings has at most
one trace element.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTraceElement_unique
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [Module.Flat A B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B)
    {τ₁ τ₂ : dualizingModule F}
    (h₁ : IsTraceElement.{u, v, w, u, max u v, max u v} F τ₁)
    (h₂ : IsTraceElement.{u, v, w, u, max u v, max u v} F τ₂) :
    τ₁ = τ₂

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isTraceElement_finiteFlatTraceElement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BT8.** For a finite flat map of Noetherian rings, the ordinary
trace of the finite projective algebra is a trace element of the relative dualizing module.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTraceElement_finiteFlatTraceElement (A : Type u) (B : Type v)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [Module.Finite A B] [Module.Flat A B] :
    IsTraceElement.{u, v, v, x, y, z} (selfFactorization A B) (finiteFlatTraceElement A B)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isTraceElement_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BT9.** The image of a trace element under the base-change map of
the relative dualizing module is a trace element over the new base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTraceElement_baseChange
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Module.Flat A B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B)
    (A₁ : Type x) [CommRing A₁] [Algebra A A₁] [IsNoetherianRing A₁]
    (τ : dualizingModule F) (hτ : IsTraceElement.{u, v, w, s, t, r} F τ) :
    letI : IsNoetherianRing (A₁ ⊗[A] B) := Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing A₁ _
    IsTraceElement.{x, max x v, max x w, s, t, r}
      (FiniteOpenFactorization.baseChange F A₁) (dualizingModule.baseChange F A₁ τ)
declarations.comment: trace_base_change

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isTraceElement_of_isLocalization_away
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BT9.** A trace element of the relative dualizing module over a
localization of the base remains a trace element over the original base, under the
identification of Tag 0BT2, part (1).

The trace-element condition over `R` tests a decomposition `S ⊗_R B ≃ C × D` with `C` finite
over `S`. Since `f` becomes invertible in `B`, it is invertible in `C`, so the same decomposition
is visible over the localization `S_f`, where the condition over `A` applies. The two
restriction functionals to `C` differ by the localization map `S → S_f`, and a functional on a
finite module is determined by its image there.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTraceElement_of_isLocalization_away
    {R : Type u} {A : Type v} {B : Type w}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra A B] [Algebra R B] [IsScalarTower R A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [Module.Flat A B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    (f : R) [IsLocalization.Away f A]
    (FR : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, x} R B)
    (FA : FiniteOpenFactorization.{v, w, y} A B)
    (τ : dualizingModule FA) (hτ : IsTraceElement.{v, w, y, s, t, z} FA τ) :
    letI : Module.Flat R A := IsLocalization.flat A (Submonoid.powers f)
    letI : Algebra.QuasiFinite R A :=
      Algebra.QuasiFinite.of_isLocalization (Submonoid.powers f)
    letI : Module.Flat R B := Module.Flat.trans R A B
    letI : Algebra.QuasiFinite R B := Algebra.QuasiFinite.trans R A B
    IsTraceElement.{u, w, x, s, t, z} FR
      ((dualizingModule_equiv_of_isLocalization_away f FR FA).symm τ)
declarations.comment: trace_base_localization

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isTraceElement_fst
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BT9.** A trace element of the relative dualizing module of a
product restricts to a trace element on the first factor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTraceElement_fst [Module.Flat A B]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, max v w, x} A (B × C))
    (FB : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, y} A B)
    (FC : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, z} A C)
    {τ : dualizingModule F}
    (hτ : IsTraceElement.{u, max v w, x, s, t, max r (max s w)} F τ) :
    IsTraceElement.{u, v, y, s, t, r} FB ((dualizingModuleProdEquiv F FB FC τ).1)
declarations.comment: trace_product_factors

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isTraceElement_snd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BT9.** A trace element of the relative dualizing module of a
product restricts to a trace element on the second factor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTraceElement_snd [Module.Flat A C]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, max v w, x} A (B × C))
    (FB : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, y} A B)
    (FC : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, z} A C)
    {τ : dualizingModule F}
    (hτ : IsTraceElement.{u, max v w, x, s, t, max r (max s v)} F τ) :
    IsTraceElement.{u, w, z, s, t, r} FC ((dualizingModuleProdEquiv F FB FC τ).2)
declarations.comment: trace_product_factors

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isTraceElement_localization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BT9.** A trace element of the relative dualizing module of a flat
quasi-finite map of Noetherian rings remains a trace element after an away localization of the
target, under the identification of Tag 0BT2, part (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem isTraceElement_localization
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {Bg : Type w} {M : Type x}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing Bg]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra B Bg] [Algebra A Bg] [IsScalarTower A B Bg]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [Module.Flat A B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    (g : B) [IsLocalization.Away g Bg]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, y} A B)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, z} A Bg)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [Module Bg M] [IsScalarTower B Bg M]
    (localizationMap : dualizingModule F →ₗ[B] M)
    (hM : IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers g) localizationMap)
    {τ : dualizingModule F} (hτ : IsTraceElement.{u, v, y, s, t, max s v} F τ) :
    letI : IsNoetherianRing Bg :=
      IsLocalization.isNoetherianRing (Submonoid.powers g) Bg inferInstance
    letI : Module.Flat B Bg := IsLocalization.flat Bg (Submonoid.powers g)
    letI : Module.Flat A Bg := Module.Flat.trans A B Bg
    letI : Algebra.QuasiFinite A Bg :=
      Algebra.QuasiFinite.of_isLocalization (Submonoid.powers g)
    IsTraceElement.{u, w, z, s, t, r} G
      (localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv g F G localizationMap hM
        (localizationMap τ))
declarations.comment: trace_algebra_localization

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isTraceElement_of_localization_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BTA.** A section of the relative dualizing module of a flat
quasi-finite map of Noetherian rings which is a trace element on every member of a finite
principal open cover of the target is a trace element.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTraceElement_of_localization_cover
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Module.Flat A B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B)
    {n : ℕ} (g : Fin n → B) (hcover : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤)
    (τ : dualizingModule F)
    (G : ∀ i : Fin n, FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, z} A (Localization.Away (g i)))
    (hlocal : ∀ i : Fin n,
      letI : IsNoetherianRing (Localization.Away (g i)) :=
        IsLocalization.isNoetherianRing (Submonoid.powers (g i))
          (Localization.Away (g i)) inferInstance
      letI : Module.Flat B (Localization.Away (g i)) :=
        IsLocalization.flat (Localization.Away (g i)) (Submonoid.powers (g i))
      letI : Module.Flat A (Localization.Away (g i)) :=
        Module.Flat.trans A B (Localization.Away (g i))
      letI : Algebra.QuasiFinite A (Localization.Away (g i)) :=
        Algebra.QuasiFinite.of_isLocalization (Submonoid.powers (g i))
      IsTraceElement.{u, v, z, s, t, r} (G i)
        (localizedModule_dualizingModule_equiv (g i) F (G i)
          (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers (g i)) (dualizingModule F))
          (inferInstance : IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (g i))
            (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers (g i)) (dualizingModule F)))
          (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers (g i)) (dualizingModule F) τ))) :
    IsTraceElement.{u, v, w, s, t, r} F τ

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.exists_isTraceElement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BTB.** A flat quasi-finite map of Noetherian rings has a trace
element in its relative dualizing module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isTraceElement (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B) :
    ∃ τ : dualizingModule F, IsTraceElement.{u, v, w, x, y, z} F τ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalClosure_iUnion_ker_topologicalClosure_le_ker
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BTD, the inclusion of subgroup (3) in subgroup (1).** Let `X` be an
integral scheme with function field `K`. The smallest closed normal subgroup of `π₁(Spec K)`
containing the kernel of `π₁(Spec K) → π₁(Spec 𝒪_{X,x})` for every point `x` of `X` is contained
in the kernel of `π₁(Spec K) → π₁(X)`.

For `X` normal the generating kernels are exactly the closed normal subgroups generated by the
images of the `π₁(Spec K_x^sh)`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.ker_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_stalk_eq_normalClosure_topologicalClosure`
together with
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.normalClosure_iUnion_topologicalClosure_eq`, so the subgroup on the left
is the third subgroup of the source and the one on the right is the first.
declarations.statement:
theorem normalClosure_iUnion_ker_topologicalClosure_le_ker [IsIntegral X]
    (p : GeometricPoint (Spec (X.residueField (genericPoint X)))) :
    (Subgroup.normalClosure (⋃ x : X,
          (((etaleFundamentalGroupMap (Spec.map (stalkToGenericResidueField X x))
            p).toMonoidHom.ker : Subgroup (EtaleFundamentalGroup
              (Spec (X.residueField (genericPoint X))) p)) : Set _))).topologicalClosure ≤
      (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (X.fromSpecResidueField (genericPoint X))
        p).toMonoidHom.ker
declarations.comment: the inclusion of subgroup (3) in subgroup (1), and only that inclusion: subgroup (1) is the kernel of π₁(Spec K) → π₁(X) rather than the subgroup fixing the maximal unramified subextension, so no Noetherian hypothesis is needed, and subgroup (3) is written with the kernels of π₁(Spec K) → π₁(Spec 𝒪_{X,x}) as generators; subgroup (2) is AlgebraicGeometry.inertiaClosedNormalSubgroup below

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ker_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_stalk_eq_normalClosure_topologicalClosure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BTD, the generators of subgroup (3).** Let `X` be a normal integral
scheme with function field `K`, let `x` be a point of `X`, let `Ash` be a strict henselization of
`𝒪_{X,x}` and let `Ksh = K_x^sh` be its fraction field. The kernel of
`π₁(Spec K) → π₁(Spec 𝒪_{X,x})` is the smallest closed normal subgroup of `π₁(Spec K)`
containing the image of `π₁(Spec Ksh) = Gal(K^sep/K_x^sh)`.

This is the local exact sequence of Stacks Tag 0BSM applied to the local ring at `x`, whose
fraction field is the function field of `X` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isFractionRing_stalk_genericResidueField`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ker_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_stalk_eq_normalClosure_topologicalClosure
    [IsIntegral X] [IsNormal X] (x : X) (κsep Ash Ksh : Type u)
    [CommRing Ash] [IsLocalRing Ash] [Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) Ash]
    [Field κsep] [Algebra (ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x)) κsep]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x)) κsep]
    [IsHenselization (X.presheaf.stalk x) κsep Ash]
    [Field Ksh] [Algebra Ash Ksh] [IsFractionRing Ash Ksh]
    [Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) Ksh]
    [Algebra (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ksh]
    [IsScalarTower (X.presheaf.stalk x) (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ksh]
    [IsScalarTower (X.presheaf.stalk x) Ash Ksh]
    (q : GeometricPoint (Spec (.of Ksh))) :
    (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (Spec.map (stalkToGenericResidueField X x))
        (q.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ksh))))).toMonoidHom.ker =
      (Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range (etaleFundamentalGroupMap
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ksh))) q))).topologicalClosure
declarations.comment: that each generator of subgroup (3) used here — the kernel of π₁(Spec K) → π₁(Spec 𝒪_{X,x}) — is the smallest closed normal subgroup containing the image of π₁(Spec K_x^sh) = Gal(K^sep/K_x^sh), which is how the source presents subgroup (3); this is Tag 0BSM applied to the local rings of X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalClosure_range_topologicalClosure_le_ker
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BTD, one generator of subgroup (3) lies in subgroup (1).** Let `X` be
a normal integral scheme with function field `K`, let `x` be a point of `X`, let `Ash` be a
strict henselization of `𝒪_{X,x}` and let `Ksh = K_x^sh` be its fraction field. The smallest
closed normal subgroup of `π₁(Spec K)` containing the image of
`π₁(Spec K_x^sh) = Gal(K^sep/K_x^sh)` is contained in the kernel of `π₁(Spec K) → π₁(X)`.

This is the first paragraph of the source's proof, one point of `X` at a time: the image is
killed already by `π₁(Spec K) → π₁(Spec 𝒪_{X,x})`, by the local exact sequence of Stacks Tag
0BSM, and that homomorphism is a factor of `π₁(Spec K) → π₁(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem normalClosure_range_topologicalClosure_le_ker
    [IsIntegral X] [IsNormal X] (x : X) (κsep Ash Ksh : Type u)
    [CommRing Ash] [IsLocalRing Ash] [Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) Ash]
    [Field κsep] [Algebra (ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x)) κsep]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x)) κsep]
    [IsHenselization (X.presheaf.stalk x) κsep Ash]
    [Field Ksh] [Algebra Ash Ksh] [IsFractionRing Ash Ksh]
    [Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) Ksh]
    [Algebra (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ksh]
    [IsScalarTower (X.presheaf.stalk x) (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ksh]
    [IsScalarTower (X.presheaf.stalk x) Ash Ksh]
    (q : GeometricPoint (Spec (.of Ksh))) :
    (Subgroup.normalClosure (Set.range (etaleFundamentalGroupMap
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
            (algebraMap (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ksh))) q))).topologicalClosure ≤
      (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (X.fromSpecResidueField (genericPoint X))
        (q.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ksh))))).toMonoidHom.ker
declarations.comment: that each generator Gal(K^sep/K_x^sh) of subgroup (3) generates a closed normal subgroup contained in subgroup (1), one point x of X at a time; subgroup (1) is the kernel of π₁(Spec K) → π₁(X), so no Noetherian hypothesis is needed; subgroup (2) is AlgebraicGeometry.inertiaClosedNormalSubgroup below

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.comap_normalClosure_iUnion_ker_le_ker_galoisToFundamentalGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BTD, the inclusion of subgroup (3) in subgroup (1), inside
`Gal(K^sep/K)`.** Transporting along the identification `Gal(K^sep/K) = π₁(Spec K)` of Stacks Tag
0BNE, the smallest closed normal subgroup of `Gal(K^sep/K)` containing the kernel of
`Gal(K^sep/K) → π₁(Spec 𝒪_{X,x})` for every point `x` of `X` is contained in the kernel of
`Gal(K^sep/K) → π₁(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem comap_normalClosure_iUnion_ker_le_ker_galoisToFundamentalGroup :
    Subgroup.comap (galoisEquivEtaleFundamentalGroup
        (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) L Ω).toMonoidHom
      ((Subgroup.normalClosure (⋃ x : X,
          (((etaleFundamentalGroupMap (Spec.map (stalkToGenericResidueField X x))
            (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint
              (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ω)).toMonoidHom.ker : Subgroup
                (EtaleFundamentalGroup (Spec (X.residueField (genericPoint X)))
                  (algebraicClosureGeometricPoint
                    (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ω))) : Set _))).topologicalClosure) ≤
      (galoisToFundamentalGroup X L Ω).toMonoidHom.ker
declarations.comment: the inclusion of subgroup (3) in subgroup (1) read inside Gal(K^sep/K) through the identification of Tag 0BNE; subgroup (3) is written with the kernels of π₁(Spec K) → π₁(Spec 𝒪_{X,x}) as generators; subgroup (2) is AlgebraicGeometry.inertiaClosedNormalSubgroup below

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.inertiaClosedNormalSubgroup
declarations.doc:
**Subgroup (2) of Stacks Tag 0BTD.** The smallest closed normal subgroup of
`Gal(K^sep/K) = π₁(Spec K)` containing the inertia group `I_y` for every point `y` of the
normalization `X^sep` of `X` in `K^sep`.
declarations.statement: def inertiaClosedNormalSubgroup : Subgroup Gal(L / X.residueField (genericPoint X))
declarations.comment: subgroup (2): the smallest closed normal subgroup of Gal(K^sep/K) containing the inertia group I_y for every point y of the normalization X^sep of X in K^sep, with the points of X^sep over a nonempty affine open U of X presented as the primes of the integral closure of Γ(X, U) in K^sep

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_etale_fromNormalization_of_inertiaGenerators_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0BTD, the inertia criterion for unramifiedness.** Let `X` be a normal integral
scheme with function field `K` and let `F` be a finite Galois subextension of `K^sep / K` whose
fixing subgroup contains every inertia group `I_y` for `y` a point of `X^sep` — equivalently,
with `F` inside the fixed field of subgroup (2). Then the normalization of `X` in `F` is finite
étale over `X`, that is, `X` is unramified in `F`.

This is the second paragraph of the source's proof. The points of `X^sep` over a nonempty affine
open `U` of `X` are the primes of the integral closure `C` of `Γ(X, U)` in `K^sep`, and the
points of the normalization of `X` in `F` over `U` are the primes of the integral closure `B` of
`Γ(X, U)` in `F`. Every prime of `B` is the contraction of a prime of `C`, and restriction
carries the inertia group at a prime of `C` onto the inertia group at its contraction, which is
Stacks Tag 0BSX. The hypothesis makes every element of the former restrict to the identity, so
all the latter are trivial and the normalization is unramified by Stacks Tag 0BTF.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_etale_fromNormalization_of_inertiaGenerators_subset
    (F : IntermediateField (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) L)
    [FiniteDimensional (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) F]
    [IsGalois (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) F]
    (hF : inertiaGenerators X L ⊆
      (F.fixingSubgroup : Set Gal(L/X.residueField (genericPoint X)))) :
    let f : Spec (.of (F : Type u)) ⟶ X :=
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
        (algebraMap (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) (F : Type u))) ≫
        X.fromSpecResidueField (genericPoint X)
    IsFinite f.fromNormalization ∧ Etale f.fromNormalization
declarations.comment: the second paragraph of the proof: triviality of the inertia groups I_y on a finite Galois subextension F of K^sep/K makes X unramified in F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ker_galoisToFundamentalGroup_le_inertiaClosedNormalSubgroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0BTD, the reverse inclusion `(1) ⊆ (2)`.** Let `X` be a normal integral scheme
with function field `K`. The kernel of the surjection `Gal(K^sep/K) → π₁(X)` is contained in the
smallest closed normal subgroup of `Gal(K^sep/K)` containing the inertia group `I_y` for every
point `y` of the normalization `X^sep` of `X` in `K^sep`.

This is the second half of the source's proof. Subgroup `(2)` is closed and normal, so it is the
subgroup fixing its fixed field `F`, and `F` is normal over `K`; hence it suffices to see that
every element of the kernel fixes each element `x` of `F`. The finite Galois subextension
generated by `x` lies in `F`, so every inertia group restricts to the identity on it, so `X` is
unramified in it by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_etale_fromNormalization_of_inertiaGenerators_subset`, so every
element of the kernel fixes it by
`AlgebraicGeometry.mem_fixingSubgroup_of_galoisToFundamentalGroup_eq_one`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ker_galoisToFundamentalGroup_le_inertiaClosedNormalSubgroup
    (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra L Ω] [Algebra (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ω]
    [IsScalarTower (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) L Ω]
    [IsAlgClosed Ω] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) Ω] :
    (galoisToFundamentalGroup X L Ω).toMonoidHom.ker ≤ inertiaClosedNormalSubgroup X L
declarations.comment: the inclusion of subgroup (1) in subgroup (2), and only that inclusion: subgroup (1) is the kernel of Gal(K^sep/K) → π₁(X) and subgroup (2) is the closed normal subgroup generated by the inertia groups I_y; the reverse inclusion (2) ⊆ (3) needs the conjugacy of I_y with Gal(K^sep/K_x^sh) from Tag 0BSW, is AlgebraicGeometry.inertiaClosedNormalSubgroup_le_stalkKerClosedNormalSubgroup below

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.inertiaClosedNormalSubgroup_le_stalkKerClosedNormalSubgroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0BTD, the inclusion `(2) ⊆ (3)`.** Let `X` be a normal integral scheme with
function field `K`. The smallest closed normal subgroup of `Gal(K^sep/K)` containing the inertia
group `I_y` for every point `y` of the normalization `X^sep` of `X` in `K^sep` is contained in the
smallest closed normal subgroup containing the kernel of `π₁(Spec K) → π₁(Spec 𝒪_{X,x})` for
every point `x` of `X`.

This is the inclusion the source gets from the conjugacy of `I_y` with `Gal(K^sep/K_x^sh)`. A
point `y` of `X^sep` over a nonempty affine open `U` of `X` is a prime `r` of the integral closure
`C` of `Γ(X, U)` in `K^sep`; the point `x` of `U` it lies over is the prime `r ∩ Γ(X, U)`, and
`𝒪_{X,x}` is the localization of `Γ(X, U)` there. Taking the integral closure commutes with that
localization and the inertia group is insensitive to it
(`IsIntegralClosure.exists_isMaximal_inertia_eq_of_isLocalization`), so `I_y` is the inertia group
at a maximal ideal of the integral closure of `𝒪_{X,x}` in `K^sep`; by
`Stacks.RamificationTheory.comap_ker_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_eq_normalClosure_inertia` that
inertia group lies in the kernel of `π₁(Spec K) → π₁(Spec 𝒪_{X,x})`.

With `AlgebraicGeometry.comap_normalClosure_iUnion_ker_le_ker_galoisToFundamentalGroup` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.ker_galoisToFundamentalGroup_le_inertiaClosedNormalSubgroup` this closes the
cycle `(3) ⊆ (1) ⊆ (2) ⊆ (3)`, so the three subgroups of the source are equal.
declarations.statement:
theorem inertiaClosedNormalSubgroup_le_stalkKerClosedNormalSubgroup :
    inertiaClosedNormalSubgroup X L ≤ stalkKerClosedNormalSubgroup X L Ω
declarations.comment: the inclusion of subgroup (2) in subgroup (3), which together with the inclusions (3) ⊆ (1) and (1) ⊆ (2) above gives the equality of the three subgroups; subgroup (3) is written with the kernels of π₁(Spec K) → π₁(Spec 𝒪_{X,x}) as generators and is read inside Gal(K^sep/K) through the identification of Tag 0BNE

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ker_galoisToFundamentalGroup_eq_inertiaClosedNormalSubgroup_and_stalkKer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0BTD.** Let `X` be a normal integral scheme with function field `K`. The three
subgroups of `Gal(K^sep/K)` of the source are equal: the kernel of `Gal(K^sep/K) → π₁(X)`, the
smallest closed normal subgroup containing the inertia group `I_y` at every point `y` of the
normalization of `X` in `K^sep`, and the smallest closed normal subgroup containing the kernel of
`π₁(Spec K) → π₁(Spec 𝒪_{X,x})` for every point `x` of `X`.

The three inclusions `(3) ⊆ (1)`, `(1) ⊆ (2)` and `(2) ⊆ (3)` proved above close into a cycle.
declarations.statement:
theorem ker_galoisToFundamentalGroup_eq_inertiaClosedNormalSubgroup_and_stalkKer :
    (galoisToFundamentalGroup X L Ω).toMonoidHom.ker = inertiaClosedNormalSubgroup X L ∧
      (galoisToFundamentalGroup X L Ω).toMonoidHom.ker =
        stalkKerClosedNormalSubgroup X L Ω
declarations.comment: the equality of the three subgroups, assembled from the cycle (3) ⊆ (1) ⊆ (2) ⊆ (3); subgroup (1) is the kernel of Gal(K^sep/K) → π₁(X) rather than the subgroup fixing the maximal unramified subextension, so no Noetherian hypothesis is needed, and subgroup (3) is written with the kernels of π₁(Spec K) → π₁(Spec 𝒪_{X,x}) as generators

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.mem_evenSubalgebra_iff
declarations.doc: The subring `k[tᵢtⱼ]` consists of the polynomials all of whose monomials have even degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_evenSubalgebra_iff {f : MvPolynomial σ k} :
    f ∈ evenSubalgebra k σ ↔ ∀ m ∈ f.support, Even (Finsupp.degree m)
declarations.comment: the invariant subring k[tᵢtⱼ]

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.mem_evenSubalgebra_iff_negVars_eq
declarations.doc: The subring `k[tᵢtⱼ]` is the ring of invariants of the `±1`-action, provided `2 ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_evenSubalgebra_iff_negVars_eq (h2 : (2 : k) ≠ 0) {f : MvPolynomial σ k} :
    f ∈ evenSubalgebra k σ ↔ negVars k σ f = f
declarations.comment: the invariant subring k[tᵢtⱼ]

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.finite_evenSubalgebra
declarations.doc:
The polynomial ring in finitely many variables is a finite module over `k[tᵢtⱼ]`: the morphism
`𝐀ⁿ_k → Spec(k[tᵢtⱼ])` is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_evenSubalgebra [Finite σ] :
    Module.Finite (evenSubalgebra k σ) (MvPolynomial σ k)
declarations.comment: the degree two morphism

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.rank_evenSubalgebra_eq_two
declarations.doc:
The polynomial ring has rank two as a module over `k[tᵢtⱼ]`: the morphism
`𝐀ⁿ_k → Spec(k[tᵢtⱼ])` has degree two.
declarations.statement:
theorem rank_evenSubalgebra_eq_two (h2 : (2 : k) ≠ 0) [Nonempty σ] :
    Module.rank (evenSubalgebra k σ) (MvPolynomial σ k) = 2
declarations.comment: the degree two morphism

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.finrank_evenSubalgebra_eq_two
declarations.doc: The polynomial ring in finitely many variables has rank two as a module over `k[tᵢtⱼ]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finrank_evenSubalgebra_eq_two (h2 : (2 : k) ≠ 0) [Nonempty σ] :
    Module.finrank (evenSubalgebra k σ) (MvPolynomial σ k) = 2
declarations.comment: the degree two morphism

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.isUnramifiedAt_of_under_ne_vertexIdeal
declarations.doc:
The morphism `𝐀ⁿ_k → Spec(k[tᵢtⱼ])` is unramified at every point of `𝐀ⁿ_k` which does not
lie over the vertex `𝔪 = (tᵢtⱼ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramifiedAt_of_under_ne_vertexIdeal (h2 : (2 : k) ≠ 0) (q : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ k))
    [q.IsPrime] (hq : q.under (evenSubalgebra k σ) ≠ vertexIdeal k σ) :
    Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (evenSubalgebra k σ) q
declarations.comment: unramified away from the vertex

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.not_isUnramifiedAt_idealOfVars
declarations.doc:
The morphism `𝐀ⁿ_k → Spec(k[tᵢtⱼ])` is ramified at the vertex `(t₁, …, tₙ)` of `𝐀ⁿ_k`, which
lies over the vertex `𝔪 = (tᵢtⱼ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isUnramifiedAt_idealOfVars [Nonempty σ] :
    ¬ Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (evenSubalgebra k σ) (idealOfVars σ k)
declarations.comment: ramified at the vertex

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.height_vertexIdeal
declarations.doc:
The vertex `𝔪 = (tᵢtⱼ)` has height `n` in `k[tᵢtⱼ]` for `n` variables: it is a point of
codimension `n` of the quotient.
declarations.statement: theorem height_vertexIdeal (n : ℕ) : (vertexIdeal k (Fin n)).height = n
declarations.comment: the vertex has codimension n

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.one_lt_height_vertexIdeal
declarations.doc:
For at least two variables the vertex `𝔪 = (tᵢtⱼ)` has codimension greater than one, so the
ramification of `𝐀ⁿ_k → Spec(k[tᵢtⱼ])` is not visible in codimension one.
declarations.statement: theorem one_lt_height_vertexIdeal {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : 1 < (vertexIdeal k (Fin n)).height
declarations.comment: ramification in codimension greater than one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalization_unramified_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Unramifiedness of the normalization of a normal integral scheme in a finite extension of
its function field.** For `X` integral and normal with function field `K`, a finite extension
`L / K` and `f : Y ⟶ X` the normalization of `X` in `L`, the following are equivalent: `f` is
unramified (which is the definition of `X` being unramified in `L`); `f` is étale; `f` is finite
étale; `f` becomes unramified over `Spec` of every local ring of `X`; the same over every
henselization of a local ring of `X`; the same over every strict henselization; and every
scheme-theoretic fibre of `f` is étale and finite locally free of some rank at least
`[L : K]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem normalization_unramified_tfae
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [IsNormal X]
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra X.functionField L]
    [FiniteDimensional X.functionField L]
    (i : Spec (.of L) ⟶ X)
    (hi : i = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
      (algebraMap X.functionField L)) ≫ X.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint X))
    [QuasiCompact i] [QuasiSeparated i] :
    let f : i.normalization ⟶ X := i.fromNormalization
    List.TFAE [
      Unramified f,
      Etale f,
      IsFinite f ∧ Etale f,
      (∀ x : X, Unramified
        (pullback.snd f (X.fromSpecStalk x))),
      (∀ (x : X) (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
        [Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) R]
        [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization (X.presheaf.stalk x)
          (ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x)) R],
        Unramified
          (pullback.snd f
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
              (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk x) R)) ≫ X.fromSpecStalk x))),
      (∀ (x : X) (κsep : Type u) [Field κsep]
        [Algebra (ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x)) κsep]
        [IsSepClosure (ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x)) κsep]
        (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
        [Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) R]
        [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization (X.presheaf.stalk x) κsep R],
        Unramified
          (pullback.snd f
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
              (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk x) R)) ≫ X.fromSpecStalk x))),
      (∀ x : X, ∃ d : ℕ, Module.finrank X.functionField L ≤ d ∧
        Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (f.fiberToSpecResidueField x) d ∧
        Etale (f.fiberToSpecResidueField x))]
declarations.comment: conditions (1)–(8)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalization_unramified_iff_trivialInertia
declarations.doc:
**The Galois case: unramifiedness of the normalization is triviality of every inertia
group.** For `X` integral and normal with function field `K` and `L / K` finite Galois with
group `G = Gal(L/K)`, the normalization of `X` in `L` is unramified exactly when, on every
nonempty affine open `U` of `X` and for every prime `q` of the integral closure of `Γ(X, U)` in
`L`, the only `σ ∈ G` fixing `q` elementwise and inducing the identity modulo `q` is the
identity; that is, exactly when every inertia group
`I_q = {σ ∈ G | σ(q) = q and σ ≡ id mod q}` is trivial.
declarations.statement:
public theorem normalization_unramified_iff_trivialInertia
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [IsNormal X]
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra X.functionField L]
    [FiniteDimensional X.functionField L] [IsGalois X.functionField L]
    (i : Spec (.of L) ⟶ X)
    (hi : i = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
      (algebraMap X.functionField L)) ≫ X.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint X))
    [QuasiCompact i] [QuasiSeparated i] :
    Unramified i.fromNormalization ↔
      ∀ (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) [Nonempty U],
        letI : Algebra Γ(X, U) L :=
          ((algebraMap X.functionField L).comp
            (X.germToFunctionField U).hom).toAlgebra
        letI : IsScalarTower Γ(X, U) X.functionField L :=
          .of_algebraMap_eq' rfl
        letI : IsFractionRing Γ(X, U) X.functionField :=
          functionField_isFractionRing_of_isAffineOpen X U hU
        ∀ (q : Ideal (integralClosure Γ(X, U) L)) (_hq : q.IsPrime)
          (σ : L ≃ₐ[X.functionField] L),
          ((∀ y, y ∈ q ↔
              galRestrict Γ(X, U) X.functionField L
                (integralClosure Γ(X, U) L) σ y ∈ q) ∧
            (∀ y, galRestrict Γ(X, U) X.functionField L
              (integralClosure Γ(X, U) L) σ y - y ∈ q)) →
          σ = 1
declarations.comment: condition (9)

declarations.name: integral_isColimit_directed_finite_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
If `S` is integral over `R`, then the algebra map `R → S` is a filtered colimit of a
directed system of module-finite ring maps `f_λ : R_λ → S_λ` whose bases `R_λ` are of
finite type over `ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem integral_isColimit_directed_finite_of_finiteType
    (R S : Type) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.IsIntegral R S] :
    ∃ D : DirectedRingMapSystem,
      -- (1) Colimit: the colimit of the system equals the structural map `R → S`.
      D.IsColimitEqual (algebraMap R S) ∧
      -- (2) Finite type base: each `R_λ` is of finite type over `Z`.
      (∀ a : D.Λ, Algebra.FiniteType ℤ (D.FR.obj a)) ∧
      -- (3) Module-finite: each `f_λ : R_λ → S_λ` is finite.
      (∀ a : D.Λ, RingHom.Finite (D.f.app a).hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.canonicalDescentData_etale
declarations.doc:
The canonical descent datum of an étale scheme over `S` has an étale underlying scheme
over `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalDescentData_etale (f : X ⟶ S) (U : S.Etale) :
    IsEtaleDescentData f
      ((DescentData.canonicalFunctor f).obj ((Scheme.Etale.forget S).obj U))
declarations.comment: étale objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleDescentFunctor
declarations.doc:
The canonical functor, given by pullback along `f`, from étale `S`-schemes to descent data
relative to `f` with étale underlying `X`-scheme.
declarations.statement:
def etaleDescentFunctor (f : X ⟶ S) :
    S.Etale ⥤ EtaleDescentData f
declarations.comment: the functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleDescentFunctor_faithful
declarations.doc:
Pullback to a surjective scheme detects equality of morphisms
between étale schemes over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleDescentFunctor_faithful (f : X ⟶ S) [Surjective f] :
    (etaleDescentFunctor f).Faithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleDescentFunctor_fullyFaithful_of_submersive_baseChange
declarations.doc:
Étale descent is fully faithful when the morphism and all its
étale base changes are submersive.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleDescentFunctor_fullyFaithful_of_submersive_baseChange (f : X ⟶ S)
    (hf : Topology.IsQuotientMap f)
    (hbase : ∀ {U : Scheme.{u}} (g : U ⟶ S), Etale g →
      Topology.IsQuotientMap (pullback.snd f g)) :
    Nonempty (etaleDescentFunctor f).FullyFaithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleDescentFunctor_fullyFaithful_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
Étale descent along a
surjective universally closed morphism is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleDescentFunctor_fullyFaithful_of_universallyClosed (f : X ⟶ S) [Surjective f]
    [UniversallyClosed f] : Nonempty (etaleDescentFunctor f).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: universally_closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleDescentFunctor_fullyFaithful_of_universallyOpen
declarations.doc:
Étale descent along a
surjective universally open morphism is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleDescentFunctor_fullyFaithful_of_universallyOpen (f : X ⟶ S) [Surjective f]
    [UniversallyOpen f] : Nonempty (etaleDescentFunctor f).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: universally_open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleDescentFunctor_fullyFaithful_of_quasiCompact_of_flat
declarations.doc:
Étale descent along a
surjective quasi-compact flat morphism is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleDescentFunctor_fullyFaithful_of_quasiCompact_of_flat (f : X ⟶ S) [Surjective f]
    [QuasiCompact f] [Flat f] : Nonempty (etaleDescentFunctor f).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: quasi_compact_flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentDatum.isEtaleEffective_of_isOpenCover
declarations.doc:
**Effectivity of an étale descent datum is Zariski-local on the base.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a
morphism of schemes and `(V, φ)` a descent datum relative to `X/S` with `V ⟶ X` étale, and let
`S = ⋃ Sᵢ` be an open covering. Assume that the pullback of `(V, φ)` to `X ×_S Sᵢ / Sᵢ` is
effective by an étale scheme for every `i`, that the étale descent functor for
`X ×_S (Sᵢ ∩ Sⱼ) ⟶ Sᵢ ∩ Sⱼ` is fully faithful, and that the étale descent functor for
`X ×_S (Sᵢ ∩ Sⱼ ∩ Sₖ) ⟶ Sᵢ ∩ Sⱼ ∩ Sₖ` is faithful. Then `(V, φ)` is effective, by a scheme
étale over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleEffective_of_isOpenCover {S X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S} (D : DescentDatum f)
    [Etale D.over.hom] {ι : Type v} (U : ι → S.Opens) (hU : ⨆ i, U i = ⊤)
    (hlocal : ∀ i, (D.baseDatum (U i)).IsEtaleEffective)
    (hpair : ∀ i j, (etaleDescentFunctor (pullback.snd f (U i ⊓ U j).ι)).FullyFaithful)
    (htriple : ∀ i j k,
      (etaleDescentFunctor (pullback.snd f (U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k).ι)).Faithful) :
    D.IsEtaleEffective

declarations.name: Stacks.Etale.exists_coprod_isFinite_and_isEmpty_closedFiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BTN.** A quasi-compact separated étale scheme over a henselian pair,
with finite closed fibre, is the disjoint union of a finite scheme over the base and a scheme
with empty closed fibre.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_coprod_isFinite_and_isEmpty_closedFiber
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : HenselianPair A I)
    (U : Scheme.{u}) (f : U ⟶ Spec (.of A))
    [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f] [Etale f]
    [IsFinite (pullback.snd f
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))))] :
    ∃ (Ufin Uaway : Scheme.{u}) (iFin : Ufin ⟶ U) (iAway : Uaway ⟶ U),
      IsIso (coprod.desc iFin iAway) ∧ IsFinite (iFin ≫ f) ∧
        IsEmpty ((pullback (iAway ≫ f)
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))) : Scheme.{u}))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fullyFaithful_quasiCompactSeparatedEtaleDescentFunctor_of_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BTP, the fully faithful half.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a surjective
integral morphism. The functor of Tag 0BTI, restricted to the schemes quasi-compact, separated
and étale over `S` and to the descent data relative to `X/S` whose underlying `X`-scheme is
quasi-compact, separated and étale, is fully faithful.

Fullness is Tag 0BTL for a surjective universally closed morphism, which a surjective integral
morphism is, and faithfulness is Tag 0BTJ.
declarations.statement:
theorem fullyFaithful_quasiCompactSeparatedEtaleDescentFunctor_of_isIntegralHom
    (f : X ⟶ S) [Surjective f] [IsIntegralHom f] :
    Nonempty (quasiCompactSeparatedEtaleDescentFunctor f).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: the fully faithful half of the equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_quasiCompactSeparatedEtaleDescentFunctor_of_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BTP](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BTP).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a
surjective integral morphism. The functor of Tag 0BTI induces an equivalence between the category
of schemes quasi-compact, separated and étale over `S` and the category of descent data `(V, φ)`
relative to `X/S` with `V` quasi-compact, separated and étale over `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_quasiCompactSeparatedEtaleDescentFunctor_of_isIntegralHom
    {S X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Surjective f] [IsIntegralHom f] :
    (quasiCompactSeparatedEtaleDescentFunctor f).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TranslationDiagram.outerIso
declarations.doc:
The outer rectangle of the diagram 2-commutes: restricting first along `h` and then along `h'`
agrees with the composite functor `H ⋙ H'`.
declarations.statement:
public def outerIso (D : TranslationDiagram F F' F'' H H') :
    (PreGaloisCategory.functorToContAction F ⋙ ContAction.res FintypeCat D.left.hom) ⋙
        ContAction.res FintypeCat D.right.hom ≅
      H ⋙ H' ⋙ PreGaloisCategory.functorToContAction F''
declarations.comment: the outer rectangle

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.nonempty_translationDiagram
declarations.doc:
Two composable exact functors between Galois categories admit fibre-functor isomorphisms whose
induced continuous homomorphisms fit into a 2-commutative diagram over the categories of finite
continuous actions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_translationDiagram
    (F : C ⥤ FintypeCat.{w}) (F' : C' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w}) (F'' : C'' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w})
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F)]
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F')]
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F'')]
    (H : C ⥤ C') (H' : C' ⥤ C'')
    (hH : exactFunctor C C' H) (hH' : exactFunctor C' C'' H') :
    Nonempty (TranslationDiagram F F' F'' H H')
declarations.comment: the two 2-commutative squares

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.normal_range_iff_connected_image_finite_coproduct_of_terminal
declarations.doc:
Normality of the image of the homomorphism induced by an exact functor of Galois categories
is equivalent to the terminal-object criterion on images of connected objects.
declarations.statement:
public theorem normal_range_iff_connected_image_finite_coproduct_of_terminal
    {C' : Type u'} [Category.{v'} C'] {C'' : Type u''} [Category.{v''} C'']
    (F' : C' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w}) (F'' : C'' ⥤ FintypeCat.{w})
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F')]
    [IsGaloisCategory (setValuedFiberFunctor F'')]
    (H' : C' ⥤ C'')
    (t' : H' ⋙ F'' ≅ F') (d' : GaloisFunctorData F' F'' H' t') :
    (MonoidHom.range d'.hom.toMonoidHom).Normal ↔
      ∀ X' : C', PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected X' →
        (∃ Z : C'', Nonempty (IsTerminal Z) ∧ Nonempty (Z ⟶ H'.obj X')) →
          IsFiniteCoproductOfTerminal (H'.obj X')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteEtale_model
declarations.doc:
**Every finite étale cover of the limit comes from a stage.** A scheme finite étale over the
limit of a cofiltered inverse system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes with affine
transition morphisms is isomorphic, as a cover of the limit, to the base change of a scheme finite
étale over one of the stages.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteEtale_model (hc : IsLimit c) (Y : FiniteEtaleOver c.pt) :
    ∃ (j : I) (B : FiniteEtaleOver (D.obj j)),
      Nonempty (Y ≅ (finiteEtaleBaseChange (c.π.app j)).obj B)
declarations.comment: equivalence of categories: every finite étale cover of the limit comes from a stage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteEtale_hom_model
declarations.doc:
**Every morphism of finite étale covers over the limit comes from a stage.** A morphism between
the base changes to the limit of two finite étale covers of a stage is, after transport along the
comparison isomorphism `AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtaleLimitCompIso`, the base change of a morphism
of the base changes of those covers to some later stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteEtale_hom_model (hc : IsLimit c) (i : I) (A B : FiniteEtaleOver (D.obj i))
    (ψ : (finiteEtaleBaseChange (c.π.app i)).obj A ⟶
      (finiteEtaleBaseChange (c.π.app i)).obj B) :
    ∃ (j : I) (e : j ⟶ i)
      (χ : (finiteEtaleBaseChange (D.map e)).obj A ⟶ (finiteEtaleBaseChange (D.map e)).obj B),
      ψ = (finiteEtaleLimitCompIso D c e).hom.app A
        ≫ (finiteEtaleBaseChange (c.π.app j)).map χ
        ≫ (finiteEtaleLimitCompIso D c e).inv.app B
declarations.comment: equivalence of categories: every morphism over the limit comes from a stage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eventually_eq_of_finiteEtaleBaseChange_eq
declarations.doc:
**Morphisms of finite étale covers agreeing over the limit agree at a later stage.** Two
morphisms of finite étale covers of a stage whose base changes along the projection of the cone
agree are already equal after base change to some later stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_eq_of_finiteEtaleBaseChange_eq (hc : IsLimit c) (i : I)
    (A B : FiniteEtaleOver (D.obj i)) (f g : A ⟶ B)
    (h : (finiteEtaleBaseChange (c.π.app i)).map f
      = (finiteEtaleBaseChange (c.π.app i)).map g) :
    ∃ (j : I) (e : j ⟶ i),
      (finiteEtaleBaseChange (D.map e)).map f = (finiteEtaleBaseChange (D.map e)).map g
declarations.comment: equivalence of categories: morphisms agreeing over the limit agree at a later stage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroup_homeomorph_compatibleFamilies
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BTV, second conclusion: `π₁(X, x̄) = lim π₁(Xᵢ, x̄)`.** Let `D` be a
cofiltered inverse system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes with affine transition
morphisms, let `c` be a limit cone on it, so that `c.pt` is `X = lim Xᵢ`, and suppose that the
schemes of the cofinal tail `Over i₀` are connected. Then for a geometric point `x` of `X` the
scheme `X` is connected, the compatible families of elements of the fundamental groups of the
stages of the tail form a topological group, and the canonical map is an isomorphism of
topological groups onto it: every coordinate of the isomorphism is the homomorphism induced by
the corresponding projection of the cone.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleFundamentalGroup_homeomorph_compatibleFamilies {I : Type u} [Category.{u} I]
    [IsCofiltered I] (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    [∀ {i j : I} (e : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map e)]
    [∀ i : I, CompactSpace (D.obj i)]
    [∀ i : I, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)]
    (i₀ : I) [hconn : ∀ j : Over i₀, ConnectedSpace (D.obj j.left)]
    (x : GeometricPoint c.pt) :
    ∃ hX : ConnectedSpace c.pt,
      letI : ConnectedSpace c.pt := hX
      ∃ hGroup : Group
          {σ : ∀ j : Over i₀, EtaleFundamentalGroup (D.obj j.left) (x.map (c.π.app j.left)) //
            CompatibleFundamentalGroupFamily D c i₀ x σ},
        letI := hGroup
        ∃ hTopGroup : IsTopologicalGroup
            {σ : ∀ j : Over i₀, EtaleFundamentalGroup (D.obj j.left) (x.map (c.π.app j.left)) //
              CompatibleFundamentalGroupFamily D c i₀ x σ},
          letI := hTopGroup
          ∃ e : EtaleFundamentalGroup c.pt x ≃ₜ*
              {σ : ∀ j : Over i₀, EtaleFundamentalGroup (D.obj j.left) (x.map (c.π.app j.left)) //
                CompatibleFundamentalGroupFamily D c i₀ x σ},
            ∀ (σ : EtaleFundamentalGroup c.pt x) (j : Over i₀),
              (e σ).1 j = @etaleFundamentalGroupMap _ _ hX (hconn j) (c.π.app j.left) x σ
declarations.comment: π₁(X, x̄) = lim π₁(Xᵢ, x̄) for a connected cofinal tail

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.connectedSpace_pullback_specMap_algebraMap_perfectClosure
declarations.doc:
**The connectedness half of Stacks Project, Tag 0BTW.** For a field `k` with perfection
`kperf` and a connected scheme `X` over `k`, the base change `X_{kperf}` is connected.

The perfection is purely inseparable over `k`, so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.connectedSpace_pullback_specMap_algebraMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem connectedSpace_pullback_specMap_algebraMap_perfectClosure (k kperf : Type u) [Field k]
    [Field kperf] [Algebra k kperf] (p : ℕ) [ExpChar k p] [ExpChar kperf p]
    [PerfectRing kperf p] [IsPerfectClosure (algebraMap k kperf) p] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [ConnectedSpace ↥X] :
    ConnectedSpace ↥(pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k kperf))))
declarations.comment: the assertion that `X_{k^{perf}}` is connected; the asserted isomorphism `π₁(X_{k^{perf}}) → π₁(X)` is not proved here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.connectedSpace_and_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_perfectClosure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BTW.** Let `k` be a field with perfection `kperf` and let `X` be a
connected scheme over `k`. Then `X_{kperf} = X ×_{Spec k} Spec kperf` is connected, and for every
geometric point `x` of `X_{kperf}` the map `π₁(X_{kperf}, x) → π₁(X, x)` induced by the
projection is an isomorphism of topological groups.
declarations.statement:
theorem connectedSpace_and_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_perfectClosure (k kperf : Type u) [Field k]
    [Field kperf] [Algebra k kperf] (p : ℕ) [ExpChar k p] [ExpChar kperf p]
    [PerfectRing kperf p] [IsPerfectClosure (algebraMap k kperf) p] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [ConnectedSpace ↥X] :
    ConnectedSpace ↥(pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k kperf)))) ∧
      ∀ x : GeometricPoint (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k kperf)))),
        haveI := connectedSpace_pullback_specMap_algebraMap_perfectClosure k kperf p f
        ∃ e : EtaleFundamentalGroup _ x ≃ₜ*
            EtaleFundamentalGroup X (x.map (pullback.fst f _)),
          ∀ σ, e σ = etaleFundamentalGroupMap (pullback.fst f _) x σ
declarations.comment: both assertions: `X_{k^{perf}}` is connected, and the canonical map `π₁(X_{k^{perf}}) → π₁(X)` is an isomorphism of topological groups

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.connectedSpace_of_connectedSpace_pullback_specMap_algebraMap
declarations.doc:
If the base change of a scheme `X` over `k` to a field extension `Ω` is connected, then so is
`X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem connectedSpace_of_connectedSpace_pullback_specMap_algebraMap
    (k Ω : Type u) [Field k] [Field Ω] [Algebra k Ω] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [ConnectedSpace ↥(pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Ω))))] :
    ConnectedSpace ↥X
declarations.comment: connectedness of `X`, implicit in the statement since `π₁(X)` appears in it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroupMap_comp_eq_one_isAlgClosed
declarations.doc:
For a field `k` with an
algebraically closed extension `Ω`, a scheme `X` over `k` whose base change `X_Ω` is connected,
and a geometric point `x` of `X_Ω`, the composite

```
π₁(X_Ω, x) ⟶ π₁(X, x) ⟶ π₁(Spec k, x)
```

is the trivial homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleFundamentalGroupMap_comp_eq_one_isAlgClosed
    (k Ω : Type u) [Field k] [Field Ω] [Algebra k Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [ConnectedSpace ↥(pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Ω))))]
    (x : GeometricPoint (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Ω))))) :
    letI : ConnectedSpace ↥X := connectedSpace_of_connectedSpace_pullback_specMap_algebraMap k Ω f
    (etaleFundamentalGroupMap f
          (x.map (pullback.fst f
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Ω)))))).toMonoidHom.comp
        (etaleFundamentalGroupMap
          (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Ω)))) x).toMonoidHom = 1
declarations.comment: triviality of the composite `π₁(X_k̄) → π₁(X) → π₁(Spec k)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_isAlgClosed
declarations.doc:
For a field `k` with an algebraically closed
extension `Ω`, a scheme `X` over `k` whose base change `X_Ω` is connected, and a geometric point
`x` of `X`, the induced homomorphism

```
π₁(X, x) ⟶ π₁(Spec k, x)
```

is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_isAlgClosed
    (k Ω : Type u) [Field k] [Field Ω] [Algebra k Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [ConnectedSpace ↥(pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Ω))))]
    (x : GeometricPoint X) :
    letI : ConnectedSpace ↥X := connectedSpace_of_connectedSpace_pullback_specMap_algebraMap k Ω f
    Function.Surjective (etaleFundamentalGroupMap f x)
declarations.comment: surjectivity of `π₁(X) → π₁(Spec k)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.shortExact_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_isAlgClosure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BTX.** Let `k` be a field with algebraic closure `k̄`, and `X` a
quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme over `k` whose base change `X_{k̄}` is connected. Then
`X` is connected
(`AlgebraicGeometry.connectedSpace_of_connectedSpace_pullback_specMap_algebraMap`), and for a
geometric point `x` of `X_{k̄}` the sequence of continuous homomorphisms of étale fundamental
groups

```
1 → π₁(X_{k̄}, x) → π₁(X, x) → π₁(Spec k, x) → 1
```

induced by the projection `X_{k̄} ⟶ X` and the structure morphism `X ⟶ Spec k` is exact. The
first map is injective, its image is the kernel of the second, and the second is surjective. The
three groups are profinite (`AlgebraicGeometry.isProfiniteTop_etaleFundamentalGroup`).

The proof is described in the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_isAlgClosure (k kbar : Type u) [Field k]
    [Field kbar] [Algebra k kbar] [IsAlgClosure k kbar] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    [ConnectedSpace ↥(pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k kbar))))]
    (x : GeometricPoint (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k kbar))))) :
    letI : ConnectedSpace ↥X :=
      connectedSpace_of_connectedSpace_pullback_specMap_algebraMap k kbar f
    Function.Injective (etaleFundamentalGroupMap
        (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k kbar)))) x) ∧
      (etaleFundamentalGroupMap
          (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k kbar)))) x).toMonoidHom.range =
        (etaleFundamentalGroupMap f (x.map (pullback.fst f
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k kbar)))))).toMonoidHom.ker ∧
      Function.Surjective (etaleFundamentalGroupMap f
        (x.map (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k kbar))))))
declarations.comment: the full short exact sequence: injectivity, exactness in the middle, surjectivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalShortExact_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_isAlgClosure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BTX.** Let `k` be a field with algebraic closure `k̄` and let `X` be a
quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme over `k` whose base change `X_k̄` is connected. Then `X`
is connected (`AlgebraicGeometry.connectedSpace_of_connectedSpace_pullback_specMap_algebraMap`)
and, for a geometric point `x` of `X_k̄`,

```
1 → π₁(X_k̄, x) → π₁(X, x) → π₁(Spec k, x) → 1
```

is a short exact sequence of profinite topological groups: the first map is injective and a
closed embedding, its image is the kernel of the second, and the second is surjective and a
quotient map. Both maps are the continuous homomorphisms induced by the projection
`X_k̄ ⟶ X` and the structure morphism `X ⟶ Spec k`; the three groups carry their profinite
topologies (`AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroupCompactSpace` and its companions).
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalShortExact_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_isAlgClosure (k kbar : Type u) [Field k]
    [Field kbar] [Algebra k kbar] [IsAlgClosure k kbar] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    [ConnectedSpace ↥(pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k kbar))))]
    (x : GeometricPoint (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k kbar))))) :
    letI : ConnectedSpace ↥X :=
      connectedSpace_of_connectedSpace_pullback_specMap_algebraMap k kbar f
    Function.Injective (etaleFundamentalGroupMap
          (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k kbar)))) x) ∧
      Topology.IsClosedEmbedding (etaleFundamentalGroupMap
          (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k kbar)))) x) ∧
      (etaleFundamentalGroupMap
          (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k kbar)))) x).toMonoidHom.range =
        (etaleFundamentalGroupMap f
          (x.map (pullback.fst f
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k kbar)))))).toMonoidHom.ker ∧
      Function.Surjective (etaleFundamentalGroupMap f
          (x.map (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k kbar)))))) ∧
      Topology.IsQuotientMap (etaleFundamentalGroupMap f
          (x.map (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k kbar))))))

morphism `V ⟶ W` over `Y`.

This is Stacks Project, Tag 0BTY read on the small étale site; the content is

declarations.name: Stacks.Etale.bijective_pullbackHom_of_universalHomeomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BTY.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a universal homeomorphism and let `A` be a
scheme étale over `Y`. For every scheme `B` over `Y`, base change along `f` is a bijection from
the `Y`-morphisms `B ⟶ A` to the `X`-morphisms between the base changes.

Injectivity holds for any surjective `f`, by
`Stacks.Etale.injective_baseChange_hom_of_universalHomeomorphism`; surjectivity is
`Stacks.Etale.exists_hom_of_pullbackHom_of_universalHomeomorphism`.

theorem bijective_pullbackHom_of_universalHomeomorphism {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [UniversalHomeomorphism f] (A B : Over Y) [Etale A.hom] :
    Function.Bijective (fun h : B ⟶ A => (Over.pullback f).map h)

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.exists_uniformizerRatioMap_to_rootsOfUnity
declarations.doc:
Let a group act on a discrete valuation ring, trivially on its residue field. Suppose an
invariant element is a unit times the `e`-th power of a uniformizer. For every group element, its
action on the uniformizer differs from the uniformizer by a unit; the residues of these units are
`e`-th roots of unity and hence define a map to the group of such roots.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_uniformizerRatioMap_to_rootsOfUnity
    (C : Type u) [CommRing C] [IsDomain C] [IsDiscreteValuationRing C]
    (I : Type v) [Group I] [MulSemiringAction I C]
    (e : ℕ) (π a : C) (u : Cˣ)
    (hπ : Irreducible π)
    (ha : a = (u : C) * π ^ e)
    (ha_fixed : ∀ σ : I, σ • a = a)
    (hres : ∀ (σ : I) (x : C),
      Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal C) (σ • x) =
        Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal C) x) :
    ∃ (θ : I → rootsOfUnity e (C ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal C))
      (θunit : I → Cˣ),
      (∀ σ : I, (θunit σ : C) * π = σ • π) ∧
        ∀ σ : I,
          (θ σ : (C ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal C)ˣ) =
            Units.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal C)) (θunit σ)
