declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.inertiaCharacter_conj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0BU5.** The inertia character is equivariant for conjugation by the
decomposition group: conjugating an inertia element by a decomposition element has character
equal to the image of the original character under the induced residue-field automorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem inertiaCharacter_conj
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L]
    [IsGalois K L] [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    (P : Ideal (integralClosure A L)) [P.IsMaximal] :
    let B := integralClosure A L
    letI := IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K L B
    let D := MulAction.stabilizer Gal(L/K) P
    let I := P.inertia Gal(L/K)
    let e := P.ramificationIdx A
    let conjugate : D → I → I := fun τ σ ↦
      ⟨(τ : Gal(L/K)) * (σ : Gal(L/K)) * (τ : Gal(L/K))⁻¹, by
        rw [Ideal.mem_inertia]
        intro x
        have hσ := (Ideal.mem_inertia.mp σ.property) ((τ : Gal(L/K))⁻¹ • x)
        have hτ := Ideal.smul_mem_pointwise_smul (τ : Gal(L/K)) _ P hσ
        rw [τ.property] at hτ
        simpa only [mul_smul, smul_sub, smul_inv_smul] using hτ⟩
    ∀ (θ : I →* rootsOfUnity e (B ⧸ P)),
      (∀ (σ : I) (x a : B), x ∈ P → x ∉ P ^ 2 →
        Ideal.Quotient.mk P a = (θ σ).1.1 →
        (σ : Gal(L/K)) • x - a * x ∈ P ^ 2) →
      ∀ (τ : D) (σ : I),
        θ (conjugate τ σ) =
          (Ideal.quotientEquiv P P
            ((MulSemiringAction.toRingEquiv Gal(L/K) B) (τ : Gal(L/K)))
            τ.property.symm).toMulEquiv.restrictRootsOfUnity e (θ σ)

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.decomposition_inertia_wildInertia_tower
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0BU6.** The fixed fields, invariant rings, contracted primes, localized
rings, and residue fields attached to the wild inertia, inertia, and decomposition groups of
a maximal ideal in a finite Galois extension form the standard ramification tower.
declarations.statement:
theorem decomposition_inertia_wildInertia_tower
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L]
    [IsGalois K L] [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    (m : Ideal (integralClosure A L)) [m.IsMaximal] :
    let B := integralClosure A L
    letI := IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K L B
    letI : SMulCommClass Gal(L/K) A B :=
      ⟨fun g a b ↦ by
        simp only [Algebra.smul_def]
        change galRestrict A K L B g (algebraMap A B a * b) =
          algebraMap A B a * galRestrict A K L B g b
        rw [map_mul, AlgEquiv.commutes]⟩
    let D := MulAction.stabilizer Gal(L/K) m
    let I := m.inertia Gal(L/K)
    let hID : I ≤ D := Ideal.inertia_le_stabilizer (M := Gal(L/K)) m
    let iID : I →* D := I.subtype.codRestrict D (fun σ ↦ hID σ.property)
    ∃ (P : Subgroup I) (hP : P.Normal),
      let PG : Subgroup Gal(L/K) := P.map I.subtype
      let PD : Subgroup D := P.map iID
      (∀ σ : D, σ ∈ PD ↔ (σ : Gal(L/K)) ∈ I ∧
        ∀ b : B, b ∈ m → (σ : Gal(L/K)) • b - b ∈ m ^ 2) ∧
      let ID : Subgroup D := I.subgroupOf D
      let LD := IntermediateField.fixedField D
      let LI := IntermediateField.fixedField I
      let LP := IntermediateField.fixedField PG
      let BD := FixedPoints.subalgebra A B D
      let BI := FixedPoints.subalgebra A B I
      let BP := FixedPoints.subalgebra A B PG
      let hPGI : PG ≤ I := fun σ hσ ↦ by
        obtain ⟨τ, -, rfl⟩

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.surjective_restrictions_commute_with_residue_and_inertiaCharacter
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BU7.** In a tower of finite Galois extensions of the fraction field
of a discrete valuation ring, restriction surjects on decomposition, inertia, and wild inertia
groups.  The induced maps commute with residue-field automorphisms and with the canonical inertia
characters; on roots of unity the latter vertical map is the `e' / e`-power map.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_restrictions_commute_with_residue_and_inertiaCharacter
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L]
    [IsGalois K L] [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    (M : Type*) [Field M] [Algebra K M] [FiniteDimensional K M]
    [IsGalois K M] [Algebra L M] [IsScalarTower K L M]
    [Algebra A M] [IsScalarTower A K M] [IsScalarTower A L M]
    (r : Ideal (integralClosure A M)) [r.IsMaximal] :
    let B := integralClosure A L
    let C := integralClosure A M
    let fBC : B →ₐ[A] C := (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom A L M).mapIntegralClosure
    letI : Algebra B C := fBC.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    letI : IsScalarTower A B C :=
      IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun x ↦ (fBC.commutes x).symm
    letI : Algebra.IsIntegral B C :=
      ⟨fun x ↦ IsIntegral.tower_top (IsIntegralClosure.isIntegral A M x)⟩
    letI : MulSemiringAction Gal(M/K) C :=
      IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K M C
    letI : MulSemiringAction Gal(L/K) B :=
      IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K L B
    let q := r.under B
    let p := r.under A
    letI : r.LiesOver q := ⟨rfl⟩
    letI : q.LiesOver p := ⟨r.under_under.symm⟩
    letI : Field (A ⧸ p) := Ideal.Quotient.field p
    letI : Field (B ⧸ q) := Ideal.Quotient.field q
    letI : Field (C ⧸ r) := Ideal.Quotient.field r
    letI : Algebra (B ⧸ q) (C ⧸ r) := Ideal.Quotient.algebraOfLiesOver r q
    letI : Algebra (A ⧸ p) (B ⧸ q) := Ideal.Quotient.algebraOfLiesOver q p
    letI : Algebra (A ⧸ p) (C ⧸ r) := Ideal.Quotient.algebraOfLiesOver r p
    let res : Gal(M/K) →* Gal(L/K) := AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom L
    let D' := MulAction.stabilizer Gal(M/K) r
    let D := MulAction.stabilizer Gal(L/K) q
    let e' := r.ramificationIdx A
    let e := q.ramificationIdx A
    ∃ (resD : D' →* D)
      (resI : r.inertia Gal(M/K) →* q.inertia Gal(L/K))
      (resP : wildInertiaGroup A K M r →*
        wildInertiaGroup A K L q),
      Function.Surjective resD ∧ Function.Surjective resI ∧ Function.Surjective resP ∧
      (∀ σ, ((resD σ : D) : Gal(L/K)) = res ((σ : D') : Gal(M/K))) ∧
      (∀ σ, (resI σ).1 = res σ.1) ∧
      (∀ σ, (resP σ).1.1 = res σ.1.1) ∧
      e ∣ e' ∧
      ∃ (residueRestriction : Gal((C ⧸ r)/(A ⧸ p)) →* Gal((B ⧸ q)/(A ⧸ p)))
        (rootRestriction : rootsOfUnity e' (C ⧸ r) →* rootsOfUnity e (B ⧸ q)),
        (∀ τ b, algebraMap (B ⧸ q) (C ⧸ r) (residueRestriction τ b) =
          τ (algebraMap (B ⧸ q) (C ⧸ r) b)) ∧
        (∀ ζ, algebraMap (B ⧸ q) (C ⧸ r) (rootRestriction ζ).1.1 =
          (ζ ^ (e' / e)).1.1) ∧
        (∀ σ b, algebraMap (B ⧸ q) (C ⧸ r)
            (Ideal.Quotient.mk q ((resD σ).1 • b)) =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk r (σ.1 • fBC b)) ∧
        ∀ σ, rootRestriction (inertiaCharacter A K M r σ) =
          inertiaCharacter A K L q (resI σ)

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.canonicalInertiaCharacter
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BU8.** The canonical inertia character, obtained by raising the
ordinary inertia character to the residue-characteristic-primary part of the ramification
index.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalInertiaCharacter :
    P.inertia Gal(L/K) →*
      rootsOfUnity (tameRamificationIndex A L P) (integralClosure A L ⧸ P)

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.canonicalInertiaCharacter_spec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BU8.** The scaled inertia character identifies tame inertia with the
roots of unity of order `|I_t|`.  Its order is the prime-to-residue-characteristic part of the
ramification index, it is equivariant under the decomposition group, and these canonical
characters form the stated power-map square in every finite Galois tower.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalInertiaCharacter_spec :
    let B := integralClosure A L
    letI := IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K L B
    let D := MulAction.stabilizer Gal(L/K) P
    let I := P.inertia Gal(L/K)
    let e := P.ramificationIdx A
    let p := ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
    let q := wildRamificationFactor A L P
    let n := tameRamificationIndex A L P
    let conjugate : D → I → I := fun τ σ ↦
      ⟨(τ : Gal(L/K)) * (σ : Gal(L/K)) * (τ : Gal(L/K))⁻¹, by
        rw [Ideal.mem_inertia]
        intro x
        have hσ := (Ideal.mem_inertia.mp σ.property) ((τ : Gal(L/K))⁻¹ • x)
        have hτ := Ideal.smul_mem_pointwise_smul (τ : Gal(L/K)) _ P hσ
        rw [τ.property] at hτ
        simpa only [mul_smul, smul_sub, smul_inv_smul] using hτ⟩
    e = q * n ∧
    (p = 0 → q = 1) ∧
    (0 < p → ∃ a : ℕ, q = p ^ a) ∧
    rootsOfUnity e (B ⧸ P) = rootsOfUnity n (B ⧸ P) ∧
    Nat.card (tameInertiaGroup A K L P) = n ∧
    ∃ θcan : tameInertiaGroup A K L P ≃* rootsOfUnity n (B ⧸ P),
      (∀ σ : I, θcan (tameInertiaMap A K L P σ) =
        canonicalInertiaCharacter A K L P σ) ∧
      (∀ (τ : D) (σ : I),
        canonicalInertiaCharacter A K L P (conjugate τ σ) =
          (Ideal.quotientEquiv P P
            ((MulSemiringAction.toRingEquiv Gal(L/K) B) (τ : Gal(L/K)))
            τ.property.symm).toMulEquiv.restrictRootsOfUnity n
              (canonicalInertiaCharacter A K L P σ)) ∧
      ∀ (M : Type*) [Field M] [Algebra K M] [FiniteDimensional K M]
        [IsGalois K M] [Algebra L M] [IsScalarTower K L M]
        [Algebra A M] [IsScalarTower A K M] [IsScalarTower A L M]
        (r : Ideal (integralClosure A M)) [r.IsMaximal],
        let C := integralClosure A M
        let fBC : B →ₐ[A] C := (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom A L M).mapIntegralClosure
        letI : Algebra B C := fBC.toRingHom.toAlgebra
        letI : IsScalarTower A B C :=
          IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun x ↦ (fBC.commutes x).symm
        letI : Algebra.IsIntegral B C :=
          ⟨fun x ↦ IsIntegral.tower_top (IsIntegralClosure.isIntegral A M x)⟩
        letI : MulSemiringAction Gal(M/K) C :=
          IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K M C
        let Q := r.under B
        let pA := r.under A
        letI : r.LiesOver Q := ⟨rfl⟩
        letI : Q.LiesOver pA := ⟨r.under_under.symm⟩
        letI : Field (A ⧸ pA) := Ideal.Quotient.field pA
        letI : Field (B ⧸ Q) := Ideal.Quotient.field Q
        letI : Field (C ⧸ r) := Ideal.Quotient.field r
        letI : Algebra (B ⧸ Q) (C ⧸ r) := Ideal.Quotient.algebraOfLiesOver r Q
        let _e' := r.ramificationIdx A
        let n' := tameRamificationIndex A M r
        let n := tameRamificationIndex A L Q
        let res : Gal(M/K) →* Gal(L/K) := AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom L
        ∃ (resI : r.inertia Gal(M/K) →* Q.inertia Gal(L/K))
          (rootRestriction : rootsOfUnity n' (C ⧸ r) →* rootsOfUnity n (B ⧸ Q)),
          (∀ σ, (resI σ).1 = res σ.1) ∧
          n ∣ n' ∧
          (∀ ζ, algebraMap (B ⧸ Q) (C ⧸ r) (rootRestriction ζ).1.1 =
            (ζ ^ (n' / n)).1.1) ∧
          ∀ σ, rootRestriction (canonicalInertiaCharacter A K M r σ) =
            canonicalInertiaCharacter A K L Q (resI σ)

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.exists_tameInertiaCharacter
declarations.doc:
The canonical tame character has a pro-primary kernel and maps onto all compatible
families of prime-to-residue-characteristic roots of unity.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_tameInertiaCharacter
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (L : Type w) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [IsGalois K L]
    [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    (P : Ideal (integralClosure A L)) [P.IsMaximal] :
    let B := integralClosure A L
    letI := IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K L B
    let I := P.inertia Gal(L/K)
    let D := MulAction.stabilizer Gal(L/K) P
    let p := ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
    ∃ S : Set ℕ,
      1 ∈ S ∧
      (∀ n ∈ S, 0 < n) ∧
      (p ≠ 0 → ∀ n ∈ S, Nat.Coprime n p) ∧
      (∀ n ∈ S, ∃ z : B ⧸ P, IsPrimitiveRoot z n) ∧
      (∀ n ∈ S, ∀ m ∈ S, ∃ k ∈ S, n ∣ k ∧ m ∣ k) ∧
      (∀ n ∈ S, ∃ (F : FiniteGaloisIntermediateField K L),
        let C := integralClosure A F
        letI : IsScalarTower A F L :=
          IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ ↦ rfl
        let f : C →ₐ[A] B :=
          (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom A F L).mapIntegralClosure
        let q := P.comap f.toRingHom
        ∃ hq : q.IsMaximal,
          letI : q.IsMaximal := hq
          n ∣ IsDiscreteValuationRing.tameRamificationIndex A F q) ∧
      ∃ θ : I →* (∀ _ : S, (B ⧸ P)ˣ),
        (∀ σ : I, ∀ n : S, (θ σ n) ^ n.1 = 1) ∧
        (∀ σ : I, ∀ n m : S, n.1 ∣ m.1 →
          (θ σ m) ^ (m.1 / n.1) = θ σ n) ∧
        (∀ f : ∀ _ : S, (B ⧸ P)ˣ,
          (∀ n : S, (f n) ^ n.1 = 1) →
          (∀ n m : S, n.1 ∣ m.1 → (f m) ^ (m.1 / n.1) = f n) →
          ∃ σ : I, θ σ = f) ∧
        (∀ τ : D, ∀ σ : I,
          ∃ ρ : I,
            (ρ : Gal(L/K)) = (τ : Gal(L/K)) * (σ : Gal(L/K)) *
              (τ : Gal(L/K))⁻¹ ∧
            ∀ n : S, θ ρ n =
              (Ideal.quotientEquiv P P
                ((MulSemiringAction.toRingEquiv Gal(L/K) B) (τ : Gal(L/K)))
                τ.property.symm).toMulEquiv (θ σ n)) ∧
        (∀ τ : D, ∀ σ : I, σ ∈ θ.ker →
          ∃ ρ : I,
            (ρ : Gal(L/K)) = (τ : Gal(L/K)) * (σ : Gal(L/K)) *
              (τ : Gal(L/K))⁻¹ ∧ ρ ∈ θ.ker) ∧
        (∀ (F : FiniteGaloisIntermediateField K L),
          let C := integralClosure A F
          letI : IsScalarTower A F L :=
            IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ ↦ rfl
          letI : MulSemiringAction Gal(F/K) C :=
            IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K F C
          let f : C →ₐ[A] B :=
            (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom A F L).mapIntegralClosure
          let q := P.comap f.toRingHom
          ∀ [q.IsMaximal],
            ∃ hF : IsDiscreteValuationRing.tameRamificationIndex A F q ∈ S,
              ∀ σ : I,
                ∃ σF : q.inertia Gal(F/K),
                  (σF : Gal(F/K)) =
                    AlgEquiv.restrictNormal (σ : Gal(L/K))
                      (F : IntermediateField K L) ∧
                  ((θ σ ⟨IsDiscreteValuationRing.tameRamificationIndex A F q, hF⟩ :
                    (B ⧸ P)ˣ) : B ⧸ P) =
                    (Ideal.quotientMap P f.toRingHom le_rfl)
                      ((IsDiscreteValuationRing.canonicalInertiaCharacter A K F q σF).1.1)) ∧
        (∀ σ : I, σ ∈ θ.ker ↔
          ∀ (F : FiniteGaloisIntermediateField K L),
            let C := integralClosure A F
            letI : IsScalarTower A F L :=
              IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ ↦ rfl
            letI : MulSemiringAction Gal(F/K) C :=
              IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K F C
            let f : C →ₐ[A] B :=
              (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom A F L).mapIntegralClosure
            let q := P.comap f.toRingHom
            ∀ [q.IsMaximal],
              ∃ σF : q.inertia Gal(F/K),
                (σF : Gal(F/K)) =
                  AlgEquiv.restrictNormal (σ : Gal(L/K))
                    (F : IntermediateField K L) ∧
                σF ∈ IsDiscreteValuationRing.wildInertiaGroup A K F q) ∧
        (p = 0 → θ.ker = ⊥) ∧
        (0 < p →
          ∀ (H : Type*) [Group H] [Finite H] (f : θ.ker →* H),
            IsOpen (f.ker : Set θ.ker) → Function.Surjective f → IsPGroup p H)
declarations.comment: the wild–tame exact sequence and canonical character

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.isAlgClosure_quotient_integralClosure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BUB**, first assertion.  The residue field of the integral closure of a discrete
valuation ring in a separable closure of its fraction field is an algebraic closure of the
residue field of the discrete valuation ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAlgClosure_quotient_integralClosure
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (L : Type w) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [IsSepClosure K L]
    [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    (P : Ideal (integralClosure A L)) [P.IsMaximal] :
    IsAlgClosure (A ⧸ P.under A) (integralClosure A L ⧸ P)
declarations.comment: the residue field is an algebraic closure of the residue field of `A`

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.exists_residueSeparableClosureHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BUB**, the first exact sequence.  Write `κ = A ⧸ (P.under A)` for the residue
field of `A` and `κ̄` for the residue field at `P`, an algebraic closure of `κ`, and let
`κ^sep ⊆ κ̄` be the separable closure of `κ`.  The decomposition group `D` at `P` maps to
`Gal(κ^sep/κ)` by restricting the residue action, the inertia group `I` is contained in `D`,
the map is surjective, and the image in `Gal(L/K)` of its kernel is exactly `I`: the sequence
`1 → I → D → Gal(κ^sep/κ) → 1` is exact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_residueSeparableClosureHom
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (L : Type w) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [IsSepClosure K L]
    [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    (P : Ideal (integralClosure A L)) [P.IsMaximal] :
    letI := IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K L (integralClosure A L)
    letI : SMulCommClass Gal(L/K) A (integralClosure A L) :=
      ⟨fun σ a b ↦ by
        simp only [Algebra.smul_def, smul_mul']
        congr 1
        exact (galRestrict A K L (integralClosure A L) σ).commutes a⟩
    let κsep := separableClosure (A ⧸ P.under A) (integralClosure A L ⧸ P)
    IsSepClosure (A ⧸ P.under A) κsep ∧
    P.inertia Gal(L/K) ≤ MulAction.stabilizer Gal(L/K) P ∧
    ∃ θ : MulAction.stabilizer Gal(L/K) P →* (κsep ≃ₐ[A ⧸ P.under A] κsep),
      (∀ (σ : MulAction.stabilizer Gal(L/K) P) (x : κsep),
        (θ σ x : integralClosure A L ⧸ P) =
          Ideal.Quotient.stabilizerHom P (P.under A) Gal(L/K) σ (x : integralClosure A L ⧸ P)) ∧
      Function.Surjective θ ∧
      θ.ker.map (MulAction.stabilizer Gal(L/K) P).subtype = P.inertia Gal(L/K)
declarations.comment: the exact sequence `1 → I → D → Gal(κ^sep/κ) → 1`

declarations.doc:
The residue field of the integral closure in a separable closure is
algebraically closed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAlgClosed_quotient_integralClosure
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (L : Type w) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [IsSepClosure K L]
    [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    (P : Ideal (integralClosure A L)) [P.IsMaximal] :
    letI : Field (integralClosure A L ⧸ P) := Ideal.Quotient.field P

declarations.comment: the algebraically closed residue field

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.primeToChar_divides_tameRamificationIndex
declarations.doc:
Every positive order prime to the residue characteristic divides a tame
ramification index at a finite Galois subextension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem primeToChar_divides_tameRamificationIndex
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (L : Type w) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [IsSepClosure K L]
    [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    (P : Ideal (integralClosure A L)) [P.IsMaximal]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n)
    (hcoprime : ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) = 0 ∨
      Nat.Coprime n (ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A))) :
    ∃ (F : FiniteGaloisIntermediateField K L),
      let C := integralClosure A F
      letI : IsScalarTower A F L :=
        IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ ↦ rfl
      let f : C →ₐ[A] integralClosure A L :=
        (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom A F L).mapIntegralClosure
      let q := P.comap f.toRingHom
      ∃ hq : q.IsMaximal,
        letI : q.IsMaximal := hq
        n ∣ IsDiscreteValuationRing.tameRamificationIndex A F q
declarations.comment: cofinality of prime-to-characteristic orders

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.exists_primeToChar_tameInertiaCharacter
declarations.doc:
The canonical tame inertia character at a separable closure has wild kernel
and reaches every compatible family of prime-to-characteristic roots of unity.
Its finite-level formula specifies the character independently of choices.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_primeToChar_tameInertiaCharacter
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (L : Type w) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [IsSepClosure K L]
    [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    (P : Ideal (integralClosure A L)) [P.IsMaximal] :
    let B := integralClosure A L
    letI := IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K L B
    let I := P.inertia Gal(L/K)
    let D := MulAction.stabilizer Gal(L/K) P
    let p := ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
    let N := {n : ℕ // 0 < n ∧ (p = 0 ∨ Nat.Coprime n p)}
    ∃ θ : I →* (∀ _ : N, (B ⧸ P)ˣ),
      (∀ σ : I, ∀ n : N, (θ σ n) ^ n.1 = 1) ∧
      (∀ σ : I, ∀ n m : N, n.1 ∣ m.1 →
        (θ σ m) ^ (m.1 / n.1) = θ σ n) ∧
      (∀ f : ∀ _ : N, (B ⧸ P)ˣ,
        (f ∈ θ.range ↔
          ((∀ n : N, (f n) ^ n.1 = 1) ∧
           (∀ n m : N, n.1 ∣ m.1 → (f m) ^ (m.1 / n.1) = f n)))) ∧
      (∀ τ : D, ∀ σ : I,
        ∃ ρ : I,
          (ρ : Gal(L/K)) = (τ : Gal(L/K)) * (σ : Gal(L/K)) *
            (τ : Gal(L/K))⁻¹ ∧
          (∀ n : N, θ ρ n =
            (Ideal.quotientEquiv P P
              ((MulSemiringAction.toRingEquiv Gal(L/K) B) (τ : Gal(L/K)))
              τ.property.symm).toMulEquiv (θ σ n))) ∧
      (∀ τ : D, ∀ σ : I, σ ∈ θ.ker →
        ∃ ρ : I,
          (ρ : Gal(L/K)) = (τ : Gal(L/K)) * (σ : Gal(L/K)) *
            (τ : Gal(L/K))⁻¹ ∧ ρ ∈ θ.ker) ∧
      (∀ (F : FiniteGaloisIntermediateField K L),
        let C := integralClosure A F
        letI : IsScalarTower A F L :=
          IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ ↦ rfl
        letI : MulSemiringAction Gal(F/K) C :=
          IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K F C
        let f : C →ₐ[A] B :=
          (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom A F L).mapIntegralClosure
        let q := P.comap f.toRingHom
        ∀ [q.IsMaximal], ∀ n : N,
          n.1 ∣ IsDiscreteValuationRing.tameRamificationIndex A F q →
          ∀ σ : I,
            ∃ σF : q.inertia Gal(F/K),
              (σF : Gal(F/K)) =
                AlgEquiv.restrictNormal (σ : Gal(L/K))
                  (F : IntermediateField K L) ∧
              ((θ σ n : (B ⧸ P)ˣ) : B ⧸ P) =
                (Ideal.quotientMap P f.toRingHom le_rfl)
                  (((IsDiscreteValuationRing.canonicalInertiaCharacter A K F q σF).1.1) ^
                    (IsDiscreteValuationRing.tameRamificationIndex A F q / n.1))) ∧
      (p = 0 → θ.ker = ⊥) ∧
      (0 < p →
        ∀ (H : Type*) [Group H] [Finite H] (f : θ.ker →* H),
          IsOpen (f.ker : Set θ.ker) → Function.Surjective f → IsPGroup p H)
declarations.comment: the wild–tame exact sequence and canonical character

declarations.name: accp_of_existsUnique_irreducible_factors
declarations.doc:
A UFD satisfies the ascending chain condition for principal ideals: if `R` is a domain in
which every nonzero element is, up to a unit, a product of irreducibles, uniquely up to
associates and order (the definition of a UFD, Stacks 034S), then every ascending chain of
principal ideals of `R` stabilizes. As in Stacks, the proof factors elements into primes.
declarations.statement:
theorem accp_of_existsUnique_irreducible_factors {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    (eif : ∀ a : R, a ≠ 0 → ∃ f : Multiset R, (∀ b ∈ f, Irreducible b) ∧ Associated f.prod a)
    (uif : ∀ f g : Multiset R, (∀ x ∈ f, Irreducible x) → (∀ x ∈ g, Irreducible x) →
      Associated f.prod g.prod → Multiset.Rel Associated f g)
    (f : ℕ → Ideal R) (hp : ∀ i, (f i).IsPrincipal) (hm : ∀ i, f i ≤ f (i + 1)) :
    ∃ n, ∀ m, n ≤ m → f m = f n

declarations.name: CommRingCat.isFiltered_costructuredArrow_and_isDenseAt_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
Let `R → A` be a ring map and let `𝓘 = CostructuredArrow P.ι A` be the category of
`R`-algebra maps `A' → A` with `A'` of finite presentation over `R`. Then `𝓘` is filtered,
and `A` is the colimit of the `A'` over `𝓘`, via the tautological cocone whose leg at
`A' → A` is that map (which is what `Functor.isDenseAt` asserts).
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFiltered_costructuredArrow_and_isDenseAt_finitePresentation
    {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (A : Under R) :
    IsFiltered (CostructuredArrow
        (ObjectProperty.ι fun B : Under R ↦ B.hom.hom.FinitePresentation) A) ∧
      (ObjectProperty.ι fun B : Under R ↦ B.hom.hom.FinitePresentation).isDenseAt A
declarations.comment:
The category `𝓘` is `CostructuredArrow P.ι A` for `P` the property of being
of finite presentation over `R`, and "the colimit of the `A'` is `A`" is
`P.ι.isDenseAt A`, which pins the colimit cocone to the tautological one. No smallness
device is needed. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperSectionsGeom.componentwiseArtinianDecomposition
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BUG] (2).** The ring of global functions on a scheme proper over a field `k`
is a finite product of Artinian local `k`-algebras, with one factor for each connected component
of `X`, the factor at a component being the ring of functions on that component and the
isomorphism being simultaneous restriction.

No hypothesis beyond properness: `X` need not be connected, reduced, normal or integral, and the
structure morphism need not be affine.
declarations.statement:
def componentwiseArtinianDecomposition [IsProper f] :
    GlobalSectionsComponentDecomposition k f
declarations.comment: clause (2): for an ARBITRARY proper scheme over a field, the global functions are a product of Artinian local algebras over that field with one factor for each connected component. The index set is the set of connected components itself, the product is finite because a proper scheme over a field is a Noetherian space, and the isomorphism is pinned to be simultaneous restriction, so the factor at a component is the ring of functions on that component. Openness of the components replaces the source's correspondence between primitive idempotents and components; the product decomposition is the sheaf condition for a disjoint open cover; each factor is Artinian because it is a quotient of the global functions, finite over the base field by clause (1), and local because its component is connected.

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperSectionsGeom.isGeometricallyIrreducible_globalSections_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BUG] (5).** Let `X` be a geometrically connected proper scheme over a field
`k`. Then the ring of global sections of `X`, with its canonical `k`-algebra structure, is
geometrically irreducible over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyIrreducible_globalSections_of_isProper
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [GeometricallyConnected f] [IsProper f] :
    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, ⊤) :=
      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k Γ(X, ⊤)
declarations.comment: clause (5): for a GEOMETRICALLY CONNECTED proper scheme over a field k, the global sections are geometrically irreducible over k: every base change to a field extension of k has irreducible spectrum.

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperSectionsGeom.isGeometricallyIrreducible_globalSections_of_geometricallyIrreducible
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BUG] (6).** Let `X` be a geometrically *irreducible* proper scheme over a
field `k`. Then the ring of global sections of `X`, with its canonical `k`-algebra structure, is
geometrically irreducible over `k`.

A geometrically irreducible morphism is geometrically connected, every base change of it having
an irreducible and hence connected underlying space, so this is clause (5) applied to the same
`X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyIrreducible_globalSections_of_geometricallyIrreducible
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [GeometricallyIrreducible f] [IsProper f] :
    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, ⊤) :=
      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k Γ(X, ⊤)
declarations.comment: clause (6): for a GEOMETRICALLY IRREDUCIBLE proper scheme over a field k, the global sections are geometrically irreducible over k. The source deduces this clause from clause (5) by the remark that a geometrically irreducible scheme is geometrically connected, and that is what is done here: every base change has an irreducible, hence connected, underlying space.

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperSectionsGeom.isField_globalSections_of_connectedSpace_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
The ring of global functions on a connected *reduced* scheme proper over a field is a
field.

This is clauses (2) and (3) read at a single connected component: a reduced Artinian local ring
is a field. The clauses in full are `componentwiseArtinianDecomposition` (clause (2)) and
`globalSectionsFieldDecomposition_of_isReduced` (clause (3)).
declarations.statement:
theorem isField_globalSections_of_connectedSpace_of_isReduced
    [IsProper f] [ConnectedSpace X] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsReduced X] : IsField Γ(X, ⊤)
declarations.comment: special case of clauses (2) and (3): X connected and reduced, where the ring of global functions is a field

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperSectionsGeom.isSeparable_globalSections_of_connectedSpace_of_geometricallyReduced
declarations.doc:
The field of global functions on a connected *geometrically reduced* scheme proper over a
field `k` is separable over `k`.

This is clauses (2), (3) and (4) read at a single connected component. The clauses in full are
stated by other declarations, among them `GlobalSectionsFieldDecomposition.factor_isSeparable`
(clause (4)).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparable_globalSections_of_connectedSpace_of_geometricallyReduced
    [IsProper f] [ConnectedSpace X] [GeometricallyReduced f] :
    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    Algebra.IsSeparable k Γ(X, ⊤)
declarations.comment: special case of clauses (2), (3) and (4): X connected and geometrically reduced, where the field of global functions is separable over k

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperSectionsGeom.isIso_globalSections_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BUG] (7).** The canonical homomorphism from a field to the global sections
of a geometrically reduced, geometrically connected proper scheme over that field is an
isomorphism.

This is the whole of clause (7): the source's conclusion `A = k` is the assertion that the
homomorphism `k ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` induced by the structure morphism is an isomorphism, the standard
identification `Γ(Spec k, 𝒪) ≅ k` being part of that map.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_globalSections_of_isProper
    [GeometricallyReduced f] [GeometricallyConnected f] [IsProper f] :
    IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop)
declarations.comment: clause (7): for a GEOMETRICALLY REDUCED and GEOMETRICALLY CONNECTED proper scheme over a field k, the global sections are k. The equality A = k is stated canonically, as the induced homomorphism from k to the global sections being an isomorphism. Geometric irreducibility of the global sections (clause (5)) makes the extension purely inseparable; geometric reducedness of a stalk makes it separable (Tag 030W, Tag 035W); a purely inseparable separable extension is trivial. No finiteness of the global sections over k is used.

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperSectionsGeom.moduleFinite_globalSections_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BUG] (1).** The ring of global functions on a scheme proper over a field `k`
is a finite `k`-module, for the `k`-algebra structure the structure morphism induces.

No hypothesis beyond properness: the scheme need not be integral, connected, normal or reduced,
and the structure morphism need not be affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleFinite_globalSections_of_isProper [IsProper f] :
    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    Module.Finite k Γ(X, ⊤)
declarations.comment: clause (1): the global sections of an arbitrary proper scheme over a field form a finite module over that field, with no integrality, connectedness, normality, reducedness or affineness hypothesis. Finiteness of coherent cohomology over a field (Tag 02O6) plus coherence of the structure sheaf (Tag 01XZ), with the degree-zero identification of cohomology and sections supplied here from left exactness of global sections.

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperSectionsGeom.globalSectionsFieldDecomposition_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BUG] (3).** The ring of global functions on a *reduced* scheme proper over a
field `k` is a finite product of finite field extensions of `k`.

The hypothesis is reducedness of `X`, weaker than the normality assumed by
`AlgebraicGeometry.globalSectionsFieldDecomposition_of_isNormal`, which this supersedes.
declarations.statement:
def globalSectionsFieldDecomposition_of_isReduced [IsProper f] [IsReduced X] :
    GlobalSectionsFieldDecomposition k X f
declarations.comment: clause (3): for a REDUCED proper scheme over a field, the presentation of the global sections as a finite product of finite field extensions of the base field. Clause (1) makes the ring Artinian; an Artinian reduced ring is the product of its residue fields. Reducedness only, where the library's normal-case decomposition needs each connected component irreducible. Separability of the factors is clause (4) and is not asserted here.

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperSectionsGeom.GlobalSectionsFieldDecomposition.factor_isSeparable
declarations.doc:
Every field factor in a finite product decomposition of the global sections of a
geometrically reduced proper scheme is separable over the base field.
Together with `GlobalSectionsFieldDecomposition.factorModuleFinite`, this says that every factor
is a finite separable extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem GlobalSectionsFieldDecomposition.factor_isSeparable
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsProper f] [GeometricallyReduced f] (D : GlobalSectionsFieldDecomposition k X f)
    (i : Fin D.numFactors) : Algebra.IsSeparable k (D.factor i)
declarations.comment: clause (4): for a GEOMETRICALLY REDUCED proper scheme over a field k, every field factor of a presentation of the global sections as a finite product of finite field extensions of k (clause (3)) is separable over k. The decomposition is an argument, so the conclusion holds for every such presentation, in particular the one clause (3) constructs.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_globalSections_of_geometricallyIntegral
declarations.doc:
The canonical homomorphism from a field to the global sections of a geometrically integral
proper scheme over that field is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_globalSections_of_geometricallyIntegral
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [GeometricallyIntegral f] [IsProper f] :
    IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop)
declarations.comment: clause (8): for a GEOMETRICALLY INTEGRAL proper scheme over a field k, the global sections are k. The equality A = k is stated canonically, as the induced homomorphism from k to the global sections being an isomorphism. The source deduces this clause from clause (7): a geometrically integral morphism is geometrically reduced, and geometrically connected because every base change of it has an integral, hence irreducible, hence connected, underlying space.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lowerSemicontinuous_numGeometricConnectedComponents
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BUI].**  For a flat proper morphism of finite presentation, the number of
geometric connected components of the fibres is a lower semicontinuous function on the base.

The count is the `ℕ∞`-valued function of Tag 055F.  The proof is the source's:  the Stein
factorization `f = f.fromNormalization ∘ f.toNormalization` has a first factor with
geometrically connected fibres (Tag 03H2), so it does not change the count, and a second factor
that is integral and, as `f` is flat of finite presentation and `f.toNormalization` is
surjective, universally open.
declarations.statement:
theorem lowerSemicontinuous_numGeometricConnectedComponents {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsProper f] [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] :
    LowerSemicontinuous (numGeometricConnectedComponents f)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.relativeDualizingModule_upperShriek_structureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BUL.** (1) Let `S` be Noetherian, `f : X ⟶ Y` a locally quasi-finite
morphism of schemes separated and of finite type over `S` and `j` any compactification computing
`f^!` (Tag 0A9Y). Then `H⁰(f^!𝒪_Y)` is the sheaf of a relative dualizing module datum of `f`
(Tag 0BVG): its sections over affine opens `V ⊆ f⁻¹U` are identified with `ω_{Γ(V)/Γ(U)}`,
compatibly with restriction; and for every relative dualizing module `ω_{X/Y}` there is exactly
one family of isomorphisms on sections, compatible with restriction, carrying these affine
identifications to those of `ω_{X/Y}` — the canonical isomorphism `H⁰(f^!𝒪_Y) = ω_{X/Y}`.
(2) Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme with a dualizing complex `ω_S^•`, `f : X ⟶ Y` a locally
quasi-finite morphism of schemes of finite type over `S` (not necessarily separated), `ω_X^•`,
`ω_Y^•` dualizing complexes normalized relative to `ω_S^•` and `f_new^! = D_X ∘ Lf^* ∘ D_Y`.
Then `H⁰(f_new^!𝒪_Y)` is the sheaf of a relative dualizing module datum of `f`, i.e.
`H⁰(f_new^!𝒪_Y) = ω_{X/Y}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDualizingModule_upperShriek_structureSheaf :
    (∀ {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian S] {X Y : FTS S} (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyQuasiFinite f.left]
        (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left)),
        (∃ D : RelativeDualizingModuleData f.left, D.sheaf = upperShriekStructureSheafZeroth f j) ∧
        ∀ ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f.left,
          ∃! E : ∀ W : X.left.Opens,
              Γ(upperShriekStructureSheafZeroth f j, W) ≃ₗ[Γ(X.left, W)] Γ(ω.sheaf, W),
            (∀ (W W' : X.left.Opens) (h : W' ≤ W) (s : Γ(upperShriekStructureSheafZeroth f j, W)),
                E W' (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentBaseChange.restrictₗ _ h s) =
                  Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentBaseChange.restrictₗ ω.sheaf h (E W s)) ∧
              ∀ (U : Y.left.affineOpens) (V : X.left.affineOpens) (hVU : V.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ U.1),
                letI : Algebra Γ(Y.left, U.1) Γ(X.left, V.1) := (f.left.appLE U V hVU).hom.toAlgebra
                ∀ (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, u, u} Γ(Y.left, U.1) Γ(X.left, V.1))
                  (s : Γ(upperShriekStructureSheafZeroth f j, V.1)),
                  ω.localEquiv U V hVU F (E V.1 s) =
                    (upperShriekRelativeDualizingModuleData f j).localEquiv U V hVU F s) ∧
    (∀ (c : ∀ {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y), IsShriekable f → CompactificationOf (Over.mk f))
        {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) {q : Y ⟶ S} {p : X ⟶ S}
        {hp : IsFiniteTypeOverNoetherian p} {hq : IsFiniteTypeOverNoetherian q}
        {ωS : quasiCoherentDerivedCategoryPlusOfModel S}
        (𝒦X : NormalizedOnOpens (UpperShriek.ofCompactifications c) hp ωS)
        (𝒦Y : NormalizedOnOpens (UpperShriek.ofCompactifications c) hq ωS)
        (_hpe : f ≫ q = p) (_hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj)
        [LocallyQuasiFinite f],
        haveI := hp.source_noetherian
        haveI := hq.source_noetherian
        ∃ D : RelativeDualizingModuleData f,
          D.sheaf = NormalizedOnOpens.newShriekStructureSheafZeroth c f 𝒦X 𝒦Y)
declarations.comment: the whole lemma: H^0(V, f^! O) = omega_{B/A} compatibly with restriction, the canonical isomorphism H^0(f^! O) = omega_{Y/X}, and H^0(f_new^! O) = omega_{Y/X}

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.upperShriekRelativeDualizingModuleData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BUL, first assertion.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-finite morphism
of schemes separated and of finite type over a Noetherian scheme `S`, and `f^!` the upper shriek
of [Stacks, Tag 0A9Y] at any compactification `j`. Then `H⁰(f^!𝒪_Y)` is a relative dualizing
module for `f` (Tag 0BVG): for affine opens `Spec(B) = V ⊆ X`, `Spec(A) = U ⊆ Y` with
`f(V) ⊆ U` its sections over `V` are identified with `ω_{B/A}`, independently of the
finite-open factorization computing `ω_{B/A}` and compatibly with the restriction maps.
declarations.statement:
def upperShriekRelativeDualizingModuleData (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left)) :
    RelativeDualizingModuleData f.left
declarations.comment: first assertion: H^0(V, f^! O) = omega_{B/A}, compatible with restriction

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.existsUnique_upperShriekRelativeDualizingComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BUL, first assertion (the canonical isomorphism).** The affine
identifications of `upperShriekRelativeDualizingModuleData` define a canonical isomorphism
`H⁰(f^!𝒪_Y) ≅ ω_{X/Y}` with any relative dualizing module `ω_{X/Y}` of Tag 0BVG: there is exactly
one family of isomorphisms on sections, compatible with restriction, carrying the identification
of `H⁰(V, f^!𝒪_Y)` with `ω_{B/A}` to that of `Γ(V, ω_{X/Y})`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_upperShriekRelativeDualizingComparison
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left)) (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f.left) :
    ∃! E : ∀ W : X.left.Opens,
        Γ(upperShriekStructureSheafZeroth f j, W) ≃ₗ[Γ(X.left, W)] Γ(ω.sheaf, W),
      (∀ (W W' : X.left.Opens) (h : W' ≤ W) (s : Γ(upperShriekStructureSheafZeroth f j, W)),
          E W' (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentBaseChange.restrictₗ _ h s) =
            Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentBaseChange.restrictₗ ω.sheaf h (E W s)) ∧
        ∀ (U : Y.left.affineOpens) (V : X.left.affineOpens) (hVU : V.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ U.1),
          letI : Algebra Γ(Y.left, U.1) Γ(X.left, V.1) := (f.left.appLE U V hVU).hom.toAlgebra
          ∀ (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, u, u} Γ(Y.left, U.1) Γ(X.left, V.1))
            (s : Γ(upperShriekStructureSheafZeroth f j, V.1)),
            ω.localEquiv U V hVU F (E V.1 s) =
              (upperShriekRelativeDualizingModuleData f j).localEquiv U V hVU F s
declarations.comment: first assertion: the canonical isomorphism H^0(f^! O) = omega_{Y/X}

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.etale_fromNormalization_of_properFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BUN.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a proper morphism of schemes which is flat,
of finite presentation and has geometrically reduced fibres, and let `X ⟶ S' ⟶ S` be its Stein
factorization. Then the second factor `S' ⟶ S` is étale.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etale_fromNormalization_of_properFlat (hfp : FinitePresentation f) :
    Etale f.fromNormalization
declarations.comment: étaleness of the second factor

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.isFinite_fromNormalization_of_properFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BUN.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a proper morphism of schemes which is flat,
of finite presentation and has geometrically reduced fibres, and let `X ⟶ S' ⟶ S` be its Stein
factorization. Then the second factor `S' ⟶ S` is finite.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFinite_fromNormalization_of_properFlat (hfp : FinitePresentation f) :
    IsFinite f.fromNormalization
declarations.comment: finiteness of the second factor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_continuousMonoidHom_isSpecializationMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BUP.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a proper morphism with geometrically
connected fibres, let `s' ⇝ s` be a specialization of points of `S`, let `s̄'` and `s̄` be
geometric points over `s'` and `s`, and choose geometric base points of the two geometric fibres
`X_{s̄'}` and `X_{s̄}`. Then there is a specialization map `π₁(X_{s̄'}) ⟶ π₁(X_{s̄})`, that is, a
continuous homomorphism satisfying `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSpecializationMap`: it is the composite
`π₁(X_{s̄'}) → π₁(X_A) ≅ π₁(X_{s̄})` for `A` the strict henselization of `𝒪_{S,s}` and a chosen
factorization of `s̄'` through `Spec A`.

The closed-fibre equivalence `π₁(X_A) ≅ π₁(X_{s̄})` is
`isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_fiberOverGeometricPointMap` (Stacks 0A48, 0BTW, 0A49).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_continuousMonoidHom_isSpecializationMap (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f]
    [GeometricallyConnected f] (s' s : GeometricPoint S)
    (hspec : s'.hom (closedPoint s'.residueField) ⤳ s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField))
    (x' : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s'))
    (x : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s)) :
    ∃ sp : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s') x' →ₜ*
        EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s) x,
      IsSpecializationMap f s' s x' x sp
declarations.comment: the construction of the specialization map: for `f` proper with geometrically connected fibres, a specialization `s' ⇝ s` and geometric points `s̄'`, `s̄` over them, a continuous homomorphism `π₁(X_{s̄'}) → π₁(X_{s̄})` which is the composite `π₁(X_{s̄'}) → π₁(X_A) = π₁(X_{κ(s)^{sep}}) = π₁(X_{s̄})` of the source, recorded by `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSpecializationMap`. As in the source the map depends on the choice of the factorization `φ : s̄' → Spec A`, so this is stated as existence. The equality `π₁(X_A) = π₁(X_{s̄})` is proved from Stacks 0A48, 0BTW and 0A49 by `AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_fiberOverGeometricPointMap`.

declarations.name: IsBaseChange.support_eq_preimage_comap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BUR**. Let `R → S` be a ring map, let `M` be a finite `R`-module and let
`f : M →ₗ[R] N` exhibit the `S`-module `N` as the base change `S ⊗_R M`. Then `Supp_S(N)` is the
inverse image of `Supp_R(M)` under the map `Spec(S) → Spec(R)` induced by `R → S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem support_eq_preimage_comap {R S M N : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [AddCommGroup N]
    [Module R N] [Module S N] [IsScalarTower R S N] {f : M →ₗ[R] N} (h : IsBaseChange S f) :
    Module.support S N = PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) ⁻¹' Module.support R M

declarations.name: Module.ringKrullDim_quotient_eq_supportDim_and_minimal_support_of_mem_associatedPrimes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BUS**.
Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring and let `M` be a finite Cohen-Macaulay `R`-module, that is,
one whose depth along the maximal ideal equals the dimension of its support. If `𝔭` is an
associated prime of `M`, then `dim(R/𝔭) = dim Supp(M)` and `𝔭` is a minimal point of `Supp(M)`.

In particular `M` has no embedded associated primes: since `Ass(M) ⊆ Supp(M)`, a prime minimal in
`Supp(M)` is minimal in `Ass(M)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ringKrullDim_quotient_eq_supportDim_and_minimal_support_of_mem_associatedPrimes
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (hCM : (depth R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) M : WithBot ℕ∞) = supportDim R M)
    {p : PrimeSpectrum R} (hp : p.asIdeal ∈ associatedPrimes R M) :
    ringKrullDim (R ⧸ p.asIdeal) = supportDim R M ∧ Minimal (· ∈ support R M) p
declarations.comment: Cohen-Macaulayness is spelled out as `depth_𝔪(M) = dim Supp(M)`, the definition Stacks 00N8 unfolds to, there being no predicate for it in this library yet.

declarations.name: coheight_eq_supportDim_of_mem_associatedPrimes_of_isCohenMacaulayModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BUS** (EGA Ch. 0, Proposition 16.5.4). Let `M` be a finite Cohen-Macaulay module
over a Noetherian local ring `R` and let `p ∈ Ass(M)`. Then `dim (R/p) = dim (Supp M)`, and `p`
is a minimal prime of the support of `M`. In particular `M` has no embedded associated primes.

Here `dim (R/p)` is `Order.coheight p` in `PrimeSpectrum R`, and minimality of `p` in the support
is spelled out as: no prime of `Supp M` is strictly below `p`.

The dimension equality holds because `dim (Supp M) = depth M ≤ dim (R/p)` (Stacks `0AUJ`, the
Cohen-Macaulay form of which is `supportDim_le_coheight_of_isCohenMacaulayModule`) while
`dim (R/p) ≤ dim (Supp M)`
since `Supp M` is closed under specialization and contains `p`. Minimality then follows: a prime
`q ∈ Supp M` with `q < p` would give `dim (R/p) + 1 ≤ dim (R/q) ≤ dim (Supp M) = dim (R/p)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coheight_eq_supportDim_of_mem_associatedPrimes_of_isCohenMacaulayModule
    (hCM : IsCohenMacaulayModule R M) {p : Ideal R} (hp : p ∈ associatedPrimes R M) :
    (Order.coheight (⟨p, hp.1⟩ : PrimeSpectrum R) : WithBot ℕ∞) = Module.supportDim R M ∧
      ∀ q ∈ Module.support R M, q ≤ (⟨p, hp.1⟩ : PrimeSpectrum R) →
        q = (⟨p, hp.1⟩ : PrimeSpectrum R)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.exists_isTrivial_restrict_preimage_of_isFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BUT**, written with `Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsTrivial`: for a finite
morphism `f : X ⟶ Y`, an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `L` and a point `y` of `Y`, there is an open
neighbourhood `V` of `y` over which `L` becomes trivial on the inverse image.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isTrivial_restrict_preimage_of_isFinite {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsFinite f] (L : X.Modules)
    [IsInvertible X.presheaf (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L] (y : Y) :
    ∃ V : Y.Opens, y ∈ V ∧
      IsTrivial (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme.presheaf
        (structureSheafRing (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace).property
        (L.restrict (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_nat_topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber
declarations.doc: The local dimension of a fibre of a locally finitely presented morphism is finite.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_nat_topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (x : X) :
    ∃ n : ℕ,
      topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: finiteness of the fibre dimension

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCohenMacaulayAt_tfae
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be flat and locally of finite presentation and let `n` be the dimension of
the fibre of `f` through `x` at `x`. Then `f` is Cohen–Macaulay at `x` if and only if some open
neighbourhood of `x` carries a locally quasi-finite `S`-morphism to affine `n`-space over `S`
that is flat at `x`, if and only if some open neighbourhood carries a locally quasi-finite flat
such morphism, if and only if every `S`-morphism to affine `n`-space from an open neighbourhood
of `x` that is quasi-finite at `x` is flat at `x`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCohenMacaulayAt_tfae {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (x : X) (n : ℕ)
    (hn : topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    List.TFAE [
      Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulayAt f
        (fun s => isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation f s) x,
      ∃ (U : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ U.1)
          (g : U.toScheme ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) S),
        (g ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) S ↘ S) = U.ι ≫ f) ∧
        (LocallyOfFiniteType g ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite g) ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatAt g.toLRSHom.toShHom ⟨x, hx⟩,
      ∃ (U : X.Opens) (_hx : x ∈ U.1)
          (g : U.toScheme ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) S),
        (g ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) S ↘ S) = U.ι ≫ f) ∧
        (LocallyOfFiniteType g ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite g) ∧ Flat g,
      ∀ (U : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ U.1)
          (g : U.toScheme ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) S),
        (g ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) S ↘ S) = U.ι ≫ f) →
        (AlgebraicGeometry.quasiFiniteAt g ⟨x, hx⟩ →
          AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatAt g.toLRSHom.toShHom ⟨x, hx⟩)]
declarations.comment: the four equivalent conditions

declarations.name: Dualizing.supportDim_quotient_add_depth_eq_supportDim
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BUX.** The depth of a finite Cohen--Macaulay module
along a proper ideal is the drop in the dimension of its support on passing to
the quotient by that ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportDim_quotient_add_depth_eq_supportDim
    {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≠ ⊤) (hM : Module.IsCohenMacaulayAtMaximalIdeal R M) :
    Module.supportDim R (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) +
        (Module.depth R I M : WithBot ℕ∞) =
      Module.supportDim R M

declarations.name: Dualizing.ringKrullDim_fiber_le_depth_add_ringKrullDim_quotient_of_flat
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a flat local homomorphism with Noetherian local target. If its closed
fibre is Cohen--Macaulay, then the depth of `S` along an ideal `I` is at least the difference
between the dimension of the closed fibre and that of its quotient by `I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_fiber_le_depth_add_ringKrullDim_quotient_of_flat
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S]
    [Module.Flat R S] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] (I : Ideal S)
    (hCM : Module.IsCohenMacaulayAtMaximalIdeal S
      (S ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (maximalIdeal R))) :
    I = ⊤ ∨
      ringKrullDim (S ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (maximalIdeal R)) ≤
        (Module.depth S I S : WithBot ℕ∞) +
        ringKrullDim
            (S ⧸ (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (maximalIdeal R) ⊔ I))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.sections_rightAdjoint_restrictionToStructureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BUZ (sections on an affine open).** If `f : Y ⟶ X` is
affine and `U ⊆ X` is affine, sections over `U` of the internal-Hom right adjoint
are the `Γ(X,U)`-linear maps from `Γ(Y,f⁻¹U)` to the sections of `F` over `U`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def sections_rightAdjoint_restrictionToStructureSheaf
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsAffineHom f] (F : X.Modules)
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
    letI : Algebra Γ(X, U) Γ(Y, f ⁻¹ᵁ U) := (f.app U).hom.toAlgebra
    (((RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.homSheaf f.toRingCatSheafHom).obj F).val.obj
        (op U) : Type u) ≃+
      (ModuleCat.of Γ(X, U) Γ(Y, f ⁻¹ᵁ U) ⟶ ModuleCat.of Γ(X, U) Γ(F, U))
declarations.comment: sections on an affine open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedRestriction_adj_derivedHomSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BV0.** For a morphism of schemes `f : Y ⟶ X`, the derived internal-Hom functor
`R ℰom(f₊ 𝒪_Y, -) : D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(f₊ 𝒪_Y)` is right adjoint to the functor `D(f₊ 𝒪_Y) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)`
induced by restriction of scalars.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedRestriction_adj_derivedHomSheaf :
    Nonempty (derivedRestrictionOfScalars f ⊣ derivedHomSheaf f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedHomSheaf_comp_derivedRestriction_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BV1.** Following `R ℰom(f₊ 𝒪_Y, -)` by the functor `D(f₊ 𝒪_Y) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)` induced
by restriction of scalars gives `R ℰom_{𝒪_X}(f₊ 𝒪_Y, -)`. The displayed compatibility with the
comparison maps characterizes the isomorphism uniquely.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedHomSheaf_comp_derivedRestriction_iso :
    ∃! e : derivedHomSheaf f ⋙ derivedRestrictionOfScalars f ≅
        derivedInternalHomPushforward f,
      compositeDerivedHomSheafUnit f ≫ whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Qh e.hom =
        derivedInternalHomPushforwardUnit f

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.upperShriekRestrictIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G4J (Lemma 48.17.2).** In Situation 48.16.1 let
`j : U ⟶ X`, `j' : V ⟶ Y` be open immersions and `f : X ⟶ Y`, `g : U ⟶ V` morphisms of
`FTS S` with `j ≫ f = g ≫ j'`. Then `j^* ∘ f^! ≅ g^! ∘ (j')^*` as functors on
`D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, for arbitrary compactifications `cf` of `f` and `cg` of `g` computing `f^!` and
`g^!`; here `j^*`, `(j')^*` are the restrictions to the opens.

This is also the first assertion of [Stacks, Tag 0BV2] (Remark 48.17.5): for open
`U ⊆ X`, `V ⊆ Y` with `f(U) ⊆ V` and `g` the restriction of `f`, `(f^!E)|_U = g^!(E|_V)` for
`E ∈ D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, stated here for arbitrary open immersions and compactifications.
declarations.statement:
def upperShriekRestrictIso :
    (ObjectProperty.ι _ : quasiCoherentDerivedCategoryPlusOfModel Y.left ⥤ _) ⋙ upperShriek f cf ⋙
        OpenImmersion.restrictedDerivedRestrict j.left ≅
      (ObjectProperty.ι _ : quasiCoherentDerivedCategoryPlusOfModel Y.left ⥤ _) ⋙
        OpenImmersion.restrictedDerivedRestrict j'.left ⋙ upperShriek g cg
declarations.comment: part (a): (f^!E)|_U ≅ g^!(E|_V) for E in D^+_QCoh, every open square and every pair of compactifications

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.restrictedUpperShriekIsoOfOpenSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BV2 (Remark 48.17.5), clause (a).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : U ⟶ V` be
morphisms of `AlgebraicGeometry.FTS S` and let `j : U ⟶ X`, `i : V ⟶ Y` be morphisms of
`FTS S` whose underlying morphisms of schemes are open immersions, with `j ≫ f = g ≫ i`. Then
restricting an exceptional inverse image to `U` computes the exceptional inverse image of the
restriction to `V`:

  `f^! ⋙ Lj^* ≅ Li^* ⋙ g^!`,

that is `(f^!E)|_U ≅ g^!(E|_V)` naturally in `E ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`.

The source's proof is reproduced. The two hypotheses `h0ATXf` and `h0ATXi` are the two instances
of [Stacks, Tag 0ATX] that it cites, for the two factorisations `j ≫ f` and `g ≫ i` of the
diagonal `d : U ⟶ Y` of the square. The passage from `j^!` and `i^!` to the restrictions `Lj^*`
and `Li^*` is [Stacks, Tag 0AU0], which is not assumed here but proved in
`Stacks.Duality.upperShriekIsoDerivedPullbackOfOpenImmersion`; it is the whole of the content
this statement adds to its hypotheses.

Clause (b) of Tag 0BV2, the affine formula `φ^!(K) = RHom(A, K ⊗^L_R P)[n]`, is not claimed: it
needs [Stacks, Tag 0AA1], which this repository does not have.
declarations.comment: clause (a) only, the restriction formula (f^!E)|_U = g^!(E|_V) for an open square; clause (b), the affine formula phi^!(K) = RHom(A, K ⊗^L_R P)[n], is NOT claimed, because Stacks 0AA1 (f^! = Lf^*[1] for A^1_V -> V) is absent from this repository. Carried: h0ATXf and h0ATXi, the two instances of Stacks 0ATX for the two factorisations of the diagonal of the square. Stacks 0AU0 is NOT carried: it is proved by Stacks.Duality.upperShriekIsoDerivedPullbackOfOpenImmersion, and supplying it is the only content this statement adds to its hypotheses. Stated for open immersions rather than affine opens, and on the unbounded D_QCoh rather than D^+_QCoh

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.upperShriekCharts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BV2 (Remark 48.17.5), second assertion.** In Situation 48.16.1 let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of `FTS S`, `j` any compactification computing `f^!`, and
`E ∈ D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`. For affine opens `U = Spec A ⊆ f⁻¹(V)`, `V = Spec R`, every presentation
`A = P/I` with `P = R[x_1, …, x_n]` and every `K ∈ D(R)` with `E|_V ≅ K~`, the restriction
`(f^!E)|_U` is the sheaf associated to `φ^!(K) = RHom_P(A, K ⊗ᴸ_R P)[n]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem upperShriekCharts
    {S : Scheme.{u}} [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian S]
    {X Y : FTS S} (f : X ⟶ Y) (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left))
    (E : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y.left) (hE : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow E.obj) :
    UpperShriekCharts f j E
declarations.comment: part (b): (f^!E)|_U corresponds to phi^!(K) = RHom(A, K (x)^L_R P)[n] for every pair of affine opens U, V with f(U) in V, every presentation A = P/I and every K in D(R) with E|_V = K~, E in D^+_QCoh, every compactification

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.fNewShriekTwistIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BV3.** `f_new^!` does not depend on the choice of the dualizing
complex on the base.

Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes of finite type over the base of [Stacks, Tag 0AU4].
Replacing `ω_S^•` by a second dualizing complex replaces it by `ω_S^• ⊗ ℒ` for an invertible
`ℒ` in `D(𝒪_S)` ([Stacks, Tag 0ATP]), and the complexes normalized relative to it by the twists
`ω_X^• ⊗ Lπ_X^*ℒ` and `ω_Y^• ⊗ Lπ_Y^*ℒ` ([Stacks, Tag 0A9T]). This says that the two resulting
functors `f_new^!` are canonically isomorphic — an isomorphism of functors, not merely a family
of isomorphisms of objects.

The computation is the one sketched in the source. The twist passes through the target variable
of `R𝓗om` by `Stacks.Duality.relativeDualTwistTargetIso`, is carried across `Lf^*` by `tw`, and
cancels against the outer twist by `Stacks.Duality.relativeDualTwistCancelIso`; each of those is
natural in the contravariant variable because it comes from
`Stacks.Duality.parametrizedRightAdjointUniq`. The source's `p^!` does not appear: it is one
route to the middle step and is not needed.
declarations.statement:
def fNewShriekTwistIso (f : X ⟶ Y)
    {ωX ωX' : DerivedCategory X.Modules} {ωY ωY' : DerivedCategory Y.Modules}
    {LX : DerivedCategory X.Modules} (hX : HasInverse LX)
    {LY : DerivedCategory Y.Modules} (hY : HasInverse LY)
    (eX : ωX' ≅ ωX ⊗ LX) (eY : ωY' ≅ ωY ⊗ LY)
    (tw : tensorRight LY ⋙ derivedPullback f ≅ derivedPullback f ⋙ tensorRight LX) :
    fNewShriek f ωX' ωY' ≅ fNewShriek f ωX ωY
declarations.comment:
RESTRICTED: the closed symmetric monoidal structure on the derived categories is
an instance argument; the invertible twist with a chosen two-sided inverse, the identification
of the twisted normalized complexes, and the compatibility of the derived pullback with the
twist are hypotheses

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.fNewShriekIndependenceIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BV3.** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme with a dualizing complex `ω_S^•`
and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes of finite type over `S`. Then the functor

`f_new^! = D_X ∘ Lf^* ∘ D_Y : D^+_Coh(𝒪_Y) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)`

of [Stacks, Tag 0AUE], formed with the dualizing complexes `ω_X^•`, `ω_Y^•` normalized relative to
`ω_S^•`, does not depend on `ω_S^•` up to canonical isomorphism: for a second dualizing complex
`ω_S'^•` on `S`, with `ω_X'^•`, `ω_Y'^•` normalized relative to it, the two functors are
isomorphic. (It takes values in `D^+_Coh(𝒪_X)`, `Stacks.Duality.plusCoh_fNewShriek`.)

The proof: `ω_X'^• ≅ f_new^! ω_Y'^•` (`stdComplexIsoFNewShriek`), and then
`Stacks.Duality.fNewShriekStdIsoOfIso`, which uses that `R𝓗om(ω_Y'^•, ω_Y^•)` is invertible
([Stacks, Tag 0ATP]).
declarations.statement:
def fNewShriekIndependenceIso (hpe : f ≫ q = p)
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj)
    (hωS' : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS'.obj.obj)
    (𝒦X : NormalizedOnOpens (UpperShriek.ofCompactifications c) hp ωS)
    (𝒦Y : NormalizedOnOpens (UpperShriek.ofCompactifications c) hq ωS)
    (𝒦X' : NormalizedOnOpens (UpperShriek.ofCompactifications c) hp ωS')
    (𝒦Y' : NormalizedOnOpens (UpperShriek.ofCompactifications c) hq ωS') :
    (plusCoh Y).ι ⋙ fNewShriekStd f (stdComplex c 𝒦X') (stdComplex c 𝒦Y') ≅
      (plusCoh Y).ι ⋙ fNewShriekStd f (stdComplex c 𝒦X) (stdComplex c 𝒦Y)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_fibreDim_eq_and_neg_le_of_nontrivial_stalk_homology_upperShriek
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BV5 (Lemma 48.21.3).** In Situation 48.16.1 let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
morphism of `FTS S` and let `x ∈ X` with image `y ∈ Y`. Then

  `H^i(f^!𝒪_Y)_x ≠ 0  ⟹  -dim_x(X_y) ≤ i`,

for every compactification `j` defining `f^!`. The local dimension `dim_x(X_y)` of the fibre
(`topologicalKrullDimAt` of the scheme-theoretic fibre at `x`) is a natural number `d`, since the
fibre is of finite type over the residue field of `y`, and the conclusion is `-d ≤ i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fibreDim_eq_and_neg_le_of_nontrivial_stalk_homology_upperShriek
    (x : X.left) (i : ℤ)
    (hi : Nontrivial (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.left.Modules i).obj
      (((upperShriek f j).obj
        (derivedStructureSheaf Y.left)).obj)).presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, topologicalKrullDimAt (f.left.fiber (f.left x)) (f.left.asFiber x) =
      (d : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ -(d : ℤ) ≤ i
declarations.comment: f^! is Stacks.Duality.upperShriek of any compactification j; O_Y is DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf; H^i(-)_x ≠ 0 is Nontrivial on the stalk at x of the i-th cohomology sheaf; dim_x(X_y) is topologicalKrullDimAt of the scheme-theoretic fibre at x, shown to be a natural number d, and the conclusion is -d ≤ i

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.fibreDim_bounds_of_nontrivial_stalk_homology_upperShriek_of_flat_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BV6 (Lemma 48.21.4), the first assertion.** In Situation 48.16.1 let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a flat morphism of `FTS S` and let `x ∈ X` with image `y ∈ Y`. Then

  `H^i(f^!𝒪_Y)_x ≠ 0  ⟹  -dim_x(X_y) ≤ i ≤ 0`,

for every compactification `j` defining `f^!`, the local dimension `dim_x(X_y)` being named by
`hd`. On a chart of `Stacks.Duality.upperShriekStructureSheafCharts` this is the ring-level
[Stacks, Tag 0E9Q].
declarations.statement:
theorem fibreDim_bounds_of_nontrivial_stalk_homology_upperShriek_of_flat_unconditional
    [Flat f.left] (x : X.left) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : topologicalKrullDimAt (f.left.fiber (f.left x)) (f.left.asFiber x) =
      (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (i : ℤ)
    (hi : Nontrivial (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.left.Modules i).obj
      (((upperShriek f j).obj
        (derivedStructureSheaf Y.left)).obj)).presheaf.stalk x)) :
    -(d : ℤ) ≤ i ∧ i ≤ 0
declarations.comment: first assertion: the bounds -dim_x(X_y) <= i <= 0 on nonzero stalks

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.hasTorAmplitude_derivedScalarRestriction_upperShriek
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BV6 (Lemma 48.21.4), the second assertion.** In Situation 48.16.1 let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a flat morphism of `FTS S` all of whose fibres have dimension at most `d`. Then
`f^!𝒪_Y` has Tor amplitude in `[-d, 0]` as an object of `D(X, f^{-1}𝒪_Y)`, for every
compactification `j` defining `f^!`.

By [Stacks, Tag 09U9] this is a statement about the derived stalks read over the local rings of
`Y`; on a chart of `Stacks.Duality.upperShriekStructureSheafCharts` it is the Tor amplitude clause
of the ring-level [Stacks, Tag 0E9Q].
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_derivedScalarRestriction_upperShriek [Flat f.left] (d : ℕ)
    (hd : ∀ y : Y.left, topologicalKrullDim (f.left.fiber y) ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude
      (RingedSpace.inverseImage Y.left.toRingedSpace f.left.base)
      ((Scheme.Hom.derivedScalarRestriction f.left).obj (relativeDualizingComplexObj f j))
      (-(d : ℤ)) 0
declarations.comment: second assertion: Tor amplitude in [-d, 0] over f^{-1}O_Y when all fibres have dimension at most d

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_isCoherent_isFlatOver_iso_single
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BV7 (Lemma 48.21.6).** In Situation 48.16.1 let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
morphism of `FTS S`. If `f` is flat and quasi-finite, then `f^!𝒪_Y = ω_{X/Y}[0]` for some
coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ω_{X/Y}` flat over `Y`, for every compactification `j` defining `f^!`.

The fibres are discrete, so by [Stacks, Tag 0BV6] `f^!𝒪_Y` is concentrated in degree `0` and
has Tor amplitude `[0, 0]` over `Y`; its cohomology sheaves are coherent by the chart models.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isCoherent_isFlatOver_iso_single [Flat f.left] [LocallyQuasiFinite f.left] :
    ∃ ω : X.left.Modules, _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent ω ∧
      IsFlatOver f.left.toLRSHom.toShHom ω ∧
      Nonempty (relativeDualizingComplexObj f j ≅
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.left.Modules 0).obj ω)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_isCoherent_isFlatOver_iso_shift_upperShriek
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be Noetherian and `f : X ⟶ Y` a Cohen–Macaulay morphism of `FTS S`. Then
`f^!𝒪_Y = ω_{X/Y}[d]` for a coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ω_{X/Y}` flat over `Y`, where `d` is the
locally constant relative dimension of `X` over `Y`: on the open where the relative dimension is
`d`, `f^!𝒪_Y` is `ω_{X/Y}` placed in degree `-d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isCoherent_isFlatOver_iso_shift_upperShriek
    (hCM : f.left.IsCohenMacaulay (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_left f)) :
    letI h := (isCohenMacaulay_iff_flat_and_fibers f.left (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_left f)).mp hCM
    letI : Flat f.left := h.1
    letI := locallyOfFinitePresentation_left f
    ∃ ω : X.left.Modules, ω.IsCoherent ∧ IsFlatOver f.left.toLRSHom.toShHom ω ∧
      ∀ d : ℕ, Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (relativeDimensionOpen f.left h.2 d).ι
          ).mapDerivedCategory.obj (relativeDualizingComplexObj f j) ≅
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (relativeDimensionOpen f.left h.2 d).ι).obj ω))⟦
            (d : ℤ)⟧)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.newShriekStructureSheaf_spec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BV9 (Remark 48.21.7).** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme endowed with a
dualizing complex `ω_S^•`, and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes of finite type over `S`,
not necessarily separated. With `ω_X^•`, `ω_Y^•` normalized relative to `ω_S^•` and
`f_new^! 𝒪_Y = D_X(Lf^* D_Y(𝒪_Y))`, Lemmas 0BV5, 0BV6, 0BV7 and 0BV8 hold with `f^!` replaced
by `f_new^!`:

1. (0BV5) for `x ∈ X` with image `y`, `H^i(f_new^! 𝒪_Y)_x ≠ 0 ⟹ -dim_x(X_y) ≤ i`;
2. (0BV6) if `f` is flat, then `H^i(f_new^! 𝒪_Y)_x ≠ 0 ⟹ -dim_x(X_y) ≤ i ≤ 0`, and if all
   fibres of `f` have dimension `≤ d`, then `f_new^! 𝒪_Y` has Tor amplitude in `[-d, 0]` as an
   object of `D(X, f^{-1}𝒪_Y)`;
3. (0BV7) if `f` is flat and quasi-finite, then `f_new^! 𝒪_Y = ω_{X/Y}[0]` for some coherent
   `𝒪_X`-module `ω_{X/Y}` flat over `Y`;
4. (0BV8) if `f` is Cohen–Macaulay, then `f_new^! 𝒪_Y = ω_{X/Y}[d]` for some coherent
   `𝒪_X`-module `ω_{X/Y}` flat over `Y`, where `d` is the locally constant relative dimension of
   `X` over `Y`: on the open and closed locus where the relative dimension is `d`, `f_new^! 𝒪_Y`
   is `ω_{X/Y}` placed in degree `-d`.

The local dimension `dim_x(X_y)` is named by a natural number `d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem newShriekStructureSheaf_spec :
    -- Lemma 0BV5
    (∀ (x : X) (d : ℕ), topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞) →
      ∀ i : ℤ, Nontrivial (((@DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules _ _
        (PerfectApproximation.standardModel X) i).obj
          (newShriekStructureSheaf c f 𝒦X 𝒦Y)).presheaf.stalk x) → -(d : ℤ) ≤ i) ∧
    -- Lemma 0BV6
    (Flat f →
      (∀ (x : X) (d : ℕ),
        topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞) →
        ∀ i : ℤ, Nontrivial (((@DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules _ _
          (PerfectApproximation.standardModel X) i).obj
            (newShriekStructureSheaf c f 𝒦X 𝒦Y)).presheaf.stalk x) → -(d : ℤ) ≤ i ∧ i ≤ 0) ∧
      ∀ d : ℕ, (∀ y : Y, topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber y) ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) →
        letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)
        letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard
          (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} (RingedSpace.inverseImage Y.toRingedSpace f.base))
        Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude
          (RingedSpace.inverseImage Y.toRingedSpace f.base)
          ((Scheme.Hom.derivedScalarRestriction f).obj (newShriekStructureSheaf c f 𝒦X 𝒦Y))
          (-(d : ℤ)) 0) ∧
    -- Lemma 0BV7
    (Flat f → LocallyQuasiFinite f →
      letI := PerfectApproximation.standardModel X
      ∃ ω : X.Modules, ω.IsCoherent ∧ IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom ω ∧
        Nonempty ((newShriekStructureSheaf c f 𝒦X 𝒦Y : DerivedCategory X.Modules) ≅
          (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj ω)) ∧
    -- Lemma 0BV8
    (∀ hCM : f.IsCohenMacaulay
        (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_of_isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian (hp := hp) hpe),
      letI h := (isCohenMacaulay_iff_flat_and_fibers f
        (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_of_isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian (hp := hp) hpe)).mp hCM
      letI : Flat f := h.1
      letI := locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian (hp := hp) (hq := hq) hpe
      letI := PerfectApproximation.standardModel X
      ∃ ω : X.Modules, ω.IsCoherent ∧ IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom ω ∧
        ∀ d : ℕ,
          letI := PerfectApproximation.standardModel (relativeDimensionOpen f h.2 d).toScheme
          Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (relativeDimensionOpen f h.2 d).ι
              ).mapDerivedCategory.obj
                (newShriekStructureSheaf c f 𝒦X 𝒦Y : DerivedCategory X.Modules) ≅
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
              ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (relativeDimensionOpen f h.2 d).ι).obj ω))⟦
                (d : ℤ)⟧))
declarations.comment: Lemmas 0BV5, 0BV6 (both assertions), 0BV7 and 0BV8 with f^! replaced by f_new^! = D_X o Lf^* o D_Y, for every morphism of schemes of finite type over a Noetherian base with a dualizing complex, separated or not

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGorenstein_of_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism
declarations.doc:
A local complete intersection morphism whose target is a Gorenstein scheme has Gorenstein
source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorenstein_of_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) (hX : IsGorenstein X) : IsGorenstein Y

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModule.baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVB.** The canonical base change map on relative dualizing
modules, computed using a chosen finite-open factorization.  On the dual factor it extends
`φ : B' →ₗ[A] A` to the `A₁`-linear map sending `a₁ ⊗ b'` to
`a₁ * algebraMap A A₁ (φ b')`; tensoring this map with `B → A₁ ⊗[A] B` gives the displayed
map.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def baseChange (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B)
    (A₁ : Type x) [CommRing A₁] [Algebra A A₁] :
    letI : Algebra B (A₁ ⊗[A] B) := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    letI : Module B
        (dualizingModule (FiniteOpenFactorization.baseChange F A₁)) :=
      Module.compHom _ (algebraMap B (A₁ ⊗[A] B))
    dualizingModule F →ₗ[B]
      dualizingModule (FiniteOpenFactorization.baseChange F A₁)
declarations.comment: the base change map

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModule.baseChange_tmul
declarations.doc:
On a pure tensor, the relative-dualizing base change map extends the dual functional
and sends the coefficient to its scalar extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChange_tmul (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B)
    (A₁ : Type x) [CommRing A₁] [Algebra A A₁]
    (f : Module.Dual A F.middle) (b : B) :
    letI : Algebra B (A₁ ⊗[A] B) := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    letI : Module B
        (dualizingModule (FiniteOpenFactorization.baseChange F A₁)) :=
      Module.compHom _ (algebraMap B (A₁ ⊗[A] B))
    baseChange F A₁ (dualizingModule.tmul F f b) =
      dualizingModule.tmul (FiniteOpenFactorization.baseChange F A₁)
        (f.baseChange A₁) (1 ⊗ₜ[A] b)
declarations.comment: pure tensor formula

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModule.baseChange_congr
declarations.doc:
The base change map respects the canonical identification between dualizing
modules computed using two finite-open factorizations.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChange_congr
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, x} A B)
    (A₁ : Type y) [CommRing A₁] [Algebra A A₁] [IsNoetherianRing A₁]
    (ω : dualizingModule F) :
    dualizingModuleEquiv
        (FiniteOpenFactorization.baseChange F A₁)
        (FiniteOpenFactorization.baseChange G A₁)
        (dualizingModule.baseChange F A₁ ω) =
      dualizingModule.baseChange G A₁
        (dualizingModuleEquiv F G ω)
declarations.comment: independence of factorization

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModule.baseChange_comp
declarations.doc:
Successive base change maps agree with direct base change after the
canonical identification of the iterated tensor product with the direct one.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChange_comp
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B)
    (A₁ : Type x) [CommRing A₁] [Algebra A A₁]
    (A₂ : Type y) [CommRing A₂] [Algebra A A₂] [Algebra A₁ A₂]
    [IsScalarTower A A₁ A₂]
    (ω : dualizingModule F) :
    (baseChangeTowerEquiv F A₁ A₂).1
        (dualizingModule.baseChange
          (FiniteOpenFactorization.baseChange F A₁) A₂
          (dualizingModule.baseChange F A₁ ω)) =
      dualizingModule.baseChange F A₂ ω
declarations.comment: composition of base changes

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.mem_associatedPrimes_dualizingModule_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVD.** A prime of an algebra with a finite-open factorization
is associated to its relative dualizing module if and only if it lies over an associated
prime of the base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mem_associatedPrimes_dualizingModule_iff
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B) (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    q.asIdeal ∈ associatedPrimes B (dualizingModule F) ↔
      q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap A B) ∈ associatedPrimes A A

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModule_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVE.** The relative dualizing module of a flat quasi-finite
homomorphism of Noetherian rings is flat over the base ring.
declarations.statement:
public lemma dualizingModule_flat
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
    [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B] [Module.Flat A B]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B) :
    letI : Module A (dualizingModule F) :=
      Module.compHom (dualizingModule F) (algebraMap A B)
    Module.Flat A (dualizingModule F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModule.baseChangeLinearMap_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVF.** For a flat quasi-finite algebra over a Noetherian
base, arbitrary base change induces an isomorphism of relative dualizing modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChangeLinearMap_bijective
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B)
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [Module.Flat A B]
    (A₁ : Type x) [CommRing A₁] [Algebra A A₁] :
    Function.Bijective (baseChangeLinearMap F A₁)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.exists_relativeDualizingModule
declarations.doc:
**The relative dualizing module of a locally quasi-finite morphism of locally Noetherian
schemes exists.** There is a coherent quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-module whose sections over every
affine chart of `f` are the algebraic relative dualizing module of that chart, compatibly with
restriction inside a chart and with the chart comparison over the adapted opens.

This is `exists_relativeDualizingModule_of_hubRestrict` with its hypothesis discharged by
`hubRestrict`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_relativeDualizingModule :
    ∃ (M : Y.Modules)
      (c : ∀ (i : AdaptedOpen f) (W : Y.Opens), W ≤ i.source.1 →
        Γ(M, W) ≃ₗ[Γ(Y, W)] Γ(adaptedChartSheaf f i, W)),
      M.IsQuasicoherent ∧ _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent M ∧
