        (∀ (i : AdaptedOpen f) (W W' : Y.Opens) (hW : W ≤ i.source.1) (h : W' ≤ W)
          (s : Γ(M, W)),
          c i W' (h.trans hW) (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op s) =
            (adaptedChartSheaf f i).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op (c i W hW s)) ∧
        (∀ (k i j : AdaptedOpen f) (hki : k.Good i.source i.base)
          (hkj : k.Good j.source j.base) (s : Γ(M, k.source.1)),
          c j k.source.1 hkj.le s =
            adaptedSheafComparison f k i j hki hkj (c i k.source.1 hki.le s))
declarations.comment: existence

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.nonempty_relativeDualizingModuleData
declarations.doc:
**The relative dualizing module of Tag 0BVG, as chart data.** For a morphism locally of
finite type and locally quasi-finite between locally Noetherian schemes, the module of
`Stacks.Discriminant.exists_relativeDualizingModule` carries the data of a
`Stacks.Discriminant.RelativeDualizingModuleData`: identifications of its sections over every
affine chart with the algebraic relative dualizing module of that chart, independent of the
finite-open factorization and compatible with shrinking the base chart or the source chart to a
principal open.

The identification over a chart `(U, V)` is the gluing comparison at the adapted open `(V, U)`
followed by the hub of that adapted open at itself.  The hubs of one adapted open at two charts
good for it agree on glued sections, so the two compatibilities are the explicit forms
`hubRestrict_of_source_eq_of_basicOpen` and `hubRestrict_of_base_eq_of_basicOpen` of the
restriction compatibility of the hubs.
declarations.statement: public theorem nonempty_relativeDualizingModuleData : Nonempty (RelativeDualizingModuleData f)
declarations.comment: existence, with the chart identifications

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.existsUnique_relativeDualizingComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVG, uniqueness.** The relative dualizing module of a locally
quasi-finite morphism of locally Noetherian schemes is unique: any two coherent `𝒪_Y`-modules
carrying the chart data of Tag 0BVG are related by one and only one isomorphism of their sections
over every open of the source which is compatible with the restriction maps and which carries the
identification of the sections over every affine chart `Spec(B) = V ⊆ Y`, `Spec(A) = U ⊆ X` with
`f(V) ⊆ U` with `ω_{B/A}` to the other.

As in the source, uniqueness is uniqueness up to the canonical isomorphism: the two modules are
two sheaves and cannot be literally equal, and what is asserted is that the identifications
`H⁰(V, ω_{Y/X}) = ω_{B/A}` determine the comparison between them completely.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_relativeDualizingComparison
    (D D' : RelativeDualizingModuleData f) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    ∃! E : ∀ W : Y.Opens, Γ(D.sheaf, W) ≃ₗ[Γ(Y, W)] Γ(D'.sheaf, W),
      (∀ (W W' : Y.Opens) (h : W' ≤ W) (s : Γ(D.sheaf, W)),
          E W' (restrictₗ D.sheaf h s) = restrictₗ D'.sheaf h (E W s)) ∧
        ∀ (U : X.affineOpens) (V : Y.affineOpens) (hVU : V.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1),
          letI : Algebra Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1) := (f.appLE U V hVU).hom.toAlgebra
          ∀ (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, u, u} Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1))
            (s : Γ(D.sheaf, V.1)),
            D'.localEquiv U V hVU F (E V.1 s) = D.localEquiv U V hVU F s
declarations.comment: uniqueness

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.upperShriekDualSection_pushforwardTrace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVI.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite flat morphism of schemes separated
and of finite type over a Noetherian scheme `S`, and `f^!` the upper shriek of Tag 0A9Y at any
compactification `j`. The trace `Trace_f : f_*𝒪_X ⟶ 𝒪_Y` of Section 0BVH corresponds under
duality to a global section of `H⁰(f^!𝒪_Y)`; via the identification `H⁰(f^!𝒪_Y) = ω_{X/Y}` of
Tag 0BUL (`upperShriekRelativeDualizingModuleData`), this section is the trace element
`τ_{X/Y}` of Tag 0BVJ.
declarations.statement:
theorem upperShriekDualSection_pushforwardTrace (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left)) :
    upperShriekDualSection f (pushforwardTrace f.left) j =
      relativeTraceSection (upperShriekRelativeDualizingModuleData f j)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.relativeTraceSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVJ.** The relative trace section `τ_{Y/X}` of a flat locally
quasi-finite morphism of locally Noetherian schemes: the global section of the relative
dualizing module obtained by gluing the trace elements of the affine charts along the cover of
the source by the source charts of the chart pairs.
declarations.statement: def relativeTraceSection (D : RelativeDualizingModuleData f) : Γ(D.sheaf, ⊤)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.localEquiv_relativeTraceSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVJ.** On every pair of affine opens `Spec B = V ⊆ Y`,
`Spec A = U ⊆ X` with `f(V) ⊆ U`, the relative trace section restricts to the trace element
`τ_{B/A}` of the relative dualizing module `ω_{B/A}`, under the canonical identification of
the sections over `V` with `ω_{B/A}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localEquiv_relativeTraceSection (D : RelativeDualizingModuleData f)
    (U : X.affineOpens) (V : Y.affineOpens) (hVU : V.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) :
    letI : Algebra Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1) := (f.appLE U V hVU).hom.toAlgebra
    letI : IsNoetherianRing Γ(X, U.1) := IsLocallyNoetherian.component_noetherian U
    letI : IsNoetherianRing Γ(Y, V.1) := IsLocallyNoetherian.component_noetherian V
    letI : Module.Flat Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1) :=
      RingHom.flat_algebraMap_iff.mp (f.flat_appLE U.2 V.2 hVU)
    letI : Algebra.QuasiFinite Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1) :=
      RingHom.quasiFinite_algebraMap.mp (LocallyQuasiFinite.quasiFinite_appLE U.2 V.2 hVU)
    ∀ F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, u, u} Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1),
      D.localEquiv U V hVU F
          (restrictₗ D.sheaf (le_top : V.1 ≤ ⊤) (relativeTraceSection D)) =
        dualizingModule.traceCandidate F

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.bijOn_diagonalAnnihilator_prod
declarations.doc:
The canonical pair of tensor-square projections identifies the annihilator of the
kernel of multiplication for a product algebra with the product of the corresponding
annihilators.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijOn_diagonalAnnihilator_prod
    (A : Type u) (B₁ : Type v) (B₂ : Type w)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B₁] [CommRing B₂] [Algebra A B₁] [Algebra A B₂] :
    Set.BijOn
      (fun x : (B₁ × B₂) ⊗[A] (B₁ × B₂) ↦
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.fst A B₁ B₂) (AlgHom.fst A B₁ B₂) x,
          Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.snd A B₁ B₂) (AlgHom.snd A B₁ B₂) x))
      (diagonalAnnihilator A (B₁ × B₂) :
        Set ((B₁ × B₂) ⊗[A] (B₁ × B₂)))
      ((diagonalAnnihilator A B₁ : Set (B₁ ⊗[A] B₁)) ×ˢ
        (diagonalAnnihilator A B₂ : Set (B₂ ⊗[A] B₂)))
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.noetherDifferent_prod
declarations.doc:
The Noether different of a product algebra is the product of the Noether differents
of its factors.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherDifferent_prod
    (A : Type u) (B₁ : Type v) (B₂ : Type w)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B₁] [CommRing B₂] [Algebra A B₁] [Algebra A B₂] :
    noetherDifferent A (B₁ × B₂) =
      Ideal.prod (noetherDifferent A B₁)
        (noetherDifferent A B₂)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.map_diagonalAnnihilator_eq
declarations.doc: The annihilator of the diagonal ideal commutes with flat base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_diagonalAnnihilator_eq (A : Type u) (B : Type v) (A' : Type w)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing A'] [Algebra A B] [Algebra A A']
    [Algebra.FiniteType A B] [Module.Flat A A'] :
    (diagonalAnnihilator A B).map (envelopingBaseChange A B A') =
      diagonalAnnihilator A' (A' ⊗[A] B)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.map_noetherDifferent_eq
declarations.doc: The Noether different commutes with flat base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_noetherDifferent_eq (A : Type u) (B : Type v) (A' : Type w)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing A'] [Algebra A B] [Algebra A A']
    [Algebra.FiniteType A B] [Module.Flat A A'] :
    (noetherDifferent A B).map
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : B →ₐ[A] A' ⊗[A] B) =
      noetherDifferent A' (A' ⊗[A] B)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.diagonalAnnihilatorBaseChange_injective
declarations.doc:
The canonical base-change map on diagonal annihilators is injective under the open
localization hypotheses. This is the injectivity implicit in the identification in part (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem diagonalAnnihilatorBaseChange_injective
    [Algebra.FiniteType A B']
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map
        (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B' B).ulift.{max v w, max v w}))) :
    Function.Injective (diagonalAnnihilatorBaseChange A B' B)
declarations.comment: part (1), injectivity

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.range_diagonalAnnihilatorBaseChange
declarations.doc:
Under the open localization hypotheses, the image of `B ⊗[B'] J'` under the canonical
map is exactly the diagonal annihilator `J` for `B/A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_diagonalAnnihilatorBaseChange
    [Algebra.FiniteType A B']
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map
        (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B' B).ulift.{max v w, max v w}))) :
    LinearMap.range (diagonalAnnihilatorBaseChange A B' B) =
      (diagonalAnnihilator A B).restrictScalars B
declarations.comment: part (1), image

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.noetherDifferent_eq_map
declarations.doc:
Under the open localization hypotheses, the Noether different of `B/A` is the extension
to `B` of the Noether different of `B'/A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherDifferent_eq_map
    [Algebra.FiniteType A B']
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map
        (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B' B).ulift.{max v w, max v w}))) :
    noetherDifferent A B =
      Ideal.map (algebraMap B' B)
        (noetherDifferent A B')
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.noetherPairingWithFormula
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVP.** The canonical `B`-bilinear pairing between the relative
dualizing module and the annihilator of the kernel of multiplication, together with its defining
contraction formula on a finite-open model.

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.noetherPairing_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVP (independence of factorization).** The canonical pairing between
the relative dualizing module and the diagonal annihilator does not depend on the finite-open
factorization: the comparison of dualizing modules of Tag 0BT1 carries one pairing to the
other.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherPairing_naturality
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B)
    (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, x} A B)
    (ω : dualizingModule F) (j : ↑(diagonalAnnihilator A B)) :
    noetherPairing G (dualizingModuleEquiv F G ω) j = noetherPairing F ω j
declarations.comment: independence of factorization

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.noetherPairing_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVR (flat base change).** The canonical pairing
between the relative dualizing module and the diagonal annihilator commutes
with flat base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherPairing_baseChange
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} (A₁ : Type x)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing A₁]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A A₁]
    [Algebra.FiniteType A B] [Module.Flat A A₁]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B)
    (ω : dualizingModule F)
    (j : diagonalAnnihilator A B) :
    letI : Algebra B (A₁ ⊗[A] B) := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    noetherPairing (FiniteOpenFactorization.baseChange F A₁)
        (dualizingModule.baseChange F A₁ ω)
        (diagonalAnnihilatorFlatBaseChange A B A₁ j) =
      algebraMap B (A₁ ⊗[A] B) (noetherPairing F ω j)
declarations.comment: flat_base_change

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.noetherPairing_prod_fst
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVR (product projection).** The canonical pairing between the relative
dualizing module and the diagonal annihilator commutes with the projection to the first factor of
a product.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherPairing_prod_fst
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {C : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A C]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsNoetherianRing C]
    [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A C]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, max v w, x} A (B × C))
    (FB : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, y} A B)
    (FC : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, z} A C)
    (ω : dualizingModule F) (j : ↑(diagonalAnnihilator A (B × C))) :
    noetherPairing FB ((dualizingModuleProdEquiv F FB FC ω).1)
        (diagonalAnnihilatorProdFst A B C j) =
      (noetherPairing F ω j).1
declarations.comment: product_projection

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.noetherPairing_prod_snd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVR (product projection).** The canonical pairing between the relative
dualizing module and the diagonal annihilator commutes with the projection to the second factor
of a product.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherPairing_prod_snd
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {C : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A C]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsNoetherianRing C]
    [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A C]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, max v w, x} A (B × C))
    (FB : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, y} A B)
    (FC : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, w, z} A C)
    (ω : dualizingModule F) (j : ↑(diagonalAnnihilator A (B × C))) :
    noetherPairing FC ((dualizingModuleProdEquiv F FB FC ω).2)
        (diagonalAnnihilatorProdSnd A B C j) =
      (noetherPairing F ω j).2
declarations.comment: product_projection

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.noetherPairing_flip_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVS.** For a flat quasi-finite homomorphism of Noetherian rings the
canonical pairing induces a bijection from the annihilator of the diagonal ideal to the dual of
the relative dualizing module.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherPairing_flip_bijective
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [Module.Flat A B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B) :
    Function.Bijective (noetherPairing F).flip

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.noetherPairingEquiv_apply_traceElement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVT.** Under the isomorphism induced by the canonical pairing,
multiplication of an element of the diagonal annihilator is evaluation at the trace
element.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherPairingEquiv_apply_traceElement
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Module.Flat A B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B) (j : ↑(diagonalAnnihilator A B)) :
    noetherPairingEquiv F j (dualizingModule.traceElement F) =
      Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A j.1
declarations.comment: commutative diagram

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.noetherDifferent_eq_range_traceElement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVT.** The Noether different is the image of evaluation at the trace
element.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherDifferent_eq_range_traceElement
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Module.Flat A B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B) :
    (noetherDifferent A B : Set B) =
      Set.range fun φ : dualizingModule F →ₗ[B] B ↦
        φ (dualizingModule.traceElement F)
declarations.comment: image of evaluation

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.zeroLocus_noetherDifferent
declarations.doc:
The primes containing the Noether different are exactly the primes at
which a finite type algebra is not unramified.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroLocus_noetherDifferent
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B] :
    PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (noetherDifferent A B : Set B) =
      (Algebra.unramifiedLocus A B)ᶜ

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.kaehlerDifferent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVW.** The Kähler different of a morphism of schemes which is
locally of finite type: the zeroth Fitting ideal sheaf of its sheaf of relative
differentials.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev kaehlerDifferent {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] : Y.IdealSheafData

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.kaehlerDifferent_comap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVX.** For a cartesian square of schemes with right edge `f : Y ⟶ X`
locally of finite type, left edge `f' : Y' ⟶ X'` and top edge `g' : Y' ⟶ Y`, the Kähler
different of `f'` is the inverse image along `g'` of the Kähler different of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem kaehlerDifferent_comap {Y' Y X' X : Scheme.{u}} (g' : Y' ⟶ Y) (f' : Y' ⟶ X')
    (f : Y ⟶ X) (g : X' ⟶ X) (h : IsPullback g' f' f g) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    @kaehlerDifferent Y' X' f'
        (locallyOfFiniteType_isStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback h inferInstance) =
      (kaehlerDifferent f).comap g'
declarations.comment: equality of the ideal sheaves cutting out R' and the inverse image of R

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.kaehlerDifferentSubschemeIsoPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVX.** The isomorphism from the closed subscheme `R'` of `Y'` cut out
by the Kähler different of the base change `f'` to the fibre product `Y' ×_Y R`, where `R ⊆ Y` is
cut out by the Kähler different of `f`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def kaehlerDifferentSubschemeIsoPullback {Y' Y X' X : Scheme.{u}} (g' : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (f' : Y' ⟶ X') (f : Y ⟶ X) (g : X' ⟶ X) (h : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    (@kaehlerDifferent Y' X' f'
        (locallyOfFiniteType_isStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback h inferInstance)).subscheme ≅
      pullback g' (kaehlerDifferent f).subschemeι
declarations.comment: the induced isomorphism of closed subschemes

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.kaehlerDifferentSubschemeIsoPullback_hom_fst
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVX.** The isomorphism `R' ≅ Y' ×_Y R` of Tag 0BVX is an isomorphism
of schemes over `Y'`: composing it with the first projection is the closed immersion of `R'` into
`Y'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem kaehlerDifferentSubschemeIsoPullback_hom_fst {Y' Y X' X : Scheme.{u}} (g' : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (f' : Y' ⟶ X') (f : Y ⟶ X) (g : X' ⟶ X) (h : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    (kaehlerDifferentSubschemeIsoPullback g' f' f g h).hom ≫ pullback.fst _ _ =
      Scheme.IdealSheafData.subschemeι (@kaehlerDifferent Y' X' f'
        (locallyOfFiniteType_isStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback h inferInstance))
declarations.comment: the induced isomorphism of closed subschemes is over Y'

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.range_kaehlerDifferent_subschemeι
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVY** and **Stacks Project, Tag 0C3J.** For a morphism of schemes
`f : Y ⟶ X` locally of finite type, the closed subscheme `R ⊆ Y` cut out by the Kähler different
of `f` — equivalently, by the zeroth Fitting ideal of `Ω_{Y/X}`, which is what the Kähler
different is — has as its underlying subset of `Y` exactly the set of points at which `f` is not
unramified.

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.fittingIdeal_kaehlerDifferential_quotient_mvPolynomial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BVZ.** The Kähler different of an algebra presented by `n` equations
in `n` variables is generated by the determinant of its Jacobian matrix.
declarations.statement:
theorem fittingIdeal_kaehlerDifferential_quotient_mvPolynomial
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (n : ℕ)
    (f : Fin n → MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) :
    let I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) := Ideal.span (Set.range f)
    let B := MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ I
    fittingIdeal (M := Ω[B⁄A]) 0 =
      Ideal.span {Ideal.Quotient.mk I
                    (Matrix.of (fun i j : Fin n => MvPolynomial.pderiv j (f i))).det}

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.one_mem_complementaryModule_iff
declarations.doc:
One lies in the Dedekind complementary module exactly when the generic-fibre trace of every
element of `B` belongs to the canonical image of `A` in its total quotient ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem one_mem_complementaryModule_iff (setup : DedekindDifferentSetup A B) :
    letI : Algebra (FractionRing A) (B ⊗[A] FractionRing A) :=
      Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    (1 : B ⊗[A] FractionRing A) ∈ setup.complementaryModule ↔
      ∀ b : B, setup.trace (algebraMap B (B ⊗[A] FractionRing A) b) ∈
        Set.range (algebraMap A (FractionRing A))
declarations.comment: trace_iff_one_mem

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dedekindDifferent_eq_map_ideal
declarations.doc:
If one lies in the complementary module, the Dedekind different is the
image of an ideal of `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dedekindDifferent_eq_map_ideal
    (setup : DedekindDifferentSetup A B)
    (h_one : (1 : B ⊗[A] FractionRing A) ∈ setup.complementaryModule) :
    setup.dedekindDifferent =
      Submodule.map (Algebra.linearMap B (B ⊗[A] FractionRing A))
        (dedekindDifferentIdeal setup : Submodule B B)
declarations.comment: one_mem_different_ideal

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.trace_algebraMap_mem_range_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BW1 (flat trace).** In the setup for the Dedekind
different, if `B` is flat over `A`, then the generic-fibre trace of every
element of `B` belongs to the canonical image of `A` in its total quotient
ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem trace_algebraMap_mem_range_of_flat
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (setup : DedekindDifferentSetup A B) [Module.Flat A B]
    (b : B) :
    letI : Algebra (FractionRing A) (B ⊗[A] FractionRing A) :=
      Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    setup.trace (algebraMap B (B ⊗[A] FractionRing A) b) ∈
      Set.range (algebraMap A (FractionRing A))
declarations.comment: flat_trace

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.trace_algebraMap_mem_range_of_isNormalRing
declarations.doc:
In the setup for the Dedekind different, if `A` is a normal ring, then the generic-fibre
trace of every element of `B` belongs to the canonical image of `A` in its total quotient
ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem trace_algebraMap_mem_range_of_isNormalRing
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (setup : DedekindDifferentSetup A B) (hA : IsNormalRing A) (b : B) :
    letI : Algebra (FractionRing A) (B ⊗[A] FractionRing A) :=
      Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    setup.trace (algebraMap B (B ⊗[A] FractionRing A) b) ∈
      Set.range (algebraMap A (FractionRing A))
declarations.comment: normal_trace

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.complementaryModuleEquivDualizingModuleWithFormula
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BW2.** The trace pairing canonically identifies the Dedekind
complementary module with the relative dualizing module `Hom_A(B, A)` of a finite map, together
with the formula characterizing it: the image of `x` is the functional `b ↦ Tr(bx)`.
declarations.statement:
def complementaryModuleEquivDualizingModuleWithFormula
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (setup : DedekindDifferentSetup A B) :
    { e : setup.complementaryModule ≃ₗ[B] Module.Dual A B //
      ∀ (x : setup.complementaryModule) (b : B),
        algebraMap A (FractionRing A) (e x b) =
          setup.trace
            (algebraMap B (B ⊗[A] FractionRing A) b *
              (x : B ⊗[A] FractionRing A)) }

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.complementaryModuleEquivDualizingModule_one_eq_traceElement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BW3, part (1).** If the Dedekind different of a flat algebra `A → B`
is defined, the canonical isomorphism `L_{B/A} → ω_{B/A}` (Tag 0BW2, followed by the canonical
identification `Hom_A(B, A) ≅ ω_{B/A}` for a finite-open factorization `F`) sends `1` to the trace
element `τ_{B/A}` of Tag 0BT6.
declarations.statement:
theorem complementaryModuleEquivDualizingModule_one_eq_traceElement :
    letI : IsNoetherianRing A := setup.isNoetherianRing
    letI : Module.Finite A B := setup.finite
    letI : IsNoetherianRing B := IsNoetherianRing.of_finite A B
    ∀ (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B) (τ : dualizingModule F),
      IsTraceElement.{u, v, w, u, max u v, max u v} F τ →
        dualizingModuleEquiv (selfFactorization A B) F
            (selfFactorizationDualEquiv.symm
              (complementaryModuleEquivDualizingModule setup
                ⟨1, one_mem_complementaryModule_of_flat setup⟩)) = τ
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.mem_dedekindDifferentIdeal_iff_smul_mem_span_traceElement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BW3, part (2), membership form.** If the Dedekind different of a flat
algebra `A → B` is defined, an element `b ∈ B` lies in the Dedekind different exactly when
`b ω_{B/A} ⊆ B τ_{B/A}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_dedekindDifferentIdeal_iff_smul_mem_span_traceElement :
    letI : IsNoetherianRing A := setup.isNoetherianRing
    letI : Module.Finite A B := setup.finite
    letI : IsNoetherianRing B := IsNoetherianRing.of_finite A B
    ∀ (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B) (τ : dualizingModule F),
      IsTraceElement.{u, v, w, u, max u v, max u v} F τ → ∀ b : B,
        b ∈ dedekindDifferentIdeal setup ↔
          ∀ x : dualizingModule F, b • x ∈ Submodule.span B {τ}
declarations.comment: part (2), membership form

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dedekindDifferent_eq_image_setOf_smul_mem_span_traceElement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BW3, part (2).** If the Dedekind different of a flat algebra `A → B`
is defined, then `𝔇_{B/A} = {b ∈ B | b ω_{B/A} ⊆ B τ_{B/A}}`, as a subset of the generic fibre
`L = B ⊗_A Q(A)` in which the Dedekind different is defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem dedekindDifferent_eq_image_setOf_smul_mem_span_traceElement :
    letI : IsNoetherianRing A := setup.isNoetherianRing
    letI : Module.Finite A B := setup.finite
    letI : IsNoetherianRing B := IsNoetherianRing.of_finite A B
    ∀ (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B) (τ : dualizingModule F),
      IsTraceElement.{u, v, w, u, max u v, max u v} F τ →
        (setup.dedekindDifferent : Set (B ⊗[A] FractionRing A)) =
          algebraMap B (B ⊗[A] FractionRing A) ''
            {b | ∀ x : dualizingModule F, b • x ∈ Submodule.span B {τ}}
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.different
declarations.doc:
The *different* `𝔇_f ⊆ 𝒪_Y` of a flat locally quasi-finite morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of locally
Noetherian schemes: the annihilator of the cokernel of the map `𝒪_Y → ω_{Y/X}`, `1 ↦ τ_{Y/X}`,
where `ω_{Y/X}` is the relative dualizing module
`Stacks.Discriminant.relativeDualizingModuleData f` and `τ_{Y/X}` is its trace element
`Stacks.Discriminant.relativeTraceSection`.

The hypothesis `LocallyOfFiniteType f` is part of the source's "locally quasi-finite", which
includes being locally of finite type; Mathlib's `LocallyQuasiFinite` does not.  The ideal does
not depend on the relative dualizing module chosen: `Scheme.Hom.different_eq`.
declarations.statement:
def _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.different :
    (SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace)).Submodule
declarations.comment: the different

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isCoherent_different
declarations.doc:
The different `𝔇_f` of a flat locally quasi-finite morphism of locally Noetherian schemes is
a coherent ideal of `𝒪_Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isCoherent_different :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent f.different.toSheafOfModules
declarations.comment: coherence

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.different_obj_affine_eq_dedekindDifferentIdeal
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BW5].** Let `f : Y → X` be a flat quasi-finite morphism of locally
Noetherian schemes and let `V = Spec B ⊆ Y` and `U = Spec A ⊆ X` be affine opens with
`f(V) ⊆ U`.  If the Dedekind different of `A → B` is defined, then the sections of the different
`𝔇_f` over `V` are the Dedekind different ideal `𝔇_{B/A} ⊆ B`.

Both `𝔇_f` and the ideal sheaf associated with `𝔇_{B/A}` are coherent ideal sheaves on the
affine `V`, and a coherent sheaf on an affine scheme is the tilde of its module of sections; so
this equality of ideals of `B` is the assertion that `𝔇_f|_V = (𝔇_{B/A})~`.
declarations.statement:
theorem different_obj_affine_eq_dedekindDifferentIdeal (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f)
    (τ : RelativeTraceSection ω) (U : X.affineOpens) (V : Y.affineOpens)
    (hVU : V.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) :
    letI : Algebra Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1) := (f.appLE U V hVU).hom.toAlgebra
    ∀ setup : DedekindDifferentSetup Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1),
      (show Ideal Γ(Y, V.1) from (different ω τ).toSubmodule.obj (op V.1)) =
        dedekindDifferentIdeal setup

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.different_sections_eq_noetherDifferent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BW6].** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be flat and locally quasi-finite between locally
Noetherian schemes, with relative dualizing module `ω` and trace section `τ`.  On affine opens
`V = Spec B ⊆ Y` and `U = Spec A ⊆ X` with `f(V) ⊆ U`, if the algebraic relative dualizing
module `ω_{B/A}` is an invertible `B`-module, then the ideal of sections of the different over
`V` is the Noether different of `B` over `A`.

The source states this as `𝔇_f|_V = 𝔇~` as coherent ideal sheaves on `V`; the different is a
coherent ideal sheaf, so on the affine `V` it is the tilde of its ideal of sections and the two
readings agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem different_sections_eq_noetherDifferent (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f)
    (τ : RelativeTraceSection ω) (U : X.affineOpens) (V : Y.affineOpens)
    (hVU : V.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) :
    letI : Algebra Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1) := (f.appLE U V hVU).hom.toAlgebra
    letI : IsNoetherianRing Γ(X, U.1) := IsLocallyNoetherian.component_noetherian U
    letI : IsNoetherianRing Γ(Y, V.1) := IsLocallyNoetherian.component_noetherian V
    letI : Module.Flat Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1) :=
      RingHom.flat_algebraMap_iff.mp (f.flat_appLE U.2 V.2 hVU)
    letI : Algebra.QuasiFinite Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1) :=
      RingHom.quasiFinite_algebraMap.mp (LocallyQuasiFinite.quasiFinite_appLE U.2 V.2 hVU)
    ∀ (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, u, u} Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1)),
      Module.Invertible Γ(Y, V.1) (dualizingModule F) →
        (show Ideal Γ(Y, V.1) from (different ω τ).toSubmodule.obj (op V.1)) =
          noetherDifferent Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.exists_bijectiveClosedImmersion_different_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BW7].** Consider a cartesian diagram of locally Noetherian schemes with
`f : Y ⟶ X` flat and locally quasi-finite, let `R ⊆ Y` and `R' ⊆ Y'` be the closed subschemes
cut out by the differents `𝔇_f` and `𝔇_{f'}`. Then `Y' → Y` induces a bijective closed immersion
`R' → R ×_Y Y'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_bijectiveClosedImmersion_different_baseChange
    (hi : i.ker = differentIdealSheaf ω τ) (hi' : i'.ker = differentIdealSheaf ω' τ') :
    ∃ (k : R' ⟶ R) (hk : k ≫ i = i' ≫ pullback.fst f g),
      IsClosedImmersion (pullback.lift k i' hk) ∧
        Function.Bijective (pullback.lift k i' hk).base
declarations.comment: the bijective closed immersion

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isIso_different_baseChange_of_flat
declarations.doc: **[Stacks, Tag 0BW7], flat base change.** If moreover `g` is flat then `R' = R ×_Y Y'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_different_baseChange_of_flat [Flat g]
    (hi : i.ker = differentIdealSheaf ω τ) (hi' : i'.ker = differentIdealSheaf ω' τ')
    (k : R' ⟶ R) (hk : k ≫ i = i' ≫ pullback.fst f g) :
    IsIso (pullback.lift k i' hk)
declarations.comment: equality under flat base change

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isIso_different_baseChange_of_invertible
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BW7], invertible dualizing module.** If moreover `ω_{Y/X}` is invertible
then `R' = R ×_Y Y'`, for an arbitrary `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_different_baseChange_of_invertible
    (hinv : ∀ V : Y.affineOpens, Module.Invertible Γ(Y, V.1) Γ(ω.sheaf, V.1))
    (hi : i.ker = differentIdealSheaf ω τ) (hi' : i'.ker = differentIdealSheaf ω' τ')
    (k : R' ⟶ R) (hk : k ≫ i = i' ≫ pullback.fst f g) :
    IsIso (pullback.lift k i' hk)
declarations.comment: equality for invertible dualizing module

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.finiteLocallyFreeNorm_app_mem_discriminantIdeal
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BW8].** Let `f : Y → X` be a finite flat morphism of locally Noetherian
schemes, with source `Y` and base `X`, and let `𝔇_f ⊆ 𝒪_Y` be the different attached to a
relative dualizing module `ω_{Y/X}` and a trace element `τ_{Y/X}`.  Then the norm
`Norm_f : f_*𝒪_Y → 𝒪_X` carries `f_*𝔇_f` into the ideal sheaf of the discriminant `D_f`: over
every affine open `U` of the base the norm of a section of `𝔇_f` on `f ⁻¹ᵁ U` lies in the
discriminant ideal of `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteLocallyFreeNorm_app_mem_discriminantIdeal (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f)
    (τ : RelativeTraceSection ω) (U : X.affineOpens) (s : Γ(Y, f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1))
    (hs : s ∈ (show Ideal Γ(Y, f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) from
      (different ω τ).toSubmodule.obj (op (f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)))) :
    letI : Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree f :=
      (Stacks.Morphisms.isFiniteLocallyFree_iff_isFinite_flat_of_isLocallyNoetherian f).mpr
        ⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩
    (Stacks.Norm.finiteLocallyFreeNorm f).app U.1 s ∈ (discriminantIdeal f).ideal U

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.finiteProjective_mem_algebraDiscriminantIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BW8, the affine computation.** For a finite projective algebra
`A → B` whose Dedekind different is defined, the norm of an element of the Dedekind different
belongs to the discriminant ideal of `B` over `A`. The norm here is the projective norm
`Algebra.projectiveNorm`, which agrees with `Algebra.norm` when `B` is free over `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteProjective_mem_algebraDiscriminantIdeal
    (setup : DedekindDifferentSetup A B) [Module.Finite A B] [Module.Projective A B]
    {b : B} (hb : b ∈ dedekindDifferentIdeal setup) :
    Algebra.projectiveNorm A b ∈ algebraDiscriminantIdeal A B
declarations.comment: the affine computation

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.range_eq_setOf_not_etaleAt
declarations.doc:
For a flat quasi-finite morphism of locally Noetherian schemes, the closed subscheme
`R ⊆ Y` cut out by the different `𝔇_f` is exactly the set of points at which `f` is not
étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_eq_setOf_not_etaleAt (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f)
    (τ : RelativeTraceSection ω) {R : Scheme.{u}} (i : R ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (hi : i.ker = differentIdealSheaf ω τ) :
    Set.range i.base = {y : Y | ¬ EtaleAt f y}
declarations.comment: the non-étale locus

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.range_eq_setOf_not_unramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
Equivalently, the closed subscheme cut out by the different is exactly the set of points at
which `f` is not unramified.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_eq_setOf_not_unramifiedAt (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f)
    (τ : RelativeTraceSection ω) {R : Scheme.{u}} (i : R ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (hi : i.ker = differentIdealSheaf ω τ) :
    Set.range i.base = {y : Y | ¬ UnramifiedAt f y}
declarations.comment: the non-unramified locus

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_differentIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BWA (3)], effectivity.**  Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a flat quasi-finite morphism of
locally Noetherian schemes with relative dualizing module `ω_{Y/X}` and trace element `τ_{Y/X}`.
If `ω_{Y/X}` is invertible and `f` is étale at the associated points of `Y`, then the closed
subscheme `R ⊆ Y` defined by the different `𝔇_f` is an effective Cartier divisor.

By [Stacks, Tag 0C17 (1)] the different is locally principal, and the local generator is a
nonzerodivisor because it does not vanish at any associated point of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_differentIdealSheaf
    (hét : ∀ y ∈ Stacks.Divisors.schemeAssociatedPoints Y, EtaleAt f y) :
    Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (differentIdealSheaf ω τ)
declarations.comment: part (3), R is an effective Cartier divisor

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.existsUnique_invertibleSheafIso_differentIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BWA (3)], the isomorphism `𝒪_Y(R) = ω_{Y/X}`.**  Under the hypotheses of
[Stacks, Tag 0BWA (3)] there is exactly one isomorphism `𝒪_Y(R) ≅ ω_{Y/X}` carrying the
canonical section `1_R` of `𝒪_Y(R)` to the trace element `τ_{Y/X}`.

The subscheme `R` is the zero scheme of `τ_{Y/X}`, so its effectivity makes `τ_{Y/X}` a regular
section of `ω_{Y/X}` ([Stacks, Tag 02OR]), and [Stacks, Tag 01X0] trivializes `𝒪_Y(Z(τ_{Y/X})))`
along it.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_invertibleSheafIso_differentIdealSheaf
    (hét : ∀ y ∈ Stacks.Divisors.schemeAssociatedPoints Y, EtaleAt f y) :
    ∃! e : Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf' (differentIdealSheaf ω τ) ≅ ω.sheaf,
      Scheme.Modules.Hom.app e.hom ⊤
        ((Stacks.Divisors.canonicalSection' (differentIdealSheaf ω τ)).eval (op ⊤)) = τ.sect
declarations.comment: part (3), O_Y(R) = omega_{Y/X}

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isLocallyPrincipal_different
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BWA (1)].** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a flat locally quasi-finite morphism of
locally Noetherian schemes with relative dualizing module `ω_{Y/X}` and trace element
`τ_{Y/X}`. If `ω_{Y/X}` is an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module, then the closed subscheme `R ⊆ Y`
defined by the different `𝔇_f` is a locally principal closed subscheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyPrincipal_different (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f)
    (τ : RelativeTraceSection ω)
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing
        Y.toRingedSpace).property ω.sheaf] :
    Stacks.Divisors.IsLocallyPrincipal
      (Stacks.Divisors.idealSheafDataOfSubmodule (different ω τ))
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.discriminantIdeal_eq_normIdealSheaf_differentIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BWA (2)].**  Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a finite flat morphism of locally Noetherian
schemes with relative dualizing module `ω_{Y/X}` and trace element `τ_{Y/X}`, and let `R ⊆ Y`
be the closed subscheme cut out by the different `𝔇_f`.  If `ω_{Y/X}` is invertible, then the
norm of `R` is the discriminant `D_f`: as ideal sheaves on `X`, `Norm_f(𝔇_f)` is the
discriminant ideal sheaf.

Every point of `X` has an affine open neighbourhood `U = Spec A` with `f⁻¹U = Spec B` free over
`A` and `ω_{Y/X}` trivial on `f⁻¹U` (Tag 0BUT), so that `Hom_A(B, A)` is free of rank one on some
`λ`; there `R` is cut out by the `b` with `Tr_{B/A} = b λ` and `D_f` by `Norm_{B/A}(b)`, and
both sides are ideal sheaves, so they agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem discriminantIdeal_eq_normIdealSheaf_differentIdealSheaf
    (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f) (τ : RelativeTraceSection ω)
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace).property ω.sheaf] :
    letI : Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree f :=
      (Stacks.Morphisms.isFiniteLocallyFree_iff_isFinite_flat_of_isLocallyNoetherian f).mpr
        ⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩
    discriminantIdeal f = Stacks.Norm.normIdealSheaf f (differentIdealSheaf ω τ)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.exists_linearEquiv_annihilator_ker_lmul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BWC**, the "more precisely" claim. For a flat quotient
`B = P/(f_1, …, f_n)` by a Koszul-regular sequence, if a Koszul-regular sequence `g` generates
the kernel of the multiplication map `P ⊗_A B → B` and `f_i ⊗ 1 = ∑_j g_{ij} g_j`, then
multiplication by the image of `det(g_{ij})` is a `B`-linear isomorphism from `B` onto the
annihilator of `Ker(B ⊗_A B → B)`, where `B` acts on `B ⊗_A B` through the left tensor factor.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_linearEquiv_annihilator_ker_lmul
    {A : Type u} {P : Type v} {B : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing P] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra A P] [Algebra A B] [Module.Flat A B]
    {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n → P) (g : Fin n → P ⊗[A] B)
    (gij : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (P ⊗[A] B)) (q : P →ₐ[A] B)
    (hf : Koszul.IsKoszulRegular f)
    (hq : Function.Surjective q)
    (hkerq : RingHom.ker q.toRingHom = Ideal.span (Set.range f))
    (hg : Koszul.IsKoszulRegular g)
    (hkerg : RingHom.ker
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.productLeftAlgHom q (AlgHom.id A B)).toRingHom =
        Ideal.span (Set.range g))
    (hcoeff : ∀ i, f i ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B) = ∑ j, gij i j * g j) :
    ∃ e : B ≃ₗ[B] (RingHom.ker
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A : B ⊗[A] B →ₐ[A] B).toRingHom).annihilator,
      ∀ b, (e b : B ⊗[A] B) =
        b • Algebra.TensorProduct.map q (AlgHom.id A B) (Matrix.det gij)
declarations.comment: more precisely: b ↦ b • δ, B ≅ annihilator of Ker(B ⊗_A B → B), B-linear

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.annihilator_ker_lmul_eq_span_det
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BWC.** Let `f_1, …, f_n` be a Koszul-regular sequence in a ring `P`
over `A` with `B = P/(f_1, …, f_n)` flat over `A`, let `g_1, …, g_n` be a Koszul-regular sequence
generating the kernel of `P ⊗_A B → B`, and write `f_i ⊗ 1 = ∑_j g_{ij} g_j`. The annihilator of
`Ker(B ⊗_A B → B)` is the principal ideal generated by the image of `det(g_{ij})`. The "more
precisely" claim of the tag, that multiplication by this image is a `B`-linear isomorphism from
`B` onto the annihilator, is `exists_linearEquiv_annihilator_ker_lmul`.
declarations.statement:
theorem annihilator_ker_lmul_eq_span_det
    {A : Type u} {P : Type v} {B : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing P] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra A P] [Algebra A B] [Module.Flat A B]
    {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n → P) (g : Fin n → P ⊗[A] B)
    (gij : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (P ⊗[A] B)) (q : P →ₐ[A] B)
    (hf : Koszul.IsKoszulRegular f)
    (hq : Function.Surjective q)
    (hkerq : RingHom.ker q.toRingHom = Ideal.span (Set.range f))
    (hg : Koszul.IsKoszulRegular g)
    (hkerg : RingHom.ker
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.productLeftAlgHom q (AlgHom.id A B)).toRingHom =
        Ideal.span (Set.range g))
    (hcoeff : ∀ i, f i ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B) = ∑ j, gij i j * g j) :
    (RingHom.ker
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A : B ⊗[A] B →ₐ[A] B).toRingHom).annihilator =
      Ideal.span {Algebra.TensorProduct.map q (AlgHom.id A B) (Matrix.det gij)}
declarations.comment: the annihilator of Ker(B ⊗_A B → B) is generated by the image δ of det(g_ij)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.flat_localizedCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BWD (1).** A quotient of `A[x_1, …, x_n, 1/h]` by `n` equations is
flat over `A` as soon as it is quasi-finite over `A`. The statement also holds for `n = 0`, when
the quotient is simply the localization.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_localizedCompleteIntersection
    [Algebra.QuasiFinite A (localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f)] :
    Module.Flat A (localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f)
declarations.comment: flatness

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isLocalCompleteIntersection_localizedCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BWD (1).** A quasi-finite quotient of `A[x_1, …, x_n, 1/h]` by `n`
equations is a relative local complete intersection over `A`. The statement also holds for
`n = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalCompleteIntersection_localizedCompleteIntersection
    [Algebra.QuasiFinite A (localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f)] :
    RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection
      (algebraMap A (localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f))
declarations.comment: local_ci

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.free_rank_eq_one_diagonalAnnihilator_localizedCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BWD (2).** For a quasi-finite quotient `B = A[x_1, …, x_n, 1/h]/(f_1,
…, f_n)`, the annihilator `J` of `Ker(B ⊗_A B → B)` is free of rank `1` over `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem free_rank_eq_one_diagonalAnnihilator_localizedCompleteIntersection :
    Module.Free (localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f)
        (diagonalAnnihilator A (localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f)) ∧
      Module.rank (localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f)
        (diagonalAnnihilator A (localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f)) = 1
declarations.comment: annihilator

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.noetherDifferent_localizedCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BWD (3).** For a quasi-finite quotient `B = A[x_1, …, x_n, 1/h]/(f_1,
…, f_n)`, the Noether different of `B/A` is generated by the Jacobian determinant
`det(∂f_i/∂x_j)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherDifferent_localizedCompleteIntersection :
    noetherDifferent A (localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f) =
      Ideal.span ({
        Matrix.det fun i j : Fin n ↦
          algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) (localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f)
            (MvPolynomial.pderiv j (f i))} : Set _)
declarations.comment: noether_different

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection_of_locallyQuasiFinite_syntomic
declarations.doc:
A locally quasi-finite syntomic morphism of schemes has, around every point of its source, a
square relative global complete intersection presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection_of_locallyQuasiFinite_syntomic
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} {f : Y ⟶ X} (hqf : LocallyQuasiFinite f) (hf : Syntomic f) :
    HasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection f
declarations.comment: the implication (1) ⟹ (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_of_hasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes with square relative global complete intersection presentations around
every point of its source is locally quasi-finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasiFinite_of_hasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} {f : Y ⟶ X} (h : HasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection f) :
    LocallyQuasiFinite f
declarations.comment: the implication (5) ⟹ (1), the locally-quasi-finite conjunct

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.syntomic_of_hasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes with square relative global complete intersection presentations around
every point of its source is syntomic.
declarations.statement:
theorem syntomic_of_hasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection {Y X : Scheme.{u}}
    {f : Y ⟶ X} (h : HasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection f) : Syntomic f
declarations.comment: the implication (5) ⟹ (1), the syntomic conjunct

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasLocalSquarePresentation_of_hasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes which is locally a square relative global complete intersection
`B = A[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_n)` is locally of the form `B = A[x_1, …, x_n, 1/h]/(f_1, …, f_n)`,
with `h = 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLocalSquarePresentation_of_hasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} {f : Y ⟶ X} (h : HasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection f) :
    HasLocalSquarePresentation f
declarations.comment: the implication (5) ⟹ (4), the presentation conjunct

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection_of_hasLocalSquarePresentation
declarations.doc:
A locally quasi-finite morphism of schemes which is locally of the form
`B = A[x_1, …, x_n, 1/h]/(f_1, …, f_n)` is locally a square relative global complete
intersection.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection_of_hasLocalSquarePresentation
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} {f : Y ⟶ X} (hqf : LocallyQuasiFinite f)
    (h : HasLocalSquarePresentation f) :
    HasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection f
declarations.comment: the implication (4) ⟹ (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_syntomic_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasiFinite_syntomic_tfae {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    List.TFAE [
      LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ Syntomic f,
      (LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f,
      ((LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) ∧
        ∀ x : X, IsLocalCompleteIntersectionOverField (f.fiberToSpecResidueField x),
      LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ HasLocalSquarePresentation f,
      HasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection f]
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1), (2), (3), (4) and (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_and_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_of_locallyQuasiFinite_syntomic
declarations.doc:
A locally quasi-finite syntomic morphism of schemes is locally quasi-finite, flat, and a local
complete intersection morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_and_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_of_locallyQuasiFinite_syntomic
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} {f : Y ⟶ X} (h : LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ Syntomic f) :
    (LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f
declarations.comment: the implication (1) ⟹ (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_lci_fibers_of_locallyQuasiFinite_flat_lci
declarations.doc:
A locally quasi-finite flat local complete intersection morphism of schemes is locally of
finite presentation and all of its fibres are local complete intersections over the residue fields
of their base points.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_lci_fibers_of_locallyQuasiFinite_flat_lci
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} {f : Y ⟶ X}
    (h : (LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) :
    ((LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) ∧
      ∀ x : X, IsLocalCompleteIntersectionOverField (f.fiberToSpecResidueField x)
declarations.comment: the implication (2) ⟹ (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_and_hasLocalSquarePresentation_of_lci_fibers
declarations.doc:
A locally quasi-finite flat morphism of schemes which is locally of finite presentation and
all of whose fibres are local complete intersections over the residue fields of their base points
is, around every point of its source, of the form `B = A[x_1, …, x_n, 1/h]/(f_1, …, f_n)`.
declarations.comment: the implication (3) ⟹ (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_and_syntomic_of_hasLocalSquarePresentation
declarations.doc:
A locally quasi-finite morphism of schemes which is locally of the form
`B = A[x_1, …, x_n, 1/h]/(f_1, …, f_n)`, with as many relations as variables, is syntomic.
declarations.comment: the implication (4) ⟹ (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_and_syntomic_of_lci_fibers
declarations.doc:
A locally quasi-finite flat morphism of schemes which is locally of finite presentation and
all of whose fibres are local complete intersections over the residue fields of their base points
is syntomic.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasiFinite_and_syntomic_of_lci_fibers {Y X : Scheme.{u}} {f : Y ⟶ X}
    (h : ((LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) ∧
      ∀ x : X, IsLocalCompleteIntersectionOverField (f.fiberToSpecResidueField x)) :
    LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ Syntomic f
declarations.comment: the implication (3) ⟹ (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection_iff
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes has a square relative global complete intersection presentation around
every point of its source if and only if it is locally quasi-finite and syntomic.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection_iff {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    HasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection f ↔
      LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ Syntomic f
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1) and (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_flat_lfp_and_hasTorAmplitude_of_locallyQuasiFinite_syntomic
declarations.doc:
A locally quasi-finite syntomic morphism of schemes is locally quasi-finite, flat and locally
of finite presentation, and its naive cotangent complex `NL_{Y/X}` has Tor amplitude in
`[-1, 0]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasiFinite_flat_lfp_and_hasTorAmplitude_of_locallyQuasiFinite_syntomic
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} {f : Y ⟶ X} (h : LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ Syntomic f) :
    ((LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) ∧
      Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude Y.toRingedSpace
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0
declarations.comment: the implication (1) ⟹ (6)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_syntomic_of_flat_lfp_of_hasTorAmplitude
declarations.doc:
A locally quasi-finite flat morphism of schemes which is locally of finite presentation and
whose naive cotangent complex has Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]` is syntomic.
declarations.comment: the implication (6) ⟹ (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_lfp_and_isPerfect_and_hasTorAmplitude_of_locallyQuasiFinite_syntomic
declarations.doc:
A locally quasi-finite syntomic morphism of schemes is flat and locally of finite
presentation, and its naive cotangent complex `NL_{Y/X}` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_Y)` of rank
zero with Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_lfp_and_isPerfect_and_hasTorAmplitude_of_locallyQuasiFinite_syntomic
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} {f : Y ⟶ X} (h : LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ Syntomic f) :
    (Flat f ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) ∧
      (Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := Y.toRingedSpace)
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) ∧
        DeterminantTwoTerm.IsRankZeroScheme
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) ∧
        Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude Y.toRingedSpace
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0)
declarations.comment: the implication (1) ⟹ (7)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_syntomic_of_flat_lfp_of_isPerfect_of_isRankZeroScheme
declarations.doc:
A flat morphism of schemes which is locally of finite presentation and whose naive cotangent
complex `NL_{Y/X}` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_Y)` of rank zero with Tor amplitude in `[-1, 0]`
is locally quasi-finite and syntomic.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasiFinite_syntomic_of_flat_lfp_of_isPerfect_of_isRankZeroScheme
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} {f : Y ⟶ X}
    (h : (Flat f ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) ∧
      (Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := Y.toRingedSpace)
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) ∧
        DeterminantTwoTerm.IsRankZeroScheme
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) ∧
        Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude Y.toRingedSpace
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0)) :
    LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ Syntomic f
declarations.comment: the implication (7) ⟹ (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_syntomic_tfae_naiveCotangentComplex
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasiFinite_syntomic_tfae_naiveCotangentComplex {Y X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    List.TFAE [
      LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ Syntomic f,
      (LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f,
      ((LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) ∧
        ∀ x : X, IsLocalCompleteIntersectionOverField (f.fiberToSpecResidueField x),
      LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ HasLocalSquarePresentation f,
      HasLocalSquareRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection f,
      ((LocallyQuasiFinite f ∧ Flat f) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) ∧
        Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude Y.toRingedSpace
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0,
      (Flat f ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) ∧
        (Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := Y.toRingedSpace)
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) ∧
          DeterminantTwoTerm.IsRankZeroScheme
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) ∧
          Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude Y.toRingedSpace
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f)) (-1) 0)]

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModule_invertible_of_squarePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BWF**, the affine case the source reduces to. Let `A → B` be a
quasi-finite flat homomorphism of Noetherian rings with a presentation
`B = A[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_n)` by as many relations as variables. Then the relative
dualizing module `ω_{B/A}` is an invertible `B`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingModule_invertible_of_squarePresentation
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B] [Module.Flat A B]
    {n : ℕ} (P : Algebra.Presentation A B (Fin n) (Fin n))
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B) :
    Module.Invertible B (dualizingModule F)
declarations.comment:
the affine case: a square relative global complete intersection presentation,
which is part (5) of Stacks 0BWE

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.exists_chart_dualizingModule_invertible_of_locallyQuasiFinite_syntomic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BWF.** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a locally quasi-finite syntomic morphism of
locally Noetherian schemes. Then every point of `Y` has an affine open neighbourhood
`V = Spec B` lying over an affine open `U = Spec A` of `X` for which the algebraic relative
dualizing module `ω_{B/A}` is an invertible `B`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_chart_dualizingModule_invertible_of_locallyQuasiFinite_syntomic
    (hf : Syntomic f) :
    ∀ y : Y, ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (V : Y.affineOpens) (hVU : V.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1), y ∈ V.1 ∧
      letI : Algebra Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1) := (f.appLE U V hVU).hom.toAlgebra
      ∀ F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, u, u} Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1),
        Module.Invertible Γ(Y, V.1) (dualizingModule F)
declarations.comment:
the scheme-level statement, stated at the charts of `f`: every point of `Y` has an
affine open `V = Spec B` over an affine open `U = Spec A` of `X` on which `ω_{B/A}` is
invertible. This is condition (4) of Stacks 0C16, which
`Stacks.Discriminant.isInvertible_iff_exists_chart_dualizingModule_invertible` identifies with
invertibility of `ω_{Y/X}` as a sheaf.

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.annihilator_quotient_span_traceElement_eq_fittingIdeal_kaehlerDifferential
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BWG]**, the affine case.  Let `A → C` be a quasi-finite flat homomorphism of
Noetherian rings with a presentation `C = A[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_n)` by as many relations as
variables, and let `ω_{C/A}` and `τ_{C/A}` be its relative dualizing module and trace element.
The annihilator of `ω_{C/A}/C·τ_{C/A}`, the cokernel of `τ_{C/A} : C → ω_{C/A}`, is the Kähler
different of `C` over `A`.

The dualizing module is invertible by [Stacks, Tag 0BWF], so the annihilator is the image of
evaluation at the trace element (`Stacks.Discriminant.range_eval_eq_annihilator_quotient_span`),
which is the Noether different by [Stacks, Tag 0BVT].
declarations.statement:
theorem annihilator_quotient_span_traceElement_eq_fittingIdeal_kaehlerDifferential
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing C] [Module.Flat A C] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A C]
    {n : ℕ} (P : Algebra.Presentation A C (Fin n) (Fin n))
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, u, w} A C) :
    letI : Algebra.FinitePresentation A C := P.finitePresentation_of_isFinite
    Module.annihilator C
        (dualizingModule F ⧸ Submodule.span C {dualizingModule.traceElement F}) =
      _root_.fittingIdeal (R := C) (M := Ω[C⁄A]) 0
declarations.comment:
the affine case, with the relative dualizing module and the trace element
constructed rather than assumed: on an algebra presented by `n` equations in `n` variables, the
annihilator of the cokernel of `τ_{C/A} : C → ω_{C/A}` — the different of Tag 0BW4 read on such a
chart — is the Kähler different

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.different_sections_eq_kaehlerDifferent_ideal
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BWG].** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a locally quasi-finite syntomic morphism of
locally Noetherian schemes — the equivalent conditions of [Stacks, Tag 0BWE] — with relative
dualizing module `ω_{Y/X}` and trace element `τ_{Y/X}`.  Then the different `𝔇_f` and the Kähler
different of `f` have the same ideal of sections over every affine open of `Y`, that is, they are
the same ideal sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem different_sections_eq_kaehlerDifferent_ideal (hf : Syntomic f) :
    letI : Flat f := AlgebraicGeometry.flat hf
    letI : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f := AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFinitePresentation hf
    ∀ (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f) (τ : RelativeTraceSection ω) (V : Y.affineOpens),
      (show Ideal Γ(Y, V.1) from (different ω τ).toSubmodule.obj (op V.1)) =
        (kaehlerDifferent f).ideal V
declarations.comment:
the global statement: the different and the Kähler different have the same ideal
of sections over every affine open of `Y`, hence agree as ideal sheaves. The different, an
annihilator subsheaf of `𝒪_Y`, and the Kähler different, an ideal sheaf datum, are compared
through their ideals of sections; the relative dualizing module and the trace element enter as
the data of Tags 0BVG and 0BVJ out of which Tag 0BW4 defines the different.

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.exists_linearEquiv_dualizingModule_jacobianDet
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BWH.** Let `A` be a ring, let `h, f_1, …, f_n` be polynomials in `n`
variables over `A` and set `B = A[x_1, …, x_n, 1/h]/(f_1, …, f_n)`, assumed quasi-finite over `A`.
Then there is an isomorphism `B → ω_{B/A}` mapping `det(∂f_i/∂x_j)` to `τ_{B/A}`.

The three parts of the statement are:

* over a Noetherian ring `A`, for every finite-open factorization `F` of `A → B` (so for the
  dualizing module `ω_{B/A} = Hom_A(B', A) ⊗_{B'} B` of Tag 0BSZ, which does not depend on `F`),
  an isomorphism `B ≅ ω_{B/A}` carrying the Jacobian determinant to the trace element
  `τ_{B/A}` of Definition 0BT6;
* over an arbitrary ring `A`, a finite-open factorization `A → B' → B` with `B'` a finitely
  presented `A`-module exists;
* over an arbitrary ring `A`, for every such factorization, an isomorphism
  `B ≅ Hom_A(B', A) ⊗_{B'} B` carrying the Jacobian determinant to the canonical element
  `Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModule.traceCandidate` (the element of the proof of Tag 0BTB,
  which is the trace element when `A` is Noetherian).

The source defines `ω_{B/A}` and `τ_{B/A}` only for Noetherian rings: Section 0BUK opens with
"Let `A → B` be a quasi-finite homomorphism of Noetherian rings ... We set
`ω_{B/A} = Hom_A(B', A) ⊗_{B'} B`", and Definition 0BT6 reads "Let `A → B` be a flat quasi-finite
map of Noetherian rings. The trace element is the unique element `τ_{B/A} ∈ ω_{B/A}` with the
following property: for any Noetherian `A`-algebra `A_1` ...". The first part is the statement at
those definitions. The last two parts extend it to an arbitrary ring, with `ω_{B/A}` computed from
a factorization whose intermediate algebra is finitely presented, the class of factorizations that
base change correctly, and `τ_{B/A}` the canonical element. Finite presentation of the
intermediate algebra cannot be dropped over a non-Noetherian ring: for
`A = k[t, a_1, a_2, …]/(t^i a_i, a_i a_j)` and `I = (a_1, a_2, …)`, the algebra
`B = A[x]/(tx - 1) = A_t` is quasi-finite, and `A → A/I → A_t` is a finite-open factorization
(`A/I = k[t]` and `A_t = k[t, 1/t]`), but `Hom_A(A/I, A) ⊗_{A/I} A_t = (Ann_A I)_t = I_t = 0`.

The proof of the last part writes `A` as the union of its subrings of finite type over `ℤ`,
descends `B`, the factorization and its local isomorphisms to such a subring `A₀`, which is
Noetherian, applies the first part there, and base changes back to `A` (Tag 0BVF). The source
assumes `n ≥ 1`; the statement also holds for `n = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_linearEquiv_dualizingModule_jacobianDet (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (n : ℕ)
    (h : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) (f : Fin n → MvPolynomial (Fin n) A)
    [Algebra.QuasiFinite A (localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f)] :
    letI : Module.Flat A (localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f) :=
      flat_localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f
    (∀ [IsNoetherianRing A]
        (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, u, w} A (localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f)),
        ∃ ε : localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f ≃ₗ[localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f]
            dualizingModule F,
          ε (Matrix.det fun i j : Fin n ↦ algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A)
              (localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f) (MvPolynomial.pderiv j (f i))) =
            dualizingModule.traceElement F) ∧
      (∃ F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, u, u} A (localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f),
        Module.FinitePresentation A F.middle) ∧
      ∀ (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, u, w} A (localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f))
        [Module.FinitePresentation A F.middle],
        ∃ ε : localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f ≃ₗ[localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f]
            dualizingModule F,
          ε (Matrix.det fun i j : Fin n ↦ algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A)
              (localizedCompleteIntersection A n h f) (MvPolynomial.pderiv j (f i))) =
            dualizingModule.traceCandidate F
declarations.comment:
the isomorphism of B with its dualizing module carrying the Jacobian determinant
to the trace element, at the source's definitions over a Noetherian ring and for factorizations
with finitely presented intermediate algebra over an arbitrary ring

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.fittingIdeal_kaehlerDifferential_localization_adjoinRoot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BWI.** For `B = (A[x]/(f))_h = A[x, 1/h]/(f)` the Kähler different of
`B` over `A` — the zeroth Fitting ideal of `Ω[B⁄A]` — is the ideal generated by the image of the
derivative `f'`.

The source's Noetherian hypothesis on `A` and quasi-finiteness hypothesis on `B` are not needed
for this formula and are not imposed; they are what make this ideal agree with the Noether
different and with the different of `Spec(B)` over `Spec(A)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fittingIdeal_kaehlerDifferential_localization_adjoinRoot
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (f h : Polynomial A) :
    fittingIdeal (M := KaehlerDifferential A (Localization.Away (AdjoinRoot.mk f h))) 0 =
      Ideal.span {algebraMap (AdjoinRoot f) (Localization.Away (AdjoinRoot.mk f h))
                    (AdjoinRoot.mk f f.derivative)}
declarations.comment: kahler_different

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.noetherDifferent_localization_adjoinRoot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BWI.** For `B = (A[x]/(f))_h = A[x, 1/h]/(f)` quasi-finite over `A`,
the Noether different of `B` over `A` is the ideal generated by the image of the derivative
`f'`.

The source's Noetherian hypothesis on `A` is not needed for this formula and is not imposed.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherDifferent_localization_adjoinRoot (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (f h : Polynomial A)
    [Algebra.QuasiFinite A (Localization.Away (AdjoinRoot.mk f h))] :
    noetherDifferent A (Localization.Away (AdjoinRoot.mk f h)) =
      Ideal.span {algebraMap (AdjoinRoot f) (Localization.Away (AdjoinRoot.mk f h))
                    (AdjoinRoot.mk f f.derivative)}
declarations.comment: noether_different

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.cokerSpanIdeal_traceElement_localization_adjoinRoot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BWI.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring and `f, h ∈ A[x]` with
`B = (A[x]/(f))_h` quasi-finite over `A`.  The different of `Spec(B)` over `Spec(A)` — the
annihilator of the cokernel of `B → ω_{B/A}`, `b ↦ b τ_{B/A}`, which is Definition 0BW4 read on
the affine `Spec(B)` — is the ideal generated by the image of the derivative `f'`.

So `(f') ⊆ B` is the ideal whose associated quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals is the different:
`Stacks.Discriminant.different_sections_eq_cokerSpanIdeal` identifies the ideal of sections of
the different over an affine chart with this ideal, and on an affine scheme a coherent ideal
sheaf is the tilde of its ideal of sections.

Nothing is assumed beyond the hypotheses of the example.  `B` Noetherian, `B` flat over `A` and
`ω_{B/A}` invertible are all derived from quasi-finiteness, by
`Stacks.Discriminant.isNoetherianRing_localization_adjoinRoot`,
`Stacks.Discriminant.flat_localization_adjoinRoot` and
`Stacks.Discriminant.module_invertible_dualizingModule_localization_adjoinRoot`; the `letI`
bindings below are those derivations, not hypotheses.  The statement is for every finite-open
factorization `F` of `A → B`, of which there is one by
`Stacks.Discriminant.nonempty_finiteOpenFactorization_localization_adjoinRoot`, and the ideal is
independent of the choice because `ω_{B/A}` is (Tag 0BT1).
declarations.statement:
theorem cokerSpanIdeal_traceElement_localization_adjoinRoot (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (f h : Polynomial A)
    [Algebra.QuasiFinite A (Localization.Away (AdjoinRoot.mk f h))] :
    letI : IsNoetherianRing (Localization.Away (AdjoinRoot.mk f h)) :=
      isNoetherianRing_localization_adjoinRoot A f h
    letI : Module.Flat A (Localization.Away (AdjoinRoot.mk f h)) :=
      flat_localization_adjoinRoot A f h
    ∀ F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, u, u} A (Localization.Away (AdjoinRoot.mk f h)),
      Stacks.Annihilator.cokerSpanIdeal (Localization.Away (AdjoinRoot.mk f h))
          (dualizingModule.traceElement F) =
        Ideal.span {algebraMap (AdjoinRoot f) (Localization.Away (AdjoinRoot.mk f h))
                      (AdjoinRoot.mk f f.derivative)}
declarations.comment: scheme_different

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.nonempty_tensorIso_invertibleSheaf_kaehlerDifferent_of_etaleAt
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BWJ], the bundle identity.**  If `f` is étale at the associated points of
`Y` then

`f^*Ω^n_{X/S} ⊗_{𝒪_Y} 𝒪_Y(R) ≅ Ω^n_{Y/S}`

as invertible sheaves on `Y`, where `R` is the closed subscheme cut out by the Kähler different
of `f`.

Both `f^*Ω^n_{X/S}` and `Ω^n_{Y/S}` are invertible
(`Stacks.Discriminant.isInvertible_pullback_relativeDifferentialForms` and
`Stacks.Discriminant.isInvertible_relativeDifferentialForms`), so `∧ⁿ(df)` admits a tensor
factorization
(`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorFactorization.exists_tensorFactorization`), and
`Stacks.Discriminant.nonempty_tensorIso_invertibleSheaf_kaehlerDifferent_of_tensorFactorization`
turns that factorization into the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_tensorIso_invertibleSheaf_kaehlerDifferent_of_etaleAt
    (hét : ∀ y ∈ Stacks.Divisors.schemeAssociatedPoints Y, EtaleAt f y) :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType f := locallyOfFiniteType_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension pX f n
    Nonempty ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨((Y.toRingedSpace)).presheaf,
        ((Y.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩).obj (((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj
        (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms pX (n : ℤ))))).obj
          ((Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf' (kaehlerDifferent f)))) ≅
      Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms (f ≫ pX) (n : ℤ))
declarations.comment:
the Kähler-different form of the bundle identity: if `f` is étale at the
associated points of `Y` then `f^*Ω^n_{X/S} ⊗_{𝒪_Y} 𝒪_Y(R) = Ω^n_{Y/S}` as invertible sheaves on
`Y`, with `R` the closed subscheme cut out by the Kähler different of Tag 0BVW. The Kähler
different equals the different of Tag 0BW4 by Tag 0BWG; the statement for the different itself
is `nonempty_tensorIso_invertibleSheaf_differentIdealSheaf_of_etaleAt`

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.exists_chart_differentIdealSheaf_ideal_eq_span_det
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BWJ], the local equation of `R`.**  Let `X` and `Y` be smooth of relative
dimension `n` over a locally Noetherian base `S` and let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a locally quasi-finite
morphism over `S`.  Every point of `Y` has an affine chart `V = Spec B` over an affine chart
`U = Spec A` of `X` over an affine chart `W = Spec R` of `S`, on which `Ω[A⁄R]` and `Ω[B⁄R]` are
free of rank `n` and the ideal of the closed subscheme `R ⊆ Y` cut out by the different of `f` is
generated by `∧ⁿ(df)`, the determinant of the matrix of `B ⊗_A Ω[A⁄R] → Ω[B⁄R]` in those bases.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_chart_differentIdealSheaf_ideal_eq_span_det (y : Y) :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType f := locallyOfFiniteType_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension pX f n
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := isLocallyNoetherian_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension pX n
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian Y := isLocallyNoetherian_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension (f ≫ pX) n
    letI : Flat f := flat_of_locallyQuasiFinite pX f n
    ∃ (W : S.Opens), IsAffineOpen W ∧ ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (V : Y.affineOpens)
      (hUW : U.1 ≤ pX ⁻¹ᵁ W) (hVU : V.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) (hVW : V.1 ≤ (f ≫ pX) ⁻¹ᵁ W),
      y ∈ V.1 ∧
      letI := Stacks.Smooth.algebraAppLE pX hUW
      letI := Stacks.Smooth.algebraAppLE f hVU
      letI := Stacks.Smooth.algebraAppLE (f ≫ pX) hVW
      letI := isScalarTower_appLE pX f hUW hVU hVW
      ∃ (bA : Module.Basis (Fin n) Γ(X, U.1) Ω[Γ(X, U.1)⁄Γ(S, W)])
        (bB : Module.Basis (Fin n) Γ(Y, V.1) Ω[Γ(Y, V.1)⁄Γ(S, W)]),
        (differentIdealSheaf (relativeDualizingModuleData f)
            (RelativeTraceSection.canonical (relativeDualizingModuleData f))).ideal V =
          Ideal.span {(LinearMap.toMatrix (bA.baseChange Γ(Y, V.1)) bB
            (KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange Γ(S, W) Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1))).det}
declarations.comment:
the closed subscheme `R` cut out by the different of `f` (Tag 0BW4) is cut out
locally by `∧ⁿ(df)`: on affine charts `V = Spec B` over `U = Spec A` over `W = Spec R` of the
base, with bases of rank `n` of `Ω_{A/R}` and `Ω_{B/R}`, its ideal is generated by the determinant
of `B ⊗_A Ω_{A/R} → Ω_{B/R}`

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.differentIdealSheaf_eq_zeroScheme_of_tensorFactorization
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BWJ], `R` is cut out by the section `∧ⁿ(df)`.**  The morphism
`∧ⁿ(df) : f^*Ω^n_{X/S} ⟶ Ω^n_{Y/S}` of invertible modules is a section of
`(f^*Ω^n_{X/S})^{⊗ -1} ⊗ Ω^n_{Y/S}`: there is an invertible module `ℳ` with a global section `σ`
and an isomorphism `f^*Ω^n_{X/S} ⊗ ℳ ≅ Ω^n_{Y/S}` carrying `x ⊗ σ` to `∧ⁿ(df)(x)`, and for every
such factorization the zero scheme of `σ` is the closed subscheme `R ⊆ Y` cut out by the
different of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentIdealSheaf_eq_zeroScheme_of_tensorFactorization :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType f := locallyOfFiniteType_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension pX f n
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := isLocallyNoetherian_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension pX n
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian Y := isLocallyNoetherian_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension (f ≫ pX) n
    letI : Flat f := flat_of_locallyQuasiFinite pX f n
    (∃ (M : Y.Modules) (σ : M.sections)
      (e : (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
          ⟨((Y.toRingedSpace)).presheaf, ((Y.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩).obj
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj
              (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms pX (n : ℤ)))).obj M) ≅
        Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms (f ≫ pX) (n : ℤ)),
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.sheaf.obj Y.ringCatSheaf.property M ∧
      ∀ (O : Y.Opens) (x : Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj
          (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms pX (n : ℤ)), O)),
        Scheme.Modules.Hom.app e.hom O
            (toTensorSheafSection Y.toRingedSpace ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj
              (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms pX (n : ℤ))) M (op O)
              (x ⊗ₜ[Y.presheaf.obj (op O)] σ.eval (op O))) =
          Scheme.Modules.Hom.app (topFormsMap pX f n) O x) ∧
    ∀ (M : Y.Modules)
      [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.sheaf.obj Y.ringCatSheaf.property M]
      (σ : M.sections)
      (e : (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
          ⟨((Y.toRingedSpace)).presheaf, ((Y.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩).obj
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj
              (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms pX (n : ℤ)))).obj M) ≅
        Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms (f ≫ pX) (n : ℤ)),
      (∀ (O : Y.Opens) (x : Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj
          (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms pX (n : ℤ)), O)),
        Scheme.Modules.Hom.app e.hom O
            (toTensorSheafSection Y.toRingedSpace ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj
              (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms pX (n : ℤ))) M (op O)
              (x ⊗ₜ[Y.presheaf.obj (op O)] σ.eval (op O))) =
          Scheme.Modules.Hom.app (topFormsMap pX f n) O x) →
      zeroScheme Y M (σ.eval (op ⊤)) =
        differentIdealSheaf (relativeDualizingModuleData f)
          (RelativeTraceSection.canonical (relativeDualizingModuleData f))
declarations.comment:
the closed subscheme `R` cut out by the different of `f` (Tag 0BW4) is the closed
subscheme cut out by `∧ⁿ(df) ∈ Γ(Y, (f^*Ω^n_{X/S})^{⊗ -1} ⊗ Ω^n_{Y/S})`: the section `σ` of an
invertible `ℳ` with `f^*Ω^n_{X/S} ⊗ ℳ ≅ Ω^n_{Y/S}` sending `x ⊗ σ` to `∧ⁿ(df)(x)`, which exists,
has zero scheme `R`

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isLocallyPrincipal_differentIdealSheaf_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BWJ], local principality.**  The closed subscheme `R ⊆ Y` cut out by the
different of `f` is locally principal: on the charts of
`Stacks.Discriminant.exists_chart_differentIdealSheaf_ideal_eq_span_det` it is cut out by the
single function `∧ⁿ(df)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyPrincipal_differentIdealSheaf_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType f := locallyOfFiniteType_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension pX f n
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := isLocallyNoetherian_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension pX n
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian Y := isLocallyNoetherian_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension (f ≫ pX) n
    letI : Flat f := flat_of_locallyQuasiFinite pX f n
    Stacks.Divisors.IsLocallyPrincipal
      (differentIdealSheaf (relativeDualizingModuleData f)
        (RelativeTraceSection.canonical (relativeDualizingModuleData f)))
declarations.comment:
the closed subscheme `R` cut out by the different of `f` (Tag 0BW4) is locally
principal

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_differentIdealSheaf_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BWJ], the effective Cartier divisor.**  If `f` is étale at the associated
points of `Y`, the closed subscheme `R ⊆ Y` cut out by the different of `f` is an effective
Cartier divisor: its local equation `∧ⁿ(df)` is a nonzerodivisor, because it does not vanish at
any associated point of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
