theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_differentIdealSheaf_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension
    (hét : ∀ y ∈ Stacks.Divisors.schemeAssociatedPoints Y, EtaleAt f y) :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType f := locallyOfFiniteType_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension pX f n
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := isLocallyNoetherian_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension pX n
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian Y := isLocallyNoetherian_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension (f ≫ pX) n
    letI : Flat f := flat_of_locallyQuasiFinite pX f n
    Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor
      (differentIdealSheaf (relativeDualizingModuleData f)
        (RelativeTraceSection.canonical (relativeDualizingModuleData f)))
declarations.comment:
if `f` is étale at the associated points of `Y` then the closed subscheme `R` cut
out by the different of `f` (Tag 0BW4) is an effective Cartier divisor

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.nonempty_tensorIso_invertibleSheaf_differentIdealSheaf_of_etaleAt
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BWJ], the bundle identity.**  If `f` is étale at the associated points of
`Y` then

`f^*Ω^n_{X/S} ⊗_{𝒪_Y} 𝒪_Y(R) ≅ Ω^n_{Y/S}`

as invertible sheaves on `Y`, where `R` is the closed subscheme cut out by the different of
`f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_tensorIso_invertibleSheaf_differentIdealSheaf_of_etaleAt
    (hét : ∀ y ∈ Stacks.Divisors.schemeAssociatedPoints Y, EtaleAt f y) :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType f := locallyOfFiniteType_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension pX f n
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := isLocallyNoetherian_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension pX n
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian Y := isLocallyNoetherian_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension (f ≫ pX) n
    letI : Flat f := flat_of_locallyQuasiFinite pX f n
    Nonempty ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
        ⟨((Y.toRingedSpace)).presheaf, ((Y.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj
            (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms pX (n : ℤ)))).obj
          (Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf'
            (differentIdealSheaf (relativeDualizingModuleData f)
              (RelativeTraceSection.canonical (relativeDualizingModuleData f))))) ≅
      Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms (f ≫ pX) (n : ℤ))
declarations.comment:
the bundle identity: if `f` is étale at the associated points of `Y` then
`f^*Ω^n_{X/S} ⊗_{𝒪_Y} 𝒪_Y(R) = Ω^n_{Y/S}` as invertible sheaves on `Y`, where `R` is the closed
subscheme cut out by the different of `f` (Tag 0BW4)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.flat_of_locallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BWJ], flatness.**  Let `X` and `Y` be smooth of relative dimension `n` over a
locally Noetherian base `S` and let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a locally quasi-finite morphism over `S`.
Then `f` is flat.
declarations.comment:
`f` is flat, the first assertion of the tag.  The base is assumed only locally
Noetherian; local Noetherianness of `X` and `Y` and flatness of `Y ⟶ S` are derived from
smoothness over `S`, not assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.exists_chart_kaehlerDifferent_ideal_eq_span_det
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BWJ], the local equation of `R`.**  Let `X` and `Y` be smooth of relative
dimension `n` over a locally Noetherian base `S` and let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism over `S`.
Every point of `Y` has an affine chart `V = Spec B` over an affine chart `U = Spec A` of `X` over
an affine chart `W = Spec R` of `S`, on which `Ω[A⁄R]` and `Ω[B⁄R]` are free of rank `n` and the
ideal of the Kähler different of `f` is generated by `∧ⁿ(df)` — the determinant of the matrix of
`B ⊗_A Ω[A⁄R] → Ω[B⁄R]` in those bases.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_chart_kaehlerDifferent_ideal_eq_span_det (y : Y) :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType f := locallyOfFiniteType_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension pX f n
    ∃ (W : S.Opens), IsAffineOpen W ∧ ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (V : Y.affineOpens)
      (hUW : U.1 ≤ pX ⁻¹ᵁ W) (hVU : V.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) (hVW : V.1 ≤ (f ≫ pX) ⁻¹ᵁ W),
      y ∈ V.1 ∧
      letI := Stacks.Smooth.algebraAppLE pX hUW
      letI := Stacks.Smooth.algebraAppLE f hVU
      letI := Stacks.Smooth.algebraAppLE (f ≫ pX) hVW
      letI := isScalarTower_appLE pX f hUW hVU hVW
      ∃ (bA : Module.Basis (Fin n) Γ(X, U.1) Ω[Γ(X, U.1)⁄Γ(S, W)])
        (bB : Module.Basis (Fin n) Γ(Y, V.1) Ω[Γ(Y, V.1)⁄Γ(S, W)]),
        (kaehlerDifferent f).ideal V =
          Ideal.span {(LinearMap.toMatrix (bA.baseChange Γ(Y, V.1)) bB
            (KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange Γ(S, W) Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1))).det}
declarations.comment:
the Kähler-different form of the local equation of `R`: on affine charts
`V = Spec B` over `U = Spec A` over `W = Spec R` of the base, the Kähler different of Tag 0BVW is
generated by `∧ⁿ(df)`, the determinant of `B ⊗_A Ω_{A/R} → Ω_{B/R}` in bases of rank `n`. The
Kähler different equals the different of Tag 0BW4 by Tag 0BWG; the statement for the different
itself is `exists_chart_differentIdealSheaf_ideal_eq_span_det`

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isLocallyPrincipal_kaehlerDifferent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BWJ], local principality.**  The closed subscheme `R ⊆ Y` cut out by the
Kähler different of `f` — the different of `f` by [Stacks, Tag 0BWG] — is locally principal: on
the charts of `Stacks.Discriminant.exists_chart_kaehlerDifferent_ideal_eq_span_det` it is cut out
by the single function `∧ⁿ(df)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyPrincipal_kaehlerDifferent :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType f := locallyOfFiniteType_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension pX f n
    Stacks.Divisors.IsLocallyPrincipal (kaehlerDifferent f)
declarations.comment:
the Kähler-different form of local principality: the closed subscheme cut out by
the Kähler different of Tag 0BVW is locally principal. The Kähler different equals the different
of Tag 0BW4 by Tag 0BWG; the statement for the different itself is
`isLocallyPrincipal_differentIdealSheaf_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension`

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_kaehlerDifferent_of_etaleAt
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BWJ], the effective Cartier divisor.**  If moreover `f` is étale at the
associated points of `Y`, the closed subscheme `R ⊆ Y` cut out by the Kähler different of `f` is
an effective Cartier divisor: its local equation `∧ⁿ(df)` is a nonzerodivisor, because it does
not vanish at any associated point of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_kaehlerDifferent_of_etaleAt
    (hét : ∀ y ∈ Stacks.Divisors.schemeAssociatedPoints Y, EtaleAt f y) :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType f := locallyOfFiniteType_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension pX f n
    Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (kaehlerDifferent f)
declarations.comment:
the Kähler-different form of the Cartier property: if `f` is étale at the
associated points of `Y`, the closed subscheme cut out by the Kähler different of Tag 0BVW is an
effective Cartier divisor. The Kähler different equals the different of Tag 0BW4 by Tag 0BWG;
the statement for the different itself is
`isEffectiveCartierDivisor_differentIdealSheaf_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension`

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.generalizedDifferent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BWM].** The *generalized different* `𝔇_f` of a quasi-finite morphism of
locally Noetherian schemes which is flat near the associated points: the annihilator of the
cokernel of the map `𝒪_Y → ω_{Y/X}` given by the extension `τ` of the trace element
`τ_{V/X}`.
declarations.statement:
def generalizedDifferent (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f) (τ : GeneralizedTraceSection ω) :
    (SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace)).Submodule
declarations.comment: the generalized different

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.generalizedDifferent_spec_eq_tilde_dedekindDifferent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BWN].** Assume the Dedekind different is defined for `A → B`, and set
`X = Spec(A)`, `Y = Spec(B)` and `f : Y → X`.  Then, for the relative dualizing module `ω` of
`f`, the generalization of the different (Remark 0BWM) applies to `f` — an open of `Y` over which
`f` is flat contains `Ass(𝒪_Y)` and `f⁻¹(Ass(𝒪_X))`, and the trace element of the flat locus
comes from a global section of `ω_{Y/X}` — if and only if `1 ∈ L_{B/A}`; this is the case for
instance if `A` is normal.  In this case the Dedekind different `𝔇_{B/A}` is an ideal of `B`,
and the generalized different `𝔇_f` is the coherent sheaf of ideals `(𝔇_{B/A})~` on `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem generalizedDifferent_spec_eq_tilde_dedekindDifferent {A B : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] (setup : DedekindDifferentSetup A B) :
    letI : IsNoetherianRing A := setup.isNoetherianRing
    letI : Module.Finite A B := setup.finite
    letI : IsNoetherianRing B := IsNoetherianRing.of_finite A B
    letI := locallyQuasiFinite_spec_map (A := A) (B := B)
    ∀ ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B))),
      ((Nonempty (GeneralizedDifferentSituation (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)))) ∧
          Nonempty (GeneralizedTraceSection ω)) ↔
        (1 : B ⊗[A] FractionRing A) ∈ setup.complementaryModule) ∧
      (IsNormalRing A → (1 : B ⊗[A] FractionRing A) ∈ setup.complementaryModule) ∧
      ((1 : B ⊗[A] FractionRing A) ∈ setup.complementaryModule →
        setup.dedekindDifferent =
            Submodule.map (Algebra.linearMap B (B ⊗[A] FractionRing A))
              (dedekindDifferentIdeal setup : Submodule B B) ∧
          ∀ τ : GeneralizedTraceSection ω,
            Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent (generalizedDifferent ω τ).toSheafOfModules ∧
            generalizedDifferent ω τ =
              (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop ((dedekindDifferentIdeal setup).map
                (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of B)).inv.hom)).unitSubmodule)
declarations.comment:
the generalized different of `Spec B → Spec A` is defined iff `1 ∈ L_{B/A}` (e.g.
for normal `A`), and then `𝔇_{B/A}` is an ideal of `B` and `𝔇_f = (𝔇_{B/A})~`

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.NodeExample.one_mem_complementaryModule_iff_natCast_eq
declarations.doc:
One belongs to the complementary module exactly when the two branch degrees have the same
image in `k`.  The source states this as `n = m`; what the trace of one, `(nx+my)/(x+y)`, lies
in `A` for is `(n : k) = (m : k)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem one_mem_complementaryModule_iff_natCast_eq
    (n m : ℕ) (hn : IsUnit (n : k)) (hm : IsUnit (m : k))
    (f : nodeRing k →+* targetNodeRing k)
    (hx : f (x k) = u k ^ n) (hy : f (y k) = v k ^ m)
    (hk : ∀ a : k, f (algebraMap k (nodeRing k) a) = algebraMap k (targetNodeRing k) a) :
    letI : Algebra (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k) := f.toAlgebra
    ∀ setup : DedekindDifferentSetup (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k),
      letI : DedekindDifferentSetup (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k) := setup
      ((1 : (targetNodeRing k) ⊗[nodeRing k] FractionRing (nodeRing k)) ∈
        setup.complementaryModule ↔ (n : k) = (m : k))
declarations.comment: complementary module criterion

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.NodeExample.complementaryModule_eq_range
declarations.doc: When the branch degrees agree, the complementary module is precisely `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem complementaryModule_eq_range
    (n m : ℕ) (hn : IsUnit (n : k)) (hm : IsUnit (m : k))
    (f : nodeRing k →+* targetNodeRing k)
    (hx : f (x k) = u k ^ n) (hy : f (y k) = v k ^ m)
    (hk : ∀ a : k, f (algebraMap k (nodeRing k) a) = algebraMap k (targetNodeRing k) a)
    (heq : (n : k) = (m : k)) :
    letI : Algebra (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k) := f.toAlgebra
    ∀ setup : DedekindDifferentSetup (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k),
      letI : DedekindDifferentSetup (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k) := setup
      ∀ z, z ∈ setup.complementaryModule ↔
        z ∈ Set.range (algebraMap (targetNodeRing k)
          ((targetNodeRing k) ⊗[nodeRing k] FractionRing (nodeRing k)))
declarations.comment: complementary module equals B

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.NodeExample.dedekindDifferent_eq_range
declarations.doc: In that case the Dedekind different is the unit ideal of `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dedekindDifferent_eq_range
    (n m : ℕ) (hn : IsUnit (n : k)) (hm : IsUnit (m : k))
    (f : nodeRing k →+* targetNodeRing k)
    (hx : f (x k) = u k ^ n) (hy : f (y k) = v k ^ m)
    (hk : ∀ a : k, f (algebraMap k (nodeRing k) a) = algebraMap k (targetNodeRing k) a)
    (heq : (n : k) = (m : k)) :
    letI : Algebra (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k) := f.toAlgebra
    ∀ setup : DedekindDifferentSetup (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k),
      letI : DedekindDifferentSetup (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k) := setup
      ∀ z, z ∈ setup.dedekindDifferent ↔
        z ∈ Set.range (algebraMap (targetNodeRing k)
          ((targetNodeRing k) ⊗[nodeRing k] FractionRing (nodeRing k)))
declarations.comment: unit Dedekind different

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.NodeExample.exists_dual_trace_iff_natCast_eq
declarations.doc:
**The chartwise form of the definedness of the different of [Stacks, Tag 0BWM].** The trace
element of the generic fibre comes from a section of the relative dualizing module
`ω_{B/A} = Hom_A(B, A)` exactly when the two branch degrees have the same image in `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dual_trace_iff_natCast_eq
    (n m : ℕ) (hn : IsUnit (n : k)) (hm : IsUnit (m : k))
    (f : nodeRing k →+* targetNodeRing k)
    (hx : f (x k) = u k ^ n) (hy : f (y k) = v k ^ m)
    (hk : ∀ a : k, f (algebraMap k (nodeRing k) a) = algebraMap k (targetNodeRing k) a) :
    letI : Algebra (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k) := f.toAlgebra
    ∀ setup : DedekindDifferentSetup (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k),
      letI : Algebra (FractionRing (nodeRing k))
          ((targetNodeRing k) ⊗[nodeRing k] FractionRing (nodeRing k)) :=
        Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
      ((∃ φ : Module.Dual (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k), ∀ b : targetNodeRing k,
            algebraMap (nodeRing k) (FractionRing (nodeRing k)) (φ b) =
              setup.trace (algebraMap (targetNodeRing k)
                ((targetNodeRing k) ⊗[nodeRing k] FractionRing (nodeRing k)) b)) ↔
        (n : k) = (m : k))
declarations.comment: definedness of the different, on the chart

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.NodeExample.dedekindDifferentIdeal_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**The chartwise form of the different of [Stacks, Tag 0BWM] being the unit ideal.** When the
two branch degrees have the same image in `k`, the Dedekind different ideal of `B` is the unit
ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem dedekindDifferentIdeal_eq_top
    (n m : ℕ) (hn : IsUnit (n : k)) (hm : IsUnit (m : k))
    (f : nodeRing k →+* targetNodeRing k)
    (hx : f (x k) = u k ^ n) (hy : f (y k) = v k ^ m)
    (hk : ∀ a : k, f (algebraMap k (nodeRing k) a) = algebraMap k (targetNodeRing k) a)
    (heq : (n : k) = (m : k)) :
    letI : Algebra (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k) := f.toAlgebra
    ∀ setup : DedekindDifferentSetup (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k),
      dedekindDifferentIdeal setup = ⊤
declarations.comment: the different is the unit ideal, on the chart

    (n m : ℕ) (hn : IsUnit (n : k)) (hm : IsUnit (m : k))

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.NodeExample.exists_dedekindDifferentSetup

theorem exists_dedekindDifferentSetup

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.NodeExample.trace_one
declarations.doc: The trace of one on the generic fibre is `(nx+my)/(x+y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem trace_one
    (n m : ℕ) (hn : IsUnit (n : k)) (hm : IsUnit (m : k))
    (f : nodeRing k →+* targetNodeRing k)
    (hx : f (x k) = u k ^ n) (hy : f (y k) = v k ^ m)
    (hk : ∀ a : k, f (algebraMap k (nodeRing k) a) = algebraMap k (targetNodeRing k) a) :
    letI : Algebra (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k) := f.toAlgebra
    ∀ setup : DedekindDifferentSetup (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k),
      setup.trace 1 *
        algebraMap (nodeRing k) (FractionRing (nodeRing k)) (x k + y k) =
        algebraMap (nodeRing k) (FractionRing (nodeRing k))
          ((algebraMap k (nodeRing k) (n : k)) * x k +
            (algebraMap k (nodeRing k) (m : k)) * y k)
declarations.comment: trace of one

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.NodeExample.trace_u_pow
declarations.doc: The trace vanishes on proper powers of the first branch coordinate.
declarations.statement:
theorem trace_u_pow
    (n m : ℕ) (hn : IsUnit (n : k)) (hm : IsUnit (m : k))
    (f : nodeRing k →+* targetNodeRing k)
    (hx : f (x k) = u k ^ n) (hy : f (y k) = v k ^ m)
    (hk : ∀ a : k, f (algebraMap k (nodeRing k) a) = algebraMap k (targetNodeRing k) a) :
    letI : Algebra (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k) := f.toAlgebra
    ∀ (setup : DedekindDifferentSetup (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k))
      (i : ℕ), 1 ≤ i → i < n →
        setup.trace (TensorProduct.tmul (nodeRing k) (u k ^ i) 1) = 0
declarations.comment: trace of u powers

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.NodeExample.trace_v_pow
declarations.doc: The trace vanishes on proper powers of the second branch coordinate.
declarations.statement:
theorem trace_v_pow
    (n m : ℕ) (hn : IsUnit (n : k)) (hm : IsUnit (m : k))
    (f : nodeRing k →+* targetNodeRing k)
    (hx : f (x k) = u k ^ n) (hy : f (y k) = v k ^ m)
    (hk : ∀ a : k, f (algebraMap k (nodeRing k) a) = algebraMap k (targetNodeRing k) a) :
    letI : Algebra (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k) := f.toAlgebra
    ∀ (setup : DedekindDifferentSetup (nodeRing k) (targetNodeRing k))
      (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → j < m →
        setup.trace (TensorProduct.tmul (nodeRing k) (v k ^ j) 1) = 0
declarations.comment: trace of v powers

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SheafHomAdj.prodHomEquivSheafHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BWQ, the bijection.** For sheaves of sets `F`, `G`, `H` on a site, maps
`F × G ⟶ H` are in canonical bijection with maps `F ⟶ SheafHom(G, H)`, where `SheafHom(G, H)` is
Mathlib's `sheafHom G H`, the sheaf `U ↦ Mor_{Sh(C/U)}(G|_{C/U}, H|_{C/U})`. It is the
hom-equivalence of the adjunction `- × G ⊣ SheafHom(G, -)`; the inverse is the source's formula
`(s, t) ↦ ψ(s)(t)` (`prodHomEquivSheafHom_symm_hom_app`), and the bijection is natural in all
three entries (`prodHomEquivSheafHom_natural`).
declarations.statement:
def prodHomEquivSheafHom (F G H : Sheaf J (Type u)) :
    (F ⨯ G ⟶ H) ≃ (F ⟶ sheafHom G H)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SheafHomAdj.prodHomEquivSheafHom_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BWQ, functoriality.** The bijection `prodHomEquivSheafHom` is functorial in all
three entries: in `F` (precomposition with `f × G`), in `G` (precomposition with `F × g` on the
left, `SheafHom(g, H)` on the right) and in `H` (postcomposition, `SheafHom(G, h)` on the
right).
declarations.statement:
theorem prodHomEquivSheafHom_natural :
    (∀ {F' F G H : Sheaf J (Type u)} (f : F' ⟶ F) (φ : F ⨯ G ⟶ H),
      prodHomEquivSheafHom F' G H (prod.map f (𝟙 G) ≫ φ) = f ≫ prodHomEquivSheafHom F G H φ) ∧
    (∀ {F G' G H : Sheaf J (Type u)} (g : G' ⟶ G) (φ : F ⨯ G ⟶ H),
      prodHomEquivSheafHom F G' H (prod.map (𝟙 F) g ≫ φ)
        = prodHomEquivSheafHom F G H φ ≫ sheafHomPrecomp g H) ∧
    (∀ {F G H H' : Sheaf J (Type u)} (h : H ⟶ H') (φ : F ⨯ G ⟶ H),
      prodHomEquivSheafHom F G H' (φ ≫ h) = prodHomEquivSheafHom F G H φ ≫ sheafHomMap G h)

declarations.name: length_quotient_span_pow_le_and_eq_of_mem_nonZeroDivisors
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BWS.** The quotients by powers of a parameter in a one-dimensional Noetherian
local ring have finite length. Their lengths grow at most linearly, and grow exactly linearly
when the parameter is a non-zero-divisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem length_quotient_span_pow_le_and_eq_of_mem_nonZeroDivisors
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (hdim : ringKrullDim R = 1) {x : R}
    (hx : x ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
    (hx_min : ∀ p ∈ minimalPrimes R, x ∉ p) :
    let P : ℕ → ℕ∞ := fun n ↦ Module.length R (R ⧸ Ideal.span {x ^ n})
    (∀ n, P n ≠ ⊤) ∧
      (∀ n, P n ≤ (n : ℕ∞) * P 1) ∧
      (x ∈ nonZeroDivisors R → ∀ n, P n = (n : ℕ∞) * P 1)

declarations.name: natCard_minimalPrimes_le_length_quotient_span_singleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BWT.** The number of minimal primes of a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring is
at most the length of its quotient by a parameter avoiding all minimal primes.
declarations.statement:
theorem natCard_minimalPrimes_le_length_quotient_span_singleton
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (hdim : ringKrullDim R = 1) {x : R}
    (hx : x ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
    (hx_min : ∀ p ∈ minimalPrimes R, x ∉ p) :
    Module.length R (R ⧸ Ideal.span {x}) ≠ ⊤ ∧
      (Nat.card (minimalPrimes R) : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.length R (R ⧸ Ideal.span {x})

declarations.name: exists_isSystemOfParameters_cons_of_avoids_minimalPrimes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BWU.** In a Noetherian local ring of dimension `d > 1`, an element `f` of
the maximal ideal which belongs to no minimal prime extends to a system of parameters
`f, g₁, ..., g_{d-1}`, with every `gᵢ` lying in the prescribed power `m ^ k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSystemOfParameters_cons_of_avoids_minimalPrimes
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (d : ℕ) (hdim : ringKrullDim R = d) (hd : 1 < d)
    (f : R) (hf : f ∈ maximalIdeal R)
    (hfmin : ∀ p ∈ minimalPrimes R, f ∉ p) (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ gs : List R,
      gs.length = d - 1 ∧
        (∀ g ∈ gs, g ∈ maximalIdeal R ^ k) ∧
          IsSystemOfParameters (f :: gs)

declarations.name: exists_isSystemOfParameters_pair_add_of_avoids_minimalPrimes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BWV.** In a two-dimensional Noetherian local ring, an element `f` of the maximal
ideal which belongs to no minimal prime can be completed by an element `g` to a system of
parameters. For every sufficiently high-order perturbation `f + h`, the pair `f + h, g` remains a
system of parameters and defines a quotient of the same length as the quotient defined by
`f, g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSystemOfParameters_pair_add_of_avoids_minimalPrimes
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (hdim : ringKrullDim R = 2) (f : R) (hf : f ∈ maximalIdeal R)
    (hfmin : ∀ p ∈ minimalPrimes R, f ∉ p) :
    ∃ g ∈ maximalIdeal R, ∃ N : ℕ,
      IsSystemOfParameters [f, g] ∧
        ∀ h ∈ maximalIdeal R ^ N,
          IsSystemOfParameters [f + h, g] ∧
            Module.length R (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList [f, g]) =
              Module.length R (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList [f + h, g])

declarations.name: multiplicity_le_length_quotient_of_isSystemOfParameters
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BWW.** If `I` is generated by a system of parameters and the leading coefficient
of its Hilbert–Samuel polynomial is `e / d!`, then `e ≤ length_R(R / I)`.

declarations.name: natCard_fullDimensionalMinimalPrimes_le_length_quotient_of_isSystemOfParameters
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BWX.** In a Noetherian local ring, the number of minimal primes whose quotient
has the full dimension of the ring is at most the length of the quotient by a system of
parameters.
declarations.statement:
theorem natCard_fullDimensionalMinimalPrimes_le_length_quotient_of_isSystemOfParameters
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    {gs : List R} (hgs : IsSystemOfParameters gs) :
    Module.length R (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList gs) ≠ ⊤ ∧
      (Nat.card {p : Ideal R // p ∈ minimalPrimes R ∧
        ringKrullDim (R ⧸ p) = ringKrullDim R} : ℕ∞) ≤
        Module.length R (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList gs)

declarations.name: exists_isSystemOfParameters_cons_stable_under_add_of_avoids_minimalPrimes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BWY.** A parameter in the maximal ideal of a Noetherian local ring which avoids all
minimal primes can be completed to a system of parameters such that perturbing the parameter by
an element of a sufficiently high power of the maximal ideal preserves both the parameter system
and the length of its quotient.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSystemOfParameters_cons_stable_under_add_of_avoids_minimalPrimes
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (d : ℕ) (hdim : ringKrullDim R = d)
    (f : R) (hf : f ∈ maximalIdeal R)
    (hfmin : ∀ p ∈ minimalPrimes R, f ∉ p) :
    ∃ gs : List R, ∃ N : ℕ,
      gs.length = d - 1 ∧
        (∀ g ∈ gs, g ∈ maximalIdeal R) ∧
          IsSystemOfParameters (f :: gs) ∧
            ∀ h ∈ maximalIdeal R ^ N,
              IsSystemOfParameters ((f + h) :: gs) ∧
                Module.length R (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList (f :: gs)) =
                  Module.length R (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList ((f + h) :: gs))

declarations.name: exists_nonzero_mem_isReduced_quotient_of_isRadical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BWZ.** A nonzero radical ideal in a catenary Noetherian local normal domain
contains a nonzero element whose principal quotient is reduced.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_nonzero_mem_isReduced_quotient_of_isRadical
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [IsIntegrallyClosed R] (hcat : Ring.IsCatenary R) (J : Ideal R) (hJ : J.IsRadical)
    (hJne : J ≠ ⊥) :
    ∃ f : R, f ≠ 0 ∧ f ∈ J ∧ IsReduced (R ⧸ Ideal.span {f})

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.ChainOfOpens.eq_bot_or_eq_top_or_eq_basicOpen
declarations.doc: **The opens of `Chain` are exactly `∅`, the whole space, and the sets `{i | i ≤ n}`.**
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_bot_or_eq_top_or_eq_basicOpen (W : Opens Chain.{u}) :
    W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤ ∨ ∃ n, W = basicOpen.{u} n
declarations.comment: the lattice of opens of the space: ∅, X and the U_n

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.ChainOfOpens.bijective_towerComparison_app
declarations.doc:
**An abelian sheaf on `Chain` is the same thing as an inverse system of abelian groups.**
The comparison map is bijective on sections over every open: the index sets of the basic opens
cover, so a section is determined by, and can be glued from, its restrictions to the basic
opens. In particular `Γ(X, ℱ) = lim ℱ(Uₙ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma bijective_towerComparison_app (W : (Opens Chain.{u})ᵒᵖ) :
    Function.Bijective ((towerComparison F).app W)
declarations.comment: an abelian sheaf on the space is the inverse system of its sections over the U_n; the clause `Γ(X, ℱ) = lim A_n` is globalSectionsAddEquiv

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.ChainOfOpens.globalSectionsAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**`Γ(X, ℱ) = lim ℱ(Uₙ)`.** Global sections of an abelian sheaf on `Chain` are the inverse
limit of its inverse system of sections over the basic opens.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def globalSectionsAddEquiv :
    F.obj.obj (op (⊤ : Opens Chain.{u})) ≃+ towerSections (sheafTower F) ⊤
declarations.comment: the clause `Γ(X, ℱ) = lim A_n` with `A_n = ℱ(U_n)`

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.ChainOfOpens.hasBasisOfCompactOpens_chain
declarations.doc:
**Condition (2) of [Stacks, Tag 02UX]**: `Chain` has a basis of quasi-compact opens, namely
the finite opens `{i | i ≤ n}`.
declarations.statement: lemma hasBasisOfCompactOpens_chain : PrespectralSpace Chain.{u}
declarations.comment: condition (2) of Tag 02UX: a basis of quasi-compact opens

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.ChainOfOpens.interCompactOpenIsCompact_chain
declarations.doc:
**Condition (3) of [Stacks, Tag 02UX]**: the intersection of two quasi-compact opens of
`Chain` is quasi-compact, both being finite.
declarations.statement: lemma interCompactOpenIsCompact_chain : QuasiSeparatedSpace Chain.{u}
declarations.comment: condition (3) of Tag 02UX: quasi-compact opens have quasi-compact intersections

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.ChainOfOpens.exists_not_subsingleton_sheafH_one
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BX0].** Let `X` be the natural numbers with the topology whose opens are
`∅`, `X` and `U_n = {i | i ≤ n}`. An abelian sheaf on `X` is an inverse system of abelian groups
`A_n = ℱ(U_n)` with `Γ(X, ℱ) = lim A_n`, and since `lim` is not exact on inverse systems there is
an abelian sheaf on `X` with nonzero `H¹` — even though `X` satisfies conditions (2) and (3) of
[Stacks, Tag 02UX] with `d = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_subsingleton_sheafH_one :
    ∃ F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology Chain.{u}) AddCommGrpCat.{u},
      ¬ Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u, u, u, u} F 1)
declarations.comment: the existence of an abelian sheaf with nonzero H¹; the lattice of opens, the identification of abelian sheaves with inverse systems and conditions (2) and (3) of Tag 02UX are given by eq_bot_or_eq_top_or_eq_basicOpen, bijective_towerComparison_app, globalSectionsAddEquiv, hasBasisOfCompactOpens_chain and interCompactOpenIsCompact_chain; condition (4), the vanishing H^p(X, j_!ℤ_U) = 0 for p ≥ 1, which the source leaves to the reader, is subsingleton_sheafH_integerExtensionByZero, proved through the identification j_!ℤ_{U n} = 𝒦ₙ of integerExtensionByZeroIsoKernel

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.ChainOfOpens.subsingleton_sheafH_integerExtensionByZero
declarations.doc:
**Condition (4) of [Stacks, Tag 02UX] over `Chain`**: the vanishing `Hᵖ(X, j_!ℤ_U) = 0` for
every `p > 0` and every quasi-compact open `U` of `Chain`.  The quasi-compact opens are `∅` and
the `U n`, the whole space not being quasi-compact; over `∅` the sheaf is zero, and over `U n` the
extension by zero is the kernel `𝒦ₙ` of the reduction of the constant sheaf `ℤ` onto the sheaf of
`cotruncTower n`, whose higher cohomology vanishes.

This is the condition the source leaves to the reader.  Together with
`hasBasisOfCompactOpens_chain` and `interCompactOpenIsCompact_chain` it makes `Chain` satisfy
conditions (2), (3) and (4) of [Stacks, Tag 02UX] with `d = 0`, while
`exists_not_subsingleton_sheafH_one` denies the conclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafH_integerExtensionByZero
    (U : Opens Chain.{u}) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set Chain.{u})) (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u, u, u, u}
      (Stacks.Sheaves.ConstantIntegerSubsheaves.integerExtensionByZero chainSpace.{u} U) p)
declarations.comment: condition (4) of Tag 02UX for this space, which the source leaves to the reader: H^p(X, j_!ℤ_U) = 0 for every p > 0 and every quasi-compact open U

declarations.name: exists_injective_localizationAwayToAtPrime_of_isDomain
declarations.doc:
Case (1): `R` an integral domain. There exists `f ∉ p` such that the
canonical map `R_f → R_p` is injective. (One may take `f = 1`.)
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_injective_localizationAwayToAtPrime_of_isDomain
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    ∃ f : R, ∃ hf : f ∉ p, Function.Injective (localizationAwayToAtPrime f p hf)

declarations.name: exists_injective_localizationAwayToAtPrime_of_isNoetherianRing
declarations.doc:
Case (2): `R` Noetherian. There exists `f ∉ p` such that the canonical
map `R_f → R_p` is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_injective_localizationAwayToAtPrime_of_isNoetherianRing
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    ∃ f : R, ∃ hf : f ∉ p, Function.Injective (localizationAwayToAtPrime f p hf)

declarations.name: exists_injective_localizationAwayToAtPrime_of_isReduced_finite_minimalPrimes
declarations.doc:
Case (3): `R` reduced with finitely many minimal primes not contained in `p`.
There exists `f ∉ p` such that the canonical map `R_f → R_p` is injective.

The hypothesis is weaker than the `(minimalPrimes R).Finite` of 0BX1 (3), which
implies it by `Set.Finite.subset _ (Set.sep_subset _ _)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_injective_localizationAwayToAtPrime_of_isReduced_finite_minimalPrimes
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsReduced R] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (hfin : {q ∈ minimalPrimes R | ¬ q ≤ p}.Finite) :
    ∃ f : R, ∃ hf : f ∉ p, Function.Injective (localizationAwayToAtPrime f p hf)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRegular_of_isNormal_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_one
declarations.doc: A locally Noetherian normal scheme of dimension at most one is regular.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpen_germ_injective_of_isIntegral
declarations.doc:
On an integral scheme, every point admits an affine open neighbourhood whose canonical
map from its ring of sections to the local ring at the point is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_germ_injective_of_isIntegral (X : Scheme.{u}) (x : X)
    [IsIntegral X] :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ U),
      IsAffineOpen U ∧ Function.Injective (X.presheaf.germ U x hx)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpen_germ_injective_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
On a locally Noetherian scheme, every point admits an affine open neighbourhood whose
canonical map from its ring of sections to the local ring at the point is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_germ_injective_of_isLocallyNoetherian (X : Scheme.{u}) (x : X)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ U),
      IsAffineOpen U ∧ Function.Injective (X.presheaf.germ U x hx)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpen_germ_injective_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
On a reduced scheme with finitely many irreducible components, every point admits an
affine open neighbourhood whose canonical map from its ring of sections to the local ring at
the point is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_germ_injective_of_isReduced (X : Scheme.{u}) (x : X)
    [IsReduced X] (hX : (irreducibleComponents X).Finite) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ U),
      IsAffineOpen U ∧ Function.Injective (X.presheaf.germ U x hx)
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_morphism_inducing_localHom_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
A compatible local homomorphism is induced by a morphism on an open neighbourhood when the
target is locally of finite type and the source is reduced with finitely many irreducible
components.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_open_morphism_inducing_localHom_of_isReduced
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ S) (pY : Y ⟶ S)
    (s : S) (x : X) (y : Y) (hx : pX x = s) (hy : pY y = s)
    (phi : Y.presheaf.stalk y →+* X.presheaf.stalk x)
    (hphi : IsLocalHom phi)
    (hphiS : phi.comp
        ((pY.stalkMap y).hom.comp
          (eqToHom (congrArg (fun z ↦ S.presheaf.stalk z) hy).symm).hom) =
      (pX.stalkMap x).hom.comp
        (eqToHom (congrArg (fun z ↦ S.presheaf.stalk z) hx).symm).hom)
    (hft : LocallyOfFiniteType pY) (hred : IsReduced X)
    (hcomp : (irreducibleComponents X).Finite) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (hxU : x ∈ U) (f : (U : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ Y)
      (_hf : f ≫ pY = U.ι ≫ pX)
      (hfy : f ⟨x, hxU⟩ = y),
      ((U.stalkIso ⟨x, hxU⟩).hom.hom.comp
          ((f.stalkMap ⟨x, hxU⟩).hom.comp
            (eqToHom (congrArg (fun z ↦ Y.presheaf.stalk z) hfy).symm).hom)) = phi
declarations.comment: local_extension

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_morphism_inducing_localHom_of_isIntegral
declarations.doc:
A compatible local homomorphism is induced by a morphism on an open neighbourhood when the
target is locally of finite type over the base and the source is integral.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_open_morphism_inducing_localHom_of_isIntegral
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ S) (pY : Y ⟶ S)
    (s : S) (x : X) (y : Y) (hx : pX x = s) (hy : pY y = s)
    (phi : Y.presheaf.stalk y →+* X.presheaf.stalk x)
    (hphi : IsLocalHom phi)
    (hphiS : phi.comp
        ((pY.stalkMap y).hom.comp
          (eqToHom (congrArg (fun z ↦ S.presheaf.stalk z) hy).symm).hom) =
      (pX.stalkMap x).hom.comp
        (eqToHom (congrArg (fun z ↦ S.presheaf.stalk z) hx).symm).hom)
    (hft : LocallyOfFiniteType pY) (hint : IsIntegral X) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (hxU : x ∈ U) (f : (U : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ Y)
      (_hf : f ≫ pY = U.ι ≫ pX)
      (hfy : f ⟨x, hxU⟩ = y),
      ((U.stalkIso ⟨x, hxU⟩).hom.hom.comp
          ((f.stalkMap ⟨x, hxU⟩).hom.comp
            (eqToHom (congrArg (fun z ↦ Y.presheaf.stalk z) hfy).symm).hom)) = phi
declarations.comment: local_extension, Y locally of finite type and X integral

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_morphism_inducing_localHom_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
A compatible local homomorphism is induced by a morphism on an open neighbourhood when the
target is locally of finite type over the base and the source is locally Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_open_morphism_inducing_localHom_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ S) (pY : Y ⟶ S)
    (s : S) (x : X) (y : Y) (hx : pX x = s) (hy : pY y = s)
    (phi : Y.presheaf.stalk y →+* X.presheaf.stalk x)
    (hphi : IsLocalHom phi)
    (hphiS : phi.comp
        ((pY.stalkMap y).hom.comp
          (eqToHom (congrArg (fun z ↦ S.presheaf.stalk z) hy).symm).hom) =
      (pX.stalkMap x).hom.comp
        (eqToHom (congrArg (fun z ↦ S.presheaf.stalk z) hx).symm).hom)
    (hft : LocallyOfFiniteType pY) (hnoeth : IsLocallyNoetherian X) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (hxU : x ∈ U) (f : (U : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ Y)
      (_hf : f ≫ pY = U.ι ≫ pX)
      (hfy : f ⟨x, hxU⟩ = y),
      ((U.stalkIso ⟨x, hxU⟩).hom.hom.comp
          ((f.stalkMap ⟨x, hxU⟩).hom.comp
            (eqToHom (congrArg (fun z ↦ Y.presheaf.stalk z) hfy).symm).hom)) = phi
declarations.comment: local_extension, Y locally of finite type and X locally Noetherian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_morphism_inducing_localHom_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BX6 (local extension), finite-presentation case.** A compatible
local homomorphism of local rings is induced by a morphism on an open neighbourhood.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_open_morphism_inducing_localHom_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ S) (pY : Y ⟶ S)
    (s : S) (x : X) (y : Y) (hx : pX x = s) (hy : pY y = s)
    (phi : Y.presheaf.stalk y →+* X.presheaf.stalk x)
    (hphi : IsLocalHom phi)
    (hphiS : phi.comp
        ((pY.stalkMap y).hom.comp
          (eqToHom (congrArg (fun z ↦ S.presheaf.stalk z) hy).symm).hom) =
      (pX.stalkMap x).hom.comp
        (eqToHom (congrArg (fun z ↦ S.presheaf.stalk z) hx).symm).hom)
    (hfin : LocallyOfFinitePresentation pY) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (hxU : x ∈ U) (f : (U : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ Y)
      (_hf : f ≫ pY = U.ι ≫ pX)
      (hfy : f ⟨x, hxU⟩ = y),
      ((U.stalkIso ⟨x, hxU⟩).hom.hom.comp
          ((f.stalkMap ⟨x, hxU⟩).hom.comp
            (eqToHom (congrArg (fun z ↦ Y.presheaf.stalk z) hfy).symm).hom)) = phi
declarations.comment: local_extension

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_eq_of_stalkMap_eq
declarations.doc:
Two morphisms over a scheme which agree on the local ring at a point agree on some open
neighbourhood of that point, provided the target is locally of finite type over the base, or
the source is integral, locally Noetherian, or reduced with finitely many irreducible
components.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_open_eq_of_stalkMap_eq
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ S) (pY : Y ⟶ S) (f g : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : f ≫ pY = pX) (hg : g ≫ pY = pX)
    (s : S) (x : X) (y : Y) (hxs : pX x = s) (hys : pY y = s)
    (hfx : f x = y) (hgx : g x = y)
    (hfg : f.stalkMap x =
      Y.presheaf.stalkSpecializes
        (Inseparable.of_eq (hfx.trans hgx.symm).symm).specializes ≫ g.stalkMap x)
    (h : LocallyOfFiniteType pY ∨ IsIntegral X ∨ IsLocallyNoetherian X ∨
      (IsReduced X ∧ (irreducibleComponents X).Finite)) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ U.ι ≫ f = U.ι ≫ g
declarations.comment: local_uniqueness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_extension_of_valuationRing_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BX7.** A morphism from an open subscheme extends across a point
whose local ring is a valuation ring, provided the target is proper over the base and the
source is either reduced with finitely many irreducible components or Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_open_extension_of_valuationRing_stalk
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ S) (pY : Y ⟶ S)
    (x : X) (U : X.Opens) (f : (U : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ Y)
    (hf : f ≫ pY = U.ι ≫ pX)
    (hxU : x ∈ closure (U : Set X))
    (hX : (IsReduced X ∧ (irreducibleComponents X).Finite) ∨
      IsNoetherian X)
    [IsDomain (X.presheaf.stalk x)] [ValuationRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)]
    [IsProper pY] :
    ∃ (U' : X.Opens) (hUU' : U ≤ U') (_ : x ∈ U')
      (f' : (U' : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ Y),
      f' ≫ pY = U'.ι ≫ pX ∧ X.homOfLE hUU' ≫ f' = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GenericPointMapContext.bijective_genericPointMapForRationalMaps_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
When the target is locally of finite presentation over the base, every
compatible collection of points and local maps at the generic points comes
from a unique rational map over the base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_genericPointMapForRationalMaps_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation

declarations.comment: finite_presentation_bijectivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GenericPointMapContext.genericPointMapForRationalMaps_injective
declarations.doc:
A rational map over the base is determined by its values and induced local
maps at the generic points of the irreducible components when the target is
locally of finite type over the base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem genericPointMapForRationalMaps_injective
    (C : GenericPointMapContext.{u}) [LocallyOfFiniteType C.toBaseTarget] :

declarations.comment: injectivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GenericPointMapContext.bijective_genericPointMapForRationalMaps_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
For a reduced source and a target locally of finite type over the base,
rational maps over the base are determined by, and realize, arbitrary
compatible local data at the generic points of the source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_genericPointMapForRationalMaps_of_isReduced
    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.toBaseTarget] [IsReduced C.X] :

declarations.comment: reduced_source_bijectivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.normalization_fromNormalization_isIso
declarations.doc:
The normalization of `f.normalization` in `X` is canonically isomorphic to
`f.normalization`.
declarations.statement:
instance normalization_fromNormalization_isIso :
    IsIso (f.toNormalization.fromNormalization)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isDiscreteValuationRing_stalk_normalization_of_isEmpty_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BXB.** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be of finite type with `Y` reduced and `X`
Nagata, and let `X'` be the normalization of `X` in `Y`. If the local ring of `X'` at a point `x'`
has Krull dimension one and the fibre of `Y ⟶ X'` over `x'` is empty, then that local ring is a
discrete valuation ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDiscreteValuationRing_stalk_normalization_of_isEmpty_fiber {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : Y ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsReduced Y] (hX : IsNagataScheme X) :
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian X :=
      ((isNagataScheme_iff_isLocallyNoetherian_and_isUniversallyJapaneseScheme X).mp hX).1
    ∀ x' : f.normalization,
      ringKrullDim (f.normalization.presheaf.stalk x') = 1 →
      IsEmpty (f.toNormalization.fiber x') →
      ∃ _ : IsDomain (f.normalization.presheaf.stalk x'),
        IsDiscreteValuationRing (f.normalization.presheaf.stalk x')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isBirational_normalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BXC.** The normalization morphism of a reduced scheme whose
quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible components is birational.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBirational_normalization
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    IsBirational (X.normalization hX)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjSerreCorrespondence.equivalence_coherentQuotientFunctor
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a graded ring such that `A₀` is Noetherian and `A` is generated by finitely many
elements of `A₁` over `A₀`, and set `X = Proj A`. Then `M ↦ M̃` induces an equivalence

`Mod^fg_A / Mod^fg_{A, torsion} ⟶ Coh(𝒪_X)`

whose quasi-inverse is `ℱ ↦ ⨁_{n ≥ 0} Γ(X, ℱ(n))`.

The third clause is what says the equivalence is *induced* by `M ↦ M̃`: composed with the quotient
functor and read in all sheaves of `𝒪_X`-modules, its functor is the associated-sheaf functor on
`Mod^fg_A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem equivalence_coherentQuotientFunctor :
    haveI := isNoetherianRing_of_adjoin_range 𝒜 x hx hgen
    haveI := finiteType_of_adjoin_range 𝒜 x hx hgen
    haveI : CompactSpace (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj 𝒜) :=
      QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.toSpecZero 𝒜)
    ∃ e : IrrelevantQuotient.{u, u, u} 𝒜 (d := 1) Nat.one_pos ≌
            Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules (projRingSheaf 𝒜),
      e.functor = coherentQuotientFunctor.{u, u} 𝒜 ∧
      e.inverse = nonnegTwistedSectionsQuotientFunctor 𝒜 x hx hgen ∧
      Nonempty (toIrrelevantQuotient.{u, u, u} 𝒜 Nat.one_pos ⋙ e.functor ⋙
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules (projRingSheaf 𝒜)).ι ≅
          finiteAssociatedSheafFunctor.{u, u} 𝒜)
declarations.comment: the equivalence Mod^fg_A / Mod^fg_{A,torsion} ⟶ Coh(O_X) induced by M ↦ M~, with quasi-inverse F ↦ ⨁_{n ≥ 0} Γ(X, F(n)), at the source's hypotheses: A_0 Noetherian and A generated by finitely many elements of A_1 over A_0. The torsion subcategory is the irrelevant finitely generated graded modules in generation degree one, which for a Noetherian A generated in degree one is the source's Mod^fg_{A,torsion}. The Noetherianity of A, its finite type over A_0 and the quasi-compactness of Proj A are derived from those hypotheses rather than assumed, which is why the statement opens with haveI. The equality clauses pin the functor to M ↦ M~ and the inverse to F ↦ ⨁_{n ≥ 0} Γ(X, F(n)) on the nose, and the last clause says the functor is induced by M ↦ M~

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjSerreCorrespondence.isZero_associatedModuleSheaf_of_isIPowerTorsion
declarations.doc: The associated sheaf `M̃` of an `𝒜₊`-power torsion graded module `M` is a zero object.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_associatedModuleSheaf_of_isIPowerTorsion
    (htor : IsIPowerTorsion S M (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal) :
    Limits.IsZero (associatedModuleSheaf 𝒜 𝒨)
declarations.comment: the functor M ↦ M~ kills the torsion modules, the step that lets it be defined on the quotient category; stated for 𝒜₊-power torsion modules, with no finiteness, Noetherian or degree-one generation hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjSerreCorrespondence.isZero_associatedModuleSheaf_of_eventually_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
A graded module whose homogeneous components vanish in all sufficiently large degrees has zero
associated sheaf.
declarations.comment: the functor M ↦ M~ kills the torsion subcategory, with torsion in the form the source defines the subcategory Mod^fg_{A,torsion}: the homogeneous components vanish in all large degrees; no finiteness hypothesis is used

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjSerreCorrespondence.isZero_associatedModuleSheafFunctor_obj
declarations.doc:
The associated-sheaf functor `M ↦ M̃` sends an `𝒜₊`-power torsion graded module to a zero
object.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_associatedModuleSheafFunctor_obj (X : GradedModuleCat.{u, v, w} 𝒜)
    (htor : IsIPowerTorsion S X.carrier (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal) :
    Limits.IsZero ((associatedModuleSheafFunctor 𝒜).obj X)
declarations.comment: the bundled functor M ↦ M~ sends torsion graded modules to zero objects, the step that lets it be defined on the quotient category

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjSerreCorrespondence.exists_coherentIrrelevantQuotientEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BXF].** Let `A` be a Noetherian graded ring and `X = Proj(A)`. There is a
degree `d` of the kind [Stacks, Tag 0BXE] asks for — the least common multiple of the degrees of a
finite homogeneous generating set of `A` over `A₀` — and for it the functor `M ↦ M̃` induces an
**equivalence**

`Mod^fg_A / Mod^fg_{A, irrelevant} ⟶ Coh(𝒪_X)`

whose quasi-inverse is `ℱ ↦ ⨁_{n ≥ 0} Γ(X, ℱ(n))`.

The two equations say that the equivalence *is* the proposition's two functors: its `functor` is
`coherentIrrelevantQuotientFunctor`, the arrow induced by `M ↦ M̃` on the quotient category, and
its `inverse` is `coherentTruncatedTwistedSectionsFunctor 𝒮 0` followed by the quotient functor,
which is `ℱ ↦ ⨁_{n ≥ 0} Γ(X, ℱ(n))`.

The degree cannot be quantified away: for `A = k[x]` with `deg x = 2` the module `A(1)` has
vanishing associated sheaf and is not irrelevant at `d = 1`, so the subcategory of [Stacks, Tag
0BXE], and with it the quotient category, genuinely depends on `d` being a multiple of the
generators' degrees. `coherentIrrelevantQuotientEquivalence` is the same statement for every such
`d`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_coherentIrrelevantQuotientEquivalence :
    ∃ (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (e : IrrelevantQuotient 𝒮 hd ≌
        _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules (projRingSheaf 𝒮)),
      e.functor = coherentIrrelevantQuotientFunctor.{u, u} 𝒮 hd ∧
        e.inverse = coherentTruncatedTwistedSectionsFunctor.{u} 𝒮 0 ⋙
          toIrrelevantQuotient.{u, u, u} 𝒮 hd
declarations.comment: the proposition: for A a Noetherian graded ring and X = Proj(A), the functor M ↦ M~ induces an equivalence Mod^fg_A / Mod^fg_{A, irrelevant} ⟶ Coh(O_X) whose quasi-inverse is F ↦ ⨁_{n ≥ 0} Γ(X, F(n)). The degree d of Tag 0BXE, the lcm of the degrees of a finite homogeneous generating set of A over A_0, is produced here as the source produces it; the same statement for an arbitrary d divisible by those degrees is coherentIrrelevantQuotientEquivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjSerreCorrespondence.irrelevantModules_prop_of_exact
declarations.doc:
The irrelevant finitely generated graded modules satisfy the Serre-subcategory condition of
Stacks 02MO inside `Mod^{fg}_A`: they contain every zero module, and they contain the middle term
of every exact sequence whose outer terms belong to them.
declarations.statement:
public theorem irrelevantModules_prop_of_exact {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d)
    (M₀ : FiniteGradedModules.{u, v, w} 𝒮) (h₀ : Subsingleton M₀.obj.carrier) :
    irrelevantModules 𝒮 d M₀ ∧
      ∀ (L N P : FiniteGradedModules.{u, v, w} 𝒮) (f : L ⟶ N) (g : N ⟶ P),
        (∀ y : N.obj.carrier, g.hom.toLinearMap y = 0 →
          ∃ x : L.obj.carrier, f.hom.toLinearMap x = y) →
        irrelevantModules 𝒮 d L → irrelevantModules 𝒮 d P → irrelevantModules 𝒮 d N
declarations.comment: only the step that the irrelevant finite graded modules satisfy the Serre-subcategory condition of Tag 02MO, which is what makes the quotient category in the statement exist; the equivalence with Coh(O_X) and its twisted-section quasi-inverse are not formalized, and exactness is spelled elementwise because this library's category of graded modules has no abelian structure yet

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjSerreCorrespondence.irrelevantQuotientFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The functor `Mod^fg_A / Mod^fg_{A, irrelevant} ⟶ Mod(𝒪_X)` induced by `M ↦ M̃`.** This is
the functor of which Stacks 0BXF asserts that it is an equivalence onto `Coh(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.comment: the arrow of the proposition: the functor out of the quotient category Mod^fg_A / Mod^fg_{A, irrelevant} induced by M ↦ M~, obtained by factoring that functor's restriction to the finitely generated graded modules through the localization at the isomorphisms modulo the irrelevant ones. Its target is written as all sheaves of O_X-modules; its corestriction to the proposition's own target Coh(O_X) is coherentIrrelevantQuotientFunctor. Of the proposition's assertion that this functor is an equivalence, faithfulness is proved (faithful_irrelevantQuotientFunctor), for the corestriction too (faithful_coherentIrrelevantQuotientFunctor); the whole proposition is now proved, as exists_coherentIrrelevantQuotientEquivalence of CoherentEquivalence.lean. The quasi-inverse F ↦ ⨁_{n ≥ 0} Γ(X, F(n)) is identified on objects, by truncatedTwistedSectionsIsoOfNoetherian, and assembled into a functor to all graded modules, truncatedTwistedSectionsFunctor

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjSerreCorrespondence.isSerreClass_irrelevantModules
declarations.doc:
The irrelevant finitely generated graded modules (Tag 0BXE) are a Serre class in `Mod^fg_A`:
the subcategory contains a zero object and is closed under subobjects, quotients and
extensions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSerreClass_irrelevantModules (hd : 0 < d) :
    ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass (irrelevantModules.{u, v, w} 𝒮 d)
declarations.comment: the Serre-subcategory step of the proposition: the irrelevant finitely generated graded modules are a Serre class in Mod^fg_A, which is what makes the quotient category on the left of the arrow exist, and which this file turns into that quotient category. The equivalence with Coh(O_X) and the identification of its quasi-inverse with F ↦ ⨁_{n ≥ 0} Γ(X, F(n)) are exists_coherentIrrelevantQuotientEquivalence of CoherentEquivalence.lean

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCohenMacaulay_iff_hasNoEmbeddedPoints_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_one
declarations.doc:
A locally Noetherian scheme of dimension at most one is Cohen--Macaulay if and only if it
has no embedded points.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCohenMacaulay_iff_hasNoEmbeddedPoints_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_one
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (hX : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) :
    IsCohenMacaulay X ↔ HasNoEmbeddedPoints X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_codimension_one
declarations.doc:
A codimension-one closed subscheme with no embedded points is an effective Cartier
divisor when the ambient local rings along it are UFDs, or the ambient scheme is regular.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_codimension_one
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hno : HasNoEmbeddedPoints I.subscheme)
    (hcodim : ∀ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents I.subscheme,
      ∀ x : I.subscheme, IsGenericPoint x Z →
        codimension (IrreducibleCloseds.closureSingleton (I.subschemeι x)) = 1)
    (hlocal : (∀ x : X, x ∈ I.support →
      UniqueFactorizationMonoid (X.presheaf.stalk x)) ∨ IsRegular X) :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I

declarations.name: Ideal.isPrincipal_of_noEmbeddedAssociatedPrimes_of_minimalPrimes_height_eq_one
declarations.doc: An ideal of pure height one with no embedded primes in a Noetherian UFD is principal.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPrincipal_of_noEmbeddedAssociatedPrimes_of_minimalPrimes_height_eq_one
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [UniqueFactorizationMonoid R] (I : Ideal R)
    (hI : HasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPrimes (R ⧸ I) (R ⧸ I))
    (hheight : ∀ p ∈ I.minimalPrimes, p.height = 1) :
    I.IsPrincipal

declarations.name: Stacks.PicardUFD.twistPicardHom_injective
declarations.doc:
**The homomorphism `ℤ ⟶ Pic(ℙⁿ_R)`, `m ↦ 𝒪(m)`, is injective** for `R` a domain and
`0 < n`. A trivialization of `𝒪(m)` makes the transition unit `(T₀ / T₁) ^ m` a ratio of
constants, which at the generic point reads `T₀^{m⁺} T₁^{m⁻} · s = r · T₀^{m⁻} T₁^{m⁺}` and
forces `m⁺ = m⁻`, hence `m = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem twistPicardHom_injective [IsDomain R] (hn : 0 < n) :
    Function.Injective (twistPicardHom R n)
declarations.comment: injectivity of m ↦ 𝒪(m), for 0 < n; the source states no restriction, but at n = 0 the map is the zero map into the trivial Picard group of ℙ⁰_R ≅ Spec R and is not injective

declarations.name: Stacks.PicardUFD.twistPicardHom_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BXJ.** The homomorphism `ℤ ⟶ Pic(ℙ¹_R)`, `m ↦ 𝒪(m)`, is surjective for
`R` a unique factorization domain: every invertible module on the projective line is a twist.
declarations.statement:
theorem twistPicardHom_surjective [IsDomain R] [UniqueFactorizationMonoid R] :
    Function.Surjective (twistPicardHom R 1)
declarations.comment: surjectivity of m ↦ 𝒪(m) for the projective line, i.e. for n = 1

declarations.name: Stacks.PicardUFD.twistPicardHom_surjective_general
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BXJ.** The homomorphism `ℤ ⟶ Pic(ℙⁿ_R)`, `m ↦ 𝒪(m)`, is surjective
for `R` a unique factorization domain and every `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem twistPicardHom_surjective_general :
    Function.Surjective (twistPicardHom R n)
declarations.comment: surjectivity of m ↦ 𝒪(m), for every n

declarations.name: Stacks.PicardUFD.twistPicardAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BXJ.** The Picard group of `ℙⁿ_R` is `ℤ` for `R` a unique
factorization domain and `0 < n`, the isomorphism sending `m` to the class of `𝒪(m)`.
declarations.comment: the isomorphism ℤ ≃+ Pic(ℙⁿ_R) carrying m to the class of 𝒪(m), for 0 < n

declarations.name: Stacks.PicardUFD.not_injective_twistPicardHom_dim_zero
declarations.doc:
**The boundary case of Tag 0BXJ.** The source states no restriction on `n`, but at `n = 0`
the Picard group of `ℙ⁰_R` is trivial, so `m ↦ 𝒪(m)` is the zero map and is not injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_injective_twistPicardHom_dim_zero :
    ¬ Function.Injective (twistPicardHom R 0)
declarations.comment: the n = 0 boundary case: m ↦ 𝒪(m) is the zero map into the trivial group Pic(ℙ⁰_R) and is not injective, so the unrestricted source statement fails there

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedSubschemeProjQuotient.projQuotientIso
declarations.doc:
**The isomorphism `Z ≅ Proj (𝒮 / I(Z))`.** It is the lift of `i` through the closed immersion
`Stacks.ClosedSubschemeProjQuotient.ambientHom`, which is invertible because the two closed
subschemes have the same ideal sheaf.
declarations.statement:
def projQuotientIso [CompactSpace (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj 𝒮)]
    {Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Proj 𝒮) [IsClosedImmersion i] :
    Z ≅ projQuotient 𝒮 i
declarations.comment: the first assertion: for `X = Proj 𝒮` quasi-compact, every closed subscheme `Z ⊆ X` has the form `V₊(I(Z))`

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedSubschemeProjQuotient.projQuotientIso_hom_comp_ambientHom
declarations.doc:
**The isomorphism is canonical**: it is compatible with the two morphisms to `Proj 𝒮`, so it
is an equality of closed subschemes of `Proj 𝒮` and not merely an abstract isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem projQuotientIso_hom_comp_ambientHom [CompactSpace (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj 𝒮)]
    {Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Proj 𝒮) [IsClosedImmersion i] :
    (projQuotientIso 𝒮 i).hom ≫ ambientHom 𝒮 i = i
declarations.comment: the first assertion: the identification `Z = V₊(I(Z))` is one of closed subschemes of `X = Proj 𝒮`, not merely an abstract isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.mem_idealOfClosedSubscheme_iff
declarations.doc:
An element of `S` lies in the ideal of a closed subscheme `Z ⊆ Proj 𝒮` exactly when, for
every `n`, the section of `𝒪(n)` attached to its degree-`n` homogeneous component pulls back to
zero on `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_idealOfClosedSubscheme_iff {Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Proj 𝒮)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (a : S) :
    a ∈ idealOfClosedSubscheme 𝒮 i ↔
      ∀ n : ℕ, pullbackGlobalSections i (twistingSheaf 𝒮 (n : ℤ))
        (degreeSection 𝒮 n (DirectSum.decompose 𝒮 a n)) = 0
declarations.comment: ideal_of_a_closed_subscheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.idealOfClosedSubscheme
declarations.doc:
The ideal of a closed subscheme of `Proj 𝒮`, generated by the homogeneous elements whose
canonical twisted sections vanish after pullback to the subscheme.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def idealOfClosedSubscheme {Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (i : Z ⟶ Proj 𝒮) [IsClosedImmersion i] : Ideal S
declarations.comment: ideal_of_a_closed_subscheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.idealOfClosedSubscheme_isHomogeneous
declarations.doc: The ideal of a closed subscheme is homogeneous: it is generated by homogeneous elements.
declarations.statement:
theorem idealOfClosedSubscheme_isHomogeneous {Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Proj 𝒮)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] :
    (idealOfClosedSubscheme 𝒮 i).IsHomogeneous 𝒮
declarations.comment: ideal_of_a_closed_subscheme

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealOfClosedSubscheme.idealOfClosedSubscheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BXK.** The homogeneous ideal of a closed subscheme of `Proj 𝒮`, generated by the
homogeneous elements whose canonical twisted global section pulls back to zero on the
subscheme.
declarations.statement:
public def idealOfClosedSubscheme {Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Proj 𝒮) [IsClosedImmersion i] :
    Ideal S
declarations.comment: ideal_of_a_closed_subscheme

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealOfClosedSubscheme.mem_idealOfClosedSubscheme_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BXK.** An element lies in the ideal of `Z` exactly when the section attached to
each of its homogeneous components pulls back to zero on `Z`.

In particular the span of the homogeneous equations is the kernel of the canonical graded map
to the twisted global sections, in every degree and also on inhomogeneous elements.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mem_idealOfClosedSubscheme_iff {Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Proj 𝒮)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (a : S) :
    a ∈ idealOfClosedSubscheme 𝒮 i ↔
      ∀ n : ℕ, pullbackGlobalSections i (twistingSheaf 𝒮 (n : ℤ))
        (degreeSection 𝒮 n ((DirectSum.decompose 𝒮 a) n)) = 0
declarations.comment: ideal_of_a_closed_subscheme

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealOfClosedSubscheme.idealOfClosedSubscheme_isHomogeneous
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0BXK.** The ideal of a closed subscheme is homogeneous.
declarations.statement:
public theorem idealOfClosedSubscheme_isHomogeneous {Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Proj 𝒮)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] : (idealOfClosedSubscheme 𝒮 i).IsHomogeneous 𝒮
declarations.comment: ideal_of_a_closed_subscheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.forall_degreeSection_quotientGradingMk_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BXK for a graded ring that is not generated in degree one: the ideal of equations of
`V₊(I)` is the set of elements that `𝒮 (n · d)` carries into `I` for every `n ≫ 0`**, where `d` is
the least common multiple of the degrees of a finite family of homogeneous generators of `S` over
`𝒮 0`:

`I(V₊(I)) = {x ∈ A | A_{nd} x ⊆ I for all n ≫ 0}`.

An element lies in `I(V₊(I)) = Ker(A ⟶ ⨁_{n ≥ 0} Γ(V₊(I), 𝒪_{V₊(I)}(n)))` exactly when the
twisted section attached to the class of each of its homogeneous components vanishes on
`V₊(I) = Proj (𝒮 ⧸ I)`; both sides of the formula are degreewise conditions, and the finitely
many components are matched by taking the largest of their exponents.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_degreeSection_quotientGradingMk_eq_zero_iff [IsNoetherianRing S] {ι : Type*}
    [Fintype ι] (g : ι → S) (e : ι → ℕ) (he : ∀ j, 0 < e j) (hg : ∀ j, g j ∈ 𝒮 (e j))
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin (𝒮 0) (Set.range g) = ⊤) (x : S) :
    (∀ n : ℕ, degreeSection (quotientGrading I) n
        (quotientGradingMk I n (decompose 𝒮 x n)) = 0) ↔
      ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, N ≤ m →
        ∀ y : S, y ∈ 𝒮 (m * Finset.univ.lcm e) → y * x ∈ I.toIdeal
declarations.comment: for `d` the lcm of the degrees of generators of `A` over `A_0`, `I(V_+(I)) = {x ∈ A | A_{nd} x ⊂ I for all n ≫ 0}`; `𝒪_{V_+(I)}(n)` is the twisting sheaf of `V_+(I) = Proj(A/I)`, the reading in which the source derives this from Cohomology of Schemes tag 0BXF applied to `A/I`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.setOf_forall_degreeSection_quotientGradingMk_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**The same, as the equality of sets the source displays:**

`I(V₊(I)) = {x ∈ A | A_{nd} x ⊂ I for all n ≫ 0}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem setOf_forall_degreeSection_quotientGradingMk_eq_zero [IsNoetherianRing S] {ι : Type*}
    [Fintype ι] (g : ι → S) (e : ι → ℕ) (he : ∀ j, 0 < e j) (hg : ∀ j, g j ∈ 𝒮 (e j))
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin (𝒮 0) (Set.range g) = ⊤) :
    {x : S | ∀ n : ℕ, degreeSection (quotientGrading I) n
        (quotientGradingMk I n (decompose 𝒮 x n)) = 0} =
      {x : S | ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, N ≤ m →
        ∀ y : S, y ∈ 𝒮 (m * Finset.univ.lcm e) → y * x ∈ I.toIdeal}
declarations.comment: for `d` the lcm of the degrees of generators of `A` over `A_0`, `I(V_+(I)) = {x ∈ A | A_{nd} x ⊂ I for all n ≫ 0}`; `𝒪_{V_+(I)}(n)` is the twisting sheaf of `V_+(I) = Proj(A/I)`, the reading in which the source derives this from Cohomology of Schemes tag 0BXF applied to `A/I`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.mem_idealOfClosedSubscheme_projMap_quotientMk_iff
declarations.doc:
**The saturation formula for the ideal of equations of `V₊(I)`.** Over a Noetherian graded
ring generated by `𝒮 1` over `𝒮 0`, an element of `S` is an equation for the closed subscheme
`V₊(I) = Proj (𝒮 ⧸ I)` exactly when one whole homogeneous component `𝒮 N` multiplies it into
`I`:

`I(V₊(I)) = {x ∈ S | 𝒮 N · x ⊆ I for some N}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_idealOfClosedSubscheme_projMap_quotientMk_iff [IsNoetherianRing S]
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin (𝒮 0) ((𝒮 1 : Set S)) = ⊤) (x : S) :
    x ∈ idealOfClosedSubscheme 𝒮 (Proj.map (quotientMk I) hq) ↔
      ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ y : S, y ∈ 𝒮 N → y * x ∈ I.toIdeal
declarations.comment: standard_saturation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.coe_idealOfClosedSubscheme_projMap_quotientMk
declarations.doc:
**The saturation formula as an equality of sets**, the shape in which the source displays it:

`I(V₊(I)) = {x ∈ S | 𝒮 N · x ⊆ I for some N ≥ 0}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coe_idealOfClosedSubscheme_projMap_quotientMk [IsNoetherianRing S]
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin (𝒮 0) ((𝒮 1 : Set S)) = ⊤) :
    ((idealOfClosedSubscheme 𝒮 (Proj.map (quotientMk I) hq) : Ideal S) : Set S) =
      {x : S | ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ y : S, y ∈ 𝒮 N → y * x ∈ I.toIdeal}
declarations.comment: standard_saturation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.exists_closedImmersion_idealOfClosedSubscheme_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
**A homogeneous ideal is the ideal of equations of a closed subscheme of `Proj 𝒮` exactly
when it is saturated.** One direction is
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.saturated_idealOfClosedSubscheme`, that an ideal of
equations is saturated; the other takes `Z = V₊(I)` and reads off the saturation formula.

"Saturated" is spelled as the source does, as the equality of `I` with its own saturation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_closedImmersion_idealOfClosedSubscheme_eq_iff [IsNoetherianRing S]
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin (𝒮 0) ((𝒮 1 : Set S)) = ⊤) :
    (∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ Proj 𝒮) (_ : IsClosedImmersion i),
        idealOfClosedSubscheme 𝒮 i = I.toIdeal) ↔
      (I.toIdeal : Set S) = {x : S | ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ y : S, y ∈ 𝒮 N → y * x ∈ I.toIdeal}
declarations.comment: saturated_ideals

declarations.name: Stacks.WeightedProjSaturation.X_one_dvd_of_mem_grading
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BXK, in the counterexample of its last paragraph: a homogeneous `f` with
`6 ∣ deg(f · y)` is divisible by `y`.** Every monomial `x^a y^b` of `f` has `2a + 3b = n` with
`n + 3` divisible by `6`, so `n` is odd, so `b` is odd and in particular nonzero.
declarations.statement:
theorem X_one_dvd_of_mem_grading (n : ℕ) (f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℚ) (hf : f ∈ grading n)
    (h6 : 6 ∣ n + 3) : (MvPolynomial.X 1 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℚ) ∣ f
declarations.comment: the counterexample of the last paragraph, `A = ℚ[x, y]` with `deg x = 2` and `deg y = 3`: for homogeneous `f` with `6 ∣ deg (f y)` one has `y ∣ f`

declarations.name: Stacks.WeightedProjSaturation.mul_X_one_mem_squareIdeal
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0BXK, in the counterexample of its last paragraph: hence `f · y ∈ I = (y²)`.**
declarations.statement:
theorem mul_X_one_mem_squareIdeal (n : ℕ) (f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℚ) (hf : f ∈ grading n)
    (h6 : 6 ∣ n + 3) :
    f * (MvPolynomial.X 1 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℚ) ∈ squareIdeal
declarations.comment: the counterexample of the last paragraph: for homogeneous `f` with `6 ∣ deg (f y)` one has `f y ∈ I = (y²)`

declarations.name: Stacks.WeightedProjSaturation.mem_squareIdeal_of_mem_span_X_one
declarations.doc:
**The degreewise test of Stacks 0BXK's general formula, for `y` in this ring:
`(A · y)_{6n} ⊆ I` for every `n`.** An element of the ideal `(y)` that is homogeneous of a degree
divisible by `6` already lies in `(y²)`: divisibility by `y` makes the exponent `b` of `y` in
every monomial positive, and `2a + 3b = 6n` makes it even, so it is at least `2`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_squareIdeal_of_mem_span_X_one (n : ℕ) (z : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℚ)
    (hz : z ∈ Ideal.span {(MvPolynomial.X 1 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℚ)})
    (hdeg : z ∈ grading (6 * n)) : z ∈ squareIdeal
declarations.comment: the counterexample of the last paragraph: `(A y)_{6n} ⊆ I` for `I = (y²)`, the degreewise test `y` passes

declarations.name: Stacks.WeightedProjSaturation.X_zero_pow_mul_X_one_notMem_squareIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BXK, in the counterexample of its last paragraph: `xⁿ · y ∉ I` for every `n`.** The
only monomial of `xⁿ y` carries the exponent `1` at `y`, which is less than `2`.
declarations.statement:
theorem X_zero_pow_mul_X_one_notMem_squareIdeal (n : ℕ) :
    (MvPolynomial.X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℚ) ^ n * MvPolynomial.X 1 ∉ squareIdeal
declarations.comment: the counterexample of the last paragraph: `xⁿ y ∉ I` for every `n`, with `I = (y²)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.projectiveSpace_idealOfClosedSubscheme_isPrincipal_of_codimension_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BXL.** Let `R` be a Noetherian unique factorization domain and let `Z`
be a closed subscheme of `P^n_R = Proj R[T₀, …, Tₙ]` which has no embedded points and every
irreducible component of which has codimension one in `P^n_R`. Then the homogeneous ideal
`I(Z) ⊆ R[T₀, …, Tₙ]` corresponding to `Z` is principal.

A polynomial ring over a Noetherian UFD is a Noetherian UFD and is generated in degree one, so
this is the general `Proj` statement
`idealOfClosedSubscheme_isPrincipal_of_codimension_one`. For the conclusion in the form of a
single homogeneous equation see
`projectiveSpace_exists_homogeneous_eq_idealOfClosedSubscheme`.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectiveSpace_idealOfClosedSubscheme_isPrincipal_of_codimension_one (R : Type u)
    [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [UniqueFactorizationMonoid R] (n : ℕ)
    {Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Proj (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin (n + 1)) R))
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (hno : HasNoEmbeddedPoints Z)
    (hcodim : ∀ W ∈ irreducibleComponents Z, ∀ x : Z,
      IsGenericPoint x W → codimension (IrreducibleCloseds.closureSingleton (i.base x)) = 1) :
    (idealOfClosedSubscheme
      (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin (n + 1)) R) i).IsPrincipal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.varietyEquivalenceFinitelyGeneratedFieldExtensionOpposite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BXN.** Varieties and dominant rational maps over a field are
contravariantly equivalent to finitely generated field extensions of that field.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def varietyEquivalenceFinitelyGeneratedFieldExtensionOpposite
    (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    Variety k ≌ (FinitelyGeneratedFieldExtension k)ᵒᵖ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Variety.nonempty_iso_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem Variety.nonempty_iso_tfae (X Y : Variety k) :
    List.TFAE [
      Nonempty (X ≅ Y),
      Nonempty (X.toScheme.functionField ≃ₐ[k] Y.toScheme.functionField),
      ∃ (U : X.toScheme.Opens) (V : Y.toScheme.Opens),
        (U : Set X.toScheme).Nonempty ∧ (V : Set Y.toScheme).Nonempty ∧
          ∃ e : U.toScheme ≅ V.toScheme,
            e.hom ≫ V.ι ≫ Y.structureMap = U.ι ≫ X.structureMap,
      ∃ (U : X.toScheme.Opens), (U : Set X.toScheme).Nonempty ∧
        ∃ f : U.toScheme ⟶ Y.toScheme,
          IsBirational f ∧ f ≫ Y.structureMap = U.ι ≫ X.structureMap]
declarations.comment: Item (1), birationality of varieties, which the source defines as Spec(k)-birationality in the sense of Tag 0A20, is isomorphism in `AlgebraicGeometry.Variety k`, the category of varieties over `k` and dominant rational maps of Tag 0BXN. The function field in item (2) is the stalk at the generic point with its `k`-algebra structure from Tag 0BXN. The opens in items (3) and (4) are nonempty, as varieties are, and the isomorphism and the morphism commute with the structure morphisms to `Spec k`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_iso_normalizationSchemeOverField_coproduct_normal_irreducible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BXR.** The normalization of a scheme locally of finite type over a
field is a coproduct of normal irreducible schemes, each locally of finite type over the field
via its induced structure morphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_iso_normalizationSchemeOverField_coproduct_normal_irreducible
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (Z : I → Scheme.{u})
      (_ : ∀ i, IrreducibleSpace (Z i)) (_ : ∀ i, IsNormal (Z i))
      (e : normalizationSchemeOverField k p ≅ ∐ Z),
      ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (Sigma.ι Z i ≫ e.inv ≫ normalizationOverField k p ≫ p)
declarations.comment: finite_normal_components

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isVariety_normalizationOverField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BXR.** The normalization of a variety is a variety over the same
field.
declarations.comment: normalization_of_variety

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_normalizationOverField
registrations.comment: finite_normal_components
