declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_fromNormalization_of_locallyOfFiniteType_over_field
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BXS.** The relative normalization of a scheme locally of finite type
over a field in a reduced scheme locally of finite type over the same field is finite, as soon as
the morphism between them is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFinite_fromNormalization_of_locallyOfFiniteType_over_field
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (f : Y ⟶ X) (hf : f ≫ pX = pY)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType pX] [LocallyOfFiniteType pY]
    [QuasiCompact f] [IsReduced Y] :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian Y := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian pY
    letI : QuasiSeparated f := QuasiSeparated.of_comp f (terminal.from X)
    IsFinite f.fromNormalization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isPurelyInseparable_isGeometricallyNormal_normalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BXT.** Let `k` be a field and `X` an algebraic `k`-scheme. There is a
finite purely inseparable extension `k'/k` such that the normalization of `X_{k'}` is
geometrically normal over `k'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isPurelyInseparable_isGeometricallyNormal_normalization
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [QuasiCompact p] :
    ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : Algebra k k') (_ : Module.Finite k k')
      (_ : IsPurelyInseparable k k'),
      IsGeometricallyNormal (normalizationOverField k' (pullback.fst (spectrumMap k k') p) ≫
        pullback.fst (spectrumMap k k') p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.projectiveSpace_idealOfClosedSubscheme_isPrincipal_of_dimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BXU.** Let `k` be a field and let `Z` be a closed subscheme of
`P^n_k = Proj k[T₀, …, Tₙ]` which has no embedded points and every irreducible component of which
has dimension `n - 1`. Then the homogeneous ideal `I(Z) ⊆ k[T₀, …, Tₙ]` corresponding to `Z` is
principal.

The dimension hypothesis is written without subtraction as `dim W + 1 = n`. A field is a
Noetherian unique factorization domain, and in projective space over a field a component of
dimension `n - 1` has codimension one, so this is a special case of Tag 0BXL in the form
`projectiveSpace_idealOfClosedSubscheme_isPrincipal_of_codimension_one`.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectiveSpace_idealOfClosedSubscheme_isPrincipal_of_dimension (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (n : ℕ) {Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Proj (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin (n + 1)) k))
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (hno : HasNoEmbeddedPoints Z)
    (hdim : ∀ W ∈ irreducibleComponents Z, topologicalKrullDim W + 1 = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    (idealOfClosedSubscheme
      (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin (n + 1)) k) i).IsPrincipal

declarations.name: Stacks.CurveProjectiveCompletion.exists_projective_completion_of_dimension_le_one
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_projective_completion_of_dimension_le_one
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (X : Type u) ≤ 1) :
    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (q : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (j : X ⟶ Y) (hj : IsOpenImmersion j),
      letI : IsOpenImmersion j := hj
      j ≫ q = f ∧ IsProjectiveMorphism q ∧ IsDominant j ∧
        Scheme.Opens.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense j.opensRange ∧
        ((Set.range j.base)ᶜ).Finite ∧
        ∀ y : Y, y ∉ Set.range j.base → IsClosed ({y} : Set Y)
declarations.comment: the whole tag: all three clauses, for every separated scheme of finite type over `k` of dimension at most one

declarations.name: Stacks.CurveProjectiveCompletion.exists_projective_completion_discreteValuation_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BXW].** Let `X` be a reduced separated scheme of finite type over a field `k`
with `dim(X) ≤ 1`. Then there is an open immersion `j : X ⟶ X'` such that `X'` is H-projective
over `k`, the image of `j` is dense and scheme-theoretically dense in `X'`, the complement
`X' ∖ j(X)` is a finite set of closed points, and the local ring of `X'` at each of those points
is a discrete valuation ring.

The first step of the proof, [Stacks, Tag 0A25], is used in its reduced case
`Stacks.CurveProjectiveCompletion.isHQuasiProjective_of_isReduced`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_projective_completion_discreteValuation_of_isReduced
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    [IsSeparated p] [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [QuasiCompact p] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsReduced X]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (X : Type u) ≤ 1) :
    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (q : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (j : X ⟶ Y) (hj : IsOpenImmersion j),
      letI : IsOpenImmersion j := hj
      j ≫ q = p ∧ IsProjectiveMorphism q ∧ IsDominant j ∧
        Scheme.Opens.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense j.opensRange ∧
        ((Set.range j.base)ᶜ).Finite ∧
        ∀ y : Y, y ∉ Set.range j.base →
          IsClosed ({y} : Set Y) ∧
            ∃ _ : IsDomain (Y.presheaf.stalk y),
              IsDiscreteValuationRing (Y.presheaf.stalk y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsConstant
declarations.doc:
**A constant morphism** (Section 0BXX): a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` whose image `f(X)` consists of
a single point of `Y`.
declarations.statement: def Scheme.Hom.IsConstant {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop
declarations.comment: a morphism of varieties is constant if its image consists of a single point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_singleton_of_range_eq_singleton
declarations.doc:
**The image of a constant morphism of varieties is a closed point** (Section 0BXX). Let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of varieties over a field `k` whose image is the single point `y`.
Then `y` is a closed point of `Y`: the image of a closed point of `X` is a closed point of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_singleton_of_range_eq_singleton (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (sY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsVariety k sX] [IsVariety k sY]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) {y : Y} (hy : Set.range f.base = {y}) :
    IsClosed ({y} : Set Y)
declarations.comment: if a morphism of varieties is constant, with image the point y, then y is a closed point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NonsingularProjectiveModel.existsUnique_iso
declarations.doc:
**The nonsingular projective model is unique up to unique isomorphism** (Section 0BXX). For two
nonsingular projective models `(Y₁, φ₁)` and `(Y₂, φ₂)` of a curve `X` over `k`, there is exactly
one isomorphism `e : Y₁ ≅ Y₂` over `k` whose map of function fields `k(Y₂) ⟶ k(Y₁)` carries
`φ₂` to `φ₁`.
declarations.statement:
theorem NonsingularProjectiveModel.existsUnique_iso (M₁ M₂ : NonsingularProjectiveModel k X sX) :
    letI : IsCurve k M₁.structureMap := M₁.isCurve
    letI : IsCurve k M₂.structureMap := M₂.isCurve
    ∃! e : M₁.Y ≅ M₂.Y, e.hom ≫ M₂.structureMap = M₁.structureMap ∧
      ∀ a : X.functionField,
        functionFieldMap e.hom (M₂.functionFieldRingEquiv a) = M₁.functionFieldRingEquiv a
declarations.comment: a nonsingular projective model is determined up to unique isomorphism, by Theorem 0BY1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_forall_not_smooth_nonsingularProjectiveModel
declarations.doc:
**The nonsingular projective model need not be smooth** (the warning after Definition 0BY2,
Section 0BXX). There is a curve `X` over a field `k` which has a nonsingular projective model, and
no nonsingular projective model of `X` is smooth over `k`.

Here `k = 𝔽₂(t)` and `X` is the nonsingular projective model `Y` of the affine line over
`𝔽₂(√t)`, which is its own model. The affine line is an open subscheme of `Y`, and it is not smooth
over `k`, because `𝔽₂(√t)/𝔽₂(t)` is not separable; so `Y` is not smooth over `k`, and neither is
any other model, all models being isomorphic over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_forall_not_smooth_nonsingularProjectiveModel :
    ∃ (k : Type u) (_ : Field k) (X : Scheme.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (_ : IsCurve k sX),
      Nonempty (NonsingularProjectiveModel k X sX) ∧
        ∀ M : NonsingularProjectiveModel k X sX, ¬ Smooth M.structureMap
declarations.comment: the warning after Definition 0BY2, its first half: the nonsingular projective model of a curve need not be smooth over k

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_extension_of_valuationRing_stalk
registrations.comment: Lemma 0BXY of the section: a morphism from a nonempty open of a curve to a proper variety extends across a closed point whose local ring is a discrete valuation ring

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.toRationalMap_bijective
registrations.comment: Lemma 0BXZ of the section: rational maps from a normal curve to a proper variety are morphisms

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFlat_of_nonconstant_of_isNormal
registrations.comment: Lemma 0CCK of the section: a nonconstant morphism of curves with normal target is flat

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_of_isProper_dimension_le_one_of_nontrivial_image_components

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_globalSections_of_smooth_model_reducedBaseChange

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curveEquivalenceFinitelyGeneratedFieldExtensionTrdegOneOpposite

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NonsingularProjectiveModel.isSmoothProjectiveCurve

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_extension_of_valuationRing_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BX7.** A morphism from an open subscheme extends across a point
whose local ring is a valuation ring, provided the target is proper over the base and the
source is either reduced with finitely many irreducible components or Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_open_extension_of_valuationRing_stalk
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ S) (pY : Y ⟶ S)
    (x : X) (U : X.Opens) (f : (U : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ Y)
    (hf : f ≫ pY = U.ι ≫ pX)
    (hxU : x ∈ closure (U : Set X))
    (hX : (IsReduced X ∧ (irreducibleComponents X).Finite) ∨
      IsNoetherian X)
    [IsDomain (X.presheaf.stalk x)] [ValuationRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)]
    [IsProper pY] :
    ∃ (U' : X.Opens) (hUU' : U ≤ U') (_ : x ∈ U')
      (f' : (U' : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ Y),
      f' ≫ pY = U'.ι ≫ pX ∧ X.homOfLE hUU' ≫ f' = f
declarations.comment: the case of a curve over a field with proper target, where the stalk is a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.toRationalMap_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BXZ.** Morphisms from a normal curve to a proper variety are in
canonical bijection with the rational maps over the base field.
declarations.statement:
theorem toRationalMap_bijective
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X Y : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [IsCurve k X.hom] [IsNormal X.left] [IsProperVariety k Y.hom] :
    Function.Bijective
      (fun f : X ⟶ Y ↦
        (⟨f.left.toRationalMap, inferInstance⟩ :
          {g : Scheme.RationalMap X.left Y.left // g.IsOver (Spec (.of k))}))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isOpenImmersion_isCurve_isProjectiveMorphism_factorization_of_isCurve
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BY0].** Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a curve over `k` and `Y` a proper
variety over `k`, and let `g : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism over `k`. Then there is a factorization
`X ⟶ X̄ ⟶ Y` of `g` in which `X ⟶ X̄` is an open immersion and `X̄` is a projective curve over
`k`, that is, a curve whose structure morphism is H-projective.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenImmersion_isCurve_isProjectiveMorphism_factorization_of_isCurve
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (pX : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    [IsCurve k pX] [IsProperVariety k pY] (g : X ⟶ Y) (hg : g ≫ pY = pX) :
    ∃ (Xbar : Scheme.{u}) (q : Xbar ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (j : X ⟶ Xbar) (G : Xbar ⟶ Y),
      IsOpenImmersion j ∧ IsCurve k q ∧ IsProjectiveMorphism q ∧
        j ≫ q = pX ∧ G ≫ pY = q ∧ j ≫ G = g
declarations.comment: the full statement with nothing assumed. Both clauses are proved of the scheme constructed: `j` is an open immersion and `q` makes `Xbar` a curve (Tag 0A23) which is H-projective over `k` (Tag 01W8). The factorization `j ≫ G = g` is part of the conclusion, together with `j ≫ q = pX` and `G ≫ pY = q`, so both halves are morphisms of `k`-schemes. Tag 09NZ is not assumed: a curve is integral, hence reduced, and the library's Tag 0BXW, `Stacks.CurveProjectiveCompletion.exists_projective_completion_discreteValuation_of_isReduced`, carries nothing for a reduced source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curveEquivalenceFinitelyGeneratedFieldExtensionTrdegOneOpposite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BY1, categories (1) and (2).** Over a field `k`, the category of
curves over `k` and dominant rational maps is anti-equivalent to the category of finitely
generated field extensions of `k` of transcendence degree one.

This is the restriction of the anti-equivalence of Stacks 0BXN,
`AlgebraicGeometry.varietyEquivalenceFinitelyGeneratedFieldExtensionOpposite`, to the varieties
whose function field has transcendence degree one; those are exactly the curves, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isCurve_iff_trdeg_functionField_eq_one`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def curveEquivalenceFinitelyGeneratedFieldExtensionTrdegOneOpposite
    (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    Curve k ≌ (FinitelyGeneratedFieldExtensionTrdegOne k)ᵒᵖ
declarations.comment: the equivalence of categories (1) and (2), as the anti-equivalence of Tag 0BXN restricted to transcendence degree one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalProjectiveCurveEquivalenceRegularProjectiveCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BY1, categories (3) and (5).** The category of normal projective
curves over `k` and nonconstant morphisms and the category of regular projective curves over `k`
and nonconstant morphisms are the same: the equivalence is the inclusion of full subcategories,
which is the identity on underlying schemes and on morphisms, and it is an equivalence because
normality and regularity are the same condition on a curve, Stacks 0BX2
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isRegular_iff_isNormal_of_isCurve`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def normalProjectiveCurveEquivalenceRegularProjectiveCurve
    (k : Type u) [Field k] : NormalProjectiveCurve k ≌ RegularProjectiveCurve k
declarations.comment: that categories (3) and (5) are the same category: the inclusion of the normal projective curves into the regular projective curves, which is the identity on schemes and on morphisms, is an equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonsingularProjectiveCurveEquivalenceRegularProjectiveCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BY1, categories (4) and (5).** The category of nonsingular projective
curves over `k` and nonconstant morphisms is the category of regular projective curves over `k`
and nonconstant morphisms.

"Nonsingular" and "regular" are synonyms, Stacks 02IS: this library has one predicate,
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular`, formalizing both, so `AlgebraicGeometry.NonsingularProjectiveCurve`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.RegularProjectiveCurve` are the same type and the comparison is the
identity equivalence. The content of the source's claim is the synonymy of the two words, which
is a matter of terminology and not a mathematical statement that can be formalized separately.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def nonsingularProjectiveCurveEquivalenceRegularProjectiveCurve
    (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    NonsingularProjectiveCurve k ≌ RegularProjectiveCurve k
declarations.comment: that categories (4) and (5) are the same category; since `IsRegular` (Tag 02IS) formalizes both `nonsingular` and `regular`, the two categories are the same type and this is the identity equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalProjectiveCurveEquivalenceNormalProperCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BY1, categories (3) and (6).** The category of normal projective
curves over `k` and nonconstant morphisms and the category of normal proper curves over `k` and
nonconstant morphisms are the same: the equivalence is the inclusion of full subcategories,
which is the identity on underlying schemes and on morphisms, and it is an equivalence because a
proper curve is projective, the case of Stacks 0A26 proved outright in
`AlgebraicGeometry.isProjectiveMorphism_of_isProper_of_isCurve`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def normalProjectiveCurveEquivalenceNormalProperCurve
    (k : Type u) [Field k] : NormalProjectiveCurve k ≌ NormalProperCurve k
declarations.comment: that categories (3) and (6) are the same category: the inclusion of the normal projective curves into the normal proper curves, which is the identity on schemes and on morphisms, is an equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalProjectiveCurveToCurveFullyFaithful
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BY1, the fully faithful functor from category (3) to category (2).**
Over a field `k`, passing from a normal projective curve and its nonconstant morphisms to the
same curve and the rational maps of those morphisms is a fully faithful functor from category (3)
to category (2).

This is the source's step "there is a fully faithful functor (5) → (1)", transported along the
identification of category (3) with category (5) and along the anti-equivalence of categories (1)
and (2); both halves are Stacks 0BXZ,
`AlgebraicGeometry.toRationalMap_bijective` — morphisms from a normal curve to a proper variety
are exactly the rational maps over the base field — applied to the normal curve `X` and the
projective, hence proper, curve `Y`.

Essential surjectivity of this functor is `AlgebraicGeometry.normalProjectiveCurveToCurve_essSurj`
below, and the two together are the equivalence
`AlgebraicGeometry.normalProjectiveCurveEquivalenceCurve`; this declaration is the fully faithful
half alone.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def normalProjectiveCurveToCurveFullyFaithful (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    (normalProjectiveCurveToCurve k).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: only that the functor from category (3) to category (2) is fully faithful, which is the source's step `there is a fully faithful functor (5) to (1)`. Essential surjectivity of that functor — the source's final paragraph, that every finitely generated field extension of transcendence degree one is the function field of a normal projective curve — is NOT proved here, so this does not cover the equivalence of categories (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalProjectiveCurveEquivalenceCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BY1, categories (2) and (3).** Over a field `k`, the category of
normal projective curves over `k` and nonconstant morphisms is equivalent to the category of
curves over `k` and dominant rational maps.

The functor is the one of `AlgebraicGeometry.normalProjectiveCurveToCurve`; it is fully faithful
by [Stacks, Tag 0BXZ] and essentially surjective by
`AlgebraicGeometry.normalProjectiveCurveToCurve_essSurj`. Together with the anti-equivalence of
categories (1) and (2) and the identifications of categories (3), (4), (5) and (6), all six
categories of the source are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def normalProjectiveCurveEquivalenceCurve (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    NormalProjectiveCurve k ≌ Curve k
declarations.comment: the equivalence of categories (2) and (3): the functor of `AlgebraicGeometry.normalProjectiveCurveToCurve`, fully faithful by Tag 0BXZ and essentially surjective by `AlgebraicGeometry.normalProjectiveCurveToCurve_essSurj`, which is the source's final paragraph — every curve over `k` is birational to a normal projective curve, obtained by compactifying (Tag 0BXV, outright for an integral scheme of dimension one) and then normalizing (Tag 0BXR, proper by Tag 0GK4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NonsingularProjectiveModel
declarations.doc:
A nonsingular projective model of a curve `X` over a field `k` is a regular projective curve
over `k` together with a `k`-algebra isomorphism from the function field of `X` to its own function
field.
declarations.statement:
structure NonsingularProjectiveModel (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k sX]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NonsingularProjectiveModel.isSmoothProjectiveCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BY3.** Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a curve over `k` and let `Y` be
a nonsingular projective model of `X`. If `k` is perfect then `Y` is a smooth projective
curve.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSmoothProjectiveCurve [PerfectField k]
    (M : NonsingularProjectiveModel k X sX) :
    Smooth M.structureMap ∧ IsProjectiveVariety k M.structureMap ∧
      IsCurve k M.structureMap

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_iso_pullback_of_smooth_models
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BY4, part (4).** Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a geometrically
irreducible curve over `k`. For a field extension `K/k` write `Y_K` for a nonsingular projective
model of `(X_K)_red`. Given a commutative diagram of fields

```
Ω  ←  K'
↑     ↑
K  ←  k
```

such that `Y_K` and `Y_{K'}` are smooth, we have `Y_Ω = (Y_K)_Ω = (Y_{K'})_Ω`: both base changes
are isomorphic to `Y_Ω` as schemes over `Ω`, and hence to each other.

The commuting square of fields is the two scalar towers `k ⊆ K ⊆ Ω` and `k ⊆ K' ⊆ Ω`. The
equality of the source is a canonical isomorphism of schemes over `Ω`: the isomorphism is
compatible with the structure morphisms, which is part of the conclusion, and it is the only such
isomorphism matching the birational identifications, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.NonsingularProjectiveModel.hom_ext`.

The three instance binders `[IsCurve K (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k K sX)]` and its analogues
for `K'` and `Ω` are not added hypotheses: each follows from `[IsCurve k sX]` and
`[GeometricallyIrreducible sX]` by the instance
`AlgebraicGeometry.isCurve_reducedBaseChangeStructureMap'`, which lives in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Curves/ModelNormalization.lean` and is not in this file's import
closure, so the facts are named instead.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_iso_pullback_of_smooth_models
    (k K K' Ω : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Field K'] [Field Ω]
    [Algebra k K] [Algebra k K'] [Algebra K Ω] [Algebra K' Ω] [Algebra k Ω]
    [IsScalarTower k K Ω] [IsScalarTower k K' Ω]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsCurve k sX] [GeometricallyIrreducible sX]
    [IsCurve K (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k K sX)]
    [IsCurve K' (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k K' sX)]
    [IsCurve Ω (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k Ω sX)]
    (M_K : NonsingularProjectiveModel K (reducedBaseChange k K sX)
      (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k K sX))
    (M_K' : NonsingularProjectiveModel K' (reducedBaseChange k K' sX)
      (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k K' sX))
    (M_Ω : NonsingularProjectiveModel Ω (reducedBaseChange k Ω sX)
      (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k Ω sX))
    (hK : Smooth M_K.structureMap) (hK' : Smooth M_K'.structureMap) :
    (∃ e : M_Ω.Y ≅ pullback M_K.structureMap
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K Ω))),
      e.hom ≫ pullback.snd M_K.structureMap
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K Ω))) = M_Ω.structureMap) ∧
    (∃ e : M_Ω.Y ≅ pullback M_K'.structureMap
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K' Ω))),
      e.hom ≫ pullback.snd M_K'.structureMap
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K' Ω))) = M_Ω.structureMap)
declarations.comment: part (4): for a commuting square of fields k to K to Omega and k to K' to Omega with the models Y_K and Y_K' smooth, the nonsingular projective model Y_Omega of (X_Omega)_red is isomorphic over Omega to the base change of Y_K and to the base change of Y_K'. The three binders `[IsCurve _ (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k _ sX)]` add nothing: each follows from `[IsCurve k sX]` and `[GeometricallyIrreducible sX]` by the instance `AlgebraicGeometry.isCurve_reducedBaseChangeStructureMap'`, which is not in this file's import closure

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isPurelyInseparable_smooth_nonsingularProjectiveModel_of_isCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BY4, part (2).** Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a geometrically
irreducible curve over `k`. There is a finite purely inseparable extension `K/k` for which
`(X_K)_red` has a smooth nonsingular projective model.

Nothing is carried and `X` is not assumed proper. The general case is reduced to the proper one
exactly as in the source: `X` is a dense open subscheme of a projective curve `X̄` over `k`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isCurve_isProjectiveMorphism_isOpenImmersion`, the compactification
behind the essential surjectivity half of [Stacks, Tag 0BY1]), which is again geometrically
irreducible; the proper case,
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isPurelyInseparable_smooth_nonsingularProjectiveModel'`, applied to `X̄`
supplies `K` and a smooth model of `(X̄_K)_red`; and that is a model of `(X_K)_red` as well,
because the reduced base change of a dense open immersion is a dominant open immersion, so the
two have the same function field over `K`, and a nonsingular projective model depends only on
the function field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isPurelyInseparable_smooth_nonsingularProjectiveModel_of_isCurve
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsCurve k sX] [GeometricallyIrreducible sX] :
    ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : Algebra k K) (_ : Module.Finite k K)
      (_ : IsPurelyInseparable k K),
      ∃ M : NonsingularProjectiveModel K (reducedBaseChange k K sX)
          (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k K sX),
        Smooth M.structureMap
declarations.comment: part (2), with nothing carried and `X` not assumed proper. Tag 09NZ is not needed: the compactification of a curve is Tag 0BXV for an integral scheme of dimension one, where Tag 0A25 holds outright, and the model of a proper curve is its normalization, again integral of dimension one. The source's reduction of the general case to the projective case is carried out with the compactification behind `AlgebraicGeometry.normalProjectiveCurveToCurve_essSurj` (Tag 0BY1) together with `AlgebraicGeometry.NonsingularProjectiveModel.ofFunctionFieldAlgEquiv`, that a nonsingular projective model depends only on the function field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_globalSections_of_geometricallyReduced_model_reducedBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BY4, part (3).** Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a geometrically
irreducible curve over `k`, let `K/k` be a field extension and let `Y_K` be a nonsingular
projective model of `(X_K)_red`. If `Y_K` is geometrically reduced over `K`, then `K` is the
ring of global regular functions on `Y_K`.

The instance binder `[IsCurve K (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k K sX)]` is not an added
hypothesis: it is a consequence of `[IsCurve k sX]` and `[GeometricallyIrreducible sX]`, proved
as the instance `AlgebraicGeometry.isCurve_reducedBaseChangeStructureMap'`. That instance lives in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Curves/ModelNormalization.lean`, which imports this file, so it
cannot be used here and the fact is named instead.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_globalSections_of_geometricallyReduced_model_reducedBaseChange
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k sX] [GeometricallyIrreducible sX]
    [IsCurve K (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k K sX)]
    (M : NonsingularProjectiveModel K (reducedBaseChange k K sX)
      (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k K sX))
    (hred : GeometricallyReduced M.structureMap) :
    IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫ M.structureMap.appTop)
declarations.comment: part (3), with the source's own footnote hypothesis: the model is assumed only geometrically reduced, not smooth. The binder `[IsCurve K (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k K sX)]` adds nothing: it follows from `[IsCurve k sX]` and `[GeometricallyIrreducible sX]` by the instance `AlgebraicGeometry.isCurve_reducedBaseChangeStructureMap'`, which is proved in a module importing this one and so is unavailable here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_globalSections_of_smooth_model_reducedBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BY4, part (3).** Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a geometrically
irreducible curve over `k`, let `K/k` be a field extension and let `Y_K` be a nonsingular
projective model of `(X_K)_red`. If `Y_K` is smooth over `K`, then `K` is the ring of global
regular functions on `Y_K`.

The instance binder `[IsCurve K (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k K sX)]` adds nothing, for the
reason given on
`AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_globalSections_of_geometricallyReduced_model_reducedBaseChange`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_globalSections_of_smooth_model_reducedBaseChange
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k sX] [GeometricallyIrreducible sX]
    [IsCurve K (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k K sX)]
    (M : NonsingularProjectiveModel K (reducedBaseChange k K sX)
      (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k K sX))
    (hsm : Smooth M.structureMap) :
    IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫ M.structureMap.appTop)
declarations.comment: part (3). The binder `[IsCurve K (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k K sX)]` adds nothing: it follows from `[IsCurve k sX]` and `[GeometricallyIrreducible sX]` by the instance `AlgebraicGeometry.isCurve_reducedBaseChangeStructureMap'`, which is proved in a module importing this one and so is unavailable here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_nonsingularProjectiveModel_iso_normalization_reducedBaseChange'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BY4, part (1).** Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a proper
geometrically irreducible curve over `k` and let `K/k` be a field extension. Then `(X_K)_red` has
a nonsingular projective model whose underlying scheme is the normalization of `X_K` over `K`.

Nothing is carried: the model is `AlgebraicGeometry.normalizationModel'`, whose projectivity is
the step "a proper curve is projective" applied to a normalization. This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_nonsingularProjectiveModel_iso_normalization_reducedBaseChange`, proved
another way.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_nonsingularProjectiveModel_iso_normalization_reducedBaseChange'
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k sX] [GeometricallyIrreducible sX] [IsProper sX] :
    ∃ M : NonsingularProjectiveModel K (reducedBaseChange k K sX)
        (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k K sX),
      ∃ e : normalizationSchemeOverField K
          (pullback.snd sX (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))) ≅ M.Y,
        normalizationOverField K
            (pullback.snd sX (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))) ≫
          pullback.snd sX (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) =
            e.hom ≫ M.structureMap
declarations.comment: part (1), with nothing carried: the source's step `a proper curve is projective` is applied to a normalization, which is integral of dimension one, so Tag 0A25 holds outright as `Stacks.HQuasiProjectiveDimensionOne.isHQuasiProjective_of_isIntegral` and Tag 09NZ is not needed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isPurelyInseparable_smooth_nonsingularProjectiveModel'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BY4, part (2).** Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a proper
geometrically irreducible curve over `k`. There is a finite purely inseparable extension `K/k`
for which `(X_K)_red` has a smooth nonsingular projective model.

Nothing is carried; `X` is assumed proper. This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isPurelyInseparable_smooth_nonsingularProjectiveModel` with the model
`AlgebraicGeometry.normalizationModel'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isPurelyInseparable_smooth_nonsingularProjectiveModel'
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsCurve k sX] [GeometricallyIrreducible sX] [IsProper sX] :
    ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : Algebra k K) (_ : Module.Finite k K)
      (_ : IsPurelyInseparable k K),
      ∃ M : NonsingularProjectiveModel K (reducedBaseChange k K sX)
          (reducedBaseChangeStructureMap k K sX),
        Smooth M.structureMap
declarations.comment: part (2) for a proper `X`, with nothing carried: Tag 09NZ is not assumed, because the model is the normalization of `(X_K)_red`, integral of dimension one, where Tag 0A25 holds outright from Tag 09ND. One hypothesis is named: `X` is assumed proper, because the source's reduction of the general case to the projective case replaces `X` by a nonsingular projective model and so uses Theorem 0BY1; that reduction is carried out in `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isPurelyInseparable_smooth_nonsingularProjectiveModel_of_isCurve`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.genus
declarations.doc: The genus of a scheme `X` over a field `k`, namely `dim_k H¹(X, 𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def genus {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) : ℕ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CurveDuality.genus_eq_finrank_structureSheafCohomology_and_eq_finrank_relativeDualizingModule
declarations.doc:
**Equation 53.8.1.1 of [Stacks, Tag 0BY8].** Let `k` be a field and let `f : X ⟶ Spec(k)` be
proper with `X` of topological Krull dimension one. Then

`g = dim_k H^1(X, 𝒪_X) = dim_k H^0(X, ω_X)`,

where `g` is the genus of [Stacks, Tag 0BY7] and `ω_X = H^{-1}(f^×𝒪_{Spec(k)})` is the relative
dualizing module of [Stacks, Tag 0AWI] — the object that [Stacks, Tag 0BS2] produces as
`H^{-1}` of the relative dualizing complex `a(𝒪_{Spec(k)})`.

The first equality is the definition of the genus,
`AlgebraicGeometry.genus_eq_finrank_structureSheafCohomology`; the second is
`finrank_structureSheafCohomology_eq_finrank_cohomologyOverField_relativeDualizingModule`.

Definition 53.8.1 of the source also assumes `H^0(X, 𝒪_X) = k`, which fixes the ground field and
makes `X` Cohen--Macaulay and equidimensional; neither equality needs it, so it is not assumed
here and the statement holds in the generality of the definition and beyond.
declarations.statement:
theorem genus_eq_finrank_structureSheafCohomology_and_eq_finrank_relativeDualizingModule
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) :
    letI : CompactSpace X := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace f
    letI : QuasiSeparatedSpace X := quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated f
    genus f = Module.finrank k (structureSheafCohomology f 1) ∧
      Module.finrank k (structureSheafCohomology f 1) =
        Module.finrank k (cohomologyOverField k f
          (relativeDualizingModule f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
            (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k)))) 0)
declarations.comment: equation 53.8.1.1: the genus is the dimension over the ground field of the first cohomology of the structure sheaf, and the dimension over the ground field of the global sections of the relative dualizing module

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.genus_eq_finrank_structureSheafCohomology
registrations.comment: genus as first cohomology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDim_baseChange

    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} (g' : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ Spec (.of k')) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))

    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.projectivePlane_idealOfClosedSubscheme_isPrincipal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BYB.** Let `k` be a field and let `Z` be a closed subscheme of
`P^2_k = Proj k[T₀, T₁, T₂]` which is equidimensional of dimension one and has no embedded
points. Then the homogeneous ideal `I(Z) ⊆ k[T₀, T₁, T₂]` corresponding to `Z` is principal.

Equidimensionality of dimension one is the hypothesis that every irreducible component of `Z`
has `topologicalKrullDim` equal to `1`; see
`TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional.of_forall_topologicalKrullDim_eq`. This is Tag 0BXU, the
statement for `P^n_k` with components of dimension `n - 1`, at `n = 2`. For the equivalent
Cohen--Macaulay form of the hypothesis see
`projectivePlane_isCohenMacaulay_iff_hasNoEmbeddedPoints`, and for the generator written out see
`projectivePlane_exists_homogeneous_eq_idealOfClosedSubscheme`.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectivePlane_idealOfClosedSubscheme_isPrincipal (hno : HasNoEmbeddedPoints Z)
    (hdim : ∀ W ∈ irreducibleComponents Z, topologicalKrullDim W = 1) :
    (idealOfClosedSubscheme
      (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 3) k) i).IsPrincipal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.projectivePlane_isCohenMacaulay_iff_hasNoEmbeddedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BYB, the parenthetical statement.** A closed subscheme `Z` of
`P^2_k` which is equidimensional of dimension one has no embedded points precisely when it is
Cohen--Macaulay.

This is Tag 0BXG for schemes of dimension at most one. Both of its hypotheses are automatic
here: `Z` is locally Noetherian because `i` is a closed immersion, hence locally of finite type,
into the Noetherian scheme `P^2_k`; and `dim Z ≤ 1` because every irreducible component of `Z`
has dimension one.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectivePlane_isCohenMacaulay_iff_hasNoEmbeddedPoints
    (hdim : ∀ W ∈ irreducibleComponents Z, topologicalKrullDim W = 1) :
    IsCohenMacaulay Z ↔ HasNoEmbeddedPoints Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.projectivePlane_isCurve_iff_irreducible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BYC.** Let `k` be a field, let `Z ⊆ 𝐏²_k = Proj k[T₀, T₁, T₂]` be a
closed subscheme of dimension one and let `I(Z) = (F)`. Then `Z` is a curve over `k` if and only
if `F` is irreducible.

The hypotheses of [Stacks, Tag 0BYB] under which the generator `F` is produced — `Z`
equidimensional of dimension one with no embedded points — are not needed beyond `dim Z = 1`,
which they give for a nonempty `Z`; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.projectivePlane_idealOfClosedSubscheme_isPrincipal`
for that production. "Curve" is [Stacks, Tag 0A23]: a variety over `k` of Krull dimension one,
with respect to the structure morphism of the polynomial model of the projective plane.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectivePlane_isCurve_iff_irreducible (hdim : topologicalKrullDim Z = 1)
    {F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k}
    (hF : idealOfClosedSubscheme (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 3) k) i =
      Ideal.span {F}) :
    IsCurve k (i ≫ projToSpecCoeff k 2) ↔ Irreducible F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.planeCurveGlobalSectionsEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BYD, global functions.** Let `Z ⊆ 𝐏²_k` be as in
[Stacks, Tag 0BYB], with `I(Z) = (F)` for `F` homogeneous of degree `d`. Then
`H⁰(Z, 𝒪_Z) = k`.

The source sheafifies the graded resolution of `k[T₀, T₁, T₂]/(F)` into
`0 → 𝒪(-d) → 𝒪 → i_* 𝒪_Z → 0` and reads the degree-zero window of the resulting long exact
sequence. Since `d > 0` by `PlaneCurveData.deg_pos`, the two terms `H⁰(𝐏²_k, 𝒪(-d))` and
`H¹(𝐏²_k, 𝒪(-d))` flanking that window vanish by [Stacks, Tag 01XT], so the restriction map
`H⁰(𝐏²_k, 𝒪) → H⁰(Z, 𝒪_Z)` is an isomorphism; that is
`Stacks.ProjectiveSpace.Cohomology.nonempty_structureSheafCohomologyIsoTwistCohomologyZero`. Its
source is `k` because the degree-zero homogeneous polynomials are the constants.
declarations.statement:
def planeCurveGlobalSectionsEquiv {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : PlaneCurveData k) :
    structureSheafCohomology C.toSpec 0 ≃ₗ[k] k
declarations.comment: global functions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.genus_planeCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BYD, the genus formula.** Let `Z ⊆ 𝐏²_k` be as in
[Stacks, Tag 0BYB], with `I(Z) = (F)` for `F` homogeneous of degree `d`. Then the genus of `Z`
is `(d - 1)(d - 2)/2`.

The source reads the isomorphism `H¹(Z, 𝒪_Z) ≅ H²(𝐏²_k, 𝒪(-d))` off the long exact sequence of
the sheafified resolution `0 → 𝒪(-d) → 𝒪 → i_* 𝒪_Z → 0`, where it is an isomorphism because
`H¹(𝐏²_k, 𝒪)` and `H²(𝐏²_k, 𝒪)` both vanish. That is
`Stacks.ProjectiveSpace.Cohomology`
`.finrank_structureSheafCohomology_eq_finrank_twistCohomology_neg`, whose input is the
identification of the ideal sheaf of `Z` with the zero scheme of the section of `𝒪(d)` attached
to `F`; `F` is nonzero because `Z` is equidimensional of dimension one. What remains is the
dimension of the right-hand side, which by [Stacks, Tag 01XT] is free on the degree-`-d` Laurent
monomials with every exponent negative, and those number `(d - 1)(d - 2)/2`.
declarations.statement:
theorem genus_planeCurve {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : PlaneCurveData k) :
    genus C.toSpec = (C.deg - 1) * (C.deg - 2) / 2
declarations.comment: the genus formula

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.genus_planeCurve_totalDegree
declarations.doc:
**The genus formula at the degree of the equation.** The genus of a plane curve `Z ⊆ 𝐏²_k`
cut out by `F` is `(deg(F) - 1)(deg(F) - 2)/2`, where `deg(F)` is `MvPolynomial.totalDegree F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem genus_planeCurve_totalDegree {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : PlaneCurveData k) :
    genus C.toSpec = (C.F.totalDegree - 1) * (C.F.totalDegree - 2) / 2
declarations.comment: the genus formula, stated at the total degree of the equation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricGenusOfCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BYF.** The *geometric genus* of a geometrically irreducible curve `X`
over a field `k`: the genus of a smooth projective model of `X` possibly defined over an
extension field of `k`, as in Tag 0BY4 — for an extension `K/k` such that the nonsingular
projective model `Y_K` of `(X_K)_red` is smooth over `K`, the genus `dim_K H¹(Y_K, 𝒪_{Y_K})`.

It does not depend on the choice of `K` or of the model, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.geometricGenusOfCurve_eq_genus`. Such a model exists by Tag 0BY4 (2)
(`AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_smoothModelOverExtension_of_isProper` for proper `X`); the value
`0` is a junk value for the case where none is supplied.
declarations.statement: def geometricGenusOfCurve : ℕ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricGenusOfCurve_eq_genus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BYF, well-definedness.** The geometric genus of `X` is the genus of
every smooth projective model of `X` over every extension field of `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricGenusOfCurve_eq_genus (N : SmoothModelOverExtension k sX) :
    geometricGenusOfCurve k sX = genus N.model.structureMap
declarations.comment: the definition is independent of the extension field and of the smooth model

declarations.name: KFlatTwoOutOfThree.kFlat_two_out_of_three
declarations.doc:
Two-out-of-three for K-flatness (Stacks Tag 0BYH, Lemma 15.60.6).
Given a short exact sequence of complexes `0 → K₁ → K₂ → K₃ → 0` with every
`K₃^n` flat, if at least two of `K₁, K₂, K₃` are K-flat, then all three are.

Case analysis on the disjunction `h`, completing the missing third K-flatness via
the corresponding directional lemma.
declarations.statement:
theorem kFlat_two_out_of_three {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (S : ShortComplex (Cx R))
    (hse : S.ShortExact) (hflat : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Flat R (S.X₃.X n))
    (h : (CochainComplex.KFlat S.X₁ ∧ CochainComplex.KFlat S.X₂) ∨
          (CochainComplex.KFlat S.X₁ ∧ CochainComplex.KFlat S.X₃) ∨
          (CochainComplex.KFlat S.X₂ ∧ CochainComplex.KFlat S.X₃)) :
    CochainComplex.KFlat S.X₁ ∧ CochainComplex.KFlat S.X₂ ∧ CochainComplex.KFlat S.X₃

declarations.name: CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalSymmetricDerivedTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYI.** The canonical derived tensor product, equipped with its symmetry functorial
in both complexes and represented on K-flat complexes in degrees `p` and `q` by the ordinary
tensor braiding with the sign `(-1) ^ (p * q)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def canonicalSymmetricDerivedTensorProduct
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)] : SymmetricDerivedTensorProduct R

declarations.name: CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.derivedTensorProduct_associator
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYJ.** The derived tensor product is associative up to a canonical isomorphism,
functorial in all three complexes. On K-flat representatives this is the standard associator
of tensor products of complexes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedTensorProduct_associator
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)] :
    let D := DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)
    let C := CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ
    let Q := DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{u} R)
    let T := canonicalDerivedTensorProduct R
    ∃ associator : ∀ K L M : D,
          (T.tensor.obj ((T.tensor.obj K).obj L)).obj M ≅
            (T.tensor.obj K).obj ((T.tensor.obj L).obj M),
        (∀ {K K' L L' M M' : D} (f : K ⟶ K') (g : L ⟶ L') (h : M ⟶ M'),
          (T.tensor.map ((T.tensor.map f).app L ≫ (T.tensor.obj K').map g)).app M ≫
                (T.tensor.obj ((T.tensor.obj K').obj L')).map h ≫
                (associator K' L' M').hom =
            (associator K L M).hom ≫
              (T.tensor.map f).app ((T.tensor.obj L).obj M) ≫
              (T.tensor.obj K').map
                ((T.tensor.map g).app M ≫ (T.tensor.obj L').map h)) ∧
        ∀ (K L M : C) (hK : K.KFlat) (hL : L.KFlat) (hM : M.KFlat),
          let hKL := CochainComplex.KFlat.tensor R K L hK hL
          let hLM := CochainComplex.KFlat.tensor R L M hL hM
          (associator (Q.obj K) (Q.obj L) (Q.obj M)).hom ≫
                (T.tensor.obj (Q.obj K)).map (T.comparison L M hL hM).hom ≫
                (T.comparison K (L ⊗ M) hK hLM).hom =
            (T.tensor.map (T.comparison K L hK hL).hom).app (Q.obj M) ≫
              (T.comparison (K ⊗ L) M hKL hM).hom ≫
              Q.map (HomologicalComplex.associator K L M).hom

declarations.name: CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.exists_derivedTensorNatTrans_isIso_of_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
A map `f : L ⟶ N` of complexes of `A`-modules induces a natural
transformation `1 ⊗ᴸ f` between any chosen left-derived models of the change-of-rings tensor
functors `- ⊗ᴸ_R L` and `- ⊗ᴸ_R N`. The compatibility equation says that this is the
transformation induced by the ordinary tensor map `1 ⊗ f`. If `f` is a quasi-isomorphism, the
induced transformation is an isomorphism of functors.

The source ring universe `uR`, the target ring universe `uA` and the module universe are
mutually independent: the two rings are related by nothing but `φ`, and the modules of both
rings have to fit in one category, so they live at `max v uR uA`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_derivedTensorNatTrans_isIso_of_quasiIso
    {R : Type uR} {A : Type uA} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] (φ : R →+* A)
    {L N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA} A) ℤ}
    (f : L ⟶ N)
    (FL FN : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA} R) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA} A))
    (αL : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ FL ⟶
      (extendScalarsLarge.{v, uR, uA} φ ⋙ tensorRightLarge.{uA, max v uR} L) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q)
    (αN : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ FN ⟶
      (extendScalarsLarge.{v, uR, uA} φ ⋙ tensorRightLarge.{uA, max v uR} N) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q)
    [CategoryTheory.Functor.IsLeftDerivedFunctor FL αL
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [CategoryTheory.Functor.IsLeftDerivedFunctor FN αN
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    letI : MonoidalCategoryStruct (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA} A) :=
      ModuleCat.liftedModuleMonoidalStruct.{uA, max v uR}
    letI : MonoidalCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA} A) :=
      ModuleCat.liftedModuleMonoidal.{uA, max v uR}
    let tensorMap :
        (extendScalarsLarge.{v, uR, uA} φ ⋙ tensorRightLarge.{uA, max v uR} L) ⋙
            DerivedCategory.Q ⟶
          (extendScalarsLarge.{v, uR, uA} φ ⋙ tensorRightLarge.{uA, max v uR} N) ⋙
            DerivedCategory.Q :=
      CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskerRight
        (CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskerLeft (extendScalarsLarge.{v, uR, uA} φ)
          ((CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor
            (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA} A)).map₂CochainComplex.flip.map f))
        DerivedCategory.Q
    ∃ t : FL ⟶ FN,
      CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Q t ≫ αN = αL ≫ tensorMap ∧
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) f →
          IsIso t)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitudeAbove_iff_exists_kFlat_flat_representative_canonical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYL.** An object `K` of `D(R)` has Tor amplitude in `[a, ∞]` — that is, the derived
tensor product of `K` with any module `M` placed in cohomological degree zero has vanishing
cohomology in all degrees below `a` — if and only if `K` is represented by a K-flat complex of
flat modules concentrated in degrees at least `a`.

The derived tensor product here is *the* canonical one,
`CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct R` of Stacks 0BYI, so the statement
is an assertion about a specific bifunctor rather than a claim quantified over certificates.
It is obtained by instantiating
`StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitudeAbove_iff_exists_kFlat_flat_representative`, which
proves the equivalence for an arbitrary certified derived tensor bifunctor, at that canonical
choice.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasTorAmplitudeAbove_iff_exists_kFlat_flat_representative_canonical
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (a : ℤ) :
    (∀ (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) (i : ℤ), i < a →
        IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj
          (((CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct R).tensor.obj K).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj M)))) ↔
      ∃ E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ,
        E.KFlat ∧
          (∀ n : ℤ, Module.Flat R (E.X n)) ∧
          E.IsStrictlyGE a ∧
          Nonempty (K ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj E)

declarations.name: Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomComparison.theta
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYM**.
The canonical morphism of complexes `Θ : Tot(K ⊗_R Hom^•(M, L)) ⟶ Hom^•(M, Tot(K ⊗_R L))`,
given in degree `n` by `thetaDeg`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def theta (K L M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) :
    (K ⊗ HomComplexR R M L) ⟶ HomComplexR R M (K ⊗ L)

declarations.name: Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomComparison.theta_natural_K
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYM** (naturality in `K`).
For `fK : K ⟶ K'`, `Θ ≫ Hom^•(id_M, fK ▷ L) = (fK ▷ Hom^•(M, L)) ≫ Θ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem theta_natural_K (K K' L M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (fK : K ⟶ K') :
    theta K L M ≫ HomCxMap M M (K ⊗ L) (K' ⊗ L) (𝟙 M) (fK ▷ L)
      = (fK ▷ HomComplexR R M L) ≫ theta K' L M

declarations.name: Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomComparison.theta_natural_L
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYM** (naturality in `L`).
For `gL : L ⟶ L'`, `Θ ≫ Hom^•(id_M, K ◁ gL) = (K ◁ Hom^•(id_M, gL)) ≫ Θ`.

theorem theta_natural_L (K L L' M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (gL : L ⟶ L') :
    theta K L M ≫ HomCxMap M M (K ⊗ L) (K ⊗ L') (𝟙 M) (K ◁ gL)
      = (K ◁ HomCxMap M M L L' (𝟙 M) gL) ≫ theta K L' M

declarations.name: Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomComparison.theta_natural_M
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYM** (naturality in `M`).
For `hM : M' ⟶ M`, `Θ ≫ Hom^•(hM, id_{K ⊗ L}) = (K ◁ Hom^•(hM, id_L)) ≫ Θ`.

theorem theta_natural_M (K L M M' : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (hM : M' ⟶ M) :
    theta K L M ≫ HomCxMap M M' (K ⊗ L) (K ⊗ L) hM (𝟙 (K ⊗ L))
      = (K ◁ HomCxMap M M' L L hM (𝟙 L)) ≫ theta K L M'

declarations.name: StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedTensorHomDiagonal_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYN.** The derived tensor--Hom diagonal is covariantly natural in `K` and `L`
and contravariantly natural in `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedTensorHomDiagonal_natural :
    (∀ {K K' L M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R)} (f : K ⟶ K'),
      (DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).map
          (f, 𝟙 ((DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).obj (Opposite.op M, L))) ≫
          derivedTensorHomDiagonal K' L M =
        derivedTensorHomDiagonal K L M ≫
          (DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).map
            (𝟙 (Opposite.op M), (DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).map (f, 𝟙 L))) ∧
    (∀ {K L L' M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R)} (f : L ⟶ L'),
      (DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).map
          (𝟙 K, (DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).map (𝟙 (Opposite.op M), f)) ≫
          derivedTensorHomDiagonal K L' M =
        derivedTensorHomDiagonal K L M ≫
          (DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).map
            (𝟙 (Opposite.op M), (DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).map (𝟙 K, f))) ∧
    (∀ {K L M M' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R)} (f : M' ⟶ M),
      (DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).map
          (𝟙 K, (DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).map (f.op, 𝟙 L)) ≫
          derivedTensorHomDiagonal K L M' =
        derivedTensorHomDiagonal K L M ≫
          (DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).map
            (f.op, 𝟙 ((DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).obj (K, L))))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.exists_away_bounded_free_complex_representing_of_fibre_vanishing_below
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYP.** Let `R` be a commutative ring, `p` a prime of `R` and `K` a pseudo-coherent
object of `D(R)` which is bounded below. Set `dᵢ = dim_{κ(p)} Hⁱ(K ⊗ᴸ_R κ(p))`. If `dᵢ = 0` for
all `i < a`, then there is an `f ∈ R` outside `p` such that `K ⊗ᴸ_R R_f` is perfect and is
represented by a complex over `R_f` concentrated in degrees `[a, b]` whose term in degree `i` is
free of rank exactly `dᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_away_bounded_free_complex_representing_of_fibre_vanishing_below
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} R))
    (hK : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K)
    (hbounded : ∃ c : ℤ, K.IsGE c) (a : ℤ) :
    let k := p.ResidueField
    let H := fun i : ℤ =>
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max v u} k) i).obj
        ((totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, v} (algebraMap R k)).functor.obj K)
    (∀ i : ℤ, i < a → IsZero (H i)) →
      ∃ f : R, f ∉ p ∧
        let Kf := (totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, v}
          (algebraMap R (Localization.Away f))).functor.obj K
        IsPerfect Kf ∧
          ∃ (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} (Localization.Away f)) ℤ) (b : ℤ),
            P.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ P.IsStrictlyLE b ∧
              (∀ i : ℤ, Nonempty (P.X i ≅ ModuleCat.of (Localization.Away f)
                (ULift.{v} (Fin (Module.finrank k (H i)) → Localization.Away f)))) ∧
              Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ Kf)

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedHom.KFlatHomComplex.homComplex_kFlat_and_represents_RHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYQ.** Let `P` be a bounded above cochain complex of projective `R`-modules which
is perfect as an object of the derived category `D(R)`, and let `K` be a K-flat complex of
`R`-modules.  Then `Hom^•(P, K)` is K-flat, and it represents `RHom_R(P, K)`: for every `n`, the
map sending a degree-`n` cohomology class of `Hom^•(P, K)` to the corresponding morphism
`P ⟶ K⟦n⟧` in `D(R)` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem homComplex_kFlat_and_represents_RHom [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
    (P K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (d : ℤ) [P.IsStrictlyLE d]
    [∀ i, Module.Projective R (P.X i)]
    (hP : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)) (hK : K.KFlat) :
    (HomComplexR R P K).KFlat ∧
      ∀ n : ℤ, Function.Bijective
        (fun (c : CohomologyClass P K n) =>
          DerivedCategory.Qh.map (CohomologyClass.homAddEquiv c))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorHomInterchangeConstruction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYT.** For complexes `K`, `L`, `M` of modules on a ringed site there is a
canonical morphism of complexes of `O`-modules

`Tot(K ⊗_O SheafHom(M, L)) ⟶ SheafHom(M, Tot(K ⊗_O L))`,

namely the one sending each homogeneous local pure tensor `x ⊗ φ` to the local section
`m ↦ x ⊗ φ(m)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def tensorHomInterchangeConstruction : TensorHomInterchangeConstruction X
declarations.comment: the canonical morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorHomInterchange_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYT.** The interchange morphism is functorial in all three complexes at once:
covariant in the tensor factor `K` and in the target `L` of the internal Hom, contravariant in
its source `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorHomInterchange_natural (f : K ⟶ K') (g : L ⟶ L') (h : M' ⟶ M) :
    tensorHomInterchange X K L M ≫ homMap X h (tensorTotalMap X f g) =
      tensorTotalMap X f (homMap X h g) ≫ tensorHomInterchange X K' L' M'
declarations.comment: functoriality in all three complexes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedTensorHomInterchange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYU.** For objects `K`, `L`, `M` of `D(O)` there is a canonical morphism

`K ⊗^L_O RSheafHom(M, L) ⟶ RSheafHom(M, K ⊗^L_O L)`

in `D(O)`: on a K-flat representative `A` of `K`, a K-injective representative `I` of `L` and
an arbitrary representative `C` of `M` it is the interchange morphism of complexes of Stacks
0BYT, followed by the augmentation of `Tot(A ⊗_O I)` into a K-injective resolution.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorHomInterchange
    (K L M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj K).obj
        (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op M)).obj L) ⟶
      ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op M)).obj
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj K).obj L)
declarations.comment: the canonical morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedTensorHomInterchange_comparison
declarations.doc:
**The comparison of Stacks 0BYU with the interchange morphism of complexes of Stacks
0BYT.** For complexes `A`, `I`, `C` with `A` K-flat and `I` K-injective, the canonical morphism
on their classes is, after the two identifications

`QA ⊗^L_O RSheafHom(QC, QI) ≅ Q Tot(A ⊗_O SheafHom(C, I))` and
`RSheafHom(QC, QA ⊗^L_O QI) ≅ Q SheafHom(C, J)` with `J` the chosen K-injective resolution of
`Tot(A ⊗_O I)`,

the class of the interchange morphism of complexes `Tot(A ⊗_O SheafHom(C, I)) ⟶
SheafHom(C, Tot(A ⊗_O I))` followed by the resolution augmentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedTensorHomInterchange_comparison
    (A I C : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
    (hA : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsKFlat X.O A) [I.IsKInjective] :
    derivedTensorHomInterchange X (DerivedCategory.Q.obj A) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I)
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj C) ≫
        (interchangeTargetIso X A I C hA).hom =
      (interchangeSourceIso X A I C hA).hom ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (tensorHomInterchange X A I C ≫
          homMap X (𝟙 C) ((kInjectiveAugmentation X).app (tensorTotal X A I)))
declarations.comment: comparison with the interchange morphism of complexes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedTensorHomInterchange_natural
declarations.doc:
**Functoriality of the interchange morphism of Stacks 0BYU in all three objects.** For
morphisms `k : K ⟶ K'`, `l : L ⟶ L'` and `m : M' ⟶ M` of `D(O)` the square formed by the
canonical morphism at `(K, L, M)` and at `(K', L', M')` commutes: the interchange morphism is
natural covariantly in the tensor factor and in the target of the internal Hom and
contravariantly in its source.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedTensorHomInterchange_natural
    {K K' L L' M M' :
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (k : K ⟶ K') (l : L ⟶ L') (m : M' ⟶ M) :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).map k).app
          (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op M)).obj L) ≫
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj K').map
          (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).map m.op).app L ≫
            ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op M')).map l) ≫
        derivedTensorHomInterchange X K' L' M' =
      derivedTensorHomInterchange X K L M ≫
        ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).map m.op).app
            (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj K).obj L) ≫
          ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op M')).map
            (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).map k).app L ≫
              ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj K').map l)
declarations.comment: functoriality in all three objects

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedPrecomp
declarations.doc:
Precomposition with a homomorphism `f : M ⟶ N` of differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodules
induces a natural transformation `RHom(N, -) ⟹ RHom(M, -)` of derived Hom functors
`D(B, d) ⥤ D(A, d)`.
declarations.statement: def derivedPrecomp (f : M ⟶ N) : DN.functor ⟶ DM.functor
declarations.comment: the natural transformation

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedPrecomp_comparison
declarations.doc:
The derived transformation is compatible with the canonical comparison maps from ordinary
internal hom to derived Hom.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPrecomp_comparison (f : M ⟶ N) :
    DN.comparison ≫
        Functor.whiskerLeft (quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q (derivedPrecomp DN DM f) =
      precompToDerivedNatTrans f ≫ DM.comparison
declarations.comment: compatibility with the comparison maps

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedPrecomp_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYV**, the last assertion. If a homomorphism `f : M ⟶ N` of differential graded
`(A, B)`-bimodules is a quasi-isomorphism of the underlying right differential graded
`B`-modules, then the induced transformation `RHom(N, -) ⟹ RHom(M, -)` of derived Hom functors
is an isomorphism.

Nothing is assumed: `DN` and `DM` range over all right derived functors of internal Hom out of
the two bimodules, of which the ones of Tag 09LI
(`DifferentialGradedModule.derivedHomData`) are instances.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPrecomp_isIso
    (DN : DerivedHomData A B N.rightModule N.leftAction)
    (DM : DerivedHomData A B M.rightModule M.leftAction)
    (f : M ⟶ N) (hf : QuasiIso ((forgetToCochainComplex B).map f.rightHom)) :
    IsIso (derivedPrecomp DN DM f)
declarations.comment: quasi-isomorphisms induce natural isomorphisms

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.DerivedHomData.isIso_comparison_of_bijective_q_map
declarations.doc:
If `Hom_{D(B,d)}(N, N') = Hom_{K(Mod_{(B,d)})}(N, N')` for all `N' ∈ K(B, d)`, then
`RHom(N, M) = Hom_{Mod^{dg}_{(B,d)}}(N, M)` functorially in `M` in `D(B, d)`.

The equality of morphism modules is the hypothesis `hN`, that the localization
`Q : K(B, d) ⥤ D(B, d)` is bijective on the morphisms out of `N`. The functorial equality of the
conclusion is the invertibility of the comparison natural transformation of Tag 09LI, from
ordinary differential graded Hom out of `N` read in `D(A, d)` to derived Hom precomposed with the
localization; `DifferentialGradedModule.DerivedHomData.comparisonNatIso` is the resulting
isomorphism of functors.

Under the hypothesis the functor being derived already inverts the quasi-isomorphisms
(`DifferentialGradedModule.isInvertedBy_homToDerivedCategory_of_bijective_q_map`), and the
comparison of any right derived functor of a functor that inverts them is invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_comparison_of_bijective_q_map (D : DerivedHomData A B N L)
    (hN : ∀ P : HomotopyCategory B, Function.Bijective
      ((quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q.map : ((toHomotopyCategory B).obj N ⟶ P) → _)) :
    IsIso D.comparison
declarations.comment: the comparison under the Hom hypothesis

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.DerivedHomData.isIso_comparison_of_propertyP
declarations.doc:
A differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule whose underlying `B`-module has property (P) computes
derived Hom by ordinary differential graded Hom, canonically and naturally in the second argument.

A module with property (P) is orthogonal on the left to the acyclic modules, which is Tag 09KM,
and the localization is bijective on the morphisms out of such a module, which is the mechanism of
Tag 09KY; so the hypothesis of the previous statement holds.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_comparison_of_propertyP (D : DerivedHomData A B N L)
    (hN : Nonempty (PropertyPFiltration N)) :
    IsIso D.comparison
declarations.comment: the property-(P) sufficient condition

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.DerivedHomData.comparisonNatIso
declarations.doc:
**`RHom(N, -) = Hom_{Mod^{dg}_{(B,d)}}(N, -)` as functors.** Ordinary differential graded Hom
out of `N`, read in `D(A, d)`, is derived Hom out of `N` precomposed with the localization, by the
comparison map of Tag 09LI and naturally in the second argument.
declarations.statement:
def comparisonNatIso (D : DerivedHomData A B N L)
    (hN : ∀ P : HomotopyCategory B, Function.Bijective
      ((quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q.map : ((toHomotopyCategory B).obj N ⟶ P) → _)) :
    homToDerivedCategory A B N L ≅ (quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q ⋙ D.functor
declarations.comment: as an identification of functors

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.General.homComplexExtEquiv
declarations.doc:
**`H^n(Hom^•_{(A, d)}(L, M)) = Ext^n_{D(A, d)}(L, M)`**, at independent universes, for `L`
orthogonal on the left to the acyclic modules.

This is the content that Tag 0CS5 and Tag 0BYW together provide, in the form Tag 0CS6 asks for:
Tag 09LC identifies the cohomology of the Hom complex with the morphism groups of `K(A, d)`
(`DifferentialGradedModule.General.homComplexHomologyEquiv`), and the localization functor is
bijective on the morphisms out of a left-orthogonal object
(`DifferentialGradedModule.General.bijective_q_map_of_leftOrthogonal`), which is the mechanism of
Tag 09KY; the shift is moved across the localization by its commutation with the translation.

With `Ext^n_{D(A, d)}(L, M) = Hom_{D(A, d)}(L, M[n])`, as everywhere in Tag 0CS6, the right-hand
side is that `Ext`-group.
declarations.statement:
def homComplexExtEquiv (n : ℤ)
    (hL : (acyclic.{u, v, w} A).leftOrthogonal ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj L)) :
    ↥((homComplex A L M).homology n) ≃+
      ((quasiIsomorphisms.{u, v, w} A).Q.obj ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj L) ⟶
        ((quasiIsomorphisms.{u, v, w} A).Q.obj ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj M))⟦n⟧)
declarations.comment: ordinary differential graded Hom out of a left-orthogonal module computes derived Hom, read on cohomology, at independent universes

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.General.homComplexExtEquivOfPropertyP
declarations.doc:
**`H^n(Hom^•_{(A, d)}(L, M)) = Ext^n_{D(A, d)}(L, M)` for `L` with property (P)**, at
independent universes.

A differential graded module with property (P) is orthogonal on the left to the acyclic modules,
which is Tag 09KM at independent universes
(`DifferentialGradedModule.General.leftOrthogonal_acyclic_of_propertyP`), so the previous
identification applies. This is the source's own sufficient condition in Tag 0BYW.
declarations.statement:
def homComplexExtEquivOfPropertyP {L M : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, v, max v w} A} (n : ℤ)
    (hL : Nonempty (PropertyPFiltration L)) :
    ↥((homComplex A L M).homology n) ≃+
      ((quasiIsomorphisms.{u, v, max v w} A).Q.obj ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj L) ⟶
        ((quasiIsomorphisms.{u, v, max v w} A).Q.obj ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj M))⟦n⟧)
declarations.comment: the property-(P) sufficient condition, read on cohomology, at independent universes

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.propertyPModelExtEquiv
declarations.doc:
**`H^n(Hom^•_{(A, d)}(P_M, P_N)) = Ext^n_{D(A, d)}(M, N)` for arbitrary `M`, `N` in
`D(A, d)`**, where `P_M` and `P_N` are the chosen property-(P) representatives.

This is the content of Tag 0BYW with no hypothesis on `M` or `N`: the property-(P) reduction is
performed by the choice of representative rather than assumed. On the representatives it is
`DifferentialGradedModule.General.homComplexExtEquivOfPropertyP`, and the two isomorphisms
`DifferentialGradedModule.propertyPModelIso` transport the `Ext`-group from the representatives
to the objects, the shift being moved across by the commutation of the shift functor with an
isomorphism.
declarations.comment: the cohomology of the differential graded Hom complex of chosen property-(P) representatives is Ext between the objects they represent, at independent universes

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorRegularRightNatIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYX, the tensor half, on differential graded modules.** Restriction of scalars
along `ψ : C → B` is tensoring with the regular `(B, C)`-bimodule, naturally in the module.

Naturality is an equality of two homomorphisms out of a tensor product, so it is checked on pure
tensors, where both sides send `x ⊗ b` to `f(x) b`.
declarations.statement:
def tensorRegularRightNatIso (ψ : C.Hom B) :
    tensorCompFunctor (regularRight ψ) ≅ restrictScalarsFunctor ψ
declarations.comment: restriction of scalars is tensoring with the regular bimodule, on differential graded modules

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorRegularRightIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYX, the tensor half, on derived categories.** Derived restriction of scalars
along `ψ : C → B` is the derived tensor product with the regular `(B, C)`-bimodule.

Tensoring with the regular bimodule already inverts the quasi-isomorphisms, so by the
construction of the derived tensor product in the proof of Tag 09LS it computes the derived
tensor product; and it descends to derived restriction of scalars through the localizations.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorRegularRightIso (ψ : C.Hom B) :
    derivedTensorFunctor (regularRight ψ) ≅ derivedRestriction ψ
declarations.comment: restriction of scalars is tensoring with the regular bimodule, on derived categories

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.regularHomFactorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYX.** Internal Hom out of the regular differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule,
followed by localization of the target, factors through the derived category of `B` as derived
restriction of scalars along `φ`.

This is the composite of the identification of internal Hom out of the regular bimodule with
restriction of scalars (`DifferentialGradedModule.homHomotopyFunctorRegularIso`) and the
defining factorisation of derived restriction
(`DifferentialGradedModule.derivedRestrictionFactorization`).
declarations.comment: the factorization of derived Hom out of the regular bimodule

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.DerivedHomData.regular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYX, and Stacks 09LI for the regular bimodule.** Derived Hom out of the regular
differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule of a homomorphism `φ : A → B`, as a right derived functor
of internal Hom — unconditionally, with the derived functor being the already-constructed
`DifferentialGradedModule.derivedRestriction`.

No resolutions are used: the hypothesis of
`DifferentialGradedModule.DerivedHomData.ofResolutions` — the existence of property (I)
resolutions, Tag 09KU — does not appear, because internal Hom out of the regular bimodule is
restriction of scalars, which does not change the underlying complex and therefore already
inverts the quasi-isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
def regular (φ : A.Hom B) :
    DerivedHomData A B (regularModule B) (regularBimoduleStructure φ)
declarations.comment: derived Hom out of the regular bimodule, as a right derived functor

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.DerivedHomData.functorIsoDerivedRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYX, Example 22.33.2.** `RHom(B, -) = (-)_A`: the functor of *any* right derived
functor of Hom out of the regular differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule is canonically derived
restriction of scalars along `φ`.
declarations.comment: RHom(B, -) is restriction of scalars, for any derived Hom datum

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.regularBimoduleStructure
declarations.doc:
A homomorphism `φ : A → B` of differential graded algebras makes the regular right differential
graded `B`-module into a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule: `A` acts on the left by
multiplication through `φ`, and that action is right `B`-linear by associativity.
declarations.statement: def regularBimoduleStructure (φ : A.Hom B) : BimoduleStructure A B (regularModule B)
declarations.comment: the regular bimodule structure

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.regularHomogeneousEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Evaluation at one.** The degree-`n` homogeneous right `B`-linear maps out of the regular
differential graded `B`-module are the degree-`n` elements of the target, by evaluation at the
unit. This is the degreewise half of Example 22.33.2.
declarations.statement:
def regularHomogeneousEquiv (P : DifferentialGradedModule B) (n : ℤ) :
    P.grading n ≃ₗ[R] HomogeneousMap B (regularModule B) P n
declarations.comment: evaluation at one, degreewise

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.restrictScalarsFunctor
declarations.doc:
Restriction of scalars along `φ`, as a functor between the categories of differential graded
modules. A homomorphism is unchanged: a `B`-linear map is `A`-linear through `φ`.
declarations.statement:
def restrictScalarsFunctor (φ : A.Hom B) :
    DifferentialGradedModule B ⥤ DifferentialGradedModule A
declarations.comment: restriction of scalars as a functor

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.restrictScalarsHomotopyFunctor
declarations.doc:
Restriction of scalars along `φ` on the homotopy categories: it descends through the homotopy
quotient because it preserves homotopies.
declarations.statement: def restrictScalarsHomotopyFunctor (φ : A.Hom B) : HomotopyCategory B ⥤ HomotopyCategory A
declarations.comment: restriction of scalars on homotopy categories

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.derivedRestriction
declarations.doc:
Restriction of scalars along `φ` on the derived categories, obtained by descending restriction
on the homotopy categories through the localization at the quasi-isomorphisms. This is the functor
`R Hom(B, -) : D(B, d) ⥤ D(A, d)` of Example 22.33.2, whose identification with derived Hom out of
the regular bimodule is the content of that example.
declarations.statement: def derivedRestriction (φ : A.Hom B) : derivedCategory' B ⥤ derivedCategory' A
declarations.comment: restriction of scalars on derived categories

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.derivedRestrictionFactorization
declarations.doc:
Derived restriction of scalars is restriction of scalars read through the localizations: the
square of homotopy and derived categories commutes up to this canonical isomorphism.
declarations.comment: the factorization of derived restriction

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.regularHomModuleData
declarations.doc:
Restriction of scalars along `φ` presents the internal hom out of the regular differential
graded `(A, B)`-bimodule: its degree-`n` part is the degree-`n` homogeneous right `B`-linear maps
`B → P`, by evaluation at the unit, and the right `A`-action matches precomposition with
multiplication through `φ`.
declarations.statement:
def regularHomModuleData (φ : A.Hom B) (P : DifferentialGradedModule B) :
    HomModuleData A B (regularModule B) P (regularBimoduleStructure φ)
declarations.comment: restriction of scalars presents the internal hom

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.homModuleRegularIso
declarations.doc:
Evaluation at the unit identifies the internal hom out of the regular differential graded
`(A, B)`-bimodule with restriction of scalars along `φ`.
declarations.statement:
def homModuleRegularIso (φ : A.Hom B) (P : DifferentialGradedModule B) :
    (regularHomFunctor φ).obj P ≅ (restrictScalarsFunctor φ).obj P
declarations.comment: evaluation at one

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.homModuleFunctorRegularIso
declarations.doc:
Evaluation at one is natural: the internal hom functor out of the regular differential graded
`(A, B)`-bimodule is restriction of scalars along `φ`.
declarations.statement:
def homModuleFunctorRegularIso (φ : A.Hom B) :
    regularHomFunctor φ ≅ restrictScalarsFunctor φ
declarations.comment: evaluation at one is natural

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.homHomotopyFunctorRegularIso
declarations.doc:
Evaluation at one on homotopy categories: the internal hom functor out of the regular
differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule is restriction of scalars along `φ`. This is the
identification `R Hom(B, -) = (-)_A` of Example 22.33.2, before localizing.
declarations.comment: evaluation at one on homotopy categories

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.quasiIsomorphisms_isInvertedBy_homToDerivedCategory_regular
declarations.doc:
The functor whose right derived functor is derived Hom out of the regular differential graded
`(A, B)`-bimodule already inverts the quasi-isomorphisms: it is restriction of scalars followed by
localization, and restriction does not change the underlying complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIsomorphisms_isInvertedBy_homToDerivedCategory_regular (φ : A.Hom B) :
    (quasiIsomorphisms' B).IsInvertedBy
      (homToDerivedCategory A B (regularModule B) (regularBimoduleStructure φ))
declarations.comment: derived Hom out of the regular bimodule needs no resolutions

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.regular
declarations.doc:
The regular differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule of a homomorphism `φ : A → B` of differential
graded algebras: `B` itself, with `B` acting on the right by multiplication and `A` acting on the
left through `φ`. Tensoring with it is the extension of scalars `- ⊗_A B : D(A, d) ⥤ D(B, d)` of
Example 22.33.2.
declarations.statement: def regular (φ : A.Hom B) : Bimodule A B
declarations.comment: the regular bimodule

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.derivedHom_comparison_eq_evaluationAtOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYX, Example 22.33.2.** The identification of derived Hom out of the regular
differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule with derived restriction of scalars is pinned by evaluation
at the unit: on the class of a differential graded `B`-module `N`, the canonical comparison of the
derived functor with internal Hom, followed by the identification with derived restriction and the
factorisation of derived restriction, is the localisation of the evaluation morphism
`Hom^•_B(B, N) → N_A, f ↦ f(1)`, transported along the identification
`DifferentialGradedModule.homHomotopyFunctorRegularIso` of the two source objects.

The transport is not optional: internal Hom out of the regular bimodule is isomorphic to
restriction of scalars and not equal to it, so the two morphisms have different sources.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedHom_comparison_eq_evaluationAtOne (φ : A.Hom B)
    (D : DerivedHomData A B (regularModule B) (regularBimoduleStructure φ))
    (N : DifferentialGradedModule B) :
    D.comparison.app ((toHomotopyCategory B).obj N) ≫
        (DerivedHomData.functorIsoDerivedRestriction φ D).hom.app
          ((quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q.obj ((toHomotopyCategory B).obj N)) ≫
        (derivedRestrictionFactorization φ).hom.app ((toHomotopyCategory B).obj N) =
      (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q.map
