          ((homHomotopyFunctorRegularIso φ).hom.app ((toHomotopyCategory B).obj N)) ≫
        (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q.map
          ((toHomotopyCategory A).map ((evaluationAtOne φ).evaluation N))
declarations.comment: the comparison of derived Hom out of the regular bimodule is evaluation at one

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor_adj_derivedRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYX, Example 22.33.2.** For a homomorphism `φ : (A, d) → (B, d)` of differential
graded algebras, derived extension of scalars `- ⊗_A^𝐋 B : D(A, d) ⥤ D(B, d)` — tensoring with
the regular bimodule, `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.regular` — is left adjoint to derived
restriction of scalars `(-)_A : D(B, d) ⥤ D(A, d)`. Nothing is assumed.

This is the displayed formula of the example,
`Hom_{D(A,d)}(M, N_A) = Hom_{D(B,d)}(M ⊗_A^𝐋 B, N)`, *bifunctorially in `M` and `N`*: an
`CategoryTheory.Adjunction` is exactly a bijection of the two morphism groups together with its
naturality in both variables, so the bifunctoriality the source asserts is carried by this
statement and needs no separate lemma. The bijection on its own is
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor_adj_derivedRestriction_homEquiv`.

The two inputs are the two steps the example takes. The adjunction with derived Hom out of the
regular bimodule on the right is Tag 09LT,
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor_adj_derivedHomFunctor`; and
`DifferentialGradedModule.DerivedHomData.functorIsoDerivedRestriction` is the example's
identification `RHom(B, -) = (-)_A`, which comes from `Hom_{Mod^{dg}_B}(B, N) ≅ N_A`, `f ↦ f(1)`,
naturally in `N`. Transporting the right adjoint along that isomorphism replaces `RHom(B, -)` by
restriction of scalars, which is the example's conclusion.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorFunctor_adj_derivedRestriction (φ : A.Hom B) :
    derivedTensorFunctor (Bimodule.regular φ) ⊣ derivedRestriction φ
declarations.comment: the adjunction Hom_{D(A,d)}(M, N_A) = Hom_{D(B,d)}(M ⊗_A^𝐋 B, N), bifunctorially

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor_adj_derivedRestriction_homEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYX, Example 22.33.2**, the displayed formula itself:
`Hom_{D(A,d)}(M, N_A) = Hom_{D(B,d)}(M ⊗_A^𝐋 B, N)`.

It is the hom-set bijection of
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor_adj_derivedRestriction`, so the
bifunctoriality in `M` and `N` that the source asserts is the naturality carried by that
adjunction; it is not restated here.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorFunctor_adj_derivedRestriction_homEquiv (φ : A.Hom B)
    (M : derivedCategory' A) (N : derivedCategory' B) :
    (M ⟶ (derivedRestriction φ).obj N) ≃
      ((derivedTensorFunctor (Bimodule.regular φ)).obj M ⟶ N)
declarations.comment: the displayed formula Hom_{D(A,d)}(M, N_A) = Hom_{D(B,d)}(M ⊗_A^𝐋 B, N)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.evaluationAtOne
declarations.doc:
Evaluation at the unit identifies the graded Hom from `B` with restriction to `A`,
naturally in the differential graded `B`-module.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def evaluationAtOne (φ : A.Hom B) :
    EvaluationAtOneData φ
declarations.comment: evaluation_at_one

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.restrictScalars
declarations.doc:
Restrict a right differential graded `B`-module to `A` along a homomorphism of differential
graded algebras.
declarations.statement:
def restrictScalars (φ : A.Hom B) (N : DifferentialGradedModule B) :
    DifferentialGradedModule A
declarations.comment: restriction_notation

declarations.name: Dualizing.derivedExtensionToDGA_adj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYX for the structure homomorphism of `E`, read on `D(R)`.** Derived extension of
scalars `- ⊗_R^𝐋 E : D(R) ⥤ D(E, d)` is left adjoint to the forgetful functor
`D(E, d) ⥤ D(R)`.

The adjunction of Tag 0BYX is between derived extension and derived restriction of scalars along
`R → E`; transporting its right adjoint along `Dualizing.derivedRestrictBaseForgetIso`, which
identifies derived restriction read on `D(R)` with the forgetful functor, gives the statement in
the form Situation 0BZB uses.
declarations.statement:
def derivedExtensionToDGA_adj (E : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R) :
    derivedExtensionToDGA E ⊣ derivedForget E
declarations.comment: extension of scalars along R -> E is left adjoint to forgetting the action

declarations.name: Dualizing.derivedTensorResolvingBimoduleForgetIso
declarations.doc:
**The tensor half of Stacks 0BYX for the structure homomorphism of `E`.** Derived tensoring
with the resolving bimodule `E`, read in the derived category of `R`-modules through the
degree-zero equivalence, is the forgetful functor `D(E, d) ⥤ D(R)`: forgetting the `E`-action is
restriction of scalars along `R → E`, which is tensoring with the regular `(E, R)`-bimodule.
declarations.comment: forgetting the action is derived tensoring with the regular (E, R)-bimodule

declarations.name: Dualizing.DGAResolution.derivedTensorResolvingBimoduleIso
declarations.doc:
**The tensor half of Stacks 0BYX at the resolving algebra of Situation 0BZB.** Derived
tensoring with the resolving bimodule of `E`, read in the derived category of `R`-modules, is
the forgetful functor `D(E, d) ⥤ D(R)`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorResolvingBimoduleIso (S : Dualizing.DGAResolution R A) :
    Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor (Dualizing.resolvingBimodule S.E) ⋙
        (degreeZeroDerivedEquivalence (R := R) (A := R)).functor ≅
      DifferentialGradedModule.derivedForget S.E
declarations.comment: forgetting the action of the resolving algebra is derived tensoring with its regular (E, R)-bimodule

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedBaseChangeFunctor_isLeftDerivedFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYZ, part (1).** The derived tensor product `- ⊗_A^𝐋 A'` with the base change
`A' = A ⊗_R R'` is the total left derived functor of base change
`K(A, d) → K(A', d)`, `M ↦ M ⊗_R R'`, followed by localization.

The functor derived here is `M ↦ M ⊗_A A'`; it is base change `M ↦ M ⊗_R R'` by the canonical map
`c_M` of the source's proof, which is `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.baseChangeTensorIso` as an
isomorphism of differential graded `R'`-modules and
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.baseChangeTensorAlgebraIso` as one of differential graded
`A'`-modules. Part (3) is
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isIso_derivedBaseChangeCounit_app_of_kFlat` of
`StacksFrontier/Algebra/DifferentialGraded/Module/BaseChangeRepresents.lean` and part (2) is
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedBaseChangeRestrictionSquare` of
`StacksFrontier/Algebra/DifferentialGraded/Module/BaseChangeRestrictionSquare.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedBaseChangeFunctor_isLeftDerivedFunctor :
    (derivedBaseChangeFunctor A R').IsLeftDerivedFunctor
      (derivedBaseChangeCounit A R') (quasiIsomorphisms' A)
declarations.comment: part (1) only, with the functor being derived presented as M |-> M (x)_A A': the identification c_M with the source's M |-> M (x)_R R' is baseChangeTensorIso over R' and baseChangeTensorAlgebraIso over A'. Corrected: the source says "right derived functor", but base change is a tensor product and so is LEFT derived, as Tag 09LS has it. Parts (2) and (3) are elsewhere, per the docstrings; nothing of Tag 0BYZ remains uncovered

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.baseChangeTensorAlgebraIso
declarations.doc:
**The `A'`-linearity of the canonical map `c_M` in the proof of Stacks 0BYZ.** Let `R → R'`
be a map of commutative rings, let `(A, d)` be a differential graded `R`-algebra and let
`A' = A ⊗_R R'` be its base change. For a differential graded `A`-module `M` the base change
`M ⊗_A A'` is `M ⊗_R R'` **as a differential graded `A'`-module**, the right action of `a ⊗ s`
on `M ⊗_R R'` being `(m ⊗ t) · (a ⊗ s) = (m · a) ⊗ (t s)`
(`DifferentialGradedModule.baseChange_smul_tmul`).

The isomorphism is the source's `c_M`, read in the direction out of the relative tensor product:
it sends the pure tensor `x ⊗ (a ⊗ s)` to `(x · a) ⊗ s`
(`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.baseChangeTensorForward_pure`), and its inverse — the source's
`c_M` itself — sends `x ⊗ s` to `x ⊗ (1 ⊗ s)`.
declarations.statement:
def baseChangeTensorAlgebraIso :
    baseChangeRelativeTensor A R' M ≅ baseChangeAbsoluteTensor M R'
declarations.comment: the A'-linearity of the canonical map c_M of the PROOF, NOT any of parts (1), (2), (3): M (x)_A A' is M (x)_R R' as differential graded A'-modules, the right action on M (x)_R R' being (m (x) t)(a (x) s) = (m a) (x) (t s). With this nothing of Tag 0BYZ is left unformalized; the module docstring says where the three parts and the R'-only form baseChangeTensorIso are, and how this A'-module restricts to that R'-module

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isIso_derivedBaseChangeCounit_app_of_kFlat
declarations.doc:
Let `R → R'` be a ring map, `(A, d)` a differential graded `R`-algebra which is K-flat as a
complex of `R`-modules, and `A' = A ⊗_R R'`. For a differential graded `A`-module `M` which is
K-flat as a complex of `R`-modules, the comparison from the derived base change `M ⊗_A^𝐋 A'` to
the ordinary base change `M ⊗_A A'` is an isomorphism at `M`, so `M ⊗_A A'` represents
`M ⊗_A^𝐋 A'`. Nothing is asked of `R'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedBaseChangeCounit_app_of_kFlat
    (hA : CochainComplex.KFlat.{u, u} (regularModule A).toCochainComplex)
    (M : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A)
    (hM : CochainComplex.KFlat.{u, u} M.toCochainComplex) :
    IsIso ((derivedBaseChangeCounit A R').app ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj M))
declarations.comment: part (3): M K-flat as a complex of R-modules implies that the ordinary base change represents M (x)_A^L A'. The representing object is spelled M (x)_A A'; it is the source's differential graded A'-module M (x)_R R' by baseChangeTensorIso over R' and by baseChangeTensorAlgebraIso of BaseChangeAbsoluteTensor.lean over A'. Part (2) is derivedBaseChangeRestrictionSquare of BaseChangeRestrictionSquare.lean

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedBaseChangeRestrictionSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BYZ, part (2).** *"Let `R → R'` be a ring map, let `(A, d)` be a differential
graded `R`-algebra, let `(A', d)` be the base change `A ⊗_R R'`. If `A` is K-flat as a complex of
`R`-modules, then the diagram*
```
D(A, d) --- - ⊗_A^𝐋 A' ---> D(A', d)
   |                           |
restriction                restriction
   v                           v
 D(R)  --- - ⊗_R^𝐋 R' --->   D(R')
```
*commutes."*

The two columns are restriction of scalars along the structure homomorphism `R → A` of
`DifferentialGradedAlgebra.baseHom` and along `r' ↦ 1 ⊗ r'`; the bottom edge is
derived base change of the base ring in degree zero, read in `D(R', d)` through
`DifferentialGradedAlgebra.degreeZeroBaseChangeUnitor`, whose derived restriction is the
equivalence `DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroBaseChangeEquivalence`.

Both composites are left derived functors of the same functor `K(A, d) ⥤ D(R', d)`,
`M ↦ M ⊗_R R'`: the comparison `c_M` of the plain functors is an isomorphism for every `M`
(`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isIso_baseChangeStructureTensorTrans_app`), and the left-hand
composite's own comparison is invertible at the modules with property (P) — which is where the
K-flatness of `A` is used, through
`DifferentialGradedModule.kFlat_toCochainComplex_of_propertyPFiltration` and part (3) in the
form `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isIso_derivedTensorBimoduleCounit_app_of_kFlat`. So the square
commutes by the uniqueness of a left derived functor.
declarations.statement:
def derivedBaseChangeRestrictionSquare
    (hA : CochainComplex.KFlat.{u, u} (regularModule A).toCochainComplex) :
    derivedBaseChangeFunctor A R' ⋙
        derivedRestriction (tensorIncludeRightHom A (degreeZero R R')) ≅
      derivedRestriction (baseHom A) ⋙
        derivedBaseChangeFunctor (degreeZero R R) R' ⋙
          derivedRestriction (tensorIncludeRightHom (degreeZero R R) (degreeZero R R'))
declarations.comment: part (2): the square of restriction and derived base change commutes. The left column is restriction along the structure homomorphism R -> A, the right column restriction along r' |-> 1 (x) r', and the bottom edge derived base change of R in degree zero read in D(R', d) through the unitor R (x)_R R' = R' of degreeZeroBaseChangeUnitor. Parts (1) and (3) are derivedBaseChangeFunctor_isLeftDerivedFunctor and isIso_derivedBaseChangeCounit_app_of_kFlat

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.baseChangeTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map `c_M` in the proof of Stacks 0BYZ, over `R'`.** Let `R → R'` be a ring
map, let `(A, d)` be a differential graded `R`-algebra and let `A' = A ⊗_R R'` be its base change.
For a differential graded `A`-module `M` the differential graded `R'`-module underlying the base
change `M ⊗_A A'` is `M ⊗_R R'`.

The source's `c_M : M ⊗_R R' → M ⊗_A A'` is a map of differential graded `A'`-modules; this is
that map after restricting the right action from `A'` to `R'`, which is where its content lies:
restricting the right action does not change the relative tensor product
(`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorCompFunctorRestrictRightIso`), and over `R'` the base-change
bimodule is the one for which `M ⊗_A (A ⊗_R R') = M ⊗_R R'` is already proved
(`DifferentialGraded.absBalanceIso`). The `A'`-linear statement, which needs `M ⊗_R R'` built as
a differential graded `A ⊗_R R'`-module and is proved by the universal property rather than by
this transfer, is `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.baseChangeTensorAlgebraIso` in
`StacksFrontier/Algebra/DifferentialGraded/Module/BaseChangeAbsoluteTensor.lean`.
declarations.statement:
def baseChangeTensorIso (M : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A) :
    (restrictScalarsFunctor (tensorIncludeRightHom A (degreeZero R R'))).obj
        ((tensorCompFunctor (baseChange A R')).obj M) ≅
      M.absoluteTensor (degreeZero R R')
declarations.comment: the canonical map c_M of the PROOF, over R' — NOT any of parts (1), (2), (3). It is what identifies the functor derived in part (1), derivedBaseChangeFunctor_isLeftDerivedFunctor of BaseChange.lean, with the source's M |-> M (x)_R R'. Part (2) is derivedBaseChangeRestrictionSquare, part (3) isIso_derivedBaseChangeCounit_app_of_kFlat. The A'-linear form of this map, which is what the source states, is baseChangeTensorAlgebraIso

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.kFlat_toCochainComplex_of_propertyPFiltration
declarations.doc:
**A differential graded module with property (P) over a differential graded algebra which is
K-flat as a complex of `R`-modules is itself K-flat as a complex of `R`-modules.** This is the
K-flatness half of the claim in the proof of Stacks 0BYZ.

The induction is `DifferentialGradedModule.propertyPFiltration_induction`; its five obligations
are, in order, that K-flatness is invariant under isomorphism, that it holds on a direct sum of
shifts of `A`, that it is stable under countable direct sums, and the two directions of
two-out-of-three along an admissible short exact sequence. The hypothesis on `A` enters only in
the second.
declarations.statement:
theorem kFlat_toCochainComplex_of_propertyPFiltration
    (hA : CochainComplex.KFlat.{u, u} (regularModule A).toCochainComplex)
    {P : DifferentialGradedModule A} (F : PropertyPFiltration P) :
    CochainComplex.KFlat.{u, u} P.toCochainComplex
declarations.comment: the K-flatness half of the claim in the PROOF — a differential graded A-module with property (P) is K-flat as a complex of R-modules. Not any of parts (1), (2), (3); part (1) is DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedBaseChangeFunctor_isLeftDerivedFunctor

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.homDualBimodule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZ0**, first assertion. For a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule `T`, the
internal hom `S = Hom_{Mod^{dg}_{(B, d)}}(T, B)` is a differential graded `(B, A)`-bimodule: the
right `A`-action is precomposition with the left action of `A` on `T`, and the left `B`-action is
postcomposition with left multiplication on `B`.
declarations.statement: def homDualBimodule (T : Bimodule A B) : Bimodule B A
declarations.comment: the (B, A)-bimodule structure on S = Hom(T, B)

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorHomDualFunctorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZ0, second assertion.** Let `R` be a ring, let `(A, d)` and `(B, d)` be
differential graded `R`-algebras and let `T` be a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule. Assume

1. `T` defines a compact object of `D(B, d)`, and
2. `S = Hom_{Mod^{dg}_{(B, d)}}(T, B)` represents `R Hom(T, B)` in `D(A, d)`, that is, the
   comparison of Tag 09LI is invertible at the regular module.

Then there is an isomorphism `N ⊗_B^𝐋 S ⟶ R Hom(T, N)` functorial in `N` in `D(B, d)`: the
differential graded `(B, A)`-bimodule structure on `S` is
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.homDualBimodule`, and the functorial isomorphism is an isomorphism
of the two functors `D(B, d) ⥤ D(A, d)` of Tag 09LS and Tag 09LI.

The map itself is `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedEvalNatTrans`: the composition pairing of
Tag 09LC, read on differential graded modules and descended to the derived category, lifted
along the localization `K(B, d) ⥤ D(B, d)`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorHomDualFunctorIso (T : Bimodule A B)
    (h1 : IsCompactObject.{u}
      ((toHomotopyCategory B ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q).obj T.rightModule))
    (h2 : IsIso ((derivedHomData A B T.rightModule T.leftAction).comparison.app
      ((toHomotopyCategory B).obj (regularModule B)))) :
    derivedTensorFunctor (homDualBimodule T) ≅
      (derivedHomData A B T.rightModule T.leftAction).functor
declarations.comment: the second assertion: the functorial isomorphism N ⊗_B^L S ≅ RHom(T, N)

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctorCounit
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison from the derived tensor product to ordinary tensoring: the counit of
the Kan extension defining `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N`. Its components are the maps
`P ⊗_A^𝐋 N → P ⊗_A N` in `D(B, d)`, which are isomorphisms exactly on the objects at which
ordinary tensoring already computes the derived functor.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorFunctorCounit (N : Bimodule A B) :
    (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q ⋙ derivedTensorFunctor N ⟶ tensorFunctorToDerivedCategory N
declarations.comment: the canonical map from the derived to the plain tensor product

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.compTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0BZ3.** The composite of a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule `N` with a
differential graded `(B, C)`-bimodule `N'`: the relative tensor product `N ⊗_B N'` of the right
`B`-module underlying `N` with `N'`, carrying the left `A`-action inherited from `N`. This is the
bimodule `N''` of Tag 0BZ3.
declarations.statement: def compTensor (N : Bimodule A B) (N' : Bimodule B C) : Bimodule A C
declarations.comment: the composite bimodule N'' = N (x)_B N' as an (A, C)-bimodule

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctorCompTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0BZ3.** *"Let `R` be a ring. Let `(A, d)`, `(B, d)`, and `(C, d)` be differential
graded `R`-algebras. Let `N` be a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule. Let `N'` be a differential
graded `(B, C)`-bimodule. Assume that (0BZ2) `N_B ⊗_B^𝐋 N' ⟶ (N ⊗_B N')_C` is an isomorphism.
Then the composition `D(A, d) → D(B, d) → D(C, d)` of `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N` and `- ⊗_B^𝐋 N'` is isomorphic
to `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N''` where `N'' = N ⊗_B N'`."*

The bimodule `N''` is `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.compTensor N N'`, the relative tensor product
with the left `A`-action inherited from `N`, exactly as in the source; the isomorphism is
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorCompNatTrans`, the transformation attached to the
associativity isomorphism of the plain tensor functors by the universal property of Tag 09LS.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorFunctorCompTensorIso (N : Bimodule A B) (N' : Bimodule B C)
    (hiso : IsIso ((derivedTensorFunctorCounit N').app
      ((toHomotopyCategory B).obj N.rightModule))) :
    derivedTensorFunctor N ⋙ derivedTensorFunctor N' ≅
      derivedTensorFunctor (compTensor N N')
declarations.comment: composition of the derived tensor functors

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.isIso_derivedTensorBaseChangeComparison_degreeZeroBase
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map of Stacks 0BZ4 is an isomorphism when the first algebra is the base ring
in degree zero.** For differential graded `R`-algebras `(B, d)` and `(C, d)`, the map
`(R ⊗_R B)_B ⊗_B^𝐋 {}_B(B ⊗_R C)_C ⟶ (R ⊗_R B ⊗_R C)_C` of `D(C, d)` is invertible, with nothing
assumed about `B` or `C`.

By `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isIso_derivedTensorBaseChangeComparison_iff` the assertion is
that the comparison of Tag 09LS from the derived to the plain tensor product with
`{}_B(B ⊗_R C)_C` is invertible at the right differential graded `B`-module `(R ⊗_R B)_B`. That
module is the regular module, by `DifferentialGraded.unitBaseChangeIso`, and the regular module
is orthogonal on the left to the acyclic modules by Tag 09K1, where the plain tensor product
already computes the derived one.

This is the hypothesis that Stacks 0BZ5 assumes and that Stacks 09S4 discharges from K-flatness
of `C`; over the base ring no K-flatness is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedTensorBaseChangeComparison_degreeZeroBase
    (C : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R) :
    IsIso (derivedTensorBaseChangeComparison (degreeZero R R) B C)
declarations.comment: the canonical map is an isomorphism when the first algebra is the base ring in degree zero

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.tripleTensorIso
declarations.doc:
The identification
`(A ⊗_R B)_B ⊗_B {}_B(B ⊗_R C)_C = (A ⊗_R B ⊗_R C)_C`: the plain relative tensor product of the
two base-change bimodules is the triple tensor product, as right differential graded
`C`-modules.
declarations.statement: def tripleTensorIso : plainTensorObj A B C ≅ baseChangeModule (tensorProduct A B) C
declarations.comment: the identification of the plain tensor products

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.derivedTensorBaseChangeComparison
declarations.doc:
The canonical map
`(A ⊗_R B)_B ⊗_B^𝐋 {}_B(B ⊗_R C)_C ⟶ (A ⊗_R B ⊗_R C)_C` in `D(C, d)`. It is the comparison of
the derived with the plain tensor product at the right differential graded `B`-module
`A ⊗_R B`, followed by the identification of the plain tensor product
`(A ⊗_R B)_B ⊗_B {}_B(B ⊗_R C)_C` with `A ⊗_R B ⊗_R C`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorBaseChangeComparison :
    (Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor (baseChangeBimodule B C)).obj
        ((quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q.obj ((toHomotopyCategory B).obj (baseChangeModule A B))) ⟶
      (quasiIsomorphisms' C).Q.obj
        ((toHomotopyCategory C).obj (baseChangeModule (tensorProduct A B) C))
declarations.comment: the canonical map in D(C, d)

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctorCompIsoDegreeZeroBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZ5 when the first algebra is the base ring in degree zero**, with nothing assumed.
For a differential graded `R`-algebra `(C, d)`, a differential graded `(R, B)`-bimodule `N` and a
differential graded `(B, C)`-bimodule `N'`, the composite of `- ⊗_R^𝐋 N : D(R) ⥤ D(B, d)` and
`- ⊗_B^𝐋 N' : D(B, d) ⥤ D(C, d)` is the derived tensor functor of the differential graded
`(R, C)`-bimodule `N'' = Ñ ⊗_B Ñ'` of Stacks 0BZ3.

This is `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctorCompIsoOfBaseChange` with its only
hypothesis — the map of Tag 0BZ4, which Stacks 0BZ5 assumes to be an isomorphism — supplied by
`DifferentialGraded.isIso_derivedTensorBaseChangeComparison_degreeZeroBase`. Here `D(R)` is the
derived category of the base ring viewed as a differential graded algebra concentrated in degree
zero, which is the derived category of `R`-modules by
`DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroDerivedEquivalence`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorFunctorCompIsoDegreeZeroBase
    (C : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R)
    (N : Bimodule (degreeZero R R) B) (N' : Bimodule B C) :
    derivedTensorFunctor N ⋙ derivedTensorFunctor N' ≅
      derivedTensorFunctor (compTensorResolution N N')
declarations.comment: unconditionally when the first algebra is the base ring in degree zero

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.compTensorResolution
declarations.doc:
**The bimodule `N''` of Stacks Tag 0BZ5.** Given a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule `N`
and a differential graded `(B, C)`-bimodule `N'`, it is the composite `Ñ ⊗_B Ñ'` of their
property-(P) replacements, viewed as a differential graded `(A, C)`-bimodule.
declarations.statement: def compTensorResolution (N : Bimodule A B) (N' : Bimodule B C) : Bimodule A C
declarations.comment: the bimodule N'' described in the proof

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctorCompIsoOfBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZ5 with Tag 0BZ4 as its only hypothesis.** For differential graded algebras
`(A, d)`, `(B, d)` and `(C, d)` over `R` such that the canonical map
`(A ⊗_R B)_B ⊗_B^𝐋 {}_B(B ⊗_R C)_C ⟶ (A ⊗_R B ⊗_R C)_C` of Tag 0BZ4 is an isomorphism, the
composite of `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N` and `- ⊗_B^𝐋 N'` is isomorphic to `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N''` for the differential
graded `(A, C)`-bimodule `N'' = Ñ ⊗_B Ñ'` of the source.

This is `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctorCompIso` with all four of its remaining
inputs supplied: the second assertion of Tag 09S3 twice, Tag 0BZ3, and the dévissage of the
present proof.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorFunctorCompIsoOfBaseChange
    (hiso : IsIso (derivedTensorBaseChangeComparison A B C))
    (N : Bimodule A B) (N' : Bimodule B C) :
    derivedTensorFunctor N ⋙ derivedTensorFunctor N' ≅
      derivedTensorFunctor (compTensorResolution N N')
declarations.comment: the composite of the two derived tensor functors is the derived tensor functor of the composite bimodule, under the Tag 0BZ4 isomorphism that the source itself assumes

declarations.name: Stacks.DGA.exists_kFlat_freeGraded_resolution
declarations.doc:
Every differential graded algebra has a quasi-isomorphic K-flat resolution
which is free as a graded algebra.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_kFlat_freeGraded_resolution
    (B : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, max u v} R) :
    ∃ (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, max u v} R)
      (f : A.A →ₐ[R] B.A)
      (CA CB : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ)
      (eA : ModelsComplex A CA) (eB : ModelsComplex B CB)
      (g : CA ⟶ CB),
      IsFreeGradedAlgebra A ∧
        CA.KFlat ∧
      IsDGAMorphism A B f ∧
        (∀ (n : ℤ) (x : CA.X n),
          (eB.equiv n (g.f n x)).1 = f ((eA.equiv n x).1)) ∧
        QuasiIso g

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedAlgebra.exists_kFlat_resolution_bijective_cohomologyMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0BZ7, in the encoding Tag 09S6 consumes.** Every differential graded
`R`-algebra `(B, d)` admits a homomorphism `φ : (B', d) → (B, d)` of differential graded algebras
with `(B', d)` K-flat as a complex of `R`-modules and with `H^k(φ)` bijective for every `k`, i.e.
`φ` an isomorphism on cohomology algebras.

This is `Stacks.DGA.exists_kFlat_freeGraded_resolution` with its raw encoding converted: the
`Stacks.DGA.IsDGAMorphism` bundled by `DifferentialGradedAlgebra.Hom.ofIsDGAMorphism`, the
modelling complexes removed and their K-flatness transported to the canonical complex `B'^•` by
`Stacks.DGA.ModelsComplex.kFlat_regularModule`, and the quasi-isomorphism of complexes turned
into bijectivity on cohomology by
`DifferentialGradedAlgebra.Hom.bijective_cohomologyMap_of_quasiIso`. Freeness of `B'` as a graded
algebra, which Tag 0BZ7 also provides, is dropped: the reduction of Tag 0BZ8 to a K-flat middle
algebra uses only K-flatness.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_kFlat_resolution_bijective_cohomologyMap (B : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R) :
    ∃ (B' : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R) (φ : B'.Hom B),
      CochainComplex.KFlat.{u, u} (regularModule B').toCochainComplex ∧
        ∀ k : ℤ, Function.Bijective (φ.cohomologyMap k)
declarations.comment: the resolution read as a homomorphism of differential graded algebras which is K-flat over the base and bijective on cohomology in every degree, which is the hypothesis of Tag 09S6

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedAlgebra.exists_kFlat_resolution_derivedEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**The derived equivalence attached to the K-flat resolution of a differential graded
algebra.** Every differential graded `R`-algebra `(B, d)` is the target of a homomorphism
`φ : (B', d) → (B, d)` with `(B', d)` K-flat as a complex of `R`-modules along which extension of
scalars `- ⊗_{B'}^𝐋 B : D(B', d) → D(B, d)` is an equivalence of categories, with derived
restriction of scalars as quasi-inverse
(`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedExtensionEquivalence`).

This is Tag 0BZ7 followed by Tag 09S6, and it is the first ingredient of the reduction of
Tag 0BZ8 to a K-flat middle algebra; the second is the transport of the conclusion of Tag 0BZ8
through the three composites `D(A) → D(B) → D(B')`, `D(B') → D(B) → D(C)` and
`D(A) → D(B') → D(C)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_kFlat_resolution_derivedEquivalence (B : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R) :
    ∃ (B' : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R) (φ : B'.Hom B),
      CochainComplex.KFlat.{u, u} (regularModule B').toCochainComplex ∧
        (DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor
          (DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.regular φ)).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the resolution together with the derived equivalence of Tag 09S6 it gives

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.exists_derivedTensorFunctorCompIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0BZ8.** *"Let `R` be a ring. Let `(A, d)`, `(B, d)`, and `(C, d)` be differential
graded `R`-algebras. Assume that `A ⊗_R C` represents `A ⊗^𝐋_R C` in `D(R)`. Let `N` be a
differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule. Let `N'` be a differential graded `(B, C)`-bimodule. Then
the composition `D(A, d) → D(B, d) → D(C, d)` of `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N` and `- ⊗_B^𝐋 N'` is isomorphic to
`- ⊗_A^𝐋 N''` for some differential graded `(A, C)`-bimodule `N''`."*

Representability is the only hypothesis: there is none on `B`. The bimodule is produced
explicitly by `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.resolutionCompTensorBimodule`, from the K-flat
resolution `ψ : (B', d) → (B, d)` of Tag 0BZ7 that
`DifferentialGradedAlgebra.exists_kFlat_resolution_bijective_cohomologyMap` supplies; the
isomorphism is
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.dgaResolutionDerivedTensorFunctorCompIsoOfResolution`. For a `B`
that is already K-flat the bimodule can be taken to be `compTensorResolution N N'`, the bimodule
of Tag 0BZ5, by
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.dgaResolutionDerivedTensorFunctorCompIsoOfKFlatBase`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_derivedTensorFunctorCompIso {A B C : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R}
    (hrep : DgaResolutionRepresentsDerivedTensor A C)
    (N : Bimodule A B) (N' : Bimodule B C) :
    ∃ N'' : Bimodule A C,
      Nonempty (derivedTensorFunctor N ⋙ derivedTensorFunctor N' ≅
        derivedTensorFunctor N'')
declarations.comment: the composition of the two derived tensor functors is a derived tensor functor, with no hypothesis on the middle algebra

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isIso_derivedTensorBaseChangeComparison_of_dgaResolutionRepresents
declarations.doc:
**The second half of the proof of Stacks Tag 0BZ8.** If the differential graded algebra
`(B, d)` is K-flat as a complex of `R`-modules and `A ⊗_R C` represents `A ⊗^𝐋_R C` in `D(R)`,
then the canonical map `(A ⊗_R B)_B ⊗_B^𝐋 {}_B(B ⊗_R C)_C ⟶ (A ⊗_R B ⊗_R C)_C` of Tag 0BZ4 is an
isomorphism — which by Tag 0BZ5 is all that the conclusion of Tag 0BZ8 needs.

The source resolves `(A ⊗_R B)_B` by `L ⊗_R B` for a property-(P) differential graded `R`-module
`L` quasi-isomorphic to `A`; the comparison of Tag 09LS at `(A ⊗_R B)_B` is then the map
`L ⊗_R B ⊗_R C ⟶ A ⊗_R B ⊗_R C`, which K-flatness of `B` reduces to `L ⊗_R C ⟶ A ⊗_R C`, and
that is the representability hypothesis. Here the resolution is an arbitrary property-(P)
resolution `Q ⟶ (A ⊗_R B)_B`, and what replaces the source's computation is that the complex
underlying `Q` is K-flat over `R` and that tensoring a K-flat resolution with `C` does not
depend on which resolution is taken; the resolution the hypothesis is evaluated at is then
`Tot(P^• ⊗_R B^•)` for a K-flat resolution `P^• ⟶ A^•` of complexes of `R`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedTensorBaseChangeComparison_of_dgaResolutionRepresents
    (A B C : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R)
    (hB : CochainComplex.KFlat.{u, u} (regularModule B).toCochainComplex)
    (hrep : DgaResolutionRepresentsDerivedTensor A C) :
    IsIso (derivedTensorBaseChangeComparison A B C)
declarations.comment: the second half of the proof: for B K-flat as a complex of R-modules, representability of A ⊗^L_R C by A ⊗_R C makes the map (0BZ4) an isomorphism

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.dgaResolutionDerivedTensorFunctorCompIsoOfKFlatBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0BZ8 for a K-flat middle algebra.** Let `R` be a ring, let `(A, d)`, `(B, d)`
and `(C, d)` be differential graded `R`-algebras with `A ⊗_R C` representing `A ⊗^𝐋_R C` in
`D(R)` and with `B` K-flat as a complex of `R`-modules, let `N` be a differential graded
`(A, B)`-bimodule and `N'` a differential graded `(B, C)`-bimodule. Then the composition
`D(A, d) → D(B, d) → D(C, d)` of `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N` and `- ⊗_B^𝐋 N'` is isomorphic to `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N''` for
the differential graded `(A, C)`-bimodule `N'' = Ñ ⊗_B Ñ'` of
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.compTensorResolution`.

This is `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.dgaResolutionDerivedTensorFunctorCompIso` with its carried
hypothesis `hbridge` discharged; the representability hypothesis `hrep` of the source is the only
hypothesis left besides K-flatness of `B`, which the source's reduction by Tag 0BZ7 and Tag 09S6
removes — that is
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.exists_derivedTensorFunctorCompIso` of
`StacksFrontier/Algebra/DifferentialGraded/Module/DgaResolutionGeneralBase.lean`, at the cost of no
longer naming the bimodule `N''`.
declarations.statement:
def dgaResolutionDerivedTensorFunctorCompIsoOfKFlatBase
    {A B C : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R}
    (hB : CochainComplex.KFlat.{u, u} (regularModule B).toCochainComplex)
    (hrep : DgaResolutionRepresentsDerivedTensor A C)
    (N : Bimodule A B) (N' : Bimodule B C) :
    derivedTensorFunctor N ⋙ derivedTensorFunctor N' ≅
      derivedTensorFunctor (compTensorResolution N N')
declarations.comment: for B K-flat as a complex of R-modules, with representability of A ⊗^L_R C by A ⊗_R C as its only other hypothesis

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.dgaResolutionDerivedTensorFunctorCompIso
declarations.doc:
Let `(A, d)`, `(B, d)` and `(C, d)` be differential graded `R`-algebras with `A ⊗_R C`
representing `A ⊗^𝐋_R C` in `D(R)` (`hrep`), and assume that representability makes
`derivedTensorBaseChangeComparison A B C` an isomorphism (`hbridge`). Let `N` be a differential
graded `(A, B)`-bimodule and `N'` a differential graded `(B, C)`-bimodule. Then the composition
`D(A, d) → D(B, d) → D(C, d)` of `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N` and `- ⊗_B^𝐋 N'` is isomorphic to `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N''` for
the differential graded `(A, C)`-bimodule `N'' = Ñ ⊗_B Ñ'` of
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.compTensorResolution`, the composite of property-(P) replacements.
declarations.statement:
def dgaResolutionDerivedTensorFunctorCompIso
    (hbridge : DgaResolutionRepresentsInvertsBaseChange A B C)
    (hrep : DgaResolutionRepresentsDerivedTensor A C)
    (N : Bimodule A B) (N' : Bimodule B C) :
    derivedTensorFunctor N ⋙ derivedTensorFunctor N' ≅
      derivedTensorFunctor (compTensorResolution N N')
declarations.comment: with the passage from the representability hypothesis to the Stacks 0BZ4 hypothesis of Stacks 0BZ5 as hbridge, which is proved for B K-flat as a complex of R-modules by dgaResolutionRepresentsInvertsBaseChange_of_kFlat and for a general B needs the transport along the Stacks 09S6 equivalence that the source's K-flat replacement of B by Stacks 0BZ7 sets up

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.exists_finite_tateResolution_of_pseudoCoherent_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**A pseudo-coherent ring map admits a Tate resolution with finitely many generators in each
degree, extending any prescribed finite presentation.** If `R → S` is pseudo-coherent and
`φ : R[x₁, …, x_k] → S` is any surjection from a polynomial ring in finitely many variables, then
there is a Tate resolution `A` of `S` along `φ` (all the conclusions of Tag 09PN: a divided power
differential graded algebra over `R` with degree-zero part `R[x₁, …, x_k]` mapping onto `S` by
`φ`, a graded divided power polynomial algebra over it, augmentation a quasi-isomorphism) whose
variables are finite in number in every degree.

Pseudo-coherence makes `S` a pseudo-coherent module over `R[x₁, …, x_k]` for the given `φ`
(Stacks 0682), so every stage of the degreewise finite tower has a finite spanning family of its
cycles, and `ker φ` is finitely generated.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finite_tateResolution_of_pseudoCoherent_of_surjective
    {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [h : Algebra.PseudoCoherent R S] {k : ℕ} (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin k) R →ₐ[R] S)
    (hφ : Function.Surjective φ) :
    ∃ A : Resolution R S (Fin k) φ, ∀ i : ℕ, Finite (A.polynomialIndices i)
declarations.comment: for a prescribed presentation

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.exists_finite_tateResolution_of_pseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**A pseudo-coherent ring map admits a Tate resolution with finitely many generators in each
degree.** If `R → S` is pseudo-coherent then there are a surjection `φ : R[x₁, …, x_k] → S` from
a polynomial ring in finitely many variables and a Tate resolution of `S` along `φ` whose
variables are finite in number in every degree.

A pseudo-coherent ring map is of finite type, so such a `φ` exists, and
`DividedPowers.TateResolution.exists_finite_tateResolution_of_pseudoCoherent_of_surjective`
extends it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finite_tateResolution_of_pseudoCoherent
    (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.PseudoCoherent R S] :
    ∃ (k : ℕ) (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin k) R →ₐ[R] S) (A : Resolution R S (Fin k) φ),
      Function.Surjective φ ∧ ∀ i : ℕ, Finite (A.polynomialIndices i)
declarations.comment: existence of some finite presentation with such a resolution

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GlobalHomBaseChange.isIso_globalHomAdjunctionMap_and_globalHomBaseChangeMap_comp_counit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZA.**  With notation as in Stacks 0AA7, the square

```
R Hom_X(M, Rg'_*L) ⊗^𝐋_R R' ----> R Hom_{X'}(L(g')^*M, L(g')^*Rg'_*L)
        |  μ                                   |  a
        v                                      v
R Hom_X(M, Rg'_*L)  ===========  R Hom_{X'}(L(g')^*M, L)
```

commutes, and its bottom map is the canonical identification.  The bottom map
`R Hom_X(M, Rg'_*L) ⟶ R Hom_{X'}(L(g')^*M, L)` of `D(R)` (`globalHomAdjunctionMap`) is an
isomorphism: it is `RΓ(X, -)` of the derived adjunction isomorphism
`R𝓗om(M, Rg'_*L) ≅ Rg'_*R𝓗om(L(g')^*M, L)` followed by `RΓ(X, Rg'_* -) = RΓ(X', -)`.  The square
says that the map of Stacks 0AA7 at `K = Rg'_*L` followed by the map `a` induced by the counit
`L(g')^*Rg'_*L ⟶ L` is the multiplication map `μ`, the counit `K' ⊗^𝐋_R R' ⟶ K'` of the
adjunction between `- ⊗^𝐋_R R'` and restriction of scalars at `K' = R Hom_{X'}(L(g')^*M, L)`, read
through that identification.  Both hold for every commutative square over `Spec R' ⟶ Spec R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_globalHomAdjunctionMap_and_globalHomBaseChangeMap_comp_counit
    (M : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (L : DerivedCategory X'.Modules) :
    IsIso (globalHomAdjunctionMap φ f f' g' w M L) ∧
      globalHomBaseChangeMap φ f f' g' w M ((derivedPushforward g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj L) ≫
          (linearSections f').map
            (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom X'.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj
              (op ((derivedPullback g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj M))).map
              ((derivedAdjunction g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).counit.app L)) =
        (derivedExtendScalars φ).map (globalHomAdjunctionMap φ f f' g' w M L) ≫
          (derivedExtendScalarsAdjunction φ).counit.app
            (globalHom f' ((derivedPullback g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj M) L)

declarations.name: Dualizing.DGAResolution
declarations.doc:
**Situation 0BZB.** A differential graded resolution of a commutative `R`-algebra `A`: a
differential graded `R`-algebra `E` together with a homomorphism to `A`, viewed as a
differential graded algebra with zero differential in degree zero, which is a quasi-isomorphism,
that is, an isomorphism on cohomology.
declarations.statement: structure DGAResolution (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
declarations.comment: resolution data

declarations.name: Dualizing.DGAResolution.derivedEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**The horizontal equivalence of Situation 0BZB.** Extension of scalars along the resolution,
followed by the identification of differential graded modules over `A` in degree zero with
complexes of `A`-modules, is an equivalence `D(E, d) ≌ D(A)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivedEquivalence :
    derivedCategory' S.E ≌ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)
declarations.comment: ordinary derived equivalence

declarations.name: Dualizing.DGAResolution.restrictionTriangle
declarations.doc:
**The first diagram of Situation 0BZB commutes.** Passing from `D(A)` to `D(E, d)` through
the equivalence and then forgetting the `E`-action is restriction of scalars along `R → A`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictionTriangle :
    S.derivedEquivalence.inverse ⋙ derivedForget S.E ≅
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{u} (algebraMap R A)).mapDerivedCategory
declarations.comment: restriction triangle

declarations.name: Dualizing.DGAResolution.derivedExtension_comp_iso
declarations.doc:
**The second diagram of Situation 0BZB commutes.** Derived extension of scalars from `D(R)`
to `D(E, d)` followed by the equivalence `- ⊗_E^𝐋 A` is derived extension of scalars
`- ⊗_R^𝐋 A : D(R) ⥤ D(A)`.

Derived extension of scalars to the resolution enters as an arbitrary left adjoint `F` of the
forgetful functor, so the statement is independent of the model chosen for it. That data is
discharged by `Dualizing.derivedExtensionToDGA` together with
`Dualizing.derivedExtensionToDGA_adj`, giving the unconditional
`Dualizing.DGAResolution.derivedExtensionToDGA_comp_iso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivedExtension_comp_iso
    (F : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R) ⥤ derivedCategory' S.E)
    (adjF : F ⊣ derivedForget S.E) :
    F ⋙ S.derivedEquivalence.functor ≅ ordinaryExtension (R := R) (A := A)
declarations.comment: extension triangle, for an arbitrary left adjoint F of the forgetful functor; its data F, adjF is discharged by derivedExtensionToDGA and derivedExtensionToDGA_adj, giving the unconditional DGAResolution.derivedExtensionToDGA_comp_iso

declarations.name: Dualizing.DGAResolution.derivedExtensionToDGA_comp_iso
declarations.doc:
**The second diagram of Situation 0BZB commutes, with no assumed functor.** Derived
extension of scalars `- ⊗_R^𝐋 E : D(R) ⥤ D(E, d)` followed by the horizontal equivalence
`- ⊗_E^𝐋 A : D(E, d) ⥤ D(A)` is derived extension of scalars `- ⊗_R^𝐋 A : D(R) ⥤ D(A)`.

This is `Dualizing.DGAResolution.derivedExtension_comp_iso` with its parameters `F` and `adjF`
discharged by `Dualizing.derivedExtensionToDGA` and `Dualizing.derivedExtensionToDGA_adj`.
declarations.comment: extension triangle, with the functor constructed

registrations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedExtensionEquivalence
registrations.comment: horizontal equivalence

declarations.name: Dualizing.DGAResolution.derivedHom_comp_derivedEquivalence_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZC.** In Situation 0BZB the functor `R Hom(A, -) : D(R) ⥤ D(A)` is the
composition of `R Hom(E, -) : D(R) ⥤ D(E, d)` with the equivalence `- ⊗_E^𝐋 A : D(E, d) ⥤ D(A)`.

The functor `R Hom(E, -)` enters as an arbitrary right adjoint `G` of the forgetful functor
`D(E, d) ⥤ D(R)`, which is what Tag 09LT says derived Hom out of `E` is; so the statement is
independent of the model chosen for it.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivedHom_comp_derivedEquivalence_iso
    (G : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R) ⥤ derivedCategory' S.E)
    (adjG : derivedForget S.E ⊣ G) :
    Dualizing.derivedHom.{u, u, u} (algebraMap R A) ≅ G ⋙ S.derivedEquivalence.functor

declarations.name: Dualizing.derivedHomIsoGradedDualTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZD.** Let `(E, d)` be a differential graded algebra over a commutative ring `R` —
in Situation 0BZB, the algebra resolving the `R`-algebra `A` — and let
`N = Hom^•_R(E^•, R)` be the graded dual of `E^•` over `R`, a differential graded
`(R, E)`-bimodule. Assume that `E^•` is a compact object of `D(R)` and that `N` computes
`R Hom(E, R)`. Then `R Hom(E, -) : D(R) ⥤ D(E, d)` is isomorphic to `K ↦ K ⊗_R^𝐋 N`.

Here `D(R)` is the derived category of `R` viewed as a differential graded algebra concentrated
in degree zero, which is the derived category of `R`-modules by
`DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroDerivedEquivalence`; `R Hom(E, -)` is the right derived
functor of Tag 09LI for the bimodule `E`, and `- ⊗_R^𝐋 N` the left derived functor of Tag 09LS.

The source deduces this as the case `T = E` of the second assertion of Tag 0BZ0, which is
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorHomDualFunctorIso`; the two hypotheses above are
exactly its two hypotheses for `T = E`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivedHomIsoGradedDualTensor
    (hcompact : IsCompactBimodule (resolvingBimodule E))
    (hdual : ComputesDerivedHom (resolvingBimodule E)) :
    (derivedHomData E (baseAlgebra R) (resolvingBimodule E).rightModule
        (resolvingBimodule E).leftAction).functor ≅
      Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor (gradedDualBimodule E)

declarations.name: Dualizing.exists_derivedHom_iso_derivedTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZE.** Let `R → A` be a map of commutative rings making `A` a
perfect `R`-module. Then `R Hom(A, -) : D(R) ⥤ D(A)` is a derived tensor product:
there is a differential graded `(R, A)`-bimodule `M` with `R Hom(A, -) ≅ - ⊗_R^𝐋 M`, whose
class in `D(A)` is the value `R Hom(A, R)` of that functor at `R`. The two derived categories of
the degree-zero world are the derived categories of `R`-modules and of `A`-modules through
`DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroDerivedEquivalence`.

A Tate resolution of `A` over `R` exists for every `R`-algebra, along the tautological
polynomial presentation; it puts us in Situation 0BZB. Perfectness of `A` makes the resolving
bimodule compact in `D(R)`, and the homogeneous pieces of a Tate resolution are free over `R`,
which makes its graded dual compute `R Hom(E^•, R)`. Both hypotheses of Stacks 0BZD hold, so
`Dualizing.DGAResolution.derivedHomIsoDerivedTensor` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_derivedHom_iso_derivedTensor
    (hperf : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfectModule.{u, u, u + 1} (R := R) A) :
    ∃ M : Bimodule (baseAlgebra R) (DifferentialGradedAlgebra.degreeZero R A),
      Nonempty (Dualizing.derivedHom.{u, u, u} (algebraMap R A) ≅
        derivedTensorBimoduleFunctor M) ∧
      Nonempty ((Dualizing.derivedHom.{u, u, u} (algebraMap R A)).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R R)) ≅
        (degreeZeroDerivedEquivalence (R := R) (A := A)).functor.obj
          ((toHomotopyCategory (DifferentialGradedAlgebra.degreeZero R A) ⋙
            (quasiIsomorphisms' (DifferentialGradedAlgebra.degreeZero R A)).Q).obj
              M.rightModule))
declarations.comment: the functor R Hom(A, -) is derived tensoring over R with a differential graded (R, A)-bimodule whose class in D(A) is R Hom(A, R), read through the degree-zero equivalences

declarations.name: Dualizing.nonempty_derivedHom_iso_canonicalDerivedTensor_of_perfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZE in the derived change-of-rings shape of Tag 06Y6.** Let `f : R → A` make `A` a
perfect `R`-module and let `L` be a complex of `A`-modules whose class in `D(A)` is the value
`RHom_R(A, R)` of derived coextension of scalars at the free module of rank one. Then
`RHom_R(A, -) : D(R) ⥤ D(A)` is the canonical derived change-of-rings tensor product of
Stacks 06Y6 with `L`.

This is `Dualizing.exists_derivedHom_iso_derivedTensor` — Stacks 0BZE through a Tate resolution —
carried across `Dualizing.nonempty_derivedTensorBimoduleFunctor_iso_canonical` and then across
Stacks 0BYK to the chosen representative `L`. No hypothesis beyond the perfectness that
Stacks 0BZE itself assumes.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_derivedHom_iso_canonicalDerivedTensor_of_perfect (f : R →+* A)
    (hperf : letI := f.toAlgebra
      StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfectModule.{u, u, u + 1} (R := R) A)
    (L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (hL : Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L ≅
      (Dualizing.derivedHom.{u, u} f).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R R)))) :
    letI := f.toAlgebra
    Nonempty (Dualizing.derivedHom.{u, u} f ≅
      (canonicalDerivedTensorChangeOfRings.{u, u, u} f L).F)
declarations.comment: in the derived change-of-rings shape of Tag 06Y6, at module universe equal to the ring universe, with no carried hypothesis

declarations.name: Dualizing.derivedHomIsoCanonicalDerivedTensorOfPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZE in the derived change-of-rings shape of Tag 06Y6, as data.** For `f : R → A`
making `A` a perfect `R`-module, `RHom_R(A, -) : D(R) ⥤ D(A)` *is* the canonical derived
change-of-rings tensor product of Stacks 06Y6 with the canonical tensor factor
`Dualizing.canonicalDerivedHomTensorComplex f`. No existential witness is chosen along the way:
the Tate resolution is the named one, `Dualizing.DGAResolution.derivedHomIsoDerivedTensor` is a
construction, and so is `Dualizing.derivedTensorBimoduleFunctorIsoCanonical`, so the isomorphism
is a function of `f` and `hperf`.

`Dualizing.nonempty_derivedHom_iso_canonicalDerivedTensor_of_perfect` is the form stated at an
arbitrary complex representing `RHom_R(A, R)`; that form is a proposition because passing from
this factor to another representative of the same object of `D(A)` goes through a fraction, in
`Dualizing.InvertibleKernel.derivedTensorIsoOfDerivedIso`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedHomIsoCanonicalDerivedTensorOfPerfect (f : R →+* A)
    (hperf : letI := f.toAlgebra
      StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfectModule.{u, u, u + 1} (R := R) A) :
    letI := f.toAlgebra
    Dualizing.derivedHom.{u, u} f ≅
      (canonicalDerivedTensorChangeOfRings.{u, u, u} f
        (canonicalDerivedHomTensorComplex f)).F
declarations.comment: in the derived change-of-rings shape of Tag 06Y6, at module universe equal to the ring universe, with no carried hypothesis; the isomorphism is built, at the canonical tensor factor, rather than shown to exist at an arbitrary representative

declarations.name: Dualizing.nonempty_derivedHom_iso_canonicalDerivedTensor_of_perfect_anyModuleUniverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZE in the derived change-of-rings shape of Tag 06Y6, at an arbitrary module
universe.** Let `f : R → A` make `A` a perfect `R`-module and let `L` be a complex of `A`-modules,
in a universe `max v u` above the ring universe `u`, whose class in `D(A)` is the value
`RHom_R(A, R)` of derived coextension of scalars at the free module of rank one on the lifted
carrier. Then `RHom_R(A, -) : D(R) ⥤ D(A)` is the canonical derived change-of-rings tensor product
of Stacks 06Y6 with `L`.

This is `Dualizing.nonempty_derivedHom_iso_canonicalDerivedTensor_of_perfect` — which holds at
module universe equal to the ring universe, the generality of the differential graded chapter —
renamed along `ULift.ringEquiv`, where the module universe `max v u` *is* the ring universe. All
three functors involved are carried across that renaming: derived coextension of scalars by
`StacksDraft.DerivedRingEquivIso.derivedHomRingEquivIso`, and derived extension of scalars together
with the derived change-of-rings tensor product by
`StacksDraft.DerivedRingEquivIso.derivedTensorBundleRingEquivIsoOfFactorIso`. The perfectness
hypothesis is the one Stacks 0BZE itself assumes, read for the lifted rings by
`Dualizing.isPerfectModule_ulift_ringEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_derivedHom_iso_canonicalDerivedTensor_of_perfect_anyModuleUniverse (f : R →+* A)
    (hperf : letI := f.toAlgebra
      StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfectModule.{u, u, u + 1} (R := R) A)
    (L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} A) ℤ)
    (hL : Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L ≅
      (Dualizing.derivedHom.{u, v} f).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) 0).obj
          (ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{max v u} R))))) :
    Nonempty (Dualizing.derivedHom.{u, v} f ≅
      (canonicalDerivedTensorChangeOfRings.{u, u, max v u} f L).F)
declarations.comment: in the derived change-of-rings shape of Tag 06Y6, at an arbitrary module universe above the ring universe, with no carried hypothesis

declarations.name: Dualizing.nonempty_restrictScalars_derivedHom_iso_derivedTensor_unitDual
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZE, objectwise and after restriction of scalars.** Let `f : R → A` be a
homomorphism of commutative rings with `A` perfect as an `R`-module. For every object `K` of
`D(R)`, derived coextension of scalars `R Hom(A, K)` of Stacks 0A70, read in `D(R)` by
restriction of scalars along `f`, is the derived tensor product of `K` with `R Hom(A, R)` read in
the same way.

Perfectness is consumed, not recorded: it is the first case of the derived tensor--Hom diagonal
of Stacks 0ATK, applied with the diagonal's internal-Hom source the module `A` placed in degree
zero and read over `R`. The two vocabularies are reconciled by
`Dualizing.nonempty_modelHomIsoRestrictScalarsDerivedHom`, which identifies the internal derived
Hom of Stacks 0A63 out of that object with restricted derived coextension, and the tensor factor
`K ⊗ᴸ_R R` is cut down by the right unitor of the derived tensor product.

Stacks 0BZE asserts more: an isomorphism of functors `D(R) ⥤ D(A)`. Both of the missing steps —
naturality of the comparison in `K`, and the identification of `Stacks0BZE.comparison` with the
diagonal that would carry an isomorphism in `D(R)` up to `D(A)` — are discussed in this module's
documentation. For the form of Stacks 0BZE that asserts the isomorphism of functors and carries
those steps as hypotheses, see `Stacks0BZE.cardIso` of
`StacksFrontier.RingTheory.Dualizing.TrivialDualityKFlat`; for the unconditional form, see
`Dualizing.exists_derivedHom_iso_derivedTensor` of
`StacksFrontier.RingTheory.Dualizing.DerivedHomPerfectTensor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_restrictScalars_derivedHom_iso_derivedTensor_unitDual (f : R →+* A)
    (hperfect : letI := f.toAlgebra
      StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfectModule (R := R) A)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) :
    Nonempty
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{u} f).mapDerivedCategory.obj
          ((derivedHom.{u, u, u} f).obj K) ≅
        (Model.tensor R).obj
          (K, (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{u} f).mapDerivedCategory.obj
            ((derivedHom.{u, u, u} f).obj
              (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
                ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj
                  (ModuleCat.of R R))))))
declarations.comment: objectwise and after restriction of scalars to the base

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isIso_torIndependentTwistedInverseImageBaseChange_app_of_perfect
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BZG].** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a perfect proper morphism of Noetherian schemes and
`g : Y' ⟶ Y` a morphism with `Y'` Noetherian, and let `X' = X ×_Y Y'`, with projections
`g' : X' ⟶ X` and `f' : X' ⟶ Y'`. If `X` and `Y'` are Tor independent over `Y`, then the base
change map `L(g')^* a(K) ⟶ a'(Lg^*K)` of [Stacks, Tag 0AA6] is an isomorphism for every
`K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, where `a` and `a'` are the right adjoints of `Rf_*` and `Rf'_*` on `D_QCoh`
([Stacks, Tag 0A9E]).
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_torIndependentTwistedInverseImageBaseChange_app_of_perfect {X' X Y' Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y] [IsNoetherian Y'] {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) [IsProper f]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.Perfect f] (hTor : TorIndependent f g)
    (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y) :
    haveI : QuasiCompact f' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback sq inferInstance
    haveI : QuasiSeparated f' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback sq inferInstance
    haveI : CompactSpace X' := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace f'
    haveI : QuasiSeparatedSpace X' := quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated f'
    IsIso ((torIndependentTwistedInverseImageBaseChange sq hTor).app K)

declarations.name: Dualizing.InvertibleKernel.conormal_invertible
declarations.doc:
**The conormal module of a surjection with invertible kernel is invertible.** Invertibility
is stable under base change, here along `R → A` itself.

This is the clause of [Stacks, Tag 0BZH] that calls `I ⊗_R A` an invertible `A`-module. Unlike
the functor identification it needs nothing beyond the two hypotheses of the tag, and it holds at
every module universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormal_invertible (hI : Module.Invertible R (RingHom.ker (algebraMap R A))) :
    Module.Invertible A (conormal.{u, v} R A)
declarations.comment: the conormal module `I ⊗_R A` is an invertible `A`-module

declarations.name: Dualizing.InvertibleKernel.conormalInverse_tensor_conormal
declarations.doc:
**`N` is a tensor inverse of the conormal module**: `N ⊗_A (I ⊗_R A) ≅ A`.

This is the clause of [Stacks, Tag 0BZH] that names `N` as the inverse of the invertible
`A`-module `I ⊗_R A`; like `Dualizing.InvertibleKernel.conormal_invertible` it is unconditional
and holds at every module universe.
declarations.statement:
def conormalInverse_tensor_conormal
    (hI : Module.Invertible R (RingHom.ker (algebraMap R A))) :
    conormalInverse.{u, v} R A ⊗[A] conormal.{u, v} R A ≃ₗ[A] A
declarations.comment: `N` is the inverse of the invertible `A`-module `I ⊗_R A`

declarations.name: Dualizing.InvertibleKernel.nonempty_derivedHom_iso_derivedTensor_conormalInverseShift_anyModuleUniverse
declarations.doc:
For a surjection `f : R → A` whose kernel is an invertible `R`-module, derived coextension of
scalars `RHom_R(A, -) : D(R) ⥤ D(A)` is derived tensoring over `R` with the conormal inverse shift
`N[-1]`, for any model of the derived change-of-rings tensor product with that factor and at any
module universe above the ring universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_derivedHom_iso_derivedTensor_conormalInverseShift_anyModuleUniverse
    (f : R →+* A) (hf : Function.Surjective f)
    (hI : Module.Invertible R (RingHom.ker f)) :
    letI := f.toAlgebra
    ∀ T : DerivedTensorChangeOfRings f (conormalInverseShift.{u, v} R A),
      Nonempty (Dualizing.derivedHom.{u, v} f ≅ T.F)
declarations.comment: at an arbitrary module universe above the ring universe, with no carried hypothesis

declarations.name: Dualizing.InvertibleKernel.nonempty_derivedHom_iso_derivedTensor_conormalInverseShift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZH.** For a surjection `f : R → A` whose kernel is an invertible `R`-module,
derived coextension of scalars `RHom_R(A, -) : D(R) ⥤ D(A)` is derived tensoring over `R` with
the conormal inverse shift `N[-1]`, at any model of the derived change-of-rings tensor product
with that factor.

This is
`Dualizing.InvertibleKernel.nonempty_derivedHom_iso_canonicalDerivedTensor_conormalInverseShift`
transported to an arbitrary model along `Dualizing.InvertibleKernel.derivedTensorIsoOfDerivedIso`
at the identity of the tensor factor.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_derivedHom_iso_derivedTensor_conormalInverseShift (f : R →+* A)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) (hI : Module.Invertible R (RingHom.ker f)) :
    letI := f.toAlgebra
    ∀ T : DerivedTensorChangeOfRings f (conormalInverseShift.{u, u} R A),
      Nonempty (Dualizing.derivedHom.{u, u} f ≅ T.F)
declarations.comment: at module universe equal to the ring universe, with no carried hypothesis

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZJ.** The algebraic upper shriek functors attached to any two polynomial
presentations of the same finite type homomorphism are naturally isomorphic, so `f^!` is well
defined up to isomorphism.

This is `Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.upperShriekFunctor_iso` with its hypothesis `hBZH`
supplied by `Dualizing.polynomialEvalDuality`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_iso {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A]
    (f : R →+* A) (p q : PolynomialPresentation f) :
    Nonempty (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, v} ≅ q.upperShriekFunctor.{u, v})

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.upperShriekFunctor_isBoundedBelow
declarations.doc:
Algebraic upper shriek carries cohomologically bounded-below complexes to cohomologically
bounded-below complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem upperShriekFunctor_isBoundedBelow (p : PolynomialPresentation f)

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.upperShriekFunctor_derivedCategoryBPlus
declarations.doc:
Algebraic upper shriek along a finite type homomorphism of Noetherian rings carries
bounded-below complexes with coherent cohomology to bounded-below complexes with coherent
cohomology.
declarations.statement:
theorem upperShriekFunctor_derivedCategoryBPlus [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing A]

      (fun M : ModuleCat.{max v u} R ↦ Module.Finite R M) K) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (fun M : ModuleCat.{max v u} A ↦ Module.Finite A M)
      (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, v}.obj K)
declarations.comment: (1), the statement that φ^! maps D⁺_Coh(R) into D⁺_Coh(A)

declarations.name: Dualizing.upperShriekFunctor_isBoundedAbove_of_perfect
declarations.doc:
Algebraic upper shriek along a perfect homomorphism of Noetherian rings carries cohomologically

declarations.statement:

declarations.name: Dualizing.upperShriekFunctor_derivedCategoryBMinus_of_perfect
declarations.doc:
Algebraic upper shriek along a perfect homomorphism of Noetherian rings carries bounded-above

declarations.statement:
theorem upperShriekFunctor_derivedCategoryBMinus_of_perfect

declarations.doc:
Algebraic upper shriek along a perfect homomorphism of Noetherian rings carries bounded
complexes with coherent cohomology to bounded complexes with coherent cohomology.
declarations.statement:
theorem upperShriekFunctor_derivedCategoryBBounded_of_perfect
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing A] (p : PolynomialPresentation f) (hf : f.Perfect)

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.upperShriekFunctor_isDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BZL.** Algebraic upper shriek along a finite type homomorphism of
Noetherian rings carries a dualizing complex to a dualizing complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem upperShriekFunctor_isDualizingComplex [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing A]
