declarations.name: Dualizing.isIso_derivedHomBaseChange_app_of_isModulePseudoCoherent_of_finiteTorDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZM.** Let `R → A` and `R → R'` be homomorphisms of commutative rings and
`A' = A ⊗_R R'`. If `A` is pseudo-coherent as an `R`-module, `R'` has finite Tor dimension as an
`R`-module, and `A` and `R'` are Tor independent over `R`, then the base-change morphism
`RHom_R(A, K) ⊗ᴸ_A A' ⟶ RHom_{R'}(A', K ⊗ᴸ_R R')` of Stacks 0E29 is an isomorphism for every
`K` in `D⁺(R)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedHomBaseChange_app_of_isModulePseudoCoherent_of_finiteTorDimension
    (hA : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsModulePseudoCoherent (R := R) A)
    (D : StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.CertifiedDerivedTensoring.{uR, max v uR uA uRp} R)
    (hFinite : StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.ModuleHasFiniteTorDimension D.tensor D.comparison
      D.isLeftDerived
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R R')).obj
        (ModuleCat.of R' (ULift.{max v uR uA, uRp} R'))))
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp} R))
    (hK : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp} R)).plus K) :
    IsIso ((derivedHomBaseChange.{uR, uA, uRp, v} hTor baseChangeR comparisonR isLeftDerivedR
      baseChangeA comparisonA isLeftDerivedA).app K)

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.isIso_upperShriekFlatBaseChange_app
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be Noetherian, let `R → R'` be flat, let `φ : R → A` be of finite type, presented by
`p`, and let `φ' : R' → A' = R' ⊗_R A` be its base change. The flat-base-change map
`φ^!(K) ⊗_A^L A' ⟶ (φ')^!(K ⊗_R^L R')` of
`Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.upperShriekFlatBaseChange`, a natural transformation of functors
`D(R) ⥤ D(A')`, is an isomorphism at every `K` in `D⁺(R)`; here `φ^!` is read at `p` and
`(φ')^!` at its base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem PolynomialPresentation.isIso_upperShriekFlatBaseChange_app [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (p : PolynomialPresentation (algebraMap R A)) (hf : (algebraMap R R').Flat)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} R)) (hK : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow K) :
    IsIso ((p.upperShriekFlatBaseChange.{u, v} (R' := R') hf).app K)

declarations.name: Dualizing.isIso_derivedHomBaseChange_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZP.** Let `R → A` and `R → R'` be homomorphisms of commutative rings and
`A' = A ⊗_R R'`. If `A` is perfect as an `R`-module and `A` and `R'` are Tor independent over
`R`, then the base-change morphism of Stacks 0E29 is invertible — as a natural transformation,
hence at every object of `D(R)` and with no boundedness hypothesis.

The proof is that of the source. By Stacks 0E2A the restriction of the morphism along
`R' → A'` is, up to isomorphisms of source and target, the derived-Hom base-change morphism of
Stacks 0E1X at the algebra `A`; this is
`Dualizing.exists_restrictScalars_map_derivedHomBaseChange_app_eq`. That morphism is
invertible because `A` is perfect, by Stacks 0ATK (1), and restriction of scalars reflects
isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedHomBaseChange_of_isPerfect
    (hA : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfectModule (R := R) A) :
    IsIso (derivedHomBaseChange.{uR, uA, uRp, v} hTor baseChangeR comparisonR isLeftDerivedR
      baseChangeA comparisonA isLeftDerivedA)

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_comp_iso_of_torIndependent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZR.**  Let `R → R'` be a ring homomorphism, let `φ : R → A` be a perfect ring map
such that `A` and `R'` are Tor independent over `R`, and let `φ' : R' → A' = R' ⊗_R A` be the
induced map.  Then `φ^!(K) ⊗_A^L A' ≅ (φ')^!(K ⊗_R^L R')`, naturally in `K` in `D(R)`.

Here `φ^!` is read at an arbitrary polynomial presentation `p` of `φ` and `(φ')^!` at an
arbitrary polynomial presentation `p'` of `φ'`, the two derived tensor products at arbitrary
left-derived models of extension of scalars, and the modules in an arbitrary universe
`max v u`.  The Noetherian hypotheses of the source are not needed.

The isomorphism is the base-change map
`Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.upperShriekTorIndependentBaseChangeLarge` at `p` and its base
change, invertible by
`Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.isIso_upperShriekTorIndependentBaseChangeLarge`, followed by the
comparison of [stacks 0BZJ] between the base-changed presentation and `p'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem PolynomialPresentation.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_comp_iso_of_torIndependent
    [Algebra.Perfect R A] (p : PolynomialPresentation (algebraMap R A))
    (p' : PolynomialPresentation (algebraMap R' (TensorProduct R R' A)))
    (hTor : TorIndependent R A R')
    (bcR : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} R'))
    (cmpR : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ bcR ⟶
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, max v u} (algebraMap R R')).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (ldR : bcR.IsLeftDerivedFunctor cmpR
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (bcT : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} (TensorProduct R R' A)))
    (cmpT : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ bcT ⟶
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, max v u}
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight :
            A →ₐ[R] TensorProduct R R' A).toRingHom).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (ldT : bcT.IsLeftDerivedFunctor cmpT
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max v u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) :
    Nonempty (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, v} ⋙ bcT ≅ bcR ⋙ p'.upperShriekFunctor.{u, v})

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_comp_iso_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZS.**  Let `R` be a Noetherian ring and `R → R'` any homomorphism, let
`φ : R → A` be flat of finite type, presented by `p`, and let `φ' : R' → A' = R' ⊗_R A` be the
induced map, presented by any `p'`.  Then there is an isomorphism of functors `D(R) ⥤ D(A')`
`φ^!(K) ⊗_A^L A' ≅ (φ')^!(K ⊗_R^L R')`, natural in `K`, at every module universe `max v u`; the two
derived tensor products are read at arbitrary left-derived models of extension of scalars.

As in the source this is a special case of [stacks 0BZR],
`Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_comp_iso_of_torIndependent`: over a
Noetherian base a flat map of finite type is of finite presentation, hence perfect by
[stacks 067J], and flatness of `A` makes `A` and `R'` Tor independent over `R`.  The source's
Noetherian hypothesis on `R'` is not needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem PolynomialPresentation.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_comp_iso_of_flat
    [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (hflat : (algebraMap R A).Flat)
    (p : PolynomialPresentation (algebraMap R A))
    (p' : PolynomialPresentation (algebraMap R' (TensorProduct R R' A)))
    (bcR : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} R'))
    (cmpR : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ bcR ⟶
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, max v u} (algebraMap R R')).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (ldR : bcR.IsLeftDerivedFunctor cmpR
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (bcT : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} (TensorProduct R R' A)))
    (cmpT : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ bcT ⟶
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, max v u}
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight :
            A →ₐ[R] TensorProduct R R' A).toRingHom).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (ldT : bcT.IsLeftDerivedFunctor cmpT
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max v u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) :
    Nonempty (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, v} ⋙ bcT ≅ bcR ⋙ p'.upperShriekFunctor.{u, v})

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.exists_upperShriekComp_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BZT.**  Let `a : R →+* A` and `b : A →+* B` be homomorphisms of finite
type with `R` Noetherian, let `p` be any polynomial presentation of `a`, `q` any polynomial
presentation of `b` and `r` any polynomial presentation of `b ∘ a`.  Then there is a
transformation of functors

`b^! ∘ a^! ⟶ (b ∘ a)^!`

upper shriek being read at `p`, at `q` and at `r` and modules taken in any universe `max v u`,
which is an isomorphism at every object of `D⁺(R)`.  The Noetherian hypothesis is needed on `R`
only; it passes to the polynomial algebras, which is all the proof uses.

It is `Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.exists_upperShriekComp_isIso_of_isBoundedBelow`, which
states it at the induced presentation `p.comp q` of the composite, transported to an arbitrary `r`
along the independence of the presentation, [Stacks, Tag 0BZJ],
`Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_iso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_upperShriekComp_of_finiteType [IsNoetherianRing R] {a : R →+* A} {b : A →+* B}
    (p : PolynomialPresentation a)
    (q : PolynomialPresentation b) (r : PolynomialPresentation (b.comp a)) :
    ∃ τ : p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, v} ⋙ q.upperShriekFunctor.{u, v} ⟶
        r.upperShriekFunctor.{u, v},
      ∀ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} R), DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow K →
        IsIso (τ.app K)

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZU.** Let `φ : R → A` be a ring homomorphism, let `p` be a
polynomial presentation of `φ` with polynomial algebra `P` and surjection `ψ : P → A`, and assume
`A` is a perfect `P`-module, which for a perfect `φ` is Tag 068Y.  Then the algebraic upper shriek
functor of `p` is derived tensor product over `R` with the single object `φ^!(R)` of `D(A)`:
`φ^!(K) = K ⊗_R^L φ^!(R)`, naturally in `K` in `D(R)`.

Perfectness of `A` over `P` is exactly the hypothesis of Tag 0BZE, and Tag 0BZE for `ψ` is the one
external input of the argument: it identifies `RHom_P(A, -)` with derived tensor product over `P`
with `RHom_P(A, P)`.  At the arbitrary module universe `max v u` of this statement that tag is
`Dualizing.nonempty_derivedHom_iso_canonicalDerivedTensor_of_perfect_anyModuleUniverse`.

The rest is the cancellation of the intermediate `- ⊗_R^L P` by the iterated change of rings of
Tag 08YU, the passage of the shift by `n` into the tensor factor through the universal property of
the left derived functor, and the evaluation of that factor at `R` by the unitors of the tensor
product of complexes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct
    (p : PolynomialPresentation f)
    (hp : letI : Module p.Poly A := Module.compHom A p.toRingHom
      StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfectModule (R := p.Poly) A) :
    letI : MonoidalCategoryStruct (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) :=
      ModuleCat.liftedModuleMonoidalStruct.{u, max v u}
    letI : MonoidalCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) :=
      ModuleCat.liftedModuleMonoidal.{u, max v u}
    let R₀ := (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) 0).obj
      (MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorUnit (ModuleCat.{max v u} R))
    Nonempty (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, v} ≅
      derivedTensorProductOver.{u, v} f (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, v}.obj R₀))
declarations.comment: at an arbitrary polynomial presentation and an arbitrary module universe

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct_of_perfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZU.** Let `φ : R → A` be a perfect ring homomorphism and let `p` be
a polynomial presentation of `φ`.  Then the algebraic upper shriek functor of `p` is derived
tensor product over `R` with the single object `φ^!(R)` of `D(A)`: `φ^!(K) = K ⊗_R^L φ^!(R)`,
naturally in `K` in `D(R)`.  A flat homomorphism of finite presentation is perfect (Tag 067J,
`Algebra.Perfect.of_flat_of_finitePresentation`), so the hypothesis is not vacuous.

Perfectness of `φ` is `RingHom.Perfect`.  By Tag 068Y at `p`
(`Algebra.Perfect.exists_finite_projective_resolution`) and Tag 066Q it gives perfectness of `A`
as a module over the polynomial algebra of `p`, which is the hypothesis of Tag 0BZE.  That is the
only thing `Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct` asks
for, so this is exactly that statement with its perfectness rewritten.
declarations.statement:
public theorem upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct_of_perfect
    (p : PolynomialPresentation f) (hf : f.Perfect) :
    letI : MonoidalCategoryStruct (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) :=
      ModuleCat.liftedModuleMonoidalStruct.{u, max v u}
    letI : MonoidalCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) :=
      ModuleCat.liftedModuleMonoidal.{u, max v u}
    let R₀ := (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) 0).obj
      (MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorUnit (ModuleCat.{max v u} R))
    Nonempty (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, v} ≅
      derivedTensorProductOver.{u, v} f (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, v}.obj R₀))
declarations.comment: for a perfect homomorphism, at an arbitrary polynomial presentation and an arbitrary module universe

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.tensorFormulaOfPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZU with the isomorphism built, from perfectness alone.** Let `φ : R → A` be a ring
homomorphism and `p` a polynomial presentation of `φ` whose polynomial algebra
makes `A` a perfect module. Then the algebraic upper shriek functor of `p` *is* derived tensor
product over `R` with a constructed complex whose class in `D(A)` is `φ^!(R)`.

This is `Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.tensorFormulaOfDerivedHomIso` at the representative of
`RHom_P(A, P)` chosen by `objPreimage`, with the isomorphism of Tag 0BZE there taken from
`Dualizing.nonempty_derivedHom_iso_canonicalDerivedTensor_of_perfect_anyModuleUniverse`. That tag
is available as a proposition rather than as data, because passing between two representatives of
one object of `D(A)` goes through a fraction, so the isomorphism is chosen; everything after the
choice is a construction.
declarations.statement:
public def tensorFormulaOfPerfect
    (p : PolynomialPresentation f)
    (hp : letI : Module p.Poly A := Module.compHom A p.toRingHom
      StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfectModule (R := p.Poly) A) :
    TensorFormula.{u, v} p
declarations.comment: at an arbitrary polynomial presentation and an arbitrary module universe, with the tensor formula built as an isomorphism at a constructed tensor factor whose class in D(A) is the value of upper shriek at R

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZU, with no carried hypothesis.** Let `φ : R → A` be a ring homomorphism and `p` a
polynomial presentation of it whose polynomial algebra makes `A` a perfect
module. Then the algebraic upper shriek functor of `p` is derived tensor product over `R` with
the single object `φ^!(R)` of `D(A)`.

This is `Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct` read at
module universe equal to the ring universe, which is the generality the rest of this module works
in; that statement holds at any module universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct
    (p : PolynomialPresentation f)
    (hp : letI : Module p.Poly A := Module.compHom A p.toRingHom
      StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfectModule.{u, u, u + 1} (R := p.Poly) A) :
    letI : MonoidalCategoryStruct (ModuleCat.{u} R) :=
      ModuleCat.liftedModuleMonoidalStruct.{u, u}
    letI : MonoidalCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R) :=
      ModuleCat.liftedModuleMonoidal.{u, u}
    let R₀ := (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj
      (MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorUnit (ModuleCat.{u} R))
    Nonempty (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, u} ≅
      derivedTensorProductOver.{u, u} f (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, u}.obj R₀))
declarations.comment: at an arbitrary polynomial presentation, at module universe equal to the ring universe; the same statement at an arbitrary module universe is Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct_of_perfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZU for a perfect homomorphism, with no carried hypothesis.** Let `φ : R → A` be a
perfect ring homomorphism and `p` a polynomial presentation of it. Then the
algebraic upper shriek functor of `p` is derived tensor product over `R` with the single object
`φ^!(R)` of `D(A)`.

This is the hypothesis shape of Stacks 0BZU itself: perfectness of `φ`, `RingHom.Perfect`, rather
than perfectness of `A` over the polynomial algebra of `p`. Tag 068Y at `p` passes between the
two, as `Algebra.Perfect.exists_finite_projective_resolution` read through Tag 066Q, which is what
feeds `Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct` here.
This is `Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct_of_perfect`
read at module universe equal to the ring universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct_of_perfect
    (p : PolynomialPresentation f) (hf : f.Perfect) :
    letI : MonoidalCategoryStruct (ModuleCat.{u} R) :=
      ModuleCat.liftedModuleMonoidalStruct.{u, u}
    letI : MonoidalCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R) :=
      ModuleCat.liftedModuleMonoidal.{u, u}
    let R₀ := (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj
      (MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorUnit (ModuleCat.{u} R))
    Nonempty (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, u} ≅
      derivedTensorProductOver.{u, u} f (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, u}.obj R₀))
declarations.comment: for a perfect homomorphism, at an arbitrary polynomial presentation, at module universe equal to the ring universe; the same statement at an arbitrary module universe is Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct_of_perfect

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.tensorFormula
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BZU with the isomorphism built, and no carried hypothesis.** Same hypotheses as
`Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct`, but the
conclusion is data: a complex of `A`-modules whose class in `D(A)` is `φ^!(R)` — by
`Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.TensorFormula.classIso` — together with the isomorphism of the
algebraic upper shriek functor of `p` with derived tensor product over `R` with that complex.

The two inputs are `Dualizing.derivedHomIsoCanonicalDerivedTensorOfPerfect`, which is Tag 0BZE in
the change-of-rings shape with the isomorphism built at the canonical Tate tensor factor, and
`Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.tensorFormulaOfDerivedHomIso`, which turns such an isomorphism
into the tensor formula. Neither extracts a witness from an existential.
declarations.statement:
def tensorFormula (p : PolynomialPresentation f)
    (hp : letI : Module p.Poly A := Module.compHom A p.toRingHom
      StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfectModule.{u, u, u + 1} (R := p.Poly) A) :
    TensorFormula.{u, u} p
declarations.comment: at an arbitrary polynomial presentation, at module universe equal to the ring universe, with no carried hypothesis, and with the isomorphism built rather than shown to exist — at the constructed tensor factor of Tag 08YU, whose class in D(A) is the value of upper shriek at R rather than a prescribed representative of it

declarations.name: Dualizing.relativeDualizingComplexBaseChange_of_perfect
declarations.doc:
Let `R → R'` be a ring homomorphism, let `φ : R → A` be a perfect homomorphism presented by
`p`, and let `A` and `R'` be Tor independent over `R`.  Then the relative dualizing complex
commutes with base change to `R'`: there is an isomorphism `ω^•_{A/R} ⊗_A^L A' ≅ ω^•_{A'/R'}` in
`D(A')`, where `A' = R' ⊗_R A` and the derived tensor product is read at the given left-derived
model of extension of scalars.  The Noetherian hypotheses of the source are not needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDualizingComplexBaseChange_of_perfect [Algebra.Perfect R A]
    (p : PolynomialPresentation (algebraMap R A))
    (hTor : TorIndependent R A R')
    (bcT : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (TensorProduct R R' A)))
    (cmpT : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ bcT ⟶
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, u}
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight :
            A →ₐ[R] TensorProduct R R' A).toRingHom).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (ldT : bcT.IsLeftDerivedFunctor cmpT
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) :
    Nonempty (bcT.obj (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, 0}.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R R))) ≅
        (p.baseChange (R' := R')).upperShriekFunctor.{u, 0}.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R') 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R' R')))
declarations.comment: case (3), R → A perfect and A, R' Tor independent

declarations.name: Dualizing.relativeDualizingComplexBaseChange_of_flatBaseChange
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, `R → R'` a flat ring homomorphism, and let `φ : R → A` be of
finite type, presented by `p`.  Then the relative dualizing complex commutes with base change to
`R'`: there is an isomorphism `ω^•_{A/R} ⊗_A^L A' ≅ ω^•_{A'/R'}` in `D(A')`, where
`A' = R' ⊗_R A` and the derived tensor product is read at the given left-derived model of
extension of scalars.  The source's Noetherian hypothesis on `R'` is not needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDualizingComplexBaseChange_of_flatBaseChange [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (p : PolynomialPresentation (algebraMap R A))
    (hflat : (algebraMap R R').Flat)
    (bcT : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (TensorProduct R R' A)))
    (cmpT : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ bcT ⟶
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, u}
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight :
            A →ₐ[R] TensorProduct R R' A).toRingHom).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (ldT : bcT.IsLeftDerivedFunctor cmpT
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) :
    Nonempty (bcT.obj (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, 0}.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R R))) ≅
        (p.baseChange (R' := R')).upperShriekFunctor.{u, 0}.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R') 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R' R')))
declarations.comment: case (1), R → R' flat

declarations.name: Dualizing.relativeDualizingComplexBaseChange_of_flatAlgebra
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, `R → R'` a ring homomorphism, and let `φ : R → A` be flat
and of finite type, presented by `p`.  Then the relative dualizing complex commutes with base
change to `R'`: there is an isomorphism `ω^•_{A/R} ⊗_A^L A' ≅ ω^•_{A'/R'}` in `D(A')`, where
`A' = R' ⊗_R A` and the derived tensor product is read at the given left-derived model of
extension of scalars.  The source's Noetherian hypothesis on `R'` is not needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDualizingComplexBaseChange_of_flatAlgebra [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (p : PolynomialPresentation (algebraMap R A))
    (hflat : (algebraMap R A).Flat)
    (bcT : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (TensorProduct R R' A)))
    (cmpT : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ bcT ⟶
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, u}
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight :
            A →ₐ[R] TensorProduct R R' A).toRingHom).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (ldT : bcT.IsLeftDerivedFunctor cmpT
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) :
    Nonempty (bcT.obj (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, 0}.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R R))) ≅
        (p.baseChange (R' := R')).upperShriekFunctor.{u, 0}.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R') 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R' R')))
declarations.comment: case (2), R → A flat

declarations.name: Dualizing.upperShriekFunctor_unit_derivedCategoryBBounded_of_perfect
declarations.doc:
Let `φ : R →+* A` be a perfect homomorphism of finite type of Noetherian rings. Then the
relative dualizing complex `ω_{A/R} = φ^!(R)` lies in `Dᵇ_Coh(A)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem upperShriekFunctor_unit_derivedCategoryBBounded_of_perfect
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing A] (p : PolynomialPresentation f) (hf : f.Perfect) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
      (fun N : ModuleCat.{max v u} A ↦ Module.Finite A N)
      (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, v}.obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) 0).obj
          (ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{v} R))))

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.relativeDualizingComplex_hasFiniteTorDimension_of_perfect
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BZW] (1)(b).**  Let `φ : R →+* A` be a perfect homomorphism, presented by `p`.
Then the relative dualizing complex `ω^•_{A/R} = φ^!(R)` has finite Tor dimension as a complex of
`R`-modules.  The Noetherian hypotheses of the source are not needed.

Perfectness of `φ` is perfectness of `A` over the polynomial algebra of any presentation
([stacks 068Y], `Algebra.Perfect.exists_finite_projective_resolution` read through [stacks 066Q]),
and that is the hypothesis of `relativeDualizingComplex_hasFiniteTorDimension_of_isPerfectModule`.

Finite Tor dimension over `R` is read at the canonical certified derived tensor product, which is
the one the definition of relative perfection ([stacks 0DHS]) is written with.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDualizingComplex_hasFiniteTorDimension_of_perfect [Algebra.Perfect R A]
    (p : PolynomialPresentation (algebraMap R A)) :
    StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasFiniteTorDimension
      (CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct R).tensor
      (StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.canonicalTensorComparison R)
      (StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.canonicalTensorIsLeftDerived R)
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R A)).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, 0}.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R R))))

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.relativeDualizingComplex_isRelativelyPerfect
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BZW] (2)(a).**  Let `φ : R → A` be a flat homomorphism of finite type of
Noetherian rings, presented by `p`.  Then `ω^•_{A/R} = φ^!(R)` is perfect relative to `R` in the
sense of [stacks 0DHS].

Nothing is carried.  Relative perfection is by definition the conjunction of pseudo-coherence over
`A` and finite Tor dimension over `R`: the first is [stacks 0BZW] (1)(a), available as
`Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.relativeDualizingComplex_isPseudoCoherent_of_flat`, and the
second is [stacks 0BZW] (1)(b), which is
`Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.relativeDualizingComplex_hasFiniteTorDimension_of_flat` above.

This is the same statement as
`Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.relativeDualizingComplex_isRelativelyPerfect_of_flat` of
`StacksFrontier.RingTheory.Dualizing.UpperShriek.RelativePerfection`, which reaches it by the
fibrewise criterion [stacks 0GHJ] and therefore carries the open projection-formula compatibility
`Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.ProjectionCompatibility` at every residue field of `R`.  Here
nothing is carried; both are kept, the two routes being independent.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDualizingComplex_isRelativelyPerfect
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (p : PolynomialPresentation (algebraMap R A)) (hflat : (algebraMap R A).Flat) :
    letI : Module.Flat R A := RingHom.flat_algebraMap_iff.mp hflat
    letI : Algebra.FinitePresentation R A :=
      Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_finiteType.mp (RingHom.finiteType_algebraMap.mp p.finiteType)
    PseudoCoherence.IsRelativelyPerfect.{u, u, u}
      (CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct R).tensor
      (StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.canonicalTensorComparison R)
      (StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.canonicalTensorIsLeftDerived R)
      (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, 0}.obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R R)))

declarations.name: Dualizing.upperShriekFunctor_unit_isIso_derivedHomothety_of_perfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BZW (1)(c).**  Let `φ : R →+* A` be a perfect homomorphism of finite
type of Noetherian rings, presented by an arbitrary polynomial presentation `p`.  Then the
canonical map `A ⟶ RHom_A(ω_{A/R}, ω_{A/R})` of [Stacks, Tag 0A7C] — the derived homothety of the
adjunction of [Stacks, Tag 0A63] at `ω_{A/R} = φ^!(R)` — is an isomorphism.

The source's proof: a perfect ring map is perfect through the polynomial algebra `P` of every
presentation ([Stacks, Tag 068Y], `Algebra.Perfect.exists_finite_projective_resolution` read
through [Stacks, Tag 066Q]), perfectness survives the universe lift to the module universe in
which upper shriek is formed (`StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfectModule_ulift`), and then
`Dualizing.upperShriekFunctor_unit_isIso_derivedHomothety_of_isPerfectModule` reads
`RHom_A(ω_{A/R}, ω_{A/R})` in `D(P)` as the double dual of `A` and concludes by
[Stacks, Tag 07VI].  Noetherianity of `A` is not needed by the proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem upperShriekFunctor_unit_isIso_derivedHomothety_of_perfect [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (p : PolynomialPresentation f) (hf : f.Perfect) :
    IsIso (derivedHomothety (StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedHomAdjunctionOverRing.{u, v} A)
      (StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedTensorUnit.{u, v} A)
      (StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedTensorUnitLeft.{u, v} A)
      (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, v}.obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) 0).obj
          (ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{v} R)))))

declarations.name: Dualizing.isDualizingComplex_derivedExtensionScalars_relativeDualizing_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BZW (2)(b).**  Let `φ : R → A` be a flat homomorphism of finite type of
Noetherian rings, presented by an arbitrary polynomial presentation `p`, and let `R → k` be a
homomorphism to a field.  Then the derived base change of `ω^•_{A/R} = φ^!(R)` along the
coprojection `A → k ⊗_R A` is a dualizing complex for the fibre ring `k ⊗_R A`.

The source's proof: base change for the relative dualizing complex, [Stacks, Tag 0BZV] case (2)
at `R' = k`, identifies the derived base change with `ω^•_{A'/k}` for `A' = k ⊗_R A`, which is a
dualizing complex by [Stacks, Tag 0BZL]; this is
`Dualizing.isDualizingComplex_derivedExtensionScalars_upperShriekFunctor_unit_of_field`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDualizingComplex_derivedExtensionScalars_relativeDualizing_of_flat
    {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [Algebra R A] (k : Type u) [Field k] [Algebra R k]
    (p : PolynomialPresentation (algebraMap R A)) (hflat : (algebraMap R A).Flat) :
    letI : IsNoetherianRing (TensorProduct R k A) := isNoetherianRing_baseChange k p
    IsDualizingComplex
      ((CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, u}
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight :
            A →ₐ[R] TensorProduct R k A).toRingHom).functor.obj
        (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, 0}.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R R))))

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.nonempty_restrict_derivedPullback_upperShriek_iso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0BZY] (makeshift base change).** In Situation 48.16.1 let `X' = X ×_Y Y'` be a
cartesian square of `FTS S` with `f` flat, let `E ∈ D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` with `Lg^*E` bounded below,
and let `j`, `j'` be compactifications computing `f^!` and `f'^!`. For an affine open `U' ⊆ X'`
mapping into affine opens `U ⊆ X`, `V' ⊆ Y'`, `V ⊆ Y` of the square (`g'(U') ⊆ U`,
`f'(U') ⊆ V'`, `f(U) ⊆ V`, `g(V') ⊆ V`), the restrictions to `U'` of `L(g')^*f^!E` and
`(f')^!Lg^*E` are isomorphic.

*The reading of "mapping into affine opens".* The source asks for `U' ⊂ X'` "affine open mapping
into affine opens of `Y`, `Y'`, and `X`", and its proof begins "we immediately reduce to the case
where `X`, `Y`, `Y'`, and `X'` are affine", which needs the four affine opens to form a cartesian
square of affines; so the opens are a compatible quadruple, `f(U) ⊆ V` and `g(V') ⊆ V`. Three
independently chosen affine opens containing the images of `U'` need not form such a square:
`U ∩ f⁻¹(V)` need not be affine (the base `S` is not assumed separated), so no single affine chart
of `f` need contain `g'(U')`.

The proof is the source's: on the charts both sides are the sheaves
associated to the algebraic base change
`Dualizing.nonempty_totalDerivedExtensionScalars_upperShriekFunctor_iso_of_isOpenImmersion`, by
the chart description `Stacks.Duality.upperShriekCharts` of [Stacks, Tag 0BV2].
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_restrict_derivedPullback_upperShriek_iso
    {X X' Y Y' : AlgebraicGeometry.FTS S} (f : X ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (g' : X' ⟶ X)
    (sq : IsPullback g'.left f'.left f.left g.left) [Flat f.left]
    (j : AlgebraicGeometry.CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left))
    (j' : AlgebraicGeometry.CompactificationOf (Over.mk f'.left))
    (E : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y.left) (hE : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow E.obj)
    (hE' : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow ((quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' g.left).obj E).obj)
    {U' : X'.left.Opens} (hU' : IsAffineOpen U') {U : X.left.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    {V' : Y'.left.Opens} (hV' : IsAffineOpen V') {V : Y.left.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (hU'U : U' ≤ g'.left ⁻¹ᵁ U) (hU'V' : U' ≤ f'.left ⁻¹ᵁ V') (hUV : U ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
    (hV'V : V' ≤ g.left ⁻¹ᵁ V) :
    Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U'.ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        ((quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' g'.left).obj ((upperShriek f j).obj E)).obj ≅
      (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U'.ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        ((upperShriek f' j').obj ((quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' g.left).obj E)).obj)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isDualizingComplex_derivedPullback_fibreι_upperShriek_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0BZZ (Lemma 48.18.4).** In Situation 48.16.1 let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a flat
morphism of `FTS S` and set `ω^•_{X/Y} = f^!𝒪_Y`, for any compactification `j` defining `f^!`.
For `y ∈ Y` let `h : X_y ⟶ X` be the projection from the fibre. Then `Lh^*ω^•_{X/Y}` is a
dualizing complex on `X_y`.

The fibre charts over the affine charts of `f` cover `X_y`; on each, by
`Stacks.Duality.upperShriekStructureSheafCharts` and [Stacks, Tag 08DW], `Lh^*ω^•_{X/Y}` is the
sheaf associated to `ω^•_{A/R} ⊗ᴸ_A (A ⊗_R κ(y))`, which is dualizing by [Stacks, Tag 0BZW];
[Stacks, Tag 0A86] glues.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDualizingComplex_derivedPullback_fibreι_upperShriek_unconditional [Flat f.left]
